Y-you'd better have proof of that, if you're so capable!
Lord, what are you saying? Please don't wrong a good citizen like me.

I was thinking... how could it be so coincidental? Out of so many rooms, he didn't steal from anyone else, yet he just happened to break into yours. And you just happened to use the sedative, which conveniently knocked this person out. You wouldn't be involved in something shady, would you?
Lord Song, why are you looking at me like that?
Heaven has eyes; by a stroke of luck, you have captured this thief. Otherwise, who knows how many innocent women's purity would have been ruined by this scoundrel.
If he were foolish, why would the authorities be so troubled? I never expected him to be so bold as to sneak into the Nangong family and plot something sinister.
He's not a foolish thief?

This scoundrel is the infamous Soul-Stealing Thief named in the wanted notices. He breaks into homes with incense smoke to rob and defile women, then kills them for their wealth after his crimes. He is utterly wicked.
Go fetch some rope, tie up that thief, and as soon as dawn breaks, deliver them to the magistrate's office.
I've never seen such a foolish thief
Hmph, I originally wanted to struggle a bit, but I can't muster any strength in my hands and feet. It seems I'm done for; do as you wish.
Are you hurt?
How despicable, what a vile person! I used a fragrant powder on you, but unexpectedly, you used it on me as well. With our fragrances mingling, I felt dizzy and disoriented.
Who is it!

...In the dream realm, serving in the bedchamber cannot lead to the bearing of offspring. If my dear wishes to seek pleasure, it would be best to come find me soon; at that time, I will submit to your wishes.
Come serve in my bed

She gives you the highest peak, gives you the hardest match, lets you climb to the summit, lets you be tempered through a hundred trials.
Just as she vowed back then, she offers this heart, this body, every stratagem, to you.
Every stone she lays is for your delight alone.

You play as Black, while Ruixing plays as White. The battle on the board resembles a tender entanglement; she is reluctant to determine a winner. With gentle guidance, she occasionally tempts you and sometimes offers you a taste of sweetness, at times warm like summer, and at other times cold and sharp like winter.
Yes
Let's play chess
Zhao Jun, come see me soon. Tomorrow is the great battle; please take care of yourself and do not forget that I am still in the Apricot Blossom Forest, waiting for your forgiveness.
To be honest, I have long wanted to try the feeling of serving someone. Just imagining it makes my heart itch, yet I can't quite reach it.
Okay
Alright, then I will massage your shoulders, knead your legs, and sing a song for you, okay?
There's nothing much to say
I only ask that Lord Zhao take care of themselves and not forget that I am still in the apricot blossom forest, waiting for your forgiveness.
...At that time, I did not yet know Zhao Jun, and I was very indifferent. You blame me, but I have no words to respond.
In summary, all the tragedies arise because of me.

Born in adversity, die in comfort.
One must shape an enemy to unite the forces of the Central Plains Wulin; there is no pawn better suited than the Mud Cult.
I seized the chance to support my cousin and have him raised to Alliance Leader, to serve one day as my hidden blade for seizing the realm.

The one who urged the old master to offer his head is also me. If he does not die, it will be difficult to awaken the various factions' anger, let alone unite them. If things remain lukewarm, the ideal of great unity will forever be unattainable.

I knew it would happen, and I intervened. All the evil consequences are because of me. It was I who ordered the Thousand Lantern Tower assassins to attack the bases of various schools and factions, framing the Mud Cult for it.
Is Lord Zhao asking about the beginning or the end?
Was the battle of Jiangling back then your doing?
What words do you wish to share with me today?
Zhao Jun, you're dreaming again
As you think and think, you eventually drift off into a hazy sleep.

No, it's better if she doesn't come. She will definitely do something ridiculous and end up getting captured by the enemy. The consequences of a girl as beautiful as her being taken prisoner are simply unimaginable.
Otherwise, the battlefield of Jiangling would be a great opportunity for Sister Xiang to make a name for herself in the world.

With such a significant matter in Jiangling, Jinxiang Palace is clearly not far away. Why haven't they sent anyone to provide support? It is well known that Nangong and Jinxiang have a good relationship, so the palace master, Lady Wen, seems a bit indifferent.

Great Hero Nangong Yuan also wished to remarry and tried every means to win her favor, but was repeatedly turned away by Lady Wen.
Still, since Jinxiang Palace's founding had relied on considerable support from Nangong, she never forbade her disciples from keeping in contact with them.
This time, however, she seemed to have made up her mind, and would not come to Jiangling's aid.
After the Great Benefactor Wen passed away, Lady Wen became a widow. As a woman of delicate constitution, she single‑handedly founded Jinxiang Palace, which is quite remarkable.

The relationship between Dongting Jinxiang Palace and the Nangong family of Jiangling is indeed quite delicate.
People say that Great Hero Nangong Yuan, in his youth, had a deep friendship with Lady Wen, Palace Mistress of Jinxiang Palace,
but somehow, Lady Wen ended up marrying Great Benefactor Wen, who knew nothing of martial arts.

Sigh... I can't possibly compete with them for the position of sect leader. Not to mention that I'm not a Kongtong Disciple and lack the qualifications; even if I were sent out, what would give me the chance to win? In the end, it's just wishful thinking.
Soon, there will be a major election for the Sect Leader of Kongtong. At that time, the Four Beauties‑Mei, Lan, Zhu, and Ju‑will all have to marry the Sect Leader as their wives.

Whether the Tang Clan truly considers me, an outsider disciple, as one of their own is hard to say. Am I really supposed to take Miss Ying back to the countryside to meet my parents? No... that must not happen. I have already severed ties with them.

Although I admire her, even if the heavens sent down a divine thunderbolt and struck Miss Ying mad,
making her willing to go home with me, how could my humble family ever compare with the Nangong family?

Miss Ying is currently staying with the Nangong family, and has also brought a group of subordinates from the Cang Gang to help.
Judging by the attitude of everyone in the Nangong household, it's clear they already treat her as one of their own.

With the old Family Head stepping in, Brother Fan should have safely returned to the Beggar Sect by now.
Tomorrow on the battlefield, it's best to keep our distance from him, so we won't feel awkward if we run into him and not know whose side to take.

Brother Ye, for his sister's sake, is still tirelessly seeking medicine, and his reputation grows worse by the day.
The once-renowned Cangsong Swordsman is no longer mentioned; people now call him a pill thief.

I wonder if Yunshang's condition has improved. I also don't know what chronic illness she has that is so difficult to treat. No matter how many miraculous medicines she has taken, even if there are a few days of improvement, she still cannot fully recover.

The junior martial sister is already a beautiful young miss, and the number of female disciples in the sect has increased. For me to squat beneath the window is no longer fitting. Perhaps it's better for me to have some self‑awareness, stick to my principles, and avoid causing any more trouble for her? Before she develops aversion towards me, I should take a step back.
The Junior Martial Sister has grown up; she no longer needs me to keep her company by the window. Sigh, I have finally fulfilled the request of the Master's Wife, but now she no longer needs me.

The Sect Leader's condition is uncertain.
Second Senior Brother has been treating him, but his complexion still hasn't improved, which worries me.

Oh no... I'm really in trouble.
Thinking back to when Master taught me martial arts, every frown and smile of hers set my heart pounding.
Not just because she's breathtakingly beautiful, but because she's cold as ice, yet smiles only for me.
A heart of respect, plus romantic feelings
You pondered over this matter, and your mood became clear and bright. The Bewitching Incense took effect, and you fell into a deep sleep.
Great!

...It's purely a heart of reverence.
The proof is that I still hold someone else in my heart.
Master's beauty may leave me in awe, but it stirs no improper thoughts in me.
A heart of pure reverence

But I might die tomorrow, and if I still run from my own feelings, that would be too pathetic.
What do I really feel for Master, anyway?
So disrespectful!
Can't blame me for that, can I? It's Master's fault for looking so good.

...Whenever I think of Master, my heart grows warm.
Could it be that I've developed improper feelings for her?
Unknowingly, you have already forgotten your unease, your heart filled only with thoughts of Xiahou Lan.
... After the six‑month period, my master no longer allows me to call her master. So how should I address her? Lady Xiahou, Miss Xiahou, or Xiahou the Female Hero?

Only Master Xiahou has truly treated me well. I don't know how much of it is teasing and how much is sincere,
but in just these few short months, the debt I owe her for teaching me is enough that I'll never forget it.
In the end, the martial arts skills I have, which are neither here nor there, were all learned haphazardly.

As it turned out, I drifted along in the Tang Clan, and so many years passed; people came and went, but I remained.
Only I'm still an outer disciple to this day. Why won't any master take me in?
If the sect leader would just permit it, even teaching me the mnemonics and Internal Method would do - I could study them myself.

The year I left home to climb the mountain and become a disciple, I was filled with hope, vowing to become a truly formidable Great Hero,
respected wherever I went, no longer mocked or ridiculed, but met with bows and words of long-held admiration.

...No, I can't sleep.
Tomorrow won't be a mere scuffle - it'll be a fight to the death the moment we meet.
I still have so much left undone. How could I resign myself to dying?
You immediately prepared the Bewitching Incense, extinguished the candle, lay down on the bed, closed your eyes, and thought of nothing.

After the two left, you filled a basin with water and returned to your room to wipe off the sweat. By candlelight, you flipped through the catalog for a while, unable to contain your joy. You compared a few things with the illustrations, feeling as if you gained something, and only then did you feel satisfied enough to go to bed.
...What a wonderful pair they are, a match made in heaven with talent and beauty. Every step taken alongside Miss Ying is a luxury I long for but cannot attain.
Farewell.
The night is deepening, Ying'er, I'll take you back to your room. Brother Zhao, the great battle tomorrow will still require your help; the Young Lord here thanks you in advance and is departing.

Damn it, with such a great contribution, if you're going to give me something, at least make it worthwhile. Sending a manual that won't help me cultivate peerless martial arts is rather stingy. Otherwise, just give me the money directly.
Well then... I humbly accept it with gratitude.

This man is truly something; first he escaped from Liu E's grasp, then he captured Tan Badao. If it were anyone else, achievements like that would have already made them famous — so how come you're still doing so miserably?
Haha, Young Lord, you flatter me. I'm just helping Eldest Senior Brother and Second Senior Brother with some chores.

You and Great Hero Tang, along with the Second Hero Tang, emerged to capture Tan Badao and clear the injustice against my clan. It would not be an exaggeration to say that you are benefactors of the Nangong family. This gift is merely a personal token of respect from this Young Lord; please do not refuse it.
Just now, the Young Lord took a trip from death back to life.
Shangguan Ying's shame was uncontainable; she instinctively raised her hand to punch him, but thankfully caught herself in time and pulled it back.

My fiancee has fallen into the hands of evil bandits. If it weren't for your selfless rescue, how could I ever hope to see her again in this lifetime? No matter how heavy the gift, you would deserve it.
Brother Zhao, how can you say it's unfounded? The relationship between the Tang Clan and the Nangong family is quite significant; you shouldn't be too distant.
How can I accept such a valuable gift without any reason?

This book is titled Wushan Cave Mansion Nine Treasures Diagram. Although studying it may not allow one to master peerless martial arts, it can help harmonize the dual principles and nurture the five elements. It is sure to be of great benefit to you.
Ying'er, you don't know this. That's exactly why he needs a gentle, moderate internal skill to balance the yin and yang within his body.
Young Lord, why are you still giving him an internal skill secret manual? Didn't you say that's very dangerous?
...Brother Zhao, if you don't mind, then this Young Lord will gift you a manual of Internal Skill.

Often, when a secret manual comes into my hands, I can only learn about forty or fifty percent of it. When I encounter a manual on Internal Skill, sometimes practicing it makes my whole body feel off. It must be a clash of Yin and Yang; that kind of martial art, I dare not force myself to practice.
Occasionally, one does encounter such situations. Since I can't force myself to succeed, I won't push it. If it works, I'll remember it; if I can't understand it, I won't seek to delve deeper.
Is that so? That insatiable Zhao Huo — surely he hasn't already given himself some lasting ailment?
How could that work? Each sect's martial arts, Internal Methods, and forms all differ. One misstep and Qi Deviation is common enough — nothing is more dangerous.

I must have embarrassed the Young Lord, sigh. It's just that for years I haven't been made an inner disciple, so I was never taught the oral formulas, and I can't fathom my school's profound martial arts. I can only gather secret manuals from all over and practice on my own, haphazardly.

However, to speak of it, as the Young Lord saw just now, Brother Zhao's techniques seemed like Tang Clan martial arts, yet not quite Tang Clan martial arts. Faint traces of other sects were discernible, but upon closer inspection, it seemed somewhat similar yet not exactly‑what could it be?
No need for such formalities, Brother Zhao
It's no big deal; my three‑legged cat skills have only made you laugh.
Not at all — this is your esteemed residence. I was worried I might disturb the peace of your household.

I wondered who it was, and it turned out to be Brother Zhao practicing here. Lady Shangguan and I happened to pass by without any intention of peeking. I apologize for the abruptness towards Brother Zhao and ask for your forgiveness.
Young Lord Nangong, good evening, Miss Shangguan
Huh, let it be like this, just for one night. Even sharpening the spear at the last moment isn't enough. As long as I sweat a little, a good sleep will be enough.

You hurried back to the Nangong estate to inform the head of the Nangong family.
The orthodox sects were placed on high alert upon hearing the news, but after a night passed, no one reported being attacked.
I hope she's not coming to assassinate the experts of every faction; I'd better hurry back to report this and warn everyone to stay on guard.

...She's gone.
Her movements were incredibly fast, her footwork exquisite, and her dagger technique a mix of styles, as if she were deliberately hiding her true school. I couldn't make sense of it.
You were suddenly interrupted, leaving you momentarily speechless.
There's no need to say more. Naturally, the deer will die by your hand, and you will die by mine.
We shall see by whose hand the deer falls.

Hmph, fine then, I won't fight anymore.
I have important matters to attend to tonight and no time to deal with you, a nameless nobody.
You've managed to save your life; remember to burn incense and pray when you get home.
I'm afraid that's difficult to comply with
Bullshit, why don't you stick your head out and let me chop it off?
Why are you so hard to kill? Can't you just be honest and offer your neck for the blade?

Seeing Xiaomei eased your anxious heart considerably.
After tidying up a bit, you returned to your room to wash up and go to sleep.
...Alright, I'll clean my backside and wait for you to come.

She's gone...
She said she wants to visit the Tang Clan, but I'll need to survive tomorrow's battle first to make it back.
Hahaha! You think too highly of yourself; just wait and see while you clean your backside!
Heroine, spare me!

The death penalty can be avoided, but the living punishment is hard to escape.
I have matters to attend to tonight, so remember that you owe me one.
Next time when Mei has free time, I'll make a special trip to the Tang Clan and stab your backside with a flurry of blades.
I didn't know it was you!
Although I am not a Lady Thief, when you shot a hidden weapon at my backside, I truly intended to kill you.
So it's you. I thought I was really going to encounter a Lady Thief today, who would kill me to silence me.
Xiaomei!
You didn't expect it, did you? It's me, Mei!
Your voice sounds so familiar...
Haha, alright, I won't tease you anymore
You tidied up the surroundings a bit, picked up the Hidden Weapons you had thrown, and then went back to your room to sleep.
Senior Brother really is Senior Brother; no matter how I think about it, I don't feel I have any chance of winning. Not to mention, I have no idea what it means for him to get serious.
I got too immersed and almost scared myself to death.
Wow──!
The things you vaguely perceive, through this hypothetical battle, gradually become clear, and finally come under your control.
The premise is that Senior Brother doesn't use his ultimate move and doesn't get serious.
I might have a chance, perhaps
You stabbed me in the butt with a hidden weapon, and now you still want to live? Just obediently go die, you filthy scoundrel.
...Oh, since the target is not me, why don't we turn our conflict into harmony?
Ha, you're quite confident for an ugly Young Hero. Then go die.
If you want to silence me for good, it might not be that easy.
My target is someone else; I never intended to harm you. However, since you've uncovered my actions, I have no choice but to eliminate you to keep my secrets safe.
Absolutely not!
If it's my body you're after... we can negotiate.
Huh?
Your martial arts skills are nothing special, and you dress so poorly. What could I possibly want from you? Do you think I desire your beauty?
Heroine, spying on others as they train is a grave taboo in the Jianghu. You're dressed all in black with your face covered; can I assume you mean me ill?
That's something you should be answering, Heroine.
Is your martial arts skill very good? Why should I spy on you?
May I ask who you are and why you are observing me practice?
I didn't expect you to be quite capable, able to sense that I was lurking nearby.
Who is it! Quickly reveal yourself!
Ah!
Ambushed Lady Thief: Ugh!
You tidied up the surroundings a bit, retrieved the hidden weapons you had thrown and the carcass of your prey, then went back to your room to sleep.
I killed quite a few livestock, then went back to skin them and sell the hides.
These animals did not provoke you, yet you are so ruthless.

Your skill in discerning sounds and locating their source has reached a considerable level; no rustle in the forest can escape your keen hearing. With hidden weapons everywhere, whether it be a deer, a poison snake, a squirrel, a rabbit, or a fox, anything that moves within your vicinity meets an untimely end.
Mass slaughter of forest animals
Clearly, you didn't hit anything, but in your imagination, the hidden weapons you launched have already taken down ten senior brothers.
That move I just performed was truly impressive. Tomorrow on the battlefield, I will use this technique to astonish everyone!
Feeling pretty cool about yourself
...Hmph.
Drink up!
No, that's not it. I can even feel the slightest rustle of the wind, the buzzing of mosquitoes, and the movement of insects. It's as if I've realized something.
Is it that my eyes have adapted to the night? Everything is becoming clearer.

It is precisely because the sky darkens and visibility becomes difficult that countless thoughts cannot disturb you. You gradually eliminate your worries and faintly touch upon a wondrous state where the eyes do not see, yet everything is within your grasp.
You swing your fists and feet in the open forest, illuminated only by a few dim candlelights.
...No, let's practice a bit longer. I still feel restless and can't calm down.
You bid farewell to Ye Yunzhou with a clasped hand, feeling much more at ease upon encountering friends in a foreign land. With tomorrow's battle ahead, you feel a greater sense of confidence.
Alright, Brother Ye, please
Brother Zhao, it's getting late; please head back. Tomorrow we will fight side by side against the enemy, please.
Younger Sister, you are truly heartless
Ah, but if the situation becomes more dangerous, just let him die.
After all, Brother Zhao can barely be considered a brother, and the least valuable kind at that.
What I ask of you is, if you see him in Jiangling and he does not value his life, only focused on fighting, then please, Brother, draw your sword to protect him.
No, that's not good either
That's good
Don't worry, I am polite to everyone and try to please them. My misdeeds have always been directed solely at Brother Zhao.
Living under someone else's roof, you really need to change that sharp tongue of yours. I can still tolerate it, but don't speak so freely to others.
Unlike you, Brother Zhao is a useless person. Not only is he unattractive, weak, and foolish, but he also has the look of someone who would easily be killed by others.
With a sword in hand, one can still manage.
Um... Brother, your martial arts skills are very impressive, right?
Speak
A little. But I called you because there's something else I want to ask of you.
What's wrong? Are you starting to miss me?
Ah, Brother, wait a moment
Brother, don't focus solely on me in everything. I'm doing well here. Whether it's you or me, we only live once; let's not leave any regrets.
Good~

...I understand. I'll buy some durable pastries for you. Since we're in Jiangling, let's handle a few matters and head back. You'd better be good, don't cause any trouble, and stop bullying Little Miss Tang.
Like the famous ones from Jiangling Prefecture.
The snacks in the nearby villages are too coarse; I don't like them. I want to eat something better, more expensive, and more exquisite.
Not that either?
Not that either.
Then I'll go help out at the shop opened by the Tang Clan, earn some money, and buy you some snacks to eat.
Brother Tang Er already said my illness needs the right medicine to match. If even he can't cure it, then you might as well stop wasting your effort.
Sigh
Brother, you pretended to leave, but you're actually hiding in the tree, aren't you?
...Alright, it's up to you.
Stop looking for more medicine. I've swallowed more medicine than I've eaten meat, and none of it has ever worked. I'm not taking any more — if you like it so much, you eat it yourself!
Younger Sister, how can you say that? I have been running around everywhere, seeking medicine for you; I may not have made any contributions, but I have certainly put in a lot of effort.

I am perfectly capable on my own, so there's no need for you to be anxious. Even if I do fall ill, Brother Tang Er will be there to treat me. Meanwhile, you just stand by, worrying and fidgeting, which is of no use at all‑it's quite useless, really.
If I were to travel far, who would take care of you?
Brother, I will stay here. You go to Jiangling; I know you really want to go.
So that's the connection behind it.

In years past, Great Hero Nangong Yuan visited Diancang. Learning of my sister's condition, he transmitted a palm strike carrying his family's protective True Qi and gave her pills to help her recover. This kindness cannot go unreturned.
With Brother Ye's assistance, I definitely won't die no matter what.

The debt has been repaid, but the favor remains. Brother Zhao, in tomorrow's great battle, Ye will hide in the shadows to assist. You only need to give a shout, and the Listening Cloud Sword will respond and unsheathe itself.
The money has been returned, yet you still dwell on this matter.

First, I repay the Nangong family head's kindness in providing medicine to save my sister from that year. Second, I repay Brother Zhao's generous assistance last year, sacrificing themselves in the boat.
Ye is here to repay a debt of gratitude.

Ye knows his own limits and dares not press too close, only moving within a certain range. Wearing a bamboo hat and not donning Diancang colors, he expects it won't be easy for others to see through the disguise.
However, Brother Ye, how did you come to Jiangling? The people of the Central Plains' Wulin have gathered here, and your sect's masters are among them. Isn't your visit a bit risky?

...She's already gone and done it. It's all just harmless fooling around, but I feared she might get carried away, so I, Ye, left the Tang Clan, hoping it would make her wary enough not to act rashly.
Yunshang wouldn't really go so far as to hurt Junior Martial Sister, would she? Would she?
How could that be? I'm just worried that with the two of them playing together, your sister might not be able to keep up.
Brother Zhao, are you worried that my foolish younger sister doesn't know her limits and has bullied your sect's Junior Martial Sister?
Indeed, the Junior Martial Sister from your esteemed sect is pure‑hearted and truly a good companion. I only hope Shang'er can exercise some restraint and not bully those who are honest and kind.
Sister Yunshang has a playmate; she must be so happy she's forgotten her homeland... forgotten Dali.
She did not come. Second Hero Tang instructed her not to move around. After she befriended the Junior Martial Sister of your sect, she no longer cared for her brother and sent me away.
Brother Ye! How did you come to Jiangling? Could it be that your younger sister has come as well?
Brother Zhao, it is Ye who has arrived.
...Who is it?

Even seasoned generals who have long endured the battlefield know to value their lives. They are not immune to blade and spear; who is so reckless as to gladly die for someone else's war? At the very least, you are not. You do value loyalty and honor, but you also want to live well.

You are still feeling a chaotic mix of emotions, knowing that tomorrow's decisive battle will be unlike any before. To this day, both sides have their reservations, but once it comes to an open break with the Beggar Sect, there will be no room to turn back, and the casualties will surely be severe.
Whew, let's do it this way. Just one night; even cramming at the last moment won't be enough. As long as I work up a sweat, a good sleep will do.

Outrageous — if you won't let me sleep, then I'll sleep no matter what.
I'd rather knock myself out with a knockout drug than stay awake. Where's my medicine box?
Persist in sleeping with anger

No, it's better to practice somewhere remote where no one's around.
I'm just an outer disciple of the Tang Clan — if someone sees me practicing in the Nangong family's courtyard,
they'll inevitably make a fuss over it, either saying I'm showing off or mocking me.
...Go to the courtyard and practice a set of punches before sleeping.
Go practice martial arts to relax

I wanted to turn in early and rest up.
But I toss and turn, unable to fall asleep.

Although I want to be famous, a clash between two armies is nothing to joke about.
When the time comes, I'll hide in the back and observe first, rather than rushing in to get myself killed.

That's great! Tomorrow I'll pull off a big job and make a name for myself sky-high.
Let's see who still dares judge me by my looks and look down on me.

Although I made an excuse that I was busy, the truth is I had nothing to do.
I lied to the old master, hehe.
Brother, see you later
I'll take my leave now; Grandfather is waiting for me.

Just kidding, don't be so anxious.
If you have something to do, go ahead and take care of it. Let's go.
No, no, no, how could I dare?
Even I, old as I am, can't get you to come when called; what airs you're putting on.
I still have a few matters to attend to.
I may be old, but my legs aren't crippled. The more I walk and move, the longer I can live. Don't you know that?
Isn't it customary for the old master to have the servants carry the sedan chair when going out?
Alright, let's go then
Alright

Although my martial skills are lacking, I'm not fit for the weighty task of a guard,
but since the Old Patriarch has called on me, it's just the rough work of carrying things, and I'm glad to help.
If the senior has given an order, the junior will certainly obey.
Kid, do you have some time right now? I plan to leave the city to chat with a junior. You seem quite free; will you come along?
Then why let him out? He won't go crazy and start hitting people again, will he?
Naturally, it was this old one who went to the authorities to ask for him. Fortunately, the standing this old one has built up over the years still counts for something.
Fan, Brother Fan, what happened to you...?
Indeed, thank you, Old Patriarch.
At last, this old one still has some face in the authorities. It's your friend, right? You haven't picked the wrong person, have you?
Grandpa Pauldron said he only spared me for your sake. Brother, you really do carry some weight.
Brother Fan, you've been released? That's great!
Brother!
Qian'er has made a friend, that's wonderful. This grandpa is very happy.
A'Qian!
A'Qian is just A'Qian; don't get all formal and awkward on account of this old one.
A'Qian – Second Young Lord, hello to you too.
Brother Zhao, h-hello.
What are you doing here, ugly brat?

Let's head back and get ready. Sharpen the blades that need sharpening, and touch the wives that need touching. Tomorrow will be different from the usual playful skirmishes; it will be a matter of life and death. Those who don't want to die should stay back, and those willing to risk their lives shouldn't leave any regrets.
Having spoken, the heroes of the Wulin bid farewell one after another, striding out of the hall with fervor and passion.
Eldest Young Lord, please!

On behalf of the Nangong family, I thank all the fellow practitioners of the Wulin for their trust. Please take your rest and conserve your strength. Tomorrow at noon, we will leave the city to settle our differences! Please!
Let's do it this way! We are willing to follow the Eldest Young Lord's arrangements!

If you do not mind, I would like to serve as a neutral coordinator, not seeking any credit, to assist everyone. I will specifically coordinate between the authorities and the Jianghu heroes to jointly resist the bandits. What do you all think?

This... you Great Heroes, it is too early to discuss this matter. I am but a person of limited talent and knowledge, relying on the protection of my ancestors to be able to speak among such illustrious figures. The Family Head is still my father; I am merely handling trivial matters on his behalf.
Don't let your passion cloud your judgment; suddenly being so bloodthirsty, have you caught some kind of illness?
Haha! Well done — cut off their heads and kick them around like balls!
Tomorrow, I will use the beggar's intestines to jump rope!

Oh, a real man's tears don't fall so easily-I mustn't go all weepy on you.
I'm glad it's nothing... I was afraid you'd be hurt and upset.
Hm? What's wrong with me?
I did hear about it... are you okay?
Didn't you hear? We're all retiring from the Jianghu-what are you still forging for?
What are you doing? Strike while the iron's hot‑I'm halfway through hammering it.
Xiao Zhu, Xiao Zhu, don't knock yet

Yes-we even used to bet on when he'd be driven off in a fit of anger. A month, two months, a year, two years-and it just dragged on until today. If Third Senior Brother didn't put out the lights, he probably still wouldn't want to go.
...He really saw it through to the end, didn't he.
You go ahead and chat; I'll wander around on my own.
Yeah...
No matter what, as long as we're alive, there's always a chance we'll meet again. Even if we don't visit each other often, it's nice to send a letter during the holidays.
You're right ‑ I hadn't thought this through before; I still need to consult with my wife.

Who told you to go around, with nothing better to do, and snatch someone else's sect leader throne? Now it's a hot potato you can't shake off. If you keep being this irresponsible, you'll find out how serious it is once you're wanted by the authorities.
I've retired into seclusion, and the Kongtong Sect still doesn't know how to explain it. Sigh.
Please, we entrust everything to you. Even if the Tang Clan disbands, we want the Junior Martial Sister to be well‑she is the Tang Clan's last true heir.
Do you even need to tell me that? I'll protect her for the rest of her life.
What are you muttering over there? I heard you!

{size=24}For Junior Martial Sister's future, shouldn't we take him out right now?{/size}
{size=24}Kill this guy, then talk Junior Martial Sister into finding someone reliable.{/size}
I will do bad things in the future. I guarantee I'll dispose of the bodies and leave no trace‑without the slightest slip‑up! I won't implicate Junior Martial Sister.
Don't worry, don't worry — how could that be?
Senior Brother, though I don't know what vicious scheme you've pulled off, you mustn't drag Junior Martial Sister into any wrongdoing now that you've brought her along.
She has stabbed a needle into my heart; I'm afraid it will never heal in my lifetime. I'm destined to endure torment, bleeding drop by drop until I die.
Senior Brother... haven't you come to terms with it yet?
Don't worry, I trust her.
That's not right — wherever I go, I'm not confident!
That makes sense. So I won't go to Jiangnan — where would be safe for me? ...Tubo? Mongolia?
Whoever dares lay a finger on my girl, I'll turn Jiangnan's misty rains red.

Putting aside any questions about her character, Little Miss Ye, judged by looks alone, is a peerless beauty of the age. In a few years she'll likely become even more beautiful. Jiangnan is full of charming, talented scholars‑aren't you afraid you won't be able to restrain yourself around her?
I'm thinking of heading east to take a look at Jiangnan; Yunshang longs for the water towns there.

I nearly forgot, you still have a female master to serve too — how vexing, it makes me both envious and resentful.
Why won't Heroine Xiahou come and enslave me instead?
It doesn't necessarily have to be Snow Mountain ‑ what matters is that it's a place where my master can be comfortable.
Being self‑sufficient is fine, but why insist on going to such a bitter, freezing place like Snow Mountain?
Maybe move to Snow Mountain and live as a reclusive hunter. Harbor no great ambitions and be self‑sufficient.
That's out of the question! Don't try to intimidate me!
Are you talking about Lady Shangguan? Senior Brother, you're dreaming. If I were her, the moment I found out you were this useless, I'd abandon you and remarry someone else.
Perhaps I'll try going into business; later in life I'll still have to rely on my wife.
Damn it!
Then you should hide in the back kitchen — don't show your face, or the customers will lose their appetite.
Maybe I'll open a restaurant and cook.
That's great — you seem like you were born to be in this line of work.
Maybe I'll become a carpenter, a blacksmith, or some kind of craftsman.
I haven't decided yet.
Senior Brother, how about you?

Hey, who hasn't gone through a bit of youthful rebellion? I didn't want to live a mediocre life ‑ I heard Mister Shu's Jianghu Tales would get your blood boiling, so I joined the Tang Clan. But look at me now; I've ended up like this, I'm a bit older, and I figure it's better to go home and settle down.
So you still have a family business to inherit — why did you even bother apprenticing here?
Me too. My family runs a dyeing workshop over in Zizhou; business is doing quite well, and Father and Mother are both hoping I'll inherit it.
I left the Tang Clan; maybe I won't be part of the Jianghu anymore. I'm planning to go back to my hometown in Juzhou to see what my relatives are up to, then slowly figure out how to make a living.
What does everyone plan to do? Join another sect or gang?
...Yes.

Third Senior Brother has always been unswervingly loyal to the sect; making this decision was something they had no choice about. No one is obliged to die for anyone else. We were brought together by fate, and now it's time for everyone to go their separate ways.
Hits the nail on the head.
That's true... for example, you.
If they don't disband, there will always be someone who won't give up.
Senior Brother... we've all heard that the Sect Leader, our own Senior Brother, truly means to dissolve the Tang Clan?
Fine ‑ it's not like we're no longer Brothers; that doesn't mean we can't still meet up and eat together.
After lights‑out, once we descend the mountain, let's go together and have a good meal.
Really? That's great!
If you can wait, I'll cook a simple dish right away‑though I can't promise it'll be very tasty.
Oh... all right, I'll just have to put up with it for now.
I just came in to take a look and reminisce; I wasn't preparing any food.
Junior Brother, I'm so glad you're here. Do you have anything to eat?

Thanks to my Brothers constantly coming up with new ways to make life difficult for me, I'm not short on dishes I can cook. If I stay out of the Jianghu and just be a cook running a restaurant to make a living, that doesn't seem so bad.
Practice makes perfect; over time, I too came to have a few signature dishes I could cook well.
Even if it doesn't taste good, at least it didn't poison anyone.
No one taught me specifically; I just copied what others did ‑ after all, clumsy hands would get beaten. Before I knew it, the old hands were gone, and it was my turn to take charge of the cooking.
...At the busiest times, the kitchen was like a battlefield every day. When things got overwhelming, I would be called in to be ordered around by the Senior Brothers and Sisters.
Good heavens!
What do you think? I, Mei, would love to bite a chunk out of you.
Wait ‑ you must be joking, right? You wouldn't actually want to eat that, would you?
Haha
Wahaha~ I, Mei, have my eye on your heart‑I want to dig it out and eat it.
I have no power or influence, no money or standing ‑ I really don't know what you see in me.
I was thinking, why don't I learn face‑changing from you? Even if it can't give you a whole new face, at least tidy you up a bit so you won't look so repulsive. Never mind ‑ this will do.

Ah‑don't be like that‑Xiaomei was only joking with you‑so petty. I won't say anything, I won't take revenge. As for whether you become Sect Leader or not, it doesn't matter. Marry a chicken, follow the chicken; marry a dog, follow the dog‑anyway, good sir, please don't drive me away.
I've retired from Jianghu, and naturally I won't show my face in Kongtong. If you think I'm ugly, why don't you‑

I, Mei, am narrow‑minded ‑ when someone bullies me, I have to get revenge. Besides, you're already ugly enough, and you keep wearing that sour‑puss face all day ‑ it just makes people angry to look at.
No. Even if we manage it, it won't change anything ‑ it would only put both our lives at risk.
You're still talking about this, huh?

If you really can't let it go ‑ so upset you can't even eat or drink ‑ how about after we come down the mountain we disguise ourselves and go assassinate the Wulin Alliance Leader or Commissioner Shangguan?

I, Mei, hate those so-called righteous Wulin factions too, always going on about benevolence and virtue. So what if Jinxiang Palace follows the Human Path? Those people were too scared to die themselves, yet still wanted to play the hero, striking first and crying for blood, pressing us without mercy. Such character is no nobler than the Supreme Bliss Cult's.
But that won't work
I hate them‑how I wish I could kill every one of those bastards and fight to the very end, only then would my courage not be wasted.
...of course I was, brimming with grievances that had to be let out.
A'Huo, do you hate them?
That's fine

We're not in any hurry to leave. Even condemned prisoners get a last meal. These rations would just go to waste if left alone, so we might as well cook it all up and let everyone eat their fill before we set off.
Xiaomei, we're about to go down the mountain‑why don't you go pack?
...How did it come to this?

However, the Sect Leader, keen‑eyed and discerning, uncovered the true culprit and beat the Eldest Senior Brother nearly to death. That year, the relationship between Second Senior Brother and the Eldest Senior Brother wasn't yet so bad, so Second Senior Brother pleaded on the Eldest Senior Brother's behalf.

These are the scribbles Eldest Senior Brother made in the book when he was little; he stuffed it back on the shelf, eagerly hoping someone would find it. The meanest part is he even signed it Tang Zheng, trying to pin the blame on Second Senior Brother.
This place is always a mess. I've resolved several times to tidy up, but whenever the weather's nice I open the windows to air the books, and it all gets messy again.
So you were planning to beat me up a lot?!
In your dreams! If I beat you one less time a day, that would already make up for it! Get lost!
How can I make it up to you? Can I live off you?
Zhao Huo... I'm partly responsible for the regrets you carry. From now on I'll slowly make it up to you; I only hope you can let go.
No matter how you look at it, the regret won't go away.
No, leave such trivial matters to me. You're about to leave home ‑ go see the world; don't leave any regrets.
Is there anything I can help you with?
I'm very gratified that you understand my intentions.
If you hadn't stepped forward, Lu Weng might not have been willing to be so generous. It's entirely thanks to Miss Ying that everyone's travel expenses have been taken care of.
Besides, everyone has already received their money and gone, so there's no harm in us making a little profit.
I've already said I don't blame you
We'll come back to redeem it when we have the money. I have not the slightest intention of selling it for a pittance or taking the opportunity to profit‑please don't misunderstand.

...I knew the books, calligraphy, and paintings in the Scripture Hall were prized treasures of the Tang Clan. I had already discussed it with Third Brother: since we couldn't take bound volumes with us, we asked Squire Lu to pawn them and convert them to cash, then distribute the proceeds among the Tang Clan's fellow disciples as travel funds.
I'm not blaming you
Whew... you scared me. That's why I hit you ‑ serves you right.
That's too much!

Why would I be afraid of ghosts? I've never done anything to have a guilty conscience, so I'm not scared of ghosts knocking at midnight. Even if there really were ghosts, I'd punch them until their souls scattered. But the problem is you are solid and corporeal‑you're a monster!
I did ‑ I said just one word and got cut off. It's broad daylight; you're not going to run into ghosts, so why be so panicked?
You're gonna die! When did you start standing behind me?! Can't you say anything?! You damn mute!
Cluck! Wah!
Why are you laughing all sneaky and mysterious... Oh well ‑ it's not like they're on their guard against me. Even if people are wary of me, it's my own fault. Sigh.
Let's go, let's go
Then we'll get to work
You hear the person you love praising you behind your back; you feel both flattered and a little embarrassed.

It's hard to say. Brother Zhao‑put nicely, he's the most loyal person in the world; put less nicely, he's stubborn as can be. No matter how earnestly I tried to persuade him, he clung on and refused to leave, which shows how hard‑headed he is. Once he decides a place is home, he won't go to even the best places, and people are likewise irreplaceable.

It's hard to say. Brother Zhao may be lacking in decency, but when it comes to loyalty there's nothing to fault. No matter how earnestly I pleaded with him, he just stubbornly clung on and refused to leave, which shows how hard‑headed he is. Once someone decides a place is home, they won't go elsewhere even if it's better; the same goes for people ‑ they're irreplaceable.
He has a beloved wife and is so content he no longer thinks of home‑how would he think of us?
When the time comes we'll go to Sister-in-Law for help-don't pretend you don't know us.
Even if it isn't worth anything, with enough hype it'll become valuable. Something worth a hundred wen, if I hold onto it a few years, I can sell it for a hundred taels ‑ do you believe that?
Madam Shangguan, are there any works of calligraphy or painting that are especially valuable?

Those marked in vermilion are texts that must be treated with great caution; they must be destroyed by immersion in water or by burning to eliminate any future trouble. Otherwise, if they spread among the populace they could be maliciously misused, and we'll be held responsible.
What does it mean when it's marked with a cinnabar check mark? Does that mean it's already been checked?
Ying......
Please, both of you, inventory the books on the upper and lower floors according to the list compiled by the Sect Leader.
Well, that's a long story - my legend begins when I was six, the day I kicked the neighbor's vicious dog.

I don't have any grand, dramatic legend ‑ I've spent half my life doing menial work. I'm just afraid the more you hear about me, the more disappointed you'll be, and sooner or later you'll divorce me.
From now on I'm no longer busy. Husband, could you explain it to me carefully?

There's not much to write. I, your humble wife, longed to lavish you with praise, yet I find myself utterly at a loss for words. Come to think of it, though we are joined by marital vows, I still only know you in part.
Me? What could I possibly write?
...I also had selfish motives, and I continued to write your story.
Is that so? That's really great.

I, your humble wife, read some of the Tang Clan's family histories. Many of the details were little known, and they moved me deeply. Fearing that, once their keepers were gone, they might be lost to the flames, I selected passages and recopied them, intending to send a copy to the Gengyang Reading Studio so that future generations might, through these manuscripts, glimpse the stories of the Tang Clan.
Xiao Ju, are you writing?
My dear.
You're welcome.
I rescued you... Yunshang, thank goodness you came back... thank you.
Yeah... I saved you. So it's not like I saved no one.

Didn't you save me?
The good medicine brewed here isn't just the pill — it's also you, who endured the bitterest of hardships.
Who said that?
The pill sat in the main furnace, refined for years on end — yet no one could be saved.
Even if the Longevity Corpse Heart Pill were completed, no one could save them.
Sigh...

Sect Leader, I left home with no support, nowhere to turn. Now Zhao Huo kneels and bows, thanking you for your kindness in taking me in. Everyone says you are Old Demon Tang, but in my heart, you are the true Great Hero.
Go ahead, then.
...I'll go and kowtow before the Sect Leader to bid farewell.

Yes—those disciples' nameplates on the wall have to come down and be burned.
Afterward, the Tang Clan's enemies will find it hard to hunt them down one by one.
Third Senior Brother, are you collecting nameplates?
Third Senior Brother, usually so well-read and courteous, had never been seen gnashing his teeth like this before. Clearly he hated Second Senior Brother bitterly.

Vengeance in this life is hopeless, but good and evil will ultimately be repaid. When I descend to the Yellow Springs, I will surely present the case to King Yanluo and have Ox-Head and Horse-Face go fetch his soul.
Ever since the Sect Leader was poisoned and confined to bed, Second Senior Brother stopped going about the Jianghu. Even if we wanted to take revenge, we had no way to do so.
Not a day will pass in which I forget this deep grudge.
Don't forget there's also the matter of Second Senior Brother betraying our sect and poisoning the Sect Leader.
Whether the actions of the Demon Cult deserve capital punishment or evoke sympathy, Tang Clan has no notion of relying on anyone else.
Yeah, I was just talking — us brothers were just having a casual chat, that's all.
Let us put the topic of the Demon Cult to rest. Regardless, our sect will not accept this slander. Never forget the teachings of our Master, the Sect Leader.
That's what I'm saying.
He's an utterly unforgivable fiend. Fortunately you didn't have a run‑in with him.
I don't know either. It can't be that he foresaw the old abbot would falsely accuse us at the Wulin Assembly and preemptively beat up his disciples and followers to vent for us, can it?
Why would he do something so utterly heartless to the abbot?!

No ‑ he really is very bad. He attacked the Southern Songshan Temple, beat the abbot with a rolling pin, forced the abbot to run naked through the street, had his accomplices cut slices of fish and place them on the abbot's torso to be eaten by dogs; that same day the abbot was emotionally traumatized and retired.
So you mean he's not actually that bad?

Actually, I met the Hungry Ghost Path Dharma King Liu E in person. He is a restless youth younger than expected. He doesn't resemble the rumors of having three heads and six arms; he's quite easy to get along with.
Even the bounty on the Heavenly King's seat wasn't as high as his.

And then there's Liu E, the Dharma King of the Hungry Ghost Path... He privately controls the White Shark Gang, has seized the sea lanes, and has even driven off officials and Imperial Soldiers at sea. Undoubtedly, after Liangshan Marsh, he is the Jianghu figure most feared by the Imperial Court.

Dharma King Zhao Kui of Hell's Path moves like a phantom, carrying out private executions everywhere — both the law and the underworld suffer for it. He also performs spirit possession, giving off an eerie presence; given the Mud Cult's foul reputation, this indeed has something to do with him.
I have not seen it with my own eyes. However, when it comes to the Hell Path and the Hungry Ghost Path Dharma Kings, they are likely not good people.
The Six Demons' notorious reputation is probably not unfounded.
Senior Brother, don't be so serious — he's just mouthing off and taking pleasure in putting others down.

You're right; Junior Brother, you have extraordinary insight. All my poring over the sages' writings was in vain ‑ I merely echoed what others said. As Senior Brother, I can only lament that I fall short.
I don't know for sure. Jianghu rumors do sometimes contain inaccuracies; it's possible that Six Paths Dharma King is actually quite a decent person.

This is so unfair! I, Tang Sheng, have followed the way of the sages my whole life‑guided by feeling but restrained by propriety, never once overstepping the bounds. How could there be such an absurd rumor! And besides, she's a woman in her sixties!

I once heard people say that Third Senior Brother specializes in kidnapping grandmothers over sixty, locking them in a room to practice together the evil demonic arts inherited from the Old Demon Cult, causing those families to bloom a second time.
I‑I‑how could I be a demon lord? You mustn't say that!
Surely others have heard of the peerless demon lord Tang Sheng (Third Senior Brother), who has killed countless people.
By this reasoning, the Asura King is not only no villain — he might even be called a guardian deity-general of our Great Song.

From the Blood Letters of Battle one can glimpse the first half of the Dharma King of the Asura Path's life. Judging only by the ghosts left in his wake, he has indeed slaughtered without number — every stroke a human life — but that all took place on the battlefield where the two nations clashed.
No, just look at those infamous Six Paths Dharma Kings — they're as bad as it gets. Each one a peerless demon lord, and there are six of them, no less.

Ah, well, actually the Demon Cult isn't so bad — it's just that their doctrines sound a little bloodcurdling. Truth is, while out on trade routes I've occasionally come across Demon Cult folk treating villagers' illnesses in exchange for firewood, rice, oil, and the like.
I was just joking, though in my view, the people in the Wulin Alliance are not much different from the Mud Cult.
Under no circumstances can this be allowed.
You're not serious, are you?
As the younger sister, I'd also like to do my part‑let me write the invitation letters to the various sects.
Hmm!
Excellent. I've been humiliated for too long; it's time to retaliate in kind and erase past humiliation!
At your command!

The meeting is adjourned for today. Once all arrangements are in order, we'll launch the operation. If we're going to do this, we'll do it on a grand, spectacular scale ‑ to live up to our ancestors' honored name!
Exactly

This matter is of the utmost importance. I will go to the ancestral hall to offer incense and present the decision to the Tang Clan ancestors. At the same time, the selection of people to send to persuade the various sects must be planned with a long‑term view.
Your talent has blossomed and borne fruit; whether it will succeed is still uncertain, but you always blaze brand‑new trails.
Thank you!
Of course I am too. There's something worth fighting for and a real chance to win‑who wants to be a coward?
...More than withdrawing into seclusion, more than submitting, more than knowingly undertaking the impossible and giving one's life for the sect, I would rather trust your plan, Junior Brother.
If we retreat, before long there will be no Jianghu left in the world.

Because the people among the authorities are human too‑they can be corrupt and pervert the law. Even with the most impartial, upright magistrates, they still can't manage all the affairs of the realm.

...That's right. Senior members of the Tang Clan travel the Jianghu on principle, staying true to our original intent and caring nothing for praise or blame. We're already part of the Jianghu‑why should we still serve the Imperial Court? Why not just report it to the authorities?

We aren't the ringleaders. Besides, if the Tang Clan doesn't lead, no other sect in the Jianghu would dare challenge the Imperial Court. We're not trying to start a rebellion, but we won't be pushed around either.
That's right, hehe
You're hardly one to talk.
The Wulin Alliance picked the wrong person to provoke — our Junior Brother's heart is blacker than the Demon Cult's.
I can't be the only one who suffers ‑ everyone in the world must suffer with me. They brought this on themselves; they deserve it! It's none of my damn business!

There's nothing to hesitate about — didn't the Wulin Alliance already act high-handedly, bossing our sect around? We used to mind our own business, but now that I feel wronged, I must return blow for blow.
I suppose it could be
Can't I take you with me?
What's wrong? You pulled me again.
Yank!
My goodness, Junior Brother, your face is really ugly ‑ it doesn't suit your soul.
You're absolutely right!
Even if our grand ambitions remain unfulfilled, this place is a fitting place for us to die.

It gives the common folk reason to hope: even in dead ends beyond the reach of Great Song law, they can still place their faith in chivalry. We dare to stand up for the weak and defy the powerful. What we protect are the small, innocent people cast out and sacrificed by the many.
We raise the banner not merely to protect ourselves; we are filled with righteous fervor ‑ to establish the moral conscience of Heaven and Earth and to secure the destiny of the people.
No need to hesitate, Third Senior Brother. The Tang Clan honors righteousness and is not afraid of slander; when they're in the right, they don't demand complete vindication.
If the Sect Leader were clear‑headed right now, what would he do?

Indeed, if this plan succeeds, it would not only relieve the Tang Clan's pressing crisis but also keep the Imperial Court in check and stabilize the situation. However, its repercussions would be far‑reaching; it would inevitably plunge the Central Plains into turmoil, and whether innocent people will be implicated is uncertain. The decision must not be made rashly.
But let's keep things separate.
Besides, they're in love with each other, and I‑this old man‑can't be too oblivious to matters of the heart.
Although I wanted to stop them... Fourth Junior Brother isn't entirely wrong. His abilities are too great; if he were to turn against the Tang Clan, the consequences would be unimaginable.
Ouch, ouch ‑ it's going to choke me to death!
Junior Martial Sister held on even tighter.
Good!
Make sure you ingratiate yourself; don't let him escape. If you can't keep him here, don't let him leave the Tang Clan alive!
What are you saying now? I don't know whether that counts as insulting me.

That's it, Junior Martial Sister ‑ make sure you hold on tight and don't let go. You won't find another ugly man this formidable anywhere. Even if you did, he might not be as formidable; and even if he were, he might not be so ugly ‑ you wouldn't be able to control that.
I was scared, that's all.
I was perfectly fine‑there's no way I'd just disappear.
Uh... no. I was just afraid you'd disappear.
What's the matter? Junior Martial Sister is tugging at my clothes‑do you have something you want to say?
Tug
I study too; I'll improve, okay?!
You weren't like this before. Weren't you a spineless little nobody? This isn't like you, Junior Brother! Wake up!

No ‑ each craft has its own specialty. I study the sage writings of Kong and Meng; it is Confucian scholarship for governing the state. What you say is not merely military strategy; it even has the manner of a zonghengjia, the school of diplomacy and statecraft.
Third Senior Brother, you're being a bit excessive in your words; you must have expected something of this sort.
Third Senior Brother, you're being too harsh; I'm just a bit underhanded in my methods. If you weren't so proper and uptight, how could you not have thought of it?
Is that so?
Junior Brother, since when did you become so capable? I could never have come up with such a plan ‑ I wouldn't even have dared to imagine it.
I can't correct you.
If I've said anything wrong, go ahead and correct me, Third Senior Brother.
That's not much better, is it?
This isn't the look you give to trash; it's the look you give to a monster.
If I've said anything wrong, go ahead and tell me.
What's going on? Nobody's saying anything ‑ everyone's just staring at me like I'm trash.

That may be so, but this plan might work ‑ or it might not. The biggest unknown is the Kongtong Sect, like a sharp sword suspended high over the Shu region. If no other sects lend support, a single strike from Kongtong and all will be lost.
Pah, forget I said that‑my wife is surnamed Wei, and that's just unlucky to say!

Once the Wulin Alliance moves to surround the Tang Clan, I'll ask Daoist Master Danxiazi to attack the other sects. If one sect withdraws, the others certainly won't be willing to fight desperately ‑ that's the strategy of Besiege Wei to Rescue Zhao.
The key lies with the Kongtong sect; it is like a sharp sword hanging over the Shu region. If we can persuade the Four Sect Leaders to ally with the Tang Clan, there may be a chance to turn the tide.

What a pity — the Kongtong Sect is closely allied with us. If the Wulin Alliance dares to besiege the Tang Clan, I'll ask Daoist Danxiazi to attack the other sects. If one sect withdraws its forces, the others certainly won't fight desperately; this is the tactic of besieging Wei to rescue Zhao.
I don't think the Diancang sect would be willing to risk their lives and shed their blood for the State of Song.
If you don't join us, the wheel of fortune will turn ‑ we'll rally our friends and go to Diancang Mountain to kill and set fires!
Even if the Diancang Sect wanted to be enemies of our sect, they'd be limited by geography and would find it difficult to act. What can they do? They're in the southwest, after all.

Quanzhen and Songshan are both outside the Central Plains, so they certainly won't actively side with the Eastern Wulin Alliance; persuading them to stand down shouldn't be difficult. Even if that fails, they'll have reservations and won't go all out.

The various factions in the Wulin are large and well-established; with their ancestral foundations at stake, it's inevitable they'll be cautious. But not everyone is willing to bow to the Imperial Court's tyranny — there are still wandering heroes in the Jianghu. If they were gathered together, they'd be a force not to be underestimated.

Moreover, not every sect in the Wulin is hostile to the Tang Clan; many are probably unhappy with the Wulin Assembly. Start by winning over the small and medium sects and building momentum ‑ once that momentum is established, the major sects will sequentially declare their positions.

Most factions in the Wulin support the Tang Clan, which shows their dissatisfaction with the Imperial Court. The Yueyang Wulin Assembly exists in name only; everyone is simply unwilling to openly break with the Imperial Court.
Therefore, if we go to war with the Mud Cult, we must first eliminate the Tang Clan to forestall any future trouble.

If they try to besiege the Mud Cult and head east to join forces with the Wulin Alliance, we will launch a swift strike on their main stronghold, making it easy for them to go but hard to return, leaving them with no home to go back to.

Assuming all six schools are enemies... The Tang Clan is here, seemingly surrounded by Qingcheng, Emei, and Kongtong, but on the other hand it can also cut off the retreat routes of Qingcheng, Emei, and Diancang.

The Wulin Alliance was formed mainly to eradicate the Mud Cult, so its focus was on the heartland of the Central Plains. It made strategic use of the Nangong family's local advantage to form an encircling network together with the other sects.

The Imperial Court set the Shangguan family in motion to seize our clan's assets and weaken the Tang Clan. They also used the Wulin Assembly to co-opt the major sects, applying both reward and punishment and putting those schools at their command — this is killing with a borrowed blade.

The Imperial Court can't get a clear read on our true strength, and it fears that acting rashly would stir the Wulin to a common indignation. So even if it is furious enough at the Tang Clan to want to strike, it has no choice but to show extraordinary restraint.

However, the Tang Clan has outer forts ‑ they are the only exception in the Wulin capable of conducting operations against regular military forces. Amituofo. Elder Benefactor Tang, long time no see; I only ran into Benefactor Zhao a short while ago.

Before any pleasantries, this humble monk must say solemnly: Dharma Master Shi Ming's words and actions have nothing to do with Songshan. I ask everyone to look into this carefully and not to blame a good person.
Good Fortune──
I'll go meet the visitors.
The Gang Leader is coming in person, so we mustn't be negligent. Please notify the Acting Sect Leader; I'll go up the mountain myself to welcome him.
Ask Third Senior Brother later to arrange a different post for you; your position is too risky.
I'd be so scared I'd die; I couldn't possibly go up the mountain to report it.

I thought there'd be a crowd, that they'd be here to pick a fight. There are hardly any people ‑ what are you so worked up about? They're being polite to you and you're already this nervous. What will you do if you run into someone who's rude?
The people who came... are so... so... so few! And they're also very polite!
Why would the Beggar Sect's Gang Leader suddenly pay a visit to the Tang Clan?
The Beggar Sect's Gang Leader is here!
Never mind Dharma Master Fu Yun - but how could the Beggar Sect's Gang Leader suddenly come calling at the Tang Clan?
The Beggar Sect's Gang Leader and Dharma Master Fu Yun have arrived!

I've only just taken off my shoes and socks.
Who's arrived that has you so on edge?
No, this is bad! Someone's here! Where's Brother Zhao? Wake up, don't sleep!
I shouldn't do anything else today. I need to calm down and think things through on my own.

If we didn't act this way, who would respect beggars like us? We have to be fiercer and crueler than others—only then will people fear us and take us seriously. All those high-minded principles are for the rich to worry about; that's none of my business. I only care about loyalty.
Buddy, your killing intent is really strong
If Master heard me speaking so rudely, she would surely tug my ear and scold me harshly. Where on earth has she gone? Why won't she come and scold me...? I'm so lonely.
If Master heard her speaking so rudely, she'd inevitably be scolded again.
Got it
Don't drag your junior sister into this. Do you understand?
Now the junior sister is in for a rough time.
You, girl, come here. As your master, I'll teach you how to behave.
M-M-Master!
How did your master teach you to speak?
Relax, I'm on your side. Except for the ones in green robes—everybody else gets a beating, damn it, no exceptions.
Oh... that really is simple and straightforward.
Woof woof woof woof woof!

This world's full of scoundrels with too much time on their hands—people who don't even know you but want to kick you around just because you look easy to bully. No point arguing. Just bite them! Take a bite of flesh out of them and they won't dare bark again!
Of course we're fighting, Brother.
Of course we're fighting, Senior Brother.
That is all I have to say; I will not say anything further to disturb you.
You can't refuse to take me far away, refuse to go along with the crowd, and still insist on staying here in the Tang Family Compound to wait for death, can you?
This is way too crazy.

You and Liu E inexplicably get along, don't you? Why not‑while the Mud Cult still has some strength‑let me try to pull some strings; how about the Tang Clan actually forming an alliance with the Mud Cult?
Go on, tell me.
I have a particularly crazy idea.
The enemy of my enemy is my friend.
I... I was threatened...!

If, on the other hand, you don't use your brain and stubbornly go off and get yourself killed, then consider yourself out of luck. I'll go find an ideal suitor at least ten times more handsome than you and drive you so mad you'll jump out of your coffin.
As long as you don't waver and don't treat your life lightly, we'll have many good days ahead.
I wouldn't dare.
I've shown enough sincerity and given enough sweetness already; any more would just look cheap. Don't you dare take me for some casual woman.
......Miss Ying.
I know you won't leave the Tang Clan‑it's out of loyalty, and that's undoubtedly the right thing to do. But I still hope you'll give me a little more of your personal attention. I'm sorry.

When a merchant offers more than the going rate, it's usually for one of two reasons: either they want to build good relations with you, or they have an awkward favor to ask. As for me pressing myself against you and fawning like this—it's both.
En-enough, that's enough.
I am Young Lady Shangguan, the proud only daughter of my house, and now I'm throwing myself into your arms like this—is that not proof enough of my sincerity?
I- is that so? I suppose it is.

Nangong Shen and I had been betrothed since childhood, yet we both held strictly to propriety. I was proud and aloof too, and never so shameless as this—he wanted to so much as hold my finger, and I wouldn't let him.
I can't just let it stop, can I?
Your heartbeat is way too loud ‑ you're asking to be smacked.
Sorry.
Your expression is so disgusting ‑ you're asking for a beating.

I‑I'm warning you, okay: I'm not good at flattering people or acting cutesy. I've already swallowed my pride and I'm doing my absolute best. If you so much as say one word of disdain about me, I will never show you any courtesy for the rest of my life!
Ying, Miss Ying... why are you suddenly so close?
My dear, I've followed you, and I've always had your best interests at heart. If there were any other way out, I certainly wouldn't be urging you to give up your ambitions like this.
So concise, yet so persuasive.
I once believed Shangguan and Nangong were my family, but I ended up at the Tang Clan. If I were stubborn and rigid, clinging only to dogma, would I have come with you?
This is our home!

If the Central Plains has no place for us, why not simply give up the Tang Family Compound? The saying as long as the green hills remain, there'll always be firewood to burn is plain enough — I refuse to believe you don't all understand it.
Withdraw into seclusion
You're loyal to the Tang Clan, and Ying'er admires that. But I gave up wealth and glory ‑ I'm not here just to accompany you to your death. You must promise me you'll carefully consider your future.

People who lack long‑term foresight will soon have immediate worries. I'm not discussing besieging the Mud Cult with you; I'm talking about the fact that sooner or later the Wulin Alliance will regard us as a thorn in their side.
......I believe.
Once the Mud Cult is eliminated, the next target will be the Tang Clan ‑ do you believe that?

The Tang Clan has brazenly defied the Imperial Court more than once; their record is riddled with misdeeds. It's only because they're far off in Western Shu, with external threats still looming, that sending troops against them has been difficult. Now, with the Wulin Alliance serving as the enforcer, it's only a matter of time before a deadly blow falls on the Tang Clan.
I knew it... you really are stubborn.
Miss Ying, the Sect Leader has already answered this question for you.

Zhao Huo, although I was about eighty percent sure of your answer, I'll ask anyway‑could the Tang Clan possibly pledge allegiance to the Imperial Court? If you and Third Brother give the nod, I can immediately mobilize my connections...
Yes, yes, very much so. Except for your face, you're handsome all over!
My other parts are more handsome than my face, so you mustn't hit those.
Hahaha, people begging for mercy always say don't hit my face, but you asked me to hit yours instead.
Pfft
Please, for the sake of this flower, don't strike anywhere except the face.
I've returned, and I've brought back this little flower whose color suits you.
One......Two~
No... I didn't do anything wrong, don't hit me!
I don't want to. You must want to hit me.
What the hell are you looking at? What the hell are you laughing at!
How can you be so soft‑hearted? If we have children in the future, you can't be the one to raise them‑an indulgent father often spoils his child.
What if I still can't bring myself to hit you?
It's truly terrifying...
But if what you say is unreasonable, I'll fight back.
Self‑indulgence is the real cruelty. Those close to the situation are often the most confused. If I've offended you in any way, please be sure to admonish me.
Are you serious...? Are you that strict with yourself, too?
Yes... When we get married, I'll give you a family‑discipline rod. You can use it to punish me then.
Owe what? Are you really planning on paying it back?
I... this is a bad habit of mine; it's hard to change all at once. I'll be more careful next time‑I'll owe you one for now.
Look, look ‑ you're making a criminal declaration again.
It's not like all I can do is hit people. You're asking for a beating.
Why do I get the feeling you're about to hit someone? Since I've been so obedient, if I do something wrong, please show mercy and hit me a little more lightly.
Oh (as you command)
...Zhao Huo, come here. I want to speak to you earnestly.
Oh, so you were here ‑ I was looking for you everywhere.
I always feel a little lonely. What can I do? Where will I be needed?
...Jinxiang Palace doesn't need me to risk my life to protect it; the Tang Clan doesn't either. If all I have to do is live my own life well, that's enough... isn't it?
That's good. Nothing else‑I'll head back for now; enjoy it. And be sure to keep a close eye on your wallet.
I'm this polite‑how could I possibly leave without saying goodbye?
If you're leaving, don't forget to come and say goodbye to me, or I'll look for you everywhere.
No way!
You'll get fat, you know.
I understand what you mean, but I need to think it over... I'll think about it while I eat.
...Alright.
People will inevitably die; since it's unavoidable, they might as well live as they please while they're alive.
Afraid of dying as I am, I'm even more afraid of a lifetime of regret. To make sure things don't turn out that way, I'll give it my all.
You're so cowardly, and yet you still brag.
Oh, please ‑ who do you take me for? I'm not crazy; of course I'd be afraid.
Aren't you at all afraid of dying?
Of course I'll stay.
What about you?
If my Sect Leader Senior Brother decides to hold the Tang Clan and fight the Wulin Alliance to the death, Sister Xiang should go down the mountain alone.
Sorry‑I promised Lady Wen I'd take in the people of Jinxiang Palace. As it turned out, we can barely protect ourselves.
You represent only yourself; you only need to answer for your own life.
I know, I know... you don't have to say that.

You're not a Tang Clan Disciple; at most you're just a passerby. I'm a member of the Tang Clan, so I won't leave. You're not one of us‑what obligation do you have to live and die with the Tang Clan? No one asked you to do this.
But you're different ‑ you still have a wonderful life ahead; you don't have to wade into this mess.

The rise and fall of the Tang Clan is the inescapable responsibility of every Tang Clan Disciple. Do everything you can and then leave the rest to fate; if the Tang Clan is truly destined to perish, that too is ordained by fate.
Sister Xiang, listen to me.
Anyway, that's it. Don't ask me. Does what I think matter? It's up to you to decide.

My master used to force me to study with a rattan cane, and I forget things as soon as I read them. If I can occasionally manage to come up with a few idioms, that's something‑don't put me on the spot.
This is a poem by Li Bai. Haven't you read it?
No, this is Li Bai's Xing Lu Nan.
You really seem to be able to do anything‑unlike me. Sigh.
No, it's not. You little liar.
That's right ‑ it's a poem I wrote.
That's right, this is a poem I wrote.
Is this a poem you wrote?

That's exactly it... This whole table of delicious food smells so good, yet I can't taste a bite of it. Not only have I let the chef's hard work go to waste, I feel guilty before every chicken I've swallowed without even tasting.

A golden cup of clear wine costs ten thousand cash; a jade plate of rare delicacies is worth just as much. I set down my cup, lay aside my chopsticks, unable to eat; I draw my sword and gaze about me, my heart lost in confusion.
A leaky roof suffers more when it rains overnight. At Fengyu Mountain, Sister Xiang's inner demon grew even stronger.
Is that so...?

I've already... had enough of swinging my sword, and I don't want to see people I know die anymore. I want to retire into seclusion, but I don't know what I can do after sealing my sword; my life feels completely aimless.
Even now, I still often dream of Uncle Wang, of Fengyu Mountain, and I keep wanting to run away from it.
Even now, I often dream of Uncle Wang ‑ I dream of the day your Senior Brother died, I dream of Fengyu Mountain, and I keep wanting to run away.
You used to always drag me into sparring matches.

This kind of Jianghu is disheartening, isn't it? I'm both furious and bewildered ‑ I want to seek justice, but the hand that holds my sword betrays me and trembles. I'm going to make my Father lose face.

Those with a large following speak with decisive authority; the isolated can only meekly comply. Those with superior martial arts can ignore reason; people who flock to them, hoping for gain, risk their lives and obsequiously flatter them.
Yeah... to be honest, seeing them like that made me very afraid. The chivalry I longed for seems to have been nothing but wishful thinking, merely a fantasy.
This is difficult. Among them some are sensible, some would rather see the world in chaos, but most simply echo others and are led by the nose.
......I wish the Wulin could be a little more clear‑headed and not so frenzied.
Never mind what the Tang Clan wants‑what do you yourself hope for?
What happened?
If the Tang Clan wants to confront the Wulin Alliance head‑on, I will, of course, stand and fall with you.
I even gave up my meal to tempt you, and you still can't change the subject?
Sister Xiang, I just mentioned the matter of the Wulin Alliance‑what would you plan to do?
Honestly.
Don't worry, I paid properly, with the reward I earned today from catching a thief. You can eat too ‑ actually, it's rare for me to treat, so I hope you'll do me the honor of accepting.
Long Xiang was inwardly anguished; she had to channel her grief and indignation into eating.
It's good that you want to work to earn money. Now please explain‑what's going on with this table of dishes?
Why are you acting like that? Isn't it commendable that I can reflect on myself? Why don't you at least comfort me!
Oh my God, Sister Xiang has suddenly attained enlightenment!
Verbal attack
I blurted it out, but luckily Sister Xiang didn't notice. She's a dignified Heroine‑how could I suggest she earn money by performing like a courtesan?
I'm that bad at performing‑what listener would be willing to be impressed?
Uh... no, it's not.
Are you trying to make me play the xiao and sing for money at an inn?
If you don't take up the sword, don't you still play music?
Just let me be like this for now, okay?
...Yeah, I know, it's just... it's just... sigh.
Then just pick up a sword; pick it up and you'll be able to do anything.
You're way too kind ‑ not even my master has ever indulged me like this.

Isn't this kind of thing perfectly normal? If you want to do a good job, you must first sharpen your tools; even the most skilled cook can't make a meal without rice. Even an imperial palace chef, if not given pots or a spatula, can't come up with any fancy dishes.
Comfort
No. To my shame, I‑I realized that I seem to be what people commonly call a useless person. If I'm not using a sword, I really can't do anything; I'm completely good‑for‑nothing.
Any results?
My heart was heavy and I couldn't calm down enough to practice swordsmanship. Wanting to earn a little money to pay the rent, I wandered the streets to see if there was any work I could do.
I've been looking for you for ages‑how come you're at the inn?
......As long as the Princess doesn't get involved, this plan is sure to succeed.
What a brilliant plan! My wife is simply amazing! I'll go tell Third Senior Brother!
What a brilliant plan! For Talented Woman Wei to still say the strategy won't work is far too modest! I'll go tell Third Senior Brother.
