My dear truly wasn't just echoing my words. Every step he laid out was close to what Senior Brother Danxiazi and I had already worked out.

However, the above assumes a scenario where all five major sects besides Kongtong turn hostile to the Tang Clan. In reality, Songshan may not be able to talk its way out of it, and the rest aren't mortal enemies who can't share the same sky with us.
Good ‑ of course we should go with the flow and draw the fire toward Qingcheng to smoke Shentu Long out. Once the fire reaches his eyebrows, let's see if he can still keep up the act.
Those who truly must be crushed in one fell swoop are the Shangguan Family, Qingcheng, and Emei.

Quanzhen and Songshan are made up of Daoist priests and Buddhist monks; apart from Shi Ming, the treacherous bald monk, they all believe in karma. Even if the Nangong Family fell out with the Tang Clan, they'd still fear public opinion, so these three forces are secondary -- as long as we don't strike hard at them, they'll leave us some leeway.

Diancang's base is in Dali; unlike Quanzhen or Songshan, they don't have local adherents to come to their aid, so in a protracted campaign they'll inevitably be depleted. If the Kongtong Sect and Jinxiang Palace can hold off the eastern forces and wear them down until Diancang is forced off the front line, the tide of the situation could be reversed.

The Tang Clan may appear to be beset on both sides, but in fact it sits where the three sects‑Qingcheng, Emei, and Diancang‑meet the Central Plains official road. It can sever the three sects' ties with the Wulin Alliance, and even if besieged, rely on the terrain to hold out in the mountains.
There are the Kongtong Sect and the Tang Clan; if Jinxiang Palace can be persuaded to join them--and with the Mud Cult lurking on the sidelines--it could form a three-way balance of power.
{size=50}!!{/size}
My dear smiled without a word... It seems he'd thought of it long ago.

The essence of being a hero lies in acting outside the law, so as to defy its constraints. Not everyone in Jianghu craves fame and fortune or clings to the Imperial Court -- they're merely scattered like sand, too few to stand against the many. The Tang Clan means to rise up, rally these people, and form the Western Wulin Alliance to stand against the Wulin Alliance!

If the nation faces peril and both court and people are united without reservation, I too support Wulin heroes loyally serving the country. But if petty, short-sighted villains use others' hands to eliminate dissenters and succeed, it will have the effect of killing the chicken to scare the monkey: Jianghu will fall silent, none daring to disobey, and chivalry will cease to exist.
They're completely different. The inferior option is mere bravado; the superior one requires that the righteous cause be on our side.
How is this different from the worst option?
‑declare open war on the Wulin Alliance
In that case, please hear the best plan I, your humble handmaiden, have devised.

This method may be clever... but it's not the Tang Clan's style. The worry is that even if it can be hidden for a while, people's resolve will evaporate; once time passes and circumstances change, no one will care what the truth actually was.
Given time to gather the evidence and lay it open before everyone, we will expose the petty scoundrels' lies and let them reap what they've sown.

The middling strategy is to break up the Tang Clan and scatter its members through Jianghu, so the Wulin Alliance can't wipe us out in one sweep. Or we could follow the precedent of the Beggar Sect Gang Leader and the Palace Mistress of Jinxiang Palace, who each took the blame upon themselves and offered up their own heads to protect their followers.
This is bad. I'd guess a Tang Clan disciple's mind, nine times out of ten, can only get as far as the inferior strategy.

The inferior strategy is to disregard the edict; let him do as he pleases, and I will follow my own path. If pressed too hard, we perish together. We pay no heed to the Wulin Alliance's edict; when they encircle us, we fight back to make them regret their actions.
I would like to hear the details.
You saw through it? That's exactly it. I've prepared the superior strategy, the middling strategy, and the inferior strategy.
Three sheets of letter paper‑could this possibly be that?
Xiaoju set down her pen and pushed three folded letters in front of you.
My dear, you're here.
Although Xiao Zhu still squinted as if glaring at people, she had worn a smile on her face for several days, patiently taking on the upkeep of every Tang Clan disciple's equipment.
Then I'll go improve the Tang Clan's existing Hidden Weapon equipment. It should still be of some use ‑ I must be able to help you.
Yeah, I'm yours.
Mine!
Oh, Madam, you flatter me.
There is no one in the world who could be a better husband than you.
Protecting your heart is my duty as the sect leader.
You actually agreed, huh.
Alright... alright, I'll do as you say.
If you're so moved, how about helping me have a big, chubby baby?
Why are you so good to me? How can I ever repay you?
That goes without saying ‑ it's definitely me!
Likewise, likewise. Tell me, which of us is a bit luckier, you or me?

Xiao Zhu, actually I'm not much of a good person. I don't really care about the fate of the common people. I'm very selfish ‑ I've always only cared about those close to me. I just can't bear to see you so anxious, blaming yourself all day.
Xiao Zhu is so fortunate to have a confidant like you ‑ it's truly a blessing across three lifetimes. Thank you, thank you! I'm truly overjoyed.
Ugh, my ribs!
Zhao Huo!
Your talent ought to be used for peaceful purposes. Craft ingenious wooden armored toys to amuse children‑bringing benefit to the world is enough.

We have our own ways. The fate of the Tang Clan concerns everyone. Even if it perishes, its downfall is predetermined by destiny‑it is what others owe us, not something we undertake for our own selfish reasons and harm a myriad of people. Nor should it be borne solely by you, little miss.
But... but what about the Tang Clan's crisis?
I'm going to burn this blueprint. This weapon's killing intent is far too strong ‑ it would bring death and suffering to all living beings. You must not bring it into the human world.
Destroy the blueprints
Mm... okay. Make sure‑absolutely make sure‑to destroy it, okay?
I guarantee that once we've driven back the Wulin Alliance, we'll destroy these weapons and the blueprints and never allow them to be leaked. Is that acceptable?
...That seems to make some sense.

He's perfectly fine as he is - if he hadn't come courting death, why would we have had to forge such weapons to protect ourselves? Every wrong has someone to blame and every debt has an owner; we ought to go and hold him to account.
I thought you wanted to shoulder the blame alone, how does this involve the Wulin Alliance Leader?

I promise, once we've driven off the Wulin Alliance, we'll destroy these weapons and blueprints and never let them leak. You're only drawing the plans; I'm the one who forges them. If Lord Yama wants someone to blame, I'll... I'll pin it on the Wulin Alliance Leader.
It's... it's to‑to protect our homeland.
In order to protect our homeland
Ah...
Let's forge this weapon
Keep the blueprints
...Xiao Zhu, you possess extraordinary talent. The design depicted in this blueprint can be considered the ultimate Hidden Weapon; if used in warfare, it could even influence the fate of the nation.

Many people might die because of me. I don't want my invention to be abused or for future histories to label me a criminal. When I reach the underworld, who will be held accountable for this debt? But I can't just stand by and watch everyone die‑what should I do?
But... but this has already far exceeded the conflicts among Wulin sects. If it were to get out, it could even be used in wars between nations.
Zhao Huo, I... should I burn these plans? When I drew them, I was so angry, thinking I'd take revenge in my own way.
They can even fire in rapid succession, leaving no way out.
Also, the arrow magazine is box‑shaped for quick reloading, allowing sustained fire to suppress the enemy.
By making good use of the Tang Clan's high‑ground advantage, one can shoot farther.
I test‑fired the prototype; with a favorable wind it can reach at least a hundred paces.

This Chain Rocket is an improved version of the Tang Clan's meteor arrows and thunder‑fire bombs. Gunpowder is packed into tubes and connected with cotton fuses in a chain; once the ignition arrow fires, the others shoot out en masse, continuing until all the ammunition is spent.
...Can you tell what these blueprints are for?
Th‑this... Th‑this...!

...Are you ready? Let me say up front: although these things were my own ideas, they still send a chill down my spine. I can't help feeling anxious‑should I really bring something like this into the world?
What did you do?
I did it. Because I'm timid, I've always kept myself on guard and stayed prepared even in peaceful times.
I may not have Sect Leader Wei's talent for grand strategy, but haven't you always told me there are some things only I can do?
Wait a moment
Alright, I won't push you; I'll think about it myself.
Don't make that kind of joke‑it's really scary!
Sigh ‑ neither of us has the makings of a great general. You're the artisan in skillful artisan, and I might well end up the sauce in meat sauce.
...You're asking the wrong person; how would I know?

I want to own your entire life for myself, yet I don't want you to resent me later for being high-handed. These extra days I've lived are already ill-gotten gains — to cling to them any longer would be greedy.
...As your master, I never had the chance back then to live and die alongside the Snow Mountain Sect, so I can't deprive you of your right to die for them.
Mm, go ahead.
Very well — this disciple will take his leave now.
Oh.
In short, I won't interfere with your decision‑making; at most I'll lend a hand. Don't come to me about this kind of thing.
Not exactly.
So what? I support whoever I want to support — what's wrong with that?
Master, could it be that whatever I say, you always say I'm right?
As expected of me!
No ‑ you weren't wrong. Isn't this perfectly clear to you? As expected of my disciple.
Did I... guess wrong?
I think that, given Master's temperament, she'd probably want to press the heads of all the Wulin heroes into the dirt.
I think Master wants to grind the Wulin Alliance into the dust
I think Master might be too lazy to bother with these trivial Jianghu matters... right?
I think Master wants to retire from the Jianghu
Stop nagging ‑ if I tell you to guess, just guess.
I only asked because I didn't know — why are you testing me instead?
Go on, guess — what is your master thinking?
Yes, I wanted to consult Master.
You good-for-nothing disciple — are you already bewildered by such a trivial matter?
Oh, all right‑then I have no other attachments. After I die, I want to share a grave with you; that will be enough.
No‑absolutely not!
A lot, but what's that got to do with me? They brought it on themselves.
How many innocent people will be dragged into this!
Hahaha!
Really? Wahahaha~!
That kind of mixed surprise and delight
Truly startled.
Ahaha, were you startled?
...It's too brutal; even I never would have imagined it.
Watch them tear at each other like dogs with the Imperial Court‑see if they've any leisure left to come after the Tang Clan!

Then you and I will assassinate Shangguan Family Head and pin it on A'Sheng. Or we'll kill A'Sheng and frame Shangguan Family Head‑let them taste what it feels like to be falsely accused, see how it suits them!

Why don't we stage it ourselves‑fake an internal conflict to lure the Wulin Alliance into attacking, bury a pile of Earth Thunder underground, and when they come, boom, boom, boom‑wipe them out completely.

Isn't that so? The Tang Clan knows how to poison people and can use hidden weapons to kill without a trace. If you hadn't been so intent on brazenly flaunting your might, no one could have stopped you.
Assassins‑an assassin organization! How did I never think of it!

There was but one reason: only the Tang Clan could be mentioned alongside the Thousand Lantern Tower. If you were to turn open enemies into hidden ones and disperse to lie in wait across various places, that would make you the most terrifying assassin organization in the world.
You wonder why the Thousand Lantern Tower fears the Tang Clan so much?
Is that so? How can you tell?
My previous remark was poorly phrased ‑ I take it back, I take it back. 'Except for you,' the people of the Tang Clan are all too kind.
This is what passes for kindness?
A'Huo, the Tang Clan is far more terrifying than you think. It's because you are too kind.
Because it's not good for others to hear this.
What are you doing?
Vicious advice
...Alright. You promised me; sooner or later we're going.
Pretty good.
...All right, we can also bring my aunt and those sisters in Jinxiang Palace who want to live in seclusion.
If you want to go, even if everyone else stays, we can go live there in seclusion once the dust settles.
See? See!
Retiring into seclusion... that doesn't sound so bad.
What do you think—what if we convinced Third Senior Brother to bring the Tang Clan's brothers and sisters into seclusion together with us?
I'm not afraid you'll sell them out; I'm afraid you'll remember the way and escape from my Five-Finger Mountain.
You don't need to blindfold me; I'm not going to betray the villagers here.

I made secret arrangements, conspiring with Thousand Lantern Tower's outside enemies, and quietly spirited them all away. Most of them were tired of Jianghu life and used the chance to fake their deaths, retiring to a secluded paradise to live out their days in peace.
No ‑ I may have pushed them down the stairs, but I didn't kill a single one.
I'll share the burden with you; from now on, let's do more good deeds to make amends.
Those weren't things you did of your own will, so what's done is done.

During the years when Jinwu Shangren monitored me, I would occasionally receive secret orders from Thousand Lantern Tower to secretly handle certain individuals. In plain terms, it was assassination. To date, there have been twenty‑seven people, and I pushed all of them down the stairs.
Alright, no need to explain. I never said I didn't like it ‑ after all, it's really funny.
Also, let me make a solemn clarification: this face of mine is natural; I didn't intentionally look this way to offend public decency.
Alright, go ahead and speak. I won't laugh anymore.

Stop with that leering smile ‑ it looks really sleazy. You're the sect leader now and you still haven't pulled yourself together at all ‑ though I do like messing around with you like this, I'm actually trying to open up and talk about something serious.
That's... that's just too good.

I, Mei, was minding my own business, and you, you lecherous scoundrel, just had to come and provoke me. You've left me hopelessly mired, unable to free myself—if you think you can shake me off, that won't happen even if you die.
Xiaomei quickly gave you a light peck on the cheek.
Oh‑wh...what is this?
I'm not saying I doubt you, but I'm not very confident.
Jealous? Nervous? Afraid that I, Mei, will step out on you?
Pfft, hahahaha, wahahaha‑how could that possibly be! Silly A'Huo.
Huh?
...Have you found another man you fancy and intend to give me up?
Ahaha, no one knows Mei better than you, A'Huo—I really do have a secret.
When you call yourself Xiaomei instead of Mei, it's because you're feeling especially guilty, isn't it?
...A'Huo, then Xiaomei will tell you.
I've come all the way here; naturally I want to hear what you think.
Kind advice
Of course.
Are you sure you want to take Mei's advice?
Neither Third Senior Brother nor I can make up our minds; we just wanted to hear other people's opinions.
Of course I'll do as you say about this.
Good, you're right - let's rename this manual the 'Same-Boat Sword Manual.' It captures the idea of weathering storms together, standing by one another no matter what comes.
Brother Ye, you've misunderstood. Chase after victory as you please - I'll be guarding your back.
It means breaking the pots and sinking the boats‑stopping at nothing to win and cutting off one's own retreat. Very apt.
Is the name of this secret manual somewhat inauspicious?

Brother Zhao, this 'Sunken Boat Sword Manual' is a sword manual I wrote. It is both what I realized after my duel with my master and the sum of everything I've gained from half a lifetime of sword practice. I hope you will keep it.
Is that so? To me, that's a compliment.
You've been shaped by what you've seen and heard; your temper's grown worse, and you're exactly like someone from the Tang Clan.
I don't seek a fight, but I'm not afraid of one; otherwise nobody should expect to get off easy.

Besides, I've endured long enough. I've seen enough greedy faces and betrayals, and have only been holding back a burning rage. We finally managed to find a place to live; if anyone tries to take advantage of us again, they'll have to pay the price.
How chivalrous of Brother Ye!

I've come to appreciate something of the Tang Clan's integrity. If you refuse to submit to the Wulin Alliance's oppressive power, disaster will surely befall you. Now, in this time of crisis, isn't it precisely the moment for me to sacrifice myself in repayment?

My sister and I have drifted through hardship, and we are grateful for Sect Leader Tang's mercy in taking us in, and for the righteousness the Tang Clan brothers showed in caring for us. I've always felt that, with my meager talents, this kindness and this debt would be hard to repay in a lifetime.
I didn't say a word ‑ it was all you talking... Forget it. Don't pay attention to her; let's get down to business.
Aah! Brother thinks I'm nothing but a nuisance! Are you even my real brother?!
Brother, you didn't have a choice ‑ you were born to end up stuck with me, this troublemaker.
He wanted to marry me ‑ serves him right!
Heh
You've given Brother Zhao a lot of trouble, haven't you?
It really seems so. I'm very useful to Brother Zhao, but with Brother I only ever cause trouble.
What am I? Am I a burden?

I used to have to be cautious for the sake of my younger sister; I had to tolerate everything and be deferential and polite. Now that my younger sister's future is settled, I, Ye, can finally go all out and take a bold gamble.
Before the fight, I thought you were cautious by temperament and would certainly avoid direct confrontation.
Let's go to war with the Wulin Alliance.
Leave it to me
Your martial arts are stronger than mine. Now that I've entrusted my younger sister to you, I no longer have any worries.
Brother Zhao, I, Ye, dare to say something presumptuous. Unless the Sword Saint is reborn, my sword is the pinnacle of Diancang.
This Brother here is broken too!
Haha!
Brother, are you okay? Did you hit your head?
Ha, hahahaha!
Brother, why are you hitting my brother?!
You were too kind!
If I storm the Wulin Alliance alone, I'd have at best a one‑in‑ten chance of surviving. But I'm not alone‑Tang Clan has so many Brothers clearing the way for me!
No! You're trying to get yourself killed!
I might be able to kill the Wulin Alliance Leader, or anyone else.
I knew it all along‑why bother fighting?

Brother Zhao, as you can see, I, Ye, have no other talents‑I only possess a little insight into the Way of the Sword. Even so, when it comes to one‑on‑one combat, there are already only a handful in the Wulin who can match my swift sword.
Brother, why are you hitting Brother!
You were too kind.
Very good!
Bring it on!
Now, let's get back to the matter at hand.
......Returns are prohibited.
This staff is too thin ‑ I'm going to find a thicker one to stab you with!
It's fine as long as you understand
Oh, is that so~
Heroine, spare my life; we're really discussing serious matters!
Is this my wedding? It's not? Preposterous. What in the world could possibly be more important than my wedding!
Don't mess around ‑ I'm in the middle of a serious conversation with your brother.
Brother, you're a dead man. I've latched onto you ‑ you have to take responsibility for me!
How could I not be afraid? I'm terrified.
Why do you act like you're so afraid I'll stiff you?

I used to have to be cautious for my younger sister's sake; I had to tolerate everything, be yielding and polite. That responsibility now falls to you, and since I no longer have any lingering worries, I can speak freely.
Huh? I thought you were cautious by temperament and would avoid direct confrontation.
I think we should go to war with the Wulin Alliance. To be clear, we should take the initiative and launch a lightning strike against the rival sects, catching them off guard.
Ye Yunzhou had originally seemed full of boundless bravado, but you so tactlessly poured cold water on it that his handsome face flushed with embarrassment.
Alright
Say it out loud! Otherwise I'll die the moment you're done speaking!
Say it out loud!
Brother Zhao, I have something to tell you‑I'll let my sword do the talking.
Weren't you going to say something? Why are you drawing your sword?
...True enough, then I won't hold back. Forgive any clumsy phrasing; take it merely for what it's worth.
Oh, you're with the Tang Clan too!
Are you asking for my opinion?
Good! Let's fight their mother!
Xu, Xu, just don't hit me

What's wrong with women? In the Wei and Jin there was Hua Mulan; in the Tang, Princess Pingyang had a women's army! In the Song there was Jinxiang Palace!
Others are already trampling all over us—are we still not allowed to fight their mother?
But you're a lady!
I don't care! I just want to fight!
Why is everyone so hot‑tempered? Eat something cooling to calm down.
Yes, fight their mother!!
Who dares tell us what to do, we fight their mother!
So that means...?

We are the Tang Clan, mighty and unbowed. When did we ever sink so low that we'd have to bow and scrape to others?
Let's be frank—people don't choose the Tang Clan because they want a stable life.
If the Tang Clan's ways weren't wicked enough, wild enough, we wouldn't even bother joining!
Most people want to fight, no matter what
Well, that's just how lax our Clan Rules are.
That's actually pretty free
Let me say this up front: if your decisions are too outrageous, someone might take it upon themself to run off at any time.
We adhere to one firm principle: this is our home, and if the head of the household decides to fight, we will fight. If not, we will pat our chests and secretly laugh at our luck.
Honestly... we don't know. Not that more people coming up with a solution always makes it better; you see, those fools in the Wulin Alliance are rather silly, aren't they?
Most people don't know
Oh... I understand.
...Everyone was on edge; quite a few wanted to leave.
Most people want to retire into seclusion
Senior Brother, originally we ordinary disciples had no say in this matter, but since the Sect Leader Brother asked, everyone has summed up their individual opinions.
That's right! Thank you for your guidance, Senior Brother! I have nothing more to say; I am willing to stand with the Tang Clan through thick and thin!
Not bad, huh? Feels good, doesn't it?
My blood's boiling ‑ this is pretty good.
......is worlds apart from the Guangzhou Tang Clan.

Having backbone is just as important. The Tang Clan may be destroyed, but we'd rather die than submit. If outsiders come meddling and criticizing us for no reason, we won't merely ignore them‑we'll twist their fingers off.
I agree with you, but that's just my personal view.
Yes, yes, it's a bit... but life comes first.

Because that's not the Tang Clan's way; it sounds more like the Nangong family's manner. Think about it ‑ if we go around making enemies and only beg others for help after we've been wronged, wouldn't that be embarrassing?
Why?
I'll pass on your thoughts to him, but chances are he won't listen.
Is that so? Please, Senior Brother, offer your advice to the Sect Leader.
Oh... that sounds very reasonable.

Openly defying the Wulin Alliance is not the best strategy. Better for us to send gifts to the various sects to make arrangements and ask the Wulin elders to intercede on behalf of the Tang Clan. Great Hero Nangong is no longer alive; the Jianghu still has other benevolent people.
This person asked me whether it would be okay, but in fact had no intention of paying any attention to me.
Thank you, Senior Brother. I'll speak now.
No, you can't
Thank you, Senior Brother. I'll speak now.
Please speak
Senior Brother, may I share my thoughts?
Driven into a corner, the Junior Martial Sister finally abandoned the naive notion of subduing opponents without taking lives.
Hmm!
That's right. Showing mercy to the enemy would be cruel to our own people.
Hahaha, that's good! I was worried you'd be soft‑hearted toward everyone.
Chase them down and beat them to death.
So what if the worst of them manage to escape?
We wouldn't indiscriminately slaughter innocents; we'd only kill a few of the worst. If the others run away, then so be it.
Alright ‑ we'll go on a killing spree then, slaughtering innocents!
Those villains kept trying to harm us, so we had no choice but to beat them to death.
Is it really that cruel?
Hmm, I want to beat them to death.
The fact that they even managed to rile you shows the Wulin Alliance is no ordinary enemy.
...I feel a little angry.
I haven't made up my mind, but the more I think about it, the angrier I get.
Let's forge a path where we can grow old together.
The days we had together were too few, and I won't accept it.
There are some treasures I can't bear to part with; I'd rather die than hand them over. Besides my important memories, there's you ‑ and you.
Oh...
Because this is my home, and everyone connected to me is here, there is nothing in the world more important than the Tang Clan.
Then why are you still...?

Although I have always clung on and refused to leave, during the years when I was shunned and looked down upon, I have also more than once grown disheartened and had thoughts of leaving, fearing that I might not become a great hero and simply waste my life.
This journey has been anything but easy. My lowly life is thinner than paper ‑ it wouldn't be surprising if I died at any moment. That I can stand before you now is, in itself, a miracle.
I was just acting more composed.
But you don't seem afraid.
I'm so scared!

This road's been anything but easy. I'm nothing but a lowly lackey ‑ my life is thinner than paper. At the slightest breeze or rustle I get all jittery, convinced even the roadside weeds want to kill me. It's a miracle I can even stand in front of you.
Of course I'm scared, scared to death.
Senior Brother, are you afraid too?
...How could that be? I want to run too.
At the time, out of selfishness I kept the Junior Martial Sister behind, causing her to share our fear and anxiety. It was my fault.
If I told you I wanted to run away, would you be angry...?
I want to retire into seclusion
Oh... what about you? Have you made up your mind?
I mean, they don't know either.
I don't know.
What do the junior sisters say?
Senior Brother
It couldn't have been kept hidden in the first place; now it's common knowledge.
I'll go ask everyone for their opinions, too.
Okay, I'll leave that to you
I'll go ask the senior sisters and tell you later.
You're right ‑ this is a serious matter. I was too impatient.
I haven't decided yet
That's right
Is it about the Wulin Alliance?
Junior Martial Sister, what do you think of what Third Senior Brother said?
I'll pat you first; everyone else's turn comes later.
Third Senior Brother and the others are having a hard time too.
Because you've worked so hard
What good fortune did I stumble into today, to earn two pats?
Pat, pat.
I, your concubine, am respectfully awaiting you in the upstairs chamber.
Okay, I'll come see you in a little while.
How can that be monopolizing? Sect Leader Brother is busy — most days he's at Zhengxin Hall. I'm merely lending a hand, keeping the accounts and other odds and ends.
The Scripture Hall used to be Third Senior Brother's turf; now you've completely taken it over.

I, your concubine, am skilled in managing the household, but no great talent when it comes to strategy; even racking my brains, I can find no perfect plan. If my husband will not disdain me, please join me at Scripture Hall so we may discuss it in detail.
Madam, do you have a good plan?
My dear, do not worry; I, your concubine, am willing to share your burdens.
The fate of our sect rests on the few of us ‑ what an enormous responsibility.
Okay
Zhao Huo, I know you carry a heavy responsibility and it will surely be very trying. Hang in there ‑ I'll give you my full support.
Understood. See you a little later, then.
A little, but I still need some time to sort things out. I'll write it down to clarify my thoughts ‑ ask me again later.
Do you have any thoughts?
That's true
Not yet. This is a matter of great importance; we can't make a hasty conclusion.
Hmm. Have you already reached a decision?
You already know?
...The Sect Leader Brother summoned us for the matter concerning the Wulin Alliance's edict, right?
Isn't this alone enough to make people worry?
Apart from that, Junior Brother, are there any other matters to discuss?
In any case, let's just wait and see‑what else can we do?
‑Oh my!

The Flying Stone Gang is not like the Wulin Alliance ‑ they're a gray gang operating between the underworld and the righteous. Offend them, and even if you leave the Tang Clan you'll be hunted down no matter how far you run; I'm afraid you won't have a good day for the rest of your life.
Well, I'm back again, aren't I?
Didn't you already bid farewell to the Tang Clan and go pursue your own dreams?
I'm not gone yet, am I?
Didn't you already say you were just going to walk away?
That's not funny. Didn't we agree to share the good times and shoulder the hard times together?
Let's just tie up the culprit, hand him over, and let the Flying Stone Gang Leader decide his fate.
Just look at the mess you've caused
That's not how I'd put it
Anyway, our sect and the Flying Stone Gang still have old scores to settle, so this one against Fourth Senior Brother won't make a difference.
My good Junior Brother, I just knew you'd stand by me.

Even if the Flying Stone Gang isn't what it once was, how could they be unbeatable? Stripped to the bone, what they're doing is only daring to bully you because they see you're down and out. If in life you can't even fight for a single breath, you might as well die early and be reborn sooner.
Even so, you still can't blame Fourth Senior Brother.
No, thank you
You want me to immediately abdicate and pass the throne to you.
I always thought you were just being polite.
Sigh ‑ just when one problem's over, another starts. Why do I have such terrible luck? I keep saying I don't want to be the sect leader!

The Flying Stone Gang has no entry threshold; they take in people from all walks of life ‑ a motley mix of dragons and snakes, the good and the bad. But they outnumber us, and with tensions high right now, if a clash really breaks out we certainly won't come out of it well.

How could it be otherwise? Sigh‑no sooner has one wave settled than another rises.
Why am I so unlucky? I told you I don't want to be the sect leader!
You're not joking? Heavens above!

Over the past two years, the Flying Stone Gang accepted all comers from both the criminal underworld and legitimate circles, rapidly expanding. By sheer numbers alone, they even surpassed the former Cang Gang and White Shark Gang, ranking only behind the Beggar Sect. They number at least tens of thousands of members; things are long since no longer what they used to be.
Huh?
It's true that the Flying Stone Gang is a mix of dragons and snakes. But if ten thousand dragons and a hundred thousand snakes were mixed together, would you still dare to underestimate them?
Junior Brother, I thought you had already completely regained your memory.

You mean the Flying Stone Gang, the one that hires out laborers for grunt work, right?
Isn't that just some low-rent gang of dragons and snakes mixed together? Why make such a fuss over it?

What is this... are you tired of living or something?
Now even whether we'll live to see the Winter Solstice is in doubt!
At present, the Flying Stone Gang is furious and intends to lead its members to seek revenge.
You robbed their money pouches?
So in a fit of anger, I lost control and beat several of them black and blue, then snatched their money pouches in return.
But lately their conduct has been downright brazen. They haven't just been extorting me; they even openly snatched my money pouch and boasted they'd treat the whole neighborhood to drinks.

When I go down the mountain on trading trips to buy supplies, I often run into the Flying Stone Gang. Usually I have to pay them off‑offer them tea and put on a smile‑and barely get away without trouble.

I do. The Flying Stone Gang has long had it in for us ‑ they kept quiet for a while when our Eldest Senior Brother passed away and seemed fairly restrained, but lately they've reverted to their old ways and keep deliberately provoking us.
Aside from that, you two junior brothers—is there anything else you'd like to discuss?
When did this guy turn so vicious?
I don't care, I want to fiiiight!
This is far too reckless! Absolutely not!

My suggestion is to go all out and fight them right now ‑ fight it out properly. They still want to boss our sect around? First we take on the Wulin Alliance, then the Imperial Court. Whoever dares to provoke us, we strike them!
They're as close as brothers—how nice. Compared with Kongtong, being here at the Tang Clan is so much more comfortable.
Junior Brother... thank you!
You two junior brothers... thank you!
That's right. Even if things really go wrong, I'll be the first to run at the critical moment to lessen your guilt.

...To make a decision like that must take tremendous courage. Third Senior Brother, you don't need to be so anxious about gains and losses ‑ do your utmost and leave the rest to fate. Even if it all goes wrong, we'll share the burden with you.
They're as close as brothers—how nice. Compared with Kongtong, being here at the Tang Clan is so much more comfortable.
Junior Brother... thank you!
You two junior brothers... thank you!
Then I'll take responsibility for devising the pathetic schemes you don't dare imagine, so they can serve as a cautionary example.
Third Senior Brother, you stick to the righteous path; I'll come up with the underhanded tricks.

No ‑ this actually puts me a lot more at ease. For such an important matter, one can never be too careful. Although my mind may not be of much use and I still feel unsettled deep down, I'll do my best.
I can't help it; if you want to laugh at me for being indecisive, I have nothing to say.
After all, they both act before they think—they lash out in retaliation before anything's even crossed their minds.

Deciding the sect's fate in three days sounds rushed, but to the sect's members it had already been carefully considered. As for the Sect Leader and the Eldest Senior Brother, they wouldn't need even the blink of an eye to decide.

Therefore, I intend to receive counsel humbly and solicit collective wisdom, yet I fear speaking too soon ‑ that my private views might unsettle everyone, causing people to take my words as a barrier and limit themselves. So I will temporarily set them aside. To settle my thoughts, let us deal with other matters today and make a decision after three days.

Wavering back and forth, always unable to make up my mind. I'm not unaware that people are panicked right now, but the grimmer the situation, the more the sect leader must stand firm. I must remain calm and clear‑headed, not give in to anxiety or make rash decisions.

Know that this matter concerns the sect's rise or fall and its very survival; whatever decision is made will have far‑reaching consequences. I have been troubled for a long time. At one point I thought I had reached a firm conclusion, but I feared my outlook was too narrow and might harm the sect.
I should keep quiet from now on; I can't repeat the same mistake.
Oh no ‑ I shouldn't have stuck my nose in and tried to show off; I've embarrassed my husband.

What is Junior Brother's wife talking about? I heard it, but I didn't understand a word. Even Third Senior Brother, that old scholar, looked full of astonishment and admiration—are her words really that convincing? Looks like I'll need to treat Junior Brother more respectfully from now on; this must be a case of a husband gaining status through his wife.
That makes sense! Talented Woman Wei truly has penetrating insight — I am full of admiration.

When the realm follows the Way, governance does not lie with the ministers. When the realm follows the Way, the common people do not question it. The court has cultivated the Wulin Alliance, thinking to loose the tiger upon the wolf, but in truth has lost the greater for the sake of the lesser. Handing down authority to the lowly is a foolish, state-harming policy; and so, in this humble woman's view, it is utterly beyond foolish.

When the realm follows the Way, rites, music, and military campaigns issue from the Son of Heaven; when the realm lacks the Way, they issue from the feudal lords. If they issue from the feudal lords, it is rare that their rule survives ten generations; if from the ministers, rare that it survives five; and when lesser officials seize control of the state's fate, rare that it survives three.
Utterly foolish
I'm afraid it's not much different. Now the Wulin Alliance has the backing of the Imperial Court, and its leader acts as if carrying out the emperor's orders.
The tone of this proclamation is practically that of issuing an imperial edict.

If various schools sit in ignorance of impending omens, they will surely incur punishment from those yet to come. We hereby respectfully invite all factions of the Wulin to widely rally a just army, uphold righteousness, and restore order. On the fifteenth day of the first month, assemble in Xiangyang, Hubei, to besiege Six Paths Canyon. This proclamation is made known to all under heaven.

The edict brands the Mud Cult as vicious past redemption, consorting with depravity, and slaughtering the loyal and the upright. Entrenched behind the walls of Six Paths Canyon, they raised troops and gathered brigands, plundering the Jianghu year after year without paying tribute, defying the law of the land. Despised alike by gods and men, unfit to be suffered by heaven or earth.
This document is rather long, so I'll skip most of it and pick out a few of the most crucial points.
That's better than attacking us. When I saw the Jianghu Bulletin, I was even mentally prepared to sacrifice myself for our sect.

The Wulin Alliance spoke with one voice, all of them bent on holding our sect at Fengyu Mountain and torturing a confession out of us. And now they have the gall to send a proclamation calling us to their side - shameless, the lot of them.
That's exactly what I'm saying!

The incident where the Wulin Alliance nearly left our people tortured and coerced at Fengyu Mountain was something I heard about during my business dealings. How can they have the face to ask us to go to war with them again?
Gah‑ you startled me!
You scared me~
Don't be nervous ‑ they're not here to attack us. The Alliance Leader has called on the various Wulin sects to join forces to encircle and wipe out the Demon Cult.

If the Junior Martial Sister could sever ties with us without batting an eye, that wouldn't be such a bad thing. Even if our sect fell, she wouldn't be gossiped about - people would praise her instead for turning from evil to virtue, for putting righteousness above kin. Without the Tang Clan, she'd still have a home to return to, safe and sound.
Sigh‑not entirely. Among those who mix in the Jianghu, whose hands are clean? How could we not have killed or wounded members of the Wulin?
But we're being falsely accused!
That's true.

This can't be blamed solely on Junior Brother; the Tang Clan bears some responsibility too, for tolerating his wrongdoing. He has likewise earned credit with the sect, and that shouldn't be overlooked.
There's nothing to be proud of, okay? You little troublemaker.
Could it be that, by my own efforts alone, I have shaken the very foundations of the sect?
But we're being falsely accused! Is it only Junior Brother who's dragging down the Tang Clan's moral standards, okay?

To him, shouldering the Wulin's fate by wiping out the Demon Cult was not merely the tide of the times - it was also where duty lay, a thing he could not refuse. Before the grand righteousness of nation and people, it's no wonder he set aside private affections of the heart.
I'm not speaking in his defense; I'm just analyzing the alliance leader's motives based on the facts.
Third Senior Brother, why are you speaking up for an outsider?

To be fair, someone with Alliance Leader Rui's character would likely have many friends and confidants. Yet, when his close family and friends all tell him that the Tang Clan are followers of the Demon Cult, how can he not believe them?
Well... that's also true.
Junior Brother, you're mistaken. Allowing Junior Martial Sister to marry was never about trading her entire life for our safety.
Word has it Alliance Leader Rui has six lovely wives, each a peerless beauty with an impressive background. He loves them all - how could he possibly choose?
That bastard married our Junior Martial Sister and took her away‑doesn't he have the slightest regard for our ties?
Alliance Leader Rui is the Son-in-Law of the Tang Clan—does he have no regard for that relationship at all?
That's outrageous ‑ I want to eat it too.
Kill us all, and you'll still have time to go down the mountain and eat yuanxiao.

They closed with a dire warning, admonishing every faction that whoever ignores the omens now will surely bring punishment upon themselves for arriving too late. Thus the Wulin Alliance will raise a righteous army far and wide to uphold justice, mustering in Shu on the fifteenth day of the first month. This proclamation is issued to the realm, that all may hear and know.

It further claims the Tang Clan gallops under demonic banners, like fish swimming in a boiling cauldron. Before the pines and cypresses are felled, before the high tower topples, one should rein in the horse at the cliff's edge while there is still time, turn away from darkness, and step into the light.

The edict brands our Tang Clan as lackeys of the Demon Cult - perverse and unruly by nature, harboring wicked designs, consorting with depravity, and slaughtering the loyal and the upright. Despised alike by gods and men, unfit to be suffered by heaven or earth.
This document's purpose is to denounce the Tang Clan and set out their charges. The text is quite long, so I'll omit most of it and pick out a few of the most critical points to mention.
This morning, arrow-borne messages arrived at the Guest Pavilion; they turned out to be a proclamation from the Wulin Alliance.
This is an official proclamation
Didn't we already declare war last time?
Unsurprisingly, the Wulin Alliance has officially declared war on our sect.
Hmm, these lines are from the memorial written by Su Jushi for King Xuan. Third Master is a scholar, yet like me, they are also a drifting soul, wandering in the Jianghu.

Therefore, I am also deeply aware of the difficulties we face now. Only by broadly soliciting counsel and by working diligently and conscientiously can we‑together with all fellow junior disciples and classmates‑advance together, joining hands in mutual encouragement. Let us stem the raging tide that has already capsized and prop up the great edifice on the verge of collapse; let us restore the bright radiance of the sun and moon and dispel the oppressive gloom!
I am ashamed: my learning is scant and my virtue unworthy of this station; entrusted with it in this time of crisis, to temporarily assume the post of Sect Leader is truly humbling.
You're right. I'll be straight with you.
Acting Sect Leader, let's skip the pleasantries. It's just the three of us here; military matters are more pressing.
Ahem. Then the monthly meeting will begin. I am ashamed ‑ my learning is scant and my virtue is unworthy of this post; to temporarily assume the duties of sect leader is truly humiliating‑
Third Senior Brother agreed too, so that's naturally fine.
I will remain at your side and will not speak out of turn. My dear, may I be permitted to sit in and listen?
I intend to rely on Talented Woman Wei's outstanding insight and have therefore invited her to join our discussion.
Xiao Ju was there too
My dear.
Junior Martial Sister really means it...!
The Junior Martial Sister is genuinely clingy toward the Junior Martial Brother; there wasn't the slightest coercion.
Good morning, Junior Martial Sister
Good morning, Senior Brother
Hehe
Sound asleep again
Junior Brother, you're here
In the end, you still hit me!
Ah!
If you don't embarrass me, I won't hit you.
Even if I don't want to, I have to go along with it‑didn't you hear her say she was going to hit me?
We're family, so there's no need to be so formal. But when you're out and about you must pay attention to your appearance ‑ you should heed Madam Shangguan's advice.
That's not true. My mother never cared whether I lived or died; now at least someone is looking after me.
Completely under their wife's thumb‑like a housekeeper
All right. I was discourteous and may have embarrassed the Sect Leader and Fourth Brother. I will take my leave now.
Th‑thank you

Your collar isn't done up properly again! Are you a child? Late is one thing, but your appearance must be appropriate and your demeanor must show calmness‑don't be so fidgety and sloppy! I'm saying this nicely only once; if you mess up again, don't blame me for hitting you.
Zhao Huo!
Ah, I almost forgot. I'm going right away.
Senior Brother, the Acting Sect Leader sent me to summon you. Come to Zhengxin Hall at once—the meeting is missing one seat: yours.
Yes
...Although he was rather deserving of pity, seeing Fourth Junior Brother return, I truly couldn't help but feel happy.
It's far too early ‑ I'm only sketching an outline. I still have countless examples I haven't mentioned; all of you, listen up. Especially you! It's all your fault! I hate you!
Didn't you already finish complaining?
Whatever, I don't care! You have no idea how hard my journey back was! I just want to eat my fill, get a good night's sleep, and wake up to keep complaining to you.
Actually, it should be 'no point, no merchant' - point as in sharp, pointed. Doesn't that phrase mean common folk kindly heap on extra when they sell rice and grain?

I even felt like taking them down with me ‑ but it wasn't on purpose. Fortune and misfortune can come in an instant; how can it all be blamed on me? They don't show the slightest loyalty. No wonder people say there's no business without deceit ‑ they really are treacherous!
How should I put it... that's really awful.
Uh...

We barely escaped with our lives, but we lost all our capital. The other investors say I should bear full responsibility and actually kicked me out of the caravan I single‑handedly founded. They even sold off the goods, personnel, and horses cheaply to the Shangguan Trading Company ‑ all of that was my life's work...!
What can I do... That's the Wulin Alliance. If I help Jinxiang Palace, we might all be finished.
That's the Wulin Alliance ‑ one person's spit could drown us. Do you think I can single‑handedly take on a hundred?
Didn't you fail to take care of her? You unreliable fool!
We're on the same side as Jinxiang Palace!
The person he was talking about is Sister Xiang!
It's not impossible.

Why would the Jin emperor's niece be in the Central Plains, and why would she have ended up in the Jianghu, and still be in Jinxiang Palace...? This is far too far‑fetched ‑ surely someone just made up a story on the spot to extort you.

Because you bunch of maniacs killed people from Jinxiang Palace at the Wulin Assembly! The Jin emperor flew into a rage, saying his niece was in Jinxiang Palace and that he would send troops to attack the Song.
I'm not that powerful; I couldn't possibly shake the situation between two countries.

I was misled by your deceptive words and forced to change our route. Originally, even when Song and Jin were at odds, they didn't prohibit trade; as long as you had a Travel Permit they'd let you through. But the situation suddenly grew tense, we were treated as spies, and nearly couldn't make it back.
They must have come for the Wulin Assembly... How can that possibly be my fault?
That's true!
You really know their methods well; of course, it's not like that...
So... would it be better to be fair and smack you with a fish?
Bullshit! Treating people differently like this‑how do you think the other investors will react?
That's good.
Not really. Dharma King Liu can be ruthless with others, but he was fairly polite to me ‑ I didn't realize you had that much pull.
Liu... did Dharma King Liu harm you in any way?

I was misled by your deceptive words and forced to change our route. It wasn't much of a problem at first, but who would have thought we'd run into the Hungry Ghost Path from the East Sea halfway there and get robbed clean!
That's going too far! How did I ever offend you?
Because you look like a monster. If I dye your skin green and take you out to perform in the streets, wouldn't I make a fortune?
Why‑why would my value rise if I go to the Jin Kingdom?
For example, you're treated like dirt in the Tang Clan; once you're taken to the Jin Kingdom, your value instantly shoots up. Do you understand that?

Put bluntly, trading is about taking things that are common in one place to places where they're scarce. Rarity commands a premium; if people want it, the price is easy to hike. That's why the season and the route are fixed before setting out ‑ they can't be compared to solo peddlers.
How so?
I did ‑ I went the moment I got off the mountain. Thanks to you, everything's been messed up.
Oh... did you go to Huashan to seek an elixir?
Oh... did you go to visit the Junior Martial Sister?
Isn't it all because of your request, Junior Brother?
Don't pull, don't pull me~
Fourth Junior Brother, how could you leave and then come back!?
Fourth Senior Brother!
You really intend to stake your lives on this, huh?
Okay
No need to say more; I'll stay and see it through.

Do your part and leave the rest to Heaven. Didn't the Sect Leader always say that? A hero doesn't let fame or profit sway them; they only seek to hold their head high with a clear conscience. Even if we can already see the end, we must still stand tall and see this journey through.
That was in the past. Who allowed you to treat disciples from other surnames as less than human, ordering me about all the time? Third Senior Brother, why don't you leave?
The person you used to admire isn't here anymore. Weren't you always saying that if the Tang Clan had no Junior Martial Sister, you wouldn't stay another moment?
That would be far too unlike the Tang Clan's ways; I'm afraid that a hundred years from now the Tang Clan ancestors will grab my beard and scold me harshly. I won't be that sinner.
Unless you, Third Senior Brother, order the Tang Clan to shut down its operations, we will collectively retire from the Jianghu.
Whether it's the person I love, my brothers and friends, or my home ‑ they're all here.
......Don't try to talk me into coming down the mountain, hiding my identity, and merely surviving, okay?
I have something to say to you ‑ not as the acting sect leader, but as Third Senior Brother.
What's going on?
‑Junior Brother.
Yes.

At the very least, the two had kowtowed in the Tang family ancestral hall and given a solemn farewell. As for leaving without saying goodbye and slipping quietly down the mountain‑that would be going a bit too far.
Sigh. Over the past few days, quite a few junior disciples have come to me to discuss where to go. When disaster looms, everyone looks out for themselves‑it's only natural.
I couldn't help myself for a moment.
Junior Brother, if they're leaving, let them go ‑ why force them to stay? Even if you can stop them for a time, they'll still leave whenever they choose.
Ah...
Senior Brother, you bastard!
Ah!
Hah!
I was wrong to blame you.
Junior Brother... I didn't realize you'd gone to such lengths.

They've practiced martial arts for so long ‑ isn't it a pity if they retire without ever testing themselves against the great heroes of their time? I'll be a roadblock and let them charge through; that's the only way to do right by their youth. Look how much gusto they showed fighting me just now.
They left ‑ so be it. Why make things harder on yourself?
Ow! Go ahead and leave ‑ and you even kicked me!
Screw you!
Seize the moment!
Wow!
That's about it
What happened? It sounds like they were about to leave but then didn't?
Of course you can — go to Zhengxin Hall and kowtow yourselves, then hang the nameplate back on the wall.
Third Senior Brother, we've had a change of heart. We'd like to stay at the Tang Clan for a while longer — would that be possible?
We should at least put on a show to keep up appearances; if worse comes to worst, we'll wait until they reach the doorstep and then figure things out.
Yes — even Senior Brother, an outsider disciple, hasn't abandoned us. When we became disciples we received countless favors; how can we, when disaster strikes, just up and leave?
Do you think so too?
Junior Brother, how about we... take it slow?
What is it...?
We were going to leave, but we changed our minds.
Yes, of course, we'll always be friends
Take care, my two junior brothers. I hope fate brings us together again someday so we can share a drink and enjoy ourselves; even if we're no longer fellow disciples, we'll still be friends.
A Polite Farewell
Yes, Senior Brother — you too. Promise us you'll be sure to wreak havoc for a thousand years to come.
Get lost, you two little scoundrels. Live a little longer.
Farewell Banter
Junior Brother, what are you doing?!
Senior Brother, you really came!
That's not what you said last time!
Trying to leave? Not so easy — you'll have to get past me first!
Thinking of leaving? No way, buddy!
Oh
Senior Brother, the two of us will be taking our leave and descending the mountain as of today.
We're leaving now

You go out alone to stroll and browse. Used to being short on money, you can't think of anything you want besides food. You grab a casual bite and a drink, soak up a bit of the lively crowd, and pretend you have a home to return to.
You snatched back the money that had just been taken.
Use Burning Knife Liquor.
You didn't care at all whether he had any excuse; with a single stroke of your sword you cut him down, wiped away the blood, and left his corpse on the ground.
Anyone who harms my master shall be killed without mercy.

You felt deep sympathy for his plight; it wasn't his fault, but his master for being too beautiful. When he heard you say that, he immediately burst into tears, felt a kinship with you, and you shook hands to make peace. Xiahou Lan looked on coldly, with nothing to say.
Let go

Along the way you encounter one of Xiahou Lan's admirers—spurned and heartlessly driven off, his love turned to hatred, curdling into envy of you, this ugly man; he wished nothing more than to kill you at once.

The notorious reputation of Soul-Stealing Orchid had even reached the county magistrate's ears, and he trembled through the whole hearing. He wished he could hack that lecherous scoundrel to a thousand pieces for his shameless audacity in dragging this witch to the yamen. Terrified that a verdict not to her liking would bring calamity on himself, he hastily sent her travel money afterward.

Xiahou Lan, finding it a hassle, wanted to kill the criminal on the spot, but you insisted on going out of your way to hand the criminal over to the authorities. She sighed and had no choice but to follow as a witness.
Arrest them and take them before the magistrate.

You killed that lecherous bandit with a single thrust of your sword and looted the valuables on his body. Though it was still one criminal robbing another, it could be considered ridding the people of a menace, so the good cancels out the bad... right?
With a single stroke of your sword you brought the evil bandit to justice, ridding the people of a menace.
Anyone who harms my master shall be killed without mercy.

Your compassion got the better of you; you were moved by the criminal's plea and easily let them go. Xiahou Lan was extremely displeased and deeply disappointed in you. Xiahou Lan ordered you to wait where you were, then pursued and killed the person.
Let go

On the way you encountered a lecherous bandit who coveted Xiahou Lan's beauty and intended to drug and assault. Xiahou Lan, knowing the tea was poisoned, still made you drink it and pushed you forward to take the blade.

Fully aware that Soul-Stealing Orchid kills without blinking, she still dared to block your path and hurl abuse, intent on violence—as if she'd already resigned herself to death. You didn't scorn her for being a woman, and with a single stroke of your sword, you granted her that resolve.
Anyone who harms my master shall be killed without mercy.
You let the challenger go, since they were the opponent you had to deal with. Xiahou Lan, though displeased, did not complain.
Let go

On the way, you ran into an enemy of Xiahou Lan's, who roared in fury, 'Soul-Stealing Orchid, your crimes are unforgivable—you'll come to a wretched end!' Catching sight of you next, she snarled, 'Rat-faced and shifty-eyed—one look and I can tell you're no good either! You can die too!' Xiahou Lan coldly shoved you aside.
Under Master Orchid's guidance, you integrated the teachings and grasped the secret of the lethal technique. The master was gratified and said you are a promising pupil.
Under Master Orchid's guidance, your techniques and footwork became even more fluid and natural. Master Orchid looked as if this were only to be expected, her expression unchanged.
Under Master Orchid's guidance, handling blade-and-sword weapons became even more second nature to you. The master acted as if it were only to be expected, her expression unchanged.

Songshan monks have many karmic ties with the Tang Clan and cannot bear to see the Tang Clan decline. They accompanied you along the way, hoping to use the Dharma to influence you and urge you all to abandon evil and return to the right path. The junior disciples, having been continually exposed to this, gradually lost their fighting spirit and even began to contemplate entering monastic life.

The Old Monk never lived to see you arrive, yet he never doubted you. The seeds of a good cause have been sown; they need no witness from me—let them grow into flourishing branches and leaves, leaving shade for those who come after.
The Songshan Sect and the Tang Clan parted ways, and the Old Monk, with a kindly face, returned alone to the monastery.
Respectfully bidding farewell to Dharma Master Juexing and Dharma Master Fu Yun.
This humble monk shall likewise take his leave.

Now that this old monk has seen you, my wish is fulfilled; whether I attend the Wulin Assembly no longer matters. I will set out to return to my mountain gate, chant sutras and pray for peace throughout the land, so that the day when you and I can delve into the Dharma may arrive sooner.
Yes, I will respectfully follow the Master's teachings.
Benefactor, please rise. You possess a root of wisdom and should not be misled by worldly appearances. Kneel to your parents, kneel to the Bodhisattvas, but do not kneel to ordinary beings.
This disciple bows in thanks, Master.
Yes

This text speaks of a future Great Hero, Zhao Huo, who will attain precepts, concentration, wisdom, and self-sacrifice to save the world by entering Songshan. Teaching this unique technique is to save one person, as well as countless good beings. Benefactor, is that correct?
No. The one this old monk passed it on to was not you.
Th‑this isn't Songshan's signature sacred technique, is it? Master, how could you pass it on to me, an outer disciple?

Benefactor Zhao, you live in a turbid world; it is rare that your heart remains clear as a mirror, unstained by dust. By sowing a good cause today and keeping your heart and intention right in the days ahead, you will surely reap good fruit. This old monk wishes to present this book to you, Benefactor.
Many thanks, Grand Martial Uncle, for enlightening me
Subhuti, the past mind cannot be grasped, the present mind cannot be grasped, the future mind cannot be grasped.
Not yet
Then, Benefactor Zhao can also be counted as one of my Songshan disciples.
Yes

Amituofo, well said. Then it is settled: so long as the Jianghu is at peace, the nation prosperous and the people secure, and the weather favorable — in short, while the world has no need of Young Hero Zhao's sacrifice — you shall come to Songshan to study the Dharma.
Being allowed to study at Songshan would be this junior's honor ‑ how could I possibly refuse?
If it's just studying at another sect, I'm naturally more than willing.
Respectfully seeing off the two Dharma Masters
Benefactor Zhao, farewell for now. See you again in Yueyang.
Everyone has their own fate; since that is so, this old monk will not press the matter. Now, this old monk and my grand-nephew disciple shall take our leave of the Young Hero.
Allow me to refuse; I don't want to become a monk.
Perhaps. I'm only asking what your intention is?
Could there really be such a day?

I wouldn't presume to press you; I'm only asking. Someday in the future, if the Jianghu is at peace, the country prosperous and the people safe, and the weather favorable, Young Hero, would you be willing to come to my Songshan to study?
Master, please speak. So long as it is within my ability, I am willing to carry out your orders.
This may be sudden, Young Hero, but this old monk has an impertinent request.
Master, you flatter me. I only seek to live well in the present.
Excellent, excellent. Young Hero Zhao, you too possess an exceptional root of wisdom; blessed to perceive the true principle, you are destined to walk the path of the sage.
Is there anyone in the world who isn't a mere mortal?

Young Hero, no need to be so modest — this grand-nephew disciple of mine is quite gifted, an outstanding talent among Songshan's younger generation. He's mentioned Young Hero Zhao more than once, which shows you are no ordinary person.
How could I ever be compared to my senior brothers?

In former times I heard that the Flying Hero, the Ruthless Young Lord, and the Scholar Hero were all heroic figures. Then a Tang Clan Ugly Hero suddenly burst onto the scene, and the Tang Clan produced talent after talent‑Old Sect Leader Tang could take comfort in his old age.

Prajna Hall, Dharma Hall, and Luohan Hall are all places within the Songshan Sect devoted to researching and teaching martial arts. Prajna Hall broadly embraces martial arts from across the realm and maintains close ties with Guest Hall.
Young Hero, there's no need to be polite.
I, this humble disciple of the Wulin, pay my respects to Master Juexing.

Benefactor Zhao, this monk is off to reunite with my fellow disciples, so we shall trouble your Clan no further. Before we part, allow me to introduce you — this is my Grand Martial Uncle, Elder Juexing, Chan Master of our sect, who oversees Songshan's Prajna Hall.
Not the same person... That's it, this one is the real one. Monk Wunian only disguised himself as this elder monk.
The hairs on your skin stood on end, yet you saw the old monk with his hands clasped, compassionate eyes lowered, and not an ounce of hostility about him.
Monk Wunian...!

The Songshan monks and the Tang Clan had many karmic ties and felt considerable goodwill toward one another. They traveled together for a while, the monks also collecting alms; so as not to delay the Tang Clan's itinerary, the monks pressed their palms together in farewell.
We've encountered Songshan's forces!

When bystanders began to comment, you twisted the truth, escalated the matter into a dispute between two countries, and kept insisting it was meant to teach Quanzhen a lesson for siding with the Jin. The crowd immediately thought you weren't so hateful.
You picked a fight for no reason, defeated the elder Daoist who was leading the team, flaunted your martial prowess to show off, satisfied your vanity, and then left.
You chose to eat in silence and paid it no mind. After hastily finishing your meal and saying farewell to your Junior Martial Brothers and Sisters, you set off early to avoid the Quanzhen Sect.
Live and let live
Driven by insecurity and eager to provoke and assert your dominance, you overturned the table and challenged the Quanzhen leader.
How dare they look down on the Tang Clan! They're asking for a beating!

They took an avid interest in Jianghu affairs and never tired of them, yet failed to recognize the Tang Clan figure in the blue robe. Proud of being the leaders of the Six Great Sects, they scorned to come over and offer a greeting.

They didn't know you at all, but the moment they saw your plain blue robe they immediately recognized you as a Tang Clan Disciple. Especially you ‑ without being acquainted, they could tell at a glance that you must be the well‑known Tang Clan Ugly Hero. After a bit of small talk and getting to know you, they'll have plenty to brag about when they return.

They encountered the Quanzhen Sect. Although Quanzhen considers itself one of the Six Great Sects, it has sided with the Jin Kingdom; when its members saw you being escorted by the Song Kingdom's Imperial Soldiers, they were even more ashamed to face you and all stepped aside to let you through.
You encountered members of the Quanzhen Sect on the road.

News that the Diancang Sect had been set back by the Tang Clan while on the road spread, and somehow it turned into a story that the Tang Clan had ambushed and treacherously plotted against Diancang. You weren't quick to explain; instead the Diancang Sect went around trying to dispel the rumors.
The Tang Clan was thwarted by the Diancang sect on the road, completely lost face, and became a laughingstock.

But the relatives and friends who were close to your adversary all looked at you with gratitude. The feud between the two families won't vanish immediately, but you have sown seeds of kindness; the next generation of Diancang people will remember your magnanimity.

In the fierce fight, you still remembered to hold back, besting the powerful enemy with your small sword while sparing their life. The master of the Diancang sect couldn't bear to lose face and left sullenly.
Show mercy

In the fierce fight you didn't hold back; a Diancang expert fell beneath your small sword. Diancang was grief‑stricken and furious, but since they had initiated the challenge, there was no grievance over life and death. They said little then, merely cupped their hands and led the corpse away ‑ this grudge is likely only to deepen.
Murder
You want to fight? Bring it on ‑ I'll fuck your mother!

They wouldn't listen to reason. Putting the greater good first and unwilling to create unnecessary complications before the Wulin Assembly, you stepped forward through the crowd, drew your small sword, crossed blades with the opponent's long sword, and accepted the challenge.
Select representatives for one‑on‑one sparring

Faced with the Diancang Sect's provocation, you put the bigger picture first and, unwilling to cause an incident before the Wulin Assembly, chose to swallow your anger and yield, allowing them to be arrogant and taunt you once before you left.
Don't create unnecessary complications; swallow your anger and keep silent.
They encountered the Tang Clan's long‑standing enemy, the Diancang sect. Old grudges flared at the sight of each other, and the situation was on the brink of erupting!

They ran into the Tang Clan's long‑time rivals, the Diancang Sect. Ye Yunzhou's cang‑colored garments didn't stand out among the Tang Clan's blue robes, but precisely because the group was so harmonious, it was all the more galling. Someone shouted traitor! and the Tang Clan members drew their swords ‑ the situation was about to erupt.

They ran into the Tang Clan's sworn enemy, the Diancang sect. Seeing the Ye siblings among the Tang Clan's ranks—the Tang Clan seemingly risen from the brink of death—and recalling rumors of the Yue family's treasure, they concluded that you had taken advantage of Diancang. Swords were drawn one after another; the situation was on the verge of erupting.

You encountered the Tang Clan's longtime rival, the Diancang sect. At first the Diancang forces, seeing the Tang Clan's colors, were eager to test them, but when they suddenly realized your party was being escorted by officials and Imperial Soldiers they were taken aback and promptly stepped aside.

You led the Tang Clan Disciples in a hard‑fought battle against Kongtong's formidable foes. Seeing that you were difficult to deal with, Venerable Golden Crow had no choice but to sound the gong and withdraw, reserving some strength for the Wulin Assembly. Although you were angry, there was nothing you could do.

The Tang Clan suffered a setback at the hands of the Kongtong sect, lost all face, and became a laughingstock. Because you carried letters of summons‑having been summoned by the Imperial Court‑Venerable Golden Crow did not dare to kill you outright. After mocking you thoroughly, he simply turned and walked away.

Having agreed to meet again at Fengyu Mountain, the Kongtong disciples one after another bowed and cupped their hands to you. You cupped your hands and nodded, signaling the Kongtong disciples to go first. The Tang Clan Junior Martial Brothers and Sisters, seeing you calm and composed and already bearing the air of a great master, were all filled with admiration.

Having agreed to meet again at Fengyu Mountain, the Kongtong Disciples one after another bowed and offered the cupped‑hand salute to you. You dared not be haughty; you quickly clasped your fist in return and respectfully saw the Kongtong Disciples off as they departed.
Sect Leader Wei really doesn't seem like someone from the Wulin; she comes across more like a government official.
When she finished speaking, Sect Leader Wei bowed with her hands clasped and withdrew from your sight. Her adherence to ceremony was so strict it could rival the imperial court.
The Sect Leader must not crush their subordinates; the duties of the Four Sect Leaders amount to little more than obeying the Sect Leader's commands and giving their all in service to our sect.
All right, thank you for your hard work, Sect Leader Wei. Kongtong isn't affected by my being a titular sect leader; without you it really wouldn't work.
Kongtong can do without me, a Sect Leader in name only, but without Sect Leader Wei, it would be a disaster.
In that case, I will accompany Senior Brother Danxiazi, assist along the way, and submit my resignation to the Sect Leader.
Xiao Ju is usually poised and composed, but at this moment her tender heart is fixed on you. After a few intimate words, she was overcome with shyness, couldn't bear to face you, and hurried away.
After the Wulin Assembly, I will go with you to the Tang Clan and kneel before Sect Leader Tang. From then on... we shall truly be husband and wife.

No... not in broad daylight ‑ it's far too embarrassing. My dear... my dear, please be considerate of your little sister; I still have to lead the Kongtong troops. If people see a young woman like me showing such coy, bashful behavior, how will I ever face anyone?
You needn't come; I'll do just as Hongfu Nü did when she fled to Li Jing by night — and rush to your side.
I'm afraid you'll change your mind. If you don't come soon, I'll have to go up to Kongtong and snatch you.

Although Wei Ju is a woman and was taught propriety and a sense of decency, how could she be fickle? Now that she has chosen her beloved in this life, she will follow you wholeheartedly and never regret it.
I was so afraid that once you calmed down and thought it over for a while, you'd change your mind.
{size=24}... But this humble one was truly delighted to hear it.{/size}
Oh.
What virtue or talent do I have to deserve my dear's concern? You are the Kongtong Sect Leader and the pillar of the Tang Clan — you mustn't let romantic feelings dull a hero's resolve.
That's wonderful ‑ I've missed you every moment since we parted.
By the end, Xiao Ju's voice was almost inaudible, and her face had flushed so deeply it looked as if it might smoke.

I have properly handed over the leadership and records of the Mystic Skill Gate. This time I wish to submit my resignation to you, Sect Leader. After the Wulin Assembly, I will step down as sect leader, go to the Tang Clan, and live with my dear...
Yes, Xiao Ju is here, my dear.
Sect Leader Wei... Xiao Ju.
But as a man, what's the big deal about three wives and four concubines? No matter how many beautiful women there are, I can handle them all.
How should I tell her that my affections have moved on to someone else?
I dare not think too highly of myself; supporting my husband is a wife's duty.
As befits Sect Leader Wei, Kongtong's foremost talented woman.
Is that so? I had thought he kept insisting I was the head of the sect, yet he didn't take me seriously.

Senior Brother Danxiazi has spent years on the front lines; because of that, the sect was nearly usurped by treacherous men, and it has weighed on him ever since. Now he is eager to atone through merit, which is why he's so anxious. He never meant to slight the Sect Leader — I beg the Sect Leader to be magnanimous and not hold it against him.
General of Dao Techniques, wait— ah, he's already gone.
Now that we have the sect leader's approval, I'll go at once to dispatch the men and horses!

Sect Leader Wei's words just woke me from a dream. To turn enemies into friends and bridge the rift between our two sects — this truly is a golden opportunity. Otherwise, even without an open fight, a grudge nursed in secret means we're bound to settle the score when next we meet in the Jianghu.
Uh... I didn't think that far ahead at all.

Kongtong clearing the way is both a show of sincerity and a statement of intent, to silence the wagging tongues of the world. When the Wulin Assembly comes, our two sects will stand as one, and petty schemers will be too unsettled to dare stir up mischief. I ask the Sect Leader to consider this carefully.
Even though, out of regard for the Sect Leader, the Tang Clan did not pursue the matter, the Jianghu will surely gossip about it. Now is an excellent chance to make amends through merit.
I would like to hear the details.
Reporting, Sect Leader: I believe Senior Brother Danxiazi's request is sound.
Our sect already has an escort of imperial troops. If Kongtong marched alongside us as well, the procession would look far too grand — it really would seem ostentatious.
There's no need for this.
Sect Leader, I humbly volunteer to serve as vanguard ‑ to lead Kongtong's men and horses forward, open the way for the Tang Clan, and clear the dangers ahead.

It's not that I don't love fame and fortune ‑ the problem is that a whole lot of people in Kongtong want to murder me. Rather than shamelessly clinging on and being resented, I'd rather retire after accomplishing my deeds and earn a good reputation.
No, how could I possibly do that?

How can I dare be called a leader? I am merely a woman holding an empty title.
When it comes to commanding troops on campaign, Kongtong rightly ranks the General of Dao Techniques first.
Now that I've had the good fortune to meet the Sect Leader, I shall naturally follow his lead.
Kongtong is held by the three Sect Leaders of Flying Heaven, Soul-Stealing, and Iron Fist. Our party here is led by Sect Leader Wei.
Indeed, heroes and heroic figures throughout the realm are likely all on the road at this moment; it's not just the Tang Clan and Kongtong.
May I ask, Sect Leader: since you are leading the Tang Clan's heroes on this trip, you are presumably headed to Fengyu Mountain in Yueyang to attend the Wulin Assembly, aren't you?
Sect Leader, what are you saying? Though it's a pity your subordinate couldn't pay respects to Lady Lan, there's no need to apologize.
She prefers peace and quiet and seldom shows herself in public, so she will not come to see you; please forgive her.
Haha!
Is that so! Hahaha!
She appears and disappears like a ghost, secretly watching me, making me so on edge that I'm all jittery even when I step out to relieve myself in the middle of the night.
Isn't Lady Lan attending to the Sect Leader?
Ah—and don't forget to let Lord Song know as well; ask the soldiers to rest and regroup where they are.
If the Sect Leader doesn't nod his consent, we're not going anywhere.
I'll go. Senior Brother Danxiazi, Sect Leader Wei, you two must wait for me to come back before you leave, okay?

I'll go tell the Tang Clan's junior disciples to rest here.
Kongtong is a friend now, not an enemy; there's no need to treat them like mortal adversaries.
At your command
Okay
Okay—I won't be coming back for a while. I'd like to go find Xiao Zhu. Is that all right?

Xiaomei, please tell our Junior Martial Brothers and Sisters to rest where they are.
Kongtong is a friend now, not an enemy; there's no need to treat them like a mortal foe.
What am I to do about this...?

Being Sect Leader is not merely a position; it is Kongtong's highest spiritual symbol, signifying the end of the chaotic era.
