Even if one could not die a hero's death for one's country upon the battlefield, to lay down one's armor and return home to the fields was, however plain, a fitting end.

Having read the letter through, Ye Yunzhou's eyes welled with tears. Eighty years had passed, but at last he had an answer, settling a wish three generations old. Recalling the years of suffering and humiliation he had endured, he felt both sorrow and joy.

Having read the letter through, the Ye siblings' eyes welled with tears. Eighty years had passed in hardship, but at last they had an answer, settling a wish three generations old. Recalling the years of suffering and humiliation they had endured, torn between sorrow and joy, they held each other and wept.

She was quite polite to you, though she couldn't hand over the four disgraces of her own sect for you to deal with. She generously admitted that Lingnan owed a debt to you and the Ye siblings, treating it as a personal favor she owed you.

She was quite polite to you; though she could not hand the four disgraces of her own sect over for you to deal with, she generously acknowledged that Lingnan owed a debt to you and the Ye siblings, treating it as a personal favor she owed you, and entrusted you with delivering a heavy bundle to the Ye siblings.

You couldn't bear your friend's constant kneeling, so you reluctantly agreed. This gift was no ordinary item; to the uninitiated, it appeared as a mere old silver spear head, but to those who knew its history, it stirred deep emotion. This weapon had been kept in a high place for over eighty years, its rusted surface marred by time. Without polishing, its former sharpness could not be revealed. Yet it had once been drenched in the scalding blood of heroes. Even if remade, it would never lose its essence of righteous spirit.
Among them, a Double Carp Box was precisely the news that the ancestors of the Ye clan had hidden in the mountains and forests, enduring hardship by sleeping on thorns and tasting gall, waiting for.
You opened the bundle on the table that Nan Xi had placed there, and couldn't help but startle.
You had never met a decent person from Lingnan, so you dared not let your guard down. Borrowing chopsticks from the inn, you used a deft touch to pry open the bundle, and couldn't help but startle.

You wanted to take a leisurely soak, washing away the dust of the day, then go downstairs to call for a pot of wine to drown your sorrows. Unbeknownst to you, you weren't seeking trouble, but trouble came to you. As fate would have it, the roads of enemies run narrow: the Lingnan sect's party had put up at the very same inn, barking orders at the waiter, demanding food, overturning tables, and letting their words run wild. You couldn't stand it anymore, intending to step in and deal with them, but upon hearing their boastful tales of framing the Ye siblings, your steps halted. The more you listened, the angrier you became, crushing the handrail on the second floor. The words they spewed were not just a few sentences but malicious rumors spread with the intent to kill, as dangerous as blades and swords. Such deep hatred could not be easily settled; you had to take them, bring them before the victims, and let the Ye siblings deal with them. However, there was another unexpected guest that night, a swordswoman dressed in Lingnan-style attire. The difference was that she was a true lineage disciple of the Lingnan sect, named Nan Xi, exuding a sharp and ruthless aura, unwilling to waste words on her wayward sect-mates. She turned on her horse and cut off four heads with a single sword strike, so decisive it left everyone in awe. You couldn't help but feel startled, not yet realizing that the Jianghu had produced such a powerful heroine.

Your junior martial brothers and sisters feared you'd embarrass yourself going out, and your explosive temper flared at once—so they teamed up, beat you down, sealed your acupoints, and left you tossed aside.

Your Junior Martial Brothers and Sisters feared you'd embarrass yourself going out, and your explosive temper flared up at once—so they teamed up and beat you down, then force-fed you the Tang Clan's Docile Draught. After a while you settled down, all serene compassion, as though worldly troubles no longer touched you. More detached than the monks of Songshan themselves—Amituofo.
Once the auspicious hour arrived, incense and candles were lit, prayers were chanted up to heaven, and an oath was sworn in blood—and so today's Wulin Assembly came to a successful close.
You also stepped down cheerfully.
Only a fool like you would dare to try to oust him from power without knowing your own limits, only to be scolded by the crowd and run away in tears‑this is what's called self‑inflicted humiliation.
Only a madman like you would be so reckless as to try kicking him off his seat, drawing the crowd's fury and nearly getting beaten to death for it.

Xiang Wuyou's smile broadened as he stepped down from the Wulin Alliance Leader's seat, putting forward Nangong Yuan and declaring himself willing to serve at his command. Nangong Yuan was taken aback and tried to decline, but it was no use. He harbored great ambitions, excelled in martial arts, possessed ample wealth, and enjoyed high prestige; he could rally the mighty warriors to gather in Jiangling, reconcile past grievances among the court and common people, and forge a united front. The cohesion of the Nangong Family was beyond doubt. Twenty years ago, when the Supreme Bliss Cult rose and Long Yuan burst onto the scene, it was the times that made heroes, and he narrowly missed the Alliance Leader's seat; he bided his time in the shadows for two decades, watching widely but taking sparingly, building deep reserves to spend them well. To ask who was fit to lead the Wulin in this age—who else could it be?

You don't agree, so you don't care about others' suffering, only seeking your own well‑being. The saying If a person doesn't take care of themselves, heaven and earth will punish them is realistic, though not entirely without merit. No one has to sacrifice for others; living well for oneself is enough.

You don't agree, but living in this era, with your wisdom, you can't think of a better way for now. Nangong Yuan smiled slightly, not showing annoyance. He didn't consider himself the wisest in the world; he only believed that by starting something now, future generations with even greater wisdom would eventually be born into the world.
You also yearn for it, embracing his vision of a harmonious society.
He and Ruixing are like two extremes‑childish and unrealistic, talkative and not worth much scrutiny, yet one can't help but want to support him and follow him.

Yet this is no easy task; trust is not given freely. Though the path is rugged and long, if it does not begin with each of us in the present moment, the ideal of great unity will forever remain an empty dream. Even if a sage rules, one person's strength alone cannot change the world's course‑only a gathering of like‑minded individuals rising in unison can make a difference. Learning other countries' languages, respecting foreign customs, releasing goodwill, and extending oneself to others. Not belittling others, yet never forgetting self‑improvement. To maintain a humble yet confident demeanor, one must first possess inner depth. Even if we cannot complete this in our lifetime, as long as there are still people in the world who share the same hope, the spark will not die out. It can be passed down, enduring for centuries without giving up. One day, the world will surely know no war. Every household will have enough to eat, and there will no longer be anyone cursing others' misfortune. Nangong Yuan spoke with unwavering confidence, just as he had in his youth, full of righteous ambition. Not only did the heroes of the world admire his benevolent heart, but Lady Wen was also deeply moved. Those who had once scattered in different directions were all drawn by Nangong Yuan's dream, bravely stepping into the storm. Drenched to the bone, they laughed heartily, and those years still shine brightly to this day.

The first two questions were just prelude; it is in this third question posed to Xiang Wuyou that the point finally comes into focus, startling all: One day, you will annihilate the Jin soldiers, march north with the army to reclaim the land, and at the command of your general, the soldiers will inevitably plunder along the way to replenish military supplies. If they meet a decisive general, they may even burn, kill, and massacre cities, cutting off the Jin army's path to resurgence. When two nations clash, it is the torrent of the times, impossible to judge good or evil in a word‑but what fault lies with the commoners? That day, when the Jin commoners perished under Song people's blades, could you still call yourselves heroes? Throughout history, kings, princes, and generals have expanded territories and built their achievements‑ask what achievements they truly build. Aren't they mostly deeds of killing? When one general succeeds, ten thousand bones wither. That is someone else's success; what pride can your own crushed bones bring you? The heroes present and the Jin people alike are caught between heaven and earth, all merely commoners sacrificed for the achievements of others. This question is both a question and not a question; each listener feels it differently. Some are shaken into reflection; some are angered beyond bearing, seeing Sect Leader Xiang, a native of the Central Plains, as betraying national prestige, no different from a traitor. Shangguan Shangzhi naturally has an answer to this question, likely the most practical one, but cannot speak it aloud, for it is not what the crowd wishes to hear, and is thus met with scorn and silence. Nangong Shangren finds this question coinciding with the longstanding wishes of his family: his predecessors, even those who once served as Wulin Alliance Leader, devoted their lives to pursuing an ideal they knew could not be attained, yet committed fully toward it. In the great way of things, the world belongs to all.

National righteousness comes first; a normal person wouldn't oppose it. Unfortunately, you're not a normal person. Spouting nonsense and pouring cold water, quenching the fervor and aspirations that the crowd had painstakingly ignited, and skillfully inciting the crowd's hostility toward the Imperial Court, intentionally sabotaging Commissioner Shangguan's imperial mission. Looking at his visibly enraged expression, it's clear the effect was significant. You've dealt a severe blow to the harmony of the Wulin Assembly. This time, you've truly retaliated against the Shangguan family.
Even if the Imperial Court does not call for it, any man of integrity would not let it go unchecked.
National righteousness comes first; a normal person wouldn't go against it. Personal grievances of the Jianghu‑how could they be more important than national righteousness?

National righteousness comes first; a normal person wouldn't oppose it. Moreover, you've studied the works of sages; compassion is the beginning of benevolence, and shame is the beginning of righteousness. Even a wicked person would maintain appearances; otherwise, how could they be called a hypocrite?

National righteousness comes first; a normal person would not oppose it, especially since you've studied the classics. Compassion is the beginning of benevolence; shame is the beginning of righteousness. Personal grievances in Jianghu are insignificant compared to national righteousness.
Your opinion is also the same; this matter has nothing to do with good and evil.

Following the second question, it was asked: The Jin Kingdom has repeatedly invaded our Great Song territory. Should the court call for troops one day, will all of you heed the orders and defend the country against the Jin? This question needed no doubt. Both emotionally and logically, in public and private, there could be no reason not to follow the command. Shangguan Family Head agreed first, followed by Nangong Family Head's immediate support.
You think it's not possible; since ancient times, righteousness and evil have never coexisted, so naturally, they cannot coexist.
You support the Nangong Family Head's opinion, believing that the path of coexistence may exist.

With no one stepping forward to compete, the Jinxiang Palace, Nangong Family Estate, and Beggar Sect showed little interest in contesting. It seemed that the dust was about to settle, with Sect Leader Xiang likely to assume the role of Wulin Alliance Leader without much doubt. However, there was still one person who refused to accept this outcome‑that was himself, Xiang Wuyou. Please have the Shangguan Family Head pause, and invite the Nangong Family Head to take the stage; unfortunately, the Tang Family Sect Leader did not attend, so it would do for you to join as well. The Three Great Families listened to his three questions. The first question was: Could the Mud Cult coexist with the Wulin's rightful path? The Shangguan Family Head, now having an official position, would naturally consider everything from the perspective of the court and could not tolerate the Mud Cult causing unrest that might undermine the state's foundation. On the other hand, the Nangong Family Head held a more reserved opinion; if it was for the benefit of the nation and its people, reconciliation with the Mud Cult was not entirely impossible.

Even knowing the court was secretly watching from behind, you of the Tang Clan could never have any claim to the position of Alliance Leader, yet you couldn't help being consumed with envy all the same, hurling barbed words at someone you barely knew.

You gave no clear answer. The Alliance Leader's reputation for benevolence and justice is a blessing for the Jianghu; even were the Alliance Leader inept, it would still be no business of you, Tang Clan of Shu, to interfere. The Tang Clan touches neither black nor white, only watching from the sidelines.

Emei's Sect Leader Xiang Wuyou, since entering the battlefield, has been invincible, defeating several powerful opponents. Throughout the fight, he remains calm, his flowing sleeves fluttering gracefully. Qingcheng's Sect Leader, the Daoist Zou Bo, couldn't help but feel a surge of competitive spirit, stepping onto the battlefield to challenge him. He employed Qingcheng's superior sword techniques and palm methods, his demeanor stern and imposing, vastly different from Emei's graceful agility. One was static, the other dynamic, representing two extremes. According to expectation, Xiang Wuyou had already fought several opponents, and even if it wasn't a life-or-death battle, his True Qi would still be drained. However, Sect Leader Zou, being a fair and upright master, deliberately avoided using Qingcheng's deep internal skills, choosing instead to rely solely on technique to determine the outcome. Naturally, he fell behind, and as the battle continued, his disadvantage became more apparent. When their palms clashed, both staggered back, then laughed at each other. They admired each other's integrity and martial arts skills. Even Qingcheng's Sect Leader Zou was willing to concede defeat. The arena fell silent; who would dare step forward to humiliate themselves? Moreover, Xiang Wuyou's extraordinary demeanor carried an ethereal and sage-like bearing, earning the crowd's admiration. No one wanted to take advantage of his exhausted state, and even if they won, it wouldn't be honorable.

Ye Yunshang vaguely knew her elder brother would never return, leaving her behind at the Tang Clan and entrusting her to you. She couldn't help but feel a wave of sorrow, collapsing into your arms and sobbing uncontrollably. You softly comforted her, promising Yunshang that once the dust settled, you would go searching for Ye Yunzhou together. Even if Ye Yunzhou wandered the world, there would always be a time they would meet again.
Fellow disciples of the clan greeted him with joyful shouts, arms slung over shoulders, and only then did Ye Yunzhou call himself a disciple of the Tang Clan.
Ye Yunshang's eyes were filled with tears, flinging herself into her elder brother's arms and then into your arms, her joy overwhelming yet still tinged with lingering fear.
Ye Yunzhou had a home to return to after all: the Tang Clan.

Ye Yunzhou was the victor, yet he had nowhere left to return to. He wasn't deaf to the deeper meaning behind his master's words-what sounded like a rebuke was in truth Ting Haisheng clearing the Ye siblings' names, declaring the treasure story pure fabrication. But before stepping into the arena, Ye Yunzhou himself had claimed to be nominated by the Yue Family's old followers, not knowing how much trouble that lie would bring down on him. The Tang Clan-he could never go back to it now. He sprang up into the treetops and vanished into the distance on his Qinggong, from that day forward a man with no home anywhere, walking the world alone.

Master and disciple, once close, were now bound for a final reckoning. The sword of Diancang is the fastest under heaven, outrunning words themselves, lighter than smoke, faster than a shooting star-it drives its young challenger to the brink of death before it ever grants him life again, like thunder rolling a thousand miles in an instant; once the blade falls, there is no second stroke. Ting Haisheng held nothing back-he unleashed the technique left behind by Diancang's Sword Saint, the strongest move of his life, the very pinnacle of the Diancang Quick Sword. But Ye Yunzhou had already surpassed that pinnacle. Ting Haisheng lost. Skilled as he was with the sword, he had never been arrogant, and he had imagined defeat before-just never imagined his own disciple would reach such a godlike realm. Even the Sword Saint reborn, he feared, could do no better than this. He could only manage a bitter, rueful smile, at once crushed and proud, as his fellow Senior Brother, the Sect Leader, helped him back into Diancang.

Ye Yunzhou had already made a name for himself before he threw in with the Tang Clan-he had once been Diancang's proudest rising star. No one had expected him to later turn traitor to Diancang and be hunted all the way from Dali to the Central Plains. Around the same time, word spread that King Yue's Treasure had resurfaced, and the world decided that the Ye siblings must have turned traitor overnight because of some crime tied to the treasure-whether to win them over gently or seize the prize outright, everyone wanted the two of them in hand so as to claim the treasure alone. Only today, hearing master and disciple confront each other, did the truth finally come clear: Diancang's warrant for the Ye siblings had nothing to do with any treasure at all-it was because Ye Yunzhou had drawn his sword and wounded a highborn relative of the Duan clan of Dali. With that, every baffling loose end fell into place at once. If the Ye siblings truly carried the treasure's secret, Diancang would long since have dug it up and spent it-why would they still be scraping by with a pack of Jianghu drifters like you? And if the treasure were real, why would the Ye siblings be treated worse than some fallen-on-hard-times distant relation of the Duan family? In the end, the whole treasure story was nothing but idle rumor spun from nothing. Ye Yunzhou had never once failed to deny it-but who was willing to believe him? Everyone was chasing the same wishful dream, hoping the legend was true, that fortune might let them defy fate and remake their lives with it. And if it drove this brother and sister to their deaths along the way-what did that matter to anyone?

Ting Haisheng had no interest in competing for Wulin Alliance Leader, yet still wouldn't leave the field-instead he challenged the Emei Sect. The two sects had no great quarrel in recent years, but when it came to swordsmanship, when had Diancang ever bowed to any hero under heaven? Legend held that centuries ago Shu had no other sect at all-Emei stood alone, supreme. In those days Emei was the foremost sword sect under heaven, known as the Mount Shu Sword Sect. Now, though Emei no longer wielded swords, it was famed for the saying 'the sword kept in the heart'-no blade in hand, yet a blade within the heart. How could Diancang bear that? So he seized the chance to call out the Emei Sect Leader, to meet blade to blade as friends and debate the sword.

You knew the grudge between him and his sister and the Diancang Sect ran too deep for words to settle; only a sword could finish it. The court would never allow a den of rebels like the Tang Clan to seize the Wulin Alliance, true, and there was no need to fuss over winning or losing-but if anything went wrong, how could you face Yunshang afterward? So you refused to put him forward. Ye Yunzhou, left with no choice, had to lie and claim he represented the six allied armies under the Red Canopy King, the old forces of the Yue Family, and put himself forward to settle the score.

You knew the grudge between the two siblings and Diancang ran too deep for words to settle; only a sword could finish it. Besides, the court would never let a den of rebels like the Tang Clan seize the Wulin Alliance, so there was no need to fuss over winning or losing. So you put Ye Yunzhou forward in the Tang Clan's name, tossing off that he was a disciple of no blood kin. Ye Yunzhou froze for a moment, then his spirits lifted, and he stepped out from the crowd into the arena.

The Tang Clan's opportunity to send someone into battle has already been used by you. Therefore, if Ye Yunzhou wishes to go into battle, he cannot represent the Tang Clan. Hence, he falsely claims to represent the Yue Family's old forces under the Red Canopy King's six allied armies, proposing himself to go into battle to settle the karmic cause.

Ting Haisheng had no interest in competing for Wulin Alliance Leader, yet still refused to leave the field-instead he challenged the Tang Clan, demanding that Diancang's renegade disciple Ye Yunzhou step into the arena to settle old scores. Though this had nothing to do with choosing the Wulin Alliance Leader, it touched on the whole Wulin's interest-everyone was burning to know the whereabouts of King Yue's Treasure-so no one objected.

Among the mid- and minor sects there was never a shortage of people itching to try their luck-even if they couldn't win the title of Alliance Leader, they meant to make a name for themselves. Seeing Shangguan Jun spar a while and then withdraw, leaving the younger fighters their full measure of face and opening his purse besides, true to his word and utterly unattached to empty glory, the smaller sects' wariness faded, and one after another they began putting forward their own candidates to test themselves in the arena. None of them meant to take the crown; they only wanted to build a name and stir up the crowd-and earn some gold-before the leaders of the Six Great Sects made their move. Not until someone called out the Six Great Sects did Ting Haisheng, one of Diancang's Twin Sages, finally step forward, and only then did the long-awaited Wulin Assembly truly begin. Diancang was now the foremost sword sect in the Wulin; with the Sword Saint retired, the Twin Swords of Diancang were held supreme, and Ting Haisheng's reputation proved well-earned-the instant he entered the ring he stunned the whole hall and drew thunderous applause. But the moment he defeated his opponent, he announced his withdrawal from the contest for Wulin Alliance Leader, and the crowd erupted in astonishment. After Quanzhen and Songshan, now even Diancang was pulling out-and was that not itself a kind of statement? They were called the Six Great Sects of the Central Plains, but Quanzhen and Songshan both lay within Jin territory, and Diancang within Dali. Twenty years ago the title of Alliance Leader might still have been worth contesting, but with today's assembly hosted by the Song court, for them to win it would amount to pledging allegiance to Song-and neither the Jin nor the Dali court would sit blind and deaf to that. They feared that before they had even struck a blow against the Mud Cult, ruin might fall on themselves first.

Shangguan Ying's heart and courage shattered, terrified that either of you might be killed or maimed; heedless of the punishment her father would mete out, she threw her own body between you two. You still meant to persuade her to stand down, but seeing her tears fall like rain on pear blossoms, hearing her sorrowful pleading, you couldn't bring yourself to refuse her after all, and sheathed your sword to withdraw. Shangguan Ying believed she alone had saved your life, never knowing that though you had taken an internal injury, you had already broken through every move Shangguan Jun had-had the bout gone one round further, he would have been at your mercy. Ruthless as Shangguan Jun was, he still kept a master's bearing: unwilling to admit defeat outright, yet unwilling to press his advantage too far either. It was called a draw, and only you, he, and a handful of other experts present ever knew who had truly won.

You underestimated the strength of the Shangguan Family Head, and were swept away by the Fulan Dao, stumbling and suffering a crushing defeat. Fortunately, Song Bei stepped in immediately, preventing you from being killed on the spot.

Even so, that you, a mere junior, could stand toe to toe with a master famed across the realm was astonishing in itself. Word had it the Tang Clan's experts were all but wiped out, yet here you were, another dangerous one risen up. Your skill ran so deep, yet you still looked like such an easy mark to bully-how sly of you.

The people of Jianghu weren't initially impressed with your new leader of the Kongtong Sect, thinking you must have done something underhanded or just been lucky to become the sect leader. Now, seeing you match a renowned master in combat, everyone is stunned. The Kongtong disciples are cheering wildly, jumping up and down, dragging people around and boasting nonstop that it was their sect leader, proud beyond measure.

Shangguan Jun grew more alarmed the longer the fight ran. Years in retirement had left him rusty, no doubt, but it still galled him that decades of skill couldn't put down a junior like you. His anxiety mounted, his blade cutting the air so hard it stung the skin; he feared that if the bout dragged on, you would strip bare everything he had learned in a lifetime and leave him with no face left at all. Left with no choice, he risked everything on his hidden trump card, meaning to cleave you and your Small Sword clean in two. Instead, that full-strength strike-Dragon King Splits the Sea-only wrung a mouthful of blood out of you. Song Bei, an old hand of the Jianghu himself, saw the change in Shangguan Jun's face and knew at once the match was decided; he rushed in to call a halt. The debt between you was far from settled, but killing him on the spot was out of the question-still, making him lose face before the whole crowd was satisfaction enough. Ruthless as Shangguan Jun was, he kept a master's bearing: unwilling to admit defeat outright, yet unwilling to press his advantage too far either. It was called a draw, and only you, he, and a handful of other experts present ever knew who had truly won.

You were carried off the field, and the next young challenger to step up received Shangguan Jun's pointed praise, every strike laced with mercy-a deliberate ploy to elevate his rival and belittle your skill, grinding down the Tang Clan's reputation. Sure enough, for martial artists who never opened a book, the trick worked a treat.

Song Bei took this blade for you, his arms left numb from the shock, nearly paying with his own life. He couldn't help but silently count himself lucky-not once in all his years in the Jianghu had he faced a blade so overbearing.

You may not be a good person, but Song Bei couldn't stand idly by and watch you spill your blood on the spot, tainting the Wulin Assembly. He took the blade for you, his arms left numb from the shock, nearly paying with his own life.

You underestimated the Shangguan Family Head's strength, swept up by the Shangguan Surging Wave Blade and left stumbling in a crushing defeat. Fortunately, Song Bei intervened just in time, and Shangguan Ying went so far as to cast aside her dignity, dropping to her knees to beg for mercy — only then did Shangguan Sun abandon the thought of killing you on the spot.

Shangguan Ying had hesitated to speak to you earlier, fearing you might act on impulse. Indeed, you were about to act impulsively, disregarding propriety, and she rushed out, spouting off without holding back, scolding you harshly. Though her words were fierce, she desperately gave anxious glances, her concern evident. You had never felt so warm from being scolded before.

The Shangguan Family was hungry for talent, and the moment you let slip a hint that you might be open to recruitment, Shangguan Sun's gaze toward you changed at once. Where the ordinary world judges people first by looks and character, Shangguan Sun judges only by ability — ruthless enough, and power follows; power, and wealth follows. Once you had both, what need would you have to flatter your way through life? He saw you as his greatest hidden threat and feared you in earnest, long wishing you gone. If you were willing to pledge yourself to him, it would be as good as delivering the Tang Clan into his hands — a contribution so great that handing you the Cang Gang to run would hardly be excessive. Then you abruptly changed tack: you didn't even care about the post of Cang Gang Leader — the position you were really after was to become his son‑in‑law! Your roundabout nonsense succeeded in enraging the shrewd and calculating Commissioner Shangguan.

The stakes were worth a fortune in gold, but life and death called for a different wager. You knew Shangguan Sun meant to kill you, and afraid you might yet lose your nerve and back out, you decided you might as well name a sky‑high price and demand Shangguan Ying from him instead. Shangguan Sun didn't take it as an insult — he simply sniffed in disdain, his eyes full of contempt. He hadn't imagined your ambitions were so small: compared to wealth or power, all you truly craved was a woman.

Shangguan Sun hadn't yet made his move against the Tang Clan when you, fool that you were, delivered yourself to be slaughtered — he could hardly believe his luck, then broke into a grin: exactly what he had searched high and low for, landing in his lap with no effort at all. He wasn't even contending for the position of Wulin Alliance Leader, so he had no rules to fear. The Tang Clan's Sect Leader lay bedridden, as good as an invalid; his finest disciple, the Flying Hero, was already dead, and the Ruthless Young Master had defected; even your Fourth Senior Brother had been lured away by a scheme of the Shangguan Family. Seizing this perfect chance, he could feign an accident and kill you, leaving only Scholarly Hero Tang Sheng to carry on the Tang Clan — no longer anything to fear.

The Shangguan Family harbored hostility toward the Tang Clan, and in the past had often resorted to underhanded tactics to harm them. This was intolerable — what else could be endured? You once considered leaping into the fray to challenge them, but fortunately your fellow Junior Brother, already on guard, hurriedly pulled you back. After some persuasion, you put the greater good first and, mastering your impulses, chose to value your sect above all.

The Shangguan family harbors deep hostility towards the Tang Clan. In the past, they have often set traps to secretly harm the Tang Clan, and now they are meddling with your beloved's future without permission. This is intolerable. You once thought about jumping into the fray to seek justice, but fortunately, your Junior Brother was already on guard and quickly held you back. After some persuasion, you prioritized the greater good over personal feelings and ultimately chose to set aside your romantic desires for the sake of your sect.

The Shangguan Family has long harbored hostility toward the Tang Clan, never sparing any underhanded tricks to sabotage them, and they even backed the Guangzhou Tang Clan, sparking civil war within the Clan. This grudge could not go unavenged; you immediately threw yourself into the fray to challenge them.

The Shangguan family harbors deep hostility towards the Tang Clan. In the past, they have often set traps to secretly harm the Tang Clan, and now they are meddling with your beloved's future without permission. This is intolerable. You once thought about jumping into the fray to seek justice, but fortunately, your Junior Brother was already on guard and quickly held you back. After some persuasion, you prioritized the greater good over personal feelings and ultimately chose to set aside your romantic desires for the sake of your sect.

The Shangguan Family harbors hostility toward the Tang Clan, never sparing tricks to sabotage them before, and now they've arbitrarily meddled with your love interest's future. This is intolerable; what else can be endured? You wanted to leap into the array to challenge them, but fortunately, your fellow Junior Brother had been on guard and hurriedly pulled you back. After a round of persuasion, you feigned being convinced, then suddenly turned and struck his nose, seizing the opportunity to escape their control.

The Shangguan Family harbors deep hostility toward the Tang Clan, having long used underhanded tricks to sabotage them, and now they have arbitrarily meddled with your beloved's future. This is intolerable; what else can be endured? You immediately threw yourself into the fray to challenge them.

If the Wulin were to form an alliance, there must be a Wulin Alliance Leader, as it has always been since ancient times. This Alliance Leader must be both scholarly and martial, benevolent and righteous, to command respect. The people's hearts were filled with unease, fearing that the court might use a hollow pretense, claiming they wished to convene a grand assembly of the Wulin while secretly planning to force an alliance leader on them in order to curb the various sects. Hearing that the method of selecting the Alliance Leader through martial contests was immediately accepted by Commissioner Shangguan, everyone breathed a sigh of relief. Commissioner Shangguan then laid down three rules: the martial contests were for an exchange of skill only, with no need to fight to the finish; each sect or faction could only put forward one representative to compete; and this would prevent endless wrangling. The Shangguan Family Head was the first to take up his blade and step onto the field to call for a challenger, startling everyone present. They all thought the rules laid down were so crude that anyone could see going first put a fighter at the greatest disadvantage. By putting himself on the line so early, the Shangguan Family Head not only offered a bounty of one thousand taels of gold to anyone who could defeat him but also seemed to be all but begging someone to unseat him. His ambitions for the position of Alliance Leader were clearly non‑existent. This could not help but inspire admiration and ease their doubts about his intentions further. However, given the Shangguan family's formidable standing and the deep rift between court and commoners, discussion buzzed on all sides, and no one dared step forward to challenge him.

You spoke not a word from beginning to end, filled with worry. The fervor of the grand assembly did not touch you at all. Throughout your travels in the Jianghu, you had indeed seen Mud Cult practitioners commit evil deeds, but evil people were not limited to just the Mud Cult; there were good and bad individuals in every sect. One should not generalize. Today, the Mud Cult is branded as a Demon Cult, and the Wulin Alliance is driven by the court to gather and annihilate it. What if next time the court declares the Tang Clan to be a Demon Cult? And what if next time they declare the Quanzhen sect to be a Demon Cult? No matter what you say, people in the Wulin will not listen. The justice they seek may not truly be fair.

With the auspicious time arrived, the Shangguan Family Head ordered drums to be beaten and stood in the middle with a resolute air. In these times of internal turmoil and external threat, with Golden Bandits eyeing with covetous glances from without, and the Demon Cult plotting sinister schemes within, the peril of Jianghu mirrors that of Central Plains, posing an even greater danger to Great Song and its very foundation. Those who uphold chivalry cannot bear to watch the Commoners suffer; in order to gather opinions widely, plan ahead, and convene this grand assembly of the Wulin, inviting heroes from all under heaven to gather here. Even if one acknowledges the rationality of the Shangguan Family Head's words, how can it be said that such an assembly truly represents the will of the martial arts community when a chill three feet deep is not formed in a day? For a long time now, there has been disaffection between the court and the people. Is this assembly convened by the imperial edict still considered the gathering of martial artists? All felt uneasy, finding it hard to fully believe the Shangguan Family Head's words. Fortunately, Divine Constable Song offered supportive advice from the side. Though a government official himself, he was upright and incorruptible, frequently seen in Jianghu while holding high office, fair‑minded, with an excellent reputation; the martial artists all respectfully referred to him as the Divine Constable. Therefore, when he spoke, his words carried more weight. Moreover, everyone knew that allowing the Mud Cult to grow unchecked would not be a wise move, and with imperial support today, eradicating this root of evil could indeed prove advantageous. Those with sharper thoughts already envisaged opportunities for merit and favor by seizing such an occasion; it was even possible that fortune might one day grant them positions in government service. As soon as someone voiced agreement, others followed suit enthusiastically.

I know it's her petty‑mindedness; I am truly ashamed and humbled. This time, opening the palace gates widely to welcome the Tang Clan as honored guests also carries the intention of atoning for past sins and offering compensation.
Let alone Yunshang looking at you, her eyes sparkle with stars‑trust that can't be faked.
Now, seeing the Ye siblings in their emerald robes mingling among the Tang Clan's blue, not looking the least bit out of place, you couldn't help clicking your tongue in quiet wonder.
It was only after she heard her disciple Long Xiang praise your integrity without end that her view of you began to change.

Only now did you learn the full story behind the Tang Clan's night raid: Duan Zhixiu, trying to save Ye Yunshang and flee the Tang Clan's clutches, had sought help from the Nangong Family and been refused — and it was this opening that Lady Wen had seized upon to incite the crime.
As for the mantis stalking the cicada unaware of the oriole behind it — her disciple, the Apricot Blossom Immortal, turned the scheme to her own ends, sending the poisoned brocade pouch in the name of a Jinxiang Palace disciple, a twist even Lady Wen had not foreseen.
With ease she had her mentor grow suspect in the eyes of the Duan Family of Dali, and had Duan Zhixiu come to be hated by Ye Yunzhou, forging a chain of grudges — then sat back to sip her tea, content to watch them tear each other apart afterward.
The Tang Clan's dignity brooked no provocation, and with the instigator standing before you, your face darkened despite yourself.
Lady Wen made no excuses and offered no denials, but bowed low to you, her junior, in shame — for she had indeed once suspected the Tang Clan, taking them in in name only while truly holding them under house arrest, meaning to claim the treasure for herself.

You laid out, in full, how Iron Crown Daoist had blocked the plank road that day and revealed his identity. But Zou Bo's face went ashen as he listened, and once you finished, he flew into a rage. You had thought you were making your case ever more clearly; instead, to his ears, it grew wilder by the word. What you did not know was that on the day of the Qingcheng Great Trial, just after you and your companions had left Qingcheng territory, Iron Crown Daoist had been killed by a single palm strike from Zhao Kui. Iron Crown Daoist had been fierce in bearing but timid at heart, and in life had been on poor terms with his fellow disciples of the same generation—but he had still been a sect brother of decades' standing, and the dead deserve respect. As leader of the sect, how could Zou Bo allow a junior like you to slander a dead man's good name with no evidence at all? Had he not minded his own standing, with his fiery temper he might well have thrust the sect leader's token on someone else, resigned on the spot, and beaten you to death then and there, and no one would have called it strange. Fortunately, disbelief and anger aside, he was in the end a reasonable, upright man; rather than waste more words on you, he flung his sleeve and departed.
You knew that mere words were not enough to convince the others, so you gave up and decided to think of a better strategy to remind Master Zou.

It was Ye Yunzhou who stepped forward instead. Though he had not witnessed it himself, he trusted your character, and was willing to stake his reputation as the Cangsong Swordsman on the truth of your words. The Cangsong Swordsman of the Diancang Sect was renowned for chivalry and was the descendant of a loyal minister—his guarantee carried real weight, one even the Sect Leader of Qingcheng could not dismiss lightly. He agreed to attend the Wulin Assembly first, then return to the mountain to investigate the matter thoroughly.

You longed to expose Shentu Long's true face, but in the Jianghu, the foulest stench was never bloodshed and violence—it was slander and rumor. Zou Bo and Shentu Long had been fellow disciples for over a decade; with no evidence but your one-sided words and Third Senior Brother's slanderous letters of accusation, how could he possibly suspect his own junior brother and leave him so disheartened?
Along the way you encountered the Qingcheng Sect. Setting aside all other grudges for now, you had once received a great favor from Qingcheng, so you were bound to call on Sect Leader Zou.

So you killed a fish for its swim bladder, filled it with air and sealed it tight to serve as an air bladder, and told Yunshang to cut bamboo into tubes, seal the ends with cloth, and hang them all around your bodies. Following the lake's flow until there was no path left, you summoned your true qi, plunged into the lake, and swam against the current, planning to swap a breath of foul air for a fresh one from a bladder or tube whenever you needed. You hadn't dared hope to make it through in one go, but no sooner had you dived under than you glimpsed a faint light far ahead; your heart leapt, and swimming with hands and feet together you made for it, broke the surface, and found the world opening wide - behind the cliff face lay another world entirely, lush with plants, alive with birdsong and the scent of flowers, home to wild hares and deer, brimming with life. A mere sheet of rock had stood between a dead end and a place of life. Just as your lives so often hung on a single thought, had you flinched and stepped back even once, heaven itself could not have helped you. All that preparation, and in the end you never even needed a single air bladder - it was maddening and funny all at once. You hurried back underwater for Yunshang, who by now trusted you completely; she filled her lungs, puffed out her cheeks, and let you tuck her under your arm and swim the both of you through. You built a fire to dry your clothes, and Ye Yunshang set traps and clubbed small animals to death, giving the two of you your first proper meal in a long while; only once you'd rested and regained your strength did you move on. A stone corridor ringed the valley, rising by degrees like a natural skywell. At first the two of you marveled at it, both thinking the place a wonder beyond the reach of human hands. The further you went, the more something felt off - signs of chisel-work everywhere - and when you came upon a mechanism-rigged stone door standing beside the path, you were certain: this was the work of the Tang Clan's ancestors. You had no way of knowing whether a tomb lay beyond the door, or something forbidden sealed away from the light. Either way, the door didn't block the path - whether it would open or not made no difference. You trekked on a while longer, crossed the valley stream, and came to the bottom of an old, weathered well. You recognized it at once as the very well in the Tang family compound - you'd been here before, and knew your own words carved into the wall: "I was pushed." The year you fell into that well, you'd only just learned to read and even carved the character wrong; broken bones, a ruined face, despair in your heart - for years after, you'd have nightmares of falling back down here. Now, in that same place, you felt no fear at all, only wild joy. Carrying Yunshang on your back, you braced hands and one foot against the well wall and slowly climbed, but the well was narrow below and wide above, and partway up your reach simply ran out. The two of you called out together for help, but no one ever answered. Caught between going up and falling back, Yunshang finally gathered her courage to risk it all - she planted her feet on your back, drew on her newly awakened Tang Clan true qi, called on the Diancang beginner's Qinggong, kicked off the wall, and shot up out of the well mouth, breaking free. She hurried to call for someone to lower a rope, and you were pulled to safety. You were bruised and battered all over, and Yunshang had only just recovered from her illness; after a full ten days of ordeal, both of you were exhausted in body and spirit, your clothes in tatters, and you went off separately to wash and tend your wounds. While you were being patched up in the alchemy hall, the whole sect had gathered in Zhengxin Hall, listening to Ye Yunshang tell, vivid and breathless, how you'd been ambushed on the road by the Thousand-Faced Demon, how you'd thrown yourself off a cliff to shield her, how you'd survived a fall into an underground stream by sheer luck, and how you'd used your own body as medicine to cure her. Only after surviving trial after trial did heaven finally show mercy, granting the two of you a way out of death itself and turning disaster into safety - and she, by that same misfortune, found fortune: a fatal illness cured without a single dose of medicine. After the Junior Martial Sister's wedding that day, no trace of the two of you could be found anywhere. People guessed at every outcome, good and bad, but not one guessed the truth was this tangled a tale - more harrowing than any Jianghu bloodbath - and all who heard it stared at one another in shock. Ye Yunzhou, Tang Fang, and the others who knew the full story listened with their hearts in their throats, their eyes wide and trembling. Who else would go on provoking King Yama again and again as if determined not to stop until truly dead? Your nerve was outrageous, and your luck was frighteningly hard to kill. This trip through hell had saved not only Yunshang's life, but also her brother's heart, which had been on the verge of breaking. The debt of gratitude he owed was still unpaid, and after this, he was utterly won over; the faith he had been slowly losing suddenly became crystal clear, and though he could neither see nor touch it, he was willing to believe that righteousness truly existed between heaven and earth. It was only because you'd insisted on being sworn brothers with him that he became your brother at all - but should you and the Tang Clan ever truly harbor treasonous intent and rise up in rebellion, he would gladly serve as your vanguard, loyal to your command alone.

Your internal skill cultivation is limited, so you cannot imitate internal skill experts, who often resort to holding one incense stick's worth of breath. You should have self‑awareness and prioritize caution.

You reckoned your internal skill cultivation was limited, unable to match the masters of the inner schools who could casually hold their breath for a whole stick of incense - and with Yunshang depending on you, you dared not be the least bit reckless.
You and Yunshang received guidance from a high‑ranking master, regained hope, and immediately set about planning an escape method.

Your heart suddenly stopped, your soul left your body, and you died in a blissful state. As the saying goes, surviving a great calamity brings future blessings. You practiced the Nine Turns Fragment, which is extremely perilous; if your mind wasn't strong enough, you risked Qi Deviation. However, the missing half of the scroll was hidden within Yunshang's body. A gift from Left Commander Li Yuanqi of the Supreme Bliss Sect, it eventually became part of Yunshang's dowry. Your mind had already become enlightened, yet the lingering effects of the foreign True Qi hadn't fully vanished when you suddenly died. Ironically, this misfortune brought you fortune, as the two halves of the scroll merged within you, achieving the state of Nirvana, the Nine Cycles of Reincarnation, rebirth, and the full mastery of the divine art. You naturally didn't know that the Supreme Bliss Cult Leader had spent countless efforts and committed countless heinous acts to master the Nine Cycles of Reincarnation. With the protection of the Left and Right Commanders, hundreds of disciples willingly sacrificed themselves to become elixirs, their bodies piling up like mountains, allowing one person to attain this technique. You, however, accidentally learned it through a kiss from your lover, dying in a blissful state and unknowingly mastering it. Who deserves the credit? Who should be thanked? Thus, it's said that Yunshang is your lucky star, and you should always be grateful and repay her kindness.

Yet someone with no feel for romance couldn't bear the sight of your two peaceful, happy faces in death, and went so far as to beg the ghosts themselves to drag you back to the mortal world to suffer on. You and Ye Yunshang woke as if from a dream, as though a lifetime had passed, unable for a moment to tell east from west, not knowing what day it now was, nor guessing what divine hand had used needles to save you both at the bottom of this desolate, uninhabited ravine. Yunshang stood stunned for a long while, then without warning slapped you across the face - and feeling the stinging heat in her palm, she finally believed that fate truly does show mercy, and that you two, brother and sister, were blessed with deep fortune indeed, or how else could you have cheated death so many times! Every trace of the alien true qi had vanished; feeling her pulse now, the flow rose to the clear yang and settled in the dantian, moving freely within and without, wholly natural - the root of her illness was gone. Still half afraid it was only a false joy, Yunshang dared not quite believe it, tried a few hops, threw a few punches with her small fists, and found her body lighter than ever, no shortness of breath, no pain, yet still solidly on the ground. Unable to hold back her feelings, she wept with you, tears of joy - the happiest moment of her whole life was this one. Well then - now that she was cured, with nothing left to fear, you rascal had thoroughly lost your use to her, and so of course the words spoken back in the illusion didn't count. So she decided to say them again. Her harsh words that day hadn't come from her heart; she simply felt your deep love and could not answer it - but now there was nothing left to hold her back. If being siblings was out of the question, why not grant your wish and marry you instead? She was like a hibiscus bloom just opening, so lovely and vivid a thing that it might wilt if left untended for even a moment - and of all the world's boundless favor, she meant to claim every last drop for herself; now, with her heart given at last, she granted you the singular honor of doting on her. She meant to bind you to this from now on: she'd take no one else's kindness, and your heart in turn must belong to her, whole and undivided. At this you could hardly believe it, half suspecting this Little Demon King was up to her tricks again, toying with you. Ye Yunshang gave a rueful laugh, steadied her resolve, screwed up her courage, and suddenly rose on her toes, tilting her face up to kiss you, and let that be her answer.

Yet sweet dreams are always the first to break, and things seldom go as one wishes — labor spent for nothing, as is so often the way of the world. Born with the blood of the Ye family in her veins, indebted to her parents for the gift of life, carrying a hundred years of karma upon her shoulders, she could not escape death. Even with your life given to save hers, Yunshang's oil ran dry and her lamp guttered out, and in the end her beauty faded and her spirit passed. Fortunate at least that you caught up with her in time, and were reunited in the underworld. Whether this scene was conjured by your own grieving heart, or whether she, in her final moments, dreamed of you — or whether your two hearts were joined as one, dreaming the very same dream together — such a thing is called dying for love.

These five strands of true qi each had their own history, and though they might seem a tangle without order, cause and effect could in fact be traced through them. At the root of it all was simply someone's selfless devotion. Each of them believed, without any prior agreement, that even if they themselves could not save her, someone else might yet succeed — and so, sparing nothing, they poured out their own vital energy and pinned their hopes on whoever would come after, leaving her to suffer through the long wait until you, at last, arrived.

The timeline goes back even further; they, the siblings, entered Diancang while ill, receiving guidance from the esteemed masters Guan Yun Ke and Ting Haisheng, and through the Diancang 'Two Principles Sword Qi,' they managed to subdue the chaotic True Qi within their bodies.

But in truth, he — frozen forever at that moment in time — was still a youth of pure heart, who had treated the Ye siblings without the least insincerity. Had you crossed paths with him then, the two of you might well have found kindred spirits and become fast friends.
The Withering and Flourishing Divine Skill that Duan Zhixiu once channeled into Yunshang, years ago, to nurse her back to health, now rises to contend with you as well.
Even the protective True Qi of the Nangong family head sees you as an enemy. In reality, what he wishes for has never been to compete with anyone for superiority, but rather universal harmony.

Whether or not Zou Bo takes action, it cannot change Yunshang's inevitable fate of death; the difference lies only in the timing. He could have stayed out of it, avoiding the karmic consequences. But he is Zou Bo.
Within the illusionary realm, the Foreign True Qi seemed to take form, manifesting as the figure of Master Zou of Qingcheng, challenging you to a contest of skill.

You set life and death aside, gradually entering meditation, moving away from noise, and your consciousness plunges deep into the sea. The three realms are but the mind, all phenomena arise from consciousness; everything seen is merely transformed by the mind.

Don't be afraid just by saying so; she truly has no fear, her heart at peace beyond words. After all, even at the end of hell, you'll be by her side. No matter how useless she is, how much worse she may be, you'd still risk fire and boiling water for her. Therefore, compared to the Great Song emperor or King Yue, who passed away over eighty years ago, the you who now loves her deeply is more deserving of her life in return.

Unprotected, you forcefully practiced the Nirvana Samadhi, sealed the Eight Extraordinary Meridians, halted fetal breathing, suppressed your heartbeat to synchronize with Yunshang's pulse, connected your meridians with hers, and opened your dantian gate wide, only to be devoured by the Foreign True Qi surging within her body, already grievously wounded, yet still persisting in your resolve. As her heart fire waned, you offered the wood element from your liver as fuel; when her spleen earth crumbled, you ignited your heart fire as a lamp to warm the spleen earth, transforming energy into her vitality; when her lung metal faltered, you excavated the spleen earth, transforming energy into metal to sustain her breath; when her kidney water dwindled, you chipped away the lung metal to create a vessel, preserving a single drop of her true yin. You gave everything you had, never sparing a morsel. Yet both of you knew, even if you burned all your Qi, it would be like burning a handful of firewood to boil the sea‑knowing it was futile, yet still choosing to sacrifice your life in vain.

However, she may have realized, but whether you listen to advice is another matter. After all, you're the kind of person who would jump off a cliff without hesitation‑crazy enough. She had a vague sense that you would come, and her guess was spot on.

However, she may have realized it, but you're not the kind of person who can be swayed by good advice. You leapt off the cliff without a moment's hesitation‑where does that confidence come from? It's as if, with just one cry from Ye Yunshang, you, this madman who can slip through any crack, would even make it into hell.

This morning I woke still heavy with sleep, and heard the rain pattering softly beyond the cave. I lowered my eyes and said nothing, for a feeling had suddenly come over me — the hour of parting had arrived. Nine days we have shared, morning and night, with no words left unspoken between us; but now that parting is near, why should I disturb your deep, contented sleep once more? I can only entrust my heart to the clouds, and through the whisper of rain, softly speak my farewell.

From the exchange between Tang Fang and your Second Senior Brother, you gathered that Nirvana Samadhi was no ordinary medical principle, but some manner of forbidden art or dark sorcery. If it were truly harmless, why would Tang Fang have faltered mid-sentence, speaking as one resigned to death, and why would your Second Senior Brother have flown into such a rage on hearing the name? Yunshang had only asked out of curiosity at the time, but the more she thought back on it, the surer she grew that you would never let it rest — you'd stop at nothing to master the technique. Yet she never dreamed that Nirvana Samadhi was in fact the Nine Turns of Reincarnation, and the realization left her stunned. This book, it turned out, once belonged to the Supreme Bliss Left Envoy, who fell at the hands of your Eldest Senior Brother and the others; the Nine Turns of Reincarnation scripture scattered with his defeat, came into the Eldest Senior Brother's keeping, and passed in turn through your Second Senior Brother and Tang Fang before reaching your hands. Just so does fate turn and wind its way, its course fixed long before you ever knew it.

A scheme flashed through your eyes, and without hesitation you smeared your own name, claiming that what you'd been reading was nothing but an erotic picture-book, hoping to make her back off in embarrassment. Ye Yunshang was startled by the claim — she'd never expected such words from you — and looked both shocked and amused. She set her pretty face into a scowl of disbelief, but you, perversely unwilling to let it go, insisted on playing the lecher caught red-handed, until she couldn't help herself and burst out laughing. Her own brother, Ye Yunzhou, was upright and handsome in every way, but stiff and humorless, not a tenth as entertaining as you; the days spent with you had brought her more laughter than the past ten years combined. If there is such a thing in this world as being kindred spirits, this was surely it.
You know you can't hide it anymore, so you can only spread your hands and speak openly and honestly.
You claim this book is a medical text; even if the methods are questionable, the purpose of saving lives isn't entirely a lie. Ye Yunshang, however, wasn't so easily deceived by your tricks.

Ye Yunshang woke up even later today, taking the initiative before you could start complaining, and then went out to forage. You saw her go far away, took out the Nine Turns Fragment Secret Manual to read, only to find that Yunshang had forgotten her sachet and returned, just in time to catch you in your secret.

She could no longer be that child, tugging at 'Brother's' sleeve to be coaxed and comforted, yet it was some comfort that in the end you were the one who saw her off. Joy brings its pleasures, parting its sorrows, and amid it all the foolish, love-struck hearts. That night, you sat alone on the back mountain, your face in your hands, for a long while. Not until the flowers' lingering scent dissolved like morning mist on the wind did you finally find release. You and Ye Yunzhou are both still alive, only you have walled yourself into this one place, trapped where you stand; he, exiled, drifts like windblown catkin-down, never free for the rest of his life.

She could no longer be that child, tugging at 'Brother's' sleeve to be coaxed and comforted. Yet it was some comfort that as Yunshang slipped away, the Junior Martial Sister arrived in time for one last look — she had her lifelong friend there, and she had you, and as she wished, was laid to rest in a place as warm as spring. That night, you held the Junior Martial Sister's icy little hand and sat with her on the back mountain for a long while; she clung to you so tightly she could scarcely breathe through her sobs. Not until the flowers' lingering scent dissolved like morning mist on the wind did she finally find release — as if she saw Yunshang once more, twirling a loose strand of hair, tickling her cheek, still smiling as ever.

Everything was done to please her; she refused medicine and acupuncture, instead carrying a food box to go on a spring outing. You strained to suppress your sobs, softly harmonizing with her song, accompanying her in laughter and conversation about stories from the past you had never known. It was clearly early summer, with mountain flowers blooming in full splendor, just like her radiant smile. Yet your heart felt like petals falling in the rain, a bleak, frosty pallor.

Yunshang woke up dazed and confused, but this was not a sign of joy‑it was the ominous Guttering Lamp, a final flicker before death. The poison had invaded her heart, clouding her mind. Alas, Yunshang, a clever and intelligent soul, now at the brink of her life, could no longer recognize the people around her, not even Tang Fang, nor you. All she could do was call out for her brother, shrinking like a startled bird into a ball. Her time was nearly up, yet the one she relied on most was not by her side. You wished to find her brother for her, but as you turned away, she seemed to awaken from a deep dream, only to fall into another, grasping your sleeve and mistaking you for her true brother, weeping and clinging to you. Her memory lingered on that day at Diancang Mountain, where her brother was, and where Duan Zhixiu had once protected her. Your heart was cut like a blade, unwilling to reveal the truth. So you pretended to be Ye Yunzhou, ensuring she would leave with family by her side, never alone.

A tremendous force yanked you back to the mortal realm, causing you to fall backward onto the ground. Gazing at the beams crisscrossing the alchemy chamber, it felt as if you were in another world, and your hands and feet seemed not to belong to you, leaving you momentarily without a sense of reality. Wiping away tears and blood, you hurriedly asked about Tang Fang's condition, but she could only shake her head with tears in her eyes.

You pushed yourself to your limits, never expecting that the illusion of Ox‑Head and Horse‑Face would collapse under a single palm, dispersing into a swirl of light dust. You had won, but with a surge of righteous passion, you remained unaware of what you had truly defeated. Not all wishes can be fulfilled through striving and fighting.
Whether true or false, it won't hinder your resolve. Having entered the underworld for her, without summoning her soul, even King Yama's command would be difficult to obey!
It stirs an involuntary dread in you. But since you ventured into the underworld for her, and have not yet recovered her soul, even if King Yama himself commands it, you will not obey!
The voice echoes like a chill wind through an ancient cave, speech as cold rain soaking clothes through the night, leaving listeners shivering from head to toe, not the slightest like a fantasy.
You mistook it for merely one of the ordinary foes you had met when Qingcheng came down from the mountain, and let your guard down — nearly beaten until your soul scattered.

Victory over all this has cost you nearly all your life; your spirit is scattered, and the illusions grow increasingly tangible, blurring the line between reality and illusion. Your footsteps tread the River of the Dead, amidst raging flames, as the underworld reveals itself.

It takes on the form of Qingcheng's Sect Leader Zou, vying with you for supremacy.
In the realm of illusions, the exotic True Qi seems to take form.

Tang Fang saw your resolve was firm, and with no choice but to abide by the agreement, she vowed to guard you. You pulled your robe open and sat cross‑legged on the ground, following the Internal Method to suppress your heartbeat in sync with Yunshang's pulse, sealing the eight extraordinary meridians to halt the fetal breath. Once the fetal breath ceased, the Internal Force, which naturally flowed like blood, could no longer sustain itself. You released your strength, placing your palm against Yunshang's back, connecting your energy circulation with hers. The Foreign True Qi overwhelmed you without your protective Internal Force, opening your dantian gate wide. Suddenly, it was as if a venomous snake emerged from its den, lunging forward to drill through your meridians and split your tendons, causing unbearable pain. Tang Fang hurriedly threaded needles to seal your acupoints, relieve the pain, and steady your mind.
You remained unmoved, appearing serene and tranquil.
Afraid as you were, your resolve was more than enough to rise above the fear.

You pressed two fingers to Yunshang's pulse gate, and before you'd even gone deep, the wild, clawing true qi within her surged against you, numbing your fingertips. The foreign qi that Second Senior Brother had long schemed to purge - the true cause of Yunshang's grave illness - only now showed its true shape. It wasn't hard to imagine: if you opened her meridian gate and drew on her dantian, you would very likely throw your life away for nothing.

You were scolded by her, yet surprisingly calm. When Ye Yunshang first fell ill, you stood motionless by her bedside for a long while, until the fellow disciples came to wash and tend her and sent you from the room. You didn't go back to see her again; instead you saw to the backlog of chores you'd left unfinished, and handed off what you couldn't finish to others. You brought wine to pay respects at Senior Brother's grave, and cooked rice porridge for the Sect Leader. Finally you entrusted what little savings you had to a Junior Brother you trusted, to be sent home, in some small repayment of your parents' kindness in bringing you into this world. You had already steeled your resolve.

Since the Junior Martial Sister got married, Yunshang lost her playmate and became listless, often appearing melancholic and downcast. She frequently ran a low fever, no longer lively and cheerful as before. On a warm, ordinary morning, she woke up and lazily flopped back onto her bed.

One warm, ordinary morning, she woke up and forced her junior martial sister to play the card game she had created. After a decisive match, she honestly admitted defeat and gave the cherished jewels as a prize to her junior martial sister, then contentedly lay back on the bed to sleep again.

Dr. Li naturally refused to agree, no matter how you softened or hardened your approach, he simply turned away and ignored you. You were as restless as an ant on a hot pan, only to waste time turning in circles at the gate, and then, with a sudden burst of anger, you decided to take matters into your own hands by drawing a blade and seizing it by force. As for whether it would damage the Tang Clan's reputation, you no longer cared. If the Third Senior Brother punished you, you would have no choice but to kneel and apologize to Dr. Li.

Though you knew full well reason and courtesy could not excuse it, you still swallowed your pride and begged for the elixir. Dr. Li refused at first, but seeing your devotion, he thought of the companion he himself would never grow old beside, and felt all at once that his remaining years held little meaning - ten more, twenty more, it made no difference - so he simply named a price and sold it to you.
You are not an emotionless person; seeing Yunshang moan on her sickbed, you resented your own helplessness, thinking of Dr. Li even earlier than Ye Yunzhou did.

Tang Fang couldn't stop him, only to encounter you, who had been missing for days, and without restraint, she vented her anger on you. Even if you're not family, Yunshang called you brother. But during her time of illness and suffering, you vanished without a trace‑what kind of brother is that?

The remaining one was prepared by Dr. Li for when his time was near its end, to take himself. By rights, having secured one pill already should have been enough - reason and courtesy said no more should be asked. But Ye Yunzhou had grown obsessive to the point of madness, his temperament far from what it once was; he would listen to no one's advice, and did not hesitate to seize the pill by force, willing to ruin his reputation if it meant saving his little sister's life.

Thinking back to the time when the siblings hid their identities and just arrived in Shu, they heard that Dr. Li had two miraculous Spirit Pills in his possession. They knelt at his gate for three days and nights, finally moving Dr. Li to give them one, which they gave to Yunshang to take, thus reducing her high fever and allowing her to survive by a hair's breadth.

Thinking back to when the siblings were hiding their identities and had just arrived in Shu, they heard that Dr. Li had two precious Spirit Pills. Thanks to your righteous assistance, they managed to obtain one, which allowed Yunshang to break out of her high fever and survive by sheer luck.

If there is a good method to extend her life, you all should make every effort. But her vitality has been lost, and there's no way to reverse the situation. The crowd avoids discussing it, but they all know this day will come. It's better to let her rest peacefully rather than cause her more fear. Yet Ye Yunzhou remains stubborn, believing he has achieved enlightenment, yet he keeps disrupting things. He can't let go, can't accept it, resenting his past ignorance of how fleeting life is and how easily things fade. He wishes he had been there to accompany her, only realizing his regret when their fate has run its course.

She lay down and never rose again. A high fever took her, and she drifted in and out all day, as though haunted by nightmares, murmuring deliriously. Sometimes she called for her brother, sometimes she called your name, sometimes she begged her master for mercy, sometimes she cried to her parents like a child.

You've caught up, but no matter how hard you try, the small sword can't pierce through the hard rock wall, and you can't stop the descent. Death looms imminent, the flickering starlight that bursts forth is the only faint light in the abyss. Ye Yunshang looked up at you, unable to believe it. In the moment of life and death, the depth of her worries and the weight on her shoulders felt as light as a feather. She tightly gripped you, but as long as her breath hadn't stopped, she wouldn't willingly die. This was her true heart. You were pinched by her, and suddenly remembered the trap in the forest. You pulled out the Brave Warrior's Flying Claw and fired it at the distant cliff pine. Fortunately, the Brave Warrior's Flying Claw caught the cliff pine without missing; unfortunately, you had no choice, for the pine was too thin to withstand the force of your fall, and it snapped immediately. You two clung together, plummeting into the abyss with screams and wails, as if breaking through the earth's crust, falling straight into the underworld.

Duan Zhixiu was a step too slow, his hand missing Yunshang's cloak, and he collapsed in defeat. You didn't care how far behind you were—with a sudden kick you launched yourself off the cliff, catching her graceful form just before it vanished into the darkness, and pulled her tightly into your arms.

At this moment, Patriarch Wuxiang found himself in a difficult position, akin to riding a tiger he could not dismount. It was utterly unexpected that these two young upstarts would dare join forces against him. Startled as he was, and angry as he was, he reminded himself that his refined skill, honed through sixty years of hard cultivation, was far beyond anything these green youths could hope to match. Regaining his composure, he prepared to counter their moves, reading their breath to gauge the depth of their skill. Confident of victory, he began to provoke them. It was not arrogance on his part, but a deliberate show of calm, meant to unsettle them and draw out their weaknesses. But to his astonishment, Ye Yunshang, whom he had written off, returned with unexpected boldness, a wooden stick in hand, daring to fight back. Even more surprising, the technique she used surpassed anything he had ever witnessed, far beyond what he could have imagined. The tip of her stick angled up toward his throat like flickering starlight, unpredictable and elusive; Patriarch Wuxiang, startled, had to pull his hand back and dodge, despite the injury it cost him. As he tilted his head back, it played straight into Ye Yunshang's hand. She followed at once with a spinning leg sweep that sent Patriarch Wuxiang stumbling off balance, and without so much as a glance back, swung the stick overhead and struck him full in the face. The three moves flowed together as one, seamless and exquisite, like a drunken swordsman treading lightly over misty river waters—his blade flashing sharp in the moment of the strike, only to let all caution go, close his eyes, and collapse into a drunken stupor. This was Diancang's consummate skill, the Sword Saint's First Ultimate: The Old Fisherman in the Misty Waves. Hard to find even in drunkenness. An old dream, let it rest on the cloud boat. For all his experience, Patriarch Wuxiang, confronted with such a peerless Ultimate, found himself unable to parry it, and collapsed onto the plank road, seeing stars, utterly humiliated. It was only a shame that Yunshang had no Internal Skill and wielded no blade—her technique, however brilliant, carried no real power, and even with every advantage she could not settle the fight. It was also thanks to her opponent's cunning caution—unwilling to engage without being certain of victory, he had tried to read her momentum and deflect it, and in doing so brought himself down. Otherwise, Ye Yunshang's skill alone could never have so much as grazed him; the moment her stick touched him, it would have shattered to pieces. Patriarch Wuxiang came to his senses, realized he had been tricked, and flew into an uncontrollable rage. You and Duan Zhixiu were not about to let the chance slip by; without waiting for him to recover his footing, you launched a full assault with everything you had, palms, blade, and legs all at once. Patriarch Wuxiang could not straighten up, barely able to parry, even calling on the Songshan Golden Bell Cover to take a kick from you outright, forced back to the very edge of the plank road, teetering on disaster. Just as your True Qi began to run thin, you two had also exhausted every technique you had, sprawled out with nothing left to give chase with. Success seemed about to slip away—the moment Patriarch Wuxiang caught his breath and steadied his footing, the tide would turn at once, and then you three would be the meat on his chopping block, certain to die. Ye Yunshang could not fight, but her eyes were sharp enough to know the chance would not come again. Gritting her teeth, she charged forward and drove him straight off the cliff.

Now Patriarch Wuxiang found himself like a man riding a tiger, unable to dismount—he had never dreamed these two green striplings would dare join forces against him. If the fight dragged on, the final victor would surely be him, but deciding it quickly was no easy matter. With the Tang family compound now thick with martial experts, someone was bound to pass this way before long, and by then he might not only fail to silence them, but might not even escape unscathed himself. He resolved to feign retreat as a strategy, pretending to weaken and hold back his strength while secretly gathering his Internal Force, splitting one breath into two—a technique unique to the Duan Family's Withering and Flourishing Divine Skill. Duan Zhixiu, who had mastered the skill himself, knew only how to split his breath to strengthen his own strikes; give him another ten years and he still would never have guessed his own internal skill held such a use. Guarding against the pressure bearing down on his palms, he never imagined Patriarch Wuxiang could also store qi in his belly and detonate it in an instant to wrench himself free. The two of you were both thrown back, staggering on your feet, and it seemed the tiger was about to slip free and return to the mountain—when suddenly Ye Yunshang burst forward, seized the opening, and drove her head straight into the enemy's Tanzhong vital point. That Tanzhong point was the sea of his ancestral qi; struck by her blow, before Patriarch Wuxiang's True Qi could gather it scattered, his strength misfired, and he flipped backward over the railing and plunged down the cliff.
It's a pity, he bet wrong, didn't expect you to be so clumsy, and both of you were struck dead by the palm force one after the other.

You were blocked by Patriarch Wuxiang, unable to look away, watching Duan Zhixiu chase after Yunshang; you grew desperate. But if you could not find a way to hold this fiend back, she would still have no hope of escape, so you had no choice but to use the terrain and fight for your life, praying only that Yunshang could get away. Yet the gulf between your skill and Patriarch Wuxiang's was vast. The moment he had first laid eyes on you at Qingcheng, he had already felt nothing but loathing, eager to kill you outright, and now that you were in his grasp, he had no intention of granting you an easy death. He toyed with you like a cat with a mouse, baiting you with feints to draw out your strikes, pitting his Internal Force against yours, channeling Qingcheng's internal skill in an effort to melt your organs to blood.
