Just as you stood isolated with your life hanging by a thread, Duan Zhixiu suddenly returned, pressing his palms to your back, channeling the Duan Family of Dali's Withering and Flourishing Divine Skill through your own palms without so much as asking, joining forces with you against this formidable foe.

It's easy enough to slander someone's good name with a mouthful of words. If anyone here is suspicious, it's Qingcheng—a traitor within their own ranks caused Eldest Senior Brother's death, and to this day it's gone unexplained. What grounds does he have to earn your trust?
You could not help but be surprised to hear this, yet you dismissed a matter so hard to prove either way as nothing but nonsense.
You could not help but be surprised upon hearing the words, yet still managed to maintain composure.

Looking back to the year Ye Yunshang and his brother took their apprenticeship at Diancang, rumors of the treasure spread widely. At that time, Duan Zhixiu was still a child, pure‑hearted and untouched by the temptations of power and wealth. He had not placed much importance on the rumors. But as he gradually grew up, he came to realize the importance of wealth‑without coins, how could he recruit soldiers and horses? Without an army, how could he reclaim the supreme honor he had missed, and restore his former glory to the throne? Thus, he placed all his hopes on this treasure, even willing to endure humiliation and make a hollow promise of the imperial consort's position. Unbeknownst to him, Iron Crown Daoist had immediately dismissed King Yue's treasure as a fabrication. If that were true, it meant not only that his restoration of power was impossible, but also that all his past sacrifices had been in vain! His aspirations vanished instantly, and he sat down on the ground, lost in confusion. Iron Crown Daoist sneered coldly, then turned back to Ye Yunshang, demanding the treasure. What he sought was not the treasure itself, but the Nine Springs Pill left behind by the Left Commander of Jile over a decade ago.

You were not the only one startled—Duan Zhixiu was just as bewildered. He had weighed his choice carefully before joining Qingcheng, never expecting Iron Crown Daoist to actually teach him anything; he had picked the old man precisely because he seemed mediocre and easy to manipulate. He never dreamed his cut-rate master concealed such profound skill—and worse, that his methods were far from orthodox, which left Duan Zhixiu troubled rather than pleased.

His martial arts far surpassed yours, and victory was already his for the taking, yet he still chose to trample and shake the walkway out of spite. Yunshang was so frightened that the color drained from her face; she crouched on the ground, clutching the railing for dear life. Determined to shield her fully, you had no way to guard yourself as well, and took several solid blows square on your own body, the force striking again and again until your skin split and your flesh tore.
You fought both of them in succession—Duan Zhixiu was the lesser concern, but the Iron Crown Daoist was truly a peerless master, one your skill today still could not match.

You fought both of them one after another—Duan Zhixiu was the lesser concern, but the Iron Crown Daoist was indeed a peerless master, the founder of the Thousand-Faced Demons; no one who ever saw his true face had lived to tell of it. Yet today you dared to be the exception, felling this peerless master with only a few blows. He was utterly stunned, having taken you for a fellow of his own kind—some old monster who lived disguised in seclusion, content to leave well water and river water undisturbed. But now that you had crossed him, he could never let you leave Meishan alive, lest it ruin his liege lord's grand design to contend for the Central Plains. He gathered his strength and stamped the plank road to collapse, meaning to drag you, Duan Zhixiu, and Ye Yunshang down with him. In midair, he unleashed the Songshan Flower-Twirling Hand, gripping your limbs so tightly that you could not summon your qinggong, and could only watch helplessly as Yunshang struck the mountain wall and died, her beauty extinguished in an instant. Duan Zhixiu could not escape either, but his own deep skill let him call on the Emei White Ape technique to break his fall again and again; he landed hard, but barely clung to life. You, unreasoning and unyielding as ever, only scraped your skin when you hit the cliff floor. Afterward, you and the Iron Crown Daoist fought day after day at the bottom of the ravine, and neither could kill the other. When hungry, you picked wild fruit to eat, never once letting your guard down. But the Iron Crown Daoist was old after all, and for all his skill, he could not outlast the years, and died before you did. You laughed until it hurt, then wept until you had no more tears, knowing that from then on no one would ever speak to you again. You could only talk to yourself, and in time you began to hear things, as though the very grass and trees were urging you on. You paced the valley floor back and forth countless times, unwilling to grow old and die there, yet unable to bear the grass and trees pressing in on you, until in despair you struck your own skull and died.

If he did not act, all was well; but the moment he did, his moves came like a hundred flowers blooming in disarray, techniques from every school flowing effortlessly from him and leaving you dazzled and bewildered. His martial arts proved no less than that of the Dharma King of the Hell Path back then, nor even the Sect Leader of Qingcheng. Only now did you realize: this man had been concealing his true skill all along.

The outcome was decided, and his newly-taken master, Iron Crown Daoist, made his presence known. You took him at first for a mere companion of Duan Zhixiu's on the road, but Duan Zhixiu himself was startled all the same—he had clearly paid a Tang Clan disciple handsomely to guard the plank road and bar passage, yet the Iron Crown Daoist had appeared without a sound. As a master of an orthodox sect, Iron Crown Daoist should have known right from wrong, but instead of reprimanding his disciple, he took his side.

He couldn't help but believe your casual lie a little more. The Duan Clan of Dali has inherited the Withering and Flourishing Divine Skill from their ancestors, and the Great Song's Zhao family, which built their empire on horseback, is no small matter either. Both are noble and distinguished royal bloodlines; losing to you isn't too shameful, he thought, and soon stopped being angry.

Naturally you couldn't stand by and do nothing, so you stepped forward. Duan Zhixiu had honed his left-handed swordsmanship to considerable skill, and the edge of Diancang Sword Technique paired well with the deep internal skill of the Duan family of Dali; with the added advantage of weapon and terrain, he should have held the upper hand. But you deliberately withheld your Tang Clan martial arts—your Small Sword held itself long, as though you gripped a spear, feinting strikes from a distance. Whenever he took it for a bluff, your Small Sword would shoot out again, truly spear-like, lengthening and shortening without warning, impossible to predict. When the fierce clash finally decided a winner, he was secretly shaken: by his own reckoning his skill had fully returned, yet giving his all, he still couldn't overcome this unknown nobody—it would hardly do the Pine-Smoke Swordsman's reputation any good.

Naturally you couldn't stand by and do nothing, so you stepped forward. But Duan Zhixiu had honed his left-handed swordsmanship to considerable skill, and the edge of Diancang Sword Technique paired well with the deep internal skill of the Duan family of Dali; with the added advantage of his weapon and the terrain, he kept you from finding room to maneuver.

On the way back, someone was waiting where the plank road had to pass, and came at you both with a menacing air. When you made out his face, it turned out to be Duan Zhixiu of the Duan Family, back from Lingnan after falling into Yunshang's trap. His face was a terrifying shade of black, all trace of his usual pampered airs gone; one moment he raged, the next he was so aggrieved he broke down sobbing—every bit the madman.   Only then did you learn how eventful his trip had been: seized and extorted by the local Lingnan Sect, stripped of his wealth, and forced to marry into the sect, taking the former sect leader's daughter as his wife. From now on, it seemed, the Lingnan Sect could even claim kinship with the royal house of Dali—what a story to tell! A real man can bend as well as stand firm, and using the standing of the Duan family of Dali to build connections would have been no bad thing in itself. But to be married off while the bride herself was off traveling the Central Plains, nowhere near Lingnan—he never even laid eyes on her before his head was forced down to bow before a hen.   Such humiliation—let alone for a scion of the Duan clan of Dali, how many ordinary men could stomach it? His hopes of bringing honor to his ancestors dashed, he had dragged the Duan family's name through the mud instead. How could he face his forebears in the next world, and on what ground could he still stand in this one!   When you got down to it, this was all thanks to that wretched girl behind you—you'd best keep your nose out of other people's business!

She was furious that you'd meddled and ruined her scheme, and stormed off; you had no choice but to follow, coaxing her gently the whole way, past the plank road and the back mountain, and across a stream. She planted herself on the one rock in the stream that offered any footing, and warned you not to come closer. No one is truly without feeling, and everything you'd done for her, she had seen and taken to heart—even a scoundrel of the world would have been moved. Knowing her days were numbered and fearing she might run out of time, she had chosen this spot with care for the one solemn farewell of her life, letting this little stream stand in for the River of Forgetfulness, a rehearsal for parting. She set her pretty face stern and let no warmth show. It wasn't that she failed to know your feelings—only that what she'd already received from you was debt enough to last a mountain's weight. She was a life already spent, with no future ahead; anything more she could never repay, nor bear to accept. And so, at the parting, she kindly pushed you a little further away and urged you to go home. Your life still stretched on ahead of you, after all, and the fate meant for you would come in its own time. Someday there would be another girl who knew how good you were, and who would be blessed with what she herself never could be. Each of you carried your own thoughts, and for a long, long while, neither spoke. The sunset's warmth faded, the moonlight turned colder still; that night, there were no stars, no insects singing. Both of you knew it in your hearts: this game of make-believe had reached its end. However unwilling you were to part, it was time to let go—time to go your separate ways.

On any other day you might have let it slide, but today is Junior Martial Sister's big day, and the greater good comes first—you truly have no patience to deal with this, so you have no choice but to invoke Ye Yunzhou's name to bring her to heel. The mere mention of her brother makes her backside ache all over again, and before you can even press her, she hurries back into Zhengxin Hall, bolts the doors, and scrambles to cover her tracks—fabricating an alibi, playing the picture of innocence as though she'd never set foot outside today. She's made up her mind: however you complain about her afterward, she'll deny it to the bitter end.

Ye Yunshang's attempt to cause a disruption failed, and you subdued her. She showed not a trace of remorse, instead turning on you in anger for ruining her scheme. This time she had good reason—it was no ordinary mischief. She meant, quite deliberately, to bring her older brother and her best friend together, so that after she was gone, the two could rely on each other, rather than have one live out his days like a hollow shell and the other fall for the wrong man and spend a lifetime in sorrow. As for what the two of them actually wanted, it could not be helped—for now, it would simply have to be set aside.

Just as Nangong Shen and Xie Wuchen, two great masters, were about to settle their duel, someone burst in waving a sword, declaring she meant to become the Tang Clan's son-in-law. The intruder wore a Diancang green robe and was small of stature; she brazenly claimed to be Ye Yunzhou, was exposed on the spot, and, her face flushing, stubbornly talked her way around it—now claiming instead to be Ye Yunzhou's younger brother and Ye Yunshang's second-eldest brother, one Ye Yunjiu. The Ye siblings' names were known to all, but few had ever seen their true faces, so when a second brother suddenly appeared, no one could say for certain who she really was. She held the crowd speechless through sheer bravado, but you had lived beside her day and night—how could you fail to recognize her? You and Third Senior Brother leapt into the arena one after the other: you whisked Ye Yunshang out of the scene while Third Senior Brother held the situation steady.

Out of her own self-interest, Yunshang was none too pleased to see the Junior Martial Sister spending the night in the pill-refining chamber, alone with you. So, with her treasured honey biscuits as bait, she cleverly lured her away, leaving you alone with the Eldest Senior Brother.

Yunshang knew you hadn't yet had dinner, so she brought you her own medicinal meal for the night - you could eat your fill, and she would be spared having to choke it down herself; wasn't that the best of both worlds? From afar you could hear the endless wrangling in Zhengxin Hall - the Sect Leader had only just fallen, and already these people dared come and run wild. Though they were not of the Tang Clan, even they could not help a pang of sorrow - the Tang Clan's twilight years, a scene of bleak decline.

However, the principal offender cannot be leniently treated; they must be eliminated to serve as a warning to others. After the disciples of the Guangzhou Tang Clan were released, they could not wait for the sect leader to return. The group became disunited, and soon they each switched to other sects.

However, the true culprit could not be easily forgiven. With the Chief Enforcer absent, they could only defer to the opinions of their fellow disciples in handling the matter. Tang Shouhong, the Tang Clan traitor, had once been a Great Hero in his own right. Yet you pack of Tang Clan fanatics forced him into the Poison Sand Vat until his skin turned blue all over, looking neither man nor ghost, and he spent the rest of his life in hiding, too ashamed to show his face to anyone.

However, the true culprit could not be easily spared. With the Chief Enforcer absent, they had no choice but to refer to the opinions of their fellow disciples, carrying out the sentence one by one. In the end, Tang Shouhong still died, suffering endless humiliation before his death. He regretted not only returning to his homeland, but even having been born at all.
The Guangzhou Tang Clan turned out in full force. Yet even the Tang Clan, however ruthless, could not disregard its standing in the Jianghu and wipe out every last one of them.

Tang Fang followed Second Senior Brother's medical strategy, first using the Balance-Viewing Needle to help Yunshang harmonize the Five Elements, then the Return Pulse Needle technique to heal her damaged meridians and Qi Sea. Only then could Yunshang take the Tang Clan's medicinal cuisine to nurture her righteous qi. This righteous qi did not need to overpower the malevolent qi—so long as it was present at all, any Tang Clan disciple of the same lineage and pulse could channel their true qi to reinforce the righteous and drive out the malevolent. Add to this the Exit-Orifice Needle technique, alternately tonifying and draining to quicken the flow, so that with an inward push and an outward pull, the foreign true qi within her could be forced out all at once, and the root of her illness pulled out for good.

During Second Senior Brother's treatment, he never once asked after the reasons behind the Ye family's troubles. It was only today that Tang Fang finally revealed the true cause of Ye Yunshang's long, incurable illness: several strands of foreign true qi ran uncontrolled within her body, straying from the normal flow of her meridians. And because her dantian had been damaged since childhood, she could never cultivate Internal Skill to transform that malevolent energy. Once that foreign true qi ran loose, it formed a cycle of its own—each small Heavenly Circuit it completed brought on a minor illness, and each large Heavenly Circuit threatened to kill her. Ye Yunzhou clearly knew all this, but for reasons unknown kept his silence throughout, leaving countless physicians to misdiagnose her until the illness had taken deep root. Each time she fell ill, they could only suppress it by force with miracle pills, driving the surface affliction deeper inward—like quenching thirst with poison—which is why it has lingered uncured to this day. Even when men of skill lent their aid, channeling true qi into her to steady her and treat her wounds, that borrowed qi could never be transformed either, and in the end simply merged with the malevolent energy—so that her condition seemed to improve, while in truth it only grew worse.

Fortunately, Second Senior Brother's many efforts were not wasted after all—the Tang Clan is not the only power under heaven who can treat her. In poison, the Tang Clan holds a slight edge; in acupuncture, none surpasses Divine Physician Liang of the Jin Kingdom. Even with the old medical immortal Liang gone, his disciple remains—the Little Medicine Immortal, Liang Youshi. Ye Yunzhou had originally been set on leaving, partly for fear of bringing trouble down on the Tang Clan, and partly because with Tang Zheng a fugitive, staying meant certain death—he had no choice but to flee and seek another way to survive. Hearing Tang Fang's words, his mind finally settled. Tang Fang gave the siblings a bottle of 'Zombie Powder,' a poison that slows the heartbeat, lowers body temperature, and brings drowsiness day and night. It takes too long to be useful in a fight, and is more often used for covert killing or feigning death—rarely for medical treatment. She warned them again and again not to take too much, for it was poison after all; but at a careful dose, it could delay the onset of her illness and keep her safe on the road ahead.
It's not that you're fearless, but rather more afraid of her passing away.

In the Jianghu, when blades cross and men fight to the death, isn't the outcome unknown until the fight is already underway? No one gives up while there's still hope—not until they've truly seen the Yellow River. So long as there's the faintest chance, treat it as though you will win.

This 'Nirvana Samadhi' is in fact the Internal Method behind the old Demon Cult's ultimate skill, the Nine Turns of Reincarnation. It runs against the grain of ordinary internal training: the practitioner must set life and death aside, seal the eight extraordinary meridians, suppress their own heartbeat, and bring their inner breath to a complete stop. The method was originally meant to extinguish worldly troubles and attain clarity, but it was twisted to evil ends by men of ill intent.   Long ago, the Left and Right Envoys of the Supreme Bliss Cult served as the cult leader's Guardians: one practiced the Nine Turns of Reincarnation, the other the Heaven-Swallowing Treasure Mirror. The Left Envoy, through the Heaven-Swallowing Treasure Mirror, drained others' Internal Force to feed and strengthen the cult leader's cultivation; the Right Envoy, through the Nine Turns of Reincarnation, lent their own dantian to absorb the backlash of foreign True Qi on the cult leader's behalf.   Now it is that very foreign True Qi, lying dormant within her, that has kept Yunshang bedridden. Her dantian was damaged, so she cannot cultivate Internal Skill to transform it—no matter how others channel their energy to heal her, or how many potent remedies she takes, none of it does any good. Second Senior Brother tried to purge the True Qi from her body, but his effort fell just short of success. The only path left is to skillfully use the Nirvana Samadhi: to link the meridians, lend her your own dantian, open a new Heavenly Circuit, and channel your True Qi into her body to transform and share the burden with her—only then is there any chance at all.   Even so, the chance of saving Yunshang remains slim, and in the end you cannot avoid staking your own life on it. And that realm is not one the living can enter and leave at will. Once you step into the underworld, without a master at your side to call your soul back with Internal Skill or a Soul-Retrieval Needle Technique, hoping to return would be nothing but a fool's dream. Even if Tang Fang were uninjured and threw her full strength into guarding you, the odds would still be under thirty percent. Even so, you made up your mind.

Everyone else had given up and scattered, leaving only you still standing there, unwilling to leave. That day when Yunshang mentioned it, you kept it in mind, and asked Tang Fang about the Nirvana Samadhi—it shocked her so much that her eyes went wide, stunned beyond measure. The origin of this technique was such that in this age, whoever learned of it would die, one fewer person with each telling, so no one dared speak of it lightly. The Tang Clan's reputation was murky enough as it was, but if it were ever linked to this, not even the Yellow River could wash it clean.

Ye Yunzhou only had this younger sister to rely on. If possible, he would willingly give half his life to her. But fate does not favor human wishes. Knowing there was no hope, he felt all hope lost and finally agreed to stay in the Tang Clan, allowing her to have a peaceful remaining life.

You regret nothing more than wasting your years on impractical dreams of being a Great Hero. Had you known, you would have clung to Second Senior Brother's side no matter how he mistreated and abused you, and studied the medical arts diligently.

The deeper you delve into the medical arts, the more you realize how hard this is; however arrogant you might be, you dare not boast lightly. What you fear most is giving her false hope, only to see it dashed.

However, unexpected changes occurred during the Qingcheng journey, and all the effort of these long years came to nothing. This method is no longer feasible, and in today's world there is no other good method left to save Yunshang. Had Tang Fang not been struck by the Bone-Embedding Needle, however slim the hope, she might still have used a forbidden technique to trade her life for another's. But things have come to this, and no one can do anything more.

At that moment, a wisp of light smoke drifted in from outside the window. Ye Yunzhou was completely focused on you, never expecting the ambush to come from behind. By the time he tried to cover his mouth and nose, it was already too late. He drew a breath of True Qi and still meant to resist, but his sister Ye Yunshang pulled out a staff and struck him across the head, knocking him out cold on the spot.   You felt a moment of confusion, thinking Second Senior Brother had returned, but it was the haggard-looking Tang Fang who stepped through the door. She had been afflicted by the Tang Clan's Bone-Embedding Needles and could not circulate her energy; even standing was quite a struggle. Had she not heard that you were all fighting over whether Yunshang would stay, she wouldn't have bothered to open her eyes at all.   She took Ye Yunzhou for a friend, so the Bewitching Incense she used carried no poison, and reckoned he would wake within the time it took a stick of incense to burn. She then asked you to seal Ye Yunzhou's acupoints and carry him to the alchemy room, while she went to wash her face and apply a little powder to hide her sickly pallor.   When Ye Yunzhou woke, he was still in a frenzy. Only after Ye Yunshang, settling an old score, forced two bowls of Gentian Liver-Soothing Soup down him did he calm down enough to listen to reason.

Ye Yunzhou wasn't skilled in endurance and had lost his usual composure. His sword's brilliance was at its peak, yet lacked the strict discipline of old, revealing countless flaws. You seized the right moment to strike continuously and defeated this renowned Diancang swordsman.

Ye Yunzhou wasn't adept at endurance and had lost his composure, his blade's edge at its peak yet lacking the strict discipline of before. Despite this, he remained Diancang's top swordsman of the era. The fight didn't last long, and you were defeated. Ye Yunshang saw the situation was dire, darted into your arms, placed her neck on your blade, and demanded you take her as a hostage.
How could you not long to have your own way for once, to be her pillar, shielding her from every storm? Heaven only knows how deeply it wounded you to summon the courage to urge her to leave.
Seeing his madness laid bare, and recalling Duan Zhixiu's already-ruined right hand, you couldn't help but feel a chill of fear.

Seeing his madness laid bare, and recalling Duan Zhixiu's ruined right hand, you couldn't help but feel a chill of fear—yet still you would not yield a single step. Having called him brother, you owed it to him to shake him awake.

You know that persuading her to stay would cut off her only chance at survival, yet you understand full well that this parting might mean never seeing her again. Ye Yunzhou probably knows it too, but he refuses to sit and wait for death. All his life he practiced self-restraint and humility, never expecting that even so small a wish would be denied by heaven. Since that is so, he means to see it through to the end, to walk the road to its close, to not betray his ancestors' trust, and to learn at last where the Ye family's loyalty and valor will finally come to rest. If heaven still has the heart to watch this unfold, he vows to become a vengeful ghost, sword in hand, cutting a bloody swath a thousand miles long across the Jianghu!

Ye Yunshang could accept her fate, but she would not allow her dear brother to have his way. This time, she was resolute, determined to die rather than yield. The members of the Tang Clan sensed something and stepped forward one after another. After living together day in and day out, they were not just fellow disciples‑they shared a bond of friendship. No one cared anymore about treasures or secrets. Their only concern was to prevent them from enduring hardship and wandering endlessly.

This journey to the Jin Kingdom lay a thousand miles away, and she was destined to go without return. And what of her brother? Many years before, one night, the two siblings had suddenly lost their home; her brother had carried her on his back, drifting until he took shelter under the Diancang Sect. Except for those two years he spent roaming the Jianghu, the two had never been apart. Because she feared the dark, and because an eldest brother is as a father, he had become a flame for her, burning on in quiet steadiness. Her master had praised him for a sword-bone rare once in a hundred years—he should have become a hero the world admired—yet for her sake he bowed his head to others, spending half his life in hardship and toil. Once she was gone, what would be left for him, and who would he light the way for then? Even onlookers could see it plainly: he was spent, utterly exhausted. He wasn't bound for the Jin Kingdom at all—he was walking, single-mindedly, toward his own death.

But Yunshang did break their promise; this parting meant no more meetings in the future. Flowers bloom and wither, and even the occasional letters sent through intermediaries eventually ceased. Life's gatherings and partings are like duckweed drifting on the water‑there are always those who cannot obtain what they desire and cannot let go. They hardened their heart and left you in the spring light of the season, bidding farewell and never returning.

You reluctantly walked them down the mountain, unwilling to part. The junior martial sister, who had been absent from the farewell, suddenly rushed over carrying a pile of snacks and candied fruits, dumping them all into Yunshang's hands. Sharing her pain and sorrow, the junior martial sister, not adept at expressing herself, folded all her words into paper cranes to pray for her well‑being. They linked fingers in a vow, promising to remain forever friends and meet again someday.

She is sharp-witted, skilled at reading people's moods, how could she not know your feelings? Her heart is both sweet and bitter, wanting to hurt you so badly that you're left with nothing but wounds, leaving an unhealing scar on your heart so you'll never forget her. Yet seeing your pitiful, weeping face, she can't help but soften. Since fate did not bring them together in this life, she decides to show you mercy and spare you this time. At this very moment, she returns your heart to you.

Your beloved one bids you farewell. No matter how far you send them, it's never enough. You long to be with them, yet fear she might despise you. How can you let go of the sect when the Tang Clan faces calamity? You can only let go, hoping she finds a future where you can never reach her.

The butterfly you hold in your palm pats its wings and is about to fly away. You are immensely reluctant, even to the point of harboring wicked thoughts, wanting to confine her forever by your side. But deep down, you know that if you do so, she will inevitably wither in your palm. Rather than doing this, it would be better to let her go and have a future where you can reach out but cannot touch.

She had been dead set against leaving, but the instant Ye Yunzhou mentioned "Miss Liang, the Little Medicine Immortal," her ears perked up. Without even meeting her, she had already appointed the girl a candidate for sister-in-law, hoping to make the match before she died—perhaps, once she was gone, Miss Liang could become her brother's pillar and keep his heart from breaking.

The internal strife within the Tang Clan left it gravely weakened. The Sect Leader lay stricken with illness, the Second Senior Brother had defected, and the Eldest Senior Brother's whereabouts remained unknown, leaving the whole sect in dread. Ye Yunshang carefully soothed her Junior Martial Sister, giving no thought to her own plight. Now that the Tang Clan could barely save itself, it had no strength left to treat her; the next time her illness struck, it might well be her last. Ye Yunzhou burned with worry, unwilling to sit and wait for death, while Ye Yunshang could only sigh with sorrow. Though she had never held high hopes from the start, to endure so long only to find it all a mirror-flower, a moon in water, still stung—hearts, after all, are made of flesh, and even the most open-minded can be wounded. But what good did it do to rail at heaven and earth? On reflection, her days in the Tang Clan, lively and full, had brought her the truest friends, an extra brother, an extra grandfather, and playmates besides. Brief as the time had been, it was the most contented stretch of her life, worth a hundred times more than going to Jiangnan. All her life plagued by illness, she had never wept or raged, for she had long made peace with dying that very day; she treated each day as her last, and lived it fully, holding nothing back—desiring nothing, she feared nothing, and clung to nothing when the time came to let go. Moling had a home, and you had the Tang Clan. The one person in this world she found hardest to leave behind was her calm, undemanding brother. From childhood on, he had always put her first, never once weighing his own likes or wants. Even in the years he ventured into the Jianghu, it was to seek medicine for her, as if he had no life of his own; the friends he made along the way turned on him over fame and fortune. In all the wide Jianghu, if he gave up on himself, who else would there be to hold Yunzhou fast?

Tang Fang had set a trap to catch any traitor fleeing the mountain, but she hadn't expected the person she caught to be no Guangzhou Tang Clan disciple at all—rather the very one who had raised her with a hand both strict and gentle. She had believed no one alive knew him better than she did, yet she could never have imagined that Second Senior Brother, whom she regarded as both brother and teacher, could bring himself to strike her down so coldly. As the Bone-Piercing Nail drove into her body, it felt as though her heart shattered along with it.
Until the siblings, after a long and arduous journey, arrived at the Tang Clan and received the protection of the Sect Leader, they were finally able to catch their breath.
Until the siblings eventually arrived at the Tang Clan and came to know you, they only then believed that there was still a sliver of light in the world.

This painful memory was not one the siblings had always kept to themselves — but rumor does its damage regardless, and a lie is always easier spread than unraveled. Set against their own account, most people preferred to believe whatever they'd already imagined, clinging stubbornly to their bias: that the Ye siblings were no good, that they'd hoarded the treasure for themselves, that they owed a debt to every commoner of the Central Plains. However they defended themselves, the world went on suspecting them. Short of Ye Yunshang baring herself before a crowd to prove her innocence, no vouching from anyone would have satisfied the doubters — they'd sooner have dug up her grave after she was dead than let her rest in peace. A rumor repeated often enough becomes accepted as truth, and so the orphans of a loyal minister found their names dragged through the mud. Hearts weary as cold ash, the siblings stumbled from one betrayal to the next until, worn down, they grew wary of everyone and trusted no one, choosing silence over ever speaking of it again.

Upon learning of the hidden hand behind the Tang Clan night raid, the Ye siblings felt guilty for failing the Tang Clan. Despite the dishonor, they could no longer hide their shame and decided to seek an audience with the sect leader to confess their sins, asking you to witness their tale. They began to recount the entangled grudge between themselves and Duan Zhixiu.  The Ye orphans had drifted from the Central Plains to the Southern Region, joining the Diancang. Duan Zhixiu was also caught up in a political upheaval in Dali and was exiled to the Jianghu, making them kindred spirits in suffering. Since Ye Yunzhou and Duan Zhixiu were of similar age and trained together, they formed a deep friendship, and along with Ye Yunshang, they swore an oath of brotherhood, vowing to share both hardships and blessings.  However, the Ye siblings, being wanderers, could not expect a stable life to last long. One day, Duan Zhixiu received a letter from home, and upon reading it, his face turned pale. The Tubo Kingdom's Maozhou tribe, relying on their geographical advantage, frequently interfered with the exchanges between Dali and the Great Song, brazenly attacking merchant caravans and extorting envoys. The Dali royal family, devoted to Buddhism and cautious of war, was reluctant to initiate conflict and thus decided to arrange a marriage alliance, elevating the legitimate daughter of the loyal Duke to the title of Lady Ningyang, sending the skilled martial artist Li Ziqiong to escort her with eighty elite soldiers.  After reading the letter, Duan Zhixiu's expression was one of despair. In his youth, he had been manipulated by the powerful Gao family, embroiled in the struggle for the throne, and had suffered defeat, leading to his exile. For over a decade, he had been law‑abiding and repentant, often copying Buddhist scriptures to present to the palace, hoping for the emperor's mercy to lift the confinement of the Duke of Loyalty's Mansion and allow him to return to his roots. While he could endure many past grievances, it was unbearable that the ruler of a nation would send his only eleven‑year‑old sister abroad for a marriage alliance with a barbarian nation.   The Tubo were known for their custom of sharing wives, which, in the eyes of the Song and Dali people, was a violation of propriety. It was easy to imagine that his precious sister, marrying into a foreign land, would suffer a fate worse than death. Yet, no matter how unwilling he was, what could he do? Ye Yunzhou and Ye Yunshang shared in his sorrow. In those years, they were still naive, blindly believing in chivalry, filled with passion, willing to risk everything for a friend, even defying imperial edicts.  They plotted to ambush the Lady's procession, even going so far as to collude with opposing forces of the Maozhou tribe, which was indeed audacious. Ye Yunshang, clever and resourceful, had countless schemes; if applied to righteous causes, she would be a rare strategist, and she took pride in this. If they had followed her plan, everyone could have escaped unharmed, but unfortunately, she underestimated the fickleness of human hearts.  From the moment Duan Zhixiu received the letter, he realized: the emperor's sparing of his life was not an act of mercy; his servility had not earned him a shred of sympathy, only intensified oppression and humiliation. The only way to avoid being manipulated was to grow strong and respond with violence, which required raising an army. However, building a military force required substantial financial resources, and with the Dali ruler focused on governance and enjoying the people's support, no one was willing to rebel against him. Thus, the secret of the King Yue's Treasure that the Ye siblings held became their only path to uprising.  Compared to his ambition to usurp the throne, the bond of brotherhood seemed trivial. The unfortunate Ye siblings, unsuspecting of his true intentions, accompanied him at the cost of their lives. Yet, Duan Zhixiu changed his mind at the last moment, bribing fellow disciples and abandoning Ye Yunzhou amidst the chaos, tricking her out of the Listening Cloud Sword and deceiving Ye Yunshang into believing that Ye Yunzhou had died in battle, hoping to win her over while she was vulnerable.  Fortunately, Ye Yunzhou's fate was not yet sealed; he had received a warning from his sister beforehand. Unable to rely on his fellow disciples, he chose to surrender to the Tubo. After many trials, he finally returned home, severing ties with Duan Zhixiu by crippling his arm with a single sword strike, and fled with his sister to the Central Plains.

You and Ye Yunshang then recounted the Qingcheng mission again to make Ye Yunzhou aware. Upon learning that the mastermind was his former close friend, Ye Yunzhou couldn't help but sigh in sorrow. On the day of Diancang, they severed his arm, which would have settled the grudge. Now the Tang Clan is further burdened by his siblings, leaving no room for either duty or personal ties. The day of their reunion will be the day of their eternal farewell.

The Second Senior Brother didn't take it kindly. Nangong Ji had already been subjected to inhumane torture at the time of his capture, and all the secrets in his stomach were spat out along with the foam, leaving him with no further use.

He arrived at the Tang Clan before you all, having heard that you were injured and had gone to Qingcheng for treatment. Yunshang had a blade pressed against your unconscious body, threatening to die with you if you didn't comply. The crowd couldn't persuade her, so they reluctantly allowed her to go to Qingcheng with you. This frightened him, and he didn't dare linger. Just upon reaching Meishan, he immediately set off for Qingcheng. Unluckily, he encountered you returning, and to avoid Duan Zhixiu's pursuit, they took a non‑official route, thus passing each other by. Though he didn't meet you, he later encountered Nangong Ji on the way back. Observing his suspicious behavior, dressed in Nangong attire, and his frantic reactions upon seeing a man in a plain robe‑either fleeing into the grass or darting onto rooftops‑along with his writing of Boshan script on walls, he became suspicious and followed him for several days before finally speaking. Nangong Ji asked him in a coded manner, but Ye Yunzhou couldn't answer. Seeing that he wasn't one of them, Nangong Ji intended to change the subject and leave, but upon glancing at Ye Yunzhou's sword hilt, he was shocked, recognizing the Listening Cloud Sword. In Ye Yunzhou's eyes, all these actions were highly suspicious, and he couldn't possibly let him go. Thinking that his eloquence wouldn't yield answers, he was fortunate that the sword could speak more than his words. Through the sword, he learned about the night attack. Poor Nangong Ji, barely surviving the attack, was now caught and returned to the Tang Clan.

On his way back, he ran into Nangong Ji, whose bearing struck him as suspicious — dressed in Nangong colors, yet startling like a bird at the mere twang of a bowstring whenever he glimpsed someone in a green robe on the road, diving into the bushes one moment, scrambling onto rooftops the next. He even left messages scrawled in Bo script on walls. Ye Yunzhou took note and shadowed him for several days before finally speaking up. Nangong Ji tried a coded phrase to test him, which Ye Yunzhou naturally couldn't answer. Seeing he wasn't one of their own, Nangong Ji tried to change the subject and slip away, but while his eyes darted about, he caught sight of the sword hilt on Ye Yunzhou's back — his face went white with shock, for he clearly recognized the Listening Cloud Sword. To Ye Yunzhou's eyes, every one of these behaviors looked suspicious, and there was no question of letting him go so easily. He reckoned his own tongue wouldn't pry out the truth, but fortunately the sword spoke louder than words, and so he learned of that night's ambush. Poor Nangong Ji, barely surviving one ordeal, found himself dragged back to the Tang Clan once more.
At this moment, Ye Yunzhou, who had gone to Jiangling to repay a debt of gratitude, finally returned and reunited with his close sister and you, and all were filled with joy.

Ye Yunshang's illness stemmed from an uncontrollable Foreign True Qi within her body. Though the two siblings kept quiet about it, Second Senior Brother and Tang Fang understood the situation and never pressed for details. They administered acupuncture and medicine daily, aligning with the Five Elements, and nurtured her Righteous Qi. On the day her injury flared, Second Senior Brother could administer strong medicine to support her, expel the evil energy, and help her transform the uncontrollable Foreign True Qi within, thus eliminating the hidden danger.

Ye Yunshang's affliction stemmed from an uncontrollable Foreign True Qi lodged within her body. Though the two siblings kept quiet about it, Second Senior Brother and Tang Fang understood well enough, and never pressed for the whole story — instead tending her day and night with needle and medicine, aligning her with the Five Elements, nourishing her righteous qi, and firming her foundation. On the day her old injury finally flared, Second Senior Brother could at last administer a potent remedy, supporting the righteous and driving out the evil, helping her channel the uncontrollable Foreign True Qi within and root out the danger for good. Things had begun to improve, but no one foresaw the sudden mishap during the Qingcheng mission — even with Tang Fang at her side, she still fell to a hidden scheme. The Other Shore Incense poison had fused with her old wound and could no longer be purged carelessly: force out her True Qi rashly, and the poison, with nowhere else to go, would plunge straight into her marrow and destroy her mind. Whoever poisoned her clearly knew medicine well and meant to strike at the Tang Clan — without the counter-formula, the poison had no cure, and with this one scheme he had undone all of Second Senior Brother's work and snuffed out Ye Yunshang's last chance at life.

Now you have no choice but to clean up after her, determined to go back and report her to her brother Ye Yunzhou and settle accounts properly. If her backside doesn't end up beaten black and blue, you'll take her surname yourself.
Helplessly, you let out a sigh and braced yourself to take the blame. Ye Yunshang saw that you weren't angry and finally breathed a sigh of relief.

Aunt Sun brought the mischievous troublemaker Ye Yunshang to you. Yunshang, upon seeing you, squealed Brother and rushed forward, but you stepped back to avoid her. It was because your living conditions were filthy and rundown, with nowhere to go and no home to return to. You had lost your dreams, your heart gradually withered, and you couldn't bear to part with the tattered Tang Clan uniform. Seeing Yunshang, you felt ashamed, yet she, clever as she was, seemed completely unaware. The more you tried to avoid her, the more she insisted on hugging you. The warmth didn't last long. When asked what great feat she had done to anger Aunt Sun, her smile froze instantly. You silently realized something was wrong‑this was why she was being cute. Don't you know this girl's tricks? Just looking at her nervous expression, you knew something bad was coming your way.

You have no fond memories of this matron. When you first arrived in Shu, alone with no kin and still young, the coins you earned each day were barely enough to live on. To save up for gifts to curry favor with the Tang Clan's elders, you often went hungry one day and ate your fill the next. The smell of braised wild game would set your stomach growling, and sometimes you couldn't help drifting over to breathe it in while eating your thin porridge and steamed bun. Every time Aunt Sun caught you at it, she'd fly into a rage, cursing you for being ugly and foul-smelling and ruining her trade. Nearly ten years on, you still hold the grudge.

She thought Fourth Senior Brother had eaten at her stall without paying and had come to settle the score with you. Little did she know — though Fourth Senior Brother truly had skimped on her braised goods, the reason she stopped you was something else entirely.
Unable to bear staying any longer, you turned to leave, only to find your way blocked by Aunt Sun, who sold braised wild game.

Today, with no work to do, you wandered aimlessly through the streets, watching a bit of street entertainment, then listened to a storyteller for free. Unconsciously, you found yourself in the Outer Fort, where the bustling noise has remained the same for decades. Thinking back to when you once lived here and tried hard to get into the main courtyard, it felt as if it were from another world, a melancholy creeping into your heart.

Recently, he discovered a mysterious herb unknown to the world, suspected to be the sovereign ingredient of the Supreme Bliss Cult's old Corpse Heart Gu. This herb is part insect, part plant, able to parasitize inside a larva's body, spreading and growing until it fully occupies the host's shell—then it forces the host to burrow into the ground and kill itself, and only then does the plant finish maturing. To confirm its properties he needed proof first, and had been planning to raid a prison for a few death-row convicts to experiment on. Then, conveniently, Nangong Ji came looking for death himself—with Internal Skill and a sturdy body, this potted cordyceps plant had no name on it but his.

You're really curious, not following Second Senior Brother's instructions and opening other medicine cabinets at will. You'd never expect that cabinets numbered one through ten all have killing mechanisms. Although Second Senior Brother gave you three keys, they can only open cabinet number four. If you use the key for cabinet four to open other drawers, it will trigger the mechanism, firing cow hair needles to kill and silence you.

According to Second Senior Brother's usual style, anyone who offends the Tang Clan is killed without mercy. But Nangong Ji was only a servant, so in the end he spared his life—after all, killing is easy, but the aftermath is troublesome. Better to let him live; he had another use for him. So he tossed you a set of keys and told you to fetch medicine from the cabinet.
You just promised to do your best, but once you got the words out, you went back on your word.

You are a long‑standing member of the Tang Clan. Second Senior Brother's strictness toward you differs from how he treats others, with a deliberate intent. You know that according to his style, anyone who offends the Tang Clan is killed without mercy, yet you still spoke up to advise him. Even though your words were harsh, Second Senior Brother couldn't ignore them. If it weren't for you accidentally saying a few extra words that damaged his image when you were startled, he would have happily adopted your opinion. Now that he has adopted your opinion, you can't avoid a bit of physical punishment as a warning.

The Second Senior Brother was clearly displeased, and it showed. Though he was never polite to you—calling you a stupid pig, feeble-minded, never sparing an insult—he still valued your opinion. After all, you were a veteran of the Tang Clan, and you knew his ways better than anyone; that you still dared speak up despite that was commendable. So he decided to split the difference: spare the man's life, but only kill him halfway—and the other half, naturally, would fall on you.

But don't you think about the fact that you left without notice, and returning would be suspicious? You just happened to uncover this group of petty villains' conspiracy. Now you're asking for mercy, and the Second Senior Brother suspects you, which is entirely reasonable. Without waiting for him to take action against you, the accumulated authority over the years has scared you to the point of losing your mind, panicking and fleeing, tripping and falling, and being pierced by a Throwing Dart embedded in the ground from the previous battle, dying on the spot.
You truly could not bear to see this man lose his life, so you gritted your teeth and spoke up in his defense.
Having exhausted everything he knew, Nangong Ji stammered, unable to give any more useful information. The Second Senior Brother's eyes turned cold, murderous intent already stirring.

Seeing that no further useful information could be extracted, the Second Senior Brother dismissed him hastily. You were astonished‑given the Second Senior Brother's usual ruthless nature, anyone who dared to offend the Tang Clan would be killed without hesitation. When would he ever show such mercy? Naturally, the Second Senior Brother had no such kindness; he had his own plans. He had recently discovered a rare herb, unknown to anyone, suspected to be the key ingredient of the ancient Supreme Bliss Cult's Heartworm Toxin. This herb resembled both a worm and a plant, capable of parasitizing within the bodies of larvae, growing and spreading until it completely occupied the host's body, at which point it would forcibly control the host to burrow and commit suicide, only then would the herb mature. To determine its properties, a case was needed first. He was already planning to descend the mountain to raid a prison, capture some prisoners for experimentation. Lo and behold, Nangong Ji himself volunteered to court death by stepping into the Tang Clan's territory. With his internal skill and strong physique, he was the perfect candidate for cultivating this parasitic herb. Though this method was horrifying, how was Hua Tuo's act of drilling into Cao Cao's skull to treat his illness any less shocking? Destruction leads to creation. If the herb's properties could be confirmed, benefiting future generations, Nangong Ji would also take pride in it. Compared to living in torment, what was death but a fleeting shadow?

As for running into the Hell Path's ghost soldiers, that had nothing to do with them. Startled awake by ghosts in the middle of the night, he was even more frightened than you, and even suspected your Tang Clan was in league with the Mud Cult.

Young Lord Duan, who traces his lineage to Diancang, having ill intentions toward the Tang Clan is not unusual. But as to what he is scheming against Nangong, it's not something Nangong Ji can easily figure out.
Not only openly attacking the Tang Clan, secretly sabotaging the Nangong family, but also wanting to seize Ye Yunshang during the chaos to uncover the secret of the treasure.

He had known since childhood that his birth was low, and that hard work was the only way to avoid being looked down on. He worked and studied harder than anyone, and to climb higher he even learned to bow and flatter, until at last he won the clan elders' favor and was recommended to the main branch in Jiangling. He thought this meant smooth sailing ahead, but instead the Nangong Family Head assigned him as study companion to the Second Young Lord. Was this turn of events anything less than a bolt from the blue? The Second Young Lord's birth mother didn't even count as a concubine — bluntly put, he was nothing but a bastard. What future could there be in following him? A promotion in name, a demotion in truth — no wonder he came to resent the Nangong Family. Lost beyond measure, all he could do was pray to gods and buddhas; he believed a rumor and went to the Apricot Blossom Forest, and though no divine answer came, he happened to meet a noble young lord from Dali touring the Central Plains. That Young Lord Duan was not only the Diancang Sect's Clear Smoke Swordsman, but also a clan relative of the Duan family of Dali — his standing was exalted, far beyond anything a Jianghu family could match. Nangong Ji saw it clearly at once: there was no place for him to make his mark in the Central Plains, so why not carve out a new path in another country? At once the thought of switching allegiance took root in him. This scheme with the bandits, raiding the Tang Clan by night under the Nangong name, was his letter of allegiance.

When you went out to take a leak and came back, Nangong Ji suddenly transformed into a different person, his eyes sparkling, his smile warm and inviting, utterly loyal as if brainwashed, constantly flattering the Second Senior Brother and patting his chest, vowing to speak without reservation.

You spouted a wild story, claiming you'd hand Nangong Ji over to a Tang Clan creditor with a taste for pretty men, to sell his body for profit. The claim was truly horrifying, and it left Nangong Ji stunned — not only trampling his dignity, but making him too ashamed to ever speak of it afterward, left to swallow his tears alone. Of course, you were only bluffing, and Squire Lu isn't even into men, but Nangong Ji believed it: the price of holding out was more than he could bear.

You know Nangong Ji is a clever man, and to pry information from him you can't rely on ordinary methods. So you pretend to give up, talk around the matter, and let his guard down. Seeing you, an outer-surname disciple, go on and on about the future, and that you don't lose heart even when he mocks you, he can't help but reconsider you. Wasn't he too born to a humble station, ambitiously hoping to rise above it, only to fall short at the last step and give up on himself? The thought sends him into a cold sweat: if he lets his pride win out and is truly killed by the Tang Clan in a single stroke, Nangong Ji will forever remain an unknown nobody, a Nangong Family Servant no one even remembers by name. He then realizes your words were all patient guidance meant to open his eyes; his resentment toward you dissolves, replaced by gratitude, and he confesses of his own accord.
It's unavoidable; in the end, we'll still have to ask the Second Senior Brother to personally step in.
Seeing his shameless act, you were so furious there was nowhere to vent it, wishing you could just stab this scoundrel to death.
You take a deep breath, there's nothing more to say. At least you've tried to advise, and you can be guilt‑free. As for whether he lives or dies, it's none of your business anymore.

The Nangong Family Teachings are rooted in Daoism, emphasizing inner cultivation and the preservation of the mind as their core. No matter what you say, good or bad, you've exhausted all your words, and he remains deaf to it, with not a single word reaching his heart.

During your first interrogation, you thought hitting hard enough would pry any mouth open. You held nothing back and ended up beating Nangong Ji to death. Fortunately the elixir room was right above the cellar, and the Second Senior Brother heard the noise and rushed down in time to save him. Having survived a brush with death, Nangong Ji finally believed the Tang Clan's reputation was no exaggeration — once you turn ruthless you disregard even kinship, truly willing to ignore old ties and cut a man down without mercy. No longer daring to talk tough, he confessed the truth honestly.

He knows how to bluff, and you are just as skilled at it. Your dagger keeps feinting at his vital points, as if to stab him dead and then find a way to revive him. Nangong Ji is no wooden post — he can't just let you stab him. Seeing you strike at his vital points again and again without warning, he finally believes the Tang Clan's reputation is well-earned: once you turn ruthless, you disregard even kinship, truly willing to ignore old family ties and cut him down without mercy. No longer daring to talk tough, he confesses everything honestly.

Interrogation seems simple, but mere torture is ineffective. There's a method to it: one must be ruthless, unafraid of bloodshed, and skilled in knowing when to apply pressure, using both soft and hard methods. Only an iron‑hearted person can do it. In the end, there's no one but Second Senior Brother himself to handle this. After all, no one else is as cold‑blooded and ruthless as he is.

You have a good temper, are not easily provoked, and are meticulous in your work, but your intentions are not upright. A hundred kinds of harsh tortures and poisonous schemes brew in your mind; after filtering out those that would result in death or disability, the remaining methods are few.
You have a good temper, are not easily provoked, are meticulous in your work, and have upright intentions. Upon seeing you volunteer to take on the task, your Senior Brothers said no more.

You have a good temper, are not easily provoked, and are meticulous in your work. However, as a Tang Clan disciple, you are far too soft‑hearted and kind. This time, when you volunteered, the Senior Brothers were astonished. Seeing you had made up your mind, they said no more.
If the Second Senior Brother had arrived just a moment later, Nangong Ji would have been handed over to you.

You have decent cultivation, can tolerate your temper, and aren't afraid of being provoked, but you don't think things through when you act. You just remember to torture, completely forgetting to ask. Once someone is handed over to you, you don't say a word and start beating them immediately, with no sense of restraint in your actions.

You volunteered. Now, as for you—your composure's decent enough, and you can hold your temper well enough, but you act without thinking, and you're a bit vicious to boot. From the start you never meant to get anything out of him, you just wanted to hit someone. The moment Senior Brother's back was turned, you started swinging without a word, holding nothing back.

You volunteered, thinking even if you couldn't get answers out of him, you could at least rough him up a little. But your motives were seen through at once, so no one dared hand the prisoner over to you—with that explosive temper of yours, a few harsh words might set you off, and there was no telling what mess you'd make.
There was nothing for it—Second Senior Brother would have to handle it himself.

Nangong Ji calculated that the Tang Clan would not go so far as to kill him due to their ties with the three great families. After being captured, he relied on his superb internal skills to withstand the torture, refusing to reveal the mastermind behind it all. His fellow disciples took turns striking him, causing their wrists to ache, but Nangong Ji only felt pain without injury, still wearing a grin on his face. Everyone was frustrated, unable to truly apply the ruthless tortures of the Tang Clan on him, which left them with a headache.

This night finally passed, and the next day you had breakfast before setting off, finally arriving home. You reported what happened on your journey to the Sect Leader. The Sect Leader stroked his beard as he listened, offering no comment, but still said: 'The Ye siblings may stay or leave as they please, but so long as she remains in the Tang Clan for even a single day, no one under heaven may touch a hair on her. Even if the Emperor of Dali himself comes in person, this still holds.'

A tangle of worries left you unable to sleep either way tonight, so you decided to go out and wander. The night market was brightly lit, but you seemed afraid of the light, deliberately avoiding it, walking into the dark alley and into the old, desolate temple. A footstep followed behind, neither far nor near, short and tense. Though this Miss may act wild and lawless, she's inherited her family's loyalty and deep sense of emotion. Having called you brother, how could she bear to see you alone disappearing into the night, vanishing without a trace? Whether she was afraid or forced herself to follow closely, she did so step by step. Back then, when you left in anger, she couldn't find you, but this time, she could make amends. This dark, desolate place isn't where she belongs, nor is it where you belong. She will take responsibility for bringing you home.

Close your eyes, and the faces of your fellow disciples from the same sect, their expressions turning cold in their final moments, immediately appear in your mind. Even if they were traitors who murdered their own brothers‑in‑arms, it remains a harsh thing to do. Everyone wants to live better; haven't you ever tried running away from home?
Washed away the residual bloodstains and dust, but couldn't wash away the sensation of killing a fellow disciple with one's own hands.

After traveling a few more miles, we arrived at the foot of Mount Meishan. Although we walked slowly, we were all physically and mentally exhausted. As the sun set in the west, it was already too late to begin ascending the mountain, so we had no choice but to stay at an inn in the town for the night.

You worked together to defeat the traitors, deliberately sparing their lives, waiting for the Second Senior Brother's judgment. Yet those people had no intention of living. Four of them went off together, leaving only two to return. You remained silent, and the rest of them also kept quiet without asking any questions. The journey was eerily silent, broken only by the clattering of horse hooves.

They returned home first and fell silent, leaving you hanging with a sinking heart. The chances of them meeting misfortune on the road made their survival seem unlikely. Yet here they are, reunited, bringing joy beyond measure. Despite their happiness, they wore unusual expressions, hesitating to speak as they pulled you and your senior brother aside to whisper. It turned out that they had harbored resentment towards the Tang Clan for a long time. Originally, believing that joining the Tang Clan would allow them to dominate both the white and black societies, they thought it would be a matter of prestige and power. However, their sect leader proved to be a sickly tiger; the Eldest Senior Brother was careless and lazy; the second senior brother was harsh and mean; the third senior brother was weak and easily bullied; and the fourth senior brother was greedy for money. Observing the vicissitudes in Jianghu, heroes from all over gathered in Jiangling, opposing the Mud Cult's Beast Path; even the Nangong Family could not stay whole and suffered heavy casualties, and the Six Sects grew fearful for their own safety. How could the Tang Clan, with its dwindling members, look out for itself? It could barely protect itself, yet their sect leader, intent on his own path, insisted on sheltering the Ye siblings, that hot-potato pair. If it were true that they had coveted treasure, they might indeed deserve their condemnation, but in reality, they gained nothing and instead became the target of public hatred wherever they went. They volunteered to go to Qingcheng this time with the intention of never returning to the Tang Clan. Moreover, Duan Zhixiu offered them generous rewards with one condition: do not return to the Tang Clan. This suited their plan perfectly. Therefore, your long wait for news was justified. Accepting bribes from an enemy faction and shaming one's own sect is a grave taboo in the Wulin; such a traitor is reviled by all and ought by rights to flee far away. But after spending the money for a few days, they inexplicably returned home to Mianshan, wandering the area, seeing you all safely return with mixed feelings. Their hearts were both relieved and fearful that you might seek retribution later, reporting them to the Chief Executioner for punishment. They exchanged glances and decided to buy your silence as co-conspirators, sharing the guilt and thus avoiding severe consequences. Their heartfelt words moved you and your senior brother as well. Who among us does not dream of being a great hero in Jianghu? Yet none of us are cut out for it. We all know deep down. To end up just being known as 'a Tang Clan disciple' without any name or recognition-what hope is there left in life? But if we could take Ye Yunshang, our lives would be secure and prosperous forever. Self-interest is a universal trait; their choice may not be moral but it makes sense. Without principles, at least they have money! We are all co-conspirators, none of us better than the others, able to live together as fellow disciples did, eating, drinking, sharing the outhouse, and laughing loudly as before. But that future will never come true. The pride of Tang Clan is not reserved for those in high positions alone. Being called a 'Tang Clan disciple,' what does it matter? As descendants of the Tang Family, you all carry your heads high with pride.

After repelling the angry forest animals, the helpers arrived late. You looked closely and couldn't help but be overjoyed: weren't these the brothers who had gone home to seek help but had subsequently gone missing?

The nun, who styled herself as the Wood Immortal Maiden, had her own school of martial arts, her internal skills formidable, and was adept at listening to sounds to determine positions. She had studied the hidden weapons of various masters and had expected to easily capture you, a junior disciple, but unexpectedly, you had reinforcements arriving. You all looked closely and couldn't help but rejoice greatly: weren't they the brothers and sisters who had gone home to fetch reinforcements but had subsequently gone missing? They immediately regained their composure and fought with all their might. The Wood Immortal Maiden feared that continuing the fight would make it impossible for her to escape unscathed, so after asking their names, she intended to use her Qinggong to flee. Fortunately, Tang Fang immediately spoke out and called Yunshang to explain, thus resolving the misunderstanding. The Wood Immortal Maiden knew she was at fault, but she considered herself a senior master and couldn't bring herself to apologize or make amends. Seizing the moment when you relaxed your guard and opened your mouth to speak, she suddenly threw a pill into your mouth, her intent clear: since you had swallowed her offering, you must not speak ill of her outside, damaging her reputation.

That Daoist nun, who called herself the Wood Immortal Maiden, had developed her own unique martial arts style. Her internal skill was formidable, and she was particularly skilled at identifying an opponent's position through sound. She had also studied various renowned hidden weapons, confident that she could easily subdue a young opponent. However, she was taken aback when you remained silent until suddenly launching a fierce attack, like a raging fire, catching her off guard. She swept her fly whisk, using a circular force to break off your attack, then grumpily leapt back several feet. Though she had not gained the upper hand today, she would not forget your name. She vowed to summon her fellow disciples and challenge you again, determined to defeat this old demon who had dared to play weak like a pig only to strike like a tiger. Your swift routing of the Wood Immortal Maiden stunned your Senior Brother and left even the Tang Clan disciples who had hurriedly arrived to support you in stunned silence. You looked closely and couldn't help but marvel: weren't these the very Senior Brothers who had previously returned home to seek help but had subsequently gone missing along the way?

The bandits were fierce and menacing, with a group of thieves trailing behind them, clearly figures from the greenwood. Normally, the Tang Clan's reputation for cruelty is well known, feared by both the righteous and the wicked. Ordinary greenwood heroes would avoid encountering Tang Clan disciples at all costs. However, these mountain bandits have a deep connection to your Tang Clan; they are victims who have suffered repeated poisoning at the hands of your Eldest Senior Brother. Their hatred for the Tang Clan can only be repaid with blood. The disparity between us is too great. You and your senior brother, having tried bluffing without success, were about to flee when a savior suddenly appeared from the sky. Upon closer inspection, you couldn't help but rejoice: weren't these the brothers who had earlier returned home to seek reinforcements but had subsequently gone missing? Although still outnumbered, your minds were clouded with emotion, and even a four-on-twelve battle felt evenly matched. First, there was indeed a significant gap in skill, and second, the bandits, having been terrorized by the Eldest Senior Brother, had no desire to fight. After a brief skirmish, realizing they couldn't win, the leader shouted and fled at full speed, vanishing in an instant.

That parrot is raised by the mountain bandits, and having been influenced by them, it has learned nothing but foul language. Accustomed to the malice and harm from humans, it harbors a deep hatred for them, vowing to never coexist under the same sky as you two‑legged beasts. When it sees passersby, it commands the wild boars to charge, truly killing without mercy; you could be next!
The one who blocks the way is not a person, but a parrot that can speak human language, driving a wild boar!

The one blocking the path is not a person, but a strange bird that can speak and rides a wild boar! You are ignorant and unlearned, not knowing what a 'parrot' is, thinking you've encountered a demon, frightened to the point of pale faces.

That nun had extraordinarily keen ears and nose, able to place people by scent alone. She caught the smell of metal and medicine on you, and since you'd been active in the Shu region, she had no doubt you were Tang Clan disciples. But amid the group of Tang Clan disciples, there was a faint trace of a young woman's rouge, oddly out of place. A thought flickered, and it struck her: you thugs must have kidnapped some innocent woman! Having stumbled onto such wickedness, she certainly wouldn't stand by.
You'd never met her before, and the moment she opened her mouth she came on strong, leaving you thoroughly displeased — so naturally, you didn't bother with any show of deference either.
You dared not be remiss, so you hurriedly bowed with clasped hands, but your politeness didn't earn a favorable response.
The visitor was a blind Daoist nun with an ethereal demeanor, around thirty or forty years old, exuding the grace of a reclusive sage.

The trail wound and dipped, and Ye Yunshang, sick and frail, truly couldn't bear it, so the carriage kept starting and stopping along the way. Everyone was anxious but held their tongues, knowing this trail was nothing like the wide, smooth official road — bandits and wild beasts lurked here, and it was truly dangerous. Sure enough, no sooner had they said so than someone sprang out to block their path.
You two chatted and laughed like siblings until Ye Yunshang grew truly drowsy, yawning again and again, and only then did you usher her onto the carriage to sleep.
No need to say it — deep down, you're utterly smitten with this lively, mischievous little sister. Not even a treasure beyond price could match her radiant smile.

You're not truly indifferent to where the treasure is; if anything, you're quite curious. But good as the treasure is, it's not yours to covet. The Tang Clan's rules are strict, and the Chief Executioner shows no mercy. Under the Sect Leader's decree, who dares speak out of turn? Fourth Senior Brother is a living example!

You're not really uninterested in where the treasure is — a gentleman loves wealth, but only wealth gained by proper means. Even if General Yue truly left a treasure behind, it would be righteous wealth for saving the nation. Besides, stepping in for justice is a chivalrous hero's nature; even if you had no tie at all to the Ye siblings, you still wouldn't regret lending them a hand.

Speaking of King Yue's Treasure, Ye Yunshang chose her words carefully, her tone laced with mockery, though deep unease lingered underneath. Since their time together, her dependence on you had only grown, and she feared that one day you might turn out like Duan Zhixiu — mercenary, and unrecognizable.

At midnight, Yunshang tossed and turned, unable to sleep, an endless loneliness sweeping over her. Not wanting to wake Tang Fang, she rolled up the curtain and saw you sitting alone by the fire. On a whim, she came out under the moonlight to sit beside you and talk.

Those who speak ill of you, you usually just laugh off; when it's the Tang Clan being discussed, so long as it's nothing serious, you merely frown. But when someone slanders Ye Yunshang to your face, how could you bear it? However well you've cultivated your temper, you still have some fire in you — if not for the bigger picture, you'd want nothing more than to tear the rumormongers' mouths apart and grind their bones to ash.

Regrettably, you cannot step forward to argue; you know well that you cannot make a case, and yet you would only cause further complications, exposing your whereabouts. You can only endure humiliation, suppress your anger, and remain silent.

You can't argue, yet staying silent leaves you bitter inside; you can't very well kill everyone who says it. You could do it, but your party hasn't gotten clear of danger yet, so it's not wise to stir up more trouble, and you can only swallow your anger.

She went off to gather herbs to ease Ye Yunshang's nausea, leaving Ye Yunshang in your care. Unable to resist her pleading, you reluctantly took her for a walk to a tea house up ahead, only to overhear the customers inside gossiping about the Ye family. The rumormonger swore up and down, insisting they'd seen it with their own eyes, claiming the map to King Yue's Treasure was hidden on Ye Yunshang's bare back. Yet even Ye Yunshang herself couldn't make it out — how absurd.

They dared not linger, urging the horses onward, everyone's hearts uneasy, fearing Duan Zhixiu might realize at any moment and come chasing after them on horseback. The trail was rough and uneven, nothing like a broad, smooth road, so the ride was bumpy the whole way. Tang Fang stayed on edge, watching Ye Yunshang's pale face, worried both that she couldn't endure the jolting and that she might lose control and vomit right on her. She hurriedly called for the horses to stop so Ye Yunshang could get out and get some air.

You strode along briskly wrapped in a cloak, only throwing it off after leaving Qingcheng Mountain town, then used your qinggong to dash off at full speed, meeting up with Ye Yunshang and the others out on the open plain.

Zhao Kui originally found your appearance quite pleasing and had considered teaching you a few moves. He even wanted to take you to the Hell Path in the underworld to serve as a ghost soldier. However, someone kept causing disturbances, making him even more irritable, leaving no time for him to pay attention. Zou Bo helped unblock your meridians and urged you to leave quickly.

You had assumed he'd believed Duan Zhixiu's account and thought nothing of you. But to Shentu Long, believing someone has nothing to do with friendship or character; what matters to him is whether you have room to lie. You are nobody, with no burden you cannot bear to lose, so your words carry no weight — even if your lie were exposed, at most it would cost you your life, and what good would that do? You have nothing; your stake is just a worthless life. Duan Zhixiu's stake, though, is family and reputation, the life he has built up until now. Weighed against each other, which matters more needs no saying.

As soon as you reached the town, Shentu Long suddenly appeared, startling you. It turned out he had deliberately followed you out to see you off, presenting a book as a parting gift, and leaving you flattered and taken aback.

Duan Zhixiu watched coldly as you were escorted out of the temple, gloating over your misfortune, unaware that you'd been longing for a chance to slip away — Qingcheng's expulsion order suited you perfectly.

The Qingcheng crowd had long found you unpleasant, but out of respect for their elders, they'd had no excuse to get rid of you. Now, falsely invoking the Iron Crown Elder's order, they seized the moment — before the sect leader and the other elders could react — to expel you from Qingcheng.

The Qingcheng disciples fell silent. Their relationship with you wasn't bad, but since the words had indeed come from the Sect Leader's own mouth, they couldn't let him break his word and tarnish his reputation — so they had no choice but to wrong you.

Zhao Kui was notorious, but in that moment, where could anyone find someone willing to side with him? He knew his Senior Brother was deliberately making things difficult, so he chose to let it go and leave; after all, the debt of explanation he owed had already been made clear, and he had returned Qingcheng's treasure. It wasn't a perfect resolution, but it was enough to satisfy him. So he pressed the matter no further and left with a clear conscience, hoping that even if the Mud Cult and the righteous sects of the Central Plains truly came to a point where they could not coexist under the same sky, it would never come to a life-and-death struggle between him and his Senior Brother. Iron Crown Daoist tried several times to put on airs, only to be rebuffed each time, and retreated sullenly into the crowd, muttering to himself, seething with resentment. Turning around, he saw the disciples all looking at him with what seemed like contempt, and his anger flared at once. Since he commanded no respect and could not discipline the eleventh-generation disciples, he fixed his sights on you instead, an innocent bystander.
