He used the excuse the sect leader had just given to fend off Zhao Kui, turning it against you instead, insisting that only Qingcheng disciples had the right to take part in the Jiangyu Rite and receive the Patriarch's blessing.

Unexpectedly, he spoke again, not to command Qingcheng disciples to apprehend Zhao Kui, but to take responsibility for Zhao's abrupt actions, declaring that the other party's visit was an invitation for discussion. This was meant to convey his intent not to cause trouble, but to let Zhao Kui leave the mountain. The Mud Cult's Six Paths each operated independently; how much less so would the distinction between good and evil be a chasm as vast as heaven and earth. Zhao's words had no expectation of his Senior Brother's understanding, yet he had to say them. Though his appearance was rough, he was shrewd beneath his rough exterior, skilled in both arts and letters. He had not rashly climbed the mountain on mere bloodlust, but had personally journeyed to the Western Regions to retrieve the Qingcheng sect's long-lost sacred relic, the Celestial Master's Token, as his trump card. Should the Qingcheng sect refuse to let him go, he would produce the Token, threatening to destroy it, thereby making the sect hesitate to act. Unbeknownst to him, over a dozen years had passed, and Zou Bo remained as straightforward as ever, prompting a faint smile. This relic was now of no use to him, merely an old piece of wood, yet it held great significance for Qingcheng. Before departing, he decided to return it intact to Zou Bo, slipping it secretly into his hand, a final contribution to Qingcheng. Sect Leader Zou broke precedent, allowing Zhao to serve as a Qingcheng disciple for one more day, personally going to the Patriarch's hall to apologize. After that day, their grudge would be settled. Yet he had to follow the rules: Sect Leader Zou issued a decree, ordering the Qingcheng elders to send representatives to compete for the Flower Cannon, with the winner first ascending the Laojun Pavilion to light an incense stick. Otherwise, he would have to endure the sect's rituals for three days before visiting the mountain as a pilgrim.

Zou Bo remained silent for a long time, deeply moved. The residual resentment that had lingered for years gradually eased. However, as the leader of the sect, he upheld the Patriarch's teachings and must preserve the Qingcheng lineage. The rise and fall of the sect depended on his every word and deed, so he dared not speak recklessly.

But when Zhao Kui questioned you directly, you still didn't dare openly accuse him, afraid he'd fly into a rage and strike you dead with one palm. He heard your hesitant, wishy-washy answers — always 'think' this or 'seem' that — your eyes darting everywhere, and couldn't help but chuckle to himself. Seeing how frightened you truly were, he had no wish to trouble a junior like you. He unsealed your blocked acupoints, picked you up, and tossed you into the crowd, giving you back your freedom.

You were willing to risk being struck dead just to openly denounce his misdeeds. Zhao Kui, far from angry, only chuckled: anyone could be killed, and so could he. Was he, Zhao Kui, not himself a reckless, lawless madman? If you had the nerve, go ahead and kill him — of course he wouldn't just sit and wait to die either. Should it come to that and you die while he lives, that death would be entirely of your own making.

You can't possibly agree with this. People's hearts differ, customs vary, and even within the same nation, moral teachings and etiquette evolve with the times. If everyone had their own concept of justice, what chaos would the world descend into?

You spoke with seriousness and boldness, drawing much discussion. Yet, after joining the Tang Clan for many years, your martial arts may not have improved, but your worldliness has increasingly taken on the Tang Clan's style. You simply scratch your ears and pretend you didn't hear it.
You wanted to take it back, but by then it was too late.
You were asked, and you answered immediately. Just the single word yes caused the crowd to gasp in shock: you openly endorsed the Demon Cult's heretical doctrines, you truly have the nerve.

Though you thought this, you never dared say so openly. Zhao Kui gave a light snort, instantly losing interest in you, grabbed you by the collar, and flung you into the crowd, giving you back your freedom.

One can't help but wonder: If the Hell Path's actions are all righteous deeds, and the ones they kill are all lawbreakers, what crime could they possibly have committed? When one sees injustice, punishing the wicked and eliminating evil is the way of the chivalrous hero. Then why has the underworld become criminals? This shakes the deeply rooted notion of good and evil within your heart.
You realize that you're relying on the Tang Clan as your backing, disregarding the law, with so many immoral deeds that they can't be written down, and can't help but tremble in fear.
You're on‑site, your heart racing

Only when neither can harm the other can they speak calmly. Zou Bo asked Zhao Kui, who stood resolute and unafraid, speaking with confidence. He hates evil as an enemy, despises the injustice in the world, and believes that the idea of karma is a mere superstition. Those who believe in it remain steadfast, while those without faith act recklessly. The wicked who evade the law have countless ways to shirk responsibility; the authorities cannot reach them. Should we wait for heaven to take them, relying on the fleeting retribution of the afterlife? No. What the heavens neglect, he will take charge of; what the authorities fail to act upon, he will handle. He is willing to burn himself, to become hellfire, to purify the world of all impurities. From afar, it is a lamp guiding the way for future generations; up close, it is fire instilling fear in the wicked. He does not seek immortality beyond the three realms, only to leave the world pure at the end. This is the very Path walked by the Mud Cult's Hell Path followers! Each word is resolute, justice is evident. Such courage and spirit, how can it be as base as Jianghu rumors?

The final blow: both men sheathed their swords and struck with their palms. Zou Bo employed Qingcheng's secret technique, Cantong Secret Covenant, while Zhao Kui unleashed his own creation, Great Scorching Heat Divine Skill, a fusion of Western Regions martial arts. The opposing yin and yang Internal Forces collided, shaking the very air and forming a whirlwind on the spot. You were inexplicably caught between their four palms, and though it lasted only an instant, you were dragged along, spun helplessly out of control, Lifeforce roiling through your chest and abdomen, yet you came out unharmed. That you survived even this left not only the onlookers stunned, but even you found it illogical.

For the final blow, both men sheathed their swords and struck with their palms. Zou Bo employed Qingcheng's secret technique, Cantong Secret Covenant, while Zhao Kui unleashed his self-created Great Scorching Heat Divine Skill, a fusion of Western Regions martial arts. The collision of yin and yang Internal Forces shook the air, forming a whirlwind on the spot. The crowd gasped in awe. Internal skills refined to this extent could summon wind and clouds, bordering on divine power.

You're sandwiched between two people, watching them prepare to channel their inner energy and unleash their ultimate move, which scares you so much that your hairs stand on end. Rather than struggling, you choose to close your eyes and accept your fate.

Unfortunately, your Internal Skill is far too weak. An internal-arts master like Zhao Kui could, with a casual flick of the finger, leave you standing there to starve to death, and no matter how hard you struggled, it would do you no good.

Two top martial artists dueling‑ask who dares to intervene? Moreover, Zhao Kui and Zou Bo were completely absorbed in each other, never expecting you to suddenly move, choosing to come right into their strike. You were just asking for it by being caught between the two mighty currents of Yin and Yang Internal Force, spinning helplessly, twisting into a helix, and exploding into pieces!
Even though Shentu Long had already called out a warning, you just had to move anyway.

You're sandwiched between the two of them, and seeing that they were about to channel their energy and unleash their ultimate moves, you're terrified enough that every hair on your body stands on end. Would you rather sit and wait for death? At once you channel your Internal Force, straining to break through your sealed acupoints.

The two of them simultaneously drew their swords and raised their hands. As fellow disciples, they had both mastered both sword and palm techniques. Each sword was as heavy as the next, each palm strike as fierce as the next. The palm wind howled, and their Internal Force collided with a resounding crash.
You nearly fainted from fright.
You were knocked out cold by the scare, then woke up again from another scare. If it weren't for you having gone to the bathroom in the morning, you'd have a bad reputation.

The two of them drew their swords and palms without prior agreement. In their past years as fellow students, both were masters of palm and sword techniques. Each sword was as heavy as the next, each palm as fierce as the next. The palm wind howled past your face, Internal Force collided and burst at your ears, and you seemed to see the figure of Grandma at the gates of Hell flickering in and out.

The two emerged from the same sect and met at the familiar old place, with the same people. Thirty years prior, they had walked side by side. Time flew, and one became the Sect Leader of Qingcheng, while the other rose to be the Dharma King of the Demon Cult. They looked at each other in silence, only for a chill to fill the air.
Zou Bo and Zhao Kui stood facing each other.
Zou Bo and Zhao Kui stand facing each other, with you in between.

The captured Qingcheng disciple escaped death, scrambling to safety. You weren't so lucky‑you were struck with an Acupoint Strike again while rolling and immobilized on the spot. Well, who told you not to take a side? You sound decently upright, and you're a Tang Clan disciple‑nobody is more suited to sit in as an observer.
You and the captured Qingcheng Disciple survived against all odds, scrambling and crawling away.
Everyone thought that by holding hostages in his hands, he meant to use them as leverage, but instead he simply, decisively let go and released them.

With the contenders settled and about to decide the order of the matches, a tiger's roar suddenly echoed through the mountains and forest. The faces of everyone present changed at once; for among the last ten generations of Qingcheng elders gathered here, who else would call Zou Bo 'Senior Brother' except Zhao Kui, the traitor who had long ago broken from Qingcheng and fallen into demonic ways? Zou Bo froze, then flew into a rage, nearly rushing out sword in hand, but Elders Buping and Huaisu talked him down, and he regained his composure, dispatching men to scout the enemy and hold the ground at Qingcheng's library. Clearing his throat, he too gathered his true qi and answered with the Tiger's Roar Skill, his voice carrying his Internal Force far into the distance, matching the newcomer's presence without yielding an inch. At the Sect Leader's invitation, Zhao Kui came up the mountain at an unhurried pace, Ox‑Head and Horse‑Face, and the hell soldiers following behind him, a person gripped in each hand‑on his left the Qingcheng disciple on greeting duty, and on his right, you. Everyone there shuddered at the sight of his crimson robe, his bristling beard, and his overwhelming, commanding presence. Only then did they realize that the legendary Dharma King of the Hell Path looked just like this‑the title 'Judge' suited him perfectly.
The people he has truly taught are few and far between, and he has not a single follower. Even if he truly wished to compete, there would be no one to send.

The few people he has actually taught are counted on one's fingers, and you are one of them. Your Internal Skill is entirely based on medicinal diets, with a weak foundation, and your techniques are mixed and not refined. However, you have a strong physique from working hard, are willing to endure hardship, and progress rapidly with slight guidance. You don't get stuck in dead ends, learning anything given to you, making teaching you particularly rewarding. Even Shentu Long has changed his opinion. As an elder, he had considered sending you to the arena, but since your experience is still insufficient, you tend to lose more than win, and would be a mere stepping stone for others. Thinking about it, he decided to call it off.

Over there, Qingcheng Sect Leader Zou Bo and several elders were still discussing the lineup for the second half of the competition. Elders Buping and Huaisu each recommended their own favored disciples, determined to claim this year's flower cannon crown. Although the Iron Crown Daoist held the esteemed rank of elder, he was mediocre and lacked martial prowess, unable to train capable disciples. No one wished to follow him, and he had sat idly in his post for decades. Now, in his old age, he suddenly found joy in taking Duan Zhixiu as his disciple. Duan Zhixiu was not only a royal relative of the Dali Duan clan but also a hero who had already made a name for himself in the Jianghu. Taking him as a disciple was a great bargain; he didn't need to spend effort training him, and the master's status would rise on the disciple's fame‑why wouldn't he do it! He had yet to pick an auspicious day to formally take him as a disciple, but he was already eager to boast about it. As for Shentu Long, though his martial arts were high, he was of few desires and never formed cliques, and being young, among the eleventh generation of disciples few truly respected him as a master; they called him Martial Uncle to his face, but in their hearts regarded him only as a peer.

Unbeknownst to them, after dealing with the ghost soldiers, Ox‑Head and Horse‑Face still emerged. After fending off Ox‑Head and Horse‑Face, even the renowned judge Zhao Kui appeared. You had fought several battles, your strength exhausted, with no proper resistance left. You were seized by the hand, scorching Internal Force poured into your back's vital points, rendering you motionless on the spot, reduced to a hostage, your life and death determined by the other's breath.

Who would have thought that after subduing the ghost soldiers, there would also be Ox‑Head and Horse‑Face? Though hard‑pressed in battle, you remained unbowed and unyielding until death. Your spirit moved not only the person you were protecting, but even the envoys Ox‑Head and Horse‑Face were touched, unwilling to harm you. Yet bound by duty, they could not be held back by you, and after a moment's hesitation pressed on. At this time, an imperial command resounded from the heavens above, ordering all yin soldiers and ghost soldiers to withdraw. The voice was loud and stern, using the same Tiger's Roar technique. You thought it might be an elder from Qingcheng coming to your aid, but instead a figure stepped forward in a crimson official robe, wearing a black silk hat, carrying a long sword on his back, and a folding fan tucked at his waist‑a true likeness of Zhong Kui from the paintings. Your hackles rose at this person's audacious attire; in this age there could be no one else but the Demon Cult's Dharma King or the Judge of the Underworld! Without even putting up a proper fight, you were seized and had searing Internal Force poured into your vital points. You were rendered immobile on the spot and became hostages, your lives hanging by a thread at another's mercy.

Who would have thought that after dealing with the ghost soldiers and Ox-Head and Horse-Face, you couldn't match them in open combat but resorted to underhanded tactics, feigning defeat and escaping by hiding. You circled back and gave them a good whack from behind, though your actions were despicable, you had no sense of shame doing such things. This instantly reversed the situation. Little did you know that while you were focused on your opponents, another predator was waiting in the wings‑immediately after creating new karma, you received its swift retribution. The Dharma King of the Mud Cult suddenly appeared behind you. With a massive hand, he lifted you up like a chicken, rendering you immobile as his internal force consumed you. Your entire body felt like it was on fire, with life and death hanging in the balance solely based on his breathing.
The Qingcheng disciples, upon seeing reinforcements, were overjoyed beyond measure, took deep breaths to recover their stance, and fought together with you.

You may indeed be eager to escape, but your chivalrous nature compels you to save a life. Moreover, Qingcheng has saved your life, making it a duty you cannot refuse. Fire a Throwing Dart and appear to rescue them.

You may be morally corrupt, but you're not entirely heartless or unrighteous. Owing someone a favor yet refusing to help when they're in danger, your heart can't help but have a knot. So, you resolve to act decisively, fire a throwing dart, and step forward to save the person.
You have no choice but to bear a reputation for injustice, swallowing your conscience to take the detour instead.
Moreover, you have a wicked heart; even if you could help, you wouldn't want to. As for favors, once the benefactor is dead, isn't it unnecessary to repay them? You've made a profit.
You can't even save yourself; how can you have the time or inclination to care about others' lives?
Rather than worrying about Duan Zhixiu, you'd be better off retreating and joining Yunshang. He is about to appear, so if you run away in front of him now, he won't be able to chase you.
You've locked eyes with him and couldn't help but laugh. If he likes to glare, let him glare. Even if he glares fiercely, it's his own eyesight he's wasting. You won't lose any meat because of it.

You're narrow-minded and vengeful, always settling every score. He glared at you, and you were fuming with anger. If it weren't for the rules prohibiting it and being stopped by others, you'd have charged forward to fight him to the death.

The second half is the main event, determining who will win this year's fireworks prize. Duan Zhixiu boasts of his genius, exuding a relaxed and carefree attitude. When he looks at you, his eyes betray mockery, and his face shows contempt.
Even with full effort, they couldn't defeat the opponent. Tingfengzi and you developed mutual understanding and affection, bowing in surrender and earning thunderous applause.

No matter how hard he tried, he couldn't win against you. Daoist Huaisu noticed that he was growing increasingly irritable, and continuing to fight would likely bring more losses than victories, so he called a stop. Tingfengzi, still unwilling to accept this, muttered a reluctant 'please,' and left in frustration.

He grew even more anxious — having taken Duan Zhixiu's bribe, he couldn't afford to let you get away now, or his patron might blame him for botching the job. He was about to unleash his ultimate move when Daoist Huaisu called a halt, and he withdrew, reluctant and sullen.

Tingfengzi was a new talent of Qingcheng, while you were merely an outsider disciple of the Tang Clan. He was confident he could win, but you employed unconventional tactics, and the two were evenly matched. If not for Qingcheng's slow but adaptable techniques, you would have ambushed him several times.

You might not necessarily lose to him, and he might not necessarily win against you. But both of you held back and only used some impressive but ineffective techniques, fighting evenly matched until each side withdrew, exchanging smiles. In this way, no one lost face. Daoist Huaisu, watching from the sidelines, also stroked his beard with a smile, thinking the young man was teachable. You didn't compete for victory or defeat, yet you earned the admiration of Qingcheng.

Tingfengzi, though merely a new rising star of Qingcheng, was a respected figure among the 11th generation disciples. To lose to you, a visiting disciple, was something he could not accept, regardless of his opinion of you. He was about to argue, but his master silenced him with a stern reprimand and sent him off the arena. You gained face, yet it only deepened Huaisu's resentment toward you.

He had intended to fight fair and square, call it a day, and exchange some compliments to wrap things up. But you, this scoundrel who doesn't play by the rules, took advantage of his courtesy and went all out against him, catching him off guard. When he finally tried to turn the tide, it was too late. How could he accept defeat like this? He still wanted to argue his case, but his master gave him a stern reprimand and sent him off the field.

As Tingfengzi exchanged blows, he used his body to block, several times attempting forbidden moves to injure you, but you had previously received guidance from Yunshang and were protected by your Leather Uniform, so you felt neither pain nor injury. Instead, you turned the situation around, catching the opponent off guard. Tingfengzi was defeated, furious and flustered, yelling and shouting, intent on making a big deal out of the hidden weapon incident. However, how sharp was Daoist Huaisu's eyesight? The trick his disciple had attempted could not have gone unnoticed. He had used the trick, lost, and still ranted. The trial revealed his character and cultivation. Now, publicly exposing Tingfengzi's underhanded tactics clearly showed Daoist Huaisu's deep disappointment in his disciple.

His original intention was to fight you fairly, to call a truce and exchange some compliments to wrap things up. But your martial arts skills are simply too poor, full of flaws. If he hesitates to act, the one who'll end up being scolded will be him. There's no choice but to let you accept your fate: the Tang Clan doesn't take you in for your own good—you're just that hopeless, so you're really better off doing menial work.

As Tingfengzi traded blows, he shielded his body to secretly work in a forbidden move, but Daoist Huaisu had far too sharp an eye -- how could such a trick get past him? With a sharp shout, he called the match to a halt. In front of the Qingcheng crowd, he didn't say anything just yet, but the glare he leveled at Tingfengzi was murderous enough to drain the color from his face. He was utterly baffled: why would you have come away unhurt, when he'd risked his master's wrath to unleash the full run of Qingcheng's forbidden strikes, his sword tip sweeping again and again across your wrist, your ribs, your knee, and you were still bouncing around lively as ever? Could it be you had some close-fitting treasure robe or soft armor hidden under your clothes? Soft armor, no -- but a treasure robe, he'd guessed right. Little did he know how tough cowhide could be; Ye Yunshang had gone to no small trouble sewing it into your clothes, and it really was a robe stitched with heartfelt effort.
But you measure a gentleman's heart with a small person's mind, having already formed a prejudice, always suspecting him of hiding a knife behind a smile.

Because your looks were so hard to ignore, Qingcheng disciples asked around about you more than a little. At first, hearing that you'd spent years in the Tang Clan without ever being formally accepted, they came away with a certain respect for the Tang Clan. Among them, the one who disliked you most was none other than Tingfengzi -- for no reason beyond an unconditional hatred of you. Only after spending time with you did he gradually change his mind, hating you on his own terms and then letting it go on his own terms too -- a shift in his thinking you naturally knew nothing about. Knowing you wanted to become a Qingcheng disciple, he meant to go easy on you and hold back, as a kind of apology.
Tingfengzi is itching to punch you, simply because your face looks like it's begging for it. He hates you unconditionally, and now that you've crossed paths, how could he go easy on you!

You are on high alert, convinced that Tingfengzi is a hired thug bought by Duan Zhixiu. However, Duan Zhixiu doesn't even consider you, too lazy to address it. Even the challenge letters sent by Ye Yunshang on your behalf were all read by others.

Tingfengzi was one of the experts Duan Zhixiu had bribed. They'd agreed beforehand: he couldn't kill you, but crippling you with a few underhanded moves was fine. If he couldn't manage that, he'd at least have to knock your teeth out and humiliate you in front of everyone.

Sect Leader Zou Bo sat in the center, with Elders Huaisu and Buping taking turns evaluating the eleventh generation disciples' martial arts skills, and they didn't forget about you either. Daoist Huaisu called you into the ring to spar with his favorite disciple, Tingfengzi.

No matter how much time passed after the match, you couldn't let it go, though win or loss meant nothing to you. Afterward you combed through every Daoist text you could find, still unable to work out the meaning of that hand seal, and it left you with a nagging grudge you couldn't shake.

No matter how much time passed after the match, you couldn't let it go, though win or loss meant nothing to you. Afterward you combed through every Daoist text you could find, still unable to work out the meaning of that hand seal, and it left you with a nagging grudge you couldn't shake.

Sect Leader Zou Bo sat in the center, with Elders Huaisu and Buping taking turns evaluating the eleventh generation disciples' martial arts skills, and they didn't forget you either. Daoist Buping called you into the ring to spar with his favorite disciple, Gao Hezi. Before the match, Gao Hezi formed a suspicious hand seal that sent chills down your spine. You steeled yourself and braced for the worst, certain Gao Hezi was a hired thug bought by Duan Zhixiu -- but you guessed wrong. He was innocent, had never taken a cent from Duan Zhixiu, and was simply an ordinary pervert. As for why: Duan Zhixiu never gave you a second thought to begin with, too lazy to bother with you. Even the challenge letters Ye Yunshang sent in your name, he handed off to others to read.

Sect Leader Zou Bo presided over the center, while Elders Huaisu and Buping took turns judging the eleventh generation disciples' martial arts. You alone they forgot -- well, whose fault was it that your name wasn't even on the roster? Duan Zhixiu didn't think much of you either, too lazy to bother with you. Even the challenge letters Ye Yunshang sent in your name, he handed off to others to read.

The names were called in order for the sparring matches, yet you were distracted, your mind drifting back several days to the inn, where you and Ye Yunshang had secretly plotted your escape. Though you dared not act rashly, you weren't sitting idle either. You'd already sent someone with a letter back to the Tang Clan for reinforcements, but of the senior brothers who'd come to Qingcheng with you, they kept vanishing one by one, and whether they'd run into trouble on the road, no word had come. You suspected Duan Zhixiu was behind it, and with your brothers' fates unknown, you grew more and more uneasy. So Ye Yunshang came up with a plan: she'd cruelly use you as bait, forging several challenge letters to Duan Zhixiu in your handwriting, packed with provocation, threatening that on the day of the Qingcheng assessment, you would carve him up with your sword in front of everyone and see if he still had the face to walk the Jianghu. Duan Zhixiu prized his reputation above all, and her constant goading had made him hate you to the bone, though he was frustrated that he couldn't have you quietly eliminated without damaging his name. As the Clear Smoke Swordsman, he held himself too high to fight you personally, but he could pay Qingcheng's finest to do it for him. Little did he know that while he was skilled at buying loyalty with money, Ye Yunshang knew a thing or two about turning people as well -- if Duan Zhixiu could bribe a hundred people with a hundred taels, she'd spend that same hundred taels bribing just one of them. First, use you as bait to draw Duan Zhixiu's attention: seeing you still in Qingcheng gearing up for a fight, he'd never expect you and your companions to leave that very day, and by the time word reached him, it would already be time for his own match. Even if he defied Qingcheng and sent men after you, Ye Yunshang's bought traitor would lead them astray, chasing you further and further off course. And in case he came to his senses, she'd sent someone ahead to light false trails along the road, keeping Duan Zhixiu forever thinking he was just one step from catching you, chasing you to the ends of the earth. Even if he truly held himself in check -- sending men to pursue first, then riding hard himself once the Qingcheng ceremony ended -- he'd still fall for the trick: before he could rejoin his own men, he'd catch up with your group first, and then be beaten senseless and hauled off to the Tang Clan. There was nothing wrong with the plan, except that it meant you had to suffer for it. After all, you were simply born to be a target -- there was no better one in the world, and when it came to taking the beating, who else could it be but you? Ye Yunshang never said so, but she felt more than a little guilty about it, and fearing you might really get hurt, she'd gone out of her way to sew cowhide into all the vital points of your uniform.
You're really bold. Except for the sect leader and Second Senior Brother, you dare to retort back at anyone who opens their mouth, not the least bit afraid, snapping back with a cutting remark.

You feel not the least bit of fear, and your tongue itches for a fight -- open your mouth and nothing but venom comes out. This bunch of Daoists is so particular about their cultivation that they stammer just trying to curse. How could they ever be a match for you at this? The fight hasn't even started, and you've nearly infuriated them to death with words alone.

You only realized the danger at this point. Your Tang Clan Senior Brothers and Sisters beat you without holding back, but they've never killed you before. However, these Qingcheng people are hard to predict.

You've stirred up plenty of trouble in Qingcheng, and people have long looked on you with disfavor -- they simply held their tempers and let it go rather than settle scores with you. Now, at last, the chance has come: under the pretext of the assessment's martial display, they can turn pretense into the real thing and resort to force. Everyone is itching for a fight, their stares more venomous than the poison in your pocket, fists looking ready to fly at your face any moment.

The Qingcheng Sect's Patriarch's Birthday is also the day, once a year, when the sect assesses its disciples' progress in their martial learning. Ten days in advance, they sent word to the local authorities and posted notices, sealing the mountain for three days and turning away pilgrims. Except for those with pressing duties they could not set aside, every Qingcheng disciple alive gathered together. That morning, once the bell rang, they lined up in the square before Everwind Temple for roll call and took their seats by master's lineage -- and you, in your confusion, found yourself placed at the very end of the line.

As she had anticipated, Duan Zhixiu couldn't bear provocation and, with a small trick, revealed the truth, confessing outright that he was the mastermind behind the bandit raid on the Tang Clan. Unfortunately, she hadn't reckoned on the hidden hand behind Duan, who turned her scheme into a scheme within a scheme within a scheme -- damaging Nangong's reputation, setting the Tang Clan against Diancang, and even now, so long after, using a borrowed knife to kill and cover his tracks. Though there's no ironclad proof to name the culprit, the Tang Clan has never needed proof for its crimes. As for who the hidden mastermind is, there's no rush to dig that up now. Once you all get out safely, go home and report to the sect leader, then double back, kidnap Duan Zhixiu, and have the Second Senior Brother put him to the question -- that'll tell you.
Early the next day, yesterday's brush with death seemed like a dream -- Ye Yunshang had fully recovered and looked radiant. She immediately gathered her followers for a secret meeting.

The next morning, yesterday's brush with death seemed like a dream -- Ye Yunshang was radiant and fully recovered, and she flung the door open and rushed out. She hadn't expected to find you dozing on the steps; caught off guard, she pitched forward onto your back, her front teeth clamping down hard on your shoulder, nearly tearing off a chunk of flesh. It turned out that, afraid she might grow thirsty or hungry in the night with no one around to help, you had kept watch outside her door all night. Seeing her much improved, her cheeks glowing rosy with health, you were overjoyed, and thought nothing more of your aching shoulder. Yunshang, seeing how haggard you looked, even uglier than usual, was deeply moved.

The poison in her body was a variant of Other Shore Immortal Fragrance. The poisoner, a master of toxic arts, anticipated that a Tang Clan disciple could neutralize it, so he laid a scheme within the scheme, swapping out one ingredient so the Other Shore Incense seemed the same but wasn't. Tang Fang, desperate to save her, failed to notice in time and used poison to fight poison, only making it more virulent. Unless the poisoner is caught and the formula wrung from him for a proper antidote, there is no way out of this — and no matter how deep Zou Bo's Internal Skill ran, it would eventually be exhausted, the poisoned blood would reach her Heart Meridian, and the girl's life would slip away. With no other option, Tang Fang took a desperate gamble, willing to harm herself to perform the forbidden Beiming Needle technique. She twisted and turned the needle to purge the poison, quickening the flow of Yunshang's Lifeforce, and turned her own body into Beiming itself, drawing Yang Qi deep within while driving the malicious Qi back out, taking on the calamity in her place — and just barely managed to keep her alive. Yet such selfless devotion still drew doubt, with people saying 'Don't exaggerate' and 'It can't be that serious.' Where in this world is the physician who pours out heart and soul for their patients that wouldn't be crushed to hear such words!

Tang Fang wiped the sweat from her brow and pushed open the door; you and Duan Zhixiu immediately closed in on either side of her, anxious for news of the patient. She had poured out everything she knew and was already drained, yet Duan Zhixiu kept interrupting with 'Don't exaggerate' and 'It can't be that serious,' gesturing away like he understood medicine. What physician who had devoted their heart and soul to studying the Yellow Emperor's Art could bear to hear such nonsense! Tang Fang exploded with fury on the spot, cursing him without a thought for her dignity. Duan Zhixiu froze, about to argue back, when a slap landed across his face, leaving him shocked, furious, and more than a little afraid. Once he knew Yunshang's life was no longer in danger, the weight lifted from his heart, and he fled for his life. You had never seen Tang Fang so furious, and couldn't help but marvel quietly. When you asked in detail about Yunshang's condition, Tang Fang explained it all.

So you lied to him, claiming you were a descendant of the Great Song's Zhao family. Duan Zhixiu's whole body trembled; he wanted to disbelieve, but doubt had already taken root in his mind. The more he thought about it, the more reasonable it seemed. Thus, everything made sense: the Ye family was known for their loyalty and patriotism. If you were a Song imperial relative, it explained why she was close to you!

Duan Zhixiu has a mountain of questions for you. First and foremost, he wants to know just who you are. As far as he knows, Ye Yunshang seems, at a glance, to be someone who causes trouble for anyone without discrimination — but look closely, and there are clear distinctions in who she keeps close and who she keeps at a distance. She calls you 'brother' and clings to you to a degree that's rare indeed. Just what is it that earns you her special regard? Of all the recent coincidences, none is more baffling or hard to let go of than this.

Asked about the mastermind behind it, Duan Zhixiu hesitated. Prideful as he was, he could still show courtesy to elders of the Jianghu, but he could not bear having his dignity trampled — let alone being set up and used by someone. He was determined to settle the score himself and would not allow the Tang Clan to interfere, and was willing to hand over his family's Secret Manual just to buy his silence.

But you've been tormented by Second Senior Brother at home, having mastered the art of poison. With narrowed eyes, you carefully examined it and immediately detected the trick. Duan Zhixiu's words were not without truth; this note had once contained characters, but they were written with a special ink that gradually faded over time, blending with the paper and the sachet to form the poison incense. This clearly showed the schemer's methods to be as cunning as they were sinister. Pitifully, Duan Zhixiu remains unaware he was ever manipulated, and now, even if he wishes to clear his name, there is no evidence to support him.

You asked Duan Zhixiu for the Message Token, brought it close to your nose and sniffed, indeed detecting a faint, subtle fragrance similar to the incense burned in the Zhengxin Hall. This Message Token must have been handled by someone from the Tang Clan. Now the toxic fragrance has dispersed, insufficient to cause death, nothing but a blank sheet of paper.

They loathed each other, both desperate to fight to the death, yet Yunshang's fate remained uncertain, so neither dared to leave. Glaring at each other in frustration, he finally proposed exchanging information‑each asking a question in turn, to ensure fairness.

You and Duan Zhixiu have mutual dislike, both public hatred and personal grudge. Zou Bo had just finished telling you not to make noise, but you couldn't hold back and started fighting. Zou Bo hadn't gone far and turned around, furious beyond control, quickly approached and slapped each of you, scolding you harshly, making you both quiet down.
He immediately felt his hands go weak, was pushed by you with disdain, tumbled back a few steps, and nearly lost his balance.
Now it's your turn to be restless; you immediately retaliate with force, countering his attack. If it weren't for Master Zou's intervention, you could have killed him on the spot.

Fortunately, they were in Qingcheng, where Sect Leader Zou used the authentic Internal Skill of the Xuanmen orthodoxy to keep Ye Yunshang's Heart Meridian from giving out, and urgently sent a disciple down the mountain to summon Tang Fang to perform treatment. Zou Bo came out looking unusually grave; blunt by nature as always, he said plainly: Ye Yunshang had suddenly fallen ill because she had been poisoned with the Tang Clan's own poison, Other Shore Immortal Fragrance. On hearing this, Duan Zhixiu's guilt and unease turned to fury—he grabbed you by the collar, cursing his own soft-heartedness for not killing you sooner. Zou Bo then added that the medium for the fragrance was none other than the blank Message Token that Duan Zhixiu himself had handed to Yunshang.

Duan Zhixiu thought she was weak and easily manipulated, but he didn't realize he was being played like a puppet. Knowing what the young Lord Duan cared about, she deliberately stepped on his pain, her words turning into sobs by the end. But besides herself, who else knew how much sincerity lay beneath her words? Duan Zhixiu was reduced to a state of utter shame, his refined demeanor shattered, his defenses crumbling. He confessed everything—his collusion with bandits to attack the Tang Clan—and handed over a sachet to Yunshang. He believed he had poured out his heart, but Yunshang took the Message Token out of the sachet, still looking doubtful. It bore not a single word, only a faint floral scent remaining. Bright red blood flowed from her nose without her realizing, and Yunshang collapsed, facing the sky.

Ye Yunshang was unwilling to passively be controlled by others, nor could she stand by and watch others suffer without taking action. After much hesitation, she finally mustered the courage to deliberately go off alone as bait. Duan Zhixiu indeed took the bait immediately, offering gifts and flattering her to seek forgiveness, but Yunshang maintained a cold expression and ignored him. Although they had fallen out, the bond between her and her brother with Duan Zhixiu, their former fellow disciples, was undeniably deep. Duan Zhixiu saw that she remained in Qingcheng and thought the young girl was easy to coax, believing there was still a chance to mend their relationship. Thus, he persistently pursued her. Little did he know that even her cold demeanor was a facade. If it weren't for her brother's example and her sense of loyalty toward the Tang Clan, Moling, and you, she would never have taken such a risk without any backing, putting herself in harm's way.

She recounted in detail her and her brother's history with Duan Zhixiu, and only then did you learn that he was the one who had spread the rumor of the treasure, forcing the Ye siblings to break with Diancang and become homeless wanderers. Duan Zhixiu needs something from Qingcheng, so he's unlikely to act rashly and stir up trouble. In that case, it would be wise to stall for now and send someone back to the Tang Clan for reinforcements — once they arrive, you can turn on him without delay.

Duan Zhixiu boldly appeared in Qingcheng, clearly well‑prepared, likely having already set up a web of traps. If you lose your composure and hastily flee, wouldn't that make you appear guilty? Conversely, if you remain in Qingcheng, you are always outsiders. Even if Sect Leader Zou is upright and resolute, he would never allow Duan Zhixiu to act recklessly. Qingcheng's entire sect must consider the Jianghu reputation; they would not easily believe one‑sided accusations and risk offending the Tang Clan.

Returning to the room, you were still fuming with anger, never expecting Qingcheng to be so biased toward appearance. Ye Yunshang was equally distracted; you called out several times before she came to her senses. You had never seen her so completely out of her wits, and you were surprised. After steadying yourself, you began to analyze the situation.
Returning to the room, you were still fuming, never expecting Qingcheng to be so judgmental based on appearances.

Returning to the room, you remained anxious and restless, fearing that lingering any longer would bring great calamity upon you. You paced back and forth, and Ye Yunshang, seeing how useless you were, had to force herself to calm down and analyze the situation.

Duan Zhixiu turned the tables on you instead, saying he had Diancang behind him and could appeal all the way up to the Duan Clan of Dali — you accused him without proof, which was slander of his character and his reputation. As a man of the Jianghu, a swordsman, and a member of the Duan clan, defending his good name was only right, and even if he drew his sword and cut you down, no one could hold him to account! Hearing this, Iron Crown Daoist rushed to speak up for Duan Zhixiu and called for you to be seized. Just as swords were about to be drawn, Duan Zhixiu called a halt, saying again and again: no one is without fault — everyone deserves a chance to mend their ways. No one expected such words, yet he seemed utterly sincere, using them to display his broad-minded generosity. Only, he believed his own gaze to be gentle as he smiled at Ye Yunshang — but the smile made her thoroughly sick to her stomach.
The Iron Crown Daoist naturally wouldn't believe it.
The Iron Crown Daoist won't believe you, and naturally neither will Shentu Long.

You recounted how you encountered Duan Zhixiu gathering bandits and launching a night attack on the Tang Clan in a ruined temple, accusing Duan, but he vehemently denied it, insisting you were fabricating false accusations. You were so enraged you could burst, but without irrefutable evidence, you had no real leverage against him. Even though you had captured Nangong Ji, the accomplice, it was still just your one‑sided account. Even if you brought all the bandit leaders to Qingcheng to confront him, it would be in vain. After all, the Tang Clan has a long history of misconduct, having produced numerous conspirators who have harmed the Wulin. Framing innocent people and colluding to falsely accuse others is a specialty of your Tang Clan elders. By common sense, who would believe your baseless accusations rather than trust the noble and dignified Duan, a royal relative of Dali?

Though he had injured his dominant hand, he was still a renowned master of Diancang, with sharp eyes for combat. What's more, the two sects were old rivals who had each spent great effort studying the other's techniques—your killing strikes all missed their mark, and your punches and kicks instead left you reeling from his Internal Skill. One stood calm and composed, the other in disarray; it was plain to see who was the better fighter.

It was Duan Zhixiu, who ended up taking the beating, who urged you. He didn't even consider you worthy of his attention; he didn't blame you for being difficult, only himself for being overconfident. One‑handed, he was evenly matched with you. If he let his superiors intervene, his reputation would be ruined.
Shentu Long won't offend his own senior brother for you, so he watches from the sidelines coldly.

Eldest Senior Brother initially remained calm, thinking Long Xiang was just boasting, a young calf not yet fearing a tiger. Even though they were of the same generation, only a few years apart, he was a renowned martial hero who had roamed the Jianghu for a decade. How could he be outmaneuvered by a girl fresh onto the scene? He grew overconfident, intending to exhaust her stamina with a Coin Dart to strike her acupoints, then decide the outcome and clear the matter. But Long Xiang's sword technique was far beyond any Jinxiang Palace disciple he had ever encountered. Combining hardness with softness, her attacks were both offensive and defensive, unimpeded in execution. The faster she fought, the more directly she targeted his vital points, leaving him secretly alarmed. He reached into his pocket, only to find his Coin Darts already spent. With no other option to secure victory, he resorted to his ultimate move. However, although this girl had been deceived, she was still fighting for the weak. Eldest Senior Brother could not bear to harm her, so he made a risky move, seeking victory within defeat — giving up every fallback and line of retreat to seize an instant's advantage, breaking through Long Xiang's sword formation and kissing her on the cheek. Had his opponent been anyone but Long Xiang, or had she been a touch more seasoned, she would have turned her blade on him at once. But his opponent was Long Xiang. Her mind was as pure as paper, as white as the robe she wore. Within Jinxiang Palace, she had only ever kept company with women; steeped in martial arts, yet yearning for a life in the Jianghu, she had never known the affection between man and woman — when had anyone ever taken such a liberty with her? In an instant her mind went blank, her face flushed red with shame and anger, and she stamped her foot and fled.

Just now you had fought so fiercely the sky itself seemed to darken, the danger extreme, and Fourth Senior Brother had not been idle either — seeing the situation turn ugly, he rushed to the yamen to beat the drum and cry injustice, a Wulin man hauling ordinary commoners before the magistrate, a first in all history. As luck would have it, the renowned constable Song Bei happened to be nearby, and knowing the Flying Hero's character, he suspected there was some injustice behind it. He led his men at once to arrest the two women who had incited the killing, and a brief interrogation soon laid the whole matter bare. Eldest Senior Brother and Song Bei were old acquaintances from the Jianghu — not especially close, but each respected the other's reputation. Guessing that Eldest Senior Brother had no wish to press the matter against the two women, Song Bei did him the favor of letting them off with nothing more than a stern warning. The affair thus came to a close, and you carried the rice and Fourth Senior Brother's private goods safely home. At the same time, Long Xiang ran to the riverbank, lay down, held her breath, and plunged her face into the water, letting the stream wash away the burning shame on her cheeks. Passersby who saw her thought someone was drowning.

Try to put yourself in Eldest Senior Brother's shoes. If you were Eldest Senior Brother, unable to win and unable to escape, with hidden weapons exhausted, at this moment there's truly no other way to protect yourself, so you'd have no choice but to offend her.

Try to put yourself in the Eldest Senior Brother's shoes. If you were the Eldest Senior Brother, you'd kiss her. Not just a kiss, but aim for her lips. If conditions permit, you'd even stick out your tongue. The Eldest Senior Brother, hearing your bold words, couldn't help but blush. The feather he had loosened was once again gripped in his palm, hesitating whether to eliminate the pest.

Try putting yourself in the Eldest Senior Brother's shoes; if you were he, you'd be on your knees begging for mercy right then. The Eldest Senior Brother was taken aback by this. Though your behavior was somewhat cowardly, it strangely commanded respect. A man's knees hold gold‑even someone as open‑minded as he couldn't kneel with such decisiveness as you did.

Try to see things from Eldest Senior Brother's perspective, yet you can't figure it out. You keep emphasizing not to be abrupt with a lady, but you don't realize that in a duel, life and death are in an instant. Long Xiang's attacks are relentless, leaving no time for careful thought. If you want to live and have a clean way out, it's unrealistic.

Try putting yourself in the Eldest Senior Brother's shoes; if you were the Eldest Senior Brother, you'd have left without a second thought. Whether Long Xiang would take out her anger on others and chop the Fourth Senior Brother into minced meat wouldn't matter to you at all.
You knew Long Xiang's martial arts were high, but you didn't expect them to be so high that they could even put Eldest Senior Brother in a dangerous situation.

At first, the senior brother remained calm, thinking that Long Xiang was just a brash newcomer, a young calf not afraid of tigers. Even though they were of similar age, he was a renowned hero who had roamed the Jianghu for ten years; how could he be subdued by a girl who had just stepped onto the scene? Thus, he couldn't help but be overconfident, planning to exhaust her strength and then use a Coin Dart to seal her acupoints, determining the outcome and clearing the air. However, he soon realized that Long Xiang's swordsmanship was far beyond that of any disciple from Jinxiang Palace he knew. It was a blend of strength and softness, both offensive and defensive, with no hindrance in her movements. As the fight progressed, she became faster, each move aimed directly at his vital points, causing him to feel a surge of alarm. He checked his pockets and found that he had already used up all his Coin Darts. To defeat her, he had no choice but to unleash his ultimate move. Yet, despite being deceived by others, this girl was ultimately fighting for the weak. The senior brother, though reluctant to take her life, realized that if he showed her any more mercy, he would end up losing his own life to her sword. He tightened his grip on the feather on his wrist, preparing to kill. At that moment, you, who had been knocked to the ground, suddenly found yourself caught between the two, colliding with the senior brother and accidentally kissing Long Xiang on the cheek. Long Xiang was momentarily stunned, her face turning bright red with a mix of embarrassment and anger. Fortunately, she did not come at you with her sword but, unable to contain her shame, stomped her foot and fled. The senior brother then let out a sigh of relief and relaxed his grip on the feather.

Long Xiang saw you all acting out betrayal dramas, laughing and fighting, causing a commotion, and felt puzzled. It was said that the Tang Clan used poison, an unorthodox and sinister method. Today's sight confirmed the reputation; they had gone mad like this, which is why they are feared.

Long Xiang was simple‑minded and still thought you genuinely meant to help her. Touched, she didn't want to put you in a difficult spot, and resolved instead to defeat him fairly, by her own skill alone.

Everyone else had already drawn their swords, yet you and the Eldest Senior Brother were still laughing and joking. Instead of rushing to make peace, you seized the Eldest Senior Brother from behind and urged Long Xiang to give him a couple of strokes with her sword.
Long Xiang took it that you were simply shielding a fellow disciple, understandable enough, and had no wish to argue with you over it.
Hearing you turn around and speak up for this wicked man, Long Xiang couldn't help but furrow her brow, taking it for favoritism, and felt disappointed.
Seeing that she had already drawn her sword—clearly she meant it this time—you hurried to speak up and talk her down.

She would have doubted these women, but she believed you would never lie to her. Tang Buyi is undoubtedly a lecherous villain, wicked beyond measure. You hadn't expected your off‑the‑cuff remarks to be taken seriously, and you were left at a loss for words. Even the Eldest Senior Brother was stunned, yet he didn't get angry; instead, he found it amusing.

You never thought that the enforcer of justice they had invited was actually Long Xiang. She saw you, displaying a cheerful demeanor, but it immediately subsided; the matter at hand is urgent, so she would first behead Tang Buyi, this lecherous demon, and discuss it later.

You saw Long Xiang and were shocked. That night, you watched helplessly as she was swept away by a mountain flood, thinking she had already passed away. You didn't expect to meet her here again, thinking at first it was a ghost from the day before. Only when you saw her shadow beneath her feet did you calm down a bit.

It was meant to be the most ordinary of days, but neither of you expected something out of the ordinary to be waiting when you came down the mountain. Two pretty young women burst into the outer fortress, crying at once that your Eldest Senior Brother had taken their virtue and then cast them aside, shouting loud enough that the whole outer fortress should come and see this heartless man's true face. The Eldest Senior Brother was known for his loose, unrestrained ways, forever coming and going from houses of pleasure—he might call himself innocent, but who would believe it? Even the heroine of Jinxiang Palace, well-traveled as she was, had heard no small number of tales about the Tang Clan's Flying Hero's philandering, and now with two wronged women accusing him to his face, however much she wished to disbelieve, she was already nine parts convinced. Women of that age set the greatest store by their chastity—many a virtuous woman, once she'd lost hers, chose not to go on living—so who would falsely smear her own name to slander another without cause? Worse still, one of them had tattooed the words Tang Buyi across her skin, as if staking a claim on property, and Long Xiang could not help but rage at the sight of it. Yet it takes all kinds, as the saying goes—the Eldest Senior Brother did owe his share of debts, but this time he truly was wronged. Of the two women, one had loved him and lost, and meant to destroy them both together—the tattoo of Tang Buyi on her skin was her own doing. The other cared nothing at all for the Eldest Senior Brother's character or looks; she framed him only because she had quietly fallen pregnant and dared not name the child's true father, for fear of being drowned in the pig-basket for it. So she laid the blame on your Eldest Senior Brother instead, hoping that once Long Xiang had cut him down with her sword, she could pin the child on him with no one left to say otherwise.

The Fourth Senior Brother's errands often went begging even when he offered to pay out of his own pocket, and it was entirely his own doing. He made a habit of using his post as buyer to talk others into hauling his private goods up or down the mountain, then turning around and reselling them at a markup, raking in a tidy profit—he'd fleece even his own brothers without a qualm. Once the disciples had all been burned by him once, no one would be fooled a second time, and whenever there was no one left to ask, they pushed the job onto you. You braced yourself to do the work of three men again and break your back over it, but the Eldest Senior Brother, as if struck by a sudden whim, sauntered up and volunteered himself. Such chores were never meant for the Eldest Disciple to do, but since he'd offered himself up, the Fourth Senior Brother wasted no courtesy and put him straight to work.

The father and daughter had only just been reunited, and already Long Yuan had to leave, promising to visit again. She watched her father's retreating figure, torn between sorrow and joy, and did not run after him—instead she leaned into your shoulder, tears streaming down her face. Though they could not marry just yet, she had already decided you were her destined partner, and gave you a dragon horn hairpin paired with hers as a token. Once you accepted it, there could be no turning back—should you dare flirt with another woman, your name would surely be added to the Flower-Cherishing Register.

Long Yuan truly did not want you as a son-in-law, but not because he thought little of you—rather, the bond the two of you had formed had won you his high regard. He passed on the sum of his life's martial arts to you, a small token of thanks for how you had looked after Long Xiang. How much of it you could grasp, and whether you could weather the storm ahead, would depend on your own fortune.
You felt this life had no hope left, and had already begun thinking of your next reincarnation.
You caught the hint of hope hidden in his words and swelled with confidence, as though even the Wulin Alliance's march from the west were but a trifling matter.

When you tried to bring up your broken engagement to Long Xiang, Long Yuan's face darkened at once. He could be careless about his own affairs, but where his daughter's whole life was at stake, he put on the stern face of a father without delay. Even if his daughter cared nothing for your looks or lineage, judged only by heart and deed—the Tang Clan could scarcely protect itself now, so how could it take her in as a bride? The question was not only for you; it was a warning for her to think twice. Long Xiang was no daughter of the Tang Clan, under no obligation to fight beside it, and so she weighed it all the more carefully. The Jianghu was not the black-and-white place she'd once believed it, where you simply killed the wicked on sight. On chivalry, opinions had differed since ancient times—was it to spare the multitude, or to sacrifice the one? Strip away self-interest, and the question only grew harder. People drifted through the Jianghu chasing fame and fortune, everyone hoping for a better life, and there was no fault in that. But if the public good was used as an excuse to trample fairness, then she, Long Xiang, would not stand for it. Standing with the Tang Clan today was not only to repay the debt of their shelter, but because she truly believed in its innocence. The day she had been driven from Fengyu Mountain by her own master, she had been unable to stand beside her Jinxiang Palace sisters through life and death, helpless and afraid. This time her resolve was clear; once she had decided a thing was right, she would grit her teeth and not yield a single step. She could not bear to watch the innocent bleed, or to hear the cries of the wronged. She refused to follow the crowd blindly, choosing instead to speak for fairness by her own judgment, and to argue for the right in the face of every injustice. Even if Heaven itself did not see it, she would see it through until her own heart was satisfied. Every word of it rang clear and righteous, and both you and Long Yuan were moved. That his daughter, in all the years he had missed, had grown into someone like this—the old father's pride was beyond words. He longed to lift her up high and boast to the whole world that she was his, Long Yuan's, daughter. His daughter, at least, was no longer a worry. But that did not mean he would consent to your marriage—courage and integrity were one thing, marrying the right man quite another. If you meant to wed his daughter, you would first have to pass him, and his test was as hard as scaling heaven itself. Beside it, surviving the Tang Clan's calamity was a small matter. If you could not clear it, that would only mean you and Long Xiang were fated never to be together—and the loss would be yours alone.

Long Yuan sneered at the current situation, his expression one of gloating over others' misfortunes. In his conversation, he showed clear disdain for the Wulin Alliance, but when asked to assist the Tang Clan, he could not. He was a dead man; if he were to return, the old grudges from the past would inevitably resurface. If used by someone with ulterior motives, this time the Tang Clan would not be seen as the Mud Cult's allies but as Jin Kingdom spies. The Imperial Court would be overjoyed, no longer needing to worry about the Wulin people's concerns of mutual destruction. Launching a military campaign would be entirely justified.

Asked why Long Yuan had hidden his identity, the question unearthed an old affair—one you had heard Long Xiang mention before, but which Long Yuan himself confirmed only today. During the campaign to wipe out Western Xia's Supreme Bliss Cult, his sworn brother Wanyan Xun was to march troops out of the Jin Kingdom in support of the Wulin alliance, blocking Western Xia's reinforcements at Hexi and cutting off the cult's escape route. But faced with a choice between power and loyalty, he chose power, reversing his word at the last moment. He meant to let the armies of the Central Plains and the Supreme Bliss Cult fight each other to exhaustion, leaving neither strength to prop up the Song or Xia courts—then ascend the throne himself, destroy Western Xia, swallow the Song, and use both nations' grain to fund a campaign north, even grinding the Mongols underfoot. It was no idle dream. Great calamity followed: the Supreme Bliss Cult was destroyed, but the righteous sects of the Wulin were also gravely weakened, with countless heroes giving their lives and never returning—the Tang Clan and Songshan losing the most. Long Yuan, half mad with fury, drew his sword to assassinate Wanyan Xun, fought through the ten great masters of the Dragon Garden, and took his sworn brother alive—only to soften at the last, and after a long howl to the heavens, cut off his own arm and vanished from the world. The world believed he had died a martyr in the battle against the Supreme Bliss Cult; those who knew better believed instead that his assassination attempt had failed and he had perished in the Jin Kingdom. To protect his name after death, they never spoke of his having a sworn brother at all. Only two old rivals of his, Wang Erzhuang and Lady Wen, knew he had survived—one sheltered Long Yuan, the other raised Long Xiang. But now that both their protections have been stripped away by the Jianghu, and Long Xiang stands ready to die alongside the Tang Clan without a second thought, he had no choice but to come forward and claim her as his daughter.

Great Hero Long had once instructed you at the inn not to reveal his whereabouts, fearing it would damage Long Xiang's reputation and put her in danger. He actually did not have high hopes for you, thinking that your martial arts skills and appearance were probably not good enough for his own daughter, making them mere casual acquaintances at best. You spoke of him anyway, but she might not have believed you even if you had. However, it never crossed his mind that you would remain tight‑lipped and almost end up abducting his daughter in the process. He feels a mix of emotions toward you. Long Xiang knows he has been keeping this from her, and she is extremely angry about it. Since her father is present now, she cannot vent her anger, so for now, she will keep quiet and wait until later to settle the score with you.

Your face is too thick, fearing that Long Yuan might despise your appearance and family background. To solidify the unstable relationship between you and Long Xiang, you rashly approached, shouting father‑in‑law first, but your sudden movement frightened Long Yuan, who kicked you so hard you flew several feet, sliding across the ground before colliding with a rock wall and fainting. If not for his mastery of martial arts, capable of dispersing the impact throughout your body, that kick would have ruptured your internal organs, not just causing you to faint for an hour.

You stepped back to the side, quietly watching Long Xiang, both rejoicing in her happiness and feeling a pang of self‑pity. Deep within, you felt a subtle sense that her willingness to marry you was merely a temporary solution after leaving Jinxiang Palace, a moment of helplessness and wandering. Now that she had a solid support, she was once again an impressive figure, and the possibility of your relationship had vanished. You stood motionless on the causeway, the wind especially cold. It was unclear how long you had stood there before Long Xiang came out to call you, her cheeks still bearing traces of tears, yet her smile was as bright as spring sunshine. You couldn't help but be entranced, sighing that dreams fade quickly.

You do idolize Long Yuan, that much is true, and it's just as true that you have your eye on his daughter. Now you are not only a thorn in the side of the reigning Wulin Alliance Leader, but a thorn in the eye of the one before him—how many in the Jianghu could boast of offending two Alliance Leaders running? He may still draw breath, but it already feels as though you can see the underworld's runners beckoning to you, and you cannot help but be afraid.
Seeing the legend himself brought so low—dressed in rags, missing an arm—you couldn't help but feel a pang of sorrow.
You were so moved your throat tightened, and before you knew it, you were crying along with her. Long Yuan, watching this, could only look on in utter bewilderment.

You, too, were greatly shocked. This man was a legend — you had grown up hearing tales of him, a hero among heroes whom everyone in the Jianghu knew by name. For fear of overstepping some forbidden line, the world had never raised so much as a statue in his honor, and his deeds lived on only in the unofficial histories of the Jianghu. Yet even now, he remained the idol that the younger generation of the Jianghu looked up to as one.

He too had summoned his courage to reveal who he was — the sword hero Long Yuan, who had faked his death over a decade ago and had lived in hiding within the Beggar Sect under a false name ever since. Long Xiang was stunned. Having just heard him speak so precisely of her family's martial teachings, she had already guessed some connection to the Long family, but never imagined this man was her own father. For a moment she could not believe it, and in her daze she very nearly let her sword slip from her hand. The image of her father from childhood, recalled a thousand times over the years, had long since blurred; she remembered only a man who commanded the wind and rain, feared nothing and lost to no one, the very picture of authority. Yet the man before her now was unkempt, his beard ragged, his robes tattered, and missing an arm — his tiger's eyes full of timidity and hope. Where was the spirited figure of old? But blood runs thicker than water, and Long Xiang felt no disappointment, only sorrow for the hardship her father had endured. She dropped her sword and threw herself into his arms, weeping without restraint. Long Yuan had feared his daughter would spurn him, but she rushed into his embrace without a moment's hesitation, just as she once had, the small girl outside Jinxiang Palace who clung wailing to his trouser leg and would not let him go. Even a man of iron could not stop his eyes from reddening; he longed to hold her close, yet feared his ragged clothes would soil her snow-white dress — just as, all these years, he had always watched her from afar, never daring to show himself.

You were defeated, then awoke to find yourself carried by Long Xiang to the alchemy room for bandaging and treatment. The black‑cloaked elder did not intervene, and the Third Senior Brother led a search but found no trace of them. Having missed the auspicious day and time, the wedding ceremony had to be postponed, yet she remained certain that her destined partner was you. She gifted you a dragon horn hairpin, a token of commitment. Once accepted, you could not retract your decision. Should you dare to flirt with another woman, your name would be inscribed upon the Flower-Cherishing Register.

Long Xiang watched you win, yet you still wore a look of deference and unease, your words seeming to favor your opponent, and she could not help but be left bewildered. She had matched her fighting to yours, yet somewhere in the battle you had let yourself be won over by the other side — how could that not leave her feeling wronged?

The opponent's every move stayed a step ahead of Long Xiang's, breaking her rhythm and pinning her down so she could not fight at full strength. Yet Long Xiang only grew bolder as the battle wore on, transforming in the heat of combat — when her rhythm broke, she fell into step with you instead, matching your every movement, shaking off the constraints of her family's teachings, and together the two of you brought the formidable foe down.

His words were full of praise for you. You had grown up hearing his legends, and to be praised now by the very hero of those stories left you overjoyed beyond words. Long Xiang, for her part, was utterly baffled — weren't you supposed to be helping her? How had you gone from fighting him to being won over by him mid-battle, you traitor.

It was not that you and Long Xiang lacked strength — the newcomer was simply too powerful, and he kept Long Xiang pinned down at every turn, never letting her fight at her full potential. Even two against one, you still lost. You were just steadying your weapons to catch your breath and fight again when the man himself called a halt.

This time he no longer held back. Gathering his qi in his palm, his severed arm and trailing sleeve moved as if guided by his true qi, weaving like a serpent as he unleashed his real skill and fought you both once more.
You suddenly felt a bit shaky and lost your confidence.

Someone connected to Long Xiang, intimately familiar with the Long family's martial teachings, fighting one-handed yet with formidable skill — you had long suspected the visitor was none other than Long Yuan.

The black‑cloaked master used a single palm to intercept your combined four‑handed attack, employing nine defenses against one offense, yet still could not fully block it. Bursting with unrestrained spirit, he removed his black robe and face veil, discarded the fake hand, and revealed his true appearance.

He was intimately familiar with the Long family's swordplay — had he not deliberately held back to guide her, Long Xiang would not have lasted thirty exchanges before her blade shattered and she was killed. He meant to draw out her full potential, and his words, beneath their air of encouragement, carried a deliberate provocation, one that touched on Long Yuan and Lady Wen with something close to insult. Long Xiang could not bear it, and stopped listening to reason entirely. That man had no idea how stubborn Long Xiang could be, but you knew all too well, and fearing she might come to harm, you forced your way into the fight.

You saw them fighting, and your heart sank. Eldest Senior Brother's nature was outgoing and unrestrained, evident in his movements of attack and defense, his attacks spontaneous and unbound, never so rigorous as this.

The newcomer seemed to bear no ill will, letting you stand and wait while he went straight to instruct Long Xiang. Much of your skill today you owed to a senior who had guided you on the back mountain years before. Though you had never spoken of it, deep down you had always felt that the masked man back then was Eldest Senior Brother in disguise, and seeing him suddenly appear now, you could not help but cry out in shock. Long Xiang, hearing this, was equally stunned, and quickly steadied her mind. She had crossed blades with Eldest Senior Brother several times before, and while she held him in great respect, she knew that for all his natural gifts, his skill had not yet reached the realm of the supreme masters. But the man before her now was a peerless fighter: one hand held behind his back, no weapon drawn, he met her sword strokes with his bare palm alone, calm and unhurried, slapping, striking, twisting, pressing — and for all the refinement of the Long family's Sword Technique, she could not so much as graze him. His palm strength, too, was immense; the Internal Force that traveled back up her blade felt as heavy as ten thousand pounds, as though she were swinging her sword in a raging undercurrent, utterly beyond her own control. Such mastery rivaled even the old Dharma King of the Beast Path; his internal skill and palm technique had both reached their very peak, undoubtedly placing him among the ranks of the Peerless Masters — far beyond anything Eldest Senior Brother could ever match.

The newcomer seemed to bear no ill will; he had you stand still while he went straight to instruct Long Xiang. Much of your skill today you owed to a senior who had once guided you on the back mountain years before. Afterward you often brought wine and food up to the back mountain to train, always hoping to see that senior once more and kowtow in thanks, but no matter how you searched the mountain, you never found a trace of him, and the disappointment lingered in your heart. Now this man in black had appeared on the back mountain, and every gesture of his carried the bearing of a master — who else could he be but that very senior? You felt both astonishment and joy. His skill was extraordinary: one hand held behind his back, no weapon drawn, he met Long Xiang's sword strokes with his bare palm alone, calm and unhurried, slapping, striking, twisting, pressing — and for all the refinement of Long Xiang's Sword Technique, she could not so much as graze him. His palm strength, too, was immense, rivaling even the old Dharma King of the Beast Path; both his internal skill and palm technique had reached their very peak, undoubtedly placing him among the ranks of Peerless Masters. Why such a man should appear on the Tang Clan's back mountain, you could not fathom.

You long to take her hand and confess your feelings, swear an oath under heaven and earth to become husband and wife. Suddenly, a masked expert bursts in. Now you and Long Xiang are both outstanding talents in the Wulin, yet you cannot resist his sudden attack and are torn apart.

You suddenly received a message by carrier pigeon from Long Xiang. It was close enough that she could simply have called out to you, yet the culprit insisted on releasing a pigeon from outside your window — the bird had barely flapped its wings twice before its task was done, and by the time you looked up, Long Xiang herself had already vanished, leaving you speechless. The message was terse: meet her at the back mountain. You knew she still resented you for having disrespected her, and guessed that after holding back for days, she now meant to strike you down for good — so you went already resolved to die. At the back mountain, she pointed you toward a mound of earth piled rather high, and your heart sank, certain it was a grave she had prepared for you. But instead her face flushed red — the earth was meant to stand in for incense, so that the two of you could bow to heaven and earth together. Stunned and overjoyed, as though caught in a dream, you scratched your head in delight, unable to contain yourself. You had poured out your deep feelings for her only so you would have no regrets, never daring to hope for more — who could have guessed she had already given you her heart? With your love now returned in kind, you had never in your life felt so happy as in that moment.

Long Xiang had trained with the sword since childhood, raised on tales of her father's heroic deeds; martial arts and chivalry filled her every thought. Even in the time she was infatuated with Eldest Senior Brother, she never once thought of love and marriage — she had never so much as considered her own future, let alone imagined that you would set your heart on her. You watched her flee in disarray and laughed at yourself, sitting at the cliff's edge, feeling as though your life was all but ruined. But you did not know that Long Xiang had not fled out of disdain — quite the opposite, she was simply too overcome with shame to stay. She ran all the way back to her quarters in the Outer Fort, torn between conflicting thoughts, and after much turmoil she recalled her teacher's old warnings and finally understood. Lady Wen had long foreseen this day, and had always cautioned her never to be swayed by a passing feeling — a decision made under the sway of emotion might not be sincere, and was irresponsible to everyone involved. One should use the mind before the heart, and think carefully before acting; it was for this very purpose that the Mysterious Candle Heart Sutra of Jinxiang Palace had been created. Long Xiang sat in meditation, circulating her energy, her mind free of doubt, and as she looked back over all that had passed, the clearer her memories grew, the firmer her resolve became.

Your patience held firm as you first hinted that the man was from the Tang Clan, not Kongtong. Seeing she still could not guess, you hinted that he wore a white robe from head to toe. Little did you know Long Xiang's thoughts were racing elsewhere — she had already suspected the Wulin Alliance Leader, Rui Sheng, never once imagining that she herself might be the one you meant. Only when you finally spelled it out did she realize, with a start, that you had set your sights on her all along.

Your eyes rolled back, almost fainting, you couldn't care less about the consequences and blurted out a correction. Long Xiang finally realized that the person you had your heart set on was actually her.

You hesitated, finally mustering the courage to speak. The woman you loved was the best in the world, and you felt unworthy of her, too afraid to harbor improper thoughts.
