She was not only beautiful, but also kind-hearted, talented, skilled in writing and calligraphy, and adept at music. She was composed and graceful, valiant and courageous, always ready to do the right thing and helpful to others. Her martial arts were also formidable. At first, Long Xiang was quite indignant, thinking that some miss had been unkind, daring to look down on her brother. She would rather not let her know, for if she did, she would definitely go and have a word with her. As you listed off all her virtues, Long Xiang tried to find fault but could not, and felt an inexplicable pang of jealousy. She unconsciously compared herself to you, realizing she fell short in every way, and the sense of defeat was heavy. After much thought, she decided that only Heroine Xiahou, the Soul-Stealing Orchid of the Kongtong Sect, might possibly fit your description. She had never even met the woman, but a promise was a promise—she would have to make the trip to the Kongtong Sect herself and play matchmaker on your behalf. Perhaps Heroine Xiahou would have the eye to recognize a true hero and take a liking to her brother. Just thinking of it made her eyes and nose sting.

You heard Long Xiang's heart, yet kept your feelings locked away, fearing that your deep affection might end in disaster, be rejected, and even lose your friendship. Long Xiang returned to her room, after a long while, and slept soundly, while you, however, were consumed by thoughts of her, lying awake all night.

You did not advise her, for fearing death is only human. But you passed on to her the words she had rushed past and never heard: 'Heaven has eyes! It has sent this White-robed Bodhisattva to save us from our suffering!' 'Thank goodness justice still lives, thank goodness there are still people who dare to act on it—this world isn't beyond saving after all.' 'If not for Heroine Long, my whole family would have died in shame.' 'She could have looked away and done nothing, but she chose to step forward—well done, her.' 'Heaven keep such a fine girl; may she live a hundred years.' These were all things said by the people Long Xiang had saved, though she always swept off before she could hear them. You reminded her that she fought for justice not only for her father's sake or her master's teachings, but because of the expectations she held for herself in her own heart—she had long since lived up to the name of hero. Long Xiang stood in silence, tears welling up, not because she had suddenly stopped fearing death, but because she had remembered something important. That small flame was enough to drive back the dark and stand against fear: its name was conviction, its name was chivalry, its name was courage. Just as you once told her: 'Having you in this world is truly a wonderful thing—thank you for coming.' She, too, was glad to have met you: fortunate beyond words.

You didn't advise her—fearing death is only human. They say life and death are trifles, but how many can truly face death without a flicker of dread? To hold your own life too dear isn't chivalry; it's a betrayal of your parents and of Heaven, disloyal and unfilial. Yet how could you not wish the same for her—that she live out her days safe and sound, to a peaceful old age? Better, then, to let her stay a little timid than to talk her out of it.

You didn't persuade her; fearing death is a natural human emotion. How could you not be afraid too? You don't have much profound reasoning to convince her, after all, you're still on the Jianghu path, going with the flow, struggling inevitably.

She once cut down all evils with her sword, but now she fears that fate will turn, and one day it will be her turn. An inexplicable fear takes over her body and mind, preventing her from speaking it aloud, for she dreads seeing her master's disappointed expression. Had you not arrived at Jinxiang Palace, she might never have confided these feelings to anyone, continuing to be strong, unwilling to show weakness before others, living in constant fear of death all her life.

The scene of Shentu Long killing Tang Buyi remains vivid before her eyes even now, and the more she recalls it, the more it fills her with dread. He spared his own life and vowed to settle the score with himself one day; that handsome, expectant smile of his became Long Xiang's Inner Demon—no matter how hard she trained, she could never imagine herself winning.

Long Xiang, having completed her training, left the palace to wander the world. When she found your Eldest Senior Brother, Flower-Cherishing Register in hand, she suffered her first defeat at the hands of a peer. Her opponent handled it with such ease that even as her teeth itched with anger, she couldn't help but admire him—deep down she had already fallen for him, though she was unaware of her own feelings. Wasn't he supposed to be forever carefree and easygoing? No hardship under heaven should have been able to stop him. Not only Long Xiang but the whole Tang Clan believed this—so how could the mighty Flying Hero have died so easily? One by one, the people she looked up to passed away, and only then did Long Xiang finally come to believe: the Jianghu truly does kill people. Looking special doesn't make you special; when it's your time to die, you die, and everyone has only the one life. Including her father, including Gang Leader Wang, including her Eldest Senior Brother, including her, including you.

Speaking of the Inner Demon, Long Xiang first brought up Wang Erzhuang, the former leader of the Beggar Sect. Her words carried endless nostalgia, for she regarded Wang Erzhuang as kin. In the years without her father, she had grown up looking up to this uncle-like figure; even her master once said Wang's martial arts might already be the finest under heaven. And what is being the finest under heaven, if not being invincible? She recalled the day Wang stood proudly upon the battlefield, alone challenging the heroes of the Central Plains, matchless against ten thousand men—what heroic spirit that was! His skill was peerless, his spirit bold beyond compare, and yet in the end he was still buried beneath the yellow earth.

Your varied and unconventional moves overwhelmed Long Xiang, leaving her unable to keep up, and she was defeated. She may not be willing to admit it, but she has to acknowledge your skill. Now, wait for you to ask her next.

You are indeed straightforward and honest in dealing with the world. Since you lost, it's natural that you can't hear her troubles. Long Xiang was taken aback again, her joy dimming as she heard that you would challenge again. Her brows furrowed, and she went to practice as well.

You take advantage of her being immersed in happiness, when her mind isn't sharp, to flip the facts and make it sound like you lost and had to accept the bet, listening to her complain. Long Xiang vaguely felt something was off, but she was genuinely complaining, so she didn't dwell on the details.
You lost, and so be it—seeing her bright, cheerful mood sweep away her recent gloom, you felt relieved as well.

Long Xiang defeated you, and this time she claimed there was nothing lacking in you, but instead, she was overjoyed. She had long regarded you as an equal peer, and there was nothing more exhilarating than defeating a strong warrior.

She hesitated for a moment, ultimately deciding not to share her thoughts with you. It was Lady Wen's task, something she wanted to complete on her own, no matter how difficult. When everything settled down and the world grew calm and clear, she would look back on it as a topic of idle chatter after tea and meals.

You didn't rush to press for answers, instead making up your mind to do everything possible to stay alive, waiting for her to prepare mentally before confiding in you. If you truly couldn't manage it and died first, you'd still beg for mercy from the ghostly hand, waiting until she confessed at your grave. Long Xiang was both moved and flustered, quickly covering your mouth while wildly waving her hands to drive away bad luck.

You turned a blind eye to her pitiful, wronged look, and even mocked her. Enraged, Long Xiang let spite get the better of her and gave you an unflattering new nickname: Stinky Little Hero. The nickname showed no cleverness at all—its only real feature was a whiff of stupidity beneath the insult. Jianghu loves gossip, and unflattering stories are always savored, so after that day your new nickname spread like wildfire across the land. Everyone knew you, and everyone laughed at you.
Seeing her pitiful, wronged look, you felt both pity and amusement, lowered your posture to ask her to speak, giving her a graceful exit. Long Xiang was very easy to please, and she was satisfied.
Long Xiang finally steeled herself and told you.
Long Xiang saw your calm and collected demeanor and flew into a rage, her pretty face flushing red with suppressed anger, then stomped off in a huff, refusing to say a word.

She thought you were just like your Eldest Senior Brother, seeing you as honest and easy to take advantage of, so she intentionally teased you, wanting to see you make a fool of yourself. She couldn't help but feel both ashamed and furious, and attacked you with her sword!
You immediately dismissed the idea and turned to leave. Long Xiang was taken aback, instead becoming unhappy, bursting into loud sobs and clinging to you, leaving you speechless.

She went pale with alarm; with you pressing so hard there was no room left to dodge, so she gritted her teeth and drew her sword. If you meant to keep prying into a young woman's private feelings, you'd have to stake your life and answer for it with your skill.
Long Xiang has been looking troubled lately, forcing a cheerful demeanor in public but appearing disoriented in private. You finally couldn't hold back and asked.

You casually placed the heavy burden on Long Xiang's shoulders, leaving her stunned and overwhelmed. Even though her martial arts skills far surpassed her peers, she couldn't single‑handedly block the Jinxiang Palace's sisters. But if she failed, a direct clash between the Tang Clan and Jinxiang Palace would ensue, resulting in the destruction of one or the other. The pressure on Long Xiang's shoulders suddenly intensified, yet a surge of warmth spread through her entire body. This time, unlike when Fengyu Mountain was excluded by her master, she carried the trust of the person, the weight of the Tang Clan, and the mutual obligations between the Tang Clan and Jinxiang Palace. Even if it were as difficult as climbing heaven, she would find value in sacrificing herself. With her mind set, she decided: if her words were insufficient to dissuade the sisters, she would confront them directly, vowing not to kill, defeating one and saving one, ensuring she betrayed neither side.

You hold Jinxiang Palace in high regard. Though one's fate in the Jianghu is not entirely one's own to command, the sword is still one's own to wield — should they come from afar, resolved to kill, the Tang Clan would not simply wait to be struck down, but would fight back with all its strength. Long Xiang knew this would be so before she even asked; there was nothing she could do, and no one to blame. Her heart was full of sorrow and regret, yet she had made up her mind: to face them honorably, sworn never to kill, defeating one to spare one, betraying neither side.

Fengyu Mountain's aid to Jinxiang Palace was given freely, from the heart — even given the chance again, it would help all the same. But if the Jinxiang women truly repaid that kindness with betrayal, the Tang Clan would show no mercy just to play the good guy. Long Xiang knew as much before she even asked, and felt helpless — there was no one to blame, only a heart full of desolate sorrow.

Long Xiang did not seem as cheerful as before; a thread of melancholy lingered between her eyebrows. One concern was about her martial sisters at Jinxiang Palace — if she could not decline the Wulin Alliance's request and was pushed onto the battlefield against the Tang Clan, how should she handle it then?

Long Xiang was hugely popular within the Tang Clan, yet she always felt a bit out of place. Knowing you were busy with many things, she didn't want to bother you carelessly. Seeing you head off alone to the back mountain, she followed after you, waiting until you finished your practice before speaking up.

To treat Ye Yunshang, the Second Senior Brother sent an urgent summons, recalling the delayed Junior Sister Tang Fang back to the sect. Tang Fang's entire set of skills was personally taught by the Second Senior Brother. Though officially referred to as brother‑sister disciples, their relationship was in reality more akin to master and apprentice. Though she was lazy and often late, in terms of medical expertise among contemporary female disciples, she was undoubtedly the best.

After you were beaten, you made the most of your situation by selling candied hawthorn. With your silver tongue, you turned ordinary candied hawthorn into a special medicinal dish from the Tang Clan, and the villagers believed it to be true, flocking to buy it eagerly. Not only were there verbal disputes, but intense conflicts even broke out, eventually escalating to the point where the authorities had to intervene to settle the matter. Later, Shangguan Ying heard about this incident and regarded you with newfound respect.

After you were beaten, they put you to good use by arranging for you to sell candied hawthorn. The villagers mostly recognized you and assumed you could no longer make it in the Tang Clan and had gone out to peddle wares for a living. Unable to help feeling for you, they all opened their purses to support your business. You made a small profit as a result.

After you were beaten, you had to make the most of the situation by selling candied hawthorns. Unfortunately, business was dismal; after all, the appearance of the seller was unappealing, which greatly affected people's appetite. In the end, to fulfill your obligation, you had no choice but to dig into your own pocket to buy some, giving them away to others to share, and returned home feeling dejected.

The conversation swerved sharply toward Shangguan Ying, veiled barbs plainly meant for her ears. Tang Xiaolou, trading on the prestige of her sect, had long strutted through Tang Clan territory unchallenged, but today she had finally kicked an iron plate. Who was Shangguan Ying? Roused to anger she was like the Hedong Lion's Roar—she gave no face even to her own fiancé Nangong Shen, and not striking Tang Xiaolou outright was already mercy; how could she spare a glance for a foolish village crone like her? Shangguan Ying strode up and met her head-on, fierce in bearing and sharp of tongue. Tang Xiaolou, all bluster and no backbone, was no match for her, and though she tried her usual tricks—throwing her seniority around, twisting words, throwing a tantrum—none of it did much good. Shangguan Ying raised a hand and slapped her, leaving her too stunned and too afraid to strike back. First, the four burly Cang Gang men at Shangguan Ying's side were no ornament; a fight would only cost her dearly. Second, she had genuinely slandered an official with witnesses present, and with officials shielding their own, taking it to court would end badly for her. Third, she truly feared the Shangguan family and had only meant to test its limits with loose talk, never expecting to strike a buried thunderclap and detonate Shangguan Ying's fury outright. Shangguan Ying knew the jibes were aimed at her closeness with Ye Yunshang, suspecting some ulterior motive, so she simply laid it bare: the rumored treasure of King Yue, she had never once taken seriously—she scoffed at it. Even if the treasure truly existed, righteous wealth should serve righteous ends, to restore the homeland; she, a mere merchant, held no such lofty ambition, nor the shamelessness to claim it for herself. Outmatched, Tang Xiaolou rubbed her nose and slunk away in embarrassment. Whether she took it to heart hardly mattered—Shangguan Ying's confession was meant for another audience entirely. It had nothing to do with the Shangguan family's interests; her closeness to the two girls was purely to satisfy her own desire. The world only knew the Shangguan family's prized daughter as shrewd and capable, a woman among men, never guessing that beneath her tough exterior she was soft at heart, still harboring the same ordinary dreams as any woman: to marry a considerate, ideal husband, to wear splendid gowns, to keep cats and dogs in her courtyard, to adore glittering gold and silver, and to be utterly defenseless before anything small and exquisite. So it was that the instant she laid eyes on Tang Moling and Ye Yunshang, she couldn't help but fall for them, scarcely believing such lovely creatures could exist—finer than porcelain Mohele Dolls, sweeter than sugar figurines! She longed to seize them then and there, force them to take the Shangguan surname, and have them call her elder sister, so she could openly dote on them both, hugging their legs and kissing their cheeks every day, buying them bright new gowns to change into daily, all for her own delight—the very thought of it felt wonderful, sweeping every worry away; what need had she for that troublesome Suffering Fist? But then she thought better of it, fearing that if her true nature came to light it would damage her authority and leave her unable to command respect, and fearing still more that the two girls, frightened by her wild words and ways, would flee her for good—a loss on every count. So she kept up her composure, playing the reliable elder sister while staying close to them. Looking back now, Second Senior Brother's wariness of Shangguan Ying was well founded—only it was never King Yue's treasure or the Tang Clan's arts she coveted, but Little Junior Sister and Ye Yunshang herself. Now, before everyone's eyes, she tore off her mask, no longer playing the upright lady, seizing the two of them and refusing to let go, as if to swallow them whole on the spot. Little Junior Sister and Ye Yunshang nearly suffocated—only today did they learn that it isn't only those who hate you who can take your life; those who love you too much may kill you just the same.
She could only swallow her anger in silence, feeling for Yunshang's bitter fate, her heart aching in shared sorrow.

Tang Xiaolou, who styled herself an elder of the Tang Clan, showed the junior disciples no courtesy at all. She got straight to the point and pressed Ye Yunshang about the mystery of the hidden treasure, plainly disbelieving Ye Yunzhou's earlier account, and took it as fact that the rumored treasure was real—and since it had turned up in Shu, it belonged to the Tang Clan. Whether Ye Yunshang's illness could be cured mattered not at all to her; even if it killed the girl, her skin would still be flayed off, seared over fire and steeped in medicine to wring out the treasure's secret. Such words were as arrogant as they were cruel. Junior though she was, Tang Fang could not bear to hold her tongue and spoke up in protest, only to be scolded soundly by her Martial Aunt. Faced with the weight of rank and seniority, unwilling as she was to yield, she dared not push further.

Ye Yunshang spotted the candied hawthorn sticks on the street the moment she stepped out, shouting for one and enticing her junior martial sister into joining her in the act. Contemporary physicians believed that sweetness enters the spleen, and moderate consumption of sweet foods could nourish the spleen and stomach, but excessive intake could harm them, leading to impaired water metabolism within the body and the formation of phlegm‑dampness. Tang Fang had been assigned by the Second Senior Brother to treat Ye Yunshang, a responsibility she took seriously, and she genuinely hoped the young girl would recover. By all accounts, she shouldn't have given in, but she couldn't help it—she had promised the girl a snack for each needle, and now Yunshang was demanding candied hawthorn sticks. Not giving them would be hard to justify, especially considering how difficult it was to resist Yunshang's pitifully pleading gaze. Soon after, the two were separated, and Martial Aunt Tang Xiaolou approached Tang Fang for a word.

Tang Fang was assigned by the Second Senior Brother to give Ye Yunshang acupuncture. She felt a sense of responsibility and genuinely hoped that this young girl could escape the illness. As soon as she saw her suddenly receive so much sweet food, she was more anxious than anyone else. The doctor believed that sweetness enters the spleen; moderate sweet food can nourish the spleen and stomach, but excess is harmful. If she didn't know restraint, damaging her spleen and stomach could lead to the body's water qi being unable to transform, accumulating into phlegm‑dampness. Would that not be a mismanagement of her care? She wanted to stop her but feared Shangguan Ying's glaring gaze. She pushed you, who was worthless, to the frontline, hoping your heroic sacrifice would awaken Ye Yunshang's conscience. Shangguan Ying saw you suddenly appear and, without hesitation, deemed you a lecher and stalker, launching into a fight with you. The Cang Gang disciples simultaneously appeared to surround and attack you.

Put that way, but in truth you were not entirely blind to Second Senior Brother's deeper meaning. Given the Tang Clan's fearsome reputation—especially here in Meishan, where even ghosts and gods would give way—if there was a real threat to worry about, it could only be Shangguan Ying, whose intentions were impossible to read. What you feared most was that those four brawny escorts were not guards at all, but rivals.

Shangguan Ying first sent several Cang Gang disciples to drive away poisonous creatures and fierce beasts, then ordered a few more Cang Gang disciples to guard the rear. She walked hand in hand with her junior martial sister, Ye Yunshang, and Tang Fang, chatting and laughing all the way. You walked behind, secretly startled: this young lady's outing was indeed quite grand. These Cang Gang disciples were all skilled warriors, each muscular and strong, seemingly capable of taking on three of you. Who would dare provoke them? You had no idea why you had come along.

The junior martial sister turned to you, only to be sternly stopped by Ye Yunshang. Who let you boast without shame and interfere with her enjoying sweets? Meanwhile, Tang Fang watched helplessly as you were dragged by the arms and legs and beaten in the street, feeling a little guilty but mostly relieved, grateful it wasn't herself. She, Tang Fang, was the Tang Clan's notorious chronic latecomer. She had been so engrossed in the scene that she didn't notice the time until her former Martial Aunt arrived on the street, grabbing her by the collar and scolding her loudly. Only then did she suddenly realize she had forgotten the time, hastily trying to leave, only to be called back for questioning.

But your martial arts proved exceptional—you took on five at once, besting Shangguan Ying and her men in fine style. Yet this drew the notice of the authorities, and every constable in town was sent to seize you and throw you in jail. It only stood to reason: you had dared to beat a court official's own daughter in broad daylight in the street. If not you, then who were they to catch? Was there no law left in the Great Song? If they let this pass, would the Tang Clan next be trampling the yamen underfoot? After a few days locked up, Third Senior Brother pleaded your case to Shangguan Ying and had Squire Lu step in to mediate, even greasing the officials' palms, before you were finally let out. In the end, Shangguan Ying still had need of the Tang Clan; having already made you pay with a few meals in jail and vented her spite, she never brought up the matter again.

He then seized your current tasks and ordered you to follow from a distance. The esteemed Tang Clan's chief executioner, the Ruthless Young Master whom everyone dreaded, rolled up his sleeves, squatted in the kitchen, and grabbed pickled gourds and eggplants.
Even with Tang Fang travelling the same road and able to look after them, he still could not rest easy.
Even with Tang Fang making her rounds at the Outer Fort and able to look out for them along the way, he still could not rest easy.

It's no wonder Second Senior Brother fussed so; your Junior Martial Sister's history of mischief meant that the moment she stepped out the gate, everyone's heart was in their mouth. He also worried that Ye Yunshang, out and about, might overexert herself and trigger her hidden ailment, with no capable physician on hand to treat her in time.

On this day, the weather was clear and cloudless, not only a perfect time for outings but also an ideal opportunity to urge the junior martial sister to learn her way around. Thus, under the supervision of their sect's senior sister, Tang Fang, they descended the mountain together with the junior martial sister, Ye Yunshang.

On this day, the weather was clear and cloudless, a perfect day to encourage the junior martial sister to learn the way. Still worried about the sect's many affairs and lack of supervision, Shangguan Ying volunteered to step forward, taking the junior martial sister, Ye Yunshang, to the town for a stroll.

The Ye siblings hid in Shu not only to escape Diancang's pursuit but also to seek treatment for the Ye family's younger sister. Do not be fooled by the girl's lively demeanor at this moment; in reality, she harbors deep‑seated dangers. Each episode brings her to the brink of death, and despite visiting renowned doctors, her condition remains untreatable. Even the Second Senior Brother, well‑versed in many matters, nearly fell for the facade. However, when he subtly channeled his Internal Force to test her, the calm exterior shattered like paper. Beneath the surface lies a heavy crisis: prolonged illness has left her Qi weak, with evil energy overpowering the righteous. Her Dantian is weak, her Qi and blood are stagnant, the five elements are in conflict, and all six organs are damaged. Though it may seem dormant now, this affliction could kill her multiple times over; the next relapse would render even the most miraculous Spirit Pills useless. This condition is profound, and should it recur, even immortals would struggle to save her. The only way to survive is to take the initiative rather than remain passive. Although the Ye siblings kept their lips sealed, the Second Senior Brother already had an inkling. The regret from years past, born of weakness and inability to let go, has come full circle, and this time, he vowed to resolve it himself.

Since you have awakened, he no longer personally tended to your injuries, instead giving you a book on Qingcheng Internal Skill and urging you to practice diligently in hopes of recovery. During your time at Qingcheng with Tang Fang, you were treated as students, with your daily routines, lessons, and cultivation left to your own discretion. As for Ye Yunshang, although Qingcheng has never restricted female pilgrims from entering, she has a blemished record, so she was ordered to remain outside the Shangqing Palace to prevent her from devising further schemes to disrupt the Qingcheng disciples' cultivation and interfere with their spiritual path.
It's better dealing with those charlatans from the Flying Heaven Gate — at least they have some humanity, not much nobler than you, so they don't make you feel ashamed of yourself.

You wished to express gratitude for the life‑saving favor, but Shentu Long insisted on refusing, revealing an extraordinary sense of magnanimity. His radiant presence, glowing as if a celestial being, made you feel uneasy. His luminous image seemed to scorch your inner darkness; too close, and you would be reduced to ashes.

Secretly thinking this is the virtue a true cultivator ought to have — unlike that whatchamacallit Flying-Something Heaven-Something Gate, wanting to become immortal while having no virtue at all, blowing hot air all day long.
You wished to bow and express gratitude for his life‑saving deed, but Shentu Long insisted on refusing, demonstrating an extraordinary sense of magnanimity, leaving you deeply impressed.

Senior Sister Tang Fang finally came ambling over with a smile, explaining what had happened. At the end of the night battle, you had recklessly taken a palm strike from Nangong Ji in Ye Yunshang's place; he had only recently begun training in the martial arts of the Duan Family of Dali, yet even so, someone as insignificant as you stood no chance against him. Fortunately the sect leader was there and immediately sealed your acupoints with a hidden weapon to keep your organs from rupturing, after which Second Senior Brother placed more than ten needles to protect your heart meridian, and only then was your injury barely stabilized. That palm strike didn't kill you, but it forced the yin and yang energies inside you apart — drawn to and attracting each other when separated, clashing and repelling when brought together — and if the two could not be reconciled, it would cause endless trouble later. With Second Senior Brother's skill, curing this would have been easy enough: a few detoxifying herbs and pills, cutting off the root by ruining your Internal Skill, and the matter would be settled for good. But you would surely have resented him for it afterward, so rather than listen to you complain endlessly, he simply sent you off to Qingcheng for treatment, reasoning that the subtle, orthodox internal skill of the Qingcheng sect would be perfectly suited to harmonizing the yin and yang energies in your body. You were hurt on Ye Yunshang's account, and she was not made of wood — she had already been worried sick, and insisted on coming along no matter what anyone said. She wouldn't listen to reason, spat out any medicine they gave her, and deliberately stiffened her body to hinder the acupuncture. The sect leader had no way to manage her and had no choice but to send Senior Sister Tang Fang along to look after you both. Of the six great sects, the one closest to the Tang Clan, besides Songshan, was Qingcheng, bound by its followers' vow to aid the world and subdue evil, and by the bond of comrades who had weathered hardship together in the Jianghu. Shentu Long, having read the sect leader's letter and learned what had happened, personally channeled his energy to heal you, and within two or three days you had improved greatly and regained consciousness.

You and Yunshang, though you call each other brother and sister, are not actually siblings. She is already a young woman waiting to marry, a tender‑aged maiden whose childishness and innocence make her unaware of boundaries. You have no choice but to consider her. But every time you step back, she takes a step forward, as if afraid you'll vanish, clinging tightly, only crying, and you can't do anything about her.
Without warning, Ye Yunshang burst out, headbutting you in the chest. She burst into tears of joy, while you, filled with doubts, almost vomited them out.

He wanted to borrow your hand to check his pulse, but you weren't close acquaintances, so how could you agree? Unfortunately the gap between your strength and his was far too great; you struggled for form's sake, but were caught all the same.
He did not take your life, but left you trapped before Yunshang's grave, tormented by guilt for the rest of your life.

He didn't take your life, yet you feared letting the tiger return to the mountain, fearing a lifetime of anxiety. You struck when he was unprepared, using the deadly poison you stole from Second Senior Brother's alchemy room. Even if his skills were unparalleled, he couldn't escape death! Ye Yunzhou was indeed doomed, yet you remained careless, underestimating him. The fastest swordsman of Diancang could still send you to the afterlife before he breathed his last.

He wanted to borrow your hands to examine his pulse, but you weren't close friends. How could you agree? In resistance, you unleashed an unjust divine destruction technique, knocking Shentu Long back. Just then, Ye Yunshang approached, and Shentu Long used the momentum to dissipate the remaining force, channeling it entirely into Ye Yunshang's body. Ye Yunshang was already delicate and frail; how could she endure such an unforgiving strike? She bled from seven orifices, her meridians split, and her life faded away. From afar in Jiangling, Ye Yunzhou heard the news and was overwhelmed with grief, disregarding all etiquette and propriety. Returning to Shu, he found his sister already separated from him by heaven and earth. Only you stood at her grave, lowering your head to accept death. The Listening Cloud Sword in your hand was picked up and then put down, finally returned to its sheath. Though sorrowful, you thought of your sister's life spent in torment; her passing was a kind of liberation. You had once saved her life, and now you repay her. The Ye siblings owe you nothing from now on.

You step outside and are momentarily stunned. Leaning against the grand Daoist temple and looking out into the distance, you see magnificent mountains, deep and lush forests, and ancient, verdant trees — Mount Emei's scenery, while far from poor, seems humble beside this. While you're still marveling, a young Daoist slowly approaches and introduces himself: Shentu Long, Junior Brother to Sect Master Zou of the Qingcheng Sect, known in the Jianghu as Daoist Yichen. You're still unclear on what's happening, and hearing this only deepens your suspicion — this Daoist looks quite young, and though his face is refined and his manner gentle and cultured, with the air of an otherworldly master, Qingcheng has no shortage of talent, so it seems hard to believe this young Daoist could be acting head of the sect.
Finding nothing worth taking only makes you feel cheated, and grumbling the whole time, you spit on the ground.
Being of such a despicable character, you rummage through everything, since there's no one around; as long as you steal without getting caught, you feel not the slightest shame.

Perhaps you were simply exhausted; this time you fell into a long dream you couldn't wake from, and dared not wake from either. In the dream you finally resolved to leave home, join another sect, and vowed to master martial arts and roam the Jianghu, until one day your name was made and those who once looked down on you would think again. But that fervor, like your youth, was spent for nothing. Born with this face, you were doomed to amount to nothing wherever you went. Years wasted, driven out again and again, drifting from place to place. However vast the world was, none of it was ever home. You woke in tears, unwilling to accept it, and once your dazed mind had settled, you looked around and saw that, indeed, this place was not your home.

Second Senior Brother arrived, his face clouded with displeasure, his gaze cold and piercing as a chill blade laid against their throats. Recalling his nickname in the Jianghu, they all fell silent as cicadas in winter. As he recounted each man's background one by one, this band of Greenwood men turned the color of ash — for the Tang Clan's narrow-mindedness was known to all, and even the smallest of grudges would be repaid no matter how far the offender fled. Their names and homes had all been traced, and there would be no escape for their whole families. Thinking of this, sorrow welled up in them, and these heroes, hardened by decades in the Greenwood, all broke down in tears. Seeing them weeping, Second Senior Brother grew even more impatient and barked at them to stop before he finished speaking. Though the four were thieves, none were beyond redemption at heart, and most had turned to banditry only because circumstances forced them to it. Your Eldest Senior Brother, on hearing of their reputation, had visited each of them once, yet only robbed them of money and never took their lives — proof enough. This attack on the Tang Clan, though unpardonable, had failed and caused no deaths, so the Sect Leader chose to show mercy and deal with them leniently. They were ordered to leave the mountain at once, their heads still on their shoulders, with a year's grace to see their families settled. On this same day next year they were to return to the Tang Clan to face death; those who remained incorrigible would have a Kill Order proclaimed to the Jianghu. On hearing this, they were overcome with mingled grief and joy, scarcely able to believe Old Demon Tang would show such mercy. Even freed of their bonds they dared not relax, and hurried out of the Tang family compound with hearts still pounding, walking faster and faster until they were certain they had truly escaped death — only then did they breathe a sigh of relief, and with one accord they turned to bow and kowtow toward the Tang Clan, grateful for the Sect Leader's mercy, their old grudge now settled.

After Second Senior Brother explained, you learned that this small sword's origin was no simple matter — this ancient Tang Clan Small Sword had been passed down to the Sect Leader from the previous Sect Leader, a weapon used to make his name across the Jianghu. Its forging method is lost, and it is without equal, the only one under heaven; though not a token of office for the Sect Leader, it has always been passed down together with the Sect Leader's token and the Blood Jade to the new Sect Leader, generation after generation, worth a hundred times more than your own life. All your grief and despair vanished at once — you weren't unvalued after all — and as you carried the heirloom blade around to show it off, the more senior the brothers and sisters were, the more astonished they became. Carried away with pride, you clean forgot about ever having run away from home.

You were stunned and at a loss, thinking perhaps the small sword in the box was coated with some miraculous poison, which had caused the senior brothers' attitudes to shift abruptly. You took it out and licked it, and it was exactly then that Second Senior Brother caught you. He was furious beyond measure, wanting to kill you on the spot.

You were taken aback and carefully examined the small sword hidden in the wooden box. You could only feel that the craftsmanship was exquisite and the style was ancient, but beyond that, you couldn't discern anything else. You also didn't understand why your fellow brothers changed their expressions drastically upon seeing it.

The Sect Leader finished questioning them, dismissed the disciples, and kept you behind for a proper word of praise. Your heart raced with nervous excitement, but to your surprise the Sect Leader merely handed you a wooden box and sent you on your way. Crestfallen, you assumed it must be money inside, and wandered back to the disciples' quarters in a daze. Your fellow disciples guessed you must have earned great merit this time and would surely be allowed to change your surname and formally become a proper disciple under a master, and they were all happy for you. Seeing you cradling the wooden box, they took it for a nameplate and clamored to snatch it open — the whole room instantly fell silent, everyone struck dumb, and they respectfully handed the box back to you.
As for Nangong Ji, he wasn't so lucky. Even without questioning who was behind it, some unlucky soul had to take the blame, so Second Senior Brother could torture him to vent his anger.

As for those mercenaries disguised as the Mud Cult and Nangong Ji, they weren't so lucky. Even without questioning the mastermind, there had to be a misfortunate soul to take the blame and let the Second Senior Brother torture them for venting.

You heard that the bandits who had caused trouble last night were actually let go and sent down the mountain by the Sect Leader, and at first you couldn't believe it. Such lenient handling was nothing like the Tang Clan's usual way, and though uneasy and unsure, you dared not question the Sect Leader's orders.

They took advantage of the four having no weapons and being shackled with cangue and fetters, utterly unable to fight back, and set upon them with fists and feet, beating and abusing them at will to vent their anger. As the saying goes, a wise man knows not to fight a battle he cannot win, and petty men are hardest to cross of all; the four finally quieted down, falling silent in sullen resentment.
You've never been short on baseless insults hurled your way. You just shrug it off, not caring in the least.

These people just repeat the same green forest tactics, nothing more than cliched phrases. How could they compare to your strong mouth power, tailoring your approach to strike where it hurts, insulting with creative flair, and not forgetting to sow discord. It's enough to make the opposing group face red and necks flushed, desperately wanting to tear you apart.
But there are four of them, four mouths against you—how can you possibly be a match for them? Every sentence you get out is answered fourfold. You gain nothing, only work yourself into a fury.
You refused to yield, quickly countering with a sharp retort.
Your composure is so poor that a few words are enough to make you stamp your feet in fury.

These bandit leaders came from all over the country, not just for wealth, but also harboring resentment against the Tang Clan. They had thought you were an ally in their shared enmity, but now they realized you were actually a spy within the Tang Clan. Seeing you now, their eyes bulged with fury. With their lives already forfeit in your hands, they resolved to curse you without restraint, spewing curses as filthy as they could, from your ancestors to your descendants across eighteen generations, greeting each one. They cursed you to be born with no bottom.

You'd worked all night and still got complained about for smelling bad; you'd just come off shift to wash up and sleep when someone dragged you out of bed again to cover for them. With no choice, you went down to the cellar to watch over the bandit leader in his place.
You didn't even forget to plunder during the turmoil while on duty, methodically sifting through their belongings for valuables, all while acting with unwavering justification.
The night of chaos had passed, and dust settled. The Tang Clan's courtyard was littered with bandits‑some with broken legs, others poisoned, crying out in agony.

When Second Senior Brother saw you return, he was not as stern as you had imagined. Although it was despicable to flee at a critical moment, bringing back the missing Junior Martial Sister to the Tang Clan was also a significant contribution. The merits and demerits balanced each other out, so it wouldn't be appropriate to hold you accountable. Third Senior Brother was even more delighted to see you, pulling you into the Zhengxin Hall to greet the Sect Leader and summarize the events of last night.
When you escorted Junior Martial Sister back to the Tang Clan, it was nearly noon. As you watched her prepare to depart, you couldn't help but feel a pang of melancholy.

Back at the Tang Clan, it was nearly noon. Ye Yunshang was delicate and frail, unlike you martial artists. After a night of constant anxiety, she had already exhausted her stamina, and as you walked she started dozing off. Counting on your reluctance to ignore her, you all dragged her along for the second half of the road, until she'd all but finished it with her eyes closed. As you watched the two of them grow distant, a pang of loss stirred within you.

The Sect Leader is here; how could he allow such reckless behavior? Secretly channeling Internal Force into the chess piece between his fingers, he snapped his finger, and the small chess piece shook violently, sending Nangong Ji staggering back several steps, his eyes rolling back as he fainted on the spot. Second Senior Brother dragged you into the Zhengxin Hall, hurriedly apologizing for his negligence and the disturbance caused by the petty criminals. The Sect Leader's face remained as usual, as if the person had come in on their own and lay there, unrelated to him. He merely waved his hand, sending you out to fetch a rope, and instructed Second Senior Brother to interrogate thoroughly.

Ye Yunshang saw you standing there blankly, eyes clouded, ready to collapse at the slightest touch, and couldn't help but be greatly alarmed — it turned out your Internal Injury was so severe that you had already fainted on your feet.
Your internal injuries were severe and your mind grew hazy, but you forced out one last bit of bravado before collapsing rigid to the ground.

The Sect Leader saw him so indifferent to others, not only ignoring his attack that injured him, but also standing in a horse stance to cultivate energy. Enraged, he couldn't help but laugh bitterly. If not for the Tang Clan's reputation and the deep ties with the Nangong family, he would have been too lazy even to capture and interrogate him, let alone tolerate such improper behavior. He fired two projectiles: one struck the acupoint to block blood flow and prevent Internal Injury from bleeding; the other struck the opponent's acupoint, disrupting his energy flow, causing him to disrupt his cultivation, injure his meridians, and collapse to the ground.

Ye Yunshang usually carries on without any restraint and seems to have no conscience at all, but she is not, in the end, an ungrateful person. She has quietly kept your kindness in her heart, and when it truly mattered, she was just as willing to risk her own life to repay your care.

The sect leader appeared calm, yet was confident. He secretly channeled his Internal Force into the chess piece in his fingers, and with a mere flick of his finger, he could secure victory. Just as the words were spoken, the moment arrived swiftly. Suddenly, someone dashed out from the side, using their body as a shield, blocking in front of Ye Yunshang and precisely intercepting the hidden weapon's trajectory. In an instant, Nangong Ji shifted from grasping to palm striking, intending to kill the intruder on the spot; meanwhile, the sect leader skillfully adjusted his technique, redirecting the hidden weapon in a curved path. The chess piece, mid‑air, circled half a rotation, striking Nangong Ji's Neiguan acupoint on his wrist, causing his Internal Force to momentarily stagnate. Though the palm strike's power was significantly weakened, it was still not something the intruder could easily withstand. A bitter taste filled his throat, and he spat out a mouthful of fresh blood. Though the sect leader had used a last‑minute palm strike to injure the opponent, the mere fact that this lowly attendant, under Nangong Ji's palm, had not died and dared to speak defiantly enraged him further. He immediately channeled all his power, intent on killing the intruder on the spot.
Nangong Ji rushed into the Zhengxin Hall, appearing mad, not even glancing at the Sect Leader, his five fingers spread wide like a basket and lunged at Ye Yunshang.
And you have always been worried about Ye Yunshang's safety; upon seeing the situation, you didn't say a word and rushed into the Zhengxin Hall.

One bandit after another fell, yet the house servant stubbornly refused to accept defeat. However, the facts were clear: surrounded by enemies, the situation was dire, leaving them with countless thoughts. Nangong Ji, gifted with extraordinary talent and sharp intellect, stood out among the younger generation of the Nangong family. Trained by the clan elders since childhood, they were recommended to the family head. Believing that such an outstanding talent would surely win the family head's favor upon arriving at the Nangong estate, they dared to dream of being adopted as a son and achieving great success.  Little did they know that things would not go as planned; they were dispatched to serve the overlooked Second Young Lord, Nangong Qian. In that moment, Nangong Ji felt as if the sky were collapsing. They could not understand how they had angered their master. A person of such talent was treated so poorly, filling them with indignation and grievance. Unable to complain to the family head, they instead directed their resentment towards Nangong Qian, not only mocking them daily but also spreading gossip behind their back, further inciting disdain for Nangong Qian throughout the household.  As Nangong Qian faced more scorn, their spirit dwindled, and they found it increasingly difficult to hold their head high. Meanwhile, Nangong Ji, feeling frustrated by their unrecognized talent, became deeply confused and even took leave to the Apricot Blossom Forest, sincerely praying to seek guidance from the deities. Perhaps sincerity brings results; soon after, they obtained a Brocade Pouch and encountered Young Lord Duan, who had come from Dali, igniting their desire to pledge allegiance.  This time, hiring bandits to raid the Tang Clan under the guise of the Nangong name was entirely Nangong Ji's plan. Besides seeking revenge on the Nangong family and tarnishing their reputation, there was a secondary objective: to seize Ye Yunshang amidst the chaos. Now, the plan to set fire to the Tang Clan had not only been exposed, but their hidden strength had yet to be revealed, and they had lost half their life to the traps set by these beasts, leaving them in utter disarray. If they did not find a way to remedy the situation, Young Lord Duan would surely blame them for their incompetence, and Nangong Ji's ambition to rise would turn to dust!  The more they thought about it, the more unwilling and indignant they became. Rather than live a life of servitude, they resolved to risk everything and muster their remaining strength, suddenly springing forth to strike at the Tang Clan female disciple, breaking through into the Zhengxin Hall.

As the enemies scattered, the Junior Martial Sister wasn't unwilling to chase, but you swiftly blocked her. Her legs kicked out, and she lost control mid‑air, colliding into your chest like a wad of cotton, blushing with embarrassment. The senior disciples all exhaled in relief; her Qinggong was exceptional, and without your timely intervention, no one could have caught up with her. If she got lost again, the group would inevitably have to search the mountains all night.
And the junior martial sister got lost. The senior siblings had to give up the pursuit mission and conduct a night‑long search of the mountain.

Alas, those ghost soldiers, beggars, and pirates were unyielding to both persuasion and force, escaping during the chaos, not only attacking people but also crossing their blades in a suicide‑like pose. The Tang Clan disciples, suspecting they had hidden reasons, feared harming allies and could only let them pass.

As long as the Tang Clan is well‑prepared, even if their main forces are not in Shu, this rabble cannot shake them in the slightest. The chaos gradually subsides, and the henchmen inevitably flee in the confusion. However, the leading figures are all captured in one fell swoop, making this campaign a significant victory for the Tang Clan.

Tang Clan disciples pursued them, finding the two factions engaged in fierce combat on the training ground. Knowing that these strange individuals were deliberately disguising themselves as members of the Demon Cult with malicious intentions, they did not waste any words and began fighting without discrimination, regardless of who was whom.

Tang Clan disciples pursued them out, the two factions on the training ground clashing fiercely. Although they suspected the Mud Cult members had ill intentions, the saying goes that the enemy of my enemy is my friend, so they immediately joined the fray, intending to first deal with the main enemy before maneuvering against the Mud Cult's strange guests.

The situation was unprecedentedly chaotic. Tang Clan disciples chased them out, stunned in silence, only to find themselves facing ghost soldiers, beggars, and pirates who had suddenly emerged and started fighting them. In the end, they couldn't stand idly by. The enemy of my enemy is my friend, so they joined the fray, intending to first deal with the main threat before engaging the unexpected visitors from the Mud Cult.

That group of villains didn't expect the Tang Clan to have precautions in place, so they ended up stealing chickens but losing rice, suffering a big loss. They were dirty and disheveled, unable to set fire anymore, and hurriedly fled. Fang Gang was about to leave when he collided with a strange man dressed as a Ghost Soldier. Both sides' forces met and both were stunned, and the battle was about to erupt.

Nangong family servants, posted to keep watch, saw you all absorbed in conversation and, patience already worn thin, came forward to hurry you along. You could hardly just wave them off, so, most unwillingly, you were once again marched up to the main courtyard. Just as everyone was dispersing to act, Second Senior Brother suddenly appeared and released a burst of poison smoke, instantly numbing several of the bandit leaders. Then, hearing Second Senior Brother's words of praise for you, they suddenly understood: so this fellow, who'd sworn brotherhood with them, was a traitor all along — deliberately luring them up the mountain just to wipe them out in one sweep! At the realization, they all flew into a rage, and with their ambush foiled, called out to their men to make one last commotion before fleeing.

They all thought it was no fluke that you were named in a Wanted Notice with your portrait plastered all over the city — after all, with your ugly face, you looked every inch the villain. It wasn't hard to imagine that, given time, you'd become a bandit chief notorious across the Central Plains, rivaling Fang La, Song Jiang, and Liu E in infamy, your name reviled for ten thousand years.

Why didn't you inform us before leaving? Where are your men and horses? Your martial arts aren't great, but you're good at sophistry. In an instant, you've already devised a plan. Be honest: your men are all with the Tang Clan. If you're pretending to be a reputable sect, why not be the Tang Clan? After all, the Tang Clan has many disciples. You might as well send all your men to become their disciples, openly study their martial arts, and eat their rice. On the day of action, it will be the day of betrayal! The crowd paled at the words. From when they first met at the Ruined Temple, they had thought you bold to impersonate a Tang Clan disciple in Shu. They never expected you to be so shameless as to send your men to become disciples. Such cunning and audacity have left these ruthless bandits who gather in the mountains and forests in awe and reverence.

Why did you leave without a word — where are your men? You couldn't come up with a decent excuse, but luckily your skin was thick enough that you bragged so convincingly even you believed it, declaring that you alone were enough. The men exchanged glances; they weren't entirely puzzled by where your confidence came from — who hasn't been young once? Everyone who walks the Jianghu has some fire in them; many a young hero, fresh out of the gate, thinks himself capable of anything, boasting he can take on a hundred single-handed. But the Jianghu is no game — the more reckless one is, the faster one tends to die. Once in a while some blessed soul survives and makes a name in a single battle, and most of those men happen to be handsome. Looking at your face, though, you seem the short-lived sort — ugly, and not even aware of it — this same day next year will most likely be your death anniversary. At the thought, the men all wore the same look of pity, and stopped trying to talk you out of it, only wishing you well silently in their hearts.

They asked why you left without a word, and where your men and horses were. Clumsy with words, you stammered without making sense — how could that not raise their suspicions? This was a matter of life and death, with no room for error, so they exchanged glances and moved together to seize you, torturing you without mercy. Unable to bear the torment, you told yourself you had already wasted ten years on your sect and now come to give warning, so your duty was done. Since you were about to leave and had no wish to throw your life away for the heartless Tang Clan, you confessed the whole affair along with your own misfortunes — less like a plea for mercy than a flood of pent-up grievances you couldn't hold back. Those men were greenwood bandits, men of no means but with some fire in their blood; hearing how hard your life had been, they felt for you. They wouldn't let you off lightly, but nor did they want to finish you off, so they broke both your legs and left you to fend for yourself. Gritting through the agony, you dosed the wound with a numbing drug and splinted your broken legs with branches. Fainting and waking from the pain again and again, you crawled down the mountain for help, and fearing the Tang Clan would come after you, you ignored your grievous injuries and fled like a hunted man, hiring a carriage to get far away, spending your life in hiding, forever on edge. Your legs eventually healed, but your pride had vanished the instant your bones broke.

You were on edge, fearing a confrontation with the bandits. Unfortunately, misfortunes never come singly; indeed, what you feared came to pass. Those travelers spotted a faint glow in the woods, approached to investigate, and caught you right in the act.

You've long been accustomed to eating and sleeping under the open sky, and after a night of toil, your body and mind are utterly exhausted, and you are sleeping soundly. Little Junior Sister approached silently and stood watching you for a while, yet you remained unaware. It was because of the fierce battle at the Tang Clan the previous night: the Tang Clan had been on guard, and the thieves failed to seize the advantage, their plan collapsing, and they scattered in all directions. Little Junior Sister, without hesitation, leapt to give chase, felling several before turning back in confusion, unable to recognize her way. She had rushed out too hastily to bring a lantern, and at home she would never have thought to carry a fire striker in her pocket. Wandering the pitch-black forest by faint moonlight, feeling as though ghostly shapes lurked about her, she grew afraid. She scraped the bark off tree after tree to mark her path, but still couldn't tell her way. In the end she did as Eldest Senior Brother would, leaping up into a tree to nap against a thick branch, and only climbed down to walk once dawn came. Partway along, she spotted you lying on the ground. She was both startled and overjoyed, silently marveling at fate's strange twists — it seemed that every time she was lost and helpless, you would step out of the darkness and lead her home. Though you had already made up your mind to leave, you couldn't abandon her, so you had to break your promise once more.

You've long been accustomed to living in the elements; after a night of hard labor, both body and mind exhausted, you slept soundly. Little Junior Sister and Ye Yunshang crept up beside you, yet you remained completely unaware, until Ye Yunshang unfeelingly prodded you awake with a stick. Seeing you leap up in a sudden fury, they couldn't help but look pleased. Last night's fierce battle at the Tang Clan had been anticipated, and the villains, failing to seize the advantage, scattered and fled in defeat. Little Junior Sister, without hesitation, flew after them, knocking down several before turning back in confusion, unable to recognize the way home. She had left in such a hurry that she hadn't even brought a lantern, and at home, she would never have thought to carry a fire striker in her pocket. As the forest lay pitch black, seeming to swarm with ghostly shapes, she couldn't help but feel afraid. Just as she was at a loss, she heard Ye Yunshang's faint sobbing and hurried toward the sound; the two of them wept with joy at finding each other. It turned out that the moment Ye Yunshang saw Little Junior Sister leave, she guessed she would get lost again and rushed out after her, only to trip, tumble down a low slope, and lose her own way when her lantern went out. Unable to find the way home, the two huddled together through the night. When dawn broke and they made out the path, they came upon you lying on the ground partway back, and were both terrified and grief-stricken, thinking you had died bravely fighting the thieves, never guessing you were merely asleep. Though your mind was set on leaving, you couldn't abandon the two little sisters, so you took one by each hand and led them home.
You carefully and cautiously left the Tang Clan, managed to get by in an empty tea house for the night, planning to set off again at dawn.

You carefully distanced yourself from the Tang Clan, not forgetting to go back and cut wild boar meat, rubbing it with Red Cinnabar Sand salt to cure it for the journey ahead. You spent the night in an empty tea house, planning to leave at dawn.

You're well aware of Senior Brother's good intentions, but the road is too long, the night too deep, the heart too cold, and you can't go on. So you silently borrowed a lamp and walked alone down the mountain. Your senior brothers and sisters watched the lamplight recede, dwindling behind the tree shadows until it vanished, and only sighed quietly, no longer trying to stop you.

These thieves were dressed in Emei sect uniforms, yet they wielded the Five Tigers' Broken Gate Blade, a weapon every greenwood hero knew. Their skill was far inferior to true Emei disciples. You, along with Third Senior Brother and several other senior brothers and sisters, fought them with small swords against single blades, gaining the upper hand. As the battle reached its peak, each of you finished with a single kick, sending every last thief sprawling. At that moment, a deafening roar echoed, shaking the dust from the beams. The thieves seized the chance to flee amid the chaos and regrouped on the training ground.

By midnight, those thieves disguised as members of an orthodox sect indeed arrived as scheduled. Before they could rummage through the cabinets, your Tang Clan disciples emerged and engaged them in combat!

While organizing the mountain of documents, I discovered the sealed Collection of Origami. This book was originally entrusted by the Sect Leader to Fourth Senior Brother to bring back and present to Little Junior Sister. However, she became so obsessed with folding that she lost herself in it, wanting to fold every kind of pattern. After exhausting the colored paper, she still refused to stop, turning her mischievous ideas toward the secret manual, tearing pages to fold. After the incident, she was beaten half to death, and the book was sealed in the Scripture Hall, unseen for years. Now it has finally been passed down to you.

While sorting through the mountain of paperwork, he discovered the schematic diagrams left behind by Fourth Senior Brother's teaching master, the 'Master of a Thousand Ingenious Devices' Tang Ling. This hidden weapon was called the Fierce Fire Oil Pump, able to transform and spew flames - there used to be one each in the compound and the Outer Fort, both put to use for roasting meat. Now that the Martial Uncle has passed away and the craft is lost, no one left in the Tang Clan is truly skilled in mechanisms or metalworking - only you, being somewhat expendable, often tinkering away in the forge. So naturally, these schematics ended up in your hands.

While sorting through a mountain of documents, he discovered blueprints left behind by a senior of the Tang Clan - to his surprise, they were for armor made of paper. No one believed such a thing would hold up; forget blades, spears, and staffs, even a little rain could finish it off on its own. Who would dare wear it into a fight? Still, since it was a relic from a senior of the Tang Clan, it felt wrong to dispose of it carelessly. So, after some back and forth, it ended up in your hands.

After a single question, it was revealed that Third Senior Brother was concerned that petty villains might damage the classics, so he needed to carefully store the books in the building and lock them securely in the warehouse.
Seeing you return after going away, Third Senior Brother was both joyful and sentimental, indeed a mix of complex emotions.
Go to the Scripture Hall, and you'll see the Third Senior Brother and several senior brothers busily moving books around.

The Big Dipper Formation is indeed formidable, but these people are not skilled enough. They were also poisoned beforehand, and despite their numbers, they could not win against the few. Instead, they were defeated thoroughly. At that moment, a deafening explosion shook the beams, causing dust to fall from the ceiling. The thieves seized the opportunity to escape in chaos and reunited at the training ground.
Fortunately, you're not fighting alone. Tang Fang, who had gone to wash her hands and forgotten to come back, hurried in to join the fight and help you fend off the enemy.

You arrive at the alchemy room, and the moment you appear, you try to flee, but your thoughts are too optimistic. Second Senior Brother won't let you off easily. Even if you can't help, you must die on the ground, faithfully fulfilling the duty of a roadblock. By midnight, the bandits disguised as righteous men indeed arrive as expected, attempting to rummage through the alchemy room to steal the Spirit Pills and poison. Unaware that Second Senior Brother had already set a trap, they open the chest, and the poison smoke immediately spreads, instantly knocking out several of them. The Ruthless Young Master emerges from the toxic mist like King Yama come to claim lives, causing the crowd to feel a chill from head to toe. The leader's eyes flicker, realizing the secret has been leaked. This Ruthless Young Master must have been waiting by the stump for a rabbit; if they don't lure him away, their comrades will have no chance to escape. Thus, they declare they will set fire to the place and leap onto the roof to fight Second Senior Brother alone. The remaining mountain bandits, though their martial arts are weak and they are poisoned, can still overcome the odds with the Quanzhen Big Dipper Formation, which is truly effective.

It has nothing to do with your good or bad intentions. If you barge into the female disciples' dormitory without knocking in the dead of night, not being killed is already a stroke of good fortune for you.

You worried the enemy would take a detour through the back mountain path, but upon arrival, you found your Senior Brothers and Sisters had already set traps on the plank road. When the Earth Thunder went off, the intruders were either blown to pieces on the spot or sent plunging to their deaths.

By midnight, the group of thieves disguised as upstanding citizens indeed arrived as expected. Before they could loot, you and your senior brother, who was hiding in the shadows, launched hidden weapons to injure them.

By midnight, that group of thieves disguised as upstanding citizens indeed arrived as scheduled. You were so impatient you couldn't sit still anymore, and without saying a word, you rushed out of the forge and kicked someone with a flying kick. The other party was caught off guard and was knocked unconscious on the spot.

By midnight, the group of disguised respectable thieves indeed arrived as scheduled. Tang Dajing was impatient as fire and could no longer hold back, bursting out of the foundry without a word to attack them. The thieves were caught off guard and were knocked out on the spot.

By midnight, the group of thieves disguised as respectable individuals indeed arrived as planned. You and Tang Dajing were impatient as fire, and couldn't wait any longer. Without a word, you both rushed out of the forge and started punching and kicking, catching the thieves off guard.
You arrived at the forge. The senior brother on watch duty was yawning; seeing you come, he felt a little reassured.
He has always believed in strength — whoever throws the bigger fist is in the right. He's the type who won't behave until he's been beaten. Now that you've beaten him, naturally he'll behave.
Thinking of Ye Yunshang's inhumane methods of tormenting people, your stomach gives a dull ache.
Thinking of Second Senior Brother's ruthless methods, your stomach gives a dull ache.
You just arrived at the forge, and the lazily inclined Tang Dajing once again wanted to get you to take his shift. As soon as he saw it was you, he immediately fell silent and said nothing.

You were told to go out to assist in defense and strive to show your performance, but this person who doesn't understand human speech kept going into the Disciples' Quarters, angering your senior brother. He didn't hold back his strength and ended up accidentally killing you.

He shaved his head bald, disguised as a Songshan disciple, and was indeed practicing the Luohan Fist of the Songshan Sect, a style characterized by its open and expansive movements, formidable power, and robust physique — a truly tough opponent to fight. However, he lacked Buddhist cultivation and failed to grasp the subtle and profound essence of the Fist Technique, resulting in overwhelming force but lacking in composure. You saw through his flaw and captured him effortlessly. At that moment, a thunderous explosion shook the beams, causing dust to fall from the ceiling. The thieves seized the chaos to escape and regroup at the training ground.

By midnight, the bandits disguised as members of the righteous sects indeed arrived on time. Your plump senior brother was just about to descend from the sky with a dashing appearance, but unexpectedly, due to the long-standing neglect of maintenance on the roof beams and his excessive weight, he failed to take off. Instead, he broke the beam and fell down, landing right there and then as well, effectively taking care of himself and one of the bandits from Songshan. As the enemy was shocked and taken aback, disaster struck once more. Your plump senior sister also tumbled down, disposing of another bald bandit. Among the attackers who sought to assault Tang Clan this night, these three were the most skilled in combat. If it had been a one-on-one duel with swords and spears in broad daylight, it would have been hard to determine the winner. However, before any of you could act, two out of the three were eliminated, leaving only the remaining person furious that you had betrayed them, swinging a punch towards your face.

In terms of martial arts, these two senior siblings are naturally far more skilled than you. You were held down and forced to eat, saying 'no, no' with your mouth but chewing it thoroughly, never experiencing such a delightful punishment.

In terms of martial arts, these two senior siblings naturally have far deeper skill than you. Unfortunately, having eaten too much, the sudden violent exertion sent their stomachs churning — you struck them, and though unhurt, they threw up.
Then you joined the two of them in wrongdoing, acting without restraint and ate heartily.
After all, those two had the look of people who'd genuinely hit you. Between "eat" and "resist, get beaten, then eat anyway," you choose to eat.
After all, they're telling you to eat, not to do work. This kind of good opportunity is so rare that even with a lantern, you can't find it. Why not do it?
You didn't even need them to force you — you surrendered on your own.
You're refusing to yield, and those two still plan to resort to violence!

As soon as you arrived at the kitchen, you caught the senior brother and sister guarding the stored grain with their mouths smeared in oil — before the enemy could even ransack it, they'd already started eating it themselves. Since you'd caught them red-handed, if they didn't let you join in the wrongdoing, wouldn't you be holding evidence against them?

You and Little Junior Sister stood side by side, chatting idly. By midnight, a thunderous explosion shook the beams, sending dust down from above. It was likely the thieves had triggered a trap, giving away their position, and you and Little Junior Sister immediately went out to confront them.

You then chatted and laughed with Little Junior Sister and Ye Yunshang, the three of you together. By midnight, a deafening explosion shook the beams, sending dust showering down. It was likely the thieves had stepped into a trap, giving themselves away, and you and Little Junior Sister immediately went out to confront them.

You go to Zhengxin Hall to pay your respects to the Sect Leader and stay behind to help with the defense. The Sect Leader remains calm and composed, burning incense while holding a tea bowl and sipping slowly.

The sect's main forces have been sent far to Jiangling for relief, leaving the remaining disciples mostly female. Upon learning that bandits will attack tonight, though they are not afraid, they dare not be careless and have raised their spirits, preparing for battle. Every part of the courtyard is patrolled. Your senior brothers and sisters cannot let you sleep through the night carelessly, missing the divine opportunity to prove your worth.

You were overcome by poisonous smoke and finally got a long‑awaited good sleep, banishing the accumulated fatigue. Awakening from a deep slumber, you felt dazed and disoriented, looking left and right, only to realize upon opening your eyes that you were no longer in the cold Ruined Temple. After a moment's hesitation, you recalled that you had returned to the Tang Clan.

You were knocked out by the toxic smoke, yet ended up sleeping soundly for the first time in a long while, completely eliminating your long‑standing fatigue. In the midst of a deep dream, you were suddenly battered awake by a stick, startled to open your eyes and found Ye Yunshang pushing the murder weapon into someone else's hands, turning around with a deeply remorseful expression, constantly claiming she had no strength. Seeing you weren't deceived and her attempt to frame someone had failed, she stuck out her tongue and ran away.

The message delivered, old scores settled, you had no wish to see the Sect Leader again. With one lingering glance back at the Tang Family Compound, you turned to head down the mountain. Before you could even step through the gate, the Second Senior Brother suddenly struck with poison, scattering a handful of Ghee Sinew-Softening Powder. Caught utterly by surprise, you were laid out flat on the ground.

You hurriedly told the Second Senior Brother what you had seen and heard in the temple - that righteous sect members were preparing to attack the Tang Clan, and that on top of that, a band disguised as the Mud Cult was discussing whether to help the Tang Clan. But their behavior was suspicious and their motives unreadable; they likely came with bad intentions - their support was a sham, and their true aim was to frame the Tang Clan and turn the world against it.

You heard him say that and immediately felt relieved. Even during the fight, you had already sensed something odd - the two had clearly wielded forks, yet failed to use their weapon's advantage, instead closing in for close combat, pitting their own weakness against your strength, which was suspicious in the extreme.

You hurriedly told the Second Senior Brother what you had seen and heard in the temple - that righteous sect members were preparing to attack the Tang Clan, and that a band of Demon Cult men had also chased you up the mountain. Hearing your account and examining your wounds, the Second Senior Brother concluded at once: those Hell Path ghost soldiers had been impersonated by others. For the Hell Path hates heaven's injustice and has forsaken gods and buddhas, swearing never to enter a temple or bow to clay idols in life or death - so you could not have crossed blades with ghost soldiers inside a temple. What's more, your wounds bore none of the marks of the Hell Path's Fork Technique.
You hurriedly told the Second Senior Brother about what you saw and heard in the temple, warning that righteous individuals were preparing to attack the Tang Clan.

Second Senior Brother had spent years holed up in the Alchemy Room, studying poison arts, and rarely stepped out unless he had to - yet he quietly kept every coming and going in the compound in view. Though others thought nothing of your days-long disappearance, how could someone as meticulous as him not know there was more to it?

Tang Dajing trembled as he struggled to his feet, his face pale and grim. Used to bullying the weak and fearing the strong, he believed that avoiding a few renowned senior brothers would suffice, as the rest were easily manageable. He had always thought that daring to act recklessly within the Tang Clan was the way to go. But he hadn't anticipated falling into the hands of an outsider disciple, which left him both terrified and fearful. From then on, his behavior became much more restrained. Second Senior Brother gave a few more instructions before sending him away.

You knew the Second Senior Brother was using you to punish this man, and dared not casually plead for him. Only once the Second Senior Brother judged the lesson enough did you play along, staging a show to end it and pardon Tang Dajing.

You knew that the Second Senior Brother was using you to punish this person. But seeing his terrible condition, you felt genuinely unable to bear it and spoke up to spare him. The Second Senior Brother was surprised by your feminine mercy and couldn't help but show a look of displeasure. Without making a sound, he flicked his sleeve, and Tang Dajing's condition eased.

The Second Senior Brother crossed his arms, watching coldly. Tang Dajing, seeing him not move, assumed he was deliberately indulging him, and his punches grew more unrestrained. Yet the Second Senior Brother wasn't simply not moving‑he didn't need to. His poison techniques were so refined they bordered on the supernatural; why would he need to flick his wrist or wave his sleeve to poison this brute? As the fight continued, Tang Dajing gradually felt something wrong with his body. First, he couldn't exert force, then his vision blurred, making him see multiple reflections. Next came an itching and pain that spread throughout his body. Even his sluggish mind eventually noticed something amiss, and he rolled around on the ground, scratching and clawing, but couldn't rid himself of the bone‑eroding itch. Finally, he begged for mercy.

In terms of martial arts, you might not necessarily lose to Tang Dajing, but first, you had run up the mountain and hadn't caught your breath yet; second, this man possessed incredible brute strength, fighting with the Cang Gang's wide-swinging blade technique, utterly unlike the Tang Clan disciples, catching you off guard; third, he attacked without warning, striking immediately, forcing you to defend, which put you at a disadvantage, letting him land several free punches on you. You had come up the mountain with good intentions to deliver a message, only to be met with such treatment, filling you with grief and anger, burning with the wish to fight to the death here. Just then, the Second Senior Brother suddenly appeared, cold-faced as ever, yet it was you he helped.

You came to report the news with good intentions, but received such treatment. The frustration was too much to contain, so you picked up the person again, raised a palm but hadn't slapped yet, when the Second Senior Brother immediately stopped you.
