However, he overestimated his own skill and underestimated you - you could have beaten him without even catching your breath, and with a single backhand blow you sent him sprawling on the ground.

You still needed to find a fellow disciple to explain things clearly before taking your leave, hoping to hurry back to town before nightfall, but trouble arrived first. That Tang Dajing ran with the Cang Gang and had always acted wild and lawless; back at the Tang Clan he fell right into his old habits. The moment he spotted you, an outsider disciple, he lit up with the thrill of the hunt. All he needed was some pretext to beat you up, take you as his little brother, and have you serve him from then on while he ate and drank first - wouldn't that be delightful?
Returning to the Tang Family Compound, you can't help but feel a mix of emotions - sweet, sour, bitter, and spicy - indeed, countless feelings well up, for this is where you lived for years.

While ascending the mountain, I picked up the lost Junior Martial Sister on the way. As soon as we entered the courtyard, she suddenly remembered her assigned task‑to light the lamp before sunset, fearing her father's reprimand. In a flash, she vanished without a trace, leaving you unable to explain the situation to her.
Running all the way up the mountain, not daring to stop for a moment, you were so exhausted that you could barely catch your breath.
As soon as you escaped, you hurriedly rushed back to the courtyard to report the news.

You were anxious and dared not drink too much yourself, so you kept urging them to drink until they were half drunk, then slipped away on the pretext of relieving yourself, and hurried back to the courtyard to report the news.

At least it's your second hometown that has sheltered you for years; the Tang Clan is unkind to you, yet you cannot act unjustly. In the end, you could not remain indifferent, and despite your embarrassment, you went up the mountain to report the news.

Those who had never even met you hated you as fiercely as if you'd murdered their whole family, pressing you relentlessly and determined to have your life. Fury rose in your chest, and malice took root — since they meant to wrong you regardless, why not make the charge true? You poisoned and stabbed to death everyone who came to join in, looted them clean, and turned lone bandit, singling out handsome young heroes. The less it cost you, the more skilled you grew at it, until even ordinary commoners were marked for your blade the moment they looked too handsome. Years later, the renowned Constable Song Bei led Imperial Soldiers to surround and capture you; mortally wounded, you were trapped inside a tavern. With no way to escape and unwilling to submit to justice, you set the tavern ablaze and died there, refusing to go quietly.

Even if you win, better to spare them where you can — but those you defeat feel it as a loss of face and come back next time with reinforcements to challenge you again. A rumor repeated often enough becomes accepted truth, and though you'd done nothing wrong, you were branded beyond redemption. People who had never even met you hated you as if you'd slaughtered their whole family, gnashing their teeth, relentless, determined to have your life. Occasionally someone is kind to you, but far more despise you, resent you, and mock you for no reason. Malice is everywhere, even outside the Jianghu — that's simply how the world is. Disheartened, you sheathe your sword and retire, never raising a hand against anyone again, and live to the age of fifty.

You fear being caught in the crossfire — after all, the Tang Clan has been unkind to you, so why should you care whether they live or die? You packed up your things and hurriedly left the scene. Without the Tang Clan as your backing, the whole Jianghu is your enemy. Young Jianghu heroes hungry for fame prize nothing more than a lone, easy target like you. Whatever your character, your face alone is reason enough to die — kill you, pin some crime on you, and wouldn't the world applaud? Who would ever clear the name of someone like you?

At least it's your second hometown that has sheltered you for years; the Tang Clan is unkind to you, yet you can't act unjustly. In the end, you couldn't help but take action, and once you were free, you went up the mountain to report the news.

The two ghost soldiers had scouted the ruined temple from inside and out before summoning their companions to convene. You watched secretly, listened intently, and couldn't help but be surprised. From their words, it seemed these people had deliberately disguised themselves as Mud Cult ghost soldiers, beggars, and pirates, specifically coming to aid the Tang Clan in defending against enemies. You hoped they'd reveal more secrets, but the group, upon seeing the dead body on the ground, felt uneasy and considered it an ill omen. After talking for a while, they moved to another location for a secret meeting.

You fought two opponents, managed to get away with it by luck, only to find out they were more than two. They called for a group of pirates and beggars to chop you into minced meat with their blades. You turned pale with fear, not stupid, so you ran away. Whether it was luck or misfortune, those bandits had planned to drink and indulge in debauchery, making a blood oath. They wanted to get you to bleed, but couldn't find you. Turning back to search, they just happened to save you. The ghost soldiers, beggars, and pirates had a major plot. They thought you were just a common fish in the Jianghu, insignificant, and pursuing you would only alert others. So they let you go back to the mountains. Alas, you had just escaped the wolves' jaws, only to be dragged by a group of Greenwood heroes to drink.
You couldn't dodge, and didn't intend to — you drew your weapon and met them head-on.

Your Qinggong has already reached a modest level of mastery; you immediately flipped and flew up onto the roof beam, holding your breath. Seeing the two ghost soldiers below, deeply suspicious, jabbing an iron fork at the corpse on the ground, you couldn't help but silently sigh in relief — glad you hadn't made the rash choice to lie down and play dead instead.

Your forehead was glistening with sweat, yet you remained composed. The ghost soldier first stabbed the person beside you, then raised his fork to strike at you as well. But he still harbored some reverence for the spirits, recalling that the dead should be respected, especially within a temple where desecration would be unthinkable. He hesitated and let it go. You let out a great breath of relief, remaining motionless, yet your heart felt as though it would burst from your chest.
You, with great patience, observed the situation develop, and so you were impaled to death.
You couldn't possibly wait to be defeated; you immediately turned over and rose, fighting fiercely against the two ghost soldiers.

Just as you had made up your mind, you heard voices again. You quickly lay down on the ground and pretended to be a corpse. This time, two oddly dressed people with long forks came. Their attire was such that anyone could immediately recognize their identity — indeed, they were none other than the infamous Hell Path Ghost Soldiers of Western Shu. The two ghost soldiers saw the two corpses on the ground, looked at each other in astonishment, but then thought it made sense. Why wouldn't they? With one in blue and the other in green, you two Tang Clan and Diancang disciples dying in a chance clash was nothing unusual. To be safe, they still stabbed the corpses a few times to make sure no one was pretending to be dead and eavesdropping on their secret conversation.
You didn't rush to make a decision, calmly thought about it for a moment, but you had mixed feelings toward the Tang Clan, and after pondering, you still couldn't find an answer.

One after another, more people arrived. This time, without hesitation, you recited first: 'In the mountains, ink-boned scholars are fragrant with books; on the flower streets, brocade-clad men reek of copper.' Hearing this, their suspicion faded, and they smiled and replied: 'Highbrow and lowbrow alike share this starlit sky, I only regret there are not years enough,' taking you for one of their own. These people wore the attire of righteous sects, but their talk marked them as outlaws banded together in the mountains, intending to unite and strike the Tang Family Compound while Jiangling was in chaos and the Tang Clan's elites were away. And the mastermind behind it all was none other than Nangong Xiu, a Young Lord of the Nangong Family who wore no pauldron! After they finished talking, the Greenwood leaders arranged to drink together. You were still racking your brains for an excuse to slip away, not realizing you'd overthought it — they had no intention of bothering with you at all. Being shunned had nothing to do with right or wrong; even among the Greenwood, you were the least welcome sort.

Then one after another, more Wulin people arrived, all dressed in the attire of righteous sects. You didn't realize it at first, missing fate's lifeline that was thrown your way, because you interrupted someone's secret meeting and brought upon yourself a deadly fate.

You vaguely discerned that this person's martial arts school was not like that of a Diancang disciple. The moves were correct, yet they lacked the essence of the Diancang disciples' swift sword techniques, as if a master from another sect had deliberately imitated them.

You fought with that person for a while, gaining the upper hand, but he seemed unwilling to stop, determined to fight to the death. Fortunately, a snake bit him, and the poison took effect. He collapsed on the spot, foaming at the mouth, and died within moments.
You fought that person for a while but fell behind. Fortunately, a snake darted out and bit him, the poison taking effect. The man collapsed on the spot, spitting white foam, and died within moments.

You were staying in a Ruined Temple when suddenly a Jianghu person dressed in Diancang attire appeared. Without saying a word, they recited a poem: In the mountains and forests, bones bear the scent of books; on flower streets, fine clothes carry the stench of copper. Before you could react, they inexplicably drew their sword and attacked you!

You readily agreed, and the old monk was very pleased. He made a pact with you, saying that when peace reigned in the Jianghu, the world was tranquil, and the time came when you wouldn't need to sacrifice yourself, you would then go to Songshan to study. He took out a martial arts manual from his robe and handed it to you. Upon careful inspection, it was the highest martial arts technique of Songshan, Nayuta Kalpa Finger. You were stunned speechless, thinking he had grown old and confused, how could he pass down Songshan's secret art to an outsider like you? The old monk, though aged, was not confused. What he was passing down was not you, but the future great hero Zhao Huo, who would one day come to Songshan to study, achieving the virtues of precepts, meditation, and wisdom, and sacrificing himself to save the world. By passing this technique, he would not only save you but countless other virtuous beings. You were suddenly overcome with emotion, lifting the book above your head and bowing in gratitude to the divine monk. Only now did you understand why the Sect Leader had always been aloof and eccentric, why he alone revered the monks of Songshan. Realizing that Master Juexing's journey was specifically to meet you, once he had seen you, his wish was fulfilled. Whether or not to attend the Wulin Assembly was no longer important. The Songshan Sect and the Tang Clan parted ways, and the kind‑faced old monk walked alone back to his temple. The old monk never lived to see you come, yet he always believed in you. Good deeds are sown, need not be witnessed by me. Let the branches grow thick and leaves flourish, leaving a legacy for future generations.

Wherever you might study was fine by you, but you simply didn't want to become a monk—afraid that too long at Songshan, steeped in it day after day, you might be talked into taking vows without noticing. So you refused. Master Juexing only smiled faintly, did not press the matter, and departed, taking his grandnephew-disciple with him.

This old monk showed no pretension of a senior Wulin figure, appearing plain and humble. Yet his identity was that of the last remaining elder of the Songshan Sect, overseeing the Prajna Hall. Having heard of your story from Fu Yun, he has come to invite you to study at Songshan‑not now, but in the future, when Jianghu is peaceful, the weather is favorable, and the country is stable and the people secure. Whether or not that day ever comes, it is merely a simple inquiry into your willingness.

When you saw his face, your hairs stood on end, thinking he was the Thousand Faced Demon, the monk Wunian. But when you saw the old monk bowing with hands together, his gentle gaze lowered, with no trace of ill will, instead radiating great compassion and serenity, you suddenly realized: this was the true one, and the monk Wunian had merely disguised himself as this old monk.
Near Yueyang, you happened upon a monk from the Songshan Sect on the road. Before Fu Yun took his leave, he introduced you to an old Chan master.

Only then did your fellow disciples understand why you had staked your very reputation, fighting to block the road at all costs. Only by doing so could Sect Leader Zou truly take the words to heart. Had you not intervened, even ten more warning letters from Third Senior Brother would have done no good.

On the journey, you encountered the Qingcheng Sect. You longed to expose Shentu Long's true face, but you knew Daoist Zou would never believe your one-sided account—it would not reach his ears at all. So you could only drive the point home with your fists. After a fierce battle, Zou Bo finally sheathed his sword, both angered and amused that you had challenged the Sect Leader on the road, yet somewhat impressed by the nerve of this young upstart. Only then did he patiently hear you explain the whole matter. He had already received more than one letter from Third Senior Brother, and had thought this so-called Third Hero Tang was behaving disgracefully, hurling baseless accusations—too bothersome to deal with.

Along the way you encountered the Qingcheng Sect. You longed to expose Shentu Long's true face, but when you spoke, Sect Leader Zou's expression soured, and he did not believe a word of it. There was no common ground between you, and further talk was useless, so he flung his sleeve and departed.
Long Xiang heard that you were coming to Dongting and went out specially to welcome you. After months apart, she seemed to be chasing after something—her martial arts had grown even more formidable.

On the way, they encountered officials and Imperial Soldiers lined up to welcome them, causing the group to be terrified, thinking the imperial court was after the Tang Clan. Song Bei stepped forward, and you realized it was him who feared the Tang Clan had too many enemies, and to prevent ambushes by rivals on the way, he had specially called people from all over to escort them. Although the Tang Clan had a history of defying imperial edicts, they wouldn't provoke the court without cause and had never withheld taxes. Strictly speaking, they were law‑abiding citizens. With the current political changes, there's a clear trend towards reconciliation. After much consideration, you decided to be the first to accept Commander Song's goodwill and travel with the officials.

The heavens turned without warning; a sudden torrential rain caught you on the road, drenching the Tang Clan party in disarray. Fortunately a tea shop stood beside the mountain path, and you dismounted to shelter and catch your breath. You ordered a bowl of plain noodle soup, and eating it hot amid the cold mountain rain had a charm all its own; you felt content, warmed through in body and mind. But when the shopkeeper asked for payment, you reached into your pocket and found your purse embarrassingly empty, so you swallowed your pride and went to borrow money from Fourth Senior Brother. The other brothers, seeing this, thought Fourth Senior Brother had had a change of heart and was treating them all, and crowded round to press him further. Stingy as he was, Fourth Senior Brother also valued his standing with the others, and found himself caught between the two. In the end he gritted his teeth and covered the whole bill, buying goodwill and a bit of reputation besides. Life drifts like duckweed, with no fixed course; so let this moment of gathering be spent in unrestrained song. You and your fellow disciples gathered in this little mountain-village shop, eating noodles, drinking wine, and singing mountain songs, happy as could be. Even after you all part ways, this day will still shine bright in memory.

You and your fellow disciples clasped your hands in salute to the crowd of beggars, and no one raised any objections. One by one, you silently mounted your horses, letting this group of enemies of the Wulin go free. Though they were enemies of the Wulin, they were also your troublesome friends. The blue bastards had their own measure of things; they didn't just offend the beggars, but even dared to defy the entire Wulin, continuing to act as they pleased.

The Tang Clan encountered remnants of the Beast Path expelled from the Beggar Sect on their journey home. Many of them were familiar faces from the Dayi Branch. If they let these men go free, they might be branded lenient toward Demon Cult followers by their fellow Jianghu practitioners; yet to strike them down would seem a betrayal of righteousness. Fourth Senior Brother could not make up his mind, so you stepped in to decide for them.

She asked what had brought you there, and though she knew you were a guest, she had no heart to entertain you; she saw you off in haste, full of regret at having mistaken you for someone else. No sooner had you left than a busybody woman came into the shop and told her the rumor going around—that you weren't even human, but a monster in disguise that ate people.
The Kongtong Sect keeps the Flying Heaven Gate for the cultivation of immortality, devoted to offering sacrifices to Heaven and drawing talismans to ward off evil; the mountain folk all credit the Flying Heaven Gate with Kongtong's good weather. And Lei Qian, Sect Leader of the Iron Fist Gate, being an incorrigible old man, loved nothing better than scaring the young disciples with ghost stories in his idle hours—so there was not a soul in the Iron Fist Gate who didn't believe in demons and monsters, none more than Xiao Zhu. Recalling the whole affair, she grew more frightened still, and decided her mistake had been the work of your sorcery, coming to fear you from the bottom of her heart.
Back at the inn, you too heard of Xiao Zhu's Jianghu nickname, the Bone-Cracking Demon. Word had it she was monstrously strong, had once ruined a Senior Brother's future without effort, and could tear a fierce tiger apart with her bare hands and forge a blade with its blood—a ruthless one indeed. Having offended her, you feared you might be next to be torn apart and forged into a sword.
Hearing it all told so convincingly, you believed a fair part of it; the Jianghu holds no shortage of strange and extraordinary folk, and it is better to believe than not. The thought alone was enough to set your heart pounding.

She asked about your intentions for coming, knowing you are from the Tang Clan and have come to the Iron Fist Gate to study. This is why she readily introduced herself. It turns out that this Young Lady Yu Zhu, a Direct Disciple of the Iron Fist Gate under the Kongtong Sect, is also the owner of the Great Iron Workshop. You never would have believed such a delicate girl could handle blacksmith work until she demonstrated her powerful skill right there by bending a copper coin with one hand without any Internal Skill. You were so astonished that you blurted out an exclamation. Unless one has mastered skills like the Songshan Eagle Claw Technique, no ordinary person could exert such strength in their hands. Although she is a woman, she is stronger than you men when it comes to handling heavy blacksmith work; questioning her ability was truly ridiculous.
You were rescued, though you felt as if a bone had cracked, with a dull ache lingering. In front of the girl, you still had to put on a brave face. She saw you so sturdy and finally sighed in relief.
You were rescued, but the first thing you did was demand compensation‑how very direct of you.

You listened from the side, wary of him starting trouble, and the instant the Soul-Stealing Disciple stepped forward, you reacted at once, snatching back your weapon to block him and closing into combat. Being clearly the better fighter, you moved to press your advantage, but the young woman, anxious to save him, hauled you back from behind—and that single pull proved overwhelming, as though seized by an unimaginable force. It felt like being snatched up by a flying dragon and flung into the vast river of stars: you soared through the air as if riding cloud and mist, crashed into the shelves, and lay half-buried in the wreckage. The Soul-Stealing Disciple, though saved by her, showed no gratitude—he spoke with cold finality, flicked his sleeves, and stormed off.

Unexpectedly, as soon as she opened her mouth, she insisted that you accompany her to the blacksmith shop, inexplicably asking you to let her work on your weapons. With a look of delight, she exclaimed that she wanted to polish your blades for free. Just as you were feeling troubled, a member of the Soul-Stealing Gate, dressed in blue, burst into the forge with high spirits. His expression froze, and he became furious, claiming that this young woman was being unfair. She had promised to polish his weapons but suddenly changed her mind to prioritize you. Enraged, he fumed with anger, his mouth running non‑stop, carelessly hurling hurtful words.

A green‑clad young woman dressed as a blacksmith stood at the entrance of the blacksmith's shop. Though her eyes were half‑closed and her brows slightly furrowed, her expression was clearly displeased, staring at you intently enough to make your heart sink slightly. You didn't know where you had offended her. But you didn't need to know her or have a reason for being disliked‑this wasn't the first time you'd encountered such treatment.

At the blacksmith's shop door stood a green‑clad young woman dressed as a blacksmith, her eyes half‑closed, brows slightly furrowed, her expression one of displeasure. Yet she resembled a spring bamboo shoot newly sprouted in the forest, fresh and beautiful, endearing. Seeing this, you couldn't help but feel a stirring in your heart.
One day, you wandered idly to Iron Fist Lane on Kongtong Mountain.
On this day, as instructed, you arrived at Iron Fist Lane on Kongtong Mountain to report in, seeking a position to earn your keep.

When you finished your set and asked Xiahou Lan to critique it, she spoke without mercy, saying that if you went out into the Jianghu, you'd lie dead in the street before you knew it—words that stung you deeply. Yet when it came to teaching, she was no less thorough: rather than simply handing down set moves, she pointed straight to the flaws in your attack and defense, explaining them so plainly that everything suddenly became clear to you. This alone showed her insight into martial arts was no small thing—she was not only formidable in her own skill, but also gifted at guiding others.

Instead of using the secret techniques taught by the Soul-Stealing Gate, you improvised freely. At first you felt a bit ashamed, but soon you let your temper loose, striking out wildly, and found it rather satisfying.
Xiahou Lan saw that you were utterly unpracticed, yet you dared to show off with this technique anyway, and she couldn't help but frown.
Xiahou Lan observed that your techniques were still somewhat proficient and gave a secret nod.
Naturally enough, you unleashed the Shadowless Claw of the Soul-Stealing Gate.
You had indeed come to the sparsely populated Soul-Stealing Forest, to seek out your newly sworn Master Xiahou.

Back at the Tang Clan, you introduced your new bride to Third Senior Brother, who nearly toppled over backward in shock; and the countless Junior Brothers and Sisters who came running at the news all found their legs going weak beneath them. Everyone felt as though the world had tilted overnight - things they had always taken for granted were apparently not so certain after all. That the ice-cold first beauty of the Jianghu had taken you as her disciple was already outlandish enough, but that she should go on to marry herself off to you, an unremarkable fellow of no particular looks, was beyond belief. Such a scandalous breach of convention, in any sect but the Tang Clan, would have brought looks of horror and desperate attempts to talk you out of it.

You traveled alone back to the Tang Clan. Word of you had already reached the Jianghu ahead of your return, and Third Senior Brother came out especially to welcome you; seeing the weariness etched into your face, he hardly knew where to begin offering comfort. Your return greatly lifted the spirits of the Tang Clan's Junior Brothers and Sisters. You yourself might not have realized it, but you had already become a figure in the tales people told with relish. Bearing your master's hopes upon your shoulders, you had already surpassed your own dreams, and pressed onward toward a still farther future.

Xiahou Lan packed your clothes and belongings for you, but she would not travel with you, for she was burdened by her renown - the moment she showed herself on the road, challengers, suitors, and those seeking revenge would come without end, and with her Power no longer what it once was, she feared exposing her weakness and dared not act rashly. So she meant to stay hidden in the shadows, following silently at a distance, and she bade you walk the Jianghu with care on your own.
She simply could not bear to part with the house you had built; she lingered reluctant to leave for a long while, even thinking of at least taking down the plaque to carry away with her.

This time, when the return to the Tang Clan came up again, your wife no longer looked so mournful. As the saying goes, marry a chicken, follow the chicken; marry a dog, follow the dog - having married you, a disciple of the Tang Clan, she would naturally follow you there as well.

Xiahou Lan's manner toward you had changed entirely; one word from her - 'Zhao-lang,' my dear - was enough to melt you to the bone. She read your every expression and, knowing you loved her to the marrow, took great and quiet pleasure in it. Yet she was still older than you, and had once been your master; the weight of that old authority lingered. She quietly steadied her nerve, forced herself to stay composed, and explained that the suggestion had come purely from goodwill, with no hidden motive, hoping the Sect Leader would not hold her poor choice of words against her. Then, retreating in order to advance, she begged the Sect Leader to accept the precious ginseng, lest ill feeling grow between their two families. Unwilling to see her go home and face her father's reproach, the Sect Leader could only accept it reluctantly — yet not wishing to take so fine a gift for nothing, he asked Shangguan Ying to stay a few days longer, so that when the Second Senior Brother's elixir was finished, he could give her a few pills in return. Shangguan Ying secretly rejoiced that her scheme had worked — now she could stay on in the open, watching for her next opening to weigh the matter further. The situation still had room to turn.

Seeing that this could not be settled in a single stroke, Shangguan Ying retreated in order to advance, asking the Sect Leader to think it over carefully. And if he was to think it over, she would naturally have to stay a few more days — leaving the matter still open to a turn of fortune.

Fearing Shangguan Ying might push too hard and make things awkward, you advised her to proceed slowly. Shangguan Ying, ever sharp-witted, took the hint you gave her and reined herself in at once, quietly grateful to you.
You support the Sect Leader's decision.

The Sect Leader's resolve had wavered, but the matter was too weighty to rush — even to act on it, he would first have to burn incense before the ancestral tablets and seek their guidance; not the slightest recklessness could be allowed. And so he asked Shangguan Ying to stay at the Tang Clan's outer fort, promising an answer once he had thought it through carefully.

Little did she expect that you, this outsider disciple who looked like nothing more than a lowly servant, would meet her expectations after all. You had no grand, high-sounding arguments, only earnest sincerity — you were weak, and it was that very weakness that let you speak for every weak soul under heaven. Neither fame nor fortune could move the old hero of the Tang Clan's resolve, yet he listened to your plea as though it were a cry for mercy.

Little did she expect that you, this outsider disciple who looked like nothing more than a lowly servant, would exceed her every expectation. The moment you opened your mouth, your words rang out startling and true, laying out the greater cause with a conviction that struck home line by line — not only did the Third Senior Brother's eyes go red with emotion, but even the Sect Leader was moved, his stance softening. Shangguan Ying watched your profile from the side, unable to keep from feeling ashamed. She had underestimated you at first; now, looking at you again, you seemed like true gold hidden inside a rotten orange peel — a rare treasure indeed.

Unexpectedly, the Sect Leader flatly refused Shangguan Ying's proposal, saying that as a rough man of the countryside, he could not stand to be driven about by the Imperial Court. Seeing that the Sect Leader would not be moved, Shangguan Ying turned to the Third Senior Brother and asked him to persuade the man — but the Third Senior Brother deferred entirely to the Sect Leader's lead, and could only turn to you, though without much hope.

Even though you could find nothing wrong with it, you refused to let your guard down for an instant, still wary of the Shangguan family. Watching the Third Senior Brother lose his wits, useless at this critical moment, you thought to yourself: if the Sect Leader ever let himself be fooled, you would have to speak up and warn him, whatever scolding it might cost you.

You thought the proposal was like a windfall dropped from the sky. If one person attains the Way, even the chickens and dogs rise with him — once the Tang Clan served the Imperial Court, you, an outsider disciple, would walk tall wherever you went, with everyone scrambling to curry your favor. You couldn't help breaking into a broad smile.

Shangguan Ying paid her respects to the Sect Leader with the courtesy due a junior, addressing him as Uncle and presenting gifts — plainly working to win him over. After some conversation, she revealed the true purpose of her visit: she meant to buy up the Tang Clan's debts and forgive them outright! Such a staggering windfall left everyone present stunned, unable to fathom how such generosity could exist. Shangguan Ying went further still, offering to fund repairs to the Tang Clan's halls and to buy the Sect Leader a fine mansion in the capital, Lin'an Prefecture — all the Tang Clan need do in return was serve the Imperial Court, brewing poisons and forging weapons against the Jin, and they would share in the Shangguan family's wealth and glory.

As an outsider disciple, it is your duty to brew tea and entertain guests. However, Shangguan Ying claimed she was not accustomed to Shu region tea leaves, using this as an excuse to politely decline. You had no choice but to accept it. As for the true reason, only she herself knows.

You were a rough son of the Wulin — what did you know of the finer points of tea ceremony? In the past, serving the Sect Leader his tea had simply meant scalding the leaves with boiling water. Ordinary tea would have been fine, but what you ruined that day was tribute tea, reserved for the royal family and hardly ever available outside an imperial grant. When Shangguan Ying refused to drink it, her servant and you both grew heated, and the argument turned into a brawl. Shangguan Ying, stunned speechless and unwilling to let the matter grow into something hard to explain before the Sect Leader, gave the two of you a sound beating — for all her air of a refined lady, her fists were little softer than a hammer. Once the beating was done, the tension in her chest eased somewhat, and that you should be beaten by her hand almost felt like a rare kind of bond.

In this refined art, you, as an outsider disciple, had served tea to the Sect Leader in the Zhengxin Hall for years and had gained considerable skill. Though what you brewed could not rival a master's craftsmanship, it was still a rare treat for a weary traveler. Shangguan Ying secretly began to prize your talent, even considering taking you from the Tang Clan to serve as her own household servant, rather than let you waste your life away in these remote mountains.

In this refined art, you, as an outsider disciple, had served tea to the Sect Leader in the Zhengxin Hall for years and had gained considerable skill. With a little deft handling, you soon made Shangguan Ying look at you with new eyes, no longer daring to look down on you.
Shangguan Ying said she wasn't used to tea grown in Shu, and had her servant hand you the precious tea leaves and favorite cup she'd brought along, for you to brew.
You alone seemed lost in thought, unmoved by her beauty, and regarded Shangguan Ying with wary caution.
Unsurprisingly, you were one of them.

You met Shangguan Ying again, the second time since the Nangong family's longevity banquet. Her impression of you was deep, though not entirely favorable — after a moment's surprise, she turned and left coolly. You felt no urge to engage with her either, though the courtesy of serving tea to guests was still unavoidable.

You and Shangguan Ying met again, the second time since the Nangong family's longevity banquet. It hadn't been long, yet it was surprising that she still remembered you — though the look she gave you remained as haughty as ever.
Shangguan Ying first set foot on Tang Clan territory, relying on her beauty and eloquence, and with just a few words, captivated all the male disciples with her charming presence.

As they spoke, a disciple came rushing in, holding up a calling card — it was the sole daughter of the Shangguan family, one of the three great clans of the Wulin, come to visit. Third Senior Brother dared not slight so distinguished a guest, and at once sent someone to receive her sedan at the Welcoming Pine.
Fourth Senior Brother didn't bring you a gift; after all, no one cares about your feelings.
He hadn't brought you a gift this time, but hearing that Junior Martial Sister was overjoyed to receive colored paper, you couldn't help but smile as well.

You received a gift too, and it turned out to be a swordsmanship Secret Manual! Your heart leapt with joy — until a closer look revealed it was nothing of the sort, just a free exercise pamphlet the Quanzhen Daoists were handing out to spread their teachings. Truly, Fourth Senior Brother's aim never wavers.
You received a gift too — a full set of kitchenware that Fourth Senior Brother picked up cheap while playing peacemaker. From now on, you'll cook with far more ease.

Who would have thought that with you and your fellow disciples working together, the Tang Clan's finances would gradually turn around, the crushing debt melting away bit by bit. Fourth Senior Brother took the funds to repay Squire Lu, and while at it, picked up a few daily items to replace worn ones.
Outmatched, you charged in anyway and were knocked senseless for your trouble. Cleaning up after your reckless mess, Third Senior Brother, despite his years, was scolded to the point of tears.

You defeated the Accountant, then immediately used your Qinggong to pursue Lu Weng — only for Junior Martial Sister to drop from the sky, having set out after you yet arriving first, and block your path, urging you to give up the chase. Her face remained impassive, yet she had already resolved to sacrifice herself for the sect. Unable to bear letting this innocent girl shoulder the burden alone, you boldly vowed to clear the sect's debts and give her a bright future. Junior Martial Sister was quietly grateful, though she said nothing of it — afraid that if you failed to keep your promise, she would spend her life haunted by an unspoken thanks.

Upon hearing the whole story, Song Bei proved understanding and chose not to hold you to account, letting you off lightly instead. Taken by surprise, you felt a new spark of gratitude toward the Song Imperial Court. There was nothing more to be done about the matter now — you had to let it go.
In your panic, you spoke rashly and offended officials across the land. Fortunately, Song Bei was magnanimous and chose not to hold it against you.

You knocked down the Accountant, then immediately used your Qinggong to pursue Lu Weng — only to run into the renowned catcher Song Bei, who happened to be passing through on the trail of a criminal, and who intercepted you halfway.

You defeated the Accountant, and immediately used your Qinggong to pursue Lu Weng. However, the Accountant was not to be underestimated; he had anticipated this and advised Lu Weng to spend a large sum to invite several martial artists from the Wulin to stand guard, just to be safe. Indeed, the coins were well spent. You went from being the pursuer to being pursued. Fortunately, that group of Jianghu individuals aimed to intimidate you and did not wish to provoke the Tang Clan, so they did not pursue you deeply, allowing you to escape with your life. Having narrowly escaped, your arrogance diminished somewhat.

You went to such lengths to hide the truth about a trifling painting that you turned murderously ruthless — attacking and killing the innocent Accountant, then framing him for stealing the painting and fleeing. Guilty as you were, you filed the complaint first, threatening to report it to the authorities. Lu Weng, with no choice left, had to pay to make the trouble go away, hoping only to settle the matter quietly. Your actions spared the sect part of its debt, but also stirred up some ugly rumors.
In the end, the Accountant secured Third Senior Brother's approval and took the calligraphy he had written in his spare time as collateral. From now on, he would have to repay the debt in earnest.

You couldn't bear it any longer and flew into a rage, rushing at Lu Weng, only to be stopped by Third Senior Brother. Dashing out of the Scripture Hall, you gave chase again like a madman, until the refined gentleman, pushed beyond endurance, came to blows with you.

Although you spoke but did not act, your eyes blazed with fury. Third Senior Brother stood with you as well, and Lu Weng, seeing he could gain no advantage, left in a huff. But resentment festered in his heart. Next time he came again, a hard fight seemed unavoidable.

You and Third Senior Brother stood united against a common foe. Third Senior Brother took it upon himself to decline Lu Weng's invitation, which only left him enraged and humiliated, and the two sides very nearly came to open enmity. Lu Weng nursed his resentment in secret — when he came again, a fierce clash seemed unavoidable.

Your words exposed Lu Weng's scheming, upholding righteousness without arrogance, each word ringing with conviction, and you even quoted Confucius himself. Third Senior Brother silently approved, though he outwardly scolded you for being disrespectful to your elders. Lu Weng gained nothing and had to leave in disgrace, his anger festering within. He vowed to get even next time.

Having secured Third Senior Brother's guarantee that there would be no more leniency next time, Lu Weng was still unsatisfied. His eyes flickered with a sudden idea, his mind already made up. He softened his tone, mounting a charm offensive and inviting the Tang Clan's Great Heroes down the mountain as his guests — but in truth, his sights were set on Junior Martial Sister. Naturally, you refused.

A minor illness doesn't require a Master Healer of the Nation. The reason the famous doctor hired by Lu Weng with a heavy bribe failed to cure him was simply because he was too wealthy. The Second Senior Brother treated Lu Weng's chronic illness without hesitation, not for coins but to destroy the unscrupulous doctor's secure position. Grateful, Lu Weng voluntarily reduced part of his debt.

Having secured the Third Senior Brother's assurance, they agreed that there would be no more leniency next time, but Lu Weng was still unsatisfied. He then approached the Tang Clan to request the Spirit Pill.
You had no choice but to force down your anxiety and try to distract yourself. You pulled over a stool and read a book at random.

You accompanied the accountant in touring the Scripture Hall's collection. He skipped over any suspected martial arts secrets, instead focusing on calligraphy and painting appraisals. Listening to his insightful evaluations, your perspective broadened accordingly.
Even if you want to come up with some tricks, there's no way to do it. So you stopped thinking, and learning to give up is also an important lesson in life.

You knew you couldn't passively wait for defeat and suddenly recalled that you still had a mysterious treasure comparable to your calligraphy masterpiece. Enthusiastically, you summoned Eldest Senior Brother's doodles, only to find they not only failed to achieve your goal but were instead taken as mockery, offending the person. All of this was thanks to Eldest Senior Brother. Thanks, Eldest Senior Brother.

Mister saw your speech as casual, not like a scholar's manner, and felt displeased. Without giving the Third Senior Brother any consideration, his scholar's pride surfaced, and he became unkind in his words toward you, leaving you feeling quite wronged.

The Third Senior Brother and Lu Weng's young Mister overinterpreted your calligraphy and paintings, causing Lu Weng to grow increasingly eager. He then invited the Mister and you to go upstairs to see if the Tang Clan still had any dust‑covered precious artworks and calligraphy worth appreciating.
A chill of alarm shot through you, cold sweat sliding down your cheek. Wasn't the painting Lu Weng spoke of exactly the forgery you'd signed with Du Fu's name?

Securing Third Senior Brother's promise to no longer grant leniency next time, Lu Weng was still dissatisfied. He raised a request with the Tang Clan‑a secret you thought could be smoothly taken into the grave. Back then, when you lied, you never imagined this secret would one day emerge like a zombie from the soil!

The weather was scorching and the mountain road treacherous; by the time he arrived Lu Weng was already worn out and resentful. Seeing you all still refusing to repay your debt, whispering and trading glances as if plotting some scheme, his anger boiled over, and he tore into you all without mercy.

Thank goodness you're meticulous in your work; without needing to be told, you'd already brewed a pot of tea to entertain the guests. Its cool, refreshing taste eased some of the heat, and having accepted your courtesy, Lu Weng could hardly keep scolding—his words turned a good deal more polite.

This day, you were sweeping when suddenly the Fourth Senior Brother rushed over, instructing you to first go to the Scripture Hall to brew tea and prepare to entertain the guests, while he hurried off to inform the Sect Leader. It turned out that the Tang Clan had accumulated massive debts and finally faced the creditors coming to collect them. However, with the Tang Clan's current situation, they even worried about having enough to eat; how could they possibly have coins to repay?
He had once been a deserter, and once a bandit; this time he wanted to become a Great Hero, and was beaten to death for it, yet never once retreated.

Even knowing that with the Flying Stone Gang added, it would be extremely difficult to resist the Wulin Alliance, he still remained obstinate. Those who were willing to follow his command listened; those who feared death or found it unworthy, he did not force them. He was not afraid of death, but only of dying disgracefully.
We must mobilize the full strength of the gang to stand together with the Tang Clan.

You led the couple to Eldest Senior Brother's grave to burn incense and pay their respects, offering thanks and receiving thanks in turn. You looked on as witness; even among the disciples who still harbored resentment, seeing their sincere devotion eased most of that bitterness. Once they had paid respects to Eldest Senior Brother, the Flying Stone Gang Leader spoke of the Wulin Alliance's advance from the east.
You rose to greet the visiting Flying Stone Gang Leader and their spouse.
Gang Leader Shi and his wife tried to enter but found no way in, both feeling disappointed. They left after having tea and snacks at a tea house.

You have a close bond with Eldest Senior Brother, but this guest disciple is new and has only met Eldest Senior Brother a few times. With the grand assembly of the Western Wulin Alliance approaching and no one to help drum up support, you were being so narrow-minded about it that the guest disciple couldn't just let your foolishness stand, so he took it upon himself to invite the guest up the mountain. Who else could go but that senior brother of yours who looks so comically unimpressive and lacks any sense of authority? He could only trail out after them, sulking, to meet them.

You have a deep friendship with Eldest Senior Brother, but this guest disciple is new and has not met Eldest Senior Brother many times. Knowing that the grand assembly of the Western Wulin Alliance is imminent and worrying about lacking support, you are surprisingly narrow-minded for thinking like this. Nevertheless, since you hold the sect leader token, even if it is a generations-old token, its authority cannot be trampled upon. Thus, you can only gently advise Shi Gongyuan and his wife to withdraw.

It was said that the Flying Stone Gang Leader and his spouse visited. Although their involvement in the death of Eldest Senior Brother did not amount to direct causation, they still could not be entirely absolved. You harbored resentment and refused to receive them.
You rose to greet the visiting Flying Stone Gang Leader and their spouse.
It was said that the Flying Stone Gang Leader and his spouse were paying a visit, and Third Senior Brother rushed out to greet them.

Under Fourth Senior Brother's persuasion, you finally resolved to leave the Tang Clan. Together with Fourth Senior Brother, you bid farewell to the Acting Sect Leader and headed eastward. Along the way, you worked as an apprentice in commerce to earn some coins. Tempted by Fourth Senior Brother, you spent your earnings on a little maidservant to wait on you. When you arrived at the next place, having saved up some coins, you bought another young lady. Whenever they grew old and their affection waned, you would give them some coins and send them away, then seek out new mistresses. In this way, you kept replacing your companions. As you grew older and sought stability, your wealth was eventually swindled away by beautiful courtesans. Fourth Senior Brother pitied your plight and helped you with his finances, but you never felt truly satisfied, and soon fell into depression until the very end. It was only at the last moment that you realized: what you truly wanted wasn't these things.

Under the persuasion of Fourth Senior Brother, you finally made up your mind to leave the Tang Clan. Before you set off, the one you thought of the most was Sister Yunshang. When she heard you were leaving, she showed no signs of sorrow, seeming to think you were just going on a short outing and would return home soon. Accompanying Fourth Senior Brother's caravan, you traveled east to Jiangnan, to Lin'an. At each place, you would buy landscape paintings and have them sent to Ye Yunshang; she would always write back, ordering you about as imperiously as ever. You heard that she had been recovering well and was in increasingly good health, which brought you great joy. After several years, you reached the borders of the Jin Kingdom, parting ways with Fourth Senior Brother. You thought it was time to return and see this sister who shared no blood with you, bringing back the wealth you had accumulated over the years. Upon returning home, you learned that she had passed away many years ago due to illness. All the replies you had received over the years were written by her own hand, enduring pain under the night lamp before her death. She had imagined what you might say, where you might go, who you might meet, and what you would look like grown old—certainly very ugly and quite amusing. In a dreamlike haze, she had vaguely envisioned a future where she grew up safely, becoming graceful and well-spoken, waiting to greet you with a smile under the trees. How long would it take for you to realize you had been deceived? This was the last time you would act foolishly. At the moment of her passing, she held your letter, tears streaming down her face yet with a smile, remembering you as she always did.

Under the persuasion of Fourth Senior Brother, you finally resolved to leave the Tang Clan. Before departing, you kept your promise and went to bid farewell to Junior Martial Sister. You stood in silence, only the soft chime of a bell replacing your words. You recalled those youthful days when you walked hand in hand, singing songs amidst the green mountains, a lively and joyous time. Time has passed like flowing water, her face still youthful, yet her heart feels lonely. To meet her once more, standing in silence, the past memories are all swept away with a smile. You mounted your horse, caught up with Fourth Senior Brother's caravan, traveled together for a while, then parted once more. Alone on the long journey, you will never see the person you love again in this lifetime. Decades later, whenever you think back on those old days, you will sing mountain songs, drowning in a deep, intoxicating sorrow. Through the myriad flowers, untouched by a single leaf, those young women may be beautiful, but none can match even a fraction of the woman in your memories. Wielding your sword across distant lands, you've grown accustomed to the color of solitude. In this vast world, none can replace her.

You finally decided to leave the Tang Clan under the persuasion of the Fourth Senior Brother. As agreed, you went to bid farewell to the Junior Martial Sister, who followed you closely and silently, accompanying you on your journey. The Fourth Senior Brother feared she might get lost, so he advised her to return home. Three thousand miles east, on the journey, you heard that the Junior Martial Sister had married into a good family and would enjoy a carefree life. You felt both sorrow and joy, drinking heavily in the inn, raising a toast from afar for her happy marriage and a life filled with descendants. Tears fell into the wine, bitter and sour, just like life itself, full of a thousand miseries, with few things going as desired.

Under Fourth Senior Brother's persuasion, you finally resolved to leave the Tang Clan. Together with Fourth Senior Brother, you bid farewell to the Acting Sect Leader and headed eastward. Along the way, you worked as an apprentice in commerce to earn some coins. Tempted by Fourth Senior Brother, you spent your earnings on a little maidservant to wait on you. When you arrived at the next place, having saved up some coins, you bought another young lady. Whenever they grew old and their affection waned, you would give them some coins and send them away, then seek out new mistresses. In this way, you kept replacing your companions. As you grew older and sought stability, your wealth was eventually swindled away by beautiful courtesans. Fourth Senior Brother pitied your plight and helped you with his finances, but you never felt truly satisfied, and soon fell into depression until the very end. It was only at the last moment that you realized: what you truly wanted wasn't these things.

Asked what medicine he'd used, that too seemed fine. Eldest Senior Brother excelled at hidden-weapon technique and rarely resorted to poison craft, though that didn't mean he was ignorant of it—he simply found it troublesome. You thought it over but couldn't come up with any better suggestion, and seeing him spry and lively, in no apparent danger, you let the matter drop.

Asked what medicine he'd used, there was nothing wrong with it, yet it fell a little short. After a moment's thought, you offered a suggestion: replace the wound salve with Three Yin Cordyceps Gel. The gel is poisonous—an ordinary person treating a wound with it would lose half his life if it didn't kill him outright—but Tang Clan disciples, skilled alike in the use of poison and Poison Resistance, could use it safely. In the right dose, Three Yin Cordyceps Gel was not only harmless but would purge the malignant qi lingering in old wounds, while also nourishing the body, stanching blood, and knitting flesh. Only someone accomplished in both medicine and poison could have prescribed it—the finest remedy there was. Even the Ruthless Young Lord himself, called in, would likely have prescribed much the same.

Yet he seemed perfectly at ease, as though nothing were truly wrong—Eldest Senior Brother prized his own life too highly for that. Known as the Flying Hero for his peerless Qinggong, he had likely, since his earliest training, always kept one thought ready: be prepared to flee at a moment's notice.
Seeing the scattered medicine jars, the scraps of torn bandage, and catching the faint tang of blood in the air, you knew at once that Eldest Senior Brother had been hurt.

As you went to the alchemy room for your usual chores, you came upon an unusual sight: Eldest Senior Brother, with Second Senior Brother away, had settled into his place like a cuckoo taking over another bird's nest.

Before Emperor Xuanzong's eyes, Long Xiang drew her bloodied sword, shook the blood from the blade, sheathed it, and cast a glance at Wanyan Xun so full of killing intent it set men shivering. All thought the same: beautiful as this woman was, she killed so cleanly and completely that even the imperial guard could not withstand her—an assassin who couldn't survive more than a few exchanges with her, best never provoked at all. After that battle, Long Xiang firmly declined the Jin emperor's urging to stay, asked only for a single carriage, and carried the assassin Tang Buyi's body back to the Central Plains alone for burial, leaving Wanyan Xun behind to sigh in sorrow. Whether from guilty conscience or some other design, he declared that Marshal Pusan Anzhen's death had been carried out on his own order, strictly forbade his soldiers from discussing it privately, and gave the court historians the same account—erasing all trace of Tang Buyi and Long Xiang from the record. What no one knew was that the duel between the two had been a scheme cooked up between them only moments before. When Eldest Senior Brother had asked by name to test himself against the Jinxiang Palace's Soft Coiling Sword, and its move called Piercing Insight, Long Xiang understood at once—perfected, that stroke could run a body through while missing every bone, every organ, every vital point, a secret art unique to the Jinxiang Palace. Had it not been a feigned death, then even with ten times his true skill, your Eldest Senior Brother could never have killed the Jin emperor and lived to break free of the thousands of soldiers ringed around him.

Eldest Senior Brother saw Long Xiang's hesitation, saw she was slow to unleash her ultimate move, and grew increasingly anxious. From the corner of his eye he caught Jin Xuanzong quietly shifting his feet, ready to bolt at any moment—there was no time to lose. He had no choice but to play his trump card: closing in with a sudden whirlwind of blows, left hand, right hand, right foot, left foot, one after another, sweeping Long Xiang's sword aside, his own momentum now spent with no attack left in him. By rights both needed speed now—whoever recovered balance first would seize the advantage—but Eldest Senior Brother cared nothing for what came after. What did the Forgetting Form chapter say? Hidden weapons take no fixed shape; hands and feet were spent, but he still had his head. The instant he saw his opening, he let the last of his spin carry him forward and pressed his mouth to Long Xiang's cheek—one stolen kiss. For that one kiss, giving up his chance to recover balance was the worst trade of blow for blow under heaven. Long Xiang froze, then flushed with shame and fury, kicked him away, leapt after him, and with a single sword-thrust in midair ran him clean through, cutting him down. Eldest Senior Brother let out a scream, groaned a few times, and lay still.

The Tang Clan's martial arts excel in ambush, striking with suddenness and unpredictability. Even Eldest Senior Brother, with his deep experience, cannot escape this tactic. In contrast, Long Xiang combines both offense and defense, mastering both family techniques and the Jinxiang Palace's ultimate skills. Her style is soft yet firm, nearly invulnerable. If Eldest Senior Brother had faced her in a direct confrontation without resorting to underhanded tactics, how could he possibly stand a chance? As the battle continued, Long Xiang grew more confident, her long sword moving with effortless grace and unrelenting precision. Several times, her blade brushed dangerously close, causing Eldest Senior Brother to break into cold sweat, secretly wondering if this girl truly intended to kill him. Though he managed to hold his own, he gradually fell behind, allowing Long Xiang to seize an opening. With a single kick, she sent him flying, then leapt into the air, delivering a fatal strike that pierced through his body, killing him instantly. Eldest Senior Brother let out a pained cry, whimpered a few times, and then fell motionless.
On a certain day when you were living a normal life, far beyond the frontier, a major event that would eventually be buried in the annals of history occurred.

Though the Flying Hero's reputation is well earned, your Qinggong today was a match for his. But a pauldroned retainer rounding the corner caught you utterly off guard—you plowed straight into his shoulder armor, unable to recover your stance, and tumbled and rolled across the ground, no telling how many bones you'd broken, able only to watch helplessly as Eldest Senior Brother vanished in a cloud of dust.

However, the Flying Hero is not without merit. Your Qinggong has always been difficult to match Eldest Senior Brother's. After chasing for a while, you saw the gap widening. With a few leaps, Eldest Senior Brother vanished from your sight. You stood in confusion for a while, and eventually gave up.

Eldest Senior Brother watched you grow from a clumsy, completely unskilled servant to a formidable fighter capable of standing on equal footing with him, and he couldn't help but feel both astonished and delighted, filled with countless emotions. If he had used his full strength, he wouldn't have been able to defeat you, let alone the fact that he was holding back his hidden trump card. Yet he chose to lose. For Eldest Senior Brother, losing to you was merely a matter of losing face, but for you, it marked a significant milestone. You had become a capable fighter in your own right. However, while you could defeat him, you might not be able to outrun him. Seizing the moment when you were overjoyed by your victory and momentarily careless, Eldest Senior Brother took off running. Naturally, you wouldn't give up and chased after him.

Eldest Senior Brother beat you without mercy, using his fists to deliver a clear message: I'm strong, I won't die, rest assured. He waved his sleeves and vanished into the air. You stared in stunned silence for a while, your restless heart subdued by his unyielding punches. Though you had just taken a brutal beating, your mood became calm. As usual, since Eldest Senior Brother said he would be back soon, he truly would return soon.

You thought it over for a moment, then resolved to go with Eldest Senior Brother and help assassinate the Jin marshal and the Jin emperor—so the Jin would no longer dare flaunt their might, and would learn at last that they had only ever been bullying and exploiting a Great Song too civil to fight back. Eldest Senior Brother couldn't help a wry laugh and agreed at once—then, the moment your guard was down, knocked you out cold with a sneak blow. The truth was, the mission was perilous enough that even he had no sure hope of success; the more people involved, the harder it would be to pull off, and the likelier someone would pay with their life. Branded and walking his lonely road, Gang Leader Wang was not, in truth, alone: just as the world failed to grasp the pains he took, there were kindred spirits elsewhere, unknown to him, already setting their own plan in motion. Different roads, one destination—half resting on fate, half on human will. The Flying Hero rode a thousand li.
However you looked at it, it seemed madness. Reckless as it was, you meant to stop Eldest Senior Brother from throwing his life away, even if it meant coming to blows with him.

You knew advising him was useless—besides, where your Eldest Senior Brother was headed was a matter of righteousness. Worried as you were, you could not find the words to dissuade him; in the end, it was because you believed utterly in his ability. Deep down, annoying as Eldest Senior Brother could be, he was invincible—no one under heaven could kill him. Surely this time would be no different. Once he said he'd go and come back, he always did come back, at most lingering an extra day or two in some Jin pleasure house; he never broke his word.

A few days later, Eldest Senior Brother reappeared and told you the conclusion he had reached after much thought. He meant to go somewhere farther than the Xiangyang battlefield—all the way to Bianjing—for only by taking the heads of the Jin emperor Wanyan Xun and the Jin marshal Zhuhu Gaoqi could the conflict be resolved at its root. It sounded simple enough, but the Song soldiers, tied down by duty however willing, hadn't the freedom for such a deed; only an unburdened wanderer could attempt it. And of wanderers, none under heaven was better suited to the task than the Flying Hero Tang Buyi himself—who else could cut off the source of the war?

The head of the Nangong household thanked you and your senior brother for tending to his son, and asked after your Eldest Senior Brother's whereabouts. To avoid arousing suspicion, you claimed he had gone to a brothel for pleasure. Nangong Yuan was taken aback for a moment, then burst out laughing—in his youth he too had been a dashing young lord, and however much he prized his reputation, he had never once passed up a night of music and soft hands. He had been displeased at your Eldest Senior Brother's aloofness, not even troubling to offer a few polite words, but on hearing of the brothel his irritation vanished at once, and he strode off smiling like a man who understood exactly what that meant.

The family head frowned upon hearing this, though he did not scold, he was displeased with your Eldest Senior Brother's independent nature, not even offering a few polite words, which was quite impolite.
The head of the Nangong family thanked you and your senior brother for saving his son, and asked after your Eldest Senior Brother's whereabouts. To avoid arousing suspicion, you feigned ignorance.

Wang Erzhuang then laid out his scheme in full. What he had in mind went far beyond anything you could have imagined. It turned out Gang Leader Wang was deeply troubled for his country, and understood well that the old grudge between the court and the Jianghu ran as deep as three feet of ice — not the work of a single cold day. All told, it was the court that had owed the Jianghu people across several generations. Unless every Jianghu soul who remembered those old debts died out, or the dynasty itself changed hands, court and Jianghu would forever stand as fire to water; one could no longer hope for a Great Hero like Nangong Zhi who served both nation and people, nor for a scholar‑alliance leader and a warrior‑overlord to stand at Marshal Yue's side as before. The Nangong family kept good relations with the court above and never shunned ties with the common folk below; given time, Old Master Nangong Heng's ideal of a world made whole might yet turn the tide — but wanting the best of both worlds meant playing the long game, never rushing to a head. Yet with the nation in crisis, the Jin would not wait for unity before invading, and every day soldiers on the frontier were giving their lives. The only course left was a jolt to wake everyone up: strike the garrison at Jiangling, then use the Nangong name to draw the great sects of the Wulin to its aid. With that fact established, the court would have no choice but to lean on the Jianghu's strength — otherwise, if Jiangling fell, Xiangyang would lose its shield, and the realm itself would be in peril. Once he had spoken, you and your Eldest Senior Brother both grew solemn, drew out cups of wine, and drank without a word. When the cups were empty, they cupped their fists in salute, and Wang Erzhuang turned and walked away — parting words for tonight, but the next time you met, you would meet as foes. The more you admired his resolve, the more you knew you had to stand against him and rally others to the cause, for the true enemy still lurked beyond Xiangyang, watching and waiting. What Gang Leader Wang's grand design lacked was never friends, but enemies. He had already chosen his own path, and would let no one walk it with him.
With no other option, Wang Erzhuang could only roll up his sleeves and wade in himself to give you a beating.

You've spent time refining your self‑practiced martial arts, and they're not entirely useless. When Wang Erzhuang's gaze fixed on you, a thought flitted through your mind, and you moved instinctively, barely dodging the flying hook. Nangong Qian, however, lacked your skill and was lured close by Wang Erzhuang, who then knocked him out with a single palm strike. Don't underestimate your seemingly ordinary act of letting it pass‑it's enough to earn Wang Erzhuang's respect, even from the senior brother. After all, Wang Erzhuang's fishing rod isn't particularly effective for fishing, but he's never failed to catch people. Being able to avoid this hook means your skills are no small feat.

But before that, the troublesome bystanders had to be dealt with first — and by troublesome bystanders, naturally, he meant you. Wang Erzhuang said nothing more, simply flinging out a fishing rod. You and Nangong Qian were startled and tried to dodge, but the two hooks had already snagged your collars, hauling you forward against your will — one palm strike each, and it was over, neat and clean.

The two Men in Black removed their masks simultaneously. The man on the opposite side was indeed your Eldest Senior Brother Tang Buyi. As for the person behind you, it turned out to be none other than the Beast Path Dharma King Wang Erzhuang, leading thousands of Beggar Sect disciples in a battle against the Orthodox Wulin in Jiangling! Now that their true faces were revealed, Wang Erzhuang abandoned any thought of hiding his martial lineage and let you go; after all, if he wanted your life, he could simply take it outright, and besides, he seemed to share some past connection with your Eldest Senior Brother. Old drinking companions from years gone by had become enemies today. Your Eldest Senior Brother got straight to the point and asked why he had laid siege to the city; given his ability, he would never recklessly besiege a city and provoke the court over some mere Wulin dispute. Wang Erzhuang, pleased to hear your Eldest Senior Brother's analysis hit the mark, was glad the Jianghu had gained such a talent, and recalling the debt of a pot of wine he once owed him, he candidly laid out the scheme he had never meant to share.

Seizing the Man in Black, you could tell from their movements that they were from the Tang Clan. Your words stunned them, and they denied it, instead accusing you of being the Flashy Hero of the Pleasure House. Upon hearing this, you immediately realized the person across from you had to be your Eldest Senior Brother without doubt, and their blunt remarks seemed deliberately meant to harm you. Unbeknownst to you, the Man in Black, upon hearing this, was greatly shaken and revealed their true identity.

From that brief clash alone, the Man in Black holding you captive could read his opponent's style, and startled everyone by declaring that the man across from him had to be one of your Tang Clan fellows. The other sneered, unwilling to admit it, and turned the accusation back, claiming he was Tang Buyi instead. This counter‑thrust worked perfectly, leaving your captor speechless. He wasn't exactly afraid, but unwilling to bear the false charge, so he pulled off his mask to reveal his true face.

The Man in Black holding you captive needed only that brief clash to read his opponent's style, and startled everyone by declaring that the man across from him had to be one of your Tang Clan fellows. The other sneered, unwilling to admit it, and turned the accusation back, claiming the black‑clad man was in fact Nangong Shen. Nangong Shen was Nangong Qian's elder brother, but with the divide between legitimate and secondary sons, he had never looked kindly on his half‑brother, never sparing him a warm glance at home — yet surely not enough to wish him dead. At these words, Nangong Qian's heart turned cold, not from disbelief, but from an unwillingness to believe. Seeing his utterly despairing look, the man could only sigh and reveal his true face.

You and Nangong Qian immediately used qinggong, chasing them out of the city and into the outskirts, where by the faint starlight the two combatants read each other's moves and traded blows at blinding speed, breaking apart after dozens of exchanges to each hold a corner. When you and Nangong Qian rushed in without thinking, you found no room even to retaliate — each of you was abruptly seized by one of them and taken as a hostage. Nangong Qian, though unloved at home, was still a young lord of a prestigious family; as for you, even wrung dry you would not be worth so much as a clipping of his fingernail, and the Man in Black who caught you felt at once that he had gotten the worse end of the bargain.

You and Nangong Qian hurriedly woke up the servants and summoned the master of the household to inform him about the unexpected visitor's nighttime visit to the Nangong estate. However, aside from the old patriarch soothing them with a few words, all other members of the Nangong family frowned deeply upon hearing this news and showed no concern for the safety of the Second Young Lord. Instead, they blamed you and Nangong Qian for disturbing their peaceful sleep at such an hour. In the end, this group of people fundamentally did not believe that anyone in the entire world would dare to attack the Nangong Family at night. If there were indeed such a person, the night watchmen would be punished. Therefore, they spread rumors, defaming the Second Young Lord as having intentionally lied to gain attention. As for the master of the household, even if he despised this unwanted child, he could not ignore it entirely. He immediately dispatched people to search for signs of the two Men in Black, but unsurprisingly found nothing. Following this incident, Nangong Qian's treatment within the family worsened; no one paid any attention to him, treating him as if he were invisible. You were also regarded as complicit and received glances from household members that contained a hint of disdain.

A masked figure in black cloaks suddenly appeared on the eastern wall, executing qinggong to leap into the courtyard, locking onto Nangong Qian, ready to strike. Yet before they could act, another masked figure in black cloaks emerged from the western wall, also employing qinggong to enter the courtyard. At first, you assumed the two were allies, but they both hesitated, uncertain, and after a brief standoff, forgot their original intent, clashing with a cacophony of sounds. The fight escalated, pushing them further apart. After you and Nangong Qian escaped unscathed, you remained in a state of bewilderment.

Tonight you tossed and turned, not because of any worries, but truly because since coming to the Nangong family, everything was taken care of, and when not fighting with fellow disciples, you just idled around. With your spirit well‑rested and the food delicious, you naturally couldn't sleep. Bored out of your mind, you decided to take advantage of the cool night and go for a walk. Arriving at the courtyard, you heard some noise. Upon approaching, it wasn't anyone but the Second Young Lord, Nangong Qian.

You stumbled straight into Di Ao's trap. Word of her habit of staging matches to win a husband had spread far and wide—only you had never heard of it. Taking it for an ordinary bout, you crossed blades with her without a second thought, and she seized the chance to fasten herself onto you. Luckily the Sect Leader saw reason and refused to betroth you to her. Undeterred, Di Ao went so far as to apprentice herself to the Tang Clan and take the name Tang Jiaojiao, meaning to use her new closeness to slowly win your heart—and if that failed, she could always challenge you to another match, this time in earnest, and beat you into submission.

The Tang Clan had much to rebuild, and it was truly the time to recruit talent. But on second thought, this man was clever and calculating, and keeping him in the Tang Clan might be like raising a tiger—asking for future trouble—so he was turned away. Tang Shan knelt outside for another night, his reverence for the Tang Clan curdling into hatred, and wiped away his tears as he went down the mountain, vowing that one day he would make you all regret this day's harsh decision.

The Tang Clan was in a period of rebuilding and truly needed capable hands. But on second thought, this man was clever and calculating, and keeping him in the Tang Clan might be like raising a tiger—asking for future trouble. So the Sect Leader refused. You recalled his words and spoke up in the man's defense, urging that he be kept on for observation and set to the menial chores you once did. As for the other disciples, it was plain they would show him little warmth—if he could not endure it, he would leave of his own accord.

Third Senior Brother saw that the man bore himself well and seemed truly repentant, and could not help but feel for him. Besides, the Tang Clan had much to rebuild and badly needed hands. So he decided to keep him on for observation, setting him to the same menial chores you once did. As for the other disciples, it was plain they would show him little warmth—if he could not endure it, he would leave of his own accord.

Other accomplices were spared their lives and secretly rejoiced, but only Tang Shan refused to give up, kneeling outside the courtyard gate, claiming he had genuinely reformed and requested to be taken in.

After the internal strife, the Tang Clan's Guangzhou branch scattered in flight, or turned to the Nangong family to plead on their behalf. The clan was thrown into such an uproar that not even the chickens and dogs were left in peace, yet there was no time to deal with these traitors. All they could do was mete out a light punishment as a warning, barring them from ever setting foot in Shu again.

Fourth Senior Brother has never claimed to be a good person, but he's still quite righteous towards family and friends. Since the coins were obtained through your blessing, he naturally wanted to split it with you. You couldn't refuse, so you reluctantly accepted the coins, fearing he might take the opportunity to lend you at high interest. The coins remained untouched, and only after some time did you realize you had overreacted.

Fourth Senior Brother has never claimed to be a good man, but he's always been loyal to family and friends — since it was thanks to you that he'd swindled the money in the first place, he naturally meant to split it with you. You couldn't refuse, and found yourself accepting the coins almost without meaning to; touched by his sincerity, your mind, worn dull and murky from days of toil, grew a little clearer.

Seeing this, Fourth Senior Brother stepped forward to ask what was wrong. Chao He took one look at this plump, guileless-looking man and judged him easy to fool, thinking rather less of him for it, and tried the same trick again. Little did he know that this man was the most cunning soul in the whole sect. His flimsy lies, which wouldn't survive a moment's scrutiny, were turned right back on him as leverage: since he himself had claimed all the mountain's recent chores, and Junior Brother Zhao was nowhere to be found, then the one who'd borrowed money from someone yesterday could only have been him, Chao He — wasn't that obvious? Chao He broke into a cold sweat, stammering as he tried to talk his way out of it, but Fourth Senior Brother was nobody's soft touch, and wasn't about to let him off the hook. He laid bare every one of Chao He's lies and squeezed every last coin out of him. Whatever he still owed would keep accruing interest — as long as Tang Weiyuan drew breath, Chao He could forget about a peaceful day.

You have clearly been busy for quite some time getting things done before you dared to take a breath and do your own things. That day, for some reason, it felt like your fellow brothers were discussing you, deliberately putting you down. You didn't understand why and could only feel a quiet discomfort in your heart.

You'd been toiling for days on end, and in one final push finished off all the sect's chores big and small before you finally got some peace; after splitting the firewood, you were too exhausted to even eat, and simply tucked a freshly steamed bun into your robe, planning to nap a while and eat when you woke. No sooner had you left than Chao He picked up the axe and made a show of splitting the already-split firewood, feigning utter exhaustion. When the fellow disciples asked what was wrong, he brazenly claimed all your days of hard toil as his own. The fellow disciples were startled and believed him, assuming it hadn't been you running yourself ragged these past few days but this man instead — as for you, they had no idea where you'd gone off to enjoy yourself.

You simply scorned his fruit and that paltry bit of coin, showing no gratitude, and turned on your heel to leave. Seeing this, he ground his teeth in hatred, thinking that now he'd been taken in as an inner disciple and given the oral formula, his peerless talent would soon let him grind you underfoot — and then you'd be the real fake.
