Yet that day of a final counterattack never came. After the Shaoxing Peace Accord, Jin Wuzhu sent an envoy to secretly meet Qin Hui, and Yue Fei and Yue Yun were put to death at Fengbo Pavilion. In the end, the Song dynasty fell. The Yin Tally was lost to the Jianghu, and the five bands of soldiers and their descendants wander to this day like lost souls, their spirits still restless. To this day, no one knows what became of the Yue Family's Treasure.

The special edition of that issue's news report featured word of King Wumu's Treasure reappearing in the Jianghu. Back then, Emperor Gaozong, heeding the words of the treacherous minister Qin Hui, was set on seeking peace with the Jin, and issued twelve golden plaques in a row to recall Yue Fei. King Yue, knowing the cause was lost, still defied the order, waiting five days before withdrawing his army from Zhuxian Town, bringing the local commoners south with the army and settling them there before returning to the capital to face the emperor. No sooner had the Yue Family's army withdrawn than the counties of Henan, recovered at such cost, fell once more into the hands of their old enemy Jin Wuzhu. Yet what was the true reason for those five days of defiance? Was it truly only to let the people of Zhuxian Town pack their belongings and move south with the army? The unofficial histories of the Jianghu tell it differently from the court chroniclers.

By the time it approached noon, only you, who had been delayed in eating due to work, had yet to have breakfast. The kitchen table had been wiped clean, not allowing you to sit and eat; thus, you had to take the cold steamed bun back to your room. You hadn't even taken a bite when Third Senior Brother burst in excitedly, waving the Jianghu Bulletin in his hand, urging you to read it, as he suspected there was something particularly interesting, making him eager to spread the news everywhere.

To know the latest news from Jianghu in the mountains, one can only read the newspaper. You bought this month's Jianghu Bulletin and read it with eyes sparkling with excitement. This issue is particularly outstanding, so thrilling that you couldn't help but want to share it with others. Just as you were about to step out to spread the word, you collided with Third Senior Brother, who had also read the same issue and was equally excited, eager to share it with someone.

You returned to the Tang Clan but were severely beaten for having no chicken to show for it. It seems you had forgotten what you even went out to do; to come back without a chicken took some nerve, practically begging to be hit.

You returned to the Tang Clan, handed over the chicken, and completed the mission without a hitch. Afterward, Second Senior Brother took credit for your effort, presenting the chicken soup to the sect leader as though it were his own gift, though he did mention your contribution.
When the rain finally ceased just before dawn, Long Xiang wanted to take Lady Fei to watch the sunrise and find a good place to lay her to rest. She patted her sleeves and bid you farewell.

You chose to settle a private grudge under the guise of justice, speaking ill of Eldest Senior Brother. Long Xiang, now fully trusting you, had already conceived murderous intent toward him without even verifying the truth, secretly resolving to eliminate this scourge.
You chose to speak up for your Eldest Senior Brother, though you yourself were not entirely certain he could be called innocent.

You asked Long Xiang what she meant to do now that this affair was settled, and where she meant to go next. Only then did she remember that in leaving Jinxiang Palace to wander the Jianghu this time, she pursued not only her own aims but also her master's charge to act with chivalry and justice, and to make a name for herself and for Jinxiang Palace. Before she had set out, Lady Wen had given her and her fellow disciples a roll called the Flower-Cherishing Register. It recorded the names of many philandering scoundrels who preyed on women, and the disciples of Jinxiang Palace were to seek them out and verify the rumors against them; where the evidence proved beyond doubt, they were to strike the culprits down. Chen Xu, whom you had dealt with today, was one of the names on that list. As for her next target — it was your Eldest Senior Brother, Flying Hero Tang Buyi of the Tang Clan. You paled at the news. Long Xiang hastened to explain that she would first confirm the truth of it and hear his own account before acting, never wronging an innocent man, and that she hoped to have you stand witness when the time came. For now, she said, she only wished to hear your thoughts.

You often did the cooking, so while hunting the mountain chicken you had naturally kept an eye out for wild delicacies along the way, and had gathered some mountain mushrooms and fresh bamboo shoots besides. Both now came in handy, stuffed into the chicken's cavity to roast. The chicken, mushrooms, and shoots set each other off beautifully; a splash of wine and a pinch of the salt you carried, and the savor came bursting forth. Though the ingredients were foraged on the spot, on this cold night of sudden rain, having roast chicken to eat was beyond Long Xiang's fondest hopes — her gratitude toward you was no less than if you had saved her life.

You suddenly remembered that you had shot a mountain chicken today, intending to clean and roast it, but then you forgot where you had put it. It was already cleaned, yet not roasted, which felt like a waste of the chicken's sacrifice. Upon hearing there was a chicken, Long Xiang immediately grew excited. You only knew she was hungry, but you didn't realize she had a lifelong passion for eating chicken. Offering her a chicken was truly hitting the right note.

She wanted to follow in her heroic father's footsteps and make a name for herself in the Wulin, and envied those renowned heroes who were greeted with open arms wherever they went, hailed as brothers by all. Today she had made a friend, and was overjoyed — caring nothing whether it made you uneasy, she insisted on calling you brother and sister. She had no way of knowing your age, of course, but going by height and skill, she couldn't possibly rank beneath you, so she simply declared herself the elder sister.
She has roamed the Jianghu for years, never having the chance to meet such a person, still believing they didn't exist at all, and now she thinks you are exactly that kind of person.

She has traveled through Jianghu all this time, never encountering such a person, believing them to not exist at all, until today when she saw you. You were surprised and flattered, repeatedly declining, the more you criticized yourself, the more she believed you were a good person.

Only those who possess the most precious virtues in the world, who have endured hardships yet still wish to treat others with kindness, even with their bodies scarred, can laugh with integrity and be worthy of befriending Long Xiang.
You felt a sudden jolt of alarm upon hearing this, sensing that Lady Wen seemed to possess profound insight, having already foreseen that her beloved disciple would meet you today.

The handsome ones you had to guard against — but that didn't mean the plain-looking ones were safe company either. Lady Wen had also told Long Xiang that a person who is constantly bullied and insulted will, in time, grow bitter and sullen, harboring hostility toward others.
You found it so amazing you just wanted to worship Lady Wen.

Long Xiang's straightforward temperament had never set anyone's mind at ease, and no one knew this better than her master, Lady Wen. When Long Xiang and her fellow disciples first ventured out of the palace into the Jianghu, Lady Wen alone felt uneasy about her, and took special care to instruct her, warning her again and again to be wary of handsome men — especially those of soft, feminine looks, or worse, the kind who wore flowers in their hair — for nine times in ten such men were no good. Handsome men, she said, won people's favor too easily from birth, and in time came to take it for granted, growing arrogant and grasping, the most skilled of all at deceiving others. As for those of feminine appearance, they too often prized their own looks above all, lacking any manly bearing, and their hearts were full of twists and turns. The advice was one-sided and not entirely fair, but Lady Wen knew Long Xiang had no gift for telling the honest from the treacherous, so she simply taught her to think the worst of everyone, lest she go about with no guard at all and be made a fool of.
She was simple‑minded and guileless, entirely unaware that the person before her was no good man either — had you Chen Xu's looks, you might have committed even worse misdeeds than him.

At first meeting, Long Xiang had seemed fierce and forbidding, yet now she seemed utterly guileless, with no trace of that imposing air, surprisingly easy to get along with — had you not seen with your own eyes her sword-light like a rainbow and her heroic bearing in besting a formidable foe, you would never have believed she was truly a master of the Wulin. Long Xiang had first saved your life from a powerful enemy, and then, thanks to your kindness, was spared the calamity of blindness — to her mind, this exchange of favors was a rare bond, and she wished sincerely to befriend you. Hearing you speak to her so formally only left her displeased. The moment you met her, you knew she would one day make a name for herself in the Jianghu. Yet you counted yourself a third-rate nobody — not only mediocre in skill, but with looks that calling merely average would already be flattering — and could not help feeling a twinge of shame beside her. Long Xiang cared nothing for such things: a plain face was simply Heaven's doing, and poor skill could be honed through practice. What she prized was a chivalrous heart, and a person's resolve.

Outside the temple the rain rumbled on, with lightning and thunder now and then, truly making it hard to rest soundly. So you and Long Xiang simply stayed up through the night, talking to pass the time.

You chased after her, hastily introducing yourself to gain her trust. Upon hearing you were from the Tang Clan, Long Xiang's mind settled, allowing you to take her hand and walk away. You led her to a nearby mountain stream, using the mountain spring water to rinse her eyes. Long Xiang was startled, thinking you intended to harm her, but soon realized you had no ill intentions. When Chen Xu attempted a hidden attack, Long Xiang instantly reacted, dodging swiftly. The lime powder that had touched her face was minimal, and the continuous flow of water washed it away, rendering the lime's heat harmless. After half an hour, she was no longer in danger.

You chased after her, but were at a loss, unable to find any cooking oil to wipe her eyes in this situation. Long Xiang was terrified, tripped, and fell into the mountain stream. Despite her superb swordsmanship, she could not resist the power of nature. The torrential rain and swift current of the mountain stream instantly carried her away. You were powerless to save her. Heartbroken and helpless, you returned to the temple to pray for her afterlife blessings. What you didn't know was that she was blessed with both fortune and robust health, her physique and fate being exceptionally strong. When Chen Xu attempted a hidden attack, Long Xiang instantly reacted, dodging skillfully and only slightly touching the lime powder on her face. Falling into the stream was actually a blessing in disguise; the continuous flow of water washed the lime powder off her face, rendering its heat harmless. After being swept downstream and drinking a lot of water, she not only survived but also preserved her life and eyesight.

Yet she was still inexperienced in the Jianghu, unaware of the treachery of human hearts. She could never have imagined that some people, aware of their own incompetence, would not allow others to succeed. As Chen Xu and Long Xiang passed each other, he suddenly sprayed a handful of lime. Long Xiang was caught off guard; though she dashed backward on the spot, some lime still got into her eyes. In a mix of shock and fury, she drew her sword and slashed at Chen Xu's back. The latter endured the intense pain and laughed mockingly at Long Xiang, in reality warning her that lime would heat up and burn her eyes if it came into contact with water, to prevent her from pursuing further. Unfortunately, Long Xiang had a straightforward temperament and, without hesitation, chased after him, delivering a fatal strike. Her face was splashed by rain, scalding her and causing her to cry out in pain.

You were calmer than her, after all, you were a Tang Clan disciple, accustomed to dealing with medicine and poison daily, and well aware that the remedy of rubbing eyes with vegetable oil was unreliable. You instructed Long Xiang to go find a place where water converges or a pool, and Long Xiang, in a state of panic, returned immediately, picking you up and carrying you horizontally, leaping several times to bring you to the mountain stream to rinse your eyes. You had already swept most of the lime away beforehand; the residual lime, upon touching the water, immediately generated heat. However, as you had anticipated, the continuous flow of water washed away the lime's heat, rendering it harmless. After a short while, there was no more danger.

You and Long Xiang trusted a folk remedy — that lime powder in the eyes must never touch water, and had to be washed out with oil. But where in these deep, trackless mountains would you find oil? A thought struck you: you asked Long Xiang to roast a mountain chicken until it rendered fat, then used the chicken fat to wipe your eyes. But chicken fat was nothing like cooking oil, and it scorched and stung against your eyes. After all that clumsy fumbling, you went blind.

Yet she ultimately lacked sufficient Jianghu experience, unaware of the treachery of human hearts. She could never have imagined that some people, knowing their own lack of merit, would not allow others to prosper. As Chen Xu and Long Xiang passed each other, a handful of lime was suddenly thrown. You had already been on guard, swiftly pulling Long Xiang away, while you yourself ended up covered in lime. Long Xiang, incensed beyond restraint, chased him out of the temple and finished off the wicked Young Lord with a single stroke of her sword. But when she came back and saw you, she was flustered and at a loss.

Long Xiang had just felt the thrill of battle and was eager to continue fighting, but her opponent unexpectedly knelt down to beg for mercy, leaving her greatly disappointed. She then heard Chen Xu proclaiming himself as a warrior from the Dragon Raising Garden of the Jin Kingdom, serving the Shandong Pacification Envoy Pusan Anzhen, tasked with ensnaring and enticing the Wulin folk of the Song Kingdom. He attempted to tempt Long Xiang, but she remained unmoved. Knowing that begging for mercy would be futile, he earnestly requested Long Xiang to allow him to leave the temple to take his own life. Long Xiang placed great importance on ambition, integrity, and dignity; since her opponent had come to this realization, she decided to let him be, believing that in his severely injured state, he wouldn't be able to pull off any tricks.

You stood there dumbstruck, yet as the one merely watching, you saw it all with perfect clarity. As Long Xiang drew her sword, Chen Xu attempted to emulate the same move as he did when seizing Lady Fei's long sword. However, Long Xiang flipped and trembled her wrist, cutting off five of Chen Xu's fingers with a sword song. Following this, she executed three flower sword moves, combining attack and defense, slicing through the fan while also shaving off a piece of flesh from the young lord's leg. Though not swift, it was seamless, without any harshness, subtle yet restrained, exquisitely elegant, yet incredibly powerful, truly broadening your horizons.
You were so startled that you were stunned, couldn't understand a bit, but you just knew it was very powerful.

The two clashed, swift as a hare's leap and a hawk's dive, exchanging seven or eight strikes in an instant. It seemed like a back‑and‑forth, but regardless of the exchange, Chen Xu would inevitably be injured. After a series of attacks and defenses, his fan was destroyed, his fingers severed at the palm, and a chunk of flesh torn from his thigh, blood flowing continuously.

When Fei Niangzi delivered her challenge, she never thought of winning. She resisted with her Internal Skill but took a heavy blow, spitting blood repeatedly, and it seemed she would not survive. Young Lord Chen recalled their past tenderness, filled with deep affection, and felt an infinite sense of regret. He thought that this infatuated Lady was deliberately provoking him to seek death, making him remember her for eternity as revenge. He was moved by his own thoughts, unaware that Fei Niangzi truly sought death, but her intentions were not what he imagined. She was determined to end her life, not only to seek liberation but also to express her feelings to Jinxiang Palace: she had made mistakes and felt remorse, and she was willing to pay with her life. After that, it would be up to Jinxiang Palace to take responsibility for her. As she faced death and saw the figure in white approaching gracefully, Fei Niangzi finally breathed a sigh of relief, letting go of years of resentment. With tear‑filled eyelashes lowered, before departing from this world, her thoughts were still on her heartless son, who, despite being her own flesh and blood born after ten months of pregnancy, looked at her with such disdain and hatred. The depth of this hatred was so profound that she would rather die than forgive him, and this life had no resolution. The Heroine in white, with a hint of sorrow on her face, promised to fulfill her last wishes and bid farewell to her senior sister. She then collected her thoughts, drew her sword, and challenged Chen Xu.

You realized the situation was dire and could only seize the opportunity when he had just finished his move, perhaps when he was unprepared, to launch an attack. But your efforts were in vain; he not only countered with composure but also faced you barehanded, which was even more skillful and ruthless than when he used the fan. You were slapped so hard your head rang, and for a moment, you lost your balance, unable to stand straight.

You and the Quanzhen junior Daoist master exchanged a glance, then both launched an attack and advanced to flank him. However, this time was no ordinary affair; he faced the opponent barehanded, proving far more skillful and ruthless than when he had used a fan before. The junior Daoist master was kicked so hard he flew backward and fainted, while you received a slap that left your head ringing, causing temporary imbalance and making it hard to stand straight.

The newcomer was a disciple of Jinxiang Palace dressed in white. Although her face bore the marks of time, she still retained an air of elegance, suggesting that she must have been a stunning beauty in her youth. Upon entering the temple, she revealed the identity of the Young Lord, who was none other than Chen Xu, one of the Four Young Masters of Lin'an's Flower City. Relying on his talent and striking appearance, he would compose a few romantic poems to flaunt, disregarding propriety, and specifically seducing virtuous women.   She was captivated by his looks and talent, believing his sweet words that true love knows no bounds of time and space, etiquette, or societal prejudices, that it's never too late to bravely pursue love, that only those unloved are guilty, and that one is willing to become a demon for love, among other passionate and heart‑stirring phrases. She was willing to abandon her husband and children to elope with him, only to find herself, after her beauty faded and love waned, abandoned and homeless, one of the many pitiful souls left behind.   That beautiful Lady was deeply ensnared, unable to extricate herself. If others tried to advise her, she would refuse to listen, considering it a ploy to sow discord between them. However, in her fervent infatuation, she was extremely jealous, able to catch at shadows even where none existed. Moreover, the expressions and tone of her beloved clearly indicated a past connection with Fei Niangzi of Jinxiang Palace. Whatever words came from her lips, whether harsh or not, could strike at the heart.   Fei Niangzi recounted her own misfortunes, shocking her to the core, as if awakening from a dream. Looking again at her beloved's handsome face, it no longer seemed so dreamlike. Seeing her reaction, Chen Xu had already given up on arguing. With a disciple of Jinxiang Palace present, the rumors would not be mere hearsay in Jianghu; thus, the thought of fleeing the scene vanished, replaced by a murderous intent.   Today, even if it meant risking exposure, he would eliminate everyone present. He gathered his energy, billowing his wide sleeves, exuding a terrifying aura. This was the true martial art he inherited, the Cloud‑Overturning Hand from the Dragon Raising Garden of the Jin Kingdom!   Fei Niangzi showed no fear; since their separation, she had been tormented day and night by her hatred. She had waited far too long for this moment of revenge and would not wait a moment longer. Drawing her longsword, she lunged at her former lover. However, at that moment, Chen Xu held a fan, but he no longer used it as a weapon. With a swift motion, he reached out with his other hand, pinching and flipping, shaking and striking, seizing the tip of Fei Niangzi's sword. With a forceful twist, he turned the blade, and with a flick, the sword returned to its original position. Fei Niangzi lost her grip on the hilt, and he struck her in the chest, causing her to spit blood and suffer a severe injury.

The Young Lord wielded a fan as his weapon, opening it to cover his hand, closing it to strike acupoints, sometimes holding it in hand, sometimes letting it fly away. His techniques were truly exquisite, and though he was not a Nangong clan member, this fan technique was indeed the Nangong Family Teachings, something formidable. You two fighting against one were still no match, and the Quanzhen disciple was kicked back, unconscious, leaving only you, who were even worse off. If the Young Lord wished to maintain his sanctimonious facade, he would have to eliminate all witnesses. Just as he prepared to kill you, a delicate scream echoed from outside the temple. Hearing that voice, the Young Lord's body stiffened, and he immediately forgot about killing you, for it was nothing more than a minor matter.

That young lord used a fan. While his moves weren't ordinary, they lacked fluidity and grace. If it wasn't due to unfamiliarity with the technique, it was because he lacked combat experience. He could still hold his own against the Quanzhen disciples, but with your assistance, it became clear that he was outmatched. At the end of the struggle, you landed a move on him. Knowing you were present made it difficult for him to succeed today, and though he regretted losing such a charming young miss, preserving himself was his priority. With a casual lie, he fled without waiting for the beautiful young lady to catch up. Before she could chase after him, he retreated again, almost causing him to trip and fall.

You supposed it must be the Quanzhen Daoist, having lured the tiger from the mountain, returning to settle the score — and you couldn't help but silently count yourself lucky. Fortunate indeed that you'd gone out chasing him and stayed away all night, or by now you'd likely be lying among the corpses yourself.
You supposed it must be the Quanzhen Daoist, having lured the tiger from the mountain, returning to settle the score — and you couldn't help but seethe with regret and self-reproach.
You were scared out of your wits and fled in a panic, rolling and crawling.
The next morning, when you returned, you found that couple lying outside the temple, somehow buried under a heap of loose stones, already dead.
Of course you weren't fool enough to actually give chase; instead, you found a big tree with dense foliage nearby, climbed up, and made do for the night.

You thought about being entrusted with a task and fulfilling it faithfully. The Daoist priest wasn't a local and lacked the courage to take the beast path, so you searched the mountain path several times.
But the sky was pitch black, and the rain came down in sheets, washing away the footprints at once, making it no easy task to track him.

You couldn't have cared less whether she'd been wronged, but the Young Lord's gift was simply too generous — having taken it, you could hardly refuse him — so you tucked the goods into your pocket and left the temple to hunt the man down.

Hearing this, you were filled with righteous indignation, never expecting that even a storied, upright sect could produce such a vile man, and at once dashed out of the ruined temple into the rain to give chase.

The Quanzhen disciple, entirely devoted to the path of cultivation, had neglected to practice diligently, relying only on the basic Quanzhen Sword Technique. He was no match for you, spitting blood and glaring at you, his eyes blazing with fury as he turned and fled into the darkness of the storm. You thought it was enough to drive him away, but the Young Lord insisted you chase after him. He handed you a generous amount of coins and Quanzhen sect's secret manuals, recounting the injustices the beautiful Lady had suffered.

You looked over and saw the female with seven holes bleeding, clearly having died from ruptured meridians. As for the male, all his fingers were severed, and he had been pierced through the heart by a sharp blade. Both had perished at the hands of a master. Reflecting on last night's events, things had been quite strange; you pondered endlessly yet could not fathom whether these two had died at the hands of a master or due to mountain spirits' interference. Shivering, you murmured a prayer and then departed.
You were scared out of your wits and fled in a panic, rolling and crawling.

That Quanzhen novice monk was solely devoted to the path of cultivation, neglecting to practice martial arts diligently, relying only on the initial Quanzhen Sword Technique he had learned upon entering the sect. He was no match for you. Spitting blood, he glared at you, his eyes blazing with fury, and dashed out through the gate, vanishing into the darkness of the stormy rain. You thought it was enough to drive him away, but the young lord insisted you chase him. He even handed you a generous amount of coins and secret martial arts manuals. You knew he was trying to get you to leave and do something improper, but you couldn't refuse when someone gave you something, so you reluctantly left. Naturally, you wouldn't be foolish enough to actually chase him. Instead, you climbed up into a dense tree, making do with a night's rest there. The next morning, you returned to find the couple lying motionless outside the temple, their bodies piled with stones, already dead.

You had been wondering why the dried rations and pickled vegetables tasted so unusually good, imagining he had some secret recipe of his own—only now did it dawn on you that they'd been poisoned. No wonder they'd had such a kick, with your tongue gone numb and tingling. Seeing you weren't just putting on a brave face, the young lord could hardly believe it—little did he know you were of the Tang Clan; was there ever a meal Second Senior Brother hadn't doctored? A mild poison like theirs, cured by nothing more than an antidote tucked under the tongue, was never going to touch you. Poisoning you was like swinging an axe outside Lu Ban's door. To actually kill you, they'd have needed a venom savage enough to strip flesh to the bone at a touch.

You had faintly sensed something was wrong with your body, but the strangeness of what was unfolding before you had drawn your attention away. The moment the young lord revealed the food had been poisoned, sickness wracked your whole body; you leapt and thrashed about, bursting out of the ruined temple into the rain, and only then calmed down—the poison, it seemed, wasn't so fearsome after all; the grime on the alchemy room's walls back home was probably more toxic than this. You went back inside and stood shoulder to shoulder with the young Quanzhen priest. It was this very poison the lady had used to kill her own husband; she and the young lord had eaten the same food and wine, yet neither was poisoned, relying entirely on the antidote tucked beneath their tongues. You, who had eaten and drunk plenty, seemed utterly unaffected, and even you couldn't help a chill of unease.

The young lord no longer bothered to feign restraint; his every gesture betrayed the bearing of a martial artist, clearly no ordinary man. He had already poisoned the food and drink, and now, confident and poised, he was ready to deal with you two small fry from the Jianghu—a matter of no trouble at all.

You couldn't help but admire your own foresight, smirking as you revealed that you'd poisoned the food earlier. The two of them were startled, and blurted out at once, "What—you too...?" You froze, then broke into a cold sweat, realizing the other side had poisoned it as well. All three of you had stumbled into a case of thieves robbing thieves—not one of you was any good.

The reason you helped the Daoist priest was that you envied every handsome man alive, and especially one so courteous, so seemingly virtuous, as him—the mere sight of him kindled a nameless fury in you.

The reason you helped the Daoist priest was that you found the couple's talk thoroughly nauseating. The young Quanzhen priest laughed heartily on hearing this; though you'd only just met and he didn't even know your name yet, he already felt drawn to you. The young lord, far from angry, laughed along, no longer bothering to feign restraint; his every gesture now betrayed the bearing of a trained martial artist, clearly no ordinary man. He had already poisoned the food and drink, and now, confident and poised, he was ready to deal with you two small fry from the Jianghu as if it were nothing at all.

Your reason for helping the Daoist priest is because you find the couple's behavior highly suspicious. The young lord no longer feigns restraint; his every movement exudes the aura of a trained martial artist, clearly no ordinary practitioner. He had already poisoned the food earlier, and now he is confident and poised, ready to deal with you two lowly Jianghu shrimp, as if catching them were effortless.

You overheard the events and decided to help the Daoist priest. The Young Lord and the beautiful Lady were both stunned, immediately panicking, never expecting you to have not the slightest trace of compassion. After hearing their tragic and touching story, you still chose to side with the enemy.
You couldn't bear to see this pair of doomed lovers separated, so you drew your weapon and stopped the Daoist priest from committing violence and harming others.

As they were speaking, a young Daoist of the Quanzhen sect suddenly leapt into the temple with sword in hand, cursing them at once as adulterer and adulteress, and demanding the two pay with their lives for his brother.
The couple's faces went pale with alarm, and when you heard the beautiful lady timidly cry out "Brother-in-law," you nearly couldn't make sense of it—could it be these two were not husband and wife at all, but lovers who had murdered her husband and fled here together?
Then you heard the beautiful lady sob out her story: she said her family was poor and her parents had sold her off to her husband; she had resigned herself to that fate, and even through days of bitter hardship had never strayed—but fate is cruel, for only after she had already become another man's wife did she meet the one truly meant for her.
The two of them, drawn together, had wanted only to be brave for love's sake and fly away as one; they never meant anyone harm. Yet the beautiful lady's husband could not bear it, and took his own life.
His younger brother, seeking the Way on Mount Zhongnan, heard the news secondhand and was overcome with grief, so he took up his sword and came down the mountain, determined to slay this adulterous pair and give his brother's spirit some peace. He had chased the pair the whole way, and only the timely downpour that trapped them in the temple let him finally catch up. He refused to believe a word of his sister-in-law's account, certain she had been consumed by lust and murdered her own husband; the two sides each held to their own story, and the standoff would not break.

Seeing the two of them so intimate, the man handsome and the woman lovely, truly a matched pair, you thought of your own lonely state, and a wave of jealousy washed over you, twisting your already plain face into something downright sinister. Malice got the better of you, and you slipped poison into their food in secret—not a poison strong enough to burst a man's guts, but one that would leave him wishing it had. Watching them eat with relish, urging drink on each other, you felt truly happy for them.
Your crafty eyes kept lingering on the young Lady, making her very uneasy.
You were an open and generous sort, and at once gave up your seat so they could warm themselves by the fire.

You were polite on the surface, declining repeatedly, yet secretly delighted in your heart, thinking this Young Lord was like heaven fearing you might go hungry and had specially sent food to satisfy your hunger.

You really were hungry, but the thought of tomorrow's uncertain weather—clear or rainy, who could say—and the fear you might not cross paths with a pheasant again made you force yourself to hold back. As you wrestled with this inner turmoil, a couple arrived, sharing a single cloak, seeking shelter from the rain. The woman was rather lovely, and, wary of strangers, clung tightly to her sweetheart; the man, though, was generous enough, coming over to greet you properly and sharing out dried rations, a small jar of pickled vegetables, and yellow wine from his pack.

Upon hearing the name of the Nangong Family, you immediately lost all sense of right and wrong. Thinking of the Nangong Family, renowned alongside the Tang Clan as one of the Three Great Families of the Wulin, this person even knows the Nangong Family Teachings, clearly indicating a close relationship. You don't intend to flatter them? He immediately stepped forward, spoke a few words to twist the facts, and the young Daoist priest was furious, drawing his sword and attacking you.

You may do bad things yourself, but hearing someone else do them sets your blood boiling — especially from a greasy young lord like this one. How could you possibly stand against them? Within a few exchanges you were in dire peril, and they mocked you all the while. Fortunately, Ye Yunzhou arrived in time, swiftly cutting down the villains, and you survived by sheer luck.

You felt uneasy inside, forcing yourself to appear calm and bluffing to buy time, as long as possible. Though the three of them hesitated, they had come forward with bloodstained hands, determined to fight. They could not simply give up, advancing step by step, subtly sensing your apparent hesitation. Suspicion grew, and they drew their blades, launching an attack to probe you.
You could no longer keep it hidden, so you smirked and admitted your identity. The three of them were furious beyond control, immediately drawing their weapons and attacking you.

You watched Ye Yunzhou return home late, and the three of them kept their eyes fixed and rolling, as if they were ready to strike at any moment. With each passing moment, you and the Young Lady in the cabin became increasingly perilous. There was nothing else to do but muster up your courage and pretend to act under Ye Yunzhou's name, inventing a story that drew Eldest Senior Brother into it. You framed Eldest Senior Brother for tarnishing your sister's reputation, thus forcing you to travel thousands of miles from Dali all the way to Chengdu to seek justice, so they would not try to appease you but merely send out a challenge, inviting heroes of the Wulin to witness. Thankfully, Eldest Senior Brother's past behavior made this story seem plausible and reasonable, causing those three to suddenly realize their doubts. They no longer doubted your identity in the slightest.  You told them a fabricated tale that calmed your expression as usual while secretly rejoicing in your heart, thinking that if you could just distract them for now, when Brother Ye returns, you would be saved. Just as you were about to accomplish your goal and have them respectfully withdraw, one of them, eager to please, brought up these unpleasant details concerning Junior Martial Sister. Upon hearing this, your reason momentarily evaporated, and you suddenly lunged at the enemy. Regardless of gain or loss, you disregarded all previous efforts; no one in the world could humiliate someone so dear to you right before your eyes.  With everything seemingly accomplished, the three were about to withdraw respectfully when one of them, eager to please, brought up these unpleasant details concerning Junior Martial Sister. Hearing this, you instantly lost your composure and lunged at the enemy without thinking. You disregarded any gains or losses and were determined that no one would humiliate someone so important to you in front of you.

You brazenly lied, claiming to be Ye Yunzhou. The three men still had some doubts, questioning how a handsome young swordsman like Ye Yunzhou could look like you. Fortunately, the name Ye Yunzhou was too well‑known, and they were overwhelmed by fear, unable to think deeply. Hearing your words seemed to suggest some room for negotiation, they immediately flattered and fawned over you, and if they could avoid getting involved, that would be best of all. You played along, probing their true intentions, but you hadn't expected that the three of them were after your sister's beauty, not coins or reputation. Upon hearing this, you were furious, having never encountered such shameless individuals. The three men, seeing your displeased expression, immediately tensed up again, and then reluctantly offered that as long as they could glimpse the beauty bathing, they would be satisfied, and would never touch her a single hair.

You spoke honestly, only realizing after the fact that Ye Yunzhou had specifically asked you to keep his movements a secret. Three Fiends of Yan Pass, upon seeing your appearance, deduced you were no good, an evil seducer intent on Ye Yunzhou's younger sister. Ye Yunshang, still recovering from a severe illness and running a fever, peeked out from the back cabin upon hearing her name mentioned. Your heart nearly exploded.
You decided to pretend to be clueless, and the three people immediately realized they had mistaken someone, their faces flushing with embarrassment, intending to kill to silence them.

Though you may not know their origins, looking at their fierce appearances and the menacing glares in their eyes, they are certainly not benevolent people, and you couldn't help but feel a chill of unease.
These three are notorious local villains, definitely not to be trifled with. You heard it and felt a chill in your heart, already on your guard.

You stepped out to take a breath of fresh air and vaguely spotted some unusual firelight flickering on the quiet shore. Before you could react, an unexpected guest leaped onto the ship's bow, introducing themselves as Three Fiends of Yan Pass, mistaking you for Ye Yunzhou, and politely greeted you.

As the sun dipped below the horizon, travelers returned home, and the streets gradually grew quiet. You felt disheartened, fearing you had been deceived. Just as your heart grew colder, Ye Yunzhou returned. He said he had given his sister the medicine, and now the medicine had taken effect; she no longer had a fever. Only then did he feel at ease and come back to find you, having prepared a few small dishes and drinks to invite you to share a drink on his boat. You readily agreed, and both of you went to his boat. The wine warmed your belly, dispelling the cold and loneliness of the quiet night on the river. Sharing the same spirit, you felt an added sense of boldness. Don't probe too deeply when the connection is still shallow; just keep exchanging cups. You and Ye Yunzhou didn't delve into each other's pasts, but instead discussed current events in the Jianghu, setting aside all sorrows. You savored the essence of the Jianghu in your heart, feeling a great sense of relief. He was refined yet had a strong tolerance for alcohol, drinking cup after cup, until you could no longer bear the wine. Only then did he suddenly remember a toast, but had forgotten the dish to accompany it, feeling a bit remiss. So he hurriedly left the table, rushing off to fetch the wild game he had hunted and sun-dried earlier that day.
To pass the time while waiting for Ye Yunzhou to return, you decided — to do nothing at all. Rare as such idleness was, you spent a leisurely day.

You volunteered to join the street performance, thinking that at least having spent a few years in the Tang Clan, even if no formal teachings were given, your techniques might be crude but your physique at least decent enough to attempt the chest‑breaking stone trick. A single strike sent you spitting blood on the spot, causing the townsfolk to panic and scatter in fear. The street performer, fearing you might suffer a fatal injury, gave you a few more coins, hoping that if you died at home, your ghost wouldn't haunt him for his kindness.

You volunteered to join the street performance, demonstrating a bit of Qinggong and Hidden Weapons. Neighbors rushed to watch, as your skills, not having been taught by a master, were somewhat off, so you weren't subject to the clan's disciplinary measures. Many villagers had never seen a Tang Clan member display their skills before, and they were all amazed. Although you were doing it for quick coins, you inadvertently spread the clan's reputation.

Just as the Flying Stone Gang urgently needed temporary workers, you boldly approached to talk, almost getting beaten. Fortunately, you worked fairly diligently throughout the day without slacking off, slightly changing the Flying Stone Gang members' opinion of you, a Tang Clan member.
To pass the time while waiting for Ye Yunzhou to return, you decided to take on temporary work to earn some quick cash.
You quietly stepped out of the crowd, decided not to get involved in this matter. It was none of your business; why bother with unnecessary interference?
The hat‑wearer deeply bowed to you, asked for your name, and hurried to leave. Seeing you didn't stop them, they paused again, removed their hat, and revealed their name.

Dr. Li was already furious, and upon seeing you, the Tang Clan scum stealing his business, stepping forward to play the good guy, he was even more enraged. However, seeing as you had coins, he still accepted your payment as a deposit. He fetched the medicine and gave a few more instructions before finishing.

You and Dr. Li have been acquainted for a long time and are business partners. Since the Tang Clan's medical clinic was shut down, the medicines prepared by Second Senior Brother have been entrusted to Dr.
You stepped forward from the crowd and intervened in the situation.
After some hesitation, you finally resolved yourself with determination.

You went down the mountain, not wanting to return empty‑handed. While wandering around, you came across a gathering of people. Upon inquiry, you learned that a hooded traveler seeking medicine had arrived at Dr. Li's doorstep. He had knelt for a day and night without moving, like a clay statue, no matter how he was beaten or scolded, he didn't budge an inch. Dr. Li was not heartless, but he had seen too many villains on his journey, and no longer trusted people easily. Moreover, the medicine he sought was Dr. Li's reliance in his old age. If he gave it away easily, with no children to care for him, who would take care of him in the future? Since the hooded traveler couldn't offer coins, there was no room for sentiment.

You fell silent at the words, then laughed it off, taking pleasure in the outcome. The younger son of the Tian family saw you laughing and felt uneasy, so he invited you to eat a bowl of soup noodles to express his apology. You sat on the field embankment, eating noodles side by side. Even common folk have their share of human warmth.

The Tian son had a sharp tongue, but he was only an ordinary man after all. Against Third Senior Brother, a gentleman who spoke nothing but morality and righteousness, he could spout all manner of nonsense and twist words to his advantage. But against you, unscrupulous as you are, it didn't work. A few sharp words from you left him so angry he went home, threw his arms around the cow, and wept.
You had come all this way for nothing, and anger surged within you; you immediately fell into an argument with the man.

Unluckily, you went down the mountain with the coins and found the Tian family, but they refused to sell after all. Talk of selling the cow had merely been an angry word spoken during a family quarrel. The cow had served them all its life, toiling to feed the whole household, and though the Tian family's youngest son was sharp-tongued and gave no quarter, he could not bear to cast the cow aside once its usefulness was done.

This day, you were scrubbing at stains on the training ground floor when the Fourth Senior Brother rushed up, seized you, and pressed coins into your hand, telling you to go down the mountain in his stead, buy an old cow from the Tian family, have it slaughtered and sold, and bring back something extra to eat on the mountain.

The Sect Leader wrote four letters especially for you, addressed to the Kongtong Sect-for Kongtong then had no single successor to its leadership, and was instead led jointly by four Sect Leaders. Relations between the Tang Clan and the Kongtong Sect were neither particularly warm nor especially cold; ordinarily the two had little to do with each other. Yet by standing in the Jianghu, Sect Leader Tang ranked on par with the Kongtong Sect Leader, while the Sect Leaders of the Four Gates of Kongtong stood a rung below-so naturally, they could hardly refuse the Tang Clan's request. Once you had made ready, you took your leave of the sect and went down the mountain, setting out for Mount Kongtong. The road was long, and Fourth Senior Brother, fearing you might be delayed, procured for you a cheap, thin horse so you could make better time. With a mount beneath you, you traveled for several days and at last reached the Kongtong Sect's territory in Qinzhou.

It was not only you who could not bear to part from Little Junior Sister-upon hearing you would be gone a full half year, she too felt an unease she could not put into words, though she knew full well her father would never allow her to leave home to study elsewhere.

Eldest Senior Brother, upon hearing you meant to go abroad to study, immediately stormed into Zhengxin Hall to plead his case. Not only did it not go as he wished, but he was instead assigned to take over your job-a fitting punishment, and a source of public satisfaction.

Second Senior Brother did not favor this-it was plain to see that having you represent the sect, given your appearance and skill, would surely invite ridicule. But since the Sect Leader had spoken, there was nothing to do but comply.

You mustered the courage to raise, at a Tang Clan council, a request to the Sect Leader to study abroad at another sect. Mindful of your many years in the sect-for though you had earned no great merit, you had endured no small hardship-the Sect Leader consented at once, without a second thought.

You knew the Jianghu was entering an age of turmoil, the Tang Clan tossing like a lone boat upon the river, yet still you proposed the Snow Mountain expedition at the Tang Clan council and took your leave of the Tang Clan. Third Senior Brother did not stand in your way-not because he thought little of your once-lowly standing and worthlessness, nor because he wished to keep you, now formidable in martial arts and heavily relied upon. An outsider disciple of the Tang Clan is, after all, not of the Tang family by blood, and need not remain forever within the Tang estate, for there are other burdens to bear. All who have known the Tang Clan's kindness and made something of themselves must carry forward the Tang Clan's will and set out into distant lands, just as the Tang Clan once dared to defy the Emperor's own wrath, fearless of what others said, never forgetting their unbending pride. Live well, and one day you will yet aid those in need. The flesh may perish and the incense be snuffed out, but the will of the Tang Clan must be passed down forever. The Tang Clan's last outsider disciple has begun the departure; the day to spread your wings and leave home has come, and at last you bid the Tang Clan farewell.

On your advice, the Tang Clan bought back its Outer Fort, easing the strain on living space; no longer crowded into common dormitories, the sect's disciples gained a measure of privacy, and secretly felt grateful to you.
Under your advice, the entire Tang Clan mobilized to repair the Tang Family Compound, completely renovating the family residence, and everyone felt a sense of pride.

With the Sect Leader's blessing, you were permitted to sit in on the Tang Clan's councils. Though it was granted so they might weigh the perspective of an outsider disciple like you, it also marked the first time in the Tang Clan's history that an outsider disciple had ever held a seat.

As they were assessing your contributions, you felt somewhat anxious, stammered for a while, and couldn't come up with a coherent explanation. Eldest Senior Brother intended to cover for you and took you away from the scene, which caused the fellow disciples to be resentful and uneasy.

As your contributions were being evaluated, you had clearly worked yourself ragged, yet still put on a hesitant, mumbling expression as if it weren't enough. No one could hold it against you after that-you and Third Senior Brother were truly the spiritual paragons of the Tang Clan.

While your contributions were being evaluated, you dared to lie blatantly to escape, exaggerating your merits. Although Eldest Senior Brother didn't care, the other disciples were very annoyed with you.
The moment you left, they took out the dice and food and drink, overjoyed beyond measure.
This day again brought the time of the monthly evaluation, when Eldest Senior Brother suddenly appeared, declaring that he meant to take you to the Zhengxin Hall.

Gengyang Reading Studio set your deeds down in a book and sold it throughout the land, titled Legend of Mortal. The name of the Tang Clan's Living Hero spread across the Central Plains overnight, known to all. It reached even as far as Xingqing in Western Xia, Lin'an in the Great Song, Yanjing in the Jin, and the desert camps of Mongolia. The emperors of all four nations knew of your existence-some with reverence, some with worry, some with fear, some with sorrow. Your name, from this day forth, was legend.

When people speak of the War between the Eastern and Western Wulins, they never tire of the tale. No one remembers your ugly appearance or humble origins, for that no longer mattered at all. They only know of the young hero atop Mount Meishan, foremost under heaven. Later, news came from the north that the Supreme Bliss Cult had led a Western Xia invasion. Heroes of the Eastern and Western Wulin alike answered your call in that hour of peril, standing united against the enemy and crushing the Supreme Bliss Cult's ambitions. The Central Plains' Wulin at last knew peace again. Gengyang Reading Studio set your deeds down in a book and sold it throughout the land, titled Legend of Mortal. The name of the Tang Clan's Living Hero spread across the Central Plains overnight, known to every man and woman, reaching even as far as Xingqing in Western Xia, Lin'an in the Great Song, Yanjing in the Jin, and the desert camps of Mongolia. The emperors of all four nations knew of your existence-some with reverence, some with worry, some with fear, some with sorrow. Your name, from this day forth, was legend.

However, at the end of the fierce battle, the Wulin Alliance Leader's true face was revealed: his reason for inciting the Alliance to invade the Tang Clan had been his ambition to unify the Jianghu all along. Mercifully, he met his end at last beneath your small sword. Only now did the Wulin Alliance Heroes realize how badly they had misjudged him, and all were consumed with shame. Some donated money in atonement, while others crippled their own martial arts and retired from the Jianghu.

Before the eyes of the multitude, you defeated the Favored Son of Heaven head-on. The Wulin Alliance was still stirring, meaning to hack you to pieces with a flurry of blades, but this time you were not alone. You stood up for the Western Wulin Alliance Heroes, and they stood by you in turn. The Wulin Alliance, leaderless and no longer of one mind, no longer amounted to anything; however many they numbered, they could not withstand the unity of the Western Wulin Alliance, and before long they collapsed entirely. Those who surrendered were judged for their crimes and pressed into service; those who refused bore the consequences themselves. Fearing for their lives, the Wulin Alliance dared not act rashly again, and with Nangong at their head, bowed the knee to the Western Wulin Alliance as vassals.

In the end, the two alliances each sent their top martial experts to clash on the peak of Meishan. Two heroic warriors, one in blue and one in white, each displayed their skills. This battle could be said to shake heaven and earth, move ghosts to tears.

When people speak of the battle between Eastern and Western Wulin, they never tire of the tale. No one remembers your ugly appearance or humble origins, for those details are long irrelevant. All that is known is that on Mount Meishan, there once stood a hero, a young man of great martial arts who could rival the Alliance Leader in swordsmanship. The outcome was said to be a draw, but it was hardly fair from the start. You earned dignity and peace for the Western Wulin Alliance, and whether you won or lost in the end is open to interpretation. In the end, you did not become the Western Wulin Alliance Leader, just as with the Tang Clan seniors‑great heroic figures have not been absent among them, but they stood apart, neither wholly righteous nor wholly evil, fighting whoever was unjust at the time. Always after affairs were settled, you would disappear, hiding in plain sight, emerging only when the world was darkest to light the way for humanity.

Long Xiang rushed to your side, tears welling up in her eyes, heartbroken yet proud. She couldn't help but want to boast loudly, momentarily forgetting your severe injuries‑unknown how many bones were broken. She grabbed you by the ribs and lifted you high, but upon hearing your cry of pain, she panicked and dropped you, causing you to fall heavily to the ground. You were still breathing, but this time, your vision darkened, and suddenly you saw a bridge where a kind old woman was giving free soup to those crossing it.

Xiahou Lan hurriedly rushed out to check your pulse. She observed that although you were seriously injured and exhausted, you were not in immediate danger of losing your life, which allowed her to exhale a long breath of relief. Compared to her own dignity, she feared more that her unborn child would be born without a father. As soon as she said this, you were stunned for a moment, then leaped up as if struck by lightning. Overcome with excitement, your blood vessels burst, and you vomited a mouthful of fresh blood before collapsing backward onto the ground.
The Junior Martial Sister saw this and ran to your side too, torn between joy and sorrow. She patted you, praised you, and her tears fell in streams onto your face.
Lingxi could no longer bear to see her beloved injured, so she hurriedly rushed into the arena, cut her wrist to feed him with spiritual blood, and saved his life.
Little Medicine Immortal Liang Youshi could no longer bear to watch and rushed into the arena to bandage and stop the bleeding for Ruisheng.

So what if he's the Wulin Alliance Leader? He's still flesh and blood, just like you — he bleeds, he eats, he defecates. Your small sword was knocked from your grip, but your heart-sword remained unbroken; you countered with a punch to the back of Ruisheng's hand, cracking his metacarpal and forcing him to drop his prized sword. Not to be outdone, he instantly returned the favor, aiming a blow at your ugly face. Fists and feet flew; what began with some pretense of dignity soon collapsed into a common street brawl, with neither side caring for form. You fought dirty, aiming straight for his face, and the mighty Alliance Leader, desperate to protect his own, was reduced to grappling you — and in his fury, even sank his teeth into you. Every hero watching from both East and West burned with secondhand shame. At last you were both bruised black and blue, faces unrecognizable, your final blows landing soft and spent; you collapsed to the ground together, still refusing to yield, still bickering — he kicked at your shin, you flung a fistful of sand into his face like a hidden weapon, trying to choke him. Then, for no reason either of you could name, it all struck you as absurd, and you burst out laughing together.

Both were locked in fierce combat, gradually entering a state of forgetting self and the world. Without prior agreement, they both recalled their youthful years, when they had dreamed of becoming heroes in the Jianghu, hearing the same story and yearning to become Great Heroes. Unlike Ruisheng, who had been favored by fate, he was an unparalleled prodigy, raised in Guyun Mountain with no worries about food or clothing, and as the sole disciple of a master who had poured all his knowledge into him. Given time, he would surely achieve great things. You, however, were born with nothing, covered in dust, stumbling along, with no strength superior to others in any aspect. To call you ordinary is already too kind; you were meant to accept your fate, to be mediocre and accomplish nothing in your lifetime. Yet the Sect Leader said: That's nonsense. Everyone has the right to dream. Rarely does one get to wander through the world of mortals; why not be reckless and unshaken? If your heart refuses to yield, then no distance is too far for you to reach. Therefore, you chose to defy fate, breaking through thousands of trials, and have arrived at this moment.

Blades and swords flash and clash as each of you unleash your finest skills — his Guyun Mountain Sword moves with effortless grace, while you, lost in the moment, embrace every martial art under heaven. At times your stance is solid as a mountain, its momentum coiled and waiting; at others you strike with the fury of thunder and lightning, crackling and roaring. When your techniques run out, you improvise on the spot — your sword outpacing a meteor, your palm wind parting clouds, your sweeping leg a whip, your breath turned to arrows. It is like a master's brushstroke sweeping out wild cursive script: seemingly effortless, yet every stroke is the crystallization of a lifetime's devotion! Had you not seen it with your own eyes, how could you believe such astonishing martial arts existed in this world?

This battle had no miracles. You could not defy fate, no matter how much courage you had; life is always so unfair. After your defeat and death, the Western Wulin Alliance lost its spirit, was absorbed by the Wulin Alliance, and the chaos was calmed, finally unifying the Wulin front, except for the Tang Clan. Yet your heroic struggle moved all the righteous warriors across the land. Even those who could not be swayed by words paid tribute to you. No one remembered your ugly appearance or humble origins, only the youth who, atop the peak of Mount Meishan, challenged the Alliance Leader with his small sword. You lived with grandeur and splendor as you had envisioned in your youth, becoming a legend, revered by all.

All of this had meaning. You said nothing, yet the ring of clashing blade and sword was your cry, Zhao Huo's cry, echoing to the heavens and commanding the world to listen. A clear will surged through the sword's edge and sank into your heart. A heavy will surged through the sword's edge and sank into his heart.

Ye Yunshang has about a hundred methods to prevent you from reaching the peak of Meishan. But she understands you more than anyone else, comprehending your pride and dignity, knowing why you would face death without hesitation. Therefore, she is unwilling to advise you, just as you would not abandon your path even knowing it is a dead end. Now she waits for you on the path, even at the end of hell, willing to go with you.

Two mighty figures stand atop Mount Meishan as morning sunlight shines, drawing the gaze of a multitude. He speaks frankly: ten days ago, taking advantage of others' peril; today, to discuss true heroes‑this is his tribute to you, here at this moment. There are countless mountains higher than Mount Meishan in heaven, but it is not about the height of the mountain; our meeting here makes us the peak of the Wulin. You each represent the Eastern and Western Wulin Alliances; a myriad of words cannot be expressed through the sword; they fail to move hearts, hence this battle!
The Western Wulin heroes await on the road, each nod from you prompting the heroes to bow in greeting, silently trailing your silhouette.

Long Xiang deliberately got up early, went down the mountain to buy chicken legs, and waited for you along the way, walking with you to the battlefield. She trusted you, just as she once followed her father's shadow, yearned for Wang Erzhuang, and revered Tang Buyi. These people were all powerful and enigmatic, but you were different‑you proved you could beat anyone, and this time was no different. She was unwavering in her belief in your victory.

Xiahou Lan rarely rose so early, but she waited for you on the path and walked with you toward the battlefield. The two of you talked and laughed the whole way; today your Master seemed unusually gentle, staying close by your side.

Junior Martial Sister is waiting for you on the path, her small hand nestled in your palm, accompanying you on a walk to the battlefield. In reality, she's very nervous, several times wanting to speak up, begging you not to go, but always reluctant to open her mouth. She also knows that not going isn't an option, after all, that's your dream, your heart's desire.

At dawn in the Training Ground, Tang Clan disciples lined both sides of the courtyard. They understood without a word: who but you could lead the Western Wulin Alliance? Even if someone tried to stop you, you would go all the same. So they bowed with clasped hands, seeing you off with the deepest respect, and you strode out the gate, carrying everyone's hopes upon your shoulders.

You knelt before the Sect Leader's bed, bowing again and again in deep reverence to thank him for taking you in all those years ago. Today was the day to repay that kindness — everything the old master held dear would be guarded in his stead by you, his Tang Clan disciple, Zhao Huo.
No one can insult the Tang Clan; otherwise, they will have to pay a heavy price. For this, even if the entire Wulin is pulled into it, it's worth it.

Perhaps the Wulin Alliance is right, perhaps this battle has no distinction between right and wrong, but you, the Western Wulin Alliance, firmly believe in yourselves, follow your hearts, and strive to give voice to the weak.

This chance to take the stage was rare, and you no longer wanted to play the tree. However small, however unremarkable you might be, born into this world it made no difference whether you were loved or not—you were never anyone's backdrop. You were simply, uniquely, yourself.
You have endured countless trials and hardships, hammered and shaped into a spirit of resilience, all for today.
So even if you're afraid of death, you will still stand up and defend your homeland.
You are surnamed Zhao, not Tang, and after holding on all this time you were still only an outer disciple—yet the Sect Leader always said the Tang Clan was your home.

You met the Eldest Senior Brother there; he had already known you would come. If you kept dragging your feet on making up your mind, then it would have fallen to him to go instead—not that he couldn't hold his own against the Alliance Leader, but he was deliberately giving you the leading role.

The night before the decisive battle, you dreamed of things long past. In the countryside, unless a family had coin enough to send a child to school and dream of an official rank, all that was left to hope for were tales of the Jianghu. Storytellers often passed through, spinning their tales session after session, and none was more beloved than the legend of the sword hero Long Yuan leading the heroes of the Wulin against the Demon Cult Leader—a story the whole village and town revered, more than they revered the reigning Emperor himself. Every time the storyteller finished, the village children's blood would race, and they'd snap branches into swords to take turns playing Great Hero and villain. You were never doted on as a child and swallowed hardship after hardship—how could you not long to become one of those Great Heroes, to master the martial arts, to right wrongs and cut a commanding figure? But the truth was that no one thought much of you. Even when you forced your way into the game, you rarely got to play the villain; nine times in ten you were cast as the tree, there only to be knocked down. When you woke from the dream, you finally made up your mind. You washed your face, straightened your collar in the mirror, buckled on your old wrist guards, and tucked your Small Sword into your belt. You walked into Zhengxin Hall and, before the Sect Leader lying ill in bed, asked leave to go to battle and bid your farewell.

Eldest Senior Brother has returned, and you inevitably grabbed him by the collar for a thorough interrogation. It was his fate to suffer this calamity; that he could come back to life at all was a miracle born of countless converging threads of fate. He had endured in silence until now, all so he could strike the mastermind behind it all at the crucial moment. Unfortunately, you Junior Martial Brothers and Sisters proved too hopeless — unable to bear watching your efforts go to waste at the final step, he finally revealed himself to resolve the Tang Clan's crisis.

Your heart is occupied by someone else; what you value most is no longer the Junior Martial Sister you've spoiled since childhood. Thinking she has grown up and will take care of herself, you decide it's better to use this time to recuperate and heal. The Junior Martial Sister feels lost and disheartened; she isn't avoiding you — just be a bit more patient with her, and she'll let you find her. Who could have predicted that a heart could change so quickly? A moment's inattention, and it becomes a stranger's.

You feared she might be injured, lost, or lonely. If she wandered off, what would the efforts of all these years mean? These thoughts brought sorrow to your heart. Seeing you visibly distressed as if overwhelmed with infinite grief, Junior Martial Sister felt compassion for your suffering and couldn't help shedding tears. She reached out and patted you gently.  Seeing your head turn with a mix of surprise and joy, she realized that among countless glances, you were always searching for her. Her heart melted at the sight; holding your rough, calloused hand, she rubbed it affectionately, making a teasing fuss. At this moment, she was certain without doubt: she was uniquely favored by you, no matter the passage of seasons or graying hair‑she would forever remain young in your eyes.

She said nothing, yet a thousand words weighed on her heart. At times, she blamed you for straying, at others, herself for growing too slowly, always leaving you in the cold. Life wasn't impossible to live, but it was no longer perfect. The closer you were, the more her heart felt distant. Junior Martial Sister silently stopped, no longer following closely.

In a short while, you couldn't find your Junior Martial Sister, growing increasingly anxious. You searched from the Zhengxin Hall to the training grounds, then inquired at the Alchemy Room, but there was no sign of her. Unbeknownst to you, your Junior Martial Sister had been shadowing you all along, not intentionally concealing her aura, but because she practiced Heaven and Earth Silent Power, moving so quietly that she stepped in your footsteps, following the same path you took, so still she seemed transparent.

Upon inquiry, you learned she had fought Xiang Wuyou, chasing him — head of his own sect — fleeing across the mountains. It wasn't that Xiang Wuyou was no match for her; no one could say how, in a conversation that had been going perfectly smoothly, something suddenly angered Xiahou the Sect Leader, who turned hostile and gave chase. Unable to catch him, she vented her anger on the Emei disciples instead.

Tang Clan's mastery of forging and mechanisms runs deep, and having spent years around the forge, mending an iron umbrella is no challenge for you at all. In the coming days of peace, you resolve to tend this umbrella properly for your master, and restore it to like-new condition.

Only when you asked did you learn she had fought Shangguan Sun. Though the Iron Bone Umbrella was no ordinary iron, it was still no match for the Golden-Backed Dragon King Blade — hacked to shreds, it couldn't even be folded shut again. No wonder it grieved her so.
You were just worrying about the master's safety when you saw her returning with a furious expression.

Long Xiang was shocked to see Eldest Senior Brother come back to life. Her heart skipped a beat, and she rushed over, staring at him with vivid clarity, yet stammered without a word. In the few days she thought she had left, the one she believed she'd never see again had returned, and unbidden, her tears fell first.

Long Xiang's face lit up with joy at the sight of Eldest Senior Brother returned from the dead. You wondered whether she might waver, but Long Xiang's nature was artless in both its virtues and its flaws — when Eldest Senior Brother had passed, her half-formed infatuation had already burned to ash. Though delighted and startled to see him alive again, her heart now belonged to you alone. Before you could even find words to explain, she openly owned your relationship in front of everyone. Eldest Senior Brother was astonished and amused all at once, touched by both wistfulness and relief, unable to say just what he felt.

She'd come back subtly changed. The long-standing sharpness and instability in her had smoothed away — her looks unchanged, but something in her seemed reborn. Someone you'd once caught up to now felt distant and towering again. Just as you were struck by this, she pulled out a chicken leg and ate it with relish, and at once you were reassured: deep down, she was still the same Long Xiang.
She was equally proud of you, and longed to tell everyone she met how remarkable her little brother was.

The dust had settled, and you scanned left and right but didn't see Long Xiang's figure. Just as you were about to ask the sister disciples to search together, Long Xiang emerged from the bath, having changed into clean clothes. She overheard you praising her heartily in front of everyone, feeling immensely pleased.
The recitation done, everyone had scattered.
This verse was crude and vulgar, a disgrace to refinement, and paired with Long Xiang's smug expression, it truly enraged the Talented Woman Wei.

The dust had settled, and you looked left and right but couldn't spot Long Xiang's figure. Just as you were about to ask your sisters to search together, Long Xiang emerged from a bath, freshly dressed. Hearing you openly praise her fondness for chicken legs in front of everyone, she not only didn't feel ashamed but took pride in it. Clearing her throat, she passionately recited a verse from Song of Everlasting Longing: Marinated chicken leg, grilled chicken leg, best when slightly charred. The sound of the stomach like thunder. Who are you? Who is he? The scent lures riders off their horses, making them forget to return. Delicious enough to make one weep.

Dust had settled, and you looked left and right but didn't see Long Xiang's figure. Just as you were about to ask the sister disciples to search together, Long Xiang had already taken a bath, changed into clean clothes, and come out. She heard you speaking ill of her in front of everyone and silently drew her sword. Fortunately, dull as she could be, she'd made some progress — she'd learned to bide her time and settle the score later, so you weren't cut down on the spot.

The dust had settled, and you looked left and right but didn't see Long Xiang's figure. Just as you were about to ask the sisters to search together, Long Xiang emerged after taking a bath and changing into clean clothes. You openly admitted your relationship in front of everyone, praising her, causing her rosy cheeks to flush. Her heart felt warm and cozy.

Long Xiang saw him from afar and came rushing over. You wondered whether she might waver, but Long Xiang's nature was artless in both its virtues and its flaws — when Eldest Senior Brother seemed to have died, her still-unformed infatuation had already burned to ash. Though she was startled and overjoyed to see him alive again, her heart, even now, belonged only to you.

Long Xiang spotted him from afar; her heart skipped a beat, and she dashed over, staring at him with vivid clarity, yet stammered without a word. In the few days she thought she had left, the one she believed she'd never see again had returned, and unbidden, her tears spilled first.

Tang Clan disciples stared in disbelief, unable to believe their eyes, muttering that either they had fainted or were under the influence of a hallucinogenic poison scent known as Daydream Fragrance. Yet, he was indeed real, growing more vivid the longer they looked. Even with blurred vision, he did not vanish. Simply standing in the Tang Family courtyard gave the Junior Martial Brothers and Sisters boundless courage.

Only then did Little Junior Sister realize that this was truly the Senior Brother himself. She burst into tears of joy and rushed forward to pat him, but though he pushed her away, she remained undaunted.

Two senior brothers stood on the training ground. The crowd looked left and right, unable to distinguish them, thinking perhaps they were hallucinating or affected by Bewitching Incense. When the senior brother returned, Xiaomei no longer needed to pretend, so she removed her makeup and revealed her true appearance. The crowd then suddenly realized the truth.
Little Junior Sister wept with joy and rushed forward to pat him, but Senior Brother pushed her away, and still she would not give up.
But this really was the living Eldest Senior Brother, returned exactly as he had been.
You even suspected he was yet another impostor, someone else in disguise.
Couldn't help but throw a punch to test his strength.

At first, you still thought this person in front of you was Xiaomei in disguise. The more you thought about it, the more something didn't add up. As to where the problem lay, you couldn't quite put your finger on it.

After sending Rui Sheng off, the Eldest Senior Brother finally let out a long breath. In that instant's clash he had already sensed that this man's skill surpassed his own — had he kept his distance and fought with hidden weapons, he might still have stood a chance. But in that urgent moment he had thrown himself in front of you to block the blade, stepping within the reach of Rui Sheng's sword. Had Rui Sheng meant to kill, then even the renowned Flying Hero Tang Buyi, famous through all the land, would have had no way to survive. Fortunately, it never came to that.
Both of you carry the hopes of all, unable to escape, a battle between you two is inevitable.

The words he spoke to you back then contained no half‑truths. It was just that both of you were burdened with everyone's expectations and couldn't escape, so a confrontation between the two of you was inevitable. Finally, A'Sheng and A'Huo found themselves at the fork in their destinies.
He is not a man without principles; it's just that the two alliances each insist on their own views, and the fierce battle has raged on, resulting in heavy casualties on both sides.

You had all fought to this point until your strength was nearly spent, and had Rui Sheng pressed his attack a few strokes further, he could have cut you down on the spot. Yet he would not take advantage of your weakness. Instead, with the authority of Alliance Leader, he commanded the Wulin Alliance Heroes to withdraw a great distance and do no harm to the West Wulin Alliance for the next ten days. He struck a pact with your Tang Clan's finest: today's unfinished contest would be settled ten days hence, in a decisive battle atop Mount Meishan.

A bolt of lightning struck suddenly, blinding everyone for an instant, leaving them unable to open their eyes. Within a single instant, the outcome was decided. That moment was too short to think deeply; one could only counter each move with all their skills to neutralize the attacks, barely saving the lives of a few Junior Brothers. But the most fatal strike severed your own Small Sword.

That moment was too brief for thought — you could only counter each move as it came, throwing every trick you had into breaking the assault, and barely saved a few junior brothers' lives. But the most fatal stroke of all was caught, just in time, by the Eldest Senior Brother stepping in to take it for you.

The moment was too brief to think deeply; you could only counter each move as it came, unleashing all your skills to deflect the attack, barely saving the lives of a few Junior Brothers. Yet the most fatal strike was unexpectedly intercepted by an unexpected person. The figure's silhouette was one you knew all too well, as if from another world, as though they had been absent for a lifetime. For a moment, you thought time had reversed. Who else could it be but the long‑deceased Eldest Senior Brother standing before you?
A bolt of lightning suddenly flashed, blinding people so they couldn't open their eyes for an instant, and the outcome was decided in that same instant.

The Tang Clan had suffered grievous losses, and the Wulin Alliance Heroes were themselves on the verge of being wiped out, when suddenly a flash of white robes appeared — Rui Sheng, Wulin Alliance Leader, arrived like a drifting cloud and carved a single sword-line into the ground, barring your path of pursuit. Your fellow disciples, their eyes red with battle-fury, cared nothing for who he was; without a word, they flung their hidden weapons and rushed him. But Rui Sheng's skill had reached a realm beyond compare — when his mind and spirit gathered, even the pouring rain seemed to hang motionless before his eyes.
