Though your Junior Brothers were many, the paths of their projectiles and the lines of their footwork ran straight and true, and their openings were laid bare before they ever closed the distance. His Internal Force surged through him, his sword-blade humming, as he caught and turned back their darts and shifted step and body in one unbroken motion.

The Wulin Alliance Heroes fought with a will to die, growing fiercer with every clash, and the Tang Clan could show no mercy in turn. This battle had no room for probing or maneuvering — it was uncommonly brutal, leaving not an inch of clean ground in the Tang Family's courtyard, the wreckage strewn with countless dead. Sons and daughters of the Jianghu contend for pride, and pride is spent all too easily; those fortunate enough to grow grey-haired and laugh about their youth have always been rare. As the smoke of battle drifted beneath the slanting evening light, the death struggle on the mountain at last drew toward its end.

They were not reckless of death, but victory and defeat are the common lot of warriors — stick out your neck and the blade falls, duck it and the blade falls just the same, so why not hold fast to one's own convictions to the end? So long as they fought for the common folk and gave their lives for a just cause, bearing honor in their hearts, they could die smiling. Once they had cast aside thoughts of gain and loss, what was there left to fear?

By now, it could hardly be denied that the ambush on the mountain had been a miscalculation, and challenging the Tang Clan was more unwise and unjust still. Yet it was no lie either that this was done for the Jianghu, for the common folk, and for the future of the Great Song. The Wulin Alliance weighed the whole picture, willing to sacrifice the few to protect the many. The West Wulin Alliance, by contrast, stood for the weak, looking only to the fairness within reach. It was a struggle of convictions, and which was right could hardly be settled. Hearing Nangong Shen's words, the Wulin heroes who had shrunk from battle felt fire rekindle in their hearts — if they fought for the common folk, gave their lives for a just cause, and bore honor in their hearts, they could die smiling. Once they had cast aside thoughts of gain and loss, what was left to fear?
But he had made his decision, choosing his side; even if it was wrong, he would see it through to the end.
The Nangong Family Head was defeated and captured, and Shangguan Jun went missing. The Wulin heroes lost their support, like headless flies, panicking and at a loss.
The two great Family Heads were defeated and captured, leaving the Wulin heroes without support, like headless flies, panicking and at a loss.

Among them are not a few who admire you. The two families have long been close, and he has become your good friend besides; but with so much resting on his family's fortunes, he cannot decide by personal liking alone — otherwise he might well have led the Nangong clan to stand with your Tang Clan.

The courtyard was in disarray, with widespread casualties, the Wulin Alliance surrounded on all sides, singing songs of despair. Nangong Shen came from a prestigious family, backed by a powerful lineage, with mentors from a young age planning his future. His life had been smooth sailing, even with occasional setbacks, he had never known the meaning of despair. Now trapped in self‑imposed entrapment, the defeat was certain, with no way to turn the situation around, he felt his myriad thoughts fade into despair, a torrent of mixed emotions surging in his heart.

Long Xiang reflected on herself and found she came up short: perhaps she truly was someone who bullied the weak and cowered before the strong, rather empty-headed, especially vicious toward those weaker than her, yet instantly meek and mild the moment she met someone stronger—and underneath it all, a coward terrified of dying, forever playing the fearsome, dangerous type, when in truth she was just a blustering coward with nothing behind the bluster. The longer Shangguan Sun listened, the more his smile faltered, until it vanished entirely. He, wielder of the Dragon King Blade, patriarch of one of the Three Great Families—how could he possibly be as contemptible as she made him sound? And yet, it was true: he did bully the weak and fear the strong, and he did have a taste for killing. Had he not been baptized in despair years ago by Tang Zhongling, he would never have later reined himself in and looked inward. He could not bring himself to admit that he both feared and secretly admired the old Sect Leader Tang, and as if to scatter these tangled feelings, he swung his blade in a wild flurry. Long Xiang refused to be outdone, drawing her sword to meet him blow for blow.

Shangguan Sun raised his blade and charged directly at the eldest brother, but it was the third senior brother who intercepted the attack. Pressed back relentlessly with no way to retreat, Xiaomei, seeing the situation, no longer hesitated. She broke free from the eldest brother's grip, kicked Shangguan Sun with a flying foot, and simultaneously launched a surprise attack. Unfortunately, the opponent was no ordinary seasoned fighter; he instantly saw through Xiaomei's ruse, severed the eldest brother's robe in two, and then turned back to strike Xiaomei with the hilt of his blade, sending her spitting blood. When the third senior brother saw the body split into two on the ground, he finally understood the situation. At that moment, he didn't know whether to feel relieved or sorrowful-those who had already died would never return. At this point, you had captured Nangong Shen and ordered the Wulin Alliance to cease their actions. Shangguan Sun was startled, realizing the situation was spiraling out of control. He intended to kill the third senior brother with one swift strike to eliminate the threat forever. But as long as the Tang Clan disciples still had breath, they would not allow his wish to come true. Without hesitation, they all stepped forward to protect the Acting Sect Leader. Shangguan Sun knew he could not gain anything from this, and with a grudging expression, he retreated.

Junior Martial Sister's Qinggong was being suppressed by Shangguan's blade techniques, making it difficult for her to display her agility. Under the relentless waves of blades, her steps became as sluggish as mud, swaying unsteadily, perilously close to disaster. Third Senior Brother, despite his desire to rush to her aid, was hindered by his limited Qinggong, unable to leap onto the rooftop in one bound. He could only helplessly worry. As Shangguan Sun ruthlessly struck down, his blade was about to slash Junior Martial Sister, Xiaomei could no longer feign composure. She broke free from Senior Brother's robe, kicked at Shangguan Sun, and launched a surprise attack. Unfortunately, her opponent was no ordinary old hand; he instantly saw through Xiaomei's trick, severed Senior Brother's robe in two, and then reversed the blade's handle, sending Xiaomei crashing to the ground, spitting blood. Before he could join forces with Junior Martial Sister to fight back, she was stunned by the bizarre and absurd sight, her face pale as a ghost, lost in confusion, having completely lost her fighting spirit. At this moment, you captured Nangong Shen and commanded the Wulin Alliance to stop. Shangguan Sun was slightly startled, realizing the situation was spiraling out of control. Knowing he could not gain the upper hand, he grudgingly retreated.

Shangguan Sun and your master fought farther and farther apart, growing more bewildered the longer the duel wore on. He had ranged across the Jianghu his whole life, always overbearing and proud, with scarcely a true friend to his name—the former Sect Leader of Snow Mountain had been one of the few. That year, when he received the plea for help from Snow Mountain, he had not, in truth, been entirely unmoved. Did he regret it? He did. But that was all long ago now. When he heard your shout ordering the Wulin Alliance to stand down, Shangguan Sun flew into a rage while Xiahou Lan looked on, delighted—and by now, there was no easy way back to the courtyard for Shangguan Sun.

Long Xiang does not deny the accusations. She is indeed combative. Although she does not wish to die, she becomes thrilled at the prospect of facing strong enemies. The more arduous the battle, the more she enjoys it. She was born with the ability to wield a sword, and her resistance to killing is lighter than that of ordinary people. Perhaps this is the talent for killing, the innate nature of a butcher. A slight misstep could turn her into a ruthless villain. But she has her father's noble back to chase; she has her mentor's strict yet gentle teachings, guiding her to cultivate her heart and Righteous Qi, then using that Righteous Qi to control her sword; she has you catching up, showing her the meaning of courage when she is lost and confused. Only now has she seen through the clouds and gained clarity. When the Wrathful Mist Sword was drawn, the clear sound of the sword cutting through the air marked the turning point. Her True Qi was contained, and her aura suddenly changed. Long Xiang was reborn, fulfilling expectations, finally growing to the point where she could respond to her destiny.

On the other side, on the plank road, Long Xiang fought a fierce duel with Shangguan Sun. His blade was heavy and forceful, her sword light and swift; each had a domain of mastery. But Long Xiang, proud of spirit, was used to being the one who backed others into a corner, and had never met an opponent as relentless as Shangguan Sun. Unable to hold back, she forced her Celestial Cup Sword against his Golden-Backed Dragon King Blade, and with every clash the shock nearly tore the sword from her hand—yet it was this very trial that revealed the true height of her swordsmanship. Her body moved as one with the blade, turning even the recoil to her advantage; in a flurry of white, she wheeled and struck, slashing up and sweeping down, each stroke ringing true, each move deadly, sparks scattering, not yielding an inch. Shangguan Sun's long-buried savagery broke fully loose; he tore off his mask of civility and laughed aloud, his face twisting into something wild and merciless, all trace of a righteous elder gone. This was simply his true nature—he loved brawling and bloodshed, killing by brute force, far more than wealth or power. Had he not been the sole heir of the Shangguan line, bound by that alone to keep his temper in check, he would surely have become an infamous, bloodthirsty brigand of the Jianghu. His savagery showed in every stroke of his blade, and in turn he sensed in Long Xiang's sword a killing intent every bit as piercing and clear, each strike aimed without hesitation at a vital point—even among cutthroat bandits who killed without blinking, few were ever this merciless. Small wonder the Jianghu called her the Murderous Demon of Jinxiang Palace; the name, it seemed, was well earned. He felt, in that moment, the sheer joy of meeting a kindred spirit.

Long Xiang knew her skill was no match for Xiang Wuyou's, and her words carried a hint of conceding weakness. Xiang Wuyou, a devout Buddhist, held great respect for those who did good and built up virtue; he honored her father for having saved the realm and its people, and had heard too of Long Xiang's name as a righteous heroine who showed evil no mercy, killing only the utterly irredeemable. Those she had saved were full of gratitude, calling her a sword-wielding Bodhisattva. Even if he could win, how could he bear to! And so he conceded cleanly and at once, withdrawing from the bout, leaving Long Xiang both startled and delighted.

Xiang Wuyou and Nan Xi fought further and further away, exchanging blows in the perilous mountain plank road. Nan Xi wielded the divine weapon, gaining an advantage with its weapon's power. However, Xiang Wuyou was no ordinary opponent; though his unarmed techniques lacked the power to split rocks, they were extremely deadly to the human body. The two exchanged over a hundred moves. Xiang Wuyou had reached the state of no fixed techniques, where his form changed instantly. Nan Xi, trying to read the pattern, found it impossible. Despite exhausting her Seven‑Star Sword Technique, she still couldn't win. She urgently attempted a counterattack, but her flaw was immediately exposed, and she was defeated. Emei didn't use a sword, but had a heart sword, so Xiang Wuyou had a unique understanding of sword techniques and didn't hesitate to praise Nan Xi's sword for its sharpness and versatility. The seven swords had seven uses, and the same move could have 49 variations, which made him admire her greatly. Fairly speaking, Nan Xi is naturally a promising talent, but she's still too young and lacks the refinement of time. She needs more time to mature and achieve perfection.
The two fought together, while Nan Xi plotted how to kill both of them at the same time.

Hearing him raise the matter yet again, Nangong Shen very nearly dropped dead of rage on the spot, his eyes rolling back in his head. Only the Nangong family's profound Internal Method, and his own hard-won self-cultivation, let him grit his teeth and hold his temper. Duan Zhixiu, though, was far more clear-headed this time, and would not be fooled again.

Nangong Shen was fed up with him. Ordinarily he'd have let it slide, but today was the day of reckoning between the Eastern and Western Wulin—could the man not see he was in the thick of a life-and-death fight? Yet here he came again, tangled up in this trivial nonsense. Enough was enough; better to just have it out with him.

This time was no different; Chen Xu had already fallen from grace, so expelling him would be just right. Duan Zhixiu, however, didn't buy into it, realizing that Nangong Shen was merely evading him, and his heart had already turned cold. The Four Young Lords of Flower City didn't regard him as a friend; he could just stop making friends from now on.

Nan Xi and Nangong Shen fought fiercely, and at first Nan Xi had the clear advantage, wielding only the mother blade of her Seven Stars Sword and forcing Nangong Shen onto the defensive. But the moment he found an opening, Nangong Shen suddenly donned his ancestral treasure, the Phoenix Battle Garb, and the tide turned at once. That Phoenix Battle Garb had been forged at the order of the Nangong ancestor Nangong Zhi; heavy as it was, it turned aside blade and spear alike, its spikes a hazard of their own, and it could even breathe fire to burn a foe. The Seven Stars Mother-Child Sword, for all it was a divine weapon from a master smith's hand, was limited in reach, and Nan Xi could not break through; each time she closed in she was driven back by flame, until she began to curse herself silently for her own arrogance in not ending the fight quickly—drag it out, and defeat was certain. Just then, a folding fan came flying in and struck Nangong Shen's chest. It did no harm, yet the shock of it was startling, for the technique was unmistakably his family's own Nangong Dashing Fan. The newcomer was his drinking companion, another of the Four Young Lords of Flower City—Young Lord Xiu of the Duan Family of Dali—who, true to form, cared nothing for the moment and at once pressed Nangong Shen: just who, exactly, were the Four Young Lords of Flower City? The Four Young Lords numbered five in truth, an awkward fact all along, and the Eldest Young Lord had no wish to offend any of them, so he always answered with vague evasions.

The disparity in strength between Third Senior Brother and Xiang Wuyou was vast; he was no match at all, and for all his effort could not so much as scratch him. Had Xiang Wuyou not been merciful, unwilling to pile up further killing and wanting only to beat the Tang Clan's Sect Leader into submission and end the bloodshed, Third Senior Brother would already have gone on ahead of you. Even so, every blow and kick struck deep into his body, tearing muscle and cracking bone, a pain no ordinary man could bear; both his arm joints were wrenched loose by joint-locking holds and his leg bones shattered by kicks, yet Third Senior Brother still would not fall. Though a scholar, mild and courteous in his ways, he had never been spineless, with or without martial skill to back him. Entrusted by the Sect Leader to hold the token in his stead, he knew that as long as one Tang Clan disciple still fought on, Tang Sheng would never go down. Moved by his resolve, Xiang Wuyou turned to look at the bloodbath in the courtyard, where every Tang Clan disciple fought as though already resigned to death, while the once boastful heroes of the Wulin Alliance were now crying for their mothers. Shamed, no longer able to face down the Tang Clan, he cupped his fists in defeat, strode in to drag the Emei disciples out of the fray, and declared his withdrawal from the Wulin Alliance.

Xiahou Lan's martial arts skill was only slightly inferior to Xiang Wuyou's, and with the advantage of weapons, even a desperate fight would at least give them a 40‑60 chance. But after transmitting the secret technique at the Snow Mountains, she had been severely weakened, and despite resting for a long time, she had not yet fully recovered. If she had truly fought to the death today, you would likely have lost Xiahou Lan. Fortunately, Xiang Wuyou is a person who cherishes old feelings and knows when to spare someone. Xiahou Lan could not fail to notice that the other party was deliberately showing leniency. The more they fought, the less killing intent she had. With extensive experience in the Jianghu, she actually understood human nature well, but after suffering a tragic event, her Temperament had changed drastically. She no longer cared for pretentiousness. Xiang Wuyou repeatedly showed goodwill, and she couldn't be too unfeeling. She used a move that was easy to block, allowing the other party to deflect it, and thus called off the fight, leaving no clear winner. They exchanged polite words, both preserving their dignity. Xiang Wuyou also addressed her as Master Xiahou, a title more effective than any compliment, striking at her heart. Even cold‑hearted Xiahou Lan couldn't help but smile broadly, a rare moment of conversation. Unbeknownst to them, they hadn't spoken much good words before, and as soon as the topic of Di San Xiang, the Snow Mountain traitor, was mentioned, Xiahou Lan turned against them, her attacks three times more intense than before. Xiang Wuyou was stunned, and was relentlessly pursued away from the frontline.

But Long Xiang could not wait for the future. The person she needed needed her; her wish and duty aligned, her belief was clear‑there was no more correct path beneath heaven. With Celestial Cup in hand, the Wrathful Mist Sword unsheathed, this moment was the instant of transcending limits. Xiang Wuyou paled in horror, witnessing a person transcend their former self within a breath, their surging True Qi converging inward, all subtle signs vanishing, no longer predictable‑without a doubt, she had entered the peerless realm of formless technique. The outcome of this battle remains uncertain.

Xiang Wuyou and Long Xiang fought further and further apart, clashing on a perilous mountain plank road. Long Xiang wielded a divine weapon, gaining an advantage through his arms, yet Xiang Wuyou was no ordinary opponent. Though his punches lacked the power to split stone, they were extremely lethal to the human body. After exchanging over a hundred moves, Xiang Wuyou had reached a state of No Technique, No Form, his form and intent shifting instantaneously. Long Xiang, despite exhausting her Long family sword techniques, could not gain the upper hand. At first glance, the battle seemed evenly matched, but in reality, Long Xiang was already at a disadvantage. Emei did not use a sword, yet possessed a Heart Sword, which is why Xiang Wuyou had a unique understanding of sword techniques. He couldn't help but admire Long Xiang's sword, which was sharp, bold, and delicate, combining hardness and softness, offense and defense. Fairly speaking, Long Xiang was a promising talent, yet her youth meant she still needed time to mature, and only with the passage of years could she achieve perfection.

Sometimes you dreamed of waking in the courtyard, weeping for joy, only to startle awake at midnight and sit by candlelight until dawn. Ye Yunshang set aside her old temper entirely, becoming obedient and careful in everything, afraid that you too might slip away without a word and leave her alone in her misery.
Sometimes you dreamed of waking in the courtyard, weeping for joy, only to startle awake at midnight and sit by candlelight until dawn.

Sometimes you dreamed of waking in the courtyard, weeping for joy, only to startle awake at midnight and sit by candlelight until dawn. Whenever Xiahou Lan noticed, she would snuff out the candle, draw you to sit at the bedside, kiss you, and soothe you.

Sometimes you dreamed of waking in the courtyard, weeping for joy, only to startle awake at midnight and sit by candlelight until dawn. Long Xiang worried for her fellow disciples, and more than once wanted to go back and seek them out, yet she could never bring herself to leave you. And so the years slipped away, until the two of you grew old together.

Sometimes you dreamed of waking in the courtyard, weeping for joy, only to startle awake at midnight and sit by candlelight until dawn. Junior Martial Sister missed home just as much — she would wrap a robe around herself, curl up close beside you, and pat you gently.

Through Nangong Shen's arrangements, you left the Central Plains Wulin's turbulent affairs, abandoned your hometown, and went to a very distant place. At that time, the conflict between the Eastern and Western Wulin had already been resolved, yet you could never believe it, and you tried every means to inquire about the rumors of the Central Plains Wulin.

The Shangguan Family Head's life was threatened, and the Wulin Alliance heroes could not continue their fight. Upon seeing the Flying Hero strike, even senior master Dragon King Blade lost to his attack, making it impossible for them to resist as well. They all looked at each other in dismay and were afraid of a reckless move leading to mutual destruction. If these madmen really killed Commissioner Shangguan, there might not be any chance left for the court to pursue the real culprit. Should they turn against the Wulin Alliance and punish them, who would dare to still claim themselves as righteous heroes? With their own survival in doubt, none had the heart to continue fighting. They all lowered their weapons, each one dispirited. Some even cursed inwardly, blaming the Shangguan Family Head for being incompetent yet causing more trouble, what good was he as a master.
You even wanted to call Junior Martial Sister over to join in, but she just thought the two of you had lost your minds.
Wicked as you were, you answered at once, and the two of you rained down kicks on Commissioner Shangguan like madmen, one foot apiece.

Shangguan Ying couldn't bear to watch, and threw herself forward to shield her father — after all, whatever else, he was your father-in-law, so you too pleaded on his behalf. Eldest Senior Brother was secretly alarmed. He had thought that killing the chief suspect would settle the feud between the two families, never expecting you to be so ruthless as to want to defile the man's bloodline and bring ruin to his descendants.

Since Eldest Senior Brother had faked his death and gone into hiding, he had already learned who set up the plot to secretly harm the Tang Clan — this Shangguan Family Head was one of the chief suspects, and there was no call to be polite to him any longer. In front of everyone he kicked him hard, deliberately trampling on Shangguan's dignity.

Eldest Senior Brother was amazed at how black your heart truly was, yet he couldn't help laughing until his sides ached — it had been a long while since the two of you had laughed together so unrestrainedly.
You're a very wicked person, wanting to strip someone's clothes, tie them up, and extort coins.

You were a cruel one indeed, wanting to strip him bare and truss him up to extort money. Shangguan Ying went pale with shock—even if she had cut ties with her father, he was still her own flesh and blood; how could she let you treat him this way?

Shangguan Jun's martial arts were formidable, but his strength was not limitless. He first fought a brutal battle against you, then was ambushed and had his Qihai point sealed, and finally took a devastating blow from your Eldest Senior Brother's sudden Ultimate Move, leaving him with no real resistance before he was brought down.

A commotion erupted in the arena, with Wulin heroes shocked beyond measure. The Tang Clan disciples were equally stunned, unable to believe their eyes, thinking either they had lost their wits or had been affected by some hallucinogenic poison like Daydream Fragrance. Yet the person was indeed alive, and the more they looked, the more real they seemed. Even with blurred vision from tears, they did not vanish. Simply standing in the Tang Family courtyard gave the Junior Martial Brothers and Sisters endless courage.

Tang Clan disciples, spying a new Eldest Senior Brother suddenly at your side, thought their eyes were playing tricks, or that they had been dosed with some hallucinogenic daydream fragrance. Xiaomei, seeing the real Eldest Senior Brother appear before her, was startled and overjoyed all at once—no longer needing to put on a brave face, she tore off her disguise and revealed her true self.

You had lost to the Shangguan Family Head, and seeing you with no moves left, he moved in to take your life. Suddenly a whistling gust sounded past his ear, and he hastily turned his blade to block—the Coin Dart, deflected by the strike, released the hidden force stored within it and veered to strike Shangguan Jun's Qihai point below his navel, so that drawing breath no longer came so easily to him. Seeing clearly the newcomer's face—dashing, unrestrained, his hidden-weapon skill nothing short of divine—who else could it be but the Tang Clan's Flying Hero himself?

You were worn out from continuous fighting, while Shangguan Jun, rested and at full strength, pressed his advantage with his weapon. His blade technique unfolded like a raging tide, sweeping every hidden weapon you threw off course. In your desperation, you snatched something from your robe without a thought and flung it like a thrown dart. It fared no better than the rest—the Golden-Backed Dragon King Blade split it clean in two, and it fell to the ground, scattering golden prayer beads everywhere. Shangguan Jun froze, bent down, and picked one up. Memories surged over him like a tide from every direction. The uproar of the Tang Family courtyard seemed to freeze in that instant; an old friend's smiling face rose clear before him, then slipped away again in a flash. Ruthless as he was, he was not without feeling. He pocketed the golden beads, the killing intent draining out of him, and for the sake of that old bond, he relented and spared your life.

With Shangguan Jun in your hands, how could the Wulin Alliance remain unmoved? They thought: if even a master like the Dragon King Blade had been defeated, they themselves stood no chance of resisting. They exchanged uneasy glances, fearing that you madmen might go too far and truly kill Commissioner Shangguan in a fit of mutual ruin—and then who could say the Imperial Court wouldn't still hunt for the real culprit, or turn its anger on the Wulin Alliance and lay the blame at their door? Who would still dare call himself a righteous hero after that? With troubles enough of their own, none of them had the heart left for further fighting. One by one they lowered their weapons, disheartened, some even cursing under their breath, blaming the Shangguan Family Head for being more hindrance than help, some master he turned out to be.
You knew he was an enemy of the sect, yet also respected his esteemed standing in the Jianghu—one who could be killed but never humiliated—and so you left the judgment to the Sect Leader.

You didn't spare him out of mercy, but to hold him hostage, so the Wulin Alliance would hesitate to strike for fear of endangering him. Once you had wrung him for all he was worth and collected a ransom, you would decide whether to kill him depending on your mood.

You didn't kill him out of mercy, but to hold him hostage and make the Wulin Alliance hesitate to act. Once he had served his purpose, you would extort a ransom, then decide whether to kill him depending on your mood. Shangguan Ying, hearing this, flew into a rage and rained kicks and blows on you: her father might show no benevolence, but children must never be unfilial.

Little did anyone know, Shangguan Ying's father was an old hand of the Jianghu, not to be underestimated until fully brought down. Seeing him fall, you pressed on without mercy, moving to throw a dart to finish him off. Ying hurriedly seized your arm. The dart, meant only for the vital point on his shoulder to disable his blade hand, was thrown off course by her pull and struck his hip instead, nearly ending the Shangguan family line.

Since Shangguan Jun dared to storm the Tang Family's estate, he had steeled himself to fight to the death, vowing to annihilate the Tang Clan. He had weighed which masters among the Western Wulin Alliance's ranks might prove his match, and whom he should avoid crossing blades with. Yet he never expected that, returning to the Jianghu at the peak of his strength, he would suffer a crushing defeat at the hands of you, an unremarkable junior.

Shangguan Ying threw herself before you to shield you with her life, not because she doubted her father's cruelty, nor because she possessed some noble spirit for grand sacrifice, but because she valued her word above all else in life, and having vowed to you, would rather die than break it. Shangguan Jun, cruel and ruthless by nature, was after all a man of flesh and blood; seeing his daughter's tear-streaked face, memories of years past rose vivid before him. She would rather die than remain under his roof any longer, no longer hoping to be cherished by him. Something in him stirred despite himself, perhaps only a passing impulse, and he spared your life, sending men to escort you both away from the battlefield and further trouble. It was the first time in his life, and the last, that he indulged his daughter's willfulness.

Shangguan Ying threw herself before you to shield you with her life, not because she feared nothing, but because she kept her word: you had never betrayed her, so she would rather die than betray you. But now that you have betrayed her, do you truly expect her devotion to remain unshaken? That is wishful thinking. Shangguan Jun wrenched his daughter aside and, with a backhand strike, cut down you, the faithless scoundrel.

Shangguan Jun, the Dragon King Blade, had reemerged into the Jianghu, having made thorough preparations. His strength was nearly what it had been in his prime; you were no match for him, and you suffered a crushing defeat under the Golden Dragon Blade.

Shangguan Jun has come having resolved to fight the Tang Clan to the death. He prayed to his ancestors, unearthing the Golden-Backed Dragon King Blade buried deep beneath the Shangguan Grand Hall to guard the vital energy. Since you wretch lack the eyes to see danger and have run straight onto the blade's edge, let your blood polish the treasure blade.

Since you challenged Shangguan Jun on Fengyu Mountain, he has regarded you as a thorn in his side, praying to his ancestors as he unearthed the Golden-Backed Dragon King Blade, buried deep beneath the Shangguan Grand Hall to guard the vital energy flow, intending to use your blood to purify and temper the treasure blade.
The crowd watched victory slip away in the final stretch, exchanging anxious glances, yet none dared refuse to comply.
Nangong Shen, facing a blatant threat to his life, was forced to surrender in order to preserve both his life and the family's heirloom Pauldron.
Nangong Shen wasn't truly intent on destroying the Tang Clan, and with a direct threat to his life, his thoughts raced like lightning, leading him to surrender.

Nangong Shen's fear of your Eldest Senior Brother ran deep. Even back when he was nothing but an idle young playboy, his philandering ways had earned him more than one beating from masked assailants - assailants who never bothered concealing their faces all that well. Nangong Shen was no fool either; he'd long since guessed who was behind the mask, but pride kept him from ever speaking of it. Instead he secretly gathered allies and laid a trap for revenge, only to be beaten worse than before. Tang Buyi, though he disapproved of Nangong Shen's ways, had always held back for the sake of the bond between their two families - but now that the Nangong Family backed the Wulin Alliance's assault on the Tang Clan, what family feeling was left to speak of?

Too stubborn to heed the warning, Nangong Shen insisted on pitting the family heirloom robe against the Tang Clan's Flying Swallow Meteor Feather. The Phoenix Robe truly was a treasure, all but impervious to blade and spear - but it had been handed down for a hundred years, and the constant gouts of flame it spewed during your fierce battle had worn its parts thin. Wherever the Flying Swallow Meteor Feather struck, its joints and rivets snapped apart, and the armor was ruined on the spot. The Wulin heroes, seeing with their own eyes how ferocious the legendary Flying Swallow Meteor Feather truly was, able to shear through steel with mere feathers, were struck with dread. Even though Tang Buyi's Internal Force would eventually run dry and he could not cut down every warrior on the mountain, who could guarantee he wouldn't come for them next? The thought alone made their blood run cold, and their will to fight collapsed entirely; none dared step forward and provoke him, for fear of standing in his path and being left without even a whole set of bones.

A commotion erupted in the arena, with Wulin heroes shocked beyond measure. The Tang Clan disciples were equally stunned, unable to believe their eyes, thinking either they had lost their wits or had been drugged by some hallucinogenic poison like Daydream Fragrance. Yet the person was indeed alive, and the more they looked, the more real he seemed. Even with tears blurring their eyes, he did not vanish. Simply standing there in the Tang family courtyard gave the Junior Martial Brothers and Sisters endless courage.

Tang Clan disciples, spotting from afar that a second Eldest Senior Brother had suddenly appeared at your side, thought their eyes were playing tricks on them, or that they'd been dosed with some hallucinogenic poison like Daydream Fragrance. Xiaomei, seeing the true Eldest Senior Brother appear, was startled and overjoyed at once - no longer needing to keep up appearances, she tore off her disguise and showed her true face.

You took Nangong Shen as a hostage and ordered the Wulin Alliance to cease the battle. The Wulin warriors, in the midst of a fierce fight, exchanged uncertain glances, each appearing troubled. The victory seemed within reach, yet they were unwilling to bear the accusation of being unfeeling.
You still worried that Shangguan Ying might be swayed by old feelings for Nangong Shen, but instead she urged you to threaten the Wulin Alliance with his life.

Nangong Zhi had forged this battle armor back in the day to intimidate the Jin army - the more exaggerated and eye-catching, the better - and on the battlefield it had indeed proven unbeatable, but against Wulin masters it turned out to be cumbersome. You punched and kicked without mercy and tore their family heirloom to pieces. Nangong Shen's wound was nothing, but the blow to his pride was more than he could bear, and his eyes rolled back as he fainted dead away on the spot.

Nangong Shen saw his chance and pushed you out of the yard, and the two of you plunged into the forested hills. It wasn't that he doubted the Tang Clan's innocence - but the Tang Clan's ruin wasn't for the Wulin's peace alone; it was the Imperial Court's own decree. Since Nangong Zhi's day the court and the common folk had grown apart, and the rift had only deepened over the matter of King Wumu and the Red Peng King. Too many before them had bled and wept and given up their lives before this chance at reconciliation finally came; even if it meant drinking poison to quench their thirst, they could not throw away all that had been won. If they set aside the greater cause for a lesser loyalty, who then would save Great Song from ruin?

The Phoenix Robe, though flamboyant to the point of absurdity, had uses without end, uniting offense and defense in one - a genuine headache to fight, especially since it could spew fire. You found no opening to attack, and, worn down by frustration, lost the bout.
You saw the Phoenix Treasure Robe's Pauldron was unusually long, resembling a pair of golden wings, and it could even spray fire. You were speechless for a moment.

You saw that Phoenix Robe's Pauldron was exceptionally long, like a pair of golden wings, and it could spew fire. You couldn't help but turn pale with fear, your courage stripped away by it. Before the battle even began, you were already three parts defeated.

Young as he still was for a Family Head, Nangong Shen had spent more of his years since coming of age on socializing than on honing his martial arts, and could not be certain of victory by skill alone. So this time, coming east, he specially brought out his family's inherited, invincible battle armor: the Phoenix Robe.

Nangong Shen was in fact conscience-stricken, but the old humiliation of being beaten and scolded by his former fiancee welled up in him, and shame turned to fury: he twisted the blame back onto her and traded insults, dragging you into it as well. Shangguan Ying's favor for you was plain for anyone to see. Nangong Shen, regretting he'd ever let it come to this, burned with jealousy and swore he would strip the sinews from your bones to vent the hatred in his heart.
He felt the guilt keenly, had no words to answer her, and dared not meet Shangguan Ying's gaze.
Shangguan Ying, stern with righteous anger, demanded of Nangong Shen whether his conduct truly matched the teachings of the sages.

You feared Xiaomei might be harmed, so you hurriedly urged the Junior Martial Sister to rush to her aid. Nangong Shen could stop you, but not the Junior Martial Sister. She darted into the blind spot of his Pauldron and cloak, passing through without hindrance. Nangong Shen tried to retrieve her, but this time you refused to agree.

Shangguan Sun feared the Eldest Senior Brother too much to face him, so he tossed you to Nangong Shen and went himself, blade in hand, to kill him. You were seized with dread, knowing Xiaomei was no match for him, but Nangong Shen held you back, and you could only watch in helpless anguish.

Nan Xi said she wanted to stand with your Western Wulin Alliance, and she meant it - she had steeled herself to be cast off for it, ready to brawl at the Outer Fort or duel one-on-one in the main hall, unwilling to miss a single fight. To cross swords alone with two Family Heads was an honor few in the Wulin ever earned; she had meant to defer to her host and take whichever chieftain you left unchallenged. But Nangong Shen went on lecturing her at such tiresome length that she lost patience, stepped in herself, and brushed him aside.

On that day at Fengyu Mountain, Jinxiang Palace had already announced its retirement, through no fault of their own conduct - merely because others had drawn the line between right and wrong and driven them to their doom. Shangguan Sun's overbearing manner had left Long Xiang nursing a grudge, and now that he had taken up his blade and returned to the Jianghu, was this not the chance of a lifetime for revenge? Shangguan Sun did not think much of this young upstart; back then he had envied Long Yuan and could not bring himself to kill him - cutting down Long Yuan's daughter today would ease his old grudge all the same. As for you, Nangong Shen would see to that.

The former sect leader of the Snow Mountain Sect and the Shangguan Family Head once shared a deep bond and had arranged a marriage pact for their children. Yet when calamity struck the Snow Mountain Sect and it sought aid from the great houses, the Shangguan Family Head begged off, citing the distance, and let them die without lifting a hand. Xiahou Lan saw Shangguan Sun, her face turning cold as frost - she would not go looking for trouble, but now that fate had crossed their paths, someone would have to die where they stood. As for you, Nangong Shen would see to that.

Shangguan Ying's Qinggong wasn't strong, and she arrived late, moving slowly. Facing her own father and her former betrothed, she remained resolute: living, she was one of your Zhao family; dead, she would be a spirit of the Tang Clan.

Nangong Shen earnestly urged you to lay down your sword, offering to mediate and requesting the alliance leader to show leniency. Though you refused to accept his kindness, the Shangguan Family Head could not allow your surrender, for he was well aware of the Tang Clan's ruthless nature. Should enmity arise, he would have no choice but to take decisive action, utterly destroy you, and eliminate any future threat.
You were eager to charge into the fray to help, but the two Family Heads blocked your way.

The disparity in power between the Eastern and Western Wulin is too great, the situation is truly not optimistic. For now, it can only be tolerated for a while. You withdrew from the front lines precisely to avoid an unexpected attack by the Wulin Alliance.

The Western Wulin Alliance relied on their Outer Fort to fight fiercely, overcoming the odds and preventing the Wulin Alliance from acting as they pleased. The Wulin Alliance had believed they could bring down everything, but now it's time to pay the price.

Tell him how your Western Wulin Alliance displayed great prowess, defeating the Wulin Alliance so thoroughly that they couldn't even stand up. Make the Wulin Alliance come with confidence, only to find they couldn't return home.
He asked about the battle situation below the mountain, and you gave him a truthful account.
Third Senior Brother saw you return and came out to greet you, asking about the situation on the mountain. Seeing that he still had the spirit for self-deprecating jokes, you felt reassured as well.

You hadn't meant to offend the fair lady — you'd simply grown careless out of concern for her. Junior Martial Sister knew how much you cared for her, and her heart glowed warm with pleasure: no one else, however wonderful, could set her at ease the way being by your side did.

You were furious to the point of madness — if not for Third Senior Brother's busybody meddling, you might have feasted your eyes to your heart's content, and likely could have pretended nothing was amiss while getting in a couple of gropes at her leg besides. Thanks to him, the dream was dashed.

You weren't satisfied and pressed her again on whether she was hurt. Junior Martial Sister wasn't the type to play coy and cute, but your question left her flustered, and she admitted, shyly, that she'd fallen and hurt her knee — half hoping, half afraid, she asked if you would put medicine on it for her. Third Senior Brother rushed out to stop you, citing the propriety of men and women keeping their distance and denouncing your scandalous breach of decorum.
When asked about the situation on the mountain, Junior Martial Sister only said she had driven them off, saying nothing about how dangerous it had been.
Seeing you safely return, the Junior Martial Sister put her anxious heart at ease and leaped down to pat you as a form of encouragement.
Ye Yunshang stuffed a piece of cake into your mouth; the sweet red bean paste warmed your heart, continuously generating strength and sweeping away fatigue.

Ye Yunshang, though no longer plagued by her old illness, remained frail in body. Tang Fang had taken great care of her, secretly giving her a Flying Legs Pill that temporarily boosted energy, instructing her to take it in case of an emergency to escape. She refused to run, crushing the pill into powder and mixing it into food to trick you into eating it. Once ingested, the pepper powder poison in your body absorbed it completely, continuously generating strength and eliminating fatigue.

Ye Yunshang fretted over Junior Martial Sister, and beside them a wicked thought crossed your mind: get through this trial, then find some way to have both girls for good, and enjoy the fortune of two wives at once — how wonderful would that be? With days so happy, you wouldn't even care to be called a Great Hero.

When it comes to the greatest contributor, it's undoubtedly the Junior Martial Sister. She stands on the eaves of the Zhengxin Hall, her gaze sweeping all directions and her ears attuned to every sound. No enemy approaching can escape her unerring gaze. Even if enemies scatter their attacks, she can use her Qinggong to simultaneously support the entire battlefield, silently approaching, striking with a single sword, and vanishing without a trace.

When asked about the situation on the mountain, she recounted everything in detail. Your defenses weren't thorough enough, and the number of enemies taking advantage of the situation to infiltrate the mountain wasn't small. The courtyard was once in dire straits, but fortunately, they managed to repel the enemies successfully in the end.

When asked about the situation on the mountain, she recounted everything in full detail. It wasn't that no one had climbed the mountain, but the Outer Fort was heavily fortified, and those who recklessly advanced were being dealt with one by one.
She asked again about her older brother Ye Yunzhou's situation, only then feeling slightly reassured.
Ye Yunshang was hiding in the Zhengxin Hall, occasionally lifting the window curtain to look out. When she spotted you returning from afar, she rushed out eagerly to fling herself into your arms.
Ye Yunshang hid in the Zhengxin Hall, peeking through the window occasionally. When she spotted you coming back from afar, she came out to meet you. She smiled, but it was polite and distant.

Junior Martial Sister meant her praise sincerely, but Xiaomei tore into her anyway, speaking in Eldest Senior Brother's name. Junior Martial Sister's pretty face flushed with irritation—she couldn't shake the feeling that Eldest Senior Brother had grown even more insufferable since his return. Xiaomei, for all that she was fond of Junior Martial Sister, could not stand her getting close to you. After all, it was Eldest Senior Brother's reputation that would take the blame, not Yu Xiaomei's—so she tormented her however she pleased.

Junior Martial Sister saw you return and bounded down the stairs to meet you, only to be fiercely chased off by Xiaomei, who invoked Eldest Senior Brother's name to do it—after all, it was Eldest Senior Brother's reputation that would suffer, and none of it was her, Yu Xiaomei's, concern.

When asked about the situation on the mountain, Xiaomei said it was not that no one went up; in fact, quite a few did. Although there were people stationed at the courtyard, it was still perilous. She expressed considerable resentment toward you, blaming you for making her work so hard.

When you asked about the mountain, Xiaomei finally told you: it wasn't that no one had gone up, but the Outer Fort was so tightly guarded that anyone who rushed ahead for glory had been dealt with one by one.
Xiaomei saw you return early and felt something was amiss. She pinched your cheek to confirm you were the real one.

Xiaomei saw the Painting Immortal arrive and hurried over in delight, still wearing Eldest Senior Brother's face. The Painting Immortal had not expected Xiaomei's disguise craft to be so masterful, and seized her in astonished delight, turning her this way and that, clicking her tongue in wonder. To fool an outsider, changing one's build is easy and changing one's face is hard—but to fool a fellow master of the art, it works the other way around, for anyone skilled in disguise reads a person's build, gait, and the rise and fall of the chest as they breathe; the more thickly padded the disguise, the smaller that rise and fall becomes. What made Xiaomei's Eldest-Senior-Brother costume so formidable was the hidden mechanism inside it—a Bellows Bag she could press in her palm to fake her breathing—so that even the Second-Generation Thousand-Face Demon failed to spot the flaw at first.

The Painting Immortal, who had arrived before you, drifted out from the kitchen at last and told you what had happened. It wasn't that no one had tried to climb the mountain—but the Outer Fort was guarded so tightly that any who pushed ahead for glory were dealt with one by one. Just before she spoke with you, she had sealed the acupoints of a Jianghu Young Hero named Fang Zhentian; unable to bear killing so handsome a face, she left him bound in the kitchen, meaning to keep him as her plaything once she had the time.
You suddenly felt a wave of panic without cause, and thought it was too late.
You hurried back to the courtyard, but found the Training Ground empty.

You rushed back to the courtyard, where the Wulin Alliance and the Tang Clan's mountain guardians were locked in battle. These dozens of elite warriors who had come to the courtyard were no pushovers, and the Tang Clan disciples were equally formidable, resulting in a fierce, evenly matched clash that remained unresolved.

The Junior Sister darted forward, leaping into the air with both feet planted, and not one of the hundred people in the arena could block her. A burly man swung a heavy copper staff, which just happened to catch the Junior Martial Sister's eye. She used his weapon's force to propel herself into the sky, rushing into the upper hall of the Zhengxin Hall.

You rushed back to the courtyard, but the Wulin Alliance's action was far swifter than anyone from your side could have imagined. Elite forces were fully deployed, launching an invasion as fierce as fire. Despite the Tang Clan's mountain guardians fighting to the death, the disparity remained immense, and they could only engage in a desperate fight around the Zhengxin Hall.

Caught between life and death, the Wulin heroes found the same doubt rising unbidden: a life is spent but once—why come here to die? Why train in the martial arts and endure such hardship, only to meet an end like this? They always said death was no great matter, a head rolls and eighteen years on you're a fine fellow reborn—but given the chance to live, who is truly willing to throw their life away? The Tang Clan, forced to defend itself, could hardly be blamed for fighting you to the death, but did they themselves really have to stake everything? Must this battle be fought at all? Would everyone truly die if it weren't? Standing on the winning side, bullying others never seemed to matter; even driving someone to their death cost nothing. But pride cannot serve as firewood, and now that death was coming for them instead, their minds cleared at last, and they finally believed themselves mortal too.

Amidst the chaos of battle, Xiang Wuyou targeted you, not out of passivity or lack of effort, but truly because you were too difficult to kill. Despite three attempts of heavy blows failing to defeat you, you could still move about freely, punching and kicking, leaving him both exasperated and filled with admiration.
The descendants of the Tang Family fought fiercely at the birthplace of their tradition, proving that the flame of the clan's legacy has never been extinguished and cannot be underestimated.

You and your comrades fought with everything you had, but human strength has its limits. The outcome was not what you wished, but at least you struck back with all your might—better to shatter like jade than survive whole as a common tile.

An uproar swept the arena, and the Wulin heroes were shaken to their core. You, a Tang Clan disciple yourself, stood equally dumbstruck, unable to believe your eyes, wondering if your head had simply given out, or if you had breathed in some hallucinogenic Daydream Fragrance. But he was truly alive—the longer you looked, the more real he became, and even when tears blurred your sight, he did not fade away. Simply by standing there in the Tang family courtyard, he gave the junior disciples boundless courage.

The two Eldest Senior Brothers stood together on the training ground. The crowd looked left, then right, and could not tell them apart, wondering if their eyes were playing tricks on them, or if they had breathed in some bewitching incense. But once the true Eldest Senior Brother had returned, Xiaomei no longer needed to keep up the act, so she wiped away her makeup and let her true face show. Only then did everyone understand.

The Eldest Senior Brother pushed aside his own men, having self-taught the Flying Swallow Meteor Feather. Due to his unstable temperament, he could not control it as he wished, hence rarely used it against enemies, because he could not show mercy. Now, on the training ground, all were enemies; it was either you die or I live. Why show mercy? The Flying Swallow Meteor Feather spread everywhere, countless weapons shattered on the spot, darting in and out, instantly causing several people to fall. Some died immediately, others clutched their broken limbs in blood pools, wailing in agony. The Wulin heroes saw this ruthless hidden weapon and were all horrified.

Amidst the chaos, the Eldest Senior Brother had held back for the longest time, and though the junior disciples were curious, they trusted him without question, certain he must have a plan. When the Flying Hero at last stepped in and drove back the enemy, everyone felt a wave of relief, but that relief lasted only a moment before confusion set in. That same hands-off Eldest Senior Brother was still standing there unharmed at the front of Zhengxin Hall. So who, then, was this figure before them?

The Tang Clan's defeat was plain to see, their stamina, fighting spirit, and morale all draining away with their blood. At that moment, an unexpected figure leapt into the arena, and with a single move astonished everyone present. Seeing his face, graceful and unrestrained, carefree and unbound, his mastery of hidden weapons beyond compare, who could it be, if not the Tang Clan Flying Hero?

You used all your skills to defeat a top-tier master. Your junior disciples, their spirits greatly lifted, refused to let you outshine them, and pressed a full counterattack against the Wulin Alliance heroes assailing the compound.

You unleashed all your skills, defeating a top-tier master, enough to make your name resound through the Jianghu. But the Tang Clan was already fighting with its back to the wall; without you and Third Senior Brother, the younger disciples collapsed one after another, and the battle was already lost.

The outcome was decided, with Xiang Wuyou refraining from using a killing move. However, the sect leader's defeat severely shook the morale of the Tang Clan disciples, scattering their fighting spirit. Immediately, they were overwhelmed by the Wulin heroes, and the situation collapsed like a snow avalanche, leaving them unable to reverse their unfavorable position.
Xiang Wuyou is simply too strong; even when you and the Third Senior Brother joined forces, you both ended up defeated.
Xiang Wuyou is truly too strong; even when you, Shangguan Ying, and Third Senior Brother joined forces, all three of you were defeated.
Xiang Wuyou is simply too strong; even you, the junior martial sister, and the third senior brother combined could not defeat him.

You and Senior Brother played off each other, making as if to finish off Commissioner Shangguan with a single blow. For rogues of the Jianghu to kill an appointed official is to challenge the authority of the Imperial Court itself, and if the court had let Jianghu wanderers run loose until now, it wasn't because it couldn't deal with them, but because it feared stirring public anger. Who could guarantee the court wouldn't seize on this to make an example, sweeping the whole Wulin Alliance up in one net? Xiaomei, hearing you two carry on like actors in a play, chimed in herself, spelling out for the assembled heroes what would become of their wives and daughters once they were dead. Jinxiang Palace had already made an enemy of the Wulin Alliance; once these men died, their wives and daughters would have nowhere to turn, better, she said, to just conscript the lot of them and let the whole family die together at the front, and save the court the cost of the pensions besides. Everyone present stared at Xiaomei in shock, unable to fathom how someone so lovely and lively could say something so cruel. Though things might not be exactly as you two claimed, Great Song still might have honest officials capable of telling right from wrong, the court had already moved against Jinxiang Palace and the Tang Clan, each time going solely on its own judgment, and it could not help feeling somewhat guilty; no one dared say it would not show the same face again. Thinking of the tragedy that would befall their own wives and daughters after they fell in battle, no one had the heart to keep fighting. One by one they lowered their weapons, disheartened, and some even cursed under their breath, grumbling that the Shangguan Family Head was more hindrance than help, some master he turned out to be.

As you both stood on the brink of peril, a flash of green robes appeared, and a figure silently materialized behind Shangguan Sun. When you both turned to look, you both felt a moment of disorientation. Shangguan Sun still thought it was another attempt at the same trick, but suddenly a sharp gust of wind whistled past his ear. He quickly swung his blade to block, only for the Coin Dart to rebound off the blade, releasing the hidden force stored within. The dart veered off and struck Shangguan Sun's lower abdomen at the Qihai acupoint, leaving him unable to summon his internal energy so easily again. Upon seeing the face of the attacker, all of you were stunned, you and Xiaomei with delight, Shangguan Sun with terror. Who could it be, so graceful and unrestrained, so carefree and unbound, his mastery of hidden weapons unrivaled, if not the Tang Clan Flying Hero himself?

You held the Shangguan Family Head's life hostage, ordering the Wulin Alliance to cease its assault. The assembled heroes of the Wulin, seeing that even a master like the wielder of the Dragon King Blade had been defeated, knew they stood no chance either. They exchanged uneasy glances, fearing that if they acted rashly, your band of madmen might go down together in ruin and truly kill Commissioner Shangguan. There was no telling whether the court would still trouble itself to hunt the real culprit, and if it turned its anger on the Wulin Alliance instead and sought to punish them, who would still dare call himself a righteous hero? With their own survival to worry about, no one had the heart to keep fighting. One by one they lowered their weapons, thoroughly disheartened, and some even cursed under their breath, grumbling that the Shangguan Family Head was more hindrance than help, some master he turned out to be.

Thinking of the generations-long ties between the three great families, you also respected him as a formidable warlord in his own right. This dart struck his vulnerable spot without taking his life, leaving him for the Sect Leader to decide his fate.

You broke his vulnerable spot but didn't kill him; it wasn't mercy, but keeping him alive was more useful. Once the Wulin Alliance withdraws, you might still extort money from him, and then decide whether to eliminate him based on your mood.

But he's ruthless; you're even more so. He thought you were helpless, your arms numb, unable to resist, even struggling to hold your throwing darts, making you a fish in a barrel. He didn't realize that dropping your throwing darts wasn't a mistake. After all, aren't throwing darts meant to be released from the hand? Before they even hit the ground, you kicked up, launching a hidden weapon with your foot. The dart came from the side, striking Shangguan Sun's vulnerable spot. He was stunned, while you stood triumphantly. You only said your hands were numb, but you didn't mention your feet. Strictly speaking, it's not even a lie. For every member of the Tang Clan, every inch of the body is a weapon; that's common knowledge in the Jianghu.

Xiaomei saw his face dark and ominous, advancing step by step as if a grim reaper had come to claim your souls. There was no need to ponder omens; she knew the next moment would mean both your deaths. In panic, she had no time to think, and lied, pretending the sect leader had awoken, tricking Shangguan Sun into turning back. Her lie was pathetically clumsy, and could not deceive Shangguan Sun, the Shangguan Family Head. He turned the trick back on her, spinning around to deliver a single strike that left Xiaomei severely wounded. By then, she had no time left to shed her disguise and fight as a cornered beast. Shangguan Sun repeatedly launched probing attacks, already knowing the man before him was not Tang Buyi. But that was of no great consequence, as long as the world believed he was. He faced two Tang Clan experts with a single blade, killing both the Flying Hero and the Ugly Hero. The world would not accuse him of bullying, and the Tang Clan, suddenly losing its pillar, would see its morale disintegrate, no longer a threat.

Shangguan Jun regards the Tang Clan as a major enemy, recently devoting himself to refining his internal skill, his spirit and Qi fully replenished. He has also skillfully studied the Hidden Weapon General Principles, and should be invincible against Tang Clan disciples. Yet, you, an outsider, do not follow the conventional path, employing strange and unpredictable moves. He is forced to defend on all sides, ultimately falling beneath your small sword. Xiaomei urgently desires to eliminate him, but she fails to realize that the master of Shangguan would also feign defeat. Unaware, she is momentarily blinded by the debris he conjures, allowing him to strike. Without a word, Shangguan Jun swings his blade downward. You are stunned, rushing forward to block with your small sword. This defense, though, cannot dissipate the force. You are able to face such a master due to your haphazard mastery of the Forget Shape technique, which has allowed you to challenge the world's top martial artists. In essence, your foundation is only comparable to Xiaomei's. Hardening your stance against this strike, you are instantly shaken, your arms numb, your blood vessels ruptured, and your small sword slipping from your grasp. The situation turns in an instant.

Xiaomei's movements were restricted, her confident Qinggong techniques easily countered by Shangguan Jun's Fulan Dao. She managed to parry a few moves, but was thrown off balance by the tail end of the blade's momentum, staggering and losing her footing. Shangguan Jun said nothing, and with a single downward slash, he struck. You were shocked, desperately rushing forward to block with your small sword, but even attempting to dissipate the force was futile. You had only been able to compete with the world's top martial artists by haphazardly learning all manner of techniques from the Wangxing Chapter, yet your foundation was only slightly better than Xiaomei's. Hardening against this strike, you were instantly shaken, your arms numb, your blood vessels bursting, and your small sword slipping from your grasp. The situation turned in an instant.

You have been weakened by continuous battles and your strength has long since waned. Shangguan Sun has come with a newfound resolve to fight the Tang Clan to the death, wielding the family heirloom blade at peak strength. The Dragon King Blade, which dominates its region, is no ordinary weapon; even with Xiaomei by your side, you still fall beneath its edge.

You have been weakened by continuous battles and are already exhausted. Shangguan Sun was defeated by you at Fengyu Mountain; although he does not show it, he personally regards this as a deep humiliation. This time, he has returned with his family heirloom blade, fighting you at his peak strength. The balance of power shifts, and the outcome is clear. Even with Xiaomei by your side, you still fall beneath the blade.

Xiaomei's disguise as Eldest Senior Brother was no mere costume — she had also used the Shrink-Bone Technique together with a mechanism-robe, which left her barely able to move. Yet she dared not drop the act for fear of breaking morale, so she left the fighting to you while she jeered and taunted from the sidelines to throw her opponent off. Certain she would not step in herself, Shangguan Sun traded a few blows with you before turning his blade on her instead, taunting her to fight.

You were about to charge into the fray when you saw Shangguan Sun, golden blade reversed in his grip, murderous intent rolling off him as he cut a bloody path from the center of the battlefield — more terrifying even than Fengyu Mountain — naming the Tang Clan's Flying Hero as his chosen challenge. You knew Xiaomei was no match for him, and had no choice but to risk your own neck and take up the challenge in her stead.

You must know that your Yunshang, playful and mischievous as she seems day to day, is in truth quick-witted and gifted — had she settled down to her books, she would surely have become a great scholar; had she been born healthy enough to study the sword, her achievements might well have matched her elder brother's. She has always answered to gentleness and quailed before force, and can tell at a glance who is easy to sway and who is better kept at arm's length. Men like Xiang Wuyou and Third Senior Brother, who argue themselves half out of their senses and nearly out of touch with reason, she can handle without the slightest effort. Her impassioned lecture was, at heart, simple reasoning — but once two people are set against each other, true meaning rarely gets through; it was precisely because Yunshang seemed so frail and pitiable that her words could sink so deep. That, and her clear speech and careful, step-by-step logic, left Xiang Wuyou utterly stunned and speechless — until at last he truly relented, cupped his fists in farewell, and withdrew. With words alone, she had dissolved Third Senior Brother's crisis.
At this moment, Ye Yunshang suddenly burst out from Zhengxin Hall.

Third Senior Brother had never quite shed the scholar's air of his youth, yet his heart held true chivalry — otherwise how could he have dared petition the court on the people's behalf, only to see his whole family made to pay for it? Presiding over Zhengxin Hall was one thing, but the clan's survival hung on this battle, and every man bore his share of the duty — who must live, who could not be allowed to die? Having taken up the Tang Clan's leadership as Acting Sect Leader, he had to set the example and could not simply look out for himself. A challenge issued openly and honorably was not one he could refuse.

This Xiang Wuyou, for all his formidable skill, was plainly a man of pure, childlike heart. Xiaomei saw her chance and lit up with delight — she could not beat him by force, but working on his mind was her specialty. Just as she moved to draw him into talk, the Shangguan Family Head stepped up to challenge her instead. You saw him holding his treasured blade in reverse grip, murderous intent rolling off him, more terrifying even than Fengyu Mountain. You knew Xiaomei was no match for him, but if you too were drawn away, Third Senior Brother would surely fall to a crushing defeat at Xiang Wuyou's hands, and the whole line would collapse. Seeing your dilemma, a thousand thoughts raced through Xiaomei's mind, and she made up her mind at once to step forward — a last resort. She claimed, with a lie, that the mountain hermit had some clever scheme to set your mind at ease; in truth, she went already resigned to die. Third Senior Brother saw all this, and so, by his authority as Acting Sect Leader, ordered you to go reinforce her while he himself held off Xiang Wuyou.

Compared to chaotic group brawls that tie up hands and feet, Long Xiang is more skilled in one‑on‑one combat, able to unleash his skills without fear of accidentally harming allies. Therefore, he took the initiative to engage in battle, though without a sure victory, yet with an unwavering resolve to fight to the death.

Seeing this, Xiahou Lan feared he alone would tie down both you and Third Senior Brother, leaving the Tang Clan leaderless. So, though she had no guarantee of victory, she still stepped forward to challenge him in your stead. The moment Xiang Wuyou heard her name herself Sect Leader of the Snow Mountain Sect, he was struck with instant respect, cupped his fists, and went off with Xiahou Lan.

Shangguan Ying visited Emei more than once to listen to high monks expound on Buddhism. She respected Sect Leader Xiang greatly and would never dare to take him as an enemy. However, even if she no longer dared, she now had no choice but to show her strength.
Little Junior Sister dashed back to stand at your side; she never chooses her opponents, only whether or not they deserve a beating.

You were about to enter the formation for battle when you saw Xiang Wuyou stride forward with calm confidence, as if moving through an empty space, crossing through blade and sword shadows without a single spark or clamor touching him. His demeanor was plain yet shocking to the world. You knew the Third Senior Brother was no match for him, and you had no choice but to face him head‑on.

The disparity in strength between the Eastern and Western Wulin was stark. What's more, the Wulin Alliance had the Imperial Court behind it — no troops sent outright, but covert support through the Shangguan Family, money and manpower both. With such backing, wiping out the Mud Cult would be no trouble at all; how much less so a hastily-assembled Western Wulin Alliance? However one looked at it, there seemed no way to lose.  Before the final battle with the Demon Cult, why not first crush the Western Wulin Alliance, both to sharpen their edge and to make a name for themselves?  Yet on reaching the Western Wulin Alliance, they found its people's methods ferocious beyond expectation — this was no mere defense but a total reversal, every fighter a snarling demon, and the Wulin Alliance's dignity and its very ranks alike were trampled underfoot.  The Wulin Alliance was routed, its early ambitions scattered to nothing. Too proud to flee outright, they followed Nangong Shen and crept up the mountain instead, meaning to strike the ringleader first and seize Third Senior Brother, so as to force the outer fort into surrender. But arriving, they found the Tang Clan still standing in such formidable array, as if waiting for them to walk straight into the trap — and their courage fled them on the spot. Life mattered more than pride, and no amount of persuasion from Nangong Shen could change their minds.
You have nothing to fear, charge into the fray, and go forth to carve a path toward the future.

You are timid by nature and loath to gamble with your life; it's only because others came looking for a fight that you have no choice but to answer. After all, duck your neck or crane it forward, the blade falls just the same — so why not seize their weapon and turn it against them instead? Stab them you shall.
You have nothing to fear; boldly enter the fray to fight and win.

Nangong Shen understood people's hearts through and through, knowing exactly what drew warriors to a life in the Jianghu, licking blood off their blades — mission, merit, renown, the words tripping off every tongue, stirring the heart and driving out fear. These men had already lost their will to fight, but at the thought of the glory and fame waiting for them, of walking tall and being envied by all, their impatience flared up again at once.

Nangong Shen's face showed concern, though in truth he secretly breathed a long sigh of relief. He stood with the Wulin Alliance, yet never took his own view as the only right one. If the Western Wulin Alliance vanished, future generations would take it as a warning, and no one in this world would ever again dare speak up for the weak on principle — that, too, was not what he wanted. One mountain cannot hold two tigers; a clash between the Eastern and Western Wulin was bound to come. If you wished to stand as equals, you had to show your strength — hold out at least until sundown, and make the assembled heroes of the Wulin see that pressing on was hopeless. Only then could he use the Nangong Family's good name to mediate between East and West, and turn enemies into friends. But Shangguan Sun's thinking ran in an entirely different direction. He had schemed for a long time, working in the shadows to weaken the Tang Clan, and now that things were out in the open, if he could not finish the Tang Clan off in a single stroke, he would know no peace for the rest of his life. He had no wish to see the matter settle quietly — even if he could not take the Tang Clan in a day, he would goad these hot-blooded but empty-headed heroes of the Wulin into throwing their lives away against it, so the grudge between the two alliances would only deepen.

After the battle at the Outer Fort, the group was already grievously wounded, and then they ran into the eighteen Bronze Men blocking the mountain path. It is said Songshan is the wellspring of all martial arts — no mere flattery, but a gentle warning: mind yourselves, and never provoke the Songshan monks without cause. These golden-robed monks may not kill, but their hands show little mercy either. Once all eighteen forms are turned loose on your body, you learn these golden-robed bald rogues are nothing to trifle with — a beating fierce enough to conjure an inner demon out of thin air. Small wonder every Songshan disciple pales at the mere mention of Wooden Man Lane.

The strength disparity between the Eastern and Western Wulin was stark, and the Wulin Alliance had the backing of the Imperial Court besides — though it sent no troops outright, it lent covert support through the Shangguan Family, money and manpower alike. With such force behind them, wiping out the Mud Cult would be no trouble at all — let alone the hastily-assembled Western Wulin Alliance, which hadn't even settled on a leader. However one looked at it, defeat seemed unthinkable.  Before their final battle with the Demon Cult, why not first crush the Western Wulin Alliance, to bolster morale and make a name for themselves?  Yet reality proved otherwise.  The Western Wulin Alliance resisted with astonishing ferocity, its ranks full of remarkable talents who used their outer forts to hold off enemies many times their number.  The Wulin Alliance's assault failed to break through; instead it came away bloodied, having lost men and officers alike, its early ambition long since spent. Forced to resort to guile, it split its forces in two, aiming to seize the main compound and force the outer fort to surrender.

The training ground was thick with a grand and desolate atmosphere; everyone knew this time there was no way back, only death. Yet those still lingering in the courtyard were people who could not be persuaded, preferring death to defeat. Even if the path before them was a mountain of blades and a sea of fire, even if it was a dead end, they would still face it head‑on, fight fiercely, and battle until their enemy was unrecognizable.

Ye Yunshang, leaning by the door of Zhengxin Hall, heard you speak as though ready to make a heroic sacrifice and rushed out to protest—she had only just recovered from her illness, how could she resign herself to your death now? Yet in truth she was just as unwilling to leave and fall into the Jianghu herself. So after her protest she went straight back into Zhengxin Hall and clung to a pillar, refusing to budge.

You were wicked, and open about it. You'd always known no good deed goes unpunished, and that heaven would scheme against you sooner or later—better to strike first. If your fists could not reach heaven, then you would ravage the people it loved instead.

Shangguan Ying is devout and sincere. Upon hearing this, she immediately gave you a punch, yet in her heart, she hurriedly prayed, blessing you and defending you. Even if the heavens deem you guilty beyond redemption, she implored them to at least grant her the chance to suffer alongside you, to redeem your sins so that you may be reborn and continue your previous fate.

After all, the physical body can be destroyed; at that time, all of you from the Tang Clan can ascend to heaven together and then complain to heaven. You don't need to ask about anything else‑just question how heaven, having unjustly received human offerings, can stand idly by as the world is filled with smoke and haze? You dare to complain to heaven‑indeed, you're quite bold. Third Senior Brother is a bit afraid of getting dragged into trouble with you.

You and the Third Senior Brother, upon hearing the bad news, remained unmoved, still as calm as ever. Life and death were irrelevant; the duties you were meant to fulfill and the tasks you had to accomplish were decided before the fight began. You've always persevered without ever compromising. As Tang Clan disciples, you have not disgraced your ancestors; as heroes, you have not betrayed righteousness. Even if you died in the line of duty, you would still stand tall and proud.

Upon hearing the bad news, you were thrown into confusion, doubting it all, your hearts already trembling with fear. Third Senior Brother, on the contrary, remained calm; life and death were irrelevant. The duties you were to fulfill and the tasks you were to accomplish had already been decided before the fight began. You had always strived without ceasing, never yielding. As Tang Clan disciples, you had not disgraced your ancestors; as heroic figures, you had not betrayed righteousness. Even if you had to sacrifice your lives, you would remain upright and steadfast.

You heard the bad news, your heart turned cold‑could resisting be a fool's dream, destined for meaningless death? Third Senior Brother remained calm, indifferent to life or death. The duties you must fulfill and the tasks you must accomplish were decided before the fight began. You have always worked tirelessly, never yielding. As a Tang Clan disciple, you have not disgraced your ancestors; as a heroic figure, you have not betrayed righteousness. Even if you sacrifice your life, you remain upright and noble.

Nangong Shen, as the Military Strategist of the Wulin Alliance, does not rejoice in a sure victory but worries instead about the shifting tides. If you are defeated now, all your grand ambitions will be mere empty talk. The victor is king; the world will only praise the Wulin Alliance leader as wise and mighty, while you will vanish, making no sound.

The Eastern and Western Alliances had vastly different strengths. Even with the advantage of terrain, they could only barely hold their ground, and it was impossible to turn the tide against the Wulin Alliance, which crushed them like withering grass.
