Those who died were dead, and those who were injured were hurt; they could only shut themselves in and struggle to survive, let alone prevent the Wulin Alliance from sending additional elite forces up the mountain. Seeing the Tang family compound reduced to such a small number of people, they all laughed together, victory, reputation, and Third Senior Brother's head‑all were theirs for the taking.

Seeing how badly you were hurt, anger flared up in her. She thought now that merely leaving them half-dead had been far too merciful. The next time the enemy came, she would seize them one by one and crush every last heart in her grip.

Xiahou Lan returned from the fierce battle at the mountain base and joined you in facing the peril. Her clothes remained untouched by dust, yet her contributions were invaluable. In the battle at the Outer Fort, she was solely responsible for defense. Anyone attempting to use qinggong to infiltrate the Outer Fort would be caught by her with a single claw, thrown out of the wall to let onlookers witness the pitiful cries of the victims. Wulin Heroes saw this gruesome scene and dared not venture alone to commit further acts of recklessness.

Long Xiang returned from a fierce battle at the mountain foot. Despite her strong martial arts, she couldn't avoid any harm in the chaos of the battle. Her skirt was torn, her white robe was dusty, stained with blood and mud, yet she still had a fierce fighting spirit, completely indifferent to it.

Long Xiang returned from the battle at the foot of the mountain, still radiant and full of spirit. Only then did anyone learn that Jinxiang Palace, which had come east with the Wulin Alliance, had switched sides in the thick of battle to join the Western Wulin Alliance. Long Xiang never had to cross blades with her Senior and Junior Sisters after all—instead she found herself sheltered within their ranks.

The brief calm of the clamor gradually swelled, growing louder from afar to near. Third Senior Brother, sensing the decisive battle was near, pushed open the door and stood beside you. The Junior Martial Brothers and Sisters left to guard the courtyard heeded the order as one, standing at the ready.

A small number of elite warriors from the Wulin Alliance stealthily ascended the mountain, only to encounter the Songshan Eighteen Bronze Men wielding staffs blocking their path. The narrow mountain path was transformed into a wooden man alley, where the bronze men arranged their bronze man formation, showing no mercy. They mercilessly struck at the martial heroes with their staffs, clearly intending to liberate them. To avoid alerting their pursuers, the martial heroes divided into smaller groups for operations‑some with just a few people, others with dozens. Even the most elite among them could not match the legendary Golden Legends, whose reputation echoed across the Yangtze and Jiangnan regions. The eighteen golden monks pushed their defeated opponents off the hillside, piling them up one after another. They knocked down over a hundred people, forming a small mountain of bodies, a sight to behold.

At that moment, the Tiger Battle Tank II, which had appeared inexplicably on the battlefield, disabled its safety measures, activated its external armor for enhanced cooling, unleashed full firepower, and rampaged through the battlefield, spewing fire to burn people. The Wulin martial artists thought they had encountered a demon in broad daylight, causing chaos in the rear, with pushing and shoving, trampling, resulting in countless casualties.

You feared the Wulin Alliance might deceitfully ambush the main courtyard, so you entrusted the heavy responsibility of guarding the Outer Fort to your comrade, returning to the mountain yourself, sensing that the decisive battle was near, and the turning point of the era was at hand.

At the moment of passing, you did not know if it was an illusion, but you faintly saw Yunshang, filled with deep regret toward you. She had not realized how fragile she was; taking a blow meant for Third Senior Brother, she perished. It moved her that you would go through fire and water for her. If it were possible, she too would want to be with you forever.

At the moment of death, you did not know if it was an illusion, but you faintly saw Xiaomei. Perhaps just as you rushed desperately up the mountain, she rushed toward you all the same—this time, never to be parted again.

You charged into the Tang family courtyard, but the courtyard is surrounded by valleys on three sides, with a mountain at its back, making it a stronghold the Wulin Alliance used against its enemies, always victorious. Clearly, it is your home; leaving is easy, but returning is difficult. It is like when you left your hometown in your youth, never to return. You fought valiantly, drenched in blood, suffering severe injuries, and ultimately perished on the mountain path, exhausted. Your wish to be buried alongside your brothers was never realized.

You found the retired enemy, intending to repay him in kind and wipe out his entire family. Yet hearing laughter and joy within the walls, you turned and saw the wistful eyes of a boy and a girl. They had grown up watching your back, longing for your affection just as you had once longed for your own parents' - yet like your parents before you, you had never once smiled at them. Overwhelmed, your thoughts in turmoil, you finally let out a long sigh, gently touched your children's heads, took one by each hand, and led them home. The children were overjoyed, and Xiahou Lan, seeing you set your hatred aside, could not have been happier. That night she cooked a great spread of dishes, poured you wine, and talked idly of old times. You drifted off to sleep in a haze, and only on waking did you realize that the day your wife had last poured you wine was long past - thirty years had slipped by. Your children had long since come of age and left the mountain to start families of their own, and Xiahou Lan now lay buried on the snow mountain. You lived alone there, going down now and then to buy wine, and heard that even the Great Song was gone - the realm was now called the Great Yuan. It all felt like another lifetime; you could not help laughing aloud, and laughing, began to weep. You had lived to see the fall of one dynasty and the rise of another, but your heart had died long before.

You had never been able to let go of your old grudges. You hunted down the enemy who had retired from the world and repaid him in kind, wiping out his entire family, and became a wanted fugitive of the court. Your son and daughter died one after another protecting you, and when Xiahou Lan learned of their deaths, she wept silently, then hanged herself that very night.

The Tang Clan was destroyed today, the Western Wulin Alliance collapsed, and allies scattered and fled, returning home to lock their mountain gates tightly, fearing that the Wulin Alliance would pursue and seek revenge.

Xiahou Lan took your ashes back to the Snow Mountain Sect and set up a tomb for you. She feared you would be lonely and cold in the afterlife, so she burned down the newly built Snow Mountain Sect and herself to give to you.

Xiahou Lan took your ashes back to the Snow Mountain Sect and continued visiting your grave every day as if you were still alive. Fan Xiaoyan, influenced by this, grew increasingly beautiful and refined in her speech and behavior. A woodcutter, captivated by her, dared to propose. After she married, Xiahou Lan vanished without a trace, and no one ever saw her shadow again.

You stormed into the Tang family courtyard, but the courtyard is surrounded by valleys on three sides and backed by a mountain, making it a stronghold the Wulin Alliance used against its enemies, always victorious. Clearly, it is your home; leaving is easy, but returning is difficult, much like when you left your hometown in your youth and never returned. You fought valiantly, drenched in blood, suffering severe injuries, and exhausted to the point of death on the mountain path, with the wish to be buried alongside your brothers unable to be fulfilled in the end.

To give her life for justice had always been Long Xiang's solemn wish; without a second word, she followed you to storm the Tang family manor. But the manor faced a valley on three sides and had a mountain at its back - ground the Wulin Alliance held to repel every attacker with ease. It was plainly your home; leaving had been easy, but returning was hard, just like the hometown you left in your youth and never saw again. Long Xiang and you cut back into the manor like a whirlwind, fighting back to back as one, long sword and Small Sword sweeping aside all before them. But even the strongest have their limits - blood soaked her white gown and your blue robe, heavier and heavier, until the two of you, gravely wounded and spent, breathed your last together, hand in hand as you died, standing unbowed beneath the setting sun, so that no one dared come within half a step.

You chased away Shangguan Ying and led your men to attack the Tang Family Compound. However, the compound was surrounded by cliffs on three sides and had a mountain as its back support. The Wulin Alliance used it to defend against enemies with great success. It was clearly your home; going out was easy, but returning would be difficult. Just like your hometown you left when you were young and never returned to. You fought fiercely, sustaining serious injuries, and finally perished in the middle of the mountain path. Shangguan Ying tried every means to find you upon her return, but she could not even see your remains. She clung to a sliver of hope, convincing herself that as long as there was no body, there might still be a chance. After waiting for three years and then another three, she finally became a nun at the age of forty. She donated all her millions in wealth to the poor, but most likely these funds ended up in the pockets of corrupt officials; no one could save them.

You charged into the Tang family courtyard, but the courtyard faced a valley on three sides and had a mountain at its back - ground the Wulin Alliance held to repel every attacker with ease. It was plainly your home; leaving had been easy, but returning was hard, just like the hometown you left in your youth and never saw again. You fought on, drenched in blood, gravely wounded, and at last breathed your last on the mountain path, your wish to be buried beside your fellow disciples forever unfulfilled. In your final moments Little Junior Sister stayed by your side, patting your back with her small hand and singing to lull you to sleep. Her voice grew hoarse, and at last she wept without a sound, pressed her small self into your arms, severed her own meridians, and followed you into death.

The Tang Clan Sect Leader who had rallied the Western Wulin Alliance had fallen in battle, and the old Sect Leader was nowhere to be found. Seeing this, the assembled factions lost their will to fight; one by one they threw down their weapons and surrendered. The Western Wulin Alliance broke apart, its cause lost beyond recovery. You had been defeated.
In a moment of peril, Ye Yunshang threw herself in the way of a palm strike meant for Third Senior Brother, coughing up blood and looking close to death.
Little Junior Sister was outnumbered, fighting off one attacker after another until her strength gave out, and she was knocked unconscious and taken captive.

You think Xiaomei fears death, but in reality, she does indeed fear death. However, she values you more than her own life, fighting to the death to protect your place of return, ultimately passing away in a graceful manner.

The two sides clashed for the second time. This time, whether from fear or some other cause, the Wulin Alliance's strength was nowhere near what it had been, and the Western Wulin Alliance beat them into a rout. Before you could even celebrate, news came down from the mountain that Third Senior Brother had died in battle. Only then did you learn that while you had been holding the outer fortress with everything you had, the Wulin Alliance had sent elite fighters on a sudden strike against the main compound. Third Senior Brother had chosen death over surrender, and died a hero's death.

The Wulin Alliance stirred restlessly, as if eager to make a comeback. As you faced a critical decision, a homing pigeon suddenly flapped its wings and flew in. Taking the message from its leg, you saw it was a letter from Xiao Ju - both a report that she was safe and an analysis of the situation for you. The letter carried a note of resentment, chiding you for not writing back no matter how busy you were. You were surprised and delighted, yet utterly baffled, for you had never received any letter from her at all, let alone had the chance to reply. At that moment your Junior Brother suddenly realized the truth, his face filled with shame, and confessed that some time ago, itching to test his darts, he had shot down a homing pigeon; he had tried to retrieve it, but a wild animal carried it off first - it must have been Xiao Ju's letter to you. You were beside yourself with rage, and nearly strangled him on the spot.

The Tang Clan Hidden Weapons are renowned throughout the world. A one‑sided barrage of attacks, before even close combat, has already caused heavy casualties to the Wulin Alliance. Their initial fighting spirit has been dampened by a third, and everyone's mind is set on waiting to climb the Outer Fort wall, open the Main Gate, rush in, and unleash a massacre, to vent their anger. Unbeknownst to them, you stubbornly refused to open the door earlier, but now you've come out to attack actively.

The Outer Fort stood tall enough to hold off attackers, but fighting Wulin practitioners was nothing like facing an ordinary army - the Wulin Alliance had far too many men, and though loosing hidden weapons and arrows could wound them, you would still be surrounded in the end; once their experts used Qinggong to vault into the Outer Fort and wreak havoc inside, the battle would turn against you. Better to blunt their offensive first than to hold out to the death, then throw the gates open and meet them head-on - you would still have hidden-weapon support, and need not hold back for fear of damaging the Outer Fort's own structures.

The roar of Wanli Pengcheng could not break through the Tang Clan's Outer Fort. Seeing that a stalemate was about to ensue, they could not afford to waste time and tarnish the reputation of the Wulin Alliance. Instantly, they ordered the gathered heroes to launch the main assault.

Nangong Shen watched from afar, from uneasy suspicion to shock and anger. He had known since he was a child of the enmity between Lady Wen and his father, with deep‑seated prejudices; for the greater good, he had been forced to kowtow to her as an elder and cater to her every whim, never imagining that this cunning woman would once again outmaneuver him. He was so incensed that steam was coming out of his ears. Had it not been for someone present, the pampered Nangong Shen might have burst with rage, smashing things and cursing. Despite his cultivation, he could barely remain calm; he issued an order to mobilize the Wulin Alliance's warriors and launched a direct assault.

Wulin Alliance experts had presumed that with many people and great power, annihilating the Tang Clan would be as easy as crushing dry wood and rotten trees. Little did they expect the Western Wulin Alliance to resist stubbornly without relying on terrain, pushing open the door and emerging one after another, each more ruthless than the last, leaving the attackers caught off guard and fleeing in disarray.

The two sides clashed, and the Western Wulin Alliance, leveraging their geographical advantage, firmly secured the upper hand, enduring this wave of attacks. Despite the Wulin Alliance's numerous skilled warriors, their efforts proved ineffective. The aggressive assaults failed to break through, resulting in heavy casualties and severe losses.

The two armies clashed. Although the Western Wulin Alliance had the geographical advantage, they were outnumbered by the many experts of the Wulin Alliance, resulting in a significant disparity in strength. Knocking down one, the next kept coming, so they had to fight and defend, waiting for the enemy's attack to weaken before retreating to the Outer Fort for a sigh of relief.

The Jinxiang Palace people meant only to save themselves; they went through the motions and slipped from the battlefield the moment chaos gave them the chance. They had journeyed far to seek refuge, but the Tang Clan proved too narrow of heart, and once the two sides had become enemies, they gave up any thought of settling at the Outer Fort. The Painting Immortal cast off her mask, showing her true face at last, and led her people west and south, away from the Central Lands, to the borderlands where the Great Song, Dali, and Tubo territories met, settling by a remote highland lake — never to return to the Central Plains again.

Shi Gongyuan cut down a dozen-odd men with a flurry of wild punches, then suddenly had the idea that he should seize the ringleader first. He broke through the ranks and charged straight for the Alliance Leader. He specialized in external hard techniques, unstoppable against weaker opponents, but against a true expert he could not last three moves before suffering grave injury. Yin Zhiping, seeing he wasn't truly a bad man, pretended to relieve the Alliance Leader's burden by taking over the fight — but in truth meant to let the enemy go.

The battle at the Outer Fort was in full swing, on the other side, Emei's Wind God Xie Wuchen was locked in a deadlock with the Alliance Leader. Xie Wuchen had gained fame earlier, though his skills were high, his temperament was too straightforward, making him predictable and not the Alliance Leader's match, ultimately leading to his defeat.

The battle at the Outer Fort rages fiercely, while on the other side, Emei Sect Leader Xiang Wuyou is locked in a fierce duel with the Alliance's leader. Both are among the world's top‑tier martial artists, and as they fight, they grow increasingly awed by each other's skills. Just as they prepare to unleash their ultimate techniques to decide the outcome, the Diancang Twin Venerables suddenly intervene with their swords. Though a single member of the Diancang Twin Venerables is no match for Xiang Wuyou, their combined swords are formidable. Even the Emei Sect Leader dares not provoke them, and thus withdraws.

The Chain-Fire Crossbow designed by Xiao Zhu was fierce and had an extraordinary range, as if a hundred well-trained archers were drawing longbows and firing rockets, single-handedly trampling the battlefield. Wulin martial heroes valued bravery, and even in group brawls with weapons, they fought openly with swords and spears. Losing was simply a matter of inferior skill, and they had no concept of war's cruelty, where there was no glory to speak of. Such a deadly weapon, crafted for mass killing, was something they had never seen before. In times of war and chaos, who could tell who was who? Pushing and shoving, even with martial arts skills, one could not fully exert themselves. Under the rain of arrows, all were equal, and lives were as thin as paper. Shangguan Sun, horrified, also felt greed take hold, secretly vowing to seize this weapon, for even seizing the country would be nothing. Later, this weapon, which had appeared too early, fell into the hands of the Mongols, leading to the fall of the Great Song, known as the Nest of Bees.

The Flying Stone Gang members couldn't match the righteous martial artists in a martial arts contest, but their stones were accurate, hitting the right spots to rescue their side when they were in danger, turning out to be unexpectedly reliable.

The Beggar Sect's members were all ruthless, setting dogs and snakes loose, lime powder in one hand and Knockout Drug in the other, their underhanded tricks never-ending. They cared nothing for the image of the righteous sects, and their filthy tactics kept paying off — not only wounding their enemies' bodies, but smearing filth on their faces to wound their pride as well.

The members of the Flying Stone Gang didn't understand tactics, so they didn't wait for the Gang Leader's orders and started fighting as soon as they heard someone causing a commotion. Their Gang Leader, who had indeed forgotten about this, joined the battlefield and was fighting fiercely.

Li Fugui and the new faction of the Beggar Sect had been lurking for a long time. Seeing that the Tang Clan finally made their move, they immediately gathered their brothers to launch a simultaneous attack from the town, harassing the rear of the Wulin Alliance.
Nan Xi volunteered to take up a post to guard another direction. You're feeling a bit embarrassed, as if you were an emperor touring the land, with two top martial artists guarding on either side.

You once received Jinxiang Palace's protection and did not wish to become their enemy, so you tried to persuade the palace maids to leave. Instead of leaving, they turned against you and defected to your Western Wulin Alliance. Lady Wen too revealed her true face — she was the Painting Immortal in disguise. These women were cunning through and through; their show of answering the Wulin Alliance's call eastward was only a pretext to have others escort their own people, spending lavishly on food, lodging, and travel the whole way, since Nangong and Shangguan would foot the bill. The moment they reached the Tang Clan, they turned coat at once and threw in with the Western Wulin Alliance.
Ye Yunzhou was extremely cautious, following you out but stopping ten zhang away to guard your rear.

When two nations are at war, envoys go unharmed, and the righteous sects of the Wulin prize their reputation above all. Send the head of the Nangong family down the mountain first — if anything befalls you going out alone, the other side will find no way to justify it, whatever they claim.

You were only joking, but Little Junior Sister took it to heart and grew terribly anxious. Beauty is in the eye of the beholder, and to her you seemed beyond compare; she dreaded that someone might truly steal you away, her heart lurching between hope and dread, both aggrieved and on edge.

Two countries are at war but don't kill their envoys; you being alone is actually safer. After all, you don't believe those women can do anything to you, do you? Are they going to tie you up and force you to marry a Tang woman and have children?
The newcomers are from Jinxiang Palace; you decide to go alone to negotiate.

Since the fight had already begun, neither side could stand idly by, and both rushed to the center as a great battle broke out. Wanli Pengcheng, fighting you and your master to his heart's content, had his pleasure interrupted; displeased, he flew clear of the battlefield.

Xiahou Lan's Internal Skill was profound, her attainment far surpassing her peers'. Shielded by true qi, she took no harm at all — at most the howling grated on her ears. But she saw the Western Wulin Alliance reeling and badly shaken by it. If that old man kept up his breath and roared a few more times, she thought, the fight might collapse before it even began, which would be a sorry way to lose. So she sighed softly, tapped her toes, and leapt from the watchtower, meeting the Songshan Eagle Claw Divine Skill with her own Soul-Stealing Phantom Claw. It wasn't that you lacked faith in your master — only that the opponent was so strong you feared for her safety, and seeing her go, you hurried out after her to fight the legendary master together.
You had no choice but to throw open the gates and strike out.

You just don't believe in superstitions, tightly closing the Main Gate. Wanli Pengcheng's lion's roar, carrying infinite Internal Force, shook the plains, causing the utensils in the Outer Fort to hum with resonance. Even if one covered their ears, they could not parry its impact. Those with weaker internal skills were instantly injured, and those with small courage died of fright on the spot.

Nangong Shen still wanted to provoke Wanli Pengcheng into roaring again, hoping he'd refuse to open the door and at least kill him to eliminate a major threat. But Wanli Pengcheng didn't buy into it. Though he looked like a wild man, he wasn't someone to be underestimated, and he completely ignored Nangong Shen, instead making him very angry.
Nangong Shen sees that you are well, feeling a mix of admiration and relief. He considers you a friend, and even in opposition, he does not wish for your demise.

Wanli Pengcheng heard this and instead secretly rejoiced. Stopping the technique was to preserve Internal Force, and also out of a desire to cherish talent. It would be easy to exhaust you, but the Jianghu would lose a promising talent.

You too have dabbled in sound-wave inner skills and know the trick of it. Though your Internal Force is far less refined than your opponent's and can't overpower his, it can still cancel out part of the force. Climbing to the fortress tower, you face Wanli Pengcheng from afar; both of you gather your true qi, channel your inner strength, and let out a long cry. The invisible currents of Internal Force clash and cancel each other in midair, so that by the time the sound reaches the outer fortress its power has already faded — loud as it still is, no longer enough to shake the inner breath or injure unseen.

Shangguan Ying's voice, like the Hedong Lion's Roar, has made a considerable contribution. She has a strong sense of righteousness and legitimacy; shouting loudly and beating people randomly can also increase merit. What day is this today? It's even better than a birthday.
Xiahou Lan only covered her ears, finding it annoying. Several times she tried to shout, but always felt it was undignified, so she gave up.

Junior Martial Sister is quiet and reserved, rarely speaking loudly, and this was the first time she had shouted so much, her voice hoarse and cheeks flushed red, both embarrassed and inexplicably excited.

Ye Yunzhou has always been humble and well‑mannered in his conduct, wielding the Gentleman Sword and following the Gentleman's Style. It was the first time he had ever let loose without worrying about his image, shouting loudly, feeling a surge of relief, and couldn't help but burst into laughter.

Nangong Shen still wanted to provoke Wanli Pengcheng into roaring again. But Wanli Pengcheng didn't take the bait. Though he looked like a wild man, he wasn't someone to be underestimated. He greatly admired the integrity of the Western Wulin Alliance, but he found the young Family Head utterly unappealing and completely ignored him, leaving Nangong Shen furious beyond measure.
Nangong Shen sees that you are well, feeling a mix of admiration and relief. He considers you a friend, and even in opposition, he does not wish for your demise.

Danxiazi had fought his way across real battlefields, and drumming and roaring were second nature to him. He had never heard a lion's roar before and had no idea how fearsome the Sound Wave Skill could be — he took it for mere cheering, thinking, shout loud enough and surely our spirit won't lose to some old man. As it happened, the Buddhist Lion's Roar Skill works by carrying Internal Force on sound waves to shake a man's inner breath and injure him — the more faint of heart the victim, the worse he suffers. Your own shouting couldn't cancel out that sacred roar, but with only friendly voices in your ears, your spirits stayed high, and Wanli Pengcheng's howl lost much of its effect.

When Long Xiang left the fortress, she had already resolved to risk her life without killing anyone, aiming only to cut the tendons of her senior and junior sisters, hoping to save a few of their lives before she collapsed from exhaustion. At that moment the unfamiliar Nan Xi stepped in to help, planting a foot three paces behind Long Xiang's left shoulder — an awkward, hard-to-guard blind spot for any right-handed swordsman. If Nan Xi wasn't an enemy, the move was as good as a silent declaration: I've got your back. The two had never met, only heard of each other's names, yet in those few exchanged words they felt a kindred spirit — even dying side by side would be an honor. But to their surprise, the Jinxiang Palace women showed no alarm at all, only smiles. Lady Wen then revealed her true face — she had been the Painting Immortal in disguise all along. This pack of women harbored no end of malice: they'd only pretended to answer the Wulin Alliance's call east so the alliance would escort their own palace attendants, squandering food, lodging and travel expenses without restraint the whole way, since Nangong and Shangguan were footing the bill regardless. The moment they reached the Tang Clan, they turned on their hosts and threw in with the Western Wulin Alliance.

When Long Xiang left the fortress, she had already resolved to risk her life without killing anyone, aiming only to cut the tendons of her senior and junior sisters, hoping to save a few of their lives before she collapsed from exhaustion. But she never expected the others to greet her with smiles instead. Lady Wen then revealed her true face — she had been the Painting Immortal in disguise all along. This pack of women harbored no end of malice: they'd only pretended to answer the Wulin Alliance's call east so the alliance would escort their own palace attendants, squandering food, lodging and travel expenses without restraint the whole way, since Nangong and Shangguan were footing the bill regardless. The moment they reached the Tang Clan, they turned on their hosts and threw in with the Western Wulin Alliance.

The person who arrived was a disciple of Jinxiang Palace. Long Xiang felt it was her duty and, disregarding any obstruction, leapt out of the fortress with sword in hand. You had no choice but to grit your teeth and prepare to use your Qinggong to chase after her, only to be pulled back to the ground from behind. As Nan Xi's voice rang out, you turned around and saw her already chasing after Long Xiang.

The one who came was a disciple of Jinxiang Palace. Long Xiang felt a sense of responsibility and, disregarding the obstacles, leaped out of the fortress with a sword in hand. You truly had no way to stop her, so you could only follow.

You have only slightly glimpsed the surface of the Sound Wave Skill. Unfortunately, your Internal Skill is far less refined than the opponent's. It's acceptable for one‑on‑one duels, but trying to affect multiple people would be beyond your capability. Even if you exhaust your Internal Force and roar it back, it's hard to counter the power.

You see her lightly scolding, slightly angry expression and think she's probably forgotten about your flirtations. But you don't realize she fears sudden misfortune — that if she dies without reconciling with you, she'll carry the regret into the underworld and delay her next life. Better to stay just friends for now; if you both survive today, there's time enough to settle old scores later.

Shangguan Ying had already set off down the mountain before you, and you caught up with her halfway, dragging her down the mountain together. She was gasping for breath, excusing herself on grounds of gender propriety, refusing to be carried or hugged, only to later blame you for not being sufficiently understanding, fuming silently.
Finally, after everyone's earnest and persistent persuasion, they managed to convince him.
It's still the Beggar Sect brothers who have been with him day and night, knowing how to handle this person, using the safety of his dog as a threat, which made Fan Xiaotian temporarily calm down.
Seeing that everyone couldn't stop her, Xiahou Lan finally stepped in, twisted her ears, and took her away.
Fan Xiaotian was the most fearless, the first to want to charge out and fight with all their might.

Fourth Senior Brother made up his mind to follow him today, but he was unaware that during Danxiazi's time in Xiangyang's military service, he had always led from the front. Otherwise, how could he have earned the deep affection of his comrades? Without a military rank, he was still respectfully called a general. Upon hearing this, Fourth Senior Brother suddenly felt it was inappropriate to follow him.
It's still the General of Dao Techniques Danxiazi who's reliable; with a single shout, he calmed the crowd down.

Fourth Senior Brother left the mountain early to hold the Outer Fort, yet he was more panicked than anyone else, jumping about frantically. Seeing him like that, the people around him couldn't help but feel uneasy.
The Western Wulin Alliance had no means of resistance; everyone was at a loss, rushing to tear strips of cloth and cover their ears in an attempt to alleviate the harm caused by the Sound Wave Skill.

Nangong Shen's pained expression struck Wanli Pengcheng as unlike him. But this troubled look on the young lord's face reminded him so vividly of the young Old Master Nangong that it stirred old memories, and moved by fondness for his late friend, he decided to step in and help. Wanli Pengcheng had once been Head of the Bodhidharma Hall of the Songshan Sect, versed in the Tendon-Changing Classic Internal Skill, his Internal Force immensely deep—with a single lion's roar, it was no wonder that the timid or the weak in internal power might be struck senseless or even frightened to death on the spot. He hastily ordered the Wulin Alliance warriors to withdraw three miles, so that when his Buddhist chant assailed their minds, the Tang Clan would have no choice but to open its Main Gate and meet them head-on.

Just at this moment, Lady Wen stepped out from the crowd to offer her strategy. Everyone had assumed that, since the Wulin Alliance had coerced Jinxiang Palace into joining, her response this time would be mere lip service, and that she would surely hold back her true effort—who could have guessed she would volunteer to lead the charge? Nangong Shen was overjoyed, though his feelings toward Lady Wen were complicated; with a great enemy at hand, he could only set aside their personal grudge. He then ordered the Wulin Alliance warriors to withdraw three li, so that Lady Wen could unleash her Sound Wave Skill, assailing mind and soul, and force the Tang Clan to open its Main Gate and face them head-on.

The Tang Clan's Outer Fort is built at the mountain pass, where everyone going up or down the mountain must pass through. It usually serves as a trading post for mountain goods, and if necessary, closing the main gate can turn it into a stronghold against outside enemies. Although the Wulin heroes can use Qinggong to bypass it, they cannot ignore the risk of your Western Wulin Alliance opening a rear gate and coordinating with the compound above and below for a pincer attack. Therefore, no matter what, they must first seize the Outer Fort. But seeing its formidable defenses, still standing after a century, they knew a direct assault would cost the Wulin Alliance dearly in casualties. Military Strategist Nangong Shen pondered deeply but could not, for the moment, devise a plan.
The current disciples take you as their leader, and the Tang Clan descends from the mountain.
Junior Martial Sister pats your back and earnestly casts her proudest spell: wishing you safety, blessing you with good fortune, and hoping you will forever be fearless.

Junior Martial Sister saw you were about to leave and wanted to say something but held her tongue in the end. Ultimately, she grew soft‑hearted, patted your back, and earnestly cast her proudest little spell: wishing you safety, blessing you with good fortune, and hoping you would always be fearless.
Let the world know that the Tang Clan has not declined and cannot be underestimated. At this very moment, you and I are present, and this is the era of the Tang Clan's greatest strength.
To make those arrogant righteous martial artists remember the terror of the Tang Clan, to ensure they spend the rest of their lives haunted by nightmares, regretting their actions every day.

You've been tempered through countless trials, hammered and shaped yet never broken, and have undergone a true transformation. You are no longer the timid outsider disciple of old, ordered and commanded by others as they pleased. Now your voice commands all, echoing through the courtyard, shaking the Jianghu.

Even channeling your Internal Skill, you could not make out what was happening below the mountain — the clash of arms had ceased, meaning either victory or defeat had been decided. Reckoning no assassin was likely to strike again so soon, you dared to sit cross-legged on the ground, steadying your breath and tending your wounds, and slowly recovered some of your spirit.

Even channeling your Internal Skill, you couldn't hear what stirred below the mountain—the clash of arms had ceased, and it was either victory or defeat. You judged there would be no more assassins for the moment, and were about to sit cross-legged on the ground, steady your breath, and tend your wounds, hoping to recover a little strength. Little did you know that the true enemy had waited patiently for this very moment to show himself—the Thousand-Faced Demon, Patriarch Wuxiang, who had come for you and you alone. The Eastern and Western Wulin Alliances were too unevenly matched; left to chance, you would almost certainly die. That he could not allow—not for anything. He would not let you see your fight through to the end and perish a hero's death. He had to act before you died, to defile your convictions and break your resolve, so that your death would count for nothing.

Fourth, lean on Third Senior Brother as support to root out any rivals and keep other women at arm's length from you. When she married, it had to be someone utterly devoted—she would allow no one else to share his favor. Apart from your Junior Martial Sister Tang Moling, she had no intention of sharing a husband with anyone else in this world. Even if you really did end up marrying them both, you'd get no joy out of it—the two of them would become true sisters, thick as thieves, and where would that leave you?

While you fought outside, Third Senior Brother and Ye Yunshang sat no less restlessly in Zhengxin Hall. But he bore too heavy a charge; until the Western Wulin Alliance settled on its new Leader, he stood as its spiritual figurehead and could not risk himself except in direst need, so he could only master his impatience and remain seated within Zhengxin Hall. When Yunshang heard the commotion outside die down, with no marauders breaking in to wreak havoc, she let out a long breath and her face brightened. She knew you would toil on without ever claiming credit for yourself, so she resolved to claim your reward for you in advance. Ever since the Ye siblings had come to the Tang Clan, she had pestered Third Senior Brother constantly, calling him Grandfather as though it were the most natural thing in the world; he could never bring himself to correct her, and so let it stand. In truth, Third Senior Brother had had no family left since the year he passed the metropolitan examination and travelled to Lin'an for his audience with the emperor. He had spoken for the common people and remonstrated bluntly at court, and for it had earned the enmity of the powerful; his family, who had given everything so he could study, never enjoyed a day's ease for it, and were dragged down with him instead. Even now, whenever the memory returned to him, it left him sunk in sorrow. Every time Yunshang called him Grandfather, the word sank into his heart, and before he knew it he had truly come to think of her as his granddaughter. Whatever Ye Yunshang wanted that he could give her, he gave without hesitation—even the modest savings he had always kept by him, he meant one day to leave her as a dowry. Yunshang and you loved each other truly, and with no elders left in her family, her elder brother stood in a father's place; besides, you were both children of the Jianghu, so a simple bow before the hall would have made you husband and wife well enough. Yet she insisted on claiming your reward first, asking Third Senior Brother to give his blessing and betroth her to you formally. It looked at first like an unnecessary flourish, but her reasoning ran deep. First, marrying as the Sect Leader's granddaughter let the wedding be held with proper pomp and honor. Second, it would raise your standing by a back door—from then on, no one could call you a disciple of another surname, only the Son-in-Law of the Tang Clan. Third, it would warm Third Senior Brother's heart. Everyone came away pleased.

Defeating the waiter left Shangguan Ying stunned—she could hardly believe a mere tavern waiter could reach such heights of martial skill, his strength rivaling any sect leader's. That a talent like this would content himself with hiding his name and living in obscurity! Had she still been of the Shangguan family, she would surely have spared no expense to recruit him.

Defeating the Thousand-Faced Demon left Shangguan Ying shaken, and she had doubted whether the legend of the Thousand-Faced Demon was real or just a fabrication. If it was true, you'd be the prime suspect‑after all, who else could look so ugly? You could only smile bitterly at this. It wasn't the first time you'd been mistaken for the Thousand-Faced Demon; some people had beaten you up, and others had even tried to tear your face off. Shangguan Ying looked at you with a mix of sympathy and tenderness, stepping forward to gently caress your face. Just as you were about to feel a surge of affection, she suddenly tugged at your skin. You were both angry and amused, but you couldn't really hold a grudge against her.
The Junior Martial Sister couldn't figure out why the Waiter's martial arts were so high and why he was at odds with the Tang Clan all along.

Junior Martial Sister had been unruly as a child, and the elders had often used the Thousand-Faced Demon to frighten her into behaving. As a result, deep down she had come to believe the Thousand-Faced Demon wasn't a living person at all, but a demon that embodied fear itself. She never expected the demon to take real form today, let alone be defeated by you—her admiration for you was beyond words. As for just how vicious her own strikes had been when she lashed out in panic, she herself remained completely unaware.

The waiter was startled into laughter. Even if the Wulin Alliance Leader himself had said such a thing, he might not have believed it—but the Tang Clan truly was different from the rest. You were not snobbish like the Shangguan, nor pretentious like the Nangong; you acted swiftly and decisively, and when roused to anger were as fearsome as madmen, enough that even the emperor held you in some wariness. The Thousand Lantern Tower's scheming treachery had enraged the Tang Clan, and it was time they tasted the consequences. He staked all his hope on the Tang Clan, cupped his fist to you in salute, and retreated, leaping clear of the courtyard.

But how could he trust you, when your Tang Clan was under siege by the Wulin Alliance and could barely protect itself? Even if the Tang Clan kept its word, it could not guarantee his wife and family from harm at the Thousand Lantern Tower's hands. Better to cut out his own heart and die to prove his resolve, buying his family a lifetime free of worry—they would only think he had proven unfaithful and abandoned them, and go to their graves never knowing he had been a murderer with blood on his hands.

Thousand-Faced Demon practiced martial arts without following the righteous path, specializing in concealment and assassination. Bearing a mission, he chose to engage in direct combat instead of utilizing his hidden skills, undoubtedly seeking self‑destruction. You put yourself in his shoes; if this person was forced by Thousand Lantern Tower with no way out, why not simply level the tower?
The Thousand-Faced Demon had run rampant across the Jianghu, killing countless people. Today he fell to your small sword and was executed by the Tang Clan.
The waiter chuckled and, in the capacity of Yang from the Chuanquan Tavern in Meishan Town, issued a challenge to you.

Xiaomei, as the fourth-generation Thousand-Faced Demon, couldn't help but feel a pang of melancholy upon hearing this. Changing faces and hearts alike, putting on airs like an actor on stage, the more skillful she became at it, the less she could recall her own true face.

No one is. Whether renowned or nameless, kings and beggars, they are all merely passing guests, gathering briefly in the world, and in an instant returning to dust. Even the Thousand-Faced Demon, with a thousand faces, still possesses only one body and one heart‑no more, no less.

He is the deepest water of Jianghu, the most intense black. His reputation has spread for a full sixty years, yet it remains uncertain whether he even exists. Those who have seen his true face have all perished.
His movements are far from ordinary; in the vast Jianghu, no one knows his name. Hinted to this extent, his identity is already clear‑

Others might not know, but you understood all too well—this man was none other than the dread Thousand-Faced Demon, whose name alone made men's blood run cold. Fail to know Mount Lu's true face, and you may brush past King Yama himself like a stranger; come to know Mount Lu's true face, and who is left to weep over your unmarked, ownerless grave? Once he showed his true skill, he never left a soul alive. You had thought he'd forsaken his evil ways and fled far away, but in the end he could not escape the Thousand Lantern Tower's clutches—too many people and things he could not let go of. He did not ask for your forgiveness, only that you accept a swift death.

Xiaomei knew the man's identity the moment she saw his face, struggling to suppress her surprise. Now the enemy was in the open, while she remained in the shadows; she must strike with one decisive blow, otherwise this man was truly too dangerous.
Even the junior martial sister recognized him.

The second assassin was the waiter at the inn in Meishan Town. He married the shopkeeper's daughter, always bowing and smiling to everyone, and had once been beaten by the Flying Stone Gang's thugs, breaking his ribs. He was the most ordinary and honest person, yet he was an assassin.

Shangguan Ying recalled past events, sorrow welling up within her, she knelt before Shi Ming's body and wept aloud. After a long while, she wiped away her tears, bowed respectfully several times, and performed the rites for his body.
Shangguan Ying recalled past events, sorrow welling up within her, and knelt before Shi Ming's body, crying aloud. Fortunately, Sect Leader Wei was there to comfort her.

You know that Shi Ming has spent decades mastering the internal skills of the Buddhist sect, which are far beyond what you can withstand. Pitting Internal Force against him would be akin to suicide. However, the Tang Clan's martial arts rely on the unexpected to achieve victory, so you deliberately attack where you are weak against his strength. Shi Ming merely thinks you are tired of living and intensifies his Internal Force, aiming to crush your insides, but he did not anticipate that you were deliberately exchanging injury for opportunity, launching hidden weapons into the sky before the clash of palms.  This hidden strike was originally enough to defeat him, but Shangguan Ying, seeing you spit blood and cry out in shock, inadvertently alerted Shi Ming, letting him evade the Throwing Dart's lethal blow and leaving you to suffer the consequences. Your cleverness backfired, and you were caught by the overwhelming Internal Force, unable to break free. Even if you strained to hold on, you would surely perish within half a stick of incense.  Shi Ming further urged Shangguan Ying to abandon darkness for light, to kill you and prove her sincerity, believing that with this merit, she would have no trouble returning to the Shangguan family. Even the Eldest Young Lord Nangong would look at her differently, and the two might reconcile. Shangguan Ying picked up the Throwing Dart that had fallen at her feet, but instead of aiming it at you, she struck at Shi Ming. She needed to prove her intentions, both to the Tang Clan and to you.  In the face of Shi Ming's harsh words, Shangguan Ying recited the Huayan Sutra, each verse striking at Shi Ming's sore spots, filling him with shame and fury, yet his rage was extinguished by a single tear from Shangguan Ying. Her invocation of the sutra was a sincere effort to help her Martial Uncle attain clarity and distance from evil deeds; no amount of eloquence could rival the compassion in her words.  At the brink of death, Shi Ming finally achieved profound enlightenment, breaking through the cycle of life and death, unwilling for Shangguan Ying to bear the burden of killing a monk, and declared his intention to return to secular life.
The Sect Leader reveres Buddhism and shows special courtesy to monks; otherwise, how could this wicked monk have survived until now? You are different. Anger you, and hair or not, they all die.

Seeing him end up like this, one can't help but feel a sense of melancholy. That year, that night, the wind and rain raged. If the Sect Leader were truly a demon, what difficulty would there be in entering the door and slaughtering all the monks to the last? He had already let go, yet Shi Ming still clings stubbornly to his past, repeatedly targeting the Tang Clan. He could have enjoyed his old age, yet ultimately died from his own obsession.

Shi Ming believed the Tang Clan had no more capable hands, so he took a reckless gamble, only to underestimate you, leading to a complete loss. Hiding for years, surviving under the sect leader's own hand, yet dying at your hands, a mere junior, regretting it too late.
The Sect Leader reveres Buddhism and shows special courtesy to monks; otherwise, how could this wicked monk have survived until now? You are different. Anger you, and hair or not, they all die.

Seeing him end up like this, one can't help but feel a sense of melancholy. That year, that night, the wind and rain raged. If the Sect Leader were truly a demon, what difficulty would there be in entering the door and slaughtering all the monks to the last? He had already let go, yet Shi Ming still clings stubbornly to his past, repeatedly targeting the Tang Clan. He could have enjoyed his old age, yet ultimately died from his own obsession.

Shi Ming thought the Tang Clan had no more capable people, so he took a reckless gamble, only to have underestimated you and Xiaomei. Hiding and concealing for years, he didn't die at the sect leader's hands, yet perished at the hands of you two juniors, regretting it in vain.
The Sect Leader reveres Buddhism and shows special courtesy to monks; otherwise, how could this wicked monk have survived until now? You are different. Anger you, and hair or not, they all die.

Shi Ming thought the Tang Clan had no more capable people left, so he took a reckless risk, only to have underestimated you and the junior martial sister. Hiding for years, he survived the sect leader's hands but fell at the hands of you two juniors, regretting it too late.

If the Sect Leader were truly a demon, what difficulty would there be in entering the door and slaughtering all the monks to the last? He had already let go, yet Shi Ming still clings stubbornly to his past, repeatedly targeting the Tang Clan. He could have enjoyed his old age, yet ultimately died from his own obsession.
Thanks to Zou Bo's great assistance, you defeated Shi Ming. How could he not hate that Zou Bo caused his scheme to fail at the very last moment?

Unexpectedly, Zou Bo did not descend the mountain but remained seated in the courtyard. Though Buddhism and Taoism differ, Zou Bo has always respected Shi Ming as a person. Unexpectedly, he would hear him utter evil words with his own ears. Thus, the accusations from Fengyu Mountain against the Tang Clan must be mere false charges.

Once the sect leader falls, Shi Ming will have no restraint, merely needing to eliminate you younglings with a single palm strike, enter the hall and strangle the sect leader, and the long‑entangled inner demon will dissipate.
When the sect leader falls, Shi Ming has no more restraint; even Xiaomei disguised as the Eldest Senior Brother couldn't scare him.

Shangguan Ying studied Buddhism and practiced martial arts at the Fujian Branch of the Songshan Sect, where she once received guidance from Shi Ming. As she grew older, she crossed paths with him again and again on her business travels, and came to see it as fate. Whenever this Martial Uncle held a sermon, she would always go out of her way to attend and seek his counsel. In her eyes, Shi Ming had always been noble and upright — how could he have become such a hypocrite now?

Shi Ming was originally a high-ranking Buddhist monk with deep spiritual attainments. At a young age, he took charge of the abbot position at the Southern Branch of Songshan Monastery. It was only because of his benevolent heart and leniency towards a criminal that the Tang Clan's demonic figure knocked on the temple door dozens of times outside one evening. That night, lightning flashed frequently, casting eerie shadows through the window like those of demons. The monks said evil spirits had descended upon them, reciting scriptures in unison. Though the sect leader's character was often capricious, he held great respect for Buddhist practices, so the chanting never ceased — yet the figure outside made not a sound, and only left when dawn broke.  That day, not a single monk within the temple was free from the inner demon, including Shi Ming himself. He returned his abbot robe and staff, setting out to preach in the secular world. Yet decades had passed since then, and he still could not rid himself of nightmares. Instead, due to his fear, he conceived evil intentions, plotting for years to destroy the Tang Clan. Today, driven by urgency, he stepped into the main hall, seeking deliverance from his torments.

Yunshang cradled her qin and played the Pu'an Mantra. Its solemn, dignified notes helped calm your mind, and in some unseen way guided the flow of your meridians; the fiery force was extinguished as it circulated, merging into your dantian to be absorbed.

As for his Daoist robe being swept by the Fire Whisk, that was another matter entirely. The Fire Whisk has a mechanism that sprays dust when waved, and that dust is extremely flammable. It needed to be washed off, to keep it from catching fire if a spark hit it during the fight to come.

Zou Bo understood the Fire Dragon Immortal Monarch's methods perfectly. He placed his palm on your back and channeled Qingcheng qigong to help you dispel the fiery energy. Though the Heartburn Seal's flames were venomous, once they encountered Qingcheng's secret doctrine, an orthodox martial arts technique, they were nothing more than a joke, easily subdued and destroyed, merging into your dantian to be absorbed.

The Fire Dragon Immortal Monarch put on a show of mysticism, but the Flying Heaven Gate's Heartburn Seal was a genuinely formidable martial art. In the clash, he struck hidden force into your body — a force so insidious it caused no harm at rest, but would suddenly erupt the moment you channeled your internal skill to fight, leaving you injured at best, or dead from a Qi deviation at worst.
Xiaomei, with a mind free of thoughts, quickened her steps towards liberation, leaping into the wind. The crane's call echoed through the vast sky, and from then on, she was free.

Xiaomei had steeled herself to die together with Venerable Golden Crow, her heart already turned to ash, burdened with too much to bear — even with a path back to life open to her, she would not have taken it. But countless invisible threads of fate bound her still, making her reluctant to leave this world, and she gathered the courage to live once more.

It was only that Xiaomei was too exhausted, too worn out; she wanted nothing more than to close her eyes and rest. However brilliant her future might have been, it no longer mattered to her. You knew this world could not keep her any longer.

You have inherited Second Senior Brother's research. Although you cannot use the Ten Thousand Longevity Corpse Heart Pill to cure the sect leader, it is no longer difficult to expel the Gu Poison from within a person's body.

Venerable Golden Crow's dying counterattack wounded her gravely as well. With death approaching, there was nothing left she could not say; she swayed unsteadily, murmuring as if to herself, as if begging forgiveness. She had only gone undercover in the Tang Clan and helped murder the Eldest Senior Brother because the corpse-heart pill controlled her — it was never of her own will. Even so, she had still committed a grave wrong, and owed a debt to others.

Xiaomei, though married to Venerable Golden Crow, hated him more than anyone else in this life. But she knew her own skill was not enough, and she was bound by all manner of constraints. The man himself was cunning and wary, and she feared that a hasty strike might miss and only put him on guard — so she had endured in silence until now, striking without mercy the moment he lay still, feigning death.

You hurriedly covered Shangguan Ying's eyes to keep her from seeing. Well-traveled and worldly as she was, she still could not help turning pale. She was used to bloodshed, yet had never witnessed such cruel butchery.

You hurriedly covered Ye Yunshang's eyes to keep her from seeing. Though noble-born, she had watched her elder brother cut down enemies with his sword before — but Ye Yunzhou's swordsmanship was clean and precise even in a kill. She had never seen such brutal slaughter, and horrified, she turned and fled at once, dashing into Zhengxin Hall and into the Third Senior Brother's arms just as she vomited on him.
You hurriedly covered your junior martial sister's eyes, not letting her see. Her heart was pounding; she had witnessed Jianghu skirmishes but never such a cruel massacre.

So saying, she knelt on one knee atop Venerable Golden Crow's remains and suddenly drew a blade, striking savagely at his corpse, every stab aimed at the neck. Venerable Golden Crow had only been feigning death through turtle's-breath, never imagining Xiaomei would dare betray him — caught entirely unprepared, he was struck in a vital point. Filled with terror and fury, pinned down and unable to rise, he lashed out recklessly with his palm. Xiaomei spat fresh blood, fighting with everything she had, hacking and stabbing in a frenzy until she severed Venerable Golden Crow's head entirely from his body. From that day on, he could never again feign death and return to life.
Seeing her determined to die, you might as well send her on her way. Just as you were about to act, Xiaomei suddenly called a halt, saying she still had unfinished wishes.

Shangguan Ying saw the killing intent rise in you and couldn't help but flinch. Though she shared your hatred for the man and seemed tough on the surface, she was in truth soft-hearted, and ended up pleading for Xiaomei's life. But Xiaomei had made up her mind to die — even if you held back, she would find some other way to end herself. Unable to leave such kindness unanswered, Xiaomei decided to give you both a great gift.
Moved by the Junior Martial Sister's kindness, Xiaomei decided to give you both a great gift.

Junior Martial Sister saw her lifeless appearance and felt deeply moved, realizing she was a helpless and pitiful soul. She couldn't bear to see such a beautiful lady meet her end in such a tragic way.

Though they had known each other only briefly, and Xiaomei's oath to the Tang Clan was never sincere, the Junior Martial Sister's generous heart would not let blood be spilled there and then — had Xiaomei only admitted her fault and apologized, she could still have been forgiven. But Xiaomei had gone too far; even had you thrown the door wide open, she would have had no time to turn back. The more the Junior Martial Sister tried to shield her, the more crushed by regret she became, until only death could atone for it.
Seeing her set on death, you thought you might as well send her on her way, but the Junior Martial Sister could not bear it and hurriedly pulled her back.
However, thanks to your kindness, she decided to give you a grand gift.
Seeing you flustered, Xiaomei laughed. She was merely mocking you; how could that be taken seriously?

You should take this opportunity to retaliate in kind, pretending to be jealous and angry with Shangguan Ying. She was both angry and amused, and could only stamp her foot. Xiaomei was envious of your young couple's quarrelsome ways, but unfortunately, you are destined to destroy each other.
Down the mountain the battle still raged, and you truly had no heart to listen to idle jokes. Seeing this, Xiaomei only smiled faintly and let it go.

Xiaomei's innocent teasing made you laugh, and she turned it back on you with some flirting of her own. Shangguan Ying's brow twitched, and before you'd even said a word, she'd already begun to sulk. Seeing this, Xiaomei secretly found it amusing, telling herself she could charm anyone, man or woman, and turned to provoke Shangguan Ying instead. The latter, hearing this, went pale and waved her hands frantically.

Xiaomei's innocent teasing made you laugh, and in turn, she playfully flirted with you. Ye Yunshang, who was in the Zhengxin Hall, immediately became anxious upon hearing this and rushed out to assert her claim. This was originally just a joke and not meant to be taken seriously, but Xiaomei was startled by Yunshang's reaction. It wasn't surprising that you were drawn to her beauty, but the fact that she genuinely loved you was quite absurd. Xiaomei secretly laughed to herself, feeling a hint of envy; it turned out that there was true affection in the world, and someone cared about you.

Xiaomei's innocent teasing made you laugh, and she turned it around to flirt with you in turn. Hearing this, Ye Yunshang, who was in Zhengxin Hall, immediately grew alarmed and rushed out, heedless of danger, to stop you from preying on another. Xiaomei's words had only been in jest, not meant seriously, but when she heard Ye Yunshang expose your history of flirtation and debauchery, whatever admiration she'd felt for you vanished completely.

Xiaomei found your innocence amusing and turned to tease you back. The Junior Martial Sister immediately bristled and stepped in front of you as though guarding against a great foe. It had only been a jest, not meant seriously, but Xiaomei was startled by her reaction — it was no surprise that you coveted her beauty, but that she truly loved you was another matter entirely. Xiaomei chuckled inwardly, a touch of envy stirring: even someone like you had someone fretting over him — so there really was true feeling in this world.

When you saw that Venerable Golden Crow was dead, yet the Sect Leader's wife wore an expression as calm as drifting clouds, you couldn't help but be astonished. It was likely that she'd had no choice in the matter, and pity stirred in you, so you spoke to let her go, only cautioning her never to return to Kongtong.

Drawing on his decades as a neighbor of the Tang Clan, Zou Bo knew that those who offended them were judged by the severity of their transgression — those whose malice was plain, man or woman, would be killed without mercy. Unable to bear the sight of a woman put to death, he sheathed his sword, turned, and walked away, leaving the defeated foe for you to deal with.
Venerable Golden Crow suffered defeat, and Lady Mei also lost all will to fight, spreading her hands and surrendering, her weapon cast aside.

Zou Bo heard the commotion and set his teacup down hard in Zhengxin Hall. He drew his sword and stepped out. In their past debates on Daoist principles at Qingcheng, this fellow had twisted the scriptures, misreading them at will to flaunt his martial prowess under the guise of Daoist learning. His own good Junior Brother, his Daoist heart corrupted by such heresy, had fallen to become the Dharma King of the Hell Path — Zou Bo had long since ground his teeth in hatred over it. Had Immortal Qiu of the Quanzhen school and Old Patriarch Nangong not interceded on his behalf when he was young, his fiery temper of those days would already have sent him up Kongtong Mountain to challenge and kill this fellow.

Shangguan Ying firmly believed in Buddhist teachings and utterly disregarded these unnecessary displays of mysticism. She immediately rebuked him. Although the Fire Dragon Immortal Monarch was fiery, he was practical enough to recognize the situation. There was a chance that this little miss might return to the Shangguan Family one day to complain to her official father. That would be trouble. He thus smiled and addressed her as a virtuous niece, praising her father as being reborn from the Eastern Sea Dragon King and suggesting they should get closer since they were of similar kind. However, this flattery only made Shangguan Ying even more disdainful.

Venerable Golden Crow has died, and the succession at Kongtong remains unresolved to this day, its four gates locked in ceaseless strife, with never a day of peace. The Fire Dragon Immortal Monarch, eager to restore his reputation and overawe the people of Kongtong, performed the Sky-Soaring Crane-Riding Technique to ascend into the courtyard, opened his mouth as if reciting from an opera, proclaimed himself a great immortal, and demanded that you, mere demons and clowns, kneel at once and submit.

Dealing with the Kongtong sect calls for a master. Zou Bo drank down his tea, drew his sword, and slowly stepped out from Zhengxin Hall. The Qingcheng Sect Leader's righteous qi pressed down, and Venerable Golden Crow's breath caught for a moment, his mind churning with doubt over whether Kongtong's Iron Pipa Divine Skill or Qingcheng's Secret Covenant of the Three held the greater power.

Kongtong and the Tang Clan now bear an irreconcilable enmity. Venerable Golden Crow has taken over as Sect Leader, and having obtained the Kongtong Secret Treasure, his skill has advanced by leaps and bounds. Accompanied by his newlywed wife, Madam Mei, he has come today vowing to annihilate your Tang Clan and end the threat forever.
Shangguan Ying had occasionally discussed Buddhist teachings with him before, and they had a considerable friendship. Seeing him end up in such a situation, she could not help but feel compassion.

You can't help but feel a sense of regret, the Tang Clan has never turned away lonely or destitute people; if he had been willing to lower his posture and start over as an outsider disciple, how could he have ended up this way?

You were always the one who envied others, yet today it was a man blessed by heaven who came to envy you—and you stabbed him dead for it, snuffing out any chance he might one day overtake you. Your heart, it must be said, was a boundless sky without a single cloud, black through and through.

In terms of raw talent, Tang Shan was as fine a prodigy as you would find, not far behind Eldest Senior Brother himself. He knew the Tang Clan's Hidden Weapon General Principles inside and out, and by every means possible unearthed lost fragments of the Tang Clan's martial arts, so that his skill leapt forward by great strides. But he forced his growth, and it left him with nothing but the outward form—and in the end he lost to you, an outsider by birth, and perished consumed by his own envy.

The one who charged first into the Tang Family's great courtyard was a disciple of the traitor Tang Shouhong—the very man who had once stirred chaos within the Tang Clan, sparked civil war, and indirectly brought on the Sect Leader's collapse into paralysis: the Guangzhou Tang Clan Disciple, Little Whirlwind Tang Shan. He had thrown himself wholly into helping his master restore the Tang Clan, only to fail at the final step, leaving the Guangzhou Tang Clan disgraced and a sect in name alone. Denied forgiveness by the true Tang Clan, his thwarted hopes curdled into envy, and now he had returned with his skills much improved. Since the Tang Clan would not have him, he would destroy it and build it anew in its place!

In terms of raw talent and bearing, Fang Zhentian lacked for nothing compared to you. If there was one place he fell short, it was that his life had been too easy, with too few hardships to temper him; his every move chased grandeur and force, with no gift for adapting. Faced with your endlessly shifting techniques, he panicked at each change—how could he not lose!

Victory and defeat are the common lot of warriors—with his talent, a few more years of seasoning would surely have brought him renown. But you were no philanthropist; would you truly show mercy to one who came to your door looking to die? One small sword thrust ended his life then and there. Fang Zhentian's fate ended here, yet the Jianghu held countless other young heroes still, and you feared none of them—let them come, and you would cut down every one.

The Flying Hero Tang Buyi made the perfect opponent for him—he leveled his blade at Xiaomei and called her out by name. Yet this Flying Hero before him was Xiaomei in disguise, her shoulders padded and her waist wrapped in sandbags, and fearing that too sudden a move would give her away, she shoved you forward in her place. Truth be told, Eldest Senior Brother himself was fully capable of such a thing. Xiaomei herself claimed she wouldn't interfere, so the two of you could face off fair and square, but in truth she already had a dagger tucked up her sleeve, ready to deal him a sudden, fatal blow the moment he let his guard down or your life was in danger. As for honor and integrity, that was all nonsense.

Born into an age of peace, where even the wish to make his name and stand tall was hard to fulfill, Jianghu Young Hero Fang Zhentian led the charge into the Tang family compound, making no effort to hide his approach, determined to storm brazenly into Zhengxin Hall and carve out a resounding name for himself.

Tan Badao had never once seen you fight; seeing only your unpleasant face and lack of any presence, he took you for some lackey guarding the gate. He had no idea how wrong he was until they crossed blades, and even as the breath left him, he refused to accept it, resenting you for playing the pig to devour the tiger. But you had never played the pig—you simply happened to look the part.

Tan Badao took you for the same negligible little flunkey he remembered from years ago, never expecting that your skill had since grown beyond all comparison. He lost the fight, and even as the life drained out of him, he still could not believe it.

Junior Martial Sister's assault fell like a sudden storm, her movements so elusive that she seemed before you one instant and gone the next—not merely fast, but deadlier still for making no sound and giving no warning, truly impossible to guard against or evade. Even you, watching from the side, found it dizzying to follow; as for Tan Badao, he could not so much as counterattack, let alone turn his blade to guard himself. In an instant came a rapid clatter of clangs as he parried more than a dozen strikes, yet was struck nearly a hundred times. Light as each blow was, no flesh could withstand the edge of a blade; within a few exchanges he had been stabbed until his body was riddled like a honeycomb, blood pouring out, and he collapsed dead on the ground. A great hero of Kuizhou, and he never managed a single decent move before he died at Junior Martial Sister's hand. You stood there dumbstruck, while Junior Martial Sister, feeling she had protected you, was immensely proud of herself.

This man had long coveted Shangguan Ying's beauty, but was held back by the Nangong and Shangguan Families and dared not defile her. Now that she had fallen so low as to join the Tang Clan, she was no longer untouchable nobility—here was his chance to have his way with her, silence her after, and pin the blame on the Tang Clan. Shangguan Ying, hearing his filthy talk, could bear it no longer and drove a fist into his face. Tan Badao took it for a showy, useless blow, never guessing that Shangguan Ying had trained under South Songshan in the Suffering Fist. She was middling at most things, but when truly angry her punches struck hard, and caught off guard, he lost two teeth on the spot.

This man, seeing Junior Martial Sister's delicate, charming looks, was instantly smitten. Taking her for soft and easy to bully, he planned to mince you to pulp and claim this young lady for his own. Setting aside his lewd, disrespectful talk about her, it was his boast of chopping you up that sent Junior Martial Sister into a fury—her Flying Shuttle left her hand at once, and she herself followed like a shadow, closing in to attack.

The assassin who charged into the courtyard first was Tan Badao of Kuizhou. He had once been bold and free with his money, with a fair name for chivalry, but he was fond of wine and women, and one day, feigning drunken madness, he defiled a woman of good family. Trusting his close ties to the local officials to keep her silent, he never expected the victim to be so fierce in her honor: the next morning she beat the grievance drum and denounced Tan Badao's crime in the open street before taking her own life on the spot. Once the news spread, the magistrate, pressed by the famous constable Song Bei, dared not show him favor and was forced to post a bounty on Tan Badao, ruining his name. This time he arrived first not for any great skill in Qinggong, but because he had been scheming all along to earn merit and wash the stain from his reputation.

Tan Badao saw the Flying Hero return to life, his eyes fit to split with fury, and swung his blade at Xiaomei, calling her out. But this Xiaomei was disguised as Eldest Senior Brother, her shoulders padded and her waist wrapped in sandbags, and she dared not move too wildly for fear of giving herself away—so she casually shoved you forward instead. Truth be told, Eldest Senior Brother himself was fully capable of such a thing. Xiaomei herself claimed she wouldn't interfere, so the two of you could fight it out fair and square, but in truth she already had a dagger tucked up her sleeve, ready to deal him a sudden, fatal blow the moment he let his guard down or your life was in danger. As for honor and integrity, that was all nonsense.

Once a great hero of Kuizhou who wielded a treasured blade to cleave mountains, Tan Badao had fallen from grace and been branded infamous after being unmasked by the Three Heroes of the Tang Clan. He licked Nangong Yuan's boots again and again and begged shelter from Chan Master Shi Ming to escape execution—nominally a guest, in truth held under house arrest. This time, the moment battle broke out, he charged recklessly up the mountain, driven by nothing but the thirst for revenge.
Shangguan Ying saw you had decided not to go down the mountain, so she gave up her desire to attack people recklessly, went away and came back, standing shoulder to shoulder with you.

Shangguan Ying descended the mountain and took some time to think calmly. This time, it was different from the Battle of Jiangling; then, all martial artists in the Wulin had stood behind the Nangong Family, with army and people united as one, while the Beggar Sect, despite its many members, had few who could actually fight—crushing the Beast Path had been as easy as turning one's hand. This time the Eastern and Western Wulin were at war, with the outcome uncertain, and every famous master in the Jianghu had been drawn into it; in scale it rivaled the Supreme Bliss Cult's War on Demons. Perhaps this quarrel would be their last meeting in this life. The thought left her uneasy; matters she had always sworn never to forgive suddenly seemed trivial beside life and death. So halfway down the mountain she turned back to the Tang Clan and stood at your side. The debt was not forgotten—only set aside, until she could beat you to death with her own hands once today was survived.

Junior Martial Sister stood beside you, still expressionless, though her thoughts churned like a stormy tide. Fortunately, in moments of fear and helplessness, she could always reach out and find your hand. Having a home, having you—there was nothing more reassuring in this world.
Xiaomei stood nearby, fighting the urge to throw herself into your arms, but for the sake of Eldest Senior Brother's posthumous reputation, she forced herself to hold back.
You decided to stay on the mountain to defend the great courtyard and guard the Tang Clan's Sect Leader.

Xiaomei's journey to Kongtong has been long delayed in returning, and there is a reason for it; to keep it from distracting you, let it rest for now — the urgent matter is the trouble at hand. She, this false Eldest Senior Brother, could not take the field herself, for fear of being exposed in a few short moves. At most, she could put on a show to intimidate the enemy. But with the Flying Hero guarding the Tang Clan, the Western Wulin Alliance's morale soared, and the enemy no longer dared to press recklessly. As for the truth coming out later, and how the senior and junior disciples would rage over it — that is a story for another day.

But you, you ugly wretch, don't appreciate what you have even with her by your side — instead of learning anything decent, you've picked up the philandering ways of some playboy. This will not simply be let go. Xiaomei's possessiveness runs fierce; if you don't set your attitude right at once, she won't hesitate to bite your nipple off to vent her fury.

Both sides drew their stances, yet you hesitated to strike, letting him mock and insult you. You always felt he resembled someone, perhaps her, pretending to be the Eldest Senior Brother to see you once more. If you uncovered the truth, she might leave immediately, or so you thought. But you were entirely mistaken. Xiaomei, having returned, had no intention of leaving; her longing for you was just as deep as your longing for her. Overjoyed that you had seen through her true identity, her heart swelled with sweet delight, as if drenched in honey.

Who could have guessed he'd crumple at the first touch, shrieking like a woman? You, the one who'd struck him, were the one left at a loss instead. The Human Skin Mask came off to reveal the face beneath, and now it was you who panicked — wasn't this the very Xiaomei you had been longing for? You were startled, delighted, and still shaken from the fright, secretly relieved you hadn't struck her too hard.

You'd already suspected as much, and a little probing was enough to make Xiaomei slip. She pulled off the human-skin mask to reveal her true face beneath — was this not the very Xiaomei you had longed for? You were both startled and overjoyed. Having been found out, she felt not the slightest dismay, only an unspeakable joy, her heart as sweet as if steeped in honey.
Still, you couldn't confirm the stranger's identity, and since he refused to come clean, sterner methods were called for — a fight became unavoidable.

Only once everyone was in position, and no one else remained in the courtyard, did you finally speak up to question him — you had already known all along that the person before you was not the Eldest Senior Brother.
