You madman, you publicly announced that Xiahou Lan, the first beauty of the Wulin, is your wife. She was stunned upon hearing the words, then blushed up to her ears. She wasn't denying it, but she was too shy. The tender heart hidden behind a cold facade was pounding. All her tender feelings turned into a light scold and faint anger, and she turned on her heel and left. To punish you tonight, you'd better not die.

You announced to everyone that the Snow Mountain Sect would join the Western Wulin Alliance. Those who heard it were all taken aback, thinking either, "Is there even such a sect in the Wulin?" or, "Didn't the Snow Mountain Sect die out long ago?" Xiahou Lan was stunned for a moment, then laughed out loud, heedless of her image for once, her heart brimming with affection for you. Now it was no longer only for you, or for her promise to the Sect Leader, but also for your Great Snow Mountain Sect — she couldn't stay indifferent, and had to give it her all.

Just as she was about to leave, umbrella raised, she heard your voice bellowing her name across the sky. You lacked her fine mastery of the art of transmitting sound secretly, but channeling your Internal Force to shout louder was no great difficulty.

Xiahou Lan had no intention of joining the chaotic brawl, but she wasn't going to stand idly by either. After all, she was your master, and she had once promised Sect Leader Tang that if the Tang Clan ever faced trouble, she would come to their aid. Though her skill was far diminished from before, she also wanted to probe the enemy leader's true strength on your behalf. If she could beat him, she wouldn't mind killing him outright; if not, she would at least make him bleed a little — her beloved disciple couldn't very well come back battered while the enemy stood there immaculate and at ease. Just thinking of it made her furious.

During the Battle of Fengyu Mountain, Long Xiang was excluded by her beloved teacher, unable to share life and death with the sister disciples of Jinxiang Palace she had known for over a decade, and she often bitterly regretted it. Now, having given her heart to you, she considers herself as good as wed into the Tang Clan, and fighting for chivalry, her mind is no longer clouded by a shred of doubt. Without hesitation, she draws her sword into the battle.

During the Battle of Fengyu Mountain, Long Xiang was excluded by her beloved teacher, unable to share life and death with the sister disciples of Jinxiang Palace she had known for over a decade, and she often bitterly regretted it. Now that she is in the Tang Clan, fighting for chivalry, though doubt still lingers in her heart, she has no time to dwell on it, and draws her sword into the battle.

Long Xiang hesitated to speak to Senior Brother; it seemed at first like a young woman's tender feelings, but unexpectedly, she meant to challenge Senior Brother to a duel, so as to overcome the weaker self she had once been. Senior Brother was thrown into a panic, unable to meet her eyes, and could only agree to speak again once the battle was over.

Shangguan Ying clenched her fists and rubbed her palms, restless with eagerness. Her face was flushed with uncontainable excitement. During the Jiangling battle, Nangong Shen had regarded her as a burden, but today, after following you, she had taken the initiative to charge into the battlefield, pummeling enemies left and right, all in the name of justice. No matter how fierce her attacks, they were justified.

Shangguan Ying felt anxious and came to greet her Eldest Senior Brother, only to be met with cold treatment. You had never seen your Eldest Senior Brother speak so harshly to a woman before, and couldn't help but be astonished. Shangguan Ying, however, thought she had brought it upon herself, and to make amends, threw herself into the battlefield without regard for her own safety. You feared for her safety and tried to stop her, but your Eldest Senior Brother pulled you back, urging you to think of the greater good — after all, the Shangguan Family Head was right there on the field; who would dare be so reckless as to harm his precious daughter?
Also conveyed a message to her elder brother, stating that he had taken the initiative to shoulder the core responsibility and commanded the Tang Clan's Outer Fort.

When a person has something they need to protect, they become strong and brave. And since you are responsible for protecting everyone, you will become stronger than anyone else. Yunshang thought like this.
As long as the qin's sound doesn't stop, it means the lights haven't gone out.

Yunshang declared she'd never spare you another thought again, though in truth she was aching inside — half wanting to throw a proper tantrum, half afraid that if you left this time, it would be forever. So she needled you gently instead, and seeing your face fall with worry eased her heart a little. She went off to Zhengxin Hall to let Third Senior Brother look after her, so you wouldn't have to fret.
Yunshang, usually such a troublemaker, is surprisingly sensible today. Not wanting to worry you, she hid herself away in Zhengxin Hall, where Third Senior Brother could keep her safe.
And now that Little Junior Sister has attached herself to you, she is ready to follow you anywhere.

Little Junior Sister is still fuming. If she weren't afraid you might vanish for good once today was over, she'd probably have kept up the sulking for half a month. Angry as she is, she still clings to you tightly.

You left Little Junior Sister behind in the courtyard to guard Third Senior Brother, unwilling to let her come to even the slightest harm — and you had to admit that, yourself aside, she was the strongest fighter left in the Tang Clan.

Fu Yun and the Eighteen Bronze Men advanced onto the mountain path, using its narrow, winding shape to recreate the Wooden Man Alley — with staffs this long, they were sure to hold the advantage. As for the other Songshan disciples who had joined the Wulin Alliance, Fu Yun's men took it upon themselves to talk them into standing down.

Since coming to the Tang Clan, Xie Wuchen has always insisted on calling you Junior Brother, leaving you no choice but to play along. This time, though, he has come to bid you farewell. With his Qinggong — famed alongside your Eldest Senior Brother's under the name Wind God — crossing the Wulin Alliance's thick encirclement should be no great trouble. But to challenge the Wulin Alliance Leader himself is another matter; he may well not return.

Xie Wuchen wanted to spar with Eldest Senior Brother, to see who could fell more foes, but Eldest Senior Brother, most unlike himself, made one excuse after another, and even tricked Xie Wuchen into going off to risk his life elsewhere. Listening nearby, you felt it sounded exactly like something he would say — yet something about it didn't sit right.

Fan Xiaotian had once been a disciple of the Beggar Sect, held under the thumb of its old faction and raised as a hired thug. Outwardly obedient, he nursed a hatred he could not let go, longing to avenge his old dog A'Hua, who had been slaughtered and eaten. Now that the Wulin Alliance was sending out all its finest, the elders were bound to take the field as well — this was his last chance. Let it slip by, and his enemies would vanish again, scattered beyond reach across the world.

Fan Xiaoyan had once been a disciple of the Beggar Sect, held under the thumb of its old faction and raised as a hired thug. Outwardly obedient, she nursed a hatred she could not let go, longing to avenge her old dog A'Hua, who had been slaughtered and eaten. Now that the Wulin Alliance was sending out its finest, the elders were bound to take the field as well — this was her last chance. Let it slip by, and her enemies would vanish again, scattered beyond reach across the world.
Tang Family Compound, united as one, their shouts shake the mountains and forests. Even if the Western Wulin does not form an alliance, they are still comrades.

Though Xie Wuchen of the Emei Sect led men to intercept Diancang's heroes, he feared even that would not withstand the Twin Swords of Diancang in unison. Dreading the battle would drag on until Diancang's reinforcements arrived, Emei's Sect Leader Xiang Wuyou had his own scheme: entrusting the disciples he had brought to the Tang Clan's care, he slipped away using his Qinggong. For if the Wulin Alliance could send men to assassinate your Third Senior Brother, why should the Western Wulin Alliance not send its own experts to bring grief to the enemy alliance leader?

Zou Bo sent Qingcheng Disciples to assist in defense at the Outer Fort, while he himself remained at the Tang family courtyard, leisurely chatting with Third Senior Brother. Brewing tea was just an excuse; in truth, he was there to protect the leader of another sect with his esteemed position as the sect leader.

The Flying Stone Gang are all ruffians and troublemakers, ineffective in solo combat, but their strength lies in being local power players with many members. Their Gang Leader, Shi Gongyuan, also joins the fray to showcase his skills.
Li Fugui went joyfully, leading his followers to hide in the alleys and Outer Fort areas, preparing for a surprise attack to catch them off guard.

You are badly outnumbered, and to you, the clash with the Wulin Alliance is the gravest challenge you face. To the Wulin Alliance, it is not so simple. The Mud Cult still endures, watching with hungry eyes; should the Eastern and Western Wulin Alliances grind each other into ruin, the Cult might well seize the chance to strike at the sects of the Central Plains. So the Wulin Alliance is bound to favor cunning over brute force — seize the leader, and the rest will scatter. For the Western Wulin, though, so long as its spiritual leader stands unbroken, even if checkpoints and terrain cannot stop every swordsman of the Jianghu, in time the Wulin Alliance's heroes will lose heart and withdraw. In the end, to hold his side together and stem the bloodshed, the Alliance Leader himself must step forth — and that is when the decisive battle atop Mount Meishan becomes your chance for victory.

The Tang Clan's compound is strategically built on this mountain peak, for it is surrounded by a valley on three sides and backed by a mountain, making it a natural fortress. Unless one risks angering the authorities by setting fire to the mountain, it is most defensible and hard to attack. Your interest in military books proved useful, as you had already set ambushes along the mountain paths and worked with the Third Senior Brother to refine tactics, utilizing the terrain to its fullest extent.

The Tang Family Compound was built on this hill with much strategic thought. With three sides facing a valley and the back resting against a mountain, it is naturally a formidable stronghold, unless one were to risk angering the officials by setting fire to the mountain. Xiaoju took note of this during her strolls and discussed tactics with Third Senior Brother. She feared that the Wulin Alliance might not take the straight path, so she even led people to repair the mountain paths, aiming to lure them in.

The Tang Family Compound was built on this mountain peak for good reason. Surrounded by valleys on three sides and backed by a natural hill, it was an inherently defensible position, nearly impregnable unless one were willing to risk angering the authorities by setting fire to the mountain. Danxiazi had already noticed these advantages and discussed tactics with Third Senior Brother, accurately predicting the Wulin Alliance's attack route and setting traps on the mountain paths.

Although they haven't yet sworn an oath of blood alliance, the Wulin Alliance is about to strike at any moment, leaving no time to dwell on details. So you all gathered together to discuss strategies.

It's surprising that the Tang Clan in modern times has produced your Fourth Senior Brother, such a genius, who came up with this scheme of cheap travel groups to deceive all the outsiders staying in the Outer Fort into going on scenic tours, calming the crowd's anger while making a profit. Third Senior Brother doesn't know whether to scold him or admire him.
But they took none of it kindly, cursing every one of your Tang Clan's ancestors down eighteen generations. That was nothing unusual—the Tang Clan has never wanted for curses in all its history.

Although the Outer Fort no longer belongs to the Tang Clan, the Tang Clan has protected Shu generation after generation and could not bear to see its villagers caught in the fires of war, so they evacuated the Outer Fort's residents early on.
The Tang Clan has safeguarded Shu generation after generation. They could not bear to see the villagers suffer from the war's reach and evacuated the residents of the Outer Fort early on.

Everyone talked over each other, crowding around Eldest Senior Brother, each vying to ask how he had come back to life, where he had gone and what he had done while playing dead. Eldest Senior Brother brushed off their questions without a real answer, but even his silence—just his standing there in the Tang family courtyard—filled his Junior Martial Brothers and Sisters with boundless courage, all of them wild with joy, as though the Tang Clan could hold its own even if heavenly soldiers and generals descended upon them.
Shi Gongyuan also rejoiced wildly; if Eldest Senior Brother had never died, he wouldn't have had to carry the guilt for the rest of his life.
Xie Wuchen came up close and was immediately struck by Eldest Senior Brother.

When Eldest Senior Brother died, Long Xiang's still-naive infatuation had turned to ashes. Now, seeing him again felt like a dream—he grabbed you, shouting and bouncing with joy. You hadn't even had time to feel jealous before Eldest Senior Brother turned sour, leaving you utterly stunned.

When Eldest Senior Brother died, Long Xiang's naive affection had already burned to ashes. Now, seeing him again felt like a dream; the sorrow in his heart was too much to suppress, and tears streamed down his face.

Eldest Senior Brother had always loved to tease Little Junior Sister, and she used to bristle at the very sight of him. Now, seeing him alive and well before her, she could not hold back her tears and threw herself into his arms—but the instant they touched, she pulled back, some nameless wrongness prickling at her, an inexplicable dread driving her to shrink behind you.

You were about to retort when a voice suddenly came from nowhere, scolding Nangong Shen, and then appeared, revealing it was your Eldest Senior Brother, the Tang Clan Flying Hero, Tang Buyi! The scene erupted in chaos. Nangong Shen was stunned beyond words, and you were also stunned, unable to believe it, saying you had lost your mind. That day was clearly not raining, yet you always remembered it as a downpour. At the back mountain, you watched your Eldest Senior Brother be buried, lying together with the Tang Clan ancestors in the ground. If you buried your Eldest Senior Brother then, who is this person before you now?
Chao He saw the Nangong family head heading down the mountain and, forgetting to keep up his pretense of playing dead, hurried after him.
Chao He hurried after them.

You were about to fire back with a sharp retort, but Third Senior Brother held you back. Without another word, he simply cupped his fists and saw the guests off down the mountain. Seeing that persuasion had failed, Nangong Shen and Song Bei had no choice but to take their leave—when they climbed the mountain again, it would be for battle.

He recited the Wulin Alliance's top experts as if he were listing his own family treasures. The Dragon King Blade Shangguan Sun, Qinghezi Yin Zhiping, Eagle Hero Wanli Pengcheng, Shi Ming... each name on his lips was a figure at the pinnacle of today's Wulin, resonating like thunder in their ears. Every title he mentioned caused a palpitation among the audience. Among them, the Alliance Leader Rui Sheng's reputation stood out the most. Not only were his wanderings across the land well‑known and popular, but even the battle on Fengyu Mountain was enough to make waves throughout the Jianghu. In the Battle of Jiangling, the turmoil of Fengyu Mountain, where the Beast Path and Human Path Dharma Kings displayed their prowess, stunned the world. The Hell Path and the Hungry Ghost Path Dharma Kings, known for their ferocity, openly defied the court and still roamed free to this day. This young Alliance Leader could single‑handedly resist two Dharma Kings, his martial arts beyond comprehension, his reputation soaring like the sun at its zenith, not inferior to Long Yuan in bygone days. Everyone hoped he would point his sword at Six Paths Canyon, face off against the Heavenly King atop the peak, annihilate the Demon Cult, and restore clarity to the Wulin. But now that he was pointing his sword at himself, things were decidedly not good.

As a negotiator for the Wulin Alliance, there is nothing to say. If the goal is to win, one should not reveal the secrets of the Wulin Alliance. However, setting aside right and wrong, as well as personal likes and dislikes, the Nangong family is still a long‑time friend of the Tang Clan. If they were to annihilate the Tang Clan in one battle, how would Nangong Shen face his father and grandfather in the afterlife?

As an envoy of the Wulin Alliance, there's nothing more to say. If the goal is to win, revealing the Alliance's secrets was never supposed to happen. But setting aside right and wrong, the Tang Clan isn't just long‑standing allies; Nangong Shen and you share a deep bond. If we were to destroy the Tang Clan in one fell swoop, Nangong Shen might pass his own test, but how would he face his ancestors in the afterlife, his elders?

Nangong Shen fell silent. He was confident that he and you were close enough that he could reason with you, and, relying on the prestige of his late father and grandfather, that he could persuade the Alliance Leader and the elder statesmen to first send the Tang Clan an offer of surrender. Even if you resisted to the last, there ought to be some words exchanged—words to fall back on once the battle was half fought, letting both sides step down with honor. Yet you spurned his goodwill, as though bent on a fight to the death.

You have recognized the true faces of the righteous martial sects, and you have not failed to plead, yet the voice of the weak is too faint, so they turn a deaf ear. Now the Western Wulin Alliance has grown strong enough to threaten the Wulin Alliance, yet they are willing to listen to your plea, but you are unwilling to speak.

You can't be bothered to argue your case—after all, the Wulin Alliance never listens anyway. Isn't the jianghu left with nothing but bloodshed and slaughter in the end? The Wulin Alliance loves to call itself the righteous path—let them. Victors are kings, the defeated are outlaws. Isn't that the whole point of settling scores exactly as you please? Fight first and talk later—isn't that far more satisfying?

Nangong Shen has always looked down on you, but at this moment, he couldn't help but be impressed by your boldness. Perhaps he could still argue a few points, yet he couldn't bear to refute the words he himself deeply agreed with. Only hindered by his status, he couldn't acknowledge it.

Back when he first met you in Jiangling, you had been just an unremarkable Tang Clan disciple, not worth his notice; what kindness he showed you then held a measure of pity and a measure of pretense, meant only to prove he knew how to treat men of worth with courtesy. Now, tempered through a thousand trials, you were a different man entirely. Nangong Shen looked at you, stunned into silence, and understood at last why his father, even after losing the race for Alliance Leader all those years ago, had spared no effort in scheming for the sake of his greatest rival. Beside the Wulin Alliance Leader's born-to-it brilliance, your own light carried something more human in it. He admired you, honestly and from the heart.

Little did they know, it was all your performance. Taken far enough, a lie becomes indistinguishable from truth—you could wear the mask of a righteous man as well as anyone, the greatest hypocrite alive in this age.

Your bold words won the whole hall's applause, thunderous and rolling. Not one person there now looked on you with scorn for your appearance; in this dark age, you shone so bright that it was hard to look straight at you, like a star come down to walk among ordinary men.

A true hero, so it's said, should not merely scrap over fleeting gains or bend others to his will by force. Standing between heaven and earth, one must carry unyielding bones and fear no power, however great; and with a heart full of hot blood, work to fix a compass for heaven and earth, to secure a fate for the living, to punish evil and uphold good, and to right every wrong. Though a blade can kill a man, it cannot kill the spirit—so why not loose a long cry to startle the age, and let a hero's name travel far, giving the common people something to hope for? Eight hundred years hence, righteousness will still walk the earth.

If the Imperial Court's mercy and authority could reach every corner alike, treating everyone with equal fairness, with no one bullied by the powerful and no grievance left to fester unredressed, and if the laws of the Great Song were sufficient to uphold justice in this world, then there would be no need for martial heroes at all.

If the Great Song's laws were sufficient to uphold justice, and if peace reigned across the four seas, the nation was prosperous and secure, and all people submitted to the king's rule, with the lonely, the disabled, and the destitute all provided for, if plots were quashed and did not arise, if theft and banditry did not occur, if doors need not be locked at night and no one picked up lost items, then there would be no need for martial heroes at all.

You spoke confidently, arguing your case with reason and conviction, causing the crowd to stare in astonishment. They all remarked that Tang Clan disciples were arrogant and unpredictable, operating in both law and underworld circles, and had always shown disdain for grand principles. Yet here you were, speaking with righteous determination and resolute strength. Nangong Shen relied on the Imperial Court's backing, yet you remained unfazed.
If your opponent insists on lofty principles, you can match him at that game too. Villains come in every stripe—take, for instance, you, the hypocrite full of feigned benevolence.
The words you were about to speak, you had once spoken to your own kin; now you spoke them again to strike a chord in others.

Golden Fu Yun, having thrown wide the vow of restrained speech, blazed with light and pressed his advantage without mercy. He too resorted to the trick of the many overwhelming the few: a few well-placed compliments turned the crowd's roar into thunder he could wield as his own, isolating and cornering his opponent until Nangong Shen was forced back step by step, drenched in sweat. The dignified head of the Nangong family, the noble Young Lord of Jiangling, found himself stammering, unable to answer.

Shangguan Ying was overjoyed. She also practiced Buddhism, though she often violated the precept against anger, but she was devout and sincere. She naturally knew the story well and immediately took up Fu Yun's words, severely scolding Nangong Shen, not at all recalling old feelings, intending to make him unable to maintain his dignity.

Nangong Shen was eloquent and had a wide network of contacts, but it was the Tang Clan's misfortune to now have Fu Yun—a ruthless man who, but for his vow of mercy, could talk a person to death without blinking, and who, once he got going, showed no restraint even toward kin. Today, he painted himself golden, fully ignited with anger, delivering a torrent of words without a single swear, yet leaving Nangong Shen unable to retort. He cited the story of King Saboda from the Six Perfections Sutra who cut his own flesh to feed the eagle, using it to subtly criticize the Wulin Alliance, speaking indirectly. The Wulin Alliance constantly boasts about upholding righteousness, urging the Tang Clan to know when to retreat and dissolve on their own, appearing sincere and well-intentioned at first glance. In reality, it's akin to King Saboda suddenly losing his wisdom and conscience, intending to cut his own flesh to feed the eagle, yet instead cutting someone else's flesh to gain glory for himself. What kind of merit is that? The person being cut certainly doesn't want it, and when they resist, they're labeled as ungrateful. Who can enjoy life under a tyrant's rule? King Saboda is a wise and benevolent ruler, so he wouldn't commit such ignorant and immoral acts. However, the Wulin Alliance does. By citing this story, he clearly explained the interests of both the Wulin Alliance and the Tang Clan, making the previously uncertain members of the Wulin Alliance suddenly understand. If the Wulin Alliance can cut the Tang Clan's flesh today, what will happen next time when the eagle comes back for more? The principle that 'when the lips are gone, the teeth feel the cold' is something everyone understands, leaving them all deeply concerned.
They volunteered to take charge of the gate guards at the Tang Clan's Outer Fort, swearing not to let petty villains cross the line.

Long-absent Cangsong Swordsman, upon hearing the news, did not hesitate to travel a thousand li to repay the favor. Fortunately, Tang Fang's vial of Zombie Powder spared her the worst of that arduous journey, keeping her from perishing along the way. Jin's Little Divine Doctor, Liang Youshi, moved by compassion for the suffering, began treating her without being asked. The more she treated, the more astonished she grew—by every sign she could read, Yunshang should already have been dead, yet the Tang Clan's own Ruthless Young Master had somehow found a way to keep her clinging to life, an utterly inconceivable feat. With Tang Clan medicinal cuisine as her base, she gritted her teeth and tried anyway, and thankfully the heavens favored them: Yunshang barely survived the crossing between life and death. Even if the hidden affliction could not be rooted out, they had at least bought her extra time—so long as she lived, the future still held hope. Ye Yunzhou, far off in the Jin Kingdom, heard of the alliance among the western Wulin and judged that the Wulin Alliance would not let the matter rest, that war between the two alliances was inevitable. So without pausing for rest, he raced back to Shu to repay the favor and lend his aid.

The long-absent Cangsong Swordsman had stabbed a Diancang expert on Fengyu Mountain and vanished without a trace. To keep his rash, unilateral act from dragging the Tang Clan down with him, he had lived in hiding in some remote backwater ever since—until word of the Western Wulin's new alliance reached him, and he hurried back to repay the favor.

Nan Xi had already guessed this visit would likely be refused, but obligation had brought her here regardless. Once she had your answer, she said no more and simply took her leave. Next time, it would likely be with blades drawn instead.

You. You believe. You all believe. A lazy gleam lit up Nan Xi's eyes, and she sighed inwardly: atop Fengyu Mountain, the Wulin's assembled heroes might well have doubted you all over nothing but rumor, yet the Tang Clan's hearts proved otherwise—what fine, forthright young men. She then swore upon her Seven-Star Sword to honor chivalry, and begged leave to go down the mountain and help the Western Wulin Alliance defend its outer forts. As for what her husband might think of it, that was none of her business. That philandering fool never asked her opinion when he went off taking more wives; getting cut down served him right.

Among the helpers, the most surprising was Heroine Nan Xi of the Lingnan School. For years the Lingnan School had kept out of the Jianghu, content in its southern corner; even the few who did travel to the Central Plains mostly did so for less than honorable reasons, ruining their own reputations until people looked down on them. And this Heroine Nan Xi, of all people, was the Wulin Alliance Leader's own beautiful confidante! She claimed she had come to repay a debt of kindness to you—but who could believe that?

He turned to Wei Ju to step in, hoping that with her eloquence, she could refute Nangong Shen's certain accusations. Wei Ju indeed had something to say, but as a guest, she was reluctant to overstep her bounds. Moreover, she was genuinely curious and wished to question Nangong Shen together, seeking to uncover the deeper meaning behind the Tang Clan's intentions.

Shangguan Ying was also anxiously worried, deeply fearing that the helpers from various sects might be swayed by him to switch sides at the critical moment. In the chaos of battle, how could she protect you?

Third Senior Brother had studied for ten years by a cold window, resolved to serve his country; even out of office, his heart still hung on the fate of the realm. How could he not know that once the Eastern and Western Wulin Alliances came to blows, it would shake the Central Plains and bring ruin to far more than themselves? Should the fires of war spread, stirring rebellion and shaking the very foundations of the state, and letting outside enemies slip in through the breach, the Tang Clan would become a criminal for the ages.
He had imagined that worst outcome more than once, and so Nangong Shen's words sank deep into his heart, leaving him silent in thought.

He reasoned with the Wulin heroes then and there, urging them to stand down before the fighting began, and pressed them with threats as well, hoping to force Third Senior Brother to yield, dissolve the Western Wulin Alliance, and atone for his sins.
He reasoned with the Wulin heroes then and there, urging them to stand down before the fighting began, and appealed to their feelings as well, urging the Tang Clan to rein in before the cliff's edge.

Nangong Shen's connections ran wide; among the heroes gathered today, there was hardly a name in the Jianghu he didn't know to some degree, and being an old family friend of the Tang Clan besides, he was the one man best suited to persuade the Western Wulin Alliance to disband.

The court had once voiced its support for a Wulin alliance, yet it also feared the Tang Clan still had strength to spare, and so its stance remained deliberately vague.
It had specially dispatched Song Bei to witness the negotiations, lest troublemakers stir up the crowd and cloud the truth, and the upheaval at Fengyu Mountain repeat itself.
Nangong Shen had come to your door on the Wulin Alliance's behalf, his purpose plain for all to see, yet he still called you 'brother' with every other breath.

Any other sect might not have dared act so rashly, but you are lawless Tang Clan disciples through and through. Before you could even say a word, your Junior Brother had already slapped him back to his true form; Chao He fled behind Nangong Shen, working up a show of tears to lodge a complaint—only for both men to ignore him completely, at which he gave up crying on the spot.
The man was outwardly fierce but inwardly a coward, certain he'd backed the winning side. His mediating was a sham; his real purpose was to swagger and humiliate the Tang Clan from top to bottom.
That slap across the face left him speechless at once, so he feigned a stomachache and pushed the trouble off onto Nangong Shen.

Before you could even confer with the Sect Leaders and Gang Leaders of the assembled sects and gangs, uninvited guests had already arrived.
Nangong Shen, newly succeeded as Family Head, had asked the Alliance Leader's leave to climb the mountain as a mediator, with the renowned Constable Song Bei accompanying him to oversee the talks and vouch for their fairness.

Before you could even confer with the heads of the assembled sects and gangs, a brash, insolent voice came blaring up into the courtyard. It was none other than Chao He, the Tang Clan's own traitor. He had volunteered to climb the mountain himself, and with the new head of the Nangong family and the renowned Constable Song Bei traveling at his side, he was certain you wouldn't dare touch a hair on his head. A petty man riding high, he strutted about on borrowed might like a fox behind a tiger, flaunting every ounce of arrogance he had—short of setting up a dye shop right there on Tang Clan land.

The disciple in charge of hospitality rushed up the mountain to report that the Wulin Alliance had completely surrounded Meishan Town, with officials and Imperial Soldiers on high alert. The scale of the situation was no less than the Jiangling Battle.
It's just that you looked around in confusion, never seeing the people of the Kongtong sect, and the Junior Martial Brothers and Sisters who were sent north to guide also vanished without a trace.
It's just that you looked around in confusion, never seeing her graceful figure. Xiaoju won't come back; perhaps we'll never meet again in this lifetime.
It was just that you looked around in confusion, never glimpsing her graceful figure. If Xiaozhu never came back, perhaps you were fated never to meet again in this life.
It was just that you looked around in confusion, never glimpsing her graceful figure. If Xiaomei never came back, perhaps you were fated never to meet again in this life.
Even the legendary Eighteen Bronze Men of Songshan had been freshly gilded in gold lacquer and brought back into the Jianghu.

On the day of the Western Wulin Alliance Alliance's gathering, leaders from all sects and factions arrived as promised, converging at the Tang Clan. The Tang Clan's Patriarch, Jie Lu, had built this Tang Family compound in the mountains, raising children, taking disciples, and expanding the clan's influence over hundreds of years. At times, the clan flourished, and at others, it declined. Sometimes it stood as a righteous partner, yet in other generations, it produced notorious villains. Independent and controversial, it has drawn both praise and criticism. Yet today, the unprecedented gathering of martial arts masters from across the Central Plains, whether allies or adversaries, all coming for the Tang Clan, is unparalleled in history.

The couple runs a tea shop business and have diligently saved thirty taels of broken silver. Adding to that, Yunshang's hoarded jewelry sold for ninety‑four thousand eight hundred taels. Recently, they are planning to close the shop and travel to find her older brother Yunzhou.

The couple ran a tea shop business, diligently saving thirty taels of silver. In addition, with the conversion of the jewelry that Yunshang had accumulated, they had a total of ninety‑four thousand eight hundred taels of silver. Recently, they were planning to close the shop and travel to find her brother, Yunzhou, who was a wandering doctor. It was said that he was a shameless quack, notorious for his poor medical skills.

The Eldest Senior Brother's fate held this calamity in store, and his return from death was a miracle born of layer upon layer of coincidence. While the Tang Clan lay under siege, he was fighting on another battlefield that needed him just as badly, having set aside old grievances to stand shoulder to shoulder with your Second Senior Brother. The people of Song thought the fall of the Great Song was like the sky itself caving in, never guessing that a catastrophe big enough to turn the mortal world into hell had, at that very time, been snuffed out in silence by these two men. When it was over they drank a parting toast, put fame and disgrace behind them, and let no one learn what they had done. The Eldest Senior Brother got his wish to retire from the Jianghu, hunted you down across a thousand miles, and pressed you into forming a crosstalk duo with him. Who would have guessed you were a natural at it—able to make people laugh just by opening your mouth—and the two of you became an overnight sensation, famous the length and breadth of the land. By the time the months turned to years and the mountains and rivers changed hands, and the two of you had spent more time trading jokes on stage than roaming the Jianghu, looking back on those old, hard-fought tales felt like another lifetime—you yourself could hardly believe you had once done such things.

You still thought your eyes were playing tricks on you, half afraid it was some Thousand-Faced Demon in disguise—even in retirement from the Jianghu, you couldn't let yourself off the hook. You looked him over again and again, threw in a few more punches for good measure, and only once the blows felt solid and real did you finally believe this was truly him.

You thought you saw a ghost, your eyes rolled back, and you died on the spot from fear, your heart stopped. Eldest Senior Brother slapped you a few times on the face, then used his Internal Skill to punch your chest, and you slowly regained consciousness.

You thought the Tang Clan was left with only you, with no relatives, destined to be a lonely outcast, wasting away in solitude until old age. Yet an old friend unexpectedly arrived‑none other than the resurrected Eldest Senior Brother.

There is no Tang Clan left in the world, only you remain. Live in solitude until the end of your days, concealing your name. Sometimes you claim to be surnamed Zhao, sometimes you dare to claim the surname Tang. After years of recuperation from your injuries, you walk with a limp, having barely saved your life. Yet, every evening's fading light brings a solitude so profound it suffocates you.

Only Zhao Huo and Long Xiang remained as a couple, often being pointed at and whispered about by others who said they were not well‑matched. Long Xiang just smiled at these comments, taking them with no concern at all, instead laughing at their ignorance. She knew her brother used to be very formidable; even the Wulin Alliance Leader could defeat him. If he had not retired when things got tough, after a few more years of hard practice, he would have been unbeatable in the entire world. Because she loved chicken legs so much, Zhao Huo and Long Xiang thus decided to raise their own chickens. They opened a mountain tea house where they sold both tea and chicken. Business was not good, but it did not matter; after all, Long Xiang would steal from the till herself. A chicken had two legs: one for the guests and one for Long Xiang.

Only Zhao Huo and Xiahou Lan remained as a couple, often pointed at and gossiped about, with people saying they were not a match. Xiahou Lan grew tired of it—she had already retired from the Jianghu, and could hardly go pull off someone's head every time they ran their mouth—so she often pressed you to close the tea house once your wounds healed and follow her back to the Snow Mountains to live in seclusion. But by the time you had healed, she found herself with child, and after much thought decided to settle here instead, reasoning the child would be lonely with no playmates otherwise. The killing intent in her faded a little more each day, though she still carried her umbrella from dawn to dusk—no longer out of some old wound in her heart, simply to keep off the sun.

Only Zhao Huo and Wei Ju remained as a couple, often pointed at and gossiped about, with people saying they were not a match. In truth, it was not only you who thought so—Xiaoju was so refined and gentle that anyone who saw her would know she was born to wealth. Rumor had it she was a noble lady of Lin'an, the treasured daughter of some prince's household, who had fled with you, her guard, into the wilds and settled for marriage out of necessity. You and Xiaoju treated each other as honored equals, husband and wife but also teacher and friend. Beyond the tea house, you grew vegetables near your home, discussed poetry, practiced calligraphy, painted, and played chess together; the years were peaceful and the harvests plentiful, your marriage harmonious, your days plain but content. But she held her liquor poorly—once drunk, her temper turned, and she would rail against current affairs, using the past to mock the present. Fortunately, her Iron Pipa Skill had by then passed entirely to you, or else no one could have reined her in once she got going.

Only Zhao Huo and Yu Zhu remain as a couple, often the subject of gossip, with people saying you two are not suited. Yu Zhu doesn't agree; she believes they are perfectly matched. Running the tea house is merely their surface effort; beneath the tea house, they have built a secret base. In their spare time, they diverted mountain stream water to create a scenic pond for fishing. After some time, they constructed a mechanical amusement park for the village children to play. They avoid Jianghu affairs and live as carefree people.

Only Zhao Huo and Yu Xiaomei remained as a married couple, often pointed at and gossiped about, with people saying they were mismatched. Xiaomei deliberately did nothing to stop them, letting them talk, using the villagers' words to remind you to treasure what you had. The Tang Clan had been destroyed by the Wulin Alliance, and Kongtong had fallen to the Western Xia army; she and you depended on each other for survival, running a small tea house and occasionally robbing the rich to help the poor. If you were good, she was good; if you were bad, she was worse still. Xiaomei obeyed you in nearly everything, unless you turned lecherous eyes on some other girl. Once, when you praised a lady guest's looks, you no sooner got home from closing up shop than Xiaomei ambushed you, knocked you flat, and kept you under house arrest for half a month, tormenting you day and night. Had you not dug an escape tunnel, it seemed she meant never to let you see daylight again.

Only Zhao Huo and Shangguan Ying remained as a couple, often pointed at and whispered about, with people saying they were not a match. Shangguan Ying was magnanimous about it, always patiently explaining your good qualities; even when others were unconvinced, she at least made them give you some face. If someone refused to give face, she answered with her fists—she held none of the noble scruple that Wulin folk should not raise a hand against ordinary commoners. She offered courtesy first and force second, and once the gloves came off she struck anyone in her path, man or woman, young or old; if you were foolish enough to try to pull her off, she struck you too. Shangguan Ying had a real head for business: even an ordinary tea shop flourished under her hand, and beyond serving tea she ran a side trade in brokering and guiding, an inspiration later generations credited for the rise of relay stations and escort agencies. Sharp and capable as she was, at home she turned gentle and dutiful, fanning you cool and kneading your legs whenever business was slow, and taking real joy in it.

Only Zhao Huo and Ye Yunshang remained as a couple, often the subject of gossip, with people saying they weren't a match. Yunshang loves to tease you, yet won't let others look down on you. She is fiercely protective, laughing off gossip at the moment but planning meticulously to retaliate tenfold afterward. Mischievous and cunning, she has innumerable schemes to harm others, and the villagers dare no longer speak ill of the couple. She uses someone else's authority to intimidate outside the home, but at home she is dependent and affectionate, loving to be spoiled, always remaining a young woman regardless of her age.

The good news is that the Ye siblings, having benefited from the zombie powder Tang Fang once gave them, traveled north in search of a cure and at last found it. The Little Medicine Immortal, Liang Youshi, spared no effort to save Yunshang, but was driven out by fellow countrymen back in Jin, and had no choice but to follow the Ye siblings in seeking refuge with you and your spouse. Ye Yunshang still calls herself your sister and has sworn never to marry, living on as your neighbor—delighting in teasing the villagers, and earning herself a reputation as notorious as it is well loved.

Only Zhao Huo and Tang Moling were left, often the target of gossip, with people muttering that the two of them were ill-matched. Moling simply let it go in one ear and out the other—whom she chose to spend her days with was nobody's business but her own. Their old uniforms, one blue and one red, had been washed pale and patched again and again, and however loath they were to part with them, the clothes could not last a lifetime. With the New Year drawing near, they planned to buy cloth for new clothes and keep the old ones, and the memories with them, carefully stored away. Since she had stopped pressing herself to train, her Internal Method had grown slack, and she smiled more easily now—though, still lacking in confidence, she stayed close by your side in everything you did.

In the mountains, time stands still; how many times have the seasons changed? Villagers worry only about food and warmth, unaware of who the current emperor is. Changing dynasties are merely rumors heard from others, only realized later.

The Western Front collapsed in a landslide, and the Jin Kingdom also launched a southern invasion. Within a few years, the Song Kingdom's territory was completely divided. The emperor moved the capital three times, with nowhere to retreat, and in despair and fury, he drowned himself in Yashan, leading to the effortless fall of the Great Song.

The heroes of the Wulin sharpened their blades, quietly watching and waiting, certain you had no strength left to fight back; once they had screwed up enough courage, they meant to cut you into a thousand pieces and take your head, to rid the world of harm. Before they could move, a great host of fleeing refugees suddenly poured into the town; seeing the Wulin heroes bearing swords and dressed in fine silks, the refugees took them for great heroes and begged for help without pause. Song Bei, finding this strange, came forward to ask what had happened, but the refugees showed him no good will for his dress, for they had fled from the north, and every city they passed through had shut its gates against them. It turned out that Western Xia had raised an army, borrowed passage through Jin, crossed the Hexi Corridor, and launched a sudden strike on Shu. Crossing the Qinling range was no easy thing, but the remnants of the Supreme Bliss Cult, lying low for years and long since grown strong again, made their return this time, acting as inside men: in the time it takes to clap, they struck down the garrison commander, seized the official post road, ushered Western Xia through the pass, and took city after city. When the heroes of the Wulin heard this grim news, they could only stare at one another. The Alliance had been formed to unite the sects of the Wulin and uphold justice—yet who would have thought that merely striking down the Tang Clan had cost them so dearly? Should they truly go to war, would any of them come back at all? And with the Alliance Leader crushed in defeat, the people's hearts had nowhere left to turn; all scattered and shrank from the fight. The young head of the Nangong family could not command respect, while the head of the Shangguan family only gloated, retreating to Fujian to enjoy his ease—worst come to worst, should Song fall, he had ships enough loaded with wealth to flee to Japan and live out his days in comfort regardless. Leaderless, the Wulin Alliance scattered in every direction. It was not that they were entirely without spirit, but all men fear death; it takes fire to heat the blood to boiling before it will rise. And on this very day, at this very hour, the Imperial Court snuffed out the Jianghu's last spark.

The Little Junior Sister did not want you to die; despite her hatred, she could not simply turn away from her gravely wounded husband. Dazed, as though caught in a nightmare she could not wake from, she longed to close her eyes and open them again in that beautiful past when no one had yet gone missing. Yet no matter how ashamed we may be, the years remain merciless.

You defeated an invincible foe and shook the whole Wulin. You proved that even one so extraordinary as him was not unbeatable, and that one so ordinary as you was never to be trifled with. Rui Sheng's beauties were all struck dumb—they had never imagined their lord could lose to anyone, let alone to some plain little ant of the Tang Clan. You won at terrible cost, with only a breath of life left in you, and now stood condemned by a thousand voices; anyone could have pushed you into the grave with a single shove. Every last one of your Tang Clan brothers and sisters was dead, none left to stand at your side—as far as the eye could see, the whole world was your enemy.

Some are blessed by heaven, born with everything: boundless opportunity, a dashing and handsome bearing, fine silk robes, peerless talent—beauties fall for him at first glance; he draws his sword, climbs the heights, and calls forth wind and cloud. For him, the Jianghu is as easy as a game. And then there is someone as lowly as you. Set beside him, the gap is like cloud and mud; your struggles are but one more line added to his legend. You were always going to lose—it was never fair. Decades later, when the young of the Jianghu asked the old Alliance Leader who, in his whole life, had been the strongest foe he ever faced, Rui Sheng answered without hesitation: you. Not the Dharma King of the Heavenly Path, whose fists were mighty enough to cleave heaven and earth; not the Supreme Bliss Cult Leader, who fused the internal force of a hundred heroes into one—neither could compare. For your final blow carried the proudest bones beneath heaven. It did not sting or ache upon his body, yet it sank through flesh and bone; blow after blow it shook him to the heart, wove itself into his heartbeat, and its aftershock echoed for decades—like poison, tormenting him with endless regret. It was the Tang Clan's final hidden weapon.

Fu Yun firmly believed the Dharma could resolve every worldly grudge; where words might serve, he would not raise his fists—though there were exceptions. Shi Ming, for all his mastery of scripture and skill in debate, had made of it his own hindrance to wisdom; only a sudden blow to the head could jolt him back to clarity.
Fan Xiaotian faced off against Li Fugui, once brothers in arms, now bitter enemies.
Diancang's Dual Revered Ones were about to come to protect the Alliance Leader, but Ye Yunzhou had them sent elsewhere for a private resolution. The outcome of this battle was unknown.
You came before the Alliance Leader covered in wounds, seeking nothing but a duel. Slowly he drew his sword—in his eyes you were no small fry of the Jianghu, but a battle-hardened and worthy foe.

He could not bear to abandon the friends he called brothers, and so reluctantly bore the crown of Alliance Leader, setting aside private feeling for the sake of Great Song's future. He knew he had wronged you, and would think it only fair should you come to take his life. Though he could not offer his neck to the blade, should he die at your hand, he would hold no grudge. And so A'Sheng and A'Huo at last arrived at the watershed of fate.

Xiaomei pretended to be taken over, crying and running to Rui Sheng, then suddenly drawing a Blade. However, Rui Sheng's agility was remarkable; with a thought, he moved like a wisp of fluff, and Xiaomei's attack missed, leading to her revealing her true form.

Xiaomei pretended to be taken over by you, weeping and running toward Rui Sheng, only to suddenly draw a Blade and turn against him. If it were in the past, relying on Rui Sheng's agility, even a surprise attack would not have harmed him. However, Xiaomei had already made some progress in mastering One-Toe Riding the Wind; things had changed. Adapting to the situation, she successfully cut Rui Sheng with a dagger. Still unsatisfied with her success, she scoffed, revealing her true form. She had originally intended to kill him in one go.

She was not adept at speech, placing her hopes on Rui Sheng, hoping her husband would recall their marital bond, to subdue the Tang Clan without taking lives. This was her lifelong wish, yet it remained unfulfilled, her heart shattered like petals drifting to the ground. The incident planted a seed, leaving her forever closed off to her husband.
Alas, the silver flowed out like water, yet still it counted for nothing.

Alas, pure of heart and utterly without guile, she placed her trust in the wrong man: Chao He. It was not that she bore him no resentment for betraying the sect, but Chao He wept and begged forgiveness, and the Little Junior Sister, being softhearted, was moved to pity; she reasoned that he had once been a Tang Clan disciple, and if he had truly repented, he might yet atone through good deeds. In the end, all her jewelry and treasures went to Chao He, squandered on his debauchery in the pleasure houses.
After marrying out, the Little Junior Sister still looked after the sect, paying frequent visits, and had every valuable thing she could spare sent through others to smooth matters over.

The Junior Martial Brothers and Sisters gave their all to open a path for you—not a path to life, but a dead-end leading to certain death. Just as they had thrown away their lives without a second thought, you too went forward without hesitation.

The rank and file of the Flying Stone Gang had little learning, but growing up in Shu, who wasn't in awe of the Tang Clan's rise? They all longed to walk with the same swagger as the Tang Clan's finest disciples. Ashamed of their own inferiority, they banded together and often made trouble for the Tang Clan, mostly out of envy. Now that old grudges had been laid to rest, marching into battle at your side was an honor to them all. Even in death, they would not yield while their blood still ran hot.

Nangong Shen heard the news and was speechless. As the Military Strategist of the Wulin Alliance, he should have been concerned about the greater good. Hearing that you were fighting desperately to the death should have caused him distress. Yet, his heart raced with a sense of anticipation as if he had been waiting for this moment. The Tang Clan of Shu, indeed, should be stubborn and unruly.

Third Senior Brother held Nangong Shen back with everything he had, refusing to let him go guard the Alliance Leader. You gritted your teeth, bearing the weight of everyone's will, and at last reached the watershed of the age.

Third Senior Brother and Fourth Senior Brother jointly defended against Nangong Shen, preventing him from guarding the Alliance Leader. You gritted your teeth, bearing everyone's will, and finally arrived at the watershed of time.

Your Junior Martial Brothers and Sisters fought with everything they had to open a path for you — not a path to survival, but a dead end leading only to certain death. Yet you went forward boldly, without a backward glance.
The people of Jinxiang Palace proved just as loyal — they turned their spears around in the heat of battle, tearing a breach through the Wulin Alliance's ranks by main force to clear your way.

The rank and file of the Flying Stone Gang had little learning, but growing up in Shu, who didn't look up to the Tang Clan? They all longed to walk with the same swagger as the Tang Clan's finest disciples. Ashamed of their own inferiority, they banded together and often made trouble for the Tang Clan, mostly out of envy. Now that old grudges had been laid to rest, marching into battle at your side was an honor to them all.

The Tang Clan's place beside the Wulin Alliance was like an ant trying to topple a great tree — laughably unaware of its own size. The moment the Wulin Alliance reached Meishan, it seized the outer forts and sent men to storm the compound, hoping to win swiftly and cheaply so as to save its strength for the Mud Cult. But it had kicked an iron plate: however diminished the Tang Clan's power, it was never one to be trifled with. You, Tang Clan from top to bottom, were ever the most defiant of all — the more hopeless the odds, the louder you sang against them, refusing to sit and wait for death, until you turned from defense to attack and struck down the mountain.
Xiaomei had never pushed anyone down with such a clear conscience; listening to their cries fade into the distance, she was fit to burst with joy.

The mountain path was narrow, and with so many crowding onto it, there was no way to avoid them. Your Tang Clan wasn't about to waste false courtesy on them — you shoved them all off the mountain in one go.

The mountain path was narrow, and with the crowd growing dense, there was nowhere to avoid. Xiao Zhu, blindfolded, could still hit his target. With a sudden charge, he delivered a powerful headbutt, knocking all the Wulin Heroes down the mountain. The trajectory of their flight was as spectacular as a horse‑drawn carriage colliding head‑on at full speed.

But your ranks had withered to a handful of battered survivors, willing but no longer able. Your Junior Martial Brothers and Sisters gave their lives to hold the rear for you, entrusting to you their sorrowful vow to avenge this disgrace.

People have already fought their way up the mountain; it's either you die or I live. Not holding back in combat is a sign of honoring their resolve. As for those who came up the mountain without clear intentions, their deaths are even more deserved.

You had never before come to blows with the orthodox sects, yet you had always found them insufferable. You could never become a great hero yourself, so why should anyone else get to shine? Today was the perfect excuse to settle old scores.

You fought a desperate, back-to-the-wall battle, sallying out in full force, and on the mountain road you unexpectedly crossed paths with a band of Wulin heroes. Your hearts were full of rage with nowhere to spend it, and before the other side even grasped what was happening, you sent them staggering in every direction.

You fought a desperate, back-to-the-wall battle, sallying out in full force, and on the mountain road you crossed paths with a band of Wulin heroes. With no heart left for fighting, you scattered and each broke through the encirclement to descend the mountain alone.

You fought a desperate, back-to-the-wall battle, sallying out in full force, and on the mountain road you crossed paths with a band of Wulin heroes. Your Junior Martial Brothers and Sisters volunteered to hold the rear at the cost of their lives, entrusting to you their sorrowful vow to avenge this disgrace.

People always hope that significant beliefs exist in reality, not just within stories. They yearn for Heaven not to forsake sincere efforts, for someone to see injustice and stand up against it, rather than merely using grandiose rhetoric to elevate some and belittle others. Though you may find this world intolerable and attempt to protest, you are but a mere mortal, an insignificant speck of dust in the vast ocean. In the end, you are washed away by the tide, your sighs barely audible, your resolve and remaining strength washed away by the rain, and the story comes to a close.
One day, spring light was warm, the weather was pleasant with gentle breezes and bright sunshine. She suddenly missed you very much. She walked to your tomb, fell asleep, and never woke up again.

Fan Xiaoyan was refined and grew increasingly beautiful, becoming more refined in speech and conduct. A woodcutter, captivated by her, dared to propose. After Fan Xiaoyan married, Xiahou Lan vanished without a trace, and no one ever saw her again.

Xiahou Lan's eyes stayed fixed on you as you fought on drenched in blood, the flame of your life guttering toward its end. It pierced her to the heart, and yet she could not help but envy you — she herself had once failed to stand and fall with the Snow Mountain Sect, and she carried that as the deepest regret of her life. Since you had made your choice, she would honor it. She carried your ashes back to the Snow Mountain Sect and had a tombstone carved for you, reading: 'Eldest Disciple of the Snow Mountain Sect.' And as though you still lived, she went to your grave every day and spoke with you.

Xiao Ju walked towards you with a gentle and graceful step, as she had done in the past, her demeanor so serene that no one dared to approach or offend her as she bid you farewell. She is the Sect Leader of Kongtong Mystic Skill, a talented lady from Lin'an, skilled in strategy and capable of securing the nation's peace in the court. Nangong and Shangguan, the heads of two prominent families, have repeatedly instructed their subordinates to refrain from harming her, insisting on treating her with respect as a honored guest.  Yet this extraordinary woman despises frivolity and has entrusted this one precious life to you, hoping only for a hand in marriage and a lifelong companionship in the mountains. Alas, human wishes are often not granted by heaven. Others tried to persuade her, but she paid no heed, gently leaning against you as if already asleep. Upon checking her breath, you found that despite her outward calmness, she had broken multiple vital points with her Iron Pipa Skill, shattering her internal organs. Her sorrow and anger remained unspoken, contained within herself, needing not to move one's soul, but only for the heavens to know.

Yunshang supported your broken body, blood and rain pouring down, accompanied by thunder and lightning, faintly sensing something drifting away. Her deep feelings about life and death were beyond what ordinary people could comprehend; she was certain of your demise, treating each day as if it were the last, always thinking that during her time in this world, she must deeply wound someone's heart, ensuring they would remember her until old age. Now, as she bids you farewell, she realizes the depth of her feelings.   Yunshang did not follow you; after all, her life was lived for you, and life must go on. Yet, with winter gone, the desolate summer no longer has you. She lived with her Junior Martial Sister for several years, moving to the water town of Jiangnan, naming their home Living Person Pavilion. Thanks to your blessing, that girl has grown up safely, becoming even more beautiful, renowned for her stunning looks. Among those seeking her hand were noble scions and talented youths from Jianghu, promising her the world, filling the Living Person Pavilion with exquisite jewels, all to elicit a smile from this ice‑cold beauty.   She looked down on everyone, simply declining with indifference: Yunshang has a husband, my lord, the greatest hero under heaven, with a heart of a swordsman and the grace of a musician, face like a jade crown. In this world, he is the only one of worth; the rest are but fleeting clouds.

Thunder cracked, and Junior Martial Sister caught sight of you drenched in blood; terror scattered her wits, and tears burst from her eyes — she hated that her hands were too small to cover your wounds, hated that her body was too slight to hold you up. The Tang Clan always had its comings and goings, new faces arriving, old ones leaving; heartbreaking as that was, there had always been you, carefully cupping her heart so it wouldn't shatter — she had never imagined that even you might break your word and leave. The sky hadn't yet darkened, but the night already stretched on without end, as though dawn would never come again. She wished she'd never spoken those words; if not for her selfish plea, perhaps you could have lived out your natural span. Somehow she knew which drops were rain and which were her own breaking heart. Even the immortals couldn't say where you found the strength to rise once more and urge her away. Whenever she wept alone, you used to sing to her — always the same song, sung now only in broken snatches. Junior Martial Sister stumbled blindly into the forest, unable to make out the words any longer, and through her tears she finished the song for you. Though your hearts had been joined, fate played its cruel trick, and in the end you could not stay together for life. Her whole body shook without end, the bell's chime and her own weeping swallowed by the pouring rain. She was alone now, with no one left to lean on. Everywhere she looked seemed fraught with dread, and the rest of her life stretched ahead in hardship and wandering.

You didn't need to say it; your hearts already understood each other. You took out your Mohele Doll and placed it in her palm. Xiao Zhu stroked its jaunty little topknot as though it were you yourself — clearly unable to put it down, yet afraid that if she held it too tightly she might crush it, hurt it, and that you, too, would abandon her.

Xiao Zhu had strength to spare, but her martial skill barely rose to third-rate — yet the world only needs the banner of righteousness to raise a hand against the old, the weak, women, and children, without a shred of mercy for the delicate. Wounded all over, she gathered you up around the waist and carried you, breaking through the encirclement and down the mountain, plunging into the forest. By then she had lost too much blood, her eyes already blind; she sank against your chest, her breath growing fainter and fainter. She seemed to murmur many things, but they were only the ramblings of the dying.

Neither Xiaomei's fury nor her pleading could keep you from dying; she hated you for giving her hope only to leave it unfulfilled. To her, more terrifying than the day of death itself was the day fate ran out, leaving her to live on alone in the world, wretched and friendless, unable to see you no matter how she longed for you. She pressed a deep kiss to your lips, then drew a dagger and plunged it into your already stilled heart — hoping that by taking your life in turn, you would remember her through every lifetime to come; and even if you returned as a vengeful ghost to claim her life for it, she would welcome it with joy.

From the very day she followed you into the Tang Clan, she had known this day would come, and she never once regretted it — you never knew just how glad she was that you had asked her along. Unable to bear seeing you grieve, she waited until she watched you vanish from sight, then took your weapon and scarred her own face, swearing never to marry another, vowing to spend the rest of her days before an ancient shrine, keeping vigil for you.

The tide had turned. The Tang Clan disciples lay dead or dying, and you too were grievously wounded, clinging to life by a single breath. Shangguan Ying was seized by grief and fury alike; no matter how she thrashed and struck out, hair disheveled, screaming until her heart broke, heaven gave no answer and earth no response. Having only heard of the world's suffering while she lived in comfort, she now tasted it for herself, and all hope drained from her.

Long Xiang stood back-to-back with you, hearts entwined, your unspoken understanding seamless, invincible together. No matter how many Wulin heroes came at you, one after another, they all fell beneath your blades — a single battle that shook the Jianghu. Yet life has its limits: for all the hero's blood that ran in her veins, she remained flesh and blood like any mortal, no different from you. When the hour came, commoner and king alike had to accept their fate. The dying sun bled crimson, and still you and Long Xiang stood unbroken, poised between the fading light and the coming stars, your shadows stretching ever longer.

Even Cangsong Swordsman Ye Yunzhou could not withstand the tide of attackers. His blade's edge was lost in blood as he cut down ten men, then twenty more came. His strength spent, his True Qi exhausted, he bore a dozen wounds large and small — gifted as he was, in the end he could not escape death.

After that, a steady stream of disciples from the six major sects under the Wulin Alliance poured into the mountain gate, chanting slogans to eradicate the Demon Cult and uphold human justice, surrounding and killing Tang Clan disciples.

In the great courtyard, every heart beat as one.
The Wulin Alliance had sent men up the mountain to claim your Tang Clan disciples' lives, but their lives proved too tough to take. It was only proper, then, that you play the host in return and deliver death to their door yourselves, letting them taste the true hospitality of the Tang Clan of Shu.

Fourth Senior Brother was the first to run, seeing the Junior Martial Brothers and Sisters safely down the mountain before turning back again.
A man who loved money and trimmed his sails to the wind, he made no secret of it: a certain death he'd sit out, but so long as the Tang Clan still had a two-in-ten chance, he could never resist wagering on his own sect.

The Jianghu, after all, is no wishing well; not every dream blooms into fruit, and a clear conscience alone does not guarantee a good end.
Tang Clan disciples fell one by one, and your struggle ended, in the end, in defeat.

The Wulin Alliance had never thought much of the puny Tang Clan; wiping it out was merely a show of strength before the road ahead, for their true rival was the Mud Cult. They reckoned that sending Wanli Pengcheng to kill your Tang Clan's foremost expert and crush its pride would be as easy as turning over a hand, and mopping up the rest with the followers who came after would be simpler still. Little did they know that for all Wanli Pengcheng's regard for talent, he held nothing back — and still you proved unusually hard to overcome. Most of the Wulin heroes who had followed him up the mountain were young disciples from various sects; as the fighting dragged on with no word of victory, their spirits sank further by the hour, and when they saw Wanli Pengcheng retreat, they panicked outright. No one could say who broke first, but the whole pack scattered and fled down the mountain.

Wanli Pengcheng kept his word and departed. Only now, having walked the line between life and death with your whole attention fixed on the fight, did you hear the commotion rising from the mountain path — what sounded like cheers. Fearing Third Senior Brother had met with trouble, you hurried to go help, but a Tang Clan disciple had already returned first with word.

Alas, all your effort, all your hard-won toil, amounted to nothing more than a backdrop for another's glory. Whether in elder Wanli Pengcheng's eyes or in anyone else's heart, there was always someone who mattered more than you. It seemed that other one was the true hero of this Jianghu, a prodigy blessed by heaven and earth, with sun, moon, and stars all turning for him.

Never had you imagined such an ending — you had defeated the strongest opponent you'd ever faced, and still you were the loser. Whether in elder Wanli Pengcheng's eyes or in anyone's heart, there was always someone who mattered more than you. It seemed that other one was the true hero of this Jianghu, a genius favored by heaven, with sun, moon, and stars turning for him.
You have resolved a karmic bond that transcends years.

In sixty years of experience, Wanli Pengcheng had only ever heard of young heroes who chanced upon fortune and rose swiftly to mastery — never had he seen one like you, whose internal skill and physique did not even reach second- or third-rate, and yet whose technique shifted through countless forms, nearing the realm beyond technique itself. Deep in the ways of attack, defense, advance and retreat, every stance concealed some hidden purpose, drawing on every school of martial arts under heaven while striking where none expected. Before he knew it, the fifteen moves had passed — to strike you dead now would only be to break his word.

In sixty years of experience, Wanli Pengcheng had only ever heard of young heroes who chanced upon some fortune, surged forward in their internal skill, and rose young into the ranks of masters — never had he seen one like you, whose internal skill and physique did not even reach second- or third-rate, yet whose techniques shifted through countless forms, nearing the realm beyond technique itself. Deep in the ways of attack, defense, advance, and retreat, every stance concealed some hidden purpose, drawing on every school of martial arts under heaven while still striking where none expected. Though you walked the edge of death nine times in ten, this was the one time in ten you lived — today was the day you called down a miracle and defeated a living legend of the Wulin.

Faced with the top martial artists in Jianghu, your defeat is inevitable, and even if you feel resentment, there's nothing you can do about it. You are compared to an unreachable hero. In the eyes of Senior Wanli Pengcheng, in the heart of the Junior Martial Sister, and in the minds of everyone else, there is always someone more important than you. It seems that person is the true protagonist of this Jianghu, a prodigy destined for greatness, with the sun, moon, and stars all revolving around him.

You have defeated a formidable opponent, but the Tang Clan no longer has a mentor to praise you. Third Senior Brother spent the first half of his life worrying for the Great Song and the latter half laboring for the Tang Clan. Unlike ordinary Jianghu individuals who wear fine garments and wield swords for fame, he lived a life of integrity. As the battle reached its conclusion, Third Senior Brother departed this world before you, sacrificing himself for the clan and fulfilling his mission as the Acting Sect Leader.

Sometimes they fought alone, sometimes they joined forces to strike as one; the three of them believed the Flying Hero was dead, the Ruthless Young Master had defected, the Tang Clan's ranks had withered, and that even you, this runt of a melon, this shriveled gourd, had only come along to pad the numbers — nothing to fear at all. Only once blades crossed did they learn how fearsome mere words could be: the world had belittled you for your looks alone, and every mention of your name came with a sneer, until the tale spread so far it was mistaken for truth — and that misjudgment brought them to ruin here.

At times they fought alone, at times they joined forces to strike the enemy. Third Senior Brother had spent the first half of his life worrying over the Great Song, and the second half laboring for the Tang Clan; unlike ordinary folk of the Jianghu who donned fine robes and wielded swords for fame, he lived his whole life with honor. As the fierce battle drew to its close, Third Senior Brother departed this world a step ahead of you, giving his life for the sect and fulfilling his duty as Acting Sect Leader.
Unless it's you, who dabbles in every school of martial arts under heaven.

Ordinarily, you wouldn't dare accept these fifteen strikes even under threat of death — but today is the exception, for today you truly are meant to die at someone's hands. Well, if you must die, better first to witness a peerless technique; coming into this world will not have been in vain.

The Eagle Hero's name meant little, but Chan Master Juekong had been a top-tier master for decades, his reputation surpassing even the sect leader's. His Vajra Finger Power splits stone and cracks monuments, and his Buddhist Lion's Roar sends ghosts and gods fleeing — without deep internal skill, none could withstand it. But the Tang Clan's greatest weakness has always been its Internal Force. Even if the Flying Hero himself rose from the dead, whether he could survive these fifteen moves would remain in doubt. Look at the Tang Clan today — whoever stepped up would walk a dead man's road.

Ye Yunzhou, with Third Senior Brother's consent, claimed the standing of a Tang Clan disciple, unwilling to let the Sect Leader risk himself, and so stepped forward — yet Wanli Pengcheng was reluctant to fight him. It was not that he feared Ye Yunzhou's swift blade, but that he could not bear to waste such talent. The essence of Diancang swordsmanship lies in a single word: speed — the blade must move like a startled hare, swift as rolling thunder, impossible to guard against — and among them all, Ye Yunzhou stood foremost; for speed, no one alive could match him. But Wanli Pengcheng had crossed blades with the Sword Saint of Diancang no fewer than a hundred times, and knew the secret technique Breakthrough of Cloud Pass inside and out. Before the Listening Cloud Sword could even leave its sheath, Wanli Pengcheng flicked a pinecone at it with Vajra Finger Power, driving it back into the scabbard and numbing Ye Yunzhou's hand at the tiger's mouth. Knowing his swift blade was countered, Ye Yunzhou realized that forcing the fight could only end in defeat and death, and would besides disgrace his sect's name — so he had no choice but to yield.

Wanli Pengcheng had not come to the Tang Clan out of hostility, but merely to keep a promise and answer for an old friend. Yet the sect leader lay bedridden, and the mighty Tang Clan had no one else worthy of his notice. Witnessing the clan's decline, he could not help but sigh. He declared he would use only fifteen moves, and bade the Tang Clan send a disciple to receive them; once fifteen moves had passed, whether the disciple lived or died, the old grudge would be settled.

The Sect Leader lay ill in bed, and in all the great Tang Clan, no one else had caught his eye — if there were to be an exception, it would be you. You, young upstart, have tricked him out of his due more than once; today the two of you must settle, once and for all, who is better.

Before the Wulin Alliance's main force arrived, a single peerless master soared ahead of them and lit atop the Tang family compound. The old man wore a straw rain-cape, his eyes sharp and piercing, his appearance strange, yet every motion of his hands and feet betrayed formidable skill. Third Senior Brother, who knew the tales of the Jianghu like the back of his hand, recognized him at a glance: the former Head of the Bodhidharma Hall at Songshan, now styling himself the Eagle Hero — Chan Master Juekong, Wanli Pengcheng.

The Wulin Alliance's great host pressed toward the border; before striking in earnest, it sent three top experts up the mountain to issue a challenge, meaning to cow the Tang Clan on the spot and weaken its will to resist.

Among them was Yunshang, who, even though she didn't know martial arts, wanted to contribute her share. She had studied the Qin at Jinxiang Palace, possessing natural talent, but her frail body had only recently recovered, and her practice of internal skills was still shallow. To wield the Sound Wave Skill like Lady Wen, capable of harming others through string vibrations, would require at least two or three decades of Power. Thus, she had a wild idea, targeting Third Senior Brother, intending to borrow his internal skill to channel the Sound Wave Skill.

From the moment you take your vows as a disciple of the Tang Clan, you are destined to be different from other sects. Those who aren't united in purpose can leave; there will always be a few like you who regard the Tang Clan as their home and swear to share its fate.

Yunshang had studied the qin at the Jinxiang Palace, possessing natural talent, yet her frail body had just recovered, and her mastery of Internal Skill was still shallow. To wield the technique like Lady Wen, who could use the strings to harm others, would require at least two or three decades of Power. She had the audacity to think of an idea, immediately targeting the Tang Clan sisters, commanding them to link up in a chain, channeling their Internal Skill into her to employ the Sound Wave Skill.
