This horrifying notion was unheard of, and even if someone had thought of it, no one had ever attempted it. After all, it was utterly impractical. Who would, during a duel, form a chain to transfer Internal Force to another? With such spare time, it would be far more efficient to simply walk forward and strike the opponent with a blade.

From the moment a Tang Clan disciple takes their vows, they are destined to be different from other sects. Those who cannot stay may go with him, but those who remain all refuse to accept their fate‑how could there be any reason to retreat? All of them clench their fists and brace themselves, vowing to share the fate of their sect.

Yunshang had studied the qin at the Jinxiang Palace, possessing natural talent, yet her frail body had just recovered, and her mastery of Internal Skill was still shallow. To wield the technique like Lady Wen, who could use the strings to harm others, would require at least two or three decades of Power. She had the audacity to think of an idea, immediately targeting the Tang Clan sisters, commanding them to link up in a chain, channeling their Internal Skill into her to employ the Sound Wave Skill. This horrifying notion was unheard of, and even if someone had thought of it, no one had ever attempted it. After all, it was utterly impractical. Who would, during a duel, form a chain to transfer Internal Force to another? With such spare time, it would be far more efficient to simply walk forward and strike the opponent with a blade.

From the moment you take your vows as a Tang Clan disciple, you are fated to be distinct from other sects. Any confrontation that comes to the door must be fought; there's no reason to retreat. All are bracing themselves, vowing to share the fate of the sect.

The Wulin Alliance's first wave of attack sent out a full hundred men, young disciples from every sect eager to make a name for themselves in a single battle, all racing to be first through the gates of the Tang Family Compound.

Ye Yunshang watched from afar, then quietly withdrew. Tears streamed down her face — she couldn't fathom what had so blinded Moling's judgment that she'd fallen for you, nor could she recall what had blinded her own, that she too had come to love you. She didn't care which of them you favored more; she had no wish to share you, and she didn't want to hurt her best friend, so quietly and sensibly, she walked out of your life.
On this day, the Wulin Alliance would eradicate the Tang Clan. A somber and desolate atmosphere hung over the Training Ground, and anyone could tell that this time, staying here meant certain death.

But you're uneducated, not knowing a single character, only focused on eating. Hastily defending yourself, you claim you didn't throw a papaya at her; you're innocent. Third Senior Brother, hearing this from the sidelines, couldn't help but feel ashamed for you.
You couldn't help but be moved, and you teased her. Even when death was at the door, laughing and joking was better than being gloomy and worried.

Shangguan Ying was one of the unseen hands behind the Tang Clan's decline — how could she not know the current situation? Not sure whether you'd truly understood as much, you brought her to the Tang Clan all the same. From the moment she stepped back into the Tang Family Compound, she had foreseen this day; it was a fruit of her own sowing, and she deserved to share the bitter harvest with the rest of you. Though she couldn't bear the thought of dying so young, she feared even more growing old and dying alone in an unfamiliar land. In the end, what she felt toward you was still mostly gratitude. She quoted the Book of Songs, Odes of Wei, "Mu Gua," pouring out her feelings and revealing her wish that the two of you remain friends forever.

You strut about smugly, flirting with other women wherever you go; even though the laws of the State of Song permit it, reason and sentiment will not allow it. You knew full well why Shangguan Ying broke with Eldest Young Lord Nangong, yet you insisted on tempting fate all the same — no wonder you're so disliked. But you've treated her, after all, far better than the Eldest Young Lord ever did. That you've wronged her is a fact, yet the debt of kindness remains. Shangguan Ying gave up any thought of marrying you, but still counts you a good friend and stands by you in loyalty — now that she goes to her death today, why should she hold it against you?

The Wulin Alliance came charging up the mountain to kill. Shangguan Ying, without the slightest regard for old ties, turned and walked away, glancing back every three steps. Seeing your utterly indifferent expression, she couldn't hold back her anger, turned around, and gave you a punch.

The Wulin Alliance came charging up the mountain to kill, and Shangguan Ying, without the slightest regard for old ties, turned and walked away. It wasn't that you didn't wish her a peaceful life living on alone, far away, but her leaving so resolutely still left you feeling deeply hurt. When Shangguan Ying turned back and saw the melancholy and loneliness on your face, she felt satisfied. Don't blame her for being harsh with you, either — who made you such an unfeeling man, always flirting around?

You've found the reclusive enemy, intending to repay them in kind, to destroy their entire family. Yet, hearing the laughter and joy within the walls, you turn to see the sorrowful eyes of your children. They've grown up watching you, as you once longed for your parents' affection. You've followed in your parents' footsteps, never smiling at them. Overwhelmed with conflicting emotions, your thoughts swirl endlessly, and finally you sigh deeply, gently caressing the heads of your children, taking one in each hand and leading them home. The children are astonished by your affection, and Xiahou Lan, seeing you set aside your hatred, is overjoyed. That night, she cooks many dishes and serves you wine, speaking casually about old memories. You fall asleep drowsily, and when you wake up, you realize it's been a long time since your wife last poured you wine. Thirty years have passed in the blink of an eye. Your children have all left the mountains to start their own families, and Xiahou Lan is buried on Snow Mountain. You live alone on Snow Mountain, going down to buy wine. You hear that even the Great Song is gone, and now the country is called the Yuan Dynasty. You feel as if you've been transported to another world, unable to restrain your laughter. Laughing, you weep, for you've lived through the change of dynasties, yet your heart has long since died.

You have always been unable to forget your old grudges, seeking out the retired enemy to repay them in kind, wiping out their entire family. You became wanted by the authorities. Your two children perished trying to protect you, and upon hearing of their deaths, Xiahou Lan silently wept that night and hanged herself.

The Tang Clan was destroyed today. You and Xiahou Lan returned to the Snow Mountain to settle down. Although you have a beautiful companion, you rarely smile. The grudge of the clan's annihilation is something you dare not forget for even a day. You practice martial arts diligently day and night, not daring to slack off, but your heart has been tainted by hatred, and you can no longer lose yourself in your training, causing your progress to slow down. Years have passed, and Xiahou Lan gave birth to a son and a daughter, fortunately, both children resemble her and not you. You constantly urge the two children to practice martial arts, so they can avenge their father in the future. Although Xiahou Lan has her reservations, she mostly concedes to you. Thirty years later, you have mastered your skills, combining the strengths of the Snow Mountain, Soul-Stealing, and the Tang Clan. You are confident that you are no less than any of the renowned experts from your earlier days. Thus, you take your children down the mountain, ready to seek revenge. However, by then, the Wulin Alliance no longer exists, and of course, neither does the Mud Cult. All the acquaintances you once knew are no longer to be seen; the new generation in the vast Jianghu is full of spirited newcomers.

She was challenged but not upset, instead taking you as a disciple to pass on her skills. Nothing brings her greater joy than seeing you surpass her, whether in martial arts or in heart. That once crying, pitiful child has now become a hero. She couldn't help but pat your head in approval. Taking you as a disciple was, in itself, the greatest pride of her life, Xiahou Lan.

Only, she couldn't set her mind at ease about your Junior Sister Fan Xiaoyan, fearing she might fall back into the worldly life, so she painfully took her leave of you.
Before departing, she touched your head in commendation.
Taking you as her disciple was, after all, the pride of Xiahou Lan's whole life.

You ultimately chose not to retreat. Xiahou Lan felt disappointed and lost, yet couldn't help but take pride in you. The disciple seeks a good master, and the master also hopes to find a worthy disciple to pass on the Robe and Bowl. The Snow Mountain Sect values integrity above all else, not martial talent. Someone like you, loyal and righteous, is an ideal choice.

Xiahou Lan really couldn't bear to part with you, she appeared in the courtyard, appealing to your emotions. Everyone understood the situation clearly; the Tang Clan has no power to reverse the situation, and if you stay, you will die. But if you are willing to endure the injustice and go with her far away, she is not unwilling to set aside her master's authority, and from then on, only be a gentle wife to make up for you.

Long Xiang threw the question back at you, thought it over seriously, and suggested charging down the mountain. You meant to say something, but in the end found no answer — after all, holding out on the mountain meant death just the same, so striking first might be better. Who could say? Perhaps you'd even have a slim chance of killing the Wulin Alliance Leader.
You had the audacity to flirt with her; Long Xiang put on a show of displeasure, but wasn't truly angry.
Long Xiang approached closely, obeying your orders

Long Xiang came closer, and hearing that you had no plan requiring her cooperation, decided to follow her own heart and act recklessly, turning from defense to offense and charging down the mountain. If things went well, she would kill everyone who had driven their master to death on Fengyu Mountain that day, avenging him; if her strength proved insufficient, she would die fighting on the road.

Suddenly a disciple came to report that someone was being carried up the mountain in a sedan chair — at first it seemed a sudden strike by the Wulin Alliance, but it turned out to be the Kongtong Guardians. When Xiaoju stepped down from the chair, your heart leapt with surprise and joy. Upon asking, you learned that a great deal had happened since you last parted — a major crisis had struck Kongtong, which was why they could not rush to the Tang Clan's aid in time. Your Sect Leader Wei, ever perceptive, had discerned the Western Xia's conspiracy to borrow a path from Jin and collaborate with the Supreme Bliss Cult to seize control of Western Shu, and so had to act decisively, leading Danxiazi and the Kongtong disciples to join forces with the region's auxiliary troops to resist the Western Xia army. Urgent dispatches had indeed been sent through the official post over eight hundred miles, but the enemy was always one step ahead: the Supreme Bliss Cult had been lurking in Western Shu for years, infiltrating every prefecture, and every message sent had vanished without a trace. It was only through the daring efforts of a Flying Heaven Disciple skilled in Qinggong, who braved the journey along the Song-Jin border to slip past enemy eyes, that word finally reached the Central Plains. But the narrow-minded Wulin Alliance took it only for a delaying trick, as though Kongtong had fabricated the intelligence. Xiaoju heard this and felt her heart turn cold — colder even than the day she, a top scholar, was married off to a coarse military officer. What had she done, caring for the realm and its people though she held no court office, loyal and devoted to the crown, that the court should now scheme so ruthlessly against the Tang Clan and her own husband? At the thought, she suddenly wanted no more part of it. She had the Kongtong Guardians carry her to the Tang Clan to be with you, leaving Danxiazi to face the Western Xia army alone. Even if she had a sound strategy to save the realm, she no longer wished to use it. She would spend all her remaining days on you, ready to die as you might have died though she need not, her heart shining bright as sun and moon, her name fit to be written into the annals. You knew well enough she was bending herself for your sake, and moved by gratitude, you resolved that if fortune allowed, you would spend the rest of your life making it up to her — the two of you retreating together to the hills, farming in fair weather and reading in the rain, keeping chickens and ducks if it came to that, living out a plain, quiet life in perfect harmony. Xiaoju trusted you. She would wait.

You have a name with Xiaozhu, yet there is no reality of marriage between you. You wish to persuade Xiaozhu to go down the mountain and live alone. She fears hearing you say such words most of all, and she is both sorrowful and furious, her tears falling drop by drop onto her collar. She was sold by the father she loved and respected to a human trafficker, beaten and scolded all the way, her body and spirit worn out. Only after being taken in by the Iron Fist Sect Leader did she find a brief respite, but even that did not last. To survive, she picked up an iron hammer, hammering and shaping, always fearing that one day she might lose her usefulness, even unable to find a place in Kongtong. Only you would unconditionally choose her, encourage her, and select her as the first master's wife despite no one else believing in her. To Xiaozhu, you are the Sect Leader and her true home. If you were to tell her you didn't need her, the rest of her life would hold no meaning. Fortunately, she is easy to please; as long as you tell her the lies you tell for her sake, she will believe them wholeheartedly. With you by her side all the way, she would find comfort in the long, lonely years ahead.

Suddenly a disciple came to report that someone was being carried up the mountain in a sedan chair — at first it seemed a sudden strike by the Wulin Alliance, but it turned out to be the Kongtong Guardians. The chair had been built unusually sturdy, and when Xiaozhu stepped down from it, you were filled with surprise and joy. Upon asking, you learned that a great deal had happened since you last parted — a major crisis had struck Kongtong, which was why they could not rush to the Tang Clan's aid in time. Sect Leader Wei had sensed the impending danger, discerning the Western Xia's conspiracy to borrow a path from Jin and collaborate with the Supreme Bliss Cult to seize control of Western Shu, and so had to act decisively, leading Danxiazi and the Kongtong disciples to join forces with the region's auxiliary troops to resist the Western Xia army. Urgent dispatches had indeed been sent through the official post over eight hundred miles, but the enemy was always one step ahead: the Supreme Bliss Cult had been lurking in Western Shu for years, infiltrating every prefecture, and every message sent had vanished without a trace. It was only through the daring efforts of a Flying Heaven Disciple skilled in Qinggong, who braved the journey along the Song-Jin border to slip past enemy eyes, that word finally reached the Central Plains. But the narrow-minded Wulin Alliance took it only for a delaying trick, as though Kongtong had fabricated the intelligence.

Xiaomei and you have only been a name without substance so far. Once you die, she still has a long life ahead, and there's no need for her to stay with you. Yet she is obsessed with you to the point of being pathological; for so long, she has managed to act like a normal person and speak to you properly, already making a full effort. After all, you are going to die today, so she no longer needs to pretend to be a proper, upright person. Remarkable words indeed—while alive, you could not possess her body, but once you die, your remains should belong to her. Then, they will be cremated into ashes, brewed into tea, and drunk, merging into one, achieving eternal union.

Upon seeing Xiaomei, they were filled with surprise and joy. After inquiring, they learned that time had passed since their last meeting, and a major incident had occurred in Kongtong, preventing them from rushing to the Tang Clan for support. Sect Leader Wei had sensed the impending danger, discerning the Western Xia's conspiracy to borrow a path from Jin and collaborate with the Supreme Bliss Cult to seize control of Western Shu. He therefore had to act decisively, leading Danxiazi and the Kongtong disciples to join forces with the region's auxiliary troops to resist the Western Xia army. Urgent dispatches had indeed been sent through the official post over eight hundred miles, but the enemy was always one step ahead: the Supreme Bliss Cult had been lurking in Western Shu for years, infiltrating every prefecture, and every message sent had vanished without a trace. It was Xiaomei, bearing the honored title of the Sect Leader's wife, who volunteered against the objections of the others, braving great danger to use her Qinggong along the Song-Jin border and slip past enemy eyes to reach the Central Plains. But the Wulin Alliance, seeing her arrive alone without going through official channels, took it only for a delaying trick, as though Kongtong had fabricated the intelligence.

In the middle of the conversation, a strange whirlwind suddenly swept in low across the ground. You flipped backward and subdued the attacker in one move, nearly crushing Xiaomei's arm in the process.

Even beating you won't ease her anger; to calm her, you must serve her well every day, treat her with utmost care, and complete a hundred days of devotion before she'll reluctantly forgive you. Therefore, you can't treat today as your last day.

Not only did you refuse to admit fault, you tried to act deep and mysterious, playing the dashing, world-weary rogue. Ye Yunshang wasn't fooled, and beat you wildly with the staff again — the blows left you hurting but unharmed; it was her heart that took the wound. She doesn't ask that you cherish her alone for a lifetime, only that you not die, for who else would listen to her grievances and complaints?

She made you bend over, drew a staff from her cloak, and beat you soundly. Serves you right, you ugly wretch, for sweet-talking your way into her heart and then going off to flirt with someone else — even Third Senior Brother says you had it coming.
Knowing you would never return, she stayed obsessed all the same, willing to wager away her best years, boiling her tears into wine as she waited for you.

Ye Yunshang flatly refused to leave, clinging to the pillar of Zhengxin Hall and refusing to let go, until everyone who tried to persuade her had left one by one. Only then did she step out, looking at Third Senior Brother and at you, wanting to burn your faces into her memory.

Your feelings for her remain steadfast and unwavering, while her mind is pure and transparent, never swayed by superficial appearances, gazing directly into your soul with deep trust. She indeed chose the right person, and thus has remained loyal and devoted by your side all along.
It isn't that she has stopped being angry with you—only that there's no more time left for grumbling, so she has forgiven you.
Junior Martial Sister patted you and Third Senior Brother, bestowing a blessing.
For your daily unjust deeds, the Tang Clan has already lost its unity; when great calamity strikes, you scatter like birds and beasts, and dying alone is your destined end.

Most people left, following in Fourth Senior Brother's footsteps, and Third Senior Brother let out a long sigh at the sight. No need for resentment — after all, life's gatherings and partings drift like duckweed on water, and a banquet meant to end will always end. Their road ahead is still long, and perhaps your story can go on, carried forward by word of mouth through them.

Some people have left; they are not untrustworthy, but it is simply a natural part of life. Those who remain regard death as returning home. Though they joined the Tang Clan at different times, none of them fail to regard the Tang Clan as their home and take pride in bearing the surname Tang.

Yet no one budged; every one of them looked on death as but a homecoming, hearts ablaze with boundless valor, fierce and unshaken. The Tang Clan had reached its final road — a family from the very start, and a family to the very end.

You survived the chaos, barely keeping your life, yet couldn't hold onto their hearts. Once they realized that they weren't the only one you cared about, the radiant memories etched in their hearts began to lose their luster.

You were beaten so badly you were smoking, collapsed, barely alive, and the culprit walked away. Hearing of this tragedy, the fellow disciples came out, saw you still had a breath left, and hastily bandaged and gave you first aid. They fed you some harmful, quick‑acting tonics that would damage your body, just enough to let you barely move the next day to be cut. You were left with only this remaining usefulness.

There's no such thing as a wall that doesn't let the wind through; you toyed with the feelings of the girls, and the secret finally came to light. Alas, pitifully, the Wulin Alliance will attack the mountain tomorrow, yet you will die today.

Fourth Senior Brother was not surprised at all and looked at you with a sympathetic gaze. He had anticipated this day would come. The Kongtong Four Maidens had been raised by the clan to become future wives of the clan leader, marrying the Sect Leader to solidify Kongtong's position. You accidentally became the clan leader, and while you were still of some use, now that you insist on staying in the Tang Clan to meet your end, why would they be willing to accompany you in your demise? Naturally, they would find an excuse to slip away, hide, and wait for your death to marry the new clan leader.
You are deeply worried, secretly regretting not having sent Xiaoju to intercept, resulting in her having no word.
You are deeply worried, not knowing how the important matter Xiaozhu spoke of has turned out — why has she still not come home?
You're anxious, not knowing where that scoundrel Xiaomei has wandered off to — still out gallivanting instead of coming home.
As for the Kongtong Sect, they had even sent messages halfway through the journey, but when they reached Shu, they instead vanished without a trace.

Flying Stone Gang Leader Shi Gongyuan has reunited with his beloved wife, and feels deep gratitude toward Eldest Senior Brother and the Tang Clan. The gang's brothers care nothing for right or wrong, only for loyalty — since the Gang Leader has spoken, there's nothing more to say: they'll stand by the Tang Clan to the end.

The Emei Sect leader decided to support the current situation, mobilizing the entire sect's strength to assist. Xie Wuchen was dispatched to block Diancang's route, while Sect Leader Xiang personally visited the Tang Clan to inform the guest disciple of their whereabouts before departing gracefully to persuade old allies.
Sect Leader Zou of the Qingcheng Sect led the sect's elite to Meishan Town to check in, ready for a grand and spectacular showdown.

Li Fugui's scheme succeeded. Taking advantage of the internal strife between the new and old factions of the Beggar Sect, he severed the retreat path for the new sect disciples. Seizing the opportunity, he established his own sect to support the Tang Clan. Leading the sect members to occupy the eastern, southern, western, and northern official roads, he constantly monitored the Wulin Alliance's movements. Meanwhile, he did not forget to send messengers to inform you that their Beggar Sect would surely honor their agreement to convene.
You've always wanted to slip out and poison them, but Third Senior Brother never lets you.

There are countless enemies, yet Fourth Senior Brother was grinning. You all thought this person had been scared out of his mind, but in fact, he had adopted Shangguan Ying's suggestion, purchasing all the old inns and empty houses in the surrounding ten‑mile villages. These wandering martial artists, traveling thousands of miles to stir up trouble, now have a place to stay. If they don't want to sleep in the wilderness, they'll have to pay to support the enemy, blissfully unaware.
You all stared at each other in stunned silence, all hopes extinguished, having toiled and struggled, yet ultimately faced this day.

The Wulin Alliance has arrived from the east. Though it has not yet dared to encroach on Tang Clan territory, it has ringed Meishan Town on every side, at most half a day's march away, waiting only for the Tang Clan's rebellion to be confirmed — once the Wulin Alliance leader gives the word, they will storm the Tang Family compound to demand a reckoning.
The Tang Clan's Junior Brother in charge of intelligence returned, his face etched with worry — for all everyone's exhausting efforts, they had failed in the end to win the other sects over.

Footsteps approached from the east; the Wulin Alliance came bearing wind and rain. Tonight, as the dying sun sank away, the eve of the decisive battle lay strangely still—all that could be done was done, and victory or defeat now rested with tomorrow.

It is said that Kongtong will arrive in Shu territory soon. Xiao Ju proactively requested permission to go to Zhaohua to confer and adjust troop deployments, ensuring the withdrawal route, and preventing the Wulin Alliance from encircling from the north.

The matter has not yet ended. Wei Ju intended to use this opportunity to resign as Sect Leader, but she was too capable; if she left Kongtong, who would take her place? The three Sect Leaders, who had always been at odds, surprisingly united and spoke in unison to persuade her to stay. With no other option, Sect Leader Wei could only retreat and request a leave of absence to go out and clear her mind. The three did not suspect anything, but unbeknownst to them, Sect Leader Wei descended the mountain and directly went to the Tang Clan, a hotbed of conflict. She was visiting a friend and also to demonstrate her resolve, offering herself as collateral to ensure that Kongtong would not break its promise.

Fourth Senior Brother returned from Kongtong, his face marked by the passage of time, and he seemed to have lost some weight. The position of the Kongtong sect leader had been vacant for too long, and the four factions had been engaged in both open and covert struggles for years. The conflicts finally surfaced, and the Soul-Stealing sect leader seized the opportunity, aiming to replace the Flying Heaven Gate and become the face of the Kongtong Clan. Unfortunately, Fourth Senior Brother found himself caught in the crossfire, nearly losing his life. However, the Soul-Stealing sect leader viewed the Fire Dragon Immortal Monarch as a thorn in their side but underestimated Sect Leader Wei of Mystic Skill. She was the truly respected and beloved figure, unyielding to threats, and instead stirred public sentiment against the Soul-Stealing leader, who found themselves in a difficult position and had to smile and submit. After the commotion caused by the Soul-Stealing sect, each sect leader reflected deeply, aware of the precariousness of their situation, and finally listened to Fourth Senior Brother's words, deciding to mobilize southward to assist the Tang Clan.

Meanwhile the renowned senior disciple of Flying Heaven Gate, Danxiazi, was gravely wounded while battling the Soul-Stealing Sect Leader in the Flying Heaven Hall—struck down from behind by his own master, the Fire Dragon Immortal Monarch. You and Third Senior Brother were both enraged to hear of it. The General of Dao Techniques was not only a Kongtong disciple but a light of the Jianghu who had guarded Xiangyang for years in service of hearth and country; whatever grudge the Fire Dragon Immortal Monarch bore his own disciple, how could he bring himself to strike him down?
Yet Danxiazi's fate proved too hard to break: after years of rolling through battlefields, cheating death more than ten times over, and bearing scars beyond counting, he had always pulled through, and this time was no different. While Fourth Senior Brother was fleeing by carriage, Danxiazi hid beneath it, then swung himself inside once they had gone some distance, nearly frightening Fourth Senior Brother out of his wits.
After treatment, he was finally out of danger. Though Kongtong would not ally with the Tang Clan, Danxiazi asked to serve as a guest general to repay the debt, meaning to strike back at Kongtong once this great matter was settled—to cleave the Forgetting-Dust Stone with an axe and free the Mystic Skill disciples, as both vengeance and repayment.
You feel a deep sense of bitterness, thinking that Shangguan Ying, upon hearing this terrible news, would be heartbroken beyond measure.
You have a fondness for Sect Leader Wei; upon hearing this bad news, you couldn't help but stagger slightly, almost fainting.

Fourth Senior Brother returned from Kongtong looking weathered, his frame thinner than before. The seat of Kongtong's overall sect leader had stood vacant far too long, and after years of the four branches feuding in the open and in the shadows, the conflict had finally broken into the open: the Soul-Stealing Sect Leader seized on the pretext to try to supplant the Flying Heaven Gate and make it the new face of Kongtong. Fourth Senior Brother, luckless as ever, had arrived just in time to be caught in the crossfire and very nearly lost his life. All he could do was watch as Sect Leader Wei led her disciples into retreat within the Mystic Skill Secret Realm, lowering the Forgetting-Dust Stone to seal the Mystic Skill Cave—vowing to die before submitting to the Soul-Stealing Gate's tyranny. When their provisions ran out, they meant to perish together as one, to rot alongside Kongtong's secret treasures within the cave.

The Junior Brother on duty at the Guest Hall came running to you with an apologetic face, having shot a dove with a hidden weapon out of boredom. Upon realizing the dove's leg was tied with a Message Token, he realized he had caused trouble. The letter came from your Lady Zhu, stating she had fulfilled her mission. The Kongtong sect obeys her orders as the sect's madam, and they will soon mobilize southward to join the Tang Clan. After reading the letter, you felt relieved but couldn't help but chuckle. The handwriting was just as messy as before, unmistakably hers, but the sentences were unusually obscure‑far beyond Xiaozhu's usual capability. It was clear someone had been guiding her. It was all trivial, but it was frustrating that she hadn't returned to reunite yet, causing endless worry.

Fire Lightning the White Crane returned to you bearing Xiaomei's message token. The note said, in brief, that the Kongtong Sect would soon mobilize south to join forces with the Tang Clan; the rest was only her usual teasing chatter. The matter had gone smoothly enough, yet for some reason she did not come back to the Tang Clan herself.
She also bestowed upon you a marvelous skill, a further token of her gratitude.

You knew who she truly was—how could you let your guard down? The Painting Immortal scorned you as a mere commoner, yet consider: had she wished your Tang Clan ill, she would hardly have bothered coming to suffer alongside you. She had only to stand aside and watch, and the Wulin Alliance would have finished you off on its own. You found yourself speechless, utterly unable to argue the point.

Tang Xian'er waved her hand to lead you into the desolate forest, only then resuming her usual tone of speech, though her manner remained unyielding. Since parting at Fengyu Mountain, she now had the chance to thank you on behalf of Jinxiang Palace for your kindness. She knew you were full of doubts, yet seemed to have a deeper intention and chose not to explain, intending to reveal everything when the time was right. For now, she only needed you to trust her as a friend, not an enemy.

As you and Third Senior Brother were lamenting, Second Senior Brother was persistently bothering you. Suddenly, Senior Sister Tang Xian'er, who had been missing since the internal conflict within the Tang Clan, returned. True to form, she looked down on you and scolded you harshly, but brought unexpected good news. She said that Jinxiang Palace had heard about the Tang Clan's intention to establish the Western Wulin Alliance and was considering moving east. With this, they would no longer leave and would become neighbors from now on.   Third Senior Brother was overjoyed and immediately became energetic, muttering that they must reciprocate kindness and not be negligent, and went off to arrange the reception. You took a few more glances, and after being scolded by Tang Xian'er until you felt thoroughly humiliated, you had to admit that you actually missed it a bit.

Among the smaller sects, plenty chafed under the Wulin Alliance. The scene on Fengyu Mountain was still vivid in every mind: Shi Ming had only to speak a single Buddhist verse and point, and whomever he named was struck down. Jinxiang Palace, once famed far and wide for its good name, was branded a demon cult overnight—old ties and old debts of gratitude counted for nothing; nothing short of its ruin would do.
Who could say which sect or gang would be next? The Mud Cult was said to menace the peace of the Wulin, but the Alliance had grown just as fearsome. Whether you stood for right or wrong was no longer yours to decide—it hung on the Alliance's whim. That the Jianghu had come to this was nothing short of shameful.
Now that the Tang Clan had risen in defiance, calling wandering heroes from every quarter to found the Western Wulin Alliance against the power in the east, it seemed to them nothing less than a ray of dawn.
In days past, the Tang Clan had stood for aloofness, defiance, and an unbending spirit—neither wholly black nor white, answering to no one, never courting a faction, rising only when the realm fell into true chaos: sheltering refugees and raising the Outer Fort against Emperor Xuanzong in the Tang dynasty, delivering the people from ruin; and twenty years past, joining hands with Songshan to break the vanguard of the Supreme Bliss Cult, when the Sect Leader himself struck down the notorious Right Envoy of the Supreme Bliss Cult with his own palm.
Now a scholar-hero had raised the banner of righteous revolt against tyranny—a moment fit to be written into the unofficial chronicles of the Jianghu. Not only did the sects and gangs of Shu answer the call at once, but word reaching even distant lands stirred people to send letters declaring themselves, vowing to stand with the Western Wulin Alliance, shoulder to shoulder against a common foe, on the day of the final battle.

Among the smaller sects in the Wulin, there are many who are dissatisfied with the Wulin Alliance. However, due to their weakness and lack of power, to ensure safety, they dare not reveal their stance too early and publicly oppose the Wulin Alliance. Although they treat your envoys with hospitality, they remain hesitant, unable to give a clear answer for half a day. They go in circles, essentially wanting to say they can help, but only after other major sects and factions arrive.

Yet for survival, most of the smaller sects still chose to fall in with the stronger side. Certain the Tang Clan was doomed to lose, they avoided you like the plague—when they were not stalling, they turned on you outright. One should remember that in the old Sect Leader's heyday, Tang Clan disciples had thrown their weight around plenty, yet never so much as touched a hair on a commoner's head, while their manner toward fellow Wulin folk had been proud indeed. These same people, once unable to curry favor with the Tang Clan, now that it stood in mortal danger, all rushed to trample it and make their allegiance plain—better not to wait until the Tang Clan fell before surrendering to the Wulin Alliance, lest by then there be no favor left to curry there either.
The disciples sent as envoys to sects and gangs great and small began returning one after another.

From the moment you sent Fourth Senior Brother out, you had all but won over every minor sect in Shu—never mind the great factions for now. In his years of business, Fourth Senior Brother had lost no time cultivating these smaller sects; who was greedy, who craved fame, who could not resist a pretty face—he knew it all, and played to each weakness with equal parts flattery and threat. Whatever the Tang Clan's reputation, it made no difference: before they knew it, he had talked them into signing the oath of allegiance. Once aboard that pirate ship, there was no getting off.
Not only the three elders of Qingcheng, but even Yichen Shentu Long, who had never once emerged from seclusion, broke his own precedent to come lend the Western Wulin his aid.

Tang Fang bore the task of winning over Qingcheng, and when she arrived at the foot of the mountain to present her letter of introduction, she found Sect Leader Zou there, sighing heavily. He had been sunk in gloom ever since the tragedy of the Wulin Assembly, justice left unanswered, and was even considering retiring from the Jianghu altogether — he meant only to brush her off. But Tang Fang, young as she was, refused to play by the rules: having promised to call on him, she dared to arrive late, leaving Qingcheng's Three Elders to sit waiting in the Laojun Pavilion. They sent disciples again and again to fetch her, yet still she did not come. Even these Daoists, so disciplined in body and mind, could not hold back their anger. At last the Three Elders went down the mountain themselves to find her, all the courteous words they had prepared now useless — they meant only to give her a scolding and send her off. But Tang Fang, as it turned out, was easy enough to find: the townsfolk of Qingcheng Mountain Town had gathered around her, laughter and cheer on every side, young and old alike praising her skilled hands and compassionate heart for healing the sick. It turned out Tang Fang had once kept a clinic here, and had stopped along the way to follow up with her old patients — that was what had delayed her. Seeing this, the Three Elders' anger melted away entirely; they stroked their beards and smiled, and let the matter of her tardiness go. Tang Fang then told Sect Leader Zou the whole story, and his blood ran hot at the hearing of it, as though he had grown ten years younger, and he agreed on the spot. Better to die for justice than keep company with devils; better to walk the rough road of a true hero than serve at the feet of the powerful. Only this could honor the vow he and his Junior Brother Zhao Kui had sworn in their youth.

Ever since the Wulin Assembly on Fengyu Mountain, Sect Leader Zou had been sunk in gloom day after day, all because of that tragedy — justice left unanswered, a wound that would not heal. He said nothing of it to his disciples, but privately he thought that while the Mud Cult was surely evil, the Wulin Alliance might not be wholly just and impartial either. He longed to root out evil and defend the true Way, yet would not let himself be used by men with their own designs. And how could he not know there was injustice in it? He wanted to step forward and speak a fair word, yet felt he stood alone. Even the well-connected Alliance Leader Nangong could not talk the heroes into peace with words alone. People fear what they do not understand, and in seeking to protect themselves, that fear curdles into anger; anger misplaced becomes malice, and malice in the end spills innocent blood. In all his years as a Daoist priest he had never once seen a demon — but if there truly were harmful spirits in this world, he suspected they most likely lodged in the human heart. Just as he was on the verge of handing off the sect leader's mantle to someone else, to give himself over to quiet cultivation rather than mingle with the worldly matters of the Jianghu, they came to him with word of the Western Wulin Alliance. Sect Leader Zou fell silent for a long while, then went inside to cast a divination before he made up his mind for good: before he retired from the world, he would be young once more, and stand with the Tang Clan through thick and thin. Better to die for justice than keep company with devils; better to walk the rough road of a true hero than serve at the feet of the powerful. Only this could honor the vow he and his Junior Brother Zhao Kui had sworn in their youth.

The Tang Clan disciples sent to Qingcheng returned with an answer both laughable and infuriating. After the battle at Fengyu Mountain claimed Alliance Leader Nangong's life, Sect Leader Zou had grown disheartened and no longer wished to involve himself in the Wulin's disputes. He would lend no strength to the Western Wulin Alliance, and turned away its envoys too, using seclusion for recovery as his excuse. At first it looked as though he meant to help neither side, yet he made no move to stop his own disciples from going down the mountain to act on their own judgment.
The Tang Clan Junior Brothers sent to Qingcheng have returned. Unfortunately, the Qingcheng sect holds deep-seated prejudice against you and has refused the request for an alliance.

When Fourth Senior Brother visited Qingcheng, Sect Leader Zou was deep in sighs, still haunted by the tragedy of the Wulin Assembly, where justice had gone unanswered — a grief that would not ease. He had said nothing of it to his disciples, but privately he suspected that though the Mud Cult was surely evil, the Wulin Alliance might not be entirely just and impartial either. He longed to root out evil and defend the true Way, yet refused to be a pawn for men with their own agendas. And how could he not know there was injustice in it? He wanted to step forward and speak plainly for what was right, but felt he stood alone — even the well-connected Alliance Leader Nangong could not talk the heroes of the Wulin into peace with words alone. People fear what they do not understand, and in seeking to protect themselves, that fear curdles into anger; anger misplaced becomes malice, and malice in the end spills innocent blood. In all his years as a Daoist priest he had never once laid eyes on a demon — but if there truly were evil spirits in this world, he suspected they most likely lodged in the human heart. Just as he was on the verge of handing off the sect leader's mantle to someone else, to give himself over to quiet cultivation rather than mingle with the worldly matters of the Jianghu, Fourth Senior Brother arrived and spoke to him of the Western Wulin Alliance. Sect Leader Zou's blood ran hot at the news, as though he had grown ten years younger, and he agreed on the spot. As it happened, an envoy from the Wulin Alliance arrived just then to throw his weight around, and Sect Leader Zou threw him out the door in anger as well. Better to die for justice than keep company with devils; better to walk the rough road of a true hero than serve at the feet of the powerful. Only this could honor the vow he and his Junior Brother Zhao Kui had sworn in their youth.

Fourth Senior Brother returned from his mission to Qingcheng, but even his age-old friendship with Sect Leader Zou could not bring back good news. After the battle at Fengyu Mountain claimed Alliance Leader Nangong's life, Sect Leader Zou had grown disheartened and no longer wished to involve himself in the disputes of the Wulin. He would lend no strength to the Western Wulin Alliance, and turned away the Alliance's envoys too, citing seclusion for his recovery as an excuse. On the surface it looked as though he meant to side with neither, yet he made no move to stop his own disciples from going down the mountain to act on their own judgment.

Still meaning to deliver some grand parting words, he suddenly saw a flash of blue before his eyes — Xiahou Lan appeared, cold-faced, and hauled him away. Xie Wuchen, his life very much on the line, was sternly forbidden from tainting you with his and Tang Buyi's way of dealing with the world. She had only just found someone to love, and life had finally offered her a sliver of hope — she had no wish to see you die too young from recklessness.

No sooner were the words out than Xie Wuchen dropped down into the center of the Training Ground. Xiang Wuyou had decided to side with neither, but Xie Wuchen was in no mood to listen — defying the Sect Leader's orders was something he and your Eldest Senior Brother had done plenty of times before. Like rivals competing to see who could give their own Sect Leader more trouble, this would be no exception.

Third Senior Brother's reputation may not ring as loud as the Eldest Senior Brother's, but since he holds the sect's leadership in all but name, most who spoke of him — the 'Scholar Hero' Tang Sheng — spoke with praise. Sect Leader Xiang held lofty standards and never mixed with commoners, yet he admired men of high virtue and moral purpose above all else, longing to befriend them. The moment Third Senior Brother crossed into Emei's territory, Emei disciples were already waiting to receive him at the market below the mountain, and Sect Leader Xiang himself came out to greet him partway up the slope. Though one studied Confucianism and the other Buddhism, the two found common ground, and after a long conversation, much of his prejudice against the Tang Clan crumbled away. Yet Xiang Wuyou, as head of his own sect, could not let his personal likings drag all of Emei into another's quarrel. And so he decided to stand aside and help neither side. Third Senior Brother's journey may not have won Emei's support, but it was far from wasted — with Emei declining to answer the Wulin Alliance's call, the plan to encircle the Tang Clan would be that much harder to carry out. Its significance was no small thing.

Martial arts secrets are kept close by everyone, and it is no different among the sects — they guard fiercely against theft of their techniques, and even a master teaching a disciple will often hold something back. At any other time, you might not have been willing to share yours either, but for the sect's sake, you hesitate only a moment before pouring out a lifetime of insight. That day on the back mountain, you received a boon from a masked senior, and now you pass it on to another. Tang Shan listens with tears welling in his eyes, his whole body trembling, wanting to kneel and kowtow to you, but you stop him. He repays the kindness in kind, sharing with you a rare fortune of his own — the divine technique won from Emei's Sword Prison, Heart Sword · Thunder God Kick. He has yet to master it himself, but you might have the fortune to succeed where he could not, and wield it to defend the Tang Clan. The two of you share a smile — only now do you truly set your old grievances aside.

The essence of martial arts is originally kept secret by each individual; not to mention the fact that each sect strictly prevents others from stealing their techniques, even when a master teaches a disciple, it's common for the master to hide a few moves. It's wise to be cautious of others. You're not being unscrupulous by hesitating and being evasive. He doesn't blame you, but he sighs deeply and leaves.

Back in the Tang Clan's civil war, you two once fought. Though your skill today far surpasses what it once was, he too had refused to stand still — reflecting bitterly on that old defeat, he trained all the harder, and after being battered by Tang Jiaojiao for so long, his own skill leapt forward. Still, it was not enough. After a fierce clash, he lost to you again, but this time something in the way you moved seemed to open his eyes, and he accepted defeat with an easy, untroubled look. Through his own wit he had glimpsed, however dimly, the surface of a deeper truth in martial learning — that its ultimate essence is to have no fixed technique at all, a truth embodied, in this world, by you. At any other time he would never have dared ask you outright, but with the Tang Clan facing a great calamity, he set his pride aside and humbly sought your guidance.

Back in the Tang Clan's civil war, you two once crossed blows. Now your skill has grown far beyond what it once was — and he has hardly stood still either; having reflected bitterly on his defeat, he trained all the harder, and after being battered by Tang Jiaojiao for so long, his own skill leapt forward. After a fierce clash, you actually lost. Only then did he reveal his true purpose: he feared that running yourself ragged for the sect's sake would leave your martial arts to wither, and that as the pillar of the Tang Clan now, you had to stand as an unbeatable master to steady your junior brothers' and sisters' confidence. So he had taken it upon himself to shoulder your extra burdens, pushing you to train harder. You accepted his good intentions, though they left you with mixed feelings.
Tang Shan invites you to the back mountain. Along the way, you feel uneasy, thinking he had something important to say about Tang Jiaojiao. Unexpectedly, he challenges you instead.

In the end, Tang Jiaojiao was punished for assaulting the Sect Leader by being confined to meditate in Emei Sword Prison. In exchange, the Emei Sect will stand with the Tang Clan, serving as a barrier to block Diancang's northern advance on the day the Wulin Alliance comes from the east to wage war.

In the end, Tang Jiaojiao was punished for striking the Sect Leader and sentenced to face the wall in contemplation in Emei's Sword Prison. As the price for it, Sect Leader Xiang gave up his plan to answer the Wulin Alliance's call and join the siege on the Tang Clan — his injuries, after all, had been no small thing. He decided Emei would side with neither.

No matter how hard Tang Shan racked his brains, he found no chance to see him. Just then, Tang Jiaojiao, who had been traveling with him, suddenly struck out, flattening a greeting disciple's face with one punch and forcing her way up the mountain. Tang Shan panicked, but could not simply abandon her, so he followed, fighting alongside her all the way to before Emei's main hall. He could not stop her from lashing out at everyone in her path, and had no idea what standing she once held at Emei — the Emei disciples who saw her all looked afraid, and even Sect Leader Xiang, in her presence, dropped his usual sect-leader air. Xie Wuchen even shoved someone else forward in his place and fled far out of sight. Yet Tang Jiaojiao showed no gratitude for it. Having finally gotten an audience with Sect Leader Xiang, she gave him no chance to speak, raining punches down on Xiang Wuyou instead. Tang Shan was frightened out of his wits, certain that day would be his last.

No matter how Tang Shan racked his brains for a way in, he found no chance to meet him. Just then, the sound of a temple bell rang out from the mountain, and the Emei disciples chanted the Buddha's name as one. Something in him suddenly stirred; he stopped thinking of anything at all and simply sat down cross-legged at the mountain gate. He knew the past could not be undone, and it was not that he felt no shame for it — only that he dared not kneel, for fear of disgracing his sect's dignity. Yet though he would not kneel, there were other ways to show sincerity. So he began to neither eat nor drink, neither sleep nor rest, but recite the sutras he knew by heart, over and over, day and night without pause, until at last his strength gave out and he collapsed. When he woke, he was already on Mount Emei. Moved by his sincerity, Sect Leader Xiang at last received him, and after hearing him recount the whole affair, came to see it from another side — most of his hostility toward the Tang Clan melted away. Yet though it grieved him to see fellow wulin brethren turn on each other, against the wishes of the late Great Hero Nangong, he was unwilling to openly break with the Wulin Alliance and drag the Emei disciples into the fire for the sake of his own convictions. And so he decided to side with neither.

Tang Shan went to Emei as an envoy but was turned away at the mountain gate, never even getting the chance to meet Sect Leader Xiang. This was all because Shi Ming had struck first, viciously turning Sect Leader Xiang against the Tang Clan with slander, fabricating ties between the Tang Clan's misdeeds and the Mud Cult, and twisting their good deeds into false benevolence. He was the aged abbot of the Fujian Branch of Songshan, who had given up a life of ease to travel and preach the Dharma far and wide. He had lodged at Emei more than once to hold sermons, and the whole of Emei revered his deep learning in the Buddhist scriptures — how could a great master's words ever be wrong? Tang Shan, by contrast, stood accused of betraying his master and forefathers, forsaking the light for darkness, and willingly wallowing in the Tang Clan's corruption — evil beyond forgiveness. Sect Leader Xiang, who held himself above such things, would not even deign to look at him.

You are filling in for Third Senior Brother, temporarily taking on the duties, and it truly is a burden beyond words. You might think that becoming Sect Leader means you can sit back and do nothing, but unexpectedly, every day brings difficult problems to your doorstep. One moment you need to keep accounts, the next you have to handle correspondence with the leaders of various factions, then there are debts to worry about, issues with the Tang Clan's properties, requests from the alchemy room for support in gathering herbs, and requests for funds due to insufficient expenses. Then there's the matter of running out of essential supplies, a fire at the forge, a collapsed plank road, rain causing landslides, cracked floor tiles, citizens seeking compensation from the Tang Clan for taking counterfeit medicine, junior disciples coming to ask about martial arts, disputes among fellow disciples needing your arbitration, and even junior disciples wanting to marry each other. After finishing your own tasks each day, you are still burdened with so many trivial matters, leaving you utterly at a loss. When you hear the announcement that Third Senior Brother is back, you hurriedly drop what you are doing to welcome him, never having looked forward to seeing him so much, just to hand the work back to him.

Fu Yun returned from his mission to Emei, bringing good news: he had won over Sect Leader Xiang. Emei is willing to stand together with the Tang Clan, and on the day the Wulin Alliance musters its forces, Emei will step forward to take responsibility for blocking Diancang's road north.

So the old faction of the Beggar Sect got their wish, driving the new faction's main strength out of the sect. The Dayi Branch was no more, and in its place the Tang Clan suddenly found itself with a great many disciples from outside the family.

Shangguan Ying stepped in herself, and with a little clever talk spun the story so the beggars were said to have been specially hired to guard Lu Weng's estate. Only then did he brighten, his resentment vanishing at once; instead he showered them with thanks and treated them to fine wine and meat. The beggars, flattered and their pride well fed, all thumped their chests and swore to keep Lu Weng's whole household safe. It made for an outcome that left everyone happy.

The Outer Fort had indeed been built by the Tang Clan's ancestors, but it was also the Tang Clan's ancestors who, lacking virtue, squandered the family fortune and sold it off. The land deed is now held by Lu Yuanwai, a creditor of the Tang Clan, who leases it to the locals. When Fourth Senior Brother suddenly brought a crowd of beggars there, Lu Yuanwai was so furious he nearly burst a lung, yet he feared the beggars might not be as reasonable as the Tang Clan — once you're a beggar, what won't you do? Push them too far and it would be no surprise if they burned your house down. As the saying goes, the wise man knows when to yield, so he had no choice but to swallow his anger in silence.

The Beggar Sect might lack other strengths, but its greatest one is numbers — the Dayi Branch alone was easily as many people as the whole Tang Clan. Fourth Senior Brother settled them at the Outer Fort; when the empty houses ran short it hardly troubled these beggars — they threw up tents around the Outer Fort on the spot, and in no time at all a new Dayi Branch stood ready.

The Beggar Sect might lack other strengths, but its greatest one is numbers — the Dayi Branch alone was easily as many people as the whole Tang Clan. Fourth Senior Brother brought them to the Outer Fort and left Ye Yunzhou, who was guarding it, to arrange their food and lodging, then took off without a backward glance, never seeing the wronged look on his face.

Fourth Senior Brother returned from his mission to the Beggar Sect's Dayi Branch, his face still shadowed with lingering fear. It turned out the Dayi Branch's new leader was a spy sent by the Beggar Sect's elders to keep watch over the branch, so that at the first excuse he could raise the banner of purging traitors and wipe out the new faction. Fortunately, the man was too rash for his own good: ever since he'd arrived at the Dayi Branch, the beggars there had always been cold toward him as their leader, while they welcomed Fourth Senior Brother, an outsider, as warmly as a brother — drinking, feasting, slinging arms over shoulders. This filled the spy with rage; he lashed out with mocking words, and in his fury let his secret slip, exposing himself on the spot. This left the Dayi Branch with no way back — whether they wished to rebel or not, rebel they now must. Fourth Senior Brother did not even need to persuade them before they came flocking to join the Tang Clan.

The new leader of the Dayi Branch was actually a spy sent by the Beggar Sect's elders to keep watch over it, so that at the first excuse he could raise the banner of purging traitors and wipe out the new faction. The Daren Branch, lying in ambush nearby, stormed into the temple and scattered lime powder, catching the Dayi Branch's beggars completely off guard. The old-guard beggars showed no mercy at all, swinging their staves straight at their own brothers' skulls, meaning to kill. Had Fourth Senior Brother not quick-wittedly reported it to the authorities and thrown the plot into chaos, scarcely a single friend of the Dayi Branch would have survived. After that, the Dayi Branch beggars lost heart — all talk of chivalry, they now knew, was a fleeting dream. Once they had walked tall and proud under Gang Leader Wang, beggars with dignity and pride of their own; but once the applause died away, they were left in rags again, unlettered as ever. So they scattered, some west, some south, with no destination in mind, only wanting to put distance between themselves and the Beggar Sect's reach, between themselves and the Jianghu, between themselves and this heartbroken corner of the Song Kingdom.
Taking along Fan Xiaotian, they nearly both perished in the wolf den.
Fourth Senior Brother was sent on a mission to the Beggar Sect's Dayi Branch, but unfortunately returned in disgrace.

The Beggar Sect sent word. Li Fugui took the letter, slapped his thigh, and shouted Good! as he came in to take his leave of you. The scheme he had been planning had succeeded: the old and new factions had split for good, and the new faction was left without a leader, waiting only for him to step forward and restore order. On the day the Western Wulin Alliance's founding assembly convened, the Tang Clan would have a mighty ally.

Xiahou Lan, who had been living in seclusion in the woods, suddenly appeared, conveying to you the one‑word truth for survival amidst the chaos of battle: Escape. Without uttering a word, she launched an attack toward you.
Fan Xiaotian just happened to pass by, saw you all looking like you were about to have a group brawl, and also clenched his fists and wanted to get involved.

Long Xiang came to join the brawl too; the female disciples nearby hastily pulled her aside. They found such rough group fighting distasteful and had no wish to take part themselves, but they had a betting pool going against you — and if Long Xiang joined your side, the fight would surely be one-sided, ruining them completely.

Yunshang was not willing to be left out; though she clearly knew nothing of martial arts, she insisted on joining the battle, causing everyone to exchange glances in confusion. Unbeknownst to them, she was confident, having mastered the qin techniques from Lady Wen, and today was the time to officially unveil them.

Ye Yunzhou values righteousness and was unwilling to reveal the secrets of the Diancang lineage. Yet he saw fit to use the occasion to display it publicly anyway, letting the Tang Clan brothers see for themselves the edge of the Diancang swift sword — so that when the fighting came, they would not crumble at the first blow.

Shangguan Ying had been cooped up for a long time, and the moment she heard the Tang Clan was holding special training for group brawls, she dropped whatever she'd been doing and rushed out, her face lit up with excitement.
Junior Martial Sister volunteered to join you, rarely seen with such determination.

You'd even wish to borrow another sixty years from heaven‑what advice can you give them then? Everything that could be thought of and done has been done. Planning is in human hands, success is in heaven's will. We can only try to leave no regrets.

You are bold to a fault; a mere melee can no longer satisfy your urge to court death, and you boast that you can take on ten at once. Your Junior Martial Brothers and Sisters eagerly sign up for the camp opposing you.

You carry yourself with bold, open-handed generosity, and in a moment of heated impulse, you abuse your standing as Acting Sect Leader, opening the treasury without leave and setting up prize money as stakes. As for Third Senior Brother's scolding, that's a matter for after he gets home.

If one walks the Jianghu without any real skills, then no matter how much they try to embellish their appearance, it is all in vain. Only by striving for self‑improvement and demonstrating determination and pride can one earn the respect of others. For this reason, you decide to embark on special training; even sharpening the spear at the last moment is better than giving up on oneself.
You're the only one we can look to for orders now; who told you to take the Sect Leader's token from Third Senior Brother? Even if only for a day, you must answer for them.

No matter how panicked you get, it's of no help. What's destined to come will come eventually. Those who refuse to run away must prepare for acceptance. Each should go about their own affairs, trying to leave no regrets.

Envoys had already been chosen and sent out to persuade the other sects, and no one imagined this could be kept from the Wulin Alliance's ears. The heroes of the Central Plains were all enraged, and sent word that they would march east on the day the Western Wulin Alliance held its conference — any who answered the Tang Clan's call would be treated as accomplices of the Demon Cult and wiped out without exception. Fellow disciples within the sect were all on edge, fearing that the allied sects would lose heart on hearing this and leave the Tang Clan isolated with no one to help.
You patiently asked him about the hidden truth, and Li Fugui smiled bitterly, realizing that if he didn't speak, you would find it hard to believe his sincerity.

Not only did he not hesitate to speak his mind, but he even cursed him as a bastard—a man so disloyal and unfilial he could kill his own adoptive father. Even if Third Senior Brother could bear it, you could not. Scolded by you, Li Fugui wore a sorrowful, bitter smile. He was the leader of the Beggar Sect, commanding beggars across the land, his standing in the Jianghu lofty; wherever he went, people praised him for putting justice above kin. But was that truly so? Only you, speaking your mind so bluntly, brought him some comfort.

You should have cared first about whether the Beggar Sect could become an aid to the Tang Clan, but seeing his contented look, you could not hold your tongue, and knowing this must be something he kept carefully hidden, you brought up the former Gang Leader Wang Erzhuang all the same.

Li Fugui would descend the mountain every day to hear reports from his trusted followers about the state of the Beggar Sect. Indeed, upon the disappearance of the Gang Leader, the new and old factions of the Beggar Sect immediately began to quarrel. The Daren, Dazhi, Dayi, Daxin, and Dayong Branches split into camps or rose up against each other, eager to overthrow one another. By then, even if the Gang Leader were to appear, the outcome would already be settled, leaving nothing more to say.  This was exactly what he sought. With one faction gaining power, the other must inevitably become a vanquished dog. The most likely vanquished ones would be the new generation disciples of the Beggar Sect. For many of these new disciples were remnants of the Beast Path who had followed Gang Leader Wang in the past and had been oppressed by the old faction since the Great Battle of Jiangling, making it impossible for them to walk among the Jianghu with any face. Although there were many young and strong ones, they did not possess the cunning of the older faction‑men like seasoned foxes full of treachery and hollow virtue‑who had forged alliances across the Central Plains for decades.  Should the Wulin Alliance make a move, it would undoubtedly be disadvantageous for the new disciples, forcing them to reach a dead end sooner or later. At this moment, his reappearance to recruit the new faction's disciples would be like water finding its way through a channel.  Li Fugui spoke in detail before you realized that Gang Leader Wang was not only Li Fugui's adoptive father, but also the very man who had murdered his birth father, the Thousand-Gold Elder.
Fan Xiaotian, who was warming himself by the fire with you, saw your face darken with displeasure and hurriedly distanced himself, abandoning his own Gang Leader as he fled.

Though Li Fugui claims to be a hostage, in reality, he is here to assist the Tang Clan. Despite his doubts, the Third Senior Brother still treats him as a guest, preparing a secluded guest room. However, as the leader of the beggars, Li Fugui couldn't get used to the comforts, and he ended up pitching a tent in the center of your training grounds, even lighting a fire.

She wanted to believe your flowery words, to be deceived into coming to the Tang Clan, only to be treated so coldly by you before even the wedding ceremony. The more she thought about it, the more she felt wronged, and she burst into tears, pushing you away and fleeing. You were also troubled, and compared to the gentle nature of the Junior Martial Sister, her kindness suddenly seemed as precious as true gold. You no longer wanted to bother with Shangguan Ying, after all, she had nowhere to go, and her outburst would eventually have to be resolved by you. But you had underestimated Shangguan Ying. After crying herself to sleep, she made up her mind to leave the mountain alone the next morning. You didn't see her for the whole day and gradually grew anxious, going down the mountain to look for her. Shangguan Ying was angry with you and intentionally avoided you, but you couldn't ignore the Tang Clan. After searching for a long time, you could only return home in disappointment. She waited for you to comfort her just a step away, but as time passed, her heart grew cold. She packed her belongings and set off on her journey alone, deciding never to see you again in this lifetime.
You hadn't the faintest gallantry toward a lady, and you struck your betrothed.

The words were barely out of your mouth before you regretted them, meaning to give way and let her land a few punches to vent her anger. But Shangguan Ying, beside herself with fury, tripped on the hem of her own skirt and fell, scraping the heels of her palms and her knees raw, which only sent her into an even wilder rage.

When it comes to fighting, would you ever admit defeat? Relying on your superior martial arts, you beat your Junior Martial Brothers and Sisters and took their coins by force. Everyone hates you for it, yet none dare say so aloud. Shangguan Ying is at a loss for words at your bandit-like robbery; won't this only worsen both your reputations? Still, since it was all for the sake of her own selfish demand, she cannot bring herself to be too harsh on you. She resolves to wait until she has earned enough coins, then repay them with interest, and see how many hearts she can buy back.

Knowing you were in the wrong, you put up only a token resistance and let your Junior Martial Brothers and Sisters beat you to let off their anger. They struck you, then threw the coins at you as though for a doctor's fee. Shangguan Ying did not expect you to make such a sacrifice; she felt heartache. Seeing your swollen face and bruised appearance, her eyes welled up with tears, and she no longer harbored any resentment. Shangguan Ying had interacted with many of the Jianghu's rough‑and‑tumble folk before, but today she realized that true Great Heroes like you do not necessarily need to win; they are willing to sacrifice themselves for others. Even your shabby appearance could not hide the brilliance of your soul. Thus, she bowed slightly in gratitude for your noble act and felt even more fortunate to be marrying you.

You spoke harshly to Shangguan Ying, berating her. She followed you back to the Tang Clan, believing that you alone would not treat her so roughly. Overwhelmed with grievances and extreme shame and anger, she raised her fist and struck at you.

Your Senior and Junior Brothers listened to your persuasion, exchanged glances, then burst out laughing, all telling you that you were being far too polite. The Tang Clan is everyone's home; those with coins give coins, those with strength give strength—how could there be any objection? Third Senior Brother, hearing of this, was deeply moved and finally agreed to use the sect's assets to make up the shortfall.

Under your persuasion, the Junior Martial Brothers and Sisters reluctantly handed over the coins. Seeing this, Third Senior Brother finally relented and used the sect's assets to cover the shortfall. Shangguan Ying held the coins with a tangle of emotions, hoping only to repay it with interest one day, so that everyone could let bygones be bygones.

You gritted your teeth and went to ask your fellow disciples for coins. As expected, it immediately angered everyone. They still had some regard for Shangguan Ying, the precious daughter, and although they were dissatisfied, they did not dare to be too rude to her. However, it was a different story with you; they all drew their weapons and charged at you!

Shangguan Ying felt lost and disoriented, tears steadily falling as she realized your words were reasonable; she had been too arbitrary in this matter. To you, Cang Gang disciples are enemies, strangers, and expendable. But to her, they were all individuals she remembered by name and face, people who had believed her words and pledged their loyalty to fight for her. She should have cared for and repaid them. It's a pity. If her heart were a bit darker, she wouldn't feel this pain.
They traveled thousands of miles from the East Sea to Shu, and the greatest honor was to let them all die as strangers in a foreign land.

After pondering for a long time, you advised her to give up. The Tang Clan is in dire straits itself; even with good intentions, there's no reason to prioritize others' well‑being over their own. Though those Cang Gang disciples are pitiable for being forced to do things they don't want to in order to support their families, what guilt does the Tang Clan bear?

You suggested raising funds from the Tang Clan brothers and sisters, but Shangguan Ying's face showed hesitation. She was in a very awkward situation. In the past, she had been arrogant and offended others, and now, in her time of need, she was relying on the Tang Clan. The Tang Clan brothers and sisters still harbored lingering grievances. If she went to them for help, they would certainly not be pleased, accusing her of turning her back on them, using the Tang Clan's resources to aid enemies. This was a situation that left everyone in a difficult position. She would have to be humble and apologetic to everyone, which she could not bear.
Her nagging at you is only because she doesn't want you taken advantage of. Deep down, she is glad for your trust in her, and silently resolves not to disappoint your expectations.

Shangguan Ying gave you a punch, to make sure you'd remember the lesson. In the future, whenever you feel like lending your coins to others or standing guarantor for someone, you'd best recall her iron fist today. This is all for your own good — you'd best not be ungrateful; even getting hit, you should be grateful in your heart.

However, you're not a pushover; you just indulge her. If she really runs off with the money, you'll definitely chase her across the country. When you catch up, you'll take away her pants, and see if she can still run away.

You argued tirelessly, laying out every pro and con, and pledged your own name and credit as surety, until Third Senior Brother finally relented and agreed to gamble on you. Shangguan Ying was taken aback on hearing it, feeling both joy and anger. The joy came from the prospect of coins, the anger from your willingness to vouch for her. In her youth she had suffered greatly from just such a thing, having guaranteed for others and nearly being sold herself for it — it was the one thing she feared most in life. Even though you are the man of her heart, you cannot cross this line of hers. That you, ever the soft touch, vouched for her today made it hard to say you wouldn't vouch for some close friend tomorrow, repeating the very mistake of her past.

You've said all you could, but Third Senior Brother cannot disregard the other disciples' feelings merely out of regard for you. Moreover, convening a Wulin Assembly is exactly when every coin must be carefully weighed, so in the end, he coldly refused your request.

You returned to find her still lingering at the cliff's edge, as if oblivious to the danger, and another wave of panic seized you; your tone grew sharper. Shangguan Ying startled at your roar, yet her heart warmed all the same. For as long as she could remember, everyone had made demands of her, asked after her results — apart from her close friend Wei Ju, only you had ever grown angry over her safety. A wave of warmth rose in her heart, and the anger she'd built up waiting for you dissipated at once.

You went to Third Senior Brother to discuss the funding request, laying out the stakes plainly. Shangguan Ying paced back and forth along the plank road, now gazing at the clouds, now at the waterfall. Lovely as the Tang Clan's mountain scenery was, she had no heart to enjoy it; anxious to the core, she blamed you for taking so long, while also resenting herself for once having schemed single-mindedly for the Shangguan family, exhausting the Tang Clan's trust in her. It was truly a fate of her own making, and that they still gave her shelter now was already great magnanimity.

You didn't say a word before pulling out your belongings. Shangguan Ying merely smiled bitterly, thinking to herself that your personal savings would be of little use. But the heavy silver in her hands immediately made her face change. After weighing it, she realized it was at least thirty taels. For commoners and merchants, earning a hundred taels in the morning would be spent by evening on gambling and drinking, enjoying the moment. Once the money ran out, they would face hunger and cold. The daily wage for common workers was no more than a hundred wen. Fish sellers, even poorer, might not even earn a hundred wen a day. Your single gesture of thirty taels was thirty guan, thirty thousand wen, enough for a common person's annual expenses. In the past, Shangguan Ying would have looked down on such wealth. But now, having been cast out of the Shangguan family and penniless, the sudden arrival of this fortune filled her with both shock and joy. She knew how hard it was for you to earn these coins, yet she unhesitatingly accepted them into her hands, her heart suddenly aching. With you by her side, it felt as if thousands of soldiers were at her back, as if everything would inevitably fall into place. Before even taking action, she was certain it would succeed.

The disciples of the Cang Gang practice martial arts to combat the disturbances caused by pirates, but whether they can truly be considered part of the Wulin is hard to say. Many of the gang members were recruited by Shangguan Ying. Although she is the daughter of the Shangguan family and is quite strict with her subordinates, she is also very righteous. To win people's hearts, she has put in a lot of effort; every one of the hundreds of gang members can call out her name, and even their families occasionally show concern. During festivals, they send vegetables and gifts, and in the eyes of the gang members, her status is even higher than that of the gang leader. They believe that following the young lady means they won't have to worry about food and clothing for the rest of their lives, and they are willing to go through fire and water to accompany her, all for the chance to earn a living and settle down.  However, when Shangguan Ying finds herself in a precarious situation, all the promises made in the past turn into empty words that can no longer be fulfilled. Moreover, due to the circumstances surrounding the Shangguan family, she is drawn into the struggles of the Jianghu, and many will inevitably die far from home, with no hope of compensation. How can she not feel ashamed? Therefore, rather than discussing Jianghu ethics with the Cang Gang disciples, it would be more effective to offer them coins to persuade them to leave the Cang Gang. It seems that if they have coins, they can settle down and would not travel thousands of miles from the East Sea to trouble the Tang Clan, which would be a win‑win situation.  However, regarding the Shangguan family's covert attacks on the Tang Clan, Shangguan Ying bears full responsibility. To this day, it is only for your sake that people give her the benefit of the doubt, trusting that she has turned over a new leaf. Yet, the Tang Clan is already poor, and she wants to ask the Acting Sect Leader for funds to earn coins to help her Cang Gang brothers settle down. How can people not be outraged? There seems to be no way out; she can only drag you into her troubles. What she owes is merely a sum sufficient to kickstart her plan, which aims to take advantage of the impending war between the Eastern and Western Wulin alliances.
