In this time of anxiety, she intends to sell a sense of security to the wealthy locals, anticipating that when chaos ensues, those who cannot bear the disturbance will consider relocating. At that time, she plans to use these coins to purchase real estate and sell it at a higher price once the conflict subsides.  Her plan is meticulously crafted to manipulate people's hearts, straddling the line between malice and goodwill. While she does take advantage of others, both buyers and sellers end up happy, so one cannot say she is entirely in the wrong.

Tang Jiaojiao's designs on you have become a laughingstock for everyone over tea and idle chatter. Ye Yunshang, however, finds it far from amusing. She is confident enough in her own looks that she isn't worried about being outshone by Tang Jiaojiao; she is simply afraid the woman might force herself on you, so she must step forward at once to stake her claim. Say that no one loves you, and she will not stand for it.

Tang Jiaojiao lay in ambush on the road, intercepting the Third Senior Brother. She was from the Emei Sect and had long troubled the male disciples of the sect, even earning the respect of Xie Wuchen and Xiang Wuyou, who feared her but had no way to make her comply. This time, as she lured the Emei Sect into cooperation, she was confident and well‑prepared. She intended to threaten Xiang Wuyou, warning that if Emei did not assist, leading to the Tang Clan's downfall, she would return to Emei and see if they would fear her.

With the Sect Leader's Token in hand, you erupted into a terrifying laugh, unabashed about your ambition to benefit personally at the expense of the sect. This scared the Third Senior Brother so much that he hurriedly reclaimed the Sect Leader's Token.
After much deliberation before setting out, he entrusted the Sect Leader's Token into your hands.

It was long said that the Emei Sect's master was a high-minded and righteous soul who disliked idle pleasantries; unless one was learned, courteous, and of unblemished reputation, even Kongtong's mountain gate would turn them away. The Tang Clan's standing in the Jianghu had always been mixed at best, and of them all, only Third Senior Brother met the standard. With no other choice, the Acting Sect Leader would have to go and pay the visit himself.

Little did you know, Tang Jiaojiao actually turned her nose up at you — chin lifted so high her eyes all but vanished — as she draped an arm over Tang Shan's shoulder. Tang Shan's face stiffened, yet he made no move to push her away.

Tang Jiaojiao's designs on you were the talk of every idle meal. Little Junior Sister paid it no mind, even thinking Tang Jiaojiao showed good taste — but when Tang Jiaojiao suddenly spoke up, asking Third Senior Brother to grant her a marriage before the mission was even done, Little Junior Sister was at once displeased.

Tang Jiaojiao's designs on you have long been the talk of every idle meal. How could Shangguan Ying not have heard of it? Now, seeing the woman step forward and speak up, asking Third Senior Brother to grant her a marriage before the mission was even done, Shangguan Ying could not help but grow anxious. She didn't feel she fell short of Tang Jiaojiao in any way, but the fiancé who once swore never to change his heart had already taken notice of a woman of humble birth from the courtesans' quarter. Who could guarantee you wouldn't abandon her and turn instead to Tang Jiaojiao's embrace?

Everyone was about to wave goodbye, but Tang Jiaojiao suddenly appeared, expressing her willingness to travel to Emei together. She was from Emei and had come to the Tang Clan to look for a husband; persuading the Emei sect leader was the perfect fit. However, the Third Senior Brother unconsciously ignored her, delaying his realization.

Tang Shan was eager to achieve merit and redeem his past mistakes, so he sought permission from Third Senior Brother to go to Emei. Though his master, Tang Shouhong, was a traitor from the Tang Clan, the two had done many good deeds in Guangzhou, earning a solid reputation. They had also been invited to Emei's Golden Summit to hear the Emei master lecture on Buddhist teachings, forging some connection with the aloof Emei sect. Moreover, Tang Shan himself was eloquent, so sending him to plead their case seemed no bad plan.

Shentu Long of Qingcheng is a menace to the Wulin. Unfortunately, no one believes your accusations, and rashly sending someone to Qingcheng is indeed too dangerous. Third Senior Brother pondered extensively but could not find a suitable person, so he had to abandon Qingcheng.

You once studied at Kongtong. The mission to send an envoy to Kongtong was none other than you. Unfortunately, Kongtong is too far away. If you go and come back, the Wulin Alliance would have to come knocking. At this critical moment, how could Third Senior Brother let you leave the Tang Clan?

The journey to Kongtong is the farthest and cannot be delayed. Third Senior Brother could not think of an appropriate person, so he sent a senior, experienced disciple from the sect to ride a horse and hasten to Kongtong, attempting to persuade the Four Sect Leaders.

Shangguan Ying and Wei, Gate Leader of Kongtong's Mystic Skill Gate, had been classmates and close friends since girlhood. Though she had to juggle the task of raising funds to win over the Cang Gang and could not get away to go herself, she still found time in her busy schedule to write a letter in her own hand, sent by carrier pigeon to the Kongtong Sect. That thin sheet of paper carried great weight—more useful than if you yourself had gone to call bearing ten thousand taels of gold.

You were just about to consult Xiaoju on how to broach the subject of seeking help from Kongtong, but she had already acted first and reported later, fully utilizing the authority of the First Master's wife to arrange everything. You hadn't even opened your mouth when the carrier pigeon from Kongtong had already finished its feed, carrying Xiaoju's reply and setting out on its way home.

Xiao Zhu always wanted to do something for you so she wouldn't be cast aside, but she could never find the right way. This time she summoned her courage, determined to be of some use no matter what, putting on the airs of the Sect Leader's principal wife to marshal reinforcements by borrowing your prestige.

Since Xiaomei was brought back to the Tang Clan by you, she has been filled with guilt. This time, she finally has a chance to make amends, so she took the initiative to request to return to her family. With her esteemed position as the first lady of the clan, she intends to leverage your influence to mobilize reinforcements from Kongtong.

Fu Yun heard that you had not sent anyone to Emei, so he volunteered to go himself. Emei has many Buddhist followers, and the Golden Summit often holds religious gatherings to discuss Buddhist teachings. While Fu Yun stayed at various monasteries across Shu to preach, he frequently visited Emei, and his relationship with the Emei sect is very friendly. With his intervention, this matter is likely to succeed.

As one of the few senior disciples of the Tang Clan, the Fourth Senior Brother feels immense pressure. He is not unwilling to serve the sect, but the problem is that he possesses too many skills, seemingly useful anywhere, yet he cannot decide where to prioritize them. You happen to arrive just in time, so he decides to place the responsibility of decision‑making on you, while he will handle the execution. If things go wrong, he can always blame you later.

A world apart, in the two hours that passed, you had only made a small gain. Meanwhile, Fourth Senior Brother was thoroughly impressed, praising non‑stop and never imagining he could do business without any goods in hand. Shangguan Ying planned to make use of the looming war between the Eastern and Western Wulin Alliances—and the public panic it stirred—to sell a sense of security to the local wealthy. She also reckoned that amid the chaos of war, people worn down by the upheaval would be more likely to think of uprooting their whole households; she meant to take that money and buy up property, then sell it at a higher price once the fighting settled. Her scheme played on people's hearts at every turn, somewhere between wicked and kind—she did take advantage of people, true, but both buyers and sellers came away satisfied, so you could not call her ill‑intentioned either. The coins Fourth Senior Brother contributed were merely to gain the trust of the wealthy as part of a pretentious display, making it a win‑win situation that delighted him as if he wanted to float away.

Two hours later, you were so drowsy you could barely stay awake, saliva dripping down your chin. Shangguan Ying raised her fist and then lowered it again. Considering how hard you've worked for the Tang Clan and haven't had a good night's sleep, it's clearly an uninteresting topic, yet you've been patient for so long. She would be inconsiderate to hit you again. Though you didn't quite understand, Fourth Senior Brother was highly interested in the plan Shangguan Ying mentioned. He's usually stingy, but this time he broke his usual habit and invested a large sum.
After an hour, you were half‑awake, drowsily sleeping, and were beaten awake by Shangguan Ying, then dragged out and severely beaten.

You entered the Zhengxin Hall, where Shangguan Ying was discussing with her Fourth Senior Brother how to raise funds to bribe the Cang Gang disciples. To know whether the Cang Gang disciples count as Wulin figures, given that they train to fight pirates, is hard to say. Many of the gang members were recruited by Shangguan Ying herself. Though she is a Shangguan noblewoman, she governs her subordinates with strict discipline, yet remains just. To win their loyalty, she has made great efforts, knowing each of the hundreds of gang members by name, even showing concern for their families. During festivals, she sends food and gifts, and in the eyes of the gang members, her status surpasses even the gang leader. They believe that following her will ensure a life free from want, and thus are willing to risk everything, traveling far and wide with her to earn coins for their families. However, once Shangguan Ying herself could no longer protect her own position, all her past promises became empty words, impossible to fulfill. Worse, because of the Shangguan family's doings, her followers would now be dragged into a struggle within the Jianghu, where who knew how many might die far from home with no hope of a pension. How could she not feel ashamed? Therefore, she is determined to make amends. Rather than discussing Jianghu ethics with the Cang Gang disciples, she prefers to offer coins to persuade them to leave. If they have coins, they can settle down, and won't travel thousands of miles from the East Sea to trouble the Tang Clan. It's a win‑win situation. But Shangguan Ying is responsible for the Shangguan family's secret sabotage against the Tang Clan. So far, she has only tolerated her reforming efforts due to your face. The Tang Clan itself is poor, yet she dares to ask the Acting Sect Leader for funds to earn coins for her Cang Gang brothers' families. How could the crowd not be shocked? Fortunately, there is her Fourth Senior Brother, who lights up at the thought of profit. Conversely, he is the most rational, without prejudice, and seeks her advice on business. This Shangguan Ying, eager to secure investment, explains everything in detail, from theory to practical methods. You also listen in, hoping to gain some knowledge.
Third Senior Brother was loath to let you risk your life, but who else could shoulder so weighty a task? After long hesitation, he finally relented and agreed.
But it was stopped by the Third Senior Brother. The Tang Clan no longer has the margin for risk. If you have any mishap in Qingcheng, the strategy of the Western Wulin Alliance will be compromised.
It's not that you're afraid, but rather that you know you can't leave it unchecked.
You knew full well that Qingcheng harbored the Tang Clan's enemy Shentu Long, a peril beyond measure, yet you still petitioned Third Senior Brother for leave to go and persuade them yourself.
Under your advice, Fourth Senior Brother stayed at home contentedly. To express his gratitude, he gave you a sugarcane.
Under your suggestion, Fourth Senior Brother decided to dispatch envoys to the small and medium sects in various parts of Shu.
Under your advice, Fourth Senior Brother decided to send an envoy to the Big Dayi Branch of the Beggar Sect to persuade those damned beggars.
Under your advice, Fourth Senior Brother decided to send an envoy to the Qingcheng Sect to persuade Sect Leader Zou.
You tried to coax the Fourth Senior Brother to go to the Qingcheng Sect to die, and he holds a grudge.
Under your advice, Fourth Senior Brother decided to send an envoy to the Kongtong Sect, to persuade the Four Sect Leaders.

Third Senior Brother bathed and burned incense, observing a three‑day fast, then offered prayers to the ancestors of Tang Clan. He was about to undertake a great matter, comparable to how Tang Clan's progenitors resisted Emperor Xuanzong by defending the outer fortress. The annals would record your Tang Clan; either in the pantheon of glory or infamy. On this scorching day, Third Senior Brother convened Tang Clan disciples and retainers, speaking openly about his intention for the clan. Since the Wulin Alliance was both constrained by and supported by the court, their elimination of the Mud Cult would mean that from now on, only one alliance would dominate Jianghu. Whose right path it is or who can survive would be decided solely by them. The silence of the Wulin would reign; righteousness would no longer exist. This time, your rebellion is not against the Wulin Alliance or the court, but a call to action for those harboring grievances and unable to act, to form the Western Wulin Alliance in opposition to the existing alliance!

Ye Yunshang could not pretend she hadn't heard this. The pills from the alchemy room could not save the Tang Clan, but you, forged through a thousand trials, saved her. Hearing this, you felt both sorrow and joy: you had saved Yunshang, and the fact that she lived on protected your heart in turn.
The fire in the main furnace burned on, year after year, yet the day it could be drawn from the furnace never came. Even with the power to raise the dead, it could not save the Tang Clan.

You poured your heart and soul into completing the Second Senior Brother's research, allowing the Longevity Corpse Heart Pill in the main furnace to emerge into the world, but in the end, it could save no one.

You stood in the alchemy room, recalling the days when you were forced to serve and be berated by the Second Senior Brother. That strict man occasionally had moments of patience. His betrayal of the Tang Clan was indeed unforgivable, but now, thinking back, it all seemed fleeting as clouds. Whether kindness or resentment, they would all fade with the dream.

You stood motionless for a long while in the empty courtyard of the Tang family, looking down at your single blue robe, tattered now and stained through with the sweat, blood, and tears you had all shed together—it had grown far too heavy to bear. This evening's fading light fell with an especial loneliness.
So she made a pact with you to meet again in three years, at the old site of the Tang Clan.

Long Xiang refused, not because she didn't want to retire to the mountains with you, but because she still had unfinished business, unsolved mysteries, unavenged grudges, and unfulfilled promises in the Jianghu. Her mouth cried out in fear, her sword trembling in her hands, yet once she fled, her faith would collapse, so she had no choice but to go.

You blocked her path and would not let Long Xiang leave. But to her you were no longer a friend—you had become no different from a bully who oppresses the weak, no different from the Wulin Alliance. However much she once trusted you, that is how disappointed she is now; she has always been in earnest, and though she fears death, she would still rather not submit to raw power. You were distraught, lowering a rope again and again to search below, but found nothing. It was as if she had scattered on the wind, unwilling to remain anywhere you were. She would rather be dashed to pieces than leave with her honor stained—whatever good the world still held, she no longer cared for it.

You regretted what you'd done, knowing you could not keep her here by force, so you silently stepped aside. Seeing your grief, Long Xiang's heart could not help but soften; she wanted to speak gentle words of comfort, but her teacher's lesson echoed in her ears once more: "Cut, yet not severed; ordered, yet still in disarray." She had never meant to hurt you, nor did she wish to fail others, so she steeled her heart and swallowed the words unspoken. As for the debt of kindness she owed you, it would simply remain owed—should you ever fall into hardship, she would go through fire and water for you, but for the rest of this life she was resolved never again to show you a gentle face, lest she mislead you, or herself. Long Xiang left without a moment's hesitation, her white-robed figure fading from sight; the wind blew past, and not even a trace of her fragrance remained, as though she had never been there at all.

Long Xiang's inner demon remained unconquered, and you were no longer who you once were—at last she fell before your hand. She admitted defeat, yet still refused to yield. You wished to take back your careless words, but it was already too late; you could not become her partner, nor could things return to how they were.

Bound by her palace's rules, her words were cold, yet her sword carried a lingering warmth—the soft sword coiled about her finger sliced your skin and flesh, but she could not bear to take your life. At first glance the wounds looked shocking, yet none struck a vital point; every stroke was a shallow, gentle cut, exquisite to the last hair's breadth. What left you powerless to fight on was not your wounds but your broken heart. With this departure, Long Xiang's ties to you were severed for good—you would never see her again.

You hesitated several times, ultimately not daring to take that step, because you had guessed the outcome. Long Xiang noticed your stammering and thought you had been struck by an invisible hidden weapon that had silenced you. You retracted the feelings you wanted to express and only invited her to accompany you, hoping to look out for each other. Even if you couldn't become partners, it would be good to walk a little further and see a few more sights, fearing that you might never encounter such a wonderful person again.

She still half-believed you, thinking you didn't trust yourself and had only brought her along to have an excuse. Yet you've never felt anything like sibling affection for her; it's been admiration all along. Why do you keep calling her Sister Xiang? Isn't it because she forced you with her martial prowess? You knew you were far inferior to the Eldest Senior Brother. As soon as you spoke, you expected to be rejected, maybe even slapped. But Long Xiang's expression was unexpectedly relieved, her smile bitter-sweet and tender. She had been taught since childhood to revere chivalrous heroes, valuing character over appearance. Since you've been friends, she has never looked down on you, nor compared you to the Eldest Senior Brother. He was the person she had longed for, like her father or Gang Leader Wang, someone born to be a hero, like a star in the sky. Now, having faced setbacks and been stained with dust, she realized how noble and brave you were, having walked through the mud step by step, finally standing equal to the world's heroes. She respected you far more than you thought, and it was you who stirred her stubbornness, inspiring her to keep moving forward bravely even when the sky was dark.

Long Xiang's face darkened at the words, and she suddenly drew her sword. Jinxiang Palace's women are all pitiful and lonely, with more than half having fallen victim to unscrupulous men. While polygamy is legally permissible, Jinxiang Palace does not tolerate unfaithful men. You have a devoted companion by your side, yet you speak these words. The more sincere the tone, the more repulsive it becomes. Did you forget why Long Xiang ventured out of the palace? Those who corrupt hearts must be named in the Flower lament.
You gathered courage to confess your feelings to Long Xiang. When you suddenly confessed, Long Xiang was greatly surprised.

You know full well she is most likely infatuated with the Eldest Senior Brother. But this might well be the last meeting of this life—are your feelings meant to stay silently hidden, carried to the grave?

You fear she has no clear purpose, fear her wallet might be stolen, fear she might end up on the streets. Thinking about it, you feel a sense of unease. A thought strikes you, and you voice an invitation for her to travel together. Where she will go next can be decided later.

You arrived at the back mountains. Long Xiang heard the footsteps and hurriedly wiped away her tears, then swung her sword a few times. You saw her boots were muddy, and knew she had come to pay respects to the Eldest Senior Brother. The Tang Clan is about to disband; there are no more old friends left here. You two part ways today, and from now on, there will be no news of each other. Whether you will meet again in this lifetime remains uncertain.

You came to the back mountain to pay respects to the Eldest Senior Brother, tidying up things. Suddenly, you let out a long howl, not caring who the elder who taught you the Forgetful Chapter truly was, whether they could hear or not. You gave your best effort, and it was enough to say goodbye. The valley echoed your howl, lasting for a long time before fading. But then came a profound silence, no one answering. Perhaps the one from back then had already passed away.
She who has weathered the rain herself now comes to shield you beneath her umbrella—well, who told you to be the disciple she holds so dear?

You hastily wiped your tears, fearing your wife might look down upon you. Your beloved wife, however, gently comforted you. In her view, natural affection is common among people and need not be regarded as shameful. Rather, those who could laugh off parting with their homeland and family, appearing smug and insincere, were the ones truly deserving of a good scolding.
You hurriedly wiped your tears, fearing punishment from your master. However, your master comforted you with soothing words, for tears shed due to missing family are not considered cowardly.
Xiahou Lan had something to tell you, and was just about to speak, when she saw you crying and fell silent instead.
Those beautiful things have already gone far and away in a blink of an eye.
Good dreams never linger long, and yet you alone hesitate to leave. Life is but a wayside inn, and you too are only a traveler passing through—it's time to go, it's time to go.
On the open Training Ground, the wind is bleak, the people are lonely, the laughter of the past is faintly heard, yet the past is not worth recalling.

I wonder if Junior Martial Sister is living comfortably now, married far from home—whether she has enough to eat and is warm enough to wear. You lot acted recklessly and ruined everything, but thankfully she wasn't dragged down by it. Looking back now, it only proves Third Senior Brother had foresight all along.

Yunshang has never cared for the struggles of Jianghu—whether she wins fame or renown means nothing to her, so long as you can find a way to earn coin for her to spend. You had best prove your worth: everything her own brother once gave her, you must take up without missing a beat and go on spoiling her with, guarding her carefully so she never suffers for having followed you.
You promised to take her to find Ye Yunzhou's trail. She does not know how much of her remaining life she has left, but from now on, she will stake it entirely on you.

You change your heart towards another woman, she sees it all, harboring resentment, wanting to retaliate fiercely, yet always can't bear to do so. Sometimes she lets go, sometimes she grows angrier, naturally having a sour expression towards you.
Just reminiscing about the past, Yunshang pushed the door open and came out to see you, reprimanding you for your improper gaze.

She looked back on her life and realized that apart from her dearest ones, the most precious treasure was nothing more than you and the inheritance from Yunshang. She wanted to clutch you tightly in her little hands, nothing else mattered.

Just as you reminisce about the past, Junior Martial Sister herself pushes the door open. She might be the most sentimental soul in the world—though she never said it, she has remembered your patient company all these years, and has also witnessed you caught and beaten more than once. At the time she thought little of it, but now she understands the depth of your devotion, and feels for you both a pure, unsullied admiration and boundless gratitude.

You leisurely stroll through the courtyard, pausing before the Women's Quarters, filled with myriad emotions. Before the Master's Wife passed away, she entrusted you to care for Junior Martial Sister, so she wouldn't be lonely. In the first few years, Junior Martial Sister missed her mother and cried every night; it was you who kept watch beneath her window, and even when the Women's Quarters stood empty, you were always there by her side. Only once she mastered the Heaven and Earth Silent Power, froze her heart, and stilled her tears—from then on wearing no expression at all—did you dare to gradually distance yourself.

You arrive at the forge, filled with myriad feelings. Here countless weapons and wooden armor were crafted—some benefited the villages, others brought ruin upon the world, yet objects themselves hold no good or evil; it all depends on how they are used. If a person loses their heart and blindly follows, are they truly any different from the objects themselves? The Wulin Alliance isn't even the Tang Clan's true enemy; it is merely a great weapon, and the one wielding it is the emperor himself. Who says he is inept? Isn't this move rather ruthless indeed?

You heard the forge still clanging, so you followed the sound and saw Xiaozhu still hammering away. She wanted to craft a wheeled cart, so that in the future, Third Senior Brother could occasionally push the sect leader out to bask in the sun and breeze. When you approached, she stopped hammering. Clumsy and lacking in strategy, she couldn't even form comforting words. As the first sect leader's wife, she could do nothing to help, constantly feeling ashamed and self‑reproachful. She could only press her small body against yours, trying to support you.

In the Disciples' Quarters, the brothers all wore expressions of confusion. Starting today, there was no need to practice martial arts, leaving them feeling lost and aimless. They began discussing their future paths; some were still attached to Jianghu, unwilling to give up on joining another sect; others were weary and wanted to return home to reconsider their plans; some already had a home to go back to, having fulfilled their youth by joining the Tang Clan, and now naturally wanted to return to the broad road paved by their parents. So what about you? You have no home to return to, your dreams can no longer be realized. Have you thought about what comes next?

You arrived at the kitchen, which was one of the reasons you were promoted from the Outer Fort to the main hall. The Tang Clan had many disciples, and the kitchen had to supply food. When things got busy, they wished everyone had three arms. There's an old saying, A gentleman keeps away from the kitchen, originally meaning a gentleman should have compassion and refrain from killing, but the original words from the Book of Rites were more subtle. It was later misinterpreted as an excuse to avoid cooking, a development that was only natural. Thus, you, an outsider with no need to practice and seemingly no talent, finally caught their attention and were moved to the main hall to serve in the kitchen. At first, you were clumsy and often got beaten. Even if they couldn't find faults in you, they'd still scold you a few words, otherwise the Senior Brothers would feel uneasy. Gradually, the scolding grew quieter. As the old disciples left, it was finally your turn to be the one in charge of the stove. After the Tang Clan disperses, you'll no longer have to wake up at dawn, wash rice, start a fire, and cook.

You encountered Xiaomei in the kitchen, where she was cooking. Not wanting to waste all this stored grain, she thought that even if they couldn't eat it all at once, they could still shape it into rice balls and dry them into rations for everyone to carry along the journey. Seeing your genuinely melancholic expression, Xiaomei felt the same way; she herself was reluctant to part with it, let alone understand the depth of your sorrow. Though she acknowledged her own inability to uphold the Tang Clan's unity, she was willing to stand by you through any hardship. If anyone dared to harm the Tang Clan, you two could mask your faces and go find trouble for them.

You went to the Scripture Hall, where motes of dust drifted through the morning light as if nothing had changed. You opened a book and found Eldest Senior Brother's childhood scribbles still inside. You quickly closed it, afraid a falling tear might smear the old ink of a friend now gone.

You arrived at the Scripture Hall, where Shangguan Ying was directing the junior disciples in cataloguing the hall's books and paintings. At Third Senior Brother's suggestion, she drew on old connections and her own good name to have everything in the courtyard appraised, then asked Squire Lü to take it all in pawn, turning it into ready cash to hand out to the Tang Clan disciples as travel funds. The Tang Clan had never set store by such old possessions anyway; she would work hard to redeem them another day. Even if you had no use for them, it was just as well to leave everything as it was, kept for you to remember.

You went to the Scripture Hall and found Xiaoju writing. She had joined the Tang Clan only recently, but loving you, she loved your home in turn, and could not bear to see it fall to ruin. Fearing that once everyone was gone the hall would stand empty and its books lost or crumbled to pieces, she had begun copying out the essential passages herself, so that those who came after would know the story of the Tang Clan. She wanted to write your story too — of an orphan loved by neither father nor mother, who endured hardship and pressed on against the wind. It need not end in glory; to grow old at her side and be her hero alone would be enough. One day, when the story was finished, it should be called Legend of Mortal.

You went to Zhengxin Hall to call upon the Sect Leader, and knelt in thanks for the shelter he gave you all those years ago. No matter what the world may say of him, in your heart, he alone is a true Great Hero.

During casual conversation, they mentioned how you had once seen the Dharma King Liu E of the Hungry Ghost Path. You deliberately concealed your involvement in the violent assault on the South Songshan abbot that you committed with Liu E.
Third Senior Brother harbors a deep hatred for the Demon Cult, as if they were enemies. Yet you didn't take the rumors to heart, instead sharply rebuking Third Senior Brother for spreading gossip.
Of course, it was rejected at once.
You half‑jokingly suggested simply defecting to the Demon Cult and using the Mud Cult's power to counter the Wulin Alliance's attack.

Tang Clan stands with an unbowed spirit, unafraid of death. But they are not those who recklessly court certain doom, knowing the end is inevitable yet rushing toward it. Given a chance to fight, who would willingly bow their neck to the blade? Your single remark at the assembly stunned everyone; all the learning you had gathered became a lamp, became a sword, pointing the way forward for your sect. You rallied rogue heroes of Jianghu who reject official rule, forming the Western Wulin Alliance to oppose the Wulin Alliance. This was sure to stir turmoil across the Central Plains. Defeat would not only bring the Tang Clan's downfall but also drag others into the mire. Should they succeed in setting East against West, adding the Mud Cult as a third force could form a three-way balance of power, each checking the other. Not to break the stalemate, but to ensnare their rivals within it. Only then would the Wulin Alliance seek paths beyond mere strife.

When she presided over the Kongtong Mystic Skill Gate, she had foreseen the shifting dynamics of the Jianghu. The Jinxiang Palace's change in leadership and Nangong Yuan's demise, though unforeseen, were secondary to the formation of the Wulin Alliance, which was manipulated by the authorities to pressure the Tang Clan. To prevent the situation from spiraling out of control, she acted without your knowledge, spreading songs that highlighted your divine mandate as the Kongtong sect's leader, reinforcing your image. She also used the mutual dependence of the sects to persuade the three sect leaders to unite and support you. Later, she dispatched Danxiazi under the authority of the First Sect Leader's wife to set up a sand table at Iron Chess Ridge, repeatedly simulating scenarios until she devised this plan. By rallying outlaws who defied the authorities to form the Western Wulin Alliance, she aimed to create a confrontation with the existing Wulin Alliance, causing chaos in Central Plains. If they failed, not only would the Tang Clan be destroyed, but others would also be dragged into the conflict. Success would mean a division between East and West, with the Mud Cult forming a tripartite balance, each checking the others. It wasn't to break the stalemate, but to drag the opponent into it. Only then would the Wulin Alliance seek alternatives beyond conflict.

Gang Leader Wang and Lady Wen's legacy plan parted the clouds and let the light through, laying everything bare before you. By rallying Jianghu wanderers who defied official authority to form a Western Wulin Alliance against the Wulin Alliance, it would surely stir turmoil across the Central Plains. Failure would not only doom the Tang Clan but drag others down with it; success might set East against West, and with the Mud Cult added, form a three-way balance, each side checking the others. The aim was not to break the stalemate, but to drag the enemy into one — so the Wulin Alliance would be forced to seek a path beyond conflict.

The Junior Martial Sister showed no mercy, siding entirely with you. The Third Senior Brother wanted to throw up his hands and surrender on the spot, but as Acting Sect Leader he could hardly refuse to fight, and felt utterly wronged for it.

Fourth Senior Brother also came to join the battle, feinting a few moves just for show. No one touched a strand of his hair, yet he proactively rushed in to collide with someone, exclaiming, Such powerful internal force! Then he rolled back and got up, still breathing heavily, looking thoroughly unwilling.
Opinions reached an impasse, so, true to Tang Clan tradition, you settled it with your fists instead. Whoever lost the bout was deemed to have no opinion at all.

The Tang Clan answers to no command from the Wulin Alliance, nor bows to the officials. But wiping out the Demon Cult and protecting the common folk from evil is a duty none can shirk. In the old days, the Old Demon Cult brought ruin to the Central Plains, and the Sect Leader once led his own disciples to stand against them. Now that the storm was rising again, your generation would not let the Wulin Alliance claim all the glory—you decided to answer the call and join the battle at Six Paths Gorge.

The Tang Clan, proud as it is, would not knowingly walk a road that led to certain death. Doing what one knows cannot be done does not always end well. You all knew this day would come, but no one dared speak first, fearing that once their resolve scattered, it would never come together again. If the ancestors of the Tang Clan could see this from beneath the earth, they would clutch their chests in grief, stamp their feet, and jab accusing fingers, cursing you, their descendants, as unworthy—eternal sinners. Having endured until today, you had at last to wake from the dream. Not every story ends in glory; most fade quietly and sadly, growing old with nothing but regret.

In the end, you made your decision. Though prudent self‑preservation is wise, you chose to stay, for this place holds the meaning of your wandering in Jianghu and the dignity of your existence. To flee, even if you live, is as if you have died. But with a clear conscience, unashamed before heaven and earth, even if condemned by thousands and opposed by all, let them be nothing but wind.
Junior Martial Sister entrusted the decision to you. She spoke little, but her resolve was unyielding.

Witnessing the decline of their family's fortunes, watching people come and go, the familiar faces growing fewer by the day, Junior Martial Sister felt countless emotions—no longer the naive young woman she once was. Silent and unspoken, she understood better than anyone how fleeting fate could be. How could she not feel anger in her heart? It was only that she could not bear to part with the people beside her now. Had she a choice, she would have wished to keep time for herself.

The Junior Martial Sister folded the paper into a crane, without making a choice. Everyone thought she had a child's heart, but in fact, the crane carried her wishes, which read: I hope everyone is safe. She feared that if it were torn apart, her wishes would not come true and would fail to reach the heavens, so she preferred that no one knew.
Fourth Senior Brother's ideas were entirely at odds, and what was written on paper was also the best plan he could imagine after exhausting his brainpower.
On the day of the decision, Third Senior Brother brought paper and a pen and wrote down his decision.

A once obscure, third‑rate gang, in just a few short years, had become a faction whose name shook the Jianghu. Hearing this, you couldn't help but feel a pang of melancholy, as if a lifetime had passed.

The feud between the Tang Clan and the Flying Stone Gang was already old news, with disputes flaring even before Eldest Senior Brother ran off with the Gang Leader's own wife. After the battle at Woyun Ridge, both sides had settled down for a time, but the Flying Stone Gang couldn't stay quiet for long and started provoking again. Fourth Senior Brother, stung on his sorest spot, flew into an uncontrollable rage—not only did he attack them, but he also stole the wallets of the Flying Stone Gang Members, handing the gang the perfect excuse to make trouble. They were spoiling for a fight, and might lead their people to seek revenge at any moment.

You received a declaration from the Wulin Alliance, and your hearts stirred with alarm. Fortunately, it was not aimed at your Tang Clan but condemned the Mud Cult instead. They intended to summon heroes from across the land to converge at Six Paths Gorge and besiege the Demon Cult.

You received an edict from the Wulin Alliance condemning the Tang Clan, which laid out the charges against you, urging you to turn back before it was too late while calling on all martial heroes to gather in Shu—a case of both carrot and stick.

Third Senior Brother saw your deep affection and couldn't help but smile. He recalled his first wife, from those years of diligent study, who had nagged him just the same, always dreaming he would rise to greatness. Unfortunately, they never grew old together. Knowing his career was hopeless, she lost heart, and the two of them parted ways; she soon remarried another man.

Third Senior Brother and Fourth Senior Brother saw your deep affection for each other and couldn't help but smile. However, they weren't the least bit envious. Lady Shangguan may be beautiful, but few can endure her Hedong Lion's Roar.

You had barely stepped into the Zhengxin Hall when Shangguan Ying hurried after you, helping to tidy your clothes and attempting to tame the disheveled, cow‑horn‑like hair that had become unruly from sleep. Unfortunately, her efforts were in vain. After another round of earnest admonition, she finally left.
One day, someone came to summon you to the Tang Clan council. You had by now become an indispensable member of these meetings.

The group survived the disaster, barely keeping their lives, but lost their fortune entirely. The investors blamed him, driving Fourth Senior Brother out of the caravan he himself had organized, and selling off the remaining goods, men, and horses to the Shangguan Guild for quick cash. Heaven brings storms no one foresees, and man meets fortune and misfortune overnight—strictly speaking, none of this was your fault. But the bitterness in his heart was such that, unless he could blame you, he could not go on.

He went off to Shaanxi Huayin to obtain an Immortality Pill, but the Song and Jin dynasties were locked in a standoff, and merchants were still allowed to travel freely. Yet suddenly, the situation turned tense. Rumors spread throughout the Jin Kingdom, claiming that the emperor's niece had been wandering in the Wulin of Central Plains at the Jinxiang Palace. The Song's Wulin Heroes gathered to attack, infuriating the Jin emperor, who mobilized troops and dispatched generals to launch an assault on the Song. The Fourth Senior Brother and his companions were detained as major suspects. They spent a fortune to clear their names and finally managed to escape back into the Song Kingdom.

Whether it was kindness or calculation, none could say—but for your sake, Liu E treated the Fourth Senior Brother with peculiar leniency, sparing him only the ordeal of sitting by, sick with dread, as his fellow travelers were stripped and made to endure live fish sucking at their nipples. Though the act took no lives, it was utterly humiliating: the bearded old men, once it was over, wept and felt too disgraced to go on living, demanding to know why the Fourth Senior Brother alone had been spared. Their resentment in this needed no words to be understood.

He changed his route to Ningguo Prefecture to see the Junior Martial Sister as you had asked of him. Unfortunately, he encountered the Hungry Ghost Path while traveling west, and the caravan he traveled with was brutally robbed.
You and Third Senior Brother were deeply concerned about the sect's future, filled with countless emotions, when Fourth Senior Brother suddenly returned.
Now you have surpassed the past, and can even defeat the Third Senior Brother head‑on.

Amidst the fierce struggle, memories surged like a tide, and you recalled the martial arts you had learned, the methods of combat, and the people you had missed. Happy moments, sorrowful moments, lifelong vows, boundless fervor, sobbing in the rain, profound loss, and the act of letting go. You awoke to a time where nothing could be done.

You awoke from the bed dazed and confused, not knowing what day it was. The past events felt both real and unreal, the surroundings just as they were yesterday, yet the people had changed. Memories were faintly remembered yet incredibly unfamiliar, as if you had lived someone else's life in a dream. Third Senior Brother ignored your confusion and strongly invited you to go to the training ground to exercise your muscles and bones.

Xiahou Lan told you to go wash up, and you took it for her usual scolding — when really she'd missed you terribly, and only wanted to call you up to the treehouse, hold you, kiss you, and turn you this way and that checking for any wound that might ache her heart. Absence makes for a sweeter reunion than any wedding night; you and Xiahou Lan lay side by side on the bed, talking and watching the stars. In all the Wulin, you alone are favored by her — the only one who knows that behind this Demoness's cold, tight-lipped front lies a tenderness like flowing water that no one else has ever seen.

Fan Xiaotian wept for joy at the sight of his beloved teacher, throwing himself into his arms like a spoiled child.
The three of you—master and disciples—had been apart for so long, and were at last reunited.

Xiahou Lan heard you had returned home and also went to the Tang Clan to look for you. You still thought she would say she wouldn't come, but would definitely appear in critical moments. Little did you know that this time she was truly staying shut inside, not ignoring you, but out of trust.

The incident at Yueyang Fengyu Mountain has already been spread throughout the Central Plains by the Jianghu Bulletin. Third Senior Brother has also heard of it; the details still need to be discussed with you for verification, but it's not urgent. Nothing is more valuable than your safe return home.

The Third Senior Brother saw Shangguan Ying heading to the Tang Clan again, his expression instantly tightening. He noticed she was unaccompanied by Cang Gang guards this time, which made him even more puzzled, thinking the Shangguan family must have some new scheme. When he heard you say she had broken away from the Shangguan family and become your fiancee, the Third Senior Brother fainted on the spot. His pressure was too great; he had been having nightmares recently, thinking he was trapped in some absurd dream, but it wasn't a dream‑it was reality, bizarre and illogical.

You introduced Xiaoju to Third Senior Brother, and his eyes went wide with shock. You should know that Wei Ju hailed from the Gengyang Study Hall — no sooner had she arrived in Lin'an than she made her name at the poetry gatherings. Still young, she was received as a scholar of the Emperor himself and took first place in the imperial examinations, but for a woman to be so gifted was itself a kind of crime: she offended powerful ministers, was stripped of her rank, and cast out into the Jianghu. The court historians dared not even record her name, and she, in defiance, swore never to write another poem under so corrupt a reign. Now not a single scroll of her calligraphy can be found, and her fame survives only in the whispers of scholars and men of letters. Since joining Kongtong, she has held her own as a woman dealing directly with the Third Sect Leader, guarding the Mystic Skill Gate, overseeing its most profound texts on one hand and every household register, livestock count, and account on the other. With her at Kongtong Sect, all runs in perfect order, and she is deeply revered for it. Such a paragon might well be called a living legend — however did you manage to bring her home with you?
You introduced Fan Xiaotian to the Third Senior Brother. The dogs and chickens, sensing the medicinal scent, became exceptionally excited and scattered everywhere.

You recommended Ye Yunzhou to join the Tang Clan, and the Third Senior Brother agreed at once. Watching him wield peerless swordsmanship yet remain wholly without arrogance, laboring without complaint as a servant to the Second Senior Brother — such humility and diligence were the very mark of a gentleman, and Third Senior Brother genuinely prized his talent. Even had you said nothing, Third Senior Brother would have tried to win Ye Yunzhou over himself.

Ye Yunshang had been bedridden for years, delicate and weak. This time, when she went out, she took a carriage and rode a horse, and walked a lot, her tender feet nearly broken from the journey. After saying hello, she went to soak her feet to relieve them.
Xiao Zhu was on edge the whole way, and only let out a breath once she was home. She said her hellos, then went straight back to the forge.

The moment Xiaomei got home, she took your dirty clothes off to wash and hang them out, speaking of it lightly enough. But once she'd made sure no one else was around, she put on your clothes, disguised herself as you, and went about flirting with the female disciples, tarnishing your name to make certain no woman could ever threaten her place at your side.
Of course, you—the one whose name she was using—knew nothing of any of this.
The Junior Martial Sister is an exception‑she is always very beautiful.
You've finally returned home after a round trip‑everyone looks ten years older.

Wind and rain sweep wild, the hour ripe for singing and shouting to the sky; let worry turn my black hair white — how could I bear to waste the wine within this cup? Rising and sinking with the surging tide: when it comes, storm clouds gather; when it ebbs, all scatter into stillness.
Then you began singing, and everyone sang together. Those who couldn't sing also clapped in response.

Yunshang learned to play the guqin at Jinxiang Palace, and today she finally revealed her skills. Accompanied by singing, she played spontaneously, creating an incredibly lively atmosphere. Even those who couldn't sing joined in by clapping their thighs in rhythm.

Everyone hoped you'd say something to lift their spirits and rally their courage, but instead you declared you'd lead a sing-along, seemingly unbothered by it all. Life, after all, was only ever a fleeting gathering — when the song ends and people scatter, leaving clear skies and a light breeze behind, wasn't that fine too? Giving up a dream took courage of its own; if this road was closed, striking out on another wasn't so bad either. No one was irreplaceable. No one had to stake their life on this, not even you — perhaps even you would set off on your own path one day. Why not simply let it go for now, drink while there was wine, and not begrudge whoever stayed or left? Years later, if the thought crossed your mind, you might ask around and perhaps still catch word of old friends — wouldn't that be joy beyond measure? Nothing mattered more than living well in the moment. The more bitter life became, the more reason to find sweetness in it.

You spoke with heartfelt persuasion. Though you were never born a hero like Eldest or Second Senior Brother, ordinary as you were, you still vowed to stand or fall with the sect together — precisely because you were mortal, capable of dying and being wounded, you needed your brothers and sisters to watch your back, just as you always stepped forward in times of danger, not out of talent but out of resolve. The Tang Clan was not merely a brotherhood but a family, and no one in it was expendable. Your words were sincere and earnest, and they moved everyone. You were not carefree like Eldest Senior Brother, nor stern like Second Senior Brother — you were, more than anything, yourself.
You tried every gentle word to persuade him, but his mind was already made up — what right did you have to demand he risk his life to stay by your side?

You scowled, trying to imitate Second Senior Brother's threats and intimidation, but unfortunately your face carried no trace of authority. Your attempt at toughness failed, and you ended up being laughed at by everyone.

Once the truth was spoken, the Tang Clan's Junior Martial Brothers and Sisters grew uneasy and restless. If they could survive, who would ever leave? When they came, they were full of ambition, but now they were listless, as if their heartblood no longer burned hot. Jianghu is so cold‑what remains worth risking one's life for?

Long Xiang listened, feeling ever more lost and bewildered. She had never imagined the Jianghu ran so thick with hidden currents — nowhere near as simple as acting on impulse and playing the hero. Those who could truly settle scores and delight in vengeance were either utterly unattached, ready to die at any moment, or else favored by heaven, with everything arranged so they could venture forth without a care. Everyone was flesh and blood, with their own private wants, and everyone would die. The dream of a single sword chilling fourteen provinces still had to bow to reality. You call me a great hero, I praise you as a hero in turn — the side with more voices becomes righteousness, and enough tongues can melt gold; no evidence is needed to claim the moral high ground. Such was this world, so far from what she had known. Thinking it through only tangled things further. Long Xiang truly could not make sense of it, and found it all absurd.

These words not only represent myself but also the sentiments of all Tang Clan disciples. Reluctantly, you must admit that you are actually weak; even if a couple of you are capable fighters, they are no more than that. Since the Sect Leader's fall, Tang Clan disciples have always relied on his former prestige to walk the Jianghu, and they no longer possess the arrogance of old. Even if you refuse to submit, once your true strength is uncovered, the Jinxiang Palace will serve as a cautionary tale.

Could the Tang Clan's innocence or guilt truly hinge on other sects voting down from their lofty perches? Who wouldn't be furious? That Shi Ming, riding on his reputation and standing, could condemn people to death without a shred of evidence — who wouldn't feel a chill? The Tang Clan escaped this time, but Jinxiang Palace nearly fell, not for any wrongdoing of their own, only for their ties to the Mud Cult — guilt by association. The heroes of the Wulin call themselves righteous, yet bound by their notions of good and evil, they follow the crowd blindly once someone dresses it up as justice. Shi Ming's slander failed only because his own name wasn't great enough. Next time some figure of even greater standing in the Jianghu steps up to accuse the Tang Clan, the heroes won't even bother asking questions before wiping out your whole clan on nothing but their own judgment.

Is the Tang Clan innocent or guilty? It's up to other sects to decide by voting from their lofty positions. Who wouldn't be angry? Shi Ming, relying on his reputation and status, can sentence people to death without evidence. Who wouldn't feel a chill? Everyone knows full well that all sects hate the Tang Clan. Whether or not they attend the Wulin Congress, the Tang Clan will become Public Enemies of the Wulin. Once the Mud Cult falls, it will be your turn. Without giving you a charge, how can they justify killing you? Without punishing villains, how can they spread their heroism? Therefore, you must be villains.

After the commotion faded, quiet crept back in. Outside the temple, wind and rain howled, and the firewood crackled now and then. Everyone lay or sat without speaking, each weighed down by private thoughts; whatever words rose to the lips were swallowed back down.  The senior Tang Clan disciple who had taken the first night watch came back. Guessing that everyone's silence hid the same worry, and having wavered over it himself for a long while, he finally spoke his mind.  He had joined the clan after you, but was formally admitted to the inner circle early. Leaving you aside — since you don't bear the Tang name — he was now, counting down from Fourth Senior Brother, the most senior in the Tang Family still alive and still loyal to the sect. He had always dreamed of making a name for himself, of measuring blades with the heroes of the land. He had to rise above the ordinary to earn a name of his own; otherwise, a lifetime of dull struggle would end with him still just another Tang Clan disciple, forgotten the moment the earth closed over him.  He had missed neither the Battle of Jiangling nor Fengyu Mountain, always thinking, this time will be my chance. But heaven never smiled on him, and things always went awry — to this day he remains utterly unknown, unable even to match Eldest or Second Senior Brother, while even you had won some fame on your looks alone.  For this Wulin Congress he had rolled up his sleeves, ready to prove himself at last. Who could have guessed it would end like this?

You saw how furious she was, yet beneath it she was as ashamed as she was worried for you; still, she couldn't help but stubbornly blame you anyway, which only made you smile. Another round of sweet talk left this easily swayed young woman blushing to her ears.

You knew full well that Xiao Zhu was afraid of ghosts, yet you insisted on telling a ghost story anyway. Before you could even begin, the terrified Xiao Zhu slapped you so hard your feet left the ground; not even the Thousand-Pound Drop could halt your fall, and you crashed down bleeding from a split scalp, nearly frightened out of your own soul.

You gambled with your Junior Martial Brothers and Sisters to pass the time. They harbored ill intent, scheming openly against you: they set the bowl far away, so that without the Tang Clan's chant and knowledge of the force-dissipating technique, it would be hard even to keep the dice in the bowl. Yet you had mastered it without a teacher, your skill with hidden weapons extraordinary and unerring — you rolled whatever number you willed, a full house every time. Your Junior Martial Brothers and Sisters were awed and impressed, but having lost their coin to you, their resentment was only natural.

You gambled with your Junior Martial Brothers and Sisters to pass the time. They harbored ill intent, scheming openly against you: they set the bowl far away, so that without the Tang Clan's chant and knowledge of the force-dissipating technique, it would be hard even to keep the dice in the bowl. Yet you had mastered it without a teacher, your skill with hidden weapons formidable, growing sharper with every throw, until you fought them to a draw. Your Junior Martial Brothers and Sisters grumbled aloud, but secretly they admired you.
And your Heavenly Junior Martial Sister used her Hidden Weapon skills to win the coins back for you.
You gambled with your Junior Martial Brothers and Sisters to pass the time, fell victim to a cunning scheme, and lost so much that even your pants weren't yours anymore.

You all scoured the area to gather dry firewood and straw, built three fires, and sat around them roasting meat and drinking alcohol. Soon the aroma of the meat filled the air, adding a touch of warmth to the cold, quiet rainy night.

The rain showed no sign of stopping anytime soon, and since you couldn't reach the town anyway, you decided to claim the wild rabbits and bamboo chickens felled with hidden weapons along the way, and roasted them to eat.
You burst into laughter, more afraid of this delicate Bone-Cracking Demon being too tense and accidentally killing you than the invisible demons and monsters.

You weren't entirely unafraid either, but you reasoned that men fear ghosts three parts while ghosts fear men seven, and with so many of you together, your Yang Qi ran strong—by rights you had nothing to fear. Besides, going out now meant risking a chill from the rain, or worse, a misstep and a fall down the mountain path, so you gritted your teeth and set about comforting her.

As the saying goes, It's better to sleep in a lonely grave than enter a temple. Xiao Zhu, who firmly believed in ghosts and spirits, couldn't help but pale, clutching your arm tightly and pressing herself close against you, never leaving your side.

The journey brought both sun and rain; as you traveled through a rugged stretch of the path, another torrential downpour targeted you, drenching you all in a sorry state. Even your umbrellas couldn't hold back the rain, and you had no choice but to take shelter in a ruined temple.

It turned out that Madam Shangguan had a sleepless night, rising at dawn to pay for several hired men to go to the neighboring town's horse market to buy horses and carts. She also sent for her own servants, instructing them to spend coins on travel arrangements, ensuring the Tang Clan's return journey would be as leisurely as a countryside outing.
You were moved by their devotion, unable to help yourself, and every last one of your prejudices against Kongtong melted away.

Kongtong disciples believed their Sect Leader was born under heaven's mandate, his fate tied to the rise and fall of Kongtong, no different from the Son of Heaven himself. Aiding the Sect Leader, they believed, would bring them great fortune, so not one complained of the hardship—instead, they counted it an honor to serve.

It turns out that the people of Kongtong followed Wei Ju's orders. Yesterday, they went to the neighboring town's horse market to buy horses and hire people. Today, they brought the horses in the early morning.
The two of you made a promise to meet again in the future, raise a toast and exchange heartfelt words, then bowed to each other and said their goodbyes.

This Young Lord held his head high, sneering at those he deemed unworthy. Yet toward those he approved of, he spared no effort in befriending them wholeheartedly, unmoved by worldly opinion.
When friends came from afar, failing to fulfill his duty as host was regret enough—how could he not do his part for your journey home?

The elders of the Nangong family all spoke out against supporting the Tang Clan. Nangong Shen could not go against the majority, but he still considered you a friend—whether or not you believed his justification, he still meant to do his part.

Shangguan Ying confided her heart to you, carefully placing her sincere feelings in your hands, from then on devoted solely to your well‑being, unwilling to let you harbor any doubts. In front of the flowing crowd and her former fiance, she adjusted your collar, her intention clear to declare her affection, her heart genuinely pounding with emotion, overflowing with sweetness. From then on, she would devote herself to you, scold you, and support you, indifferent to others' opinions. Nangong Shen watched from the side, waves of regret surging in his heart, yet what could he say now, having already broken their engagement with his own words?
From what he said, Sect Leader Wei of Kongtong had also gone to the horse market, hoping to arrange mounts for the Tang Clan, but simply couldn't outdo him.

As you stepped outside, Shangguan Ying was talking with Nangong Shen. You didn't hear anything, but just seeing the two of them standing together caused a pang in your heart. Shangguan Ying noticed your misunderstanding and found it both amusing and exasperating. She lightly punched you and decisively stood by your side. It turned out she had sent someone to the nearby town's horse market early in the morning, but unfortunately, Nangong Shen had acted first and secured all the horses yesterday, even hiring the drivers. When Shangguan Ying tried to pay, he stubbornly refused to accept it, which is why they were at a stalemate outside.

It was Nangong Shen, the newly appointed head of the Nangong family, who had prepared the horses for you. His father had just passed away, and grieving to the point of despair was not unreasonable. Yet this Eldest Young Lord possessed a resolute spirit, managing to hold back his tears and being attentive to every Jianghu friend, including the Tang Clan, without any oversight.

Just as they were about to step out of the inn, the waiter came to inform them that the horses and the carriage were all prepared. You were taken aback upon hearing this and had no choice but to follow him out to check.
You packed your luggage and valuables, filled the gourd with water, bought some emergency dry rations for the road, and set off for home.

Hearing this, your feelings were a tangle you couldn't quite name. Wasn't this the very person you had dreamed, through countless days and nights in the Jianghu, of becoming? And yet, in the end, he was not you.
Hearing this, you felt truly a whirlwind of mixed emotions—startled, then unable to help a rueful laugh, a touch of envy, yet also a quiet gladness.
With such peerless achievements to his name, it was only natural that he was hailed as Wulin Alliance Leader by common acclaim—not a single soul dissented.
The young swordsman's name was Rui Sheng.
That young swordsman was none other than Rui Sheng, the Young Swordsman in White—one half of the celebrated Twin Heroes of Life, paired with you in renown.

The next morning, before you set out, you heard from a youth who dreamed of becoming a great hero how the Wulin Assembly's aftermath had played out. It was said the Hell Path of Western Shu and the Eastern Hungry Ghost Path, unwilling to sit and await their doom, had gathered at Yueyang to lay siege to Fengyu Mountain. The righteous and the wicked fought until the sky darkened and the earth dimmed, blood staining wide swaths of Dongting Lake red. Though the heroes of the Wulin were mighty in their arts, their strength had been sorely spent; the great sects and clans, leaderless, had scattered like sand, driven back step by step. Then, at the moment the righteous path teetered on the brink, a hero in flowing white robes raised his sword and loosed a long, ringing cry, transforming into a white dragon, cutting through the enemy as though the field before him stood empty, turning back a million soldiers with a single blade. In that hour between life and death, every sect and clan at last set aside their old grudges, heeded a single command, and together turned the tide, crushing the two Paths in one resounding victory.

You embraced each other beneath the moon; she felt as though she might melt away, unsettled by the storm-tossed times, unable to shake her unease, yet still she resolved to stand by you, making the place you longed to go her own dream.

Xiaozhu paid constant attention to you and knew how hard things had been for you. It wasn't that she didn't want to comfort you—she was just clumsy, unable to find the right words. They often hovered on the tip of her tongue, only for her to swallow them back down.

You woke up at midnight to find Xiaozhu by your side. She had been worried ever since you went into the room and never came out, so she used the excuse of bringing your food to come in and look in on you. You had remembered to lock the door, but the latch was too flimsy to survive a single push, and it gave way cleanly under her hand—she even thought you'd forgotten to lock it at all. Seeing you sound asleep, not even stirring at her entrance, she set down the warm tray and meant to leave, but then heard you murmur her name in your sleep. Pleased and aching at once, she sat quietly in the room writing in her diary, wanting to stay by you a while longer.

Yunshang still carries a childlike air, yet she has long been tormented by illness, crossing the gates of death several times. She has grown indifferent to life and death, viewing worldly matters with clarity. Though she appears childish, her inner maturity far surpasses her outward appearance. She never considers herself a Jianghu person; accompanying you is merely out of attachment. She waits for you to waste your youth, give up hope, and then it will be your turn to spend the rest of your life traveling with her through mountains and rivers.

Ye Yunzhou didn't take care of her because of your presence. He first circled around for a while, then used his Qinggong skills to return to Fengyu Mountain to observe the aftermath of the Wulin Assembly.

You woke in the middle of the night, startled to find something small and soft nestled in your arms, sweet-scented—Yunshang. You went pale with alarm, and before you could even ask how she had slipped in, climbed into your bed, and stolen your blanket, she struck first and accused you of being the noisy one. Little did you know how cunning Yunshang truly was: she had slipped into the room even before you did. Worn out in body and mind, you had entered without checking your surroundings, and only once you were asleep did she show herself, tiptoeing to the bedside. She had meant to play a prank, but seeing how haggard you looked, she couldn't bring herself to do it, and instead showed you a rare kindness, drawing the blanket over you and curling up in your arms to keep you warm—only to doze off herself and steal the blanket back.

You woke in the middle of the night to find the Junior Martial Sister asleep at your side, and you sat bolt upright in fright. She stirred awake too, her face flushing faintly. Though you had barred the door before bed, the Junior Martial Sister had never taken the ordinary way in—thanks to your own bad example, she had come through the window, and to this day believed it was an understanding between the two of you. She had meant to find you for a meal, but seeing you asleep, and hearing you murmur her name in your dreams, she supposed you missed her; a quiet sweetness filled her heart, for she had had no chance to be alone with you all this while. So she nestled quietly against you, and before she knew it, had fallen asleep herself. Both of you were doing everything you could to protect the sect, yet the Jianghu was perilous and life was hard, and no one person's courage alone could command the wind and rain. The harder you tried, the more powerless you felt. The Junior Martial Sister had grown up a good deal on this journey with you, and had begun to think of stepping back from the Jianghu. She had never sought fame or fortune—only to be with the family and friends she loved.

You were truly exhausted—you hadn't eaten, and you were caked in dust—so the moment your head touched the pillow, you fell into a deep, death-like sleep. Faintly you heard the weeping of Jinxiang Palace's innocent and the furious cries of the Wulin heroes on Fengyu Mountain. You wavered back and forth, torn both ways, tormented and lost, afraid of choosing wrong and dragging your sect down with you. The deeper the dream ran, the further back you went, to a time when everyone was still alive, when the sky could fall and someone else would hold it up, when nothing was yours to worry over, and all you had to do was mind yourself and dream, day after day, your unrealistic Great Hero dream.

Life is unpredictable; a person in good health can vanish in an instant, especially in the Jianghu. Xiaomei's inner turmoil far exceeds her outward composure, only allowing people to see her vibrant exterior. She has no family left. Her time with you carries the innocence of a young woman, yet she fears you might one day vanish without a word, leaving her alone in this world. At least, she wants to have your child, so that for the next several decades, she can pour her heart into loving the only family she has left.

Xiaomei called you to eat, only to find you taking a bath. Seeing you, she felt a surge of excitement. She plucked a strand of hair, bound a silver needle to it, and inserted it into the door crack. Using a magnet, she pulled it back, hooking the door latch in the process. With a gentle lift, she disabled your defenses and burst into the room. She had used this trick to break into the rooms of Xiahou Lan, Yu Zhu, and Huyan Ju countless times before. Your frantic attempts to cover up only made her more excited. Ignoring that you were still dressed, she leaped into the tub, pushing and shoving with you, tearing it apart and leaving you to pay for the damage.

You had the inn boy bring up a bucket of hot water and soaked yourself in its warmth. The late sun of day's end slanted through the window, and the motes of dust hanging in the air were plain to see. The dust upon your heart could not be washed away; so weary were you that closing your eyes was enough to fall asleep.

You've heard that heroic figures in the Jianghu live freely, quick to revenge and unrestrained, but the reality is far from that. Only by venturing into the Jianghu do you realize the coldness of the waters; only after enduring hardships do you come to understand the bitterness of the heart. Storms have raged for a long time, and through arduous trials, you've transformed from an unknown soldier into the pillar of your sect. This was never mere chance. As responsibility grows heavier, your footsteps grow deeper. Burdened with too much, you can no longer take a step without difficulty, and your pace has never been light again.

The stormy conditions on Fengyu Mountain left the Tang Clan unscathed, with no casualties, a true miracle. A single misstep could have led to their complete annihilation, and even now, the thought still leaves you with a chill.
Because of your decision, someone can no longer go home.
Because of your decision, many people died.

You disbanded the group on the spot, letting your junior brothers and sisters rest and catch their breath, so they could face tomorrow with spirit. The moment the door of your room closed, your shoulders sagged, and alone at last, you let show the exhaustion you dared not reveal before others.

Fan Xiaotian was a disciple of the Beggar Sect, had never stayed at an inn, and was feeling cramped and uneasy with the dog. He had intended to briefly part ways and make do for the night at a nearby beggar's den, but you insisted on pulling him into the shop. The shopkeeper had initially looked ashen-faced, but the moment you pressed a heavy string of copper coins into his hand, his expression brightened at once.

Fan Xiaotian was a disciple of the Beggar Sect, had never stayed at an inn, and was also carrying a dog, feeling extremely cramped and uncomfortable, so he temporarily bid farewell and went to a nearby beggar's den to make do for the night.

Long Xiang and Lady Wen were called master and disciple, but in truth were as close as mother and daughter. Having lost the one she relied on in a single night, Long Xiang was especially spent — her white robes travel-worn, her face haggard, unable even to touch her beloved chicken legs.
But you're really reckless, completely ignoring the Wulin Alliance's threats.

You're not without worry, but with the world turned upside down in a single day, everyone looked worn and weary. They could not run far, and fleeing in disarray would be humiliating, expose their weakness, and only invite ambush — so you could not press on through the night.
You had barely escaped the tiger's mouth, yet you still trembled with anxiety, dreading that once the ten-day pact expired, the Wulin Alliance would descend to attack.

Descending from Fengyu Mountain, dusk was already gathering. Press on, and you might not reach the next town before it grew dark, so you had no choice but to rest in a nearby village. Fortunately, the village still had a tavern and an inn, so it was not too desolate a place.

Although Tang Clan was spared, you still felt a complex mix of emotions. Tang Clan had gained and lost reputation, yet could still be accepted by the Wulin. Why then couldn't Jinxiang Palace, whose fame spread far and wide, be allowed? Was it just because its palace mistress was the Dharma King of the Mud Cult? Was all her lifetime efforts to do good for naught because of a mere identity? You spoke out of emotion, but when you brought up Jinxiang Palace again, everyone looked solemn, thinking you were impractical and deliberately stirring up trouble. Lady Wen quickly stepped forward through the crowd, whispering gently to you to stop speaking. She implied that her true self was not the Palace Mistress of Jinxiang Palace. You stood there speechless, bowing in farewell.

You remembered everyone who had put their trust in the Tang Clan‑thanking none of them, but counting them all as friends instead. Everyone else in the Wulin, anyone with two legs to stand on and a human tongue to speak with, was now an enemy of the Tang Clan, and any who dared wander onto Tang Clan territory would be shown no mercy. You let these words fly with a voice that commanded awe, and those who had kicked you while you were down felt a sudden chill, recalling the terrifying legends of the Tang Clan in its prime, and shuddered. Having spoken, you did not look back, but led your fellow disciples away.

You are far from content. You were unjustly accused and nearly voted to be killed. Do you expect us to thank everyone for letting the Tang Clan off? You were so furious that you immediately lashed out on the spot, clearly seeking revenge by questioning Shi Ming, the thief monk, as the Dharma King of the Demon Cult, forcing everyone to vote whether he should be executed. Then, you indiscriminately questioned each person who had just dealt with the Tang Clan. Of course, you knew they wouldn't follow through, but only intended to ridicule them. This statement was extremely impolite, and everyone was taken aback by your narrow‑mindedness, your grudge‑bearing nature, and their faces turned sour.

You were anything but content. Your words were neither servile nor arrogant, polite yet utterly resolute‑you simply lacked the magnanimity, after being falsely accused for no reason and nearly voted to death, to turn around afterward and thank everyone for letting you off.
You arrived at the gathering with nothing left worth thanking anyone for, and your foul attitude stirred up the crowd's resentment.
Thus, I shall part ways
Then, you also issued death threats to the leaders of various factions, and to the wandering heroes, who had shown you no goodwill today.
You arrived at the gathering, paying respects and expressing gratitude to the leaders of various factions friendly to the Tang Clan, and saluting the wandering heroes.

Shi Ming's schemes backfired, leaving him heavily criticized and humiliated, his face burning with shame. Snorting disdainfully, he activated his Qinggong and vanished from the scene. Chao He, suddenly without support, was scared out of his wits and hurriedly followed to leave.

You took advantage of the chaos and turmoil caused by war, led your fellow disciples to charge toward the weakly guarded areas, and finally broke through the heavy encirclement to escape the battlefield.

You stood at the center of the Wulin Assembly, surrounded by Wulin Heroes, and let out a deafening laugh. Since the decline of the Tang Clan, the people of the Wulin had gradually forgotten the shadows. Your sudden, thunderous laughter sent a chill through all present, prompting them all to recall the terrifying legends of the Tang Clan‑anyone who offends the Tang Clan will be hunted down, no matter how far they flee. In the past, without the Supreme Bliss Cult, Old Demon Tang was the most wicked villain of his time. Unbeatable in the world, he left no survivors among his enemies, their deaths often gruesome. The Tang Clan Flying Hero was free‑spirited, well‑liked among the Jianghu, but his second disciple, the Ruthless Young Master, was a fearsome figure, reclusive and deadly, causing calamity wherever he went. A chill ran through their bodies, as if a bucket of cold water had been poured over their heads, extinguishing the wild fervor in the crowd, and no one dared to stop you from leaving with your sect.

Rushing to the foot of the mountain by Dongting Lake, where the battle between the forces of good and evil raged fiercely, the Dharma King of Hell's Path and you met each other. Both were taken aback. He had come solely to rescue those on the Human Path; though he arrived late, revenge was not too late. He thought you were in the same camp as the Wulin Alliance in harming the people of Jinxiang Palace, and he nearly slashed his sword at your face. You hastily explained yourself, but he trusted your character and immediately stepped aside, leading the ghost soldiers to cover your retreat.
If the Tang Clan didn't flee now, when would they? So you gave a shout, and led the group breaking through the encirclement to descend the mountain.

Just then, suddenly Mountain Bandits stumbled up the mountain, shouting loudly.
