Song Bei recognized these as Mountain Bandits from the nearby Catch the Mountain, Catch the Wind Fort, and couldn't help but be taken aback; this Wulin Assembly only invited the White Way, and did not send invitations to the Green Forests‑why would they willingly court trouble? Upon inquiry, everyone was shocked. It turned out that while the grand assembly was being held on the mountain, the Eastern Sea Mud Cult's Hungry Ghost Path and the Western Shu Hell Path could not sit idly by either; they had surrounded Fengyu Mountain, planning to set it ablaze. The Wulin Heroes on the mountain, without a leader, were instantly thrown into chaos upon hearing this news, scrambling desperately down the mountain. The Six Great Sects and other major sects also could not remain idle, hastily summoning their disciples to descend the mountain to confront the enemy.

You sighed, threw out a small sword, knowing that a direct confrontation would be doomed, and only hoped that there were still wise individuals in the Wulin Alliance who could open their eyes and restore fairness to the Tang Clan. Your fairness lies not in the Wulin, but in Song Bei, the Divine Constable. He serves as an official not merely obeying the Imperial Court; despite his high rank and wealth, he still voluntarily roams the Jianghu in pursuit of justice. How could he tolerate such injustice? The people of the Wulin are poorly educated and lack insight, yet he cannot be swayed by this evil monk. This matter is no longer solely a Wulin affair; his mediating justice does not constitute overstepping his authority. He is not favoring the Tang Clan, but rather targeting Shi Ming, the one who falsely accused them. A few sharp words, the weight of official authority, stripped Shi Ming of his smug expression, his palms sweating, his eyes darting, trying to use his status to intimidate. Commander Song didn't care about his status; with the Imperially Bestowed Gold Plaque in hand, he dared to arrest anyone who committed crimes, except the emperor himself.

It's said they will surrender their weapons and discuss in detail to prove their innocence, but the Wulin Alliance doesn't trust the Tang Clan, and how can the Tang Clan trust them? Merely relying on Shi Ming and Chao He's unsubstantiated, one‑sided words to detain someone, then when you're at their mercy, they can fabricate false evidence to force a confession‑what difficulty is that? With the Tang Clan's numerous enemies, by the time the ten‑day period ends, the officials and Imperial Soldiers lift the ban, and all their rivals lie in wait on the roads, attacking from all directions to annihilate the Tang Clan's elite forces‑this would not be an unusual occurrence.
In vain had you led the Tang Clan to stand shoulder to shoulder with the Wulin Alliance and fight as one side; in the end, they turned on you the moment it suited them.

When you came, you had anticipated that the Imperial Court might have ulterior motives, yet you hadn't foreseen the Tang Clan turning into a public enemy of the Wulin, which can be described as utter despair.

Ye Yunshang had always been mischievous, full of schemes, and now she looked eager to act. You thought she wanted to scold someone, but instead she pleaded with Shi Ming, treating him as a good person, saying it was all a misunderstanding, and that she had evidence to prove the Tang Clan's innocence. As soon as she presented it, anyone would immediately change their mind. Shi Ming's heart raced upon hearing this. If such evidence truly existed, wouldn't he be disgraced? Naturally, he refused to acknowledge it and even scolded her harshly. Seeing her refusal to show it, Ye Yunshang wanted to call Song Bei and Shangguan Jun over, which made Shi Ming even more anxious. If this item fell into the hands of the two Lords, he would still be doomed. So he patiently recited Buddhist chants, pretending to be solemn and dignified, asking her for the evidence, while secretly signaling Chao He behind him to destroy the evidence at any cost. Ye Yunshang pulled out a steamed bun from inside her robe, about to say, The evidence is inside this bun, when Chao He snatched it away. You angrily tried to reclaim it, but Shi Ming intervened, blocking the way. After a few moves, the bun was already swallowed by Chao He. This method of destroying evidence was utterly despicable. But once the evidence was gone, he would deny it to the end, and you would have no recourse. No matter what, you had to stay and clarify everything. At that moment, Shi Ming would pretend to help Chao He induce vomiting, using false evidence to send you all to your deaths. Ye Yunshang turned pale, tears streaming down her cheeks, desperately seeking help. The Tang Clan had become the Wulin's enemy. When she and her brother sought refuge with the Tang Clan, they had broken ties with old friends, and no one dared to help. In her desperation, she blurted out, Our ancestors, map, and so on. Upon hearing this, people immediately thought of Yue Wang's Treasure. What other evidence could there be? Anyone who saw it would change their mind. Only coins, only bribery. It's better to believe in the existence of such evidence than to doubt it. Greed sparked, and even those who had nothing to do with it rushed to chase Chao He, forcing him to reveal the evidence. The more people chasing this lie, the more credible it became. Even Shi Ming was left in despair, no longer having time to argue, shouting that the evidence belonged to him and fighting with the others. Ye Yunshang pulled you back, smiling cunningly. In reality, where was the evidence? She grabbed your hand and led her fellow disciples quietly down the mountain. This time, no one cared about Chao He's crying and begging. He was held down, savagely beaten, and force-fed emetics until even his bile came up, but where was there any sign of a map? Shi Ming was especially furious, thinking he had missed out on Yue Wang's Treasure, and his anger turned into a murderous intent. He drew a dagger from his monk's robe and disemboweled Chao He alive on the spot. This heinous act destroyed Shi Ming's reputation, and from then on, no one would believe his words.

Xiaoju, for all that she was a frail woman, moved among Kongtong's Four Gates and not only came away unscathed but earned genuine respect—naturally sharp-witted, with schemes to rival even the Human Path Dharma King's. Walking gracefully into the arena at your side, she had already mastered her temper and laid her plans. She knew full well that the Tang Clan and Kongtong together could never stand against the Wulin Alliance—defeat was certain. But that certain defeat held true only for the Tang Clan pitted against the Wulin Alliance; to escape the predicament, both sides need not be ruined. Wulin folk mostly acted on hot blood, quick to rashness and prone to following the crowd—if Shi Ming could stir the masses to his cause, why should she not do the same? So Xiaoju, like Lady Wen before her, began by using the Tang Clan's accumulated authority to intimidate the Wulin, cowing them with threat of force. But where Lady Wen's goal had always been to win respect and end in reconciliation with the Wulin Alliance, Xiaoju meant instead to deliberately stoke panic and fury, then turn that fire back on the one who had lit it. Seizing the initiative, she demanded Shi Ming as a hostage in exchange for the Tang Clan laying down its arms and submitting to questioning—otherwise the Tang Clan would rather die than yield, and every hero of the Wulin would be dragged down by one man's cowardice. It was precisely because Shi Ming feared death that he sought to use the Wulin Alliance's hand to destroy the Tang Clan; there was no higher purpose in it at all, only an attempt to hide behind the standing of Wulin elders and muddy the truth with fine words. Then Shangguan Ying suddenly stepped forward to stand at Xiaoju's side; the two exchanged a glance, understanding each other at once, and together laid bare the stakes, citing precedent and turning Shi Ming's own logic back upon him, their words never failing to hint at lethal intent. Shi Ming was driven back step by step, nearly coughing up blood on the spot—an eminent monk, reduced to cursing crudely before fleeing in disgrace. The onlookers, who had thought his fanning of the flames righteous and just, saw him waver and make excuses the instant the fire reached his own head, and came to their senses at once—furious, regretful, and ashamed, they cursed Shi Ming seven or eight hundred times over in their hearts, rued their own rashness, and fretted over what revenge the Tang Clan might exact in days to come.

Seeing which way the tide had turned, even the voices that spoke for the Tang Clan were too few against the many, drowned beneath the clamor of condemnation. Looking around at Fengyu Mountain, enemies met the eye on every side.

After speaking of the Tang Clan, he turned to Eldest Senior Brother. It turned out that on that day, he and Eldest Senior Brother had been ambushed while traveling together; he himself was gravely wounded and nearly died, but Eldest Senior Brother fought them off and saved him, then arranged for someone to treat his wounds. Eldest Senior Brother himself, still carrying his own injuries, went on to keep his appointment with Shi Gongyuan—and it was those very wounds that proved fatal in the end.
Shi Gongyuan, a plainspoken and forthright man, had also sensed something amiss about that duel. As he listened, he grew more and more alarmed, realizing he might have unwittingly struck down a good friend, and broke out at once in a cold sweat.
You and your fellow disciples were seething with anger, but the cacophony of voices drowned out your protests.
Before your journey to Fengyu Mountain, the fact that you had once been guests at Jinxiang Palace was seized upon and made into a grave matter.

All major sects expressed their positions, with both sides holding equal views. Shi Ming hurriedly rushed to Shangguan Jun, showing a look of flattery. Although Shangguan Jun had washed his hands in the golden basin, his family's influence still loomed large, capable of shaking the Jianghu. With just a word from him, the Tang Clan could be arrested on the spot. However, Shangguan Jun, deep in strategy, would not act on impulse. The Tang Clan and Jinxiang Palace were fundamentally different; they could not be crushed by public opinion alone. Thus, they firmly refused.

The major sects had made their positions known, and most sided with the Tang Clan. Shi Ming had not a shred of credible evidence, hoping only to exploit the panic and let rumor become truth through sheer repetition—his scheme was far too obvious.

The Flying Stone Gang had risen to prominence with astonishing speed, but for all their numbers, they were little more than a disorganized mob. They had come to the Wulin Assembly merely to gain exposure and cultivate goodwill. By rights, with so many eminent masters and elders present, Shi Gongyuan should have had no standing to speak at all. But seeing the Tang Clan surrounded, every eye among the great and orthodox sects gleaming with hostility as if blades might be drawn at any moment, something stirred within him, and he blurted out his support for the Tang Clan—whether or not they were truly in league with the Mud Cult, the Flying Stone Gang stood with you on the same side. The Tang Clan needed no flattery in its glory days, but in its hour of need, it deserved a helping hand. After all, hadn't he always owed a debt to your Eldest Senior Brother?
Fan Xiaotian found the Beggar Sect unreasonable and without hesitation, he took his dog and joined the Tang Clan, preparing for a major showdown.
Li Fugui ultimately chose to conform, considering the interests of the million Beggar Sect disciples.

Gang Leader Li, though taciturn, was a man of fiery spirit; otherwise, Wang Erzhuang would not have taken him as an adopted son and entrusted him with heavy responsibilities. On minor matters, he followed the old sect elders to solidify unity, but on major issues, he could not compromise. Otherwise, if the Beggar Sect abandoned righteousness, it would be equivalent to abandoning its dignity and could no longer claim to be a Hero. Therefore, he resolutely decided to support the Tang Clan.

The Beggar Sect friends who once competed with you over vegetables, sparred at the market entrance, and shared hot pot together belonged to the Dayi Branch of the New Faction. After Wang Erzhuang fell, power within the Beggar Sect passed into the hands of the Old Faction, and the Dayi Branch was ruthlessly suppressed—they dared not breathe a word of protest, for going hungry was the least of it; many had their limbs broken for less.
Now, seeing you at a disadvantage, they cast aside their own safety and stepped forward one after another to plead your case to Gang Leader Li.
Fan Xiaotian saw the situation as unfavorable and immediately caused a commotion. No matter how his uncle tried to persuade him, he refused to listen or pay attention.
The majority voice wanted the Tang Clan to stay and submit to questioning, but Gang Leader Li hesitated once more.
Seeing that most voices favored the Tang Clan, the Beggar Sect too resolutely threw its support behind them.
Both sides held equal sway in opinion, so the Beggar Sect took no stance either.
The Beggar Sect watched the situation, ready at any time to join the side with more people.

Since the Nangong Family had earned the reputation of "Heart of the Wulin," it had to remain scrupulously impartial. Newly appointed Family Head Nangong Shen dared not defy the ancestral teachings, and so the Nangong Family declared its support for the Tang Clan.
Shi Ming had expected that the Nangong Family's way of conducting itself would, as always, hew strictly to the middle path, offending neither side, and had never counted on their support. He had not expected Nangong Shen to speak of fairness while backing the Tang Clan, and flew into a rage, pointing at Nangong Shen and cursing him without pause.
But he had underestimated the Nangong Family. What they meant by impartial was remaining neutral only when both sides had merit, not blindly crediting slander.
Everything the Tang Clan had once done for the Nangong Family, every soul in the clan, from the eldest to the youngest child, remembered clearly.
They were merely good-natured in their dealings with the world—not fair-weather friends.

Nangong Shen personally hates the Tang Clan, but those in power most dislike stubbornness. The sea can hold myriad rivers; only by being inclusive can one be great. Naturally, one must accept the elders' advice.

Nangong Shen took over the position of family head, still needing the support of the elders, and couldn't act alone. He had to compromise by citing family traditions, insisting on impartiality. It seemed fair, but actually intended to first ease the tension of the Wulin people. He would wait for the situation to ease before defending the Tang Clan. Otherwise, even if you shout loudly, no one would believe you.

The Nangong Family is reputed as the Heart of the Wulin and mediators in Jianghu, always dealing with matters most fairly and justly. With the great unity as their ultimate aspiration, even though Nangong Shen personally dislikes the Tang Clan, since he has taken over as family head, he must uphold the family traditions. Even if you from the Tang Clan are indeed Demon Cult villains, he cannot let your fate follow that of the Jinxiang Palace.

Nangong Shen had only just taken up the post of Family Head and had yet to prove himself. The clan elders, each speaking up in turn, vied to assert their voices and sway the great clan's affairs. To win the elders' support, Nangong Shen had no choice but to go along with the tide, planning first to detain the Tang Clan, then work in secret to clear your name.

Nangong Yuan sacrificed the greater good for his own small gain: no sooner was he raised to Wulin Alliance Leader than he threw it away for a private affair, leaving the disgrace for his eldest son, the young master Nangong Shen, to bear. Nangong Shen was just then fretting over how to shift attention elsewhere when, like a pillow falling into a drowsy man's arms, someone handed him the perfect chance—make an example of the Tang Clan, and give the gossips a fresh topic after supper, so that the scandal of the Family Head's secret affair with the Human Path Dharma King would naturally fade from talk.

Kongtong and the Tang Clan, though not without old grudges, were equally grateful for your part in exposing Jinwu Shangren, and for that alone they could not repay kindness with enmity. But with the Sect Leader still undecided, strife among the four gates only grew fiercer; consumed by their own troubles, they could raise no new enemy, and so could only stand by and watch. Yet Sect Leader Wei spoke up with reasoned words—not to exonerate the Tang Clan outright, but striking at the root of the matter, to dissolve the very source of suspicion. If the Wulin Alliance let the Jinxiang Palace affair breed mistrust among its own, she said, that would betray the very purpose of the Wulin Assembly, harming the public good and private virtue alike—today it was the Tang Clan, but who would it be tomorrow? Hearing her say this, everyone exchanged glances, each growing more ashamed the more he thought on it.

Kongtong and the Tang Clan, though not without old grudges, were equally grateful for your part in exposing Jinwu Shangren, and for that alone they could not repay kindness with enmity. But with the Sect Leader still undecided, strife among the four gates only grew fiercer; consumed by their own troubles, they could raise no new enemy, and so could only stand by and watch.
Jinwu Shangren had waited for this day with unbearable anxiety. Could he possibly pass up any chance to annihilate the Tang Clan?

The four gates of the Kongtong Sect, which had feuded among themselves for years, suddenly stood united, howling at the other sects like men possessed, rolling up their sleeves and itching for a fight, each desperate to outdo the others in proving loyalty to the Sect Leader.
Sect Leader Xiang of Emei showed no courtesy at all, saying only one thing—that he trusted the Tang Clan—and stood behind you.

Emei's Sect Leader Xiang was also quite troubled. He rarely ventures out and remains untainted by the secular world, yet the secular world taints itself, and he couldn't help but utter a few polite words against his will, indicating he couldn't make a hasty judgment.
Sect Leader Xiang of Emei showed no courtesy at all, saying only one thing—that he did not trust the Tang Clan—and backed Shi Ming's demand to detain you.

Diancang Sect is the long‑standing archenemy of the Tang Clan, the greatest obstacle for Diancang's entry into the Central Plains. They have long desired to eliminate the Tang Clan, yet Diancang firmly believes that swords are instruments of seeking truth, and every formidable enemy is a test sent by heaven to temper one's mind and body. They must be respected, for to insult them is to insult oneself, causing the sword heart to become clouded and preventing the revelation of heavenly omens. The Tang Clan, without doubt, is the grinding stone sent by heaven to sharpen Diancang's sword, their most revered adversary. Especially since Old Sect Leader Tang's temperament is proud and aloof, he would absolutely never conspire with the Mud Cult.

Diancang Sect is the long‑standing archenemy of the Tang Clan, the greatest obstacle for Diancang to enter the Central Plains. They have long desired to eliminate you, but Diancang firmly believes that swords are tools for seeking enlightenment, and every powerful enemy is a trial sent by heaven to refine their minds and bodies. They must be respected, not insulted, for to insult them is to insult themselves. A clouded sword heart would prevent them from glimpsing heavenly omens, hence they refuse to comment.

The Diancang Sect is the Tang Clan's long‑standing rival, having clashed in conflicts large and small no fewer than a hundred times. Naturally they would not stand on your side, and at once echoed Shi Ming's words.
Even if you accuse Qingcheng of harboring the Supreme Bliss Cult's wickedness, it won't change his view. He believes you have misunderstood Qingcheng, and Shi Ming has misunderstood you.

Qingcheng has long resided in the Shu region and has had numerous dealings with the Tang Clan. Zou Bo, the Sect Leader, once fought side by side with your Sect Leader against the Seven Immortals of the Supreme Bliss Cult. Their relationship was relatively friendly in the past, and they have also had considerable dealings with the younger generation of today's Tang Clan. However they turn it over, they cannot believe you would be of the Demon Cult's ilk.

Qingcheng has long resided in the Shu region, having had countless dealings with the Tang Clan. Zou Bo, the Sect Leader, once fought side by side with your Sect Leader against the Seven Immortals of the Supreme Bliss Cult. Their past relationship was still somewhat friendly. However, Shi Ming was also a former associate of Sect Leader Zou, so they could not take sides, and thus remained silent.

Qingcheng has long resided in the Shu region and has had countless dealings with the Tang Clan. Zou Bo, the Sect Leader of Qingcheng, once fought side by side with your Sect Leader against the Seven Immortals of the Supreme Bliss Cult, and their relationship remained fairly friendly in the past. But now you accuse Qingcheng of harboring Supreme Bliss Cult evildoers, and today Qingcheng itself stands accused.
Guilty or wronged, Qingcheng will offer no comment.

Qingcheng has long resided in the Shu region and has had countless dealings with the Tang Clan. Zou Bo, the Sect Leader of Qingcheng, once fought side by side with your Sect Leader against the Seven Immortals of the Supreme Bliss Cult. Their past relationship was still amicable, and they know that rumors in Jianghu are not to be trusted. However, it's hard to judge the character of your younger generation of Tang Clan disciples, so they also advocated for you to stay.

The Tang Clan and the monks of the Songshan Sect once united to resist the Supreme Bliss Cult's dominance over Central Plains. The old abbot, who had not transcended life and death, was filled with great fear. Reflecting on his deceased fellow disciples who had sacrificed themselves for their cause, he often awoke from nightmares in terror and shed tears. How could he bear to see the reputation of the Tang Clan heroes besmirched? Therefore, while he could endure much, he could not tolerate this matter. He openly distanced himself from Shi Ming before everyone, and henceforth, the northern and southern courts of Songshan held no allegiance to each other.

After the Songshan Sect suffered a great loss of vitality, they ceased to concern themselves with worldly affairs and had little contact with the Tang Clan. Not knowing your character, and likewise unable to fully trust what Shi Ming said, they dared not speak rashly.

After the Songshan Sect's vitality was greatly damaged, they ceased to interfere in worldly affairs and had little contact with the Tang Clan. They did not know your character, but seeing Shi Ming insist so much, they hesitated and wished to ask you to stay and discuss in detail.
The Quanzhen Sect has an excellent impression of the Tang Clan and strongly disagrees with Shi Ming's statement.

The Quanzhen Sect had long heard of the Tang Clan's reputation and had always kept a respectful distance. Hearing this dispute, they found themselves at an awkward loss, and so chose to remain neutral.

The Quanzhen Sect has long heard of the Tang Clan's reputation and has always kept a respectful distance, not viewing you as enemies. However, please stop and clarify the matter; it will never be wrong.
Shi Ming incited the crowd with everything he had, trying to blow the matter into something far larger, dragging the Sect Leaders and Gang Leaders of every faction out to make them take a stand.

He used a clever trick to lure Shangguan Jun into revealing the ten‑day period, leaving him speechless with words, making him unable to change his mind. He intended to fabricate a pretext to detain the Tang Clan at Fengyu Mountain for several days before releasing them. Even with their high-level Qinggong, they couldn't escape the pursuit by the Wulin Alliance, and they would surely be destroyed on their way back. Shangguan Jun was stunned, then furious. He was not an easy man to deceive, but he hadn't expected his dog to bite him. Shi Ming believed he had eliminated a major threat, and Commissioner Shangguan would be pleased and let the matter pass. However, he didn't realize he had already stepped into his coffin. The Tang Clan may not have the time to deal with him, but the Shangguan family had plenty of time and energy to train their unfaithful dogs.

Song Bei and Shangguan Jun were in the hall debating whether to postpone the Wulin Assembly for another auspicious day or press ahead regardless, when word of the uproar brought them hurrying out. Seeing the scene, both were startled - how could one storm settle before another broke? If the Tang Clan's guilt were as plain as Jinxiang Palace's had been, there would be nothing more to say, but this whole dispute was of Shi Ming's own making. It was not that Shangguan Jun had no wish to move against the Tang Clan, but before setting out he had been expressly instructed by the Emperor to treat the Tang Clan with leniency, so as to show the court's magnanimity - and now here was Shi Ming, stirring the crowd against them at the very worst moment. Wasn't he all but forcing Shangguan Jun himself into defying the imperial edict? Shi Ming had never expected Shangguan Jun to shield the Tang Clan, and now he was caught astride a tiger he dared not dismount - his worry was not that the Tang Clan could not leave the mountain, but that the moment he himself did, the Tang Clan would seize and poison him. Yet even at the risk of offending Commissioner Shangguan, he had no choice but to grit his teeth and press on.
You fiercely refused, but your struggles were in vain; your Junior Martial Brothers and Sisters happily accepted the Tang Shan, and at the same time, they became even more hateful of you.
You gladly accepted, and Tang Shan finally officially joined the Tang Clan.
Tang Shan landed and walked toward you; even if it could not make up for his fault, it could at least be counted as laying his true heart bare.

You ground your teeth, and though you had not yet moved, in your heart you had already killed Tang Shan a dozen times over. Yet to your surprise, he had not opened his mouth to back Shi Ming, but to speak up for the Tang Clan. His reputation was spotless, his eloquence sharp, and his case so well reasoned that public opinion swung the other way. Twisting truth and falsehood together, he painted the Tang Clan as loyal, patriotic folk who had never once wavered in their allegiance, until even you, his fellow Tang Clan Disciples, began to feel a little uneasy. Shi Ming, standing on the ground below, was so furious he stamped his feet, but Tang Shan paid him no mind at all.

Suddenly, another unexpected guest flew in and landed beside Shi Ming. Upon closer inspection, it was none other than the Guangdong Tang Clan disciple Tang Shan, who had volunteered to accompany the Eldest Senior Brother to the appointment at Woyun Ridge but had vanished without a trace. Shi Ming was overjoyed beyond measure, for Tang Shan was a standout among the younger generation of the Wulin. If he also gave false testimony, the Tang Clan would be as stained as if they had jumped into the Yellow River, unable to cleanse their name. Tang Shan loved showing off, as on the day of the Tang Clan's internal conflict, he had first demonstrated his excellent Qinggong, flying up to the rooftop and using his internal skills to speak loudly.

Shangguan Ying, though she had once obeyed her father's orders and travelled with Shi Ming to back the Guangdong Tang Clan's power grab, had in the end made a grave mistake. Since then she had often recited sutras and prayed for the Sect Leader's health, aching that she had no way to undo it - how could she bear to err again? She now stepped forward without hesitation to refute him, admitting openly that the Tang Clan's civil war had been stirred up by her and Shi Ming together. Not only was Shi Ming caught utterly off guard, but when word reached Shangguan Jun, deliberating in the hall, it left him livid, his face turning ashen. Ever since Miss Shangguan had taken charge of the family's affairs, she had traded across the Jianghu and cornered no small share of profit - that much was true - but her word and her wares had never once come up short; she prized honesty above all, and was far more to be trusted than Shi Ming, this former abbot of Southern Songshan with nothing to his name.

Sect Leader Wei was furious at heart, yet his words remained calm and measured. Though softly spoken, they carried the force of profound Internal Skill, carrying clear across the hall as he publicly asked why the monks of Songshan stayed silent - did the Songshan Sect agree with what Shi Ming had said? Only then did the old abbot of Songshan realize he had been lumped in by default, and he hastened to explain that the northern branch of Songshan and the Fujian branch had governed themselves separately since their temples were founded, each keeping to its own affairs. The Songshan named among the Six Great Sects of the Jianghu meant the main temple, not the Fujian branch, and the two could not be conflated. Hearing this, the Wulin crowd finally understood: Shi Ming had come to the Grand Gathering alongside the Songshan monks, yet he spoke here for no one but himself, and not a single monk from his own Southern Songshan had come to stand behind him. This left Shi Ming's accusations suddenly awkward, and as the crowd fell to murmuring, his old face flushed red.
The Kongtong Sect, upon hearing these words, were even more furious than all your Tang Clan members. They all flung their sleeves, waiting for your command to carve this bald donkey into pieces.

At that moment, Chao He - who had once impersonated you and done all manner of vile deeds - stepped forward as well, loudly declaring that the Tang Clan was none other than the Demon Cult's Asura Path, swearing it so fiercely he seemed ready to stake the lives of his whole family on it. Ordinarily no one would believe the word of such a nobody, but with Shi Ming, the old abbot of Songshan's Fujian branch, testifying to it, the claim could no longer be dismissed. This venerable monk was known for his high moral standing - hadn't he just revealed the true face of the Human Path Dharma King moments before? In truth this old monk feared the Tang Clan and wanted it destroyed as soon as possible. Years earlier, Southern Songshan had once sheltered an enemy of the Tang Clan out of a moment's misplaced compassion. No one had expected Sect Leader Tang to hunt them down a thousand li to Putian, Fujian, where eighty-one knocks shook the monks to their very core; they sat in a circle chanting scripture until dawn before finally letting Tang Zhongling go. Afterward Shi Ming resigned as abbot - not because his heart had found peace, but because fear had curdled into hatred, and he was tormented by his inner demons for the rest of his life. Unable to shake the Tang Clan by his own strength, he had worked behind the scenes instead, drawing in the Guangdong branch of the Tang Clan and binding it to the Shangguan family to spark civil war within the clan - a scheme that failed at the very last step. Old Demon Tang fell, yet the Tang Clan still held the grudge against him. For a time, with troubles enough elsewhere, an uneasy peace had held, but there was no telling how long that would last; rather than let the tiger return to the mountain, better to gamble everything here and use the Wulin Alliance's hand to be rid of him for good. Everyone who walks the Jianghu longs, somewhere, to be a great hero admired by all - but wanting is one thing, and more often what people wear is a borrowed righteousness, hiding in the crowd, dressing their malice up as fairness. Those hurling insults at you might not even know who you are; his guesswork alone was enough to condemn you with a single word.

Venerable Golden Crow had remained low-key throughout the conference, his kind and gentle features betraying nothing as he stayed silent. Only now did he finally speak up in support, and on hearing that even the Kongtong Sect Leader had said as much, the Wulin crowd grew still more wary of your Tang Clan.

Although it was plain to all that you stood beside the righteous of the Wulin, Shi Ming still refused to relent, insisting that the Tang Clan was merely putting on a show. The remark left the crowd around them furrowing their brows.

Though it was plain for all to see that you stood alongside the righteous of the Wulin, Shi Ming still refused to relent, insisting that the Tang Clan was merely staging a show to distance itself from the affair. The remark left the crowd around them furrowing their brows. Fu Yun could scarcely believe it: Shi Ming had once served as abbot of Songshan's Fujian branch, had studied Buddhism for decades and spoke on the scriptures with total fluency, yet here he was, uttering such a forced, far-fetched claim.
Yet despite knowing full well that Jinxiang Palace was the Demon Cult's Human Path, you deliberately stood by and did nothing.
Yet even knowing full well that Jinxiang Palace belonged to the Human Path of the Demon Cult, he insisted on standing against the Righteous Wulin Alliance.
Clearly there was no evidence, yet he kept branding you heretics and devils.

Dharma Master Fu Yun startled, and hurried through the crowd to counsel this Grand Martial Uncle of Southern Songshan. But Shi Ming seemed dead set, iron-willed and unmoved, and though he plainly had no evidence, he kept branding you heretics and devils.
Just as your group was about to leave, Shi Ming suddenly leapt out again, climbed to higher ground, and called out, cursing you all as villains who could not simply be let go.

Miss Shangguan managed both the wine and the dishes. To silence the two disciples from the Cang Gang who were responsible for monitoring her, she spared no expense and offered a hefty reward of fifty years' worth of pay. The two members of the Cang Gang were both skilled experts appointed by the gang leader and had originally been loyal. However, Shangguan Ying's offer was simply too generous to refuse, and they felt compelled to help the young lady keep this matter under wraps, no matter what.

Today, as we part ways, it will be difficult to gather again in this lifetime. Shangguan Ying not only wishes to reunite with you and Kongtong's Mystic Skill Gate Leader Wei once more, but also hopes to take this opportunity to apologize to the Tang Clan for past grievances.

Today, once you part, it will be hard to meet again in this life. Shangguan Ying not only wishes to reunite with you and Xiaoju once more, but also hopes to use the chance to apologize to the Tang Clan for the past.
You called your Junior Martial Brothers and Sisters together, planning to head down the mountain and spend the night in Yueyang, then continue home the next day.

You and Nangong Qian may have some camaraderie, but it isn't your place to comment on another family's affairs. Going after him would be like smearing mud on the newly appointed Nangong family head's face—as a Tang Clan representative, you naturally couldn't ignore the weight of the situation.
You said nothing, turned and hurried after Nangong Qian, afraid he might do something rash.

As the representative of the Tang Clan, they went to express condolences to the Nangong family. Noticing that they were discussing family matters, it was inappropriate to intrude, so they waited quietly on the side. Nangong Shen, having just assumed the role of family head, immediately questioned his half‑brother. If it weren't for his greed for credit in reporting Jinxiang Palace, how could the Nangong family have suffered such repercussions, losing not only the position of alliance leader but also causing their father to die in despair, leading to a complete loss of reputation?   The one he referred to as Brother, Yuan Wuxian, was the infamous traitor of Emei, Yuan Chengfeng. This person had committed countless evils and had a notorious reputation. Although he had not been active in Jianghu for many years, if he had taken the time to remember the history of the Wulin, he would not have mistaken a villain for a benefactor. By publicly acknowledging a thief as his brother, how could this biological brother still show him any mercy? Thus, he ordered him to leave the Nangong family. His tone was calm, having exercised great patience, both to maintain face and to signal that there were no longer any expectations for Nangong Qian.

Painting Immortal called her over not for any other reason, just afraid she would forget to eat and drink. Before, fearing she would take her own life, he had urged her to take revenge; now, however, it's not necessary at all. Xiaomei finally wiped away her tears and laughed, her heart's hatred having eased by half. But this hatred would eventually have to be avenged, though not to the point of killing people. Today, those who forced Jinxiang Palace, when an opportunity arises, will all be pushed down the stairs.

Lady Wen remained calm and unruffled, boasting that she only needed to say three words for Xiaomei to not only abandon her murderous intent but also willingly surrender. Those three words were completely unreasonable, simply Oh, hehe, the Painting Immortal's signature strange laughter. Xiaomei trembled all over, charging forward with her blade but suddenly pulled her horse to a halt, nearly falling into the other's embrace. In that instant, tears filled her eyes, and with open arms, the Painting Immortal welcomed her, causing Xiaomei to leap into their embrace, overwhelmed with joy and weeping.

Lady Wen dismissed the attendants and spoke alone with Xiaomei. However, Xiaomei showed no trace of joy; her gaze fixed intently on Lady Wen, as if trying to pierce through her very essence. She instantly realized that the person before her was not the true Lady Wen, despite their identical appearance and bearing. This was clearly not Lady Wen. Among those in the world who possessed such adept skill in disguise, Thousand Lantern Tower was most suspicious. Xiaomei spoke frankly without reservation. Upon hearing this, Lady Wen also admitted freely. Xiaomei immediately harbored murderous intentions.

Considering the Tang Clan's reputation, the thanks should have been given after the gathering ended, not at this sensitive moment, to avoid arousing suspicion among the other sects. However, the Palace Mistress of Jinxiang Palace was eager to invite Xiaomei for a talk, so she had no choice but to come. Xiaomei had long wanted to probe the Palace Mistress of Jinxiang Palace's true intentions and agreed at once.

At this moment, a Jinxiang Palace attendant suddenly approached to pay respects, bearing a sorrowful and pitiful expression, and bowed gracefully to you, stating her purpose: we deeply appreciate Xiaomei's noble deed, for she risked her life to save us in our time of peril, and all the attendants are deeply grateful.

At this moment, a Jinxiang Palace attendant suddenly came forward to pay her respects, with a sorrowful and pitiful expression, bowed gracefully to you, and explained her purpose: grateful for the Tang Clan's great virtue, Jinxiang Palace had been able to escape calamity.

Jinxiang Palace suffered countless casualties, and no trace of the Painting Immortal was seen in the flames. You were especially worried about Xiaomei, but her expression remained calm, with hatred quietly churning in the depths of her heart.

She became suspicious, finally starting to doubt others, but unfortunately her suspicions were misplaced, as she suspected you of having designs on her purse. You rolled your eyes in disbelief. In truth, Long Xiang was just joking; she owed you too much, and it was no longer something coins could repay. You wanted neither her money nor her treasured sword; you had always been wholeheartedly devoted since you first met. An indescribable gratitude welled up in her, and her heart finally felt more at ease. Unable to help herself, she leaned closer to you, thinking she could happily see her master retire from Jianghu, yet it turned out to be the worst day of her life. In truth, her heart was in turmoil, and holding back her tears had taken all her strength, grateful that you were still in this world.

She became suspicious, finally starting to doubt others, though the direction was off‑she doubted your martial arts skills. Your rapid progress was suspicious, but the problem was you didn't even understand why yourself. Unconsciously, the once‑unreachable experts were now being caught up with, and techniques once considered flawless now seemed full of flaws. The only difference between you and your fellow disciples was that you were particularly unloved, having been an outsider for years without ever being allowed into the inner circle to learn the secret formulas. The Tang Clan Hidden Weapon General Principles' intricate techniques and Internal Skill were off‑limits to you, and you could only mimic them on your own. Only the Forgetful Form was worn out from study, memorized by heart. Long Xiang was skeptical yet intrigued, for the first time showing curiosity about techniques from other schools.

She had grown suspicious of everything, finally learning to doubt people — only in the wrong direction, suspecting you were some scion of the imperial family, just because you too bore the surname Zhao. You were quite at a loss for words; you actually wished she had guessed right, but fate had other plans — your ancestors were plain commoners, generations of farmers tilling the fields. Seeing you as unruffled as ever, at once exasperating and amusing, Long Xiang finally felt steadier, and couldn't help leaning closer to you. She had thought she could gladly see her master off into retirement from the Jianghu, yet it turned out to be the worst day of her life; in truth her heart was in turmoil, and holding back her tears had already taken everything she had.

Long Xiang stood among the Tang Clan crowd, feeling somewhat uneasy. She dared not return to Jinxiang Palace, fearing that the sight would stir painful memories, yet to go with you might bring future troubles, leaving her momentarily at a loss.

The intense battle has ended, with both sides suffering heavy casualties. The Tang Clan disciples are all shaken with lingering fear, secretly rejoicing that you didn't get involved in this mess, as winning or losing brings no real benefit.

You weren't unwilling to detain them for questioning, but your injuries were too severe. You've barely survived several near‑death moments, winning only through risky tactics. Pursuing further might be dangerous‑if they spot the signs, they could turn around and kill you, which would be a costly mistake. You sighed deeply and returned to the mountain to reunite with your fellow disciples.

Yuan Wuxian was the first to slip away, but the helper he summoned, Jing Hong, still scrutinized you, marveling. According to her, she had once been a Kongtong disciple, the chosen Direct Disciple of the Soul-Stealing lineage before Xiahou Lan joined the sect. Unfortunately, her pretty face had been marred, making her fierce and cruel. She had defected from Kongtong, no longer obeying the Sect Leader's orders, yet still harbored old grudges, determined to settle scores with the new Sect Leader.

Yuan Wuxian was the first to slip away, but the ally he'd called in, Jing Hong, stared at you, stunned, catching the shadow of Xiahou Lan in your moves. The moment she heard you openly admit to being Xiahou Lan's disciple, it all clicked into place; she clicked her tongue in wonder, smiled, and waved goodbye as she left.

You've fought to the point of exhaustion, yet the more injured you are, the stronger your fighting spirit becomes. He is skilled with a long staff; if he can control the area around him, keeping his enemies at a distance, then the outcome would be entirely in his favor. However, your small sword is extremely aggressive, closing in for close combat with each move perilous. Your attacks force Yuan Wuxian's staff to constantly retreat and defend, and even when he summons two hidden allies to fight you, they both fall to your skill, leaving you drenched in cold sweat. These two are both top‑tier martial artists, yet they still lose to you in a desperate situation. In this dire predicament, you prove your transformation and rebirth, now far surpassing your former self. In the Wulin, you are a martial artist who can be compared with the sect masters, and even if you haven't yet reached the peak of mastery, you are already remarkably strong.

You're so furious that even if you can't catch up with Nangong Qian, you'll still beat Yuan Wuxian to vent your anger; otherwise, this mountain monkey will think causing chaos comes with no consequences.
There's nothing to be done, one can only sigh and give up, hoping that after the storm passes over Fengyu Mountain, Nangong Qian's heart can find peace.

You were about to advise further when Nangong Qian had already fled. Yuan Wuxian blocked your way, making it difficult to catch up easily. With the Tang Clan junior disciples and their companions following you, you couldn't just leave without saying goodbye, truly in a bind.

Nangong Qian was overwhelmed by great sorrow and anger; you only defended without attacking, secretly alarmed. After a while not seeing him, Nangong Qian's martial arts had advanced so much that even disregarding the chaos and disorder of his techniques due to his fluctuating mood, his Internal Force alone was even more robust than yours.
Nangong Qian was overwhelmed by great sorrow and anger, his techniques chaotic and lacking structure; even if his strength had increased, he still wasn't your match.

Urged on by Yuan Wuxian, Nangong Qian killed you by mistake, and your death became one link in a chain of tragedies. Not long after, the Tang Clan sought revenge and killed Nangong Qian, breaking with the Nangong Family — and was itself annihilated in the Wulin Alliance's siege.

Nangong Shen, who had personally broken off their engagement, now feels another wave of jealousy rise as he watches Shangguan Ying laughing and teasing with you. He coldly accuses her of provoking him on purpose, but Shangguan Ying only finds it amusing, pays him no more mind, and pulls you away.

Nangong Shen, who had personally broken off their engagement, now sees Shangguan Ying laughing and joking with you, and a wave of jealousy rises unbidden in his heart, making him suspect she is provoking him on purpose. Yet he also feels it makes no sense — if he were meant to grow jealous, it should be over some fine young lord like Young Lord Rui, not someone who looks like you. The more he has to admit your worth, the colder his heart grows, sensing, however dimly, that Shangguan Ying has truly taken her heart back.

She does care about the Eldest Young Lord, even without any claim on him; after all, they were once classmates and childhood playmates. Since parting in Jiangling each had faced their own troubles, spinning like tops without pause, and without anything held tight, the faster they spun the more their hearts drifted, until they simply came apart. By comparison, she now cares even more about your feelings, and is loath to be misunderstood by you. Unlike the Eldest Young Lord, who cannot be scolded without starting a quarrel, being with you is far more relaxed — only you can pick out the care hidden in her words and patiently talk her round; even after a scolding you just turn around and smile, until she can hardly bear to be harsh with you anymore, and values you more and more.
You showed good faith by bringing up Xiaoju, and only then did Nangong Shen understand — she had invited you for a drink for the sake of Talented Woman Wei, out of necessity. That explained it.

Not wanting to disturb the two of them, you touched your nose and tried to leave, but were stopped by Shangguan Ying. She was such a perceptive person that just by looking at your expression, she could tell what you were thinking. With the intention of showing sincerity, she didn't hide anything from the Eldest Young Lord and openly admitted that she had made plans to drink with you.

Thus, after parting ways, you left. The former classmates, childhood companions, and unmarried partners parted ways upon the passing of Old Patriarch Nangong, and upon meeting again at the time of the Nangong Family Head's death, both felt deep sorrow. Had they not been without name or status, they would have embraced each other in tears. Nangong Shen had already begun to regret, but Shangguan Ying was resolute in her decision. No matter where their future paths led, she would never return to the Nangong family. She was like Lady Wen, iron‑hearted, bound by vows of life and death, and once abandoned, could never be won back.
Seeing her like this, a pang of pain struck your heart. You thought she could never forget the Eldest Young Lord, leaving no room for anyone else, least of all someone like you.
Shangguan Ying also heard the bad news and hurried to console Nangong.
You came to bid farewell and pay your respects. Nangong Shen, his face set stern, cupped his fists and saw you off.

You came to bid farewell and pay your respects; only you happened to catch Nangong Shen unguarded, his sighs impossible to hide from you. A thought suddenly struck you—perhaps he doesn't despise this half-brother as much as the world believes.

At first, every word out of Yuan Wuxian's mouth seemed to counsel Nangong Qian not to abandon himself to despair, to set his sights further, to break free of the Nangong family's constraints, and carve out a path of his own—making it hard even for you, who disliked the man, to find fault with him. But then his tone turned, and he suddenly began praising Nangong Qian for his righteousness in cutting down his own kin, for personally burying his parents, growing wilder and wilder with each word, dragging up grudges from the last generation that had been tangled long before any of you were born. Nangong Qian did not know Yuan Wuxian, yet Yuan Wuxian had hated him since childhood; through more than a decade adrift in the Jin Kingdom, from the day he learned his own parentage, there had not been a single day he did not curse you Central Plains heroes. It turned out the woman Nangong Qian had taken for his mother was not his birth mother at all, but Yuan Wuxian's mother. And Nangong Qian's true mother was none other than Lady Wen of Jinxiang Palace. All those memories rose vivid before him, leaving him no choice but to believe it. He had already been driven half out of his mind with grief after exposing the truth of the Human Path, which had ended in his father's death and his own exile from the family—and now, learning this new truth, his last thread of reason snapped. He had been loved all along, and with his own hands he had destroyed it. Nangong Qian looked half mad; no words could calm him. Though the sky was still bright, it was as if he had sunk to the bottom of the sea, crushing torrents of water rushing at him from every side, leaving him unable to breathe, able only to swing his blade wildly to protect himself.

You paid him no mind at all, dismissing him as no more than a mountain monkey's fart, and turned your full attention to supporting Nangong Qian. Ignored, Yuan Wuxian's face couldn't hide his displeasure, and inwardly he grew only more wary—your unruffled composure made you seem like just another small fish in the jianghu's shallows, yet clearly you were no such thing.
You glared at him, with Nangong Qian being the immediate priority, so you didn't argue with him. Yuan Wuxian, seeing that you didn't retort, laughed more mockingly and wildly.
You didn't let him have the last word either, snapping back with a sharp retort at once.

Nangong Qian broke from the crowd and fled weeping down the mountain, dazed and disoriented, his skill in the martial arts rendered entirely useless. When he was due to stumble, he simply fell and ate dirt. You hurried after him, meaning to offer some words of comfort, when Yuan Wuxian—who had vanished amid the earlier chaos—suddenly reappeared. Meeting you for the first time, with no grudge between you at all, he opened his mouth only to hurl insults.
Every family has its own troubles. Why do you insist on meddling? Nangong Shen couldn't help but sigh deeply, feeling deeply disappointed in you.

Danxiazi came to ask your wishes for what followed. Having received such great kindness from Kongtong, you now truly believed their loyalty ran true, and every last grudge against them dissolved into gratitude. With the propitious hour past, and blood already spilled, today's grand assembly could go no further. The Tang Clan had come as bidden and made its stance plain—it was time to withdraw while still ahead. Danxiazi agreed at once, turning to summon the Kongtong disciples to descend the mountain together with the Tang Clan.

With the propitious hour now past, and blood already spilled, today's grand assembly could go no further. The Tang Clan had come as bidden and made its stance plain—it was time to withdraw while still ahead.

Kongtong Sect's forces, under the command of the General of Daoist Law, fully supported the Tang Clan. They served as vanguard, provided cover, and took the rear guard, allowing the Tang Clan to retreat safely. Kongtong can be said to have made great contributions.

After all, when the many overwhelm the few, everyone is eager for glory. You followed the Wulin Alliance in laying siege to Jinxiang Palace. Few were hurt in the actual fighting—most were injured by their own comrades' jostling, which was no cause for pride at all.
This wasn't some miracle or stroke of luck—Jinxiang Palace's sword formation counted you among those it protected. You acted with honor, and they simply returned the courtesy.

The fierce battle ended, with both sides suffering heavy casualties. The Tang Clan had many injured, yet no one died. You were overjoyed, momentarily unable to believe it, and finally let out a big sigh of relief.

The fierce battle has ended, both sides suffering heavy casualties, the Tang Clan is no exception‑some have died, others are injured. It's not about defending the country or vying for glory, merely spilling blood to cool their hearts. You can't help but feel a sense of melancholy, realizing the weight of responsibility on your shoulders. It's no wonder the eldest senior brother refuses to take up the position of sect leader, no wonder the second senior brother is so strict, no wonder the third senior brother is always on edge, no wonder the fourth senior brother bids farewell and leaves.

The fierce battle has ended, with both sides suffering heavy losses. The Tang Clan is no exception. Brothers who laughed together yesterday are now separated by heaven and earth. It's not about defending the homeland or fighting for glory, is it? Their blood has been spilled, their hearts cooled, and is it truly worth sacrificing their lives? You can't help but feel a deep sorrow, realizing the weight of responsibility on your shoulders. No wonder the Senior Brother refuses to become Sect Leader, no wonder the Second Senior Brother is so strict, no wonder the Third Senior Brother is so nervous, no wonder the Fourth Senior Brother left in farewell. Quick revenge is but one side of the Jianghu, while regret and parting form the other.

You of the Tang Clan are masters of poison—how could you be kept in the dark? But speaking out would gain nothing: no one would believe you, and it would only give offense, so it's better to feign ignorance.

You of the Tang Clan are masters of poison—how could you be kept in the dark? But speaking out would gain nothing: no one would believe you, it would only give offense, and it would squander Lady Wen's painstaking effort, casting others in the wrong besides. Better, then, to feign ignorance.

You of the Tang Clan are masters of poison—how could you be kept in the dark? But speaking out would gain nothing: no one would believe you, and it would only give offense, so it's better to feign ignorance.

How could you, a Tang Clan master of poison, be kept in the dark? But saying so would have done no good—no one would have believed you, you would only have made enemies, and it would have wasted all of Lady Wen's careful effort, casting others in the wrong. So you feigned ignorance instead.
The poison fragrance Lady Wen had used was never truly lethal—only a powerful anesthetic incense. A single dose of the antidote restored one at once.

In their remaining days, they strolled unhurriedly along the green shores of Dongting Lake, chatting of small, everyday things. The wind was gentle and the sun warm, the perfect hour for a nap—except once they fell asleep, they never woke again. A pair of star-crossed lovers, twenty years of love and hatred between them, unable to fulfill their vow to grow old together, had found at last, in death, what they could not in life.

Finally, Lady Wen counted out the beats and let her strength fade note by note—this, too, was a secret code of Jinxiang Palace, telling her sister: it was time to say goodbye. The Painting Immortal gritted her teeth and suddenly struck with full force, driving Lady Wen back. Her white robe was stained with blood, her hair in disarray, like a wounded beast baring its claws, cursing foully and urging Su Yingxiang to strike the final blow at once. The Painting Immortal could not bear to see her proud, high-spirited sister debase herself so, and raised her palm to send her on her way—only for Alliance Leader Nangong Yuan, who had stood apart from it all until now, to suddenly step in and knock the blow aside. Everyone assumed his old soft-heartedness had gotten the better of him again and rushed to talk him out of it. The Painting Immortal steadied herself and, mimicking Lady Wen's habitual haughty, icy tone, rebuked him without a single false note—every word and inflection was the very image of the Palace Mistress of Jinxiang Palace the world knew. Lady Wen, by contrast, crawled over and clung to Nangong Yuan's leg, wailing 'save me, my dear' with heartbreaking cries, insisting she had always wanted reconciliation, that she longed to marry into the Nangong family, fawning shamelessly, like a stray dog thrashing in its death throes—not a trace left of her old cold, noble grace. Only Nangong Yuan recognized the true Su Yingxiang. He had longed twenty years to hear such words from her, and felt both sorrow and joy at once; he no longer cared who would rule Jinxiang Palace hereafter, his eyes fixed only on this precious woman from his past. Unsettled by his gaze, Lady Wen steeled herself, drew a hairpin, and stabbed herself with it, hoping to provoke him into rage—best of all, into killing her himself. But Nangong Yuan only reproached her for not being ruthless enough, drew his own hairpin, and plunged it into his own chest without hesitation, and both the true and false Lady Wen went pale with shock, as did everyone who witnessed it. Nangong Yuan then declared to the world that he was coarse and lacking in virtue, now beguiled by a woman's charms and unfit to be trusted, and so resigned as Wulin Alliance Leader, entrusting the Nangong family to his eldest son. Taking Su Yingxiang's hand, he walked away from all the clamor, and not a soul in the crowd could stop them; they all stepped aside and watched the two depart hand in hand.

Jianghu legend says that duels can open hearts. These sisters, in their first half of life, each served their own masters, clashing in battle, never believing in such superstitions. Of course, they could not hear each other's thoughts, yet every punch and kick seemed to express their resolve, with unparalleled clarity. Parting sorrow, gratitude, affection, longing, and hopes‑all resonated deeply in their hearts without a word.

Just as Nangong Yuan stood torn between two courses, and Shangguan Sun, growing ever more impatient, moved to end things swiftly by killing every poisoned soul before matters worsened further, a noblewoman in white suddenly used qinggong to leap into the field, holding a vial of medicine aloft, declaring that she carried the antidote and that no one need submit to the witch. Everyone stared in disbelief, certain their eyes deceived them—the woman before them matched Lady Wen in face, dress, bearing, and voice down to the smallest detail; not even twin sisters could look so alike, and standing the two side by side, no one could tell true from false. Yet one spoke with venom, holding the antidote over everyone's heads to force them to swallow poison; the other spoke with righteous conviction, offering to save everyone without asking anything in return. Whoever they were, people were far readier to believe the latter was the true mistress. And Lady Wen herself all but confirmed it: her face twisted with fury, as though the words had slipped out of her in desperation, exposing her own identity. From then on no one doubted it—they all took the newly arrived Lady Wen for the true Palace Mistress of Jinxiang Palace. She told them how she had been held prisoner beneath Jinxiang Palace by the Human Path Dharma King, and how even the people of Jinxiang Palace had been controlled through the Corpse Heart Pill and demonic sound. This witch, she said, meant to work her old trick again today and prey upon the heroes of the realm, but with her here, the scheme would never succeed. At this the crowd erupted in cheers. Even those who had just turned coat to beg for their lives now changed their tune, loudly proclaiming that they too had been beguiled by the demonic sound of the Human Path Dharma King and that nothing they had said should count. Lady Wen only laughed inwardly, knowing that from here on the attendants would need no defense of their own—these deceived, storied heroes of the Jianghu would fight to clear Jinxiang Palace's name for them. On the surface, though, she had to play the part of a schemer whose plot had unraveled, feigning fury and humiliation as she pointed at the Painting Immortal, disguised as herself, and hurled curses at her. Vicious as they were, every curse named Su Yingxiang by name—and so every one of them struck at herself. 'You wretched, shameless woman,' she cried, 'you should have died with honor twenty years ago!' and 'I spared your worthless life, let you cling on all this while, and still you show no gratitude—you slattern who'd bed any man!' Every word was a condemnation and a curse aimed at herself. The Painting Immortal, unmoved by the abuse, matched blows with her and the duel began.

The fuel for the fire was limited—once it burned out, no more than eleven could be poisoned senseless. Even if they seized hostages and broke through down the mountain, the people of Jinxiang Palace would still be cut down nearly to the last in the pursuit, and those who escaped would know no peace; once the Imperial Court or the Wulin Alliance put a price on their heads, they would spend their whole lives in hiding. Lady Wen, confident in her plan, only smiled calmly and told her attendants to drop where they stood and not rise no matter what they heard or saw. She alone stepped across the ring of fire, her once-dignified bearing gone, and threw back her head in a long, mocking laugh, jeering at the Wulin folk. She declared the poison was called Bone-Dissolving Poison Incense—as its name promised, without the antidote the bones would turn to pus and blood within two hours, leaving one a heap of rotten flesh for life, unable to live, unable to die. Just picturing it was enough to make everyone's hair stand on end, trembling with dread. Those with backbone still held their tongues sharp, cursing her and refusing to yield even unto death; those who prized their lives turned coat at once and began to beg for mercy, the sixth-rank Vice Magistrate among them. The others, untouched by the poison, she held hostage with the antidote itself, warning that anyone who came too close or displeased her would see it destroyed, dooming those already poisoned beyond saving. Lady Wen tossed the antidote about in her left hand while drawing out another poison in her right—none other than the notorious Corpse Heart Pill once used by the Supreme Bliss Cult to plague the Wulin. The young knew nothing of its horror, but those with any experience paled at the very name: swallow that pill, and even with the antidote for the fragrance, one became a puppet on strings forever after, a fate worse than death. And yet refusing the pill meant no life either—boneless, one became a useless husk, and who would want to live like that? So, knowing full well it was poison, they scrambled to pledge themselves to Lady Wen, willing to become dogs and horses for the Mud Cult.

Lady Wen seemed to have foreseen this calamity long before, for when she came to the gathering she had not kept to the mountain path but had instead seized the upwind position. Setting herself ablaze was only for show; her true, final scheme was only now about to be revealed. Even the people of Jinxiang Palace did not know their own sword sheaths and silk cords had been tampered with—either alone would have released only a harmless scent, but burned together they mixed into a poisonous smoke. Such a masterful use of poison came from no one else: it was your Tang Clan Second Senior Brother, who had arranged it in secret years before at Lady Wen's request. By the time anyone noticed, it was already too late; the poisoned fragrance rode the wind everywhere, and in moments a great swath of people fell. For a while, Fengyu Mountain rang with cries of anguish.

Yet no one's scheming ran as deep as Lady Wen's—to conspire with her attendants, she hardly needed to speak at all. The melody suddenly shifted, an unfamiliar note woven into the tune; no one but the people of Jinxiang Palace could tell the difference, and each of them, catching their mistress's hidden meaning, was startled and overjoyed. Lady Wen, it turned out, had long foreseen this very disaster and had already briefed the Painting Immortal beforehand. Only it was unclear why the Painting Immortal looked so troubled—speaking through the strings of a qin was, after all, no substitute for plain words, and left no room to haggle. The Painting Immortal seized on the roaring flames, crouched low, and picked at random a reckless Wulin swordsman who had charged the formation and been killed within it. Pressing his features into the clay beneath her own Human Skin Mask, she remade her face in an instant, stripped off her clothes for his, and shoved the corpse into the fire to burn. Then, feigning a daze, she screamed and stumbled out past the ring of flame; those who knew her saw only a face full of terror, hair singed, screaming and cursing, and none suspected a thing.

Among the Wulin folk gathered that day, no few still cherished chivalry and righteousness. Even though good and evil could not coexist, most only meant to capture the poisoned and question them closely, not to wipe them all out. But with the Imperial Court's word given and the crowd's mood running high, the trend was plain, and they could only stand by and watch. Hearing the music and catching the fragrance, they all felt a pang of melancholy and a wish to withdraw from it all. Several hot-tempered ones shouted a curse or two, and getting no answer, stalked off in disgust.

The people of Jinxiang Palace gathered together, sitting in a circle, following the palace master's orders to shatter the wooden sword sheaths, tear the silk ropes, and pile them up in front, then set them on fire. After all, they had already stepped away from the Jianghu, no longer needing to fight. Wiping away their tears, they each took out their instruments, accompanying Lady Wen's playing. The melody was melodious and sorrowful. At first listen, it seemed like whispered words from a secluded chamber, or the weeping of a child at midnight, as if one could faintly see a boat drifting through the rain over the river. The fine rain fell steadily, unable to be held back, dripping onto the heart. Twenty years had passed, and every glance up and down was filled with helplessness. The western window's candle had been cut to its end, yet there were still countless heart‑wrenching stories to tell. Carefully twisting tears into poetry, they strummed the strings to speak to you. This melody was not only Lady Wen's heart, but also the farewell poem of the palace's people.

Lady Wen gathered the attendants, seating them in a circle. Her white robes, like snow, were stained with mud and blood. Realizing her death was near, she grieved for her sister's recent loss and lamented her own frail fate. She could no longer hold back her tears, which mixed fear, a sense of wrongedness, and resentment.

Jinxiang Palace people gathered, and Xiaomei also came over, no matter how they tried to persuade her, she wouldn't budge. She had only this family, not something to be earned through effort, but an inherent kinship, an unbreakable bond. There was still time ahead, time to indulge in filial piety, to act spoiled. But heaven does not grant wishes. Just as they had opened a window for her, letting in the light of the sky, the sun set again in a moment, how could she accept this? The Painting Immortal knew she couldn't be cheered up. To keep her alive, they couldn't use the gentle persuasion they used with Long Xiang. Instead, they had to make her harbor hatred. As long as the enemy lived, she would relentlessly pursue them. After decades, when she eventually realized she had been deceived, perhaps she would no longer seek death or despair.

Lady Wen's final lesson for Long Xiang was not hatred. She came from the mud, letting rain wash away the dust, her white robe calm and serene, seeing the world with clarity yet not detached, full of feeling but not indifferent. Her strength couldn't reach all people, so she carefully guarded the heart of her beloved disciple. It was the same fleeting decades of life, and she hoped she would never be tainted by hatred, always smiling joyfully. Before departing, Long Xiang turned back three times, reluctant to leave, kneeling and bowing three times, then covering her face and leaving the home she had known since childhood, heading toward your direction.

Long Xiang wept silently, gripping Lady Wen's sleeve tightly, unwilling to part ways. Lady Wen smiled gently, smoothing Long Xiang's hair, and together they walked a short distance home, just like before.

The reigning Emperor Zhao Kuo wished to make peace with the Wulin, and so had to earn trust in the Jianghu. Before issuing the imperial decree, he specifically named the Tang Clan, instructing Shangguan Sun to show it special tolerance—at the very least, he was not to move against the Tang Clan at the Wulin Assembly, or every soul in the Jianghu would share the same peril. Shangguan Sun could only swallow his anger and warned you in a low voice that you would be wise to bow out while you were still ahead. Lady Wen let out a long breath of relief, and she too urged you to look after yourself. You had already done all that honor demanded; to persist further would only mean throwing your life away. Rather than drag them down with you, better to part ways now and leave a glimmer of hope for the world.

Lady Wen weighed the situation: the formation was broken, many palace attendants were dead or wounded, and she herself had suffered internal injury, making it hard even to use her Sound Wave Skill to turn the tide. The outcome, in truth, was already settled. She let out a deep sigh, yet remained composed, saying to herself that she could accept death, but was unwilling to die by blade or sword. If the Imperial Court and the Wulin Alliance could not tolerate the Human Path's people leaving Fengyu Mountain and meant to hunt them down to the last, then better to set herself ablaze and take her attendants with her—a death both dramatic and beautiful.

Lady Wen saw her beloved apprentice act, and instead of being pleased, she grew angry. She had barely managed to drive Long Xiang away to keep her safe, yet this innocent young woman still could not hold herself back and rushed home to die—how could she not be furious? Long Xiang had lost her father as a child and was raised by Lady Wen, who treated her like a daughter and showed her special favor; even her punishments were never delivered with the rod. No matter how much she tried to counsel her, Long Xiang would not listen. Lady Wen could not bear to see her go astray and was forced to strike her awake with a harsh blow. This palm strike, infused with Internal Force, landed heavily. Long Xiang, caught off guard, took the blow and was left internally injured, coughing blood. She staggered back several steps, her face aghast. Long Xiang was driven away once more, feeling as though the vast world held no place she could call home. She stood alone at a distance, not daring to approach, yet unable to bring herself to leave. That day Fengyu Mountain lay bathed in sunshine, but for the rest of her life, whenever she recalled it, she would remember only wind and driving rain.

Lady Wen saw her beloved apprentice act, and instead of being pleased, she was furious. She had barely managed to send Long Xiang away to ensure her safety, yet this innocent young woman could not hold her temper and rushed back to die, how could she not be angry? You immediately spoke up in her defense, giving Long Xiang a strong support, and she hurried to your side, eager to speak with confidence. She is now accompanying the Tang Clan to help, and does not fall under Lady Wen's jurisdiction. If Lady Wen wanted to chase her away, that would be overstepping her bounds. Lady Wen was both angry and amused. From now on, with you taking care of Long Xiang, she could finally resolve this long‑standing matter. Even if her death was approaching, she would still feel content.

Li Fugui fought an internal battle, ultimately choosing to sacrifice the small self for the greater self, taking on the task. He gripped the staff tightly, eager to end things quickly so Lady Wen would suffer no further disgrace. Yet just as he prepared to strike, a cold blade of light shot out from behind Lady Wen, slicing his weapon in two and touching his chest. Dazed, he saw Long Xiang already standing before Lady Wen with sword in hand, her face grim, flicking a drop of blood from the tip of her blade. Li Fugui recoiled in horror, certain he was already dead, but looking down he found himself unharmed, only a thin trickle of blood seeping from his collar—clearly the opponent had held back. Such precise swordsmanship had no equal under heaven, save for Jinxiang Palace's Soft Sword. Shocked and admiring, relief and shame mingled with a hundred other feelings; he dared not fight on, his legs too weak to stand for a good while.

The name of the Murderous Demon of Jinxiang Palace rang through the Jianghu. His own men had swindled and cheated her, tricked and conned her, and pilfered who knew how much of her wealth — the grudge ran deep. She might not know whom exactly to blame, but she would surely come for him, the Gang Leader, to pay with his life; of that there could be no doubt.
Ox-Head and Horse-Face he had never seen, but here stood the true Death God, clad in white. Should she ever move against him, the Beggar Sect would need a new leader before the day was out.
Li Fugui's face went ashen with fright; he backed away again and again — this was a job he dared not take, no matter what.

Li Fugui waged war within himself, and in the end chose to sacrifice the small self for the greater good, and shouldered the deed.
Long Xiang could never stand by and let her mentor be harmed — she stood before her mentor, sword raised, killing intent blazing.

Li Fugui was caught between loyalty and righteousness, and the only thing he could do was consult his own heart. His heart told him not to do it. Li Fugui turned around and walked away, leaving the act of killing to Shi Ming. Though Shi Ming appeared as a high‑ranking monk with no trace of compassion, he had no difficulty in killing the wounded Lady Wen. The real challenge was dealing with this fearsome evil spirit with a terrifying face. As he struggled, his condition worsened, and the even more terrifying Murderous Demon of Jinxiang Palace brandished a sword and leaped into the fray. He had no intention of even moving a finger, and to prevent himself from trembling, he even used his Internal Force.

Li Fugui indeed yearned to build his reputation, but that was to fulfill his adoptive father Wang Erzhuang's dying wish to care for the Beggar Sect members, ensuring they were not looked down upon, did not forget their dignity, and did not return to their former days as street rats. He could not help but recall his adoptive father's constant thoughts of Lady Wen, and deep down, he truly did not wish to harm her.

Shi Ming feared Li Fugui might be swayed by old sentiment, too soft-hearted to bring himself to strike — and in warning him, he cursed you along with him.
Though Li Fugui had stammered since birth and looked the simple, honest sort, he was no dumb ox or wooden horse to swallow whatever anyone said. The insult to you struck a nerve at once, and he shot back at Shi Ming with a sharp retort.
Had he not borne the weight of being Gang Leader of the Beggar Sect, and feared the Imperial Court's crackdown on its tens of thousands of disciples, he would sooner or later have taken his staff to crack Shi Ming's skull, and broken with Shangguan Sun besides.

Shangguan Sun was no military officer, and taking Lady Wen's life himself would draw far too much notice — the court was unlikely to look kindly on it. And ruthless as he could be, he had no wish to stain his own hands with an old acquaintance's blood unless truly forced to it.
So he sheathed his blade and handed this great credit to Li Fugui instead, signaling him to take Lady Wen's life as the Beggar Sect's pledge of loyalty, to wash the stain from their name.

The Kongtong Sect had numbers on its side, and a general skilled in the Daoist arts to direct them, so for a time it showed no sign of faltering. Yet they knew well that a lone hand could not clap — this could not last — and so they shifted from attack to defense, falling back around the palace folk and standing ready in tight formation.
Your Tang Clan had the heart but lacked the strength to turn the tide, and was beaten to a sorry state by the Imperial Soldiers and the Wulin Alliance working together.
Outnumbered and overwhelmed, their defenses were breached, and they retreated step by step.

Although the outcome was decided, a sudden scream shattered the battlefield. The white‑robed figure was drenched in blood, and one corner of the formation showed a gap. The stalemate, painstakingly maintained, collapsed at once. Shi Ming, the Venerable of the South Court of Songshan, and Li, the Gang Leader of the Beggar Sect, broke through the formation and entered the fray, bolstering Shangguan Sun's position.
