Jinxiang Palace's cause was all but lost, and Lady Wen tried to drive back her foes with her Sound Wave Skill, but her heart was in turmoil, her emotions assailing her, every note wounding herself. She could no longer hold back the bitter taste in her throat, and spat out a mouthful of blood — she had already suffered severe internal injury.

But a scream was heard, a white‑clad figure stained with blood, a gap appearing in the formation, the hard‑pressed balance collapsing instantly, Jinxiang Palace's fortunes now in dire straits. Lady Wen attempted to repel the enemy with her Sound Wave Skill, but her heart was in chaos, her seven emotions attacking her mind, each cry self‑inflicting. She could no longer suppress the bitter taste in her throat, spitting out a mouthful of blood, having suffered a severe internal injury.

However, Xiaomei's martial arts were precisely countered by the Shangguan family's skills. The Wave Riding Technique was specifically designed to disrupt Qinggong. If they faced each other, Xiaomei couldn't even fight if she wanted to, as her fast attacks couldn't be unleashed, and she would be killed within two rounds by the blade. Xiaomei sacrificed herself to help, but how could Lady Wen let her die for nothing? She called her over, gave her some instructions, and sent her away. Shangguan Jun remained calm and patient, carrying a Blade and silently waiting, fulfilling the old year's offerings.

Although the outcome was decided, a sudden scream shattered the battlefield. The white‑robed figure was drenched in blood, and one corner of the formation showed a gap. The stalemate, painstakingly maintained, collapsed instantly. Shi Ming, the Venerable of the South Court of Songshan, and Li, the Gang Leader of the Beggar Sect, broke through the array to enter the fray, bolstering Shangguan Sun's position. Jinxiang Palace's cause was all but lost, and Lady Wen tried to drive back her enemies with Sound Wave Skill, but her own heart was in turmoil, her emotions assailing her, each note wounding herself. She could no longer contain the bitter taste in her throat, and spat out a mouthful of blood, already suffering from severe internal injury.

Ahead stood a formidable foe, and behind him you jeered on, ever the sardonic troublemaker — Shangguan Sun was caught between advance and retreat, truly a dragon in shallow water, toyed with by shrimp.
Ahead lie formidable foes, and behind you comes someone wielding a small sword, advancing slowly as if a death‑dealing King Yama.

With strong support at her side, the situation turned in Lady Wen's favor almost immediately. Using her Sound Wave Skill, she performed a melody titled 'Xianlv Gong: Nezha Order: Dragon Roaming Shallow Waters.' This piece seemed specifically crafted to target the characteristics of Shangguan Blade Technique, deliberately inducing him to lose his rhythm. The continuous flow of her intent was disrupted and struggled to manifest fully. Even as the Dragon King Blade stirred the turbulent waters of the river, it still failed to keep up, being relentlessly pressed back by the female adversaries who had been looked down upon. Lady Wen could now move closer without interference.
The Painting Immortal, freed at last with your help, meant to hold Shangguan Sun back with all their strength, so that Lady Wen could play her pipa — the tide was bound to turn.

At this moment, you have finally arrived late, crossing a small sword on your chest. This time, fighting the Shangguan Family Head isn't just about humiliating him; it's truly a matter of deciding to fight to the death.
At this moment, you have finally arrived late, holding a small sword at the chest, not only for Jinxiang Palace but also to seek justice for the sect.

Long Xiang feared that the Junior Martial Sister, having never practiced the Jinxiang Palace Internal Method, might not withstand Lady Wen's sound waves and thus be unfit for the guardian's role. Unbeknownst to her, the Junior Martial Sister's Heaven and Earth Silent Power far surpassed even the Mysterious Candle Heart Sutra. With unwavering focus, she rendered the world around her utterly silent, so that Sound Wave Skill had almost no effect on her at all. No one was better suited to guard than she.

Junior Martial Sister landed lightly beside Lady Wen and, without a trace of hostility, urged Shangguan Sun not to do this. Seeing her, he could not help but freeze, for a moment taking her for an old friend returned from the dead; then he shook his head with a bitter smile and shook off the fancy, silently resenting how Lady Wen's pipa could so unsettle a man's heart.
Although there's no Sheng Xue as a partner, if she tries a bit harder, it's still okay.

There was no Sheng Xue to pair with her, but there was Xiaomei. Seeing Long Xiang arrive, Xiaomei let out a breath of relief - she was terrifying as a foe, but no comrade was more reassuring than Long Xiang.
Long Xiang, in the nick of time, wheeled her sword about and took her stand at Lady Wen's side.

At this critical moment, Xiaomei arrived. She knew she was no match for Shangguan Sun, but threw herself into several rounds of rapid attacks all the same, enough at least to keep the Shangguan Family Head too occupied to trouble Lady Wen. If she could turn the tide, she would gladly burn away her remaining years for it.

Over there, Lady Wen faced off against Shangguan Sun. She was highly skilled at channeling her Internal Force into the Sound Wave Skill, whose reach and impact were no less than a duel fought with naked blade and spear - but close combat was not her strength, and she could not manage without palace guards at her side. Mingyu, the Painting Immortal, Long Xiang and Sheng Xue had each mastered paired attack-and-defense techniques with silk and sword, making them the ideal guards, but not one of them was present now - only two junior disciples, their skill still shallow, struggled to hold the line, tossed about by Shangguan Sun's blade and spitting blood before both fell defeated. Lady Wen's peerless mastery had no room to unfold, and she was left at his mercy.
You defeated Nangong Shen but did not deliver the killing blow. Nangong Shen, his face utterly lost, hated you bitterly enough to grind his teeth, without a shred of gratitude.

You defeated Nangong Shen in a life‑and‑death battle, reaching out to help him up as if two friends sparring, without any lingering animosity. He could no longer stop you, watching you run toward the next formidable enemy. A quiet, unspoken passion stirred within him, a desire to follow your steps, stand by your side, and fight together against common enemies. If only he hadn't been born into the Nangong family, perhaps joining the Tang Clan wouldn't have been so bad.

To you none of it made sense. If you accepted his reasoning, the Wulin would be nothing but a game of mutual flattery, with chivalry gone from it entirely. No wonder the Sect Leader held such 'righteousness' in contempt - standing apart from the crowd was not arrogance, but a refusal to hedge and second-guess, to twist one's own will out of shape. Nangong Shen had no answer for this; he understood your thinking, even agreed with it. But he spoke for everyone who shared his view and could not easily back down - a clash between the two of you was inevitable.

Nangong Shen lived up to his name, deep and calculating; unlike others, his refusal to tolerate Jinxiang Palace was no hot-blooded impulse but a reckoning with a far more distant future. Even knowing Jinxiang Palace was innocent, he had to steel his heart and cut his losses, lest the tiger return to the mountain and drag every soul in the Wulin into calamity - once they became a thorn in the Imperial Court's side, no one's days would be easy again. To his mind, this was a sacrifice the greater good demanded.

Pressed so hard, you had no wish to hide the truth - beyond simple justice, you could not deny there was some private feeling in it too, and you very nearly let slip your unspoken love for Long Xiang. But to your surprise, the Eldest Young Lord's face cleared with sudden understanding, as though it all made sense to him now: since ancient times heroes have stumbled at beauty's door, and hunger and desire are simply human nature - he himself had once wronged his own betrothed for a woman he loved and borne the world's scorn for it, so of course he could forgive you too, and his anger toward you drained away at once. Only for the sake of the Wulin's greater cause could he still bring himself to wrong you, forced against his will to stand as your enemy.

Nangong Shen was furious at your betrayal, struggling to suppress his anger as he asked, Are you a member of the Mud Cult? Why did you assist the demon woman of Jinxiang Palace? Are you entranced by her beauty?

The Painting Immortal did not just calculate this in her mind - she said it plainly aloud: with your skill, you should be able to hold your own against the Eldest Young Lord. Even if you don't win, you won't be beaten outright. And even if you are beaten, you won't die; and even if you die, it's no great loss - so the Eldest Young Lord is yours to deal with. She then went off to help Lady Wen.
Nangong Shen loathed you, feigning contempt though in truth he was quite wary of you; seeing you arrive, he could not help but feel troubled.
Nangong Shen initially thought you were there to support him, his eyes lit up with joy, but soon realized he had misunderstood, and his heart sank instantly.
You entered the formation and saw Nangong Shen facing off against the Painting Immortal.

At that moment, the Junior Martial Sister burst into the formation. Before the Eldest Young Lord could react, she borrowed his own cloak and dove into his blind spot; the Painting Immortal, taking her for an enemy, reached out to seize her, but Junior Martial Sister kicked off and bounced clear again, turning the trouble aside so that Nangong Shen had to meet the Painting Immortal's strike himself - and in that instant she slipped past them both and made her escape. It all happened in the space of a breath, as smooth as if the three of them had rehearsed it. The Painting Immortal, whose own lightness skill was formidable, could not help but marvel: this girl's footwork was far more than mere Qinggong! She had used Nangong Shen's own cloak against him, then goaded the Painting Immortal into striking so that the blow fell on him instead - she had all but made a hidden weapon of herself. Was this not the Chapter on Forgetting Form made flesh?

Long Xiang entered the formation, and the Eldest Young Lord knew things were about to go badly. He could parry the Painting Immortal's soft, deceptive moves well enough, but he knew Long Xiang's skill for what it was - hard and soft combined, needing no clever tricks; one stroke of her sword and fan, cloak, even the man himself would be cut clean in two. Just as he moved to strike at her resolve, invoking her father's name to freeze her in place, the Painting Immortal seized the gap in his words to launch a covert strike of her own, only for Long Xiang to get in the way, leaving him momentarily stunned. Long Xiang was no traitor; she was simply helping Jinxiang Palace in her own fashion, and precisely because the righteous had misjudged her, she could give them no further grounds for slander - she had to act in the open, or she could never be true to heaven and her own conscience. The Painting Immortal laughed despite herself in exasperation - even at this life-and-death juncture, Long Xiang could still be so naive. She hurried to send Long Xiang off to help Lady Wen, dreading what other foolish thing she might say and afraid it would be the death of her from sheer aggravation. Little did they know, Nangong Shen had already been deeply moved; unable to hide his shame, his fighting spirit largely spent, he stood there lost. The Nangong clan could always be counted on to be driven half out of their minds by anyone surnamed Long - twenty years ago it was the father, and twenty years later, the same for the son. He was merely a man of deep and guarded schemes, but a man of chivalry all the same; he took the debt to heart and secretly vowed that even if Jinxiang Palace fell, he would keep her - Long Xiang herself - safe, and one day lend the Nangong family's reach to guard her path through the Jianghu. Besides, she was both delicate and spirited, a rare beauty in her own right; if the sole daughter of the previous Wulin Alliance Leader were to marry the legitimate son of the present one, would that not make a fine tale? The longer he dwelled on it, the more he liked the idea, until a smile crept across his face.

Xiaomei entered the formation and, without a word, launched a fierce attack on Nangong Shen; the Painting Immortal wasted no time talking either, striking out in perfect concert with her. In an instant dozens of clangs of blade on blade rang out almost as one, the attacks eerily fast, the defense eerily flawless. Xiaomei and the Painting Immortal, their true qi spent, sprang back one after another for fear of a counterstrike, both astonished at heart: the Nangong family's reputation was no exaggeration - their own strikes had come so fast that even they themselves could barely follow them, and yet the Young Lord had taken every one, without a scratch from head to toe. Little did they know, the Young Lord himself was just as astonished, thinking privately how these two women could strike with such ferocity, every blow aimed at a vital point - one slip and it would mean instant death for him. By then he had no time left to counter move for move; he threw everything he had into defense, calling on every guard his fan and cloak could offer, yet even that was not enough to withstand the joint assault of two generations of Thousand-Faced Demons. The true miracle was his pauldron. It was the pauldron, forever in the way, that knocked Xiaomei's hand aside as it swept for his throat, and that snagged the Painting Immortal's silk cord as she tried to loop her golden bell around his chin - unseen, it had shielded most of the threat to his upper body, and only by its grace did he escape unscathed, a cold sweat soaking through him. The Painting Immortal longed to go to Lady Wen's aid, but fearing Xiaomei alone was no match for Nangong Shen, she could only send Xiaomei ahead and stay behind herself to hold him off.

Over here, the Painting Immortal of Jinxiang Palace was clashing fiercely with Eldest Young Lord Nangong. Though the Painting Immortal's martial arts were superior by more than a margin, her style emphasized evasion and defense, while the Nangong Family Teachings prioritized protection, with nine defenses and one attack. When fully defensive, they were impenetrable, and even the formidable Painting Immortal could not overcome him.

And you led the group to attack from the rear, carving through the tide of people, arriving alone at the front of the Jinxiang Palace formation. The people of Jinxiang Palace were both startled and delighted; trials reveal true feelings. Now, despite your unattractive face, you are more appealing than those chivalrous young heroes and young lords. Opening the gates to welcome you into the formation, you are their hope.

Junior Martial Sister stepped on a palace attendant's head, leaping with several bounds to the front of the formation, saying only, I'll help you all, before darting onto the palace attendants' sword edges and vanishing into the formation. The crowd stared in disbelief; none dared to stop her, for who could possibly block her?

Long Xiang wielded her sword, forcing the crowd aside and rushing to the front. She ignored her sisters' attempts to block her, forcibly breaking through the formation. Her sisters couldn't actually strike her with their swords, couldn't block her, so they had no choice but to let her go.
Xiaomei let out a cry, and the Jinxiang Palace attendants without hesitation opened the door to let her through.

Jinxiang Palace's ladies, relying on the ingenious array formation, did not fall behind for a moment. However, with the Wulin Alliance having such numerous people, they gradually felt at a disadvantage without Lady Wen's assistance with her Sound Wave Skill.
Danxiazi immediately guessed your intention and led the Kongtong disciples of all Four Gates into the array to answer the call.

You have decided to support Jinxiang Palace, which is clearly going against the Wulin Alliance and the court. Although the junior disciples of Tang Clan did not lack compassion, they all found it hard to be willing to risk their lives for this. Many of them were already looking for ways to sneak out even before taking the field.

You have decided to follow your conscience and support Jinxiang Palace, clearly setting yourself against the Wulin Alliance and the court. Even if you survive this peril today, endless trouble may follow in the days ahead, but the light of your humanity will shine all the brighter for it. Your Junior Martial Brothers and Sisters of the Tang Clan are not without fear of death, yet they are glad you did not choose to smother your conscience just to survive.

You immediately issued orders to align with the righteous Wulin Alliance. The Tang Clan members were already boiling with passion, eager to pull off a big operation to gain fame and establish their reputation.

You decided to align with the righteous Wulin Alliance to protect the Tang Clan, although this left your Junior Martial Brothers and Sisters greatly disappointed. Still, it was understandable enough—who doesn't have some selfish wish to go on living? Even if it goes against conscience and principle, life can still be lived.

You are even surprised by yourself, though heartbroken, but when weighing against the greater good, letting go of Xiaomei seems less difficult than imagined. The person you once loved more than life is no longer in your heart; you can have another lover.

You are grievously wounded in heart and mind, desiring to share life and death with her. But it cannot be, for you have already made a decision to safely bring your Junior Martial Brothers and Sisters back to the Tang Clan; they are all your responsibility.

Xiaomei isn't like you, burdened by so many hesitations. To her, distinctions between right and wrong are as foul as a fart, something she has always treated as a joke. She is most loyal to people rather than matters, biased to the extreme. If you are in trouble, she would risk anything for you. Now that her only remaining relative is in grave danger, she wouldn't hesitate to kill or destroy. This journey is likely to be fatal, so she specially comes to say goodbye. If you find her amidst the dust, hope you can cremate her body and scatter her ashes to the wind, so she can truly become a Flying Heaven and be free.

It's not that you lack spirit, but when everything unfolds, you remain as calm as still water. In truth, you carry too much trust from others, so you dare not act recklessly. You can only remain passive, not helping either side.
Danxiazi immediately guessed your intention and led the Kongtong disciples of all Four Gates into the array to answer the call.

Long Xiang faintly sensed that another important person was about to leave, terrified to the point of losing herself, her grip on the sword unsteady. She longed to stay with her palace sisters and help them, but her master forbade it, fearing she might perish in the chaos or align with the Mud Cult, tarnishing her father's honor and leaving him restless in the afterlife. You've never seen her so disoriented, like witnessing her former self—timid, weak, and homeless, wanting to flee yet unsure where to go. How much determination does it take for a person to become brave, you know better than anyone. Until you can walk with your head held high, the Tang Clan will be your shelter, and now she has you. From your simple words, Long Xiang found immense encouragement; her heart pounded, warming her blood through her body. Though caught in confusion, she hasn't yet grasped everything, but if she lets her master and sisters face the chaos alone, she'll regret it later. So she must go now. You don't need to issue orders; your Junior Martial Brothers and Sisters have already followed her raised sword to the battlefield.

But these stories were known only to himself. Twenty years of time, torn away page by page, were cast into the fire, smoldering quietly like a covered tinder-roll that never quite went out, ready to flare back to life at the first breath of wind. Thinking of old ties, he might have shown mercy where interests did not clash; but now the outcome was plain to see. At a single command, the Imperial troops raised spear and blade, surrounding Jinxiang Palace's rebels, and the Wulin's own were not to be outdone, each unleashing their finest skills against Jinxiang Palace's people.

At that time, Shangguan Jun was a dandified young lord, often bullying her with his playmates. Su Yingxiang, due to her training at the music house, was timid and fearful of this wealthy young lord, believing she could never escape his clutches. After they both grew up, Su Yingxiang became increasingly beautiful and talented, renowned far and wide. Shangguan Jun regarded her as a forbidden treasure, frequently pressuring the music house to obtain her. Su Yingxiang gave up resisting, accepting her fate. However, a young hero, Nangong Yuan, rescued her with a heroic act, leaving behind a fan with lingering fragrance, winning her heart without ever meeting her face-to-face. His promise remained unchanged for twenty years. Only then did Shangguan Jun realize that he had been utterly disliked; what he considered favor was, to Su Yingxiang, a humiliation. A nobleman of a prestigious family, he reformed himself completely, subdued his arrogant nature, practiced martial arts, recited scriptures, and worshipped Buddha. All the rare treasures that Nangong Yuan could not obtain were painstakingly presented to Su Yingxiang, yet they were all rejected as vulgar. He envied Nangong Yuan, yet had to feign agreement, hoping to change Su Yingxiang's opinion. Unfortunately, his dream ended in vain. Su Yingxiang could not marry Nangong Yuan and refused to accept him, eventually becoming Lady Wen. From then on, Shangguan Jun lost all interest in love and never took a wife for the rest of his life; even Shangguan Ying's mother was never more than a plaything in his hands. Memories of the past surfaced and then faded, for she no longer remembered them. To Commissioner Shangguan, they were no longer important.

For Shangguan Jun, it seemed there was no need for hesitation in either public or private matters. The Vice Magistrate of Yuezhou, who was originally not invited and at most would have assisted, suddenly pushed forward, shouting for everyone to stop. Although he was only sixth rank, one level below Song Bei and Shangguan Jun, and this matter was not even his to handle, so there was more than a little overstepping in it, he was an official sent down from the capital to Yuezhou and thought highly of himself, thinking nothing even of the Magistrate, let alone looking down on mere Jianghu folk. Meaning to let Shangguan Jun feel his weight, he forced his way to the front on the strength of his office and threatened Shangguan Jun: if he dared defy the imperial edict and act on his own authority, he would surely be impeached for it.  Shangguan Jun was a local magnate with both wealth and power, all but a king unto himself in Fujian, and had never wanted to dirty his hands with Jianghu affairs; he had not even wanted to be Wulin Alliance Leader. To be impeached for plotting rebellion and collusion with the enemy, and so fall under the emperor's suspicion, would surely cost him more than he gained.  His ties to Su Yingxiang went back further than Nangong Yuan's did; the two of them had known each other since they were small children.

Lady Wen gave the command, and the array opened a gate, letting Shangguan Jun and Nangong Shen in together; it at once shifted and closed in. The array was complete both within and without—easy to enter, but to leave again was as hard as scaling heaven.  Shangguan Jun was a wulin elder who had weathered many storms, while Nangong Shen, gifted in both letters and arms, was a rising star of the new generation with the bearing of a great general. Deep within the encirclement, neither showed the least sign of fear, and all present silently applauded them.  The three conversed loudly from within the array, deliberately letting everyone present hear, to show they dealt openly and fairly.  Lady Wen asked outright what monstrous crime Jinxiang Palace had committed, that the court and the Wulin Alliance were so bent on hounding them without mercy.  Shangguan Jun, seasoned in official circles, could hardly miss the needle hidden in Lady Wen's words; she seemed intent on driving a wedge between the court and the Wulin Alliance. If he could not answer clearly, the consequences might be dire.  The two sides still circled each other, testing with evasive words, while Nangong Shen, eager to prove himself, spoke each word ringing and firm, but his delivery lacked polish. He never expected that Lady Wen was simply waiting for him to tear through the last pretense, so she could seize on his own words and calmly refute them one by one, turning the threat back on the righteous factions of the Wulin: if the two sides could not come to terms and truly broke, her palace women could hold this array for a time even as their strength failed, and all the while she would strike up her lute and use her Sound Wave Skill to strike down her foes. Anyone whose Internal Skill and composure were not equal to it would, even if not driven mad on the spot, suffer ruptured meridians and lasting harm never to be cured.  The Jianghu had long held a saying: true feeling or false, the lute reveals the heart. Lady Wen's Sound Wave Skill was famed throughout the Jianghu, and not one hero present took it for an empty threat; not a few had felt its sting firsthand.  For anyone hoping to wed a woman of Jinxiang Palace, no matter who, must first sit through a tune from Lady Wen's lute.  Those who heard it without sufficient Internal Skill and composure would fall into illusion that stripped bare their true nature. Lightly affected, they might dance and caper in shame; severely affected, their meridians would be damaged and their qi run wild, leaving them scarred for life.  Everyone had assumed they had the enemy surrounded and could count on numbers to secure an easy victory.  They never imagined the threat would be turned back on them, and every face changed with sudden fear.  If the Wulin Alliance took heavy losses, its name would survive while its substance did not. As for the Imperial troops whose skill fell short, not one of them stood a chance of living.  If the Imperial troops were wiped out at Fengyu Mountain, the throne would surely lay the blame on Shangguan Jun for bungling the affair, and that would end in the worst outcome of all, with no victor on either side.  But such a ruinous stalemate was not at all what Lady Wen wanted.  The righteous heroes of the Jianghu had shown no mercy first, yet Jinxiang Palace could not bring itself to answer injustice with injustice; though clearly holding the upper hand, they chose to lay down their weapons and surrender.  The Mud Cult's Hungry Ghost and Hell Paths were notorious, but the Human Path carried no such infamy, and its mysterious membership meant the court had never put a price on their heads. So what Lady Wen offered was not truly a surrender at all, but a change of allegiance.  Everyone had braced for a fierce battle at the end of the talks; instead, they heard Lady Wen cow the assembled heroes with only a few words, then abruptly announce her surrender. The swing of feeling was so violent it was like soaring to the heavens and plunging to the earth in a single breath—no one could say what they felt.  Anyone with a shred of conscience could not help but feel shame on hearing it, and deep down began to ask themselves: was the Mud Cult truly beyond all forgiveness? Had they merely echoed what others said, condemning an entire boatload for the sins of a few?  Only the few who were shrewd enough never to let their guard down grew more alarmed the longer they listened, until cold sweat ran down their backs.  With Lady Wen's learning and foresight, once she changed allegiance, offering up her array to the throne against foreign threats, and having the Mud Cult pacified to steady the realm, what merit that would be! With the Mud Cult removed, Song territory would hold no more hidden dangers; and if one insisted a danger still remained, it would be the so-called righteous factions of the Wulin themselves.  The knight-errant defies the law with the sword, and the throne cared nothing for whether one was good or wicked; it kept a wary eye even on the generals of its own appointing, so how could it tolerate bands of Jianghu commoners gathering to practice arms and threaten its rule?  By then it might no longer be the court courting the Wulin Alliance to wear down the Mud Cult, but the righteous and the wicked reversed entirely, with the court using the Mud Cult to annihilate the Wulin Alliance instead.  Neither overbearing nor servile, she showed both her strength and her goodwill, while in truth stirring up discord between court and Jianghu, without spilling a drop of blood, meaning to kill with a borrowed blade.

You may want to keep her, but at this moment, her identity is too controversial. She is both the descendant of a hero and suspected to be a follower of the Demon Cult. If you were to take her in, it might jeopardize your fellow disciples. Long Xiang has a deep friendship with you, and the safety of your Junior Martial Brothers and Sisters is equally important.

You caught her by the arm. If the Tang Clan doubts her, then you'd sooner leave the Tang Clan yourself. Seeing where you stood, your Junior Martial Brothers and Sisters of the Tang Clan spoke up to keep her too—her days in the clan hadn't been spent making friends with you alone. Though the Palace Mistress of Jinxiang Palace had cautioned her again and again to choose her friends carefully, who wouldn't warm to someone so sweetly artless and open-hearted? Without even meaning to, she'd already made many friends there. No one could bear to see her cast out with nowhere to go.

Long Xiang felt like a lost dog, with nowhere to go. It wasn't that no one approached her; rather, she was overwhelmed by sudden changes and felt that her entire life had been a lie. Her support systems crumbled one after another, leaving her filled with grievance and helplessness. She couldn't trust anyone, as those sweet words seemed to have ulterior motives, and those pleasant smiles might hide other intentions. She hid and wandered anxiously, yet dared not venture too far. Now, the only one she could possibly trust was you. She approached you with trepidation, wanting to lean on you, but when her gaze met that of others, she flinched away like a startled bird.

Your side was in an uproar too—remembering how comfortable and pleasant those days at Jinxiang Palace had been only made the fear now sink in deeper. You'd thought it a tender paradise; it turned out to be a den of dragons and tigers! Had they truly meant you harm, they could have slit every one of your throats in the night without a second thought.

Shangguan Sun was already immensely wealthy, and now with an official post besides, his standing was beyond words—by rights he shouldn't have risked himself. But the boldness he'd picked up rolling through the Jianghu in his younger days hadn't faded one bit, and he agreed at once, gladly. It was Nangong Yuan who was left torn. He wanted to go more than anyone, but as Alliance Leader he had to avoid any hint of favoritism, or every word he spoke afterward would draw criticism—how then could he win people's trust? With no other choice, he sent Eldest Young Lord Nangong Shen in his place.

Nangong Yuan wanted to defend Jinxiang Gong, but even as the Alliance Leader, he could not favor old affections at the expense of justice. Moreover, after being deceived for years, everyone was now filled with shock and anger; for a moment, all emotions surged, leaving no room for anyone to speak. In his urgency, he paid no heed to others, nearly breaking ties with his former brothers‑in‑arms and engaging in conflict. Suddenly, Lady Wen called out, inviting the Alliance Leader and Commissioner Shangguan into the arena to converse.  Now everyone fell silent, eager to see if the Alliance Leader could still uphold tolerance and peace as he sang from within the arena. After all, the Shangguan Family Head was a high‑ranking official of the court; his position was incompatible with that of the rebels. With him watching over, there was no fear of the Alliance Leader's partiality affecting matters. Furthermore, if anything happened to Commissioner Shangguan in the arena, the Alliance Leader would be harder to exonerate.  The atmosphere calmed as everyone waited to see how the Alliance Leader would handle the situation.

The women of Jinxiang Palace were well-trained; sensing the situation turning against them, they instantly fell into formation. Once the array's axis was set, it began to flow without end—one swordswoman struck while the other eight compassed round to back her up. This formation was adapted from the Eight-Array Diagram devised by the famed Three Kingdoms strategist Zhuge Liang. Though the martial artists of the righteous Wulin outnumbered Jinxiang Palace more than tenfold, they were nothing but a loose crowd, only good for shouting and pressing forward—how could they ever break such a formation? So they were held back outside the array, and the standoff dragged on. Since its founding, Jinxiang Palace had taken in nothing but poor women who had suffered under the world's prejudice; of everyone in the palace, only Long Xiang had not come by her own choice—she had been raised at Lady Wen's side since childhood, called master and disciple, though in truth closer to mother and daughter. Only today did she learn that Jinxiang Palace was in truth the Human Path—and in that instant it was as if she had fallen into a dream, her feet unable to find solid ground, her mind reeling, desperate to wake but unable to break free. Cast out of the palace by Lady Wen, she was left adrift, with no idea where to turn.

Chan Master Shi Ming of Songshan's Southern Hall stepped from the crowd radiating righteous solemnity. He took the letter, glanced it over, then put on an exaggerated look of shock before presenting it to the Alliance Leader. When Nangong Qian spoke, the crowd only sneered—on Shi Ming's word alone, they weren't ready to believe it either. But Nangong Yuan's face turned ashen as he read the letter, and that said more than a thousand words could; who could doubt it now?
You broke into a cold sweat and felt an urgent desire to immediately step forward and silence him.

The women of Jinxiang Palace all looked as though a great weight had lifted—some meant to wander the Jianghu alone, others to sheath their swords and retire, marry, raise children, each bound for her own path. The friends of the Jianghu who had been close to Jinxiang Palace were sorry to see them go, but did not try to hold them back, offering their blessings instead. When the tide rises, there is thrilling vengeance and a season in the spotlight; when it ebbs, one washes one's hands and retires in peace—is this not exactly what every soul of the Jianghu longs for? The Wulin Assembly was about to draw to a close when Nangong Qian, the ever-overlooked Second Young Lord of the Nangong family, came rushing out in a panic, waving a secret letter and publicly denouncing the Palace Mistress of Jinxiang Palace's true identity: the Human Path Dharma King of the Mud Cult! The heroes on the mountain didn't know whether to laugh or cry at this. They had long heard that the Nangong family's Second Young Lord was a lowborn son who could never be presented in polite company, forever embarrassing his family with foolish stunts—and now, having swallowed some back-alley rumor, he was clearly just grandstanding again.

By the time the Six Great Sects, the Beggar Sect, the Cang Gang, and the Flying Stone Gang—the Three Great Gangs—along with the lesser sects and leagues of every province, and even the Fire Mountain Sword Pavilion, had all come to pay their respects to the Alliance Leader, the Palace Mistress of Jinxiang Palace still had not arrived. They had waited twenty years for this day. Twenty years ago, Su Yingxiang had stood at Nangong Yuan's side, offering him counsel. Countless worthy souls had flocked to him, won over by his lofty ambitions, ready to give their lives to change this world. Twenty years on, the world had moved on, and all that remained was regret too late to chase down. Lady Wen's face was cold as frost, her words sharper still; ice three feet thick does not form in a single day, and nothing Nangong Yuan said could thaw the chill in her heart. She dissolved Jinxiang Palace before the whole assembly rather than acknowledge Nangong Yuan as Alliance Leader.

All sect and clan leaders approached to congratulate the Wulin Alliance Leader. Though the Tang Clan does not claim to be part of the righteous, as fellow Wulin members and long‑standing allies of the Nangong family, they naturally stepped forward to exchange pleasantries. While they offered their congratulations, the Tang Clan's independent nature could not be altered. If an event benefiting the people and aligned with chivalric principles arose, they would participate, but they would not necessarily follow the Alliance's orders. You didn't need to speak; Nangong Yuan had already intercepted your words. After years of dealing with the Tang Clan, he knew well their pride. The Tang Clan should remain unyielding and defiant, for if their noble spirit were eroded, it would be a great loss. The Wulin should have unrestrained heroes and chivalrous individuals willing to heed the Imperial Court's commands, with the Nangong family serving as the mediator. You heard the sect leader's words from the Nangong family head. Reflecting back on twenty years ago, the sect leader stood apart, looking down upon all martial heroes of his time, wandering alone. How magnificent was his spirit then, how grand his demeanor? It stirred your heart, and you felt proud to be a Tang Clan disciple.

Even a household can quarrel over the smallest trifles, let alone nations. Ruisheng sighed, reflecting on the grand dream of Great Harmony under Heaven—truly no small task, and the worst fear was that all one's painstaking effort would come to nothing in the end. Xiaoju disagreed: to strive on knowing full well it might fail—was that not itself the mark of a sage? Clumsiness was no obstacle either; not everyone in the world is gifted, so it was all the more reason to stay grounded, taking things one step at a time, using ordinary means to do what anyone could manage, so that later generations might follow the example. Ruisheng was deeply impressed, praising her exceptional insight, and you basked in a little of that glow yourself.
For the wives to live in peace, they would all have to learn from Little Junior Sister—never vying for favor, never jealous—only then could one stay outside it all, feeling neither sorrow nor joy.

Yunshang, hearing this, hit upon a scheme: just hand each of them a knife, then go out and get roaringly drunk—by the time he came home, the problem would have resolved itself, blade and all. Ruisheng could only smile bitterly; how was he supposed to take advice that only poured oil on the fire? Little did he know your sister meant his wives no harm at all—she only wanted to spur them to join forces and do him in.

You meant to call on the Guyun Mountain Sect, only to run straight into its young Sect Leader Ruisheng, fleeing in disarray from a family quarrel. By the sound of it, his several beloved companions, however beautiful, were each rather quick-tempered. Small wonder, really—no one is a sage, and who is without some selfish want? Wanting sole claim on a husband's favor is only human, especially since these young women had come to him not through a matchmaker's word but on nothing but courage and a burning heart, defying the world's judgment. And yet true devotion cannot be traded one-for-one; they were forced to share it after all. How could that not leave them feeling wronged? Asking them not to squabble with jealousy was no small task.

Intending to pay homage to Emei Sect Leader Xiang Wuyou, many people of the Wulin share the same thought. They all vie for his attention, eager to befriend this suddenly renowned Wulin master. Seeing that entry is impossible, you give up and turn away, but Sect Leader Xiang notices your retreating figure and takes a liking to you. The fundamental truths of martial arts converge regardless of their paths. After years of seclusion from the world, he had nearly perfected the Invisible Fist he grasped from Xingyi Fist, reaching a state of no technique, no form. At this moment, observing your movements as you evade the crowd, he finds them strangely similar, and is secretly startled. Curious about a Tang Clan disciple who specializes in hidden weapons and poisons, he wonders what martial art you practice. Unbeknownst to him, you indeed practice Tang Clan techniques—specifically the Chapter on Forgetting Form, stated plainly from the very opening, yet whose true essence no one has ever grasped.

Lady Wen had been too preoccupied with the palace servants earlier to worry about her own affairs. Today's respite allowed her to relax and see Xiaozhu. She realized that Kongtong's Bone-Cracking Demon was renowned for his craftsmanship, while Fire Mountain Sword Pavilion specialized in weapons, yet she could make anything. Lady Wen considered herself a remarkable woman of the era. Thus, she ordered Xiaozhu to custom‑make a carriage. It had a roof to shelter from wind and rain, and windows to enjoy the scenery along the way. The exterior needed no embellishment, but the interior should be comfortable and spacious, sturdy enough to withstand bumpy roads. She planned to travel to Mount Changbai, where she heard that it was perpetually covered in snow. This place held memories of her dear departed friends. Since she would have nothing to do after retiring from Jianghu, why not take a carriage filled with the faint fragrance of flowers and travel far away? She could pay respects to her old friends and tell them that Nangong Yuan had finally become the Wulin Alliance Leader, and their dreams would continue.

Xiaomei came forward to pay her respects, lively and radiant before the bold and hearty, demure and proper before the refined—her smile flawless, winning hearts of men and women alike. Yet the trick found no purchase on Lady Wen, a seasoned hand of the Jianghu who had read a thousand hearts; how could she miss Xiaomei's flattery? She knew, too, that Xiaomei was a killer of the Thousand Lantern Tower with a clouded past, and the more Xiaomei fawned, the more guarded and unsmiling Lady Wen grew. Xiaomei paid it no mind. She turned and threw herself into Painting Immortal's arms, crying "Auntie" with such warmth that Lady Wen froze—she and Painting Immortal were sisters, so if Xiaomei called her own sister Auntie, what did that make her? Her mind raced through the family tree before she called Xiaomei to her side, voice stern. Painting Immortal panicked, certain her lie was about to be exposed on the spot—but instead of her earlier cold severity, Lady Wen acknowledged the kinship then and there, even promising to pass down everything she knew as amends. Raised from childhood by the Thousand Lantern Tower to be a killer, then steeped in the ways of Flying Heaven Gate, Xiaomei had inevitably picked up some of their ruthless, twisted cruelty—yet at heart she remained guileless, quick to deceive others and just as quick to be deceived herself. In that instant she truly believed she had found family again, and her eyes brimmed with sudden tears; she gave no thought to how precious the skills or learning were, only joy that she now had someone to lean on.

Xiaoju stepped forward and bowed. The two women famed across the Jianghu for their wit had finally met, and as they traded lines, each quoting the classics, praise passed between them like old friends meeting too late. You had long known Xiaoju's reputation as a gifted scholar and admired her learning, yet you had never seen her this animated before, talking freely with words like scattered pearls—so swept up in the moment that she nearly broke her vow never to compose verse again.

You now know that Lady Wen is the Human Path Dharma King of the Mud Cult, yet she dares to bring courtiers to the Wulin Assembly; her courage is not to be underestimated. Should you slip up, their group might not leave this place alive. Yet Lady Wen is certain you won't speak out. She knows people well; she has a clear sense of who can be trusted. Risking great peril to inform you, her intention is not to have you expose her, but to express deep expectations.

Long Xiang saw you approaching, smiled warmly, and came forward, still holding a chicken leg from a street vendor. You couldn't help but laugh. This person could be colder than a sword's edge at times, yet at others, as sweet and charming as a young woman on a spring day outing. But to be honest, being able to eat is better than not being able to.

When you visited the Jinxiang Palace people, a group of white‑robed women were chatting and laughing, appearing relaxed and carefree, with no sense of the solemnity of participating in the Wulin Assembly. Those who didn't know the situation laughed at them for not understanding the world, treating Jianghu as a game. Unbeknownst to them, for the Palace people, today marked the graduation ceremony of their Jianghu life.

You feel as if you're in a dream, unreal and distant, always blaming fate for never belonging to you. When it truly comes your way, you doubt and hesitate, one moment thinking you're still dreaming, the next suspecting there's some trick. Yin Zhiping has no intention of earnestly persuading you; he's merely delivering a message from his master. Whether you believe it or not, whether you can seize the opportunity, the decision is entirely up to you.

This was a great good thing, but Yunshang immediately got angry and found a branch on the spot to fight Yin Zhiping. Yin Zhiping hurriedly explained that it was not to make you a Daoist priest, but to register you to practice at

Wonderful news though this was, your junior martial sister grew anxious the instant she heard it, fearing you'd be tempted to truly become a Daoist priest. And could you blame her? Number One Under Heaven breaking precedent to take you as his disciple—what fortune could rival that? How could the Tang Clan ever hope to keep you? Yin Zhiping hastened to explain that you needn't renounce the world and become a priest at all—only be registered under his name and cultivate at home as you pleased. Only then did the junior martial sister finally breathe easy, feeling as if she'd gotten back something she'd feared lost, and unconsciously clutched at the hem of your robe—deep down, she couldn't shake the feeling that everyone wanted to steal you away. She really had been worrying over nothing.

On a sudden whim, he instructed his disciple to test you. If you failed to come, so be it—it would only mean there was no bond between you, and nothing worth forcing. But if you came before him, and he found in you a true affinity for the Dao, no master to call your own, a pure heart, and an unbending will, then he would not hesitate to open his humble gate for you, breaking precedent to take you on as his final disciple.
The more he heard of your stumbles and setbacks, the more Immortal Qiu's interest grew, admiring your unyielding will and your resolve to press on against the wind.

Back on that journey through the desert, Immortal Qiu had already taken note of you—your face, after all, was far too memorable, and your conduct had been far from ordinary. At the time he hadn't yet come to understand your character, not until he heard Yin Zhiping recount, laughing, how you'd stumbled and struggled your way forward without ever giving up. Only then did his interest truly deepen, and he came to admire your unyielding will and your resolve to press on against the wind.

Yin Zhiping had been waiting for you to come to him all along. The poem he'd just recited was no idle expression of feeling, but a deliberate test of how deep your bond with the Quanzhen Sect truly ran. Before this journey south, he had discussed the heroes of the age with his master Qiu Chuji over tea, and Daoist Yin had singled you out by name. In Jianghu, new waves forever push the old ones aside, and every generation throws up its share of prodigies; live long enough, and such wonders stop seeming strange at all. Yet among these heroes who rose above the crowd, not one was an ordinary man—save you, who were strange indeed. Mediocre in talent, never taught the true arts of the Tang Clan, with no extraordinary fortune to speak of, you were no different from the countless common men adrift on the current of the age, who either give up and let the river sweep them away, or are ground down and forgotten, their names remembered by no one. So how was it that you alone rose above them all?

You still took what he'd recited for an impromptu verse and were about to praise it aloud, when Xiaoju stopped you just in time, whispering that it was in fact a quatrain by Patriarch Chunyang, Lü Dongbin—sparing you from making a fool of yourself.
The instant you heard it, you knew he was reciting a quatrain by Patriarch Chunyang, Lü Dongbin. Yin Zhiping's eyes lit up with an unusual brightness, plainly approving.
You went to pay your respects to Daoist Yin of the Quanzhen Sect, who stood alone at the cliff's edge, gazing out over Dongting Lake.

A wife this virtuous—what more could a husband ask for? Xiaoju heard this and smiled radiantly, caring nothing for the authority in her hands. This one word of praise from you was enough to wash away the old disgrace of being decreed, despite having placed first in the imperial examination, to marry a mere martial artist. To her, you were her sovereign.

Fortunately, Wei Ju stepped in, having already arranged everything thoroughly, considered all aspects, managed with composure, and maintained order. She even attributed all the credit to you. Upon hearing that it was at the Sect Leader's behest, the Kongtong crowd obeyed without hesitation.
The reason you couldn't answer isn't about how much knowledge you have, but rather that your understanding of Kongtong's situation is too superficial to make a hasty decision.

With the dignity of a Sect Leader, you made your first appearance before the Kongtong Sect, still fearing a knife from those who resented you. Yet with Danxiazi at their head, everyone showed you nothing but respect and courtesy, not a trace of insolence to be seen, and your mind finally eased. But when asked about Kongtong's future direction, you found yourself stammering, unable to get a word out.

How could you be here just to take abuse? When someone needled you with a snide remark, you struck right back with your verbal attack, your words just as sharp and barbed, naming no names either—yet the force behind them was on another level entirely. The old beggar's self-control proved poor; provoked to fury, he swung his staff, ready to fight to the death. The commotion drew the surrounding crowd's eyes, and at the sight of these beggars squaring up fierce and thuggish, ready to strike, brows furrowed all around—the image the Beggar Sect had been fighting so hard to rebuild now cracked open.

You knew well enough that the Beggar Sect was now ruled by its old-school elders, and though the Gang Leader was nominally in charge, his word did not always carry weight. Not wishing to put the Dayi Branch in an awkward position, you merely smiled, cupped your fist in farewell, and took your leave.

The elder of the old faction of the Beggar Sect stepped forward, pretending to advise the Gang Leader to be cautious in choosing associates and avoid unscrupulous villains. As he spoke, his gaze kept scanning you, his face betraying a mocking expression, subtly implying his meaning without needing to say it outright.
You had assumed the Elders of the Beggar Sect's Old Faction would look down on the Tang Clan, but to your surprise, one of them came forward and urged the Gang Leader to deal more with the Tang Clan.

Ye Yunshang saw you getting beaten and at once grabbed a staff to strike you from behind. There was method to it: she knew you'd whip around in shock to demand why, giving her the chance to answer in front of everyone, 'A beating means affection, and cursing means love.' So her blow was meant to remind you of your own feelings—and as for your Beggar Sect friends calling you a Blue Devil, well, that plainly meant they loved you too. At that, everyone present fell speechless; however close they were, no one could bring themselves to hit you or curse you further. Yunshang had protected you in her own way.

The Junior Martial Sister saw you being beaten and immediately became displeased; she didn't understand the camaraderie forged through punches and kicks between you. Old Beggar Brother was both surprised and admiring to see you had actually managed to win over the Tang Clan's daughter. He even wanted to secretly learn a few moves from you to marry a beggar woman, but you had no insights at all. Up to now, you still worried that the Junior Martial Sister was just a mirage, vanishing the moment touched.

Old friends from the Dayi Branch—the ones who'd once scrapped over food and shared hot pot with you—came rushing out, cursing you as a Blue Devil, tears brimming in their eyes all the same. The world changes as unpredictably as drifting clouds; it wasn't only the Tang Clan that had changed beyond recognition—the Beggar Sect's Dayi Branch was no different. Gang Leader Wang had died, and the old guard of beggars had seized power again, bearing down hard on the branch; only a handful of old faces were left now, and seeing you again felt like waking from another life. Swept up in the emotion, they naturally threw a few punches your way, to see if you could still take a beating like you used to.

He caught sight of Xiaoju at your side and flinched, startled, and lowered his head. It turned out Li Fugui's family had once been well-to-do, before their fortunes fell—back then he'd tagged along with his disreputable friends to a poetry gathering, drawn by this great talent's reputation, and had fallen for her dazzling gifts. He'd felt ashamed of himself even then; now that he'd become a beggar chief, he was all the more afraid she might recognize him.

You went to greet the Beggar Sect. Gang Leader Li was a young man who appeared hesitant and cautious at the Wulin Assembly. When you approached, he greeted you with a beaming smile and came running up.

You meant to pay your respects to the eminent monk of Songshan, to show a measure of admiration, but ran into Dharma Master Fu Yun on the way, who urged you not to go. Abbot Juehui preferred quiet and kept no company with people of the Jianghu; soon after returning to the mountain he would hand down his robe and bowl, with no wish to be touched by worldly affairs any further. You said you'd hoped to deal with the monks of Songshan—but wasn't dealing with him just the same thing? After all, it was all but certain he would become abbot of Songshan himself one day. You were taken aback, thinking privately how brazen this young monk was—even with ambition, how could he declare it so openly? But you had underestimated him. Fu Yun spoke so boldly because he understood that only by holding the position could he accomplish anything: to reorganize the monks, set the generational naming order, rouse them to renewed spirit, and spread the Dharma, he would first have to hold power and lead by example—so the abbot's seat was something he meant to claim. To want it and yet hide that wish would only have been dishonest. By the time the assembly ended, his near decade of wandering pilgrimage, begun on an old vow, would draw to a close, and he would return to the temple to deepen his practice. If you did not come to Songshan, your next meeting might not be for many years. Monk and layman though you were, the two of you had grown close, and your friendship by now ran deep—hearing this, you couldn't help feeling wistful.

The Righteous Path had chosen its Wulin Alliance Leader, and even though the Tang Clan had no intention of obeying his every word, they still had to make the rounds, deal with the other sects, and remind everyone they existed.

Wei Ju talked with you a while, and seeing you showed no sign of holding it against her, she finally relaxed. In truth, she had come meaning never to leave. As agreed, she had already handed over everything at Kongtong; she simply hadn't brought her belongings along, for fear you might not want her. If you didn't mind, then from today she would no longer be Sect Leader Wei—only your Xiaoju.

You caught the admiration in her words for the Nangong family, and couldn't help worrying she might be swept away by the Nangong family's eldest son. Your probing was carefully oblique, but Xiao Ju read the situation at a glance and knew at once what was on your mind—secretly amused, and rather pleased besides, though she also worried that after months apart, you might have grown fickle and forgotten her. A gentleman disdains to speak ill of others, and she herself was loath to criticize anyone, but to lay her heart bare she held nothing back, and her complaints about the eldest son poured out like a river in flood. You were left speechless—you'd thought this brilliant lady of Wei was easygoing, only to find her standards for character so exacting, and you quietly congratulated yourself for being steady enough not to have earned her dislike. She had never told even her closest friend, Shangguan Ying, any of this, since the eldest son had once been Shangguan Ying's betrothed. Though the words out of her mouth spoke ill of another, she felt as if you now held something over her.

Xiao Ju came to you shamefaced to confess. She had planned to use pressure from the Quanzhen, Songshan, Diancang, and Kongtong sects to stir the crowd and force the assembly free of the court's control, helping you rise to Wulin Alliance Leader. She never imagined that Quanzhen and Songshan would withdraw from the contest without a second thought, leaving Kongtong—caught in a similar bind, and more contentious still for having taken in refugees from every land—unable to find its footing to speak up. So for the whole assembly, Kongtong stayed silent. The one saving grace was that the Nangong Family carried the day; by both sentiment and geography, the Tang Clan should be safe from harm, which finally set her mind somewhat at ease.
Xiao Zhu is gradually becoming familiar with you and can also be humorous.
His love fortune was flourishing, and he unexpectedly acquired four beautiful female companions in one go, his tone revealing a sense of satisfaction.
His romantic luck was flourishing — he had won over five beautiful confidantes in one go, his tone carrying a clear air of pride.

His romantic luck was flourishing — he had won over five beautiful confidantes at once, his tone brimming with pride. You didn't find it at all strange; with Rui Sheng's talent and skill, he had only ever picked the wrong opponents before, and it was simply bad luck. Otherwise, having a harem would hardly have been out of reach. The conversation was going smoothly until Rui Sheng carelessly said, "I might not lose to Miss Tang after all," offending you, an unrefined man. Suddenly, you squared up for a fight, which grew funnier the longer it went on, until you ended up with arms slung over each other's shoulders, laughing heartily. Compared to those who greeted everyone with empty flattery, he valued a friend like you far more.

You don't find it strange at all — given Rui Sheng's talent, looks, and skill, striking out everywhere before could only be put down to picking the wrong opponents and having bad luck; otherwise, a harem would hardly have been out of reach. Everything had been going well, until Rui Sheng carelessly said, "I might not lose to Miss Tang after all," offending you, ever the petty one, and you suddenly squared up for a fight. Your Junior Martial Sister, not realizing this was just camaraderie and rapport between men roughhousing, hurried to jump between you and break it up, and once she learned the reason, felt sweet inside.
Soon, Cang Gang hands will come to receive you, collect your invitation, and lead you to rest beneath the shade pavilion.
Even though you, who have seen much, can't help but get nervous, your Junior Martial Brothers and Sisters, seeing you like this, become even more panicked.
Even you, worldly as you were, could not help feeling nervous — though you still wanted to put on a brave face and refuse to admit it.

You had no idea how reassuring your calm, steady expression could be.
Your smile was as unappealing as ever, yet somehow it never failed to put people at ease.

Ascending Fengyu Mountain, one could see the Wulin Assembly's venue, where banners of various sects fluttered in the wind. The field was densely packed with people, surely numbering over a thousand. Although the Shangguan Family Head, who had been entrusted with organizing the gathering, had retired from Jianghu, his lingering authority still held sway. Most Wulin figures gave him face, especially since this was a significant meeting to discuss the future of the Wulin. Out of a hundred invitations sent, ninety‑nine were returned. At that moment, heroes from all over Central Plains gathered at Fengyu Mountain, creating an unprecedentedly grand scene, filled with the clamor of voices. The Six Great Sects occupied their respective areas, their disciples dressed in colorful uniforms, making them easily distinguishable. However, those without a sect or affiliation wore less formal attire, making it hard to tell one from another. Seasoned old hands, mindful of social etiquette, greeted acquaintances warmly. Younger, more ambitious individuals, however, were like porcupines, unwilling to yield. Some particularly liked to pretend, each carrying a blade of grass in their mouths, claiming to be solitary lone wolves wandering Jianghu, proud of their homelessness. Even if they had parents at home, they would boast of their families being destroyed, as if having a complete family was a disgrace.

You recalled your journey through the vast desert, when Ruixing had urged Genghis Khan toward bold, sweeping action — already showing the ruthless, decisive cruelty behind it. Lady Wen was taken aback to hear this, reading it differently.
She had assumed Ruixing simply chose to back Mongol rule over the realm, and so offered Genghis Khan her strategies. But when the war against Jin stalled, the campaign turned west — on the surface an expansion of territory, but in truth a scheme to exploit the moment and split the Mongols apart.
Jochi, farthest from the succession, would seek to protect himself by volunteering for the western campaign — earning merit to clear his name while putting distance between himself and the storm at court. Given time, with an army of his own behind him, he could turn his blade toward the Onon River, becoming a lurking threat to the rightful heir — one misstep, and civil war would follow.
Years later, events unfolded much as Lady Wen had foreseen — but she had only gotten half of it right, for Ruixing changed her mind partway through.
Jochi rode west and was enfeoffed as khan of the distant Kipchak.
Later, Jochi was framed by Ruixing, fell under Genghis Khan's suspicion, and in his despair was, at her urging, put to death in his own tent — his death reported falsely as illness. The guilt weighed on Genghis Khan's heart, and before long he too passed away.
Without shedding a drop of blood, the Apricot Blossom Immortal brought down the Mongols' strongholds, then passed through Song territory to encircle Bianjing and destroy the Jin.

A girl of otherworldly beauty swept the curtain aside, and in an instant the whole room filled with radiance; about her curled an indescribable aura, sacred and inviolable — she was none other than the elusive Apricot Blossom Immortal of the Apricot Blossom Forest of Nanyang.
She called Lady Wen Master, dismissed her own attendants, and settled gracefully into her seat to play a game of chess with Lady Wen.
As the two of them spoke, every word struck like a blow; you broke into a cold sweat, afraid even a single drop might fall.
Only now did you know Lady Wen's words were no exaggeration — the storms of the Jianghu, even the wars among the Four Kingdoms, had all been orchestrated from the shadows by this one person's hand.
She had used the rivers and mountains of the realm as her chessboard: playing against Lady Wen, against Zhao Kuo, against Wanyan Xun, against Genghis Khan.
Every living soul was drawn into her game, their lives and deaths no longer their own to command.
Blood rained from the sky when she came, and the land lay in ruins when she left — this was the true face of the Apricot Blossom Immortal, most wicked in all the mortal world.
Long after she took her leave, you still dared not rise from where you hid; for all your martial skill, you had been left weak-kneed with fear by one frail-seeming girl.
The moment Lady Wen asked you to stay behind, she knew this matter could not be hidden from you forever.
She cleared nothing up, but in her sharp exchange with Ruixing she had already poured out her lifelong resolve. A heart that cherished noble ideals yet harbored private designs, cunning and false, yet still seeking peace — complicated and contradictory: this was what it meant to walk the Human Path.

You looked again, and saw the maid leading them wore a water-blue dress, her skin dark, her face strikingly lovely — who else could she be but the long-absent Miss Shu Rong?
The two bearers were none other than Wanli Pengcheng, once Head of the Bodhidharma Hall, and the Sword Saint of Diancang.
The true identity of the one inside the palanquin was all but revealed.

The guests proved insufferably arrogant, having their palanquin carried straight into the hall.
Your eyes had opened wide to the world by now, and at a glance you saw the two bearers giving off an uncanny aura of power — your hairs stood on end. Only then did you understand why Lady Wen had been so careful: had she not first sealed your pulse and slowed your heartbeat with her internal skill, these two masters would surely have detected you the instant they arrived.

The residual True Qi of the Venerable Golden Crow's Scorching Sun Hammer lingered in your body like a parasite, feeding itself on your dantian.
Sensing the music, it seemed to stir, drawn out to join the flow of your qi, dancing along with it.
You were startled at first, then overjoyed, and hastily sealed your acupoints to trap it. The Scorching Sun Hammer's True Qi could neither advance nor retreat, and with no strength left to sustain it, dissipated into nothing within moments.

Her pipa's sound, laced with Internal Force, tugged at the heartstrings. The melody seemed to hold countless stories — joy and sorrow, parting and reunion, every bitterness and sweetness — like poetry, like song, like weeping. Even with Lady Wen's warning, you could not help but be moved to sorrow, drifting into self-pity, tears falling before you knew it.
Her pipa music, laced with Internal Force, stirred the heart. The sound seemed to conceal countless hidden emotions, leaving listeners with a lump in their throat upon hearing it.

The pipa's melody tugged at the heartbeat, unsettling mind and spirit.
Fortunately Lady Wen had warned you beforehand; otherwise, hearing this music without warning would surely have shaken your composure.

Lady Wen strummed the strings of the Three Yin Pulse-Severing Hand, sealing your Lifeforce and slowing your heartbeat until you seemed lifeless. She sent you up onto the rafters to hide, and ordered her attendants to tidy the hall and bring out an unfinished game of chess. Then she straightened her robes, took her seat at the qin, and plucked a few notes — and outside the hall, her attendants, hearing the signal, went out to receive the guests.
You had assumed Lady Wen's words meant the Supreme Bliss Cult was rising again, but that was not so — even Li Renyou was merely a 'general' on the chessboard, not the hand moving the pieces.

Watching your retreating figure, Lady Wen was suddenly struck by an impulse and resolved to gamble everything, speaking with total candor.
She revealed to you the unspeakable figure hidden behind the scenes of history.

After you left, you gathered the Tang Clan's junior disciples and had them pack their bags.
You set out a step ahead of Jinxiang Palace, and the next morning you were on the road to Fengyu Mountain.

You went out and gathered your Tang Clan Junior Martial Brothers and Sisters, ordering them to pack their bags. You set off a step ahead of Jinxiang Palace, and early the next morning were already on the road to Fengyu Mountain.

You had been cared for by Jinxiang Palace, and such kindness deserved to be repaid many times over. It was the Tang Clan's creed to turn away no one adrift in the world, be they peddler or beggar — how much less would it turn away women of the renowned Jinxiang Palace? Taking the palace's people into the Tang Clan could only bring benefit, with no drawback at all, so you resolved then and there to agree.

This matter sounds too good, beneficial to the Tang Clan in every way without any drawbacks. You dare not be careless, stating you cannot decide alone and need to return to the Tang Clan's headquarters to consult the Sect Leader. Lady Wen also did not speak much; insisting would be inappropriate.
You lingered in the nearby town for the night, and the next day led your group onward to Fengyu Mountain.
You lingered in the nearby town for the night, and the next day led your group onward to Fengyu Mountain.

Your fellow disciples, dragged into it through no fault of their own, were driven from the palace without even knowing why. Once they learned the truth, they gritted their teeth in hatred of you — living under another's roof, hearing words not to your liking, could you not simply have held your tongue? Did you take this palace for your own home? And now see the result: swept out the door like rubbish, with more than a few of the female disciples turning on the spot, abandoning the Tang Clan to throw in with Jinxiang Palace. Hearts scattered and morale collapsed, all for your folly.

Lady Wen's words were far too radical, bordering on heresy — if this could be borne, what could not? To defend a thousand years of orthodox tradition, you slammed the table and rose in fury, jabbing an accusing finger and cursing her outright, breaking with Lady Wen then and there, and were thrown out of the palace for it.
Lady Wen's words are too contrary to tradition; you refrain from commenting.
Unorthodox as it was, breaking with tradition, you nonetheless thought Lady Wen's ideal was not a bad one.

Even outside Jinxiang Palace, how could there be a lack of female heroes and outstanding women? Among the examples she cited was your beloved Shangguan Ying. Lady Wen, well‑versed in current affairs, naturally knows about your shared hardships and deep bond with Shangguan Ying. On one hand, it's indeed admiration for Shangguan Ying's business acumen, and on the other, there's an intentional mention to gain your approval.

Even beyond Jinxiang Palace, when had there ever been a shortage of heroines and outstanding women? Among the examples she gave was your own wife, Lady Ju, and hearing it, you felt rather proud. Lady Wen, well versed in the affairs of the world, naturally knew of your rise to lead Kongtong Sect and your marriage to Wei Ju — she admired your wife, true, but naming her was also meant to win your approval.

The journey was about to begin, and only then did Lady Wen finally have the attendants summon you into the hall to discuss matters. She came straight to the point, telling you of her plan to disband the attendants and retire from the Jianghu once the Wulin Assembly was over. You were stunned — Jinxiang Palace, unlike the Tang Clan, had already won widespread renown over a decade ago, back when it was still called Jinxiang Estate, then Jinxiang Pavilion; in the past ten years it had moved to Dongting Lake, and as Jinxiang Palace its fame had only grown greater still. More and more women had come flocking to it for refuge, and it now stood at the very height of its power — why disband it all at once? Lady Wen explained unhurriedly: she had taken these women in to teach them skills and Martial Learning, to give them self-respect, self-worth, and self-love, all to prove a point for the women of the world and put men to shame — proof that what men could do, women could do just as well.
Only you have always been lonely, with loneliness embracing you for eternity.

Invited to remain at Jinxiang Palace, they stayed for half a month. After spending days and nights together with the palace ladies, opinions about the Tang Clan underwent significant changes. They found that you did not match the low and treacherous reputation in the Jianghu rumors. Many young ladies who had never left the palace and whose thoughts were still simple held many affectionate feelings for the Tang Clan men after seeing their bold spirit. Those with hearts secretly smitten were also quite a few.
The Wulin Assembly is imminent, and the brothers and sisters are all rubbing their fists and sharpening their palms, eager to test themselves and make a name for themselves.
The Wulin Assembly drew near, and thanks to you, the brothers and sisters were brimming with confidence, itching for a fight, eager to show their mettle before the great sects.

Teaching Xiaomei the Mysterious Candle Heart Sutra was meant to ease her anxiety, though even without it, staying on in the Tang Clan a while longer and eating a bit more rice would let the pepper poison eventually devour the heat poison anyway. Giving her the book was only icing on the cake — no harm if you took it to read yourself. Yet the martial art now being passed on was no small matter: like Kongtong's profound Iron Pipa Divine Skill, it too sprang from the Nanyue True Scripture, a lost art called One-Toe Riding the Wind. Once mastered, force flowed from the body through the legs, from the legs to the feet, and from the feet to the toes, so that without ever bending the knee, on Internal Force alone one could glide and streak across the ground, hiding every sign of movement, like an immortal riding the wind — flawless, and the finest Qinggong under heaven. Too abstruse and difficult, it was eventually lost; Flying Heaven's successors simplified it into the Crane's Mysterious Steps Fist, which remained too intricate still, and was pared down again until it sank to the common Flying Heaven Kick. Even the Painting Immortal's skill could not grasp the whole of it, and yet that mere glimpse of its principles already left her movements peerless. Xiaomei, with this divine art, could in time contend with the greatest masters under heaven. She believed the Painting Immortal's words, and took her for a true distant relative, the last of her own blood left in the world — a third person, after her closest friend and her companion, willing to show her unconditional kindness, and she treasured it, overjoyed beyond measure. But was it truly so? Perhaps she sensed the truth all along, and simply dared not say it.

You took the manual, planning to master it yourself, so that in time you could help Xiaomei suppress the burning poison inside her. It was a foolish method, one that treated the symptom and not the cause, and it would keep Xiaomei under your thumb for the rest of her life — once it was Thousand Lantern Tower that held such power over her; now it was you. Xiaomei was not blind to your scheming, and yet she handed the reins over to you all the same.

You coaxed her at once into learning without worry — whatever the Heartburn Seal cost her, whether she could stay by your side for life mattered far more. Even if she ended up without the strength to truss a chicken, you vowed the two of you would always treat each other with the respect due an honored guest. Xiaomei, hearing this, was not pleased at all; in truth, she'd hoped you might be a little more forceful now and then.

You immediately coaxed her into learning it without worry — whatever the Heartburn Seal cost her, whether she'd stay by your side for life mattered far more. And once her martial arts were gone, leaving her without even the strength to truss a chicken, wasn't that better still? All the mischief you'd never dared play on her before, you'd now play in full, once the moment was ripe.

The Painting Immortal then secretly taught Xiaomei the forbidden secret of Jinxiang Palace, the Mysterious Candle Heart Sutra, earnestly advising her: this technique is of a cold nature, capable of subduing heartburn and fiery temper, specifically countering the Heartburn Seal. Practicing it can neutralize the poison within the body. However, she relied on the rapid progress granted by the Heartburn Seal, and thus the power inevitably dissipated. Xiaomei, upon hearing this, felt greatly troubled. Naturally, she desired to rid herself of the poison, yet she could not bear to part with her acquired strength. If she did not preserve her power, how could she assist you in times of need?

You may be the winner, but the prize was meant for Xiaomei—none of it was yours. A slap across the face, though, you could certainly expect. You rubbed your stinging cheek, feeling a little hard done by.
You may be the winner, but the prize is meant for Xiaomei, and you're not entitled to it. You smiled and accepted it happily, and Xiaomei, seeing your generosity, was secretly moved.

Despite her mastery of Tang Clan, Jinxiang Palace, and Thousand Lantern Tower martial arts—her techniques unpredictable, balanced in attack and defense—she was undoubtedly a master of her generation. But you were no longer the callow novice of old; you unleashed everything you had, matched her blow for blow, and in the end won through by the narrowest margin.
You let Xiaomei guard the rear while you yourself stepped forward to learn the high moves of the Second-Generation Thousand-Face Demon.

Xiaomei stepped forward to accept the challenge, and the two generations of the Thousand-Faced Demon engaged in a formal confrontation. However, regardless of experience, foundational skills, the intricacy of techniques, or the depth of Internal Force, Xiaomei was completely outmatched. Even when she unleashed the Heartburn Seal to amplify her power, she was still no match for her opponent. This was partly because the Painting Immortal had full knowledge of Xiaomei's techniques, but also because her own strength was formidable, allowing her to remain composed even as Xiaomei's poison burned through her.
