Xiaomei wasn't entirely without cunning; she intentionally feigned weakness to conserve her final reserve of strength. However, in a direct confrontation, she had no chance of victory.

As night fell, you and Xiaomei met Hua Xian'er at the Painting Immortal's rendezvous. She still smiled cheerfully, waving you both out of the palace to spar in the woods. Though Hua Xian'er's steps were small, she moved surprisingly fast, as if gliding across the ground. You both had to use Qinggong to keep up.

Though your appearance is unattractive, you pretend to be affectionate, taking advantage of this girl's low skill and numerous weaknesses. You deliberately attack her lower body, causing her to become flustered and nearly fall backward. Then, you reach out and grab her waist to steady her. The girl, inexperienced in the world, sees your high skill and reputation, and despite your unattractive face, your polite manners make her blush. She can't tell what's wrong with her eyes, but she finds your face somewhat handsome. As she flees in embarrassment, you feel proud. As for the later incident where Xiaomei dragged her to the corner and threatened her, you have no idea.

This miss was inexperienced, seeing your high martial arts skills and good reputation, and mistook you for a hero. Unbeknownst to her, you were flirtatious and lecherous, with a bold and shameless nature. You used the excuse of a sparring match to touch her face and hands several times, and even pat her bottom. She was both ashamed and furious, fleeing in embarrassment.

It's not that you're upright and honest; it's just that you're in a dangerous situation. If she accuses you of being indecent or improper, you might be mobbed on the spot and cut into minced meat. The young palace attendant, hearing you say this, thought you were trying to cover up your shame by acting tough and causing trouble. She found you somewhat cute despite your appearance, and developed a bit of fondness for you. As for the incident later when she was dragged to the corner by Xiaomei and threatened, you would have no idea.
You held back in your moves, fearing you might accidentally touch your opponent's body, and when she asked why, you told her plainly.
It's not that you're pretentious; you're just in a dangerous situation. If she accuses you of being lecherous and improper, you might be surrounded and attacked on the spot, minced into meat.
You held back in your moves, fearing you might accidentally touch your opponent's body. This, of course, you couldn't say aloud, so you claimed you'd simply forgotten the technique.
This day, you once again sparred with the attendants of Jinxiang Palace.

Having been together so long, you had already figured out Xiao Zhu's temperament—this girl was easy to handle, easily settled with a little flattery. Since she was already yours for the taking, there was no need to bother with cherishing her anymore. A bit of flattery, and she was sent on her way.

You won Xiao Zhu over with the strategy of self-sacrifice, then swept her up in your arms and carried her back to her room. Her heart fluttered like a startled deer as she clung to your neck, too flustered to speak. She had thought herself utterly without charm, which was why the sect leader had neglected her until now—never knowing that you too had trod carefully, afraid of scaring her off. Now, cherished and cared for like this, Xiao Zhu was overjoyed. Only now did she feel she had truly claimed her place as the sect's first lady, one no one could take from her.

Feeling guilty toward Xiao Zhu, you took a technical beating and let her vent her anger. Though you lost, you became the biggest winner. Xiao Zhu suddenly threw her arms around you, and all her grievances of the past few days vanished into thin air.
Seeing you couldn't win her over so easily, and that waiting outside the door was no solution either, your heart was already elsewhere. After a while, your patience ran out, and you simply left.

You deeply regret your rashness, and seeing that you can't easily win her over, you sit outside the door, waiting. This girl is quite easy to deal with; seeing you with your face to the ground, blood from your nose, and still trying hard to please her, she can't help but feel both heartbroken and amused. Although you are clumsy and not gentle, your heart is always focused on her, isn't that just like her? All your grievances seem to dissipate.

Everyone else can see her intentions, but you can't, not understanding the consideration for others, your pride is so strong that you beat your own wife in public. Although you know how to control the strength, Xiao Zhu only hurts but not harmed, yet being treated this way in public still makes her feel deeply wronged. She runs back to her room, locks the door, and sobs and weeps on the bed.

Ever since arriving at Jinxiang Palace, Xiaozhu had remained cautious to a fault, so dazzled by its splendor at every turn that she feared her stride might crack the floor tiles, or that a careless touch might tip a lamppost or crush a garden rockery. This was no place to hammer iron, either, which left her stifled and feeling entirely out of place. She also saw that every day palace attendants flocked to surround you, begging for pointers in martial arts. Simple-hearted as she was, it still left something gnawing at her; though she had no real interest in martial arts herself, she began asking you to teach her too, if only to make her presence known.

Ye Yunshang went to Huayin Pavilion at first only out of curiosity, plucking a few idle notes on the qin. The older Jinxiang Palace attendant, seeing this delicate, timid slip of a girl, was reminded of her own daughter, who had died at her father's hands before she ever reached marriage, and felt a pang of sorrow. So she drew Yunshang close and taught her a few basic fingerings, if only to ease her own grief. Yunshang, quite unlike herself, became utterly absorbed, reporting to Huayin Pavilion every day and forgetting to eat or sleep as she practiced. You worried she might be scheming some new mischief, but the qin was plainly no cheap instrument, so you could only pray that, mischievous as she was, she would leave that one alone. Yet seeing her so rapt in concentration, playing until her fingers split and bled without ever resting, you could not bring yourself to deny her — you only tended her wounds in silence and watched over her from the side. What you did not know was that the piece she was mastering was the final trial of Jinxiang Palace's qin examination, Midnight Letter to You, composed by Lady Wen out of sorrow for her own life, her midnight longing for the young man she once loved, wrought from a thousand tears. Few today can still play it with that same depth of grief. Yunshang, in practicing it, did not simply strain to render its sorrow, for she herself was still young, and had come through her own long night with you cutting a path through the thorns to lead her into the light. Her rendition of Midnight Letter to You, though sorrowful, never surrendered hope — it was light, lively, innocent, and tender. Lady Wen listened, deeply moved, old memories rising vividly to mind, and sat lost in thought long after the piece ended, as if returned from another age. Hers had been a hard life, and she no longer believed in love between man and woman, and yet she still longed to shelter every child in the world brave enough to love. Yunshang, knowing that passing the trial would earn a fine reward, hoped to ask on your behalf for one of Jinxiang Palace's formidable martial arts. But Lady Wen refused, and gave her instead a piece called Song of the Phoenix Seeking a Mate. This was a melody Lady Wen had composed in her youth, when she still believed in life, secretly holding within it an Internal Method — one that, driven by Internal Force, could govern the rhythms of the heart and breath. Yunshang's practicing it would not only benefit her, but would also help you return your energy to its source and harmonize the Five Elements within you. And so, for the rest of your life, you would never be free of her.

You intended to visit Jinxiang Palace, but the guide you were given was none other than the Painting Immortal, who had once appeared in the Kongtong dungeon, aiding you and Xiaomei in resisting the Mindless Monk. This was none other than Senior Sister Tang Xian'er, who had always been infatuated with Second Senior Brother back then. She carried herself with a carefree and composed demeanor, completely unafraid of you uncovering her identity. You couldn't tell whether she was an enemy or an ally, but considering she had once come to your aid, you couldn't bring yourself to confront her on the spot. You chose to hold back.
After washing up, you changed into wide-sleeved robes and attended the welcome banquet at the palace. From then on, you were a guest of Jinxiang Palace.

You wonder whether Miss Ying will attend the Wulin Assembly, and whether, seeing someone by your side, her heart might ache with the faintest pang. Even a thousandth part of wistfulness would make your devotion worthwhile.

You can't keep thinking about Miss Xiahou all the time; she is like a cloud at the edge of the sky, separated from you by a hundred and eight thousand miles — a distance measured not in roads, but in reincarnations.
One can't keep thinking about Master all the time; it would be a grave offense.
Work hard, and perhaps you can still manage, by next spring, to bring your wife to the Great Snow Mountain to sweep Master's grave and offer incense.
Otherwise, what else could you do? The one you admire is the wife of the Kongtong Sect Leader — not in this lifetime could she ever be yours to long for.
After all, Junior Martial Sister has already married and become another man's wife; you cannot remain rooted in place forever.
If Yunshang could know of this from beyond the grave, she would surely be glad.

You have long admired Jinxiang Palace and felt that it is filled with fragrance everywhere. It's possible that one of the young ladies might pity your loneliness and solitude and be willing to marry you, thus sparing you from a tragic life of isolation in old age.

You have long admired Jinxiang Palace, feeling that fragrance filled every corner like a paradise beyond compare, and at once your heart stirred with restless longing. Who could say — perhaps your future wife awaited discovery in this very place.

You've long admired Jinxiang Palace, but today, now that you've come, you find that after looking everyone over, Long Xiang is still the finest of them all — dignified and spirited, unlike anyone else.

Though you don't know what the palace master is discussing, you suspect it's likely related to the Nangong family. A lingering sense of unease creeps in, fearing that the Nangong family might take offense, leaving you in a difficult position to explain.

Jinxiang Palace is located in Hunan, and harbors a long-standing feud with the Nangong family, but has had little dealing with the Tang Clan of Shu. Such warm hospitality was truly unexpected. Lady Wen made no secret of it: she wished to enlist the Tang Clan's help against a band of unscrupulous men. There was a matter to discuss, but since you had traveled long and far and were weary from the road, it was set aside for now, left unspoken.

Before the Soul-Stealing Orchid rose to fame, Lady Wen was once hailed as the first beauty of the Wulin. As one would expect, her age should be comparable to the Nangong Family Head, at least in her forties, yet there was no trace of aging.

Before Master Xiahou Lan became famous, Lady Wen was once hailed as the first beauty of the Wulin. She should be around the same age as the Nangong Family Head, at least in her forties, yet there's no trace of her age.

You entered the palace to pay respects to Lady Wen. Though she was a woman, she maneuvered within the Wulin, single‑handedly founding the Jinxiang Palace to shelter all vulnerable female warriors, teaching them martial arts to protect themselves, ensuring that power could not harass them. She can be called a remarkable woman of her time.

In order to demonstrate to Junior Martial Sister how to call for help, you shouted loudly outside Jinxiang Palace, causing the people of Jinxiang Palace to become anxious and rush out, surrounding you completely. It took a lot of explanation afterward to clarify the situation. Not everyone in Jinxiang Palace judges others solely by appearance, but they certainly look down on those who lack common sense. This also led to your fellow disciples being looked down upon, and they truly did not want to admit they were associated with you.

Upon reaching Jinxiang Palace, the attendant palace women showed you all into the outer hall for tea and refreshments, then took their leave to inform the Palace Mistress and prepare to receive her honored guests.

You politely declined Jinxiang Palace's kind offer and continued walking. The Jinxiang Palace people had no choice but to follow the guest's lead, accompanying them all the way, relying on the palace's prestige to ensure calm and peaceful travel.

She was either lying down or vomiting the whole way, constantly ill and miserable. There was no other way, so her elder brother had to carry her off the boat and walk, making an appointment to meet you at Jinxiang Palace.

With everyone aboard, there was no good way to build a fire and brew medicine. Luckily you had Panacea Oil; you rubbed it under her nose, and she perked right up, causing chaos all over the boat—she all but sank it herself.
Ye Yunshang, who had clamored to come along on the boat, got seasick.

At first Xiao Zhu was afraid the boat would sink. As soon as she learned you would be boarding, she hurried to the market and bought sheepskins and leather to make floats, clutching them the whole way and refusing to let go. Only after the boat had sailed the river for a while did her fear ease, and she ran back and forth between bow and stern, too excited to sit still.
Junior Martial Sister seemed afraid the boat would sink and held you tightly throughout the journey.

The Tang Clan's group boarded a large ship prepared by the Jinxiang Palace people, enjoying the river scenery along the way. Accompanied by beautiful women, the gentle breeze and enchanting scenery left the disciples entranced, losing themselves in the moment.

Bidding farewell to your Imperial Soldier comrades and fellow travelers, the Tang Clan boarded the great ship Jinxiang Palace had prepared, admiring the river scenery along the way. With fair companions beside you and a gentle breeze under bright skies, the disciples quite lost themselves in the moment.

However, the Jinxiang Palace and the Nangong Family are at odds, and the greatest fear is that the invitation to the Tang Clan is a ruse, with the true intent being to humiliate the Nangong Family. Whether to go or not, it seems inevitable to offend someone, leaving you in a difficult position.

But you haven't forgotten‑this journey's purpose is indeed the Wulin Assembly at Fengyu Mountain. However, before that, you must first go to Jiangling to discuss the alliance with Nangong. Yet Jinxiang Palace and the Nangong Family are like water and fire. If you are invited to visit Jinxiang Palace first, it might not be easy to leave for Jiangling later. Whether you go or not, you might end up offending someone.

The Palace Mistress of Jinxiang Palace is a Wulin elder; though she lives in seclusion and rarely appears, her standing in the Jianghu is by no means low. Since the Palace Mistress has extended an invitation, how could you, a junior disciple of the Jianghu, refuse to answer it?

The two Jinxiang Palace disciples saw their junior sister angry and felt a chill in their hearts. They quickly remembered why they had come: if they offended you and the Tang Clan refused their request, what then? They could only force themselves to calm down and offer smiling apologies.

Long Xiang, who was traveling with you, heard the senior sisters approaching, gulped down her chicken leg in one bite, and hurried forward to greet them. She introduced you eagerly, only to meet with disappointment, dejection, disbelief, and even indignation from the two senior sisters. It turned out that whenever Long Xiang spoke of you, she always compared you to the senior brother, so the sect sisters who had never met you had built up their own fantasies—imagining you as dashing and skilled as the Tang Clan Flying Hero, only to find, on meeting you at last, nothing of the sort. Their hearts brimmed with the grievance of feeling deceived and made fools of; they could not have been more disappointed. You had heard such cutting words often enough to grow used to them. But this time Long Xiang did not stay silent—she turned on the two senior sisters with a sharp rebuke. Raised under her master's teaching, she had worshipped her heroic father since childhood and believed a man should be bold and generous, upright and unrestrained, ready to stand up for justice against wrongs, for country and people, with spirit enough to brave the Jianghu's fiercest storms and lay down his life on the battlefield. Such worth was not handed down at birth for one to coast through life and flaunt, but forged through your own hard trials. Beside qualities so truly precious, good looks or bad hardly bore mentioning.
On this day, they finally reached the territory of Jingzhou. They asked a waiter at the tea house and learned that continuing for several more days would lead to Jiangling and Yueyang.
Halfway along the road, Dharma Master Fu Yun slipped into the Tang Clan's ranks without anyone noticing. You only kept watch for stragglers, never realizing an extra person had joined.

Under immense pressure, you fell ill again and again, laid up in bed, and only learned on recovering that your Junior Brothers and Sisters had already taken the invitation and set off for Yueyang without you, leaving behind only the unlucky few who had lost at a game of finger-guessing to nurse you. All the merit you had built up over the years was squandered by your outrageous conduct—you had gone out with your head held high and come home crestfallen, and even Third Senior Brother could not hide his disappointment, though he said nothing. In his heart he kept turning over Confucius's words: 'Rotten wood cannot be carved; a wall of dung cannot be trowled.' Either way, you were surely one of them.

You swallowed your pride, resolved to get past Third Senior Brother first and worry about the rest later. Third Senior Brother was diligent and honest, but he had not addled his wits with too much reading—of course he saw straight through your utter lack of scruples. He turned instead to make Junior Martial Sister swear an oath: should you take liberties with her on the road, she must strike you down without mercy. Touch her anywhere but her head or hands, stare at her for more than half a stick of incense, or fail to reach an inn before nightfall, and she was to kill you on the spot, no exceptions. Junior Martial Sister agreed at once, and all your hopes collapsed—your scheme to grow closer to her in one stroke was stillborn.

Honesty being a virtue, you followed your heart and refused to guarantee Junior Martial Sister's safety—you could shield her from the wind and rain, but you were certain you could not control yourself. Third Senior Brother heard this and flew into a rage, at once placing Junior Martial Sister under house arrest.

Though he could no longer insist on keeping Junior Martial Sister with him, he remained uneasy about you. Yes, you had indeed worked hard and earned your merit, but that did not erase the fact of your poor character. He had to make you swear to hold strictly to propriety before he would allow Junior Martial Sister to travel with you.
Third Senior Brother felt very uneasy, hesitated for a while, and finally gently let go, freeing her.
Junior Martial Sister was sullen but still obediently followed you.

Your eyes blazed as you gave a lofty, passionate, yet utterly contrived speech, which made the junior martial sister shiver slightly, though Third Senior Brother was deeply moved and secretly cheered you on.

You long to journey through the Jianghu hand in hand with your junior martial sister, yet fear she might suffer hardship along the way. Should anything happen to her, would you not become a sinner for a thousand years? Since Third Senior Brother forbids her from going, you add your voice to persuade her as well.

You didn't have high expectations to begin with, so you merely clicked your tongue lightly at being stopped, not at all annoyed. Though you've won the junior martial sister's heart, you're not yet recognized by the sect. If you insist on marrying her, you'll surely face scorn. The Wulin Assembly is your chance to build a career, to display your skills and restore the Tang Clan's prestige. Once you seize the right opportunity, who would dare oppose your union with the junior martial sister? If Third Senior Brother is still ungrateful, you might just refuse to let him stay Acting Sect Leader!
Third Senior Brother couldn't possibly allow such a thing to happen; on both official and personal grounds, he wouldn't want Junior Martial Sister to travel with you.
Junior Martial Sister immediately became eager to try and wanted to go along.

Who else but you can represent the Tang Clan at the conference? This is the opportunity you've longed for, a chance to shine, while at the same time, you carry the reputation of your sect, and your honor and disgrace rest entirely on you.

Although your martial skill has come a long way since before, your character still raises too many concerns. Third Senior Brother originally intended Fourth Senior Brother to represent the Tang Clan, but unfortunately, Fourth Senior Brother is away on a long journey and not at home. There are no other capable leaders, so they reluctantly sent you out to wreak havoc in the Central Plains.

The invitation states that the Wulin Assembly will be held on October 15th this year at Fengyu Mountain. Fengyu Mountain lies south of Yueyang, west of the Dongting Lake, and is not a renowned mountain, but rather a remote and secluded place. The Shangguan family has chosen this location to host the gathering, with a deliberate intent to embarrass the Nangong family by leveraging the Jinxiang Palace. It is well known that the two factions have long‑standing conflicts due to old disputes between the Family Head and the Palace Mistress, forcing the Nangong family's members to bow whenever passing through Jinxiang Palace's territory. Hosting the gathering at Fengyu Mountain is a calculated move to humiliate the Nangong family further, ensuring they can no longer claim the title of leading figure in the Wulin.

You and Third Senior Brother discussed it. Though you had real misgivings about the Imperial Court's interference — the Tang Clan disdains to scheme with officialdom, and has never styled itself one of the righteous sects — still, when the realm rises or falls, every commoner bears a part of the burden, and defending one's home admits no refusal. Otherwise, the sect leader of old would never have led the sect to stand beside the righteous factions of the Central Plains against the Supreme Bliss Cult, a stand that ended in the sect's own ruin. Whatever the case, this Wulin Assembly could not be missed.

The Imperial Court's involvement in the Jianghu turmoil effectively allows major sects to consolidate their power on the surface, yet is this not also a test? Song Bei, holding an official position, should remain loyal to the court and not speak out, yet out of consideration for your friendship, he still subtly advised the Tang Clan: no matter how proud they may be, they must send representatives this time, or face dire consequences later.

Third Senior Brother had just come out to welcome the two guests into Zhengxin Hall and serve them tea. After some formal greetings, the Cang Gang disciple finally explained his intentions. It turned out that he was not a regular follower of the Cang Gang but an Incense Master of the Five Halls, Zhu Wu of the Nine Immortal Hall. He reported directly to the Shangguan Family Head, ranking second only to one person within the Cang Gang. Song Bei's mission this time was merely to accompany him as an observer.  Zhu Wu modestly spoke at first but then went on and on, summarizing the Tang Clan's and Shangguan family's grudges lightly. He constantly emphasized the greater good and said that since the siege of Jiangling, the Jianghu winds had been turbulent like a river, ceaselessly continuous. The Nangong Family had lost its respected elders, while various sects in the Central Plains were injured by the Demon Cult's diversion tactics, suffering greatly. Furthermore, internal struggles persisted without the Heart of the Wulin to mediate. Unity against the Demon Cult was proving difficult if not impossible.  If the Mud Cult took advantage of the six sects' mutual hindrance and launched another assault with a hundred thousand troops, invading Xiangyang and allowing Jin soldiers into the pass; and southwardly attacking the Nangong Family to seize control over the Wulin, it would be nothing short of disaster. This not only threatened the court but also posed an imminent danger to the country and its people, like a sword hanging precariously above their throats.  He spoke with great passion, his sincerity evident. His aim was clear: he wanted the Tang Clan to participate under the guise of righteousness to ensure they could not simply look out for themselves. Both you and Third Senior Brother felt a shiver down your spine at his words; though this man claimed to be from a humble fisherman's family with no schooling, his eloquence was impressive and well‑founded, leaving no room for debate.  He then continued by saying that although the Shangguan Family Head had retired from the Jianghu, he could not bear to see such suffering. Therefore, he petitioned the court, and having received an imperial edict and a promotion to the third rank, he convened a grand Wulin assembly, calling on righteous sects to discuss countermeasures against the Demon Cult.  In the presence of Song Bei as witness, he presented the invitation to the Great Assembly and then respectfully took his leave.

Although you've met Divine Constable Song before, you've never had the chance to get to know him, and today is the first time you've spoken. He heard of your many deeds, all of which are infamous, and upon meeting, he spoke in a harsh tone, giving a proper warning.

You welcomed the guests into the courtyard. Besides Divine Constable Song, there was also a Cang Gang disciple. Although Madam Shangguan switched sides at the last moment, the Cang Gang disciples remained inactive, and this grudge ultimately took root. At this moment, when the fellow disciples saw the Cang Gang disciple, their eyes seemed ready to burst into flames.
You remained unmoved upon hearing the words. That Junior Brother, seeing you so composed, felt his remaining worries vanish.
You were secretly startled, thinking you hadn't done anything wrong, but upon hearing it was an official, your heart had already quivered.
Your conscience was guilty as a thief's, and you immediately assumed the officials had come to arrest you.
You felt a chill down your spine, thinking that some misdeed had finally come to light.

An officer had come up the mountain, he said, and this was not something to be careless about — he told you to go out and greet the man first, while he hurried to the Scripture Hall to fetch the acting Sect Leader.
He didn't find the Third Senior Brother, but upon seeing you, he seemed to have swallowed a calming pill and relaxed.
He saw you lose to Jinwu Shangren, didn't take you seriously, and you didn't get angry, just listened to his rude, haphazard commands.
He saw you lose to Jinwu Shangren and didn't think much of you — not until you slapped him across the face did he finally behave himself.
You had just checked on the Sect Leader's condition that day, came out of Zhengxin Hall, and just encountered a clumsy junior brother rushing into Zhengxin Hall, shouting to find the Sect Leader.

Fourth Senior Brother ordered the dishes, Third Senior Brother saw to the wine, and you did the cooking. To see Fourth Senior Brother off, you spent the whole night reliving old memories both sweet and bitter, sometimes in tears, sometimes doubled over with laughter. During this month's gathering, Fourth Senior Brother arrived late. Asked why, it turned out the trade caravan he'd talked about for so long had finally set out. With the worst finally behind them and an auspicious day at hand, he steeled his resolve and set the departure in motion at last, afraid that if he waited any longer he'd never bring himself to go. You and Junior Martial Sister waved goodbye, promising to see each other again soon. Her heart brimmed with a sweetness she couldn't put into words; she went back to her room, bathed, changed, and settled in for more sleep. But the moment you returned to yours, your fellow disciples subjected you to private punishment.

He had spent the night at the Tang Clan waiting for the two of you to return, and seeing now how intimate you both seemed, clearly of one heart, he finally let himself relax—and was about to tease you further when the senior and junior sisters, all smitten with his Pan An-worthy looks, heard the commotion and, most unusually, rose at dawn to come make a nuisance of themselves. At this moment, an unexpected figure casually stepped out of the Disciples' Quarters, clad in a white robe‑Rui Sheng.

Third Senior Brother's anger, however great, was ultimately no match for his own Junior Martial Sister's coaxing pats; her small hand patted the anger clean out of him, blow by blow. Seeing her face aglow again, the gloom of recent days swept away, he could not help but feel his old heart eased, secretly grateful he had not acted the tyrant and disregarded her convictions.

Xie Wuchen had never meant to compete for her hand when he entered the fray, and this was just the moment to bow out; he even offered a few words of generous encouragement. The Eldest Young Lord had already struck a private agreement with you, so this came as no surprise to him; seizing the chance to make such a magnanimous, fitting speech, he moved Third Senior Brother almost to tears.

Xie Wuchen had never meant to compete for her hand in the first place, so he seized the moment to bow out gracefully, offering a few magnanimous words of encouragement. Rui Sheng was of noble bearing and fine cultivation, and he was glad to see two lovers united at last. Only Nangong Shen's face darkened, his displeasure plain to see—though that, too, was understandable.

As they spoke, Fourth Senior Brother's sharp eyes caught two figures on the plank road, one in green and one in red—wasn't that you and Junior Martial Sister? She had been riding coquettishly on your back, but the moment she spotted someone, she leapt down at once, both of you wearing the guilty look of thieves caught in the act, and shuffled over to confess. Third Senior Brother, seeing Junior Martial Sister safely home, felt a great weight lift from his heart, yet he was still no small measure angry, and could not help but lecture her at length, so she would understand the gravity of what she'd done.
It was your character he looked down upon.

Fourth Senior Brother returned early in the morning and found Third Senior Brother pacing back and forth. Once he heard the whole story, he was stunned, mouth agape—he had always mocked you as a hopeless dreamer, and never imagined Junior Martial Sister would truly run to your side. He couldn't help but wonder what had become of this world. Was it still the world it used to be? Third Senior Brother, well-read as he was, knew the old truth that in knowing another, it is the heart's understanding that matters most. Even Confucius once regretted judging people by their looks. And so Third Senior Brother had never thought less of you for your appearance.

The fact that Junior Martial Sister has not returned home at night is already enough to make one's stomach ache with worry. What's even more terrifying is that the person she is looking for is you. How can she be so naive, not realizing that she is heading into a den of dragons and tigers? The most dangerous place in the world is right by your side.
The mere thought of Junior Martial Sister not returning at night is enough to make one's stomach churn. The worst fear is that she might not find you and get lost in the mountains. What then?

The Junior Martial Sister had lived through too much in a single day—sorrow, fear, anger, panic—all compounded by the failure of her Heaven and Earth Silent Power, until she was overwhelmed by a flood of feeling. Only with someone to shield her could she finally let herself relax, and the moment that tension eased, a deep weariness swept over her; she swayed unsteadily toward you, leaned against you, and fell asleep. The two of you heartless souls, lost in tender feeling and quiet bliss, while poor Third Senior Brother's old bones suffered through the whole night—forced to swallow his pride and clean up the mess of the Junior Martial Sister's runaway bride affair, his reputation left in tatters. He paced back and forth between Zhengxin Hall and the training grounds, craning his neck for your return.

Her innocent eyes saw no beauty or ugliness in appearance; she simply loved the sense of peace she felt at the sight of you. She wasn't unaware that you were born with striking looks that had drawn no end of mockery from the world, but that was plainly not your fault—mere appearance could never erase your efforts, and she had always seen the brilliance in you. Besides, what did the world's prejudices have to do with her? She couldn't understand why she should have to take everyone else's opinion as her own. There were men like the Eldest Senior Brother, praised by all yet spiteful and cruel underneath; and there were men like you, who respected and cherished yourself, and who, whenever she drew near, would go to every length to make her happy. Wasn't the whole point of choosing a partner to make life better? Only a fool would choose the former and suffer for it every day. You were deeply shaken to hear it, and though your heart brimmed with happiness, you also felt a nagging unease you couldn't shake, and pestered her with endless questions, each one needling her judgment, stubbornly bent on making her see reason. You dragged her into a long debate on worldly opinion, even accusing her of having no eye for looks. Junior Martial Sister couldn't follow any of it, only felt the weight of it and found you tiresome. She had never thought ill of you at all—it was you who insisted she bow to worldly prejudice. The folly was yours to choose, and if she came to resent you for it, you had earned it.

At the very least, you should take advantage of her dazed state and coax her into marriage, then proceed with the wedding. Once the rice is cooked into porridge, there's no turning back‑she won't dare defy you afterward! A pure and innocent Junior Martial Sister, like a forest animal, has no idea of your cunning plans.

As you walk away, your Junior Martial Brothers and Sisters all snort in disdain at your affectedly sentimental expression. Knowing you should give up hope, you still dare not believe this is the end, hoping there's still a chance, wanting to confirm her feelings. As if your hearts were joined, you faintly heard someone calling out to you, and rose to hurry home, quickening your step with every stride, rushing to close the distance between you. The mountain was so vast, the night so dark, yet still you found her, and she found you.
Stepping out of Zhengxin Hall, she spared not a glance for the handsomest young lords or heroes.
Stepping out of Zhengxin Hall, she found that Ruisheng had already pointed her the way you had gone.

Since she reached its first mastery, her temperament had grown ever more detached and serene, her heart pure as jade, untouched by a speck of dust. No joy, anger, sorrow, fear, love, hatred, or desire—this was both her shield and her seal, locking her feelings deep within, where no one could see her true face. Not until the Sect Leader fell ill did the world she knew seem to overturn overnight, heaven and earth tilting beneath her. Pressure pressed in from every side until she could hardly breathe, as though her feet no longer touched solid ground, and though she longed to give something of herself to the sect, her strength wasn't equal to her will, and she could only fret in helpless silence. She had told herself she'd already made peace with it all, but she hadn't. As the day she was to leave home drew nearer, it grew harder and harder to keep the bell from ringing. Once that first tear fell, there was no holding back the rest, and a thousand thoughts came flooding in. Yet alongside the fear and sorrow was something else: the pride and courage of the Tang family, a resolve that rose above notions of right and wrong, setting her apart from the crowd. She would not drift with the current or bow blindly to others' wishes; small as she was, she meant to protect the family she treasured. And that included you. Just as she had once lost her way in the mountains, trembling, and you had always come with a lantern to find her—this time it was her turn to come find you.
Third Senior Brother was badly startled and hurried over with soothing words, asking the three groom candidates and the matchmaker to step aside for the moment.
Yunshang and Third Senior Brother were both alarmed, and hurried to her side with soothing words, asking the three groom candidates and the matchmaker to step aside for the moment.

At the same time, at Zhengxin Hall, the junior martial sister remained hesitating without making a decision. The three young lords who had come to propose were all descendants of prestigious families, well‑educated and handsome. By all accounts, accompanying any of them would not be a mistake, and her life would surely be peaceful and fulfilling. Yet she could not choose, for all three were equally good, and all three equally unappealing. When pressed, she wanted to blindly select one to appease them, but suddenly her mind conjured the image of your retreating figure, as if you would never return. A wave of sorrow surged within her, and she stood motionless, tears streaming down her face.
Memories are vivid in mind, yet this is the final day. You must conceal your recollections and transform your deep emotions into blessings.

That day, you single-handedly challenged Venerable Golden Crow, forcing him to reveal his true form before the eyes of all and sending him fleeing in disarray — word of it resounded throughout the Jianghu.

That day you single-handedly challenged Venerable Golden Crow, saw through his true form, and cut him down with your sword — word of the deed spread throughout the Jianghu. Even the Kongtong disciples who had opposed you could not help admiring your skill and spirit. Back in the mountains, whenever they spoke of your feat of breaking through and cutting down every foe, they took pride in having crossed blades with you. No matter how he was killed, he would not die, and after he mended his ways and took the tonsure, he sheltered under Kongtong's roof, so that his old enemies never had the chance to settle their scores. The Tang Clan was swept up in your notoriety because of it — its name rang louder, but its good repute took a little more damage besides.

A clash of blades and swords may only end in death, but if the Junior Martial Sister rejects you, the heartache would be enough to kill you ten times over. Therefore, they sacrificed their own wishes to ensure the completeness of all.
So she gave up her own wish, to spare everyone else. You turned your back to the light and walked into the night, believing dawn would never come again.

You can endure that kind of thing, but others might not be able to. While you were wallowing in self‑pity, a Tang Clan disciple burst in, flustered and agitated, informing you that Rui Sheng had suddenly changed her mind and decided not to seek a marriage. Instead, she wanted to become your matchmaker and was currently helping you court the junior martial sister.
You had come to see how limited your own power was. There was no way to have both; letting go was the best choice, and the better one for everyone.

At the moment of parting, you stood silently facing each other, spontaneously recalling your youthful days, hand in hand singing songs among the green mountains, how lively it was. Regrettably, time flows like water, desolate; beauty has not aged, yet the heart is lonely.

The night journey up the mountain was both brief and long. The junior martial sister, no longer the quiet one of old, kept asking questions, and you answered every query. The sibling pair chatted and laughed, also wiping away tears in the dark. Afraid of being seen, you set her down before reaching the main courtyard.

Junior Martial Sister hesitated, unwilling to go up the mountain. Once she did, the last moment they could be together would be over. She suddenly wanted to play a childish trick, pretending her foot hurt and unable to move. You became concerned, wanting to check her injury, but she dodged you, thinking she still resented you. Yet you didn't realize that at this moment, looking at you made her heart race. Thinking that after today, there would be no more opportunities to be spoiled, Junior Martial Sister gathered her courage and asked you to carry her. You were both sad and happy, overwhelmed with a complex blend of emotions. Her dependence on you was different from others, like water but deep as the sea. You knew she was no longer a child, and after tonight, tomorrow she would become a wife. By etiquette, you should have kept your distance, but at this very moment, she was still your Junior Martial Sister, your family, with a bond deeper than that of a younger sister. You loved her so deeply it was incurable. So you turned around, knelt on one knee, and Junior Martial Sister watched you bow for her, revealing your back. She felt both bitter and sweet, hesitantly approaching, and leaned her soft, yielding body against your back.
The dust has settled below the mountain, but the matter is far from over. Tonight is the pivotal moment in Junior Martial Sister's life, a decision she must make at home.
You thanked Rui Sheng for her help, but the matter was far from over. Tonight was the pivotal moment in Junior Martial Sister's life; she had to go home and make her decision.
Jinwu Shangren's Golden Cicada Sheds Its Shell strategy had even caught Rui Sheng off guard, chasing further than you did, yet ultimately failed to capture the person.
After expressing thanks, the four of them successively bowed and departed.

Your senior sister from the Mystic Skill Gate spoke to you at this moment, her tone a bit more intimate, hinting at pride. The sect leader's junior sister has a discerning eye, going against the majority to accept you into the sect, facing quite a bit of criticism for it. When she hears about your remarkable achievements, how delighted she will surely be. The three people nearby, upon witnessing this, all felt a pang of jealousy, thinking that if it hadn't been for Sect Leader Wei stepping in to draw lots at that time, you might have joined their sect instead, and it wouldn't have been Ju Dongyin basking in such glory.

Though the Kongtong sect is at fault, they have promised all compensation and proper courtesies, which will not be lacking. However, the enmity between you and the Kongtong sect is a separate matter. As long as your martial arts are not yet ruined and you still draw breath, the Kongtong Mystic Skill Gate will pursue you to the end.

Kongtong is a reputable righteous sect. Though it has been misled by villains, leading to wrongdoing, once the truth is clarified, they will not argue, admitting they cannot distinguish right from wrong. They will report to the four sect leaders, accept punishment themselves, and rectify the discipline within the sect. They will then go to the Tang Clan to apologize humbly.

Yan Jiang wore a sheepish, brazen look - but he was straightforward to the bone and saw no graceful way down, so he simply resolved to jump off the stage, broken legs be damned, and bowed his head to you in both thanks and apology.
You were furious with Kongtong beyond measure, and stepped forward with no patience left. If he still wanted a fight, you were ready to see it through to the end.

Though you were furious with Kongtong, propriety held you back from letting it show. You swallowed your temper and stepped forward to hear what he had to say - and if he meant to fight, you weren't afraid of that either.

Though you were still angry with Kongtong, you had, after all, once studied under the Flying Heaven Gate, and you found yourself calling him Senior Brother before you could stop yourself. Yan Jiang beamed, his face glowing with pride, and turned at once to boast: though the Flying Heaven Gate had produced one disgrace, it had also produced a hero like you! He was thoroughly pleased with himself, having entirely forgotten his own part in bullying you back then. He swore he would tell the Fire Dragon Immortal Monarch of your deeds and claim credit on your behalf - never once saying a word of thanks, though his gratitude showed plainly all the same. You were taken aback for a moment, then found yourself smiling, your anger fading somewhat.
Yan Jiang couldn't help but shout for you to come over.

The thought alone made them shudder in retrospect - had you not forced this demon to reveal his true form, who knew how much longer they would have been deceived? Once the election for Sect Leader had passed and power fell into Venerable Golden Crow's hands, how could a hundred years' foundation have possibly survived?

Before Venerable Golden Crow took his monastic vows, people were not ignorant of his past misdeeds - they simply believed the former Sect Leader had tamed and reformed him, and that after he entered the monastic gate he had truly repented, so even if his character remained questionable, he stayed devoted to Kongtong. Only now did they realize that what Tang Clan had said was not baseless after all. Whether Venerable Golden Crow truly hailed from the Thousand Lantern Tower, as Tang Clan claimed, remained unknown - but wearing a Human Skin Cloak was far too sinister a thing, and no one of the righteous path would ever do such a deed. Iron Spine Mountain King had once, in his younger years, taken on the grim work of preparing corpses for burial to make a living; stepping forward for a closer look, he declared at once, without doubt, that the flesh Venerable Golden Crow had shed was made from real human blood and flesh.

Before Venerable Golden Crow took his monastic vows, people were not ignorant of his past misdeeds - they simply believed the former Sect Leader had tamed and reformed him, and that after he entered the monastic gate he had truly repented, so even if his character remained questionable, he stayed devoted to Kongtong. Only now did they realize that what Tang Clan had said was not baseless after all. Whether Venerable Golden Crow truly hailed from the Thousand Lantern Tower, as Tang Clan claimed, remained unknown - but that he killed people to sew himself a Painted Skin robe, he had admitted with his own mouth.

Everyone at Kongtong saw with their own eyes as Venerable Golden Crow shed his skin and fled, and all of them went pale with shock, unable to speak for a long moment. Among them were not a few who had been close to him, in frequent contact - yet not one had seen through his true face.

Joyful as this was, you did not forget that behind Venerable Golden Crow stood another - the true mastermind of it all. Only by bringing down that hidden schemer could this vengeance truly be settled.
Only by clutching at your sleeve could she feel at ease again.

Junior Martial Sister was overwhelmed with joy, on the verge of tears. She felt both grateful and proud toward you. She wasn't sure if it was an illusion, but she always felt you had suddenly grown a bit taller, making you seem a bit farther away from her.

Eldest Senior Brother's great vengeance was avenged at last. Not only did your Tang Clan brothers and sisters admire you to the point of prostrating themselves, but the guests in attendance - heroes and heroines of the martial world, kinfolk and elders alike - broke into thunderous applause.
The Nine-Lives Leopard's last remaining life was snuffed out by your hand, never to revive.

Consumed by desire, his ambitions still unfulfilled, he refused to accept death and clung desperately to the mortal world. Other insolent words you might have borne, but when he insulted the one you loved, that you could not forgive. You loosed another dart, finally bringing this great evil to justice.

The instant his hand brushed the smoke bomb in his robe, you knew he meant to flee. The moment Venerable Golden Crow performed the Golden Cicada Sheds Its Shell, you sprang into the air without hesitation, moving after him yet arriving first, and cut him cleanly out of the sky, felling him to the ground.

Hindered by the smoke, you couldn't stop him in time - amid wild laughter, Venerable Golden Crow got away, vanishing into the flowing crowds. You had no idea what he truly looked like; how could you ever find him now? Consumed by grief and rage, you threw back your head and howled, the sound shaking the four directions until everyone at Kongtong trembled with fear. Your fellow disciples crowded around, offering comfort in one voice - look on the bright side, they said: you had stripped Venerable Golden Crow of his disguise and sent him fleeing in disgrace before everyone's eyes. That monster could never again hide within the Kongtong Sect, and a great orthodox sect had narrowly escaped falling into a traitor's hands.

Junior Martial Sister had been watching you the whole time. When Venerable Golden Crow suddenly performed the Golden Cicada Sheds Its Shell and fled, she was startled for an instant, but Heaven and Earth Silent Power trains not only the body and the qi but the mind as well, and within a breath she steadied herself, will and action moving together. With a leap she soared into the sky and kicked him down to the ground.
Only then did you see his true face - a gaunt, skeletal monk beneath the thick suit of flesh he wore.
Knowing his doom was sealed and all hope gone, his malice had not lessened one whit; even facing death he wanted to unsettle others, boasting proudly of his cloak of flayed skin, sewn from real human flesh and blood - every so often he would claim to go into secluded cultivation, only to kill and skin another victim to sew a new one.
Such a vicious, depraved man could not be suffered by the world. You raised your hand and loosed a dart, finally bringing this great evil to justice. The Nine-Lives Leopard's last life was spent by your hand, never to rise again.

His eyes bulged, disbelieving that you had seen through his feigned death; your small sword had carved a grievous wound, the blade sinking to the hilt and tearing open a great gash - no living creature could survive such a blow. Venerable Golden Crow's heart turned to ice; only now did he believe he would truly die, not at the hands of some peerless master, but at the hands of you, an underling he'd never thought twice about. The realization struck him: he had been wrong. You were no mere underling - you were strong, not to be trifled with. In this dire strait, there was no room left to save face; escape came first. He drew out a smoke bomb to blind their eyes and hurled it down, then performed the Golden Cicada Sheds Its Shell, shedding his bulky flesh-suit, and shot skyward.
Without needing anyone else's cry of warning, you spun round in an instant, your sword arcing down, and drove Venerable Golden Crow back.

You couldn't say how long the torment lasted before the sounds gradually faded into silence. You pushed open the door and stepped out; the rain still fell, smoke and gunpowder drifting through it, the ground littered with spent firecrackers, cold and bare. She was already gone, the old courtyard left with nothing but a lingering scent. However reluctant you were, you had to let go. May she find a place warm as eternal spring, her smile blooming like a flower in full bloom.

The deafening sound of firecrackers and gongs echoed through the sky, yet you ignored it. You deliberately chose not to hear about her, unwilling to know who she had finally chosen. Even more, you dared not go to see her off, hiding your head under the quilt.

Because of your efforts, the Junior Martial Sister's wedding was carried through smoothly after all. That night the rain began, and it still hadn't stopped by the next day when she married. As the old saying goes, rain on a wedding day is heaven's blessing- as if hinting that the Tang Clan too was about to be reborn anew.

You don't believe you can win, yet you refuse to surrender without a fight; even if you lose, you'd rather do so with honor. This matter is more than life or death. A clash of blades and swords may only end in death, but if the Junior Martial Sister rejects you, the heartache would be enough to kill you ten times over. Perhaps even in your next life, your heart would still ache. Yet, despite all this, you still muster the courage to fight for the person you love most in this lifetime.
So you set aside your own wishes, to spare everyone else. You turned your back to the light and walked into the night, believing there would never be a dawn again.
You have realized that your abilities are limited. There is no win‑win solution; letting go is the best choice, beneficial to everyone.

You couldn't say how long the torment lasted before the sounds gradually faded into silence. You pushed open the door and stepped out; the rain still fell, smoke and gunpowder drifting through it, the ground littered with spent firecrackers, cold and bare. That night the rain began, and it hadn't stopped by the next day when she married. Since ancient times it's been said that rain on a wedding day is heaven's blessing, yet the two of you felt only cold and desolate, wretched and forlorn.
You turned your back to the light and walked into the night, believing there would never be a dawn again.

Just back in the courtyard, people congratulating and celebrating surrounded you, their words full of cutting compliments. You ran into the night as if fleeing, afraid that the joyous candlelight would catch your face.

Beautiful time slips away swift as a shuttle, and the days that follow all blur past like flowers glimpsed from a galloping horse. Each time you startle back to the present, it feels as if you are living it all over again.

Yunshang clung tightly to you, afraid you would vanish. She, who always needed to be doted on, turned it around to comfort you instead, begging you not to be afraid, not to cry, pleading, almost desperately, that you not forget her. You didn't know why the tears fell, wanting to hold time still in that moment, reaching back to take her small hand- but when you came to yourself, it was already all in the past. The memory scattered on the wind in an instant, and even ██'s name, you no longer remembered.
Burying your head under the quilt, you needn't worry about looking dignified. No one can hear you scream.
You hadn't noticed Rui Sheng's arrival, hadn't even had the chance to tease him about becoming a bridegroom, when you saw the alarm on his face.
You might be tired, or perhaps the wine's fragrance has lured you into a daze, leaving you drowsy and reluctant to wake up.

You would certainly say you'd give everything, wager your very life. But who in this world isn't struggling just to survive? If no one had stepped in a moment ago, you would have died at the Venerable Golden Crow's hands. Your utmost effort, even your life, isn't enough to protect the one you love. He knew full well it wasn't fair to say this to you, but he steeled himself to say it anyway- he wouldn't let you run from it and spend a lifetime in regret. Honest words are hard on the ears, but that's a friend's duty.

But you lost to the Venerable Golden Crow. Only then did Rui Sheng realize you weren't up to it. Your breadth of mind and your boldness, he had always admired- but with your current skill, walking the Jianghu, you could scarcely take a step. If Miss Tang went with you, what could you protect her with?

But you lost to the Venerable Golden Crow. Only then did Rui Sheng realize you weren't up to it. Your breadth of mind and your boldness, he had always admired- but your Internal Skill was ruined, your power far below what it once was. Walking the Jianghu in your current state, you could scarcely take a step. If Miss Tang went with you, what could you protect her with?

When he came down the mountain and saw you talking with your junior martial sister, he had already caught the deep concern beneath your words, and the longing and reluctance in her eyes. As any onlooker could tell, however you looked at it, the two of you were plainly in love with each other. You surely wouldn't believe it, so he said no more, but in truth his regard for the Junior Martial Sister surged in that instant: he had always thought her merely delicate and lovely, but glimpsing her unstained heart then, he felt still greater admiration. He was envious of you and glad for you both at once, and counted himself fortunate; from that moment he resolved to step aside gladly. The world ought to have such a fine tale, one to tease a certain immortal with someday.

You saw him grow strangely anxious and suspected he meant to murder you now that you were alone. It was only a joke, but the flicker of fear in your eyes left Rui Sheng at a loss for words. He had thought himself a man of the righteous path — he couldn't fathom how he had become so contemptible in your eyes, and to think he had once counted you a friend.

Fourth Senior Brother had meant to ask Rui Sheng to escort her, but Rui Sheng declined on grounds of fairness and went on ahead with you. Only once you had gone deep into the woods did you stop to talk.

Fourth Senior Brother feared the Kongtong men might double back and strike again, so he wanted more hands escorting the Junior Martial Sister up the mountain, to leave nothing to chance. He asked you to fall back a few steps and take the rear, and together they closed ranks around the Junior Martial Sister and bore her safely back up the mountain.
Though the Kongtong men had all been sent packing, the matter still wasn't over — the pressing task now was to get the Junior Martial Sister safely back up the mountain.

Even the Kongtong men who saw it frowned and pointed in disgust. However ruthless and overbearing a man might be, he still could not flout the code of the Jianghu.
In a duel between two men, life and death are fated, and neither can blame the other — but to trick someone into standing down and then strike from ambush was conduct no righteous path could tolerate.
Seeing that Venerable Golden Crow had brought the crowd's fury on himself, cursed till he could not lift his head, unable to defend himself and with no face left to stay, discord broke out among his men: the Mystic Skill Guardian, least willing of all to stand by him, led the way in taking his leave, and the Soul-Stealing Guardian soon followed, not troubling to hide his satisfaction. With Kongtong's position lost, they cleared out entirely in the blink of an eye, leaving Venerable Golden Crow beside himself with fury, not daring to linger even a moment longer.

Jinwu Shangren's strike was never meant to take your life, but rather to apply a hidden force. Although ambushing is frowned upon, if others saw he didn't intend to kill, they would likely say nothing at first, then pretend to be a righteous monk, warning you not to be careless in battle, to avoid the main point, to obscure the truth, and to twist black into white. At that moment, you would inevitably become enraged, and a fight would ensue. When the hidden force surged up to your head, you would no longer have the strength to resist, and he would then launch a final assault, defeating you before letting you go. Would the onlookers not praise his compassion and magnanimity? However, things did not unfold as he had planned. His ambush failed, instantly inciting the guests into a surge of anger, who all cursed him as a wicked monk. On a fine day, he had caused trouble, and during a duel that was supposed to be a fair contest where neither side would take a life, they had already decided a winner, yet he had ambushed and attacked when the opponent was unprepared. Was this not a case of using words to trick the other side into holding back, while himself attacking with all his might? Jinwu Shangren had thus trapped himself, unable to defend himself, for he could not claim that his strike would not kill, but would only leave the opponent as a fool.

Fourth Senior Brother stayed behind to clean up the aftermath and entrusted you with escorting the Junior Martial Sister home — a piece of quiet kindness on his part, giving you a little more time alone with her. Whatever still needed saying, better say it now and leave no regrets. Tonight was the pivotal hour of the Junior Martial Sister's life; she had to go home and make her choice.
You thanked Rui Sheng for lending a hand, but the matter still wasn't over.
Though the Kongtong men had all been sent packing, the matter still wasn't over — the pressing task now was to get the Junior Martial Sister safely back up the mountain.

Before he died, he wanted to ask you to cremate him, scatter his ashes on the wind, and let him fly free to ascend as an immortal. You couldn't care less — he had come to the Tang Clan to cause trouble, died of his own doing, and still had the nerve to make demands. Not only did you not care, you meant to throw his corpse by the roadside to feed the wild dogs. Those words left him unable to die in peace, and even Fourth Senior Brother broke into a cold sweat — he had always known you were ruthless, but never imagined you were this ruthless. You weren't merely a mix of good and evil; you were downright wicked, wicked enough to make the Four Great Bandits — Song, Wang, Tian, and Fang — turn pale at the sight of you.

You honored him as a true man and asked for his last words. His eyes, no longer full of hostility, met yours as he asked you to cremate him and scatter his ashes on the wind, to let him fly free and ascend as an immortal.

You had not gone without his cold looks back at Flying Heaven Gate, yet seeing him like this, you still could not help feeling a pang of sorrow. You wanted to bring him back to Kongtong for burial, but he would have none of it — though his eyes no longer held any hostility. Once you were willing to call him Senior Brother, he counted you as one of his own. He gave you the secret manual he carried and asked you to cremate him, scatter his ashes on the wind, and let him fly free to ascend as an immortal.

Venerable Golden Crow had not dared to kill you moments before, but now, past caring, he turned on his own man without the least mercy. Yan Jiang had never imagined Venerable Golden Crow would strike him; he could not summon his qi to resist or dodge in time, and was struck squarely, his ribs and organs shattered, seemingly beyond saving. He proved himself a tough one all the same — he asked you to carry him far away while breath remained in him, unwilling to die on Tang Clan soil.

Venerable Golden Crow feigned defeat and struck from ambush — the blow was never meant to take your life, only to plant hidden force in you.
Though a sneak attack was beneath contempt, onlookers who saw he had not gone for the kill found little to say for the moment, while he himself put on the pious air of a virtuous monk, lecturing you that a duelist must never let his guard down, twisting the truth and calling black white.
He reasoned that you would surely fly into a rage, and it would do no harm to trade a few more blows; once the hidden force surged up into your skull, you would have no strength left to resist, and he could finish you with one more assault before letting you off lightly.
Would not everyone then praise his compassion and magnanimity?
But it did not go as he planned. The failed ambush at once set the guests seething, and they all cursed him for a wicked monk — not only had he made trouble on a day of joy, but bested in skill, he had feigned defeat and struck from hiding besides; for a proud elder of Kongtong, one of the Six Great Orthodox Sects, to stoop to such baseness — how could he ever win men's respect?
Even his own Kongtong men frowned and pointed in disgust at the sight.
Venerable Golden Crow had not yet risen to lead his sect; he was merely seizing the pretext to win the Four Sect Leaders' trust, which alone had let him swagger all the way to distant Shu to stir up trouble and seek revenge on someone's wedding day — already unreasonable, and losing the duel made it shameful besides.
Winning and losing is the way of contests, and that alone would not have stirred such fury — but his feigned defeat, and the ambush he sprang the instant his opponent's guard was down, were conduct no righteous path could tolerate.
Seeing that Venerable Golden Crow had brought the crowd's wrath on himself, cursed till he could not raise his head, unable to defend himself and with no face left to stay, discord broke out among his own men: the Mystic Skill Guardian, least willing of all to stand by him, led the way in thanking the Tang Clan and taking his leave; the Iron Fist and Soul-Stealing Guardians followed soon after; only the Flying Heaven Guardian, Yan Jiang, remained, still unwilling to let it go, shamed and furious both.
Though he seethed inside, he still meant to shield his senior brother — men in the same boat, after all, must row together.
However grave the offense, it was not for outsiders to judge; once they were back at Kongtong's Flying Heaven Hall with the doors shut, he would ask the Flying Heaven Gate Leader to mete out punishment by the sect's own rules.
He held to loyalty; Venerable Golden Crow did not. His scheme had failed, and with the crowd baying for his blood, he was already beside himself with fury — seeing Yan Jiang still dare to press him, he showed no mercy in his rage, and one blow to the chest struck the man down before he fled.

Not long after you fled, the Blazing Sun Hammer's true qi flared up inside you; you collapsed, convulsing, and burned with fever. When you woke, you could remember nothing at all — only the malice in Venerable Golden Crow's smile remained, and it never left you.

That night, Third Senior Brother and Fourth Senior Brother set out wine and drank with you. Speaking of the old days when the Tang Clan had flourished, all three of you were overcome with feeling, as though a lifetime had passed; sorrow welled up unbidden, and the three of you wept together, shoulder to shoulder. Those lively days seemed only yesterday, yet the moons had waxed and the stars had wheeled on, and of the once-mighty Tang Clan, only the three of you old hands remained.

Third Senior Brother wanted to prepare wine to drink with you, but you politely declined. You were simply too tired. There was no Junior Martial Sister here anymore, and you could no longer be as you once were — able to wake the morning after some grievance as if nothing had happened. One more shock and you might drop dead on the spot. Third Senior Brother wanted to reason with you, but you only smiled faintly — matters of the heart, if you can understand them, understand them; if you can't, no amount of reasoning will get through. You had waited many years for this day; it was something long since decided. The only thing left you could do for her in this life was to exit quietly. At this moment, all you wanted was to sleep well, to sleep until you woke naturally, or perhaps never wake again.

The rain pattered softly, the sky had cooled somewhat, and the mountain air had turned chill and quiet. You, Third Senior Brother, and Fourth Senior Brother sat in the Scripture Hall drinking tea while you told them everything that had happened that day. Third Senior Brother did not blame you two for acting on your own; instead he was grateful — with you two junior brothers sharing his burdens, he could barely hold the Tang Clan together. Now that the Junior Martial Sister had married and the Tang family's bloodline was secured, one great weight was finally off his mind.

No matter how long the torment lasted, the sound gradually faded into silence. You pushed the door open and went outside; the rain was still falling. Amid the rain hung the smoke of spent firecrackers, and the ground lay strewn with cold, quiet debris. She was already gone, the old garden left with only her fading fragrance. However unwilling you were to let go, you had to. May she find a place where it is always spring, and may her smile bloom like flowers in full bloom.

The deafening sound of firecrackers and gongs echoed through the sky, yet you ignored it. You deliberately chose not to hear about her, unwilling to know who she had finally chosen. Even more, you dared not go to see her off, hiding your head under the quilt.

Thanks to your efforts, the Junior Martial Sister's wedding was able to proceed smoothly after all. That night the rain began, and it still had not let up by the time she was married off the next day. Old legend has it that rain on a wedding day is Heaven's blessing, yet the two of you felt only cold and cheerless, bleak and forlorn.

Jinwu Shangren shouted loudly and took the Kongtong disciples away without leaving a trace. At first glance, it seemed as if they had hit a snag, being driven away without gaining any advantage. In reality, after causing a commotion for an entire night, they had tested the depths of the Tang Clan. All the guests had heard of the Tang Clan's thunderous methods, both righteous and wicked, with clear distinctions between grace and blame. Thus, even though the Tang Clan had declined, no one dared to casually provoke them. Today, the people from Kongtong had caused a ruckus and surprisingly left unscathed, leading everyone to think that the Tang Clan truly was diminished, like a tiger with its teeth pulled. Relying solely on their past reputation, how long could they maintain their imposing presence? Unanimously, they all harbored a sense of contempt.

Jinwu Shangren grew more afraid the longer the fight dragged on. He had brought his people to make trouble today ostensibly to demand an explanation, not to take open revenge — so he had to mind his limits, or risk drawing criticism. If Sect Leader Wei of the Mystic Skill Gate seized the chance to denounce him, his bid for the sect leader's seat would only grow more complicated. So he dared not push things too far. Seeing you fearless of death, he felt an inexplicable stab of panic and held back, stopping short of a killing blow. Onlookers, seeing he clearly had the upper hand yet offered to call it a draw, praised him as a man of true magnanimity.

Jinwu Shangren grew more fearful the longer the fight went on. Though his surprise strike had landed, his earlier defeat at your hands had already left him badly hurt. You refused to yield, and as the bout dragged on, he could no longer hide his injuries — a sweetness rose in his throat, and he spat blood, the signs of defeat plain to see. His mind raced: you were willing to fight to the death here, but his own life was worth far more than that, his skills still had much use left in them — why strain himself to the bone over a nobody like you? In that instant he made his choice, and conceded defeat before the whole crowd. You were caught off guard; today was a wedding, and with all the guests looking on, you could neither strike nor stand down, unsure for a moment what to do.

Jinwu Shangren is inherently cruel, having killed many renowned heroes and heroines. Before taking their lives, he always humiliates and desecrates them, capturing their final moments of disgrace and treasuring them as trophies. You are not even worthy of being remembered, lacking the qualification to die in his hands. As an ordinary person, you should know your place, content like countless mediocre commoners, to be trampled upon by others. If others wish to kill you, you must die; if others threaten you, you must flee immediately, leaving behind a trail of shame. You should be ignorant, cowardly, and fragile as paper, merely a fleeting mention in someone's legendary story. Yet you are not. You were not born brave, but your accumulated will has driven you forward. Though there is a path to retreat, you still carry the hopes of the Tang Clan's brothers and sisters, unyielding and resolute.

But you would never admit defeat, and pressed forward into the fight. Jinwu Shangren, certain of victory, held nothing back — striking with several heavy blows from the outset that you had no hope of matching, and you were battered into a stumbling, utterly wretched state. All the while Jinwu Shangren kept mocking and goading you, using a top-tier voice-transmission technique that carried only to your ears; too far away, none of the onlookers caught his ruse, and outwardly he dropped his arrogant tone for a mask of solemn virtue, gently urging you to give up. The onlookers, not knowing the truth, genuinely believed you outmatched, and thought you simply too proud and humiliated to yield, stubbornly clinging to a hopeless fight.

You clashed again at once, but within a few exchanges you were suddenly seized by dizziness, your ears ringing. It was only when Jinwu Shangren smugly boasted of his method that you realized you had fallen for his trick. His earlier blow had spared your life, but it carried a hidden strike from a vicious art called the Soul-Destroying Pestle, of which the verse runs: one strike dims the fetal light, two strikes scatter the spirit, three strikes dissolve the hidden essence. Most vicious of all, this technique need not kill outright — its true qi burrows into the skull and runs wild, in mild cases leaving one drowsy and forgetful for good, in severe cases turning one into a mute, witless puppet who obeys every command.

You were struck by Jinwu Shangren's pair of Fiery Sun Hammers, and as the crowd gasped in alarm, you did not die as expected with your skull crushed, as if your opponent had shown mercy. Jinwu Shangren did not kill you, but it was not out of kindness. In his eyes, you were as low as a bug; killing you was effortless. He spared your life to use your humiliation and disgrace to destroy the prestige of the Tang Clan.
You were caught off guard and struck on the forehead with a heavy punch, causing stars to flash in your eyes at once.

Jinwu Shangren, feigning defeat before launching his surprise strike, showed not the faintest trace of shame — claiming instead that he'd done it out of kindness, to teach you a lesson, since if you'd been caught unguarded by that blow, your brains might have been dashed out. Specious as the excuse was, it almost held together; in the end, the fault lay with your own carelessness. When it came to right and wrong, Kongtong always had some argument to twist things its way.
You were utterly unaware, struck on the forehead by a heavy punch, and suddenly your eyes flared with stars.

You hadn't even thought about it, yet your thoroughly honed punches and kicks reacted naturally, spinning to dissipate the force, raising your arm to block, and executing the move in a single motion. Jinwu Shangren had expected this move to succeed, but it had missed, leaving him stunned into silence. Others watching were even more impressed, exclaiming well done!

At the critical moment, Rui Sheng, watching from the sidelines, saw how dire things had become. With no time to draw his sword, he summoned the whole of his True Qi into a single thunderous roar, unleashing the technique of Songshan's Lion's Roar. The blast left both your skull and Jinwu Shangren's ringing — startled as you were, neither one was hurt. Jinwu Shangren, rattled by the sudden roar, missed his chance to strike and could only clench his fists in regret.

Yet you remained oblivious. Rui Sheng, watching from the side, saw the danger and had no time to draw his sword. He summoned his True Qi and loosed a single thunderous roar — unleashing the technique of Songshan's Lion's Roar — that set both your skull and Jinwu Shangren's ringing. Startled as you were, neither of you was hurt, but Jinwu Shangren, rattled by the sudden roar, missed his chance to strike and could only clench his fists in regret.
At the critical moment, Ye Yunzhou stepped in promptly, using a swift sword to drive back the enemies.

Yet you remained wholly unaware. At the critical moment, Ye Yunzhou — whom you had thought long gone — suddenly struck like lightning, driving Jinwu Shangren back with a single sword stroke. In truth his mind was calculating: certain that Jinwu Shangren still had cards left to play and would never be finished off so easily, he had waved his sleeve and walked away only to let the enemy grow complacent and drop his guard. Once the enemy broke the rules of the Jianghu by attacking again, he would have his excuse to step in.
At the critical moment, your junior martial sister, single‑mindedly focused on you, stepped in promptly and used hidden weapons to drive back the enemies.

But you remained utterly unaware. At the critical moment, your junior martial sister, her attention fixed wholly on you, stepped in without delay and drove Jinwu Shangren back with a hidden weapon. You turned around in shock, only then realizing that the man had merely feigned defeat!

The Kongtong Sect had swaggered in to make trouble, only to end up covered in dust and disgrace — how could they possibly stay and save face? Those thick-skinned cupped their fists, murmured a few polite words to make their exit graceful; the thin-skinned ones simply walked out without a word.

Nor did you mince words, declaring that revenge would surely come one day — this score to be settled at their next sect leadership election, when you would go to Kongtong and repay them in kind, just to see how they liked it. Hearing this, the people of Kongtong were mortified beyond words, with no face left to stay. Those thick-skinned cupped their fists, murmured a few parting words to save face; those thin-skinned walked out without a word.

Bold and forthright as you were, you had no patience for false courtesies. Sparing them not a shred of face, you showed them the door without ceremony, sending them back the way they'd come. As for the instigator who had fanned the flames and spread the rumors, him you kept detained.

Though you had won, for Junior Martial Sister's sake you had no wish to stir up further trouble, and in words neither arrogant nor servile you sent the guests on their way. But Venerable Golden Crow, the very man who had stirred up the crowd and spread the lies, you could not let go — him, you had detained.
Junior Martial Sister's heart overflowed with joy; she murmured 'Senior Brother, Senior Brother' again and again, unable to contain her happiness.
The Tang Clan brothers and sisters rejoiced with great enthusiasm, sharing in the honor.
