Junior Martial Sister's heart overflowed with joy; she murmured 'Senior Brother, Senior Brother' again and again, unable to contain her happiness.
The Tang Clan brothers and sisters rejoiced with great enthusiasm, sharing in the honor.

The Kongtong disciples watched their own sect's expert issue the challenge himself, only to suffer a crushing defeat — every face went pale with shame, heads hung low, each of them wishing they could bury their face in the earth.

You captured the enemy leader, raised your voice, and called out. The Kongtong disciples saw their own sect's expert fall in battle, all of them pale‑faced, unable to resist, lowering their heads and quickly sheathing their weapons.

Nobody believed in you; they even said that once the Flying Hero died, the Tang Clan had no one left who could be called a master. Yet before everyone's eyes, you singlehandedly defeated the formidable Venerable Golden Crow, stunning all present.

Venerable Golden Crow lowered his hands, put on a solemn face, and declared the outcome decided, ordering you to put up your weapon. But no sooner had he spoken than, seeing your fighting spirit spent and your guard down, he suddenly swung his iron hammer and smashed it down at your skull.
For all your burning fury, you were still no match for him, and you fell in defeat.
Your Internal Skill had been crippled; however exquisite your moves, their power was limited, and in the end you were defeated, swallowing your bitterness.
Your Internal Force had been dissolved by Shentu Long, and Venerable Golden Crow judged you no better than a cripple — he did not think you worth a second glance, and grew careless in his contempt.

Venerable Golden Crow raised his voice in a fierce shout, declaring that he, Venerable Golden Crow, would represent Kongtong and challenge a Tang Clan master. Until the outcome was settled, neither side was to make any reckless move. It would be one against one, fair and open, with absolutely no interference from either side permitted — whoever broke this would be named the common enemy of both sects. These words were meant for both sects to hear, but even more for the guests present, to show off his fairness and honor.

You gripped the Thunderfire Bomb in your fist and struck Venerable Golden Crow's front teeth loose, and the bomb burst inside his mouth. He bled from all seven orifices and died on the spot — so much for the 'Nine-Lives Leopard'; there would be no coming back from this one. You too lay there in a pool of blood, your arm severed, your life ebbing away. In your final moments, it was your master who came to see you off; you could not make out her face, and as your breath grew faint, you sank into deep sleep to the sound of her gentle murmuring. Sparks from the Thunderfire Bomb caught the drapes, and in an instant flames swept through the Flying Heaven Hall, burning the clouds at the horizon a fiery red. All grudges turned to ash, swept up into the sky, and carried off on the wind.

On the day the Snow Mountain Sect fell, she vowed to make Kongtong pay in blood for blood. Yet even with her divine skill perfected, she still remembered the kindness of the Former Sect Leader who once sheltered her, and could not bring herself to strike without mercy. Today, seeing Kongtong so far decayed, she resolved to settle both old grudges and new at once. The Soul-Stealing Orchid struck without mercy now, cutting down anyone who barred the way. Together with the two of you, she stormed up Kongtong Mountain, unstoppable, straight for the Flying Heaven Hall — Xie Wuchen alone held off the Kongtong disciples, Xiahou Lan made straight for the Fire Dragon Immortal Monarch, and left the Tang Clan's blood debt for you to settle. You raised your Small Sword to meet Venerable Golden Crow's pair of hammers.

You stood motionless in the desolate and cold Tang Family Compound, as if hearing laughter that pulled you back into the past. Xiahou Lan called out to stop you. She had changed her mind, choosing not to go to the Snow Mountain Ruins, but instead to travel with you and Xie Wuchen to Kongtong, to fulfill the vow she had longed for nearly twenty years, yet could not bring herself to fulfill.

Eldest Senior Brother's enemy stood right before you. You gripped the small sword tight in your hand — this battle was fought not only for Junior Martial Sister, but for Eldest Senior Brother, and for the Tang Clan.

Having circled back around to the outer fortress, the Venerable Golden Crow had worn down a good deal of your strength. Knowing his cunning scheme had paid off, he was insufferably pleased with himself.

Having circled back around to the Outer Fort, the Venerable Golden Crow found his smile freezing on his face. He had counted on the Tang Clan having no one capable left, and had come to stir up trouble on that assumption — never guessing he had underestimated you, unremarkable as you seemed. No one could say quite what you had done to draw so many capable people to your side, enough that even his own Kongtong disciples turned against him and stood aside.

You did not feel you owed her anything: since Kongtong had struck at the Tang Clan first, no small kindness was going to buy your forgiveness. She sighed. Today's offense to the Tang Clan had not been her intent, and she felt truly ashamed of it; that you refused to forgive her was only natural.

You felt indebted to her, yet she would not accept your gratitude. Offending the Tang Clan today had not been her wish, and she felt truly ashamed of it. She hoped only that one day, should you cross paths in the Jianghu with a Mystic Skill disciple wearing robes like hers, you would remember this day and spare them, rather than show no mercy.
You were defeated by Ju Dongyin, yet she did not go for the kill. Her orders were only to block the enemy. Since she successfully held you back, her mission was considered accomplished.
As for your theft of the Kongtong secret treasure, she could only swallow her anger for now, resolving to find a better chance for revenge later; sooner or later, you would pay the price.

Before you could say more than a few words, Junior Martial Sister had already caught up to your side. During the fierce clash between the two factions moments earlier, Ju Dongyin had kept a careful eye on Junior Martial Sister, dreading that her own people might strike without restraint and injure this precious girl, for if that happened, the feud would run so deep that one side might have to be wiped out before it ended. She had thought little of it until she actually looked, and then broke out in a cold sweat: for an instant she thought her eyes were playing tricks, seeing three of her at once, as a red shadow flickered, now in front, now behind, impossible to guard against. Even the direct disciples of her own sect's Flying Heaven Gate, famed for their lightness skill, were swift enough, but none moved with such elusive, unpredictable footwork, let alone in the thick of chaotic battle. The moment she saw Junior Martial Sister coming, Ju Dongyin surrendered without a second thought. She told herself that if she could not even be sure of beating one Junior Martial Sister, how could she hope against the two of you together? Since there was no stopping either of you, better to offer little resistance and spare herself a beating.

Seeing her truly helpless, unable to act by her own will, you had no wish to make things hard for her, and besides, even in an actual fight you had no confidence of winning within so short a time; one careless slip might even cost you the match. So you sat down and called for a pot of tea. Ju Dongyin glanced sidelong at you, unable to help admiring your self-restraint, and felt genuinely grateful. The moment came, and she respectfully let you pass.

Though she had no wish to cross blades with you, bound by the mountain's rules she dared not defy Venerable Golden Crow's order, and had to hold you back for at least a quarter hour before she could report back.
Bearing Sect Leader Wei's hopes upon your shoulders, you girded yourself once more and returned to the fray.

After a while of talk, the tea you had drunk earlier had already taken effect. It was no ordinary tea, but the Rhinohorn Lotus Seed Decoction of the Kongtong Mystic Skill Gate, brewed to nourish the qi and clear the mind, and with its benefit, the fatigue built up from your recent battles vanished all at once.

Ju Dongyin then relayed Sect Leader Wei's decree to you, putting it plainly: she was summoning you to Kongtong to represent the Mystic Skill Gate in battle, and contend for the title of Kongtong Sect Leader. You were dumbfounded. How could such a weighty matter fall to a mere visiting disciple like you? However many doubts churned in you, Ju Dongyin would entertain none of them. If you wished to protest, you would have to go to Kongtong yourself and take it up with Sect Leader Wei in person.

Little did you know, this tea had all been carefully arranged by Sect Leader Wei as a means to counsel you. It meant only to tell you: haste cannot drink hot tea. The more anxious you are, the calmer your head must stay. Lose your ordinary composure, and even a cup of tea can harm you. That Venerable Golden Crow was deep and calculating, deliberately leading you in circles, setting others to block your path and wear down your strength, so that once your battle-strength was spent, you would be left as meat on his chopping block. Then it would not be you who seized him and ordered the Kongtong disciples to stand down, but he who had seized you, forcing the Tang Clan to surrender. This was why Ju Dongyin had made you sit: she was certain Venerable Golden Crow could not get away, or rather, that he dared not try. Having acted on his own authority, stirred up sentiment, petitioned the Four Sect Leaders, come to stir up trouble at the Tang Clan, and then fled the scene, how could he ever win the sect's trust again? Having earned everyone's wrath, did he still mean to remain Kongtong Sect Leader? Hearing this, you understood at once, and your admiration for this senior sister's uncanny foresight deepened, never knowing that all her words and deeds were at Sect Leader Wei's direction. That seemingly frail girl's ability to lead the Mystic Skill Gate and stand against the other three gates was no accident at all.

You were as meticulous as dust, glancing at the tea in Ju Dongyin's cup, which was steaming away on its own, while your own cup of tea seemed cool. You pondered: she could have arrived at most just a step ahead; could the waiter have brought her cold tea? Upon closer inspection, the style of this cup was different from those used in the shop, clearly not a set. She saw you not drinking, not angry but smiling, slightly changing her opinion. She took back the tea, poured it into an empty cup, and the steam only dispersed once the tea was stirred. Originally, this cup was hers, with an insulating effect. The tea was sealed with oil to trap the heat, making it appear as if it were cold at first glance. Those in a hurry would naturally miss the clue. She said that, endured the heat, and drank it all at once as a self‑punishment.
Already restless and impatient, and now finding yourself so toyed with, you flew into a fury beyond control, slammed the table, rose to your feet, and made to storm off with a flick of your sleeve.

You were scalded and cut a pitiful figure, yet you did not complain, blaming only your own impatience. Hearing this, Ju Dongyin's opinion of you rose a little; such patience, she thought, was more than an ordinary man could muster, and her Sect Leader Junior Sister truly did have an eye for people.

You're restless, how could you have the patience to savor tea? You picked up the cup and drank it, only to find the tea seemed to have no heat, yet it nearly scalded your mouth, burning your insides as if they were on fire. Originally, this cup was hers, with insulating properties. The tea surface was sealed with oil to trap the heat, making it appear as cool tea at first glance. Impatient people naturally fail to notice the trick.

The fellow disciples from the same sect were still engaged in fierce combat. They could not call off the battle until they captured the enemy leader. Although you were anxious to the point of distress, you dared not disobey Sect Leader Wei's command and sat down as instructed. Ju Dongyin then pushed a cup of tea in front of you, ordering you to drink it.

Your fellow disciples were still locked in fierce combat; only by seizing the enemy leader could the order go out for both sides to stand down. Where would you find the leisure to sit and hear her out? Whatever she had to say could wait until Venerable Golden Crow was dealt with. Ju Dongyin sighed inwardly, truly wondering how her exceptionally clever Sect Leader Junior Sister could place such high hopes on this fool.

She saw your face filled with anger but remained as composed as ever. When you called her Senior Sister, she also called you Junior Brother. She said she had brought a message from Sect Leader Wei for you; if you wished to listen, just sit down. However, if you were in a rush to chase Jinwu Shangren, she would not stop you.

Yet she harbors a resolute intent to kill you alone. Her actions are driven by nothing else but the truth that an innocent man is guilty only by possessing a precious treasure. Since you carry the Iron Pipa Skill of Kongtong, your fate is sealed. What you deem unimportant, she considers of utmost significance. What you regard as life‑or‑death, she sees as irrelevant. You showed disrespect for the Kongtong sect's traditions, and on that day, you ignored Sect Leader Wei's goodwill. Don't expect others to accommodate you. This resentment will never be resolved, and you should have foreseen the consequences long ago.

The one guarding the final barrier was the Mystic Skill Guardian, 'Warm Wind' Ju Dongyin. This Ju Dongyin was a senior expert, second in status within the Mystic Skill Cave only to Sect Leader Wei. She despised what Jinwu Shangren had done, but had come only because she was ordered to, and she said not a word throughout. Amid the chaos of battle she outwardly obeyed while secretly working against it, merely putting on a show — not one Tang Clan disciple struck by her whisk was actually hurt, only left with Sealed Acupoints.

Junior Martial Sister leaped out to take this tough battle for you, and Yu Lin was delighted, half wishing he could just let you through. He toyed with the pretty young lady, deliberately keeping the bout undecided — how charming, he thought. He never realized how badly he'd underestimated Junior Martial Sister's skill, until she unleashed her Unpredictable Flying Shuttle, and Wave Illusion Silverfish never got another chance to catch his breath.

Ye Yunzhou leaped out to take this tough battle for you. The instant Yu Lin saw him, the hair on his body stood on end, as though facing a mortal enemy — instinct telling him this was an opponent he could not defeat.
You didn't know he harbored ulterior motives, wanting to borrow your blade to eliminate Jinwu Shangren — one less rival in his race for the position of Sect Leader.

You didn't know that he harbored ulterior motives — his letting you through wasn't out of kindness, only fear of the one behind you. Xiahou Lan's martial arts were extraordinary; even the Soul-Stealing Sect Leader turned meek and deferential before her. As her disciple, you were surely not one to trifle with either — better to grant you this favor, and eliminate Jinwu Shangren in the bargain, one less rival for the position of Sect Leader.

When you studied at the Soul-Stealing Gate of Kongtong, you only heard of him, but because he was in seclusion for training, you had no opportunity to meet him. Unexpectedly, when he saw you, he immediately let you pass.
At the third checkpoint, the one who blocked the way was the Soul-Stealing Guardian, 'Wave Illusion Silverfish' Yu Lin.

Junior Martial Sister leaped out to take this tough battle for you. Seeing her in her red dress, Yan Jiang was struck by the image of the woman he loved, his heart brimming with tenderness — he couldn't bring himself to strike to kill. He had no idea how badly he'd overestimated his own skill; in moments, quite literally, he'd be flying to heaven.
Ye Yunzhou jumped out to take the tough battle for you, and Yan Jiang's heart suddenly raced with a premonition of impending death.

Rui Sheng stepped forward to take this tough battle for you. Yan Jiang, though ill-tempered and no paragon of virtue, valued loyalty highly — seeing that Rui Sheng meant to make trouble for him, his bluster vanished at once.

At the sight of the weapon in your hand, he widened his eyes. He remembered it slung at the slender waist of that person — red skirt, faint shadow, her smile sweet and radiant, at once near at hand and impossibly far. It was the cherished keepsake of the one he thought of day and night, never far from her side; how could he not know it? He had never dared entertain such hopes, never dared to covet the position of Sect Leader, nor even once found the courage to speak his heart — and to smother his own feelings, he had married early. Seeing that she had entrusted even her beloved Jade Sky Divine Dagger to your hands, he felt a sudden pang, and stepped aside unconditionally, his heart a tangle of conflicting feelings.

When you studied at Kongtong, he thought little of you — mocking you or glaring you into silence whenever your paths crossed. Now, seeing how bold you'd become, his view of you had changed. When you cursed Jinwu Shangren as vermin, he couldn't help but agree, and stepped aside to let you pass. In his mind, only one man from the Flying Heaven Gate was fit to contend for the position of Kongtong Sect Leader — General of Dao Techniques Danxiazi, never Jinwu Shangren.
Next to block the way was the Flying Heaven Guardian, 'Mountain Fire' Yan Jiang.

Junior Martial Sister leaped out to take this tough battle for you. Seeing her so delicate and soft, Iron Spine Mountain Lord Tong Dachong meant to go easy on her — not realizing how badly he'd misjudged the gulf between their skills, until the consequences caught up with him fast.
Ye Yunzhou leaped out to take this tough battle for you, and a bead of cold sweat rolled down Iron Spine Mountain Lord Tong Dachong's forehead.
Rui Sheng stepped out to take this hard fight off your hands. The moment Iron Spine Mountain Lord Tong Dachong saw that fighting him would mean becoming enemies, all his will to fight vanished.

During your time studying at Kongtong, the two of you were never close, but you were familiar faces who crossed paths often. Iron Spine Mountain Lord blocked your way for the briefest moment — enough that it wouldn't count as defying orders — before letting you through.
The first to block the way was the Iron Fist Gate's Guardian, 'Iron Spine Mountain Lord' Tong Dachong.

A fierce battle raged back and forth. Though Kongtong was strong, the Tang Clan was no easy foe. The Kongtong disciples' faces turned pale, their earlier air of arrogance gone, replaced by fear. Deep within, they silently cursed Jinwu Shangren for provoking the Tang Clan of all sects — was the Tang Clan so easily bullied? Your Fourth Senior Brother cleared the way for you; to catch the bandits, catch the chief first, so you leaped straight at the ringleader. Jinwu Shangren, terrified, fled in blind panic, constantly dragging his own men in to block blades and stall your pursuit.

Song Bei received orders from the Imperial Court to lead ten palace elite in capturing you. You fought desperately, sustaining injuries, and used hidden weapons and poison to kill two, then laughed maniacally before drinking the poison and dying.
You became a nameless, factionless lone thief, robbing houses far and wide, and were wanted by the Imperial Court.

You became a wandering hero without affiliation to any sect, traveling the land to right wrongs, and your reputation gradually grew. When a full‑scale war broke out between the Wulin of the Central Plains and the Mud Cult, you took up your sword to defend the Commoners, never to return, with no place left to go. During a ritual held by the Nangong family, your name was read, and after that, no one in the world knew your surname or given name again.
You approached the Sect Leader's sickbed and bowed, thudding sounds echoing. Shouldering your pack, you descended the mountain and departed.

After this battle, the Tang Clan's reputation was utterly ruined. The Jianghu all say that a strong dragon doesn't fight ground snakes. It's pitiful that the Tang Clan isn't even a snake, at most a ground bug, and yet they lost badly by outnumbering the enemy, a truly tragic and laughable outcome. No one in the Jianghu now holds the Tang Clan in any esteem; the disciples, many with hearts as dead as ashes, began to bid farewell to Third Senior Brother and leave the mountains. You stood motionless in the empty Tang Family courtyard for a while, then looked down at your tattered blue robe, soaked with your sweat, blood, and tears, now far too heavy to bear. The evening light was unusually lonely.

The Tang Clan's morale shattered after this battle, leaving them with no face to stand in Jianghu anymore. The disciples scattered, each leaving the mountain. Second Senior Brother, Third Senior Brother, and you were left to guard the courtyard, parting ways in opposite directions. Rui Sheng managed to retrieve his junior martial sister, but she had been struck by the exclusive weapon of Jinwu Shangren, her True Qi surging to her brain, leaving her dazed and confused, as if transformed into a different person. She often spoke to herself. Suitors, seeing her condition, abandoned their intentions, none willing to take her home as a wife, for she was mentally unstable and her purity uncertain. Only Rui Sheng showed her no disdain, yet his junior martial sister was so foolish and simple‑minded that she would weep the moment she left his side. In the end, he could only give up helplessly. You took her with you, seeking remedies everywhere, but found nothing. One day, while traveling, you encountered Second Senior Brother, who poisoned you and took the junior martial sister away. You died on the road, but not at Second Senior Brother's hand. Long ago, you had already died alongside the Tang Clan's honor, long past due to be buried. The mere shell that remains is nothing more than a body without a soul.

After this battle, the Tang Clan's spirit was broken, and it had no face left to show in the Jianghu. Disciples left the mountain one after another; Third Senior Brother, Fourth Senior Brother, and you sealed the great courtyard and went your separate ways. Ye Yunzhou managed to bring Junior Martial Sister back, but she had been struck by the Venerable Golden Crow's signature weapon, her true qi surging up into her skull, leaving her dazed day and night, as though she had become another person, often muttering to herself. Seeing her condition, her suitors all gave up the thought; none wished to marry home such a simple-minded wife of uncertain purity. You took Junior Martial Sister with you and sought treatment everywhere, but found nothing. One day on the road you chanced upon Second Senior Brother, who moved to poison you, then carried Junior Martial Sister off with long strides. You breathed your last on that road, yet it was not by Second Senior Brother's hand. Long before that, you had already died together with the Tang Clan's honor, long overdue for the grave; what lingers on today is merely a body without a soul.

After this battle, the Tang Clan's spirit was shattered, and they had no face left to stand in the Jianghu. The disciples bid farewell and descended the mountain, while the Third Senior Brother and Fourth Senior Brother sealed the courtyard, each going their separate ways. Although Ye Yunzhou managed to rescue the Junior Martial Sister, she had been struck by Jinwu Shangren's unique weapon, causing her True Qi to surge to her head. She spent her days in a daze, as if she had become a different person, often talking to herself. Suitors, seeing her condition, abandoned all hope; no one wanted to take home a foolish woman whose purity was uncertain. Only Rui Sheng did not despise her; however, the Junior Martial Sister would cry whenever he left her side, and in the end, he could only give up in despair. You took the Junior Martial Sister and sought medical help everywhere, but to no avail. One day, while on the road, you unexpectedly encountered the Second Senior Brother, who poisoned you and took the Junior Martial Sister away. As you gasped for breath on the road, it was not by the Second Senior Brother's hand that you would die. Long ago, you had already died along with the dignity of the Tang Clan; what lingered on was merely a soulless shell.

Junior Martial Sister paled with fright at the sight of your wound — an opening the Venerable Golden Crow was quick to seize. He seized you as a hostage, sealed Junior Martial Sister's acupoints, and carried her off.

The Tang Clan collapsed into disarray, their Outer Fort overrun by the Kongtong Sect, forcing them to kneel and beg for mercy, their humiliation laid bare. You, too, were overpowered by four opponents, severely injured in the assault and fainted from the blow.
With a single command, the Tang Clan disciples launched a coordinated attack, and the Kongtong disciples were equally determined, immediately clashing into a chaotic battle.

You surveyed the gathered brothers and sisters in your sect, noticing various expressions. Some looked hesitant, while others bore injuries yet remained unyielding. Still, some yearned to engage in a fierce battle. Not one of them spoke; they merely stared at you, awaiting your commands. They trusted you as you once trusted others in the crowd. For now, only you can lead the way for the sect!

Junior Martial Sister was itching to volunteer herself, but Fourth Senior Brother held her back — this could absolutely not be allowed. Right now, talented suitors from every quarter were waiting eagerly to hear the happy news of whom she would choose to marry, yet she had suddenly rushed down the mountain and personally beaten this foul-mouthed, wicked monk. It was easy to imagine how the loose-tongued troublemakers of the Jianghu would twist the story beyond recognition and spread it in the ugliest light, seeming to confirm the very rumors the Venerable Golden Crow had spread.
Fourth Senior Brother has been injured and is unable to take the field.

When the Venerable Golden Crow arrived, he had already judged the Tang Clan's ranks thin of talent, and that only an attack in numbers could overcome you. Yet with today's wedding feast underway, the mountain could not be left unguarded, so he could never bring his whole force to bear; even with fewer men, his side's superior skill would let him hold his ground for now. If the Tang Clan fell upon him with numbers, that alone would hand people grounds to condemn you and ruin your own name. Should the Kongtong Sect retreat, he could still claim the strong dragon does not crush the local snake, and go home to gather reinforcements for another try. But if instead you followed his proposal and put forward a single champion to duel him, that suited him even better: cripple the one master the Tang Clan had left, and it was as good as snuffing out the Clan's guttering flame. The disciples would feel their future gone dark, and once they scattered like startled birds, the Tang Clan would be left an empty shell.

During his studies abroad, Rui Sheng visited various sects and had even gone to Diancang to meet the famed Cangsong Swordsman. At that time, Ye Yunzhou was already abroad, so they never met. Now, these two young experts were seeing each other's true skills for the first time. One side remained steady, like hidden thunderlight behind clouds, silent until it struck with a startling impact. The other side moved naturally, like wind and mist, with its weaknesses and attack signs constantly shifting. Without hesitation, both placed their hands on their weapons, their minds already clashing before any moves were made. You hurriedly stepped between them, fearing these two might clash in battle and start a fight.
Ye Yunzhou arrived just in time. Had his sister not summoned him up and down the mountain at her whim, the Venerable Golden Crow would never have dared be so brazen.

Junior Martial Sister had come down with you, and fearing something might go wrong, you told her to hide first. She obeyed, staying hidden for a while before finally stepping out. The moment she appeared, the rumors vanished like smoke. The crowd saw this young woman's gaze, clear and cool, her beauty untouched by the dust of the world, pure as ice and jade. Who would still believe what the Venerable Golden Crow had said? Opinion turned sharply against him. The Venerable Golden Crow tried to force out a few more vile words, but when his eyes met Junior Martial Sister's clear gaze, he found himself speechless, unable to utter a word.

These four were all renowned masters of the Jianghu; their very bearing and presence set them worlds apart from the other Kongtong disciples. You and Fourth Senior Brother both felt a secret chill on seeing them-one alone would already be hard to handle, let alone four, and Venerable Golden Crow besides. Your own side, by contrast, though numerous, had few fighters who could truly match them; the outcome of a fight was impossible to predict, and win or lose, others would only mock the Tang Clan for bullying the few with many-losing face and substance both.

Your temperament was fierce and unyielding; how could you be scared off just by the sound of a name? It was Fourth Senior Brother instead who kept his head, quickly talking you down and urging a more careful plan.

You had once studied at Kongtong, and knew well that these Four Guardians were no ordinary men-each was among the finest of the Four Gates, and it was not impossible that some among them were even stronger than Venerable Golden Crow. You could not help feeling a secret chill of apprehension.

The reason Venerable Golden Crow had held back from striking, and instead loudly proclaimed his challenge to the Tang Clan's finest, was simply that he did not want the reputation of bullying the few with many. Your coming down the mountain with your people played right into his hands-he merely stepped back into his own ranks and summoned the Four Guardians.

Slinging mud back was something anyone could do-since he showed no mercy, why should you show him any? A torrent of curses tumbled out of you at once. Venerable Golden Crow was both cunning and sharp-tongued; if you tried to reason with him face to face, you would only end up in the same spot as Fourth Senior Brother. But you refused to do that. Once your tongue turned vicious, you spared no one, kin or stranger alike-ordinarily you could curse a man to death without a single foul word, but Venerable Golden Crow was so loathsome that you let loose with everything you had, as crude as could be, every sentence laced with obscenities, merciless to the extreme. Even Venerable Golden Crow, who had kept up his hollow smile all along, was cursed until his true face showed through, and had no one held him back, he would have flown at you at once to fight to the death. Your tirade made no concession to reason and was vulgar in the extreme, yet it left Venerable Golden Crow's own filthy words looking feeble by comparison, as if they were no longer so credible after all.
You arrived just at that moment, and upon hearing these words, were overcome with fury, and drove Venerable Golden Crow back with a single punch.

With those earlier words as prelude, Venerable Golden Crow turned his attack, aiming it squarely at Junior Martial Sister. Clad in a bright red monk's robe, one would expect him to be a man of piety and good works, yet the words from his mouth were utterly venomous. He slandered Eldest Senior Brother and Junior Martial Sister as having lain together before marriage-if Junior Martial Sister were not already with child, why else would the Tang Clan be so eager to marry off their daughter and summon heroes from across the realm to gather in Shu? It was, he claimed, nothing but a scheme to find some fool willing to serve as a cheap father for the child in her womb. Such words were of course malicious fabrication, unable to withstand scrutiny, lies that would collapse on their own in time-Fourth Senior Brother had no need even to refute them. But Venerable Golden Crow's aim was never to win the argument, only to spread rumor. He knew well the Jianghu's taste for gossip and spectacle, and said whatever was most scandalous, so that once word got out, the Tang Clan's reputation would be ruined beyond repair. Whether his lies were exposed first, or the Tang Clan became the target everyone cried out against, by the time the truth came to light it would be too late to undo the damage-and once he had ascended to become Kongtong's Sect Leader, a single turn of his hand would be enough to silence the entire Tang Clan for good.

Eldest Senior Brother, wandering the Jianghu, had always been free-spirited and unrestrained, drawing both praise and blame. Whether friend or foe, people felt for him a mixture of longing and resentment. He himself felt he had nothing to hide, yet without meaning to he had won the secret hearts of countless young women, and those who envied him, and those who spread rumors to blacken his name, were beyond counting. Now Venerable Golden Crow used this as material, half true and half false yet made to sound utterly convincing. Every Kongtong disciple believed it without question and burned with righteous indignation, and even the guests and villagers present could not help but half believe it themselves.

Meanwhile, Venerable Golden Crow led his people to cause trouble outside the Outer Fort, using as pretext Eldest Senior Brother's old infatuation with Xiahou Lan's renown-having broken into the Kongtong Sect three times to catch a glimpse of her beauty-and twisting his past conduct to slander him for harming her with sorcery and aphrodisiacs. To ruin the Tang Clan's reputation utterly, he even dragged in his own people, claiming the two had carried on an illicit affair that corrupted public morals; and Xiahou Lan, he claimed, had been so steeped in such influence that she had turned sinister and ruthless. Now Xiahou Lan had been missing for months, and he claimed she too had fallen prey to some lecherous scoundrel of your Tang Clan, just like the Flying Stone Gang Leader's wife. Xiahou Lan was no ordinary female disciple-she was a direct-line disciple of the Soul-Stealing Gate of Kongtong. The Kongtong Four Maidens are all direct disciples of the Four Gates, destined sooner or later to marry the Sect Leader, serving as crucial pawns to secure their own families' standing. To defile the Kongtong Sect Leader's betrothed is to insult the entire Kongtong Sect-an outrage no one could tolerate, and how could the disciples of Kongtong not be filled with righteous indignation? Eldest Senior Brother, wandering the Jianghu, had always been free-spirited and unrestrained, drawing both praise and blame; friend and foe alike felt for him a mix of longing and resentment. He himself felt he had nothing to hide, yet without meaning to he had won the secret hearts of countless young women, and those who envied him, and those who spread rumors to blacken his name, were beyond counting. Now, with Venerable Golden Crow speaking so convincingly and so fiercely, everyone could not help but believe him.

On the other side, Jinwu Shangren led people to cause trouble outside the fortress, using the excuse that Xiao Zhu Zeng had temporarily stayed at the Tang Clan for study, and fabricated the master's virtuous reputation to slander him as plotting treason, persecuting the direct descendant female disciples of Kongtong. The Kongtong Four Maidens are all direct descendants of the four sects, destined to marry the sect leader, serving as crucial political pawns to solidify their family's status. Disgracing the sect leader's unmarried wife is tantamount to insulting the Kongtong Sect; what can be tolerated, what cannot? How could the disciples of Kongtong not be filled with righteous indignation?

Meanwhile, Venerable Golden Crow led his people to cause trouble outside the Outer Fort, using the pretext that Xiaomei had once stayed at the Tang Clan, and twisting Eldest Senior Brother's past conduct to slander him as harboring dishonorable designs, persecuting Kongtong's own direct-line female disciples. The Kongtong Four Maidens are all direct disciples of the Four Gates, destined sooner or later to marry the Sect Leader, serving as crucial pawns to secure their own families' standing. To defile the Kongtong Sect Leader's betrothed is to insult the entire Kongtong Sect-an outrage no one could tolerate, and how could the disciples of Kongtong not be filled with righteous indignation?

Over there, Jinwu Shangren led people to cause trouble in the Outer Fort, using the fact that Xiaomei and Xiao Zhu had temporarily stayed at the Tang Clan as an excuse, and pretended to be Eldest Senior Brother's virtuous conduct, slandering him for plotting treason, and persecuting Kongtong's Direct Disciples.

Junior Martial Sister's heart, so hard-won open, closed tightly shut once more. The soft ringing of her bells gradually settled into stillness, and she went home alone, obedient, never again to act coquettish with anyone.
You did not hesitate to put on a stern face and be harsh with her-this was the first time, and probably the last in this life.
Although you smiled and spoke sweet words, your mind was already made up.
Even so, you remained iron-hearted; since making up your mind, you had never wavered.

You knew it was wrong, yet you still tugged Junior Martial Sister's hand and led her down the mountain to confront the enemy. Junior Martial Sister was both startled and overjoyed, finally wiping away her tears and smiling. Acting so recklessly, you were practically a traitor to the Tang Clan. But in Junior Martial Sister's eyes, you were the most trustworthy person in the world. She would willingly place her hand in yours, ready to face any danger alongside you.

At this moment, Rui Sheng gracefully landed ahead, startling Junior Martial Sister, who immediately crouched behind you for protection. He had seen Junior Martial Sister leave her seat and fail to return for a long while, and had exchanged awkward glances with the two competitors and Third Senior Brother, their talk circling endlessly through empty pleasantries, until he could not help but feel stifled. Excusing himself under pretense of relieving himself, he slipped out to stroll, and from afar spotted flickering lights along the deep forest path-likely someone descending the mountain with a lantern. Curious, he drifted down to look. His Internal Skill was so deep that before he had even drawn near, he overheard your conversation, and felt astonishment, shame, envy, and relief all at once, with a faint urge to laugh-a hundred feelings tangled together. He made a point of showing himself, volunteering to drive off the enemy for the Tang Clan, and without waiting for you to talk him out of it, he used his Qinggong to leap down the mountain. You and Junior Martial Sister had no choice but to follow.

Junior Martial Sister blocked your path, demanding to know where you were going, and no amount of persuading could change her mind. Her stubbornness was unprecedented. She was inept at expressing herself, her words falling short, her eyes brimming with tears. She had been on the mountain all along, and had even forgotten the way home. Every time she watched someone leave, she feared they might never return-first her mother, then her father, then Second Senior Brother, and finally even Eldest Senior Brother vanished without a trace, never to be seen again. Now, would you also leave without a word? It was her joyous day; shouldn't you stay by her side? If not that, then at least you should take her with you. As she cried out her feelings, tears cascaded down her cheeks, the bell chimed softly, and the Heaven and Earth Silent Power broke at the sound.

Junior Martial Sister stared at the three potential husbands, unable to bring herself to eat. At the banquet, she seemed lost in thought, and everyone assumed she was shy, paying her no mind. None realized she was as anxious as if sitting on pins and needles. She made an excuse to go alone and think, heading to the window to breathe in the fresh air. Leaning against the railing, she watched the guests below laughing and chatting, the scene reminiscent of the past. She was lost in melancholy when she caught sight of you carrying a lantern, striding out of the mountain gate. A sudden wave of panic and heart palpitations surged through her, and without hesitation, she leaped after you, and in a few bounds had already overtaken you. You were startled, abruptly stopping in your tracks. The Junior Brothers who had followed behind were caught off guard, colliding into a heap and pinning you underneath, a Throwing Dart still lodged in your body. Junior Martial Sister helped you up. Seeing that she had something important to discuss with you, the others gradually dispersed.

Anxious as you were, you knew there was no avoiding it—Third Senior Brother had to hold the compound, and could not be expected to come down the mountain to face the enemy, lest it alarm the wedding guests and tarnish the Junior Martial Sister's good name. With that thought, you could only steel your courage and step forward for the sect.
You were taken aback first, completely at a loss as to why the Tang Clan had ever offended the Kongtong Sect.
You first froze, then erupted in fury. Even if the two factions were at odds, there was no justification for deliberately choosing someone's wedding day to stir up trouble.

Hearing this, you flew into an uncontrollable rage: you hadn't yet settled the score for Eldest Senior Brother's death, and now here he was, daring to bully his way right up to your door—arrogance beyond enduring.

Just as they were about to go in for dinner, a Junior Brother suddenly came dashing up the mountain with a lantern, breathless with news: Kongtong's Venerable Golden Crow had brought men to make trouble, raising an uproar outside the Outer Fort and declaring he'd challenge the Tang Clan's foremost master. Anyone could tell the man meant no good—coming neither too early nor too late, but at this exact moment, clearly aware the Tang Clan was celebrating a wedding and deliberately picking a fight. Fourth Senior Brother, who was entertaining guests at the Outer Fort, led men at once to block him, but the enemy had plainly come prepared and could not be held back; all they could do was hold the line and send someone up the mountain for reinforcements.

Fourth Senior Brother drew funds from Third Senior Brother, then dipped into his own pocket to hire the Four Departments and Six Bureaus as well, borrowing the Outer Fort's stoves to cook up fine dishes, which were set in warming plates and carried up the mountain for the feast. It could not match the Nangong family's lavish spending, but everyone did their part all the same.

You were ordered by Second Senior Brother to recall the old Senior Brother, who had spent years drifting through the kitchen bureau and become a master of the craft. He had long wanted to do his part for the sect, and this time he pulled out all the stops, calling on his old connections to bring the Four Departments and Six Bureaus together in force at the Outer Fort—a grand display that let not only the Outer Fort's own residents but the local villagers as well share in the glow. Fourth Senior Brother even sent men to the yamen with dishes to smooth things over; when the County Magistrate stepped from his residence and saw the whole street ringing with laughter and cheer, he marveled in secret, wondering what high official from the court had arrived to command such a spectacle.

The outcome had already been settled. Though it was said one must weigh not just martial skill but conduct, virtue, talent, and lineage as well, everyone knew the gap in strength was too wide to leave room for hope. Still, it was fortune enough to have witnessed such a grand occasion—not only to drink the wedding wine and share in the joy, but to meet heroes from across the realm and broaden one's horizons. Of today's contests, the final bout was by far the most breathtaking, drawing thunderous applause; that fight alone was worth the thousand-mile journey to gather in Shu.
Shameless rascal that you are, you didn't scold them for it—you joined right in.

You weighed it back and forth, and in the end you still wanted to see with your own eyes the bearing of today's suitors, so you leapt up onto the roof to watch the bouts—only to find your fellow Junior Brothers already gambling up there.

You sat alone at the edge of the bed, at a loss. Today the person you loved most was to be married to another—by rights a joyous day, yet no matter how you tried, you could not smile. The revelry outside felt separated from you by a great chasm: out there the sun blazed bright, while you belonged in the shadows, in the embrace of solitude and darkness.

The Tang Family Compound had little open ground to begin with, and once the scaffolding went up, what space remained shrank further. Apart from the Junior Martial Brothers and Sisters on duty keeping order outside and guarding key posts like the Alchemy Room, the Scripture Hall, and Zhengxin Hall, everyone else was left crammed into the Disciples' Quarters, peering out through the windows—some, finding even that too tight, climbed onto the roof to watch.

Not until Emei's Xie Wuchen stepped onto the field did the Junior Martial Sister truly look twice. Whoever squared off against him, he would simply cup his fists in salute and drop them with a single kick—if one kick didn't finish it, he'd land two, or three. His flying kicks were unmatched for speed; through bout after bout, not one opponent managed to land so much as a single move on him—every exchange was his alone. This time it wasn't only Third Senior Brother who cheered; even the Junior Martial Sister found herself impressed: if Xie Wuchen's skill ran this high, why had Eldest Senior Brother always called him weak? In truth, Xie Wuchen, styled the Wind God, stood on par with the Flying Hero, and in raw physical foundation he even surpassed Eldest Senior Brother. Yet he often lost out in the Jianghu, his record far behind Eldest Senior Brother's—because Eldest Senior Brother was cunning by nature, and would never provoke a fight that brought no gain or wasn't a sure win. Xie Wuchen, by contrast, loved battle for its own sake and cared deeply for his name; wherever he traveled he'd seek out famous heroes to test himself against, and inevitably ran into opponents too tough for him. When Eldest Senior Brother called him weak, he meant something other than martial skill.

This was Yunshang's first sight of the Nangong clan, and the grandeur of the Eldest Young Lord's robes and pauldron left her staring, mouth agape. She glanced anxiously left and right, only to find everyone else's expression unchanged, as if she alone found it strange—and all at once she felt cast out and betrayed, the world turned suddenly unfamiliar.

Nangong Shen crossed blows with each opponent like a seasoned peacemaker of the Jianghu—never flustered, never overplaying his hand, standing unbeaten while still leaving room for others to save face. Every other pairing left its loser more red-eyed with envy the longer they fought, but his own opponents, facing the Eldest Young Lord himself, more often than not walked away smiling even in defeat, full of genuine admiration.

One pair of young heroes after another took the stage and stepped down again, each showing off their skill, yet to the Junior Martial Sister's eye none of it amounted to much. She had scarcely set foot in the Jianghu, and had little experience trading blows in real combat—yet years of single-minded focus had let her glimpse the deeper mysteries of Tang Clan's arts, and her judgment now surpassed even Third Senior Brother's. The very heroes Third Senior Brother praised without end struck her as thoroughly strange: they seemed to care only whether a move looked imposing, never whether overextending their strength left an opening. These men couldn't even best themselves—so what right did they have to such pride?

Third Senior Brother accompanied Junior Martial Sister, commenting on the martial artists in the arena while secretly observing her expression. However, the Junior Martial Sister remained expressionless, revealing nothing.

Yunshang appeared at the Junior Martial Sister's side as though it were the most natural thing in the world, offering her opinions on every bout. Almost nothing that left her mouth was kind—if it wasn't nitpicking, it was kicking someone while they were down, and she spared not even her own Senior Brother from Diancang. In Yunshang's eyes, no man under heaven was worthy of Moling; she feared that behind Moling's icy purity and innocent heart, everyone looked good to her, and she'd end up giving her whole life to the wrong man. Yunshang could only curse that she hadn't been born a man herself, or she'd have carried this girl off long ago instead of fretting over her now.

A canopy went up over the training ground, and suitors from every sect took their turns in the ring, matching not only skill but character and virtue as well. Who wouldn't want to shine before the Junior Martial Sister, leave a deep impression, and win the beauty's heart?
After a few words, Xie Wuchen flew into the sky and vanished. You looked at the night, still unable to figure out why he had come.

But you refused.
You wanted fame and glory as a great hero, sure enough, but you had no wish to be beaten black and blue — least of all by tangling with someone like Xie Wuchen, a martial fanatic notorious for his love of a fight. Eldest Senior Brother was proof enough of that.
The idea of 'no fewer than a hundred duels' sounded ordinary enough on its face, but think it through, and would any normal person let himself get dragged into such an endless mess? Small wonder Eldest Senior Brother always looked so put out whenever Xie Wuchen's name came up.
You were delighted to the utmost and swore an oath by clapping hands with him.

Seeing the eagerness brimming in your eyes, he told you: wait until you had truly mastered your art, until the storms of the Jianghu passed and the sky cleared, the wind died and the waves stilled — then come spar with him again.

Xie Wuchen challenged you to a duel, seeming to have a deeper intent. He intentionally allowed you to fully display your skills, and you didn't disappoint him, exchanging moves skillfully. You identified a weakness in his technique that wasn't exactly a flaw and launched a fierce attack, emerging victorious. Xie Wuchen smiled happily as he withdrew from the duel.

Xie Wuchen seemed to have some deeper purpose in mind — deliberately holding back so you could fight freely, so he might gauge your true skill, before finally defeating you.
He could teach you no technique, but he meant to temper your heart and make you strong and unyielding; a single change of mind might alter your whole fate.
With those words, Xie Wuchen soared into the sky and vanished. You stared into the night, still unable to puzzle out why he had really come.

Xie Wuchen was a martial arts fanatic, and hearing this sent him into a rage. He had long since heard the rumor, though the great sects of the Central Plains all dismissed it, insisting the Tang Clan had fabricated the story to slander an innocent man out of some hidden agenda.
Xie Wuchen alone stood against the consensus. Sooner or later, he vowed, he would storm Qingcheng and settle things with Shentu Long once and for all — to clear Eldest Senior Brother's name, and avenge you in the same stroke.

As he traded blows with you, he could sense your Internal Force failing to keep pace with your technique — moves that should have carried follow-through fell flat, though he couldn't say why.
Only when he asked did he learn you had been struck down by the Devouring Heaven Demon Technique, your Internal Force ruined beyond use. Worst of all, you might never recover it for the rest of your life.
After a fierce battle, you were crushed by Xie Wuchen's storm‑like assault.
Though you had no idea what he was really thinking, the manual was without doubt a genuine treasure. Fearing he might change his mind, you thanked him at once and tucked it away inside your robes.

You really couldn't bring yourself to accept it so easily, so you asked him again — only to learn Xie Wuchen was just as desperate to be rid of the manual. Besotted with martial arts, he had no wish to take a disciple who might slow his own progress. But night after night, the portrait of Emei's founding Patriarch scolded him in his dreams for his unfilial neglect — for minding only himself and letting the sect's legacy go to waste — until Xie Wuchen took to waking in terror at midnight, half-convinced the manual itself was haunted. He wanted to burn it, yet never dared. And there you were, conveniently: disciple to his old friend, and so as good as his own junior. Since you were already headed to Kongtong to study, he reasoned you wouldn't mind letting him hang your name on Emei Mountain's rolls as a nominal heir — a mere formality. With the manual passed to a successor, he'd have discharged his duty to the sect at last, and everyone would come away happy. Before you could so much as object, he was gone in a flash.

Xie Wuchen drew from his robes a secret manual, Snake, Rabbit, Eagle, Ape Combat, and gave it to you. This was no ordinary martial art — it was one of the Emei Sect's finest secret arts, and among the most masterful Xingyi Fist techniques in the world.
Such a precious manual could not help but delight you. Yet precisely because it was a sect's guarded secret, it was nothing to take lightly — unlike lesser techniques, which others might overlook if practiced only half right.

You suddenly felt the urge to show off your wide network, so you immediately claimed to know Liu E and that you had a great relationship with him. Liu E also had a fateful connection with Xie Wuchen; he not only defeated Xie Wuchen in public but also forced him to rename his exclusive ultimate technique, Wind-Thunder God Kick, to Very Forceful Kick, going to great lengths to humiliate him. Because of this, Xie Wuchen could no longer face using his unique martial arts skill. You kept bringing up this issue, so he hesitated and then changed his mind, deciding to cut ties with you. Originally, he had planned to give you a gift, but he abandoned that idea. You're so annoying; it's only natural to be disliked, isn't it?

He gave you his secret manual as a gift. He had once lost a wager to Dharma King Liu E of the Mud Cult, and been forced to rename his signature technique 'Very Forceful Kick' — a humiliation that meant he could never bring himself to use it again. Such a magnificent skill deserved better than to fade into obscurity, so he passed the manual to you both as a token of their friendship and in hopes you might make a name for yourself in the Jianghu with it, and clear its name of shame.

You suddenly heard Xiahou Lan's name pass his lips, and fearing he wouldn't believe it, you performed a stroke straight from Xiahou Lan's own teaching — the Snow Mountain Sword Technique.
Xie Wuchen stood dumbstruck a moment, then was overjoyed almost beyond reason — who could have guessed the world's threads of fate ran so deep? You were Junior Brother to his lifelong rival and disciple to his old friend both; your bond with him ran deeper than either of you knew.

Xie Wuchen recalled their dealings across the past ten years — he and Eldest Senior Brother had both been green striplings fresh to the world, and even then, Tang Buyi got the better of him at every turn. Whether by some quirk of fate, the two seemed doomed to cross paths wherever they went; young and hot-blooded, they matched wits and blows without ever backing down, so that almost every meeting ended in a contest, and if not martial arts, then something else.
The famous Mianyang Lake Incident in the Wulin was their doing: racing ahead of the imperial troops, the two of them took apart an entire pirate stronghold between them, yet still couldn't settle which of them had won. Xie Wuchen later joined the army's ranks, while Eldest Senior Brother turned around and rallied the water bandits to hold the stronghold, defying the troops for ten days. Only when the two sect leaders and the Nangong Family Head arrived in person was the crisis defused; through the Nangong Family Head's mediation, the soldiers were compensated and the bandits granted amnesty to the last man, so that everyone came away with a good outcome.
Only Eldest Senior Brother and Xie Wuchen came home beaten to a pulp, each sent back up the mountain to reflect.
Xie Wuchen could never let this one go — he'd fought on the government's side, so how was that supposed to have been wrong?
Stories like this were beyond counting, and Xie Wuchen never failed to fume whenever Eldest Senior Brother's name came up.
Sworn enemies as the two of them were, forever bickering or brawling whenever they met, they had once walked the Jianghu together as companions all the same.
Tang Buyi of the Tang Clan, Xie Wuchen of Emei, Xiahou Lan of Kongtong, and a nameless pair of sworn lovers who, their deeds done, had vanished beyond the frontier pass to herd sheep — the five of them traveled as one, righting wrongs wherever they saw them. As the saying goes, foes who cross blades become friends: from that beginning they went on to overpower champions of the Jin court, beat back the Goryeo demon cult, and leave the Lingnan Sect reeling. At their journey's end, the five joined forces to crush the ambitions of the old demon cult's remnants.
All of it felt as though it had happened only yesterday — as if he'd only just waved his friends off in their separate directions, and in the blink of an eye, here he was: the green hills unchanged, but everyone and everything else gone.
Life rushes by like a white colt glimpsed through a crack in the wall — some arrive, some depart, gathering and scattering like duckweed on the water, leaving one with nothing but a sigh.

Xie Wuchen thought nothing of the risk and trespassed into the Tang Clan's back mountain — only to explain that he had merely brought wine to pay respects at Eldest Senior Brother's grave.
You said nothing for a long moment, then led him there; Xie Wuchen stood in silence for a good while, saying nothing at all.
Only after a long pause did he speak, and the first thing out of his mouth was suspicion that Eldest Senior Brother had faked his death — he meant to dig up the grave and open the coffin to check. Only after you talked him down did he let the idea go, and accept that his lifelong rival truly lay at rest beneath the earth.
He uncorked his wine gourd — no drinker himself, he still took a mouthful in Eldest Senior Brother's memory, then passed the flask to you.
The wine was fragrant and fine, yet neither of you had the heart to taste it; you poured it into the soil instead, leaving it for the departed.

Xie Wuchen was so besotted with martial arts it bordered on madness. Stumbling upon you at practice, he felt an itch he simply couldn't resist scratching, and clean forgot what he had come here to do.

While the sun had not yet set, you went alone to the back mountain, took your stance, and threw punches and kicks — this was simply your habit on days when no one came to press you. Before you knew it, night had fallen, and you were about to head back when a figure in white suddenly darted up over the cliff's edge. Looking closer, you saw it was Xie Wuchen, the very man you had all worked so hard to send down the mountain. No sooner had he been persuaded to leave than he doubled back partway down the mountain, followed the stream upward, and drew out the grappling rope he used for scaling cliffs. Trusting to his formidable Qinggong, he shunned the plank road and leapt straight into your Tang Clan's back mountain.

Nangong Shen came to propose the match with full sincerity, yet without pressing the matter. Were he fortunate enough to welcome Junior Martial Sister into his household, he vowed to treat her as an honored guest, and spare no effort to see her fed, clothed, and living in peace and happiness. And even should the blossom's longing go unanswered by the indifferent stream, it must not cost their two houses one shred of the friendship between them.
As for the alliance, weighty as it was, there was no need to rush to a decision — so you were asked to present the Immortality Pill first, and take up the matter with Third Hero Tang and Fourth Hero Tang later.

You didn't buy it at all — fine words aside, wasn't this just having the bear paw and still craving the fish?
Junior Martial Sister hadn't even set foot through the door yet, and already he was scheming to take a second wife. Outrageous.

Hearing this, you couldn't help but admire him. The Eldest Young Lord, scion of a great house, feared no ridicule from the world for his scandalous devotion to a courtesan, and never once wavered. And though you yourself were not of that debased register, you were every bit as low-born in others' eyes, long since used to being looked down upon—yet the Eldest Young Lord had been willing to set aside his rank and befriend you all the same. Such magnanimity was rare indeed.

He did not want to hide it from you, and admitted that he did have feelings for Young Lady Yue Ping, a courtesan of the entertainers' register. They were confidantes as much as they were in love, and he had already made her a promise: to have her freed from that low status and restored as a commoner, and only then take her into his household. So even if it meant marrying her as a secondary wife, he was bound to bring her in—he could not spend his whole life with only one wife.

In front of everyone, the Eldest Young Lord had to keep up appearances, and every word he spoke had to sound proper. Now that you asked, he finally let the truth slip, laughing at himself: 'I'm no naive boy anymore—what's this business of an opposite-sex confidante?'
The only thing to fear was that the Junior Martial Sister wouldn't be pleased.

Only now did you see the Eldest Young Lord's true colors—such wolfish ambition hidden beneath it all—and you couldn't help but laugh. That he was willing to be so open with you showed real sincerity; this conversation alone had deepened your friendship considerably. As for the matter of the alliance, important as it was, there was no need to rush to a conclusion. So he asked you to deliver the Immortality Pill, and said the rest could wait to be discussed with the Third Hero Tang and Fourth Hero Tang.

The Nangong Family were all refined, cultured people, versed in both letters and martial arts, masters of the four arts, and especially fond of romance. Faced with a woman as gifted and beautiful as Young Lady Yue Ping, how could he not fall for her? One careless night left her with child, so after the Jiangling battle he had no choice but to send Shangguan Ying away—otherwise, with her fiery temper, if she learned that her betrothed had barely so much as held her hand yet had already lain with another woman as husband and wife, would she not have beaten him half to death and then taken her own life? Shangguan Ying had been a woman of rare beauty, and if it were possible, the Eldest Young Lord would gladly have married her too and enjoyed the good fortune of two wives—but the world rarely offers such perfect arrangements; the finest things remain only dreams. The finest dream of all would have been to marry Yue Ping, Shangguan Ying, and Talented Woman Wei all at once, the three of them serving one husband in perfect harmony—but it was nothing more than idle fantasy. Neither Shangguan Ying nor Talented Woman Wei was a woman easily bent to a man's will.

In front of everyone, he'd had to keep up appearances, and every word he spoke had to sound proper. Only now did the Eldest Young Lord let the truth slip, laughing at himself: 'I'm no naive boy anymore—what's this business of an opposite-sex confidante?' He was simply fond of Yue Ping.

For example, instead of marrying the Junior Martial Sister, he could marry one of your other senior or junior sisters. That way he'd have it easier still—no need to tread carefully around your Junior Martial Sister—and could follow his own heart: marry his beloved Yue Ping first, then take one of your Tang sisters as a secondary wife.

Regarding the alliance matter, although it is of great importance, there's no need to rush to a conclusion. Please pass on the Immortality Pill and discuss it further with the Third Hero Tang and Fourth Hero Tang at your convenience.

Besides, he also found Nangong Qian a nuisance, so it would kill two birds with one stone to use the chance to be rid of him: let Nangong Qian change his surname to Tang. From then on he would be both a Tang Clan disciple and still tied to the Nangong Family—the perfect candidate to serve as the bridge between the two houses.

Nangong Qian greatly admired you; every time he spoke of you, he praised you without end, as if he thought of you as his own elder brother. With that bond between you, there was more than enough trust to go on.

Thanks to the Old Patriarch's foresight, Nangong Qian had once studied at the Tang Clan, making him something of a half-disciple of the sect. That connection alone was enough to serve as a bridge between the two families.
For example, betraying Nangong Qian.

Even so, you were consumed with worry. You feared the Junior Martial Sister wouldn't be happy, feared she wouldn't adjust to Jiangling's climate, feared that as a young mistress she'd be run ragged managing the household accounts, feared she'd have to accompany her husband in entertaining guests—hard enough on her shy nature as it was. What if Nangong Shen took a second wife? What if that second wife saw how soft-tempered she was and bullied her? Nangong Shen, well versed in human nature, read your face and knew exactly what you were thinking. He couldn't help but laugh, and at once dropped the idea of the marriage. As the saying goes, a gentleman does not take what another loves, and does not do to others what he would not have done to himself. Besides, that young lady of the Tang seemed to feel nothing for him at all. Shangguan Ying, at least, was fully herself—angry when angry, warm as a spring breeze when she smiled. Never had he seen anyone like your Junior Martial Sister: cold as carved jade, showing neither joy nor anger, beautiful past compare yet utterly without human warmth. If an alliance was the goal, why worry there'd be no other way?

Nangong Shen had come to propose the marriage because he was drawn to her gentle, kind nature—hoping she might set old grievances aside and accept Yue Ping, so the two could live in harmony. Sincere as he was, he did not insist on it. Should he be fortunate enough to welcome the Junior Martial Sister into his household, he would treat her as an honored guest and do everything in his power to see that she never wanted for anything, that she lived in peace and happiness. And even if the flowers had feeling but the stream did not, that alone would not diminish the bond between the two families in the least. As for the alliance itself, important as it was, there was no need to rush to a conclusion—he asked only that you deliver the Immortality Pill, leaving the rest to be discussed later with the Third Hero Tang and Fourth Hero Tang.

As for what I said in front of everyone earlier—that she's merely a confidante—that was only for the sake of appearances; what a man says in public must always sound proper. Now that you ask me outright, I'll tell you the truth, with a self-mocking laugh: I'm no naive boy anymore. Since when is there such a thing as an 'opposite-sex confidante'?

Compared to Shangguan Ying, Lady Yue seemed all the more gentle and charming, always speaking in a soft, delicate voice like a little bird nestled close. Her looks fell somewhat short of Shangguan Ying's, but her inner qualities were beyond compare—and it was just when Nangong Shen most needed comfort that she won his heart.

You've also been scolded by Shangguan Ying, even beaten by her. You feel a deep sympathy for the Eldest Young Lord's plight. In all the world, no one gets scolded by her more than you—except perhaps the young lord before you now. He is richer and more highborn than you, yet before Shangguan Ying the two of you are treated just the same: both get scolded.

You too have been scolded by Shangguan Ying, even beaten by her. You didn't need to be there to picture her that day—eyes brimming with tears, torn between anger and worry—and it's hard not to envy the Eldest Young Lord for taking his good fortune for granted. Shangguan Ying's scoldings, after all, were always meant for the other person's good, like an old nanny's earnest nagging, nothing at all like the curses and insults of others.

However, you found it hard to let this go.
It was not that you meant to make things difficult, but the fact remained: Nangong Shen had broken the engagement in public, leaving Shangguan Ying with nowhere to hide her shame. How could you believe he would not fail the Junior Martial Sister too?
Nangong Shen let out a long sigh. He did not mean to hide anything from you—if truth be told, he had wanted to unburden himself to someone for a very long time.
Was the engagement to Shangguan Ying ever his own choice? One day his father simply summoned him to pay respects to Uncle Shangguan, and told him, 'This is your betrothed.'
Shangguan Ying had been beautiful from birth, and he had liked her on sight; the two of them, still children, got along easily. Her temper ran a little stubborn, but it was no great fault—give her room, and once her anger cooled she would repay him twice over in tenderness.
The two even studied together at the Gengyang Study Hall, becoming classmates and friends with Mystic Skill Gate Leader Wei of Kongtong.
As the years passed, Shangguan Ying grew ever more beautiful, a radiance beyond compare. As her betrothed, the Eldest Young Lord felt both pride and shame, for even as a girl she had run the family's affairs in her father's stead, traveling far and wide and setting the household in perfect order.
The Eldest Young Lord, by contrast, remained only the Eldest Young Lord for as long as he was not yet Family Head. The few shops and taverns he had invested in around Jiangling might not even turn a profit, and he still needed his betrothed's constant help and guidance.
With such a gulf between their abilities, how could he not feel ashamed?
He urged Shangguan Ying not to show herself too much in public—partly because he did not want the world coveting her beauty, but partly because he feared her ability would leave him hopelessly behind and hard to govern after marriage. To put it plainly, it was pure selfishness.
Worse, after her years in the marketplace Shangguan Ying grew only more stubborn and headstrong—gracious to her superiors, but arrogant and rude to those beneath her. She was petty, jealous, sharp-tongued, and loved nothing more than to lecture and put on airs.
Among her peers, only Sect Leader Wei of Kongtong could get a word in edgewise.
Nangong Shen had taken up with the entertainer only to give Shangguan Ying something to be wary of, to make her rein in her temper. The trick worked all too well: it made her cry, and he felt both satisfaction and relief.
During their cold war, the brothers Nangong Shen and Nangong Qian were ambushed by masked men and beaten badly.
Word reached Shangguan Ying, and she forgot her sulking and rushed over to see him. The moment she saw her betrothed lying there, bruised and battered, grief welled up and turned to fury. She had meant to say so many gentle, comforting things, but what came out was nothing but reproach and scolding—she cursed him before his friends for keeping bad company, and before his teaching elders for learning nothing.
How could Nangong Shen not have felt his heart go cold?

The Eldest Young Lord's gift of the treasure was not purely for the sake of friendship. The Jianghu was now in ceaseless turmoil, with no one willing to bow to another, everyone scrambling for fame and gain, and families ruined and lives lost overnight. What was needed was a figure of great standing to rise up and call out, rallying the Wulin's fellows to stand together against the coming calamity. As for who might fill that role -- aside from Immortal Qiu of the Quanzhen Sect, whose standing was beyond compare -- none held greater prestige than the Three Great Family Heads. The Nangong Family seemed the obvious choice, but since the Old Patriarch's death, its head had never recovered his footing; Nangong Shen knew his own experience was still shallow, and a single hand, as they say, cannot clap. As for the Shangguan Family, they had withdrawn from the Jianghu, and still nursed a grudge over the broken engagement -- cooperation with them was out of the question. That left only the Tang Clan: they would have to call Tang Zhongling out of seclusion, join hands with the Nangong Family, and only then would they hold prestige enough to set the Central Plains in order and stand united against the Demon Cult's threat. Though the gift of medicine was no bid for repayment, the marriage proposal was meant to bind the two families to the same cause. You reckoned in your heart that, whether for the greater good or your own family's sake, marrying the Junior Martial Sister into the Nangong Family would be a wise move. For the greater good: the two families, already old friends, would become bound by marriage into an unbreakable alliance, standing together through thick and thin -- should the Tang Clan ever fall into hardship, the Nangong Family would surely not stand idly by, and this bond alone could shield the Tang Clan from ruin amid the Jianghu's turmoil. For your own family's sake: the Nangong Family's connections ran wide and their wealth was vast, with friends from officials and nobles down to heroes of the Jianghu -- wherever she went, doors would open for her. When the Mud Cult's Beast Path attacked the Nangong Family, it drew the whole Central Plains to Jiangling's defense, proof enough of their reach. Should the Junior Martial Sister marry into Jiangling, she would surely want for nothing all her days, clothed in fine silks and waited on by maids and servants, and anyone who thought to trouble her would find it no easy task.

You could scarcely believe such a priceless elixir could be given away so readily by the Eldest Young Lord. You couldn't help feeling that away from prying eyes, this Eldest Young Lord wore a different face altogether -- warm and full of chivalry -- and your prejudice against him eased somewhat.

You wanted to find him, and he was just about to seek you out. Drawing you aside to speak in private, he reverently produced a Qingcheng elixir, the Returning Void Pill. This pill had been a birthday gift from Sect Leader Zou of Qingcheng for the Old Patriarch's hundredth birthday, but since the old man had passed so suddenly, he never had the chance to take it. The dead are gone, but the living may still be helped -- better to give it to the Sect Leader to cure his illness and prolong his life, a small gesture that would not shame the long friendship between the Nangong and Tang Clans.

Nangong Shen bristled inwardly, and thought little of you for it, but this was a question he could not avoid answering. After the Jiangling battle, he had investigated far and wide, hoping to catch the Tang Clan's tell-tale sign of guilt. Heaven did not forsake those who toiled, and before long he truly did find evidence of the Tang Clan's wrongdoing -- the trouble was, the evidence was so overwhelming that none of it held up to scrutiny, and it was plain that the real culprit behind it all meant to frame them. Though he no longer suspected the Tang Clan for the time being, he still could not bring himself to trust them fully; yet even so, he had to think of the Wulin's fate, and could not let private feeling harm the public good or ignore the righteousness of the realm. He had come to propose the marriage precisely to unite the strength of the two great families, to rise up and rally the righteous path, and stand together against the Demon Cult.

Simply put: after the Jiangling battle, when the Old Patriarch passed away, the Tang Clan fell under the Eldest Young Lord's suspicion, and he treated you all as though you were sworn enemies who could not share the same sky. So why does he come seeking a marriage alliance today?
You weren't about to back down, and right then countered with a sharp retort.
Setting aside the Eldest Young Lord's views on the Tang Clan, he made no effort at all to hide his contempt for you.

You had something to say, but courtesy before confrontation -- you offer the Eldest Young Lord a cup. He tilts back his head and turns his cup upside down to show nothing is left, a show of forthright spirit. Inwardly you applaud his boldness, and follow suit, draining your own cup.

You had something to say, but courtesy before confrontation -- you offer the Eldest Young Lord a cup. He covers his mouth with his sleeve and tilts back his head, looking every bit the bold drinker, but in truth pours the wine straight into his sleeve. You see through the trick but say nothing, and drain your own cup to the last drop.

You laughed it off, using his own words to smooth things over, then turned and apologized to the assembled heroes, asking them to forgive unfamiliar fare. As the crowd breathed a sigh of relief, they also felt sheepish for having judged a person of honor with such petty suspicion, and could not help but blush. Seeing how gracefully you had handled it, they warmed to you all the more.

You showed no mercy, exposing the truth in one sentence. Not only did it make the other party blush, but all the guests also looked ashamed. After all, the Tang Clan is renowned for their poison and hidden weapons. Who would dare not be cautious and feast freely on Tang Clan territory? The full table of dishes had few people touching their chopsticks; everyone was eating their own brought food.

You went down the mountain to the Outer Fort to call on Nangong Shen. No sooner had you arrived than you saw the Nangong Family Servants bringing in food. Elder Hero Nangong, who was serving as matchmaker, wore a look of embarrassment, unable to say outright that one must be wary of others -- he was, in truth, wary of the Tang Clan.

At noon, you were all crammed together in the disciples' quarters, sitting casually on beds or the floor. Compared to the outside guests, the meal was very simple, with each person getting one rice ball. Yet, despite this, the rice balls seemed to have a unique flavor, and everyone ate them with great enjoyment. Perhaps such moments of togetherness are rare, and everyone silently understood.
