Later, the Third Senior Brother exerted great effort, managing to temporarily persuade the person to hold back and advised him to rest briefly after dinner before proceeding with the sparring. Many people had come to join the gathering, hoping to try their luck. When they saw that Xie Wuchen was competing, they didn't even eat dinner and hurriedly left the mountain.

You stepped forward to reason with him, trying to appeal to his sense of logic, asking him if he could still take responsibility if he caused the Junior Martial Sister to be unable to marry. Xie Wuchen didn't care about responsibility, but he still wanted to fight. Watching him rub his hands together, eager to send all the suitors back to their hometowns, Third Senior Brother's stomach began to ache, unable to believe this fool was the legendary Emei Wind God.

You stepped forward to mediate as well, only to be won over instead, itching to join him on the field as the Junior Martial Sister's Guardian. Third Senior Brother had arranged for the suitors to duel in pairs specifically to keep you from losing control and hurting someone, and so had left you out of it -- who could have guessed that Xie Wuchen would suddenly charge in from the side? Watching him crack his knuckles, looking ready to send every last suitor packing, your stomach began to ache.

After interviewing all the suitors, the Junior Martial Sister had found no one to her liking -- as if anyone would do, yet no one would do. Third Senior Brother was torn between reluctance and dismay, but the Tang Clan stood in dire peril, and only by hardening his heart and marrying her off could he honor the Sect Leader's charge. Just as he was about to leave for the meal, a Tang Clan disciple in charge of announcing names hurried in to report that another suitor had arrived -- none other than Xie Wuchen, the "Wind God" of Emei, as famed as the Eldest Senior Brother and long acknowledged as his lifelong rival. Third Senior Brother was overjoyed, his words full of reverence, and hastened to welcome him in. Xie Wuchen was a fine figure of a man, handsome of feature and upright of bearing, a bold spirit shining between his brows. Famed for years, all one ever heard of him was his chivalry and justice -- never a hint of any sweetheart. He kept himself above reproach, and besides, Emei ranked among the Six Great Sects of the Central Plains and lay close to the Tang Clan -- he seemed a fine match indeed for the Junior Martial Sister. Yet Third Senior Brother had misread Xie Wuchen's intent. Though he had come for the Junior Martial Sister's sake, it was not to seek her hand. Beside a worthy rival, this martial fanatic cared nothing for women -- as Tang Buyi's match in a hundred bouts and more, the two had long come to admire each other in their hearts. How could he let the Junior Martial Sister, who by rights should have been Tang Buyi's bride, fall into the hands of some common mediocrity? So he had come uninvited, taking it upon himself to stand in for the Eldest Senior Brother and screen suitors on the Junior Martial Sister's behalf.

The Eldest Young Lord knew this matter could not be sidestepped forever, and so had no choice but to speak plainly. Unexpectedly, he did not dwell on personal feelings at all, but looked to the larger picture: though the two families had been betrothed since childhood, Shangguan Ying herself was without fault -- it was simply that times had changed. The Shangguan family had withdrawn from the Jianghu and pledged themselves to the Imperial Court, while the Nangong family, though on good terms with the authorities, had never forgotten its roots and remained devoted to the Wulin. He asked those present: if the two families were joined in marriage, could their fellows of the Jianghu still call the Nangong family upright and impartial? As for the singing girl and himself, theirs was a pure friendship of kindred spirits -- talk of him being besotted with a woman and neglecting his betrothal was nothing but slander. Hearing him speak so, everyone present finally understood -- only this way could the Nangong family's good name as the Heart of the Wulin be preserved, and the Eldest Young Lord Nangong, in giving up his own feelings for the greater cause, was not only blameless but could even be called a model of chivalry. Only the Junior Martial Sister remained sullen and displeased. She understood his words well enough, but did not think them reasonable -- must a fiancee who was like family be wronged, all for the sake of Wulin's public good? She would never in her life accept it. Beneath her calm, faintly displeased face, the blood of the Tang Clan was beginning to boil. The Eldest Young Lord thought she was merely a little dissatisfied, never guessing he had already crossed her limit, and might at any moment find himself on the receiving end of her fury.

You are deeply concerned for Shangguan Ying; how can you not feel indignant about this? Hearing it makes you want to shout in approval. You must see how the Eldest Young Lord has caused Miss Ying to be heartbroken and in tears, and how he will try to justify himself. If he cannot provide a reasonable explanation, even if it costs you your life, you must seek justice.

Shangguan Ying was extremely indulgent towards her junior martial sister during her time in the Tang Clan, even more so than with close relatives. The junior martial sister, overwhelmed with gratitude, could not bear to see Sister Ying weep over this unfeeling man, and she confronted him on the spot, asking why he did not want Shangguan Ying but wished to marry her instead. Since the Jiangling battle, rumors about Nangong's broken engagement have spread, but no one dared to inquire about others' private matters. The moment she spoke these words, the crowd in the hall immediately erupted into heated discussion.

Third Senior Brother heard out this lofty discourse without agreeing or disputing it, and pressed no further, inviting him in for tea as planned, with the martial test to follow after the meal. Nangong Shen, reading the room, already knew his answer had dodged the heart of the question and could not have fooled the discerning eye of a Confucian hero like him—but he didn't mind. His words today had already won over countless hearts, and that served the family well.
But you quickly came back to your senses—you knew exactly what sort of person you were. If even you could feel flattered, then this Young Lord truly had a golden tongue, remarkably impressive.
You listened from the sidelines, feeling as if some of that glory rubbed off on you too, so pleased with yourself you could have floated up to heaven.

You listened from the sidelines, feeling quite skeptical. Perhaps he genuinely believed as much, given how forthright he seemed. However, what is the reality? In the Jianghu, those who only consider themselves make up the vast majority. Discussions should be based on facts rather than empty rhetoric; otherwise, they risk appearing disingenuous. Such words may inspire those in the Jianghu to hold their heads high and walk with confidence, but they provide no real help in the current situation. Selfish individuals remain selfish, and the Imperial Court continues to fear the unruly elements of the Jianghu. If they cannot find acceptance from the Son of Heaven, then the fate of the heroes of Liangshan is a cautionary tale not far off.

You listened from the side, sneering to yourself. Crooked as your own heart was, you had enough learning in you not to be so easily played for a fool. Folk of the Jianghu fought for fame and fortune—who among them wouldn't rather be an official and rise in the world, if only they could? They drew no salary from the court, ate not a single grain of the emperor's rice, and yet were expected to die defending someone else's throne?

Third Senior Brother turned his thoughts, and then posed a difficult question. The question was: A farmer cultivates rice to sustain the common people, a woodcutter fells trees to make paper for the spread of knowledge. What use is a martial artist who has mastered his skills but does not serve the country, only seeking personal gain? A scholar may disrupt laws with his words, while a heroic martial artist may defy regulations with his strength. How can they be tolerated by the heavens? As soon as this question was posed, the hall fell into silence. Those with little education did not understand the question, while those who did understood it and felt a chill. They had thought that this Confucian hero, Third Master Tang, would be lenient toward the Eldest Young Lord, but they had not expected such a difficult question. This question asked: A farmer's rice sustains the common people, a woodcutter's trees provide firewood for cooking, and paper for spreading knowledge. Yet we people of the Jianghu have painstakingly cultivated our skills, yet we do not serve the country, only seeking fame and profit. What benefit do we bring to the common people? Far from being heroic, the state has its laws, and families have their rules. Even scholars, who call upon benevolence and human feelings, may hinder the imperial court's legal governance. How much more so for martial heroes, whose skill alone could challenge the state's regulations? The answer is simple, yet no one is willing to voice it. One word said wrong could offend the entire Wulin. Nangong Shen thought for a moment and had a plan. He cited The Great Learning, from the Book of Rites, speaking confidently. He said that whether in the arts or in martial skills, one must first cultivate oneself, understand the great principles, know honor and shame, be sincere in heart and upright in conduct, and use the mind to guide both literature and martial arts. All are for self‑cultivation. When a school or sect is established, that is to govern the family. Only when the family is well‑ordered can one discuss governing the country. If it benefits the country, even a common man has a responsibility. Soldiers defend the country abroad, while heroes keep the peace at home. Therefore, I argue that all people of the Jianghu are dedicated to the country and the people. This speech elevated everyone in the Wulin to the status of heroes who serve the country and the people, adding gold to their faces, earning thunderous applause and roaring approval.

The Nangong family is not only a great house of the Wulin but also a lineage steeped in scholarship. As heir apparent to the position of Family Head, the Eldest Young Lord had been immersed in both martial arts and learning since childhood, excelling at each without effort. In the battle of Jiangling, he even led a company of heroes against the invading Beast Path, and his feats there spoke for themselves. For the Third Senior Brother to test him again on the classics and histories would mean little; it would only expose the shallowness of the examiner.

The Junior Martial Sister met the Eldest Young Lord for the first time at Nangong's Birthday Banquet. The Eldest Young Lord praised her at length, laying his feelings bare, saying that even a single fleeting encounter had left him unable to forget her. At the time the Junior Martial Sister was too absorbed in the delicacies to take much notice of him. Instead she was captivated by his fiancée, Shangguan Ying, whose radiant beauty stirred a quiet admiration in her even as a woman, and she entirely forgot to eat.

You stood with your fellow disciples by the hall, passing your own judgment on the candidates. The morning wore on, and you saw all manner of remarkable and eccentric characters—the search for a husband wasn't limited to martial artists, and no few talented scholars and wealthy young lords came drawn by reputation, hoping for a glimpse of the Junior Martial Sister's beauty. Some were dazzling in both talent and looks; others were laughable oddities. Anyone arrogant in speech, rude in manner, frivolous, given to empty posturing, or flaunting his wealth was shown out of the hall at once, regardless of rank. Among today's young heroes and lords, Nangong Shen, Eldest Young Lord of the Nangong family, was thought the most promising by far—unmatched in lineage, wealth, renown, martial skill, and learning. Even the matchmaker who came with him was a renowned elder of the Jianghu and an old friend of the Third Senior Brother; by every measure he seemed the perfect choice. Only one thing courted controversy: Nangong Shen was already promised in marriage to the Young Lady of the Shangguan family.

Contests of arms for a bride's hand are no rarity in the Wulin, but the Tang Clan ranks among the three great families—though not as glorious as in its prime, still far beyond what any minor sect could match. Word spread that the Young Lady of the Tang Clan sought a husband, and unmarried young heroes of the Jianghu flocked to Shu from every corner, until the Tang family compound was packed to bursting. A canopy had been raised over the training grounds to shade the suitors and their matchmakers. Every face wore some shade of unease: some huddled over strategies, some crammed at the last minute on hearing there would be a literary test, and a few sat calm and certain of victory. Called forward by roll, each entered Zhengxin Hall to present himself, where the Third Senior Brother posed questions to test his literary grace, eloquence, and insight.

Since the family crisis, the Junior Martial Sister has matured greatly, having experienced the bitterness of life's joys and sorrows. She once refused to accept, denied, raged, resisted, and felt despondent, but eventually came to understand that this is the impermanence of human affairs. She is about to marry far away and has come to see you tonight. She has no other wish but to spend a little time with her family and thank you.

Junior Martial Sister cried for a while, and you didn't rush her, letting her express herself freely. Gradually, she stopped sobbing, wiped away the shimmering tears from her lashes, and when she turned back, her usual indifferent expression had returned.

The Junior Martial Sister received your promise, gradually stopping her sobs, wiping away the shimmering tear drops from her lashes, and when she turned around, it was her usual indifferent expression.

You yielded this once, call it repayment for your master's grace. Next time, though the whole world stood against you, you would not turn back—though it meant flouting heaven's own law, you would seize her for your own.

You urged her to go, but not before making her a promise: if ever she felt lonely, she need only call your name. No matter how far the ends of the earth, you would come for her with everything you had, and bring her home.

Even as she spoke, the bell rang, and her tears began falling in a rush. The Junior Martial Sister had always been delicate and shy, never good at showing her feelings; since perfecting Heaven and Earth Silent Force, it had grown even harder to win a smile from her, let alone see her weep so openly as tonight. It wasn't insomnia—she was only afraid that once she closed her eyes, another day would pass, and her time left in the Tang Clan would shrink by that much. Your heart clenched, a tangle of feelings, but you couldn't find the words to comfort her. In the end you came up behind her and patted her back the way she used to pat others, certain that she, of all people, would understand what the gesture meant: I hope you are well—a kindness pure and unadorned, without a word of flattery, untouched by anything false.
You had only been joking, with no real hope in your heart, yet your single joke somehow hit the mark, revealing her true feelings‑she had indeed come out of fear of never seeing you again.

You were only joking at first, thinking she was probably anxious, curious what sort of talents had come to seek her hand, and asking you to take her down the mountain to see. Just as you went to fetch a lantern, the Junior Martial Sister stopped you—in truth she had not the slightest curiosity about the suitors below, only fear. Your joke had hit home; she truly had come because she was afraid of never seeing you again.

How bold of you to make light remarks about the soon‑to‑be married junior martial sister of our sect, not even bothering to examine your own appearance, shamelessly claiming she came because she feels lonely after marrying and can't see you anymore.

Asked if it sounded good, the Junior Martial Sister didn't spare your feelings, bluntly saying it was awful. You'd expected as much, mortified enough to wish you could melt into the night and vanish forever.
She couldn't help herself and laughed aloud, a rare thing. She used to cry easily, and after losing her mother she wept from dawn to dusk; if this song could lull her to sleep, it wasn't because it sounded pleasant, but because it was ridiculous—you were even more ridiculous getting beaten by everyone over it.
She called your name softly, and you braced yourself, thinking she meant to be cruel and make you sing it again. You were wrong.
Since the family's ruin, the Junior Martial Sister has grown up a great deal, come to know the bitterness of parting and reunion. She refused to accept it—denial, anger, resistance, despair—before at last understanding that this is simply the world's impermanence.
She is to be married far from home. Tonight she came to see you for no other reason than to spend a little more time with family, and to thank you.

You immediately wanted to roll up your sleeves and storm inside to give these no-good junior brothers a piece of your mind—can't a senior brother sing a song? Is a senior brother in the wrong? Back in the day, the Eldest Senior Brother used to stir up trouble outside and drag people out to fight! Does one song disturbing your sleep really cost you your life? The Junior Martial Sister quickly caught hold of your sleeve; without a word, one pitiful, pleading look was enough to dispel your urge for violence.
You really began to feel afraid—if they ganged up on you, you'd be in real trouble.
You were incensed by humiliation and snapped back with a sharp retort, inciting widespread outrage.
You were scolded harshly, ashamed to the point of wanting to dig a hole and crawl in.

You guessed she couldn't sleep, had gone out for a walk, and unwilling to be alone, had come to pester you. The Junior Martial Sister was to choose a husband the next day, and hadn't slept well that night—what if she was groggy and sluggish come morning? It was a fate she had arranged with her own hands, yet she regretted it all the same, and wept alone in her loneliness.
Her troubled heart worsened her illness; unseen, the poison had already eaten into her marrow, scrambling her memories, until she seemed to dream herself back at Diancang—still believing her brother was out roaming the world, her true brother and sworn brother both absent, and her fellow disciples too busy at swordplay to spare her a thought. So Yunshang wiped her tears alone, went back to her room, and loneliness gnawed at her until her illness ran deeper still.

Your cultivation is remarkable; you didn't take her brutal antics to heart, only responding with a bitter smile. After she caused a commotion, the sorrow and resentment knotted in your heart seemed to dissipate a bit.

You were so furious you vowed you wouldn't stop until you'd beaten her black and blue. So you said, but under your junior martial sister's icy stare, you could only grudgingly let it go. Angry as you were at her antics, the sorrow and bitterness knotted in your heart seemed to ease a little.

Ye Yunshang had no other choice but to step in and pat you herself. Her pat had not the slightest intention of comfort; it whipped through the air and caught you full in the face, leaving you dazed. She turned and ran, not forgetting to play the aggrieved party and blame you first, guilty as she was.

Yunshang had thought the Junior Martial Sister was kind-hearted, unworldly, without a trace of temper, and never one to judge by looks—surely she wouldn't refuse. But Yunshang had badly underestimated your gift for provoking people. The Junior Martial Sister's delicate brows furrowed; she said no, just the one word, and walked away without another glance.
Ye Yunshang saw that you looked gloomy and felt a pang of sympathy herself. On a whim, she invited her friend Mo Ling into the room to pat you.

The Jianghu is full of deceit and unpredictability. With the recent bad news, the relationship between the Kongtong and Tang Clan has become tense. Since receiving the news, someone from Kongtong had already sent a letter carrier to summon Xiao Zhu back to Kongtong. She has come today to say her farewells. Xiao Zhu and you have known each other for a short time, but in this world, it is hardest to find a true friend. As she departs, it is hard not to be sad. However, to repay the kindness of the former Sect Leader, Iron Fist, who took her in, she cannot abandon Kongtong. Tang Clan may be good, but ultimately, she must return to her lonely home.

Jianghu is full of twists and turns, unpredictable. Now that such tragic news has emerged, the relationship between the Tang Clan and Kongtong has become tense. Since Kongtong received the news, messengers have already been sent via carrier pigeons to summon Xiao Zhu back. She has come today to bid you farewell. Xiao Zhu has known you for not long, yet in this world, it's hardest to find a true kindred spirit. As she departs, her heart is filled with sorrow. She had someone deliver you a set of uniform clothes, which she handed to you. Though the stitching is rough, she had cut up her only treasured possession—a pair of gloves woven from Tianshan Black Silk—and sewn them into the garment. On the clothes, faint spots are visible, varying in depth. The darker ones might be from her clumsy hands, bleeding from a cut she inflicted upon herself, while the lighter ones could be her tears. Upon receiving the gift, you felt a surge of emotions, and hurriedly rushed to the blacksmith's shop, only to find her small figure gone. With the vast sky and distant waters, it's likely you'll never meet again in this lifetime. Yet, with this garment, our bond will forever remain.
Ye Yunshang came to visit you, but you didn't have the heart to respond.
You were feeling disoriented, lacking the energy to play with Ye Yunshang, so you sent her away, only to realize that Xiao Zhu had disappeared without notice.

Just as she was about to leave, Ye Yunshang accidentally barged into the Disciples' Quarters and collided head‑on with Xiao Zhu, causing her to fall back. Xiao Zhu hurriedly helped her up but found a bloodline streaming from the delicate Young Lady's nose. She was in utter panic.   Ye Yunshang smiled and leaned close to you, not hesitating to smear your clothes with her nasal blood. No matter how low‑spirited you might be, it would be hard for you to ignore such an outrageous act; immediately, you got tangled up with her. Xiao Zhu laughed helplessly, feeling extremely envious in her heart. She and Ye Yunshang were like two extremes‑Yunshang's straightforward and candid manner, her frail and lovable demeanor, made others envy her. On the other hand, she, as a woman yet incredibly strong, could not gain anyone's favor; with poor eyesight, looking at anyone would make them feel she had an evil gaze; obsessed with forging and ingenious Mechanisms, even with talent, she was envied and constantly criticized. Though she wasn't completely blind or deaf, the contemptuous and mocking faces of Kongtong people and their sarcastic laughter still pierced her deeply.  The days you spent studying at Tang Clan seemed like a dream to her. She cared about you, but unfortunately, you didn't care for her; those flattering words could be said to anyone. Xiao Zhu spoke almost in a whisper, as if she wasn't sure whether you had heard or not‑it was more for herself than for you. Now that Kongtong and Tang Clan have faced these matters, the order has summoned her, so even if she wanted to stay, she couldn't. Today's meeting with you is simply to say goodbye.

Xiao Zhu came to visit, bringing a bowl of bamboo shoot porridge, and told clumsy lies to keep you from knowing it was she who cooked it, fearing you might hate Kongtong and thus hate her too, or dislike the taste and leave her ashamed beyond measure. Seeing you so downcast, she felt pity, but being inarticulate, she didn't know how to comfort you. So she let you be alone, hoping that out of sight, out of mind.
They had agreed to meet again in the Jianghu, parted with a bow, and Long Xiang departed briskly.

Long Xiang gave a faint smile. She didn't want to come back to Shu anymore, but that didn't mean she didn't want to see you. Upon hearing you were going to visit her, she couldn't help but feel delighted, eagerly waiting for you to find her. When the time came, you would walk hand in hand with her to tour Dongting Lake. She knew your place had plenty of mountain delicacies but lacked seafood. At that time, she couldn't help but boast, making you realize how exceptional the pot dishes of Dongting's Xiang cuisine truly were.

She was heartbroken, unable to think of anything else, and only then did she forget that there was still you in Shu. Her heart felt warm, her expression gentle and smiling. She might still come to see you, though it's unclear how many years from now. You'll have to treat her as before with good wine, good meat, and good chicken legs. The two of you exchanged a glance and a smile, everything understood without words. This departure is as light as mist, a light promise made. Perhaps there will be no more meeting, yet entrust feelings to time, holding onto hope. After many years, when we meet again, we can still hold hands and reminisce, addressing each other as siblings.
Long Xiang was stunned upon hearing the words, then burst into laughter.
You said nothing to dissuade her, but suddenly startled her with your words: next time, it would be you who came to Jinxiang Palace to see her.

You hurried over, and Long Xiang, seeing you approach, smiled brightly and asked you to walk with her a little further. The two of you chatted idly along the way, each understanding the other without needing to speak of the Eldest Senior Brother. Halfway there, Long Xiang raised her hands in a bow and bid you farewell. Reluctant to part, you wished to see her further still, but she politely declined.
Long Xiang met you with just a greeting—no need to see her off—and so parted with a bow.

Long Xiang greeted you with just a nod, needing no farewell. As she was about to leave, she warned you not to do evil again. Should she catch you, she would be merciful the first time, but not the second. She said it with a smile, yet you shivered with fear. You knew she was not joking, and there was no room for negotiation.

Fourth Senior Brother sought you out to tell you that Long Xiang was leaving and had come to bid farewell. Within the Tang Clan she knew no one besides the Eldest Senior Brother and you, so naturally it fell to you to see her off.

You said yes with your mouth, but did not mean it in your heart—only a careless lie to brush him off. Fu Yun read your face and knew you were merely humoring him; he sighed inwardly. He had already given what counsel he could—good deeds bring good returns, evil deeds bring evil ones—and could only hope you would look after yourself. He pressed his palms together, bowed once, and departed.

Though you cared for loyalty and sentiment, you were simply too wicked at heart, and so refused. Fu Yun let out a long sigh, thinking that the evil in your heart had its roots—your six senses unclean, stained by the dust of the world; so long as the world remained unclean, you would answer it in kind. This could not be laid wholly at your feet; only the teachings of the Buddha, in time, might yet temper you. He pressed his palms together, bowed once, and departed.

Though you are wicked, you hold fast to loyalty and sentiment, and agreed at once. Fu Yun's face broke into a smile; he uttered "Excellent," pressed his palms together in a single bow, and took his leave.

Before he left, he couldn't help but add one more word—not reasoning with you this time, but appealing to your heart, hoping you'd remember the hardships you'd shared and endeavor to leave others a little room in your future dealings, to do evil no more, lest the day come when your sins overflow their measure.

You hurried to see Fu Yun, who was pleased to see that you were unharmed. After a brief conversation to ease your mind, Fu Yun bid you farewell. After all, those alive still have duties in the world to attend to; they cannot allow Jianghu disputes to harm the state and its people. Time is of the essence, for he must join his fellow brothers to tour various sects and persuade them to unite against the Demon Cult.

Fourth Senior Brother has come to inform you that Fu Yun the monk has regained consciousness. Upon hearing this, you finally put down the heavy stone on your heart. Fortunately, this young monk has been protected by heaven and survived the incident. Otherwise, it would be a great pity, and the Tang Clan would be in an even more dire situation, as even jumping into the Yellow River wouldn't wash away the stain.

You are also a close friend of Master Fu Yun; though you could not save him, you at least wished to see him off. You dared not get too close, only murmuring prayers from afar. Watching as the fierce flames consumed his withered body, Master Fu Yun relinquished this physical form, ascending to the Western Paradise, while you remained in the mortal world suffering, tormented by fear and distress, unable to attain liberation.

Fourth Senior Brother came to inform you that Fu Yun has passed away. He endured many days of suffering, but ultimately couldn't withstand the torment of the poison; even the Panacea Pill couldn't save his life. The Songshan disciples arrived, saw their junior brother's tragic death, which occurred on Tang Clan territory and resulted from poisoning. How could they not suspect the Tang Clan? The Songshan monks concluded that the Tang Clan had killed Fu Yun, took his body out of the mountain gate, and burned it in a secluded place after chanting scriptures.

Fourth Senior Brother, down below, caught sight of you and felt a sudden jolt of alarm—others climbing up wouldn't have troubled him, but seeing you at such a height set his heart racing, and he hurriedly called you down. You didn't use Qinggong, but climbed down the stairs like anyone else.
Only when the responsibility truly settled on your shoulders did you understand that carrying the weight of others' expectations was no easy freedom.

Your silhouette under the sunset cast a dark shadow, and the junior martial sister naturally felt a flicker of timidity, timidly grasping your sleeve. She feared you might fall or vanish entirely. You let her hold on, watching her grow from childhood. You admired her increasing martial arts while pitying her enduring vulnerability. She most feared loneliness. Love without bounds filled your heart, even though you knew you were unworthy of a lifelong partnership. Yet you wished to volunteer to protect her, declaring you would never leave her side, staying by her until she found her own home and no longer needed you. Then you would solemnly bid farewell, folding memories into your heart, tears streaming down as you left. She didn't understand your realization, didn't consider the underlying meanings, only listening earnestly. Her anxious heart finally calmed, for she relied on you more than you knew.
Junior Martial Sister seemed to sense it too, and climbing to the rooftop, found you there. She said nothing, only came to your side and stayed quietly beside you.

You paid no mind to having lost all your Internal Force, your hands and feet clumsier now than a farmhand who'd never learned martial arts—one careless step could send you tumbling headfirst from the tower. You just wanted to see the view of the Tang family compound.
You gave no thought to the dizzy spells that might send you pitching headfirst from the tower—you only wanted to see the view of the Tang family compound.
You climbed alone to the top of Zhengxin Tower and gazed into the distance.

Parting by life or death — all of it is impermanence.
Knowing you had lost your elder brother, she grieved for you without end, yet Yunshang herself was also fading by degrees, no longer quite herself. Ordinarily so quick of tongue, today she could only choke on her words, unable to speak.
All she could do was weep silently at your side.

The sky had cleared everywhere but over the Tang Clan, where dark clouds still hung heavy. Scattered raindrops fell, dampening sleeves, as though the whole world had been washed by rain and left cold and desolate.
Life was like duckweed, drifting together and apart with no design — who could say tomorrow would be the same?

Long Xiang clenched her lips tightly, trying to escape as quickly as possible before the tears fell. But you pulled her sleeve, and even a light tug couldn't free her. That was all her strength‑unable to shake you loose, she could no longer take another step. This Heroine, for once, let you see her helpless and vulnerable side.

Long Xiang pressed her lips tight, trying to flee the truth before her, racing to escape before the tears could fall.
A thousand thoughts choked in your throat, you could not speak them, could not hold her back — she slipped gently from your grasp, and your heart shattered to pieces along with her tears.

Long Xiang clenched her lips, trying to escape the reality before her, fleeing at full speed before the tears could fall. But who can escape the pursuit of memories in the end? Sorrow follows like a shadow, compelling tears to fall like rain.

The Junior Martial Sister stared at Eldest Senior Brother's tombstone, dazed and lost. She had been parted from her mother since childhood, and now her father lay bedridden, with no knowing how many days he had left. The two senior brothers she had looked to as elder brothers had also, one after another, left her. The Tang Clan was still the Tang Clan, only the people had changed. Before she knew it, the quiet, ordinary years of mountain life had drifted away from her, and living had become one long nightmare — no matter how she struggled or denied it, she could not wake from it. So much suffering, so much helplessness. She crept a little closer to you without a sound, afraid that if she so much as blinked, you too might vanish.

For a long while you could not believe it, wishing again and again that it was only a nightmare, that when you woke once more, Eldest Senior Brother would pop up grinning as always — he was the Tang Clan's Eldest Senior Brother, after all, and should always be effortless and unstoppable.
You could not tell how much of this waking dream was real, or where the illusion had begun.
Perhaps it had all been illusion from the start.
Your martial siblings buried Eldest Senior Brother on the mountain behind the sect, beside the Tang Clan's fallen heroes. The tombstone read: 'Here lies Tang Buyi, the Flying Hero.'
Even the Junior Martial Sister's small hand, patting you again and again, could not dispel the sorrow.

When you woke up, you had already returned to the Tang Clan. Third Senior Brother, Fourth Senior Brother, and Junior Martial Sister saw you awake and all showed happy expressions. However, when they asked about Eldest Senior Brother, their expressions turned to sorrow.

You filled the cup and drained it in one draught—there was nothing so satisfying. Though the two of you had been wandering far from home, your hearts had already returned. The fear of death faded slowly; the sky in the distance had turned a deep black, and neither of you needed to say it—you both knew the moment of parting had come. Eldest Senior Brother pointed at the leaden clouds pressing down ahead, telling you dawn was near. If you would not flee, then you should stand and fight. The world said the Tang Clan's talents had withered away, but you were still here. His part in the play was done; he would step down and watch from the wings, cheering you on. The next act was yours to lead. Your time was now.

You answered: it was Mongol kumis, carried in a leather pouch—it had both the taste of milk and the mellow warmth of wine, the flavor of the desert and the steppe. Eldest Senior Brother was taken aback; even he had never tasted this wine, and pressed you with questions. You recalled the desert scenery from that time, and smiled, lost in memory.

You couldn't answer, so Eldest Senior Brother decided for you. You drank Lamb Wine brewed by the government‑run wine shop in Lin'an Prefecture. This wine was quite expensive; ordinary households might not even get to taste a single pot in a whole year. Though you had never tasted it before and didn't know its flavor, you weren't after the wine's aroma at the moment.

You answered: it was the monkey wine he'd secretly stashed away. Eldest Senior Brother didn't hold back, and pointed you to where it was—three zhang up the cliff face, tucked in a hollow shielded from wind and rain. You seemed to summon true Qinggong, and retrieved it without mishap.

Eldest Senior Brother used the last of his strength to slap you again and again, refusing to let you drift off to sleep. You didn't know whether to laugh or cry—the man was dying and still causing trouble; you had no idea what debt from a past life had earned you such treatment in this one. Both of you were badly hurt, and every breath was agony, yet even with death closing in, he still had to crack a few crude jokes to feel like himself. Those who arrived in this world crying ought, at the very least, to leave it laughing. As your breath grew shallow and you began to fade, Eldest Senior Brother finally let you close your eyes, saying he would pass on his Mental Formula—telling you to picture the Tang Clan's back mountain before dawn, the two of you brothers drinking in the cool night wind, just like old times. In your final moments, that imagined scene felt clearer than reality itself, as though you had truly come home. He asked you: what wine was it you were drinking?

Struck down by the Blazing Sun Hammer, you fell into a swoon and dreamed a long dream.
In the dream, Zhao Huo was the most favored of all his brothers and sisters, cherished above the rest by his father and mother.
When he went to the Tang Clan to become a disciple, he was given an exceptional promotion, made an inner disciple early on, and took the Tang surname.
The Sect Leader, his Master's wife, and his Junior Martial Sister all held Zhao Huo in special regard. The Tang Clan faced no trouble from within or without, unstoppable in every battle, its branches and offshoots spread across the Central Plains—the greatest sect in the Jianghu.
Zhao Huo's fortune ran deep and never failed him; even when he lost his way, he would stumble into some hidden paradise. He won the favor of reclusive masters who freely passed on eighty years of cultivation, and his gift for the martial arts was beyond compare—he had only to glance at any manual to master it at once. Even without hard training, wandering idly from place to place, his skill grew stronger by the day. To Zhao Huo, those who trained hard and diligently looked as laughable as monkeys, needing a lesson now and then just to show off how mighty Zhao Huo's own skill truly was.
In the dream, Zhao Huo stole the show at the Wulin Assembly, his fame eclipsing Eldest Senior Brother's; every hero of the Jianghu revered him, every heroine adored him.
He had four radiant wives: the Tang Clan's own Junior Martial Sister, Diancang's Pearl Ye Yunshang, and Jinxiang Palace's Long Xiang. Even the Shangguan Family, hearing of Zhao Huo's fame, longed to push their daughter Shangguan Ying into his bedchamber, willing to offend the Nangong Family over it.
On the Jiangling battlefield, Zhao Huo single-handedly took on ten thousand beggars. With a divine palm honed over three thousand years, he smashed the Mud Cult's Dharma King Wang Erzhuang to dust, damning him never to be reborn—blasting him so thoroughly that even in his next life he'd have to be a beggar again. The force of the blow carried for hundreds of miles, rocking Six Paths Gorge, where countless unseen Demon Cult vermin were blown to ash.
Zhao Huo was hailed as the Wulin Alliance Leader; the Kongtong Four Maidens vied to flatter him. Even the reigning Emperor dared not lift his eyes past Zhao Huo's toes, meekly abdicating the throne to him.
Zhao Huo possessed everything—wealth, fame, beauty, martial power, authority, the realm itself—yet felt hollow, at a loss for what to do next. Should he ascend to the heavens, storm the Celestial Palace, and knock the Jade Emperor off his own throne?
At the end of boundless desire lay nothing but emptiness.
The Eldest Senior Brother who abruptly appeared wasn't looking for this Wulin Alliance Leader, this Emperor of Great Song—he was looking for you.
Seeing him, shame and self-loathing welled up in Zhao Huo, and he wanted to shut Eldest Senior Brother out of the dream. But Eldest Senior Brother wasn't blasted to nothing like everyone else—he simply stepped up and slapped him, snapping 'shut your mouth, you wretch'—and your inner demon dissolved into nothing.
You looked up to Eldest Senior Brother, and he never once looked down on you. He dragged you into mischief, teased you, sometimes got you into trouble or dragged you down with him—but he respected you and stood behind you all the same.
That was because he truly counted you as a friend.
Only today, with your knot of years finally untied, did you understand—you could shed the shadow others had cast over you, and live as yourself.

Seeing the great enemy gone, Fu Yun could hold on no longer and collapsed. He had stayed wary of the enemy the whole time and never spent his energy fighting the poison—but after that one strike, he was truly a guttering lamp, its oil spent, not far from death. You lay unconscious, while Eldest Senior Brother felt his True Qi scattered, all but gone, no longer able to hold back the poison consuming him from within—this time, he feared, there would be no coming back.

Long Xiang channeled her energy to purge the poison in the middle of the fight, already a reckless and bold move given her agitation. When the moment came that she could no longer hold back, she couldn't even spare the effort to properly close her circulation—a grave breach of internal-arts discipline—and she suffered an Internal Injury, giving the lingering poison the chance to invade her organs. Seeing the great enemy gone, her guard dropped, and she could hold on no longer, slipping at once into unconsciousness. You lay unconscious, while Eldest Senior Brother felt his True Qi scattered, all but gone, no longer able to hold back the poison consuming him from within—this time, he feared, there would be no coming back.

Before leaving, he did not forget to bring along Xiaomei. Her power had been nullified, and she could no longer be used as a killer. Thus, she was discarded by her master. However, even though Xiaomei's abilities were gone, she remained the direct disciple of the Flying Heaven Gate of Kongtong Mountain, with significant potential for exploitation. Never mind her beauty; in the future, when he took control of the Kongtong Sect, marrying this Little Miss into his household could be a pleasant affair.

Shentu Long turned to leave, but the Venerable Golden Crow suddenly sprang back to life and leapt out, and the crowd paled in shock. Little did they know this man had once borne the underworld name Nine-Lives Leopard—legend held that he had glimpsed the path of the Nine Turns Reincarnation Grand Technique; though unable to be reborn, he possessed nine lives, was a master of feigning death, and had escaped his end countless times. Unwilling to simply let them go, he tried hard to convince Shentu Long to finish them off and leave no future trouble, but Shentu Long paid him no mind, clasping his hands behind his back as he walked away—by his own words, he didn't regard you as worth noticing at all; the true enemy lay far off, in the lands where Song and Jin were at war. Hearing this, the Venerable Golden Crow trembled all over and couldn't help but grin, unable any longer to deny it: that fearless king who once ruled over Western Xia had truly returned. Next to 'that man,' you younglings meant nothing at all—the Flying Hero's death alone would be enough. And with that, he happily accepted the order and departed with his master.

In a moment of crisis, Fu Yun threw himself into the fray, using all his strength to unleash the Prajna Palm. Its power was enough to shatter stone and split boulders, yet it was still difficult to withstand. Little did he know that Shentu Long merely waved his dust whisk, and Fu Yun's palm energy instantly dissipated into nothingness. He was then struck by a tremendous force, staggering back several steps before barely managing to regain his footing.   Shentu Long, a master from Qingcheng, had long been reclusive, and Fu Yun had heard of him before. However, he never expected to encounter such a young and extraordinary master in the world, leaving him utterly astonished. The Songshan Sect had once been the leader among the six sects, but after sacrificing themselves to resist the Supreme Bliss Cult, the experts of his elders had suffered heavy casualties, many perishing in their devotion. It was said that they remained steadfast in their beliefs even in death, sitting together to chant Buddhist scriptures, a display of such compassion and solemnity.  Though Fu Yun could not receive teachings from his elders, he firmly believed that no matter how evil or powerful the foe before him, capable of destroying his physical form, it could not shake his faith. He stood his ground, resolute and unyielding.   Western Xia revered Buddhism, and the roots of the Supreme Bliss Cult were also tied to Tibetan Esoteric Buddhism. However, later generations twisted and fabricated its teachings for their own desires, distorting its true nature. Witnessing the unwavering determination of the monk from the Central Lands, how could a practitioner of Zen not be moved? Shentu Long was no exception; he recalled the massacre of the monks from Songshan. While he could extinguish their physical bodies, he could not diminish their noble souls. The chivalrous warriors of the Central Plains were inspired by them, uniting in their righteous cause to eradicate evil, ultimately leading to the collapse of the Supreme Bliss Cult's ambitions to dominate the Central Plains.  Clearly, he could raise his hand and kill everyone present, yet he hesitated before Fu Yun's righteous aura and chose not to strike. After all, even without intervening, the younger generation would not be far from death.

In a critical moment, Long Xiang held the sword and stepped forth. The long sword's dust whisk struck with a tremor that sent him stumbling back several steps to dissipate the residual force. Since he had mastered his arts and roamed the Jianghu, Long Xiang had never met an opponent. Even when Senior Brother was at full strength, they were merely evenly matched. Yet this young Daoist master, with one wave of his dust whisk, had almost caused her half her body to go numb, nearly dropping her sword. Such a formidable Internal Skill required at least six decades of hard work before it might be achieved, and even Lady Wen was slightly outmatched. Among all her enemies, only the late Gang Leader Wang could match him in battle, but she did not know where such a young peerless master had come from, leaving her feeling shaken.  Long Xiang did not recognize Shentu Long, yet the latter instantly recognized this unknown comrade of his father's. After all, it was well‑known that his father, Long Yuan, was the previous Wulin Alliance Leader. Twenty years ago, in a battle against the Supreme Bliss Cult Leader, their might and prowess were unmatched; they fought to a standstill until the Heavenly Withering Sword could not overcome the Ghost Lotus King's ruthless killing, resulting in its breaking from the grief of his victims. Shentu Long felt an infinite longing for his father when mentioning him.  Now that Long Yuan had been reborn, with his archenemy no longer alive, it was even more saddening. Although Long Xiang's remaining poison had not fully subsided and she could only draw her sword out of necessity to protect herself, if they truly engaged in battle, the poison would flow into her heart meridian, making recovery impossible. The loss of such a beauty was regrettable, especially since she was the offspring of his old enemy.  After some thought, Shentu Long impulsively decided to nurture this foe for future trouble. He hoped that Long Xiang could follow in her father's footsteps, reaching new heights. In the future, they would settle their battle and reclaim the humiliation from their past defeat. Of course, Long Xiang needed to survive this poison's torment first.

He claimed his old, decaying body was beyond saving, and that by means of one of the Supreme Bliss Cult's Three Treasures, the Nine Turns Reincarnation Grand Technique, his soul had slipped free of its shell, seized another's flesh, and been reborn anew. Such a claim was too outlandish to believe—who would dare trust it? And yet, if he were merely spinning tales, how else could one explain this world-shaking Internal Skill and bearing?

Shentu Long no longer wore the ethereal, ascetic air of old; his face now showed only savage cruelty. He forced Xiaomei to reveal his true identity—he was no reclusive Daoist dwelling apart from the world, at peace with all things. In truth, his true self was none other than the former Supreme Bliss Cult Leader who had once ravaged the Central Plains, the Master of the legendary assassin organization Thousand Lantern Tower, and even the biological father of today's Emperor of Western Xia.

Shentu Long no longer wore the air of a Daoist of old; his face now showed only savage cruelty. By his own account, he was no hermit dwelling apart from the world, at peace with all things—his true self was none other than the former Supreme Bliss Cult Leader who had once ravaged the Central Plains, the Master of the legendary assassin organization Thousand Lantern Tower, and even the biological father of the present Emperor of Western Xia.

You knelt on the ground, gravely wounded, still unable to believe that the man before you who had struck you down was truly Daoist Shentu of the Qingcheng sect. Had that old air of quiet detachment and indifference to fame and fortune been nothing but a mask all along?

Eldest Senior Brother was usually carefree and unrestrained by nature, but in truth his mind was as fine as dust. He had stayed wary the whole way, sensing something was off without ever spotting the trap—never knowing his enemies had laid ambush within ambush, one ring inside another. First they goaded old rivals into blocking his path and picking a fight, to draw his attention away; then, through the hand of a blacksmith from the Fire Mountain Sword Pavilion, they stripped him of his allies. Not only did they dare to set an ambush and attempt murder near the Tang Clan's very own territory, they had also bribed a spy to lace Eldest Senior Brother's tea with the Mud Cult's antidote. Harmless to ordinary people, this drug was gravely harmful to Tang Clan disciples, who cultivate their energy through poison—had it not scattered his cultivation and left him unable to hold his True Qi, how else could Shentu Long have drained his Internal Force so easily? Even now, thinking back on it, Eldest Senior Brother could not help but shudder; the depths of malice his enemy had gone to in order to destroy him were beyond anything he had ever heard of.

Eldest Senior Brother fought on, willing to shatter his own dantian to retaliate, sweeping out a meteor-like strike to slash through the darkness and drive the enemy back. Unfortunately, his Internal Force had been reduced to a mere tenth, making it impossible to unleash his Ultimate technique to full effect—the feathers swept across the enemy's body as gently as a breeze, cutting only a few shallow, thin wounds. Shentu Long had never imagined Eldest Senior Brother capable of such a desperate counterattack, and his guard rose in alarm—but Eldest Senior Brother was already spent, a Guttering Lamp; his last, desperate strike failed to bring victory. Shentu Long struck you and your Senior Brother down with a single palm each, leaving you both spitting blood and powerless to resist.

You again recalled the words Zhao Kui, the Dharma King of Hell's Path, had once spoken. He seemed to have foreseen this very day, and broke his own rule to teach you the Great Scorching Heat Divine Skill he had created. You gritted your teeth and did as he had instructed—since you couldn't hold onto it anyway, you poured your entire reserve of Internal Force into this thief who was stealing it, to see whether he could stomach it. Shentu Long had already sensed a searing heat buried deep within your Internal Force, growing hotter the closer it reached its source, and was straining to contain it—when suddenly you stopped resisting and instead forced it out of you. The Great Scorching Heat Divine Skill was born in Zhao Kui's youth, when he stood for the righteous Wulin in its decisive battle against the Supreme Bliss Cult and was defeated by the demonic arts of their Left Guardian; out of that bitter regret he forged this technique in the fire of his own remorse. Now, at last, it was repaid to that enemy through your hand. The searing force sent Shentu Long flying backward. The moment Eldest Senior Brother was free, he fought on though it meant shattering his own dantian, unleashing the Flying Swallow Meteor Feather—but with his Internal Force all but gone, he could not drive the technique to its full power, and the feathers only brushed the enemy like a passing breeze, cutting a few shallow, thin wounds. Shentu Long's own Internal Breath felt set ablaze, wrapped in flame he could not dispel, and he could only force it into his body and absorb it. It was not fatal, but it threw his balance of Yin and Yang into disarray, leaving him gravely injured within. He had feared your Eldest Senior Brother greatly, yet thought nothing of you at all, seeing you merely as a convenient bonus, not without its use—never expecting that by strange chance he would nearly meet his end at your hands. But your mastery was still too shallow, and the gap in power between you and Shentu Long too wide; even fighting alongside Eldest Senior Brother to the last, you could not overcome him. Shentu Long struck you down with a single palm, and you spat fresh blood, left with no strength to resist.

You once again recalled Wei Ju's words—always so gentle and refined, yet never once untrue. Your Internal Force was all but spent, yet the more desperate your plight, the clearer your mind grew. Shentu Long felt a flicker of surprise, as if all he had drawn in was dross; he sensed, faint as a heartbeat, a tremor along your meridians, like a plucked string—and was suddenly seized with alarm: was this not the very reason he had long plotted to destroy the Kongtong Sect? The Iron Pipa Skill was the natural bane of the Heaven-Swallowing Treasure Mirror. The instant that string trembled, every meridian rang in answer. The alien True Qi Shentu Long had drawn in was not yet fused into one, and the shock of the Iron Pipa Skill sent it careening out of control, tearing wildly through his body and hurling him backward. The moment Eldest Senior Brother was free, he fought on though it meant shattering his own dantian, unleashing the Flying Swallow Meteor Feather—but with his Internal Force all but gone, he could not drive the technique to its full power, and the feathers only brushed the enemy like a passing breeze, cutting a few shallow, thin wounds. Shentu Long forced his energy to suppress the injury, feigning composure, though in truth he was drenched in cold sweat. He had feared your Eldest Senior Brother greatly, yet thought nothing of you at all, seeing you merely as a convenient bonus, not without its use—never expecting that by strange chance he would nearly meet his end at your hands. But your skill was still too shallow, and the gap in strength too wide; even fighting alongside Eldest Senior Brother to the last, you could not overcome him. Shentu Long struck you down with a single palm, and you spat blood, left with no strength to resist.

You were born neither a prodigy nor blessed by heaven with any extraordinary gift. Everything you have achieved in martial arts today comes from your own refusal to give up, from practicing morning and night until you had something to show for it—not much, not mighty, but yours to treasure all the same. Just because fate never favored you, must you be forbidden to dream, forced to accept your lot? Does hard, bitter practice not deserve to succeed—do you deserve to be preyed upon and trampled? This world should not be like this. Yet your deafening, silent roar is heard by no one but yourself.

You thought of your master. She was unrelenting when training you, nor was she reluctant to show affection. She was both strict and gentle towards you, genuinely hoping you would become talented, possibly the most biased person in the world towards you.
You recalled the time you spent honing your skills with Nangong Qian—clumsy yet fulfilling, brimming with vigor.
You recalled the moment in Zhengxin Hall when you mustered the courage to request to study abroad, the Sect Leader's surprised yet relieved gentle smile, and his gaze that subtly conveyed approval.

You recalled the day of the mid‑term exam, when you openly and honorably defeated the Senior Brother in the training grounds, the crowd's astonished gazes, and from then on, they regarded you with newfound respect.
You recalled the night on the back mountain when a masked senior gave you guidance, and felt grateful you hadn't given up.

In your mind, memories of the past suddenly surfaced, like a fleeting glance, vanishing in an instant. Living as an outsider among the Tang Clan's disciples for years, you've often felt resentment. Those who bullied you never ceased, advising you not to dream, to be honest and diligent in your daily work. Did the Tang Clan elders not clearly show their stance by refusing to take you in? You didn't give up despite the humiliation and hardships. You are not special; you are just one of countless ordinary people striving in the world. Can mediocre talent and ordinary potential not make a difference? Can being 'ordinary' justify being bullied, mocked, and robbed?

The Heaven-Swallowing Treasure Mirror was incredibly domineering; unless one's internal skill was exceptionally profound, surpassing that of the practitioner, it was nearly impossible to resist. The Tang Clan's martial arts relied on technique rather than Internal Skill, making it futile to struggle against the artifact. Now, held captive by the enemy, they could not even lift a small sword. Sweat dripped from their brows, yet they could not utter a word of complaint. Shentu Long, however, remained composed and carefree, taunting them with cold mockery. He scornfully remarked that a common person like them should be a sheep in the crowd, unable to see their faces, destined to be slaughtered. All their power, effort, and dreams were not theirs to claim. The world was meant to be a battlefield for the Chosen One, and to challenge him, they were utterly unworthy.
You stared intently at the person in front of you, unable to believe that Daoist Shentu from the Qingcheng sect would actually use such wicked magic to harm someone.

You and your Senior Brother were in the middle of conversation when suddenly the scene shifted, and a figure abruptly appeared between the two of you. With your and your Senior Brother's experience and internal skill, it had never been possible for anyone to approach so closely without being noticed. The intruder's ability to suppress the sound of his robe with Internal Skill was remarkable; if he hadn't practiced the Heaven and Earth Silent Power of your Junior Martial Sister, it would mean his Internal Skill had reached an unimaginably high Realm. Before you and your Senior Brother could react, his pulse points were seized, and an overwhelming pressure like a collapsing sky descended upon you. Under his Internal Skill, your control over Internal Force was stripped away, and your Internal Force flowed out continuously. Your Senior Brother's face turned pale with horror, recognizing this sinister technique as the unparalleled Taotie True Scripture and Heaven-Swallowing Treasure Mirror, the lost and feared arts once eradicated by the former Left Guardian of Supreme Bliss.

As they were speaking, the intense pain from the Blazing Sun Hammer struck again, instantly causing the world to spin and the ground to feel as if it were pulling them down. It was more painful than death, making it impossible to balance. Attempting to stand firm, they instead lost their footing, their foot slipping and their head slamming against the ground. With a loud thud, they collapsed into unconsciousness. Eldest Senior Brother, witnessing their dire condition, couldn't help but bitterly smile. He had no idea how to counter the Blazing Sun Hammer. Suddenly, he sensed an unusual sound behind him. The intruder made no attempt to hide their presence, their breathing steady and deep, revealing an immense mastery of internal skill. Without hesitation, Eldest Senior Brother turned around and launched the Coin Darts, only for them to be swept away by the fly whisk and embedded in the tree. The intruder caught them effortlessly, and Eldest Senior Brother immediately sensed something was wrong. He was swiftly overwhelmed by Shentu Long's internal skill, his Internal Force being drained continuously. Eldest Senior Brother's face paled in horror. He was all too aware of this sinister technique, a skill unparalleled in the world, identical to the one used by the former villain, the Left Guardian of the Supreme Bliss Cult. It was undoubtedly the long‑lost, terrifying Taotie Zhen Jing, the Heaven-Swallowing Treasure Mirror.

The Eldest Senior Brother had long seen through your feelings for Xiaomei. Even though deep down he thought the odds were slim, what if — by some million-to-one chance — she really became your wife? So during their sparring he was especially careful with his restraint, afraid that if he hurt her badly enough to make her cry out, you would hear it and fly into a rage, turning against him mid-battle. Hearing this, you laughed. Turning traitor to gang up on the Eldest Senior Brother alongside Xiaomei — that you would never do. What was the point of winning, if not fair and square? Xiaomei's acupoints were sealed, her limbs unable to move, but her ears and eyes were still keen. Hearing your words, she flushed crimson like a plum blossom blooming in the snow, her heart pounding rapidly.

She thought you, this scoundrel, meant to torture her — forcing the Eldest Senior Brother, who had already fought two battles, to duel you a third time out of desperation. Little did she guess your wicked scheme wasn't satisfied with mere torture: you meant to seize her while she couldn't move and make her your wife, tormenting her for a lifetime. Hearing this, Xiaomei under the tree flushed crimson like a plum blossom blooming in the snow, her heart pounding rapidly.
You asked about Xiaomei, and the Eldest Senior Brother only said he had struck her down and laid her under a tree.

As for the Lady Thief, her fierce assault failed, and reckoning she was no match for you one-on-one, she didn't linger to fight — feinting a few strikes before abandoning her companion and fleeing. Her Qinggong was extraordinary; the Eldest Senior Brother could have given chase, but how could he dare? He had no choice but to let her go.

Jinwu Shangren's Blazing Sun Hammer has a long history; it is not a righteous martial arts technique but a sinister method from the Supreme Bliss Cult, known as the Soul-Stealing Pestle. This technique can inject toxic Internal Force into the body, targeting the brain, and causing damage to the mind. One strike darkens the mind, two strikes disperse the spirit, three strikes dissipate the soul. Once the three strikes land, regardless of whether one is a loyal subject, filial son, or chaste woman, they will all become obedient fools. He was about to strike you twice when his senior brother secretly attacked from behind, delivering a subtle strike into his skull, shaking his brain. He mistakenly believed the senior brother's words, thinking he had been poisoned, and chased after the senior brother to seize the antidote, only to faint from the commotion.

Jinwu Shangren was thick‑skinned and tough, both in body and spirit, harder to contend with than Shi Gongyuan. Ordinary hidden weapons could not harm him. Though the Eldest Senior Brother had an ultimate technique to defeat him, he hesitated, fearing excessive exertion might create an opportunity for the other party. Thus, the ultimate technique remained unlaunched. Upon your arrival, the weight on his heart finally lifted. He did not need you to intervene; the Eldest Senior Brother plucked a feather, transforming it into a meteor, and slashed with swift, intersecting strikes. Jinwu Shangren, even in death, still did not believe there existed such a fierce hidden weapon in the world.

Xiaomei thrust her blade into your chest, knowing exactly how to ensure a fatal blow. She was not skilled in showing mercy, and fearing she might truly harm your life, she knocked you unconscious and whispered a farewell.   Then, she used her Qinggong to intervene in the battle between the Eldest Senior Brother and Jinwu Shangren, but her target was not the Eldest Senior Brother; it was an accomplice. The Eldest Senior Brother vaguely sensed that Xiaomei was being coerced and that her betrayal of the Tang Clan was not voluntary. He decisively joined forces with Xiaomei, coordinating with her agility and techniques, creating new moves on the spot to cut off all escape routes for Jinwu Shangren. The battle quickly turned in their favor, with flashes of blades and swords, and Jinwu Shangren fell dead.  Just as they breathed a sigh of relief, before they could ask any questions, a figure suddenly intruded between them. With Xiaomei and the Eldest Senior Brother's experience and Internal Skill, they had never allowed anyone to approach them so closely without noticing. The newcomer could suppress the sound of their robes with their Internal Skill. If they had not also practiced the Junior Martial Sister's Heaven and Earth Silent Force, it indicated that their Internal Skill had reached an astonishing Realm.  Before the two could react, they were seized at their acupoints, and an overwhelming pressure descended upon them, stripping them of their Internal Force control as their power flowed out uncontrollably. The Eldest Senior Brother's expression changed in shock; this kind of sinister technique was unparalleled in the world, reminiscent of the infamous Left Guardian of Supreme Bliss who had been executed years ago. It was undoubtedly the long‑lost and terrifying Taotie True Scripture, the Swallowing Heaven Treasure Mirror.  As it drained their Internal Force, Shentu Long let out a loud shout, forcing the Eldest Senior Brother and Xiaomei back.
You brought out all your skills to drive back the Lady Thief, then joined the pincer attack on Venerable Golden Crow.

Xiaomei was unlike before, every move a killing move, as fast as ever, yet ruthlessly savage. Even so, she was still no match for you. In the final moments of the fierce battle, you struck her with a finger to the acupoints, subduing her. Xiaomei showed no fear, instead urging you to flee quickly. You had a thousand words to ask for clarity, but the Eldest Senior Brother was still locked in fierce combat. The full story would have to wait until the dust settled before you could ask.
You and Xiaomei fought as you retreated, slipping into the woods.
Outmatched in skill, you were struck a grievous blow to the head by Venerable Golden Crow's signature weapon, the Blazing Sun Hammer.

You subdued your enemy and were about to go help the Eldest Senior Brother when a sudden chill ran through you; without thinking, you dashed forward, narrowly dodging Venerable Golden Crow's ambush after his feigned death. He was utterly astonished, never expecting such alertness from an unremarkable underling like you. This time you showed no mercy — a stroke of your small sword ended his life.

Although you were technically superior, your lack of Jianghu experience meant you hadn't prepared for this. You hadn't anticipated that this person seemed invincible, seemingly mortally wounded yet suddenly launching an attack. You were caught off guard, and he used his secret technique, Blazing Sun Hammer, to strike you, severely injuring your head.

Although your skill surpassed his, you never underestimated him, even considering whipping his corpse once you saw through Venerable Golden Crow's trick of feigning death. Yet you never imagined this man seemed truly undying — struck down twice, he rose again both times. In the end, you fell for his ruse, ambushed by his signature technique, the Blazing Sun Hammer, and struck a grievous blow to the head.
Your opponent is Venerable Golden Crow, the renowned master of the Kongtong Sect.

Although you have never once seen her true face, ever since your meeting in Jiangling the two of you have clung to each other like fated rivals — she has wanted you dead for longer than a few days now, and yet you can recognize her even masked.
Your opponent is that graceful Lady Thief.

You face Xiaomei, with no fighting spirit left, yet you can't just wait to be slaughtered. Xiaomei puts away her usual bright smile, and the small sword and short dagger clash. Former close friends, today's enemies, the deadly battle is about to erupt.

You face Xiaomei with no fighting spirit left, hoping desperately that all this had been mere playacting on her part — you would rather die than raise a blade against her. But Xiaomei will not relent.

Faced with a traitor, you are consumed with fury. Xiaomei, too, sets aside her usual bright smile. Small sword and short blade cross — old confidants now today's enemies, a deadly duel about to erupt.
Your opponent is Xiaomei.

Over there, Eldest Senior Brother was locked in a fierce battle with two assassins, each move a split‑second decision. Both were skilled fighters, and their styles complemented each other perfectly‑one calm and one dynamic, one light and one heavy, forming a seamless partnership. Even in his prime, Eldest Senior Brother found it difficult to hold his ground, let alone considering he had been secretly poisoned. The tea he had just drunk had been laced with the Mud Cult's Five‑Colored Mud, a potent toxin. Though harmless to ordinary people, it was extremely dangerous to members of the Tang Clan who practiced poison cultivation, as it worked similarly to the Tang Clan's Panacea Oil. Eldest Senior Brother's expression darkened with concern, realizing he had fallen into a trap. Fortunately, your return to his side allowed the two of them to stand together and resist.
Thinking that even if you couldn't win, you ought at least to help pin down the enemy for Eldest Senior Brother.

Fu Yun was extremely cautious. Though he appeared to sit cross-legged with his eyes half closed, circulating his energy, in truth he was gritting through excruciating pain, fully on guard against any sneak attack, and simply letting the elixir take its course. Ordinarily this would have been perilous, but fortunately this pill was distilled from the very dregs of the Tang Clan's Panacea Oil vat, its potency rich, enduring, and mild — worthy of being called the king of pills for men — so that even without circulating energy to absorb it, its effect came on with remarkable speed. After all, the Wanling Pill was itself a kind of poison, one that could kill every manner of evil lurking within the organs. Fierce as the Fire Scorpion King's Poison was, the poisoner, needing to hide it within another's body, had been forced to blunt its potency with a compound formula, so the deadly poison could not claim a life outright — and against the Wanling Pill, it stood no chance at all, and could only be hunted down and destroyed. Seeing the Wanling Pill take effect, Fu Yun let out a breath of relief and turned to rejoin the fray.
Thinking that even if you couldn't win, you ought at least to help pin down the enemy for Eldest Senior Brother.

Although Long Xiang had been poisoned, her mastery of Internal Skill was profound — she was among the finest of the younger generation of heroes — and Eldest Senior Brother's aid had come in time, bringing the poison under control. Long Xiang swiftly completed a minor circulation to speed her blood, then urged you to hurry and support Eldest Senior Brother. Seeing the Wanling Pill take effect, you too let out a breath of relief and turned to join the fray.

Eldest Senior Brother entrusted you to detoxify someone, leaving the enemy for him to deal with alone. Another graceful masked female thief has now joined Venerable Golden Crow's side to help him, making it two against one.

You were entrusted by Eldest Senior Brother to detoxify someone. Xiaomei arrived shortly after and collided with you head-on. You still wanted to shield her, keeping her from being seen by the Kongtong people, when suddenly your lower abdomen ached — you had been struck by a treacherous stroke of Xiaomei's sword. Fortunately the blade hadn't gone deep enough to harm anything vital, but the shock you felt was no small matter. Xiaomei flipped and leaped to Venerable Golden Crow's side. Your heart went cold, for you realized she had never meant to flee Kongtong and join the Tang Clan at all — it had only ever been to strike today.

He needn't have worried himself with deduction — the culprit couldn't wait to show himself. The one who appeared was Venerable Golden Crow, a renowned master of the Flying Heaven Gate of the Kongtong Sect.

Fu Yun, with a monk's compassionate heart, could not stand idly by — especially since the robber was himself a monk who had broken his vows. As a fellow follower of the Buddha, if Fu Yun did not step in to punish him, it might harm the good name of Songshan; reputation may mean nothing to one who has left the secular world, but it bears on whether monks everywhere can spread the teachings and benefit all under heaven, and could not be treated lightly. He struck at once, felling the robber with a single palm strike — he had not even used much force, yet the renegade monk, for all his bulk, could not withstand it, collapsing at the first blow and spitting out a mouthful of blood that left Fu Yun stunned. Unfortunately the man who had been robbed was too badly hurt to live, and rather than let his treasure go to waste, he resolved to give the sword he had forged to his benefactor. His throat was too injured for words, but the longing in his eyes spoke plainly enough. Unwilling to let him die with regret, Fu Yun declined the sword but promised to find it a worthy new owner, and asked Eldest Senior Brother to help him dig a grave while he himself recited the rebirth mantra to deliver the departed soul. Eldest Senior Brother turned the small sword into a makeshift shovel, and after only a few strokes heard Fu Yun's chanting falter; turning around, he saw Fu Yun spit out a mouthful of blood. Eldest Senior Brother had never cared for poison himself, but from long exposure he knew Second Senior Brother's methods better than most — a glance told him the renegade monk's face had turned purple, poisoned to death, and the truth dawned on him. He snatched up the sword and flung the blade, and sure enough another wisp of poison smoke leaked from the broken steel. It seemed both the sword's owner and the renegade monk were victims, manipulated without knowing it — whoever was behind this had tampered with the sword and poisoned the monk besides, so that whether Fu Yun drew the blade or touched the monk's poisoned blood, he would be struck down either way. Such careful planning spoke of no small cunning. Without a second thought, Eldest Senior Brother gave Fu Yun the life-saving Wanling Pill he carried, unused until now, to hold back the poison.

Witnessing such an injustice, Long Xiang could not let it pass. Her brows arched, she drew her sword and closed the distance in one smooth motion, cutting the villain down without a single drop of blood touching her hem — utterly clean. Unfortunately the man who had been robbed was too badly hurt to live, and rather than let his treasure go to waste, he resolved to give the sword he had forged to his benefactor. His throat was too injured for words, but the longing in his eyes spoke plainly enough. Unwilling to let him die with regret, Long Xiang accepted the sword and vowed to use it to slay demons and root out evil. Eldest Senior Brother, watching from the side, saw nothing amiss — perhaps it was only the instinct of years spent roaming the Jianghu that made him suddenly uneasy just as Long Xiang lifted the sword to draw it from its sheath. He shouted for her to stop, but he was a step too late: the sword had been tampered with. Its blade snapped in two, and the sheath had concealed a hidden poison smoke. Long Xiang took the worst of it and was instantly struck with a deadly toxin. Eldest Senior Brother rushed to her side, pulled out the Tang Clan's life-saving Wanling Pill he carried, crushed its wax seal, and forced it into her mouth to keep the poison from killing her outright.

Eldest Senior Brother and his companion walked ahead, and they also saw someone coming from not far away. However, this person was limping, frequently looking back, and bloodstained. They were not there to challenge but had fallen victim to bandits.

Eldest Senior Brother and his companion walked ahead, arriving at a tea house in the mountains. This shop was originally set up by the Tang Clan for serving tea, but since their family fortunes declined, they sold it. Upon seeing this shop, Eldest Senior Brother knew they had arrived home. The Tang Family's main compound was at most ten li away, and another half‑hour at most, they would be home. He exhaled a long breath, this journey, though filled with strange occurrences, fortunately saw no mishaps, and they arrived safely.

The Eldest Senior Brother and his companion walked ahead, arriving at the Tang Clan Tea House. Inside, apart from customers, everyone wore blue or red robes. Upon seeing their own kin, the Eldest Senior Brother knew they had reached home. The Tang Family's main courtyard was no more than ten li away, and with a little over half an hour, they would arrive. He exhaled a long breath, for though there had been many strange incidents along the way, fortunately, nothing had gone wrong, and they had arrived safely.
You had a sense of foreboding, thus hastily said goodbye and left swiftly.
Although the misunderstanding has been resolved, he can't just believe you based on a few words. He doesn't want you to come to treat his injury. As long as you let him go, he has his own solution.
