You were scolded with a sudden torrent of curses that left you utterly bewildered, growing more far-fetched the longer he went on, until the two of you both stopped short, realizing it had all been a misunderstanding. He leaned in for a closer look at you, clicking his tongue in astonishment - he'd never imagined anyone would go to the trouble of impersonating someone as ugly as you, so it had to be for some ulterior motive.

You were stunned for a moment, but without hesitation, you had already guessed the truth of the matter. You couldn't help but become furious, deciding in your heart never to be lenient again. This time, you would definitely eliminate this harmful element for the sect.

In the heat of battle, the two of you caught the odd look on each other's face and both sensed something was off; when you stopped to ask, you found you had each mistaken your opponent. You had taken him for an enemy come to make trouble for Eldest Senior Brother, while he had taken you for a bandit come to steal his prized sword, claiming he had only just run into you and been ambushed by you.

You felt the same; the matter was plain enough, and only Eldest Senior Brother avoided speaking of it, while Long Xiang merely believed she had hidden it well. You and Xiaomei deliberately fell behind, giving this exasperating pair of martial lovers a chance to be alone together.
You were none too pleased to hear her arrangement - if only you had known this crazy girl would get in your way, you wouldn't have brought her back to the Tang Clan.

You were fought over by two beauties; even though, had you gone with either, you wouldn't truly have wanted it - it was only ever a matter of pride - it was still enough to give you bragging rights later. The mountain path was narrow, and Xiaomei, using the excuse that Long Xiang was a guest, asked Eldest Senior Brother to walk on ahead with Long Xiang. In public it was reasonable enough; in private, sharp-eyed as she was in matters of the heart, she had noticed the faint stirring of feeling between Long Xiang and Eldest Senior Brother, and she chuckled to herself, meaning to play matchmaker.
You volunteered to take on the mission, and the two of them had no choice but to shrug and hand over the opponent to you to deal with.

This mountain path is narrow, allowing at most two people to walk side by side, so Xiaomei asked Eldest Senior Brother and Fu Yun to go first. Not only does the taboo of male-female contact apply, but it is also inconvenient for a monk to walk with a woman, and Fu Yun genuinely fears this female patron. When he traveled to Kongtong to spread the teachings, he once witnessed her laughing with a Daoist one moment and pushing him down the stairs the next, leaving him half-dead. He deeply sensed her sinister nature, realizing she is beyond his own poor power to convert or save, and so he has always kept his distance, vowing never to walk beside her on dangerous terrain.
Both of them didn't get along. No matter what they were fighting over, it was all about pride. Refusing to let go, when their eyes met, they simultaneously channeled their True Qi, tearing you apart.
Xiaomei may be playful, but she deeply values you as a friend. As soon as you cried out in pain, she immediately let go.
In the end, it was Long Xiang who feared that you would feel pain and let go first.

You were deeply afraid of being torn apart, reluctant to wait passively for death, so you exerted a forceful pull from the center. Though the two women were skilled in martial arts, their strength wasn't as great as yours, and they were immediately pulled into your arms, surrounded on both sides. As the two women tumbled into your arms, they immediately jumped back, their faces flushed with embarrassment, and to cover their shyness, they pushed you back and forth.

This time it was Xiaomei who couldn't sit still, hurrying over to pull you away. Long Xiang, unable to hold back her anger, refused to let go, and the two women seized your arms from either side, nearly tearing you in half.

Unwilling to be left out, she called you over to her side. Though you were nowhere near Eldest Senior Brother's equal in conversation, having you there as a decoration was still better than being left out in the cold.
Long Xiang didn't know Xiaomei, and seeing her getting along so well with Eldest Senior Brother, she couldn't help but feel stifled with annoyance.

Looking closely, the one who had arrived was Xiaomei. She said she feared someone might take advantage of Eldest Senior Brother's unrecovered strength after his duel to strike while he was vulnerable, so she had come down the mountain specially to meet you all.
As usual today, someone could be seen approaching from a distance on the mountain path.

Thankfully, you and Fu Yun were accompanying him, dealing with the opponents on his behalf, allowing the Eldest Senior Brother to rest and recover his strength. Otherwise, even if he didn't lose, he would have been worn out to death.

Fortunately, you and Long Xiang traveled with him, seeing off his challengers in his place, which let Eldest Senior Brother rest and recover his strength. Otherwise, even if he never lost, he would have been worn out to death.

It's easy to go, but returning is not so smooth. Along the way, rivals, love enemies, and those who wish to defeat Eldest Senior Brother for fame come unending, now and then blocking the path to challenge him.
You defeated Dharma Master Fu Yun, and he was not ashamed of his defeat, merely laughing it off.
You lost to Dharma Master Fu Yun; he took no pride in his victory, merely smiling it off.

You performed exceptionally, defeating the Heroine Long Xiang, whose sword skills were unparalleled. She was shocked, momentarily unable to believe it, and then her face lit up with delight. Seeing her sweet smile, you felt a sense of relief and joy, unaware that her smile was because you were on her mind. Next time she challenged you, she would no longer take the time to guide you, but instead fully commit to challenging you.

Long Xiang's absentmindedness is something you know best. To prevent her from being tricked again by the schemes of the Jianghu, you remain ever vigilant, ensuring no one approaches her under any pretext. Your sharp eyes shine brightly, scaring off street ruffians, and Long Xiang's wallet mysteriously survives. She began learning swordsmanship from a young age, with remarkable talent, surpassing all her peers. She has never needed protection before. With a pure and open heart, she never suspects others, so since leaving the palace on her travels, despite her undefeated sword skills, she has suffered many hardships and felt deeply defeated. Today, seeing you protect her, she is surprised and feels a mix of emotions she cannot put into words, finding it very comforting. Her feelings for you are different from those for her Eldest Senior Brother, growing deeper over time.
Long Xiang had originally meant to treat you, but her purse had gone missing again.
You and Long Xiang wandered through the village market, and as the sun was about to set, you saw the night market setting up its stalls. So you were pulled along to explore it all over again.

You vaguely sensed that you were merely the companion she dragged along as cover, tasked with testing for poison and picking out the tasty finds before they went to Eldest Senior Brother.
Even so, being able to wander the streets with her was no small joy in life.
Long Xiang encouraged you for a while, giving you no chance to catch your breath before pulling you into the street, and whatever novel delicacy caught her eye, she refused to pass up.

Long Xiang gave you some words of encouragement before leaving, and you spent a while alone, turning her swordplay over in your mind again and again.
Back at the inn, whether eating, bathing, changing, or lying in bed, your thoughts were filled with sword-shadows.
The clearer they grew, the deeper your despair, until you began to think of retiring from the Jianghu.
Long Xiang approached smilingly, bent down to pick up the weapon for you. Even though she had no ill intentions, seeing the gleaming blade in her hand still made you feel a moment of hesitation.
Unsurprisingly, you were thoroughly defeated by her, your weapon knocked away by the sword hilt, sending you staggering back a few steps, your face ashen.

You pretended to side with Long Xiang, comforting her while also scolding Eldest Senior Brother on her behalf — a tactic that let you advance or retreat as needed. Even if the consolation failed, you could distance yourself and leave Eldest Senior Brother to face the chicken leg's wrath alone. Fortunately, Long Xiang was good-natured at heart, and it was only because she'd so often been wronged and pushed around that she'd been driven to tears. Helping her was like a small boat, starved at sea, finally reaching shore — no longer forced to turn pirate just to survive. After a proper scolding, and once Eldest Senior Brother personally apologized and promised to clear her name, her temper cooled by some sixty or seventy percent, and her tears gradually stopped. Seizing the moment, you changed the subject to the chicken leg, and the crisis finally passed.

With no other choice, Eldest Senior Brother had to brace himself and step forward to try to soothe her. But he couldn't hold his tongue; seeing Long Xiang crying and wailing, he couldn't resist tossing out some crude jokes at her expense. Long Xiang's mind was simple, and she had almost no tolerance for that kind of talk — good words or bad, she took everything to heart. Overcome with grief and fury, she swung the weapon in her hand, meaning to strike both Eldest Senior Brother and you dead on the spot. She really did swing her chicken leg at Eldest Senior Brother's throat, a vital point; had he not been on guard, she might well have severed his life's pulse and killed him outright. Both Eldest Senior Brother and you were badly startled and dared not talk nonsense again. Only after Eldest Senior Brother offered a solemn bow of apology and thanked her for all her past kindnesses did Long Xiang gradually stop crying, silently finishing the chicken leg in her hand with tears still in her eyes. Watching her cry one moment and eat the next, Eldest Senior Brother couldn't help laughing, then slipped right back into his old ways, telling her to step aside and stop blocking his way to the brothel. Long Xiang froze; her lovely face turned to frost, and she drew her sword with a chilling look. This time she had made up her mind to ignore anything Eldest Senior Brother said — today, she meant to kill him. Eldest Senior Brother knew that Long Xiang, serious and thin-skinned as she was, could normally be teased half to death without real danger, so long as he was at full strength; if she truly came for him, he need only run until her anger cooled. But he had forgotten, for the moment, that he had just fought a brutal battle — his old wounds unhealed, his true qi badly spent — and there was no way he could outrun her blade today. His only recourse was to brazen it out to the end: he loudly claimed he had suffered internal injuries, and feared the poison inside him might flare up, so he needed to find a woman at the brothel to play music and sing for him before his wounds could heal. You were left speechless — who in the world would believe such an excuse? Yet hearing Eldest Senior Brother speak with such solemn conviction, Long Xiang was struck by a thought: her own Lady Wen was deeply versed in music theory, able to play Pipa tunes with her Sound Wave Skill to wound enemies with sound, or help soothe and heal them. At once she was struck with realization, ashamed that she had judged a gentleman's heart by a petty one's measure. She sheathed her sword, her face softening, and offered to go with Eldest Senior Brother to pay respects to that master musician at the brothel. Eldest Senior Brother's face fell — bold as he was, he hadn't the nerve to bring this pure-hearted young woman into a brothel. Even if Lady Wen turned a blind eye, your Tang Clan's Sect Leader would never forgive it. Long Xiang, though, seemed entirely at ease with the idea; she had no scorn for courtesans who earned their own keep — women who sold themselves to survive, without robbing or cheating anyone, were far nobler than those born to wealth who did every manner of wrong while putting on airs of virtue. She only didn't want Eldest Senior Brother growing close to other women. Even wine and meat pass through the body without staining the heart — how much less, then, a fleeting, playacted romance? Eldest Senior Brother fell silent, his view of Long Xiang much changed, and lost all desire to go to the brothel after all. The two of them went off together to find bamboo for a flute, leaving you alone to guard an empty room, still shaken.

You finished your meal, bathed, changed, and went to sleep. In the middle of the night, Eldest Senior Brother rolled you up in the quilt, dragged you onto the floor, and claimed the bed for himself alone.

You sought instruction in martial arts from Master Fu Yun. Though this young monk was deeply versed in Buddhist doctrine, eloquent and persuasive, never losing an argument when preaching to others, he could not help but stir up a sense of competition due to his youthful passion and unquenched worldly desires, especially as a martial artist. Having witnessed the duel that day, he eventually agreed to the invitation and used Songshan martial arts to spar with you.

You claimed to be the very bandit he feared, and sought instruction in martial arts from Master Fu Yun, arguing that vanquishing demons and evil was a Buddhist disciple's sacred duty. He was persuaded at once.

Not wanting to disturb the monks, you made your apologies and took your leave, heading back to the inn. There you ordered a bowl of plain noodle soup to fill your stomach, ate your fill, washed up, changed, and then slept slumped over the table — for who else but Eldest Senior Brother would sprawl starfish-wise across the bed and claim it all for himself?

Fu Yun followed the sound and came over to check. Originally, the temple where he had stayed was nearby, and he had heard some noise in the temple, fearing that bandits might attempt to harm the Buddhist temple, so he came out to look.

Long Xiang approached, hearing your practice, and was also eager to demonstrate her skills, so she volunteered to spar with you. You considered the disparity in strength and realized you were no match for her, expecting the fight to be one‑sided, and you'd end up losing without cause. However, seeing her eager and determined expression, you couldn't bear to discourage her, so you gritted your teeth and agreed to the duel.

You thought back to the fierce battle that morning between Eldest Senior Brother and Gang Leader Shi, your heart still pounding with excitement, and went out to find a quiet, open place. While the memory was still fresh, you worked to internalize all you had seen and make it your own.

Eldest Senior Brother raised an eyebrow, meaning to test your martial arts, but his vitality was weak, and even lifting a hand felt like too much bother, so he sat there sparring with words instead. Though mere talk without real combat has its limits, debating on paper has its own virtue — with no life-or-death stakes to rush you, you could think things through calmly, like a game of chess. He had meant this kind of mental training to help you, thinking it especially useful for someone stuck at a plateau, never suspecting your grasp of the martial arts was extraordinary. Without lifting a hand, you could picture the exchange as vividly as real combat, and though your reactions weren't as swift as his, you kept producing unexpected moves, until in one unguarded moment you turned the tables and beat him. Eldest Senior Brother laughed in astonishment, lost for a moment in reflection. Years ago he had secluded himself in the Tang Clan's back mountain, pondering for half a year until, at the very limit of thought, he distilled the ultimate principle of the martial arts. Rooted as he was in Tang Clan technique, even his most natural, unstudied moves could never quite shake off its deep-set habits — only through someone else's practice could the idea finally be proven, and it had taken far too long. Even had he been willing to refine it with others, where would he find one with no preconceptions at all, whose Internal Skill was solid and whose build was balanced, yet who had come to it late? Fortunately, he had you. Only through you did his envisioned Formless Form finally take shape — proof that it was not for nothing that he had quizzed you again and again on the Chapter on Forgetting Form, or that he had once, his face hidden, guided you in secret on the back mountain.

Eldest Senior Brother raised his eyebrows, meaning to test your martial arts, but his vitality was weak, and he was too lazy even to move a finger, preferring to sit there and verbally spar. Though mere talk rather than actual combat had its limits, debating on paper had its own virtue; with no life-or-death stakes to rush you, you could think things through calmly, much like a game of chess, honing focused thought. This kind of mental training was especially effective for someone stuck at a plateau. A hint from him set you thinking, and your grasp of the martial arts deepened further. You also heard Eldest Senior Brother reveal the profound secret of the Shangguan Family's Wave-Riding Formula. Though you had no idea how he came to know it, the technique was truly ingenious — merely imagining it was hard enough to counter, let alone facing it in real combat. You couldn't help but feel a new respect for the Shangguan Family, long faded from the Jianghu.

Eldest Senior Brother raised his eyebrows, meaning to test your martial arts, but his vitality was still spent, and even lifting a hand felt like too much bother, so he sat there sparring with words instead. Though mere talk without real combat has its limits, debating on paper has its own virtue — with no life-or-death stakes to rush you, you could weigh each move calmly, the way one studies a game of chess. Such mental training is especially useful for one stuck at a plateau, and sure enough, a hint from him set you thinking, and your grasp of the martial arts deepened a shade further.

Eldest Senior Brother raised an eyebrow, meaning to test your martial arts. But his vitality was still weak, and even lifting a hand felt like too much bother, so he sat there sparring with words instead. Unfortunately, you were far too shameless, throwing out one impractical move after another just to win the argument, until Eldest Senior Brother lost all interest and gave up playing with you.

You had been entrusted by Third Senior Brother with keeping a close watch on this man, so how could you let him bolt straight into the pleasure quarters? You planted yourself at the door and window, blocking Eldest Senior Brother's escape — let him so much as twitch, and you were ready to fight him to hell and back.

Long Xiang also stayed at the same inn. After setting down her belongings, she went out to summon the waiter, ordering a pot of light wine, several small dishes, and three-spiced chicken legs. She was enjoying her meal when she overheard your Eldest Senior Brother boasting about going to a brothel. A surge of anger rose in her, and she shouted to stop him, only to be accused by your Eldest Senior Brother of being a female lecher for eavesdropping. Since she began wandering the Jianghu, Long Xiang had dedicated herself to upholding justice and righteousness, afraid of letting her father's reputation down. However, after being deceived by others and sparring with your Eldest Senior Brother several times, he had carelessly given her the nickname Murderous Demon of Jinxiang Palace with his foul mouth. She had longed and struggled hard, hoping someone would give her a glorious title, but she never received one. Instead, the nickname Murderous Demon of Jinxiang Palace spread overnight across the Jianghu. Now wherever she went, people saw her as a cold-blooded killer. She could not argue her way out, and it galled her bitterly. Worse still, she feared that if she slunk back to Jinxiang Palace, Lady Wen would find out and take a cane to her. With the stain of Murderous Demon of Jinxiang Palace still unwashed, Eldest Senior Brother's careless 'female lecher' was more than Long Xiang could bear, and she furiously kicked the door open. Blind with rage, she never noticed that what she had snatched up was not her sword but a chicken leg. You and Eldest Senior Brother went pale with alarm — comical as it was, Long Xiang's swordsmanship was so fine that even a chicken leg could kill in her hand. If she truly meant to fight, given his wounds and your own strength, the two of you might actually die today beneath a chicken leg and become the Wulin's ultimate laughingstock — hardly a good outcome. And if the Sect Leader ever learned of it, he would surely chase your souls down to the underworld and haul you both out of the oil cauldron for a beating.

You could see Eldest Senior Brother's restless expression and sensed a vague foreboding, so you asked him outright before he could leap through the window and escape. Turns out Eldest Senior Brother, fresh from a fight, was already restless again, itching to go to a brothel.

You and Eldest Senior Brother share a room, which is not stinginess but follows the teachings of the ancestors. The Tang Clan's forebears repeatedly instructed their descendants to uphold frugality and cherish belongings, avoiding extravagance, quite unlike the Nangong and Shangguan families. Eldest Senior Brother is accustomed to using Coin Darts precisely to defy the ancestors. Now that he has passed his rebellious years, he can't change the habit, so he simply lets it be.

The battle at Woyun Ridge came to a conclusion, putting an end to the conflict with the Flying Stone Gang. You, Eldest Senior Brother, and Fu Yun went down the mountain together to rest in the village. You and Eldest Senior Brother checked into an inn while the Dharma Master went to lodge at a nearby temple, and the three of you agreed to meet again early the next morning.

Seeing Long Xiang and the Eldest Senior Brother playfully bantering with each other, their bond clearly deep, you couldn't help but feel a sense of joy. Although you couldn't help but envy the Eldest Senior Brother's fortune in having such a wonderful person pursuing him, if things were to develop between them, the Eldest Senior Brother would likely no longer be able to marry the Junior Martial Sister. After all, the Junior Martial Sister is the only beloved daughter of the Sect Leader, and it wouldn't do to let her be a concubine or a secondary wife. Moreover, this Miss Long doesn't seem like the type to settle for a subordinate position, especially with Jinxiang Palace as her backing. In this case, the Eldest Senior Brother would have to give up the Junior Martial Sister. Even if the Junior Martial Sister ultimately marries someone else, at least he could accompany her for a few more years, creating memories to comfort them throughout their lives.

Seeing Long Xiang and the Eldest Senior Brother joking and teasing each other with such deep affection, you couldn't help but laugh. The Eldest Senior Brother was clever, cunning, wild and unrestrained; were it not for Long Xiang - this plain-spoken, forthright woman, strong in martial arts yet endlessly exasperating - chasing after him, bickering with him, now and then giving him something to worry over, and now and then making him eat dirt, he might well, sooner or later, have dissolved into a wisp of smoke and drifted off into the sky.

Seeing Long Xiang and the Eldest Senior Brother laughing and teasing each other, their deep bond stirring a pang of jealousy within you, you realized she was never meant for you. This lifetime's fortune of meeting her, treating her as a sister, may have already exhausted your entire fate. A white-clad fairy like her is destined to match with someone as outstanding in appearance and martial arts as the Eldest Senior Brother. As for you, it's best to break free from this attachment, to avoid self-torment and futile efforts.

The battle at Woyun Ridge brought the feud with the Flying Stone Gang to a close, for now, and you, the Eldest Senior Brother, and Long Xiang went down the mountain to rest for the night in the village.

You set out alone to return to the Central Plains. The road was long, and along the way you caught a chill without meaning to. You gave every coin you had to a young, strong member of the Flying Stone Gang and asked him to carry you up the mountain — and there, at the old site of the Tang Clan, you died just as you had wished.

You threw down the Tang Clan Small Sword, swept your sleeves, and departed. This time when leaving the village, no one blocked your way; the villagers all came to see you off, bowing deeply to the ground.

You did not grant her that wish — this was not mercy. You knew well that the bitterest thing in this world is not death, but separation from kin. So you kept her on this island, to suffer in your place the slow torment of longing, until twenty years on, when those she longed to see could be found no more — only then would you let her return to the Central Plains. Whether she obeyed or not, in this life she would never earn your forgiveness.

All these years, not a day has passed that you did not long to avenge yourself on her — the Tang Clan's fall was no small part her doing. Yet in confining you here she may not have lacked good intentions, and once the blade fell the dead would never return to life. So in the end you never struck.
You executed Xiaomei. No one in the village dared to speak of it, but the old warmth was gone without a trace — your wife and children now looked at you as though you were a stranger.

Xiaomei endured for many years before she dared to see you. She suffered for her own beauty, taken by the Thousand Lantern Tower as a girl and raised as an assassin, a Corpse Heart Parasite planted in her breast that flared into agony each time it woke. To survive she had to smother her own conscience, always smiling sweetly, seldom from the heart. The thing she regretted most in her whole life was underestimating you — letting your foolishness amuse her, letting you win a place in her heart, and then, on a whim, going to the Tang Clan only to repay kindness with betrayal. So the years after she bid you farewell were bitter beyond bearing; through decades of suffering not a day passed that she did not think, "if only I hadn't been so obedient back then." Decades as the mighty, powerful master of the Thousand Lantern Tower brought her less comfort than those brief months at the Tang Clan. She brought the Tang Clan Small Sword, sank to her knees, and begged you to kill her and hold no more grudge against her.

Hearing from her lips about Master Xiahou Lan's passing, you couldn't help but feel a wave of sorrow. Yet before her death, Master had avenged you: she stormed alone into Kongtong's Flying Heaven Hall, her left hand knocking out the new sect leader with a swing of her umbrella, her right hand seizing Xiaomei's slender neck like a claw, lifting her clean off the ground and slamming her against the wall as she snarled her threats. Had Xiaomei not revealed your whereabouts then, her neck might well have been snapped. Yet even after learning you were safe, Xiahou Lan did not come to see you. Instead, following Kongtong Mountain's rules, she had Xiaomei stripped of her clothes and hung naked over the cliff's edge for questioning — trivial questions, really, for the torture and humiliation were the true point, her way of venting her anger.

A few hurried years later, you still often sat alone by the river. Your martial arts had long since been stripped away, and you lived under soft confinement in a small, remote fishing village. The place was desolate, beyond the reach of Song or Jin rule, a world apart and forgotten by time. The village folk had all once owed Xiaomei their lives, spared from the tiger's mouth through her help, and now lived here as recluses; hearing that you were her close friend, they treated you with great warmth, and some women even came to you of their own will and bore you children. Ten, twenty years slipped past in a blur, until you no longer knew what year it was. Then one day, as you sat alone by the river as always, an old friend came to call — Xiaomei, still as lovely as the young girl she had once been, untouched by the years. In the time since, her hands had grown stained with countless killings, and her achievements had carried her ever higher, her standing now surpassing even Jinwu Shangren's — so that even the dignified Sect Leader of Kongtong had to bow and scrape before her, the Master of the Thousand Lantern Tower.

After the two of you wed, your life together was harmonious, and having gained so lovely a wife, the many cares once weighing on your heart slowly faded. What remained of that burned-away youth was only ash — now and then the wind would stir it, and a little grit would sting your eyes to tears, nothing more. More than a decade later, Xiaomei came to visit, and seeing your brood of children, she could not help smiling through tears; the three of you set aside all old grievances and made your peace. By then the Central Plains had settled — Song, Jin, and Xia had each fallen in turn, and a new dynasty had begun. Xiaomei invited you both back to the Central Plains, but after a night's discussion, you and Xiao Zhu gently declined; you had grown used to so quiet a life, and asked only that she take your children away from the island. Xiaomei cherished your children even more than her own — shamelessly so — for they were, after all, the offspring of the two friends who mattered most to her. On a bright, sunlit morning, you and Xiao Zhu sat hand in hand, talking of ordinary things. As you talked, both of you grew drowsy, and leaning together you fell asleep — and never woke again.

Confirming each other's intentions, both were overjoyed, but unfortunately, the island lacked resources, so they had to make do. You took her hand to greet the islanders one by one, borrowed two red candles, cut a piece of red cloth as a veil, and married that night, becoming husband and wife.

You spent an unimaginable stretch of time preparing to marry her. With the island's resources so limited, you had to see to everything yourself, and it took half a year — not just the sedan chair, but the house itself was rebuilt from the ground up. During this time, Xiao Zhu stayed with an elderly couple in the village, who doted on her so much that she simply took them as her adoptive parents. On the wedding day, you and she knelt before her adoptive parents, then had the bride carried into your home in a flower sedan chair. You were not only her confidant, you had also fulfilled her dream, and she loved you with utter devotion — she would have given her life for you.

You too were overjoyed, yet you still worried: if she refused you, given that the islanders' five-colored mud had already stripped you of all your power, trying to force her would be no different from courting death. If it truly came to that, you would have no choice but to set honor aside and drug her senses instead.

Xiao Zhu made certain, again and again, that she wasn't being foolishly sentimental or misreading your meaning, and grew so happy she nearly wept. She drew close with care, softly murmured "my love," and gave herself and her whole life over to you.
You mustered the courage to invite her home.
You mustered the courage to invite her home, but were so nervous that even a simple sentence came out stammered.

You were overjoyed, yet still too timid to be rash, and swallowed the words back down. For decades afterward you lacked the courage to tell her your true feelings. Little did you know Xiao Zhu was just as timid as you, torn between fondness and exasperation. She waited a lifetime for you to speak, and only on her deathbed did she finally hear you voice your heart — and so she passed away smiling, without regret. After Xiao Zhu died, you went to great lengths to obtain bamboo seedlings and planted a grove of them on the island, proclaiming yourself lord of the settlement, and lived out your remaining years amid the bamboo.

It turned out that after Xiaomei became the Sect Leader's principal wife, she used her new authority to have Xiao Zhu banished. Xiao Zhu had originally been an orphan sold into Kongtong, with no home of her own, and had hoped to rely on her skills to join the Fire Mountain Sword Pavilion, never expecting to be seized and brought here instead. She spoke of it lightly, but never mentioned how many she had injured resisting. In the end, Xiaomei, left with no choice, came herself to subdue Xiao Zhu and gently told her the whole truth. Xiao Zhu finally understood, and these two Kongtong sisters, who had quarreled the moment they met, at last made peace. It was only through Xiaomei's arrangement that Xiao Zhu was able to come here.

You are well‑versed in military affairs, deducing the general situation from just a few hints from Xiao Zhu. Upon hearing this, Xiao Zhu couldn't help but feel immense admiration. Her gaze toward you carried even more reverence. She imagined that if you had joined the military, you might one day become a renowned general, which would make her, as a commoner, unable to associate with you. She felt both sorrow for you and secretly relieved for herself.

One day, you were sitting idly by the riverbank, when suddenly through the misty mountains and rivers, it seemed as if a boat's shadow was approaching. Upon closer inspection, wasn't it the green‑clad girl you've been longing for all along?

Under Xiaomei's threat, you ultimately valued your own life, ceased your training, interrupted your breathing techniques, and abandoned your senior brother. Xiaomei knocked you out, applied a few pressure points to prevent you from waking up, and carried you on her back, using her Qinggong to swiftly descend the mountain.   When you regained consciousness, your hands and feet were bound, unable to move. Cursing was of no use; you could only let the carriage driver take you away from the Central Plains, far from the world. You were placed under soft confinement on a secluded island, where the villagers were all Jianghu people who had benefited from Xiaomei and sought refuge there.   The island seemed to have a barrier; you attempted to escape several times, but whether swimming or building a boat, all your efforts ultimately failed. Each time you reached the river mouth, thick fog and hidden currents would push you back. You couldn't help but feel despair, knowing that without help from others, you would be trapped here for the rest of your life.

Life and death, parting and reunion, are all impermanent. Knowing that you have lost your elder brother, your sorrow is profound. Yet Yunshang, though a person who usually speaks eloquently, is now gradually retreating into silence, choked by sobs and unable to utter a word. She can only silently weep with you.

The sky had cleared everywhere but over the Tang Clan, where dark clouds still hung heavy. Stray raindrops fell, wetting your collar, as though the whole world had been washed by rain and left cold and desolate. Life drifts like duckweed, gathering and scattering without warning — who could promise that tomorrow would be no different?

Junior Martial Sister gazed at Eldest Senior Brother's tombstone, feeling utterly lost. She had been parted from her mother since childhood, and now her father lay bedridden, his days perhaps numbered, while the two senior brothers she had loved like elder brothers had both left her, one after another. The Tang Clan remained the Tang Clan, but its people were no longer the same. The quiet, ordinary mountain years she once knew were gone; life had become one long nightmare from which no struggle or denial could wake her, full of pain and helplessness. She crept silently closer to you, afraid that even a blink might make you vanish too.
Even though Junior Martial Sister pats you with her small hand, she cannot dispel your grief.

When you startled awake, you found yourself already lying on the bunk bed in the disciples' quarters. Third Senior Brother, Fourth Senior Brother, and Junior Martial Sister all brightened with joy to see you awake, but when you asked what had happened, their faces turned grim. That night, after you were injured and fainted, the Tang Clan, Kongtong, and Qingcheng broke out at once into fierce fighting, and each side suffered heavy casualties. A deep blood feud had been forged, and with Eldest Senior Brother's death, the sect itself had taken a crippling blow, left in ruins, the whole of the Tang Clan wrapped in gloom.

Disturbing one's circulation of internal energy is a grave danger for any internal-arts practitioner. Mildly, it causes Internal Injury; severely, it sends the qi astray and kills. The stronger one's internal skill, the greater the peril. This is why those in the Wulin who train or heal seek out quiet places to seclude themselves, and the cautious keep someone at hand to guard them, so their minds may rest easy. Disturbed again and again, your thoughts in turmoil, you had already suffered severe Internal Injury, and now, unable to hold on any longer, you fainted dead away. In the half-lit haze between waking and dream, you seemed to receive some final words from Eldest Senior Brother, though whether real or imagined you could not say. In dream and in waking both, your face was wet with tears.
Seeing that you would not hesitate to risk your life for his, he could not help but smile.

Eldest Senior Brother laughed silently, never thinking you always opposed him, in the end it would be you who sacrifices your life to save him. You don't think so. You're helping the Tang Clan, not intending to sacrifice your life. If you knew it wouldn't work, you wouldn't have done it.

Ever since someone had broken into the alchemy room, you had been on edge, your thoughts in turmoil, and every time your mind stirred, the stray true qi would seize the chance to flare up, leaving you in agony. Still, you gritted your teeth and held on, unwilling to let go so easily. The clash of steel, the cries of battle, never let up, and each ripple of feeling set your wandering true qi stirring anew, tormenting you all the more—yet still you held on, refusing to let go. Now, hearing the din of battle roaring outside and the anguished cries of the sect's womenfolk, your mind grew ever more unsettled, and you longed to rush out and defend your home. But the more anxious you grew, the deeper your internal injuries sank, until at last you could hold back no longer and coughed a mouthful of blood onto Eldest Senior Brother's back. Warmed by your blood, he slowly stirred awake, and hearing the commotion, understood at once that enemies had struck the sect and the situation was dire. He gave a faint struggle, unwilling to let you spend any more of your true essence on him. He meant to stop here—there was no need for you to die alongside him. You still had use in you yet, and the Tang Clan still needed you.

You hurriedly lifted Eldest Senior Brother up. Cutting off his circulation in that moment of panic just now had done him grave harm—his meridians were damaged, his breath now thread-thin. Even if it was like mending the pen after the sheep had already bolted, so long as a shred of life remained, you had no intention of giving up so easily.

Moreover, there are also spies skilled in ingenious techniques, capable of mimicking others' voices, seizing the opportunity to incite discord, leading to a battle among three factions, poised to erupt at any moment.

As Venerable Golden Crow fled in disarray, the Kongtong men blanched as well, and dared not linger, bursting out through the gates. Neither Tang Clan nor Qingcheng could well detain them, so they were left to go. After this scene, Qingcheng too began to suspect Tang Clan of ill intent—the compound felt thick with danger—and using the lateness of the hour as pretext, they declined Third Senior Brother's offer to stay, traded a few parting courtesies, and hurried down the mountain. Not long after, word spread through the Jianghu that Tang Clan had staged a Hongmen Banquet, inviting Kongtong and Qingcheng to the Tang Family compound under the guise of discussing weighty matters of the Jianghu, when in truth they meant to serve as mouthpieces for the Demon Cult and press the two sects to surrender. The representatives of both sects held to their principles and refused to yield, and the meeting broke up in discord. On their way home, both sects were ambushed again, this time by Tang Clan in league with the Demon Cult, and suffered heavy losses. The survivors swore up and down, denouncing Tang Clan as a scourge upon the Wulin and a lackey of the Demon Cult. With Qingcheng and Kongtong counted among the Six Great Sects of the Wulin and their names held in high regard, while Tang Clan's own reputation straddled the line between righteous and wicked, the world naturally believed the accusers far more readily.

Although your skills are superior, your experience in the Jianghu is too shallow. You were caught off guard, not having prepared for this person who seems to be immortal. Clearly suffering a fatal injury, they suddenly launched an attack, and you were unprepared, struck by their unique martial arts, severely injuring your forehead. You attempted to gather your energy to fight back, but felt a surge of sinister True Qi rushing to your head, causing dizziness and disorientation.   The Jinwu Shangren, who hides a blade behind a smile, was known as the Nine‑Lives Leopard before joining the Kongtong Sect, skilled in the unique weapon Soul‑Seizing Staff. It is said: One knock dims the fetal light, two knocks scatter the spirit, three knocks disperse the ethereal essence. With the True Qi from his Soul‑Seizing Staff invading your mind, it wreaked havoc, turning even the most loyal subjects, filial children, and virtuous women into obedient, mute fools.   People say he was defeated by the hands of Kongtong's Former Sect Leader, seeking forgiveness and having long since reformed, with all his malice transformed. He abandoned his martial arts, realizing the righteous Solar Hammer, but it turns out he still employs the same tricks. The creation of such sinister martial arts was not merely for killing, but rather to torment others, causing suffering, while wearing monk robes, he fundamentally does not believe in retribution.   Just as he was about to strike you with two blows, intending to smash your head to pieces, the severely injured senior brother suddenly intervened, using the Flying Swallow Meteor Feathers to heavily injure the enemy and drive them back. You were about to pursue, but were called to stop. Turning around, you saw blood spilling from the corner of senior brother's mouth; he had reached the end of his strength, and despite giving it his all, could only scare off the enemy.   Your heart trembled at this moment, realizing that there is no true invincibility in the world. Even a prodigy like senior brother is merely a mortal, with flesh and blood, capable of illness and death, just like you, a mere mortal. Time has not spared anyone, and fate does not only keep a watchful eye on you.

This was too grave a matter to set aside; the sect's survival had to come before all else. You were just stepping out to warn Third Senior Brother when, without warning, one among the pile of corpses stirred back to life, swung his iron hammer, and struck a savage blow to your head.

Unable to attend to anything else, you feared Eldest Senior Brother would pass away in an instant. You hurriedly lifted him up and channeled the remaining power to heal his wounds. Unbeknownst to you, among the pile of corpses, one person silently revived and swung his iron hammer, delivering a devastating blow to your head.
You had stabbed him dead, yet stood there dazed, unable to understand why this Kongtong monk had sought his own death.

You can't help but feel deep respect for this upright assassin, imagining he must be someone in the Jianghu, bound by circumstances. Such a person, yet to fall under your small sword, is truly lamentable.

You fought him half in doubt, and sure enough the enemy kept his word, sealing off one arm and enduring grievous wounds rather than break his promise. Formidable as his martial arts were, he was defeated in the end.

You'd have to be a fool to bother with him. Just now the fighting had been too fierce to think of calling for help, but now that your mind was a little calmer, and this was your own home—why bother with courtesy? Naturally, you shouted at the top of your lungs.

Three consecutive battles have left you exhausted; though you still don't fully understand the enemy's intentions, Qingcheng and Kongtong sects both have spies. Considering further, if the Six Great Sects of the Central Plains and the Three Great Families have all been infiltrated, the consequences would be unimaginable. Thinking about it, a chill runs down your spine. At this moment, another fat Lama in a red‑robed monk's robe enters the alchemy chamber. His aura is incomparable to the previous three, yet he smiles, openly admitting his identity as an assassin, and requests to learn from you without seeking an advantage. Since you've already fought three opponents, he voluntarily seals one arm to demonstrate fairness.

Hearing them speak with mocking sneers of how the two brothers who had stood guard over the alchemy room were struck at their acupoints, left unable to move, and hurled alive off the cliff, you flew into an uncontrollable rage.

You were simple-hearted and desperate to save Eldest Senior Brother, taking these two at their word as well-meaning, so you entrusted them to haul the man before Zhengxin Hall for questioning. But no sooner had you turned your back than you fell prey to their ambush.

You were deeply wary, quietly on guard, and deliberately turned your back to bait them into striking. Sure enough, the other side couldn't hold back and attacked you. Fortunately, you had already prepared, and came to no harm.

After defeating the enemy, disciples from Qingcheng and Kongtong entered, looking bewildered. They said that outside they had come upon the brothers standing guard, gasping their last breath, and calling out for help; to avoid further trouble right after the talks had barely ended, they came together so each could vouch for the other's innocence.
Even if the junior martial sister tries to pat you with her small hand, she cannot dispel the sadness.

When you woke up, you were already lying on the bunk bed in the disciples' quarters. Third Senior Brother, Fourth Senior Brother, and Junior Martial Sister all showed joy at your awakening, but when they asked about what had happened, their expressions turned grim. That night, after you were injured and fainted, the Tang Clan, Kongtong, and Qingcheng immediately erupted into a fierce battle, resulting in significant casualties on both sides. Deep‑seated enmity had formed, and with the passing of Eldest Senior Brother, your sect suffered heavy losses, leaving it in a state of devastation and despair.

You suddenly recalled a long time ago, when you tried to win the favor of the elders by personally carrying several buckets of mountain spring water for others to bathe in. Exhausted, you took a shortcut, slipped, and fell into a mountain stream, breaking your limbs. A patch of water plants covered your face, leaving you in utter darkness, and you thought you had gone blind. Your desperate and helpless cries for help went unheard, and your prayers to gods and buddhas received no response. None of your wishes came true; fate has never stopped at a suitable point. Everyone thought you had finally had enough, like others, and threw everything away, storming off in anger. Thus, no one truly cared for you. Only the Eldest Senior Brother and Second Senior Brother didn't believe you'd leave without saying goodbye. As soon as it was dawn, they searched the mountains and fields for your trail, and finally rescued you. That is why, in your moments of despair, you always dreamed of the Eldest Senior Brother or the Second Senior Brother.

You finally glimpsed a sliver of hope in the void of despair, determined not to give up, yet no matter how you prayed, no miracle came to pass. A sharp pain pierced your back, the sword had pierced through your body and driven into the Eldest Senior Brother's back. He had deliberately missed the vital spot, intending not to kill you immediately. Even deep within, he secretly didn't want you to die, wanting you to live through the despair, to later regret this day and be tormented by hatred, transforming you into someone like himself. You lay in a pool of blood, your tilted vision stained red by blood, the ringing in your ears growing louder as consciousness faded, turning from red to black, until you could see nothing at all. In your dying dream, you saw the Eldest Senior Brother leading you, not knowing where they were going, speaking with calm indifference, which made you growl in frustration. You had given your life to save him, yet in the underworld, he still carried himself with such carefree indifference. The Eldest Senior Brother brought you to the edge of the dream, turned back, and spoke earnestly, telling you not to keep gazing at his back, not to regard him as a goal, to not remain stagnant. You have your own path, and from now on, you must take care of yourself.

In the space of a breath, before you could think it through, refusing to simply wait for death, you broke off at once and forced the enemy back. The circulation was not yet complete, and cutting it short made Eldest Senior Brother cough up a mouthful of blood; you fared little better, your Internal Breath churning wildly in your chest, wounded badly. The man no longer bothered to hide his strength, and turned his full killer's skill against you.

More disciples came after that—from Kongtong and Qingcheng alike—and each was stopped by Xiaomei's Thousand Lantern Tower cant, which exposed them as assassins; then, while they stood dumbfounded, she cut them down without a flicker of hesitation. No one knew how the Tang Clan had drawn such murderous intent from the Thousand Lantern Tower: assassins kept coming, and now even the Kongtong master Venerable Golden Crow had arrived. Clad in a great red monk's robe and always smiling, he seemed harmless enough, but Xiaomei knew him through and through—before she ever went undercover at Kongtong, it was this very man who had personally trained her killing skills. He held the rank of Five Incense in the Thousand Lantern Tower, second only to the Tower Master, and before Kongtong's Sect Leader subdued him he had committed countless crimes under the name Nine-Lives Leopard. The world believed he had turned over a new leaf, taken Buddhist vows, and cast off his poisoned arts to become an upright man. Little did they know his smile was only a mask; he still answered to the Thousand Lantern Tower, lying low within Kongtong for some greater scheme. This time, to eliminate you and Eldest Senior Brother, he had risked exposing himself—my, weren't you something, to be worth all that. Xiaomei knew this man was both a formidable fighter and a schemer, and that she was likely no match for him alone, but she was too cunning to be talked in circles, and with her cover already blown, why not simply call for help? Junior Martial Sister had been dozing in the women's quarters, her face nearly buried in her rice bowl as she ate, when the commotion jolted her awake. She flew from the room into the alchemy chamber, hurling a hidden weapon even as she moved, and arrived just in time to shield Xiaomei. The Venerable Golden Crow's face changed—he had heard of this Tang Clan Junior Martial Sister's peerless Qinggong, but never expected her to arrive so fast and so silent, more like an assassin than any assassin; only his deep experience and quick reflexes let him knock the weapon aside in time. Xiaomei and Junior Martial Sister both moved with supple Agility, and together their forms became twin streaks of red. The Venerable Golden Crow's Internal Skill ran deep, but his heavy build left him no room to parry—he could just about read Xiaomei's style, but Junior Martial Sister's Unpredictable Flying Shuttle had him crying out, and before thirty exchanges had passed he was studded with weapons like a hedgehog; had his skin and flesh not been so tough, he would have died long since. His mind raced, and he abandoned the fight at once, bursting out and crying to his Kongtong brothers, crying thief to catch a thief, and accusing the Tang Clan of ambush. Xiaomei and Junior Martial Sister gave chase. The Venerable Golden Crow fought as he fled, his body bristling with Tang Clan hidden weapons; even Third Senior Brother, seeing it, was too stunned to defend himself.

Faced with Xiaomei's threats, you still refused to abandon honor to save yourself, and her repeated bluffs proved useless. Formidable as the Thousand-Faced Demon was, killing without a flicker of hesitation—she had coldly shoved countless preening young lords and handsome suitors down the stairs, leaving them dead or crippled—she had underestimated you, this Ugly Monster, let her guard down, and grown too attached to harden her heart. Again and again she raised her dagger, only to lower it again. Furious with herself, she finally reversed course, betraying the Thousand Lantern Tower on the spot and defecting to the Tang Clan.

Just as your heart was about to turn to ice, Xiaomei suddenly struck without mercy, cutting down her own accomplice, then stepped before you and smiled, radiant and sweet. That smile seemed as light as drifting clouds and passing wind, yet none could guess what depths of despair, what heavy resolve, lay hidden beneath her bright eyes.

The more you listened, the further your heart sank. Xiaomei had not only joined the Tang Clan with ill intent—even her identity as a Kongtong Sect disciple was false. Her true identity was an assassin of the Thousand Lantern Tower: the Thousand-Faced Demon, feared throughout the Jianghu, whose true face no one knew, for any who saw it were doomed to die.
You remained silent, silently swallowing the bitterness in your throat. As your heart strings trembled, you endured the torment of True Qi's damage.

Just as the enemy meant to strike the killing blow, and you faced the agonizing choice of whether to break off and save yourself, Xiaomei suddenly rushed in. The man was startled at the sight of her, then his face darkened with anger as he accused her of repeatedly defying orders. You listened, your heart sinking further with every word—only now did you realize Xiaomei was a mole. Startled as you were, you found you were not truly surprised; old memories rose up in your mind, and understanding settled over you: so that was it. Otherwise, with her beauty, as the revered Flying Heaven Direct Disciple of Kongtong and the undisputed choice to become First Lady of the Kongtong Sect, why would she lower herself, ignoring every suitor vying to flatter her, to befriend an ugly fellow like you? What could she possibly want from you—your money, your martial skill, or your good looks?

Just as you were relieved that things seemed to be improving, a Kongtong disciple suddenly appeared in the alchemy chamber. Your heart lurched—something felt wrong. When Third Senior Brother left, he had clearly posted two fellow disciples to guard the chamber's entrances against intruders. How had this man gotten in? Then, as if showing off, the man revealed himself as a mole, hidden within Kongtong solely to stir up conflict between the righteous sects. His words left you trembling with fear—exactly what he wanted. His endless prattle was meant to provoke you, to throw your breath into disorder and drive you into Qi Deviation, so that you would die and no one would suspect murder. Seeing that talk alone would not kill you, he had no choice but to draw his weapon and move to strike.

You staggered, injured by the reverse flow, then steadied your mind, bracing yourself, gritting your teeth to endure the agony of True Qi surging backward through your meridians. It was sharp and numb, and you nearly vomited, yet you forced yourself to hold on. Sweat dripped from your forehead in large beads, evaporating into steam. Fortunately, the Tang Clan does not rely on Internal Force; Eldest Senior Brother's True Qi was hard to control, causing an involuntary reversal, not an intentional act against you. Now his energy has subsided, and the situation is gradually stabilizing. You survived, and your heart swells with immense relief. Once the circulation is complete, the task will be accomplished.

You panicked at the counterflow, sustaining an injury, but quickly steadied your mind, braced yourself, and gritted your teeth to endure the agony of your True Qi reversing through your meridians. Fortunately, the Tang Clan does not specialize in Internal Force, and Eldest Senior Brother's Internal Skill cultivation was only slightly superior to yours. Having weathered that fierce current, his strength was spent, and you gradually gained the upper hand and brought him under control. Now the flow had steadied. Once the circulation was complete, the task would be done.

You panicked, injured by the reverse current, but quickly steadied your mind, prepared yourself, and with your left palm absorbed the scattered True Qi of your Eldest Senior Brother, which he could not control, gathering and condensing it within your body. With your right palm, you channeled your own Internal Force, guiding the flow of energy, exchanging the true energies between the two of you. You acted naturally, as if it were the most logical course, yet you were unaware that while this method was easy to understand, it was extremely difficult to execute. Unbeknownst to you, you had already employed an extremely profound internal cultivation technique. Your Eldest Senior Brother's Internal Force alone was still inferior to yours, so his True Qi could not harm you at all. You absorbed, purified, and filtered out the toxins, then returned the energy to your Eldest Senior Brother. Once the meridian system was fully circulated, the task would be complete.

You steady the senior brother, place both hands on his back, employ Internal Skill, and slowly channel True Qi. However, the chaotic True Qi within him, once stimulated, immediately rebounds, surging back into your body and spreading wildly throughout.

How could he claim every advantage, only to walk away so easily? Wasn't he supposed to stay forever carefree, forever in command? As if he'd heard your grumbling, Eldest Senior Brother stirred from the brink of death to argue back. His last, brief words shook you to the core—only now did you believe there was no true invincibility in this world. Even a prodigy like Eldest Senior Brother was just an ordinary mortal, flesh and blood, able to sicken and die, no different from you. Time had spared no one, and fate's hungry eyes were not fixed on you alone.

You don't envy him for drifting through life, carefree among the flowers—you only envy him for winning Junior Martial Sister's hand. How you envy him, how you envy him! A whole lifetime of hardship, and still you couldn't win her.

It's you who's jealous of him, possessing everything you long for‑handsome, talented, renowned, well‑liked, even his enemies dare not look down on him. When it comes to the Tang Clan Flying Hero, who wouldn't raise a thumb to praise him?

Back when you and Eldest Senior Brother used to scuffle and jest, you'd cursed at him to drop dead, but none of it was ever meant. He always let your words pass like wind past his ear—why take them to heart now?
Though you two never got along, you were always hoping he'd get scolded, hoping he'd have bad luck. But no matter what, you never truly wished for his death.
Though you two never quite got along, you'd cursed him to die more than once. Now you regret it, hoping he won't die after all.
You listen to Eldest Senior Brother's gradually weakening breath, knowing he is about to leave. Both sorrowful, yet helpless.

Then you thought of the Tang Clan. You could not bear to part with these people, these houses, this land, these years, this long stretch of time. The Tang Clan would not feel your absence at all — it wouldn't even sting. Yet with Eldest Senior Brother gone, all these good and beautiful things would be reduced to ashes. Your resolve outweighed your fear, your thoughts reached beyond yourself, and with a clear and settled will, you made your decision.
This matter is a gamble with one's life. With your current level of Internal Skill, you have no certainty. Even if you survive, you may still suffer injuries from the counterflow.

You dare not call yourself a healer fit to cure a nation, but you have steeped yourself in medicine and pharmacology long enough to have real insight of your own. You said nothing of it before, though you had already worked out a plan in your mind — you simply dared not risk it short of the direst need. Eldest Senior Brother's wound, though severe, carries no hidden strike‑force or lingering aftereffect; if Internal Skill could be used to forcibly suppress it, it need not prove fatal. The difficulty is that his cultivation is scattering even now — his true qi has not simply vanished into nothing — and if someone rashly poured their own internal force into him, it would surely provoke a violent backlash. The slightest misstep could sever his meridians outright, and even the one lending aid would risk their own life. Whoever helps him, then, must be a fellow Tang Clan disciple who cultivates the very same Internal Skill, so that the same true qi meets the least resistance. Yet even this is not the hardest part. What truly leaves everyone helpless is that the Tang Clan's Internal Skill is nourished on poison — every Tang Family disciple's strength carries venom in it — and venom, by its nature, is undone by the Five‑Colored Mud. The instant such true qi enters a body, it would scatter at once; to try to save someone with it is sheer folly. For all the Tang Clan's generations of talent, the only one alive today who might save Eldest Senior Brother is you — the outer disciple who belongs to the Tang Clan and yet was never counted among its true bloodline. You alone, on the training ground, drilled the very same forms, laid the very same foundation of Internal Skill — yet were never favored by your elders, never admitted inside to learn the secret formulas, never able to use it to temper the poison in your training meals and grow your Internal Force. So for you, every gain has cost twice the effort, and countless doses of medicine have gone to waste — others grow stronger merely by eating and sleeping and doing nothing at all, while you alone have had to grind through endless hours on your own to reach the modest skill you now hold. You are the only one who shares Eldest Senior Brother's very origins and yet was never wholly given to the Tang Clan. Perhaps only you could coax his chaotic true qi back to its source without being harmed by its backlash, or offer up your own cultivation without being undone by the Five‑Colored Mud. Spend the whole of your Internal Force — even if only two or three parts in ten take effect — and Eldest Senior Brother could yet be saved.

Xiao Zhu, too, did not wish to linger, unwilling to run into her fellow disciples, and went straight down the mountain, back to the Outer Fort.

The senior sister was thoughtful - fearing that if the Junior Martial Sister spent the night keeping watch in the pill-refining chamber, it would tarnish a young maiden's good name, she woke her and sent her off, leaving you alone with the Eldest Senior Brother.

Xiao Zhu also shaped a rice ball and came to find you. Upon hearing this, she couldn't help but feel ashamed. Though she was a direct disciple of the Iron Fist Gate, her status compared to the other three beauties was as different as clouds and mud. Her voice was not heard, and no one expected her. Preoccupied with her own affairs, how could she possibly speak up?

A fellow disciple, a senior sister, noticing you had not yet eaten dinner, went to the kitchen and shaped a rice ball seasoned with nothing but salt, and brought it to you. She also told you that the Kongtong and Qingcheng sects had come to argue, and that no resolution had yet been reached. Her words carried more than a little resentment - she blamed the Third Senior Brother for taking over the sect without the boldness to act. If the Sect Leader were still alive, how could outsiders ever have dared come and upstage the host? You could not help but feel a pang of sorrow: this ancient sect and lineage was slowly fading, as everyone well knew, yet no one could bear to let it go.
The sky had already turned dark. The Junior Martial Sister spent the entire day in fear and anxiety, couldn't eat a meal, and curled up to fall asleep.

The Tang Clan has produced many outstanding individuals throughout history, but in this era, the only one capable of saving the Eldest Senior Brother is likely you-this outsider who is a Tang Clan disciple yet not part of the main family. Only you, drilling the same set of forms at the Training Ground, laying the same foundation of Internal Skill, yet never favored by the masters, never granted entry to the inner circle, and never taught the secret formulas, cannot neutralize the toxicity of medicinal diets to enhance your Internal Force. Thus, you achieve double the effort for half the result, wasting countless resources. Others can grow stronger simply by eating, sleeping, and doing nothing, but you must rely solely on your own relentless training, spending endless time to reach your current meager skills. Only you, being from the same sect as the Eldest Senior Brother yet not fully bestowed with Tang Clan's teachings, might be able to skillfully guide his chaotic True Qi back to its origin without being harmed by the reverse flow, or offer your own cultivation to prevent being consumed by the Five-colored Mud. Even if only two or three parts of your tenfold Internal Force are effective, the Eldest Senior Brother might yet be saved.

Unless a peerless master with supreme internal skill descends, Master Wuju's Eldest Senior Brother's Qi Backflow cannot be suppressed by sheer force or guided gently to return to origin and assimilate. Otherwise, one must seek someone with the same internal skill, yet through a fortunate coincidence, whose internal force has changed. For instance, someone who takes medicinal herbs or switches sects, cultivating a different internal skill. The later‑developed internal force would be ordinary internal skill, naturally unaffected by the five‑colored mud.
What the two of them said matched your own guess exactly, down to the last detail, and you could not help but manage a bitter smile, marveling at the strangeness of fate.

This one word sounded simple, but achieving it was as hard as scaling heaven itself. Severe as the Eldest Senior Brother's wounds were, they carried none of the hidden aftershocks of suppressed or backlashing force - had someone been able to force qi through him to hold the wounds in check, his life need not have been lost. The difficulty lay in this: now that his cultivation had scattered, his true qi had not simply vanished into nothing, and for anyone to recklessly pour internal force into him would provoke a violent backlash - the slightest miscalculation would sever his meridians outright, and endanger the life of whoever tried to help him. For this reason, the one to attempt it had to be a fellow disciple of the Tang Clan, training in the very same lineage of technique, so that their true qi would clash with his the least - a simple enough principle. Yet this was not even the hardest part. What truly left everyone helpless was that Tang Clan Internal Skill is nourished on poison, so that every Tang Family disciple's strength carries a toxicity of its own - and being toxic, it was naturally overpowered by the Five-colored Mud. The instant true qi entered his body it would scatter at once; to think of using it to save him was nothing but wishful fantasy.
That method was but a single character: Qi.
You were anxious, and upon hearing there was a method, you hurriedly inquired.

You dare not call yourself a master physician, but long immersion in the study of medicine and pharmacology has given you no small insight of your own. Even if the two of them said nothing, you already had a plan in mind. The three of them, as if of one mind, spoke the very same word at once: Qi - then exchanged a glance and laughed.

Now that the Second Senior Brother is away, no one can handle such a difficult case. You were just about to invite the two physicians to discuss it when they arrived on their own. These two physicians are different from ordinary jianghu physicians; they have a strong sense of integrity. They came to Shu to study, and they observed proper etiquette, showing sincere intentions without any sense of owing you anything. They had made up their minds: if your Tang Clan were to act like ordinary people, showing no mercy and immediately labeling the Mud Cult as enemies, pressing forward aggressively, then even if they were killed, they would not cooperate. However, your magnanimity far exceeded their expectations, and they were deeply moved, so they spoke openly from the start, explaining that the poisoning was not done by them. The Five-Colored Mud belongs to the Mud Cult, and it is unique to them alone. Naturally, others would assume it must be connected to the two accused individuals. But the truth is different. While the two physicians were drinking tea in a teahouse, they recognized the distinctive lotus scent in the Five-Colored Mud and realized that the Tang Clan's reputation was not exaggerated. They had independently created a similar herbal tea, as this tea is highly beneficial to people. Since they had already entered the Tang Clan's territory and were relaxed in their guard, they did not think much of it, not realizing they had been played for fools. The tea itself was harmless to anyone - someone had simply waited for the moment it was the Tang Clan's own pot that got brewed, and struck then. The one who poisoned the tea was not anyone else, but you yourself-or rather, someone who looked exactly like you, deliberately impersonating you with the intent to mislead others into thinking it was you. This is why the two physicians were startled when they met you. This matter is indeed strange and hard to believe, yet upon careful examination, it is meticulously detailed. After the two physicians explained the truth, they had fulfilled their duty. Whether you believe it or not, they did not care much. After all, they had already prepared themselves for death on this western journey. If you choose to disbelieve, you would be responsible for letting the real culprit escape, not them.

In the refining pill room, the Senior Brother lay unconscious on a bed, his breathing labored and his face pale. There was not a hint of the usual flamboyance or fearlessness that he had displayed in the past. The Senior Brother had been defeated by another's hand, severely injured, and returned near death; this outcome was unforeseen by anyone. However, the truth laid bare before everyone: with his sternum fractured inch by inch, it was clear that he had indeed been struck by a highly domineering external martial art‑the Iron Arm Divine Fist of the Kongtong Sect's Iron Fist Gate. Nowadays, no one in the Iron Fist Gate could use this skill; the secret manual had flowed into Jianghu, and it was the Flying Stone Gang Leader who had made a name for himself with it, defeating the Senior Brother at Woyun Ridge under everyone's watchful eyes. The fellow disciples accompanying the Senior Brother were nowhere to be found. Qingcheng felt sorry for the Tang Clan Flying Hero, seeing his severe injuries, so he took steps to protect him and sought out Physicians from all directions to treat his wounds. Unfortunately, due to their remote location, there was no skilled physician available; they could only treat minor ailments like bruises and colds but were at a loss with the Senior Brother's severe injuries.  Just as this situation unfolded, two itinerant physicians passed by the area and heard of Tang Buyi's condition. Qingcheng had been studying alchemy and thus had some knowledge of medicine, recognizing that these Physicians' prescriptions were all on target. After treating him with needles and herbs, Tang Buyi's condition improved immediately, dispelling any doubts, and he was treated kindly as they journeyed to the Tang Clan. When the two physicians revealed later that they came from Six Paths Gorge‑a place known for the Mud Cult's 'Heavenly Path'‑Qingcheng realized that these were no ordinary Physicians.  Six Paths Gorge was the Wulin's greatest scourge and a notorious stronghold of the Mud Cult, situated in Xiangyang, a land contested by Song and Jin. Surrounded by steep mountains, it was easily defended but hard to attack. Many who had fled the ravages of war sought refuge there; neither side dared to provoke them due to rumors of magical powers that could bewitch minds, leading to certain death for any intruders‑making it a mysterious place feared by both civilians and martial artists.  If not for having known these two physicians beforehand with respect, Qingcheng's people might have fallen into the same trap as others. However, Qingcheng had the magnanimity to trust their intentions, while Kongtong was less certain. Hearing of this situation, they believed the Tang Clan Flying Hero was in dire straits and that the Mud Cult was weakening. Considering the bond between martial artists, they could not stand idly by.  At that time, Qingcheng's group had already entered Tang Clan territory and were resting at a mountain tea house, preparing to send a letter of introduction first before having Tang Clan's welcoming disciples bring them down the mountain according to proper etiquette. Kongtong's party arrived with an imposing presence, but they did not immediately turn hostile. Seeing no signs of fear or doubt in Qingcheng's demeanor, and noting that despite his pale complexion, Tang Buyi was still jesting with passing ladies, they suspected the rumors might be incorrect.  Upon hearing Kongtong's purpose for coming, Qingcheng's group took it in stride without blaming their recklessness, instead feeling relieved. They thought of Kongtong's adherence to martial virtues and found them worthy allies. Just as they were about to offer tea as a sign of friendship, Tang Buyi suddenly vomited blood, his condition worsening dramatically, causing him to fall into unconsciousness. The doctors diagnosed this as an effect from the medicinal properties in the tea‑specifically, the Mud Cult's famous 'Five‑colored Mud', known for its ability to cure various ailments and similar to Tang Clan's Universal Oil.  Unlike Panacea Pill, which could only be used by those who had been poisoned, Five‑colored Mud was more versatile, both externally to stop bleeding and internally to enhance one's health. However, this medicine proved to be a curse on Tang Clan practitioners since they practiced Internal Skill through unconventional means, relying heavily on medicinal diets, nourishing their inner breath day and night with Pepper Powder Poison, making them toxic from the inside out.  Tang Buyi had accidentally ingested some of this poison, leading to a collapse in his Internal Force, and thus his injuries worsened. This led both Kongtong and Qingcheng to clash. One side accused the other of poisoning him, while the other defended themselves, urging everyone to focus on saving Tang Buyi's life rather than arguing. The outcome was uncertain, but the tea house suffered collateral damage as well, with many casualties.  Now weakened by his condition and affected by Five‑colored Mud, Tang Buyi could not use the poison‑curing method again; Universal Oil was of no help, and they were hesitant to administer any more medicine for fear of overburdening their organs. Although brought back to Tang Clan, everyone was at a loss as to what to do next.

You led your fellow disciples into fierce battle against both sects, badly blunting their fighting spirit. As you listened to the two sects trade accusations, the more you heard, the more alarmed you grew, until you learned that Eldest Senior Brother had been gravely wounded. You hurried down the mountainside with the Qingcheng Daoists to bring Eldest Senior Brother home.

After defeating the Qingcheng sect, the two sects kept arguing fiercely. You and your fellow disciples listened from the side, growing more alarmed by the moment, until at last you learned that Eldest Senior Brother had been gravely wounded. You hurried down the mountainside with the Qingcheng Daoists to bring him home.
After driving off the Kongtong sect, you heard from the Qingcheng disciples and only then learned their purpose‑they had come, in fact, to escort Eldest Senior Brother home to the Tang Clan.
You drove off the Kongtong sect, then hurried down the mountainside with the Qingcheng Daoists to bring the gravely wounded Eldest Senior Brother home through the mountain gate.

Hearing from the Kongtong disciples, you and your fellow disciples only then learned their intentions: originally, they had come across Eldest Senior Brother held captive by Qingcheng's men, and, unwilling to stand by at such an injustice, had stepped in to save him from their hands.
Hearing from the Qingcheng disciples, you and your fellow disciples only then learned their purpose: to escort the Eldest Senior Brother back to the Tang Clan.

Despicable as you are, you plan to wait until they both suffer defeat, then reap the fisherman's profit. Your well‑constructed plan sounds impressive, but unfortunately, you forgot that you're fundamentally incapable of calculation. Watching the situation calmly until both sides are exhausted, yet still remaining inactive, you've angered both sides.

You may be an outsider disciple, but your credentials are deep, and through constant exposure, your martial arts may not be up to par, yet your mannerisms have been fully learned. Anyone who dares to provoke the Tang Clan, regardless of the circumstances, would have the Emperor drag them down and beat them. Let alone the minor sects of Kongtong and Qingcheng.
You chose to support Kongtong in their effort to jointly resist those fellow travelers from Qingcheng of the Demon Cult.
You chose to support Qingcheng and join them in resisting Kongtong.
You and the other disciples were greatly alarmed upon hearing the news, without uttering a word, rushed into the formation, and joined Qingcheng to resist Kongtong.

Right and wrong cannot coexist; without hesitation, you drew your sword to fight, fought fiercely and emerged victorious. The other physician needed no words from you, took out the rope to tie their companion and themselves, then handed you the end of the rope, sufficient to show their sincerity.
