Good and evil cannot coexist; you acted without hesitation, drew your sword to fight, and still lost. Unexpectedly, the opponent won but then took out a rope, tied themselves up, and handed you the end of the rope. By showing weakness in this manner, it clearly demonstrates their sincerity.

You have deep ties to the Mud Cult, and you know that righteous and evil are not simply a matter of faction. These two physicians clearly do care about Qingcheng, and their willingness to declare their allegiance so openly shows real integrity. Though you still don't know their purpose, you have no wish to see them killed in the chaos, so you take it upon yourself to invite them into the Tang Clan for shelter. The two of them were startled at first, then their faces lit with relief, and they spoke without holding back, telling you that your Eldest Senior Brother had been defeated at the hands of Flying Stone Gang's Shi Gongyuan, was now gravely injured, and was being escorted home by Qingcheng.

On this day, you were at home discussing the day's cleaning duties with your fellow disciples. Suddenly, you heard someone calling for help outside the courtyard, and faintly caught the clash of steel on steel. Startled, you hurried out and found Kongtong and Qingcheng disciples inexplicably fighting on Tang Clan's own territory. Two physicians, each carrying a bamboo basket and a medicine chest, caught sight of you‑first startled, then quick to beg your help, asking you to aid the Qingcheng Daoists against their foes.  Only when you asked did you learn: these two seemingly harmless physicians were in fact members of the Demon Cult!

That bickering couple could only glare wordlessly at each other‑one wore an ingratiating smile, the other looked ready to breathe fire. Had Eldest Senior Brother not sealed the pair's mute acupoints, the wife would surely have unleashed a torrent of curses; even now, thin-skinned as she was and desperate to snap back some sharp words to cover her embarrassment, she simply couldn't get them out. After a long while, the resentment slowly melted into tenderness, and they gazed at each other as shyly as if meeting for the first time. An hour later, the acupoints released on their own, and at Gang Leader Shi's sincere pleading, Lady Shi finally agreed to go home.
You then went down the mountain together with Eldest Senior Brother and Long Xiang.
Xiahou Lan smiled faintly, without going over to exchange words with Eldest Senior Brother, gently pushed you down from the branch, and drifted away.
Xiahou Lan smiled faintly, without going over to greet Eldest Senior Brother, and gently pushed you down from the branch before gliding away with your Junior Sister.

This was exactly what Eldest Senior Brother had been waiting for.  He heard the urgent cries drawing closer but pretended not to hear them. Gang Leader Shi caught the sound too, faintly, and his heart lurched with alarm, forgetting entirely that he was still mid-duel. The instant he turned, Eldest Senior Brother seized his chance: a dart, its force driving clean through muscle and bone, struck the acupoint on his back. At once his blood and breath seized up; he could neither move nor speak.  His gaze alone crossed the crowd of onlookers and fell upon her, the one he longed for like a madman.  Before she left home, this was the very yellow robe she wore.  Just this one more glance, and he could die without regret.  Eldest Senior Brother, afraid she hadn't heard him, deliberately called out the name Flying Swallow Meteor Feather. Several streaks of cold light flashed past, slicing seven or eight shallow cuts across Gang Leader Shi's body.  This wasn't because Eldest Senior Brother's mastery of the technique let him gauge the force so precisely; in truth he was forcing himself through his wounds, fighting on until his strength finally gave out, and by the time the feathers reached Shi Gongyuan, they had already gone soft.  When Lady Shi first left home, she had once tried to take her own life. Eldest Senior Brother had performed this very Flying Swallow Meteor Feather before her then: a flask of poisoned wine looked whole and untouched at first, but the instant Lady Shi raised it to drink the poison and die, the flask shattered apart into ring after ring of neatly sliced shards, spilling the poisoned wine across the table.  The instant Lady Shi caught that flash of silver light today, she saw her husband go rigid and still. Her heart plunged as if into an ice cellar, her hands and feet trembling with cold. She dared not believe it, yet could not help but believe.  The husband she hadn't seen in a year‑one glimpse, and now the living and the dead would be parted forever.  She was both grieved and furious. Instead of reflecting on how her own flight from home had caused this whole disaster, she turned to blame Eldest Senior Brother instead: why had he kept his word so faithfully and never revealed the secret, and why wouldn't he simply let her husband kill him? She unleashed an unreasonable tirade on him without pause. Gang Leader Shi, unable to move or speak, caught every word, and each one sweetened his heart; he instantly believed his wife had kept her chastity, that nothing improper had ever passed between her and this cunning young rascal, and he was overjoyed. Then he heard his wife declare she would die to prove her fidelity, and he was so terrified his soul nearly fled his body. Luckily, Eldest Senior Brother's golden coin dart struck Lady Shi's acupoint too, forcing the couple to stand face to face, staring at one another.  Once Lady Shi steadied herself, she saw her husband's eyes rolling about, very much alive and well. Shame and fury swept over her at once, and she cursed herself silently for losing her composure like that, tricked by that sly young rascal Tang Buyi. Now that she'd said all that in front of so many people, where could she ever show her face again, how was she to go on living it down?  Most who tread the Jianghu live with blood on their blades; they had come to Woyun Ridge today for the spectacle, hoping for nothing less than a killing. Who could have guessed your Eldest Senior Brother would scheme it all into something out of a stage drama, and pull off a happy ending? Everyone couldn't help but laugh, and, taking the hint, dispersed. Before long, all the clamor had died away.  Except for the Flying Stone Gang's own men, the ridge emptied out completely within moments.

Among the onlookers, a plainly dressed young girl noticed this and hurried back toward the nearby Ciyun Nunnery. No one else noticed her, except your Eldest Senior Brother, who caught her out of the corner of his eye and quietly let out a breath of relief.

Though the Flying Stone Gang's members were a mixed lot, mostly unschooled ruffians, they were not without a sense of honor. They remembered every kindness the Tang Clan had once shown them, and seeing that today's trouble could not be easily settled, they rushed out one after another to hold back their Gang Leader. Shi Gongyuan was a man of deep feeling and loyalty; now that his wife had left with another man and his own sworn brothers were turning against him, grief and fury warred within him. All thought of glory, wealth, and renown fell away. He gave himself over to despair, swinging his fists and smashing everything in reach, deaf to every plea, wanting only to perish together with his enemy.

Eldest Senior Brother took advantage of Gang Leader Shi's busy defending. He withdrew a single Tang Clan Flying Locust Stone from his pocket. This was no ordinary stone; it was forged from refined iron and exceptionally heavy. Eldest Senior Brother did not use such a stone casually, but threw it among the storm of stones in this moment, so swiftly that nobody saw clearly. It struck Gang Leader Shi's vital point, rendering him incapacitated. Others thought Eldest Senior Brother had defeated his opponent using the opponent's own martial arts, unaware that he had secretly attacked. Although it was likewise a loss, this did not mean Tang Clan's martial arts were superior to Flying Stone Gang's. However, Shi Gongyuan was not placated; due to his resentment over the stolen wife, they could never coexist under the same sky. A mere victory or defeat was not enough for them to reconcile. With trembling resolve, Shi Gongyuan stood up and vowed to fight Eldest Senior Brother to the death.

You too had once studied that secret manual - to call it unremarkable would be generous - yet you never imagined it could be used in such a way, and it truly broadened your horizons. A thought struck you all at once, and you suddenly recalled the words of the masked elder from behind the mountain that day, crying out: "...the Tract on Losing Form - isn't this the Tract on Losing Form!"

At the height of their battle, Eldest Senior Brother suddenly employed the Flying Stone Gang's martial art 'Throwing Stones to Question Heaven'. This secret manual was merely a summary by Shi Gongyuan of his stone‑throwing insights before he tied his hair up. Later, it was duplicated by Lady Shi, who claimed that the book contained advanced techniques and could only be read by the gang members, not counting as true skills at all. Unbeknownst to them, when used by Eldest Senior Brother, it immediately underwent a transformation. The stones flew spinning and leaping, able to change direction to attack the back of their opponents. Although the power was limited, the stones could be picked up instantly, making hidden weapons inexhaustible. Eldest Senior Brother continuously tossed out one stone after another in rapid succession. In an instant, Gang Leader Shi found himself surrounded by a rain of stone projectiles from all directions.

Eldest Senior Brother and Gang Leader Shi exchanged several more moves, both realizing the fierce battle was nearing its end. As they clashed, the one who fell was none other than Eldest Senior Brother. This outcome was unexpected to all present. Though Flying Hero Tang Buyi had wandered the Jianghu for years, his reputation was not particularly good, and hatred toward him was not uncommon. Yet, no one could deny his genuine martial arts. Many renowned martial artists of the Wulin had fallen to him before, making him no easy opponent. In contrast, Gang Leader Shi had once been a mountain bandit, his martial arts skills borrowed from various schools, combining Songshan's Iron Cloth Shirt and Kongtong Iron Arm Divine Fist. His body was sturdy, his arm strength formidable, but in the end, he was merely a brute relying on brute force. Among the onlookers, most had looked down upon him, expecting Tang Buyi to win. Yet, as the fight progressed, something felt off. Gang Leader Shi had killed Tang Buyi outright. The crowd, now silent, felt uneasy, sensing something amiss. With no words to say, they gradually left, turning the once bustling Woyun Ridge into a desolate place. Only you and Fu Yun the monk rushed forward, attempting to save Eldest Senior Brother. However, when you touched his pulse, he suddenly sent a light Internal Force, shaking you. Observing his expression, though pale and sweating profusely, he seemed to be smirking, leaving you both shocked and confused. At this moment, the source of all the conflict, Lady Shi, arrived late, greeting her husband and apologizing to Eldest Senior Brother. Seeing his long‑separated wife, Gang Leader Shi was both sorrowful and joyful, unable to focus on anything else, and followed his Lady with a forced smile. Eldest Senior Brother then sat up, having deliberately chosen Woyun Ridge for the duel, feigning defeat and even pretending to die to tarnish his reputation. His aim was to force Lady Shi to emerge from her secluded Ciyun Nunnery. Fu Yun the monk greatly admired this Benefactor Tang, believing him to be compassionate and indifferent to fame and fortune. Yet, he did not realize that Eldest Senior Brother's true intention was simply to retire from the Jianghu. He had merely set the stage to let his fellow disciples know not to expect him to take over as Sect Leader, leading the Tang Clan to glory. If they all remained stagnant, clinging to him, how could he ever pursue his dream of performing on stage in the playhouses? It was utterly unreasonable.
Even though you wanted to call your master back, however you looked at it, your Eldest Senior Brother's situation was more urgent, so you could only let her go without giving chase.
Xiahou Lan watched from afar, her face clouding with displeasure, and without waiting to see how the fight would end, she swept her sleeve and turned away.

Though the Flying Stone Gang's members were a mixed lot, mostly unschooled ruffians, they were not without a sense of honor. They remembered every kindness the Tang Clan had once shown them, and seeing that today's trouble could not be easily settled, they rushed out one after another to hold back their Gang Leader. Shi Gongyuan was a man of deep feeling and loyalty; now that his wife had left with another man and his own sworn brothers were turning against him, grief and fury warred within him. All thought of glory, wealth, and renown fell away. He gave himself over to despair, swinging his fists and smashing everything in reach, deaf to every plea, wanting only to perish together with his enemy.

Putting on a show for onlookers, Eldest Senior Brother sized up the situation: Gang Leader Shi's hard-body technique was tougher than expected, and beating him without causing real harm would not be easy. What was more, he had come here already injured, making it hard to judge his own strength - the slightest slip could kill. There was nothing for it now but to swallow his pride and resort to an old Jianghu trick: feigning death. Tang Buyi had taught himself this technique long ago, and had only ever used it to duck a tavern or brothel bill he couldn't pay. Now, forced to feign death before a crowd of witnesses, he found it strangely thrilling. As Gang Leader Shi's fist came at him, he read the blow, drew in his chest, and leapt backward - a mere graze sent him flying, dissipating seven-tenths of the force. To Gang Leader Shi, the punch felt like it had struck worn leather, the sensation oddly hollow, but seeing him cough up blood put any suspicion to rest. Little did anyone know that the blood was real, though it came not from the blow but from an old wound reopening, bleeding within. Among the onlookers, a plainly dressed young girl noticed this and hurried back toward the nearby Ciyun Nunnery. No one else noticed her, except your Eldest Senior Brother, who caught her out of the corner of his eye and quietly let out a breath of relief.

Among the onlookers, a plainly dressed young girl noticed this and hurried back toward the nearby Ciyun Nunnery. No one else noticed her, except your Eldest Senior Brother, who caught her out of the corner of his eye and quietly let out a breath of relief.

Though the Flying Stone Gang's members were a mixed lot, mostly unschooled ruffians, they were not without a sense of honor. They remembered every kindness the Tang Clan had once shown them, and seeing that today's trouble could not be easily settled, they rushed out one after another to hold back their Gang Leader. Shi Gongyuan was a man of deep feeling and loyalty; now that his wife had left with another man and his own sworn brothers were turning against him, grief and fury warred within him. All thought of glory, wealth, and renown fell away. He gave himself over to despair, swinging his fists and smashing everything in reach, deaf to every plea, wanting only to perish together with his enemy.

However, the hatred of having his wife taken from him was one that could not exist under the same sky. Winning or losing was not enough to settle it. Shi Gongyuan rose to his feet, trembling, and vowed to fight your Eldest Senior Brother to the death.

As for Shi Gongyuan, he looked every bit the rough, brutish sort, his sheer toughness plain for all to see - forcing his opponent to resort even to the Divine Spear Finger just to bring him down. To lose like that was no disgrace; though defeated, he lost with honor.

But the trouble was that your Eldest Senior Brother had no idea that the Beast Path Dharma King of the Demon Cult had once used this very technique in Jiangling. This inevitably raised suspicions, and speculation among the crowd grew rampant, even though there was no evidence. Nevertheless, unfounded rumors spread far and wide, until at last the whisper took hold that the Tang Clan's Flying Hero shared some close, ill relationship with the Dharma King of the Demon Cult.

The Wulin onlookers all around dissolved into chaos, like a pot boiled over, for none of them had expected that coming here today, they would have the good fortune to witness the emergence of the Four Supreme Techniques.
You're absolutely stunned, never imagining that your Eldest Senior Brother still has this ultimate move hidden away - this certainly isn't Tang Clan martial arts at all.

Never mind that you were stunned - even your master Xiahou Lan changed countenance. She had believed that after all these years apart, her own martial arts had grown immeasurably, far beyond what they once were, and that unless your Eldest Senior Brother trained himself half to death, he would be no match for her. Moments before she had been drowsing with boredom, but the instant this technique appeared, you realized she too was so startled she nearly toppled out of the tree.

The duel reached its peak, and Eldest Senior Brother's fighting spirit soared. A sudden inspiration struck him, and he immediately unleashed the newly mastered technique. Shi Gongyuan, relying on his solid physical training, was unafraid of direct confrontation, yet he hadn't anticipated Eldest Senior Brother's finger shooting out an invisible force that pierced through his protective aura, breaking through his body. It is well known that the only techniques capable of piercing through the body with invisible force are the four ancient supreme skills, the Songshan sect's profound secret art, the Vajra Divine Spear Finger. However, the Songshan sect was destroyed twenty years ago during the Supreme Bliss Cult's attack. This technique, whether lost or not, remains a subject of debate, and along with the Kongtong Sword-Riding Technique, it is merely a legend in the Jianghu. Today, many still doubt its existence, but now, with Eldest Senior Brother demonstrating it before all eyes, the people have finally believed that such a divine skill truly exists, capable of killing an enemy from a distance. If this technique were in the hands of Songshan monks, the world would only admire and respect it. But if the Tang Clan, masters of hidden weapons, were to possess it, it would be terrifying. For the Tang Clan has no regard for social conventions; they are unafraid of ambushes, treachery, or poison. Even their visible weapons can be defended against, but Tang Buyi, having mastered the Vajra Divine Spear Finger, could kill even if stripped naked and bound with ropes. Who in the world could possibly defend against him?

Fan Xiaotian, standing nearby, cried out in dismay - so many copper coins spent as thrown hidden weapons, and even once retrieved, some would surely be lost, which seemed far too wasteful. If those coins went to her instead, wouldn't the dogs in her den get meat buns to eat every day?

Your master Xiahou Lan also lost interest, for the skills your Eldest Senior Brother demonstrated today still fell short of those from when they traveled together in the Jianghu. She had come to observe the battle in order to verify her own progress; how could it not leave her deeply disappointed?
Unless he has ulterior motives and is intentionally concealing a move while holding back, this wouldn't make sense.
You didn't know, though, whether he was holding back because his wounds hadn't yet healed, or because he was hiding a technique.

At a glance you could tell your Eldest Senior Brother wasn't fighting at full strength. Gang Leader Shi trained in an external school of hard qigong that toughened muscle and bone, backed by a body-guarding technique — his physique was solid enough, true, but the Tang Clan was the foremost house of hidden weapons under heaven. How could they simply lay down and be taken just because the enemy was built a little sturdier? Guiding force through the Coin Dart to pierce an acupoint took nothing more than a touch of Internal Force and a deft hand — even you could barely manage it, let alone your Eldest Senior Brother.
As the Coin Dart proved ineffective, you couldn't help but feel secretly anxious.

Over there, the Eldest Senior Brother and Shi Gongyuan had already begun fighting. Their martial arts styles were two extremes: one light and agile, like wind without a fixed form; the other heavy and solid, as stable as Mount Tai. The Coin Dart could not pierce Shi Gongyuan's Iron Cloth Shirt, and the Iron Arm Divine Fist could not even touch Tang Buyi's sleeve. Their movements, one dynamic and the other static, clashed in a thrilling exchange, leaving the onlookers cheering with delight.

At that moment a voice reached your ears — low and rasping, yet warm and sweet — and your heart leapt with joy, for you knew your master Xiahou Lan had come. You loosed your Qinggong and sprang up into the treetops to meet her.

At that moment a voice reached your ears — low and rasping, yet warm and sweet — and your heart leapt with joy, for you knew your master Xiahou Lan had come. You loosed your Qinggong and sprang up into the treetops to meet her, and there too was your Junior Sister, dishevelled and disguised as a beggar boy.

By the time the hour was almost up, you and your Eldest Senior Brother finally sauntered onto the scene. When enemies come face to face, their eyes burn red with hate — with no time wasted on pleasantries, a few words were exchanged and then fists flew. You stepped back to watch the fight.

Long Xiang, who was also present, drew eyes she never meant to draw — unaware that even as men admired her beauty, they laughed at her behind her back. Word of how easily she was swindled out of her money spread further than tales of her chivalry; every time she went out, Beggar Sect disciples would spot her and light up like hunters sighting game, for she was more free with her coin than the legendary alms-giving maiden herself. Had it not been for the old friendship between Gang Leader Wang and Lady Wen, and for Jinxiang Palace's standing in the Jianghu, she might well have been swindled out of not just her money, but her virtue besides.

Long Xiang, who was also present, picked up another nickname there: Chicken Leg Assassin. Though most who coined it meant it as a joke, she rather liked it herself. Preening, she even composed half a verse: "Slay every wicked soul on earth, savor every fine chicken upon it." Word of it reached Jinxiang Palace, and Lady Wen was mortified by her beloved disciple's antics — she ordered a rattan cane made ready, meaning to thrash Long Xiang within an inch of her life the moment she returned, then hire a tutor to teach her to read from the beginning.

Long Xiang, who also arrived on the scene, found herself unwillingly drawing every eye, and the name Murderous Demon of Jinxiang Palace spread further still. She had always walked Jianghu upholding justice — how had she ended up with such an infamous name instead? The root cause was your Eldest Senior Brother; he was the one who had coined it. There were times Long Xiang resented him so bitterly she truly wanted to strip the tendons from his bones.

By the time the Tang Clan Flying Hero and the Flying Stone Gang Leader's scheduled duel arrived, martial artists from all over Shu gathered to witness the event, as expected. Young talents from Emei and Qingcheng arrived on time, and even the Soul-Stealing Orchid from distant Kongtong was present. The Flying Stone Gang Leader waited impatiently, yet your Eldest Senior Brother, the main event, was still nowhere to be seen as the appointed time neared.

Through your persistent questioning, Eldest Senior Brother finally revealed his grudge with the Flying Stone Gang. It turned out that he had already investigated the gang before it became a formidable force. Coincidentally, he witnessed Gang Leader Shi and Lady Shi arguing in the courtyard. Perched on the rooftop, Eldest Senior Brother couldn't help but chuckle: the gallant leader, so imposing and full of bluster in public, was submissive at home — a henpecked fellow who feared his wife as though she were a tigress. Amusing as it was, the longer he listened to the couple talk, the more astonished he grew. It turned out that it was not Gang Leader Shi but delicate Lady Shi who harbored the ambition to build up the Flying Stone Gang and rival the Tang Clan. Gang Leader Shi, for his part, bowed and pleaded with her, urging that one must never forget a kindness, however small. He told her that in years past they had abandoned their mountain stronghold and fled as refugees from Tanzhou, journeying all the way west into Shu with no idea how to earn a living — forced to hide from officials, unable to do business. The locals, wary of his fierce looks and foreign birth, refused to hire him, nearly starving them into gritting their teeth and returning to the mountains to take up their old trade. It was the Tang Clan's Righteous Field that had taken them in; the pay was meager, but enough to give them a foothold in life, pulling them back from the brink and letting them set aside the thought of risking everything again. In time they were able to make their own way and found the Flying Stone Gang, taking on rough labor and odd jobs to survive. Now that the Flying Stone Gang had grown big and strong, they had set their sights on the Tang Clan — was that not the height of ingratitude? Their argument grew heated. However hard Gang Leader Shi's outer skills, they were no match for his wife's volley of slaps; raising a hand to block her, his fingers brushed her tender cheek by accident. His three fingers held together were bigger than her whole palm — the touch, though unintentional, only stung and did no harm — but ever since she had known him, he had always cradled her in his palm like a flower he feared to crush with the slightest carelessness, never once bearing to speak a harsh word to her, let alone strike her. In an instant her heart brimmed with hurt, tears welling in her eyes; furious beyond bearing, she stamped her foot and stormed off. Gang Leader Shi, tongue‑tied, dared not chase after her; by the time he finally came to his senses and went after her, she had already vanished. Eldest Senior Brother was unsure whether to comfort this fellow or go after Lady Shi. After much thought, he decided that with Lady Shi alone and unaccompanied, not even a maid at her side, trouble might easily befall her, so he followed in secret to protect her. Only after exhausting every kind word did he talk her out of throwing herself from a cliff, and he found her a place to stay. Lady Shi's temperament was fierce; she threatened to take her own life if Eldest Senior Brother ever revealed her whereabouts, warning that her death would turn the Flying Stone Gang and the Tang Clan into deadly enemies beyond any reconciliation. Unable to find a way out, Eldest Senior Brother reluctantly agreed. Clever as he had been his whole life, this was his single greatest blunder — for he assumed Lady Shi would cool down within a few days, think things through, and return home. Who could have known this lady was as stubborn as an ox — she truly held her grudge, and to this day refuses to come out, turning a trivial domestic spat into a feud between two whole factions.

With Eldest Senior Brother's pace, this trip's progress was unusually slow. Sometimes walking, sometimes hiring a vehicle, they leisurely walked for several days before finally reaching the village near Woyun Ridge, staying at an inn to rest and regain their strength.

Except for Junior Martial Sister. One troubled glance from her, without a word spoken, said more than anyone else's thousand words could. Only then did everyone finally set their hearts at ease. If Eldest Senior Brother traveled with someone else, people would not feel nearly so easy about it, but with you it was different. Though you are the Tang Clan's last outer disciple, never granted its true teachings, you stand as steady as an old tree or a stubborn boulder — as if even burning the Tang family compound to the ground couldn't drive you off. Now and then you wander out, but however far you travel, you always come back. With you at his side, even if Eldest Senior Brother sprouted wings, he'd find it hard to fly away.
Eldest Senior Brother specifically called out your name to join him, but as soon as you heard, you immediately didn't want to go. No one could persuade you.

It's fortunate that Eldest Senior Brother named you specifically to come along; the others aren't trusted quite so much, but you are different. Though you are the Tang Clan's last outer disciple, never granted its true teachings, you stand as naturally as an old tree on the mountainside or a stubborn boulder — as if even burning the Tang family compound to the ground couldn't drive you off. Now and then you wander out, but however far you go, you always come back. With you along, even if Eldest Senior Brother sprouted wings, he'd find it hard to fly away.
Third Senior Brother was really uneasy, and since there were fellow disciples who volunteered to follow, he immediately agreed.

On the day Eldest Senior Brother was to set out, all the martial siblings living in the main compound gathered at the training ground. Eldest Senior Brother was to duel the Flying Stone Gang Leader on Woyun Ridge, taking no one from the sect along to help him, which left people both reassured and uneasy. Reassured, because he seemed to have a plan and this feud might finally be settled. Uneasy, because with no one to watch over him, what would they do if he were struck by some sudden whim along the way, lured astray by a pretty face, and wandered off to vanish without a trace?

While discussing strategies against the Kongtong sect, you dragged everyone into the water by revealing the secret of the Kongtong Secret Treasure. Soon after, word spread, and all the world knew the Kongtong Secret Treasure had fallen into outside hands. Kongtong was thrown into turmoil — some fled, others schemed to seize power. Sect Leader Wei, blamed for failing to guard the Secret Treasure, was showered with criticism and forced into seclusion in his cave, rarely emerging from then on, sighing the whole day through, lamenting only that he had once again trusted the wrong person — for it is not only handsome men, fair as Pan An, who tell lies; even the ugly ones may be no good either.

Third Senior Brother was entrusted by the Sect Leader with arranging Junior Martial Sister's lifelong affairs. Though Junior Martial Sister is simple‑hearted and rather clueless about matters of love, perhaps she is merely a late bloomer. Yet in this turbulent Jianghu, there's no telling how many peaceful days remain, and with fierce enemies lurking on every side, a decision must be made without delay. If Eldest Senior Brother and Junior Martial Sister truly harbor no feelings for one another, then eyes must be kept open to find her a good, dependable husband. Once she marries out, she will no longer belong to the Tang Clan — save for a calamity grave enough to implicate the whole clan to the ninth degree of kin. Otherwise, an invisible wall will stand between her and her natal family's feuds and debts from then on: none of it hers to answer for, none of it to touch her.

Eldest Senior Brother recounted vividly the thousand‑mile journey since his disappearance from Jiangling. He first intervened in the battle at Xiangyang, aiding the Song soldiers to repel the Jin forces, meeting and drinking with the Daoist general Danxiazi and the Xiangyang commander Zhao Fang. The next morning he vanished without a word, heading north, along the way casually looking after the business of a few brothels, and skillfully pilfering from Jin travelers to relieve the girls who worked there — the rarest kindness they'd known. Over drinks, flushed with wine, he learned that the mountain bandits of Yingtian, Kaifeng, Henan, and Hezhong seemed to be banding together for some grand oath-taking assembly, though what great venture they planned he could not say. After much more asking around, he learned that the Jin emperor Wanyan Xun, on receiving some secret letter from who-knows-whom, had suddenly decided to visit the front lines to comfort his troops. To the Song these bandits were rebels, but to the Jin they were righteous men — and so they had banded together to plot this venture: success would bring fame and fortune, perhaps even a place in history; failure would mean only death. Eldest Senior Brother's eyes lit up, and he alone strode into the bandits' stronghold, offering his fists as a calling card. Skilled as he was, even he could not fight off the whole gathered host of that greenwood alone. Reckless as Eldest Senior Brother's ways were, he was no mere brute — that day, only by putting his own life on the line could he fully show them his admiration. He held off a hundred men single-handed, facing death without flinching, while the bandit brothers ambushed the Jin emperor's procession — an equally noble act of sacrifice. Had he not fought until he was spent and reeling, how could these greenwood heroes ever have been won over by words alone? After that battle, Eldest Senior Brother was hailed as king of the bandits, given command of every stronghold's righteous men, and led them in ambushing the Jin emperor Wanyan Xun. He had first meant to emulate the assassin of Bolangsha, who once hurled his blow at the First Emperor of Qin, by flinging a heavy hidden weapon from the high ground of the gorge road to smash Wanyan Xun's carriage. But the man was suspicious by nature, and had his attendants ride the main carriage while he himself rode humbly in a second — and so he narrowly escaped that blow. His first strike having failed, Eldest Senior Brother seized the moment before the Jin emperor's convoy could join the main Jin army, and called the bandits down the slope for a charge. The fighting turned to slaughter; seeing no way to break through the ranks of defenders, he simply seized a banner and a horse to draw the Jin soldiers into giving chase, waving the banner as he charged straight for their camp. The marshal Pusan Anzhen, riding out to meet him, saw how fiercely he came on, and cursed him loudly, crying that he was a rebel and that he himself came under the Emperor's own order to lead the troops and seize him. Eldest Senior Brother turned the charge straight back on him, in the same breath swearing that it was he who bore the Emperor's secret command to arrest the marshal for treason. Pusan Anzhen's face went the color of ash; he dared not resist, telling himself the innocent need fear nothing, and so stripped off his armor and let himself be bound, crying out his innocence and begging that the Emperor look into the matter. But before the Emperor could ever clear his name, Eldest Senior Brother had already struck off his head with a single blow. Though the plot to assassinate the Jin emperor came to nothing, cutting down the Jin's own marshal in its place was still no small feat. The three of you, and Junior Martial Sister besides, listened utterly dumbstruck. You, at least, held your tongue, but Third Senior Brother and Fourth Senior Brother refused to believe a word of it — Eldest Senior Brother's boasting was, after all, notorious. Eldest Senior Brother only shrugged, smiling ruefully: believe it or not, as far as he was concerned, he'd done his duty in the telling.

Eldest Senior Brother treats the Flying Stone Gang, the sect's great looming threat, as nothing at all; he has his own clever plan to subdue them without bloodshed and turn foe into friend. As the saying goes, he who tied the bell must be the one to untie it, and with such confidence in him, everyone breathed a sigh of relief. As for the matter of Second Senior Brother, Eldest Senior Brother seemed lost in thought, unwilling to readily believe his junior brother would betray his master and desert the Tang Clan — there had to be some hidden reason. Once the pressing matters were settled, he would surely set out one day, hunt him down, beat him soundly, and force the truth out of him.

Junior Martial Sister was overjoyed to see Eldest Senior Brother return. However, he did not wish for her to cling to him, so he shooed her off. Junior Martial Sister reached out to pat him but couldn't, and at a loss, could only puff her cheeks in a sulk and retreat to one side.

Eldest Senior Brother didn't want her clinging to him, so he shooed her off. Junior Martial Sister wasn't persistent either; she let go of Eldest Senior Brother's hem and came to grab onto you instead. You were flattered and surprised, thinking she had grown up and would no longer depend on you like that. Unexpectedly, today's emotional turmoil made her involuntarily grab your sleeve. This shows that although she cultivates her mind and restrains herself daily, deep down she still greatly depends on you. Regardless of your appearance, as long as you are close to her, it's enough to set her mind at ease.
This time, Eldest Senior Brother came downstairs with Junior Martial Sister in tow.

Eldest Senior Brother heard of the Tang Clan's string of recent misfortunes yet remained as calm as ever, leaving the three of you brothers both angered and reassured, as if the sky had not yet fallen — mere trifles to him. Eldest Senior Brother politely declined the Sect Leader's token, letting Third Senior Brother go on holding it in his stead; he judged his own judgment inferior to Third Senior Brother's, so it was best each attend to his own charge — internal affairs to Third Senior Brother, and outside threats to himself. Once this was swiftly settled, Eldest Senior Brother went upstairs to see the Sect Leader, while the three of you went off to spread word of his return, and the whole clan was lifted in spirit.

As the three of you argued the situation without end, swearing oaths and praying for Eldest Senior Brother's speedy return, he suddenly appeared, as unconcerned as always, as if nothing had happened. In an instant, you three felt both joy and anger: joy that the Flying Hero had returned, giving the sect a pillar to lean on; anger that he had vanished for so long without a word, leaving you all needlessly worried he had met with danger, only to find it was all for nothing, for he was simply an unreliable wandering rogue. It was strange, really. Whenever he was away, you always hoped he had merely been delayed by pleasure and was simply late to return, yet the moment he came swaggering home with that foolish grin, the urge to kill him surged up despite yourselves.

Perhaps it is more accurate to say that Eldest Senior Brother saw the situation clearly and lured the Gang Leader's wife away into hiding. This left the Flying Stone Gang Leader too wary of endangering her to act rashly, and that is why the situation has held stable until now.

It would be better to thank Eldest Senior Brother for his foresight. He lured the gang leader's wife away and hid her, leaving the Flying Stone Gang Leader too wary of endangering her to act rashly, and that is why the situation has held stable until now. Unfortunately, you have no idea where Lady Shi is hiding. Otherwise, you could capture her, poison her, and torture her, and see if Gang Leader Shi still dares to be so aggressive.

Third Senior Brother and Fourth Senior Brother are the only senior brothers left in the Tang Clan today. They have witnessed the Tang Clan's decline from prosperity, its resurrection, and its survival to this day. With rich Jianghu experience, they understand that the conflict between our clan and the Flying Stone Gang is not solely due to the misconduct of Eldest Senior Brother. At most, it's just a pretext. The real cause, in truth, lies in fame and profit. You must know that the Tang Clan has taken root in Shu, and our reputation and influence have been built up over generations. In our territory, the people of the villages and towns have received the Tang Clan's kindness for generations. Though the younger generation may not yet realize it, the elders do. When the Tang Clan was at its peak, its prestige was unmatched. In times of natural disasters or human calamities, people would not first turn to the authorities, but instead seek the Tang Clan. The official court is full of officials who collude and cannot deliver justice, but at the Tang Clan, grievances are surely resolved. Among the three great families, only the Tang Clan dares to confront the Imperial Court head‑on. Now, if the Flying Stone Gang wishes to gain people's support and expand its territory to become a top‑tier martial gang in the Wulin, the Tang Clan of Shu is its number one rival. Even if the Tang Clan has no intention of competing, the Flying Stone Gang will certainly not tolerate it. Once they spot an opportunity, they will provoke a conflict, defeat the Tang Clan, and take its place.

You've hesitated to speak several times, though you know the Eldest Senior Brother's whereabouts. However, considering the Sect Leader's intention to keep the disciples unaware, even the Third Senior Brother and Fourth Senior Brother cannot speak out. You fear that rumors might spread, causing the disciples to panic and lose their composure.
It isn't as though you and Third Senior Brother didn't try to make peace—but plead as you might, the man's wife was simply nowhere to be found, and however sincere you were, it came to nothing.

Since the day Eldest Senior Brother's figure vanished from Jiangling, the vast Wulin of the Central Plains has not heard anyone speak of the Flying Hero's deeds, as if this person had vanished into thin air. This has greatly distressed your Third Senior Brother. Shi Gongyuan, Leader of the Flying Stone Gang, had once agreed to a duel with Eldest Senior Brother—Shi Gongyuan set the date, while Eldest Senior Brother chose the location; your Eldest Senior Brother has never been one to shy away from battle, yet unexpectedly, he missed the appointment. In the usual Wulin, if one party fails to show up for a duel, the witness would declare the opponent a coward, resulting in a loss without a fight, which is more humiliating than losing the duel itself. If this could settle the matter, though embarrassing, it would not be without merit. However, the unfortunate situation is that Eldest Senior Brother took the gang leader's wife away, and her whereabouts remain unknown to this day. As long as she has not returned, how can Gang Leader Shi save face and let the matter rest? Time and again, he has sent challenge letters to the Tang Clan, but Eldest Senior Brother has not responded to any of them. This has left Shi Gongyuan furious, and in this latest letter, he has cut out the usual Jianghu pleasantries, stating plainly that if there is no response to the challenge, he will lead the entire Flying Stone Gang to attack the Tang Clan and bloody the Tang Family Courtyard. Even if you all possess great martial skills and are not afraid of the Flying Stone Gang, they will employ a strategy of overwhelming numbers, burying you under a mountain of corpses, and they are willing to suffer mutual destruction.

Before leaving, Shangguan Ying suddenly turned around and began speaking about her own story. She once had a personal maid, Shu Rong, who was like a sister to her. Although she was deeply reluctant, she could not disobey her Family Head's orders and could only watch helplessly as her personal maid was given away to someone else. After that, no matter how good or numerous the people who came after, they could never fill Shu Rong's place. The Eldest Young Lord Nangong didn't want her, yet Shangguan Ying still cherished the memory. Wei Ju, Sect Leader Wei, was the one she considered her closest friend, irreplaceable. The bond you share is also a treasure she would never trade. Even if you don't appreciate it, she still has to help you. Who hasn't rebelled before, and argued with their parents? After parting ways with you, Shangguan Ying's first action was to visit Lu Weng, the Tang Clan's creditor, and under the name of the Cang Gang Ship Company's chief organizer, she promised to let them have a share of the profits, thereby relieving part of the Tang Clan's debt. Upon learning of the Sect Leader's serious illness, Lu Weng felt countless emotions and generously waived the old debt from the previous generation, which had been used to buy grain and aid the people during a year of famine.

Shangguan Ying, though she had decided at the last moment to switch sides and support the Tang Clan, at most it was just her own opinion. Amid the chaos of battle, her Cang Gang disciples, following their Family Head's orders, remained neutral, and even if they did not help either side, it was enough to show their stance. That day, the discarded Tang Clan disciple Tang Shouhong, who had led the Guangzhou Tang Clan to cause trouble, and Chan Master Shi Ming were seasoned veterans, vastly different from the greenhorn Flying Stone Gang Leader. They had witnessed the Tang Clan at its peak and the full glory of Tang Zhongling. At that time, the Tang Clan Sect Leader was more fearsome than gods; when he stood on the same side as the righteous, all the villains retreated; when he opposed the righteous, even the six major sects' experts had to be summoned by the Nangong family to mediate. Because Tang Zhongling had been the Sect Leader for decades, the two had dared not approach Shu for years. Today, without the backing of the Shangguan family, how could they dare to come and cause trouble? In the end, the Shangguan family bears the responsibility. Shangguan Ying could not command her servants, nor could she show weakness to others, enduring the sneers of the Tang Clan disciples. Upon hearing you had awakened, she was overjoyed and rushed to the Zhengxin Hall, only to be immediately asked to leave. Shangguan Ying ordered her servants not to approach you, walking beside you in silence, her heart full of anxiety, vaguely knowing that things had already gone beyond repair, and the moment of parting had arrived. How could you not want to travel with her, to laugh and enjoy life together? Yet, people do not live solely for themselves. Behind you was the Tang Clan, and behind her was the Shangguan family. Parting from her and drawing a clear line was your way of protecting her. Such a good person should stay as far away from the chaos of the Jianghu as possible.

You arrive at the Zhengxin Hall to pay respects to the Acting Sect Leader. Fellow disciples met just yesterday, yet today's encounter brings a sense of melancholy. Despite Tang Clan's internal strife and the widespread chaos with bloodstains everywhere, even within Zhengxin Hall, there still hangs a light smoke, giving an air of seclusion from the world, though people have changed. Though they repelled their powerful enemy, the victory was bittersweet, leaving them in a state akin to strays. Shi Ming, the Zen Master, escaped and spread rumors that turned right into wrong. One side portrayed him as a benevolent hermit, while the other depicted Tang Clan as a family of both good and evil, making anyone inclined to believe the former. Within just one night, Tang Clan disregarded their kinship and indiscriminately killed their fellow disciples, causing rumors to spread far and wide. The whispers that Tang Clan were followers of the Demon Cult also joined these tales, gaining momentum on its own. They say the Tang Clan's Sect Master has too much malevolence, and that even Zen Master Shi Ming's teachings could not reform him. In the end he reaped what he had sown: his own cultivation turned against him and consumed him from within, and the once-legendary eccentric was left bedridden, reduced to a ruined man. At this time of peril with formidable enemies surrounding them, should Third Senior Brother punish these fake Tang Clan members who caused trouble, it would confirm such rumors and expose their weaknesses. When the Songshan Sect or Nangong Family comes to mediate, how could they explain themselves? Third Senior Brother finds himself in a dilemma and can only take precautions by withdrawing the order for searching Eldest Senior Brother, instructing disciples to defend the stronghold to avoid enemies taking advantage of their vulnerability.

You slowly regained consciousness the next day. Fellow disciples came to summon you, and at first, you thought it was because the sect leader had revived, which filled you with joy. But soon you realized that everything you feared was reality. The pleasant days of the past were now distant memories. Society suddenly changed, and even though we tried our best to resist, we could not hold back the tide. We were left without choice, swept away by a great flood, floating and sinking helplessly. The tears in your mouth tasted both bitter and salty. Only now do you realize that this is the true face of the Jianghu.

Third Senior Brother held the token entrusted by the sect leader, commanding the disciples to descend the mountain in pursuit, yet all returned empty‑handed. Junior Martial Sister returned home in a state of disarray, but could not even speak a word to her father before collapsing by the bed, her small hands gently tapping the sect leader's body, silent tears cascading onto her chest. Without the sect leader, the disciples lost their support, and with Eldest Senior Brother missing and Second Senior Brother having defected, the Tang Clan faced internal and external troubles. Even if they drove away the strong enemies, there was no cause for celebration; no one was without worry, their expressions solemn. That night, many disciples left without saying goodbye.

You and Third Senior Brother have fought battle after battle today and are already exhausted. What's more, learning of your true origins has left your Mood shaken, and the paralytic poison from Second Senior Brother has robbed you of the strength to give chase. You can only watch helplessly as Second Senior Brother strides away.

Among the Tang Clan, you are the one who gets scolded the most by the Second Senior Brother. As your friendship deepens, you can faintly glimpse the compassionate heart of a healer behind his iron face. Your trust in him is no less than your trust in the Eldest Senior Brother.

Second Senior Brother, disregarding his own severe injuries, hurried into the hall and pushed you aside to reach the Sect Leader's pulse. His expression changed at once. You and Third Senior Brother still hoped for a miraculous recovery, but instead Second Senior Brother suddenly and without warning asked about the Sect Leader's token of authority. The moment he had his answer, he showed no mercy—he forced a pill into the Sect Leader's mouth and clamped a hand over it to make him swallow. Third Senior Brother recognized the pill and tried to stop him, but it was already too late; shocked, urgent, grieved and furious all at once, he demanded to know what Second Senior Brother meant by this. The pill was the Corpse Heart Pill, the living poison the Supreme Bliss Cult had once used to control figures of the Jianghu twenty years ago, in the days it plagued the Wulin. On contact with blood this poison breaks its wax seal and bursts free, burrowing into the body and disguising itself as living flesh; no physician, however skilled, can drive it out. Once the poison-worm has lodged in the brain, the victim cannot even end their own life without the poisoner's leave—it is a thing of utter malice. Third Senior Brother had seen countless hardened heroes reduced by this poison to something neither man nor ghost; even the Master's late wife had once been struck by it and held in another's power, the root of endless sorrow to come. After the Supreme Bliss Cult fell, he had believed this poison burned with it—never dreaming that, years later, it would be used against his own Sect Leader. How could this not fill him with shock and rage?
The Sect Leader inquired about your symptoms, intending to test you, yet you were overwhelmed with grief, tears bursting forth uncontrollably.

The Sect Leader inquired about the symptoms, intending to test you. You hesitated, unable to speak, and instead claimed you were not skilled enough in your craft, unable to recognize this pulse, and insisted that Second Senior Brother must return to make the diagnosis. Your nervous lie did not escape the Sect Leader's notice, who merely smiled knowingly.

You respectfully approached to take the pulse, and couldn't help but feel alarmed and pale. But upon feeling the pulse, it was shallow, extremely weak, yet accompanied by a rapid heartbeat. This was no ordinary condition‑it was a cut‑off pulse, symbolizing the Sect Leader's qi and Lifeforce nearing exhaustion, an extremely perilous situation. Fortunately, the Sect Leader's profound Internal Force allowed him to force the use of Internal Force to sustain his life; otherwise, no ordinary person would have survived until now.

You respectfully stepped forward to take the pulse, your heart suddenly filled with alarm. The pulse was superficial, extremely weak, yet the heartbeat was abnormally rapid, indicating a severed pulse. This signified that the Sect Leader's qi and Lifeforce had completely depleted, their Internal Force utterly exhausted. Ordinary human techniques could no longer save them, and within moments, they might ascend to the heavens.

Second Senior Brother isn't here, so it wasn't supposed to be done, but since you're really worried about the Sect Leader's condition, you dared to ask for a pulse check. The Sect Leader was surprised and laughed, immediately agreed, called you forward, and handed over the pulse gate. He has many enemies in his life and never easily handed over the Pulse Gate to others, except for his master, his deceased wife, and Second Senior Brother, only you.

The first person you thought of was the Junior Martial Sister. Raised under the Sect Leader's strict discipline, she had never once been allowed past the gate of the Tang Family Courtyard without an elder brother or sister at her side, and even now she still couldn't tell one mountain path from another. Lost alone somewhere in the woods, there was no telling how frightened she must be, so you asked to go and bring her home yourself. The Sect Leader had always doted on this precious daughter of his above all else, yet today, quite unlike himself, he insisted on keeping you there instead. It was not only the Junior Martial Sister he was anxious about—he was worried for you as well.

The master saw you hesitating to speak, how could he not know what thoughts were burning in your mind. His eyes lowered, even though he was still awake, he seemed to have fallen into a dream, recalling the year you came. A weak, dirty, ugly boy, barefoot, carrying three ripe chicken eggs as a token of respect, knocking on the mountain gate. You probably yourself no longer remember, back then the boy could barely speak, tears streaming down his face, the hardships of the world clouding his eyes, despair washing over you like rain, thin and pale. The master said nothing, but the other disciples laughed, not even worth the trouble of taking your eggs, let alone giving you ten to send you away. Yet the master alone made a decision, seeing the small flame in your heart about to fade, he carefully protected it in his hands. He had some words in his heart, but didn't say them to you back then: Hope you still believe in hope. There will be good things. You were brave. From that moment on, the master in your heart quietly took the place of your father. But you didn't know that on the day you left home, your biological father couldn't sleep, suddenly rising, telling his wife he was going out. He took the only poultry in the house, followed you all the way from Mianyang, secretly protecting you. Seeing you fall, he dared not help you up; seeing you cry, he dared not recognize you, fearing he would be unable to part with his flesh and blood. The master thought you father had brought two chickens, silently taking them, requesting the Tang Clan to take better care of you. However, the simple farmer's request was entirely opposite. He believed you were dull‑witted, even if you practiced martial arts, you would still be of no use, and one day, in an ordinary life, you would lie dead on the road, no one caring. Therefore, he begged the master to swear not to take you as a disciple, keeping you away from the chaos of the Jianghu, making you an outsider disciple, serving the great heroes, that was your farmer's child's destined path. When you grew a bit older, you would go down the mountain to find your own place in life, not expecting you to achieve fame and return home, only hoping you would not quarrel with others, be free from misfortune, and grow up safely in places unseen by him. You only now learn the truth, both sorrowful and furious, overwhelmed with mixed emotions. Now your father's face has gradually faded from your memory, but his wish still shapes your life. The master originally thought you would stay only a few years, then become disheartened and seek another master. Who would have thought the Tang Clan's branches would scatter, yet you remained by his side. Everyone laughed at your ugliness, but the master took pride in you, watching you grow up, even if you didn't learn martial arts, each of you would have a promising future. He knew his life was coming to an end, fearing that after his passing, you would have no one to protect you, he wished you to be more outgoing, find a good place, and leave far away, no longer thinking of the Tang Clan, not wasting your life. But if you wished to stay, the mountain gate would always be open to you, even if you didn't bear the Tang surname, you would still be a member of the Tang Clan.

The outcome had been decided, but the dust had not yet settled. Second Senior Brother was locked in a brutal struggle with Shi Ming the Zen Master, its result still unclear; Third and Fourth Senior Brother were busy restoring order; the Junior Martial Sister was stranded somewhere in the mountains, unable to return for now. Zhengxin Hall stood empty, with only you left waiting at the Master's side. The Master sat with his eyes closed, resting, unmoving for a long while, his breath faint. Had his chest not still risen and fallen ever so slightly, you would almost have believed he had already passed from this world. Thinking back over everything that had happened, you were overcome with feeling—unwilling to watch the Master die before your eyes, yet unable to keep resentment from creeping in. The words the Martial Uncle, Tang Shouhong, had spoken moments ago were like poison dropped into the well of your heart; even now it was spreading, seeping outward, tinting your whole self some other color. You wanted to ask him outright, but the words would not come.
Seeing that matters here were settled, and with no wish to watch others sort out their family affairs, Xiahou Lan took her leave first.

Xiahou Lan paused in thought, then said something startling: she asked the sect leader to look after Xiaomei with special care. To anyone else, the remark would have passed unnoticed, but Xiaomei herself was struck dumb. Ever since that regrettable incident years ago had changed Xiahou Lan so utterly, the Kongtong Four Maidens had never again been as close as they once were; no matter how hard Xiaomei tried to win her back, Xiahou Lan had looked straight through her. Why, then, only now that Xiaomei had left home, did she suddenly put on the airs of an elder sister?

Soul-Stealing Orchid was renowned and infamous in the Jianghu. Her name echoed far and wide, yet she also faced widespread controversy. The reason she avoided being the target of mass criticism was due to her respect for Kongtong Sect and her reclusive nature. Even so, many virtuous individuals from various sects looked down upon her and strictly forbade their disciples from befriending her. When Xiahou Lan initially met her friends in the Jianghu, almost all of them distanced themselves from her, cutting off all ties. She did not care for their flattery or expect to be well‑liked.   She had heard that Tang Clan's patriarch was known for his fiery temper and thought he would erupt in anger upon learning she had been admitted as his disciple. However, the patriarch remained unconcerned; having established himself over the years, he had offended people from both the righteous and dark sides of society‑how could one be blinded by rumors to judge others' character? Moreover, today's success in repelling the enemy made this junior particularly significant. Xiahou Lan found a profound sense of mutual admiration upon meeting her senior master, who was well‑known for his worldliness and persona. The elder and younger met with a clear understanding and respect.  With the patriarch's approval, Xiahou Lan agreed to occasionally visit Tang Clan as a guest. If confronted by troublemakers, she would deal with them as gifts. This implied that she intended to unleash a massacre. Fortunately or unfortunately, those who crossed her path today were not spared.

Tang Shouhong kept Master Shi Ming around, and then he crowned his disciples with praise. Noticing that he didn't mention himself, you stepped forward and awkwardly inquired about joining the sect. However, Tang Shouhong showed a troubled expression, quickly putting on a smile and kindly advising you not to rush, saying you needed to find an auspicious day to announce it. Before that, he suggested you should put in more effort and accomplish a few significant tasks. When the time came, your master would accept you into the sect, ensuring that it wouldn't attract gossip. This was for your own good, do you understand? You understood.  After that, the Jianghu was filled with unending storms. Under the leadership of the new sect leader, the Tang Clan relied on their connections and indeed stood firm. However, in order to please the righteous and demonstrate loyalty, they changed their name, no longer calling themselves the Tang Clan, but instead the Wulin Alliance Shu Branch.  After the Mud Cult was destroyed and the situation stabilized, Tang Shouhong served as the sect leader for a few more years before stepping down as promised, restoring his ancestral surname to 'Zhuang.' He then took the elite disciples of the sect to the Wulin Alliance's base, where he was honored as a Military Strategist, second only to one, held in high esteem.  After taking office, he continued to issue commands, remotely controlling the Wulin Alliance Shu Branch to work for him, while deliberately suppressing any signs of dissent among you. For his verbal promises, you risked your life and achieved countless merits, yet all your contributions were cleverly taken away by your master and attributed to others, benefiting them instead. The Tang Clan was gone, and you remained an outsider disciple.  Later, the Wulin Alliance Shu Branch reformed, no longer practicing martial arts, but specializing in the production of weapons for the Great Heroes of the Wulin Alliance. You felt disheartened and withdrew from the Jianghu, but you had long lost your home.
Shangguan Ying came to bid farewell, not even sparing you a glance. She also practiced Buddhism, but she and Tang Shouhong had little in common, and after a brief exchange, she left.

Shangguan Ying, having switched sides in the thick of battle, was met with scorn on every hand, and came to take her leave. Tang Shouhong could not touch her, but threatened her all the same with a smile that never reached his eyes. Shangguan Ying had obeyed her father without question her whole life; this once she defied him, and this was how it ended. Dwelling on what might follow, she could not stop herself from shaking. You tried to speak up for her, only to be met with a furious tirade—she wanted nothing to do with a beast's false benevolence. She had taken a stand for what was right, throwing in her lot with the Tang Clan; you, for your own gain, cut down the head of your own house with your own hand, and drove the Junior Martial Sister who had doted on you since childhood to take her own life. If that is not a beast, then what manner of man deserves the name? Your heart is uglier than your face, and nothing you have suffered in this life was undeserved. After she severed all ties with you, within a few years word came that she had married off to Japan, and after that, no news of her ever reached you again.

With the greater good in mind, he could no longer shelter Ye Yunzhou and Ye Yunshang, the two Diancang traitors. Ye Yunzhou was away gathering medicine and not on the mountain, so Tang Shouhong took it upon himself to send Ye Yunshang back to Diancang, vowing he would write a letter pleading for the two siblings; on the strength of his life-and-death friendship with the Diancang Twin Venerables, however grave their offense, they would surely be dealt with leniently. Reluctant as you were, you could only trust him. It was said afterward that Ye Yunshang, shamed and wronged, hanged herself in grief and fury. Her brother, desperate to save her, stormed Diancang alone, sword in hand, cutting down countless men until the snow on Diancang's peaks ran red. In the end he never even saw his sister's face one last time before he fell beneath the black and white blades of the Diancang Twin Venerables. The Diancang Sect, its strength shattered, closed its gates to recover, and for a hundred years thereafter had no dealings with the Central Plains—struck from the roll of the Six Great Sects.

Putting the greater good first, Tang Shouhong ordered Xiaomei to be sent back to the Kongtong Sect to quell their anger and reestablish friendly relations. Rumors spread across the Jianghu that the Kongtong Four Maidens had all married the new sect leader. The Lady Mei you saw at the Wulin Assembly was not the Xiaomei you knew, but another woman named Xiaomei. The Xiaomei you knew vanished like a wisp of smoke, her traces erased as if she had never existed.

With the Master dead, the sect's fate was sealed. Tang Shouhong took command of Zhengxin Hall and set himself up as the new sect leader. Those who refused to submit were driven off the mountain, though not slaughtered outright. Whether from false pity or true, this act won him applause on every side, and the Jianghu spoke of him as a man of great benevolence and honor.

The Junior Martial Sister never dreamed that you would turn on her so viciously. Her heart was already in turmoil, and the Mental Formula, Heaven and Earth, Soundless, crumbled of its own accord as she fought. The longer the battle went on, the colder her heart grew; all she could think was: Father is gone—from now on I am an orphan. If I go now, can I walk the road to the underworld beside him a little further? She gave up resisting, flung a hidden weapon to force your attention elsewhere, then spun about and, without a second thought, leapt from the rooftop. You were struck with horror and tried to save her, but the Junior Martial Sister's resolve to die was absolute. With all her strength she launched herself from the roof toward the ground, and a brilliant bloom of blood burst forth, redder than her robes, branding itself on your heart like fire and searing your insides black.
Even though she feels not a shred of romantic affection for you, nor even much fondness, she still counts you as family.
You're probably unaware; she trusts and depends on you, far more than you can imagine.

The Sect Leader had long since burned through his last reserves, oil gone and lamp guttering, yet he forced himself to draw breath, pressing what little Internal Skill remained against his own heart to keep it beating. He could not withstand more than a few rounds with you before he spat a mouthful of fresh blood, cut down by your fatal blade—so a singular figure of his generation perished. The Junior Martial Sister broke free of her own opponent and rushed back in alarm, only to find her father's body slumped on the eaves of Zhengxin Hall. In an instant the whole world seemed to tilt. It was like being trapped in a mad nightmare, half lucid, half lost, as storm winds battered her until she could not keep her footing, the weapon slipping from her grasp. You had no way to defend yourself, and shame turned to fury; facing the Junior Martial Sister's accusations, you threw all your own grievances back at her—all these years, when had you ever given her less than everything? Yet when had she ever once looked at you with any regard? In truth it was your own ugliness, your weakness, your self-doubt that clouded your eyes, a fog that kept you from seeing anyone clearly. Desperate to shed this wretchedness yet unable to find the way, you gave up thinking for yourself and waited for someone else to decide for you. The moment the Martial Uncle gave the order, you struck at her without a second thought.

You were thrown to the ground by the Sect Leader, enveloped by a soft and subtle force, yet your center of gravity remained steady, allowing you to land safely. Immediately following, a torrent of blood rain descended. The Sect Leader forcefully channeled the remaining internal skill, striking with a single instant of action to decide the outcome, swiftly subduing the defeated opponent and landing them before the enemy's blood splattered across their bodies. The Sect Leader appeared calm, hands clasped behind, his gaze sweeping the courtyard, and no one in the Tang Family dared to move again. The internal conflict of the Tang Clan had thus concluded.

You were thrown to the ground by the Sect Leader, enveloped by a soft and subtle force that kept your balance steady in mid‑air, landing you safely on the earth. Soon after came a shower of blood, and Tang Shouhong rushed down in panic, barging through the crowd to flee. The Sect Leader's illness was too severe; he couldn't even move a feather. He failed to complete his final killing move and lost his strength, only cutting the opponent's skin slightly. Though relying on his past authority, he scared off the enemies, yet had already exhausted his remaining vitality.

The Sect Leader let out a long sigh. By now even his heartbeat and pulse depended on what little Internal Force he had left, pressed by hand against his own heart to keep it going—a spent force at its very last gasp. He clung neither to power nor to any favorite disciple; he simply could not hand the Tang Clan to some hypocrite full of unrealistic, empty talk. He looked once more upon his sect, and let that be his farewell. From his sleeve, the Sect Leader drew forth a single feather—this would be his final battle in this life.

He had no idea that Xiahou Lan never took the Fire Dragon Immortal Monarch seriously at all. With her current skill, only two men in all of Kongtong—General of Dao Techniques Danxiazi and Mystic Skill Gate Leader Wei Ju—might stand a chance against her; the rest would not survive a single blow. By now, Xiahou Lan was in truth the foremost master of Kongtong. But she lived in seclusion in the forest, and killed only when she must, so the world never learned her true measure. Cross her, though, and she showed no mercy. Sensing the danger, the Guangzhou disciples deliberately hurled filthy abuse at her, hoping to break her spirit so their fellows would fear her no longer—then, when the moment came, mob her all at once, a feat that would daunt even a Great Luo Golden Immortal. Xiahou Lan had just been wishing for someone to make an example of, and here one came, begging to die. She walked toward him at an unhurried pace; somehow he was too frightened even to flee, and she wrenched his joints from their sockets, killing him beneath her claws. Xiahou Lan's methods were ruthless, the kind no follower of the righteous path would condone. That single death silenced the whole yard, and only then did everyone truly feel that today might be their last. You had just come down from the roof of Zhengxin Hall and charged into the arena to shield your master. The crowd fell silent, not out of fear of you, but of the one you were shielding. Seeing you so furious, leaping about in a rage, Xiahou Lan could not help a small laugh; the killing chill in her eyes eased, the ruthless resolve of a moment ago gone. She called out to you, then left the crowd behind and walked straight across the training ground to formally pay her respects to the Tang family's sect leader.

Xiahou Lan heard this and loudly called out to Xiaomei. Xiaomei, who was lying on the ground pretending to be a corpse, shuddered but refused to give up, ignoring the call. Xiahou Lan frowned and issued her final warning: she would count to three. If she continued to feign death after that, she would turn her pretended death into an actual one. Upon hearing this, Xiaomei was so startled that she revived from her pretend state, leaping skyward, and rushed to Xiahou Lan's side. However, Xiahou Lan did not intend to punish her; instead, she handed Tang Shouhong over to her for disposal. When Tang Shouhong saw Xiaomei coming, he thought he had found a savior and began putting on airs of seniority again. Little did he know that Xiaomei loathed the Fire Dragon Immortal Monarch so much that she kicked him right then, sending him tumbling down. Thankfully, you managed to intercept her in time to prevent an additional life from being claimed. Xiahou Lan called out to you briefly before leaving everyone behind and proceeding directly through the training grounds to formally meet the Tang Clan's Sect Leader.

Unexpectedly, your master showed remarkable humility, bowing as a junior to the sect leader, and was instructed to spare Tang Shouhong's life. Though reluctant, she complied, then turned and flung Tang Shouhong off the building with a single claw, nearly killing him. She descended gracefully with an umbrella in hand, her piercing gaze sweeping the scene, coldly surveying the battlefield, remaining silent. Her chilling aura silenced the fierce battle instantly. The crowd looked up, seeing a woman of unparalleled beauty and coldness, as if from another world, her fragrance intoxicating. They thought her either a celestial being or a mountain ghost. A living beauty, yet even the most beautiful has a human touch; how could she be so ethereal and otherworldly? Yet, the next moment, witnessing her ruthless strike, they were startled, quickly withdrawing their thoughts and retreating to the sides. Tang Shouhong and Xiahou Lan's clash wasn't a duel but a one‑sided execution. Tang Shouhong, known as Buddha's Hand Fragrance, was the last surviving elder of the Tang Clan, capable of establishing a new sect in Guangzhou, not an ordinary person. However, facing Xiahou Lan, who was just short of reaching the peerless Realm, he was clearly outmatched. Every hidden weapon he launched was effortlessly absorbed by her umbrella. In close combat, he couldn't withstand her balanced Internal Force of soft and hard. A respected elder of the Jianghu was effortlessly controlled by her, treated like a monkey in a performance. Though not killed, she deliberately humiliated him in front of everyone, crushing his fighting spirit, exposing his true self, stripping away all his noble demeanor. Even so, he resorted to invoking the Fire Dragon Immortal Monarch of the Flying Heaven Gate of the Kongtong Sect, hoping at least to evoke some sentiment, if not to make her hesitate to harm him.

During the fierce battle, Xiaomei heard your shout, looked up, and was so terrified that her soul flew out of her body, thinking Xiahou Lan had come specifically to capture her. In her panic, she darted around in all directions, and finally lay down pretending to be dead.

Disciple to disciple, master to master — the words had scarcely left his lips when your vision blurred for an instant, and a strikingly beautiful woman in blue, holding an umbrella, appeared before you. Overjoyed beyond measure, you blurted out, "Master!"

Tang Shouhong feigned composure once more, yet he knew that delaying would bring complications. Since the favored disciple had arrived, he would entrust you to him for the fight, while he himself went to seek advice from the senior brother. Disciple to disciple, master to master‑how neat and proper it was.

Grief welled up in you, and love curdled into hatred; the reverence you once held for the sect leader turned entirely to poison, corroding your mind. When your Martial Uncle Tang Shouhong promised that if you performed well, he would take you on as his disciple once the matter was settled, you hesitated no longer. At once you turned against the sect leader, weapon in hand.

Anyone with half a brain wouldn't have believed his nonsense. You coldly asked, "You're not even part of the Tang Clan — what right do you have?" The taunt so enraged and shamed him that he meant to kill you outright. At this moment, Tang Shan had already lured the Little Junior Sister into the woods. He knew, first, that his own skill fell short of hers, and second, being of the same sect, he could not bear to harm this sweet and lovely Little Junior Sister, so instead he tricked her into wandering in circles until she lost her way, then doubled back to the mountain alone, flew up onto the roof once more, and asked his master's leave to fight you.

Taking advantage of the chaos among the sects, Shi Ming used their Qinggong to stealthily approach, intending to take down the sect leader while they were weak. However, the Tang Clan was renowned for their hidden weapons; how could they overlook a living person sneaking in? The sect leader smirked slightly, employing their Qinggong to lift off the ground and engage in battle on the rooftop, to avoid collateral damage. Yet, when their palms met, the sect leader staggered back several steps, spitting out a mouthful of fresh blood. Shi Ming had only used fifty percent of their strength, intending to test the waters, but they were surprised to see the once‑feared Tang Clan master in such a pitiful state. Overcome with both shock and joy, they momentarily lost their composure, abandoning their solemn demeanor to bring up old grievances, wanting to settle past scores.  The junior martial sister saw her father at a disadvantage from afar and, disregarding everything, quickly grabbed someone nearby, performing a somersault off their shoulder. With a push of her feet, she soared like a butterfly, her red attire fluttering as she spun around the eaves, resembling a wisp of light smoke, rushing into the sky. The tall building, dozens of zhang high, felt weightless as she didn't even touch the walls, leaving the onlookers below in awe, unable to believe such Qinggong existed in the world. She arrived ahead of Tang Shan, who was still on the way up, launching an attack at Shi Ming. Although she didn't succeed, her martial arts were characterized by agility and swiftness, allowing her to unleash a flurry of Flying Shuttles, leaving Shi Ming overwhelmed. The moment Shi Ming exposed a flaw, they drew a small sword, preparing to deliver a lethal blow, but Tang Shan suddenly attacked from the side, intercepting the move.
