Shi Ming felt a surge of joy, fearing that the night would be long and unpredictable, and decided to use all their strength to immediately strike down the sect leader. However, before they could unleash their palm strike, they were forced back by a wave of green poisonous smoke, as Second Senior Brother arrived just in time to intervene. With two against two, one side fought swiftly while the other hesitated, as if they shared a telepathic connection, shifting the battlefield accordingly. The sect leader sat alone on the rooftop, feeling an emptiness in their dantian, their True Qi dissipating without return, unable to gather the Internal Force scattered throughout their body. They couldn't help but feel despondent, reflecting on a life of prestige, relying on their formidable martial arts, never fearing anything. Now, with their skills lost and powerless, they felt like a useless person. Even if they lingered in Jianghu, they would merely be at the mercy of others. How could they maintain a stern face and command authority?  Just as one wave subsided, another arose. The once‑hidden junior brother, Tang Shouhong, calculated that no one in the Tang Clan could protect the sect leader anymore and finally revealed himself. He remained calm, not rushing to strike, even if no one was there to appreciate his performance; he wanted to ensure his reputation for compassion. The killing blow he dealt was out of necessity, a matter of great righteousness, and he believed that the heavens and the ancestors of the Tang Clan would not blame him for his ruthlessness.   Thus, in a moment of hesitation, he missed a good opportunity. You arrived just in time to protect the sect leader, knowing full well that you were no match for the elder. But the Tang Clan had more than just you. No matter how strong and ruthless the enemy was, as long as they targeted the sect leader, brave warriors would come forward one after another, unless the enemy had the ability to wipe out everyone in the Tang Clan. Tang Shouhong saw your resolute expression and forced smile. Although he had been away for many years and had never met you, the outsider disciple, he had heard of your reputation. With a sigh, he felt sympathy for you, wondering how you had been in the Tang Clan for so long without catching the eye of your superiors, never fortunate enough to be accepted into the fold.  It turned out that all of this was at the sect leader's behest, a strict order from them prohibiting anyone from teaching you martial arts. You were taken aback, but seeing the sect leader's expression, it seemed they did not deny it, and your heart sank immediately.

Although they all come from the same sect and practice the martial arts from the Tang Clan Hidden Weapon General Principles, the disciples of this sect are mostly new initiates with poor skills and insufficient dedication, and they were even defeated by the disciples of the Guangzhou New Tang Clan.

Although they came from the same sect and practiced the martial arts from the Tang Clan Hidden Weapon General Principles, the Guangzhou New Tang Clan could never match the original, and they were defeated in battle.

At that moment, strangers clad in Tang Clan attire, along with a band of martial monks, surged into the Tang Clan from every direction — clearly having lain in ambush for some time — and a chaotic battle was about to erupt!
Knowing he had nothing to gain, Shi Ming's expression darkened, and he signaled to Tang Shan to send a signal.

Shangguan Ying's mind stirred, recalling your past kindnesses, and her resolve was set. Although the Shangguan Family Head had instructed her to support Tang Shouhong's coup, she had been captured by the White Shark Gang, facing dire circumstances. Without your protection, she would not have turned misfortune into good fortune. She reflected that she had received much favor from the Tang Clan and owed you a debt of unrepayable affection. No matter what, she could not act against her gratitude, and thus switched sides at the critical moment, standing by your side.

You stood by, furrowing your brows, watching the sect leader remain unmoved; by rights, there was no room for you, a junior disciple, to speak. Yet as the other party's words grew increasingly unreasonable, even a virtuous monk had no right to force his way into another's house and lecture them. You could no longer restrain yourself: if he could play the sanctimonious monk, you were not afraid to play along in his act. Pretending to agree, you subtly exposed his ulterior motives with every word. Every ambiguous phrase was magnified by you, and among the Tang Clan disciples who had been uncertain before, the truth suddenly dawned on them: this wicked monk, for all his talk of righteousness, was full of mischief. They immediately abandoned any thought of throwing in with Tang Shouhong.

Since Shi Ming became famous, everyone has respectfully called him Master, even those who don't believe in Buddhism dare not lose decorum. Never have I seen you berate someone so bluntly, your face alternating between red and pale, furious to the extreme. You didn't even notice Third Senior Brother standing below, already scaring you so much that your soul has flown to the heavens. Tang Shan saw the old Chan Master's face was wrong, hurriedly interjected, reminding the sect leader to discipline you, but didn't expect to hit a snag. In the sect leader's eyes, even an outsider like you is no better than an uninvited guest, regardless of whether you're a revered monk or a Wulin celebrity, they are all treated equally, no face given. Knowing they couldn't get away with it, Shi Ming's face darkened, and he called out to Tang Shan to send a signal.

You drew out the Fish Knife given to you by the White Shark Gang and brandished it a few times, to see whether this senior monk from the Fujian branch of Songshan recognized the blade. Shangguan Ying was deeply moved. Though the Shangguan family had intended to support Tang Shouhong's bid for power, she had been captured by the White Shark Gang that day, facing dire circumstances, and without your protection, she would never have turned misfortune into good fortune. Reflecting on the many favors she had received from the Tang Clan and the unrepayable debt of feeling she owed you, she could not bring herself to act ungratefully. She immediately switched sides in the middle of the fight, standing by your side. Shi Ming, enraged, stamped his feet and immediately turned hostile, signaling Tang Shan to send a signal.

You sat listening, furrowing your brows, watching the Sect Leader remain unmoved. By rights, there was no place for you, a junior, to speak. Yet as the other person's words grew increasingly unreasonable, even a seasoned monk would not dare intrude into someone else's domain and offer unsolicited advice. Finally, you could no longer restrain yourself and burst into a tirade. Who cares if he was a master? To intrude and meddle was surely deserving of a scolding.

You listened in silence, furrowing your brows. Seeing the sect leader remain unmoved, there was, by rights, no place for you, a junior disciple, to speak. Yet as the other party's words grew increasingly unreasonable, even a virtuous monk had no right to force his way into another's house and lecture them. You could no longer restrain yourself and retorted. Your words were polite yet sharp, cutting to the heart of the matter. Shi Ming's face flushed red; he apologized aloud, then turned to remind the sect leader to discipline you. He did not expect to hit a wall. In the sect leader's eyes, even an outer-clan disciple like you outranked an uninvited guest. Whether the intruder was a revered monk or a renowned figure of the Wulin, he was treated the same, and given no face. Knowing he couldn't win the argument, Shi Ming's expression darkened, and he immediately signaled Tang Shan to send a message.

Shangguan Ying had learned commerce since childhood, managing the Shangguan family's affairs on behalf of her father. Despite being in her teenage years, she already exhibited the demeanor of a female head of the household, being eloquent and well‑connected as the legitimate daughter of a prominent family. It was only natural for her to recommend Tang Shan's master, which seemed fair and just, leading Shi Ming to bring her along for advice. However, the stance of the Shangguan family did not necessarily reflect her personal wishes. She had plenty to say but feared that a passionate speech might betray her own feelings, knowing that no matter how persuasive she was, it wouldn't sway the hearts of the Tang Clan disciples. Even with the sect leader's gentle encouragement, she hesitated for a long time, unable to utter a single word against the Tang Clan.  Seeing this, Shi Ming grew impatient and took the initiative to speak on her behalf, strongly recommending Tang Shouhong, a former disciple who had defected from the Tang Clan. He claimed that this person was kind‑hearted, had a good reputation in Jianghu, and had a connection to Buddhism. If he were to become the sect leader, the Tang Clan would have no worries about receiving the protection of the high monks from Songshan. This speech was based on what he had heard from Shangguan Ying, but coming from him, it inevitably sparked discussions. Those with keen insight immediately sensed something suspicious, detecting a hint of conspiracy mixed with the smell of copper. The aura of the enlightened monk diminished sharply in that moment.

Shangguan Ying stepped forward, speaking confidently. She had been raised in the business world, managing her family's affairs since childhood. Though still in her early twenties, she already exuded the air of a capable leader, eloquent and persuasive. As the daughter of a prominent family with longstanding ties, she was the ideal person to recommend Tang Shan's master. Her suggestion seemed entirely reasonable. At that moment, everyone found her arguments convincing. Martial Uncle Tang Shouhong was a kind‑hearted man with a good reputation in Jianghu, blessed with a deep connection to Buddhism and close ties with monks from Songshan. With such support, the Tang Clan would surely weather any storm in Jianghu. Only the Second Senior Brother remained unmoved, speaking coldly to challenge her. Yet Shangguan Ying remained calm and composed, effortlessly countering his objections.

His words struck home in every Tang Clan heart. The clan was beset by trouble within and without, and its disciples had suffered more than words could say. Without a word passing between them, they all thought the same thing: they had climbed the mountain and taken up discipleship out of admiration for the Tang Clan's fame, never dreaming that a hundred-year-old house would sink to such a state — its dignity gone entirely, its people met with cold shoulders wherever they walked the Jianghu. As for the Eldest Senior Brother: put kindly, he was easygoing and free of spirit; put plainly, he hadn't a shred of authority to his name. How could anyone feel at ease with him at the Tang Clan's helm — now of all times, with the Jianghu in one crisis after another and people's hearts harder than ever to settle?
His scheme in ruins, Tang Shan flew into a rage, drew a hidden arrow from his sleeve, and loosed it into the sky, where it burst into crackling sparks.

Seeing this situation, Shangguan Ying felt joy instead of worry and secretly let out a long sigh. In this case, no matter how eloquently she spoke, it would be difficult to turn the tide, so she would not have to feel guilty towards you all.

His words, though logical, lacked sentiment. After all, the Tang Clan was a noble family, not an ordinary sect. If their own wouldn't protect their own, what would they be called? United as one, the Tang Clan heard these words and erupted in fury. Everyone wanted to rush forward, grab Tang Shan by the collar, and beat him to a pulp before he could speak another word.

Master Shi Ming exchanged pleasantries with the Sect Leader. Although the two were old acquaintances, they were neither friends nor enemies. In their youth, the Sect Leader had once pursued a frivolous young lord who had disrespected his master's wife for a thousand miles. No matter how many people tried to persuade him, he would not listen, forcing the young lord to flee in disgrace to the Fujian branch of the Songshan Sect, seeking refuge under Master Shi Ming. Though the Sect Leader was both righteous and unrighteous, he held great respect for those of the Buddhist order. He kicked the thin wooden door open with a single blow but remained outside, knocking hundreds of times, listening day and night to the monks reciting scriptures. Eventually, the heads of the Nangong and Shangguan families came to persuade him, and only then did he relent, returning with some reluctance.  In a long dream, the Sect Leader had once seen Master Shi Ming. That year, he had just been appointed as the abbot and was quite ambitious, declaring that he would not open the door. Today, however, he had passed on his robes and bowl to a successor, having traveled for many years, and had become kind and benevolent, showing signs of age. The person he once knew was gone, and all the past seemed like smoke, as if it belonged to another world. The anger he once felt towards Shi Ming had faded significantly, and he could no longer summon any hatred, not even recalling what the young lord he had pursued looked like.  Unbeknownst to Shi Ming, the Sect Leader was lost in thought. After exchanging a few more pleasantries, Shi Ming got straight to the point. He had brought the legitimate daughter of the Shangguan family with him to support a disciple who claimed to be from the Tang Clan, ensuring that they could speak freely and advise the Sect Leader without worry. Once the Tang Shan received the Sect Leader's permission, they leaped onto the eaves of the Zhengxin Hall, gathering their breath to speak loudly and clearly, presenting the pros and cons. They repeatedly identified as a disciple of the Tang Clan, expressing deep concern. Although the eldest senior brother was generous and righteous, they were also free‑spirited and undisciplined, making it difficult to manage the disciples. With the Jianghu still turbulent, if a person of high virtue and reputation was not chosen to succeed the Sect Leader, the century‑old foundation of the Tang Clan might be in jeopardy!

Shangguan Ying and you went back a long way. Standing across from you that day, this ever-spirited heroine, who was rarely anything but radiant, wore for once an awkward, shrinking look. The moment her eyes met yours, she glanced away in haste, as though a guilty conscience weighed on her.

Seeing that the newcomer meant trouble, you didn't bother with false courtesy — high monk or no, you strode forward and let loose with harsh words, delivering a show of force before he could open his mouth. This suited Second Senior Brother down to the ground; rarely did he break form to play along with you, and it left Tang Shan quailing inwardly before he'd said a word.

After the two of them, another figure glided into the courtyard, clad in fine purple robes, with phoenix eyes and cherry lips, her features delicate and beautiful, carrying both the refined bearing of a great lady and the commanding spirit of a heroine among women. She was Shangguan Ying, daughter of the Shangguan family, one of the Wulin's three great clans.

After the two of them, a third figure glided into the courtyard — clad in fine purple robes, with phoenix eyes and cherry lips, of striking and elegant bearing, carrying both the poise of a great lady and the commanding air of a heroine among women. She was none other than the Shangguan family's cherished daughter, the one you had longed for day and night: Shangguan Ying.

Amid the uproar, someone suddenly raised their voice in protest, and everyone in the crowd froze, wondering who would dare openly defy the Sect Leader's decree in front of them all. Turning to look, they saw a young man of delicate, handsome features, dressed in Tang Clan colors, though no one recognized where he came from. He introduced himself as Tang Shan, a disciple taken in by a Martial Uncle of the Tang Clan after that Martial Uncle had broken away from the sect. Before anyone could respond, an old monk with a kindly face came shuffling into the Tang family courtyard, chanting a Buddhist invocation — none other than the renowned Chan Master Shi Ming of the Songshan Sect's branch. With his backing, Tang Shan's identity was beyond doubt, and those who had been seething with anger could hardly denounce him to his face before a revered monk of Songshan.

Yet the Sect Leader's words left the disciples speechless and chilled to the bone. Between the lines, he confessed that age and failing health had left him with no strength to keep leading the Tang Clan, and that he meant to send disciples down the mountain to find the eldest senior brother — who had not shown himself in a long while — and bring him back to take up the position of Sect Leader.

The Sect Leader came straight to the point, announcing before all the disciples his intent to step down and pass his mantle to his eldest disciple as successor. But since the eldest disciple was away on a secret mission of great importance and could not be present, he entrusted the Sect Leader's Token to his third disciple, Tang Sheng, to hold in his place until the Eldest Senior Brother's return — when they would offer prayers to the ancestors and he would formally take up the post.

All Tang Clan disciples still active in Shu obeyed the sect leader's command to gather at the mountain gate. At that moment, the Tang Family courtyard was filled with people, a scene of such liveliness not seen for a long time, exuding a few traces of the former glory.

Junior Martial Sister felt an unhappiness she couldn't put into words pressing on her heart. Just then, she had no wish to pat you in comfort — instead, an urge rose in her to draw a weapon and spar with you. She shook her head, chasing the thought of a fight away, but she was still fuming. Then she saw the clear tooth marks on your hand and could hold back no longer: opening her small cherry mouth, she copied Yunshang and bit down hard. But she was tender-hearted, and the instant her teeth touched flesh, she seemed to feel your pain as her own, a faint ache stirring in her own chest. So instead she simply cupped your hand and nibbled at it lightly, tooth by gentle tooth, as if trying to cover over the marks someone else had left. Lost for a while in what she was doing, Junior Martial Sister suddenly came back to herself, blushed scarlet, and fled.

Junior Martial Sister couldn't make sense of it: with your martial arts, you'd surely be able to overpower Ye Yunshang without trouble. Yet recalling how she had fled in such disarray, she felt certain you must have bullied her — and since she knew nothing of martial arts herself, she'd had no choice but to bite you in self-defense. You had no way to explain yourself and could only swallow the endless grievance and bitterness. Small mercy amid misfortune: for all the pain across your body, not one bit of your flesh had actually been bitten off.

Unbeknownst to you, Yunshang found the food too spicy and stopped after just one bite.
Wasteful as it was, propriety left you no choice but to cut away the part she had bitten. But before you could even start, the young lady was back, her pretty face flushed with anger — as though your rejecting the food she'd bitten had cost her all her dignity, and if you meant to cut away anything she so much as touched, you might as well flay yourself alive while you were at it. With that thought, she lunged and began biting wildly.
When she bit you, it was no game — she meant it. You never expected that this delicate young lady's teeth would prove so sturdy: once she clamped down, she would not let go even if your neck were about to snap.
Hearing your anguished cries, Junior Martial Sister came in to find the two of you tangled on the ground. Yunshang fled in disgrace, while you, clothes in tatters, looked as though you'd suffered the utmost humiliation, mauled from head to toe.
Wasteful as it was, propriety left you no choice: gritting your teeth, you cut away the part she had bitten and tossed it into the scrap bin.

You weren't held back by worldly propriety or scruples between men and women — only by dread of her brother's merciless, lightning-fast blade. So you cut away the part she had bitten and tossed it into the scrap bin.
Unluckily, Yunshang found the food too spicy, took a single bite and then refused to eat more, slipped the pancake into your hand and darted away.

Yunshang promptly left and returned, snatching the cake she had bitten but refused to take. She also went out, only then feeling increasingly ashamed, muttering a complaint with a flushed face before stomping away, exuding the delicate shyness of a young woman.

Unluckily, Yunshang found it too spicy, took a bite, and stopped eating. Your eyes rolled, as if putting on a show for Heaven itself, and you declared it a shame to waste food — so you simply ate it for her.
Unfortunately, Yunshang found it too spicy and stopped after a single bite. Coming from farming stock and thrifty by nature, you couldn't bear to see such waste, so you ate it for her.

You just took a bite, and Ye Yunshang smelled the aroma and burst through the door. As the saying goes, those who see share; you had no choice but to split the pepper cake in half, offering the untouched half to her.

You just took a bite, and Ye Yunshang caught the scent and burst in through the door. You were startled, fearing she'd come to compete with you for the snack, so you turned away and devoured it greedily, leaving not a single crumb for her. She wasn't really after your snack, but seeing you so selfish, she couldn't help but get angry, feeling a sense of being bullied and wronged, with nowhere to vent.

While Second Senior Brother was away from home, you secretly took his treasured Pepper Powder.
