As long as his adopted son Li Fugui and his sworn brother Nangong Yuan remain, the Mud Cult and the righteous path will never again come to blows like they did today in Jiangling. They are bound to look further ahead, see their true enemy, and lead a thousand troops together as the shield and wall of the Great Song. Twenty years late, Commandant Dingyuan Wang Shi finally made good on the bold promise he had made his friend as a youth: One day, I will gather a thousand troops under your banner and follow your every order, just like your great-great-grandfather, Wulin Alliance Leader Nangong Zhi. You have to train hard and grow stronger than me first! Once we're both grown up...

You've worked all day and returned to Nangong Manor, where the household servant invites you to bathe and change clothes. Today's great victory will be celebrated with a lavish feast later, to honor the heroes and uplift the prestige of the righteous.

After that, Gang Leader Wang stood alone against the righteous forces and consecutively defeated their skilled opponents. He showed no signs of fatigue, appearing spirited despite the intense consumption of his True Qi. Knowing that the drama was reaching its climax, and reluctant as he was, it was time for the curtain to fall. Steeling himself, he raised his voice and challenged the Nangong Family Head, who was holed up in the city. If Nangong Yuan did not come out to meet him, he would earn a reputation as a cowardly warrior, unable to walk tall in the Jianghu again. There was no other choice but to grit his teeth and come face Wang Erzhuang. As he looked at the scruffy man before him, he found himself both amazed and delighted upon realizing that it had been twenty years since they last met. He appeared like a youthful friend from days gone by-wasn't this very person the old friend he had searched for so desperately all these years? That year, in his quest to fulfill his own aspirations, he had left home feeling despondent and abandoned his life as the highborn son of the General Dingyuan's household, leading his horse north alone. He wandered the Jianghu for who knows how many years, and twenty years passed without a single word from him. Nangong Yuan believed he was no longer in this world, and often wept alone late at night. He never imagined his friend had changed his name and become the Gang Leader of the Beggar Sect. Feelings of joy mixed with sorrow welled up as tears filled his eyes. Yet, despite their past loyalty and camaraderie, this meeting could only end in a final confrontation. For one was the leader of the righteous forces, while the other was the Dharma King of the Demon Cult; righteousness and evil were incompatible, and for both personal and public reasons, this battle was inevitable. Gang Leader Wang had endured to this very day just to fight this one battle again. In their martial exchange, every punch and kick held countless unspoken words between them. They had been evenly matched twenty years ago. After parting ways for two decades, neither of them remained the young men they once were; Nangong Yuan had divided his attention among the qin, chess, calligraphy, and painting, while Wang Erzhuang had devoted himself wholly to perfecting his unparalleled martial arts. Just as Wang Erzhuang raised his hand to decide the match once and for all, someone from within the Beggar Sect suddenly rushed out with a sharp blade and drove it through Wang's body. Yet the wounded man's expression never changed, while the one who struck the blow wept openly, and the man he had saved was seized by both shock and fury. For this was all part of Wang Erzhuang's own plan. He meant to make himself the enemy of the world and draw every last grudge onto himself, so that his adopted son could set family ties aside for the sake of justice. With his death, the Mud Cult's Beast Path, which had followed him alone, would lose its footing and be unable to stand against the old factions-forced to flee or surrender. From then on, the Beggar Sect would never again answer to the Mud Cult. He meant to give his life to hand the Beggar Sect back, clean, to the righteous Wulin. He meant to spend every last drop of his restless blood washing away old grudges between the Jianghu and the Imperial Court, so that once the blood dried, those who shared it could stand united again. Overwhelmed with grief, Nangong Yuan had waited twenty years only for this reunion to become a final farewell. He carried his old friend on his back, rushing into the city to find a healer-never knowing that Wang Erzhuang had already walked his road to its end by his own choosing, content, owing nothing to anyone in this world. At the last, hearing the sound of a pipa, Wang Erzhuang closed his eyes in contentment, his mind drifting back to the best years the three of them had shared. At the same time, high above under the full moon, a peerless beauty stood alone, watching the sun go down, tears staining her sleeve. The Beggar Sect's internal strife collapsed along with the siege, and the infighting ended in the old faction's total victory. Afterward the Beggar Sect turned over a new leaf and returned to the ranks of the righteous, the crisis in Jiangling was lifted, and the whole city celebrated-every household hung lanterns, and even after nightfall the lights still burned bright.

In an instant, thirty‑two moves had passed. At first glance, it seemed a draw, but only the two combatants knew the truth. Rui Sheng sweated profusely and respectfully bowed before retreating. After this encounter, his skills had reached a new level.
Although you can't understand, you find it very impressive.

You were stunned, and if you hadn't seen it with your own eyes, you'd never have believed such wondrous martial arts could exist; the more you watched, the more you felt ashamed. In truth, it's precisely because your Realm is only one step away from mastery that you were moved by it. On this plain today, few were moved to sigh; most people remained clueless about its subtleties. Only someone like you, who gathers knowledge like converging rivers, could internalize what you've seen and enhance what you lack.

You watched from the sidelines, observing the scene where Wang Erzhuang unleashed a continuous sequence of finger techniques, his demeanor grand and majestic, his skills unfolding in layers of brilliance. Rui Sheng, holding his sword, moved with effortless grace, his techniques ever‑changing and unpredictable. At times, he was as swift as lightning, closing in for close combat, exchanging dozens of attacks and defenses in an instant; at other times, he stood motionless, facing his opponent in a tense standoff, remaining still for several breaths before launching a single, perilously precise move that reached the pinnacle of mastery. Since the fall of the Songshan Sect, the world had not seen the true form of their peerless martial arts for many years. Now, as Wang Erzhuang performed it, the atmosphere was solemn and imposing, his divine aura formidable, with not a trace of the heretical sects' influence. Even those who had sworn eternal enmity couldn't help but admire his unparalleled martial arts. As for the nameless young swordsman, clad in a white robe, he darted through the palm shadows. His sword dance was magnificent and exuberant, his style fresh and elegant, blending grace with unrestrained vigor. His movements were like Flowing Clouds and Water, naturally formed, as if the reincarnation of a sword immortal. Not only was his skill unparalleled, but his artistry was equally breathtaking, leaving onlookers unable to resist applauding.

You thought you would surely die this time, your mind going blank for an instant. Then a current of energy entirely unlike anything you knew rose from your dantian, pulsing with your heartbeat and pulse, trembling violently. The stagnant blood in your body was swept away in an instant, and your internal injuries healed without treatment-even Sect Leader Wei was thrown back by the force. She was astonished, and when she took your wrist to check your pulse, she could hardly believe it: it resonated like a plucked string, its sound lingering long after. Judging by your pulse just now, wasn't this the very Kongtong Iron Pipa Skill? Through this misfortune you had gained fortune-your own Internal Skill was wiped clean, but in its place you had somehow gained the notoriously difficult Iron Pipa Skill's power. There was no time to work out why; you could only steady your breath first, gather the True Qi coursing through your body, and still the faint tremor in your hands.

Sect Leader Wei saw you cough up a large amount of blood, your pale and exhausted expression causing her to panic instantly. Tears welled up in her eyes, struggling to hold back, yet you refused to cooperate and go with her to find someone to treat you.

Rui Sheng took over the difficult fight, and you retreated with Sect Leader Wei to the rear. She was only concerned about your injury, but you refused to miss the moment the two of them clashed, ignoring her gentle pleas and insisting on staying to watch.

Then a figure drifted down on the wind into the center of the arena and announced himself: Xie Wuchen, an Emei master known as 'Wind God,' whose renown matched Eldest Senior Brother's own. This Xie Wuchen had once run into another Dharma King of the Mud Cult in Fujian; trying to act as heaven's justice, he was instead publicly humiliated by Liu E of the Hungry Ghost Path, unable to bring his great skill to bear at all, and in fury vomited blood and swallowed his defeat. Per their wager, he was forced to rename his signature move 'Wind Thunder Divine Leg' to 'Very Forceful Kick'-the ultimate humiliation-and it broke him so thoroughly that he shut himself away in the Emei Sect, never setting foot outside. The world assumed he was finished and slowly forgot him; his return to the Jianghu today clearly meant he intended to collect what the Hungry Ghost Path owed him, from the Beast Path instead. Ever since that battle in Fujian he had been a laughingstock; people assumed he was chasing fame and braced to watch him embarrass himself again-but the moment he moved, everyone's opinion changed. This Xie Wuchen, called the Wind God, had truly mastered the essence of Emei's fist and leg techniques: nimble footwork, one kick flowing into the next, borrowing his opponent's own force, landing dozens of kicks in a row without ever touching down, each fiercer than the last, light as wind and fierce as thunder. Such Qinggong and leg technique had few equals in this generation! Even so, he eventually had to catch his breath, and Wang Erzhuang waited for the instant his True Qi grew turbid and he touched down to put distance between them, then flicked out a fishing pole, reeled him in close, and settled the match with a single palm strike. Utterly despondent, Xie Wuchen cupped his hands in salute, resolved to quit the Jianghu for good-but Wang Erzhuang instead offered him comfort and guidance, and through this battle his skill rose to a new level. Though Xie Wuchen lost, it was a loss with honor; everyone agreed Emei's Wind God lived up to his name-had his opponent been anyone but Wang Erzhuang, who could have withstood that storm of relentless kicks?

Who would have thought that even this strike would be intercepted, this time by an uninvited guest cutting in from the side. Wang Erzhuang could tell from the sound of the wind alone that the newcomer was no trivial threat; he shifted his footing and stepped back, and with a thud the white-robed youth leaped backward, while Gang Leader Wang funneled all the incoming force into the ground, taking not a single scratch. Even so, he couldn't help but marvel-how could so many heroic youths have sprung up in the Jianghu after just a few idle years? First came Young Sect Leader Wei in her yellow robe, and now this white-robed young swordsman. His Internal Force was not yet as deep as Young Sect Leader Wei's, but his palm technique was unmatched in its subtlety; the instant their palms touched, he withdrew his stance at once and released most of the force. Rui Sheng himself was secretly startled, thinking the Demon Cult Dharma King lived up to his reputation-his Internal Force was unlike anything he had ever seen, and that single strike alone nearly buckled his knees.

Who could have guessed that the third strike would be intercepted by an uninvited guest cutting in from the side. This time, from the sound of the wind alone, Wang Erzhuang knew the newcomer was no ordinary foe; he shifted his footing at once, and with a loud crack the white-robed youth leaped back a step, while Gang Leader Wang funneled the whole force of the blow straight into the ground, taking not the slightest injury. Even so, he couldn't help but marvel-how, after just a few idle years, had so many heroic youths sprung up in the Jianghu? First that yellow-robed girl, Young Sect Leader Wei, and now this white-robed young swordsman. His Internal Force wasn't yet as deep as Young Sect Leader Wei's, but his palm technique was matchless-the instant their palms met, he withdrew his strength at once, dissipating most of the blow. Rui Sheng himself was quietly startled, thinking that the Demon Cult Dharma King's reputation was well earned; such Internal Force he had rarely seen in his life-that single strike alone nearly buckled his legs-and he found himself deeply admiring the young man's readiness to risk himself to save another.

As the woman you loved stepped out of the crowd, your heart lurched with dread. You had never once seen her come off worse in a fight, so you assumed she must have a plan-but when you saw her staggered back, you realized something was badly wrong. Hearing that she meant to be stubborn and take yet another strike, you panicked, and heedless of your own safety, rushed forward and took Wang Erzhuang's blow yourself. Gang Leader Wang's Internal Force had reached such total mastery that he could unleash or restrain it entirely at will; after trading just one blow with Sect Leader Wei, he already knew her measure. His second strike looked fearsome, but it was really a clever Jianghu trick: he split his force into two strands that would collide the instant they touched an opponent's own strength, producing a thunderclap out of nothing and driving the foe back-creating the illusion of an even match, sparing both sides injury, and letting everyone save face. If the other party played along, a few polite words all around, and the peace of the Jianghu stayed unbroken. He had no wish to strike down a defenseless flower and meant to hold back, but you suddenly darted out. Unable to either release or recall the blow, he let it turn solid halfway through, and it slammed your inner breath into turmoil until you nearly retched up your very organs. You forced yourself to stay standing, determined to take the last strike for Xiao Ju.

The challenger's voice was clear and bright, and a young woman in yellow emerged gracefully from the Kongtong sect, who was none other than Wei Ju, the current Sect Leader of the Kongtong Mystic Skill Gate. Upon seeing her approach, Wang Erzhuang was taken aback. Although he was accustomed to encountering seemingly frail yet highly skilled martial artists, this girl displayed no stance or readiness typical of a martial practitioner, appearing completely unguarded. With just one strike, she could easily meet her demise. He couldn't help but admire her courage. As soon as Sect Leader Wei arrived, she began with a mix of praise and subtle criticism, intending to elevate the reputation of righteous individuals. Wang Erzhuang was increasingly astonished, having never known that the Kongtong sect had produced such a remarkable woman. Although he understood her intentions, he did not resist; instead, he secretly admired her. When she challenged him to three strikes, he decided to play along, using only three-tenths of his strength to test her while reserving seven-tenths for defense. He did not underestimate her simply because she was a delicate woman, and indeed, there was a trick to her approach. When their palms met, Wang Erzhuang suddenly realized that she was fearless because her Internal Skill was astonishing, harmonizing yin and yang, and was as rich as his own. However, she did not know how to utilize it effectively, and his seven-tenths of defensive force absorbed her strike and gently sent it back. Wei Ju had no intention of harming him; she merely wanted to seize the moment while Wang Erzhuang underestimated her and went easy on a seemingly frail woman, using the Kongtong Iron Pipa technique to awe him so he would not look down on the heroes of the world, giving the righteous martial artists an advantage. However, she had never encountered such an internal martial arts master before, and suddenly being pushed back by her own internal force caused her to retreat several steps. Although she did not suffer Internal Injury, she was left pale and shaken. Fortunately, her kind heart meant she did not harbor malicious intent or strike too hard; otherwise, after that shock, her life would have been in danger. Wang Erzhuang claimed he would not show pity, yet the three-tenths of internal force he had used was all to protect his opponent. He kindly advised her to stop, suggesting that the agreement of three strikes could be disregarded. Despite her pale face, Wei Ju was unwilling to break her word and steeled herself to receive two more strikes.

A disciple of the Flying Heaven Gate of Kongtong sect was lamenting his lack of opportunity to showcase his skills. Just as he reported his name, he rushed forward and was instantly flattened by a single palm strike. His Senior Brother, seeing the situation, rushed forward to avenge him but was easily dismissed. Righteous martial artists from other sects stepped forward to challenge him, none returning without humiliation. As the disciples of the six sects suffered consecutive defeats, the righteous forces were left disheveled and devoid of their former confidence.

As the situation gradually became clear, the Beggar Sect was losing more than winning. Continuing the fight would only result in more casualties, so Wang Erzhuang stepped forward, gathering his True Qi, and let out a roar akin to a lion's, shaking the plains. Both sides' forces were startled, and without hesitation, they ceased fighting. Wang Erzhuang looked around, declaring his intention to challenge all heroes under heaven with his own strength. Anyone, regardless of age or gender, was welcome to come at him. If they defeated him, they could behead him, and the Beggar Sect's disciples would be bound without resistance. This was an audacious statement. The martial artists present could not tolerate such arrogance, and immediately, someone stepped forward to challenge him.

After that, the two armies engaged in fierce battle. The Eldest Young Lord activated his ambush plan, causing the Beggar Sect to retreat continuously. The remnants of the Asura Path hidden among the auxiliary troops protected the Beggar Sect disciples as they withdrew, one by one revealing themselves. The battle had reached its final stage.
Shangguan Ying was also being chased and took refuge behind you, and you escorted her to a safe rear area.

The Tang Clan is relatively weak and cannot be compared to the other major sects that are at their peak. After a fierce battle, they are struggling to continue. Nangong Shen fears that a defeat might affect morale, so it would be better for you to retreat first, regroup, and guard the flank to prevent the Beggar Sect from launching a surprise attack on Jiangling City.

Amid the chaos, Shangguan Ying suddenly jumped in, yanking a whole string of copper coins from her waist and flinging it at someone's face as a hidden weapon, calling it a Coin Dart. You, the Tang Clan's Eldest Senior Brother, are yourself a master of the Coin Dart—ordinarily it's thrown with a deft touch to strike an enemy's vitals or acupoints, but here was this young lady Shangguan hurling an entire string of coins at once with such extravagance. Whoever took the hit spurted blood from the nose on the spot, their facial bones cracked, and collapsed unconscious. Having struck her blow, Shangguan Ying was still itching to go again; terrified she'd come to harm, you had no choice but to stick with her at the risk of your own life.

Xiao Zhu's meticulously crafted mechanical tiger battle tank made its debut here. This vehicle doesn't require human operation; it not only drives automatically but also spits fire. It's so cool you can't even describe it. Those beggars had never seen such a monster before and were all terrified and shocked.

The Eldest Young Lord roared from a high place, ordered people to beat the drums to boost morale, and led the charge into the enemy ranks. Jianghu heroes responded to the call, rushing together to the battlefield.

Shangguan Ying was still like a pear blossom drenched in rain, finding it hard to control her emotions for a moment. Your kind words offered her comfort; although the Eldest Young Lord did not understand her worth, you were all too clear about it. She need not learn to flatter anyone; her sincerity was already precious enough. Not to mention, Shangguan Ying's talent and courage made her a role model among women of her age—even you, who admired her, could not have her. How could you bear to watch her suffer for love, pitying herself and swallowing her pride? Whenever Shangguan Ying saw that Lady Yue Ping, her heart would become flustered. Deep down, she envied Yue Ping's delicate and fragile appearance, which seemed so pitiful. It was not that she did not wish to please the Eldest Young Lord, but her upbringing had taught her to be dignified and composed, making it difficult for her to lower herself to flatter a man. Now, hearing your praise brought her a sense of relief; it turned out there were still people in the world who did not find her proud and could see her true heart.

Seeing Shangguan Ying still in tears and unable to compose herself, you boldly declared that amid the chaos you would go stab the Eldest Young Lord to death, or else turn back and stab his beloved instead, to avenge her. Shangguan Ying was startled to hear it; knowing full well you were capable of anything you threatened, she quickly stopped you. Even in her fury, she did not want the Eldest Young Lord harmed, nor would she let you so much as touch a hair on Lady Yue Ping's head. It wasn't pure kindness on her part—if you harmed the frail and delicate Yue Ping, it would not only give people grounds to gossip and tarnish the Shangguan and Tang Clan's reputations, it would make her look savage and cruel, damaging her bond with the Eldest Young Lord. Not to mention, Shangguan Ying was proud; if she resorted to violence for losing his favor, wouldn't that be admitting her looks were inferior to someone else's?

You know she is proud and in a fury—reason will not work with her now. The only way is to goad her on with provocative words. The trick worked: Shangguan Ying knew full well that her rival wanted her to let rage cloud her judgment and lose her composure, ideally coming to some harm on the battlefield—even if she did not die, a scarred face or a broken arm would do, or better yet, being seized and defiled by beggars. That way, she and Nangong Shen could not marry, leaving Lady Yue Ping free to win the Eldest Young Lord's heart alone. At the thought, Shangguan Ying's teeth itched with rage, her sorrow faded, and she gave up all thought of despair.

You know she's proud and haughty, and she's in a rage; reason won't work. The only way is to comfort her well, letting her scold and hit as she wishes. Shangguan Ying scolded and hit, seeming to blame you, yet also blaming her unfaithful lover. After a while, she stopped sobbing, regained composure, and though she didn't say it aloud, she was genuinely grateful in her heart.

She is not a naive child who fails to understand the bigger picture; her feelings are deep and sincere. Her concern clouds her judgment, and when you block her, she calms down slightly. Yet she is overwhelmed by a mix of sorrow and anger, unable to control herself. She punches you a few times but remains unsatisfied, forcing an argument and blaming you for not defending her.

She is not an unwise child, but her deep and sincere feelings cause her to lose composure when she is concerned. When you block her, she calms down a bit, but she is overwhelmed by sorrow and anger, unable to control herself. She punches you twice and then stomps back to the city.

She is not a childish person who doesn't understand the bigger picture, but she is deeply sincere in her feelings, her concern causing confusion. When you block her, she calms down a bit, but overwhelmed by sorrow and anger, she struggles to control herself, punches you once, then stomps back to the city.
Shangguan Ying was extremely angry and was about to give chase, but you hurriedly pulled her back and spoke kindly to calm her down.

Watching from the sidelines, you couldn't help feeling embarrassed for him—a hero's resolve undone by tangled romance, causing such a scene right on the eve of battle would surely draw mockery from every hero in the realm, and only diminish his own standing. But that's someone else's family matter; short of blows being exchanged, it is not your place to interfere no matter what.

Nangong Shen strode out of the city with an imposing presence, gazing into the distance, filled with ambition. His fiancee, Shangguan Ying, chased after him, wanting to gift him a string of prayer beads she had earnestly sought from the temple. However, this touched upon Nangong Shen's taboo, as his family held a deep belief in Daoism, which conflicted with her faith. His expression turned cold, and he refused to accept the gift no matter what.  At the same time, it was rumored that the Eldest Young Lord's confidante, the renowned courtesan Yue Ping from Jiangling City, also rushed out of the city, offering him a sachet. One was a gift obtained through coins at the temple, while the other was hand‑stitched overnight; it was clear which one came from a sincere heart. Nangong Shen was deeply moved and, in front of his fiancee, accepted Yue Ping's sachet. Shangguan Ying, filled with rage, could no longer contain herself and openly reproached Nangong Shen for losing his decorum.  Nangong Shen despised having his face publicly undermined, especially today as he was representing his father in battle, embodying the demeanor of a righteous leader. How could he endure such criticism in front of everyone? He became furious, threw down harsh words, and left in a huff, ignoring Shangguan Ying's heartfelt pleas.

By the break of dawn, it would be the moment to decisively settle the issue between the Mud Cult and the Beast Path. Guided by the Nangong Family, righteous martial artists from various sects and soldiers of Jiangling prepared vigilantly with weapons at hand. The Family Head remained in the city while Nangong Shen led a group of elite warriors out to confront them, with his brother Nangong Qian providing support from the side.

Nowadays, Nangong Qian's family background, appearance, and martial arts skills are all outstanding; there are few things in the world that he fears. Can you still call him brother? As you think this, you feel as if you've been abandoned, following him step by step, yet your heart gradually drifts away from him.

Nangong Qian had turned misfortune into fortune, and his grandfather felt easier for it as well; the two of them bid their farewells and walked back to the city together, hand in hand. You deliberately hung back a step or two—after all, however kind the Old Patriarch might be, you were still, in the end, an outsider. Such good fortune had never been meant for you.

Nangong Qian's half-baked family Internal Skill was now spent, and his internal power now had to follow an entirely different path. From now on, every time his True Qi completed one cycle through the Heavenly Circuit, his internal power would grow a fraction stronger on its own; given years to accumulate, it wasn't just wishful thinking that he might one day rank among the Peerless Masters.

It was only because you rushed in to intervene that Wang Erzhuang couldn't land all eight palm strikes in a row, and Nangong Qian's family-taught Internal Skill never fully dispersed—which, as it turned out, was no bad thing at all: it left him a measure of his family's teaching to guard his heart, so that he wouldn't forget where he started.

Nangong Heng, being knowledgeable and well‑versed, found Wang Erzhuang's sudden attack unexpected, but soon turned his anger into joy and calmed down. With the lack of profound martial power from Gang Leader Wang, how could a junior withstand such a blow without dying? It was clear that he had used his deep Internal Force to open the extraordinary meridians for his grandson, employing a technique reminiscent of the Red Pine King under General Yue from years past‑this was indeed the legendary Songshan Marrow Cleansing Skill. Nangong Qian coughed up several mouthfuls of stagnant blood, and the toxins accumulated over the years in their body were expelled as well. Once calm, not only did it not hurt, but they also felt refreshed, with a stream of True Qi circulating within, initially elusive and intangible, but as the circulation progressed, it grew thicker and thicker, until later, every part of their body was filled with strength, and their Internal Force seemed ready to burst forth.

Nangong Qian, terrified, ducked behind you, and you panicked too, afraid of being caught in the crossfire, shoving back and forth with him. Gang Leader Wang ignored the pair of you making fools of yourselves, and without a word, gave his fishing rod a flick, yanking Nangong Qian forward, then sent him flying into the air with a flurry of two palms.

Gang Leader Wang was pressing to continue the attack, and how could you just stand by and watch? With Nangong Qian injured and Nangong Heng too old to hold off a powerful foe alone, who else but you could step up? Even knowing the other man's martial arts far outstripped your own—by ten times over—you had no choice but to grit your teeth and meet him head-on.

Nangong Heng spoke frankly, and asked Wang Erzhuang outright just what he meant by leading his men to besiege Jiangling. If it was only to seize the city, the Beggar Sect had already let slip more good chances than could be counted. If the Beggar Sect's leader were some ignorant fool, that would be one thing—but this Gang Leader Wang was a man of strategy with the bearing of a great general, and would never misjudge his military timing so badly. As it turned out, Gang Leader Wang was troubled for the sake of the nation, and understood well how the old grudge between the Jianghu and the Imperial Court ran as deep as three feet of ice, not frozen in a single day—and if it came down to it, it was the Emperor, across several generations, who owed the people of the Jianghu the greater debt. Unless every person of the Jianghu who knew the old stories died out, or the dynasty changed and the realm passed to new hands, the court and the Jianghu would forever stand opposed like fire and water. One could not hope for the Jianghu to produce another Great Hero like Nangong Zhi, who lived for the nation and its people, nor another Civil Alliance Leader and Martial Overlord to stand at Marshal Yue's side. Though the Nangong family kept good relations with the court above and never refused to mix with the common folk below, given enough time, Old Patriarch Nangong Heng's ideal of a world united as one might yet turn this situation around—but anything done well takes careful, patient planning, and could not be rushed. Yet with the nation in crisis, the Jin would not wait for unity before striking again, and even now soldiers on the border were giving their lives every day. The only course left was to strike hard and sound the alarm—attack the garrison at Jiangling, then use the Nangong family's standing to call the great sects of the Wulin to the rescue. Once it was an accomplished fact, the court would have no choice but to lean on the strength of the Jianghu; otherwise, once Jiangling fell, Xiangyang would lose its shield, and the whole realm would be in peril. Hearing Wang Erzhuang out, Nangong Heng felt nothing but admiration, deeply regretting they had not met sooner, and wished he could speak up for him, clear his name of its stain, and let every hero under heaven come to know this great man for what he truly was. But Wang Erzhuang cared nothing for his own reputation, thinking only of the greater cause—this battle had to be fought in earnest, using the hands of the Jianghu's common folk to break the siege of Jiangling, so that the court would learn gratitude and forge a new path where court and commons stood as one against foreign insult. Nangong Heng sighed deeply, knowing Wang's mind was made up, and said no more. But just as he was about to leave, something occurred to him, and he asked, almost in passing, about a Man in Black who had come to the Nangong estate one night not long ago, meaning to harm Nangong Qian, only to be caught and driven off by the head of the family—did Wang have any idea who it might have been? Gang Leader Wang admitted at once that the intruder in black had been himself, and showed not the slightest trace of guilt. At the Old Patriarch's mention of it, he suddenly recalled that night's unfinished business, and called Nangong Qian over to him—then, without warning, struck him with a palm that sent him spitting blood. The change was so sudden that neither you nor the Old Patriarch could move in time to shield him, and both of you were seized with shock and fury.

As for you, he had also long since heard the legendary tale of the Tang Clan's last outsider disciple. Nangong Heng had seen countless people in his time, and was well used to rising talents with good family backgrounds and both talent and looks. But you, at a glance, had the kind of face that was never welcomed anywhere, which stirred a quiet sigh in his heart—and made him resolve all the more to lift up someone unwelcome, as a kind of protest against the world.

As for you—since A'Qian can call you 'Big Brother,' and loosely speaking, you could be considered a grandson of Nangong Shen too—with a face that suggested you'd never be welcomed anywhere you went, how could the Old Patriarch, in the role of grandfather, not spare a thought for you as well? Wang Erzhuang couldn't help laughing to himself, admitting that his own breadth of heart didn't measure up to Nangong Heng's—for this Old Patriarch, he held nothing but the deepest admiration.

When Wang Erzhuang returned, he no longer beat around the bush. He said that since they had accepted the gift, it was time to take the bait for once and hear what the Old Patriarch had to say. Listening to the two of them trade words back and forth—probing, threatening, and mocking in turn—it was clear why one was a veteran elder of the Jianghu and the other the leader of the Beggar Sect. The exchange showed just how deep their backgrounds ran; neither was a mere brute who relied on force alone. You and Nangong Qian both found yourselves sweating through your clothes. As for why the Old Patriarch had brought the two of you along, Gang Leader Wang's guess was reasonable enough, but he never expected that the Old Patriarch's real reason was one of the heart. He had brought this unloved, illegitimate grandson along to temper his courage and win him a good name. Once Nangong Qian returned home safe and sound, everyone in the Jianghu would praise his extraordinary courage—daring to venture into a dragon's den and a tiger's lair, and rare enough, emerging without a scratch. It turned out the Nangong family's excellence wasn't limited to the Eldest Young Lord; even the Second Young Lord was not to be underestimated.

He fought with both hands at once, dividing his attention—pummeling Nangong Qian with one hand while dealing with you with the other. Even so, his deep Internal Force was still more than you could withstand; after only a few exchanges you were sent reeling by a single palm strike, stumbling back several steps and retreating more than a zhang before you could dissipate the force. What was shocking was that, having taken that blow, you came away only bruised, not truly injured. Gang Leader Wang forced you back and, without another word, gave his fishing rod a flick, yanking Nangong Qian forward, then sent him flying into the air with a flurry of palm strikes.

He fought with both hands at once, dividing his attention—one hand pummeling Nangong Qian without letup, the other holding you off. Though he used only one hand against you, every strike carried tremendous force, cutting the air with a fierce hiss. You could just barely manage to parry and defend yourself, but you couldn't fully shield Nangong Qian, and could only watch helplessly as he was knocked about, staggering from blow after blow.

He fought with both hands at once, splitting his focus—one hand fending you off, the other landing blow after blow on Nangong Qian. In your desperation you fought with everything you had, enough to visibly impress even the Mud Cult's Dharma King, forcing him back half a step. But mindful of the important business awaiting him tomorrow, he decided it wasn't worth expending more strength, and simply broke off the fight.

The Old Patriarch's face, once puffed up with pride, instantly turned to shock and disbelief upon seeing the catch in your fish basket. You hadn't been seated for even an hour, yet you'd caught so many fish, all plump and large! He hurriedly set aside his dignity to ask you for guidance, and you held nothing back, immediately revealing your underhanded trick: first scattering bait on the river to lure the fish to the surface, then shooting them with hidden weapons tied to fishing lines before reeling them in. The old man and his grandson had never seen anyone fish this way, and both were stunned. The Old Patriarch offered to buy the fish off you, meaning to hand them out to the Beggar Sect disciples—even if tomorrow brought a fight to the death, that didn't mean today they couldn't get along.

Because your Little Junior Sister loves to eat fish, you often went to great lengths catching stream fish up on the mountain, and had grown quite skilled at it—skilled enough to manage anywhere else too. You landed three fish in a row; though they didn't match the Old Patriarch's earlier catch, they were still nice and plump. Hearing you bring up the Tang Clan, memories came flooding back to the Old Patriarch, and he told of how, in his youth, he had become close friends with your sect's Sect Leader from three generations back, running naked around Tang Mountain together, jumping into ditches to spear fish with pauldrons, and mischievously splashing water to soak the robes of the Tang Clan's Senior Sisters, speaking of it all with endless fondness. The two of you couldn't help smiling at these amusing tales, laughing without a care and putting the danger you were in completely out of your minds. The Beggar Sect disciples, hearing your laughter from afar, secretly admired your bold, carefree spirit—that you could still laugh even with death staring you in the face.

When Gang Leader Wang went off to roast the fish, the Old Patriarch turned to you both, looking mighty pleased with himself, and asked how the fishing had gone. Your mind was in turmoil and you had no heart for it, so you hadn't caught a single fish. Nangong Heng smiled and, taking the opening, shared his views on worldly wisdom and martial arts. The reasoning was simple enough, but unless you had lived it yourself, you could never have grasped its true meaning—you would have taken it as nothing but an old man's rambling. But here, in the heart of the enemy camp, with your heart pounding like a war drum, hearing these words, you suddenly saw the light, gaining insight not only into worldly wisdom but also into the way of martial arts.

The Nangong disciples carried the scent of books, yet also had a touch of the Jianghu about them. At a hundred years of age, Nangong Heng had seen everything the world had to offer, and being from a Jiangling family besides, he had probably caught more fish in his life than you'd eaten. He said he'd show off a trick, and indeed astonished Gang Leader Wang: barely had he sat down when a big fish took the bait, and he even had Gang Leader Wang help reel in the line, teaching him on the spot how to play the fish, wearing down its strength before finally landing it. Nangong Heng then presented the fish to Gang Leader Wang as a gift. He'd reckoned that a gift brought all the way from Jiangling City would only raise suspicion and controversy, and that Gang Leader Wang would surely decline it—but this fish had been caught right in front of him, and in giving it, he credited the whole catch to Wang. This hit the mark exactly, delighting Gang Leader Wang, who happily took the fish off to roast.

You're also scared out of your wits, and it has nothing to do with courage or anything like that. Even the most reckless hero, faced with a dog-head guillotine, wouldn't stick his neck out to test fate with his own life for no reason. For now, all you can do is entrust your fate to the old patriarch and to heaven.

You remain calm and composed, not because you are fearless, but because you know that once you are here, vigilance is futile. You possess both broad‑mindedness and hidden depths. You know that your journey here is not to fish, yet it is still fishing. You are not fishing for the fish in the river, but for the leader of the Beggar Sect. You and your companions are the bait.

Nangong Qian held the fishing rod tightly, trembling with tension. He would occasionally sneak glances back at Wang Erzhuang, thinking that this Demon Cult Dharma King, renowned across the land, was seated behind him right now. And he was also the Beggar Sect Gang Leader. Nangong Qian reckoned that his martial arts were utterly insignificant compared to such a formidable opponent. His grandfather, though experienced, was old and frail; even if he had deep insight, it would be foolish to engage in combat. If Dharma King Wang were angered, he could easily snap them all with just a flick of his fingers. With their lives hanging by a thread, what use was fishing?

Gang Leader Wang looked tired and listless, sitting by the riverbank fishing; it turned out he had refused to come in person simply because he wanted to fish. Seeing him act with such arrogance, Nangong Qian could not help feeling annoyed: the invitation had been polite, yet his conduct was so rude. His grandfather, however, paid it no mind, feigning ignorance, and instead asked Gang Leader Wang how his catch had been, then asked to borrow a rod so he could show off a trick of his own. Gang Leader Wang's eyebrows rose with interest, and he went to the gang members for rods, bringing enough even for you two juniors. You had assumed the two men were old acquaintances, but asking around, you learned they had never met before; one was affable, the other blunt, and they had simply struck up a friendship within a few words.

Nangong Heng is a centenarian, generous and warm-hearted, with connections throughout the Jianghu. Who in the Jianghu is not his junior? Wherever he goes, he is shown great respect. Even before the Beggar Sect had risen to its current stature, it had always enjoyed his patronage. Even now that the two sides are locked in bitter conflict, they still treat the old master with the utmost courtesy, not daring to offend him in the slightest. Among the old-school elders of the Beggar Sect especially, there is not one who has not received his kindness. With just a few words, Nangong Heng got the other side to swallow their reluctance and go request the Gang Leader's presence for your group; and even though Gang Leader Wang would not come in person, he agreed to meet and speak with you all himself.

Fan Xiaotian, who had been released, returned to the Beggar Sect. His foster uncle, who had raised him, hurried out to greet him, his eyes filled with hostility, without offering any formalities, and dragged Fan Xiaotian away.
Surrounded by a mob of fierce, menacing beggars, you thought you were surely doomed this time, and nearly died of fright.
You never expected that the visit the old patriarch mentioned ended up at the Beggar Sect's territory.

You smiled, knowing your Master had traveled thousands of miles just to see you again. This sentiment was an unparalleled treasure for you, enough to boast about for a lifetime. Xiahou Lan gave a faint smile, put away her umbrella, and rarely wanted you to see her face clearly, remembering it well. She still didn't urge you, only expressing her wish: if possible, she hoped you could live. Even if disabled, it was better than dying, after all, your face was hopeless to begin with. Being insulted by an unusual term didn't anger you; instead, you were delighted, for this was the first time in your life.

You spoke without hesitation: Then you can commit suicide. Xiahou Lan's expression darkened as she thought you despised her and wished for her death. You smiled and said the girl you had fallen for was Xiahou Lan herself, so if anyone had to be buried alongside you, it could only be her. Xiahou Lan stood rooted to the spot, stunned, before finally understanding. She panicked and frantically shook her head, never having imagined you were so cunning, intending to commit such a heinous act as insulting your teacher and disgracing your ancestors. After Xiahou Lan fled in panic, you also broke out in a cold sweat, truly unsure where your courage came from to confess to her. Even if it meant stripping naked on the battlefield tomorrow, it wouldn't have been this dangerous. Thankfully, you managed to coax her into adhering to her fabricated identity with your earlier jests, ensuring she couldn't lash out at you despite her shame and anger. Otherwise, hearing those words, she might not know how to react other than slapping you dead. Sliding down from the roof, you shook off a cold sweat as your limbs trembled. You sat in the courtyard for a while before returning to your room to sleep; by then, the soporific incense had dissipated, yet you still felt dazed and confused.

You lit the lamp and got up, fetching paper and ink to prepare a letter for your distant benefactor Master. However, you hesitated and could not bring yourself to write. Thoughts kept coming, but no matter how hard you tried, you couldn't put them into words. With a long sigh, you suddenly heard a female voice from the roof‑a voice that seemed like your master's‑but whether it was due to the soporific incense or if she had truly traveled a thousand miles to Jiangling, you could not be sure.  Xiahou Lan did not stop you from going to your death but asked about your last wishes. Though her intentions were good, she had already presumed that you faced certain death. When she first entered the Jianghu, she was gentle and quiet, renowned as the First Beauty of the Wulin. After encountering a terrible misfortune, her temperament changed dramatically, becoming the feared Soul-Stealing Orchid.  Although she treated you kindly, her methods were somewhat offbeat. She warned you that if you had any particular fondness for a young miss, she would capture and kill her to accompany you in death; or if you desired coins, you should plunder the prefect's office and fill your coffin with gold and silver.

Because of your poor conduct, the renowned detective Song Bei reasonably suspects this is a case of one crook preying on another. Unfortunately, he lacks evidence to arrest you. Although you are innocent this time, your defense has made you highly suspicious.

In the midst of a deep sleep, you suddenly hear a crashing sound, startling you awake. You see a figure in black, a notorious thief listed on the Wanted Notice as the Soul Snatcher, who is infamous for using hallucinogenic smoke to break into homes, robbing and killing. He has never failed, growing bolder with each crime, taking advantage of the impending war, knowing the Nangong family has no time to pursue him. However, during his night visit to steal from the Nangong family, his usual hallucinogenic incense mingles with the Bewitching Incense you used to hypnotize yourself, amplifying its effects. As he enters and catches a whiff, he realizes something is wrong and tries to flee, but his limbs go weak, and he collapses. You grab some rope and tie up the foolish thief, then head to the magistrate's office just as dawn breaks.
As you think and think, you eventually drift off into a hazy sleep.

If there is any regret to speak of, it is that you were unable to see Long Xiang one more time. You do not know how Lady Wen of Jinxiang Palace and the head of the Nangong family came to harbor such a grudge. Their descendants have always been on good terms, yet the palace and family heads are irreconcilable. Even though such a major event occurred in the Wulin, Lady Wen remained cruel and refused to send her people to help.

If there is any regret, it is that you were unable to see Long Xiang again. You have heard of the old feud between the Palace Mistress of Jinxiang Palace and the Nangong Family Head. Yet, after twenty years have passed, how could one disregard Jianghu righteousness for personal affection?

You went to Kongtong once and left your heart there. But soon, the Kongtong Grand Selection is approaching. Don't even mention you're not a Kongtong Disciple, and your martial arts are weak. The position of the Sect Leader is beyond your reach, and whether you can survive tomorrow is uncertain.

Thinking again of Shangguan Ying, your sincere feelings are in vain‑she is ultimately not yours. She is already half of the Nangong family; what makes you, a mere outsider disciple, harbor such foolish hopes?
Still thinking about Fan Xiaotian's affairs for a while, hoping for a decisive battle tomorrow, to avoid meeting him in arms and preserve honor.

Also worried about Yunshang's illness, thinking that even though she takes medicine all day, she hasn't recovered, and instead her brother has been humiliating himself seeking medicine everywhere, his reputation getting worse, not knowing how he could stand in the Jianghu in the future.
Also feeling melancholy because the Junior Martial Sister no longer needs their care.
A myriad of worries flooded in: you were worried about the Sect Leader's illness, and

You've never given much thought to your feelings for your master. If you keep avoiding your own feelings, you risk regretting it bitterly should anything happen. You thought it over carefully, and the more you thought, the more alarmed you became - you realized you really were a shameless wretch: she had kindly taken you in and taught you martial arts, and here you were harboring dishonorable thoughts about her.

Your feelings for your master have never been thoroughly examined. If you continue to avoid your own thoughts, you risk regretting it should anything unforeseen happen. You carefully considered it all, realizing that no matter how beautiful she may be, she could not disturb your heart, for your affection for your master is pure reverence, devoid of any improper desire. Once you understood this, your heart grew clear as a mirror, and everything fell into place. The Bewitching Incense took effect, and you sank into a deep sleep.
Unknowingly, you have already forgotten your unease, your heart filled only with thoughts of Xiahou Lan.

Thinking of Master Xiahou warmed your heart just now. Though you don't know how much of her calling you her disciple is playful teasing, the brief months of teaching you received from her are enough to make you remember her forever.

You are troubled, restless and unable to sleep, your nameless anger flaring up, and you rise to prepare some Bewitching Incense, intending to knock yourself out. However, you possess an immunity, rendering your efforts futile. You know well that tomorrow's battle will be unlike any before. Both sides have thus far kept their cards close to their chests, but once you break all ties with the Beggar Sect, there will be no room for retreat, and the casualties will certainly be severe. What assurance do you have that you will not die tomorrow? Your life has been one of hardship, yet you have not yet reached the end of suffering and the beginning of peace. There are countless things you wish to accomplish, how can you be content to die?

After the two of them bid farewell, you filled a basin with water, returned to your room, and wiped your sweat. By the candlelight, you flipped through the map for a while, overjoyed and unable to contain your delight. You traced the diagrams a few times, as if gaining some insight. Only after feeling satisfied did you go to bed.

Outwardly grateful, yet secretly grumbling inside, cursing him for being stingy - giving you nothing but a map that can't produce peerless martial arts, when he could have just given you money instead.
Seeing how earnest he was, you felt refusing would be discourteous, so you swallowed your embarrassment and accepted the book.

Last time at the old patriarch's birthday banquet, the three martial artists of the Tang Clan captured Tan Badao, clearing his uncle's name before all the heroes in the land. To call them benefactors would not be an overstatement. A great debt of gratitude is hard to repay; even if this map is precious, it is worth no more than a thousand gold pieces, merely a token of thanks.

You have done a favor to Shangguan Ying, equivalent to having done a favor to the Nangong family. Although this favor has been acknowledged, Nangong Shen still keeps it in mind. Today, he finally has the opportunity to present the treasure map to you.

The techniques are not the issue - it's the practice of internal skills that is truly perilous. Nangong Shen knows you have never had a master to guide you, and fears that forcing your training of internal skills unaided will pull Yin and Yang apart, harming your body and damaging your meridians. So he gives you a map of internal skills known as the Nine Treasures Map of Wushan Grotto. Nangong Shen modestly says that practicing it won't produce peerless martial arts, only harmonize the Two Principles and nurture the Five Elements - which will surely benefit you all the same. In truth, he fears that if you learned how precious the map was, you wouldn't accept it so readily. The map is carved into a mural inside a stalactite cave where Wushan meets the Yangtze, its age unknown through however many dynasties, utterly mysterious - and that cave is now submerged beneath the river, making this the only surviving copy. The internal skills in this map reach the same end by a different path from the Nangong family's own teachings; useless to Nangong Shen himself, perhaps, but worth a fortune all the same.
Shangguan Ying couldn't help but worry about you after listening to her fiance's kind advice, thinking you were too greedy and hoping you wouldn't catch any illness.

Nangong Shen was very polite to you, and though you were only an outsider disciple, he still treated you with courtesy, apologizing that he hadn't meant to spy on your practice. You had taught yourself all your martial arts, so you didn't mind people watching, but you were afraid of being laughed at. Nangong Shen was startled to hear this. Though your drawing from so many sources showed real talent, he worried that the Internal Methods and forms of different schools were all different, and if you tried to learn too much, you might end up hopelessly mixed up. Losing the essence of your practice wouldn't be the worst of it - what he truly feared was a moment's carelessness leading you into Qi Deviation.

You were in a quiet corner of the courtyard, practicing your martial arts freely for a while. After breaking a light sweat, you decided to stop, as it wouldn't be practical to overexert yourself right before the battle; too much fatigue could lead to a reversal of priorities. At that moment, the Eldest Young Lord, having heard the commotion, arrived with his fiancee, Shangguan Ying, to see you.

You are immersed in immense pressure, the surrounding darkness resembling a thousand horses charging, with blades and bows hidden in all directions. Your senses are unusually sharp, and your body trembles. In this situation you sense a flicker of insight, and to seize this fleeting moment, you imagine Eldest Senior Brother as your opponent and wage a silent battle. You show yourself no mercy: in your mind, Eldest Senior Brother drops his usual grin and comes at you in earnest, and you find yourself dreading even the signature moves of his you've never seen. Finding no way to win in a battle of wits is nothing unusual. But to exhaust every trick and still go down in defeat says a great deal about how seriously you took it.

You are immersed in immense pressure, the surrounding darkness resembling a thousand horses galloping, with hidden blades and bows lurking on all sides. Your ears and eyes are unusually sharp, your body trembling. In this state you sense a flicker of insight, and to seize this fleeting inspiration, you imagine Eldest Senior Brother as your opponent and wage a silent battle. Finally, needing only one last step, you ascend to a new realm, your presence vanishing into the darkness, every stir around you within your grasp, free to do as you please within its reach. Through your own wit, you glimpse the path into what is called the Ruyi Realm.

Had it not been for your restless heart tonight sending you out to practice, Ye Yunzhou wouldn't have dared show himself so readily; he met you in haste and then took his leave. Thanks to this strong support, your restless and agitated heart immediately calmed down considerably.

He couldn't abandon Jianghu, couldn't forsake his debts of gratitude, and even for his sister's sake, he had no choice but to take this journey. That girl is mouthy, every time she mentions your affairs, she has to mock a few words to get her satisfaction. Yet you are one of the few she truly cares about. In her heart, you as Brother Zhao rank only below her own brother, worth as much to her as a single fingernail of Ye Yunzhou's - which, believe it or not, is no small thing.

You faintly heard a sound, only to find Ye Yunzhou arriving unexpectedly. You thought he had concealed his movements so thoroughly that he couldn't be found, and he would certainly not come to Jiangling to fall into a trap. Only after asking did you find out that it was still the old kindness of the Nangong family that prompted him to come.

You are still in a state of utter confusion and turmoil, knowing that tomorrow's battle will be unlike any other. Until now, both sides have been holding back, but once they tear their relationship with the Beggar Sect apart, there will be no turning back. The casualties will inevitably be severe. Even seasoned veterans who have seen countless battles know the value of life. Not everyone is invulnerable to blades and spears; who among us is so callous that we would willingly sacrifice ourselves for others' wars? At least you are not like that. You cherish honor, but you also want to live a full life.
You were unwilling to show off your skills within the Nangong Courtyard for fear of gossip, so you went alone to an open spot in the woods, set up a light, and began practicing your forms.

On the eve of the decisive battle at Jiangling, your mind churns like a tide, restless and uneasy. No matter how you toss and turn, you can't fall asleep. You can only get up to practice martial arts, hoping to become slightly exhausted so you can finally sleep.

The Old Patriarch said he wanted to go out for a walk and find someone from the younger generation to talk with, and invited you along. This old man is a Wulin elder whom ordinary people could hardly get close to no matter how they tried, yet here he was personally inviting you — and still you made excuses and refused to go. Nangong Heng was startled for a moment, but he did not dwell on it, just laughed, waved his hand, and walked off. In truth you had nothing else to do; you simply did not want to go.

The Old Patriarch said he wanted to go out for a walk and find someone from the younger generation to talk with, and invited you along. This old man is a Wulin elder whom ordinary people could hardly get close to no matter how they tried, yet here he was personally inviting you. You agreed at once — even just tagging along to run errands for him would have been an enormous honor.

The two of you were overjoyed to see each other again. Knowing Fan Xiaotian was your friend, the Old Patriarch meant to pass some of the credit onto you, telling him he had been let out of prison as a favor to you. Fan Xiaotian admired you all the more for it.
Even Fan Xiaotian, who had been captured earlier, was gotten out of the authorities' hands by the Old Patriarch.
Just as you were about to head back to your room for a good night's sleep, Old Patriarch Nangong suddenly turned up looking for you, his grandson Nangong Qian in tow.
Once the discussions were finalized, each respective force began to bid farewell one after another, ready for battle at dawn.

You and your fellow martial brothers were all whipped up by the crowd's fervor, itching for battle, wishing you could storm onto the battlefield this instant and kill off that pack of unloved, stinking beggars.

You, however, are not in agreement with the passionate sentiments of the heroes. When the Beggar Sect was strong, they never launched direct attacks on cities. Now that the righteous forces have united, they leave no room for mercy, loudly demanding total annihilation, which seems to contradict the chivalry you uphold.

Wulin sects gathered in Jiangling, with the Eldest Young Lord in high spirits, directing operations and deploying each sect's forces into hiding, waiting only for the Beggar Sect to walk into the trap the next day. Once it sprang, every sect would move together with the Imperial Soldiers, cutting off their retreat from every direction and wiping out the Beggar Sect's forces in one sweep. This time it would be nothing like before, when both sides had held each other in check, sparring in small skirmishes, catching and releasing prisoners, always leaving some room to back down — this time it would be an open fight to the death on the battlefield. The heroes gathered there all itched for action, blood boiling with eagerness, reckoning that with the gap in resolve between the two sides, they could catch the Mud Cult's Beast Path completely off guard, sweeping away the wicked and restoring the Central Plains Wulin to a clean, bright order.

The three of you had very different levels of martial understanding; even though the first few moves showed hints of what was to come, as the bout wore on, divergence and misunderstanding were bound to arise, until the true shape of things was long lost, leaving only each person's own sense of it. After a dozen-odd moves, fear filled all three of your hearts, especially the Beggar Sect disciple's — back home he had nightmares for days on end, and could never shake off the Tang Clan's sinister methods for years after. Though no one knew what he was thinking, you had scared off your enemy. After that, strange rumors about you spread through the Jianghu like wildfire.
Never expecting it, a fierce glint suddenly flashed in your eyes — taking advantage of him lowering his weapon, you struck one merciless, no-retreat stance after another, every move meant to kill.

You and the opponent exchanged over ten moves in the clash of thoughts, each secretly impressed by the other's formidable martial arts skills, and both felt mutual respect. You intended to end it politely, deliberately leaving a small opening, and the opponent understood the hint, refraining from pressing further. They also took a step back, lowered their staff, and bowed respectfully to you. The Beggar Sect's tea arrived, and thankfully, no conflict erupted with the Tang Clan, concluding peacefully.

You remained silent, but locked eyes with the leading Beggar Sect disciple in a silent contest, sizing each other up through the smallest cues, probing each other's mindset again and again, waging a life-and-death battle within your thoughts.

The Nangong Family Servant watched you two sides going at it nonstop, and rather than fearing he might get splashed with blood, he found it funny, taking it for dancing. He could not help joining in himself, showing off some free-form moves of his own — not realizing you had long since reached a stalemate, neither side willing to yield, worried about how to save face. Without any agreement, both sides turned their anger on him instead, and after beating him up to vent their frustration, the Beggar Sect's tea finally arrived. In the end there was no clash with the Tang Clan, and it all ended peacefully. Only the version of events where the Nangong Family Servant got hurt actually came to pass.

After a fierce battle on the empty street, you finally overcame the numbers with sheer hard technique and drove back the Beggar Sect. The Nangong Family Servants had already changed their tune, calling you "Great Hero" with every other word, showering you with flattery until the whole crowd felt pleased with themselves.

Having avoided battle once, you all felt a little guilty coming back to Jiangling this time. When the Eldest Young Lord Nangong saw you, his face was none too friendly either — it turned out he had long since been tracking the Tang Clan's movements, and suspected your side had been fighting half-heartedly, as though in league with the Demon Cult. Even if not, such treacherous conduct was unfit to keep company with the Nangong Family. That you had been afraid to fight was the truth, and you were struck speechless; matters had gone so far it amounted to a total break. Just as you all felt your hearts sink, Old Patriarch Nangong got word and came at his grandson with his staff, swinging for his head — but Nangong Shen's mind was already made up, so the blow failed to knock any sense into him. Luckily you and Fourth Senior Brother talked him down, or he would have either beaten his grandson to death or died of rage himself. Afterward, Fourth Senior Brother explained the whole affair with real remorse. The old patriarch, over a hundred years old yet still sharp, thought nothing of it. He said: everyone fears death; that you had come so far already showed great goodwill, and being unable to fight all-out for a moment was no great sin — after all, it was not your Tang Clan that laid siege to Jiangling. These words moved you lads almost to tears.

Having once avoided battle and now re‑entering Jiangling, your group felt a bit guilty. Fortunately, the retainer was grateful for being saved by you and greatly praised the Tang Clan. Upon hearing this, the Eldest Young Lord immediately changed his expression to one of friendliness and came to greet you with courtesy. His change from arrogance to humility seemed somewhat forced. You all believed that the Eldest Young Lord was opportunistic and only showed favoritism after achieving some merit, thus unconsciously looked down on this noble prince, thinking him a spoiled good‑for‑nothing. Little did you know that Nangong Shen's thoughts ran much deeper than yours. His arrogant attitude was not out of contempt for the Tang Clan but from deep‑seated suspicion that they might be undercover agents of the Demon Cult. He let Fourth Senior Brother provoke them without getting angry, all to maintain his own psychological balance.

The Tang Clan and the Beggar Sect each occupied a corner of the inn, not speaking to each other, yet the air was thick with a sense of impending conflict. You feared that a fight might break out at any moment, so you mentioned your senior brother, hoping to instill some caution in the other side. You falsely claimed that your senior brother was nearby, just out looking for friends. The Beggar Sect disciples scoffed at this; they knew you were trying to leverage the reputation of the Flying Hero to intimidate them. They retorted by bringing up the recent humiliation of a righteous hero at the hands of the Dharma King of the Hungry Ghost Path, which dampened your spirits. That hero was none other than the Wind God, Xie Wuchen, renowned alongside the Flying Hero. Unbeknownst to you, although your claim about your senior brother being nearby was a fabrication, Xie Wuchen actually was close by. Upon hearing your words, he appeared, thinking your senior brother was indeed looking for him. Overjoyed and filled with enthusiasm, he stepped forward to defend you, leaving you with no choice but to follow along. Fortunately, while Xie Wuchen did lose to Liu E, his skills were nonetheless genuine, and the average Beggar Sect disciple was no match for him. They were sent fleeing, knocked about by his flying kicks. Xie Wuchen, known for his good reputation, initially wanted to boast a little, but then recalled how he had been forced to change the name of his signature move, 'Wind-Thunder God Kick,' to 'Very Forceful Kick' after losing to Liu E. Embarrassed, he called you over and insisted on selling you the ancestral secret manual for 'Very Forceful Kick' for a thousand coins, before leaving in a huff.

You and your companions retreated to the town, only to find it desolate and quiet, with few people around.
