Knowing that many righteous warriors held wealth in contempt, seeking only fame, those with proper decorum might remain silent but leaving without even a word of thanks or ceremony was exceedingly rare. Thus, from this simple matter, suspicion arose. After the sect leader's inquiries and dismissal of his disciples, he verbally commended them for bringing the junior martial sister up the mountain and thanked them for relieving him of worry. You were nervous and agitated, thinking you might have established a significant achievement by chance. You imagined that it could lead to your conversion into the Tang Clan or formal initiation as a disciple.  Instead, the sect leader gave you a wooden box and dismissed you with this. Disappointed, you assumed it contained coins and returned to the Disciples' Quarters, only to find your fellow disciples had been waiting for your return with resentment for days. They surrounded you, pushing and berating you, snatching the wooden box as they opened it; immediately the hall fell silent, everyone dumbfounded. They respectfully returned the wooden box to you.
You were momentarily out of it, missing the opportunity to bid farewell and depart.
You left the Tang Clan, sheathed your sword for good, and never fought again for the rest of your life, living to the age of fifty.
You tried to switch to the Emei Sect, but Emei found your talent mediocre and politely declined.

You left the Tang Clan, wandering the Jianghu aimlessly, with no clear destination. Roaming the farthest reaches of the world, you traversed mountains and gazed upon the sea. Initially, you had a desire to settle down, but that longing gradually faded. You once lived in the Jin Kingdom and visited Mongolia. You spent time in each place, yet none became your true home. In one year of your journey, you succumbed to a mysterious illness while traveling, ending a life of freedom and solitude.

Only when you enter do you realize that many fellow disciples were so frightened by this battle that they have all sought leave from the Sect Master, returning to their surnames and no longer considered part of the Tang Clan. Last time, your impulsive departure without notice did not count as formal resignation. If you leave with everyone else now, it would truly be cutting off both your obligations and ties with the Tang Clan.
Early the next morning, you were summoned by the Sect Leader to Zhengxin Hall. Before you even stepped inside, you saw many fellow disciples heading down the mountain with bags big and small.

You served as Second Senior Brother's assistant, working through the night to stitch up your fellow disciples' wounds and dress them. Several senior brothers hesitated, then finally decided to go see the Sect Leader, and Second Senior Brother urged you to come along. Just as you stepped out of the Alchemy Room, you saw many disciples coming out of Zhengxin Hall, heading down the mountain.

Only when Sect Leader Wei's trusted Mystic Skill Gate disciple came to wish her a good morning did Sect Leader Wei ask her to explain things to you on her behalf.
The disciple was earnest and roundabout about it, gently walking you through the reality.
The Kongtong Four Maidens—Mei, Lan, Zhu, and Ju—were all promised to their gates' future sect leaders, Xiaomei and Sect Leader Wei included.
Their marriages were never just their own affair; they bore on the rise and fall of their sects. It's a custom Kongtong Mountain has kept for centuries, and outsiders have no say in it.
You listened with a sour taste in your mouth, and the food lost its flavor, your heart full of feeling.
Once in the Jianghu, you're not your own master—but then again, where in this world isn't the Jianghu?

Sect Leader Wei gave you another secret manual, and overjoyed, you thanked her again and again.
The disappointment you'd felt when she first said you weren't suited to Mystic Skill Gate's internal qigong had long since vanished.
You were moved to the core, and thought Mystic Skill Gate was simply the best.

This is the second time you've had tea brewed by Sect Leader Wei's own hand. Strong, her tea is as rich as flung ink; light, it's as thin as mist over the river.
In that tea are the four seasons, mountains and rivers, and years without a care.
Saying nothing, yet brimming with talent—what a wonderful person.

When it comes to the elegance and vulgarity of tea drinking, you spoke of your past experiences and observations, unintentionally giving Sect Leader Wei a lesson. It made her recall her teacher's teachings from many years ago, suddenly enlightened, and she felt a bit more grateful and respectful towards you.
Before that, Sect Leader Wei brewed a pot of light tea for you to aid digestion, making it easier to feel full and thus avoid gaining weight, a trick to maintain one's figure.

Before this, she tested your progress in martial arts. You came here to learn, but due to various reasons, you didn't master the secret manual she gave you last time, especially the latter part, which you hadn't even fully memorized. You just improvised, doing whatever felt right, and barely finished the entire set of martial arts. You thought you'd be scolded, but to your surprise, Sect Leader Wei remained smiling, showed no sign of disapproval, and even praised your progress, suggesting you should draw from a broader range of sources.

Before that, she tested your progress in martial arts. You were here to learn the arts, having seized the opportunity, so you naturally couldn't be careless. Strictly adhering to the teachings, Sect Leader Wei saw it and was very satisfied, praising you without hesitation. In the Tang Clan, you were either scolded for being ugly, stupid, lazy, or a monster, or something like that. In any case, no one had ever praised you so kindly as Sect Leader Wei did. You couldn't help but feel elated and gain some confidence.

Sect Leader Wei had her reasons for keeping you here against your will.
She just couldn't explain it to you directly, and wanted to wait for her trusted disciple to arrive and have her explain it to you instead.

Even short one Mystic Skill Gate fighter, the three's formation was still three against one, and you struggled to keep up, barely holding on through several rounds. Suddenly a young swordsman in white, unable to stomach the many bullying the few, leaped in to help you. The moment the three saw how handsome he was, they turned on him instead, six fists and six feet all aimed his way.
Luckily his skill was considerable, and by defending without attacking he let you free your hands to finish the rest of them off.
Afterward you traded names and learned this youth, who'd stepped in for a stranger, came from an obscure little sect nobody had heard of—his name was Rui Sheng.
Fearing you'd get beaten up again without knowing why, he kindly explained the story of Kongtong's sect leaders marrying the Four Maidens.
He was frank and easy to talk to, and still fresh to the Wulin, so you found the conversation with him effortless—never guessing this chance meeting was the moment your fate crossed with that of a legend of the Jianghu.

The three clearly underestimated your skill, taking your scrawny look for an easy mark, never guessing how tough you'd turn out to be. Even short one Mystic Skill Gate fighter, it was still three against one, yet you took them down in just a few punches and kicks.
When it comes to martial arts, you're no longer the outsider disciple of the Tang Clan that anyone could push around—now you're the outsider disciple of the Tang Clan that only a master could push around.
You couldn't recall doing anything out of line that warranted being pressed like this, so you shot back at once and threw yourself into the fight.

You feel hard done by. Back in your room, the moment you answered Xiaomei's call, you'd already had a bad feeling about it.
But you couldn't well refuse, and truth be told you were happy to go along, so you accepted the invitation anyway.
As for this trouble now—well, you might say it was only to be expected.

After parting with Xiaomei, you wanted to wash up and get breakfast, but ran into three ill-intentioned Kongtong disciples at the guesthouse.
The four gates of Kongtong usually can't stand each other, but over your stroll with Xiaomei they'd banded together to make trouble for you. They declared the Kongtong Four Maidens were the future sect leaders' betrothed, and even Kongtong men who fancied them had to swallow it—how dare a mere visiting disciple like you make a move?

You suddenly thought of the Tang Clan's Little Junior Sister, your heart full of tenderness.
Kongtong has everything—except her.

Having finally escaped, the two of you were still shaken, hearts still pounding.
You agreed to race along today's route again next time.

Sect Leader Wei had originally intended to keep you here by claiming you were a registered disciple of Mystic Skill Gate.
Seeing Xiaomei's troubled look, you played dumb and joked your way past the tension, and Sect Leader Wei finally relented and let you go.
Sect Leader Wei insisted on keeping you here, claiming that you are a registered disciple of Mystic Skill Gate.

It's only because you interceded that Sect Leader Wei did not severely reprimand Xiaomei. Not only did Xiaomei feel deeply grateful, but Sect Leader Wei was also deeply impressed by your upright and courageous spirit.

Wandering along with a beautiful companion at your side, there is no greater joy in life than this. In the early morning, with few people about, even those you did meet treated Xiaomei with special courtesy, and the two of you went the whole way without a care. In the end you ran into trouble at the Mystic Skill Cave, a place that guards all of Kongtong's texts and scriptures. Even as a direct disciple of the Flying Heaven Gate, Xiaomei had no business trespassing there, let alone bringing you along too-and the two of you were caught red-handed by Sect Leader Wei.

Seeing that you had come to study at Kongtong yet had always been excluded by your peers, Xiaomei guessed it was either because of your looks or because your sect's reputation had dragged you down. Unable to help feeling for you, she came looking for you and struck up a conversation, volunteering to be your guide and show you Kongtong's scenic spots.
The young woman's name is Yu Xiaomei. As the direct disciple of the Flying Heaven Gate, she currently holds the highest status on Kongtong Mountain, second only to the four Sect Leaders.

You saw the visitor, pale with a hint of red, as pure and charming as plum blossoms in the snow. If the plum blossom had the ability to cultivate and become a fairy, it would be such a beautiful person. You couldn't help but be entranced, lost in admiration.

You saw the visitor, whose complexion was as pale as plum blossoms in the snow, white with a hint of red, pure and charming. If plum blossoms could attain immortality through cultivation, they would be a woman like this. However, you praised her, yet remained unmoved. Instead, she saw your indifferent expression and looked a bit resentful.

You spoke to Crane Hand through the window, but even though you turned her down, she kept pestering you relentlessly. With nothing else to be done, you had no choice but to go out and meet the visitor.
You gave Crane Hand a series of strange and witty words, suddenly feeling enlightened and setting aside the matter of training, then hurried out to meet the visitor.

On this day, you once again woke up early, with enough time before breakfast to practice a set of martial arts. At this moment, a voice suddenly called out to you. You looked around, and only after focusing did you realize it was a Crane‑Form Trick Hand by the window speaking, encouraging you to go on a trip.

You received a secret manual from the Flying Heaven Gate and were sent to stay at the guesthouse, instructed to study it on your own first. After a few days, someone would come to guide your martial arts. Since joining the Tang Clan, this was your first time leaving home so far; a bit of anxiety was inevitable. But now, holding the manual, your heart brimmed with determination and a boiling passion. Your six‑month study abroad at the Kongtong Sect had officially begun.

You followed the Flying Heaven Disciple to the Fire Cloud Pavilion atop Kongtong Mountain to pay respects to the sect leader, Fire Dragon Immortal Monarch. Observing the Fire Dragon Immortal Monarch, his appearance was not ordinary, his attire as fiery and vibrant as flames, indeed living up to his name. Yet he was clearly supposed to be a high‑ranking sage, but upon meeting you, he spoke as if he were still a worldly mortal, which greatly disappointed you.

You followed the Flying Heaven Disciple to the Fire Cloud Pavilion atop Kongtong Mountain to pay respects to the sect leader, Fire Dragon Immortal Monarch. Observing the Fire Dragon Immortal Monarch, his appearance was far from ordinary, his attire as fiery and vibrant as the name suggests. Someone like you, who understands the ways of the world, wouldn't hesitate to address monks as Master and Daoists as Immortal, indeed earning a favorable impression.

You followed the Soul‑Stealing disciples to pay homage to the sect leader of the Soul‑Stealing Gate, but the leader wasn't there. The Soul‑Stealing disciples didn't hide the truth from you and explained the upcoming ceremony to appoint the new Sect Leader, the Soul‑Stealing Gate's unwavering determination to secure the position. The sect leader had already taken their most promising disciples into seclusion for cultivation and had no time to attend to you, an outsider. Whether you accepted or not, it didn't matter. Although that was the case, after all, you were a guest from afar. The Soul‑Stealing Gate didn't want to leave you empty‑handed, so they took charge on behalf of the sect leader, gifted you the initiation Secret Manual, sent you to the guesthouse, and told you to study it on your own. After a few days, someone would come to guide you in your martial arts. This was the first time since joining the Tang Clan that you had traveled so far from home, and a certain amount of anxiety was inevitable. But now, holding the manual, your heart brimmed with determination and fervor. Your six‑month stay at the Kongtong Sect as a student had officially begun.

Although the disciples of the Iron Fist Gate are not particularly skilled in martial arts, they rely on their strength and robustness. Charging forward with iron hammers, they create a fearsome display, causing disciples from other sects to flee in disarray. Only you remain. After some explanation, Gate Leader Lei realizes his own recklessness and allows you to stay.

You traveled far to the Kongtong Mountains to learn, only to be surrounded and beaten on the first day, pitifully returning to the Tang Clan and truthfully reporting the incident to the sect leader. The sect leader sighed deeply. Though he didn't hold much hope for Old Patriarch Nangong's dream, he still harbored some expectations. Now it has ended in a hasty manner, though not unexpected, yet it's undeniable that it's a great disappointment. His spirits sank, and his illness worsened further.

Gate Leader Lei gifted you the secret manual he had himself compiled, led you to the guesthouse, and instructed you to study it on your own first, learning through practice. After a few days, someone would come to guide you. Since your initiation into the Tang Clan, this was the first time you had been away from home for so long; hesitation was inevitable. Yet, now holding the manual, your heart brimmed with determination and fervor, your passion boiling over. Your six-month stay at the Kongtong Sect marked the official beginning of your training.

Although you heard this harsh speech and felt genuinely furious, the disciples from other sects who had come together to study all protested together. As soon as the Nangong Family's financial support was mentioned, the Iron Fist Gate erupted into chaos, grabbing their weapons and launching a fierce attack.

Though you felt uneasy hearing those harsh words, you endured the humiliation for the sake of your martial arts training, watching as other disciples from different sects couldn't bear the pressure and left one after another, while you stood firm until the end. Only then did Gate Leader Lei explain that the coins had never been distributed to the Iron Fist Gate at all‑it had all been held by the Mystic Skill Gate, not that they had taken advantage and then turned against them. Upon hearing this, you finally felt at ease.

You were assigned to apprentice under the Iron Fist Gate, and the Sect Leader himself came to meet you. He was a big, rough man who immediately said you could stay, but if you wanted to loaf around and expect food without working, you could think twice. If you didn't find work to earn your own meals, you might as well pack up your belongings and go home to cry about it. The Iron Fist Gate doesn't offer free meals. This was, in effect, a veiled way of telling you to leave. After pocketing a large sum of silver from the Nangong Elder, wasn't treating disciples from other sects with such contempt deliberately provoking fellow Wulin practitioners?

You were given a secret manual and led to the guesthouse to stay. Sect Leader Wei and you made an agreement that after a few days, he would visit you, and it's likely that he would personally guide you then. Since joining the Tang Clan, this is the first time you've been so far from home, and there's a lot of anxiety. But now, holding the secret manual, your heart is full of determination and fervor. Your six‑month study period at the Kongtong Sect has officially begun.

After finishing the tea and getting down to business, Sect Leader Wei explained to you that the arts of the Mystic Skill Gate are not external skills that can be mastered in a short time — your six months of study here would be but a drop in the bucket, nothing but wasted effort. As an alternative, she could use her authority as the Mystic Skill Gate's archivist to borrow the martial arts secret manuals of the other three gates for you.

Jianghu people are generally bold by nature, and even though you are only an outer disciple, you are no exception. You've never cared for genteel airs, drinking the tea the moment it's offered and calling it good the moment you find it to your taste. It isn't a lie, but to a connoisseur's eye, such drinking looks no different from gulping water — crude, lacking refinement, not something a person of taste would care to see.

You are also someone who often burns incense and prepares tea in Zhengxin Hall, so you know a little about such refined pursuits. You never rush the tea to your lips — first you take in its fragrance, note its color, and only after savoring it carefully do you slowly sip. Though not a word of praise passed your lips, having a connoisseur taste it was already reward enough for the tea preparer's care.

The Mystic Skill disciple led you to the Mystic Skill Cave, where you waited until Sect Leader Wei had finished her tasks before she came to meet you. She was humble by nature, and despite her esteemed rank as Sect Leader, treated you with no arrogance or pretense, still receiving you as an equal, speaking with refined courtesy, and personally brewing and serving you tea.

As expected, Sect Leader Wei suddenly praised you a couple of times in front of everyone, leaving the other three quite embarrassed. You had never been praised before when meeting strangers; you were always scolded immediately. This unexpected praise stirred a deep sense of gratitude within you.
At first glance, it might seem unremarkable, but you know that the art of worldliness is far from simple.

You drew the Flying Heaven Gate, foremost of the four Kongtong gates. Among the group, someone had come specifically to witness the Flying Heaven Gate's divine arts firsthand, only to find the chance taken from them by you. Furious, they even tried to force the spot away from you outright — had Sect Leader Wei not been present, fists might already have landed on your nose. Yet Sect Leader Wei merely smiled as though it were nothing, drawing the barbed words meant for you onto herself and deftly defusing them, leaving the others no outlet for their resentment but to swallow it back down.
You drew the Soul-Stealing Gate.
After going around in circles, you still drew the Mystic Skill Gate.
You were selected to join the Iron Fist Gate.
You didn't want to be gossiped about, so you went ahead and drew a lot of your own accord. Sect Leader Wei was a little surprised, but rather appreciated your backbone.
You agreed immediately, leaving the remaining three to gnash their teeth in frustration, but with Sect Leader Wei present, they dared not act recklessly and had no choice but to obediently draw lots.
Sect Leader Wei intends to favor you and has directly invited you to join their Mystic Skill Gate for training.

Little did they know that the girl in yellow spoke up at this point, introducing herself as Wei Ju, the current Sect Leader of the Kongtong Mystic Skill Gate. Everyone present was stunned into silence, their eyes wide with disbelief, desperately wishing they could swallow their earlier grumblings back into their stomachs.

You disagreed with the disciples of each sect and refused to associate with them, immediately being mocked by everyone, who said you lacked the bigger picture. In the future, it would be said throughout the Jianghu that the Tang Clan is so easy to bully, that the Kongtong sect sent only a young female disciple and sent you off.

You, for the sake of your sect's honor, went along with what the disciples of the other schools were saying. Whatever else, the elders from this girl in yellow's sect had to be summoned to meet them properly, or else, though your own embarrassment would be a small matter, it would be no small thing for the Jianghu to mock the Tang Clan from then on as a sect so easy to fob off.

The Kongtong disciple responsible for receiving them briefly explained the situation and left them at the Wuse Square, saying they would go report and ask a master to come meet them. After waiting for half a day, the person who arrived was merely a young and refined girl. This caused some dissatisfaction among the group; after all, they were all selected representatives from various sects, capable of showcasing the prestige of their respective schools as new talents in Jianghu. Even if the Kongtong sect leader held their status in high regard and did not come personally to welcome them, they should at least have sent some venerable elder of considerable standing to meet them and exchange courtesies, so as to show some sincerity. Consequently, protests began to arise.

On the day you ascended the mountain, you were greeted by the disciples of Flying Heaven Gate, who came down from Kongtong Gate to provide a brief overview of the current situation of the Kongtong Sect. The Kongtong Sect is located in Qinzhou, at the junction of the Song, Jin, Western Xia, and Tubo states. Throughout the changes in power and territory over various dynasties, it has shifted allegiance multiple times and has welcomed many talented individuals from foreign lands to settle in the mountains, resulting in a particularly weak sense of loyalty to the country and the emperor.   At one time, Kongtong Mountain had more than ten different sects and gangs, each occupying a corner of the mountain and governing themselves. After undergoing several dynastic changes and mergers, they eventually came under the banners of Flying Heaven, Soul-Stealing, Iron Fist, and Mystic Skill, with each of the four sects having its own leader. In order to stand on equal footing with the major sects of the Central Plains, they united and collectively referred to themselves as the Kongtong Sect, with one person elected from the four sects to serve as the Sect Leader.   Now, with the previous Sect Leader having passed away, the Kongtong Sect is left without a head, and none of the four sects is willing to yield to the others, marking a tumultuous period. Your arrival at the Kongtong Sect during this time could be seen as a matter of fate.

After you were defeated, Liu E tied you up with ropes and joined with the White Shark Gang brothers. The White Shark Gang took you all the way back to the sea and then pushed you into the water to feed the sharks.

You lured the Junior Sister out of the Tang Clan, intending to force yourself on her, but while you kept watch for anyone nearby, you failed to notice that she'd wandered off, distracted by a squirrel, and lost her way. As if fate had decreed it, the harder the two of you tried to find each other, the farther apart you drifted, and in the end you never found her — instead, she was abducted out to sea by Liu E, Dharma King of the Hungry Ghost Path.
The Junior Sister eventually realized who Liu E really was, but though startled she wasn't afraid, and went on eating and dressing well, writing home to say she was safe. The Sect Leader rushed in a fury to Fuzhou, only to see his daughter come running up to him joyfully, not a hair out of place and even looking a little plumper — he was struck speechless.
Not long after, the Jianghu fell into chaos: the Sect Leader was left dazed with grief, the Eldest Senior Brother died at the hands of the Flying Stone Gang leader, the Second Senior Brother defected, and the Tang Clan was falsely branded a faction of the Demon Cult, besieged by the Wulin Alliance in a crisis as precarious as a stack of eggs.
Liu E stormed the Tang Clan alone, fighting hundreds of the Wulin Alliance's finest single-handed. After several fierce clashes and heavy losses among his own men, he finally cut the Junior Sister free of the encirclement.
You had already heard about all this and lay in ambush along the road, meaning to kick her while she was down. Kind-hearted as the Junior Sister was, she was no fool — yet even with how suspicious you looked, she had trusted you without reservation. It was you who betrayed that trust, and left her heart cold.

Having heard the Second Senior Brother's words, you truly dared not stray a single step.
Even when the county magistrate wanted to haul you into court or set you free, you refused to budge, and so you spent decades in that cell through the changing seasons, until at last you died there.

You thought he was just talking nonsense, but the moment the Second Senior Brother turned to leave, you seized the chance — with the jailers still sprawled unconscious on the floor — and broke out of prison. You hadn't been back in the light of day long before you felt something was terribly wrong: your heart raced, your head spun, your blood seemed to boil in your veins, and blisters rose on every patch of skin the sun touched. Only as you lay dying did you realize this must be the Second Senior Brother's doing.

You rented two palanquins, paid a substantial sum, and even bought them outright. The porters, though suspecting your treachery, were too soft‑hearted to refuse for the sake of their families, and thus accepted the job, carrying Ye Yunshang and the junior martial sister away from their hometown. The farther you got from the Tang Clan, the more elated you became. When you reached a secluded spot, you confidently assumed the Tang Clan members would not be able to track you down for a while, so you dismissed the porters and prepared to poison them as they were carried away. However, you underestimated Ye Yunshang's intelligence. She noticed the smooth journey and had already suspected something, bribing the porters along the way and secretly sending messages to the junior martial sister. She used this to her advantage, subduing you. Though they knew you were no good, a beast with a beast's heart in human form, they could not bring themselves to take your life, considering your past kindness. Instead, they struck your acupoints, reported you to the authorities, and had you arrested. After several days in prison, one day you awoke to find your Second Senior Brother sitting silently before you, his gaze and tone as cold as a frosty blade. Looking around, you saw the constables and jailers all lying lifeless, unable to stop him from doing anything to you. The Second Senior Brother did not take your life but demanded you never step out of this cell again, or he would.

The Second Senior Brother saw you return and wasn't nearly as stern as you'd feared; the Third Senior Brother was delighted to see you. Never mind that you'd never formally left or been expelled — even if you truly had been expelled, the mere merit of escorting the Junior Martial Sister home would be enough that the Tang Clan couldn't turn you away.

It was already dark by the time you escorted the Junior Martial Sister back to the Tang Clan.
Watching her about to walk away, you couldn't help but feel a pang of loss.

Back at the Tang Clan, the sky had already gone dark.
Ye Yunshang had dozed off, and after getting down from the sedan chair she wouldn't walk properly at all, leaning lazily against the Junior Sister and acting coy. Seeing this, you couldn't help a bitter smile, and as you watched them walk off into the distance, you felt a pang of loss.

You found two sedan chairs in the village and had the two young ladies carried back up the mountain. Ye Yunshang was perfectly at ease, chatting and laughing with the old chair-bearer the whole way, but the Junior Martial Sister was riding in a sedan chair for the first time and felt rather uncomfortable, feeling quite apologetic toward the bearer.

Everyone has already clearly stated they're hungry, yet you keep asking endlessly. Yunshang and the junior martial sister couldn't help but get angry. Yunshang took off a hair ornament from her head, called a waiter, and asked him to help pawn it. She also ordered tea and dishes, making sure not to miss out on desserts, fruits, and fragrant drinks. She invited the junior martial sister to eat together, leaving you coldly outside. After eating for over an hour, feeling satisfied and their anger subsided, they returned to talk to you.

Opportunity is rare; you won't let it pass even if it's a matter of life and death. You volunteered to join the battle, aligning with the Thousand-Faced Demon to fight against the legendary Hero Long Yuan.
Opportunity being rare, you volunteered without hesitation to join the battle and aligned yourself with the former Wulin Alliance Leader, confronting the legendary assassin Thousand-Faced Demon.

You knew you were no match for the two experts. Although once mistakenly identified as the Thousand-Faced Demon by Great Hero Long and allowed to mingle in from the side to hear the whole story, there was no need for a fight. You retreated to one side and witnessed the confrontation between the two great experts. Until just before that waiter made his move, you did not believe he was truly the Thousand-Faced Demon. At this moment, you could not help but feel a sudden shock, thinking that this person's martial arts were several times stronger than yours, yet they bore grievances with dignity and served as a waiter in this remote place for three years. You recalled how you had relied on being a guest to treat him harshly, always ordering tea and washing buckets, which now made you feel regretful. Looking at Great Hero Long again, though he was missing an arm, he still fought effortlessly, channeling his Internal Force to roll up his sleeves, fighting with both offense and defense. The two combatants fought like divine beings, their exchange profoundly moving. You were lost in thought for a moment but did not expect that even from such a distance you would be affected; suddenly, you were knocked unconscious by the collision. When you woke up, you found yourself in a clinic. On the street, villagers gathered around the burned inn, discussing heatedly with expressions of profound sorrow. Only you knew that it was those two who had started the fire, burning down the inn without any casualties.

They did not show anger but exuded an imposing presence, their sense of justice striking like a thunderbolt, causing the worries that had weighed on your heart to dissipate. Suddenly, you felt a clarity wash over you when a waiter from the shop rushed out and bumped into you, their eyes reddening with excitement as they inadvertently revealed their identity as the infamous Thousand-Faced Demon of the Wulin! Hearing this, the Great Hero Long Yuan decided to turn over a new leaf.   Not only were you left speechless in shock, but even Long Yuan wore a bewildered expression, his gaze towards you losing its earlier sharpness, replaced by an apologetic look, as if he had mistaken you for the Thousand-Faced Demon. After all, who could blame him for finding you suspicious?   He had been ordered by the master of Thousand Lantern Tower to assassinate Long Yuan, going so far as to change his appearance and name. He had lived in a village at the foot of the Tang Clan's mountain for three years, and now, the locals no longer regarded him as an outsider; even the initially strict innkeeper had entrusted his own daughter to him.   Despite never completing the assassination mission, the cold‑hearted Thousand-Faced Demon gradually developed a sense of belonging to this land, becoming anxious and fearful of leaving one day, worried that Thousand Lantern Tower would erase everything he cherished, including the traces of his life here, his family, and friends.   After listening to Long Yuan's words, he finally resolved to abandon the darkness and embrace the light, regretting only that he was bound by constraints. Even though he wanted to protect his family, he felt powerless, believing that the only way to ensure their safety was to sacrifice his own life and entrust their future to Long Yuan.   Long Yuan's expression turned strange as he took out a brocade pouch, which was said to be the legendary Apricot Blossom Pouch. It was rumored that in the apricot blossom forest of Nanyang, there existed an immortal who bestowed this pouch upon those who were virtuous, allowing them to avoid misfortune and attract good fortune, with its efficacy never failing.   The immortal not only revealed the hiding place of the Thousand-Faced Demon but also understood their situation thoroughly. With a casual remark, it was as if a light bulb had gone off, resolving the deadlock that had troubled them for so long. Following this plan, not only could he ensure the safety of his wife, children, and father‑in‑law through Jinxiang Palace, but he also wouldn't have to face death. He could continue to feign compliance, deceive them for the antidote, and seek a future opportunity.   In the end, he would still have to fight, but the key details would differ, leading to entirely different outcomes. When you heard the Thousand-Faced Demon call out his name, you finally realized that Long Yuan was none other than the Sword Hero Long Yuan, a figure who had once made waves in the Jianghu during a previous era, only to vanish after the peak battle, never to return as the Wulin Alliance Leader.

You sensed he meant you no good, so you poured yourself cup after cup of wine and forced down a few more mouthfuls, but felt so uneasy that you meant to leave. Seeing this, the big man came right over, picked up his chopsticks without the slightest courtesy, and began eating, insisting you keep him company. You were none too willing, but he pressed so hard you had no choice but to comply.

Look at his tattered attire, yet he radiates heroic vigor, like a chivalrous hero. If you intend to befriend him, after all, a table of dishes won't be finished, inevitably wasted, so why not invite him to a meal?

In the blink of an eye, you have been staying at the inn for quite some time. The initial excitement has faded, and everything you do feels dull and uninteresting. After leaving the Tang Clan, even the most leisurely days seem insufficient, leaving you feeling empty and at a loss. You indulgently ordered a table full of delicious dishes, the kind that would make your mouth water, yet you find it hard to swallow, feeling that sharing a simple bowl of noodles with your brothers would be more satisfying. You were startled, but couldn't help thinking, 'that was close' — luckily the Beggar Sect was foolish enough to besiege Jiangling. What is Jiangling? You read through the Jianghu Bulletin, stammered for a moment, unable to speak. It's no wonder the Emperor refused to send troops, dismissing it with a laugh. Even you don't believe beggars can rebel; they're so poor they can't even afford armor and weapons.

These few days, the town has seemed rather unsettled. One day, you stopped the waiter to ask, and only then learned that something significant had happened in the Jianghu.

These few days, the town has seemed rather unsettled; occasionally, you can see Jianghu martial artists in tight‑fitting attire riding horses out of the town and dashing eastward. On that day, when you entered the store and asked, you learned that something significant had happened.

You considered Kongtong, hearing that it has a low threshold and is not exclusive. In the past, you were dead set on not leaving the Tang Clan, always using Little Junior Sister as an excuse; in reality, your heart had long since stopped caring for her.

In the past, you stubbornly refused to leave the Tang Clan, always using Little Junior Sister as an excuse, claiming it was a request from the Master's Wife. However, Little Junior Sister has long since grown up and no longer needs your care; you know this better than anyone.

Di Ao saw this and secretly smiled, feeling proud in her heart.

After accompanying you up the mountain to pay respects to the sect leader, they settled down in the Tang Clan.

But upon reflection, considering the sect's interests, you fear being accused of hoarding knowledge, leaving you in a conflicted state of mind.

Under the leadership of the newly appointed Wulin Alliance Leader Long Yuan, they united in purpose and launched a comprehensive assault on the Supreme Bliss Cult. Ultimately, at the decisive battle atop Mount Huashan, the chief villain 'Joyful King' was subdued; the Left and Right Guardians died or escaped. Without a leader, the remaining Supreme Bliss sect members were routed and collapsed like a falling mountain, being thoroughly annihilated, thus averting the crisis of a change in power. The whereabouts of Alliance Leader Long Yuan after the battle remained unknown; the Tang Clan Sect Leader suffered severe injuries and was left with an incurable illness for life; a skilled Qingcheng practitioner, defeated, had his conviction shattered and let evil grow from within, becoming one of today's Six Paths Dharma Kings of the Mud Cult. That decisive battle had few witnesses, and its outcome was more than lamented. Now that the Supreme Bliss Cult has been extinguished but the Mud Cult has risen again, Nangong Heng's mention of the Mud Cult at the banquet immediately stirred a commotion; there was a desire to nip this nascent threat in the bud before it could spread like wildfire.

That's you. You were the only one asleep in the entire hall; even the unrestrained Eldest Senior Brother was awestruck by your nerve. Everyone is speculating about what the Nangong Family could have done to make you so disrespectful to the old man, truly outrageous.

Nangong Heng told of the times when people from the Jianghu gathered under the summons of the Wulin Alliance Leader to form an army and resist external threats, protecting their homeland. However, the endings were not pleasant. These two occasions led to a complete rupture between the Jianghu and the court, with deep‑seated grudges that would take more than a hundred years to heal. With the old tales finally reaching the main point, he woke those who had dozed off.
You, this madman, really did fall asleep, leaving the guests on either side unable to believe their eyes. Could this fellow possibly be out of his mind?

The old master has a wish that can only be fulfilled by widely inviting fellow Wulin practitioners to jointly participate in the event. It's unclear what the wish is, and it seems like he's going to elaborate for a while. He also jokingly said his story is as long and boring as a stink. Impatient young people can take a nap first; we'll call you back when we get to the main point.
The joke wasn't particularly funny, but you found the old man's cheeky disregard for his years rather endearing, and couldn't help smiling.

You completely disregard others' feelings; if a joke doesn't meet your approval, you quietly insult the old man at their birthday banquet. Coincidentally, that old birthday star may be old, but he is far from decrepit. His gaze is sharp, and he can spot your unsmiling face in the crowd. He can even read lips, and when you secretly curse his intentions, the old birthday star picks up on it.
You didn't find it funny, but you laughed along with everyone else out of courtesy, if only to save the old man's face.

Nangong Heng, Retired Family Head of the Nangong Family, is the last living elder of the Wulin, revered for his standing and virtue. For his birthday feast today, he has widely invited friends from every corner, and of the notable figures still active in the Jianghu, few indeed are absent. Though Nangong Heng is old and greatly respected, his temperament is easygoing and full of humor; whatever he says turns into a joke, sending the guests into laughter.

You act cautiously, knowing that the classmates sitting next to you are typical troublemakers who always look for reasons to stir up trouble. If they don't find someone to bully, they'll feel restless, and such people are bound to appear wherever you go. You've seen plenty like them in the Tang Clan. So you adopt a strategy of retreating, claiming to be an outsider and thus not qualified to discuss clan affairs. If they insist on knowing the clan's secrets, you suggest they consult the Second Senior Brother.

You are plain-spoken and couldn't be bothered wasting words, making it clear from the start: fight, or shut up. A few sharp words were enough to silence them for good, not that they truly feared this obscure nobody, only the trouble of angering the Nangong Family. They fell sullenly silent and said no more, but quietly marked you down, thinking there'd be another day in Jianghu to settle the score with you.

Soon, the Junior Martial Sister returned. It turned out she'd noticed the food on your table wasn't as good as the guests', and unable to bear it, she'd brought you a plate of chestnut rice cake. Before you even took a bite, you felt a sweet, warm feeling in your heart, and found it deeply satisfying.

They spoke freely about a famous woman in the Jianghu, and then turned their talk to the Tang Clan. In a fit of anger, you brought up your Junior Martial Sister. This only made her the subject of ridicule, with people saying she had never left the mountain and must be hideous and unfit to be seen. It mattered not that they insulted you; insulting your sect was hateful, but insulting your Junior Martial Sister was unforgivable. You immediately slammed your fist on the table, intending to take this enemy down with you in mutual destruction. But at that moment, the Junior Martial Sister appeared as if gliding in. The men present, seeing her face, had no more words to say and regretted their rash comments, all scrambling to make excuses. Even members of the Diancang Sect, rivals of the Tang Clan, harbored wicked thoughts of winning the beauty's favor, turning on the friends they had just made, and a chaotic brawl broke out. The Junior Martial Sister, however, never took any of their words to heart. She patted your back to calm you down, told you not to be angry, and went home.

They spoke freely about the famous women of Jianghu, and then turned the conversation to the Tang Clan. In a fit of anger, you brought up your Junior Martial Sister, which only led to her being mocked, with people saying she had never left the mountain and must be ugly and unpresentable. It was one thing to insult you, but to insult your sect was despicable, and to insult your Junior Martial Sister was unforgivable. You immediately slammed your hand on the table and pinned someone to the ground, beating them furiously. The Nangong clan members rushed over to separate you both. Each side held firm to their own words, making it difficult to determine right from wrong, and with many voices chiming in, you found yourself wronged. Except for the Eldest Senior Brother, the other Senior Brothers couldn't help but blame your impulsiveness, saying it tarnished the sect's reputation.

You've read so many books; it's not in vain. At that moment, you remained calm, maintaining composure, explaining the greater principles without arrogance or humility, citing the wisdom of ancient sages to make your argument unassailable. These outlaws of the Jianghu had no words left to counter, trying to stir trouble only to end up with their noses in the dirt. Though they didn't fully listen, they began to hold a grudging respect for you.

At the banquet, the disciples from various sects were clamoring and making a fuss, with no one bothering to acknowledge you with any pleasantries. You simply decided to enjoy yourself, savoring your own food and drink, feeling quite content. Unexpectedly, as they chatted away, they suddenly turned their attention towards you, who had always been indifferent to worldly affairs, and their words even insulted your sect.
At the banquet, disciples from various sects were noisily arguing, and since nobody thought you worth a polite word, you simply amused yourself, eating your own food and wine, quite content.

This banquet is grand, organized by the Nangong family at great expense, with arrangements made by the Four Offices and Six Bureaus. The upper seats are reserved for esteemed guests such as officials, leaders of various sects, and renowned figures from the Wulin; the middle seats are for disciples and students from different sects, as well as well‑known lone heroes; the lower seats are set up outside the estate, welcoming the informal members of Jianghu, the Beggar Sect, and even local villagers who can come freely to share in the feast.

This banquet is grand, organized by the Nangong family at great expense, with arrangements made by the Four Offices and Six Bureaus. The upper seats are reserved for esteemed guests such as officials, leaders of various sects, and renowned figures from the Wulin; the middle seats are for disciples and students from different sects, as well as well‑known lone heroes; the lower seats are set up outside the estate, welcoming the informal members of Jianghu, the Beggar Sect, and even local villagers who can come freely to share in the feast.

You and your Eldest Senior Brother acted in tandem, improvising spontaneously with effortless naturalness and seamless coordination. Though not as eloquent as the clever wordplay of theatrical performers, your performance was original and distinctive, half‑serious and half‑playful, recounting clearly and distinctly the incident of the grain heist on the official road in Jiangling Prefecture over a decade ago. You exonerated Niu Changshou, rehabilitated Nangong Yu, and restored justice for the delayed righteousness. Tan Badao, the instigator who had ruled for years by sheer force, finally surrendered as the tide turned. Your performance, interwoven with thunderous applause, resonated through the Jianghu, bringing a perfect and triumphant close.

A wave of uncontrollable grief and anger surged within you. You couldn't hear Eldest Senior Brother's true intentions; it felt as if his call blended with the mocking voices, taunting and manipulating you. You rushed out without a care, but soon regret filled your heart, and you wept bitterly. Gradually, you distanced yourself from the crowd, from those you knew well, wanting to escape as far as possible, to a place devoid of Jianghu, where no one could mock or discuss you. The place you reached was desolate, utterly silent; finally, even your heartbeat was inaudible.

Thanks to Eldest Senior Brother's sharp rebuke, you were pulled out of your self‑pitying and self‑indulgent fantasies. You forced yourself to accept Eldest Senior Brother's invitation and took the stage to perform. A clown is a clown; it's inherent, why belittle yourself? Life is filled with sorrow and joy, beyond one's control. Whether this play receives roaring applause or utter silence, only after the curtain falls will you know. Once you've stepped onto the stage, you must play your role as 'you'‑no one can replace you.

Eldest Senior Brother meant to achieve this effect, letting out a shout to call you up to perform with him. But you didn't think yourself close enough to Eldest Senior Brother to deserve this, and never having expected he'd pull such a move, you were suddenly overcome with embarrassment. You felt every burst of the guests' laughter was aimed at you — some perhaps mocking your plain looks, others your lowly birth — and you wished you could dig a hole and bury your head in it.

Eldest Senior Brother had aimed for exactly this effect: with a single shout, and you — so in tune with him — answered the call and made your entrance. Amid the astonishment of all the guests, the host, and even your own companions from the Tang Clan, the two of you launched into a splendid duet performance.

Eldest Senior Brother acted mysteriously, saying he would present a formidable weapon as a birthday gift. The Tang Clan is renowned for its hidden weapons and poison techniques; forging metal is not unusual for them, and even the Nangong family's favored weapon, the Dark Iron Yin-Yang Chessboard, was crafted by the Tang Clan. Presenting a weapon is a noble gesture, but the timing spoils it. Offering a weapon at the birthday banquet of the patriarch of the Wulin's esteemed Nangong family, especially a blade with a rather unrefined name, would openly provoke the Nangong family. Nangong Yuan's anger simmered, and the guests burst into laughter, all wondering if the Tang Clan Flying Hero, known for his eccentric behavior, had lost his mind, daring to disrupt the Nangong patriarch's banquet. If the Nangong family, Master of Fairness in the Wulin, turned against him, would the Tang Clan still have allies? Just as Nangong Yuan was about to explode in anger, someone in the crowd suddenly recognized the weapon's origin — it was none other than the Broken Mountain Slash, the famed weapon of the Four Blades of Jianghu and the Kuizhou Great Hero Tan Badao. This revelation stunned the crowd into silence, and Nangong Yuan, upon closer inspection, confirmed it was indeed the weapon the Nangong family had long wanted to eliminate but hesitated to act against. Yet the question remained: why had it ended up in the hands of the Tang Clan?

The Second Senior Brother represented the sect leader and presented a single Spirit Pill. This pill was the result of the Second Senior Brother's painstaking effort, taking several years to refine. Though it was merely a son pill created by dividing a mother pill and adding other ingredients, its efficacy had already reached the limit of what a flesh-and-blood body could endure. Taking this pill would not extend one's life by ten years, only make one ten years younger. You too had a share in the toil that made this pill possible. After Nangong Yuan listened to the instructions and smiled, he accepted it, unaware of the pill's true value. In contrast, Zou Bo, the Qingcheng sect leader who had presented his own pill just before, secretly gasped upon hearing this — yet from the Second Senior Brother's few words alone, he could tell that this young man's mastery of alchemy and pharmacology was no shallower than his own, worthy of the name grand master, and felt deep admiration.

To know the scholars of Gengyang Reading Studio is to recognize their unrivaled pride of spirit; within the studio are reclusive talents unmatched in their era. They cultivate their fields in the wild, shunning vanity and eschewing fame. When the Chancellor Shi Miyuan sent someone to extend an invitation, they were driven out with a flurry of staffs. The master of the studio once said, In times of peace, one can sing and dance; in chaotic times, one should not compose poetry. I would rather be among the inept in a well-governed world than serve as a useful minister in a corrupt court. They vowed to remain in seclusion until there were no more frozen bones in the world, at which point they would emerge to sing of universal peace; otherwise, they would rather die than accept a single grain of rice from the Imperial Court, to demonstrate that their studies were meant to serve the heavens, earth, and humanity, rather than a mere ruler. This studio has always focused on writing the Jianghu Bulletin; other works are priceless and hard to come by. The head of the Nangong family, upon acquiring such a work, was overjoyed and praised the Tang Clan's gifts in front of the guests, drawing countless gazes. Even guests lacking literary talent had seen the Jianghu Bulletin; those who hadn't seen it understood the expression on the Nangong family head's face. It is said that although the Tang Clan is not as powerful as it once was, the friends they have made are all extraordinary individuals, not to be underestimated.
This artwork is hard to come by, and you also have a share of the merit.
Third Senior Brother represented the sect leader, presenting a piece of calligraphy and painting from Gengyang Reading Studio as a birthday gift.

Nangong Yuan heard that Junior Martial Sister had also come to the banquet and was overjoyed. He called her over for a closer look, and at first glance nearly mistook her for his deceased mother, feeling for a moment as though a lifetime had passed. Seeing how beautiful she was, he felt happy for her parents' sake as well.
Nangong Yuan, the head of the family, greeted you with great warmth, showing not the slightest coldness for the Tang Clan's decline — a clear sign of his magnanimous spirit.
Despite having some psychological preparation, you were still startled by the Pauldron. It felt like something that shouldn't exist in this era‑or any era. Who started wearing such gear...?

The Nangong Family is indeed one of the Wulin's Three Great Families — this birthday banquet drew nearly every person of standing in the Wulin. Not to mention that past generations of the Nangong Family had produced a martial arts champion and even a Wulin Alliance Leader; with two generations of far-reaching connections, the family had stood unshaken for centuries no matter how the Jianghu's winds blew, and there was no one in the Wulin who didn't know the Nangong name. Servants called out names from the guest list and received gifts as the head of the household greeted arrivals up front, with guests filing in one by one to exchange pleasantries. At last it was your Tang Clan group's turn.
Then the Third Senior Brother and Fourth Senior Brother arrived. You all then presented the letter of introduction and entered the Nangong family's gate.

You felt a strange flutter in your heart, sensing that Junior Martial Sister's group had also arrived. Eldest Senior Brother and Second Senior Brother saw you having one of your fits and thought nothing of it, but the next moment Junior Martial Sister came running up to join you.

After finishing the task and traveling for several days, they finally arrived at the Nangong family's territory in Jiangling Prefecture. The city featured stone‑paved roads, with every household's door freshly painted, bustling with people coming and going, lively and vibrant, completely different from the simple scenery of the Tang Clan's mountain village below.

Upon hearing this, Junior Martial Sister wanted to turn back and give the carriage to Third Senior Brother. You immediately jumped in to object: letting Junior Martial Sister travel alone with Eldest Senior Brother would be the most dangerous thing in the world. It wasn't that you feared Eldest Senior Brother meant her harm — what you feared was that he meant too well. What if he suddenly took a notion to bring her along to rob mountain bandits? What if on a whim he decided to take her to Tianshan to admire the snow? Junior Martial Sister was obedient and had no mind of her own; if she were left in Eldest Senior Brother's care, it wouldn't be far-fetched that years later she'd turn up abandoned in Japan, with no idea how to find her way home.

After a month's journey, they finally arrived at the Nangong family's estate in Jiangling Prefecture. The city's roads were paved with gravel, and every household's door was freshly painted, bustling with people and thriving with activity, a stark contrast to the simple scenery of the mountain town beneath the Tang Clan's mountain. The senior brothers who had gone ahead had already arrived earlier, and Third Senior Brother had been handling matters along the way, keeping a watchful eye on the Eldest Senior Brother to prevent him from straying off course or disappearing, clearly having been troubled quite a bit.
Junior Martial Sister and you were both riding in a carriage for the first time, and you were both thrilled about the trip.
Time was approaching Nangong's birthday banquet, so the Fourth Senior Brother rented a carriage and hired a driver, intending to take his time setting off to avoid looking dusty and unrefined.
The goods Manager Jiang owed the Zhong family, once lost, had been recovered, and he no longer had to face the Cang Gang's harassment—he didn't know how to thank you enough.
The goods Manager Jiang owed the Zhong family, once lost, had been recovered, and he no longer had to face the Cang Gang's harassment—he didn't know how to thank you enough.

You feared chaos across the land and, with a bold heart, joined the White Shark Gang. You swaggered through the market, knocking on the door of An Ji Apothecary, storming in, and tossed all the rice, food, and medicinal herbs to these poor orphans and widows. Your band of lawless ruffians were friends of the poor and enemies of the rich, also the bane of the officials' eyes. Despite accomplishing this great feat, you had no idea how to escape the pursuers from the Imperial Soldiers. Just as you were troubled by this, the Beggar Sect disciples at An Ji Apothecary revealed their identities‑none could have imagined that the Gang Leader of the largest sect in the world was actually the Dharma King who oversees the Beast Path of the Mud Cult. The Big Benevolence Sub‑division of the Beggar Sect, which is also part of the Mud Cult's Beast Path, had been deliberately stirring up trouble at the West Gate to attract attention from the guards and cooperate with you from within and without, catching the Imperial Soldiers off guard.

After that, the group of White Shark Gang members ran around aimlessly in Jiangling City, fleeing from the pursuit of the Imperial Soldiers. Amidst the chaos, they sent grain to Anji Hall and received assistance from the Beggar Sect, finally escaping alive.

You tried to persuade the White Shark Gang members to risk their lives for the group, but they refused. It wasn't because they could set aside life and death, but because their Gang Leader was scarier than King Yama. King Yama could make you reincarnate as an animal, but the White Shark Gang Leader could make you regret being born—unable to live, unable to die. You had no words left to say, and could only step back and stay out of it.

You talked the White Shark Gang members out of it. Though you'd known each other only a short time, you were already companions who'd shared a meal of fish sashimi together. After a moment's thought, they decided to leave the cargo in your hands and set sail while the soldiers had not yet arrived.

You were listening to a friend from the White Shark Gang explain the situation when you suddenly launched a deadly strike, knocking him down. The pirate accomplices were both startled and enraged, drawing their blades and attacking. Before you could explain, the Flying Stone Gang also joined the fray, and the two groups immediately clashed in a chaotic battle.

That group of pirate bandits was muttering some incantation, and you immediately realized upon hearing it—they weren't speaking any other language, but White Shark Tongue! You immediately responded in White Shark Tongue to introduce yourself. The White Shark gang members recognized you and were overjoyed. They pretended to fight with you while using White Shark Tongue to explain the situation. It turned out they had accidentally seized a ship belonging to the Cang Gang, who distribute grain to the poor. How could they bear it? Any act that could embarrass the authorities or cause trouble for the rich must be carried out with great fanfare.
You and the Flying Stone Gang members managed to repel these lawless pirates who attacked ships, but you yourselves also suffered severe injuries.

Those ship-robbing pirates were muttering some incantation you couldn't make out, chanting until it made your skin crawl. Fortunately, the Flying Stone Gang members arrived in time, standing shoulder to shoulder with you, and clashed with the pirates in a chaotic melee.

That day, the ship lent to the Cang Gang was about to arrive at the shore. Guildmaster Jiang was both anxious and proud, ordering his men to line up in two rows to welcome them. Unbeknownst to him, the people who disembarked were neither Cang Gang disciples nor sailors from other ships. Without a word, they drew their blades and attacked. Fortunately, you intervened in time, saving his life.

You were invited to the ferry dock to serve as Guildmaster Jiang's bodyguard. He had a favor to ask of you, treating you as a guest of honor and even going to the tea house to invite the Tea Server to brew a pot of hot tea. You had never been treated so generously before. Watching the ferry workers and the hired Flying Stone Gang members toil back and forth, sweating profusely, while you lounged comfortably, you felt a bit uneasy and volunteered to take on the rough labor. The Flying Stone Gang had long had tensions with your Tang Clan, but not with you personally. In the first few days, they mocked and jeered at you, but they weren't deep‑thinking people. After working alongside you on the same grueling tasks, shouting and sweating day after day, and then drinking cheap yellow wine at the tavern after finishing their work, they soon became close to you.

You were invited to the ferry dock to serve as Guildmaster Jiang's bodyguard. He had a favor to ask of you and treated you as an honored guest, even specially visiting the teahouse to invite a Tea Server to brew a pot of hot tea. You had never experienced such hospitality before. Watching the ferry workers and hired members of the Flying Stone Gang toil busily, drenched in sweat, while you lounged leisurely, you felt a bit uneasy. Yet you didn't want to cause trouble, so you accepted Guildmaster Jiang's kindness and truly spent your time with him sipping tea and chatting. Though not a scholar by background, Guildmaster Jiang had considerable business acumen, and every day he taught you to appreciate ceramics and antiques. After several days of deep discussions, your eyes were truly opened.

A month has passed, and today marks your final day helping at Anji Pavilion. Your senior sister settled the accounts and saw you off politely, only to call you back and confess she had bravely struck her husband. She had thought herself wrong in her choice, destined to endure her life honestly, but upon actually resisting, she realized it was far more difficult than she had imagined. Even after being cast out, with her in‑laws refusing to accept her, as long as the Tang Clan still exists, she would never be without a home.

You also treat the sick and injured of the Anji Hall without charge. They are all overwhelmed with gratitude, their tearful eyes blurred by tears as they see your face, not finding it unattractive at all.

You're not just hanging around in the Tang Clan's kitchen for nothing; as soon as you took action, you significantly improved the diet at Anji Pavilion. Not only did you save costs, but you also took care of health.

Finally, the source of malicious trouble was driven away, but the troubles ahead were far from over. From that day on, you were constantly shuttling between the inn and the Anji Hall, taking charge of cooking, distributing porridge, and doing whatever needed doing, overwhelmed by the workload. The once‑popular senior sister, who had been everyone's favorite, rolled up her sleeves, revealing her pale, slender wrists, and helped you with all the tasks, moving about busily.
You defeated the wicked beggar, who left grumbling, and the senior sister was quite surprised. After several years apart, your martial arts have become so strong.

You and your Senior Sister were unable to retrieve the evil beggar at that moment, allowing him to spread rumors and summon many helpers. As the situation grew dire and you were contemplating your escape, your Eldest Senior Brother suddenly appeared to assist. He flicked his fingers, launching the Coin Darts, and effortlessly repelled the group of beggars. He came suddenly and vanished just as quickly; your Senior Sister was still eager to catch up, but your Eldest Senior Brother had already disappeared into the shadows.
You are brave and bold; whoever dares insult a Tang Clan member will have their mother suffer your wrath. He roared a curse on the spot and immediately engaged the evil beggar in combat.

You pressed your advantage without mercy, taunting him with words and demanding he apologize to your Senior Sister. Little did he know, that evil beggar was no pushover; cornered, desperate thoughts took hold, and he told himself: however frightening your Second Senior Brother might be, he'd simply beat you up and flee — surely he wouldn't bother hunting down a nobody like you over a thousand miles just for revenge.

As for your hand skills, let's not discuss them, but your verbal skills are truly impressive. A few words from you left the evil beggar both furious and fearful, neither able to fight nor retreat. His heart already wavered, yet he couldn't bring himself to back down, so he resolved to fight you head‑on.

Having just scared off that thug, you still pressed your advantage without mercy — catching him off guard, you wet your blade with saliva and stabbed at him without hesitation, truly vicious to the core. That thug, no stranger to dirty tricks himself, had never seen anyone as shameless as you, and on the spot was stabbed half to death.
You immediately invoked the name of the Second Senior Brother to intimidate them, and it worked all too well — but your Senior Sister's eyes immediately lost their spark.

As soon as you arrived at Anji Hall, you found Beggar Sect disciples harassing Young Madam Zhong, hurling crude insults with no regard at all for her husband, Young Master Zhong. Young Master Zhong was incorrigibly unruly, having been fond of fighting in his youth and once joined the Beggar Sect. When your Senior Sister was still unmarried, she saw him with a reckless, devil‑may‑care air that seemed to echo something of Eldest Senior Brother's unrestrained spirit, and touched by how attentively he cared for her, she finally agreed to marry him — only to find her judgment had been far off the mark. It was the same carefree attitude, but where Eldest Senior Brother roamed the world as a hero, her husband was merely a bully riding on borrowed menace, fierce on the outside and craven within. In the Beggar Sect he was nothing more than an errand boy for the beggar chief, and without the Nangong family stepping in, he couldn't even manage to leave the sect. Even as his own wife was bullied, he stayed meek and submissive, both fearing scoundrels and currying favor with them. Slow as Senior Sister Xin Ru could be, even she knew she had married the wrong man. She simply couldn't bring herself to admit it, telling everyone she met that she was living well. Humiliated by the wicked beggars today, she could neither seek help from her husband's family nor gain anything from complaining to the Nangong family beyond a quiet hushing‑up — and in the end her husband would only scold her for making a scene and shaming the Zhong family. But she was not only the Zhong family's wife; she was also a daughter married out from the Tang Clan. You stepped forward, standing boldly in front of her to shield her.

You have extensive research in medicine and poison, and with your internal skill, your pulse diagnosis is precise and your discernment sharp. You are adept at fighting poison with poison, with swift effects, embodying the style of the famed Ruthless Young Master of old. Within a month of practicing at Qianjinfang Clinic, the reputation of the Ghost-Face Physician spread throughout Jiangling Prefecture, eventually reaching the ears of the Second Senior Brother. Even those who are usually strict found themselves unable to suppress a rare smile.

You have only slightly touched the surface of medical skills and lack mastery. During this month of practice with the senior doctor, you have gained substantial benefits, expanded your knowledge, and deepened your understanding of pharmacology.

You have learned through practice; though you've only had a month of training, you've indeed gained a great deal. You've gained a good grasp of the medical arts — besides interning, you also earned a bit of pocket money.
You followed the instructions of the Second Senior Brother and went to the folk clinic where he had once served as a guest doctor, to gain experience there.
You smiled sheepishly, having heard him out, but whether you could hold your tongue next time remains uncertain.

Who would have guessed that you, with a smile that was not quite a smile, said these few blows today were meant to awaken the two scholars, done for the sake of the common people. If they truly attain official status in the future, if they enter government service and assist the Emperor in governing the country, how could they, merely because they passed each other by, judge others by appearance and speak lightly of them? Ask yourself, can such a person truly love the people? Therefore, we must take advantage of this moment to let them remember the taste of the commoners' fists, to make them understand that all people are flesh and blood. All people are to be feared; do not look down upon yourself. Otherwise, with only poetry and books in your belly, speaking eloquently, yet without a heart of benevolence, when you hold office, you will only mislead the country. A few words spoken lightly, as if carrying infinite strength, as if all the people of the world stand behind you. Commander Song fell silent, only considering his official position, and could only nod slightly in respect. He did not agree with your methods, but he admired your character.
Chief Inspector Song has some camaraderie with you and trusts you aren't someone who ignores reason, so he kindly advised you.

It's a shame you, a martial artist, failed to subdue two frail scholars in time, letting them shout and cause a commotion that drew in the neighborhood and the constables, leading to your arrest. If it weren't for the Nangong family intervening, you wouldn't know how long you'd have to spend in jail.

You looted their silver taels, took them to the local branch of the Flying Stone Gang, and sold them at a low price. After many twists and turns, the two scholars finally met the Flying Stone Gang Leader to explain the situation and were released back to Jiangling Prefecture. The scholar who only knew how to compose poetry and write articles put theory into practice by working as a laborer for several months, becoming much stronger. He also realized that the so‑called hardships of the common people were not just four inked characters on paper. One of them later determined to strive, indeed passed the imperial exams and became a pillar of the state, the people's voice. The other person simply gave up books and joined the Flying Stone Gang, becoming as strong as an ox within a few years.
And looted their silver taels.
You put your words into action, using your fists to teach a lesson to the two scholars who had grown up in comfort and luxury.

The man named Guildmaster Jiang spoke at length: It was Shangguan Qianjin who, on her way to deliver birthday gifts, encountered an urgent matter that required her personal attention. At the time, a north wind was blowing, so she entrusted the gifts to a ship company for transport. However, the homing pigeon sent by the branch office to notify them went missing, arriving late. This led to a collision between the same ship company's merchant vessels on the river. The ship company had spent a great deal of gold and silver to secure the exclusive right to transport grain, having won the trust of the Imperial Court. How could they allow others to use the ship company's name to share in the profits? The sailors immediately demanded to board the ship by force, demanding tolls for crossing the river. Unbeknownst to them, the people on the opposing vessel were members of the Cang Gang, under the Shangguan family's command. Though not pirates, they were no saints either, and they refused to comply. In a fit of anger, they seized all the grain, medicine, and dried goods on the other ship. This was a problem, as those goods were ordered by the Zhong family, a relative of the Nangong family, who had contracted the official Anji Hall business. In the end, you let out a long sigh, gently stroking your children's heads, one in each hand, and led them home. The children were flattered and delighted, and Xiahou Lan, seeing you finally set aside your grudges, was overjoyed as well. That evening she cooked a great deal of food, poured wine for you, and chatted idly about old times.

You stand outside the wall, listening to the laughter of others, and turn to see a pair of children with wistful eyes. They look at you, growing up just as you once longed for your parents' love and care. Like your parents, you have never smiled at them.

You drank yourself to sleep, and that night, Xiahou Lan hanged herself.
Her shadow swayed in the firelight, feet not touching the ground, like a ghost.

You returned to Snow Mountain in defeat, bearing news of your wife and children's deaths.
Xiahou Lan wept in silence, raising her hand as if to strike you, yet in the end could not bring herself to do it.

These people had retired and were now simple commoners; by striking at commoners, you drew the wanted notices of the Imperial Court.
