You issued an eviction order. Neither Gang Leader Shi nor his lady could gain entry and both felt disappointed. After having tea and snacks, they went home.
Well... the Sect Leader's token is in your hands. I'll do as you command.
I don't care!

Hey? Really, we should expel them? The Western Wulin Alliance's conference is approaching, and we're in need of help. The Flying Stone Gang has a large number of people. It's rare for them to show sincerity; shouldn't we take the opportunity to turn enemies into friends?
Their marital strife is what implicated Eldest Senior Brother in his death. Even if I could forgive it, the others cannot. I regret that they are not welcome — please ask them to leave.
If not for their couple's petty, trifling squabbles, Eldest Senior Brother would still be alive. What are they doing here now? Tell them to get lost.
Enemies of the Eldest Senior Brother are not welcome.
Is the Flying Stone Gang Leader here?
Senior Brother, the Flying Stone Gang Leader and his wife have sent in a visiting card, hoping to call on us. They're at the tea house now — should we let them up the mountain?
Flying Stone Gang Leader? Quickly, show them in!
Sect Leader, the Flying Stone Gang Leader and his lady have sent in a visiting card requesting an audience. They're waiting at the tea house — shall we let them up the mountain?
I was in a state of ecstatic joy, yet a touch of worry lingered. This father‑daughter pair truly tests one's patience.
A-anyway, just remember—you'd better behave yourself!
Calm down, don't let it get more real!
Damn it! You dare! I'll kill you!

From now on, we have a commitment; you can no longer be distracted or look elsewhere. At that time, don't claim that our relationship is merely sibling‑like, trying to deceive or evade; I won't accept that. If you dare to be unfaithful to me... for example, by flirting with other women...
I was afraid you'd change your mind and snatch it back anyway.
You've received it, you know. You can't return it, you know.
Thank you, Sister Xiang

This jade hairpin is for you—doesn't a dragon have a pair of horns on its head?
So this one and mine make a pair, to serve as... to serve as a token that our two hearts beat as one.
Long Xiang drew a jade hairpin from within her robe, carefully wrapped in a square of silk.

Don't talk like that～cheer up.
Didn't you say you're quite fond of your big sister? Then you'll have to risk your life to come and get me.
Ah, the road ahead is long, and beset with obstacles.
Okay, I'll wait for you
It's a matter of time, wait for me.
Since my father has spoken, our future together will simply have to wait until you've mastered your martial arts.
It's probably the effect of the Mysterious Candle Heart Sutra from Jinxiang Palace.
That is your biological father whom you haven't seen in over a decade; you only cried twice before managing to hold back your tears, which shows your extraordinary composure.
Alright, alright, let's start over

You're right... Why must you pick at my wording, you little brat?
Can't you say something warm and comforting instead of running your mouth and needling me?
Isn't that obvious? If you can hold it back, naturally you won't cry.
I—I'm not usually such a weepy coward, I'm tough as nails. I only cry when I truly can't hold it back.
I'm sorry, I got your clothes wet
You tried gently patting her back to help her breathe, and Long Xiang found it very comforting. Without realizing it, she began sniffling and stopped crying, no longer weeping.
You dared not move a muscle, standing stiff and straight, letting her bury her face in your shoulder and weep freely. After a long while her sobs finally quieted, and the tears stopped.
I never dreamed it would be true—wuwu waaah～～

Waah... this is wonderful... how could something this good happen...
I... actually, when I was little, every time Master beat me, I'd hide and cry, and while crying I'd think,
maybe Father wasn't dead—only hiding to frighten me... and sooner or later he'd come for me...
And he's still alive! Living well, living well all along...
...Brother, do you believe it? My father is the Wulin Alliance Leader, an absolute master, and number one under heaven.
Yes

Only after you've weathered this hard battle will your life's true trial begin—and that trial is myself, Long Yuan. Unless you defeat me until I'm utterly convinced, I will not let my daughter give herself to you.
You too, lad—not that I have much hope for you, but put your back into your training.
Yes!
Little Brother, you as well. If you mean to be worthy of my Xiang'er, you'd best not fall behind her — wouldn't you agree?
Yes, Xiang'er will certainly study hard.
I still have matters to attend to, and it wouldn't do to bring you along. I'll come see you again another day and test how far your skills have come — you mustn't slacken.
These matters — I'll leave them for next time, and explain everything to you then.
I'll save the rest for when we meet again, and explain it all to you then.
My mother was such a wonderful person... I'm so glad.

She and I did not know each other until we fought, then shared hardship together and broke down the prejudice between our two nations. She gave her whole life to peace between Song and Jin, and earned merit beyond counting. The Bizarre Acupoint-Striking Rope and the Xuanxuan Ruyi Finger — both she taught me herself, hand in hand.
You reap what you sow. It's not my fault I'm scatterbrained — it's yours.

She was every bit as beautiful as you, a formidable martial artist, deeply learned, and graceful with horse and bow — valiant and spirited, yet noble and refined. A woman I never deserved. That scatterbrained, carefree streak of yours most likely comes from me.
What kind of person was she?
Judging a person's good or evil by their status or background is the height of foolishness. My master already taught me that... at Fengyu Mountain, she showed me through her own example.
I know.

Song and Jin are enemies because of scheming by the rulers of both nations — it's the common people who suffer for it. Why hate someone you've never even met? Jin people are people too; there are good ones among them, and your mother was the best of them.
My mother is a Jurchen, named Wanyan Meng...
Your mother was the daughter of the late Jin emperor Wanyan Yungong — Wanyan Meng, Princess of Yiguo.
Princess?!
I only know that she is a princess.
Didn't Lady Wen tell you about your mother?
I have so much I want to say, I want to hear you talk about Mother's stories...
What? Are you not staying with us? We've only just met less than two hours ago, and you're leaving again.
Father is leaving, Xiang'er.
You still hold the unyielding belief, as steadfast as I once was. I once fled from my duty, making a decision that would haunt me for a lifetime. I hope you take it as a warning.
Thank you, Father...!
This is the sword your mother wore in life, named Wrathful Mist. The Celestial Cup Sword was my own blade in years past — it may be too heavy for you. This one should suit you better.
A beautiful sword.
Xiang'er, I have an item for you.
I also have something for you.
Is the talk over?
Xiang'er, come back.
No need to kneel. If you're fortunate enough to live to see that day, you can bow it back to me then.
Yes! Thank you, Senior.
There isn't much time left; how much you grasp is up to you. If you can't master it, don't force it — that will do more harm than good.
I understand.
But you are different — you have the Chapter on Forgetting Form.

And the book I am handing you now is a summary of extracts drawn from those seven arts — less a secret manual, really, than a distillation of my own understanding. Without the foundation of the seven arts, anyone else who got hold of it could learn nothing from it; the book would be of no use to them at all.
Oh

Xiang'er has devoted herself wholly to swordsmanship, and her skill surpasses mine. That foundation took more than ten years of hard cultivation to lay; for you to think of starting from scratch now is just a pipe dream.
Indeed. Unless one possesses extraordinary talent and the right opportunities, it is difficult to attain mastery, let alone integrate and understand thoroughly.
I know, according to Jianghu legends, the original masters of those seven martial arts were all renowned experts. The martial arts by which they became famous were certainly not ordinary.

Listen, my martial arts skills actually come from Seven Secret Manuals, which are interconnected and indispensable. Each of the Seven Secret Manuals requires both internal and external cultivation, making them quite difficult to learn.
For now I'll just call you Little Brother—what to call you needs more thought yet.
They just call me by my name.
So, how do your father and mother call you? Work? Work sounds odd. When they call you, it feels like they're summoning you to do chores.
Good~
Men are talking—you keep quiet. Keep interrupting and I won't teach it at all. Off you go.
T-that's wonderful!
Great, brother! This is our family's secret technique; my father has acknowledged you.
You've looked after Xiang'er a great deal in the past. Since she calls you her brother, then this Long and you must share some manner of bond. Take this Secret Manual.
No way! Don't give up so fast!
I might as well reincarnate sooner
I might as well reincarnate sooner
Unworthy daughter

I will definitely do it—and show you.
I will definitely do it

That's your own affair—you'll have to find a way to survive until then. If you die at the hands of the Wulin Alliance, it only means you and my Xiang'er were fated to meet but not to stay together. Better hurry and get yourself reincarnated.
Even if I have the heart, I might not make it to that time.

I am missing an arm and growing older, while you are young and strong, full of potential. How can you say you are at a disadvantage? If you want to marry my daughter, then grit your teeth and train hard for ten years. If you can't even muster this bit of pride, I suggest you give up on this idea.
No backbone
That's asking too much! Even reborn in another life, I might not manage it!

I won't budge unless this kid's martial arts skills surpass mine. He can't win by cheating or trickery; he must win ten matches out of ten, with complete victories. Only when he's strong enough will I feel at ease entrusting my daughter to him.

No wonder—that's just like me, hahaha!
Now that's satisfying to hear, hahaha! Well said, well said—no wonder you're a true daughter of Long Yuan, hahaha!
You silly girl, isn't this your own answer? Where does the correct answer come from?
How does that sound...? Did I say that right?

I can't bear to see innocent people bleed or hear the cries of the innocent. I don't want to blindly follow the crowd; I wish to speak up for fairness based on my own judgment. Whenever there's injustice, I will strive to argue for it with reason. Even if Heaven doesn't see it, I will do it until I am satisfied with my own heart.

Sister Xiang's style of conduct is remarkably similar to the Tang Clan. However, we walk the line between righteousness and wickedness, acting only according to our own hearts, while she carries herself with unwavering integrity.
No wonder she's the killer of Jinxiang Palace—her threshold for turning to violence is remarkably low.

It makes no difference. Not even ten thousand lives added together can excuse twisting right and wrong. If they insist on trampling the weak with their strength, then let them be ready to kill and be killed in turn.
Even if killing one person can save ten thousand, is it the same?

Thanks to Brother Zhao's reminder, I've remembered what I set out to do. Let them chase fame and fortune if they like, let them gather to flatter one another—that's none of my concern. But when so-called righteousness or the greater good tramples fairness underfoot, that I will never accept!
Sister Xiang's words sound sweeter than a song—almost too smooth. I wonder who taught her to talk like that.
Sister Xiang's words are more beautiful than poetry; she spoke beautifully.
Long Xiang gave you a glance, her eyes carrying a smile, pride unmistakably evident: She found you.
Having seen the darkest night, still believe in light; wade through the mire, always with a heart as pure as ice. Find a radiant star in the endless crowd.

So my Master sent me out of the palace to make my way through the Jianghu—not to fight and kill, but truly so I could meet all sorts of people: the good, the wicked, and those in between. To broaden my experience, take the occasional loss or hardship, and grow stronger for it.
Yes—it really was hard to endure.
If this is true, one can never truly retreat; it's merely an escape. No matter how far one hides, grudges still brew in the heart, the bitterness and sweetness known only to oneself, to endure alone.
This was just a sentence‑no one would take it seriously. Sister Xiang is overthinking.

I once heard someone say: 'Wherever there are people, there is the Jianghu.' Is that true? If so, then the Jianghu is truly everywhere—one needn't even learn martial arts. Every villager in every village is part of the Jianghu. The Emperor himself is part of the Jianghu. Even between you, Father, and me, the Jianghu lies between us.

In this world, it would be strange not to chase fame and fortune—everyone hopes to live a better life. If you've grown weary of it, or can't stomach it anymore, the two of us can simply retire from the Jianghu together.

I've heard tales of your deeds since I was a child, and I longed for the Jianghu. Once I finally walked it myself, I found that nearly everyone I met belonged to one of these three kinds, and my heart couldn't help but grow cold.

Chivalry, in its literal sense, means the spirit to act bravely for justice and to uphold the weak against the strong. Yet the so-called heroes of the Wulin all claim to walk the righteous path, while what they truly struggle over, day and night, is first fame, then profit. Worse still is the third kind—those who pose as noble and above worldly gain, yet kill merely to put on a show of nonchalant grace. The sight of them is enough to make one furious.
I wasn't born to be who I am, hero or not, it's hard to say.
I'm not like you, who are born a hero. I fear death, fear pain, and sometimes cry. For a while, I've been very confused‑what exactly is Jianghu, and what does chivalry mean? It's truly perplexing.

Father, are you also testing me? I've thought about this question for a long time, but I've pondered it a hundred times and still can't figure it out. The master also said that I need to figure it out on my own; I can't copy others' answers as my own beliefs, or I'll end up regretting it in the end.
Very well.
Little Brother, let me answer this one—I know it.
Great Hero Long, permit this junior a word—
As a father, I cannot let you charge ahead without a thought for what may come after.

His martial arts aren't bad, but they're still just the valor of a single man. Let a thousand soldiers and ten thousand horses come charging in, and even someone with three heads and six arms would end up trampled into the mud all the same. If you marry him, what happens if the Tang Clan vanishes overnight?
No, I do have a Master—he's just not from the Tang Clan.
What else could it be? His martial arts skills are also very high. Among his contemporaries in the Wulin, few can reach his level, let alone the fact that he is self‑taught.
I'm not looking down on him because of his appearance... Perhaps a little, but not entirely.
Father, he is a good man—upright and righteous, brave and steadfast, of truly fine character. Don't look down on him just because he isn't handsome.
Indeed!
I might as well be straightforward‑I disagree with this marriage.
Uh...

Xiang'er, what sort of joke is this? Scooping up dirt to use as incense is only for when there's truly no other choice—incense sticks are easy enough to come by, yet you were so careless. Honestly, you're driving me mad with anger.
Uh...
Don't even think about it. I only showed myself because you two were about to bow to Heaven and Earth, and you actually have the nerve to bring it up with me?
In short, since you, young man, dragged my daughter into this, you're responsible for her safety. Fail to protect her, and I'll mask up and kidnap her myself.
So complicated.
Right, right!

Once you're tied to me, the Tang Clan stops being the Mud Cult's puppet and becomes a Jin state spy instead. The Imperial Court won't even need to worry about the Wulin banding together in mutual defense—sending troops to wipe you out will be perfectly justified.

I'm a dead man already. If I returned to the world, the old scores from those years would inevitably be dragged back into the light. Losing my reputation would be the least of it—if someone with an agenda seized on it to attack me, that would be a case of cleverness undoing itself.
You give your old man too much credit. Show me a qigong so powerful it can sweep away a thousand troops—I'd love to see it.
You can't destroy the Wulin Alliance with just one qigong?
Missy, you make it sound far too simple.

I always hoped you would come out of seclusion to be the Alliance Leader of the Western Wulin Alliance. With Great Hero Long Yuan holding court in Western Shu, the Eastern Wulin Alliance would be nothing but an empty name.
What's that 'huh' for? Don't look at me like that.
Huh?

Nevertheless, I have no intention of getting involved; the situation might become quite troublesome as a result. It's best if you two keep quiet and even conceal it from Third Hero Tang so that no one knows my whereabouts.
Ha ha! Indeed—giving back exactly what you got is practically a time-honored Tang Clan virtue.

Stop overthinking it. Since when do you need grand principles for this? If someone comes after you meaning to kill you, who cares about their reasons—thrash them! Isn't tit-for-tat the Tang Clan's specialty?
That's true!

Sacrificing the small self for the greater good is a noble thing, but it's no excuse to trample the weak. It only counts if I choose it of my own will. Being sacrificed against my will, that's not sacrifice—that's called 'getting killed,' isn't it?
Oh... what a vivid and striking metaphor that was.

What did you say? Who's been filling your head with such heresy? How could that nonsense possibly be right? Ten beggars could surround me swearing dog shit was edible, and I still wouldn't believe them.
Father, is the justice recognized by most people truly justice? Is sacrificing the small self for the greater good the right thing to do?

Hmm... I can't help feeling a flood of emotion, as if a lifetime had passed. Most of the masters of my generation perished in the decisive battle at the Supreme Bliss Cult; few of us remain. Though it's still called the Wulin Alliance, I hardly know a soul in it.
Yes.
Are you asking me about my opinion on the Wulin Alliance?
Even the Great Hero Long has to fear Sister Xiang.
Spare me, please.
But you acting on your own and leaving me behind is a different matter. I won't let this go.
Of course, the master is the best master in the world.
As it turns out, Lady Wen was a fine mentor indeed. You've grown up so well — I'm truly gratified. Your mother's spirit in heaven must be glad too.
...I prefer it this way now.

I really don't think I could have raised you to be this proper. Even if your mother were still alive, her temper was fierce too. If we'd raised you, you'd probably be dressed all in black by now, a fierce little hellion, picking fights everywhere and swaggering about.
Even if that's the case... ignoring me for over ten years is too much.

Only the dead are heroes; if I still cling to life, I'll inevitably face the wrath of the masses. Acknowledging you would only drag you and me into a life of wandering, like a wanted criminal on the run.
You are a hero indeed; your good and bad deeds offset each other, and the world will understand you.

I cannot bring myself to kill him, and heaven sends no lightning to strike him down either. So countless soldiers and commoners of the Great Song have suffered terribly for it. What face do I have to return in triumph as the Wulin Alliance Leader?
Wanyan Xun is at least an emperor; this kid is just a mountain village farmer, what power does he have?
Not everyone is like that. My Junior Brother is a good one — once looked down upon, and now a pillar of the Tang Clan, yet he hasn't turned bad.

If he hadn't had the slightest sincerity, I wouldn't have been deceived. In my youth, I boasted grandly, claiming that if he ever came to power, he would surely bring about reconciliation between the Song and Jin. Ha, yet when he changed positions, he changed his mind entirely, forgetting all those vows.
I have also met with Prince Yi, and it seems he has not forgotten the old friendship he had with you.
Now that I think about it, it was really foolish. I cut off my own arm, yet he still became emperor as usual, completely useless. It was just a one‑sided wish from my youth.

...in the battle of the Supreme Bliss Cult, my sworn brother broke his trust and changed his stance at the last moment, leading to the sacrifice of countless heroes from the Central Plains. I came to understand his true nature and should have resolutely severed our brotherhood and slain him to console my fellow warriors. But I am weak and compassionate, ultimately unable to bring myself to strike. Thus, I only cut off one arm as a penance for him.

It's no matter; those who know of it keep it quiet, but there are more than a few. Lady Wen, Gang Leader Wang, Nangong Family Head, and the Old Master all know the Emperor of Jin is my sworn brother. Only their concern for my name after death has kept it from becoming public.
Can I hear this?
She did — it's Prince Yi, isn't it? My Junior Brother and I have spoken of it before too.
Then she told you that your father has a sworn brother.
This bedtime story is too bloody... and Lady Wen's patience is too good.
Of course I've heard it; it's my favorite bedtime story. I've begged the master to tell it over a hundred times.
Has Lady Wen ever told you about what happened with the Supreme Bliss Cult, back in those years?
Were you planning to never recognize me?

I never imagined that in the blink of an eye all would change — Gang Leader Wang and Lady Wen passed away, one after another, and the umbrella that sheltered the two of us, father and daughter, from wind and rain was torn away, piece by piece. Fearing you would suffer hardship and humiliation, I came to the Tang Clan.

If the world were at peace, I had meant to spend my life in hiding, a living corpse of my own making — lost among the rank and file of the Beggar Sect, drowning myself in wine and dreams, content only to know that Xiang'er was safe.

Don't be fooled by that righteous act of his—his heart is petty as they come.
I only had one hand free, yet he kept kicking at me high and low, without a shred of a true master's grace.
There are only a handful of fighters in this world who could match him, yet he fights this shamelessly.
Half of it. This technique came out of a drunken brawl between him and me.
Oh, isn't this Uncle Wang's martial arts?
So you can take more of a beating.
I'm about to lose my life—what do I need a manual for!

...I hear you can master any manual you get your hands on. Might as well take this one too—
call it payment for your life.
My life is at an end!
Let me say this up front: I'm truly furious, so you'd best brace yourself.
Can't save you; this is your destined calamity. You must take care of it yourself.
Ah! Great Hero Long, save me!
So you do have honor, you little rascal—but you sure put me through hell keeping this from me.
I merely accepted a charge, and stayed true to it—nothing more.
I'll settle the score with you later

It was truly not easy—I wanted so badly to boast that I know the Great Hero Long.
Hiding it from Sister Xiang made my conscience ache all the more.
I mentioned it offhand at the time, but you kept your word and concealed my whereabouts until today‑it wasn't easy.
Wedding Ceremony
Current Situation
Why I hid my identity
Keeping my word
Just joking, just joking
Father~!
I've heard the whole story from Xiang'er. You little brat, daring to covet my precious daughter — come here and die!
You really can sleep, can't you.
A little over two hours.
I— how long was I unconscious?
You did not know how long you had lain senseless before you slowly stirred back to consciousness.
He came rushing at me all of a sudden, and that face of his gave me a fright.
Father, why are you hitting him?
Brother!
Lord Father‑in‑law~
Lord Father‑in‑law!
May I ask, Senior, what is your command?
Okay, okay, I'll go right away
Brother, what are you daydreaming about?

Sister Xiang truly is beautiful — her robes white as snow, her face like an immortal's. A commoner like me was never meant to touch such a thing.
I can only regret that so fine a dream wakes so soon.
Long Xiang's cheeks still bore traces of tears, yet her smile was as bright as spring sunshine, and you couldn't help but stare in rapture.
Brother, my father has something to say to you.
While I wear the Tang Clan uniform, just like the other brothers and sisters, I am merely a replaceable subordinate at any time.

We're hardly a match in station — Great Hero Long may walk among the Beggar Sect dressed like a vagrant, but in truth he's a Wulin master
of towering renown in the Jianghu. The son-in-law he seeks is bound to be a dragon and phoenix among men.

...Even if Sister Xiang truly doesn't mind my looks or my birth,
Great Hero Long surely wouldn't stand by and watch her throw her life away on folly, would he?

Deep down you sensed that she'd agreed to marry you only out of desperation, a moment's helplessness with nowhere else to turn.
Now that she has someone to rely on — and someone so extraordinary at that — there's no chance left between the two of you.

You withdrew to one side of your own accord, silently watching over Long Xiang.
Glad for her, even as you pitied your own reflection.
Let me provide this long‑separated father and daughter with a place to talk.
Quietly step aside
It's no wonder he intervened... I coveted his daughter, am I now in life‑threatening danger?
Fear

A man fit to be a legend of the Wulin, yet this is what he looks like!
How did he lose an arm, and why is he dressed in such rags?
Calm
Why did that kid start crying too?
Oh my, I'm so moved, I'm about to cry, sniff sniff.

Wow, my luck is just too good!
I've actually had the fortune to meet a living legend of the Wulin!
I'll have plenty to boast about to the Tang Clan lot when I get back!
Worship

Long Yuan's name rings like thunder — every soul who walks the Jianghu has heard it.
In the Supreme Bliss Cult affair, the sword hero Long Yuan met the Cult Leader in a battle at its peak, and the tale of his Celestial Cup Sword shattering the Ghost Lotus King's Blade
is told with relish to this day.
Former Wulin Alliance Leader?!
Is that person really the Great Hero Long Yuan?
No matter how reckless I am, I wouldn't go that far.
Stay calm, don't let your thoughts become too vivid, or you might kill someone in a fit of anger.

From now on, we are bound to each other, and you can no longer let your eyes wander.
Don't you dare then claim we're nothing more than brother and sister, trying to talk your way out of it — I won't stand for that.
And if you ever dare betray me… by going off to seduce some other woman…
I still fear that you might regret and take it back.
You've received it, you know. You can't return it, you know.
You're welcome. It's only right.
Thank you, Sister Xiang
Tsk, you bad little brother, who taught you to talk like that? So annoying.
I was joking, I was joking
I would never! What do you take me for, some fickle, faithless woman? This pair of hairpins is carved from a single dragon's two horns—there's no third, no fourth to be had!
You don't happen to have a whole stash of these hairpins you hand out to everyone, do you?
See? I wasn't lying to you.
Hmm, don't worry, I have another one exactly the same, let me show you.
This is your hairpin
There was no wedding today, but our two hearts are as one—we should still have some proof of it. Here, take this and keep it safe.
No matter what I say, you're always uneasy, you coward, aren't you? Here—take this as a token.
Why do you still think I have ill intentions and want to hurt you?
And here I thought you wanted to murder me to keep me quiet.

A woman marries but once in her life—and I have no father, no mother, and to this day no master to guide me patiently. Is it not my right to arrange my own life's greatest affair myself? I may be clumsy, but that's no excuse to call it laziness or carelessness.
So it turns out yesterday was an auspicious day—I didn't know you were so particular about such things.
Turns out yesterday was an auspicious day?
Hehe, what's the big deal? I'm not really praising you, so why are you so happy?
Hehe, you flatter me, you flatter me.
Feasting on delicacies while the injured person is nearby, you're really heartless.

The case is surprisingly simple. I was eating a chicken leg next to you, but who knew it was so juicy and delicious. I took a bite, and the chicken juice splattered, dripping onto your bandaged wound.
Mmph... erm...
That's not right, so why were you just bandaging me?

Yes, a Junior Sister from the Tang Clan skilled in medicine examined your wound and said it's nothing serious. But you've been overtaxing your mind and sleeping poorly for so long, so she burned some incense to help you sleep more soundly.
Could I really have fainted and slept straight through the midnight hour?
It made us waste the auspicious day and hour—how infuriating. Now our affair will just have to wait for another lucky date.
I don't know what that person's business is here, just causing a ruckus for no reason. It's... it's...
That's no surprise—true experts are always like a spirit dragon: you glimpse the head, never the tail.

I saw you injured and carried you back. The skilled warrior didn't pursue, so I left it at that. The details of what happened, I reported to Third Hero Tang. However, when they sent people to search the back mountain for signs of the high‑ranking figure again, they found nothing.
Come to think of it, how did we get back? And what happened to that masked expert from the back mountain?
I acted on impulse, lost control, and didn't mean to hurt you.
You slashed me, and you're still feeling wronged?
I didn't mean to—why are you being like this? I've been worried sick about you all this while, yet you're still so harsh with me. It's really hurtful.
No more next times! I'll strangle you to death this time!
Did I hurt you? Sorry, I'm doing this for the first time. Practice makes perfect, I'll improve next time.
You're awake; I'm bandaging your wound
Help me!

I'm dead, I'm dead!

Hmm, Second Senior Brother wishes me to first harmonize the Five Elements and restore balance, then gradually repair the meridians and replenish the Qi sea. Later, we can expel the pathogenic factors externally, thus eliminating the root cause.
Yes
Slow down, slow down — what do you mean, "exit the orifice"? My soul, you mean?

Starting tomorrow, you will be responsible for administering acupuncture to Miss Ye. First use the 'Observing Balance Needle,' then the 'Returning Pulse Needle,' and finally the 'Exit-Orifice Needle.'
Fine, I can't say no anyway
Anyway, I'll leave my things to you — recover what you can, that's fine. Hurry, hurry, hurry!
That's right
I'm definitely smarter than my senior sister Xin Ru. If it were her, she wouldn't even be able to keep the medicine box's strap.
You still have the nerve to say you're not muddleheaded.
I felt my luggage growing lighter, and I supposed it was due to my eagerness to return home, my steps becoming brisker as well.
How could you not have noticed even a bit?

Alright, don't talk about this anymore, help me quickly. I'm almost there, but I just realized the medicine box has a hole, things are falling out all the way, and I can't retrieve them alone. Plus, Second Senior Brother is worried about me. I'm afraid of being scolded and also afraid that the medicines will be eaten by wild animals when I go back.
I'm just late. Life is so long; why worry about moving a bit slower?
You and Senior Sister Xin Ru are both called the Tang Clan's Muddleheads—one can't sleep straight, the other's always late.
I've been late for so long? I'm doomed... That's why Second Senior Brother's letter had such a harsh tone.
And another thing, Senior Sister Tang Fang—you haven't been gone just a couple of months. You've been down the mountain practicing medicine and traveling for over two years now.
Oh, close enough!
All wrong! Not one word right—my name is Zhao Huo, all right?!
I still remember your name... what... what... Chen Guandong.
Senior Sister hasn't been gone more than a couple of months, and you've already forgotten me, Junior Brother?
You...?
"Your Excellency," is it? I've only been gone a month or two, and you've already forgotten me, Junior Brother?
Wearing the red attire of our sect's female disciple, may I ask who you are...?
Only you, an outsider disciple, are left—sent on a mission and still hoping to play dumb and slip away? Dream on!
I still have my own tasks to finish, not going!
Not going
Let's go out and take a look
Go out and take a look
That voice sounds oddly familiar.
Is there anyone there? Come on, someone help me!
Outrageous!
Ah!
Don't worry, I'll never throw the leftover banana peel carelessly. Because this is going to be thrown on your face!
Senior Brother, I just wiped that area, don't step on it. Also, don't hold the banana while walking and eating, can you do that?
Lowlife, wipe the floor carefully for me, don't even think of being lazy! Chew chew chew.
Ugh, my back and waist are sore‑let me stretch a bit.
Okay
Well, I can't convince you. Finish work early and come play cards‑the one Yunshang invented.
It's just habit, is all. Leave the floor be, and I never think of it—but once I start scrubbing, I can't do it halfway, or my whole body feels wrong.
Now, where are there still so many senior masters in our sect? It's certainly not the Sect Leader who will take you in.
I've gotten used to it, always wanting to go all out, hoping a master will notice my diligence and take me in as an apprentice.
You don't need to clean the floor tiles so meticulously every time. Even if they're clean, when the Fourth Senior Brother walks by eating, it's still going to get oily and greasy.
Good. Thank you, Senior Brother.
Junior Brother, I'll put the water bucket behind for you. When you turn around, don't kick it.

With your silver tongue, you turned ordinary candied hawthorn into a special medicinal dish of the Tang Clan. The villagers believed it to be true, flocking to buy it and eagerly pulling out their money. Not only were there verbal disputes, but intense conflicts even broke out, ultimately escalating to the point where officials had to intervene to settle the matter.
Received widespread acclaim

You rallied your spirits and went about peddling candied hawthorn sticks. Most of the villagers recognized you, and assumed you'd finally washed out of the Tang Clan and taken to peddling wares to scrape by. Unable to help feeling for you, they all opened their purses to patronize your stall.
Manageable
In the end, you had to pay out of your own pocket to buy the candied hawthorn, then gave it to others to share, and returned home feeling lonely.
Candied hawthorn sticks are delicious, but the seller's unattractive appearance affects the appetite. Plus, they're a coin more expensive than usual, so they don't sell at all.
Gloomy and dull
Delicious... candied hawthorn skewers, six wen a string... Kind uncles, aunties, little young masters, come and buy!
Oh~ Looks like there's another fish caught in my net! Get over here!

Reporting to the authorities is useless, hahahah, the officials are all my people, have you heard of officials covering for each other? Just give up, you little cuties like you are born to be tormented and destroyed by me!
Oh! Sister Fang, don't go, help us report to the authorities!
I do, and the price is negotiable.
You still want another time?
Oh dear! Look at me, I've been holding back for too long, couldn't help it this time, next time I'll be more restrained.
No... no, I was wrong. Sister Ying doesn't want a treasure map; she wants our lives!
Hoo... hoo...
Oh, okay, take care
I've been delaying for so long; I need to hurry to the Outer Fort. See you later at the mountain.

Madam Shangguan's gaze was exactly like my sister's back then... just as dangerous. So it wasn't put on after all. No wonder Yunshang gets jealous when Junior Martial Sister gets close to me. Now the truth is clear.
It's not that I can't understand Madam Shangguan's feelings. When I was little, my Junior Martial Aunt... no, my own sister, also doted on me like this, tossing me every which way.
Senior Brother, save me!!!
Guh! This isn't about money, I'm about to run out of air!
Don't struggle, little darling! Let me hold you for a while! Just close your eyes and count to ten! I'll give you some pocket money! How about ten coins for a breath?

My goodness, what stroke of fortune let someone be born so pale and dainty, more adorable than a Mohele Doll or a porcelain one? Come here quickly, let your big sister hug you and squeeze you and have a good look!
Huh?
Uh
Actually, I, your elder sister, love small and delicate things most of all. So the moment I laid eyes on you two, I liked you so much I wanted to keep you both for myself.
Since you've already said that, I don't need to pretend to be a gentleman anymore.
We're very cute, we know it ourselves. Why hold back on something like this? You could just be a bit more forthright~ Honestly, grown-ups have so many hang-ups.
Great! Great! I can't help but want to get close to you all, fearing that I might scare you, so I've been pretending to stay calm all along.
Empty words are not enough; you must prove it with action, hurry and pamper us!
R-really!
I believe you.
I think so too, sigh, who would believe that?
No matter how you say it, it's all empty talk.
...What must I say, before you'll believe me?
Then it must be meant for me to hear?
You assume others feel the same as you, and since you already have preconceptions, I suppose you won't believe it. After all, this isn't meant for you to hear.
I won't argue with you. It's impossible to communicate with you. I won't talk to you anymore.

How could I not want? Why can't I? Yunshang and Moling are so pretty and charming; every time I see them, I can't help but like them. I want to be close to them and pamper them. But what does that have to do with you?
It sounds nice, but who knows what mischief you're hiding in that belly of yours. Do you really expect me to believe you see those other girls as nothing more than sisters?

Even if there really were treasure, it would be silver the common folk gave to King Yue to fight the Jin — righteous wealth for a righteous cause, to prop up the Song. A mere merchant like me has no such grand ambition, and certainly not the gall to pocket it.

I just love to talk, so what of it? Since when is idle chatter against the law? Mind your own business. Who doesn't want to get rich? And don't you go playing the saint either — can a good person even be a merchant?

A word of advice: even if you believe those rumors about the treasure, you'd do well to watch your tongue. To spread rumors is to sow bad karma with your words — it marks a low character and does no small harm. And repeating hearsay, passing on lies as truth, is just as guilty.
What do you want now? Don't be so pushy, or you'll push me to the point where we both end up in a bad situation!
Hold on.
Alright, let's not talk anymore. Let's just stop, okay? For real, the daughter of an official is just different. Her words, once spoken, are sharper than a palm strike.
If you dare slander an official with rumors again, I'll drag you before the authorities myself, with no mercy. Don't believe me? Go ahead and try — see if I dare.
No, there isn't, I was just saying something random...

May I ask which article of the Great Song's penal code stipulates that officials' children cannot engage in commerce? What you just said seems suspiciously deceptive; are you trying to challenge me in court?
He's the father who holds office, you're the daughter who plays the crooked merchant — what's the difference!

Since you're ignorant, I'll say this once — listen well. My father is an official of the Imperial Court, not a merchant. The family's trade and commerce are managed by me, Shangguan Ying, and have nothing to do with Commissioner Shangguan.
You dare to hit me! You... You dare to hit me on Tang Clan's territory!

Why are you treating an old woman like me so harshly? Is this how a young miss of an official oppresses common folk? An official and a merchant both — isn't that just profiting off yourself? In other words, corruption. Where have I said wrong?
That Martial Aunt's bluster has been utterly crushed.
Sister Ying is so fierce
You... you...

If not for your ties to the Tang Clan, I could have you hauled before the local magistrate for slandering my father just now. As it is, I've held my temper and only called you Auntie — you'd best know what's good for you.
How come I'm nobody anymore? I used to be a Tang Clan female disciple, the same generation as the sect leader. Tell me what you should call me!
Do you know me?
You're the wife of Zhang, the face-wash peddler of Meishan Town. Born into the Tang Clan, perhaps, but you married out — now you're nobody.
Don't you dare! Don't you touch my godson!
When I come to collect, I'll send men to break every precious bone in your godson's body. Then you can go cry to the magistrate or to Sect Leader Tang — whichever you please!
It's a debt in black and white — unless you turn robber and tear up the paper, you'll have to pay up. Go on and make your scene; roll around on the ground again if you like.
You unscrupulous swindler, tricking my precious boy into borrowing money on purpose! You did it deliberately — you'll come to a bad end!
How could I not know? Your godson still owes me a mountain of debt.
What do you want? Do you know who I am?
Alright, you go to the back first and keep an eye on the two little girls for me.
This... this...
Those few roars could be heard all the way to the end of the street. I'm not deaf.
Lady Shangguan, you — you didn't hear all of that, did you?
Other matters aside, I can't just turn a deaf ear to this.

No one lets good water spill into another man's field — that's exactly how the Shangguan family got so rich: nothing but greed and corruption. Do you really think she came all this way just to flatter that Ye girl out of kindness? You'd best wise up and get your hands on it first!
Finally, I'm going home. This time, I can finish the task.
The three of them chatted and laughed, strolled and wandered, until dusk fell, when they finally walked home together.
As long as you know fear, that's enough.
Spare me, please.
Oh, really? Are you sure? Are you not afraid that next time during acupuncture, I'll get really upset and throw a tantrum so intense it would reach the ceiling?
I don't... I um... um...
You all ran around recklessly, no more for you!
Fang Sister, where's my candied hawthorn stick?

Yunshang sister is truly unfortunate. A person of integrity, a descendant of loyal and virtuous officials, yet she was unjustly slandered by those unscrupulous people, becoming the target of everyone's criticism. If it weren't for her brother's protection and the sect leader's shelter, she might have ruined her life.
Ah... These days the Tang Clan has no elder to rely on, but I rather enjoy the quiet. If Martial Aunt hadn't married out and nagged me every day, I'd hardly have been able to stay.
Respectfully seeing off Martial Aunt — safe travels, Martial Aunt.

Since you are so unteachable, there's no point in wasting words with you. I will go back and speak to the sect leader's junior brother about this. This is all I have to say; you should take care of yourself.
That is even more humiliating than death!
Even if there's truly no treasure, this girl's looks are decent enough. Marrying her to my foster son would still be acceptable. I'll just set a few rules for her and properly train her.
Hmph... You dare not.
Your niece dares not.
Understand? What a joke! No respect, lowlife! Are you the superior or am I? A mere junior, daring to scold me? Daring to teach me to do things? Have you gone mad?
Forgive your niece for disagreeing, but as I understand it, that is surely not this sect's creed!

Don't go saying I, your Martial Aunt, am cruel and unfeeling. If the Ye siblings forsake the dark path and turn to the light, shed those garish green robes, and hand over the treasure to join the Tang Clan, I might just make an exception.
How could this be... That's too unreasonable.

Remember: Any descendant of the Tang Clan, even if they are the worst, you must treat them as your own flesh and blood; conversely, those from the Diancang sect, no matter how good they are, you cannot treat them as humans, but as animals! Upon seeing them, just kill them on sight!
Is it really me who is unscrupulous?

Not only her, but every future disciple and descendant of the Diancang Sect should be wiped out to the last! As a Tang Clan disciple, you should love your own clan — who gave you leave to use that clever head of yours to judge right and wrong? Too clever by half, and rotten in your heart!

Nonsense! That is the Diancang Sect! They are the barbarians of Dali! The Diancang Green Robe Tortoise has killed countless talented youths of the Tang Clan; this hatred cannot live under the same sky! Regardless of their innocence, once they enter the mountain gate of the Diancang Sect, they deserve to die!

Martial Aunt! Even though the Tang Clan and Diancang had a grudge in the past, how does that concern Miss Ye? She is so innocent and carefree, even not knowing martial arts. How could you say such evil and cruel words!
If she can't be healed, her death would be convenient, perfect for skinning her and studying at leisure.
Could there be some potion that washes a tattoo away? Like a blank book that needs fire and water before the map and words appear.

Regarding the treasure rumor, Young Hero Ye has already refuted it, it's purely a rumor. Miss Ye's skin is as smooth as jade; not to mention tattoos, she has not a single flaw, how could there be a map?
Is the rumor about the treasure map true or false?
Yes, although my skills are not refined, Second Senior Brother has to avoid suspicion of impropriety between genders, so I can only take over.
Enough of that empty flattery — I didn't come here to chat with you. This young girl came to the Tang Clan for treatment; Zheng'er is the lead physician, and you administer the needles, correct?
What Martial Aunt says is right.
She has a pretty face, a rare beauty in the making. In a few more years, once she sheds her childish air, she's sure to grow into a true beauty.
Yes.
I heard that the Ye siblings from the Diancang Sect are now taking shelter under the Tang Clan. That mischievous girl, it's Ye Yunshang, isn't it?
Yes — this Martial Niece will answer everything she knows, holding nothing back.
Enough, none of that matters — this Martial Aunt has a question for you.
It's not the Sect Leader's fault — I entered the sect too late, and had no master to instruct me in the arts. These days my lessons are all given by Second Senior Brother.

The one who plays elder sister is my Junior Sister, and the one who plays younger sister is a generation below me. That Junior Brother of mine, the Sect Leader, grows more absurd by the day — what is he playing at now.
My elder sister... I mean, Little Martial Aunt — she's simply not to be compared with someone like me.

Not all sisters take after each other — your elder sister was far steadier in her ways than you.
If she were here, I'd need to give her a piece of my mind too.
That's good, I'm relieved now. Thank you, Martial Aunt.
It's really...
Look, the person you're looking for is there, and there's an ugly brute secretly looking after it; don't be alarmed.
Little, Martial Aunt Xiaolou, I haven't been in touch for a long time, Tang Fang, the niece of the teacher, paying respects to you.
Be quiet! You are a female disciple with some standing in the current era; shouting loudly in the street, what kind of decorum is this!
Where is !!
Huh?
I'm back with the candied hawthorn──
That'll be ten coins — much obliged, good lady~
Just said not to run around, and immediately ran around. Second Senior Brother really wasn't being overly worried; I need to go and keep an eye on them.
Secondly, it wouldn't hurt to build a little goodwill — maybe she'll go easier on me when it's time for the needle.
You're so kind.
Oh, so that's how it is...
Earlier, Sister Fang couldn't take her eyes off a hairpin on that stall. I want to buy it for her, to thank her for looking after us.
That won't work either
It's just over there; we won't get lost.
Eh, we can't do that.
Let's run around now!
Ahh, I'm at a loss with you. Stay here and don't run around; I'll go buy something for you.
Oh, my little heart!
Hmm～ I just want to eat candied hawthorn, okay? Okay?
Let's buy something else to eat. How about the five‑spice cake?
......I really did say that. But money isn't the issue; the problem is Second Senior Brother instructed that you can't eat sweet things.
Yes, you said it! You said if I quietly let you give me acupuncture, you would buy me something to eat. Now you want to back out?
I never said I'd buy any for you two.
Two skewers!
I do.
So do you want to eat it or not?
You're lying
You didn't say a word, but the drool that dripped down gave you away.
There's no such thing.
Sister Fang, Mo Ling said she wants to eat candied hawthorn~
Don't go running off, there's such a crowd. If we get separated, Great Hero Ye and Second Senior Brother will have my hide.
That's right, candied hawthorn.
Candied hawthorn?
Mo Ling, look over there!
Weren't you the one who came to hurry me along? And don't talk about fees—you and Martial Uncle never take payment when you treat people.
Yes. Your martial niece will answer everything she knows, without holding back.
Slow down. The patient won't heal on his own anyway, so the fee isn't going anywhere. Now, as your martial aunt, I have a few things to ask you first.
Yes, yes. I'll go right away.
Uncle Zhang said he had severe back pain and went to the Outer Fort early. What time is it already? You're still loafing around here! Always being late, if you're late again, it'll be dark by then!
Martial Aunt Xiaolou! It's been too long—your martial niece Tang Fang greets you and pays her respects.
Tang Fang, you are indeed late again
So he really did get beaten... Good thing it wasn't me.
Ah‑!

Third Senior Brother pleaded with Shangguan Ying and had Squire Lu step in to mediate, greasing the yamen's palms to secure your release. Shangguan Ying, being someone who needed the Tang Clan's help, let it go once she'd vented her anger, and never spoke of the matter again.
Be quiet, are you complaining that you weren't locked up long enough?
I don't care what rank her father holds; if it provokes me, even the princess won't be spared.
Ah, the reasoning may hold, but the consequence is still a jail cell.
She struck first—it's only right that I hit back, isn't it?
The magistrate's office is right next door, and you, you lunatic, dared to strike the daughter of the Imperial Shipbuilding Supervisor. I don't know whether to call you reckless or brave.
......The course of events is like this.

Uh... so, um, what a coincidence, running into you all here. I'm not following you, I just came to tell Yunshang not to eat so much sweet stuff... Wait, why are you looking at me like that? Like a knife's edge—hold on, let's talk this through... Ah!!
Junior Brother, you're built sturdier—you can take a beating better than I can. I'm begging you!
How could I not be afraid of being beaten?
Because I'm afraid of being beaten by Madam Shangguan. I don't know why; although she speaks to me politely, her gaze has been unfriendly all along.
Why?
......You go.
Should we go stop it?

Sweet flavors nourish the spleen, and sweets in moderation can strengthen the spleen and stomach, but too much does harm. If she doesn't restrain herself, it could injure her spleen and stomach, keep the body's fluids from transforming properly, and let phlegm-damp collect—wouldn't that undo her recovery?
Speaking of which, Madam Shangguan is far too free with her money—buying all this, how could anyone finish it? And Sister Yunshang shouldn't eat so many sweets anyway!
You two are speaking sweet words, yet your hearts are in agreement. One must not harbor the intent to harm others, yet one must not lack the caution to guard against them.
It's said like that, but Second Senior Brother is probably thinking the same thing as me. Not afraid of external enemies, but afraid that Madam Shangguan has ulterior motives.
Fear that Second Senior Brother is not guarding against poisonous insects and fierce beasts, but rather Lady Shangguan.

When the young lady goes out, two men clear the path ahead, two more guard the rear. Just look at them—strapping and fierce, each one could strangle a wolf bare-handed. Who'd dare cause trouble? Sending me along on top of that, isn't it a waste of effort?
I see—that's exactly like Second Senior Brother.
Second Senior Brother insisted I come along in secret—needless fuss, if you ask me.
Junior Brother, how come you're also here?
This plan is brilliant, exactly what I wanted, let's go!

Not our business, so don't meddle. The young lady gave us half a day off; she's not likely to stir up trouble out on the streets. We'll just settle in at the tea stall on the corner, order a bowl of something cold, and keep a lazy eye on her from a distance.
The young lady usually doesn't spend money like this, how come today?
Worship!
Ha ha, you flatter me, you flatter me — go on and worship me!
Well, it's no wonder you're Sister Ying! Your haggling skills are exceptionally skillful!
Why aren't you coming to get it? I won't eat it, so take it all.
The vendor reckoned the three girls had bought more candied hawthorn than they could ever finish, and dreading they'd have second thoughts and ask for a refund, he hurried away.
Thank you for your patronage!
Deal!
What's the problem then? A straw stick, how could it be worth anything?

I taught you such a fine trick — aren't you going to thank me? With so many candied hawthorn sticks, how are the three of us to carry them all? Why don't I add five more wen, and you throw in your carrying pole as well?
Well, well, all right — as the young lady says, fifty wen it is, fifty wen!
You want to be large, I don't mind.
Is that referring to me?
Have you noticed that little fierce beast next to me? She's most skilled at eating things deliciously! Others see her and can't help but be tempted.
Think again, how delightful it is to watch these two lovely young women contentedly munching. It's also a form of promotion for your candied hawthorn, making it a win‑win situation.
Right... I didn't think of that!

Why don't you have a cup of cooling tea, go home for a nap, there's still enough time to make new ones. Re‑open your stall in the evening market, which will be cool and refreshing. At that time, a round trip, how could you not earn more than a hundred wen a day?
Even a thin profit is still profit. Earn yourself a free morning, and you need not keep hawking here.
This... this... heh heh, neither a loss nor a profit, only earning a dozen-odd wen — wasn't this trip to set up my stall just a waste of time? Nobody does business like that.

This is meant to be sold — how could you eat it yourself? Doing business like this, you'll either work yourself to death or go broke. Don't think I don't know the going rate; I'll simply buy your candied hawthorn for fifty wen, and you won't lose a thing.
Worst case, I'll just eat them myself.

It's still early, and the sun is scorching. How long will these candied hawthorn sticks have to remain under the blazing sun before they sell out? By then, some will melt in the heat, and others will get covered in mud and sand when the wind blows‑you'll lose a lot, won't you?
Young fellow, you really don't know how to reckon accounts. I'm in a fine mood, so why don't I teach you?

This... this... small business, please don't make it difficult for me. I set up my stall every day, standing until the sun goes down, selling until I'm done, just hoping this little bit of change will fill my stomach. The lady comes up and cuts the price in half, which is really ruthless.
No miscalculation at all — I'm the one asking you for a bargain.
Wait, no, no, that won't do — Miss, you've miscounted. I have twenty pieces in all, four wen a string; that comes to eighty wen.
Alright then──
You have a total of twenty pieces here. I'll take them all. Charge me fifty wen. How about that?
Five wen a string. Seeing how lovely the young lady and her two little misses are, I'll make it four wen a string! How many will you have?
Shopkeeper, how much does your candied hawthorn cost?
You two heroines can stand down — no need to look at me like that. I'll go buy it for you.
Hoo...
Trouble! A wild candied hawthorn has appeared ahead! Moling, quick, join me — form up for battle!
Candied hawthorn~ sweet and tangy candied hawthorn! Five wen a string~ come and buy, quick!
Huh? For real? Me? Help you? With pickled greens?
Come here and help me.
I do know how... but why ask all of a sudden? Are you hungry for some?
Do you know how to pickle spicy gourd and eggplant?
Second Senior Brother, are you calling me? What is it you want me to do?
You.
Honestly, even if you hadn't hit me, isn't it terrifying enough having an ugly face come barreling straight at you?
Sorry, sorry! I'll make it up to you properly when I get back, Senior Brother.
Whoa! Watch where you're going, you wretch!
Run faster, are you disabled?
N-no need, really~ Ah, they're— they're getting away, I'd better hurry after them!
Hmph... look at that smug look on your face. This may be my first time pickling vegetables in a jar, but pickling a living man in poison? That, I'm quite skilled at. Care to try my methods yourself?
Not as simple as you imagine, right?
No need. Catch up with them, and don't let them see you.
......Shall I say it again?

Another hour later, take it out again to dry. This time, add bamboo shoots and mushrooms, which should all be chopped. Repeat this process three times, slowly simmer over low heat until dry, caramelize the sugar, then splash with vinegar and oil. Transfer to a ceramic jar, stir well, and seal tightly.
By midday, take advantage of the intense sunlight to dry them out, pressing each one with stone weights. Then sun‑dry for an hour, add perilla leaves, and re‑submerge them in the brine.

Make sure the mustard root and stem are good and clean, grind them fine, and strain out the grit with cloth. Prepare a big batch and set another jar aside — add a little pepper and vinegar when you need it, and you'll have mustard-chili paste. Buy cucumbers at tomorrow's morning market and you can pickle those too.
This isn't complicated at all──

Peel the eggplant and cut it into strips. For every pound, use eight coins of salt. Grind together Sichuan pepper, mustard greens, star anise, dried tangerine peel, ginger, Bai Zhi, hawthorn, and licorice, then mix with water to form a paste. Combine this paste with the eggplant and marinate it in a jar.
Alright
A thing you can manage? Hardly a challenge for me. Enough talk, tell me the method, start to finish.
Second Senior Brother, do you know how to pickle gourd and eggplant?
Huh? You're going to do...?
I'll do it for you instead. That should settle it.
Isn't that leaving me no way out at all!
If you don't go, I'll kill you right now.

I can't stop halfway; if I leave it, it'll go bad when I come back. This is half a month's side dish, and right now, no one is coming to replace me. If I mess it up, I'll have the senior brothers and sisters tear me into pieces.
Set aside the matter; follow them secretly and take care of them.
Pickling vegetables, spicy sauced gourd and eggplant.
What are you doing right now?
Yes!
Here! Second Senior Brother, you called, is, is there something you need?
Zhao Huo! Show yourself, now!
True enough; can't very well tie her to the bed and stop her from moving.
Climbing mountains exercises muscle and bone, gets the blood and qi flowing; it'll do her good.
I was actually worried about Yunshang's condition, which might flare up during the journey.
Hmph... May it be so.
Little Junior Sister getting lost was years ago. She's all grown up now, with Senior Sister and Yunshang accompanying her, strolling on their own turf; I doubt there'll be any trouble.
Okay, okay
Don't talk nonsense
Here we go again, don't be shy──
I am not.
How can we blame everyone? After all, she's the Little Junior Sister. She's so rare that one can't help but be fond of her. Second Senior Brother, aren't you also quite partial to her?
It's your fault for spoiling her; grown as she is, she still can't find her way.
Heroes see eye to eye
