Every menial chore and miscellaneous task will still fall to you, and the other disciples' resentment toward you won't easily fade. If you can't endure it,
just leave on your own.
Ah... Our sect is short-handed as it is. If your remorse is truly sincere, I'll give you one chance.
Probation
If I die, it's just to show that I deserved it.

Even your master crippled his own martial arts before the ancestral hall and gave up the Tang name.
We never came looking for you—yet here you are, delivering yourself to our door?

...My master forgot his roots and betrayed his ancestors; this retribution was only what he deserved.
If that isn't enough, then let me, his disciple, make up for the rest.
How can we possibly trust you?
What a cold, heartless man.
Your master was already put to death for his crimes—are you not secretly seeking revenge for him?
I can see you don't have a clue—don't know a single thing—and still want to go into the Poison Sand Vat?
What? What is the Blue Shouhong Legend?
Don't you know the 'Blue Shouhong Legend'?
Are you serious? These two are among the harshest punishments in our sect. Throughout history, few have endured them.

How could I not know this request is absurd? Yet I beg Third Master to grant me one chance to atone.
It is no other sect I wish to join—it must be the Tang Clan!
I am willing to submit to the Tang Clan's Precepts: to kneel before the ancestral hall and confess my sins, to enter the Poison Sand Vat, to walk the punishment grass—without a single complaint.

The teachers and brothers of your sect came a thousand miles to turn ours upside down.
That we haven't wiped you all out already is only for the sake of shared kinship—and yet you shamelessly wish to join our sect?
Young Hero, you think too highly of yourself; there's no need to waste your talents here. Please, leave!
This humble one dares to request that Third Master Tang take me under his wing and train me.
Then what would you have me do? Must we kill you to satisfy you?

Now that the truth is revealed, a grave mistake has been made, and death itself cannot redeem it; regret comes too late. Third Master Tang is a man of good character and does not delve into this deeply, but I, Tang Shan, find it impossible to feel at ease in my heart.
Yes, what Young Hero Zhao says is true.
That is also the Tang Clan's ancestral legacy—it is none of your concern, outsider.

Everything I know of the Tang Clan's history, I heard from my master, Shouhong.
I believed... that you had seized the Tang Clan's ancestral inheritance, clinging stubbornly to your own foolish notions.
If left unchecked, I thought, the ancestral legacy would be destroyed in an instant.

Since I was a boy I heard tell of the Tang Clan's great name and my heart filled with longing; I had long wished to find a master and learn its arts.
It happened that my teacher, Tang... Tang Shouhong, was then residing in Guangzhou, so I went to become his disciple.
Tang Shan bowed his head low and struck it several times with a rhythmic thud.
Third Hero Tang, please wait!

I'm afraid I can't accept that. Young Hero, if you have anything to say, just speak plainly, no need to beat around the bush. Our sect has many affairs; I'm sorry, I can't spare the time to deal with you. Junior Brother, see him off!

I have heard that Sect Leader Tang... that Senior Tang lies ill in bed.
This junior studied under Master Foshouxiang, and though I dare not call myself skilled in the medical arts, I carry a few life-saving Spirit Pills with me.
I would offer them with both hands, and hope the Great Heroes will not refuse.
...Our sect won't hold a grudge against you all. Why are you kneeling here now? What does that mean?
Third Senior Brother! Come quickly!
That's the one kneeling at the door...

What weather is this—changing in an instant, like it's about to rain again.
Fellow disciples, whoever's free, come help bring in the wash... hm?

But Second Senior Brother enforces the rules with iron impartiality.
When Martial Aunt insisted on shielding him, the sect rules were applied to her as well; when her husband came to plead his case, he too was punished right along with them.
The three of them shared the punishment between them—three backsides blistered raw with poison—and barely pulled through, though no one died.

Before Chao He was punished by the Second Senior Brother, he first tore his clothes and ran to the street to seek help from his Godmother, crying and shouting. He then caused a commotion, disturbing the neighbors, hoping the Second Senior Brother would consider the sect's reputation and refrain from using deadly force.
In short, I'm here to confirm that it's fine if it's not you. You don't need to worry; since Second Senior Brother has taken the initiative, the truth will surely come out.
He impersonated you again, trying to make you take the blame. We all told them the criminal wasn't you, but the Beggar Sect just wouldn't believe it. Sigh.
Brother Fan always recognizes me
He wanted to impersonate you again, making you take the blame, and was beaten by Little Brother Fan of the Beggar Sect to the point of almost dying.
Ugh...

Passersby understood his shouting well enough, but the dog didn't—Tang He rode it straight down and trampled it to death, a dog that belonged to someone from the Beggar Sect.
Its owner broke down weeping, but he wouldn't even dismount to apologize, sneering down from the saddle and daring them to take it up with the Tang Clan if they had the nerve.
The moment they dragged him off the horse, though, he was suddenly shaking all over, sobbing his heart out.
Uh
The Second Senior Brother has already handled it, as this matter has escalated.
Need to go tell the Second Senior Brother, this will eventually cause trouble.

He rode along cursing at passersby to get out of his way—one moment railing that they were blind, the next asking if they even knew how to walk.
His temper was several times more vicious than usual, and the villagers, seeing him like this, all gave him a wide berth.
Didn't he say he couldn't ride a horse?

Tang He got a fine new horse from Martial Aunt and went tearing through the busiest street in town,
showing off his horsemanship.
What's the situation?
It's nothing—I think I've got the gist of what happened.
Senior Brother, are you looking for me?
There you are.
Hmm-hmm~ Hmm-hmm~

The enraged Second Senior Brother cut the festering wound right out of him with a blade and slapped a handful of medicinal powder behind his ear, the pain knocking him out cold on the spot. But the wound healed in the end. Once the storm blew over, he dried his tears and was lively as ever.

He didn't know that the Second Senior Brother's medical skills were superb, and he could see through his pretense of illness. Under the Second Senior Brother's fierce interrogation, Chao He finally revealed a pus‑filled abscess on his ear, already blackened and seemingly severe, yet painless. The cause was an infection from not bathing for too long.

After the incident, Chao He sobbed uncontrollably, tears streaming down his face, saying he also wanted to work properly. He had taken several days off because he had suffered from a serious illness and didn't want everyone to know and be worried.
Let's go! Grab him and report to Second Senior Brother!
Ah... was it two days ago? I was just not at home for dinner. I was just busy, so I ate the biscuits I had on me.

The most infuriating part is that everyone went hungry all night, waiting for him to finish chopping wood the next day before he'd even light the stove. And he still put on that smug look like the world owed him, claiming he'd been up all night chopping wood. Damn it, wasn't that his job to begin with? I was so mad I could've spat blood!

The result was that the firewood ran out, and he was scolded before rushing to fetch more; the training ground was so oily it could make people slip, and he was scolded before rushing to sweep it; for alchemy, he hasn't even managed to make the basic stomach powder yet, and he's even reluctant to do blacksmithing because it's tiring and hot.
At the start of the month, he talked a big talk and took on a pile of chores. Then every day at work, he'd hang up his name tag to show he'd shown up, and sneak off to sleep!
Do you know what the most detestable kind of laziness looks like? It's being lazy and dragging everyone else into your mess.
What happened?
Senior Brother, I've found him! He's sleeping soundly behind the kitchen.
Ah, sorry
He doesn't live in a big courtyard!
Oh, he lives in the Outer Fort below the mountain!
Uh! Senior Brother, it's Zhao Huo!
Tang He! Get up! Damn it!
Be careful, Senior Brother, let me lead you.
Ah, no good, the eyes are still stinging; I need to go get water to wash my eyes.

Asking people afterward would've been fine, but the strangest part was he'd ask, then not follow through. He had a pile of his own ideas, and even when Second Senior Brother got angry and told him to change his ways, he'd nod along and do as he pleased behind his back. The moment no one was looking, he'd think himself clever and sneak in a bunch of extra odds and ends — and that's how it blew up.

It's that Chao He again, no telling what's wrong with him. When he first came to sit in on lectures, he put on a show of taking careful notes, all serious — but it wasn't long before his true colors showed. Whenever Second Senior Brother was teaching, he'd keep fishing some little gadget out of his pocket to fiddle with, not listening at all.
Someone came out. Hey, what's going on up there?
Cough, cough, cough
The Alchemy Room's billowing thick smoke!
What's going on? What exploded?
You were on edge while collecting the money, and only later realized you were overthinking.
...Something's off. Just who does Fourth Senior Brother think he is? Could he be strong-arming me into some loan-shark deal? I'd better hold onto this money and not spend it.
Fourth Senior Brother can be a decent guy sometimes.
Think it's too much? Next time you spend it at the shop, it'll just end up back in my pocket anyway. Don't argue.
Ha ha, have you never heard? When a penny-pinching merchant suddenly offers you a discount, there's only one reason — he's buying your goodwill, hoping to keep things friendly between you.
Ha... that much?! I figured you'd give me fifty or sixty coins at most — even a hundred would've been odd. Handing over this much all of a sudden? There's definitely a catch!
Here, two guan for you.
You're awfully petty — I only got the better of you a few times before, and you've held a grudge ever since.
So you're harboring some ill intentions? Giving me money out of the blue is absolutely unusual.
Is it really that good?
I came to find you because I've recently made a windfall, thanks to your blessing. I especially came to share the profit with you.
Oh please, as if you'd actually be grateful.
That said, if you're offering to split the steamed bun with me, I'll gladly accept it — with gratitude.
No need for that. I didn't come find you tonight to ask for a midnight snack.

After finishing dinner and splitting firewood, I was so exhausted I couldn't eat, and only now have I woken up. This isn't also not yet had time to eat? I have a steamed bun here; let's split it, each having half to get by.
No need for that. I didn't come find you tonight to ask for a midnight snack.
Alright, come on, let's head to the kitchen and get you something to eat.
Damn it, I was already asleep and you had to go dig me out of bed. There's really no dealing with you, Fourth Senior Brother.
What's wrong? You're hungry again?
Junior Brother, come here for a moment.
By the way, are we that close? By seniority and rank, you should call me Fourth Senior Brother. When did we get so close that you can give me a nickname?
Ugh, if you were a beautiful young miss, I might have been moved by your tears.
...Boo-hoo~ I really am so very sorry to all of you...!
No money? Then go borrow some. Didn't you claim to have brothers who'd take a blade to the ribs for you? One word from you and hundreds of Chao He's own army come running?
I... My family's estate is still being divided up. I can't get my hands on any money right now...

No 'buts.' I've already asked around. Didn't you tell people one moment that your family's ruined, and the next that they're rich landowners who donate to the Tang Clan? I'll go with the rich story, then.
Wait, but that......!

Remember to pay me back, Junior Brother — five guan. We're all fellow disciples with no note signed, but everyone saw it happen, so don't think you can weasel out. As everyone knows, borrowing from me comes at a steep price.
Huh?
So that means the person who borrowed money from me at the training grounds yesterday wasn't Junior Brother Zhao, but you?
Heh.
That's sheer nonsense!
What! All the hustle and bustle lately has been on you? I thought it was that smelly kid Zhao Huo, but turns out he wasn't even on the mountain; all the work was done by you!
I've been here all along, but I haven't seen Senior Brother Zhao for a while. I wonder what he's been up to; he only comes back to sleep every night.

So diligent! I was wondering where you'd gotten to, but here you've been quietly slaving away the whole time. If you hadn't said so, I'd have thought that lowlife Zhao Huo had grown a conscience and suddenly turned hardworking.
Yes, I want to finish it all at once, then take a few days to rest and seriously train.
...Did you chop all this firewood by yourself? That's a lot indeed!
Heh, so it's Brother Roly-Poly~
I am Tang Weiyuan, the fourth disciple of this sect.
I suppose it's because I'm often sent out to do shopping.
Eh? This senior brother, how come I've never seen him before?
Phew~ so tired, finally done.
As soon as Fourth Senior Brother arrived, he swung the axe down and knocked over wood that was already split in half.
Chao He restacked the wood you had split, preparing to employ the same method once more.
Someone else has come; looks like a kind‑hearted fatso.

You had clearly been busy for a good while getting everything done before you dared to catch your breath and see to your own affairs. That day, for some reason, it felt as though your fellow disciples were all talking about you, needling you on purpose. You couldn't fathom why, and could only nurse the hurt in silence.
Heh.
I don't mind; it's up to you all.
This time, since you've just finished, that's enough. Go rest. Next time if he pushes his own affairs onto you again, you just tell us.
You are the inner disciple; he is the outsider disciple. You need to get this clear. Don't be so naive, doing whatever they tell you to be a pushover.
Senior Brothers, please, don't say that. I'm doing this of my own will. I'll finish whatever needs doing—it's only right for the new disciple.
Oh wow, so this guy pushed all the responsibilities onto the new Junior Brother and took off to relax.
What! All the recent hustle and bustle has been on you? I thought it was that little brat Zhao Huo.
I've been here all along, but I haven't seen Senior Brother Zhao for a while. I wonder what he's been up to; he only comes back to sleep every night.
So serious, I thought you were never around, turns out you've been quietly working.
Yes, I want to finish it all at once, then take a few days to rest and seriously train.
So much firewood, are you the only one who carried it back and split it?
I recognized you, Chao He with the jutting chin. But can't you change your look? Why copy Junior Brother Zhao's hairstyle? I don't even know how you got your hair to curl like that at the ends.
I am Chao He.
Oh, Junior Brother... you are...
Phew! Finally finished with the busy work.
Whenever someone came by, he'd swing the axe down and knock over wood that was already split in half.
Chao He picked up the split wood you had prepared and stacked it neatly.
...Heh.
Let's take it easy for a while, then get up early to train tomorrow.
Ouch, my back... finally got the firewood all split. I've been hard at it for days—time to rest a bit now.

You dare get cocky with me again? I'm an inner disciple now — call me Tang He from here on. You're just an outsider disciple — the hell do you have to be arrogant about! Once I've mastered martial arts, I'll damn well beat the piss and shit out of you.
You stepped forward and struck once, knocking the fruit and copper money from his hand onto the ground.
Save it, I certainly won't take your stuff.

Heh heh... heh heh, what a fool, turning down free money. I suppose I needn't apologize to every last one of them — those too weak to matter, I'll skip. Toss the candied fruit, but the money, I'll keep.
Very well.
Then I'll keep the money and return it to the Godmother later.

I suppose Martial Aunt only meant well out of concern — no blame to her. Since it was all a misunderstanding, there's no offense to speak of. I'll take the candied fruit, but the money, I'll have to decline with thanks.
Decline
Damn it, so this one's cut from the same cloth — playing dirty right back at me. Fine then, bring it on. As if I'm scared of you — we'll see who laughs last!
But I still have to take this money; after all, if I don't, you'll tell everyone I took it.
I never took you for a brother disciple — I see you clearly now. Sooner or later, your fox's tail will show.

What's with the attitude? I'm an inner disciple now — from now on it's Tang He to you. You're just an outsider disciple; who are you to talk about things vanishing like smoke? Once I've mastered martial arts, I'll damn well beat your soul clean out of you.
Well, I suppose Martial Aunt only fretted out of concern — no blame to her. Since we've become brother disciples, let all that's past vanish like smoke, shall it not?
Accept
Senior Brother Zhao, all that was a misunderstanding. I feel particularly indebted to you. Please be magnanimous and don't hold it against me; accept this money for the wine.
I'll just drink this cup of wine you offer me, giving you a chance to show off. Come on, come on, everyone, let's go drink.
I want to buy a new weapon; I'm just a few coins short. That's great! From now on, let's get along well, Junior Brother!
You... you're not such a bad sort after all.
So I left the money as an apology gift for everyone—not much, just enough to cover the wine. I didn't expect it to be found so quickly.

Naturally, it was me. Godmother feared that as a newcomer I'd be looked down on, so she'd rather be resented by everyone than not put on a show of force first. I tried to stop her but couldn't, and I've felt guilty ever since—truly sorry to you all.
This money... did you leave it, or was it the Great Martial Aunt...
What! There's money? I didn't even know! Damn fatso, you have money but don't give it directly to me! I... I'll make you cry from anger.
Hey, there's money down there!
It's funny, do you think we're three‑year‑olds? You think you can just buy us off with candied fruit...?
Senior Brothers, I offended you all earlier. I've brought some candied fruits and fresh produce from the foot of the mountain—one share for each of you, as a token of respect.
Ah, he's here, he's here!

I have no children of my own, and it's kind of you to take me as your Godmother—it makes me very happy. I'm off now; next time I'll cook you a chicken to build you up, look how thin you've gotten... put on some flesh and you'll look better.
Godmother, you've thought of everything for me, just like my real mother.

Godmother has already given them a taste of her power on your behalf; now take these candied fruits and make your apologies. A firm hand and a gentle gift together, and everyone will think better of you.
Ah, your looks aren't much, but that's no great matter. What Godmother fears most is that you're too soft-hearted and always come out the loser.

Don't go picking and choosing among the chores and errands—we're all family here, so help out wherever you can. I know you won't slack off, but don't let people bully you either, and don't keep forcing yourself to endure it.
With my innate talent, I'm certain to have everyone look at me with new eyes soon.
Child, you can leave here now. Go back. The sect leader has allowed you to study in the Tang Clan; you must do well and not let people look down on you.
Look at you, so happy and showing off, forgetting your manners. Your Godmother's time in the Tang Clan is longer than your age. How could you not know the way? Go on.
This way, please, Godmother.
Such a formidable Martial Aunt; the Sect Leader agreeing to it does not seem like a strange thing. Even I feel somewhat relieved upon hearing this.

The Sect Leader gave her his word: whatever she asked, so long as it wasn't some heinous crime or a betrayal of her own ancestors, the Tang Clan would move heaven and earth to grant it. That Chao He actually talked her into taking him as her godson—I'd say this is eighty percent certain to work.

Before the Third Senior Brother took over, it was the Great Martial Aunt who kept the accounts, and hard she labored for it. She gave up her youth to the sect, and wasn't married off until she was nearly forty.
How do you know that?
...I'm not even sure the Sect Leader will agree, honestly.
To talk nonsense.
What's this person here for?
Hahaha! I'm off!
Screw you!
Junior Brother, don't misunderstand. What I said earlier was definitely not about you. I have great respect for the Beggar Sect.
Senior Brother, you weren't around earlier; you only appeared after everything was done.
Speaking of character, let's talk about his face too. An ugly mug like his, I'd say the Beggar Sect suits him better.
Haha

It's nothing more than begging the Sect Leader to take him as a disciple. Never mind his face—with a character like his, saying whatever pleases whoever he's talking to, I'd say the Beggar Sect suits him better.
They've been inside for a while, and I don't know what they said.

I wonder how that impostor of yours managed to trick the Great Martial Aunt into taking him as her godson.
She even wants to recommend him for discipleship.
Still forcing us to fight seriously, I'm dead tired.

Said it was a test... had us fight it out... didn't offer so much as a cursory pointer,
isn't this deliberately messing with us?

You're just sweet-tongued. Mind your mouth later when you meet my Junior Brother the Sect Leader.
You haven't been formally inducted yet; by the rules, you can't learn our sect's martial arts. Go.
It must be Godmother's teaching that's so profound — their moves all looked so clumsy to me, that's why I gained no insight.
No
How's it going? Have you gained any insight from the real battle?
I'm damned tired of this... I'm going to leave and go back down the mountain...
Huff... huff... if we don't fight for real, we'll only get scolded later by the Great Martial Aunt.
Huff... huff... you're really going all out...

Hmph, what kind of Tang Clan martial arts is that? He's probably never been let into the inner hall, never received the true verses—just copying the shapes blindly, stumbling into it by luck. Come, don't mind him. Auntie will take you to meet the Sect Leader and become his disciple; in three days you'll surpass him.
Auntie, why isn't he using Tang Clan martial arts?
Uh...

And you, you little brat surnamed Zhao—where did you pick up such crooked, heretical martial arts? It's all specious nonsense, doesn't hold together at all. Is that what Tang Clan martial arts looks like?
Auntie, Junior Brother's skill—I truly couldn't match it.
You lost on purpose, didn't you?
I—I've lost. Junior Brother, what fine martial arts.

Junior Brother, I tried to choose spots that would only injure skin and flesh.
Your actual wounds shouldn't be as bad as they look... you'd best go stop the bleeding first.
You're just sweet-tongued. Go on, go see the Sect Leader.
If it were Auntie, he wouldn't even last one move—she wouldn't have to lift a finger.
Your technique is really clumsy; it takes so much effort to deal with even a disciple from another family.
I'm sorry, Junior Brother, please forgive me
That man's gone and provoked Second Senior Brother—he's in for it now. If I were him, I'd finish myself off now while I've still got arms and legs; wait till I don't, and it'll be too late.
Hmm‑hmm, hahaha!

Enter my mountain gate, and you'll abide by my house rules.
If he keeps himself out of trouble, fine. If not...
...Him, joining the Tang Clan? Wonderful. Just wonderful.
Second Senior Brother's calling me. I'm off.
Stop patting him, come with me. You touched something filthy—wash your hands with wine.
Hmm
Little Junior Sister is the best!
Pat, pat.
But you can't bully Senior Brother anymore.
Either way is fine.
You don't want him to?
Is that person also going to join the Tang Clan?
Enough, enough, I don't have time to talk to you lot of juniors. Come on, child, follow Auntie to pay respects to the Sect Leader.
Don't talk nonsense—however harsh I get, I'd never go that far!

Brothers, this is all Auntie's tough love!
Without this drubbing from her, how would we ever know our own shortcomings?
Too hopeless!

Clearly you lack discipline—too comfortable these days, is that it?
Starting today: morning runs around the mountain, double lessons, no lunch break, and meditation in Zhengxin Hall come nightfall.
Monthly exams become fortnightly ones. Fail, and I'll personally see to your training.
A whole pack of failures, and you still couldn't handle one lousy outsider.
Second Senior Brother really doesn't show any mercy at all!
After the fierce battle, the Tang Clan disciples lay sprawled left and right, unable to stand up, grumbling on the ground.

One stick of incense, then fight! Fight hard—fight for real, strike to kill!
Anyone who isn't serious will regret it soon enough!
You observe from the side, verifying the few moves I taught you.
Wow, my godmother is so impressive! No wonder she's my godmother—so amazing!
On the center file as your mark—form up, drill formation!
Everyone's getting it! Fall in! Right, dress! Eyes front!
You all spar together
...Junior Brother, I have no choice, don't blame me!

Li Quan! Get over here—will you fight or not! Refuse, and I'll give you special training later.
Lose, and you'll get after-school lessons all the same. Everyone clear out!
Heh.
I knew you'd deny it to the death—my godson called it exactly.
When did I hit him? It's a misunderstanding!
Not at all, not even a bit

You haven't seen him wander through hardships, how pitiful, his heart is far better than yours. Even if he made mistakes, you deliberately magnify minor issues to undermine him, this kind of thing must have happened, right?
Has he ever told Martial Aunt the reason for his punishment?
You're being disrespectful, aren't you? A mere outsider disciple, in essence, nothing more than a servant, a household servant. Don't you know your place, dare to hit my adopted son?
I certainly don't!
Pfft, I don't have any!

Then you go spar with Zhao Huo. I'd like to see what remarkable skills this senior outsider disciple of the Tang Clan has learned while I'm not watching. Is it the sweeping broom technique, the rag technique, or has he secretly learned the Inner-Chamber Mnemonic?
Li Quan, go and spar with Zhao Huo

You... you're rebelling against me, is that it? Have you no respect for your elders and betters!
Fine then—I'll go tell the Sect Leader, my own junior martial brother, and you'll wish you'd never been born! Let's go!
Senior Brother, there's no need to say that.
You're right—if I wanted to bully Zhao Huo, that would be my own choice!
Brothers and Sisters...!

You said it yourself—you married out of the Tang Clan, yet you still come back to your old home to throw your weight around.
Making things hard for everyone is one thing, but now you want us all to gang up on one of our own brothers.
What exactly is your mindset! I'll be the first to refuse!

I married out of the Tang Clan in grand style, and from that day on I belonged to another family.
What of it? Must I still wipe your noses for you, you pack of brats?
I come back now and then, and if I find my own kin's young disciples turning out worthless, what's wrong with a scolding or two?
Pfft! I respect you as a senior, so I only call you Martial Aunt once. You really think you're virtuous and respected? When our sect faced difficulties, where were you?
Everyone's getting it! Fall in! Right, dress! Eyes front!
Too much bullying, none of them will comply.
Ugh!
You're a waste, go to the front and block the arrows.
Zhao Huo has come!
Junior Martial Sister—and you, useless one—follow me.
Seeing Second Senior Brother's chillingly sinister smile, the Tang Clan disciples all shuddered. They longed to switch sides at once and join your camp.
Martial Aunt speaks rightly—if we're to fight, we ought to fight in earnest.
What is this nonsense? Our sect's practice of martial arts is a serious matter.
I'm afraid there might be someone else who acts superior by relying on their age.

But Zheng'er, weren't you so busy?
How is it you've come to romp about with your junior brothers and sisters today, with not an ounce of grown-up dignity.
Shut up.
Yes, yes, sorry.
You useless thing, why can't you be useful? This trivial matter requires me to step in, don't you know I'm very busy?
Second Senior Brother, will you help me?
Very original indeed. I'll join this side, then.
This... this... it's testing his Qinggong and his will to survive.
Group training? So many people fighting one person‑what kind of group training is this, unheard of!
Tang Zheng! Have I been bothering you? Sorry, this is group training.
Second Senior Brother!
What's all the shouting about! What nonsense are you people up to?
Second Senior Brother! Are you also coming to help me?
Why should she listen to you?
You dare disobey your Great Martial Aunt?!
No.
Mo Ling, you also go to that group over there.
Junior Martial Sister!
......Senior Brother, I'll help you.
One stick of incense‑fight! Fight fiercely, fight for real, kill for real! Those who don't take it seriously will have no good end coming!
You observe from the side, verifying the few moves I taught you.
Wow, Godmother's so formidable—truly worthy of being my godmother, how amazing~
Center squad sets the mark—form up, drill formation!
Alright, come on!
You‑you...!
Everyone's in! Fall in! Right dress, eyes front!
Compelled by tyrannical power, they dare not follow.
In any case, when I, Tang Xiaolou, give the order, which of you dares disobey?
Heh.
I knew you'd deny it to the very end—my adopted son called it exactly.
When did I hit him? It's a misunderstanding!

Everyone, at him! Take this young dandy's money!
The Lingnan Sect? You didn't say - I took it for some bandit chief's mountain lair.
Who the hell are you? Dare to intrude on our Lingnan School's territory‑damn it, are you seeking death?
Meanwhile, a thousand miles to the south
What did you do to him?

As for Duan Zhixiu himself, he should be chasing the bait I scattered, still galloping a thousand miles away. If that's the case, based on the horse's pace, he should have reached Guangdong or Lingnan by now.
What did you just call Sect Leader Zou?

Hmm... our siblings are Diancang defectors. Zou Feibo naturally can't be too courteous, otherwise he might risk offending the Diancang sect. He didn't force you to stay, which is already very reasonable.
No. I went to Qingcheng and paid my respects to Sect Leader Zou, but the Immortal made no mention of Duan Zhixiu.
Brother, didn't you meet Duan Zhixiu when you went to Qingcheng?
You and Ye Yunzhou suddenly started a fight because of boredom.
What...?
The remnants of those pastries from Yunshang belong to me! Even Brother Ye, you cannot dispute with me!
Those snack leftovers belong to me
Stop, Brother Zhao, your words are too harsh. For the sake of Ye's face, let's stop here.

Full of malicious intent, when the shit hits the fan, his excrement flows backward. He spits out excrement and spreads rumors the moment he opens his mouth. His stench is unbearable, making people sick to their stomachs. He himself can't smell his own foulness and is still smug. A stinking beggar who acts as if everyone owes him, and when he can't beg for food, he becomes enraged.

Who could it be‑so capable, lowering the moral standards of the world with their own power, spreading stench throughout humanity? Indeed! It's none other than the Young Master of the Loose Eunuch Pavilion. His anus is also loose, and he's a eunuch, hence the nickname: Loose Eunuch!

Not his fault, not his fault - after all, he's been motherless since the day he was born.
His mother never got the chance to raise him; shamed by having borne him, she took her own life to atone to the world.
And thanks to him, even in death she must be reborn nine lives running as a sow.
Lacks both verbal virtue and rationality
Brother Zhao... that's not wrong, I suppose.

If such a person were to hold power, the Dali Kingdom would be on the brink of destruction. His Majesty the Emperor of Dali sent him to Jianghu‑how could he be a fool? Isn't this a wise move? The only drawback is that he was sent to the wrong place. He should have gone to the Beggar Sect to learn.

"A kinsman of the Duan clan of Dali" - what nerve he has to keep it on his lips, the vain wretch.
No upbringing as a child, no virtue as he grew, and after all these disgraceful deeds he still fancies himself someone special.
Emotional speech

Brother Zhao's words are indeed correct. If he takes pride in being a descendant of the Duan family, he should indeed hold pride. Otherwise, even if he fulfills his desires, in a hundred years he would be ashamed to face his ancestors.

He couldn't stand staying beneath others forever, and wanting to reclaim his place among his own kin was only natural.
But no reason that merely sounds righteous excuses abandoning basic human decency.
Otherwise, even with his name entered in the ancestral hall, he'd still be an unworthy descendant - after a hundred years, how could he face his Duan ancestors?
Still has some manners, making a reasonable complaint
Berate Duan Zhixiu
Ye was utterly drained, already unable to bear the burden. Sometimes he longed for an end to it all - thankfully, taking shelter under the Tang Clan in time let him catch his breath.

Ye Mou was utterly drained, already unable to bear the weight. Sometimes he longed for it all to end - thankfully it was you, Brother Zhao, who let him still believe a sliver of light remained in this world.
Only someone as strong and resilient as you, like a pine tree, could have endured this. If I were in your place with my bad temper, I would have fought someone long ago.
You've truly suffered for this - it's remarkable that you managed to endure it. Such firmness of spirit is beyond what most people could ever manage.
I was utterly disheartened. In time, I simply stopped speaking of it at all.

Not without a single person who speaks up for justice, but merely relying on words cannot convince people. Many are nothing but insincere, going in circles, yet still heading toward the treasure. The world does not trust us, and I have also become suspicious, harboring three parts of doubt whenever someone remains silent.

Compared with the truth, people would rather believe their own fantasies.
Afraid of missing out, they take sides without reason - there's always someone ready to gossip.
They'd drive a man to his grave and still dig it open just to be sure, and even then, never be satisfied.
Ah, I too count myself among this brother and sister's close confidants, and know well how fearsome cruel words can be. Sometimes malicious slander cuts no less than blade and spear.

I spoke of my hardships, and they didn't believe me; when I fell silent, they accused me of courting a reputation instead. The world has decided we're guilty at heart — however we explain or try to clarify, it's always taken as a clever excuse to shirk blame.
In truth, have I not tried to explain myself? But thanks to that rumor, everyone suspects the two of us of embezzling King Yue's treasure.
Now I understand the whole affair. Aside from you two and those directly involved, does anyone else know of this?
Ah, that's true enough.

Defying the imperial decree to raid the marriage procession, colluding with foreign enemies, abducting the Lady of Dali, and gravely wounding the heir of the Zhongguo Gong house — do you think it wise, Brother Zhao, to broadcast such things far and wide?

Here I thought it was something too painful to speak of, which is why you two never breathed a word of it. Now that I've heard it all, isn't this entirely Duan Zhixiu's fault? Why be so secretive about it?
Hidden Circumstances
You flatter me.
Brother Ye truly is one of the most clear-headed men in the Diancang Sect.
I suppose that's right. Alas, a sword is just a sword, a mere iron weapon. It doesn't hide any treasures or secrets, nor does it spew fire, nor does it house a spirit.
He's kept himself well hidden all these years — coveting the treasure all along, and deceiving you both. I'd wager the moment he got his hands on the sword, he pored over it endlessly.
I suspected nothing and trusted him readily, giving the Listening Cloud Sword into his keeping, with instructions that should anything happen to me, the sword be passed on to Yunshang.

Alas, it was my own fault — naive back then, with no guard against others. At the critical moment, he claimed the Listening Cloud Sword was too well known, and that Li Ziqiong might recognize me by it, so he had a near-identical blade forged to give me instead.
How could Brother Ye hand over the sword to that person?
It is indeed... though not passed down through my father's line, it is most certainly the sword bestowed by Lord Yue Yun.
Isn't that sword your family's heirloom?
Why is the Listening Cloud Sword in someone else's hands?
That takes some nerve, I'll say.

I'm not dead — I survived. That leopard was no ordinary beast, indeed, quite spirited: it only closed its jaws lightly on my arm, never biting down. It stared at me a good while, then turned and walked away.
Come off it, by that test everyone's a villain!
In short, they set the leopard loose to bite you. If you're truly innocent, you survive; if not, you die.
The trial of the divine leopard — what does it actually involve?
What is the trial of the divine leopard?

Brother Zhao, don't tease me so. My mind is troubled and my great ambitions still unfulfilled — how could I think of settling down? I dared not keep the princess waiting, so I declined, as courteously as I could.
So you're already married? I didn't even know you had a wife.
So you got married?
Of course not. A dozen or so Tubo warriors drew their bows and aimed their arrows. If I were to injure the divine leopard, I would be pierced by ten thousand arrows.
Can I carry weapons?
This opportunity has never belonged to me...
What? There's such good fortune to be had in this world?
...They intend to make me their Prince Consort to marry the tribal princess. If I refuse, they will force me to face the trial of the divine leopard.
Then what more could they possibly want?
If they listened to reason and only kicked up a fuss when they had real grievance, they wouldn't be called barbarians in the first place.

The Tubo people knew Ye Mou hailed from the Great Song, so naturally they opposed the Maozhou tribe's marriage alliance with Dali. Their interests aligned with his, and though they wouldn't go so far as open violence, they weren't especially reasonable either.
Oh, so that's the case... That explains it. Without that sword, Yunshang wouldn't have been so easily deceived.

Brother Zhao, you may not know this: the sword in my hand, though a fine blade in its own right, is not the Listening Cloud Sword. It was forged by Zhi... by Duan Zhixiu, to trick me out of my real one.
The Listening Cloud Sword is said to have been bestowed by Lord Yue Yun, and is the Ye family's heirloom. Brother Ye would even part with such a treasure.
Indeed.
They were unaware that the sword given by Brother Ye was not your own sword; it was taking advantage of others' generosity.

That's right—they say Diancang swordsmen love their blades as their own lives, so offering one up is about as sincere a gesture as there is.
Just that difference between giving freely and having it taken—the treatment that follows is worlds apart.

I kept Yunshang's words in mind and didn't stubbornly fight to the death.
Once I fell back, rather than wait for the Tubo to demand my weapon, I offered my sword myself, to show goodwill.

But what about after the fighting's done? Isn't that just leaping from the tiger's jaws into the wolf's?
I'd worry that once they calm down, it won't take them long to realize they were used.

The enemy of my enemy is a friend—brilliant, simply brilliant.
No wonder it's Yunshang; she never runs short of clever schemes.

Li Ziqiong ground his teeth in fury but didn't dare risk his own neck charging into the fray after me.
With so many Tubo shields to borrow, so long as not all of them came for me, I had more than enough cover to save myself amid the chaos.

Sand swirling, blades clashing—who has time to think it through?
The angrier the Inner Discipline Camp soldiers fought, the more fiercely the Tubo warriors rallied to my side against the common enemy.
Oh, oh～!
But what if I suddenly rushed into the chaotic battle formation and fought side by side with the Tubo warriors?

Yes.
Alone, with no one to back me up, I was no match for Li Ziqiong—that was a dead end.
And even if I'd won by sheer luck, spent and unable to break through the siege, there'd still be no way out alive.
Speaking of it, she seemed to have mentioned another plan earlier.
Before my two senior brothers joined the battle, Yunshang had already thought of a way for me to escape.
You're right... I just can't figure it out.

Fortunate that my opponent back then was Li Ziqiong, and not Brother Zhao.
Otherwise, if you'd cried out and given it away on the spot, making the Tubo warriors suspicious, I'd have been in real trouble.
Seems Yunshang and I think alike—heroes see eye to eye, as they say.
Hmm, this is exactly the first retreat plan that Yunshang thought of for me.
You guessed right?
You guessed right...

As for getting captured by the Tubo afterward—well, that's a story for another time.
But the enemy of my enemy is a friend; with a bit of negotiating, there's always a chance things turn around.

Fight one man, and it's win or lose, nothing more. But fight ten thousand, and there's still an opening to exploit.
Were I in your place, I'd charge into the chaos of battle, pretend to cover the Tubo warriors' retreat, and throw in with their side—
really just borrowing their blades to keep myself safe.
That leaves only one possibility.

Li Ziqiong is a general of real skill, but his only worry is having no war to fight—no chance to win merit and make a name for himself.
When the Lady's carriage was ambushed, his protection failed, and if he can't hand over a culprit to answer for it,
the moment the Emperor's wrath falls, forget a promotion—he'll be lucky to keep his official cap at all.
That's out of the question too.
So, could it be that Li Ziqiong intentionally let you go?

Pick one man out to duel, and he's no match for a Wulin master.
But when it comes to marching an army and arraying troops, they're nothing an ordinary martial artist can compare to.

Brother Zhao, you overestimate me.
Those were soldiers of the Dali Inner Guard Camp—well-trained, the fiercest elite unit in the whole Dali Kingdom.

But those men betrayed you in the heat of battle, and no one came to your aid—Brother Ye, how did you manage to escape?
Don't tell me you single-handedly cut through the army's encirclement with just one sword?
Pretty much, that's about the size of it... alas.
I suspect those two senior brothers of yours were bribed by Duan Zhixiu.
Speaking of Brother Ye, how did you survive the battlefield?
I see. Very well then—see you around.

I still have a few words to share with Yunshang in private, so I'll wait here.
I appreciate Brother Zhao's kindness, but let's drink together another day when we're both free.
It's getting late; it's time for us to go find some wine and get completely drunk.
Understood, so we'll have another drink on another day when we're free.

I still have a few words to share with Yunshang in private, so I'll wait here.
I appreciate Brother Zhao's kindness, but let's drink together another day when we're both free.

It's getting late—you've been rushing back and forth, and must be worn out.
Why don't we head to Chuanquan Tavern? My treat, to give you a proper welcome home.
Let's rest early
You went home resentfully, nursing a grudge, yet dared not report it to the Sect Leader, for fear it would only invite even harsher retaliation.
Damn it, Second Senior Brother really threw me out to feed the wolves!

Still, sparring with Brother Zhao isn't a fight to the death, just a friendly exchange — and it has been too long since our last one. It brings back fond memories of the years spent training swordsmanship at Diancang.
Why is she scolding me like this? Where did I offend this Heroine?

What are you staring at? Don't think you can eat bird's nest just because you're handsome — you can't even flash a smile to charm anyone. You've got hands and feet; if you want to eat, go pick it yourself, or sell those looks of yours. Understand? You good-for-nothing freeloader.
I don't care! I said go, so go!
And what's this about you 'thinking' he wants it? I bet you just dreamed that up out of nowhere to give me trouble.
What? Where am I supposed to get bird's nest for him at this hour?
Junior Brother, I think Second Senior Brother wants to rinse his mouth with bird's nest for dinner; you handle it.
That's just you deliberately going easy on me. I can already fight you to a draw even while you're holding back — next time, why not add a bit more force?
You flatter me, you flatter me. I know you're still holding back, not giving it your all — next time, why not go all out?
Brother Zhao, it's been quite some time — your martial arts have grown once more.
You've lost part of your memory; others only think you're diligent, staying overnight in the alchemy room. They can't help but feel a bit admiring of you.
...How could I be in the alchemy room? I have no memory of it at all.

How come you're also following Second Senior Brother to stay overnight in the alchemy room? Even if you're trying hard, there should be a limit. Don't rely on your youth to overexert yourself; it's not worth it.
Senior Sister... Good morning.
Junior Brother, wake up.
Hey! Beast, what are you trying to do!
Oh, I forgot that Second Senior Brother lives in the Alchemy room! This is a major problem!
Silence, you noisy waste of space! Besides making an ear-piercing racket to bother people, what exactly can you do?
Damn it~ I missed out on those delicious snack crumbs!
Oh, I remember now! I was careless for a moment and didn't dodge, so Brother Ye knocked me unconscious with the sword handle.
Huh! Wh-why am I here?
There are still snacks left; I'm off to eat with Moling. Elder Brothers, farewell. Since you two have nothing better to do, why not fight it out—the survivor gets our leftover crumbs.
Don't say such foolish things; haven't you already caused enough trouble for others?
Brother, how about we just join the Tang Clan? What do you think?
As long as you siblings remain within the Tang Clan for a day, what enmity or hatred outside can possibly matter? What's the harm in confronting the Tang Clan? Just charge ahead!

I still say what I said before: I respect your Ye family ancestors for their loyalty and valor, and will look after you on their behalf. You may stay here, or you may go - the choice is yours. Once you leave, whatever befalls you, no blame will fall on me.
This, but...

The grudge between you two siblings and him, you can sort out yourselves. As for the disputes between our sect and him, those should be settled separately. This matter will not be held against you; there's no need to worry over it.

You can only mutter about this in your heart, deeply afraid that when the Sect Leader seeks out Second Senior Brother for a talk, Second Senior Brother will hold a grudge and turn around to torment you until there's nothing left but bones.
Reporting to the Sect Leader: it's the Second Senior Brother.
What nonsense are you talking about? Who made you act like a gatekeeper?

Senior, this time it was my negligence and unauthorized departure from duty, for which I bear full responsibility. Henceforth, I will strictly guard the mountain gate. Should that person harbor unrelenting malice and intend to harm the Tang Clan, I shall personally resolve the matter, ensuring my personal grudges do not burden the Tang Clan.
That's all, then
In the end, it's still all about that baseless rumor.

What I cannot forgive is his act of murdering my brother. He thought that since I had no one to rely on and was united with him against a common enemy, I would do anything to reveal the treasure's location. Heh, what a clever plan he has!
Everyone has their own selfish motives. He wanted to save me and break free of his troubles - how could I refuse to plan for him? We are sworn siblings, after all.

Even wicked men, in doing evil, still draw a line between friend and foe. A man like him, who'd sell out even his own sworn brother and turn his back on kin, doesn't even count as a villain - he's nothing but a beast that happens to walk on two legs.

Now you should understand why my brother has become so suspicious, and from then on, he's been afraid to believe others' words, right? It's not that he's deep in scheming, but that he's been deeply wounded.
He is unrighteous, I cannot be unjust. Disabling his arm to render him unable to wield a sword for life‑this is the way to sever the bond of brotherhood.

Brother Ye, you're too soft-hearted! Why cut off just his hand? Cut off his head instead! It turns out this scoundrel broke faith and betrayed trust - he never came to your aid at all, he meant to trap you into deadly danger!
Sigh.

I still thought Brother Ye was usually gentle and humble, how could he suddenly attack his sworn brother with such cruelty! Turns out this scoundrel broke his word and betrayed trust, never went to support, intending to trap you into death!
Well struck.
Aaaargh—! My hand! My hand!!
How come, how could you... no one to support you, how did you manage to break through and survive?!
Brother, Brother...?
Duan! Zhi! Xiu!

I'm telling you to speak! Hurry up! Want to die holding onto the treasure? On the Yellow Springs Road, you can't use gold, silver, or jewels! If you're going to die, say where the treasure is first, then die!
{size=24}It's all my fault......{/size}
Your brother has already died. If you don't speak, the world will never know! I have no military resources; how can I avenge Yunzhou?
Brother...
Don't be afraid, Brother Duan is here, nothing will happen to you. Rather than that, hurry and tell me - where exactly is the treasure hidden?
It's so cold... so painful... I can't see anything... Brother, where are you? So scary, so scary, so scary!
Yunshang! You... you've relapsed again? How could this be? I thought you had recovered completely.
Cough, cough, cough... Brother...

However, to avenge your brother, we need to recruit soldiers and acquire military resources; otherwise, everything is just empty talk. By the way, doesn't your Ye family have that treasure map? How about...
Wait for me to overthrow the tyrant and ascend the throne, and you will be the Princess of Dali! No... if you like, I can even make you the Empress!
I don't want it anymore... I, I just want Brother to come back to life... cough, cough‑cough.
Don't be afraid, I won't leave you behind. Yunzhou is no longer here, from now on, Brother Duan will take care of you for a lifetime. Whatever you love to eat or drink, I will never refuse you!

Yunshang, you can rest assured! Brother Duan swears to heaven, this blood debt of deep hatred I will surely settle in due time! At that time, not only Li Ziqiong, but even the dog emperor will have to pay the price! Blood debt must be repaid with blood!

I've come to realize it now – groveling and begging for others' kindness will never end well. To be free of others' control, I must be crueler and more ruthless than they are! Strive, fight, and seize what I want!
We grew up together since childhood, bound by a sworn brotherhood. He would risk his life for me, yet I couldn't even bring back his body‑how ashamed I am!
It's my fault...? It's my arrogance that caused this, harming my brother?

The disciple of Diancang, seeking the way with a sword, for a wife or a friend, where the sword exists, so does the person; if the sword is destroyed, the person perishes. Moreover, this sword is the treasured heirloom of the Ye family, more precious than life itself. Now that the sword is in someone else's hands, what else could they possibly not understand? If they wish to doubt, how could they possibly not believe?
Ah... Ah ah...

If it weren't for me, Yunzhou would not have suffered this calamity. It's my fault, I've wronged you and Yunzhou! At that time, I was so close to him, yet I could only watch helplessly as he died at the hands of the tyrant's henchmen...!
I won't listen, you're lying! My brother is clearly alive and well! Why are you deceiving me!
Yunshang, listen to me
Where are you going? Speak up!
This... I... sigh. Your Highness, please tell Junior Sister Yunshang yourself; we take our leave.
Senior Brother, you're not saying anything? My brother... really... did something happen?
Yunshang, the battlefield changes in an instant; it cannot be captured by mere theoretical discussions. My Senior Brothers and I gave our best.
What...? How... how could this be? This shouldn't be the case! I clearly told him that if the situation was unfavorable, then... .

After securing the situation, worried for Yunzhou's safety, we left Wanqing nearby and rushed straight back to his aid. Unfortunately, the soldiers of the Internal Guard Camp were too strong – even the combined strength of the four of us couldn't overcome their formation. We very nearly failed to escape ourselves, and in the end... in the end it was Yunzhou who gave his life to cover our retreat.
Yunshang, be calm and listen to me.
Seeing the two of them look troubled and speak hesitantly, Ye Yunshang realized that something had changed. Her heart suddenly plunged as if into a cold pool, chilling her from head to toe.
This...
Senior Brother! How could you all be injured like this?......Where is my older brother?
I don't care, the Lady isn't my relative; I only care about my own family.
Yunshang, we've just escaped from the Tiger's mouth. My younger sister is still shaken, her thoughts are unsettled‑it's understandable, don't quarrel with her.
Hey, Brother, don't interrupt, I'm telling a story, you know.

This Lady Ningyang has even read Zou Yang's Letter to King Liang from Prison from the Western Han dynasty, and yet knows how to cite the classics. Unfortunately, she has some learning, but her conduct is not commendable.
Damn it, you risked your lives to save her, and this little brat acts like that? She really thinks she's some high‑and‑mighty Lady! I'm so furious!
...So be it. Elder Brother, keeping company with oxen and fine steeds alike, it's little wonder you don't know the manners of a great house. In time, I'll go over it with you in detail.
This... you don't need to be difficult, I need to talk to her about some things, I'll be there soon.

Brother Senior, I don't have any maidservants with me to attend to me. Being a newcomer, without anyone to guide me, how can you let me travel alone? It would be better if you had this young miss serve me instead.
Go straight ahead; that building is my residence. You go ahead first, and after Brother finishes his urgent matters, he'll come find you.
Older brother, I'm utterly exhausted. Where is your residence? Take me there to rest.
That's my sister then!
This little miss is surely Brother Duan's dear sister, isn't she?
Yunshang...
Brother Duan! You've come back!
If only I weren't so weak, I could learn swordsmanship and go out into the Jianghu with my brother and others.

No one listened to her being cute and causing trouble. Ye Yunshang put away her sad expression, brushed off the snowflakes from her clothes, smeared the blood from her nose on the snow, and stood up resolutely.
Ah, right, the brothers aren't here.
Ugh~ Brother~ This wretched stone intends to murder me! You all hurry and help me beat this stone! Use your skulls to hit it hard!
Puwa!
First Ultimate!
She's in top form. If it's now, she might just be able to pull off that move──
You two, be quiet
Brothers, shut up!
I don't believe it either — this guy's just talking big again, as always.
Y-you stop making things up and bragging — have you no shame? How could you possibly pull off a signature move like that?
Wow, wow! I really am a genius! Did I already recover from my illness?
Traceless Sword Technique. Boundless Kick!
It worked out... I even scared myself.
Wow! Wow! What's going on!
Meteor Sword Technique, Seventh Form: Wearing the Stars and the Moon!
Hah! Hah! Diancang Sword Technique, Third Form, Wind and Lightning!
The story starts from when the brothers set out to raid the Lady's bridal procession — I was at Diancang.
Brother, get lost.
Very well.
Since what happens to Brother next isn't important, nothing worth telling, it's my turn to tell the next part — is that all right with you?
I got so caught up talking that I didn't notice Senior Tang looked worn out. Luckily, little sister came to my rescue.
Good, Shang'er, you're thoughtful. Uncle is feeling quite tired and needs something to invigorate; this cup of tea you brought came in time. As for the snacks, you can eat them yourself.
Uncle Tang, please have some tea and the snacks Shang'er has treasured.

At that moment, this junior was locked in fierce combat with Li Ziqiong. A glance caught dust rising in the distance — the Senior Brothers riding back to relieve him. His nerves steadied, and he loosed a move: Stirring the Soup to Quell the Boil...
Good, tough as they come. Then this commander won't waste more breath — I'll grant you your wish!

...I'm grateful for the regard the Left Commandant of the Imperial Guard shows me. This lowly one dared attack the Lady's carriage, well aware it's a capital crime; if I cannot escape with my life, I harbor no illusions of survival. As for laying down my blade — forgive me, but I cannot comply.

I too am a man who values talent, and I'd rather not see you lying dead in the dirt. While I'm still questioning you, you'd best be sensible — put down your weapon, submit quietly, and answer in full. Then perhaps I can show you leniency.

That should hold. Your main force is busy with the Tubo warriors, and your trusted men have been lured away too. I only need to hold out until my Senior Brothers ride back to relieve me, and I'll be safe. Everything is going exactly as Yunshang planned it. I'm her brother — I can't let her down.

Silence? If you want to delay time, that's not a wise move. Your sword skills may be high, but you can't pierce through my war armor. Your strength will eventually run out, and your defeat is inevitable. At that point, there's only a path to death.
Yet I wonder, which path's hero or magnate might you be? And is your target Tubo, or is it my Dali?

You little brat dares to face me, you're bold and resourceful; this borrowed knife to kill strategy of yours is truly masterful. Did you accurately assess the Tubo factions' disunity and deliberately leak information to their rival tribes?
This officer obeys!
Take my token and lead the men in pursuit at once — I'll deal with this one and follow right after.

Lord, bad news! Masked men have sprung up from the side—unlike the barbarians, their moves are vicious. The Inner Discipline Camp brothers couldn't hold them back, and the Lady... the Lady's been taken!
Young man, your skills are really impressive. Are you from the Jianghu?
Haha, then that settles it—you're exactly who I'm after! Tubo is more than just the Maozhou tribe—now die, the lot of you!

You see our ceremonial procession and still ask something so foolish? Isn't the answer plain as day? So used to playing bandit that you don't even keep your eyes open, robbing whoever crosses your path! If this breaks the alliance between the Maozhou tribe and my Dali Kingdom, you won't have heads enough to pay for it!
You're the escort for Lady Ningyang's marriage convoy, aren't you?
What's going on? These Tubo people are going crazy? Stop! All of you, stop immediately!
Yes.
If that brat heard this, his tail would shoot straight up to the sky. Enough—don't bring up that rascal. Go on with your story.
Senior speaks too kindly—junior dares not accept such praise. Great Hero Tang carries himself with a chivalrous, forthright bearing I could never match. I have long admired him from afar.
The Sect Leader thinks so highly of Brother Ye, so free with his praise, yet still won't take me on as an inner disciple. How I envy him.

Young Hero Ye carries himself with such steadiness, and acts with righteousness and courage—worlds apart from my sect's unworthy eldest disciple. This old man is quite taken with him. What a pity he took his vows under Diancang, all those years ago.

Five people? I suppose you've counted me in there. How could you bear to send someone as delicate and pitiful as me into battle? Naturally, my job is just to talk—offer up the plan, then go home and eat grapes.
Five of you in all, and you actually went and attacked the marriage convoy? And here you call us Tang Clan lunatics—you lot are every bit as mad.

Yunshang has caused you no small trouble, Daoist — for saving her life twice over, I am endlessly grateful.
Oh

I just wanted to play a prank on you, so I got a rope, meaning to dangle myself from the beam. Then, once you fell asleep, I'd lower myself down to give you a fright.
Well...

No, not long

Why are you in my room?
That this lad can master his temper and steel his will is rare indeed.

Not angry
Alas, rotten wood cannot be carved
Old Daoist, this Zhao is nobody of consequence — there's no offense to give. If you don't wish to teach me, why not just say so plainly, instead of making up all these excuses!
Angry

With time, once you have mastered the Qingcheng Internal Skill and solidified your foundation, I will teach you then. Patience and perseverance, as firm as pine and as flexible as wind, are the Internal Method of Qingcheng. Remember this well.

Qingcheng disciples have cultivated for years, and only now have they reached a small degree of mastery, allowing this old Daoist to offer a word of advice. Young Friend Zhao, don't be anxious. Let this old Daoist speak to you earnestly.

Not so

How should the mind be stilled? How should the qi be channeled? These precisely accord with cultivating the Way. Thus, more than intricate sword techniques, you should attend to your state of mind...
Yes, I'll go right away

Young friend, you were too slow to withdraw your strike — you arrived a step too late. This old Daoist has said everything there is to say. Why not go over there? My Senior Brother is also expounding on his martial principles.

Wind Beneath the Pines you just used was too fast and urgent; your Internal Force had not yet reached the sword's tip. If you were to clash weapons with an opponent, it would then come down to whose blade was sharper, which contradicts the true essence of Qingcheng martial arts...

Okay

Still your disciple all the same.
A reliable disciple... isn't it a disciple?
Have you decided what to sell? I'll help you build the stall and the cart.

You needn't worry about such things. Your master here is so lovely to behold, there's never a moment someone isn't coveting me. Surely I can't hole up indoors and stop living my life just for the likes of them? My years in the Jianghu run deeper than yours, so spare me your fretting.
I'm afraid you're being watched!
It doesn't matter what I'm selling; the main thing is to try to reconnect with people. Perhaps people aren't as bad as I imagined.
Even if I were to engage in this kind of business, do you think we could attract customers by operating in the outer fortress?
What kind of business do you want to get into? Assassin organization?
You're thinking too much
What business do you want to do? You can't do illegal or taboo dangerous things, you know.
Perhaps I will go to the Outer Fortress to do business.
Mm, your master enjoys peace and quiet, as you well know. Don't fuss over me too much; just as always, I'll find something to occupy myself.
Are you really okay staying here?
I thought your Third Senior Brother was surely a rigid old fossil. Yet even this he can tolerate — the Tang Clan truly doesn't bow to convention, quite rebellious indeed.
Haha
I also need some time to calm down and thoroughly process this matter.
First, go and arrange for the Lady's affairs, then return to participate in the Tang Clan meeting. I'll wait for you.

Junior Brother, as for this matter of yours... sigh, I won't pass judgment, though it's truly hard to swallow. Strange as it is, then again — a son of the Jianghu who lacks even this much breadth of heart has no business making his way in it.
Wait, Master, this kind of thing is indeed hard to accept. Give the Third Senior Brother some time to come to his senses.
Disciple, if the Tang Clan does not welcome us, then we shall leave.

Song people were overly rigid in their adherence to rituals and laws; even people of the Jianghu could not truly be free‑spirited. Third Senior Brother had thoroughly studied the teachings of Confucius and Mencius, taking the way of the gentleman as the foundation of his existence, especially strict in following rules and regulations. Upon hearing such a shocking case of incest, he was stunned in silence for a long time.
Third Senior Brother nearly toppled over backward, and the Junior Martial Brothers and Sisters who came running at the commotion soon found their own legs going weak too.
What!?

Yes
May I say that?
You— what are you doing? Why so formal all of a sudden?
Third Hero, greetings.
Junior Brother, and Heroine Xiahou, have you finished your business?

Thank you.

I've had enough quiet - I need some liveliness now. Wait for me.
Junior Brother, today is the day of the Tang Clan's family gathering - do you need some time alone, or shall we wait for you?
Yes, yes, you're right.
Third Senior Brother, will you no longer acknowledge me as your Junior Brother? I am a disciple of the Snow Mountain Sect, and also an outsider disciple of the Tang Clan.
Junior Brother - no, Young Hero Zhao. I've heard everything... you... you must try to bear your grief.
...I'm back.
That's true.

If I team up with you, won't that give the game away? What if the enemies learn my martial arts have declined, and keep coming after me one after another? If it were just me, with nothing to lose, that would be one thing - but you still carry a heavy burden, so listen to me.
If we run into enemies, we can just gang up and beat them down.

Getting carried away so fast - teasing me like that, with no respect for your elders.

No

No matter what, you truly won't stay?
No

Otherwise, hehe, I might have to give you a calf massage.

Hmm, it's serious. I haven't felt this weak in a long time; even standing up makes my legs tremble.

How do you feel right now?
Does she really dislike me this much?

It's nothing
Ah, sorry, Master, are you unharmed?
Ah

If I could have retreated, I wouldn't have resisted so fiercely. I mustered up the courage to say it out loud, something I would only do once in a lifetime.
There's absolutely no choice.

This mortal world must still hold good things worth our lingering for.
Let all of yesterday die as yesterday did; let all of today live as today does.
Phew, what a close call.
......If you weren't my disciple, I might have killed you.

Tsk, you have quite the sharp tongue.

You have never harmed an innocent person, proving your heart is pure. Without guilt, why fear others' words?

You simply chose unwisely in marriage—how can that be your fault? Why do you speak of it as though it were some flaw of yours?

Even so...
I've been married before, no longer chaste, my reputation in ruins, my temper vicious, and my hands cold and merciless.

Could it be that the aloof Soul-Stealing Orchid, who disregards worldly customs and etiquette, would still worry about the opinions of others? What others think is not something you would consider, right?

Not anymore—just now, you expelled me from the sect.
We are master and disciple, aren't we? This would be like incest, wouldn't it...
Shameless to the extreme!

I have plenty of ways to make you hate me and hunt me down—that way, you'd have another seven years.
Nngh...!
Since I've already said it, the worst that can happen is death, so I might as well speak my mind and say what I want.
Since I've expressed my heartfelt feelings to you, I've already made the resolve to face death.

I know I'm being rather thick-skinned.
But my feelings are beyond my control—I cannot help myself.

Shameless...!

yet you harbor such filthy thoughts about your own master! A disciple who betrays his master and dishonors his ancestors!
I hold both reverence and affection for you, as well as love and longing. I vow to walk hand in hand through life with you, remaining unwavering and unchanging for the rest of my days.
Then let me be your family.
Why must I live? Life is like a walking corpse, dull and meaningless. In this world, there are no hopes, no loved ones. Why should I remain in this world?

I missed out on your youth, so full of regret—like you, I too am a person scarred all over.

You, don't say anymore......!
I channeled my qi to resist just now, and nearly died from your Internal Skill. Having survived that calamity, what is there left to fear?
You! How dare you be so insolent with me! Are you trying to get yourself killed?
What...!
Every word of that, I said while fully in my right mind.
This savior isn't anyone else‑it's my unassuming disciple.

Could it be that my weak-hearted flaw isn't fully rooted out yet, that deep down, I still hope someone will save me?
No
......Did you, in your half‑dreaming, half‑awake state, dream of anything or say anything?
Xiahou Lan raised her hand, and the slap hung there in the air, unable to fall.
You still dare to look so wronged!
That's better than watching helplessly as you exhaust and wither away to death!

Uh
