Aren't you that self‑proclaimed cold‑hearted swordsman? How do you get rid of one, only for another to come along? You're always surrounded by companions. That's truly revolting.
I don't care about the past. From now on, Xianglang's wife can only be me.
...Perhaps that's so.
Stop spewing this unpleasant nonsense. Di San Xiang, your wife is already dead—killed by your own hand.
What nonsense are you talking about, you Ugly Monster? You're full of lies, falsely accusing my lord. With your behavior, even if you were born a woman, no one would want you!
Indeed. He is a disciple I'm proud of.
......This is the disciple you've raised?
Xiahou Lan couldn't hold back—she nearly burst out laughing.
......That's enough out of you.

But you said that lady isn't your wife; my master is far too particular to ever look twice at you.
So, thinking it over, that leaves only me here.
So you have a taste for men after all.
What did you say?

Huh? Were you talking to me just now?
Sorry, I wasn't listening—husband, what was it you were saying?
When I speak with my wife, it is not your place to interrupt.
Silence!

I—I took an arrow for you too. You sucked the poison from my wound and even smiled at me—
how can you turn cold the instant you see her? I won't stand for this injustice!
You don't need to scare her; she's not my wife. I have nothing to do with her. A coincidence saved her, and she's been clinging to me ever since.
That's because you don't know me yet, and have no idea what my Soul-Stealing Orchid methods can do.
Are you not afraid of me?
Th-that's right! I truly am Xianglang's wife. Others may fear you, but I don't.
Who is this lady? Is she your wife?
Nothing wrong with that.
Not allowed?
You? Take a disciple?
A disciple I've taken in.
Who is this person?
So are you.
You're early.
You and that woman, the two outsiders here, glared at each other, while the two who bore the actual grudge remained utterly composed.

This Xiahou Lan, keeping company with such a hideous man—she has no shame at all.
No wonder the Jianghu says her name is tarnished; she truly is fickle to the bone!
So this is the Di San Xiang my master spoke of.

What do you mean, don't want? Don't you dare shed tears and shame the Snow Mountain Sect.
Otherwise, I'll send you off first! Step aside!
No... I don't want this!
Disciple, the day of parting with you seems to be today.
Ah, ah, Master has waited for this day for six years. It's time to make a final decision.
Master! Someone is coming this way.
......Earlier than I expected.
You thought through the matter by yourself, and only then extinguished the fire to go to sleep.
Feels like I'll have good dreams tonight.
Now get some sleep.

These words, your master has never told anyone else.
Now that I've told you, I feel so much better for it.
Ha, and who do you think you are? Don't get carried away, you overconfident disciple.
But you'll still have to get past me!
Nobody could ever pull that off.

Anyone who wishes to wrong me will get it back a hundredfold. I don't think I've killed the innocent, but the name 'She-Devil' still spread like wildfire all the same. Whatever — if someone wants me dead, let them come.

From that day on, I swore that never again in this life would I let anyone bully me, or waste a kind word on someone I despised. Humility, meekness, the three obediences and four virtues — all that garbage invented to keep women in their place — to hell with it.
Let's talk about that after I've won.
If you win, everything's okay, right?

Even though I've fused the internal arts of both schools and reached the pinnacle realm where yin and yang are in perfect harmony — I'm no longer who I once was — he's spent these six years hidden under a false name, and there's no telling how far his skill has advanced. Which of us will win is truly hard to say. If I should fall, then as my disciple, it will fall to you to gather my remains.
Yes. Next year will be the seventh year.
Master, is that why you came to the Snow Mountain Sect — just to keep that old appointment?

He captured me, humiliated and scolded me thoroughly, eventually feeling merciful and refraining from killing me. He also made a pact to meet seven years later at the Snow Mountain Ruins for a final showdown.

Third Fragrance came from the same lineage as I did, having mastered the strengths of both the Snow Mountain and Soul-Stealing branches alike, and Xiaoju had even passed him the true qi of Kongtong's Iron Lute Divine Skill. I was no match for him at the time.
Third Fragrance and I were released because the Sect Leader shielded us. The moment I walked out of prison, I challenged him to a duel.
Master, please... please don't cry.
All he had to do was order our execution, and he could have stepped down to enjoy a peaceful old age. But he never hated me for his daughter's death — his last words to me were: 'Don't be afraid.'
......No, that's exactly it.
So that's how it was... no wonder you said it was you who cost the Sect Leader his life. But even so, it isn't entirely your fault.

In the end, the Sect Leader took all the blame on himself, saying it was his own lack of virtue that had torn the sect apart. He summoned his distant relative Wei Ju to take over as Mystic Skill Gate Leader in his daughter's place, then afterward, at the Flying Heaven Gate, gave up his internal force and ascended through corpse-release.

I hated him more than he hated me, cursing him with every vile word I could imagine. I wanted so badly to claw through that wall with my bare hands, to strangle him myself before the execution and perish together with him.
Isn't that obvious? Harming our own sect-mates, causing the death of the Direct Disciple — and by two conniving orphans of the Snow Mountain Sect, no less.
They're going to execute you both?

This scandal reached the Sect Leader's ears. He came in person, leading the four Sect Leaders, subdued Third Fragrance and me, and had us locked away on Soul-Stealing Peak to be executed on a chosen day, by the mountain's law.
Mm. A pity it was just wishful self-deception. To think I believed it so completely — turns out there are no ghosts in this world after all.
Is... is that Huyan Ju?
Now you know why I carry an umbrella no matter the weather — you know whose ghost I've been hoping would stay, don't you?
...Perhaps she is also suffering, carrying guilt towards you.

...I was every bit as surprised as you. I longed for that hateful woman to live, so I could hate her to the bone. But she wouldn't even let me hate her — her dying words were that she hoped we could be sisters.
Never thought that Huyan Ju would die for you.
That's true.
That doesn't matter. Besides, she's older than you, and she knew me long before you ever did. If anyone's the newcomer here, it's you.
Who is Jing Hong again? A suddenly appearing new character.
So amid the chaos, Third Fragrance tore Yan Luosheng's guts out; I clawed Jing Hong's face bloody; and Xiaoju took the Judge's Pen meant for me, and gave up her life for it.
He must have been furious indeed.
If it were me, I'd hold my tongue and quietly poison a whole crowd of people to death.
If it were me, I'd be so furious I'd burn Kongtong Mountain to the ground and go down with it.

Isn't that right? Even if everyone believed he couldn't match the Third Senior Brother, he still didn't give up. Imagine, the competition hadn't even started yet, and the prize had already been claimed by someone else‑how angry he was!
He didn't even get to compete and was immediately declared the loser; he's truly unlucky.
In the end, the only ones who cared were me, and that forgotten Yan Luosheng.

That's why you, standing on the teacher's side and imagining things, feel it's unfair. Back then, all the people in Kongtong used every means to lock me firmly on the mountain to seize the glory of my exploits.
This... how absurd... what kind of natural order is this? It's completely unfair. If he hadn't deceived you, how could you not escape Kongtong and look out for yourself!

One man presiding over four women—isn't that the kind of good fortune everyone envies?
Even Master herself gave her word to it.
He was bent on winning the position of Sect Leader—doesn't it all amount to the same thing?

To outsiders, this counted for nothing at all—what heroic young man doesn't have three wives and four concubines?
Besides, for the Sect Leader to marry four beauties was only to balance the power of the four families—simply the natural order of things.
I acted like a brawling woman, hitting and shouting, desperately wanting everyone to know their scandals, but the result was that everyone acted as if it had nothing to do with them.
Haha, don't make me laugh, Master is just getting to the exciting part.
Huge hidden weapon
So I grabbed Xiaomei and threw her into the room.

I hated everyone, and could no longer bear even the smallest grievance.
I wanted to destroy them all, and drag them down into the grave with me.
Nothing could be more right!
Right?
You should hate

I hated him for his cold-blooded greed, for forgetting the debt he owed the Snow Mountain Sect for sheltering him, and for trampling on my devotion. I hated Xiao Ju for stealing away my only family; even her smile turned my stomach. I hated Xiaomei—why couldn't she have just let me stay blind to it all?
From that time on, the gentle and kind Xiahou Lan died, vanished without a trace, and everything became unforgivable.

A love story as moving as verse, a friendship as fragrant as orchid blossoms—all of it was nothing but deceit. I thought I possessed everything, yet in truth my hands held nothing at all. My gentle temperament, shaped by years of propriety, only became a weakness, making me seem easy prey.

...When Master came upon them locked in an embrace, it felt as though the whole world had tilted, as though nothing was right anymore. Everything I had once believed turned out to be nothing like what I'd thought—it only seemed the same, while underneath it was something else entirely, and every memory was tainted.
Shameless! Shameless!

He believed that with my weak and easily exploited nature, once the situation was cooked up, even if I eventually learned the truth, I would only endure it passively. Once he became the Sect Leader, incorporating the four beauties into his inner circle, everything would be harmonious, and the truth would no longer matter.

When your Eldest Senior Brother and the rest of us were roaming the Jianghu, Third Fragrance and Xiaoju exchanged vows of love.
Fearing I'd learn the truth and turn against them, Third Senior Brother struck first, accusing me of misconduct and forcing me to prove my innocence.
Keep dreaming. Now don't interrupt.
Then I'll strive to secure the position of the Kongtong sect leader and then give it up for you to witness.

Only a spineless wretch like you would say such a thing. The day you hold real power, matters of the heart will seem far less important. In the end, Master too was seen as nothing more than a prize worth possessing.

Everything! You are the one and only, finest woman in the world.
You are the Wulin's greatest beauty—no one can compare to you.

You think, one is the only beloved daughter of the Sect Leader who has nurtured him, and the other is the snow mountain orphan who once mocked and despised him. In public and private matters, how could I have won over Xiao Ju at all?
Impatient disciple, sit properly
I'm about to die of anger!
Oh! Oh! I'm so angry!
I... My heavens!

She did it on purpose. She intentionally lured me to ask questions, provoked me into anger, got me to hit her, then ran away so I'd chase her, leading me to stumble upon Third Senior Brother and Xiao Ju's secret rendezvous.
How could she be like this?
She said that since I can't become the first wife of the sect master, the second or third also make little difference, she no longer needs to bother flattering me.

The Kongtong Grand Selection was drawing near, and Master spent every day embroidering in her chamber, filled with joy, waiting to become a bride.
One day, Xiaomei, who had always been sweet and ingratiating, suddenly turned cold and mocking towards Master.
Take it easy, and continue listening
What!
I
Who would dare to be so bold as to murder the Sect Leader of Kongtong?

Yes—because someone had the Sect Leader murdered, the whole sect entered three years of mourning. After that, the four ladies passed away one by one, and the Iron Fist Sect Leader also died of old age. The Sect Leader Election kept being postponed, dragging on until today.
However, the Kongtong Sect still has no Sect Leader to this day.

At that time, everyone believed that the Sect Leader's position could only belong to the Third Senior Brother. After all, he was an orphan from Snow Mountain, leaping through the dragon gate to take the title of Kongtong, which would also be a way to avenge the Snow Mountain Sect, right?

Yan Luosheng wasted his ambition on idle pursuits, firmly believing that peerless martial arts were hidden within paintings and calligraphy. The closer it got to the time of the sect's Sect Leader Election, the more he devoted himself entirely to studying his paintings and calligraphy. It wasn't a contest of literary talent; how could he be a match for the Third Senior Brother?
Thus, the only one who can truly compete with the Third Senior Brother is Yan Luosheng from the Mystic Skill Gate.
Very likely
Fortunately, she has little interest in martial arts; if she had learned powerful skills, she would have become the Number One Under Heaven.

Never mind how old she was—her monstrous strength is half natural gift, half thanks to the Iron Fist Gate's secret medicine. Not even I, with the martial arts I've perfected today, would dare meet her head-on. Take a full blow without using Transforming Energy to deflect it, and you would surely die.
That... how old was she even, back then?
While the Iron Fist Gate's Bai Mei Hu Meng Chen had their palm bones crushed by Xiao Zhu, they retreated from the Jianghu.

At that time, Flying Heaven Gate's Danxiazi met one fortunate encounter after another, his martial arts advancing by leaps and bounds until he even surpassed the Fire Dragon Immortal Monarch. That old charlatan, eaten alive by his own sense of inferiority, destroyed his own greatest shield—talking Danxiazi with honeyed words into throwing himself onto the battlefield to earn merit for his country.
My disciple, it's rare for you to speak with wisdom, you are much more lucid than I was in my youth.
Not worth it. Even if true feelings are hard to come by, once it can be divided, it's already not worth that price anymore.

I was once very foolish, firmly believing that true love exists in this world, that love is supreme, and worth debasing myself for. As long as the Third Senior Brother genuinely cherished me, and gave a little care now and then to the other three sisters, I would force down my jealousy and turn a blind eye.
I'm listening.
Still listening?
I'm back

You throw yourself into punches and kicks in the snow, hoping to burn away all your strength and jealousy alike, but in the end only a deep helplessness remains. You know these are already old matters, long since settled as fact.
Even my own unworthy disciple knows to cherish his master—so why was I, all those years ago, so careless with myself, not knowing how to value my own worth?
...Heh.
I... I'll go over there to practice a set of martial arts, then come back to listen.
Why did you suddenly get so angry?
How absurd! How absurd!

Though I had no wish to share one husband with three women, my travels had already broken the Third Senior Brother's heart, and to carry on our affair in secret would only shame him as the future Sect Leader—so I had no choice but to make myself accept this compromise.
That is, I hoped the Third Senior Brother could seize the position of Sect Leader, so that he could legitimately marry me as his wife.

The Kongtong Sect already had a Sect Leader, and his wife Xiaoju, along with two younger sisters, Xiaomei and Xiaozhu. Back then I was soft-hearted and truly could not bear to leave, but if I stayed, I feared this secret affair would eventually come to light. Caught in this dilemma, there was only one way to have both.
This is just the beginning
So you've simply stayed settled here in Kongtong ever since, Master?

After all, the years we spent together in Kongtong were longer than those in the Snow Mountain Sect. We both regard Kongtong as home. The grudges offset each other, so we'll let the Snow Mountain Sect's grudge go.
Why? Staying in Kongtong, isn't that just waiting to die?
But he suddenly refused

Since I was now a married woman, I could no longer also become the Sect Leader's wife. I feared the secret would not stay hidden forever, so I pressed the Third Senior Brother urgently to take me away as soon as possible—after all, both of us had mastered martial arts and earned some renown; walking the Jianghu, we would not be easy prey.
Fortunately, Xiahou Lan was staring at the fire, lost in memories, gazing blankly, and didn't notice your mixed expression.
I need to stay composed, pretend nothing is amiss, and not let her notice the slightest clue.
I already understood, deep down; I simply didn't want to know the truth. And what right do I have to think such thoughts anyway? I'm only her disciple — I have no business harboring such feelings.

Of course — Master is the most beautiful woman in the Jianghu, with a face like the moon and beauty like flowers, and suitors beyond counting. And scorning to be some sect leader's wife, how could she never have had a man she favored? So she had already been married, all this time.

I was but sixteen then, my heart just awakening to love, given over wholly to Third Senior Brother. When he grew suspicious that I'd been unfaithful with a man on our travels, I married him not long after we returned, if only to prove my innocence.
Forget it — I, Xiahou Lan, am already notorious; there's nothing left now too awkward to speak of.
Master, why aren't you speaking?
Once the new sect leader was chosen, I had no wish to marry — yet marry I did.

We banded together and defeated the Supreme Bliss Left Envoy, whose skill at the time was far beyond what any of us could match. After that, Third Senior Brother brought me back to Kongtong, and it was about time to decide the new Sect Leader.
How enviable. With looks like mine, no one would ever want to invite me along to roam the Jianghu.

Back then everyone's martial arts was so poor that whenever we saw someone who looked hard to handle, we'd all pile on together. Looking back now, that journey has become one of my most treasured memories. Sometimes leisurely, sometimes hair-raising — truly, it was such fun.
How come none of them have any sense of Jianghu honor, ganging up on anyone they meet?

Later, Xie Wuchen of Emei came looking to pick a fight with your Eldest Senior Brother. I thought I'd found my savior and begged him to rescue me, but he ended up beaten as well and got dragged into the group for no good reason.
I pleaded with them to let me go, using my status as a Direct Disciple to pressure them, but they remained unmoved‑it was truly infuriating.
How should I put it... I always feel a bit apologetic.

How is it not? My Third Senior Brother tried to shield me, but your Eldest Senior Brother and two others ganged up and beat him. I wept my heart out, but your Eldest Senior Brother's group still dragged me away by force.
Is this considered kidnapping?
One day, your Eldest Senior Brother and two certain people whose names you don't need to know rushed into Kongtong. I was confused and taken down the mountain, and we roamed the Jianghu together.
How could that become so strange and distant later on?
Hmm. Later, Xiaomei and Xiaozhu came too. The days gradually grew lively, and although I still disliked the Kongtong sect, I never came to dislike these people.
Oh, so that's how it was... So he became an accomplished disciple of the Soul-Stealing Gate.

Xiaoju wasn't really trying to stop me from leaving back then; she was only afraid that Senior Brother and I would drift through the Jianghu with no one to rely on, left to be bullied by anyone. So she feigned cold mockery, urging Third Senior Brother to endure hardship in secret and enroll as a disciple under our enemy's gate.
True enough, I suppose.
What good would being born earlier do? Without me as your master, who would have taught you your skills? You'd have died for nothing.
Damn it, I wish I'd been born ten or twenty years earlier — I would have saved you and gotten you out of that hell for certain.
At that time, I was extremely weak both physically and mentally, even more helpless than you. Otherwise, how could I have been so easily controlled?
The way you beg for mercy is truly hard to imagine.

The two of us fled together, but were discovered by Xiaoju. It's laughable — our martial arts were both so poor that combined, we still couldn't beat her alone. I cried, clutching her leg, begging desperately for mercy, all but kowtowing.

When I was in the Snow Mountain Sect, I looked down on him because he was an orphan and taunted him endlessly. However, when we reunited in Kongtong, I was so overjoyed that tears streamed down my face.
He's really lucky

He came for me. In the decisive battle between the Snow Mountain Sect and Kongtong, he was knocked into the snow valley and survived by sheer luck. When he heard I'd been captured by the Kongtong sect, he slipped in to rescue me.
No
Neither.
Or perhaps he is our Snow Mountain Sect's traitor?
He was also captured by Kongtong?
That Third Senior Brother of mine—Disan—is a descendant of the Tian clan.
Hmm, their clan members probably thought the same way, so once the Liu clan lost the Mandate of Heaven, they all changed their surname back to Tian or to Wu.
It's really disrespectful

'Disan'—'Third'—is an extremely rare surname, descended from the Tian clan of the Warring States. When Han Gaozu resettled them in Guanzhong, they were renamed First through Eighth according to their order of arrival.
That's right
Is this not an alias or nickname?
You actually know
What a rare surname!
......The expert of the Soul-Stealing Gate was my Senior Brother—Di San Xiang, of the Snow Mountain Sect.
Oh

But Master, why haven't you mentioned the expert from the Soul-Stealing Gate? Could it be Senior Brother Yu Lin?
I am a faithful reader of Jianghu Bulletin.
They made their names before I did, so if you've heard of them, you're remarkably well-informed.
Except for Danxiazi, they were all once renowned but have vanished without a trace.
They made their names before I did, so it's only natural you haven't heard of them.
Except for Danxiazi, they are all people I haven't heard of.

I grew up in Kongtong. Later, the four gates of Kongtong produced outstanding disciples, all cultivating young talents with sufficient strength to compete for the next generation of sect leaders. The Flying Heaven Gate had Danxiazi, the Iron Fist Gate had White-Browed Tiger Meng Chen, and the Mystic Skill Gate had Danqing Rakshasa Yan Luosheng.
It's hard to imagine

As an aside, since they are distant relatives, Huyan Ju and Wei Ju look quite alike, though their personalities could not be more different. Wei Ju is much more gentle. Huyan Ju, relying on her status as the daughter of the Sect Leader, tends to boss people around and is quite sharp‑tongued.

Of course not. The previous Xiaoju was the sect leader's only beloved daughter, named Huyan Ju. She was also my closest friend in this life. Without her, without the sect leader, I—steeped day and night in hatred—would surely have become unrecognizable myself.
That Xiaoju, isn't it Sect Leader Wei?
At that time, neither Flying Heaven nor Iron Fist had yet chosen their Direct Disciples. The Kongtong Four Maidens consisted of only Lan and Ju.

I hail from the Snow Mountain Sect—this much you already know. After Snow Mountain was destroyed by Kongtong, I was taken to Kongtong Sect's Soul-Stealing Gate, where I endured endless humiliation, and was forced to change my name to Lan.
You, though you dare not mention it again, have kept this matter in mind. Xiahou Lan's figure, faint under the glow of the firelight, seemed to fade slightly, as if about to dissipate.
Alright
It's not like I'm going to kill you; why are you so anxious? If you keep nagging, it might not be good.
And she insists on telling it anyway... it's truly unsettling.
Since there's nothing else to do, let your master tell you some Kongtong secrets that hardly matter anymore.
She's changing the subject.
Since there's nothing else to do, let your master tell you some Kongtong secrets that hardly matter anymore.
What?! M-Master, you're in perfect health—how can you make such a joke?
It's not seclusion, but eternal rest. I'm truly too exhausted; I brought you here to have you arrange my affairs after I'm gone.
Master, do you intend to live in seclusion here?
That's good.

What's the rush? No one said you'd be tied to me forever. This master brought you along because there's a place your skills will be needed. Once the matter is settled, you can head down the mountain on your own.
Th-that won't do! Didn't we agree on at most a year or two?
I never told you this before, but this master had already resolved, on this trip back to the Snow Mountain Sect, not to leave again.
I was just joking, of course I want to listen, I really want to.
Are you trying to be expelled from the sect? If you don't want to listen, then kneel and listen!
Hey, come on, it's already so late. Even if I'm not sleepy, I still want to wind myself down for bed.
No
It's all about listening to you chatter endlessly about your own affairs or the Tang Clan's matters. I, the master, rarely have such a mood; you just listen.
Don't slap my face.
Thousand-faced, my foot!
Thousand-Faced Demon!
Master, you're acting strange, you know, coming to talk to me on your own.
Sure
How about we chat for a while?
Not yet sleepy, but Master, is there anything you need to tell me?
Disciple, are you about to rest?
Petty
Thinking you're so smart
Hurry up and give me more praise.
Hehe, small matter.
My disciple, how capable he is!
...Hmm... delicious.
I took the dried food from the Tang Clan, mixed it with water, pounded it, added honey, and re‑dried it. When the heat from the tea softens it, it's delicious. Master, you might as well try it.
Where did you get the cookies?
Got cookies too, here you go.
Oh.
Master? Tea.
Master, the tea is ready.

Indeed, since returning home, Xiahou Lan often gazes into the distance, her face flickering through a range of expressions. At times she murmurs to the umbrella, dancing with it in silence, and stands dazed for a long while once the dance ends.
You have real patience, training diligently every day and attending to your master without a single complaint.

You're ultimately young and impetuous, with an unstable disposition; as time goes on, you can't help but have complaints. You keep thinking of finding an excuse to go down the mountain for a walk, but you always dare not speak up.
You spend every day and night with the one you adore, as if living in a dream, without a trace of weariness. You only wish this happiness could last forever.
Days pass one by one, and before you know it, you and your master have spent over half a month on this desolate, uninhabited snow mountain.

Xiahou Lan looks coldly upon your undignified, sprawled-out sleep, then wordlessly seals your acupoints and drags you off to abandon you in the icy stream. Only by desperately forcing your Internal Skill through do you break the seal and escape freezing to death.
You're worn out; even with the sun high overhead you can't rouse yourself. You sleep the whole day through, and remarkably, Master doesn't come to bellow at you for it.
Rest
Build a house
Practice martial arts

Ever since arriving at Snow Mountain, Xiahou Lan — cold and aloof by nature — has grown only more withdrawn, often lost in thought, silent for long stretches. Save for teaching martial arts, she rarely speaks of anything else.
But I only came to ask for your guidance in martial arts...
...It's none of your business. Shut your mouth and get back to your training.
What's got you in a bad mood?
What's wrong?
So, Master...
Xiahou Lan

Xiahou Lan carved the three great characters 'Snow Mountain Sect,' but wasn't quite satisfied. She went back down the mountain for gold lacquer and returned to repaint the letters, then hung the sign beneath the eaves of the wooden house — however she looked at it, she was pleased.
Later, she searched everywhere for suitable wood, brought it back without a word, just looking at you. You laughed sheepishly, took it over, planed the surface, and returned it to her.
The new Snow Mountain Sect main hall... how could it not have a dignified plaque?
Xiahou Lan studied the house you'd built, looking it over again and again, and smiled softly.
Okay, okay.
There's no 'next.' You neglectful disciple, get to your training this instant — or I'll give you a thrashing.
Heh heh... now then, I suppose it's time for a courtyard.

Done at last! I've redone the layout entirely — a living space where we can gather round the fire and cook hot pot together, with partitions dividing off our own bedrooms. I even put in a swing for you, Master.

You reinforced the walls, leveled the ground, and laid down wooden planks. You added a table, chairs, and windows, and turned the hide of a hunted boar into a mattress and quilt. Life here grows more comfortable by the day.
You've built a wooden house that shelters you from wind and rain — simple, but you can light a fire inside it. It offers a sense of security no tent could match.
Still neglecting your training, you spend today once more absorbed in building your house.
...It's up to you, treat it as a remedy, don't overthink it.
Picked it up nearby — the handle's half rotted through, so I'll just fit a new one. Even rusted, it's fine; a bit of grinding and it'll do well enough.
Where did you get the axe from?
Xiahou Lan looked as though she were somewhat tempted.
Master, weren't you quite pleased with the treehouse we built? Given a year or two, I could build one even better.
I'm preparing to make some furniture and build a house — I can't just let you keep sleeping out under wind and dew forever, Master.
Disciple, I told you to train, and this is what you're doing instead?
Heh, the craftsman who would do fine work must first sharpen his tools. At the very least, I need a table.
You've neglected your training again, taking up carpentry instead, laboring to build yourself a house to live in.

You found a flat and soft open space before it got dark and set up a tent for the night. The next morning, you woke up early, went to the stream again to fetch water and boil it, and attended to Xiahou Lan's hygiene.
Got it.

In the days to come, Master will not urge you to practice every day. If you have any doubts, you may come to ask me, but when you ask questions, it's best to think it through first and don't be too bothersome.
Thank you, Master!

This counts as my master's renowned martial arts technique. It is based on the Snow Mountain Sect's internal skill and the Soul-Stealing Gate's techniques, which originally belonged to two different schools. I, the master, have specially refined and compiled them into a manual for you.
How could you possibly be sure we would definitely fight?

Do you have that kind of luxury? Young Lord Rui's martial arts are far superior to yours. If you mean for the weak to overcome the strong, you can't afford to hold back at all — otherwise it's certain death for you.

The second question: the Jin Kingdom has repeatedly invaded our Great Song's territory, burning, killing, and looting. It is all thanks to the border guards garrisoning Xiangyang that we can ensure the people's safety. If one day the Imperial Court calls upon you, would you obey the orders to defend the Great Song and resist the Jin?
...The Tang Clan is treacherous and vicious, but on matters of real consequence, they still know right from wrong.
But the Wulin righteous might not consider the Tang Clan as their own.
However, whether the Tang Clan can be considered part of the righteous remains debatable.
Right and wrong cannot coexist; therefore, they naturally cannot coexist.
The Mud Cult and the righteous of Central Plains... I fear they cannot coexist.
The righteous and the Mud Cult cannot coexist.
Little brat, dare you speak to me like that!
They offended the Imperial Court, not me, how strange. I didn't shelter them; the authorities have the ability to arrest people themselves.
That's certainly a traitor!

...The Mud Cult kills people—how are the righteous any different? Since the Six Paths Dharma Kings each act on their own, then every grievance has its debtor; just seize whoever's actually guilty. Why must you wipe them all out?
The righteous can coexist with the Mud Cult.
Young Hero Zhao, what do you say?
This...

Great Hero Nangong, you are being a bit naive. The Demon Cult is an uprising that challenges the imperial authority and repeatedly tests the limits of the court's power. Heaven's wrath is fierce; their crimes are unforgivable. You stand alongside traitors and rebels‑do you not harbor rebellious thoughts as well?

However, the Six Paths Dharma Kings each go their own way and do not interfere with one another. The Beast Path Dharma King's bearing is plain for all to see; both the righteous and the wicked hold him in awe—how is he not a hero? If it truly serves the state and the common people, reconciliation is not impossible.

Brother Shangguan, to knock over an entire boat with a single pole is not advisable. The Mud Cult's wickedness is indeed true; we have made preparations to prevent being at a disadvantage after others have acted.

That's not possible. The Mud Cult has committed countless evils, their sins in the realm of hungry ghosts and hell are innumerable. The country has its laws; how can a single reconciliation statement erase all that?
And here I thought Sect Leader Xiang was going to ask something else.

First question: The Mud Cult has caused chaos in Central Plains, making them enemies of the Wulin. But if the Mud Cult intends to reconcile and coexist with the righteous, and the three of you hold the power of life and death, what should be done?
I have three questions. Let's get straight to the point and ask them. If any of you have something difficult to say, you can choose not to answer; it's perfectly acceptable to turn a deaf ear.
I wonder, Brother Xiang, in gathering the representatives of the Three Great Clans... what is it you wish to ask?
Young Hero Zhao, a hero indeed while still so young—that I should have the fortune to meet you is a blessing in itself.
The Tang Clan and Brother Shangguan are at each other's throats with no end in sight; since I'm here, I suppose I'll have to step in and mediate.
Junior Zhao Huo of the Tang Clan pays respects to Senior Xiang, Sect Leader of Emei.
No choice but to grit one's teeth and go ahead; a dead pig isn't scared of boiling water.
No choice for it—I'll be right back.
Ah, the beginning was quite touching, but the last line, when said directly to someone, isn't a good thing!
If you don't go to hell, who will?
Who else but you?
Everyone's putting this on you because they trust you.
Of course it's you.
Right, it's not like you're promoting yourself; it's that people are inviting you. Go quickly, go quickly.
Don't you worry about that—if you've got a chance to shine, hurry up and go.
However, the Tang Clan's opportunity to go out to fight has already been used up.
Me?

Shangguan prizes wisdom, Nangong prizes benevolence, Tang Clan prizes valor. It's a pity Sect Leader Tang could not come; asking one of his disciples, I suppose, should offer some insight of its own. Tang Clan's Young Hero Zhao, please come over as well.
...Sect Leader Xiang, I don't know what you're about to ask, but I urge you to speak and act with caution.
Wait a moment, Commissioner Shangguan, please stay. This matter of mine is also a question shared by all heroes across the land.
In that case, I will step aside first.
Who said anything about fighting? Since Great Hero Nangong calls me his brother, I'll dare to speak my mind. Please, Brother Yuan, enlighten me.
Brother Xiang, what do you mean by this? This foolish elder brother has long admired you. Must you still drag your old brother onto the stage to beat him up and humiliate him?
Great Hero Nangong Yuan, please enter the ring. I wish to seek your guidance.
Myself.
Who?
There is still one person who refuses to yield.

Sect Leader Xiang, look — the Beggar Sect's Gang Leader, the Nangong family head, and the Jinxiang Palace Mistress have all nodded in agreement. Who else remains unconvinced? This concerns the fate of the Wulin; you mustn't refuse.
If Brother Xiang becomes Alliance Leader, he will surely benefit the Wulin — how could I possibly object? Even if he doesn't step forward himself, the Nangong Family will nominate him all the same.
Jinxiang Palace regards fame and fortune as fleeting clouds and has no desire to contend for the title of Wulin Alliance Leader.

People won't let a woman lead the martial artists anyway; it's just for show. There's no point in us competing for the position of Wulin Alliance Leader, much less bowing to authority. Becoming the Wulin Alliance Leader would only tie us down and put our palace women in more danger.
Forget it, just let her eat.
Of course not!
...Then may I continue eating?
Junior Sister... do you mean to hide it? Hiding the chicken leg now is already too late.
Oh no! I've been found out!
Xue'er, you don't think you can shield your junior sister. This Palace asks you, how do you explain that thing in her hand?
Encountering a boastful man blocking the road... I and my Junior Sister were in the process of teaching him a lesson. This caused an accidental delay; please forgive the sect leader's anger.
Why are you all just coming back now?
During the day, the moon cannot be seen; at night, the sun cannot be seen. The sun and moon hang high in the sky; it's not that they are not there, but that your time has not yet come.
Can I really do it...? But no matter how hard I try, I can't even imagine it.
But one day, if you cross this threshold, you will be reborn.

It's alright to run from it. No one says that when you meet hardship, you must charge it head-on until you're left bloodied. Life still holds many possibilities. To put it another way, even if you gave up martial arts from now on, there are other ways to realize your ambitions. You needn't rush; there's still a long road ahead, and you can take your time finding your way.
Xiang'er, you're at a difficult juncture. This trial is hard, but I, as your master, don't blame you for it.
Lady Wen reached out her hand. Long Xiang braced herself for a blow, but Lady Wen merely patted her beloved disciple's head, her face brimming with tenderness.
Don't hit me...
No, don't go, come here.
Master, are you angry...? Then, if not, I'll still go.

Indeed, Junior Sister has been particularly strange since returning from the Woyun Ridge mission. This talk of cowardice has never been said before; it's really unlike her. Earlier as well, the opponent was merely boastful, yet she was intimidated.
But disciple fears they may not be Sect Leader Xiang's equal, perhaps it's better not to go up and embarrass ourselves.
Forget it. Xiang'er, are you thinking of seeking instruction from Sect Leader Xiang?
Encountering a boastful man blocking the road... I and my Junior Sister were in the process of teaching him a lesson. This caused an accidental delay; please forgive the sect leader's anger.
Why are you all just coming back now?
I, I'm nervous!
{size=24}Gang Leader, why didn't you read from the script? What's with this irrelevant talk!{/size}

Great Hero's martial arts are breathtaking. The later‑generation practitioners in the Wulin only regret being ten years too late; otherwise, they would definitely seek instruction... This time, let's not hold the Martial Conference!
All present, is there still any hero who wishes to come up and learn martial arts from Sect Leader Xiang?
Commissioner Shangguan, your words are incorrect. The grand assembly has not yet ended; how can it be determined that I will serve as the Wulin Alliance Leader?
It is rare for a Sect Leader to be of such noble character and yet so humble. With Sect Leader Xiang as the leader of the Wulin Alliance, its future looks bright.

Commissioner Shangguan, you're being too kind. Each sect and school of thought has its own strengths, and their applications vary. Today, I am fortunate to have the opportunity to exchange skills with the heroes of the world, which is indeed a blessing.

Sect Leader Xiang's martial prowess is unmatched, renowned throughout the Jianghu. Though I dwell far off in Fujian, I have long admired you from afar. Having witnessed Emei's divine skill today, I see the reputation is well earned.
Senior Brother's mouth is downright venomous.
You don't need to eat it to know it's smelly, who would want to be a puppet alliance leader?
Is this considered jealousy?
Looks like the court's new lapdog is about to come out of the oven~
That's not so bad, I guess
At this rate, Sect Leader Xiang is going to end up as the Wulin Alliance Leader.
That's true
But when Dharma King Wang fought that day, men swarmed the hills wanting him dead — and still he stood unshaken.
It's still Lian Zhan, but today's sparring is all Sparring Courtesy. The more skilled fighter will win, and they won't exert their Internal Force to the end.
Sect Leader Xiang is without doubt a peerless master. But today's situation is nothing like it was against Dharma King Wang.
As they say, a lesser hermit hides in the wilds, but a greater hermit hides in the city.
He is a proper sect leader, after all; when has he ever been a recluse?

Senior Brother, Sect Leader Xiang is truly formidable — fighting master after master without so much as a flicker of expression. Who knew the righteous sects hid talent like this, giving no ground even to Dharma King Wang at Jiangling that day!

Even the Sect Leader of Qingcheng bowed in humility. The arena fell silent; who would dare step forward to humiliate themselves? Moreover, Xiang Wuyou exuded an otherworldly grace, reminiscent of a reclusive scholar. The crowd admired him deeply, unwilling to seize the opportunity when he was exhausted. Even if they won, it would lack luster.
Does anyone else care to enlighten me?
That's right
...Junior Brother, only one person may be put forward from each sect. You and I share the same master; how can we fight each other?
Senior Brother, your martial arts are excellent; watching you makes me itch to try. Let me take a turn to learn from you a bit!
You've fought several battles and still engaged this old Daoist, how can it not be showing mercy, please.

A trivial skill, far inferior to Daoist Zou's chest full of ten thousand true scriptures. Besides, Qingcheng is famed for its Internal Skill — if Daoist Zou withholds his, he is plainly letting me win. Forgive any offense, Daoist.
Sect Leader Xiang, this old Daoist submits. You rarely let yourself be tainted by the mundane world; your character is noble, and your martial arts are equally remarkable.

Emei, Sect Leader Xiang, has been invincible since entering the battlefield, defeating several powerful enemies in succession. Throughout, his flowing sleeves fluttered, and he remained calm and composed.
...One leaf heralds the coming of autumn.
How could that be the case? You're overthinking it.

You said 'okay' three times, and your tone sounded impatient, like you were just brushing me off.
Is there someone else in your heart?
What's wrong?
Okay, okay, okay~
I'll spur you on ruthlessly.

I will cherish you more than before.
If I'm too busy and neglect you, please don't hesitate to remind me.
Brother... Come back quickly, otherwise Shang'er will be in trouble.
I can't guarantee that, you know. Haha.
Brother, my brother isn't here. From now on, I'll have to rely on you. You can't bully me, right?
Haha, he's getting what's coming to him, he loves to run around!
He just got off Diancang's wanted list, and now the Tang Clan wants him too — he really is unlucky.
You're still trying to make your move on me, even now?
Indeed, someone as brilliant as him can't hide his tracks for long. And if not that, then once our child is born, how could this uncle not come to see his nephew?
......Really?
He won't come back. Then we'll go find him.
No, I know... Brother... Brother will never come back... He doesn't want me anymore... Wah‑wah... Wah‑wah!
Don't cry, what are you crying for? He can't come back right now; once the Wulin Congress ends, you'll be able to meet again, won't you?
No, he made that decision on his own.
We were the ones who forced him... It's all my fault.
This...
Brother... My brother, where is he going? Why isn't he coming back?

After leaving Diancang, Ye Yunzhou now considered himself a Tang Clan disciple, having found a new affiliation. Seeing him return to the Tang Clan group and being warmly welcomed, the Wulin people all sighed in regret. Why would such a young master not join their own sect, but instead choose the Tang Clan?
Th-thank you, Junior Sister.
Young Hero Ye... Senior Brother Ye, take this pill I made — the Dragon and Tiger Vigor Pill.
That last strike cost me dearly — I can't fight again for now. I need to rest a while. Forgive me, Brother Zhao.
Brother Zhao, please don't tease me anymore
You there! Hurry and bring some water!
Well fought, Great Hero Ye. Please, sit, sit.
I have not disgraced the mission
You've had a hard time of it.
I'm not tired of living
Brother! He scared me! You must punish him!
It's okay, be good
Brother! You scared me! Bad!
I'm back

It's said the Cangsong Swordsman betrayed Diancang and went into hiding, his fame undeserved. Now that I've seen him for myself, I realize just the opposite — the title 'Cangsong Swordsman' doesn't do justice to his skill.
It wasn't just you who was frightened — everyone present broke out in a cold sweat. Never mind profound techniques or deep internal power; who could survive a sharp sword through the heart?

What kind of sword is this? How fast is it that no one can block it? Even if it were the Hegemon-King of Chu reborn, with strength enough to lift a tripod, he would still be flesh and blood. A single strike from a sharp sword would finish him, what's the point of fighting?
Brother Zhao, I entrust Yunshang to you

...Right, I'm fighting for myself here. That cry of mine, declaring myself a former retainer of the Yue Family — who knows what trouble it'll bring down on me. The Tang Clan... I suppose there's no going back now.
Conduct yourself well from now on.
Thank you, Master, for upholding justice
......Thank you, Sect Leader Guan, thank you, Great Hero Hai. After you.
So be it.

Don't call me Senior Martial Uncle anymore — Diancang Sect doesn't deserve to claim that honor. From now on, the enmity between your siblings and our sect is settled, once and for all. ……Will that do, Junior Brother?
Senior Martial Uncle, you overstate it.
Not only today, Diancang has more than once sought to kill you, yet you still showed mercy. This demonstrates Young Hero Ye's kind and benevolent heart, and Guan Yun Ke feels deeply grateful.
Damn it, Senior Brother, I told you not to underestimate this kid. I wasn't holding back at all, and yet look... His sword's fast enough that he still found time to dodge every vital strike of mine.
But moved by the deep bond between them as brothers, he shoved Ye Yunzhou aside and rushed to check on his Junior Brother's wounds.
Let me through!
Guan Yun Ke had never known that this Nephew-Disciple's sword technique had reached such a divine realm. At this moment, seeing him again, he could not help but feel a chill.
Junior Brother!

I still meant... to use this chance to show you the Third Legacy Move once. With your talent... one look might've been enough anyway. Seems it was pointless. You little brat... the student has surpassed the master.
Breakthrough of Cloud Pass · Thunder Shakes the Nine Heavens. It is a move I created myself.
...What move is this?
Diancang's sword is the fastest sword in the world, transcending speech, as swift as lightning.
I offer this sword as a token of my gratitude to my teacher.
After this move, if you can still live, then you and I — master and disciple — will owe each other nothing more.
Yes

Come then. Diancang Sect's sword is the fastest under heaven — it needs no second stroke to kill. As your master, I will unleash Diancang's secret art, never before passed down: the Sword Saint's Third Legacy Move, and kill you with everything I have.

No need for thanks — saying it out loud eased something in me too. All those tangled feelings, tossed aside now, and my sword moves lighter for it. I'll kill you shortly; just don't go complain to King Yama, and we'll call it even.
......Thank you, Master, for speaking to me so honestly, and untangling a knot I've carried in my heart for years.

Everyone was chasing the same wishful dream, hoping the legend was true, that fortune could let them defy fate and rewrite their destinies. And if it drove this pair of siblings to their deaths — what did that matter?
In the end, the treasure story was nothing but fabrication out of thin air. When had Ye Yunzhou ever failed to defend himself? Yet who was willing to believe him?
Damn, if only I had known there was no treasure map, why would I have risked challenging it? I ended up losing two fingers and have since switched to left‑handed Blade Art!
Damn it, if only I had known there was no treasure map, why did I have to be brothers with that Ye Yunzhou, and even invite him to drink and eat meat? It's a real waste.
Damn it, if I had known there was no treasure map, why would I have to be toyed with by that mischievous girl?

Not a chance — if they'd truly gotten the treasure, why would they still be slogging through the Jianghu? The Diancang Twin Venerables would have sheathed their swords and retired to lord over some corner as petty kings long ago. Why come running all the way to the Central Plains just to join the fun?
Is it possible Diancang already seized the treasure, and now tosses them aside like a spent donkey once the millstone's done turning?

It seems the treasure map story truly was just a rumor — otherwise the Ye siblings would be darlings everyone rushed to please. How could they be treated with such contempt? Worse off than some fallen royal relative drifting through the Jianghu.
Is Ting Haisheng implying that the relatives of the Dali Duan family are more important than the Ye siblings?
At least you're no longer worth covering up for.
So that's the case. Without the treasure map, we siblings would have no use, right?
Is there anything else you want to ask?

Guan Yun Ke never expected his junior brother to strike without warning; caught off guard, he was struck in an acupoint by the sword hilt and staggered backward. Though he kept his footing, his face went ashen, and for a long while he could not say a single word.
Wait‑ I'm not here to...
Senior Brother, subduing a mere junior hardly needs your hand—leave it to your Junior Brother here!
Junior Brother, you...!

That young master of Songyan Pavilion is kin to the Duan clan of Dali! A distant relative of King Shenzong himself! The two of you are nothing but orphans—be glad you have a roof over your heads, and don't you dare talk to me about fairness!
This justice was one I sought for myself—not one my elders presided over.
You have already sliced his right arm into two pieces with one sword; even if you glue it back, he will remain permanently disabled. What else can you say?

...Diancang's debt of gratitude to my sister and me is real enough, but the young master of Songyan Pavilion used the excuse of glimpsing the treasure map to try to molest my sister, and the elders all covered for him. What do you say to that?
My intention was indeed improper, but humans are not heartless; who can be emotionless? Therefore, it's half true and half false.
Whatever else is true, my Diancang Sect never once stinted you two siblings food or clothing. Having raised you this far, do we still owe you anything?

It's half true, half false. If it weren't for wanting to uncover the treasure's secret through you and your siblings, my master and the four elders of Diancang would never have spent years taking turns to cultivate and keep your sickly sister alive.
So the master‑apprentice bond over the years was all fake?

Now, in this public setting, this master and disciple duo directly discuss this matter, everyone fully focused, straining their ears to listen, fearing they might miss a single word, and worried they won't get their share of the fortune.

The rumors of the Yue Family's treasure have stirred the Jianghu several times, and every time there's a whisper, it inevitably brings about countless misfortunes. Many have attempted deceitful schemes to seize it, once fearing the Diancang, now fearing the Tang Clan, so they only discuss it in private, none daring to act rashly.

That's right—no use hiding it from you now. King Yue's Treasure—who wouldn't envy it? If not for King Yue's Treasure, why would I have traveled all the way to the Central Plains to take you and your sister as my disciples?
Over a decade ago, you rescued my sister and me on the road and brought us back to Diancang as your disciples. Was that when you first set your sights on the Yue Family's treasure?
Speak
...Since mutual killing is inevitable, the disciple also has one matter to inquire about.

The Diancang Sect has come to the Central Plains—we cannot contend for the position of Wulin Alliance Leader, but neither can we go home empty-handed. Today we must purge our own ranks to bolster our sect's standing. This Ye Yunzhou boy is such a rare talent; it's hard for my junior brother to bear parting with him.

The crowd murmured on, all despising Ye Yunzhou's character, yet still hoping to stay in his good graces, in case the treasure surfaced and he might share a cut out of old feeling. Of course, plenty who were certain they'd get nothing cursed him outright without a second thought.
Let all the heroes of the world be the judge—a rebellious disciple who dishonors his master and defiles his ancestors, should such a man be put to death!

Yet how could you be so ungrateful and treacherous—wounding your fellow disciples, stealing away the Sword Manual and medicine pills, fleeing far from the Central Plains, and with no shame at all, running to hide in the Tang Clan until this very day!

In the presence of all the heroes under heaven, I will ask you this myself. Diancang has treated you well, nurtured you with care, and let you rise to fame and fortune, earning you the fine name 'Cangsong Swordsman.'
...Very well. The Wulin fellows are all waiting to watch master and disciple clash—enough small talk. And don't let it be said I used my rank to silence my own disciple without a word in his defense.

This is where my heart leads me. Besides, this disciple is slow-witted—even now I still don't understand what sword heart or sword bones truly are. Better to study medicine and save lives; that, at least, is real.

It's rare enough to find one so gifted—born with a swordsman's very heart and bones, the kind that appears once in a thousand years. And yet you forsake the sword for medicine—is that not a waste of such talent?
Are you studying medicine?
Your disciple has made no progress at all in martial arts at the Tang Clan—I've only been studying medicine.

I'm not that old—my hair's still black; what could possibly be wrong with me? But you, who wounded a disciple of our own sect and fled to Shu, seem to have been living quite comfortably. That fierce edge you carried the day you fled is gone now.
Master has summoned me; how could this disciple dare not come? It's been too long since I last paid my respects—are you and the Sect Leader both still keeping well?
So you've come.
Master

Two top martial artists of their age clashed with peerless skill, evenly matched, leaving the crowd in awe. The victor stayed humble rather than proud, and his modest words gave Ting Haisheng ample face. Though defeated, Ting Haisheng lost with honor; the two exchanged a smile, and he cupped his fist and withdrew.
Sect Leader is too kind. Please.

How could Listening Sea Layman not have also shown restraint? I've heard the Diancang Twin Venerables practice the Dual Sword Harmony Strike Technique. If you were to join forces with Diancang's Sect Leader, the Cloud-Gazing Layman, even two of me would be no match.
Ha... Sect Leader Xiang's martial arts skills are divine, Ting Haisheng humbly bows in submission. Deeply grateful for Sect Leader Xiang's leniency, I am overwhelmed with thanks.
What──Oh!
No moves, no form‑this seems to share a similar effect with our sect's Forget Shape chapter.

Sect Leader Xiang was a grand master of Xingyi Fist, his Realm far beyond what ordinary people could imagine. The forms he embodied were no longer those of living creatures like apes, mantises, or cranes, but of mountains, flowing water, and clear wind. His moves flowed seamlessly, with barely a gap to speak of—no fixed forms, no set techniques, all as natural as if born of nature itself.

Diancang sword technique is indeed exquisite, fully deserving of the honor of being called the foremost sword school of the present era. Yet all martial arts ever created in this world are meant to be used against people. However...
Now you're feeling the fear in hindsight, aren't you?
Senior Brother! Um, Sect Leader Xiang...!

These two truly live up to being the heads of their sects, both using speed against speed, yet none of their moves are random; they all target vital points, adapting on the fly and countering each move with precision, how formidable they are!
Then come!
I'm not worthy, but taking this meeting as a bond to exchange sword techniques with you, sword hero, is also a cherished pleasure of a lifetime.
Can you generously allow me to glimpse the arcane?
Events from hundreds of years ago, this Xiang wouldn't know either. But the Heart Sword is indeed the essence of our sect's martial learning.
May I ask, Sect Leader Xiang, whether this tale from the jianghu is true?

The Emei sect, though it doesn't use swords, is said to hold to the concept of a 'sword kept within the heart.' It's said that hundreds of years ago, Shu had no other sects, and Emei alone reigned supreme. In that era the Emei sect was the foremost sword sect under heaven, known as the Shu Mountain Sword Sect.
Diancang's Ting Haisheng, pleased to meet you, Sect Leader.
This humble one is Emei's Xiang Wuyou, pleased to meet you, sword hero.

Ting Haisheng named the Emei Sect Leader, a man of few words. The crowd's hands were clammy with sweat, their hearts pounding. They all knew in their hearts that the excitement of the Wulin Assembly was only just beginning.
Sect Leader Xiang of Emei, may I have the honor of learning your sword technique?
Why don't I, Ting Haisheng, take the liberty of being this gatekeeper?

But the Diancang Sect was fully in favor of the formation of the Wulin Alliance. Since I have taken action, I should at least contribute something to the Wulin Alliance. Just as Qi Young Hero said earlier, the Wulin Alliance Leader cannot be a weak person with low martial skills.
Brother! Quick, stop him! He's lying, there's no such thing as the Yue Family's old retainers! He's going to get himself killed!
The Yue Family's former retainers, the six allied armies under the Red Canopy King's command,   nominated Ye Yunzhou to enter the array!
You have no one to recommend you, how could you...
I have severed all ties with the Tang Clan; I will fight on my own behalf.
I will! If you let my brother die, I'll cut off all ties with you forever!

It's not possible...... Ting Haisheng doesn't regard the position of the alliance leader as something to be taken seriously; the rules can't bind him. If you have any mishap, Yunshang will hate me to death.
Not possible
Ye Yunzhou, the outsider disciple, accepts the command!
{size=50}Tang Clan nominates outsider disciple Ye Yunzhou!{/size}
Understood.
I will! If you let my brother die, I'll cut off all ties with you forever!
Winning or losing doesn't matter, but don't die. Otherwise, Yunshang will hate me to death.
Hard to say. But I have to go.
...Can you win?
Dispatch Ye Yunzhou in the name of the Tang Clan.

Since we can't contest for the position of Alliance Leader anyway, having traveled all this way, we might as well show our skills. Now that Brother Senior is excluded, Young Hero Ye is the only one from the Tang Clan more trustworthy than you.
Senior Brother, let Brother Ye go. A true man must scale the high wall someday—better that than hiding forever.

I know this is an unreasonable request.
At most, it's a personal grudge, unrelated to the Tang Clan, but...
Don't mess around.
No, I didn't want to be the Wulin Alliance Leader. Even if I did want to, the court wouldn't let the Tang Clan succeed either.
With the Imperial Court behind the scenes, I want to be, but I can't become.
Don't listen to him, Brother. Aren't you going to be the Wulin Alliance Leader! How can you let someone else have the chance to go out and fight?
Brother! Quick, stop him! He's lying, there's no such thing as the Yue Family's old retainers! He's going to get himself killed!
The Yue Family's former retainers, the six allied armies under the Red Canopy King's command,   nominated Ye Yunzhou to enter the array!
You have no one to recommend you, how could you...
I have severed all ties with the Tang Clan; I will fight on my own behalf.
However, the Tang Clan's opportunity to take the field has already...
Don't worry, we can't keep hiding in the Tang Clan forever. We must settle this today.

Brother... Master is incredibly powerful, stronger even than our Senior Martial Uncle the Sect Leader.
You've never once beaten Master!
No way!
Brother Zhao, I will go.
Diancang's wayward disciple Ye Yunzhou, step forward! Don't rely on the Tang Clan's protection anymore! Enter the array, and let's settle our past grudges and enmities!

Since all you good friends have gathered here today, such a rare opportunity presents itself.
The Diancang Sect makes so bold as to use this grand assembly to settle a private grudge, and asks all of you to bear witness.
Though this is not the final selection of the Wulin Alliance Leader, it concerns the good of the Wulin — I beg your understanding!
This...

You can't say it like that — Ugly Hero Zhao Huo is Kongtong Sect Leader now!
Even the General of Dao Techniques respects him. You two bad-mouth him so loudly — aren't you afraid of earning Kongtong's grudge?
Besides, that's the Tang Clan we're talking about — the authorities not making an example of them already counts as mercy.

The Tang Clan has hardly any powerful warriors left. You didn't see that leader they brought; I have no idea what kind of ugly creature it is. Such trash is being paraded out, which shows the Tang Clan is nothing but a flicker in the wind, with only a mob left. Ohoho, you've come, Junior Brother, Junior Sister.

The anesthetic hadn't worn off yet, and hooded, you took a flurry of kicks, collapsing to the ground unable to move, your whole body covered in shoe prints.

Still, after your Tang Clan Junior Brothers beat you as one in shared hatred, their bond with you grew deeper.
Alright, alright, kick him again and he'll die. Let's go.

Hearing you say this, it seems as if she has a one‑sided love for you, which is even more annoying!

Although you two are in love, it doesn't prevent us from envying you.

I feel it's unfair too. Junior Sister Xiaomei is wonderful in every way, a pity she's mad. Of all people to fall for, she had to fall for you, Senior Brother. You too? Me too!

...Senior Brother, while you're face-down and can't turn your neck,
let me tell you something from the heart: I've actually wanted to hit you for a long time.
...Who can help me a bit? I'm really numb.
Alright, alright, not worth it, really not worth it.
Let go of me~ I want to hit him~ I want to hit him~!
I want to tattoo the mark of the plum blossom on your thigh! And also carve the four characters Loyal and Devoted to the Plum Blossom on your back! I wonder what face you have left to flirt around!
Didn't this Mei warn you? Not to get too close with other women. Clearly I'm good enough for you, yet you covet more than you have—it's really too much.
What...?
Sect Leader, your mastery of poison is formidable—no ordinary drug could fell you. The dose this Mei gave you probably won't keep you senseless for long. Don't worry, I'll make this quick.
Got it.
Pah, shameless~
Aren't you just feeling sorry for me?
You'd better not push yourself too hard trying to do well, or you'll wear yourself out. Otherwise, this heartless bad woman Mei won't feel sorry for you at all.
Thank you.
Sect Leader~ you've worked so hard. Even here in a foreign place, you never stop training. Here, have some tea—Xiaomei will wipe the sweat from your brow.

This miss has not seen much of the world; upon seeing your high martial arts skills and good reputation, although your appearance is unattractive, your manners are refined. When you tease her, she blushes instantly, her face turning red. She doesn't know what's wrong with her eyes, but looking at your face, she still finds you somewhat handsome.
Eek~
You saw that her footwork was unsteady, so you pressed the attack, rattling her completely. She nearly fell flat on her back, but you reached out and caught her slender waist.
If you still want to practice, I'm at your service anytime. But you'd best work on your footwork so you don't slip again.

This young lady was inexperienced in the ways of the world; seeing your formidable skill and shining reputation, she took you for a hero. Little did she expect you'd prove so shameless—using the guise of a sparring match to grope her face and hands more than once, and even pat her behind.
Shameless...! I'm telling the Palace Mistress!
It's I who should be thanking you for your hospitality, hehe.
You're not trying to cover up your shame by acting tough and causing trouble, are you? Hehe.
That's not necessarily so. I'm afraid your senior and junior sisters will accuse me of impropriety, and turn their blades on me—mincing me for real this time.
Young Lord Zhao is truly a gentleman; we have you to thank for that.
I see.

You left your guard down back then. If I hadn't stopped my attack and pressed against you, you would have spat blood. It wasn't a life‑or‑death battle, so I naturally wouldn't use heavy hands. Plus, pressing against you was always improper, wasn't it? That's why I halted my attack at the last moment, letting your weakness slip by.

There's something this young woman doesn't understand, and she'd like to ask Young Lord Zhao: when I used the move Evening Breeze Combing the Clouds just now, was something wrong? Why did it look as though you were about to attack, yet you suddenly shuddered and fell over on your own?
No need to stand on ceremony.
If ever Jinxiang Palace turns against me and accuses me of being disrespectful or improper, I fear I will be chopped into minced meat.

Your guard was wide open back then. If I had pressed in against you, you'd have spat blood on the spot. It wasn't a fight to the death, so naturally I wouldn't use full force—besides, it would hardly have been proper for me to press against you. That's why I broke off the move and let your opening go.
Well... fine, let's just say that.
Is that so? But...
...I... I just forgot the move for a moment.

There's something this young woman doesn't understand, and she'd like to ask Young Lord Zhao: when I used the move Evening Breeze Combing the Clouds just now, was something wrong? Why did it look as though you were about to attack, yet you suddenly shuddered and fell over on your own?
No need to thank me; after all, our sect borrowed your Wuying Hall.
Ah... my thanks, Young Lord Zhao, for your generous guidance.
Ha!

The longer you've spent together, the better you've come to know Xiao Zhu's temperament - this girl is easy to handle, simple to win over. Since she's already yours, there's no need to trouble yourself caring for her anymore. So you merely humored her with empty words and sent her on her way.
Okay
You're right, I need to go practice
Oh, how embarrassing! I really want to go pound some iron!
Alright, go on, quickly!
Ah...
I meant massaging your shoulders, pounding your legs, helping you dress and wash up!
You mean...?

...Zhao Huo, don't think that just because I'm short, I haven't grown up.
The Iron Fist Gate has all sorts of people passing through; I've understood a wife's duties since I became a direct disciple.
I'm prepared for it too.
Alright, I'll be going
I-I already let you hold me, what more do you want? Go on, get out!
But I haven't even tasted the sweetness yet.

Alright, Sect Leader, you've successfully coaxed me. Now get out. The Heroine of Jinxiang Palace gave orders - even as partners, men and women must avoid being overly familiar. You've lingered in my room too long already.
Xiao Zhu was all soft and yielding, not by intent, but due to the intense affection that had numbed her bones. After a long while, she reluctantly parted ways.
...Yes.
Lady Zhu, are you afraid I'll eat you? I'm right here.
...Do as you please.
My Lady Zhu, it's not too much if I hold you gently just once, is it?

Xiao Zhu approached you cautiously; though married, she had not yet shared physical intimacy with you. Partly from shyness, and partly for fear of repeating past mistakes and crushing one of your bones, she fought hard to rein in her affection and dared not get too close.
I can't see things clearly, but I recognize you. I remember your silhouette, your voice, your scent, your gait. Even if I go completely blind in the future, I won't mistake you.
My eyes aren't working well; there's no way around it. When I'm a bit farther away, everyone looks the same, just a blurry mass.
Haha, you're even weirder, you're into an ugly monster!
Pfft, you strange man. So many delicate beauties out there you don't fancy, yet you set your heart on a little roly-poly like me.
You have no ulterior motives; it's my own downfall that I can't escape from.
When did I ever manipulate you! Do I look like such a shrewd woman?
That's it; where would I find someone as easy to handle as me?
...Even if Kongtong truly turns hostile and comes to drag me back, I won't go.

You're worrying yourself over nothing - I'm not really the Kongtong Sect Leader. That I managed to steal you away in all that chaos was pure heaven-sent luck; I'll never dare hope for such fortune again in this life. I'm too afraid you'll be taken back to have any thought of coveting anyone else.
...Just make sure you don't regret choosing the wrong person.
Stop, stop talking! That's too embarrassing!
First, you are talented; second, you are petite and adorable; third, you are gentle and considerate. Fourth, you...

Have you never looked in a mirror? You only see the good in others, but you're every bit their equal.

After all, Xiaomei is so beautiful, with such a graceful figure, and Sister Lan's beauty could topple kingdoms. Sect Leader Wei is cultured and refined, every bit the noblewoman of Lin'an. Only I could never belong among such refined company...
You're the Sect Leader, after all. You only took me away because you were briefly out of your mind - who's to say that the more you think about it, you won't end up regretting it?
Xiaozhu, what wild thoughts are you off imagining again? Why would you be the one who's uneasy? If anyone should be afraid of being cast aside, it's me.

Otherwise, you might as well just plainly say you don't want me anymore... I still have other uses.
I don't need to be too showy; I just want the recognition to live securely with you.
Xiaozhu! Oh, my heart is so happy it feels like it's about to burst.

You... you're teasing me... Don't do this - didn't you hear the warning? You mustn't act recklessly here in Jinxiang Palace.

Got you.

You're bleeding like this, and you're still talking such nonsense?

I won.

This girl is really easy to win over. Seeing you face-down with a bloody nose, still so eager to please, she couldn't help feeling both a pang of tenderness and amusement. You deeply regret your impetuousness, seeing that you couldn't calm her down at once, so you waited outside her door. Xiaozhu cried herself to sleep, and when she awoke, it was midnight. As she pushed the door open, she knocked you down.

Sorry — are you hurt? I misjudged the force for a moment.
Ah, Senior Sister, please be gentle.

All worldly things are suffering, I alone am sweet.

Oh, good
Young Lord Zhao, please step this way to speak.
Oh no, I've been found out!

If you don't come after me, I'll be eternally grateful.
I want the kind that's really powerful. Otherwise, if Shang'er loses favor in the future, Brother will beat me, what should I do?

Still lovable

This Palace should reward you with something
Hehe, thank you, Madam, for your praise

You're not exactly modest, are you?
Lady, it's not that Shang'er has a talent for playing the zither; it's purely because Shang'er is overly smart and good at anything, you know.
After the song ended, Ye Yunshang smiled gracefully and jumped up.
