No, and unattractive people can still deceive just as effectively, right?

You don't have an ounce of caution in you, you're really dense.
Didn't your mother ever teach you? The prettier a woman is, the more likely she is to trick people.
How can that be reasonable? I clearly did trust you.

Actually, no one's a sage—who doesn't covet gold, silver, and jewels?
Even if you told me you weren't curious about the treasure's whereabouts, I wouldn't quite believe you.
This...
Brother Zhao, aren't you curious about where the treasure is hidden?
Please don't put so much painful effort into it—I'm afraid I can't bear it.
That's correct, so I occasionally hurt you for a good reason.
The closer someone is to you, the deeper they get hurt.

I adapt to the moment and tailor it to the person.
I only act spoiled and playful with people I'm close to—for those I dislike, I won't waste a single word.
You're usually so scatterbrained, yet you think things through so carefully.
If you've already gotten angry on my behalf, then why should I be angry? I'll just pretend to be magnanimous.
Why are you still laughing?
Ah, said the beast
Hm, they clearly know nothing, just rambling on over there!

There are more people spreading and passing along rumors than just them—how could you ever hold them all accountable?
Don't get so worked up, sit down and cool off.
I'll go wake up Senior Brother. You guys can head out first; I'll find those noisy fellows later and settle this with them.

Brother, let me tell you the truth.
Actually, about what happened today—I acted like it didn't bother me, but really my heart felt like it was soaking in brine, so painful. There was just nothing I could do about it.
No, hmph.
No more talk; it's still early in the morning. Go back and sleep for a while longer.
The Tang Clan truly lives up to being the most vicious, most dangerous place in the Jianghu.

That person had a terrible way of sleeping—not only would she end up on the floor beside the bed, she'd also grab whatever was nearby to use as a pillow.
The worst part was that she'd end up head-down, pinning Junior Martial Sister's head between her scissoring legs.
If I hadn't deliberately made noise outside the window to wake Senior Sister, Junior Martial Sister might not be with us anymore.
How so?
The Tang Clan once had a Senior Sister who, together with her, was called the Tang Clan's Two Fools. Be glad your traveling companion in the carriage isn't her.
Blame Sister Fang—she fell asleep and kept tugging at my cloak, thinking it was a quilt. That's why I woke up.
If you're not delicate, then no one in this world is delicate.

Hmm, I can't sleep either, so I've come to keep you company out of the goodness of my heart.
But don't get the wrong idea—I roamed the Jianghu with my brother, so I'm not that delicate.
Why are you still awake. Is it because the carriage is too small for you to sleep comfortably?
Why did I stay awake? As a martial artist, fully alert, you couldn't have taken me by surprise.
Hmph~ I was planning to scare you, but it turns out I was discovered.
What are you sneaking around for?

Duan Zhixiu would undoubtedly not rest easy. It's not strange for her to catch up at any time. Is it really no trouble to just lounge around like this? Alas, but there is nothing that can be done; it truly is vexing.

Yunshang's body was too frail to handle the jolts, and at this pace, she could cover no more than thirty or forty miles a day.
Tomorrow she might have to sleep under the stars again. Although the road had been smooth so far, I still felt uneasy.
Night passed uneventfully
There's a ghost! The ghost saw your face clearly and was startled, mistaking you for one of its own kind, so it drifted away.
You caught the Mountain Bandits but did not wish to expose your identity by leaving a name. Instead, you bound them and brought them to the market so others could claim the reward.
Mountain Bandits are attacking!
You killed the wolf and went to the market to trade it for some silver taels with a game trader.
Lone wolf attacked you!
Fair scheduling rotations
Of course it's you, keeping watch all night.

You all parked by the roadside, letting Yunshang and Tang Fang rest in the carriage while you led the horses under the trees to get out of the rain.
You took turns standing watch over the carriage, not daring to let your guard down.
Why didn't you stay in the carriage instead of coming down to stand in the rain? Go back, quickly.
Ugh, who does this kind of thing, going all out just to torment me.
It's all my fault. You can hit my brother or scold him. Just don't keep it bottled up inside you; it could harm your health.

To dodge our pursuers, we deliberately avoided the main roads. The carriage and horses were slow, and we even had to stop partway, which cost us a good deal of time.
It looks like we won't reach the town at this rate. We've no choice but to camp outdoors tonight — best find a place to shelter soon.
Senior Brother, the sky is darkening, and it looks like it's going to rain. We might want to find a safe place to stay before it gets worse.
Deliberately pretending to faint to get off the carriage, just to come back and take one last look. But the stream is still the same stream, while my home is no longer there.
When did you become a general, with all these tricks up your sleeve?
Good~ Brother, take the order and go on ahead, clear the way for this general.
Alright, we should probably head back now.
Why so serious all of a sudden? Of course I won't hold it against you.
Sorry, I was just joking. Brother, could you pardon a lesser one like me? You're a big‑hearted person; don't take it to heart, alright?
...That makes sense.
I had no choice... I also wanted to be born into a wealthy family, eating delicious food every day. It's destiny, and I was unwilling about it as well.
I truly am a toad hoping to eat swan meat.
Pah, dream on. You're a toad craving swan meat. I'm the good stuff, and you're not even a thing.

So which are you, little devil, a good thing or a bad thing? If you're a good thing, then hold your arm out and let me take a bite. From then on I'll have seen the world and won't be ignorant anymore.
I figured you wouldn't recognize it, tsk tsk. My poor, ignorant brother has probably never eaten anything truly good in his life.
...I don't recognize a single dish you named.
Ha ha, all right, it's a deal then.
Did you see my little fangs? Those little fangs won't let you have an easy time!
We have a deal. When we get back, you're supposed to prepare something for me to eat. If you dare to break your word...
I can stay with my brother, but I won't be intimidated by you.
You probably gave him quite a headache, didn't you.

I only memorized these dish names to give my brother a hard time and play tricks on him—pestering him, begging him to take me through the Central Plains to see the sights and taste every delicacy there is, so this life won't be wasted.
So that's how it is
People from Dali don't eat with as much fuss and fanfare as the Song do. Of course, I also learned about these dishes from reading Pure Offerings from the Mountain Home.
You haven't tasted them? Then how do you know these dishes? I thought you had eaten all manner of mountain delicacies and sea treasures in the past.
...How am I supposed to know? I haven't tried it myself.

You don't believe me? The Scripture Hall has a copy of Pure Offerings from the Mountain Home, and everything you mentioned is recorded in it. With my skill, given the ingredients, I can make it. Try it yourself, then tell me whether it's authentic.
Can you do it? You're just bluffing.
Why don't you write it down, and I'll make them for you bit by bit.
That's not it. Don't rattle it all off in one breath; I can't remember so much at once, and you probably can't eat that much anyway.
How about that? Scared now? Can't afford it anymore?

Then a few delicate fruit platters and sweet snacks too—candied cherries, crab-stuffed oranges, honey-preserved plum blossoms, sponge cake, and fragrant drinks and cooling waters are a must as well~ Like... like... ugh, there's too many. Anyway, bring two of everything sweet—one for me, one for Moling.

As for rice, I want golden rice and jade well rice; the soup should be jade rice-grain soup and mountain-and-sea soup.
For two-legged fare, mandarin duck grill or vegetarian steamed duck, either is fine.
For four-legged fare, I want lychee beef and stewed venison, and the soup should be scallop and chicken breast soup.
I want to eat something good, a real feast! Fish is fine, but not just roasted and left at that—don't shortchange my appetite.
Then what do you want to do?
I am not as easy to please as Moling; a fish won't do the trick.
Did you see it? A big fish! I'll go catch it for you to eat.
Oh, right, you're right. I got so worked up I nearly forgot the main point.
Are you really going? Don't forget that there are still wolves, tigers, and leopards behind. Better hurry back to the Tang Clan.
Okay, wait for me here, I'll go kill her right away.
Okay, I'll go kill her right away
Heroes see eye to eye
...No, we should hurry back to the Tang Clan. Safety comes first; it's not wise to cause more trouble.
Return to the Tang Clan promptly
That's correct. Are you going to help me kill her?
That's not just being sharp-tongued. She kept insisting she'd seen the treasure map, but she didn't even recognize you standing right in front of her. Isn't that just spouting nonsense?
No matter how good our intentions or actions are, there will always be people who are sharp and critical.
Hey, your hands are wet. Don't... this isn't a pat. You just want to use my clothes to wipe your hands, right! How can you be like this!
Okay, don't be upset. There, there.

Saying bad things about me is of no concern; I can dismiss it with a smile. When someone speaks ill of the Tang Clan, it depends on the situation‑my tolerance for such remarks is still bearable, at worst I might step forward to defend myself. But if someone says you are not good in any way, all I can think about is tearing him to pieces.
It may seem commonplace, but as just a common person, hearing it on the spot still doesn't feel right.
Don't worry too much about it. I've seen plenty of people like this. As a Tang Clan disciple, you should be used to such things by now.
You were right; the more I think about it, the less comfortable I feel.
Brother, why are you frowning so much? Is it because the more you think about it, the angrier you get?
Puhah～Feeling refreshed and revitalized
What happened? She had a sword on her back, so I figured she must be quite something. Sure enough, even a villager with no martial arts like me couldn't beat her.
Waaah, help! This is a den of murderers! Someone, help!
I will kill you and use your fresh blood to write the two big words 'Justice' on the wall, and sign below: 'Ye Yunzhou was here'!
It is. I gave you fifty coins, so you damn well owe me the whole world!
Is it really worth that? It's only fifty wen. Don't be so reckless!
Right, kill him. He will die a terrible death!
Not enough? None at all? Didn't you say you'd sell anything? You took my money and won't even give me lobster and abalone to eat! You bastard! I'll kill you! I'll kill your whole family!
Are you trying to tease me on purpose? In the time it takes to brew a pot of tea, where am I supposed to get abalone and lobster for you? Not to mention that fifty wen isn't even enough.
Without the lobster, you wouldn't go get it either? I'll wait for you here; in the time it takes to brew a pot of tea, cook the dishes for me.
What? You must have mistaken something. You only gave fifty wen, and you still want beef? Are you not afraid of the authorities catching you?
Abalone, lobster, two pounds of beef, Lamb Wine.
Much obliged. What would you like to eat?
Of course, here are fifty wen for you.
Heroine, are you going to drink tea or not? Can you not lose your mind in someone else's shop?

Now I am just like you all, a top‑notch rumor‑monger! A single word from my mouth can kill! And I won't have to take any responsibility for it either! I will redouble my efforts and continue spreading rumors, making this world a chaotic mess!
See that, Senior Brother Lin Zhiheng, Senior Brother Chao He!

Oh... oh oh... I did it... I successfully spread the rumor, and it feels so good...! Even the illustrious Cangsong Swordsman was swayed by nothing but my words, and I don't even have to take responsibility. This is the power of speech!
Okay
Brother, let's go
Hahaha, go ahead then! Will that cost me anything? Congratulations, you've won big again! Even my illustrious 'Breaking Boulders on the Chest' wouldn't stoop to associate with you! We're through!
How unpleasant. This one has no wish to sit with the two of you any longer. Farewell. Innkeeper, I've left the tea money on the table.
It all depends on who gets struck by lightning. I'm not afraid, but are you brave enough to swear a bet on it!
Forcing someone to their death and then taking it back - what good does that do? The moment you commit such a sin, you're doomed to be struck by lightning.
Scared, huh? Good, you should be. Anyway, if they won't hand over the treasure, we'll band together and use public opinion to punish them! I'll take back my words the moment they're proven innocent.
...I've never met you before. There's no evidence, and I have no wish to gamble with you.

Do I have some obligation to tell you? And what evidence do you have that I'm lying? Or would you like to bet on it? If she really has a treasure map on her back, you bet your head on it - dare you or not?

If this humble student is not mistaken, that attire marks Heroine as Lingnan school. The Lingnan school rarely sets foot in the Central Plains and is separated from Diancang by countless mountains and rivers - how would you know something so private?
Is this really true? I knew it! I knew it!
I know them - they're both rotten to the core, a pair of mongrels who'll skip town the moment they've made some money!
Martial Heroine, who are you?
I have a stiff neck from sleeping wrong, okay? Mind your own business.
Just shake your head, why are you shaking your whole body?
I saw with my own eyes - Young Lady Ye has a map to King Yue's treasure tattooed on her back!
You blame them whether they clarify or not - what would ever satisfy you?
You believe them just because they said so? Not me - there must be treasure, they're lying!
Didn't they clarify at Tang Clan that there was no treasure in the first place?
Then you have no evidence to know that they don't have the treasure? They haven't come out to clarify anything yet, so isn't it reasonable to guess that they ran away with it?
Whether the treasure really exists or not, this doesn't count as objective.
Ye Yunshang shook her head with a bitter smile. All was left unsaid.
Why did I just spread rumors? The objective fact is that they are in a state of fleeing; what is there to refute?
I've heard about it, but, are the rumors about the treasure actually true? Don't spread unfounded tales; remember, idle talk can harm people.
Which other Ye siblings could there be? Obviously the traitors who used to serve under Lord Yue Yun, embezzled the treasure, and fled!
Those Ye siblings?
Hey, do you know about the Ye siblings' affair?
Such a gloomy shopkeeper, never mind, I suddenly don't feel like eating anymore.
...What do you have to say?
Ugh!

The things in my shop are both unpleasant to eat and drink, and they're also expensive. You should think it over yourselves. Don't end up spending a few copper coins there and then acting like big shots picking and choosing, cough~

There's no point in having any illusions about this place. A shop like this, in a desolate area, definitely doesn't have anything good to eat or drink. The only things they have are coarse tea, steamed buns, and plain noodle soup. If you can afford ten taels of silver, I could sell the whole shop to you.
Shopkeeper, what do you sell here?
There's no dealing with you.
What if they do have some? Even without sweets, there should still be thirst-quenching water, boiled water, or medicinal water, right?
Such mountain tea houses usually don't sell sweet treats.
Brother, Sister Fang said there's a tea house ahead. Let's go take a look.
You should have a drink of water and rest for a while.
I haven't even needled you yet, and I'm already hated for it.
No! Don't needle me! I hate you!
This is simple; I'll just needle you.
Chest tightness, nausea.
How do you feel now?
Give me the herbs, I'll go brew them.
Whatever works, can you all stop chatting? Mainly, I just hope Brother doesn't keep moving around in front of me; it's making me feel nauseous.
Ah, if you don't want them, you could give them to me! Don't I need your charity too?
I travel far and wide, where can I carry so many things? As usual, I bring what I need. What I don't need, I pawn for money. What can't be pawned, I donate to the local relief office.
You were invited to be a guest doctor and treat people's illnesses. The citizens of Qingcheng all praised you and sent you gifts. Why don't you bring those things with you?
No one needs it, so the medicine won't go to waste. A doctor's heart is for helping others; I shouldn't blame you for that.
Blame me. I was sitting in at the Qingcheng Medical Hall and didn't have time to restock.

Out on the road, shouldn't you always keep various medicines on hand? Senior Sister, you carry a medicine chest and travel around treating people, yet you're missing exactly these few herbs—that's what puzzles me.
Really? If it's got dried tangerine peel, that would be great. I just asked casually, but I didn't expect you to actually have some.
Is it to descend rebellious Qi and stop vomiting? I also have some dried tangerine peel I made myself. Can it be used?
Yes
I'm only occasionally late; it doesn't mean I'm destined to be late! Haven't I offered you juice as a way to make amends every time? How can you be so resentful and petty!
You should bring someone along, in case you're late again and don't think to come back until three days later.
There's no help for it; I'll go around nearby to see if there are any herbs that could be useful.
I am not a wandering physician; why would I carry these around for no reason?
Of course not
Yunshang isn't feeling well. I want to prepare a remedy for her—do you have any mint or pinellia on you?
Yunshang's face had lost all its color.
Junior Brother, come over for a moment
Sure, I'll go to the back and have a look to see if there are any pursuers.
Let's rest for about an hour and give Sister Yunshang a chance to catch her breath.
I wonder if there are pursuers behind, so we can't be too leisurely.
Good...
Yunshang, sit on the stone and rest for a moment.
Senior Brother, stop the carriage! Stop it quickly! Something bad is about to happen!
Ugh... this is bad, I'm... about to throw up.
That won't do; we can't forget that we're running away. If they remember our faces at the tea shop, that would be trouble.
Senior Brother, I remember there's a tea shop ahead. Can we stop there for a moment to rest?

Yunshang's Lifeforce is out of balance, leaving her extremely weak. Even the jolting of a carriage can make her ill. Acupuncture at the Laogong point hasn't helped either, so it seems medicine will still be needed.
No, not good. It seems like motion sickness, something I never used to get before.
Yunshang, how are you doing?
Hoo... hoo...
Okay, get in the carriage quickly, I'll follow.
Don't talk anymore. Let's set off right away. Delay could bring trouble, and even a well‑laid plan shouldn't be taken lightly.
Junior Brother, only you could handle this task—it's not fair to blame Yunshang for it.
If you're really worried about me, would you still send me out as bait?
You made it out unscathed, that's really great!
Your hands are still there, your feet are still there, and your bottom isn't split open either.
Brother!
I'm here!
The two of you told Third Senior Brother what happened, and his eyes rolled back as he fainted dead away on the spot.
You can't do that... really.
I insist
One person's actions must bear their own consequences. You cannot shelter me like this.
If he starts to blame me, I'll just have to say it was my idea.

Things haven't been settled yet; they might not turn out that way.
It's too early for you to accept punishment now. Still, I should let Third Senior Brother know first.
Take me to see Third Brother, I'll confess my guilt and accept whatever punishment comes.
What do you think?
...D-did I cause trouble?
Bought it already! But with expedited shipping, it's still a few thousand miles each way. I'm afraid it might not arrive in time!
That urgent dispatch service of yours — hurry and buy one to stop them! Don't cause us more trouble!
That's true!

Don't talk nonsense! Have you not thought about the consequences at all?
Even if we could win, you can't wipe out the Wulin Alliance completely, can you?
Kill them all and the Tang Clan becomes the target of everyone's wrath — not to mention the court won't let you off either!
Isn't that also pretty good?
I'm panicking too! If the fire really goes ahead, it'll turn into a fight to the death!
Oh my heavens! This is going to be a big problem!

So... so they're planning to stab the Wulin Alliance in the back. When the Wulin Alliance marches west,
the Cang Gang brothers mean to lag behind on purpose, torch the Nangong Family Estate, and avenge me.
Isn't this a good thing? Why are you pale like that?

...They received the vouchers, and used them to buy an urgent thousand-li dispatch back to me.
Saying I was a woman of honor, they were all deeply moved and swore they'd rather die than betray my sense of loyalty.
Alas, not that either
This was originally something I owed them anyway; fulfilling a promise isn't the same as doing business. Besides, with such a long journey, there's no time for this kind of hassle.
A misstep—you should have settled the terms before handing over the money.
Why then are you still smiling sadly and looking so worried? Could it be that they took the money but refused to heed your advice, insisting on causing trouble for the Tang Clan?
Yes, they received it—and my personal message got through as well.
Then what happened? Did the Cang Gang brothers receive the Substitute Vouchers?
Definitely, definitely
In the future, I'll be relying on you to help me out. Boss Zhao, for old times' sake, must take extra care of Ying'er's modest little business.
That's not bad, but now it's even better.
It's broad daylight; what are you talking nonsense about?
Fortunately, I didn't listen to you; now you belong entirely to me.
If you'd been good and listened to me back then, I could have helped you become the boss of some Exchange House somewhere, you know?
Brilliant. Truly brilliant.

At worst, they simply refuse to take it—but once they've taken the money and issued a Substitute Voucher, they're bound to honor it. I borrowed the name of your creditor, old Lu Weng; the Exchange House master suspected nothing and accepted it readily.

Why wouldn't they honor it? Would they destroy their own reputation over a mere few thousand taels of silver? I personally trained every Exchange House boss in every region myself; I don't recall raising anyone foolish or shortsighted under me.
You still keep your money at the Shangguan Exchange House—aren't you afraid they won't honor it?
These business strategies really make my head spin.
I wasn't complimenting you.
One can say that. Thank you for the compliment.
...Is this a way of forcing people to spend only at your store? Such harsh measures.
Though so, by taking detours to exchange for Salt Certificates, tea permits, and incense permits, and then trading at other shops, one can still get money in return—but it's likely to come at a loss.

So it can only be used internally. This is done to facilitate the circulation of goods and reduce money transport risks. Holding a Shangguan Substitute Voucher allows one to exchange for goods at all shops within the reach of the Shangguan trade route, but they cannot withdraw cash.
Y-you people actually have your own currency... isn't that skirting the imperial court's taboos?
It's paper currency issued internally by the Shangguan Trading Company, similar to Huizi or Jiaozi.
What are Substitute Vouchers?

Fujian is too far; carriage and horseback travel are slow, making it difficult for letters to reach back and forth. Given such a large sum of wealth, I cannot be so foolish as to entrust someone with its transport. Thus, I deposited it in Shangguan's establishment and requested an exchange voucher from the draft shop.
My intention was to use the money to help the Cang Gang brothers settle down, so they wouldn't have to keep living by the blade's edge for a living.
Pfft— ahem!
Oh my, so I've become Master? Quite the glory.
The title 'Master' is one I dare not accept—I fear if I did, you'd turn around and give me a beating later.
Then let this humble one report to Master on how things stand so far.
You're welcome. Be good.
Much obliged to Miss for the generous reward.
No, so far everything has gone smoothly, and I've even earned more than I expected. Here, take this for some pocket money.
...Is everything not going smoothly?

Ye Yunshang came to the clinic to find you and was lured by the pastries. She extended her pale wrist for you to take her pulse. As your understanding of medicine deepened, you increasingly admired the profound medical skills of Second Senior Brother as if they were divine.

Ye Yunshang came to the clinic to find you, lured in by the pastries, and offered her pale, slender wrist for you to take her pulse.
Her pulse showed the same signs Second Senior Brother had described—bizarre and impossible to diagnose—and as for how to go about treating it, you hadn't the faintest idea.
Heaven has a benevolent disposition towards all life; whether someone is good or evil, you cannot refuse to help when they are in need.
That's settled
Righteousness and evil cannot coexist; you chose to let a person die without helping them.
I don't care if you die
The Hell Path ghost soldiers who came to the clinic seeking treatment vowed that they would trouble the Tang Clan no more.

The world holds four hundred and four ailments; even those who cultivate the Way in mortal flesh cannot escape the five exhaustions and seven injuries, and must still see a physician. Mindful of the kindness Qingcheng once showed in treating you, you decline to accept payment.
You treated a cripple with both legs broken without charge.
You treated a blind person who couldn't find their way home without compensation.
You treated an elderly person who couldn't afford medical care without charging them.

You treated a disfigured poor prostitute for free. While treating her, she resented your ugliness. When she left, she suddenly slapped you, blaming you for being lecherous. Your plight was met with sympathy.
You cured a patient with a stubborn illness. Though it earned you little money, it won you the unanimous respect of the local physicians.
Patients who benefited from the art of medicine brought fruits as a token of gratitude. Then, Ye Yunshang ate the fruits.

The art of forging Mechanisms is also a specialty of the Tang Clan. The elder from Qingcheng has long admired this skill and has placed an order with you to forge a new sword. He boasts about it everywhere, causing the disciples in the sect to salivate with envy.

You went to town and spent money borrowing a hammer. Following the diagram in the Tang Clan Hidden Weapon General Principles, you integrated your own experience to craft high‑quality iron tools. Having grown accustomed to the hot environment, you seemed to have picked up some fire energy, becoming slightly more temperamental.
You go to town and spend money borrowing a hammer to forge iron, but with distracted thoughts, you accidentally hit your own hand. Even uncivilized monkeys could do better than you.

You go to town and spend money borrowing a hammer, but the blacksmith keeps peeking at you, trying to steal your technique. Distracted, you turn out mediocre work and can only sell it cheap to the smithy.

You went to town and spent money to borrow a hammer. Following the diagrams in the Tang Clan Hidden Weapon General Principles, you hammered and shaped the iron, enduring high‑temperature environments to forge the tool. The results were satisfactory.

Ignorant villagers spread rumors that you are a monster — your true form a fish, tamed and put into service by a Qingcheng Immortal Elder, turned from evil to good. So they took to feeding you fresh fruit and vegetables.

You were enjoying a bowl of noodles while listening to a storyteller at the tea house when you turned around and found Ye Yunshang sitting beside you. Not only had she taken the liberty to order a whole table of dishes for you, but she had finished them all, flashing you a proud smile. Of course, you were the one who had to pay the bill.
You wandered around, spending some money to satisfy your hunger and content your spirit.
While out shopping, you ran into the Demon King of Chaos, Ye Yunshang. Leave your money, or leave your life!

You were so engrossed in watching the street performers that you lost track of time. When you came to your senses, you found a hole cut in your bag. Though it held no money, it did hold Tang Clan poison — you can only hope it doesn't fall into the wrong hands.
You wandered around, although your purse was empty and you couldn't afford to spend much. But walking down the mountain just to look around brought you some peace of mind.
Though it was a misunderstanding on the part of the Qingcheng disciples, you did attack them as well. So, this matter is settled.
After your explanation, I finally understood what happened.
Let's talk clearly, it's me! I'm from the Tang Clan and I've come to study here!
What a ominous Diyuan meeting!
If you won't run, then I will! See you in the Underworld!
No, but I'm not—
Not good, with many enemies and few of us, brother, let's hurry!
Senior Brother, Master, come quickly! There are Demon Cult villains here!
Damn it...
Some people have to be slapped before they can listen properly to others. You do not pursue this, sparing him from being disciplined by his superiors; he is deeply grateful for this.
Not pursuing it
You beat the man down and dragged him before the Qingcheng elders, earning a little compensation for your trouble.
Pursue

You followed the Qingcheng disciples down the mountain to set up an altar for blessings on the nearby towns, seeking to ward off calamity and repel evil spirits. While relieving yourself alone, an unfamiliar Qingcheng disciple mistook you for a Hell Path ghost soldier!
Evil cannot prevail over the righteous, especially when the righteous are many and strong. Combining your strength with Qingcheng's, you drove off the Hell Path ghost soldiers.

It wasn't that I worked hard, but rather that I tried my best to make a good impression and win the favor of my teachers.
There's no way around it; something has to be done. Since the other senior disciples are lazy, can't I be a bit more diligent?
One can read your character in your conduct — I'd guess you were a diligent sort back in the Tang Clan too.
Thank you, Daoist, for your encouragement!
I— is that so? I thought I was in for some bad luck.

In your short time here in Qingcheng, you've done quite well — word of it has reached even this old Daoist's ears now and then. There's no other purpose today; I simply wish to offer you a few words of praise.
Nothing so formal as instructions — just idle chat, that's all.
Daoist, do you have some instructions for me?
You are overthinking it
Call it experience. I haven't broken a leg, yet my teachers turn concerned — that's usually when a storm's brewing.
Why would you think that?
...Daoist, you called me. Could it be that junior has done something wrong?
Boredom can be a blessing too — look at it differently, and it's called tranquility. One of life's greatest pleasures, in fact, is having nothing to do.

Qingcheng's mountains stand green, its waters run clear, with birdsong and flowers everywhere — every corner of it is lovely. It's only that I've grown so used to being busy that I can't sit idle for long; I feel a bit lost with nothing to do.
The Qingcheng Sect has everything, but it's just too boring sometimes. I often don't know what to do.
Qingcheng is good in every aspect, but it's a bit too idle.
That's good

You remembered how, back when the Tang Clan's martial uncles were still alive, they cared for you time and again, earnestly urging you to leave — and your heart couldn't help but sink at the memory.

Suddenly becoming casual?

Ah—I feel a wave of relief, and only now realize I'd let myself fall into rivalry.
Ah, so that's it. And here I'd thought he was truly extraordinary.

Only auxiliary troops attacked the White Wind Army — the true elite of the Great Song stood guard at Xiangyang. Li Yuanqi wanting to become emperor probably won't be so easy.

That is why I have been bedridden and could not recover. That is why Second Hero Tang devoted so much effort to help me dispel my internal power and preserve my life.
Yes, it's a pity my dantian was shattered, so I couldn't circulate that rich true qi. Not only was the pill wasted, but it left me with endless trouble besides.
Ten years of Power? No wonder Patriarch Wuxiang must have it.
Yes, the pill is extremely potent. Not only can it bring the dead back to life, but it's said to add ten years to one's Power as well.
That is what Patriarch Wuxiang left behind, then.

Eldest Senior Brother has always been carefree and reckless. How did he dare cross blades with such a ruthless figure back then, and even win? The more I think of it, the more it unsettles me — I can't help but sweat for him.

Although the Supreme Bliss Left Envoy claims he cannot stand alongside us heroes of the Central Plains, he is clear about debts of gratitude and grudges alike. In spirit and ambition, he is truly a remarkable figure of his age.
I will win. This century‑old grudge, I shall personally sever.
Do not try to bear others' obsessions. Those old matters have nothing to do with this generation; you cannot shoulder them.
Loyalty, righteousness — such empty, intangible things. You should value your own life more than that.
Your father and mother's betrayal of me — call it settled, evened out by that bowl of thin gruel all those years ago.
When Li Yuanqi heard me say this, he didn't take it well at all and tapped a sharp rap on my forehead. Since I hadn't listened to his earnest advice, I had exposed my flaw the moment I tried.

I was young and didn't understand things, so naturally I copied my father's manner. My heart was choked with resentment, and I felt utterly wronged. Everyone pressing me so hard, I thought, could only mean they wanted me dead — so wouldn't everyone be pleased if I died?
Forgive me, but I can't accept that kind of loyalty — that being cleared of blame requires dying for it. And even once it's proven, whether others believe it is another matter.
I was different back then compared to now; I grew up around it. I was practically my younger sister's brother from a young age.

At that time, I was still clueless, much more foolish than I am now. They replied, I am willing to die to plead with the heavens, only asking for the heavens to open their eyes, to restore the Ye family's innocence and prove my ancestors' loyalty and valor.

He paced back and forth before us, hands clasped behind his back, and at last asked me: "Shang'er, do you want to live?"
Poor child, you're so young and have endured so much suffering.
That night he left the camp alone to find us. Seeing my meridians shattered, I was already at the brink of death, breathing out more than in — it looked as though I would not live.
Ah, it turns out to be this way. I was momentarily angered and didn't think of this possibility.

If Li Yuanqi took my brother and me in, wouldn't that hand people exactly the pretext they wanted? Then, with him already branded a rebel, the good name the Ye family had guarded for generations would be ruined in an instant.

The Emperor did not expect my father and mother to use their deaths to prove their innocence. Senior Ye values the honor of his house, and holds a kind heart besides - a worthy descendant of the loyal and the good. Alas, it was that very moment of kindness that sowed endless trouble to come.
My father-in-law was far too soft-hearted - the compassion of a woman, they'd call it. And it was that single moment of misplaced mercy that sowed endless trouble to come.

When my father saw him arrive bearing Ye family tokens to claim kinship, he learned the Ye family still had a distant branch. At the decisive battle for Supreme Bliss Cult, he won by a narrow margin but suffered severe injuries. He staggered to my house, looking like a man drenched in blood.

Haha!

When the situation is settled, not only will they not speak of compensating the Jianghu martyrs, but they will also forbid the historians from recording this matter to save face. The Emperors of the Great Song have always been quite foolish.

The Imperial Court merely regarded it as an ordinary disturbance, seriously underestimating the situation. If it weren't for the heroes of the Wulin stepping forward, by the time the Emperor realized what was happening, the country would have already changed hands.
Naturally, all my subjects of Song know this matter well.

Figured it out
Although it's surely not that she's taken a liking to me, smiling at me is still better than her drawing a sword on me.
Sister Xiang, what's going on? You keep moving around, alternating between looking surprised and blushing. Now you're smiling at me again.
Long Xiang got it wrong, thinking that you were chosen by Lady Wen as the caretaker, and thus became even more reliant on you.
My brother is really impressive; even Master agrees.

What if I'm not wrong? Master must have foreseen that after her passing I wouldn't return to Jinxiang Palace, so he'd already arranged a place for me and entrusted him to look after me... yes, that must be it.
How could it be possible? I must have misunderstood something...
...In other words, did Master entrust me to Brother Zhao?
Wait—it seems I was the only Jinxiang Palace disciple who ended up at the Tang Clan! Could Master have foreseen even this?
Master summoned Brother Zhao alone and entrusted him with what matters...?
No, I'm too stupid; I still can't understand.
Don't understand

Master is preternaturally wise—he must have known the court would set the Wulin Alliance against the Tang Clan. The Tang Clan has all but become the Wulin's public enemy; everyone knows it cannot withstand the Wulin Alliance, like a mantis trying to stop a chariot. Why did Master still urge my senior and junior sisters back then to go to the Tang Clan if they didn't wish to retire?
Yes... why didn't Master take everyone and disband while the days were still fair? Why go to the Wulin Assembly at all?

...Later, this Palace Mistress of Jinxiang Palace was almost identical to the previous one in appearance, voice, and bearing. Yet her manner was entirely different. I still admired the original one, proud and aloof, unmoved by the accusing fingers of a thousand men.

...Perhaps they should have done so from the beginning. Closing the palace gates and leaving under circumstances where no one would know, each taking off their white robes and departing one by one. They wished to retire openly and honestly, but ended up with such an outcome.
What's so hard to guess about that? She's just angry, that's all.

Later, this Palace Mistress of Jinxiang Palace led her attendants back, rescinded her order of retirement, and paid her respects to the Alliance Leader. Yet citing grave injuries suffered at Fengyu Mountain, she has kept the palace gates locked ever since, declining every visit and refusing every apology, her true intentions impossible to guess.

Lastly, there is Jinxiang Palace. Whatever the truth of it, the Dharma King of the Human Path suffered wounds beyond all hope of recovery, and lay down to eternal sleep alongside the Nangong Family Head, a fact witnessed by all present.

The Shangguan Family dismissed all the Jianghu retainers they had kept over the years, but the Cang Gang still remains under their command. We don't know how many will come; it's precisely this group we need to guard against.
I cannot say that I acted on a whim just for Miss Ying, sigh.
At the time, everyone was still criticizing me for being reckless.
That's right! He fought well! He just wanted that fellow to know the Tang Clan isn't to be trifled with! Even if he couldn't win, he wasn't about to let that bastard off easy!
Junior Brother, challenging the Shangguan Family Head at the Wulin Assembly may have been reckless of you, but I couldn't have held back either! You fought well!

No wonder our sect has faced continuous misfortunes. Our business has suffered consecutive losses year after year, and all sorts of strange coincidences have occurred. I must admit, it's hard to believe anyone would be so unlucky. It turns out that someone has been deliberately causing these problems!
By now, the situation could not be clearer. The Shangguan Family's talk of retiring from the Wulin was a lie; they willingly became the court's hounds, tormenting their fellow denizens of the Wulin.
Sorry to have spoken so abruptly, I will take my leave now.
...I'm not saying I don't trust your business acumen. However, our sect's finances are not optimistic. This matter needs careful consideration; I will provide more details later.
Where there's a will, there's a way; I will do everything in my power.

Then I have no objections at all. Sister-in-law, if you can persuade the Cang Gang not to make trouble for our sect, I'll thank you on behalf of the whole sect. If you can't, I still appreciate the sentiment.

Third Senior Brother, you are too generous. Seeing an opportunity to benefit, yet still considering others? There's no need to be so reserved. I am also a Tang Clan disciple. We can just contribute money or strength when needed.

The money you put in will naturally end up in your pocket if you make a profit. If we lose, our sect won't be at a disadvantage either; there's only benefit to be gained. Are you really willing to give it up?
Of course, if there's profit left over, I'll take it all for myself, call it my return on investment. Fair, isn't it?
This...

Third Senior Brother, for the matter with the Cang Gang, let me, Junior Brother, and Young Lady Shangguan work something out. I'll wait to hear the detailed plan before deciding; if it's feasible, I'll fund it entirely myself.
I was just joking! I was just joking! Heroine, spare me!
Fourth Senior Brother, stop bothering her. Miss Ying will repay debts and avenge grievances. If you take the joke too far, you'll be dragged to the outhouse for a beating later.
Alright, Sister-in-law, I was just playfully teasing you.
Fourth Senior Brother, don't bully Miss Ying. Can you bear to watch me get beaten?
Uh...
The dignified Young Lady Shangguan now has to call me Brother Four! Who's the rich one now! Who is it!
Ha! Ha! Ha!
Right, Brother Four. You are a merchant too, so you should have some financial backing. I'll detail the key points to you, and you'll understand the importance right away.
Lady Shangguan, how does one roll wealth into more wealth? Please elaborate.
Oh dear, this woman gets so ruthless that she even beats her own husband.
Hey!
If you're being unwise, just kill them again.

If some aren't suited to a new place or unwilling to relocate, persuading them to step aside is better than needless bloodshed. Saving one person is like saving their whole family. As for those truly resolved to fight to the death, there'll be time enough to cross blades with them later.
Third Senior Brother, Miss Ying is loyal and righteous towards us. She would naturally extend the same loyalty to her followers. If scattering some money can pacify them, why not do it?
Oh, oh
{size=24}Say something for me, you dolt — aren't I your woman?{/size}
If the Tang Clan were ever to disband, I would certainly do everything in my power to raise funds for everyone to settle down. But I can't say this aloud, lest it tempt bad luck.
...I know it's not reasonable, but they're brothers who've risked life and death alongside me. If... if it were the Tang Clan...
Besides, hosting the Wulin Assembly costs money too — what sense would there be in funding the enemy on the eve of battle?
I'm embarrassed to admit it, but our sect's debts aren't even paid off yet... conjuring money out of nowhere is no easy thing.

Though the mountain of debt the Tang Clan carries is partly of its own making, the Shangguan Family has done no small amount of scheming and sabotage behind the scenes. For this young lady to now ask the Sect Leader for funds again — how could that not stir gossip?

So... could Third Brother perhaps allocate a little money for me to handle this matter? It wouldn't need to be much, just enough to smooth things over and get the ball rolling. With that, it would all pay back quickly.

I really wanted to make a bold promise: 'Third Brother, give me a little time and I'll find a way to raise the money.' But now that the Shangguan Family Head has stripped me of my authority and cut off all support, without the Tang Clan as my backing, I can't even scrape together the capital to start over.

If we can help the brothers of Cang Gang settle down and secure their livelihoods, so that they no longer worry about making ends meet, it will be much easier to persuade them to leave Cang Gang at that time.
When it truly comes to blows, I wouldn't have the nerve to beg you all for mercy. But... but we're all just people trying to get by and feed our families.
...I promised the brothers of the Cang Gang that I would ensure they never lacked for food or clothing. In the end, I was unable to fulfill that promise; I couldn't even protect myself.
But don't forget the Cang Gang! The Shangguan Family cultivated the Cang Gang not just for profit, but specifically for today.

It's not hard to see that the Shangguan Family stands behind the Imperial Court. The Court still fears the power of the Wulin and dares not bare its blade openly, so the Shangguan Family Head — who withdrew from the Jianghu and now holds the post of Imperial Inspector — cannot intervene in the open either.
{size=24}Don't worry about me, I'm not that fragile.{/size}
Miss Ying, you...
As for the matter of the Shangguan Family, Lady Shangguan surely has something to say. Please, come over here.
Third Brother, may I say a few words?
As Third Senior Brother spoke, his gaze flicked toward Shangguan Ying.
As for the Shangguan Family...
Fourth Junior Brother speaks the truth!
They may not be helping directly, but they are doing a tremendous favor.
Conversely, the Nangong Family might also consider the code of conduct in the Jianghu and refrain from aiding either side.

The Nangong Family has always been called the peacemaker of the Jianghu, the very heart of the Wulin. Moreover, with Jiangling sitting in the heart of the Central Plains, asking them to side with the Western Wulin Alliance would be asking too much.

In recent years, the Jianghu has been in turmoil, with many people leaving. Not that they left because of conflict; rather, it's because the Nangong Family promoted peace. Didn't the Jianghu used to be too peaceful for too long? Perhaps this is the true face of the Jianghu after all?
Yes... just thinking about it makes one feel sad and regretful. Sigh. Such good people had to leave like this.
...We can't expect the Nangong Family to treat us the way they used to. Grandfather and Elder Nangong have both passed away.

Excluding the Six Great Sects, there's the matter of the Nangong and Shangguan Families' stance. The Nangong Family has been on good terms with our sect for generations, but their ties with other sects run just as deep — how they'll lean when the time comes is hard to say.
One can say that those guys think differently from most people.
It seems there's no persuading them to change their minds.
Ah, right. The Diancang Sect are all warlike fools. Always raving on about asking the Way through the sword, like a pack of freaks.
That's just crazy talk.

Brother Zhao's words are correct. The Diancang Sect pursues the way of the sword by seeking a long‑term enemy as an insurmountable barrier. The more difficult the checkpoint, the greater its value to overcome. Once the Western Wulin Alliance is formed, Diancang will only feel delighted at the prospect.
Now that we have formed the Western Wulin Alliance to stand against the Eastern Wulin Alliance, it seems we may have fulfilled the intentions of the Diancang Sect.
Previously, it was always the Nangong Family who mediated, otherwise the Diancang Sect would have long drawn their swords and attacked.
In my opinion, the Tang Clan and the Diancang Sect might be able to turn enemies into friends. However, a battle between them is inevitable.

At the Wulin Assembly, although they temporarily supported the Tang Clan, it was merely to prevent their arch‑enemy from being harmed by treachery. They wanted to defeat the Tang Clan in a fair and honorable manner.
Finally, there is Diancang. The long‑standing grudge between our sect and Diancang... is likely irreconcilable. A battle seems inevitable.
Alright, I get it. If there's no one else, will you let me try then?
Why are you looking at me like that~
Are you kidding? Of course I'm not willing‑that's a death sentence, you know~
Fourth Junior Brother, are you willing to go?
For example... me?

Junior Brother, with your eloquence, you would indeed be an excellent choice for an envoy to Qingcheng. However, there are many places where you might use your martial skills, so don't decide too early.
...Isn't that me then?
Thus the choice must be made with care‑someone eloquent, with a silver tongue, would serve best.
As you command. This is about all the help I can offer these days.
That makes sense! Then might I trouble Junior Sister to make the trip to Qingcheng on the sect's behalf.

I once practiced medicine in a clinic at the foot of Qingcheng Mountain, and made something of a name for myself. The local folk there owe me their goodwill‑I'd be far more persuasive going to speak with them than Junior Brother would.
So it's me‑

The Qingcheng Sect and our sect are neighbors, with frequent interactions between the disciples of both schools. However, times have changed, and they now bear a grudge against us. Without clearing up this misunderstanding, the question of forming an alliance is simply out of the question.
...Even so, persuading Qingcheng remains an exceedingly dangerous task.
Junior Sister Xiaomei is a wild one, all right‑a born troublemaker of the Tang Clan.
It's too optimistic, isn't it?
Besides, once it's out in the open, being hunted hardly matters. As long as A'Huo's alive and the Tang Clan doesn't throw me out, not even the Heavenly King can touch me‑hahaha!
...Eldest Senior Brother's passing, and I cannot escape my part in it. It was Xiaomei who brought harm to everyone; if I don't show real sincerity now, I'll never forgive myself.
Even so....
I might not say it, but the Wulin Alliance would still not leave us in peace with this commotion. The only way to gain Sect Leader Zou's trust is by doing so.
What... why are you so careless? While we know among ourselves, it's better not to say this to outsiders. If it gets out, do you still want to have a peaceful life?
Third Senior Brother, you know now what my original identity was. I also told Master Zou about the same thing.
Huh? Are you serious... can you really say that?
Third Senior Brother, Fourth Senior Brother‑ you both know what my original identity was. I also told the same thing to Master Zou.
Yes!
Xiaomei
Ah, why so formal, calling for me like that?
Xiaomei, may I ask you to come here for a moment.

This is not so easy to say. On our way to the Wulin Congress, we did have a brief encounter with Sect Leader Zou. He has already promised to thoroughly investigate this matter upon his return to the mountain. If Shentu Long still hopes to slip through, it may not be so simple.
In any case, with Shentu Long lodged in the heart of Qingcheng, it would be incredibly difficult to persuade Qingcheng to support us.
Fourth Senior Brother has been influenced by you and his moral standing has declined even further.
This has potential! I'm going to go through everyone's old debts with them and get my money back!
Wait, after Third Senior Brother paid the money, he felt at peace. Isn't this also a form of business deal?
My junior brother really acted like a thug, exploiting Third Senior Brother's sense of guilt. If I don't give it to him, he can't do anything to me anyway.
This... well, I don't have much personal savings either, so perhaps this can ease your mind a bit. Take it then.
How dare you doubt me... Pay up! Pay up!
It's fine as long as you don't blame me.
This matter is hard to believe, and it's only natural to doubt it.
Junior Brother, I unjustly doubted you; I apologize.
No, I believe you.
It's alright, I believe you.
Ah...
Junior Brother... have you forgotten? Master Fu Yun passed into nirvana right here in our sect.
Fu Yun of the Songshan Sect was also present that day and can testify for me.
If even Master Fu Yun says so, it must be true.

Amituofo. Benefactor Tang, this novice dares to interject for a moment. If it weren't for my own eyes witnessing this matter, I wouldn't dare to readily believe it either. What Benefactor Zhao said is true, and he has not uttered a single falsehood.
No, I believe you.
The Heroine Long Xiang from Jinxiang Palace was also present at the scene that day and had a brief encounter with Shentu Long, and can testify for me.
If even Heroine Long says so, it must be true.
Third Hero Tang! That Shentu Long is the prime culprit behind it all, and I saw it with my own eyes! I can testify to it!
Let alone Sect Leader Zou being unable to trust this easily — in truth, even I have my doubts. I suspect you were struck in the head by an enemy and, your wits addled, said such an incredible thing.
Reincarnation and body swapping are just fanciful notions. No matter how much we speak, how many people will truly believe in turning back the clock?

Qingcheng harbors remnants of the Supreme Bliss Cult, which are not only enemies of our sect but also a hidden threat to the Central Plains. However, Shentu Long, while not exuding an immortal aura, is still a young and handsome individual.
Junior Brother, calm down. Let's analyze the pros and cons first before proceeding.
I studied at Qingcheng, making me the ideal choice.
As for Qingcheng, what do you think?
There's no other way. I'll see about handing over my duties as Sect Leader and go to Emei myself.
Then I'd best keep this useful body of mine and serve the sect instead.
You crooked merchant, you'd get about the same treatment.
The Emei Sect is known for its fierce hatred of evil; that person will likely be beaten to death by a flurry of punches.
Junior Brother, that you'd offer speaks well of you — your Senior Brother is truly touched. But your reputation... I fear you might go and never return.
Then who do you plan to send? Me perhaps?
Hmm...
I don't mind going, but I'm afraid I'll be turned away at the gate and have made the trip for nothing.
Junior Brother's reputation... is neither particularly good nor bad. The Sect Leader of Emei might not take him seriously at all; it's uncertain whether he can even ascend to Mount Emei.
Then who do you plan to send? Me perhaps?
Haha! Exactly!
So, where is your Tang Clan disciple's pride? Tang Clan disciples should be shameless about their flaws and loud about their strengths, so the world has something to imitate!
Humility is a good thing, but you shouldn't be too humble and undervalue yourself.
Third Senior Brother, you flatter me. I don't have much to be proud of.
In my opinion, Junior Brother, you are quite suitable. Your life has been full of twists and turns, yet you have managed to stay on the right path, maintaining a sense of integrity.
This... I am the Acting Sect Leader, after all—can I really get away?
Isn't that you then?
Isn't that you then?

Emei's Sect Leader Xiang keeps himself well hidden, never one to contend with the world. At the Yueyang Wulin Assembly he outshone every rival, yet willingly cast aside fame and glory to put forward Nangong the Hero instead. This shows clearly how benevolent and righteous he is at heart—so whoever we send to persuade him should be a person of virtue above all.
Indeed, it would be more appropriate to regard Kongtong as an enemy.
Kongtong's Sect Leader, Jinwu Shangren, bears an unforgivable, mortal enmity toward our sect. Between that wretch and us it's a fight to the death—there's no possibility of reconciliation.
...Whether we should ask Fourth Junior Brother to handle this, let's discuss later.
Doing business, how can one not be greedy for profit? I made a lot of money, and they don't even know they've been cheated. Isn't that everyone being happy?
How could you say such a thing?
You didn't swindle them out of money, did you? I'd hate for there to be no trouble at all, only for you to go and get hunted down for your trouble.
There's no way around it; I can go and handle it. At the very least, I have a familiar face and can say a few words.
With Lady Shangguan in action, it's nine out of ten chances to succeed!
Is Lady Shangguan truly saying this? That would be wonderful indeed.

Third Brother, when the time comes I'll write a letter too, and have it sent along with yours. Mystic Skill Gate Leader Wei and I were classmates as children, the closest of friends. If I step forward to plead your case, she surely won't remain unmoved.
This is exactly what troubles me; if things go wrong, it will create enemies. Therefore, the selection of those sent to Kongtong cannot be taken lightly.

Jinwu Shangren is dead, and the position of Sect Leader remains vacant. The Four Gates of Kongtong still stand in opposition to each other. Although Daoist Law General and Mystic Skill Sect Leader Wei are friendly towards their respective sects, the intentions of the other Sect Leaders are unknown.
I never thought that studying at another sect at the time would lead to such good fortune. This is all thanks to Elder Nangong.
Kongtong's first lady is out, there's no reason for anything to fail! Everything is under control now!
Excellent!
I've already made the arrangements. The Kongtong Sect stands ready to send reinforcements at any time, awaiting the Sect Leader's command.
Don't judge me by this, but I am the First Palm School Lady of Kongtong.
...Kongtong, I'll go! I'll head back for a visit and call in reinforcements to build momentum.
Third Senior Brother‑there's no need to worry about Kongtong. Plum Blossom has long desired to show off Lady First Palm's might. Once I speak my piece, it will definitely go smoothly!

Next, let us discuss the support of the remaining four of the Six Great Sects. Qingcheng and Emei are located in the Shu region, so it is particularly important to secure their backing. Following them are Kongtong in the north and Diancang in the south.
That makes sense.

The Beggar Sect are nothing but spineless turncoats, each looking out for his own skin. Without a leader like Gang Leader Wang to give the orders, what good are they to anyone? Once our Western Wulin Alliance grows in strength, they'll all pull their heads into their shells.

The Beggar Sect is a mixed lot, all opportunists who shift with the wind, with nothing to their name but their own lives. Without a leader like Gang Leader Wang giving the orders, they're nothing to fear. Once the Western Wulin Alliance grows in power, not one of them will dare take the lead and throw his life away.
The bond you forged fighting over vegetables for hot pot is a kind of fate too. Let's hope old friends never come to blows.

The new and old factions of the Beggar Sect are still at odds; ever since Gang Leader Wang passed away, the new faction has been kept under their heel. We were able to form Eastern and Western Wulin Alliances—why can't the Beggar Sect split into Eastern and Western branches?
The Beggar Sect is a mixed lot, with no moral boundaries to speak of. Those like the Great Righteousness Branch who still adhere to principles are worth cultivating connections with.
Oh... That makes a lot of sense. For example, if the Tang Clan from Guangdong doesn't cause us trouble, the Sect Leader would turn a blind eye to it.

The new and old factions of the Beggar Sect are still in conflict; however, since Gang Leader Wang passed away, the new faction has been under greater pressure. We can form eastern and western Wulin Alliances; why cannot the Beggar Sect divide into eastern and western branches?
Not everyone in the Beggar Sect necessarily holds a grudge against our sect. The Great Righteousness Branch's bond with us was forged in battle—it's no ordinary friendship.
Good. At that time, I still need Young Hero Fan to exert yourself and mediate. Tang San thanks you in advance.
Could A'Hua be a dog's name? The name sounds too much like a dog, making people skeptical.
The Junior Sister was so enraged that her speech became crude again.

Third Master Tang! When it's time to attack the Beggar Sect, let me take the lead! Some of those old geezers should have died long ago; it's the sect rules that are getting in the way. I'm just holding back for now. Damn it, it's time to avenge Ahua! Just watch me beat those old bastards to death!
That kind would be terrifying even for someone with no extra flesh on them.
Slow slicing. I have too much flesh; it would take a while to die, just from cutting. Just thinking about it makes me feel queasy.
And what's number one?
Starve to death? No way! That's my second worst way to die!

Moreover, the greatest adversary might be the Beggar Sect. Not because of any other reason, but simply due to the sheer number of people. If we were to surround our sect as was done with Jiangling, and without support from officials, we would surely perish, being slowly starved to death.
Right, you didn't bring any baggage at all. You're... first!
Gang Leader, I arrived first for the Tang Clan, and I value honor more!

Sect Leader Tang, we-we-we-we can't lose on numbers either, the Beggar Sect won't fall behind! Let, let-let～let the new and old factions fight a while longer. Once the mud settles, the water clears. Then our Beggar-Beggar～Beggar Sect brothers will lend a hand too! The brothers of the Great Righteousness Branch are the most loyal of all!

You must understand, every Quanzhen disciple, young or old, carries a copy of the Quanzhen Sword Technique. It's no use in a one-on-one duel, but in a group battle, the Big Dipper Seven-Star Formation they form in groups of seven holds deep mysteries and is extremely hard to fight.
Exactly
Quanzhen sect followers are widespread in the Central Plains. In terms of numbers, they can rival the Beggar Sect, and we cannot afford to ignore them.
Not only do I intend to underestimate them, but I also plan to stab them to death.
Junior Brother, you also must not underestimate the Quanzhen disciples.
You really talk big
Although the Quanzhen sect has many followers, only a few are truly formidable. I would rather they were not intimidated and came down from Mount Zhongnan to compete with me.
Well, if that's the case, it naturally would be good. But it's better not to hold out hope, as they might still be oppressed by the Imperial Court.

The Quanzhen Sect once expressed support for the Tang Clan at the Wulin Assembly, so I believe Quanzhen is likely heeding the call of the Wulin Alliance for the sake of justice in the Wulin, rather than aligning with the Imperial Court. We call for unity in the Western Wulin, and the Quanzhen Sect should not strongly oppose this.
If that's the case, that would be great!

In summary, the Quanzhen sect's impression on me should be a good one. They follow the Wulin Alliance, likely for the sake of Wulin righteousness rather than aligning with the court. We are calling for unity among Western Wulin; the Quanzhen sect probably won't strongly oppose this.
I can. I love him just for being this foolish, this stubborn. A pretty pebble held in my palm—I wouldn't trade it for pearls.
Yes, I admire him, but in the end, I just can't do it.
Although he's quite ugly.
I started training later and never met the Eldest Senior Brother—I only know Brother Zhao. As long as Brother Zhao is around, I always believed things could be worked out.
I can't help but feel he's more of a role model than even the Eldest Senior Brother or the Senior Brothers.
This person is truly foolish; he won't take the good opportunities offered. He's so obstinate and unyielding. No wonder he's still an outsider disciple after all these years.
Oh
Junior Martial Sister, let's talk about business. Don't tease now.
Ow! Junior Martial Sister, why did you headbutt me?
Senior Brother, Senior Brother, Senior Brother!
Third Senior Brother...?
Haha! I'm even stronger than the old stains in the Training Ground!
I knew you'd say that. Our sect got stuck with you—we can't shake you off no matter how hard we try.
You have to wait until the wind passes and the sky clears before going abroad to study. Without the Tang Clan backing me up, who knows what kind of treatment I would get?
Of course, the world out there is far too wonderful—do you think I'm really planning to renounce it all and become a Daoist priest? It's just an exchange; I'll be going home eventually.
Did you go and come back?
Don't worry about it if you can't. Mount Zhongnan is so far away; going there and back would be quite a hassle.
Are you sure he'll still be willing to accept you as a disciple by then?
Once we've beaten the Wulin Alliance into silence, it won't be too late to go seek a master.
Of course I'm seizing it. Aren't we just busy right now?

Junior Brother... To become the closed-door disciple of Immortal Qiu is a blessing that countless people seek but cannot attain. You have such a tremendous opportunity; how can you not seize it properly?
Bet you didn't expect this, huh? Neither did I.
Hahahaha! Now you're all dying of envy, aren't you? Your day's finally come!
Hmph. Hmph. Hmph.
That's Immortal Qiu! Even my adoptive father admires him—he might just be the finest martial artist in the Wulin today!
What's going on? Why is everyone so surprised?
Hmph
Why are you speaking so cautiously, Third Senior Brother? It's not much of a secret—they say the old master just wants to take me as his closed-door disciple.
Immortal Qiu has summoned you to personally impart some heavenly secret—would Junior Brother be willing to share what it is?
First Under Heaven!
Quanzhen Grand Master Changchunzi.....!
It's not Daoist Yin who summoned me—it's Immortal Qiu.
Oh... I wonder what Daoist Yin has to teach you.
No, I remember Daoist Yin said I should go to the Quanzhen sect.
But where did I say anything wrong?
Then what else could it be? Daoist Yin is such a venerable elder of the Wulin—if he's summoned you, what could he want besides giving you a beating?
That's where you're wrong. How can you tell it was I who offended them?
What have you done this time? You can offend people even from as far away as Mount Zhongnan?
No, I recall that Daoist Yin said I should go to the Quanzhen Sect. It's all because of that mess at the Great Wulin Assembly; I momentarily forgot about it.
But where did I say anything wrong?
What is it? What are you 'ah'-ing about?
Ah

I thought that among the major forces in the Wulin Alliance, it was the Quanzhen sect that held the top position. With Senior Immortal Qiu, the First Person Under Heaven, residing there, it truly deserves to be called the first great sect of the Wulin.

The monks of the Songshan Sect are compassionate and would likely not be aggressive, given their historical friendship with us in resisting the Old Demon Cult. Even if they must go against the prevailing trend, they probably won't be overly pressing.

The monks of the Songshan Sect are all compassionate at heart, and we share a bond forged from once standing together against the Old Demon Cult. Alas, Dharma Master Fu Yun passed away from poison within the Tang Clan, and this bred ill will between us — whether that injustice can ever be cleared remains uncertain.

Among the Six Great Sects, Quanzhen and Songshan stand foremost. Though the sect itself lies enclosed within the territory of the Jin, its followers are scattered throughout the Central Plains — truly, one summons and a hundred answer.
Next, unavoidably, we will have to stand against Quanzhen, foremost among the Six Great Sects.
If the people of the Wulin refuse to lend their strength, the Imperial Court can fret all it likes — it will do them no good.
In that case, the other fickle individuals would also waver.

The Songshan Sect has long been revered as a paramount force in the Wulin. Although they have stepped back recently, they are still deeply respected by the people. If we stand idly by, the Wulin Alliance will not only lose a significant support but also face widespread doubt in our endeavors.
With the words of the master, I can rest assured.
Junior Brother Fu Yun speaks truly!

In sending us, his Songshan brothers, here, he has already shown his true heart. Even if Songshan is too far away to lend real strength to the Western Wulin Alliance, we would never be willing to serve as the imperial court's hounds!

I think the Venerable Abbot, being compassionate of heart, surely cannot bear to see the people of the Central Plains reduced to ashes and ruin, nor would he wish to see righteousness itself decay. Otherwise, what difference would it make who ruled the Central Plains?

Worthy Tang benefactors, please do not worry. This humble monk has already penned a letter, sent by carrier goose to report to the abbot. Though no reply has come as yet, this humble monk once heard the Venerable Abbot's teachings, and dares guess something of his mind.

Among the Six Great Sects, Quanzhen and Songshan stand foremost. Though the sect itself lies enclosed within the territory of the Jin, its followers are scattered throughout the Central Plains — truly, one summons and a hundred answer.
Exactly

The Western Wulin Alliance would need the support of several major sects to gain strength, and this is closely related to our faction's reputation. Otherwise, small and scattered sects dare not align themselves.
{size=50}The Tang Clan's flame burns on, from ancient times to this day!!{/size}

A true hero of the Jianghu is not bound by fame or fortune, but seeks only to live without shame before heaven or earth. Right and wrong lie within myself; my name I leave for you all to judge. I am not defiant or unruly — it is only that the flame of the Tang Clan burns on, from ancient times to this day!
I will quote the old words of our Sect Leaders: whether the Tang Clan flourished or declined, this we would always say──

We of the Tang family from Shuzhong stand tall between heaven and earth. For a century we have spread our branches here, true to our convictions — we curb the strong to aid the weak, root out tyranny to shelter the innocent. We have wronged no one, and no one shall drive us out!
Even if I have to die, I will smear mud on the faces of those self‑proclaimed carefree heroes! If I'm not doing well, no one else will have it easy! Bastards!

If someone bullies you to your face and you don't give them a taste of their own colors, what kind of good man are you? Even as a woman, I won't stand for being pushed around like that — otherwise what damned Jianghu is this! Others get all the glory — where's the justice in that?
Indeed! If your conscience is clear, then say the word — we'll all have ourselves one glorious fight, and this life will not have been wasted!
That's more like it! Third Senior Brother, you just have too many things on your mind to fly up high!

To kill over a word is to value righteousness above one's own life. Nothing is more valuable than righteousness! I wish to climb high and summon the bold adventurers of Jianghu, gather under the Western Wulin Alliance, and confront the Wulin Alliance. By no means should they dominate all with their single hand!
The old Sect Leader handed over the affairs of the Tang Clan to me not to make us into timid turtles.

──But I am too cowardly and fear death; I dare not run away either! Although fleeing might seem clever, it would not uphold the spirit of Tang Clan. If I flee, I will never straighten my back in this lifetime and would shame my ancestors of the Tang Clan!
Or we could flee with our tails between our legs, scattering to survive as we may — while the green hills remain, we need not fear for firewood.

Now the court intends to use the Wulin Alliance as a tool to eliminate their opponents and purge the Jianghu. The Mud Cult will be the first to fall, followed by the Tang Clan. If we do not submit, we will inevitably be destroyed by the Wulin Alliance at some point.
In the eyes of the officials, our deeds are too numerous to tally. Though we have not been branded rebels, it has always felt like a thorn lodged in the back.

As you all know, our sect upholds chivalry and righteousness. Save in times of dire calamity across the Central Plains, we have never banded into factions. Yet the poisons and hidden weapons we study are despised by those of the righteous path, and no few have found fault with us for it. We walk uprightly and sit upright, yet the world does not call us one of the Wulin's righteous sects.

Junior Martial Brothers and Sisters, disciples of the Tang Clan, gathered here to bear witness — I, Tang Sheng, in my capacity as acting Sect Leader, am about to declare a decision of the utmost importance.
Second-born of the Ye family, known as the First Demented Hand of Diancang. This was Ye Yunshang's secondary identity, adopted after committing a crime to shift responsibility away from herself.
Diancang's Fastest Swordsman, Cangsong Swordsman...?

Trained at the Fujian branch of the Songshan Sect, she was steeped in Buddhist teachings from childhood and picked up some martial arts for self-defense; her skill isn't especially high, but she has one extraordinary gift -- she is a prodigy able to push the Vexation Fist past its twelfth level of power. You'd best keep your wits about you and not provoke her temper. She was betrothed to the Young Lord of the Nangong family from childhood, and though she's tried her best to make the match work, the two have never gotten along. She was once dormmates with Wei Ju of the Kongtong Sect and counts her among her closest friends -- as children, she often paid Wei Ju to do her homework for her. Grown up, she returns the favor, visiting Kongtong now and then to bring her family's tribute tea as a gift. Both women hold the legendary Apricot Blossom Immortal in reverent awe.

One of the Wulin's three great clans, the Shangguan family has resided in Fuzhou for generations; she is their only daughter, a renowned beauty across the Wulin. Proud and strong-willed, though born to wealth and privilege, she refused to be raised in seclusion. At a young age she took over the Shangguan family's affairs on her father's behalf. Women can match men in capability; her sharp business acumen has made the vast estate flourish.

Led into the Wende Hall by the Apricot Blossom Immortal, Wei Ju finally realized that the court she had long admired was as murky as a quagmire. This group of high‑ranking officials, living in luxury and looking down from their lofty heights, were born without worries. They had the leisure to pursue elegance, and each of them was well‑versed in rhetoric, yet the suffering of the common people and the dire situations at the borders were merely subjects for their literary embellishments. The principles found in books had become superficial for the literati of the time; they were arrogant and dismissive, reciting verses about beauty while looking down on the common folk, lacking even the strength to bind a chicken, yet still proud of their so‑called integrity. Every soldier who died at the borders had their own sense of honor; everyone faces death, so why do the historical records only note the names of these ministers? Because the historians are also literati.   After traveling from Xiangyang to Lin'an Prefecture, Wei Ju wept bitterly and abandoned her thoughts of entering the court to serve as an official, vowing, In times of peace, I will sing and dance; in chaotic times, I will not compose poetry. I would rather be among the incapable in a well‑governed world than serve as a useful minister in a corrupt court. Even so, she often found it hard to resist the urge to write, managing to salvage her vow by ruining her verses just in time. She could gladly work in the fields alongside the honest villagers who were illiterate, but she held a deep disdain for those literati who, having read a little, prided themselves on their talent. That she could refrain from losing her temper was a testament to Wei Ju's exceptional self‑cultivation.

Once a daughter, the contemporary prodigy who dominated the top ranks, in Jinling City, everyone knew the name of Talented Woman Wei. Every day, countless scholars offered gifts, hoping to catch a glimpse of her; this talented woman, having read extensively, became proud and often challenged others with couplets, refusing to meet them. Like many literati, she held herself in high regard, with aspirations for the world. Thus, she bound her hair and took the imperial examination, achieving the highest honors and entering the palace to become a student of the emperor, dazzling the court with her remarkable talent and becoming the top scholar.  It was thought that even if she could not be appointed as an official like Lin Youyu, she would at least leave a name in history like Wu Zhiduan, proving her extraordinary abilities as Wei Zhaodi. However, the high‑ranking officials in the court had grown weary of these women taking the lead, each one too talented, making themselves appear incompetent. They exerted great effort to persuade the emperor to decree, This woman is both talented and beautiful; she should be matched with Commandant De, essentially arranging her marriage to a man who was merely a low‑ranking military officer. That man admired her reputation but was rejected by Talented Woman Wei due to his infamous history of abusing and causing the death of his wife. Now, having spent a fortune to curry favor with the higher‑ups, he finally brought her into his household.  On their wedding night, Talented Woman Wei wept bitterly, wishing to preserve her honor, but could not find a piece of white silk to hang herself with. After crying for a while, she noticed an unusual silence in the General's residence. Pushing open the door, she discovered that all thirty members of the household had hanged themselves. Wandering through the forest of corpses, the Apricot Blossom Immortal seemed to smile, beckoning her to join in a journey together.

Before the previous Sect Leader passed away, he specially summoned a distant relative from Gengyang Study Hall, renamed her Ju, and had her succeed him as Mystic Skill Gate Leader, while also naming her his Direct Disciple. Though she seems soft-spoken and always ready with a smile, she in fact manages her subordinates deftly.
