She now serves as the Kongtong Sect's archivist, overseeing everything from its most arcane texts down to household registers, livestock and expenditures -- with her in charge, the whole sect runs like clockwork. She never raises a hand in combat, yet commands deep respect throughout the sect. It's said her martial skill is so extraordinary that even the Flying Sect's unrivaled Fire Dragon Immortal Monarch, who rules unchallenged deep in the mountains, holds this young lady in wary regard.

Kongtong Sect. Mystic Skill Gate's contemporary Direct Disciple and also serves as the current sect leader. Dignified in manner, well‑versed and refined, gentle yet exceptionally elegant and distinct, a peculiar lady who stands out from the ordinary members of Kongtong Sect.

Her hazy dreams gradually took on a vivid form, resembling you. Even with poor eyesight, she would never mistake you for anyone else. She remembers your outline, your voice, the rhythm of your footsteps, and the faint scent of medicine mixed with the aura of iron and steel that surrounds you. In her eyes, you are unlike anyone else; finding a kindred spirit in life is a rare fortune. Although her eyesight is poor, she can see beyond the surface. Xiaozhu's feelings were not deeply analyzed; she simply let things unfold naturally. You can see her true heart, and she recognizes the real you. With shyness, she adorns herself for you, wearing that vibrant emerald outfit, which no one else has seen but you. Moreover, compared to being a blacksmith or forging swords, she actually prefers making toys. Now that she is of marriageable age, she still loves delicate dolls like Mohele Doll, but she is afraid of breaking them, so she dares not possess them.

Endless strength came from swallowing the spirit drug 'Iron-Scaled Black Python Blood' as a child, after being deceived by Xiaomei into doing so. A raging fever followed, leaving her eyesight much diminished; her body changed like a leopard's, and she stopped growing taller. Instead, even without practicing martial arts, her strength and weight kept increasing day by day‑if it went on like this, who could say she wouldn't one day grow strong enough to move mountains and overawe the world. Although Xiao Zhu acted nonchalant on the surface, she secretly harbored a faint hope for the future sect leader she had never met: hoping that he would be good; hoping that he would value her more than anyone else; hoping that his martial arts would be unparalleled, making her seem pitiful by comparison. With unrealistic fantasies in mind, this pining maiden continued to hone her skills day after day, preparing to contribute to her future husband's endeavors. Beneath the wardrobe, she cherished and carefully stored a vividly colored garment, one she hardly ever wore even during festivals, because of the old calluses and scars on both her hands that she did not wish others to see.

Because she was sold to Kongtong at a price of five thousand guan due to her father's gambling addiction, they valued her for her natural beauty and purity. They expected great things from her future. However, unbeknownst to them, this girl stopped growing taller unexpectedly, greatly disappointing the Iron Fist Gate elders. Xiao Zhu herself did not harbor any expectations of becoming the sect leader's wife. Yet, she could never get used to the contemptuous glances others cast at her. The more she felt inferior, the stronger she became.  In her heart, she envied the common folk's young misses for their slender and delicate beauty that won people's pity. Unfortunately, fate was not kind; this girl possessed boundless strange strength despite her seemingly frail frame, lacking any good fortune but with a body weight far from ordinary. The only thing to be grateful for was that the old sect leader, who had purchased her as an apprentice, left her his Great Ironworks before passing away. From then on, Xiao Zhu handled all aspects of woodworking and ironwork in the mountain, sometimes casting farming tools, sometimes forging weapons. In idle moments, she would tinker with mechanical tricks, immersing herself fully whenever inspiration struck, finding contentment even if she could not become the sect leader's wife.  Her dream was to be like Lu Ban or Ou Yezi, a peerless master craftsman of the world.

Due to poor eyesight, she frequently squints when looking at people, giving off a menacing glare that left a bad impression on everyone. In reality, she is a pure and kind‑hearted girl. As the contemporary Direct Disciple of Iron Fist Gate, she has the right to compete for the position of future sect leader's wife, and should be highly respected. However, in reality, no one takes this scowling short‑statured person seriously. The Iron Fist Gate seems to have given up on her struggles, allowing her to stay in the Great Ironworks, hammering away without resembling a refined lady. Although the iron mallet she often uses is just a common tool, a pair of unremarkable‑looking gloves are worth their weight in treasure‑crafted from the legendary Black Silk of Tianshan, resistant to water and fire, and impervious to blades and spears.

The contemporary direct disciple of the Iron Fist Gate of the Kongtong Sect is a petite young woman in green with a fierce gaze. Renowned for her exceptional blacksmithing skills, it is said that she possesses immense strength, capable of crushing the bones of others with her bare hands. Thus, she is known in the Jianghu as the Bone-Cracking Demon.

By now, she could no longer take her eyes off you. Witnessing your growth and strength, seeing you become more resilient, filled her with greater pride than any personal achievements of hers. She wished to see you achieve even more and watch from the sidelines as you reached new heights. Even without the master‑disciple relationship, she could consider herself your friend or, if that suited you, offer herself as a reward for becoming your wife. You surpassing her like indigo outshining blue ‑ Xiahou Lan would boast about being your master and the one you hold dear to your heart. You are the reason she yearns to be human.

You are the last person in the world who knows her original name‑Xiahou Mei. After being brought to the Kongtong Sect, her parents' chosen name was usurped, and under her master's orders, she was renamed Xiahou Lan. Later, she received direct teachings from the sect leader, mastering both the Soul-Stealing technique and the Yin-Yang Internal Skill of the two families from Snow Mountain, achieving a level of skill that makes her the foremost expert of her time in Kongtong, just one step away from a transcendent realm. Your presence has filled the last void in her heart, after all, she has never taken on a disciple. What started as a joke became increasingly serious, and she couldn't help but find it incredible; she has no patience for others, yet your clumsiness and foolishness can make her smile. Even your appearance evokes her pity, fearing that if you were to live alone in this world, you would suffer greatly. Should she cherish the time and impart all her knowledge to ensure you are not bullied, or should she take you with her when she departs from this world...?

Xiahou Lan is a survivor of the Snow Mountain Sect, whose family was annihilated. Even before her birth, she had an engagement to marry from the Shangguan Family. Her parents wanted their child to be born in a warm place, far from this harsh land, to grow up without worry. Now, all that has become nothing but a dream. She has walked through rain and frost, seen the warmth and cold of human nature, bravely stood against powerful authorities she could not fight, and battled enemies she could not overcome. She deeply loved someone, only to have her heart scarred. Desires unfulfilled, what little she had clung to slipping away. Xiahou Lan's story has come to an end. Whatever happens in the future, meeting you will be nothing more than a tasteless afterthought.

With a stunning appearance and exceptional martial skills, she captivated many young heroes and was once the most promising candidate to become the first Lady of the Kongtong sect. Unfortunately, a tragedy years past rewrote this young woman's life. Since that day she has seemed like a lost soul, never smiling again, her gaze wandering nowhere in particular. Even on sunny days she carries an umbrella, as if in her eyes the rain has never once let up.

Kongtong Sect·Soul‑Stealing Gate's contemporary Direct Disciple is known in the Jianghu as Soul‑Stealing Orchid. She is notorious for her vicious and perverse ways, residing in the Soul‑Stealing Forest, where none should enter.

Whenever you appear nearby, Xiaomei experiences a contradictory flutter of love and hate in her heart. She wishes to stab you several times but ultimately cannot bear to do so; she complains about how ugly you are but still can't put you down. After all, at least you have an unsightly appearance; unlike others who all look the same, dull and uninteresting, making it hard to tell one from another. Although she hides her attachment well, Xiaomei's obsession with you has almost become a pathological fixation. If you were to be disloyal and take multiple wives or concubines, she would smile and agree, then find an opportunity to push you down the stairs, leaving you half‑dead and half‑alive, subjecting you to a mind‑entrancing confinement that would leave you unable to go anywhere, relying solely on her for the rest of your life. But if you were faithful and innocent, she would gladly sacrifice her life for you. Your distant gaze is her future, no matter how far away it may be; she will see it through with you, being both a lifelong friend and a companion.

Even her pitiful background was a fabrication, merely a deliberate creation to win the trust of the Kongtong Sect. Her true identity was that of a cold‑blooded assassin carefully cultivated by the mysterious organization 'Thousand Lantern Tower,' a candidate for the new Thousand-Faced Demon, skilled in disguise, poison techniques, cunning schemes, and rhetoric. She secretly sowed discord among the Four Gates of Kongtong, luring countless talented men from Kongtong with her beauty to kill them, waiting only for the right moment to destroy the vast Kongtong under her own hand, thereby claiming merit and inheriting the name of Thousand-Faced Demon. All this, too, was mere pretense‑a smokescreen laid to win the trust of her watcher, the Soul-Hooking Elder, and trick him out of the antidote to the Corpse-Heart Gu. Deep within Xiaomei's heart, hatred was directed solely at the master of Thousand Lantern Tower; her heart held no love, and she merely lingered on life to kill one person.

It is said that Xiaomei's birth mother was a demoness of the Supreme Bliss Cult. After she escaped that cult's clutches, her mother married and bore a daughter, content with a modest, quiet life — but the good times didn't last. The Fire Dragon Immortal Monarch, styling himself a scourge of evil, cruelly tore the family apart and forced the orphaned Yu girl into becoming his disciple, renaming her Xiaomei. He groomed her with care, hoping to secure her the position of the sect's first lady and so cement his own power. So while Xiaomei looks innocent and carefree on the surface, she in fact harbors deep hatred for the Kongtong Sect, and behind her smiles she is forever pulling strings to steer events toward ruin, as her revenge. She has even secretly taught the sect's secret manual, the Immortal Crane's Elusive Fist, to Fire Lightning, forcing the bird to learn martial arts with no regard for its feelings at all — utterly unreasonable of her.

Dressed in a red robe and white dress, she resembled a plum blossom in the snow, exuding an elegant and transcendent beauty. Despite her youth, her position was high; she was more precious than even the Eldest Disciple of Flying Heaven Gate, ranking only behind the Four Sect Leaders. Even so, she showed no hint of arrogance. She frequently roamed around Mount Kongtong every day, enthusiastically helping others, lively and cheerful, loving to joke and make friends. She kept a tame crane named Fire Lightning. Among the Kongtong Four Maidens, she had the highest reputation; it seemed inevitable that she would marry into the Kongtong Sect Leader's family as their Lady in due time.

Kongtong Sect · Flying Heaven Gate's contemporary Direct Disciple was a lively and cheerful young woman, innocent and carefree. Though she had an unremarkable reputation in the Jianghu, among Kongtong Sect's four main gates' Direct Disciples, she received the highest support for the position of First Lady, with her succession as such a certainty.

Throughout the Jianghu, no one has endured more of her vicious beatings than you. No matter how she beats you, she never gives up — and the more she beats you, the harder she finds it to stop. She grew weary of young heroes who were all handsome faces and fine silks, flaunting their dashing airs, and came instead to love your unbending spirit. 'My beloved is the greatest hero under heaven, a true paragon, iron-boned and unyielding, standing firm between heaven and earth' — so she declared, echoing words her father once used. Long Xiang blushed for three days afterward, and would draw her sword on you the instant she saw you again. Yet she cannot do without your care, and in the end she always swallows her shame and returns to your side. Now and then she tries to rise to a wife's proper duties — and tears your robes while mending them, or burns the house down while cooking. You'd best not pin your hopes on this one.

In practical combat, she gradually grew skilled, able to wield her swordsmanship with composure and at will, becoming a renowned heroine, beautiful as a flower, and drawing a steady stream of suitors. Long Xiang, experiencing the stirrings of love for the first time, couldn't help but feel secretly delighted. Yet clumsy and unschooled in matters of the heart, she hid her embarrassment by making friends through martial arts, speaking her heart through the sword. As a result, suitor after suitor fell beneath her blade and slunk away in disgrace; even her kind words of consolation could not soften the blow, and it was no surprise that some proud souls sheathed their swords and retired from the world. Over time she grew indifferent to it all, striking hard at anyone who came courting, the harder the better to see their true character. After all, men of the Jianghu prized their pride above all‑who could stand being bested by such a fierce woman? Skilled as she was in martial arts, her daily life was a shambles; left to her own devices, she was quite capable of coming to grief.

Her memories of her father have grown quite faint now. In one distant memory, he patted her little head, smiled, and walked out the door — and never came back. Later, Lady Wen of Jinxiang Palace took her in and brought her into the household. Only through scattered rumors did she learn her father had been a legend of the Wulin — she felt sorrow and pride at once. Following in his footsteps, she visits old acquaintances, hoping to gather more stories of her late father to hold his memory by. All her swordsmanship comes down from a family secret manual; among Long Yuan's Seven Absolutes, she excels above all at the sword. As a child she practiced with a chicken leg for a blade, and without ever meaning to, grasped the deeper truth of man and sword as one — even now she isn't quite sure whether she counts as a master. But however high her skill, she still gets lost, gets swindled, and faints from hunger by the roadside — and somehow survives it all. Her luck really is something else.

Trained at Jinxiang Palace, an exquisite beauty whose swordsmanship is peerless. She walks the road her father once walked, hoping to carry on his ideals and roam the four corners of the world as a champion of justice. Yet for all that, her innocence about worldly affairs makes her surprisingly easy to deceive.

Trained under Jinxiang Palace, an elegant beauty with exquisite swordsmanship. Walking in her father's footsteps, she yearns to fulfill his aspirations by roaming the four quarters as a wanderer of justice. Yet for all that, her innocence of worldly affairs makes her surprisingly easy to deceive.

On the day her family was destroyed and she lost everything, the young Yunshang was struck by a Wulin master sent by the Imperial Court. Her dantian shattered, her meridians severed; it seemed she could not survive. Later, after enduring countless hardships, she barely managed to preserve her life, entering the Diancang sect as an apprentice. Though she appeared innocent and carefree, she was always wary and cautious, even of the master who saved her life. It wasn't until you and Moling appeared that things changed. She bitterly regretted that, being a woman, she could never hope to marry Moling in this lifetime. But at least she could settle for second best‑marrying you. Although you are ugly, she would have preferred death rather than consent to such a union; who knew that you were so determined and persistent, chasing her even into hell? Having been treated with such care and affection, can anyone in the world remain untouched by such devotion? In any case, she could not accept it.

She carries a significant secret. The ancestor of the Ye siblings was one of the capable generals under Yue Yun, the son of the renowned anti‑Jin general, King Wumu. It is said that Emperor Gaozong issued the Twelve Golden Plaques in a row, but Yue Fei, loyal and righteous, willingly met his death, lamenting that the great cause against the Jin had not been completed. If military power were to be seized by treacherous individuals, the Great Song would be powerless to turn the tide. Therefore, the main force of the Yue Family army was dispersed, and treasures were hidden in the mountains. Iron Military Tokens were cast and entrusted to the eldest son, Yue Yun, in hopes that in the future, they could use the tokens to command the old troops and continue the mission of protecting the nation. Unexpectedly, Yue Yun died before his father, and in a moment of crisis, he entrusted the Iron Military Tokens to a subordinate, instructing them to hide in Jianghu and wait for the descendants of King Wumu to come for them. That subordinate then concealed their identity, living in seclusion in the mountains, and has since guarded the Iron Military Tokens through generations. When chaos erupted in Baifeng Cave, the Ye family was implicated and suffered the wrath of the current emperor, leading to a tragic massacre of their clan, leaving the Ye siblings orphaned.

She never knew why she came down the mountain with her elder brother, only to be seized by men sent by Diancang Mountain. No shortage of people in the Jianghu coveted her besides, so she had no choice but to keep to hiding. Rather than live out carefree, worry-free days, she chose to wander the world as she pleased instead. The journey was hard, and it left her falling ill with fever more and more often; whenever her mind grew hazy, she needed only to clutch her brother's robe to fall peacefully asleep. "As long as I have my brother, I don't need anything else. To go on like this, relying on each other, just like before..."

Ye Yunzhou's fraternal sister, the sickly beauty Iseeandlament. Born weak, she often falls ill and lies in bed with fevers, but fortunately her nature is optimistic, so she does not take it to heart much. She loves to act coy, and the people of Diancang both above and below adore her, calling her a bringer of wind and rain. Although she practices the Diancang Internal Method under her brother's urging, limited by her constitution, even if she memorizes it perfectly, she makes little progress; even walking a bit faster would make her catch her breath, let alone wielding Blades or sabers. She has no special hobbies, but she is full of curiosity about the world below. She detests hardship and medicine; force‑feeding her only results in vomiting, after which she grins sardonically to mock others.

Ye Yunzhou's younger sister. Even in the sweltering summer, she never parted with her fox-fur cloak. Though she was a mischievous and playful beautiful girl, she would always fall ill after half a day of causing trouble.
Ruixing
Ruixing

Originally, he was more rebellious and unyielding, with a touch of recklessness. He believed his sword techniques had reached perfection; in the entire world, there was no one who could match him. Eager to make a name for himself, he was about to venture out from the mountains when his cousin called him to the Apricot Blossom Forest of Nanyang. There, he was confined for three whole months using a Qimen Formation. He cried out to heaven and earth but no one answered; even trying to escape by flying or digging underground did not work, as he was trapped under Apricot Blossom Immortal's Five-Finger Mountain. After being released, he had lost several pounds and became humble and kind. At the same time, he understood that she was a dangerous person he could not interfere with. He was also ordered not to entice Wei Ju, which made him feel very wronged.

At a young age, he somehow came to possess an extraordinary level of martial skill. He claims to hail from the Guyun Mountain Sect, though no one has ever heard of this obscure little school. Full of dreams of the Jianghu, he carries a sword and wanders far and wide, meddling in other people's business and standing up for the wronged. Modest in his ways yet deeply loyal, he's well-liked everywhere and has made friends in every faction. Since coming down from the mountain, no shortage of young women have fallen for him at first sight, but the ones he himself cares for are never easy conquests, leaving him no end of frustration.

A young swordsman making his debut. Handsome and elegant, a straightforward gentleman, he conducts himself with worldliness yet harbors boundless heroism within. Wielding his sword to right wrongs and settle grievances, he always appears at critical moments.

One of Rui Sheng's beautiful confidantes, the Holy Maiden of the Miaojiang Witch Spirit Cult. While she was still in her mother's womb, the tribe's witch had already named her the dragon's bride. Rui Sheng and a handful of friends ventured into Miaojiang, broke through the Five Immortals Array, and cut down a giant serpent with his sword, exposing the scheme of Golden Toad Lady and Silver Snake Young Lord -- a welcome tale of the hero saving the beauty. She spends her days sparring in jealousy with his other beautiful confidantes, but for all her sharp tongue, she's soft at heart, and in the end could never bring herself to use Gu to harm a rival, leaving her to nurse her own quiet misery for life.

One of Rui Sheng's beautiful confidantes, the Holy Maiden of the Witch Spirit Cult of Miaojiang. Even while still in her mother's womb, she was foretold by the clan's witch to be the wife of a dragon. Rui Sheng, along with a few close friends, ventured into Miaojiang, broke through the Five Immortals Array, wielded his sword to slay a giant serpent, and uncovered the schemes of the Golden Toad Lady and the Silver Serpent Young Lord, in a heroic rescue of the damsel in distress.

Before his father joined the Beggar Sect, he had held official rank and position. He only had one son, Li Fugui, whom he doted on immensely. Li Fugui was uneducated but showed no lack of mischief; by the age of five, he would even pull up a girl's skirt. Later, after Thousand-Gold Elder disbursed his family wealth and joined the Beggar Sect, Li Fugui remained arrogant and willful, relying on his father's influence to act with impunity. It wasn't until Wang Erzhuang took over from Thousand-Gold Elder and became the Gang Leader that there was no one to shield Li Fugui. Only then did he begin to rein in his arrogance, changing his name and acknowledging Wang Erzhuang as his father, with the intention of assassinating him. Unbeknownst to Li Fugui, Wang Erzhuang had been watching all this carefully. He believed that such a boy could endure hardships and was worth training. However, Li Fugui couldn't hold back for long; he attempted the assassination on the same night he became his father's son, but of course, the attempt failed miserably. The punishment was inevitable, but it wasn't physical abuse or execution; instead, Wang Erzhuang forced him to study and train in martial arts, tormenting both his mind and body.

A new rising star in the Beggar Sect, despite being a beggar, he was named Fugui. Being both an orphan of Thousand-Gold Elder from the old faction and an adopted son of Wang Erzhuang, the Gang Leader of the new faction of the Beggar Sect, he stutters when speaking, yet isn't unintelligent.

Xie Wuchen, though a member of the righteous sects, is competitive and eager for a fight; whenever a famous master appears, he can't resist picking a challenge, and it's cost him more than a few defeats. His signature technique, the Wind-Thunder God Kick, fuses his family's Wind God Steps with Emei's supreme Thunder God Kick -- unleashed, it lets him kick while borrowing his opponent's own force, and a kick thrown in mid-air can be lethal. As for the nickname 'Wind God,' he paid five taels of silver to have someone spread it around -- how else would he have gotten such an impressive title?

The contemporary famous young master of the Emei Sect, known as the Wind God, is renowned in the Jianghu alongside the Tang Clan Flying Hero, Tang Buyi. This Emei master excels in leg techniques and claims to be a formidable rival to your Eldest Senior Brother. He is quite bothersome, often getting into fights upon meeting, but there are also tales of them adventuring together in the Jianghu.

He once caught a young girl who had been locked in a cellar to be used as someone's plaything, and who, in her escape, killed her captor to save herself. Out of pity, he let the innocent girl go free — but his brother's political rivals seized on this and reported him to the Court of Judicial Review. Song Bei argued sternly: "The penal code has stood for two hundred years, but the customs of the people have shifted; it is wrong to cling blindly to old rules. Besides, the law was written by our forebears, who, however high they sat in the halls of power, could not have known every hardship of the common people, and so must have left gaps — gaps that, followed blindly, would only harm the realm. Where the law falls short of reason, I have shown mercy, and my conscience is clear." Yet his defense failed: Song Bei was stripped of half a year's salary and confined to his residence. Fortunately his brother Song Ci worked on his behalf at court, and with the people's own petitions besides, the Court of Judicial Review at last rescinded the sentence and granted him a special pardon.

Though only a Seventh-Rank Security Officer by rank, the added title of Imperial Swordbearer means not even a first-rank official can insult him as he pleases -- he is, after all, the emperor's blade, and he wears that pride openly. Save for the Son of Heaven himself, he bows to no one and grovels before none, both because the court expects it of him and because he earned that nerve the hard way, out in the Jianghu. Uncover a corrupt official and he'll arrest a prince without blinking; yet he's no less full of human feeling -- he can recite the Song Code word for word, but when the law offers no mercy for a case that deserves some, he's often willing to look the other way, or to plead for leniency.

Divine Constable of the Great Song, granted with the Imperial Silver Fish Bag and the title of Swordbearer to the Emperor. Acting as the chief commander for all law enforcement across the land, they have the authority to apprehend suspects beyond the state borders. Roaming through the Jianghu, they are considered somewhat part of the Wulin.

It was common for female admirers to feign being tormented by demons in order to catch a glimpse of his handsome face, pretending to seek his magical help at Qingcheng. Shentu Long, fully aware that it was a ruse, never exposed their deception out of consideration for their feelings. The Daoist priests of Qingcheng took it upon themselves to exorcise demons and eliminate evil, but Shentu Long did not believe in the existence of such creatures. If there were truly anything in the world that could be deemed evil, it would be humanity itself.

Qingcheng Daoist Yichen Shentu Long was a Daoist cultivator from the Qingcheng Sect. Although young in years, his seniority was high as he was a closed-door disciple of the former Sect Leader of Qingcheng. He had a clear and handsome face, and was easy‑going and refined. When not practicing daoist techniques, he often roamed around the mountains, paying little attention to Jianghu matters. He rarely quarreled with others; his martial arts were only displayed during the monthly examinations at Qingcheng Sect. Despite this, his reputation still spread quietly.

He was straightforward, honest, and single-minded in his pursuit of immortality, following the Fire Dragon Immortal Monarch in cultivation, and deeply ashamed that after all his years of training he still could not breathe fire. Though he never mastered the immortal arts, he was in truth a man of great fortune: by pure chance he learned the Wind Blade and Fire Sword, which stirred his master's envy. So his master told him that to break through to the Mahayana stage he needed to accumulate merit, and that the fastest way to earn merit was to go fight for the nation -- and with that excuse, sent him off to the Song-Jin battlefield to die. Yet he lived on at the front and never died; instead he won the deep trust of officers and soldiers alike, earning the title 'General of the Dao,' with a record of victories so distinguished that even old General Zhao Fang, the defender of Xiangyang, showed him extraordinary respect.

Kongtong Sect · Flying Heaven Gate Sect Leader Fire Dragon Immortal Monarch's senior disciple. Also known as the famed 'Way of Dao Military General' on the Xiangyang battlefield, undefeated in a hundred battles, revered by Song people and civilians, feared by Jin troops.

Wang Chunxiao, whose ancestral lineage consisted of military officials, benefited from their legacy and was granted the title of Commandant Dingyuan. However, he was cultured and refined, preferring poetry and chess over martial arts. Although he had read military texts, the thought of going to battle to defend his homeland made him tremble. It wasn't until he met Nangong Yuan and encountered Su Yingxiang that he reluctantly ventured into the Jianghu to win the favor of the beauty. In every aspect, he excelled beyond Nangong Yuan, but in Su Yingxiang's eyes, she only favored Nangong Yuan. This left Wang Chunxiao heartbroken, weeping and despondent, even running to Donglin Temple in tears, contemplating shaving his head to become a monk. It was there that he encountered an opportunity that would change his life. He became a disciple of Master Chunmian, intending to learn Buddhism, but Master Chunmian insisted on forcing him to practice martial arts. It was only much later that Wang Chunxiao learned that his master was the renowned Red Peng King, the Martial Overlord of the Eastern Thirteen States.

His gaze is lazy, tinged with defeat and gloom, and his one passion is fishing. He claims not to care for drink, yet he's often blind drunk. Wang Erzhuang was the linchpin in the Beggar Sect's turn from darkness to light -- since taking command, he has championed chivalry with all his might, rekindling the light in young Beggar Sect disciples' eyes and convincing them that even mired in filth, one can still rise unstained. So long as one's heart holds to chivalry, even rags can be worn with pride -- after all, aren't the most incorrupt officials the ones with empty sleeves? The new faction has risen and swept away the sect's old vices; everything it does is now open and above-board, with no more petty thievery, only a hunger to right wrongs. The old faction, still strong in numbers, sneers that the new lot are neither one thing nor another -- mere beggars putting on airs of nobility -- even as they bask in the good name the new faction has earned.

The Gang Leader of the Beggar Sect, the number one sect in the world, took office with decisive action, promoting new disciples while sidelining the old-school elders. He used the spirit of chivalry to deceive the sect's members into reclaiming their dignity, making them believe that being a beggar was a choice.

Gifted with sharp intellect and Mouth Power, he frequently traversed between Emei and Kongtong, promoting Buddhism while soliciting donations to construct temples on Songshan. He treated good people with respect but was stern with those who were obstinate. His attitude toward you depended on your character; he would inevitably chatter, though the difference lay in whether his words irritated you or not.
The young disciple of the Songshan Sect traveled throughout Great Song to propagate Buddhism and raise funds for the restoration of the dilapidated Songshan Temple.

In their youth, they had successively taken Ma Yu and Liu Chuxuan as teachers, but were caught by their parents and locked in the woodshed. Seeing their urgent desire to seek the Dao, their family finally let them go.

Quanzhen Qinghezi Yin Zhiping was the favored disciple of Qiu Chuji, the Quanzhen Sect's 'First Under Heaven.' During his revered teacher's travels, Yin Zhiping managed Mount Zhongnan's Longmen Temple and there were whispers that he might succeed to the position of Grand Master in the near future.

The moment Nangong Qian laid eyes on the grand five‑court residence of the Nangong family, his eyes sparkled. The clothes these people wore were so fine; some even had gold threads on them. It seemed that princes and young lords were no different. His father was more dashing and formidable than he imagined, someone even officials would greet respectfully. His brother was well‑versed and courteous; during their first meeting, he even offered Qian a sweet treat. He actually became part of their family, thinking good times were ahead. However, it wasn't like that at all. The patriarch treated everyone kindly except for him and his mother, whose disdain was obvious to everyone. As a result, the family members and servants grew increasingly contemptuous. After his mother passed away, no one protected him anymore, and he declined day by day, even being bullied by mere servants. Although living in the Nangong family wasn't worried about food or clothing, the Nangong household didn't even worry about feeding their dogs. The carefree child of old now walked with a timid gait, constantly reading people's expressions to get through each day.

In his earliest memories, he was with his mother alone. Back then he knew nothing of poverty; life was simple and good. He was good-looking, lively, clever, and kind-hearted -- everyone loved him, and the children of the village all wanted to play with him. He wasn't called Nangong Qian back then; he seems to have had another childhood name, though he can no longer recall it. One day he came home covered head to toe in mud and asked his mother, out of curiosity, 'Why don't I have a father? Where did my father go?' That was the moment his happy childhood came to an abrupt end.

An illegitimate son of the Nangong family, born of a concubine. His birth was not what people had hoped for, and his mother was deeply loathed by Nangong Yuan. As a result, even Nangong Qian was not favored; though he is the second young lord, his treatment at home is no better than that of the servants.

Inspired by the story of the Hegemon-King of Chu ending his life by suicide at the Wu River, he took it as a warning and believed that mere martial arts were not enough to achieve anything. He asked, Has there ever been an emperor who relied solely on his own combat skills? Those who rely on brute strength are merely wasting their lives. Therefore, with all these matters, he only dabbled superficially. The Great Prince excelled in the Four Arts‑calligraphy, music, chess, and painting‑but did not pursue them deeply. His attitude toward learning was simply to get by, relying on his eloquence to cover up any shortcomings. He believed that his true challenge lay in knowing people well and making good use of their talents, mobilizing the strongest warriors and the most learned scholars. Although he possessed some talent and strategy, he could not escape the habits of a pampered young lord‑greedy for pleasure and fond of beauties. Together with three or five friends, he was known as one of the Four Young Lords of Flower City, frequenting brothels and courtesan quarters. If Shangguan Ying did not have a thin skin but a hard punch, they might have had problems even before their wedding.

Grown up hearing and seeing the ways of the world, and being both intelligent and quick‑witted, they adeptly utilized family assets and connections. They learned martial arts directly from the Family Head and practiced calligraphy under guidance from a master. Their lifestyle was as luxurious as that of the nobility in Lin'an, despite lacking official titles or honors. Considering themselves above others, they often displayed a certain level of worldliness in their dealings. They had an engagement with Shangguan Ying, the only daughter of Shangguan Family, but their meetings were either arguments or physical confrontations.

The Nangong Family's legitimate Eldest Young Lord. He bears all the attention upon himself as the heir, continuing his family's legacy with a scholarly and graceful demeanor. Skilled in all four arts, he is not only widely known among the people of the Jianghu but also has connections within the circle of literati and refined scholars.

All began with a misunderstanding, yet the mistake proved grave and none was willing to back down. In the end, it was you who stepped in, turning swords into plowshares and broken mirrors back together, making all past grievances as fleeting clouds. Although Shi Gongyuan has now washed his hands of Tang Clan's affairs, retired with his beloved wife from Jianghu, he still harbors a debt to their family. Secretly vowing that should the Tang Clan ever face difficulties in the future, he cannot watch idly.

With the support of his virtuous wife, Shi Gongyuan gathered former bandits and started anew, founding the Flying Stone Gang. They specialized in renting out labor for heavy manual work and miscellaneous tasks, engaging in outsourcing businesses. While they did not discriminate in recruiting people based on their character, they strictly adhered to the gang rules, ensuring that none of them disturbed the peace or livelihood of the common folk. Shi Gongyuan himself underwent a transformation, becoming a righteous and benevolent person. The Flying Stone Gang rose to prominence rapidly, achieving hundreds of members within less than twenty years and being able to challenge the Three Great Gangs in the Jianghu.

After the Magistrate's daughter became the wife of the bandit leader, Shi Gongyuan's carefree life came to an end. No one knew that the delicate young lady was actually a fierce tigress, more formidable than the burly man himself. The poor bandit leader found himself under strict control of his wife. Under her gentle persuasion, he went to the yamen to plead for forgiveness, facing imprisonment and torture, believing he would surely die this time. However, it was his young wife who interceded and secured his release. The Magistrate brought him into the inner hall, pardoned his past crimes, and ordered him to bow down, finally acknowledging him as a son‑in‑law.

Shi Gongyuan, in his youth, had once joined the military, serving as a minor soldier under General Bi Zaiyu. Later, he deserted and took refuge in Mount Maoshi in Maozhou, becoming a mountain bandit. Shi Gongyuan lacked grand ambitions; he lived day by day, drinking and eating with his companions. He drunkenly lived life to the fullest, viewing violence as courage. His external skills were well‑developed, making him strong and muscular. This only made him more unrestrained. He even brazenly kidnapped a newly appointed magistrate during his walk and forcibly married the magistrate's daughter as his primary wife.

The Flying Stone Gang Leader was a robust and daring hero. Initially, he was a bandit operating in Maozhou. After getting married, he retired from that violent life, ceasing to disrupt the people's lives. Instead, he rented out manpower to handle rough work, and the Flying Stone Gang's reputation gradually spread far and wide, becoming a force that could challenge the Three Great Gangs.

That battle left the Songshan monastery greatly weakened. The Abbot's Power was exhausted, without attachment, yet his faith in Buddhism grew stronger. His fellow monks were inspired by his dedication and returned to their original aspirations, abandoning martial arts and other minor skills for profound Buddhist teachings. Only he remained, restless from the lingering warmth of that battle. Unwilling to let go of his attachments, he resolutely stepped down as abbot and traveled far to the Mud Cult headquarters in Six Paths Canyon, where he sat alongside Heavenly King Che Xuanyuan to debate and spar with him. Surprisingly, this lifelong Buddhist found himself unable to dissuade a mortal, instead being enlightened by this ordinary person's insights into his own biases. Sitting for several days, he finally decided to return to secular life, though regretting that his hair was already balding in large patches. He recalled 'The Tale of the Curly-Bearded Guest' he had read long ago and wove a cloak from eagle feathers collected over many years. The new martial artist Wanli Pengcheng began wandering Jianghu, completing his youthful journey.

Many years ago, someone slipped a legendary novel, 'The Tale of the Curly-Bearded Guest,' into the Scripture Repository. The young monk Juekong stumbled upon it by chance and was deeply moved. He longed for the bold spirit depicted in the book and became obsessed with martial arts. Unfortunately, he had been ordained at Shaolin Temple since his youth and knew nothing about worldly affairs. All that he heard and witnessed were doctrines of abstaining from killing and distancing oneself from greed, anger, and delusion. Even if he wanted to venture into the world for a tour, it would be difficult for him to surpass himself. At such times of restlessness, he could only relieve his frustration by practicing Vexation Fist. Although he lived outside the world, his heart lingered in this realm. He endured through several seasons, and even as the Head of the Bodhidharma Hall, he could only find emptiness. It wasn't until the time when the Old Demon Cult, Supreme Bliss Cult, became rampant that the young hero Long Yuan rallied the heroes. Shaolin responded immediately to his call. Juekong was fortunate enough to be part of this event and gained a great reputation in that battle, impressing everyone with his skills as Head of the Bodhidharma Hall.

To make a name for himself he ventured into the Jianghu, but no matter how hard he tries, the name Eagle Man never seems to spread. He still wanders endlessly along the Song–Jin border, and rumor has it he sometimes lends a hand to tyrants in their cruelty, dousing cold water and unwanted lectures on victorious Song soldiers after minor skirmishes, which people find deeply annoying. Old as he is, he acts with real hot blood; the heroes of the Central Plains won't befriend him, but he's quite popular among the common folk of both nations. He's fond of drink, though he can't hold his liquor well.

He was once a figure in tales, the chief of the Dharma Hall at Songshan Temple, with the dharma name Juekong. Chan Master Juekong ranked among the Wulin's Ten Greatest Experts. He mastered seven out of the Seventy-Two Arts, excelling especially in external skill Dragon Claw Hand. His martial arts were on par with his senior brother, Abbot Fangzhuang. Though highly esteemed for his virtue, he seldom wandered through Jianghu. At the age of fifty, he resigned from his chief position and journeyed far to Xiangyang's Six Paths Canyon to challenge the Mud Cult Heavenly King. Afterward, he vanished without a trace. When he reappeared, he had renounced his vows, adopting the pseudonym Eagle Man.

A robust elderly man dressed in a tattered straw cloak woven with eagle feathers. Despite his unusual appearance, his martial arts style is vast and profound, exuding an extraordinary demeanor, clearly indicating he is a master of his craft. It is unknown why, at this age, he remains unsung and unrecognized.

Her graceful name is Fan Xiaoyan — her mother, having learned some Chinese, chose it hoping she would live a carefree life and always wear a radiant smile. But misfortune struck: an evil beggar who dealt in the vile trade of maiming living captives abducted her as a child, meaning to turn her into a 'human dog.' Fortunately, her natural beauty spared her that fate — he decided instead to claim her for himself, keeping her hidden away in the beggars' den to torment and toy with, waiting only for her body to mature before he meant to violate her. Only Gang Leader Wang's intervention kept it from happening. Even so, being kept and raised like a dog left no part of her, body or spirit, unscarred. Perhaps this world holds havens somewhere — even amid endless border wars there are quiet corners of peace; even in the dark of night there are markets lit with light, and homes to return to. But nowhere was there a place that belonged to her. Not until you appeared. She believes in you, devoted to you heart and soul — you alone are home to her.

The incident where he once attacked the Eight-Bag Elders with poison had its reasons. He was a descendant of the Khitan Liao people who destroyed a nation a hundred years ago. Since his birth, all he could remember was following his parents as they wandered through Central Plains. Now those memories were already quite hazy. After his parents passed away, he was left only with an old dog named A'Hua. A'Hua had a discerning spirit; it would drive away mosquitoes and snakes to keep him safe when he was young, always by his side like a family member. One night, he woke up feeling cold and found that A'Hua was gone. Instead, the elderly beggars were holding bowls of dog meat soup and sharing it among themselves. He felt lost and heartbroken for a long time before finally shedding tears. From that day on, he became an orphan with no one to care about or cherish.

In the Beggar Sect, he also stood out like a sore thumb. He had few close peers and could be persuaded by very few to do things. Since childhood, his rendition of Lianhua Lao was always poor, leading him to often fail at begging. Without the care of an elderly beggar named Uncle, he might have starved to death long ago. Perhaps because of this, he had always been willing to follow Uncle's instructions. In front of others, he acted like a Mad Dog, but by Uncle's side, he was very obedient. Although he didn't get along well with people, he seemed to have a fondness for small animals, often seen sharing hard‑won food with stray animals.

From the Beggar Sect, a rising new talent in recent years in the Jianghu. He believes in the survival of the fittest. The weak are destined to be oppressed, while only the strong can survive in this world. Don't underestimate him just because he is short; when it comes to fighting, he fights like a Mad Dog, using every part of his body‑punches, claws, knees, elbows, and teeth. He is fearless, ruthless, and deadly. He learned a set of 'Dog-Beating Fist' from somewhere, the name crude but cleverly devised, emphasizing a Mental Formula: 'ruthlessness.' Each move aims to finish the opponent off. Once, he followed an elderly Eight-Bag Elder at midnight as he went to use the bathroom, brutally beat him until he was unconscious, breaking his limbs and pushing him into a latrine. Since then, even the long‑tenured Many-Bag Elders in the sect dared not act old‑fashioned or presumptuous in front of this man, for he is mad. Not only would he dare to fight anyone regardless of gender or age, but rumors have it that even Emperor of the Great Song might be within his reach.

A new rising star from the Beggar Sect of Jianghu. Known as 'Mad Dog,' don't underestimate his small stature; whenever he gets into a fight, it's all‑out war. Not only do outsiders fear him, but even members of the Beggar Sect dare not easily provoke this mad young man.

He is constantly testing you, placing great hopes in you while also waiting for you to betray him. The moment you show a greedy face, he will run you through with his sword, extinguishing his own last shred of conscience and becoming a vengeful demon who hunts down every enemy. Yet it seems you have disappointed those expectations — you are no saint, only someone whose devotion to human bonds outweighs the pull of treasure, and this has convinced him that 'righteousness' truly exists in this world. He has slowly come to understand his great-grandfather's selfish decision. You saved the life of his only remaining kin, and in doing so revived his heart as well, so that he is no longer a walking corpse driven only by vengeance, unable to picture a future. Only now has he begun to live for himself.

In his heart lies a boiling passion; gripping his treasured sword, he has rehearsed the moment of drawing it countless times in his mind. 'Ye' is not actually his family's true surname‑to keep faith with a promise that might never be fulfilled, his family gave up its own name. The 'Yun' shared by him and his sister was chosen to honor the master their great-grandfather once served, Yue Yun. As the third-generation male heir of the Ye family, his life was mapped out before he was even born: to be a vessel, to serve the country with loyalty, and to die in that service. The world calls Diancang's Ye Yunzhou a prodigy with the sword, but he himself thinks nothing of it‑is there really such a thing as genius in this world? It is only the fruit of relentless practice, day and night, painstakingly honed.

Even with his unparalleled skills, he always approached the world with diligence and seriousness, neither arrogant nor rash. He never easily engaged in disputes; when Listening Cloud Sword emerged, all who faced it met their end without mercy. Since venturing down the mountain, there had never been an exception to this rule, yet fearless individuals continued to rush forward to meet their doom. Perhaps because of his sister traveling with him, he was extra cautious, avoiding even fellow clansmen and disciples. His high skill, cool composure, and cautious nature, combined with a handsome appearance, made Ye Yunzhou a legendary swordsman. Various titles began to be imposed on him without regard for his feelings, but personally, he preferred the title Cangsong Swordsman. Before meeting you, his impression of Tang Clan was not favorable.

The Diancang Sect's foremost swift swordsman, one of the most celebrated young heroes in today's Wulin. His title comes from the world's admiration for his unbending character, as hardy and resolute as pine and cypress, standing firm against the wind. His swordsmanship is exceptional -- since joining the Diancang Sect in his early teens, within just a few years he had read through all seventeen sword manuals held in the Songyun Pavilion on Diancang Mountain. Not even his fellow disciples can keep pace with him, and even his own master admits to falling short.

A young swordsman dressed in Diancang sect attire. The name seems familiar, but you can't recall where you've heard it. For some reason, they are hiding their face beneath a bamboo hat. Judging by their handsome features, they don't seem like a Notorious Bandit.

One of the most talked‑about legends in the Wulin among Jianghu practitioners. Among his many legendary exploits, his final showdown with the Supreme Bliss Cult Leader was the most notable. Following the annihilation of the Old Demon Cult, the strongest virtuous and evil experts disappeared without a trace, bringing an end to an era.

In the Tang Clan, everyone surnamed Tang is family. You alone don't carry the name, yet somehow you're just as close — impossible to say how to place you. Moling became extremely attentive towards you, constantly seeking to be near, quietly staying by your side. Her innocent eyes see nothing of outward beauty or plainness; she simply craves that feeling of safety. She pays little mind to matters of the Jianghu and can barely find her way down the mountain, yet she knows with total clarity that she adores you. The expressionless girl blooms like a flower beside you — every ordinary day spent together beyond compare.

Before the Sect Leader's wife passed away, she had deceived their daughter by saying, I will retreat to Tang Clan's Secluded Valley for ten years of seclusion. If you miss me, fold a paper crane and send it down to the bottom of the valley. I will see it and know that you are thinking of your mother. Therefore, the junior martial sister folded paper cranes by her window every night for ten years, filled with thoughts of her mother. She feared the world, fearing that those she knew would leave one after another, and was terrified every night to the point of being unable to control herself.

Although she continued to practice kung fu, she did not particularly like it. At first, she often cried during the training. Practicing kung fu was extremely arduous, and she was also afraid of her father's punishment. Whenever she felt sad, she would run to her mother's embrace or seek refuge with the senior brother and second senior brother. After her mother passed away, she no longer ran away. Without realizing it, she had already mastered a set of punches and could finish her practice without sweating a single drop. She even forgot how to cry. She locked her emotions deep in her heart, keeping her true self hidden from everyone.

The Tang Clan Sect Leader's only beloved daughter. Worried over her frail, delicate health, the Sect Leader secluded himself for three years of meditation, and from his own unique martial art forged an entirely new path, creating the 'Heaven and Earth Soundless Force' for his beloved daughter. Its practitioner must tie seven strings of bells about her body and train relentlessly until she can sprint, leap, and throw hidden weapons without a single chime -- only then is her training complete. Shaped by this mental formula, she has grown detached by nature, rarely shows her feelings, dislikes conversation, and seldom smiles. Her hobby is paper folding.

Named Moling, the Sect Leader's only beloved daughter, a young woman like a forest creature. Her disposition is distant and indifferent, with seven silent bell-pendants that never jingle. Her interest lies in paper folding.

He rescued his Junior Sister, whom he had loved in secret for years, but he could never win back her tears. The wrong already done could not be undone, and neither of them would ever be free of it for the rest of their lives. Even so, he still asked for his Junior Sister's hand in marriage, and vowed himself to her for life. After several years of marriage they were blessed with a beloved daughter, yet his wife remained quietly unhappy throughout; for all that he could command the Jianghu, he could not bring peace to his own home. In the end, his wife succumbed to despair and leapt from a cliff, and Tang Zhongling's illness grew graver still.

He once led his disciples in a great battle to wipe out the old Demon Cult. Fighting alongside the Abbot of Songshan Temple against the Seven Immortals of the Supreme Bliss Cult, he broke their Ten Thousand Immortals Formation, thwarting the Supreme Bliss Cult Leader's ambition to seize the Central Plains — halted at Qinzhou. In the climactic battle, chosen as one of the five representatives of the righteous factions, he faced the Right Guardian of the Supreme Bliss Cult, forcing down poison to push his power past its limits. He won that desperate fight and slew the great evil, but it left him with an illness that never fully healed. After that battle, both the Tang Clan and Songshan were gravely weakened — yet Songshan remained honored by the world, while the Tang Clan became the stray dog everyone wanted to kick.

The twenty-seventh generation Sect Leader of the Tang Clan. In his youth he had a fiery temper and a deep hatred of evil. He roamed the Jianghu, using his signature Ultimate, the Flying Swallow Meteor Feather, to defeat every challenger he met. The Tang Clan's name spread far and wide, but it also earned him more than a few enemies among the heroes of the Jianghu. Only after he married a junior sister among his fellow disciples and took over as Sect Leader did he grow more reserved. Over a decade spent managing the clan's affairs has aged him considerably. In recent years stress has brought on illness, so he has handed the clan's day-to-day matters to his third disciple to manage in his stead.

True name Tang Zhongling, he is the current Sect Leader of the Tang Clan. With a fierce temper and a hatred for evil, he was once one of the legendary figures listed among the Wulin's Ten Greatest Experts. Unfortunately, after middle age, his physical condition had significantly declined, and the Flying Swallow Meteor Feather became a technique never again heard of.

Fourth Senior Brother learned the truth of his birth and discovered that his parents were alive, with nine brothers and sisters who had grown up well-fed. The news stirred both envy and resentment, yet still the stone weighing on his heart finally lifted. Grievances he had swallowed for years failed him when at last he faced his blood parents — he could not voice them, could not even say why; it simply felt as though these people were not people he could turn to for comfort. In the end he politely declined his birth parents' pleas to stay and returned to the Tang Clan. Given fine food, he'd still shamelessly fight his fellow disciples over plain fare. He remained just as sly and greedy as ever, and just as devoted to the Sect Leader. Fourth Senior Brother has his own family too — right here in the Tang Clan.

Though Fourth Senior Brother made a fortune from dubious dealings, he also helped many in need. He sold treasured swords and Spirit Pills to warriors about to face death; secret manuals to youths avenging blood feuds; and carried letters across thousands of miles for those who wished to send them home. As long as the deal was struck, he would do his best to see it through. Although he coveted wealth, he did not look down on the poor or consider helping them a foolish investment. He was willing to assist, assuming that everyone had a long life ahead of them. He took on arduous mercantile missions no one else wanted in order to meet more people, establish his reputation, and find kin who might already be gone.

Often traveling south and north, he worked as a peddler. Though young in years, his experiences in the Jianghu were remarkably rich; he was well‑informed and had extensive connections. He could be found almost anywhere and sell anything. He had a not‑so‑flattering nickname: Gets-in-Everywhere. He would always appear unexpectedly at critical moments where he was least expected, selling the goods you needed, which was extremely suspicious.

The closed-door disciple of the Tang Clan's Sect Leader. Their background is unclear; they were discovered in a box of fruits while being brought up the mountain, and even as an infant, they had a remarkable appetite. On the surface, they are obedient and uphold honesty, particularly skilled at playing the innocent, earning the Sect Leader's trust and being entrusted with important financial responsibilities. They often take advantage of trips to purchase daily necessities like firewood, rice, oil, and salt to acquire various rare items, reselling them at high prices to the disciples within the clan for personal profit. If you can afford it, they will naturally be happy to help you smuggle in contraband.

His real name is Weiyuan, a closed-door disciple of the Tang Clan's leader. He has been entrusted with the task of going down the mountain to sell medicine and purchase daily necessities, which he enjoys immensely. He often exploits loopholes in the Clan Rules, smuggling goods to sell at inflated prices to fellow disciples, earning a profit from the price difference.

He had once seen the emperor of the Great Song. I have strategies for stabilizing the nation and securing its borders, methods to nourish the people, plans to break through enemy lines‑only by purifying the palace can such things be achieved. He dared to offer this advice during his imperial audience after passing the imperial exams, but it offended those in power who accompanied the emperor. As a result, he was wrongfully accused and imprisoned under a false charge. His aged parents back home and his wife all died unjustly. In jail, he wept for tens of days; on the day he was escorted to the execution ground, he was rescued by Tang Zhongling and two young disciples. Listen carefully, fellow villagers and elders‑this man suffered imprisonment merely because he sought to ensure the safety of the common people. He is truly the greatest hero in the land! Remember this! Tang Zhongling said thusly, and those words stayed deeply embedded in his heart, still unforgettable to this day.

That year, under a pavilion in the pouring rain, he met Tang Zhongling by chance, and the two talked freely of the world's affairs — what joy that was! One a poor scholar, the other a drifter of the Jianghu; one lettered, one skilled in arms. For all their differing views, a mutual respect grew between them. Even after he joined the Tang Clan to study martial arts, the two got on more like old friends than anything else, often sharing tea and talk of passing seasons. The Eldest Senior Brother and Second Senior Brother had grown up right under his eye, and though they now held high standing, he never once presumed to call himself their elder. It's only a pity he took up the martial arts too late to vie with the heroes of the world — he was always going to fall behind. Still, it was never in his nature to show off strength or pick fights. As Sun Tzu's Art of War says, the highest form of war is to defeat the enemy's plans. The one who never fights is the true winner.

The third Direct Disciple of the Tang Clan Sect Leader. In his youth, he was full of fervor, studying hard in seclusion for over a decade, vowing to earn office and rank so he could use his learning to benefit the realm. Unfortunately, he offended men of power and failed the imperial examination, bringing mortal danger down on himself. Fortunately, he had once shared shelter from the rain under the same pavilion with Tang Zhongling, who had not yet succeeded as Sect Leader. In his hour of danger, Tang Zhongling saved him from death's door. Having stared death in the face, his hopes turned to ash, and he gave up on serving the court, joining the Tang Clan instead. His hobby is storytelling; in his idle hours he loves to spin tales of the Jianghu, untroubled by matters of life and death, and easygoing besides.

With the single name Sheng, he is the Third Direct Disciple of the Tang Clan Sect Leader. Having joined as a disciple already skilled in his arts, he is older than his two senior brothers. Once an ambitious scholar, he fled into the Jianghu after offending the nobility. His interests are storytelling, teaching promising students, and jesting about the affairs of the world.

Compared to his biological father, from whom he parted ways in childhood, he holds a deeper affection for his master, Tang Zhongling. The Tang Clan feels more like home than the Mud Cult. He has not forgotten his mission, but his heart is no longer in it; he complies with the Mud Cult's envoy while secretly finding ways to protect the Tang Clan. He has searched through ancient and modern texts for a cure to the sect leader's old ailment, and feels a deep jealousy toward his Senior Brother, who is favored by the sect leader. He shares a maternal bond with Junior Martial Sister Mo Ling; even though his words can be sharp, he dotes on this half-sister of his.

His true identity was that of an undercover agent from the Mud Cult's Human Path. Sent by the Demon Cult, he had been initiated into the Tang Clan since childhood to respond to the needs of the Mud Cult. He gained the trust of the Sect Leader and was taught the secret formula for 'pepper powder.' Originally, he was supposed to use this to control Tang Clan disciples and serve the Mud Cult, but due to the Sect Leader discontinuing the practice of using pepper powder as a poison in cultivation exercises, his plans did not come to fruition.

The second disciple under the Tang Clan Sect Leader. Skilled in the use of poison, his knowledge of poisons surpasses that of his teacher. He is a meticulous and solitary individual, strict with himself and others. Ordered by his master to oversee discipline, he is greatly feared by his fellow disciples. He rarely leaves the alchemy laboratory and seldom ventures into Jianghu. Thus, his reputation does not extend as far as his senior brother's. However, those who have clashed with him admit they tremble even without cause. He has an unusual obsession with pepper powder, not only enjoying it himself but also forcing others to partake in it.

With the single name Zheng, he is the second disciple under the Tang Clan Sect Leader. Skilled in the use of poisons, he excels particularly in the study of poison and drug techniques, surpassing his own master. He is meticulous in thought, solitary and deeply introspective, rarely venturing down the mountain. Thus, his reputation does not extend as far as that of his senior brother. He is known by others as the 'Ruthless Young Master' or the 'Ruthless Young Lord,' and people respect him from afar, avoiding direct contact with him.

Seeming carefree and indifferent to worldly matters, his demeanor was actually deeply rebellious and stubborn. As a young boy, he had tried every possible means to escape the Tang Clan, fleeing back home. His parents were at a loss for what to do, so they finally revealed his true identity to him, guiding him to seek out his birth mother. At Flower Moon Tower, he saw his mother, who was suffering from syphilis and had lost her mental clarity. From others, he learned that his mother had exhausted all her savings and entrusted someone to adopt him, clearing his name and then sending him into the Tang Clan to learn. Her intention was not to let her beloved son suffer as she did, always at the mercy of others and treated with contempt. After that day, Tang Buyi underwent a transformation, vowing to support women across the land.

Frequenting the Flower Moon Tower, he scattered silver like flowing water, earning the playful title of Owner from the girls there, and even the madam doted on him. His reputation as a hero spread far and wide, yet he was also notorious. People of the Jianghu feared this young hero, but with no official standing to restrain him, they kept their own wives and daughters under close watch, fearing he might steal their hearts. As for his Junior Martial Sister, he has always cherished her like a sister born of his own blood — nothing more.

The Eldest Disciple under the Tang Clan Sect Leader. One of the most renowned young heroes in the Wulin, he is free-spirited, cheerful, and unconcerned with trivial matters. Having once heard of an injustice, he descended the mountain and crossed provinces to slay a corrupt official, then opened the granaries to aid the people, leaving without a trace once the matter was resolved. He once fell for a beauty's fame as well, traveling a thousand miles just to meet her, only to vanish without a word after a brief encounter, earning himself an unjust reputation for fickleness. Coming and going like the wind, he is known in Jianghu as the Flying Hero. He scoffs at the Tang Clan's practice of distinguishing between inner and outer disciples, often egging his fellow Junior Brothers of other surnames into slacking off and playing with him, and is remarkably skilled at getting on his master's nerves.

Named Buyi, he is the Eldest Disciple under the Sect Leader. Gifted and bright, with a free-spirited nature, he is known in the Jianghu as the Flying Hero. His mastery of hidden weapons and Qinggong has reached the pinnacle of the contemporary realm.
This important Song Dynasty medical text records illustrations of a wide variety of herbal plants.
Classified Materia Medica

This manuscript records a fragment of the Secret Manual 'Nine Turns of Reincarnation Grand Technique,' one of the Three Treasures of Supreme Bliss Cult. This volume is only the upper half and focuses on the Internal Method; the cultivation techniques are not entirely complete.
Nine Turns Fragment

This book includes popular paper‑folding schemes from ancient to modern times, such as paper boxes, boats, frogs, cranes, fish, flowers, swords, and cloud‑ladders. The illustrations are detailed, and the instructions are clear. With this book, anyone can become a paper‑folding warrior.
Collection of Origami

The full title is Huangdi's Eighty‑One Difficulties Classic, a renowned medical work aimed at elucidating the doubts and key points of the Huangdi Neijing. Traditionally attributed to the famous physician Bian Que, it emphasizes the theories of Five Evils Interference and Ten Transformations, explaining the relationships of the five organs, discussing pulse theory, meridians, organs, and even acupuncture methods, profoundly influencing later generations of medicine.
Nanjing

The medical book compiled by the Hanlin Medical Officer under the decree of Emperor Taizong includes methods of diagnosis, prescriptions, diseases of the five organs, internal and external medicine, gynecology, pediatrics, dietary practices, medicinal pills, external treatments, acupuncture, and more. The original text consists of a hundred volumes, but what you have received is merely an outline, as Second Senior Brother believes that the omitted content is common knowledge that you should already know.
Taiping Sacred Prescriptions

Wei Ju carefully selected a collection of contemporary outstanding literary works in verse, excerpting one hundred Song Dynasty ci poems. Her curation was precise and balanced, akin to a mirror reflecting the words with clarity. Not all of these may be penned by renowned masters, but they are certainly masterpieces. This book is a hand‑copied edition by Wei Ju, with delicate handwriting that resembles flowers adorning a beautiful lady, as graceful as a phoenix's flight or a swan's wander, frustrated in its ambitions. Yet any literati would delight upon seeing this volume; it alone was given to you, a person of the Jianghu. She adhered to her vow but harbored a private desire, secretly including some of her own old works under an anonymous name.
Selected Lyrics of the Song Dynasty

The ancestral medical book of the Tang Clan is the only one in the world that uses poison as medicine. It combines the teachings of the Miaojiang and Buddhism, observing that a bowl of water contains eighty‑four thousand insects, which represent poison. These poisons are also categorized into the five elements and six harmonies, corresponding to the five organs and six viscera. Too much leads to harm, too little results in illness, depletion causes weakness, and imbalance leads to madness. It is not that people are not harmed by the five poisons; rather, their toxic properties have yet to manifest. Only by using medicine to nurture them, allowing them to flow harmoniously, can one turn poison to their advantage, making it difficult for a hundred ailments to invade.
Tang Clan Pharmacopoeia

Written by Zhang Zhongjing, the Eastern Han dynasty's renowned Healer of the Nation, this is a classic of Han medicine. The original text was lost amid the chaos of war, and this book was later compiled by scholars from the Shanghan Lun and the Jingui Yaolue.
Treatise on Cold Damage and Miscellaneous Diseases

The Medical Classic written by the Medicine King Sun Simiao is a monumental work that encompasses both empirical and theoretical prescriptions. This book is based on the organ theory of the Huangdi Neijing, collecting medical theories, prescriptions, medicinal uses, and acupuncture techniques, totaling two hundred and thirty categories and five thousand three hundred prescriptions. The opening chapter, On the Absolute Sincerity of Great Physicians, discusses medical ethics and the compassion for the world, leaving a profound impact on future generations.
Essential Formulas for Emergency Treatment

The Heavenly Way internal method of the Mud Cult, a Demon Cult. A qi-cultivation technique developed from medical texts, grounded in the traditional Chinese medicine principle of the 'Warming Method.' It uses warm, pungent herbs to moxa the acupoints, dispelling cold qi while also replenishing qi and nourishing the blood-remarkably effective, with the power to restore yang and reverse collapse.
Warm Yang Blood Circulation Talisman

A brand-new book, after many twists and turns, has finally found its way into your hands. The first half collects celebrated lines from recent Ci poets, including masterpieces by Yan Shu, Fan Zhongyan, Ouyang Xiu, Liu Yong, and the Three Sus. The latter half gathers works by present-day literati, but the final pages have been deliberately defaced beyond reading, leaving only a faint trace of the author's surname, Wei.
Selection of Contemporary Ci Poetry

Not only does the book cover the various weapons and tools of the Fire Mountain Sword Pavilion, including their ironware blueprints, but it also encompasses undisclosed forging secrets. It records the characteristics, formulas, and properties of different metals and alloys. The book details processes such as annealing, quenching, and tempering utilizing the geothermal heat from Fire Mountain, which is more authentic and rigorous compared to the forging techniques you are familiar with in the Tang Clan.
Fire Mountain Forging Manual

A hand-copied manuscript by Nangong Zhi, founding patriarch of the Nangong family and Wulin Alliance Leader. His brushwork is bold and forceful, each stroke sweeping like an army on the march, and it is often used by Nangong clan members as a model for practicing calligraphy. Though it records no martial arts, it gathers Nangong Zhi's reflections on life-his military strategy, scholarship, medical knowledge, personal musings, the fashions of the day, and jokes. Truthfully, it's a rather entertaining read.
Nangong Martial Preparedness Treatise

It records the forging methods for the secret weapons handed down within Kongtong's Four Gates, many of them ingenious feats of craftsmanship worthy of the gods. The Mother-and-Son Mandarin Duck Axes, the Mechanism Saw, and the Hooked Rope Flying Claw are all included. Even if you never wield these weapons yourself, forging and studying them can still sharpen your own skills.
Kongtong Arcane Weapon Forging Method

Renowned throughout the realm, the Nangong Family Teachings should not be judged by its fan's gentle, scholarly sway-it is nothing to be trifled with. The fan technique unites offense and defense: the handle can strike acupoints, while the fan's fluttering motion conceals a follow-up strike. Feint becomes real, and real becomes feint; a master with strong Internal Force can harm an opponent with nothing but the wind of the fan. Once loosed, it spins and darts unpredictably, making it hard to block or dodge. Rarest of all is its deep scholarly bearing-never arrogant, never disheartened, humble and at peace.
Nangong Dashing Fan

During his travels among the states, the Confucian war god Mencius bested one rival after another in debate, using pointed words as blades to bring peace to the Central Plains. The source of these sayings is unknown, but local legend holds that the 'cannon' piece in chess actually represents Mencius's mouth-it can strike from afar, and the truly terrifying part is that once the angle is right, no one is safe. No matter how exalted the opponent's standing or how humbly they sought his counsel, they would still be soundly lectured by Mencius. He is even said to have drawn on Sun Tzu's Art of War and Internal Skill while arguing, leaving people unable to talk back, and it would hardly be strange if some were scolded to death. He railed against every school of thought, yet would not suffer anyone to criticize him, snapping back in fury: "Am I fond of debating? I have no choice in the matter!" And so his words became an echo that has rung through the ages.
War God's Sayings

Records of Jianghu Ghosts and Spirits: Continuation is an anonymous victim's plea, written by holding the brush in his mouth in place of his missing hands. It recounts how he went from an innocent, able-bodied child to a man swindled into ruin, his family destroyed, and cast adrift in a foreign land. Struggling to survive on his own, he was then falsely accused of theft, thrown into prison, and had both arms cut off. In the end he escaped with his life and took his revenge with the Jujube-Pit Dart he had painstakingly mastered in prison.
Records of Jianghu Ghosts and Spirits: Continuation

A chronicle of various tricks and schemes in the Jianghu, the author's intent was to warn innocent Commoners not to be deceived by others and to remember that one should not have thoughts of harming others but must always be wary. Unfortunately, this book fell into the wrong hands and was instantly transformed into a fraud manual, employing whatever means necessary to maximize its potency.
Records of Jianghu Ghosts and Spirits

Notes written by Lei Qian, the current Sect Leader of the Kongtong Iron Fist Gate. Aware that his own talent is unremarkable, he fears the refined skills of earlier generations may be lost forever. Though he cannot break new ground himself, he has resolved on a grand ambition: to gather every manner of forging method for exotic weapons into this one book. This is a book written for mortals.
Notes on Eighteen Exotic Weapon Forging Methods

Author Ye Yunshang's handwriting is very elegant and delicate, with a hint of juvenile fun, much like herself. This writing details her snowball fighting techniques, seriously dividing them into 'main attack' and 'sneak attack' sections. Most of the moves in this book are imagined by her. They include hiding stones or caterpillars in snowballs, stuffing snowballs into pants‑she leaves no stone unturned in her cruel tactics.
Snowball Combat Manual

Written by Sun Wu, the Sage of War of the Spring and Autumn period, Sun Tzu's Art of War is the earliest military treatise in the Central Plains, revered as a classic by strategists. It comprises thirteen chapters discussing military strategy and summarizing the lessons of war, exerting a profound influence on military thought for generations to come.
Sun Tzu's Art of War

Composed from the sayings of Confucius, a prominent thinker of the Spring and Autumn period, this text is one of the most important classics in Confucianism. This simple vernacular version was compiled by Third Senior Brother when he served as a private school teacher to instruct children who could not read.
Analects
