The mystical martial arts of the Qingcheng Sect blend the principles of Taiji, drawing qi into the bones to strengthen the spirit. In their palm, they cultivate all things; with each contraction and expansion, yin and yang, calm and movement are harmonized. Regardless of whether the opponent's force is yin or yang, it can be transformed and absorbed as if a clay ox entering the sea, dissipating without trace.
Yin-Yang Theft
Withering and Flourishing Divine Skill, Vol. 1
Withering and Flourishing Divine Skill, Vol. 1

The Daoist Tiger's Roar Skill takes the tiger's mighty roar as its image, likening a cultivator's fierce, unyielding progress to a tiger's power that drives off swarms of evil. The technique releases inner qi outward from the dantian; in battle, the practitioner unleashes it with a thunderous roar that carries for a thousand miles, stealing the opponent's wits and sometimes even inflicting internal injury.
Tiger's Roar Skill

This Internal Method of the Qingcheng Sect holds to non-action, guarding emptiness until it becomes void. A heart at peace, free of striving, is itself the truest striving; a mind empty of thought and will marks true mastery — shun every mental image, and the Dao arises on its own. It is hard to learn and harder to perfect, but the day it is mastered is no small thing.
Wuwei Elixir Method

The Internal Method of the Shangguan family, the Wulin's Three Great Families, the essence of the Surging Wave Blade Technique. It requires training with turbulent currents to hone one's skills, achieving the ability to stand firm in raging waves and slash through them. The techniques flow like the endless tide, pressing forward relentlessly, amplifying Internal Force even further. Even if one manages to parry them, they would stagger a few steps.
Wave Riding Technique

The legendary former Wulin Alliance Leader Long Yuan owed his fame not to a single style, but to seven Signature Skills he was known to wield. His blade and sword: Cleaving Star Threads. His fist and palm: Carving Mountain Palm. His leg technique: Shooting Sun Leg. His spear and staff: Little Overlord Spear. His long rope: Bizarre Acupoint-Striking Rope. His hidden weapon: Ruyi Finger. His Internal Skill: Xuanxuan Creation Skill. In his day, Long Yuan rallied the heroes of the land and stormed the old Demon Cult's Paradise Headquarters, fighting the Supreme Bliss Cult Leader single-handed. Cleaving Stars, Shooting Suns, and Overlord Mountain-Cutting flew one after another, stunning the finest masters of both the righteous and the wicked path. Without a word passing between them, every one of them thought the same thing: 'This, surely, is the finest under Heaven today.'
Long Yuan Seven Absolutes

The Nangong family's generational legacy of the Internal Method is passed down, with each person receiving a copy, and the verses elegantly transcribed on the inner pages of the book. It blends Daoist philosophy, emphasizing that amidst countless changes, one remains steadfast; tranquility of spirit leads to calmness of mind, guarding the mysterious gateway, subduing malevolent energies, maintaining humility, and achieving clarity of heart and mind. The foundation of the Nangong Family Teachings lies in safeguarding the heart, followed by protecting oneself, preserving the family, and defending the nation.
Nangong Internal Method

The Palace Mistress of Jinxiang Palace poured heart and soul into crafting this technique, evolved from the Nangong Internal Method. Its purpose is to help one find stillness of heart, so that sorrow does not wound the body. Mysterious Candle refers to the moon, and so this technique is also known as the Moon-Gazing Heart Sutra. People know joy and sorrow, parting and reunion, just as the moon waxes and wanes — such things have never been perfect since ancient times. Yet even scattered across the ends of the earth, all are bathed in the very same moonlight. Whenever grief overwhelms you, practice this technique: gather your spirit, turn sorrow into strength, and go on living well.
Mysterious Candle Heart Sutra

The Internal Method of the now non‑existent Snow Mountain Sect is practiced with very special methods. One must first inhale true qi deeply, then strip naked and insert their body upside down into the snow, only exposing their feet. Someone else would then apply moxibustion to the Yongquan acupoint on their soles, using the heat from the moxa to activate the meridians and adjust their body temperature to resist the cold and ice. If there is no snow water available, a nearby cool stream can be used as a substitute.
Snow Mountain Internal Method

The Flying Heaven Gate and the Soul-Stealing Gate are locked in a struggle over who gets to be the face of Kongtong. Craving quick results, they drink poison to quench their thirst — inflaming their Internal Force with Fire Scorpion Poison to force their way through a bottleneck. By working the Heartburn Seal, they can briefly quicken the heartbeat and drive the blood, boosting the whole body's power at the cost of burning away their remaining years. But that price is only the start: the fire-poison builds up inside the body, and each time it peaks it shows on the surface — a dry mouth and bleeding gums, insomnia and short temper at best; at worst, the heat surges to the head, leaving them either witless or suddenly dead. The danger is sharpest each year at the Dragon Boat Festival, when yang energy runs highest — a risk not to be taken lightly.
Heartburn Seal

Practitioners must stand on one leg, supporting the pipa with their leg; this is the Qinggong of the Flying Heaven Gate's Crane Stance. To stir the strings of the Iron Zither, one must first practice the Soul‑Stealing Gate's Frost Blade Breaking Bamboo Finger. Next, to activate the sound box, one must utilize the Internal Force of the Mystic Skill Gate to create resonance. In combat, one can even wield the pipa as a weapon, executing the Iron Fist School's Ruyi Smash technique to crush the enemy's skull. When mastery is achieved and the mind moves, all meridians resonate, moving like a vibrating string, enduring through time; this is the foremost divine skill of Kongtong.
Iron Pipa Skill

Hidden in a stalactite cave where the Wushan mountains meet the Yangtze, a mysterious martial art is painted across the walls, its origin and age both unknown. Nine drawings unfold the training method as a connected series — at once righteous and depraved in flavor, certainly no ordinary path of cultivation, and yet so terse and pointed that a single glance can jolt the mind awake. A fisherman who lost his footing and fell into the water discovered it, traced the drawings, and presented them to the Imperial Court for a reward. The court thought little of it, though, and the technique was left to gather dust on the shelves of nobles and officials. As for the cave itself, rising waters have long since swallowed it whole.
Nine Treasures of the Wushan Grotto

Although the effects are powerful and widely known, no one wishes to practice this qigong. This is because it is the Virgin Boy Skill, which is quite regrettable. It is said that once a man marries, the hard‑earned power from practicing will dissipate. No one wants to end their days alone, so few are willing to train in this martial arts skill. However, this is a misunderstanding. The term Virgin Boy Skill refers to preserving the primordial energy to nourish the body's vitality since childhood. Thus, it is most effective when started from a young age. If one begins practicing immediately after birth, they can achieve great success within twelve years. Starting at the age of adolescence will reduce the effectiveness because the muscles and bones are already formed, and the primordial energy has dispersed. After reaching the age of thirty, there is no point in learning it at all. It has nothing to do with whether one marries or not.
Primordial Youth Qi

Daoist Azure Dragon's Cry is likened to the Nine Heavens Dragon's Roar, describing a cultivator ascending to transcendence with a clear and resounding exhalation, akin to a dragon's cry piercing through the air. This cultivation technique requires the internal qi from the dantian to be externally emitted. When engaging in combat, one releases this power with a fierce howl, the sound like thunderbolts cascading for miles, capturing the opponent's soul and even causing Internal Injuries.
Dragon's Cry Skill

The military training exercises of the Yang family from the Northern Song Dynasty, known for their loyalty and bravery, are referred to as gymnastics. However, in order to truly enhance survival rates on the battlefield, the intensity of this training far exceeds that of the Imperial Court's regular army and is even stricter than the techniques of smaller sects in the Wulin. It incorporates staff techniques, the One Hundred and Eight Formation drills, and the Eighteen Strikes with the bronze hammer. This set of exercises would be challenging for even those from the Wulin to endure.
Yang Family Military Drill Manual

This mysterious Chan technique, transmitted from the Western Regions, is utterly unlike the martial arts of the Central Plains — not just in its strange postures, but in its obscure phrasing; its last two chapters read like a horse mouth stitched to a cow's head, all but unreadable. Practicing this Zen technique demands real physical toil: one must light charcoal, lay a bed of jagged stones, and train atop them, all while channeling Internal Skill to vent the heat from the body — or risk being burned alive. It is said that at its highest realm one can sit in meditation and float, dislocate and extend the joints to strike, and breathe raging fire. But with the final two chapters lost to translation, no one truly knows if that realm can ever be reached.
Fiery Zen

The Quanzhen Sect deliberately spread this Qi-cultivating Internal Skill beyond its walls to promote its teachings and open the minds of the common people. They pared down the sword formulas, blended in methods for nurturing life, and rewrote it all in plain speech anyone could grasp — a first taste of Daoist learning that also lengthens one's years. Every village elder owned a copy, and everyone practiced it, a national health exercise in all but name. But hoping to defeat an enemy with it would likely prove futile.
Quanzhen Sword Technique

Lianhua Lao, the anthem every beggar in the Beggar Sect learns to sing, is in truth an Internal Skill chant built around the art of survival. After each night's work, elder beggars lead the younger ones in singing it together, tapping chopsticks on their bowls to keep time; matching breath to the song lets proper respiration take root naturally. The lyrics, though, are often crude and hardly fit for polite company — sung to a young lady, they might even get you reported to the authorities.
Lianhua Lao

A classic dirty trick of the Jianghu, favored by many a scoundrel. When the enemy is too strong to fight, seize the moment to seal off your own meridians, stilling the blood and stopping the pulse, so you seem as good as dead. Once the enemy leaves, quicklime hidden in your palm can be heated to revive you. But this Internal Skill carries great risk: should the revival mechanism fail, oxygen deprivation to the brain may leave you addled for life. And should you cross a truly ruthless foe, seeing you fall they may finish you off with two more blows without a word — turning a feigned death into a real one.
Turtle Breathing Technique

Tang Fen, a heroine of the Tang Clan, drew on the Five Elements theory behind Qingcheng's Eight Immortals Sword Technique, replacing its elements with the Five Poisons to create her own singular martial art. Its moves are, at best, second-rate, but woven through them lies the Tang Clan's deep knowledge of medicine and poison, making it fiendishly hard to grasp — and even mastering it is no guarantee of real accomplishment.
Eight Immortals Finger

This lost Divine Power of the Flying Heaven Gate springs from the same source as the Soul-Stealing School's Soul-Quelling Skill, the Iron Fist School's Injury Fist, and the Mystic Skill School's Iron Pipa Skill — all originating from the Nanyue True Scripture. It is the original form from which the Flying Heaven Kick and the Immortal Crane's Elusive Steps were later derived. Once mastered, one can stand balanced on a single toe without bending the knee, gliding at great speed on Internal Force alone. Upon releasing the foot, power flows from body to leg, leg to foot, and foot to toe, concentrating tremendous force into a single point; depending on intent, it can strike fierce or gentle — hard enough to shatter the Golden Bell Cover with one toe, or soft enough to seal an opponent's acupoint with the faintest pressure.
Barefoot Divine Power

This extremely deranged Blade Technique was created by a third‑rate blade-wielder consumed by the hatred of having his wife stolen from him. During his 13 years of wrongful imprisonment, he pondered his enemy's fighting style thousands of times in his mind, and imagined torturing the man who took his wife tens of thousands of times more. Not long after his release, the shocking bloodbath known as the 'Crimson Blood Massacre' erupted, sending shockwaves through the Jianghu.
Death by a Thousand Cuts

Your mentor, Xiahou Lan, gathered the essential spirit of both the Soul-Stealing School and the Snow Mountain Sect, refined away the dross to keep only their essence, and blended it with Crane-Controlling Qigong to finally create this divine skill. Its purpose is not to kill but specifically to deal with experts; even the most skilled Qinggong techniques in the world cannot escape its grasp. The force is akin to a flying goose treading on snow, leaving only the faintest traces on the mud, while the goose itself pays no mind to east or west. With a light touch, it captures its target, revealing three parts of its strength while holding back seven, and the follow‑up move is hidden, unseen. It disrupts the enemy's stance while I swiftly recover my energy, launching a deadly assault.
Snow Mountain Flying Goose Claw

This move, called the Treading-on-the-Moon Style, was devised by your eldest senior brother of the Tang Clan amid his skirt-chasing escapades, and is recorded in the sequel to the Cloud-Ascending Ladder. To catch a glimpse of a beauty, one could scale the clouds atop the Cloud-Ascending Ladder to reach her balcony; the Treading-on-the-Moon Style is an offensive move derived from this Qinggong. Moon here refers to brilliance, a veiled reference to any blade brought against oneself — thus the true meaning of the Treading-on-the-Moon Style is to step squarely onto an opponent's weapon and tread down upon their face from on high.
Ascending Cloud Step · Moon Gazing

Jianghu's foremost beauty, Soul-Stealing Orchid, is renowned for her signature skill. Combining the Snow Mountain Sect's Internal Skill with the Soul-Stealing Gate's stealth techniques, her agility is like that of a ghost or demon, capable of ensnaring one's soul. The four devastating moves — Crumbling Heart, Corroding Bone, Soul Devouring, and Soul-Stealing — are each more ruthless than the last, extremely poisonous. Practicing them might even harm the harmony of heaven.
Soul-Stealing Phantom Claw

The signature skill of the White Ape Patriarch of the Emei Sect is, strictly speaking, a form of monkey fist, yet it diverges significantly from the folk versions of monkey fist. Its power emanates from the back, travels through the shoulder and past the elbow to reach the fingers — hence its name, Through-Arm.
White Ape Connecting Arms Fist

It is said that this is the martial art practiced by Xu Qing, the third of the Five Heroes of Xiankong Island. Xu Qing, born to a blacksmith, possessed immense strength and had the unique ability to burrow underground, earning him the nickname Mountain‑Burrowing Mouse. The Five Rats pledged their loyalty to the Kaifeng Prefecture and assisted Bao Zheng. In the seventh year of the Jiayou era, Lord Bao passed away, and the following year he was buried in Hefei. The Five Rats accompanied him on his journey, bowing in farewell before parting ways. Later, Xu Qing retreated to Kongtong, passing down the Iron Arm Divine Fist and blacksmithing techniques, and he passed away at the Great Iron Forge in Iron Fist Alley.   Practitioners must apply oil to both arms, pass them through iron rings, and circulate their energy to make their arms engorge and harden. They then strike wooden stakes; after breaking the wooden stake, they move on to stone stakes; after breaking the stone stake, they strike iron stakes. If an arm breaks, they apply ointment and continue training until healed. Over time, their hands will become as strong as iron.
Iron Arm Divine Fist

The claw technique uniquely created by the once-renowned, enigmatic thief known as Iron-Face Man. Rather than following orthodox principles, it strikes from unconventional angles — lurking in darkness, becoming one with the shadows, slipping into the night to deliver a single fatal blow. Iron-Face Man was ordered by Grand Tutor Pang to assassinate Bao Zheng, but was instead won over by Lord Bao's awe-inspiring impartiality. Unwilling to harm the Blue Sky for a private grudge, yet unwilling to break his word, he gave up his advantage and went forth in secret to challenge Southern Hero Zhan Zhao, losing the bout honorably and cutting off his own ten fingers in atonement. Bao Zheng then spared his life, and Iron-Face Man withdrew into seclusion at Kongtong, had an iron claw forged as a prosthetic hand, and wrote this manual.
Shadowless Claw

Kongtong Sect. Flying Heaven Gate's martial art passed down through the generations. Their agility is light and graceful, with quick punches and loose steps, making them most nimble and versatile. At times they move like a leisurely wanderer, at others like a bird suddenly diving into attack, leaving one unsure and constantly on guard. However, this style of fist technique is overly complex, consisting of thirty‑six paths, seventy‑two transformations, and one hundred and eight subsequent moves, making it very difficult to master. Therefore, few within Flying Heaven Gate ever delve deeply into it.
Immortal Crane's Elusive Fist

Kongtong Sect · Flying Heaven Gate's secret manuals. The Former Sect Leader simplified 'Immortal Crane's Elusive Fist' into these versions for initial discipleship instruction. They omit the bewilderment and fist routines, focusing solely on lower‑body Qinggong training, making them simple and easy to understand.
Flying Heaven Kick

The Fist Classic stolen from Songshan Temple is the foundation of Songshan's martial arts, easy to learn but difficult to master. The Luohan Fist manual that has circulated among the people has given rise to many different forms over the centuries, each with its own unique flair, and each version is somewhat different. You cannot be sure if the manual in your hands is the original. Since you have come across this manual, you have a connection to the Buddha; practice it.
Luohan Fist Manual

The meaning of the two characters Amo is ultimately unknown; not even the Beggar Sect's Skill-Transmission Elders, nor the walking bookworms of Gengyang Study, know it. However, the term tangqiang has been interpreted as to smear, meaning that this set of Fist Techniques can only exert its maximum effect in extremely confined spaces: pushing the enemy against the wall and beating them mercilessly until they are reduced to a pulp smeared on the wall. Although the concept is simple, this martial art cannot be established without a foundation in External Skill; techniques like inch power, sudden elbow strikes, and Iron Mountain Lean are all practical combat skills.
Amotang Wall Fist

The Beggar Sect has established customary escape techniques that are particularly impressive when employed by a large group. In such situations, they scatter like a startled flock, bursting out in every direction, feinting east while bolting west as though of one mind, making it difficult for enemies to net them all at once; there is always some fish who slips the net and lives to carry word home. These escape methods are passed down through song, with the verse going: Look to the east while running west, nowhere to hide up in a tree's height, three or five together defy ironclad fate, life and death preordained no need to hesitate. Though the words may be simple and straightforward, they contain cunning strategies and also provide psychological preparation for the possibility of being caught.
Eight Wildernesses Escape

The Qinggong and leg technique of the Quanzhen Sect. Carefree Wandering takes its name from the book of Zhuangzi, and is also a piece for the guqin. Every day when Quanzhen disciples practice, the master of transmission plays this piece — through its nine movements, The Kun Becomes a Peng, Wings Like Trailing Clouds, Journeying Across Heaven and Earth, Soaring to the Azure Heights, Riding the Whirlwind for Ten Thousand Miles, Gliding Cool upon the Wind, Breath Settling over the Northern Sea, Might Overwhelming All Things, and Soaring Free in Vast Harmony — only once all nine are played do they conclude their exercises.
Carefree Wandering Leg Technique
Casual notes jotted down during the military career of the Dharma King of the Asura Path. What is recorded here is less a matter of martial arts than of things witnessed on the battlefield.
Blood Letters of Battle

Qingcheng is renowned for its seclusion. It boasts thirty‑six yin‑yang peaks, backed by the snow‑capped mountains. The forests are dense and verdant, with greenery persisting through all four seasons. Legend has it that in the Tang Dynasty, a wealthy merchant feared death and sought immortality. At the foot of the mountain, he asked a boy. The boy replied: It is among the trees. In the forest, he asked another boy: It's by the stream. By the stream, yet another boy said: It's on the pinnacle. After asking thirty‑six peaks in succession, he once again saw a boy. Realizing the extraordinary nature of this place, the merchant prostrated himself and said: You may instruct me. The boy smiled and said: A child can be taught. Pure cultivation need not involve hardships; humility can lead to enlightenment. After many years of solitary practice, the wealthy merchant took over as the Sect Leader and wrote this book. Its every word reflects his joyful spirit from leisurely strolls among the thirty‑six peaks, long forgotten now since he first entered the mountain.
Qingfeng Thirty‑Six Techniques

The Beggar Sect is skilled in Snake Herding. The Beggar Sect's Snake-Form Fist not only mimics the movements of a snake but also genuinely fights with live snakes. When executing punches and kicks, it must coordinate with the snakes. Besides striking with beaks, wrapping, and seizing, there is a hidden lethal move. When this technique is perfected, the snakes will suddenly burst from the sleeves to bite their targets unawares!
Snake-Form Fist

The Emei Sect's leg technique is the finest, leaping into the sky, lurking amidst the shifting clouds and waves, unpredictable in its movements. When it strikes, it is astonishing; its motion is like the thunder of the heavens, breaking through the clouds, akin to the wrath of the Thunder God, with immense power. This leg technique has no fixed forms or patterns; it is formless yet effective, representing the ultimate manifestation of Xingyi Fist. Its embodiment is the shape of heavenly thunder, known as the Thunder God Kick.
Thunder God Kick

An ancient manual written in Sanskrit, hidden beneath the Scripture Repository - had it not been for the earthquake, it might never have seen the light of day. 'Nayuta' is a Buddhist term for a number, meaning countless beyond reckoning. 'Kalpa' is the general Indian term for an age of time; after the phases of formation, existence, destruction, and emptiness, one such cycle makes a great kalpa. To practice this skill, then, one must fathom the essence of Zen, realize the state beyond birth and death, and endure endless kalpas in the flesh before attaining the Great Way.
Nayuta Kalpa Finger

The Wulin Alliance Leader Great Hero Long Yuan is known for one of his seven world‑renowned techniques: Xuanxuan Ruyi and Miao Shou Kongkong. With bare hands, he can intercept an opponent's weapon, probe a person's pocket, and succeed wherever he goes. Young Long Yuan often used this technique to pilfer others' coins during his youth. It was only when he came to realize and mature that he removed the method of stealing from the Secret Manual, shouldering the fate of the Wulin on his own.
Xuanxuan Ruyi Finger

It is said that on a day of leisure, White Ape Patriarch of Emei Sect went to seek amusement with his mountain friends. Unintentionally, he stumbled upon a scene so shocking and unforgettable that it left an indelible impression. A monkey was holding onto a white rabbit, while a snake encircled the body of the monkey. An eagle descended from the sky to attack the snake. The white rabbit managed to escape and stepped on the eagle's eye. This scene flashed before their eyes in an instant; all four creatures were greatly startled and scattered in panic. Only the White Ape Patriarch stood there stunned for a moment before returning to his quarters. For three days, he could not eat or drink, lost in thought. Finally, on the third day during breakfast time, he suddenly understood the sequence of events and stood up, demonstrating the Snake, Rabbit, Eagle, Ape Combat in front of all the disciples. Each disciple tried to understand it based on their capabilities; some grasped more than others. However, only one person mastered the Rabbit Shape Fist.
Snake, Rabbit, Eagle, Ape Combat

Originally named 'Wind and Thunder Divine Foot Technique,' it was the signature leg technique of the handsome Hero Wind God Xie Wuchen, known for his prowess in leg techniques. Unfortunately, during his challenge against the Hungry Ghost Path Dharma King Liu E, he suffered public humiliation with the 'Provoking Sword' move. Enraged and overcome by sudden anger, Xie Wuchen vomited blood and lost the battle, forcing him to rename his 'Wind-Thunder God Kick Technique' to 'Very Forceful Kick.' Very Forceful Kick is extremely fierce when used, swift in speed, like a gust of wind or thunder striking. It can crack mountain rocks with a single kick and conquer all before it; truly unparalleled in its power.
Very Forceful Kick

One of the Songshan Sect's most renowned feats of hard training, built on the Kicking Post Technique: practitioners tie sandbags to their legs and take turns kicking a wooden post a hundred times per round. Beginners kick three rounds a day - morning, noon, and evening - and as their skill deepens, ten or even twenty rounds a day becomes routine. By the hundredth day, once the sandbags come off, the legs move light and nimble while striking as fiercely as ever - the foundation is set. From there, one trains the finer techniques: spring, stamp, kick, smash, swing, point, lift, and sweep - the Eight-Word Leg Formula - each one executed with effortless mastery.
Vajra Leg
Four-Level Spear Manual
Four-Level Spear Manual

The venom techniques of the Five Poisons Cult of Miaojiang are said to be on par with those of the Tang Clan Poison Classic, each excelling in its own right and employing different pharmacological principles. Borrowing from other disciplines can provide new insights.
Secret Record of Five Poisons

A mysterious martial arts technique whose author and name have been lost over time. It is both a palm strike method and a sword technique; one can wield it with or without a sword, as long as the spirit of the sword is within their heart. The moves are exquisite but devoid of any lethal intent, seemingly intended only for personal amusement. Executed, it flows like the bright moonlight, freely and exhilaratingly.
Drunken Mystic Sword Palm

The Tao Te Ching says: Heaven and earth are not benevolent; they treat all creatures as straw dogs. Dog-Beating Fist refers to the dog not as a real dog, but rather as any enemy in this world. Whoever it is, they are treated equally, beaten like a dog. A mere pup, what should one fear? As long as one believes they will win and their momentum surpasses the other, even wolves or tigers would have to cower and run away from them.
Dog-Beating Fist

Named after Emperor Taizu, Zhao Kuangyin, this style stresses practical combat, strict forms, and agile footwork. The body coils like a cat, shudders like a tiger, flows like a wandering dragon, and strikes like lightning. Though it bears the founding emperor's name, it is in truth Songshan Fist Technique.
Taizu Long Fist

In the Songshan Temple, the monks engage in meditation and ascetic practices, needing to sever the three unwholesome roots: greed, anger, and ignorance, which are the fundamental causes of all worldly afflictions. These afflictions drive people to commit various evil deeds. To attain liberation, one must understand the five aggregates and distance themselves from inverted dreams, thus achieving ultimate nirvana. However, how many in this world can truly accomplish this? At this moment, the practice of suffering fist serves as a good temporary solution; through practicing martial arts and sweating it out, one becomes so exhausted that there is no energy left for wild thoughts.
Sorrowful Fist

This book records the original Quanzhen sword technique that Hao Datong - the Taigu Daoist - brought with him when he founded the Quanzhen Huashan Sect. Written personally by Wang Zhe, it was transcribed into seven volumes by Ma Yu, styled Danyangzi, and given to his Junior Brothers as a keepsake in memory of their master. Cultivating both Qi and swordsmanship together is difficult to learn and hard to master, profoundly deep.
Quanzhen Heavenly Escape Sword Technique

In his middle years, before he was to serve in the Hanlin Academy, Li Bai left behind this sword technique of thirty-six forms prior to sealing his sword and retiring from the world. This set of swordsmanship was demonstrated only once, before his disciple Wu E, and even then Li Bai was quite drunk. It seemed a careless, free-flowing display, yet every stroke carried a touch of genius, exquisite beyond compare - resembling a sword technique yet not quite one, breaking every ancient convention to create something never seen before. When the set was finished, he stood alone at the treetop, his robes fluttering, as if he were an immortal himself. Wu E, watching below, was drenched in sweat. It is said that Wu E, puzzled by certain difficult passages, wished to ask his master for guidance, but Li Bai only said, 'Do not ask me - if you ask, you will never learn it.' Wu E suddenly grasped the meaning and went off overjoyed, never realizing Li Bai was merely deflecting him because of his hangover.
Taibai Immortal Footprints

Ye Yunshang took the liberty to alter the stick techniques created in the Diancang Sword Manual. While lacking lethality, it filled in the unsatisfactory gaps of the Diancang Sword Technique. In terms of unexpected tactics and variations, it could be considered a clever move, though it was somewhat underhanded; a normal person would not act this way.
Diancang Staff Technique

The disciple of Diancang Sect, one in ten thousand, can enter the Sword Lodge for three days to comprehend the three sword intents left there by the Sword Saint of Diancang. Each of the three sword intents holds its own profound meaning, with no ranking between them; mastering even one is enough to stand unrivaled in the Jianghu. Yet nine times out of ten, a disciple may dwell there ten days or half a month and gain nothing at all. Driven by curiosity, Ye Yunshang slipped in to play, and was hauled back out within moments. Though she knew no martial arts, she was remarkably clever and unconventional, and in that brief moment she seemed to grasp something - only she was too young, and it passed in a daze. Today, bidding farewell, she finally tastes the flavor of parting sorrow; old memories well up in her heart, and in a flash of understanding she sets down this move. Though it is but a single stance, it carries endless lingering feeling. This sword is the Sword Saint's fourth Ultimate Move - 'The soul roams its homeland, sleeves brimming with fragrance; spring birds cry at dawn, do not linger.'
Yunshang Sword Technique

After a lifetime of practicing swordsmanship, Cangsong Swordsman Ye Yunzhou finally attained enlightenment as he bid farewell to his beloved master on Mount Fengyu. His sword strikes like rolling thunder, surpassing every swift blade of Diancang - for it is, in truth, a Tang Clan sword technique.
Sword Manual of the Same Boat

The Diancang Sect's Sword Manual focuses on lightness, softness, speed, and adaptability. Once unleashed, the sword intent flows endlessly, moving with the grace and fluidity of clouds and flowing water.
Diancang Sword Manual

The Mud Cult's Six Paths Dharma King, 'Judge' Zhao Kui's renowned ultimate technique. Its movements resemble those of spirit summoning, astonishing and unfathomable, unleashing chilling winds and a ghostly aura. Although it is a sword manual, it also contains records of talismans and other strange arts, making it quite eerie. In truth, how can righteousness and evil be judged by appearances? It all resides in one's heart! With my righteous Qi strong, why should I worry about the idle gossip of the world? Unfazed, I exude an aura of authority, like Zhong Kui reborn, wielding a three‑foot Celestial Master Sword, vowing not to rest until I vanquish all demons and evils.
Celestial Master Sword Technique

Fang Zhentian, the junior alliance leader of Jingjiang Nine Counties, became famous for a unique skill in blade art. Originally, it was Unorthodox Weapons that required the use of an iron hammer and nails together. By chance, Fang Zhentian obtained this technique, claiming it was his painstakingly created exclusive martial art. To avoid giving away its secrets, he changed the original mallet techniques into Blade Techniques, omitting the nail methods altogether. As a result, many of the moves became confusing and had significant flaws.
Pangu Opens Heaven and Breaks the Earth
Pine Wind Sword Technique
Pine Wind Sword Technique

Qingcheng Sect's unique sword technique, handed down from the Eastern Han Daoist Zhang Ling and blending the teachings of Zhengyi Daoism. It emphasizes commanding the sword with one's qi and seeking the Way within the blade, its path clear and righteous, cutting down demons and subduing evil.
Three‑Five Demon‑Slaying Sword

The Qingcheng Secret Manual outlines a solo formation based on the eight gates' directions, celestial phenomena, and terrain as described in Qimen Dunjia. By deconstructing and simplifying this formation and integrating it into blade techniques, it transforms into the Eight Gates Locking Gold Blade, full of exquisite intricacies.
Eight Gates Locking Gold Blade

When Emei was still a Sword School, the ancient body cultivation methods passed down had simplified complex techniques into broad and open forms. Despite their straightforward appearance, these methods were anything but simple; they retained strategic flexibility even in their brute force aspects, allowing for room to maneuver. The Eight Slash Technique might seem ordinary, yet it significantly bolstered physical strength and helped stretch and strengthen one's muscles and bones.
Firewood Blade Eight Slashes

This sword technique was first drafted by Confucius himself, a swordsmanship taught to his disciples alongside mounted archery. Later, as Confucius traveled from state to state, he gathered sword techniques from the Seven States and refined them continually. After his death, it passed through dynasty after dynasty, each age honing it further, embodying the hexagram's meaning: 'As Heaven's movement is ever vigorous, so the gentleman ceaselessly strengthens himself'—resolute and unyielding, never at rest. Conducting oneself with reverence, contending with none, favoring neither this nor that, unshakeable when great principles are at stake—this is called the sword of humility and harmony, the gentleman's sword.
Confucius Sword

It requires the use of both Blade and Sword to be effective. The name is grandiose, but the moves themselves seem flashy and hollow, relying on momentum for a series of chaotic slashes. Surprisingly, many people fall for this.
Heaven-Slaying Black Wing Twin Dragon Sword

A combined-strike technique developed through secluded study by a devoted couple, one from Emei and one from the Tang Clan. One wields the fist while the other wields the sword, each complementing the other in perfect harmony, like a lute and zither in tune—the more closely their hearts are joined, the greater the power. You have the manual, but you lack a partner.
Mandarin Duck Fist and Sword Manual

The renowned Confucian hero Mr. Zeng Wen wrote this work, distilling the Four Books, the Five Classics, and the Thirteen Classics. It holds that a gentleman is watchful even in solitude, that the heart shows itself in conduct and knowledge takes form in ritual, that he is neither arrogant nor servile, and that his words and deeds are one. Let the months and stars turn as they will; let mountains and rivers change hands as they may—I hold fast to my own heart and cultivate myself. However good the world, I am still only myself; however wicked the age, I am still only myself. And should I shed this mortal frame, it would remain so. All of us who study the sword and the martial arts must guard our true heart, take the sword's two edges as a mirror, never be ashamed to ask and always seek the answer within ourselves, stay humble yet never cease striving, feel no dread in hardship, remain watchful even at feasts and revels, and show no fear before the powerful. This is the Gentleman's Sword.
Gentleman Discusses Swordsmanship

The martial arts practiced by Cang Gang disciples active in the Fujian region. The Cang Gang has the backing of the Shangguan Family—a secret everyone knows but never speaks of. Even their Surging Wave Blade Technique evolved from a Shangguan family blade style, now wielded with oars and sculls instead, which only draws more attention to its origins. When unleashed, this blade technique surges like river waves, wave after wave without end: against a weaker foe it presses on relentlessly, against a stronger one it holds back and waits. An enemy who resists with all their strength only grasps at empty air, and the moment an opening shows, the next wave crashes in. Hardness within softness, softness within hardness, offense within defense, defense within offense—it is a blade technique of the highest order. But learning it with an oar, you're bound to pick up all the wrong habits.
Surging Wave Blade Technique

The profound sword techniques of the Diancang Sect shine like shooting stars, rushing forth with unstoppable momentum. They do not seek elegance, only instant release. Delving into the essence of the swift sword, body and sword unite, intention and action advance together, so fast that even shadows cannot keep up with their agility. Plant the Feet, Draw the Bow, Release. Regardless of their form, one cannot stray from these three Mental Formulas. Their speed is like an arrow leaving the bowstring, arriving in an instant, capable of deceiving the enemy in a heartbeat; if they do not succeed, they will sacrifice themselves for the cause.
Meteor Sword Manual

Created by the great hero Lei Zhan of the previous dynasty, it is named with great power. The techniques are also straightforward and unambiguous, each move wide and expansive, as if truly embodying the momentum of thunder striking from the heavens. At the moment of drawing the blade, it is accompanied by a roar that pierces the air, shattering the enemy's protective energy.
Cloud Sky Thunderbolt Blade

The classic hard qigong of the Songshan Sect is the specialty of the Eighteen Bronze Men of Songshan Temple. The Golden Bell Shield cultivates both internal and external strength, fortifying the muscles and bones externally while solidifying the organs internally. Those who achieve mastery have bodies akin to bronze and iron; even when struck by fists and kicks, they feel neither pain nor discomfort.
Golden Bell Shield

Renowned across the land, the Songshan finger technique draws from the anecdote of Shakyamuni Holding a Flower and Kasyapa Smiling. Nirvanic wondrous heart, ineffable and difficult to describe in words, formless and shapeless, beyond comprehension. The profundity and subtlety of this Martial Learning can only be grasped by those with wisdom.
Flower-Twirling Finger Technique

The secret manual of the Flying Stone Gang is a unique hidden weapon technique taught to the gang leader by a master during their youth. It is said that when practiced to perfection, one can strike the surface of calm water with a flying stone, bouncing it eighty‑eight times.
Throwing Stones to Question Heaven

The Tang Clan disciples each possess a martial arts manual that ranks alongside the 'Poison Classic' as one of the two treasures. Without guidance from mentors to teach the Mental Formula and force application, self‑study would be immensely challenging, making progress virtually impossible. You have already memorized the opening section, 'On Forgetting Form.'
Hidden Weapon General Principles

Records the messy days you spent knocking about in the Tang Clan. You write in it whenever you have time. It's already quite filthy, and a few pages are missing—torn out back then when you had no toilet paper in an urgent moment.
Your Diary

Okay
No need to say more; I'll stay and see it through.

Do what one can, then leave the rest to Heaven. Didn't the Sect Leader always say so? A true hero is never swayed by fame or fortune, and asks only to face Heaven and earth without shame. Even with the end already in sight, we must stand tall and walk this road to its finish.
That was the past — it's only because you lot never treated outsider disciples as people, ordering me around day after day. So why haven't you left either, Third Senior Brother?
The person you admired is no longer here. Didn't you always say that if the Tang Clan didn't have the Junior Martial Sister, you wouldn't want to stay even for a moment?
......Don't try to talk me into coming down the mountain, hiding my identity, and merely surviving, okay?
I have something to say to you ‑ not as the acting sect leader, but as Third Senior Brother.
What's going on?
—Junior Brother.
Sigh, I'm just deceiving myself, otherwise, what else can I do?
It's great that you can think this way.
Fortunately the Junior Martial Sister has already married out and is safe — at least her life won't be thrown away here for nothing.

True, even though this feud began as a misunderstanding, our sect let the moment to clear its name slip by. Since then we've cut down countless good people and made bitter enemies of every faction — we can no longer call ourselves wronged.
After the Wulin Assembly, we were branded a branch of the Demon Cult outright. Not even leaping into the Yellow River could wash us clean — there was no chance to argue our case.
Exactly
They are gathering strength, preparing to annihilate the Tang Clan in one swift move.

Wulin Alliance...... hmm, I remember, they are the alliance of the Wulin's Five Sects, Three Palaces, and Two Great Gangs. Once established, they acted swiftly and resolutely, sweeping through various branches of the Demon Cult across different regions. Last year, they eradicated the Underworld of the Demon Cult; now.......
Junior Brother, do you still remember the Wulin Alliance? Do you recall what kind of threat our sect is currently facing?

It sounds like a joke; this is clearly the scenario I used to fantasize about every day. When I was still an outer disciple, I often imagined that one day I would stand out and possess great martial arts. But in the blink of an eye, here I am today, and I am not happy at all.

Don't say something so discouraging where the junior disciples can hear. You're no longer the outsider disciple you once were — the Tang Clan never taught you its true arts, yet you found your own extraordinary fortune. Now you are truly a pillar of this sect.

Venerable Golden Crow? The one from the Kongtong Sect?
I actually managed to beat him? That's downright bizarre.
One day, not long after you finished your meal, you fell asleep. I thought you were just tired, but unexpectedly, you slept for three days and three nights.

...Recently you fought on our sect's behalf against Venerable Golden Crow of the Kongtong Sect and narrowly won, but he struck your head hard with his signature weapon, the Blazing Sun Hammer. At first it seemed no serious harm was done, but his True Qi crept into your body, leaving you dazed and half-dreaming all day long.

I remember everything, but it feels hazy, almost like a dream that isn't quite real, as if I am reading someone else's story. It seems that from today onward, I am beginning to take over the life that someone else has lived.
The Junior Martial Sister married a rising young hero. On her joyous day, I hid under the quilt and cried like a woman.
The sect leader is paralyzed and bedridden, and Third Senior Brother has been appointed as the acting sect leader in this critical moment.
Eldest Senior Brother and Second Senior Brother are both no longer here.
Yeah, that's right — I remember it all now.
A little exercise gets the blood flowing — your head must feel a lot clearer now, doesn't it?
Heh, I certainly didn't go easy on you.
Third Senior Brother, even if you were feeding the move, you went a bit easy on me, didn't you?
It seems you haven't fully recovered yet, Junior Brother. We'll have to proceed gradually with your rehabilitation.
No problem, no problem. Think of it as a way to flex our muscles and bones. Let's go.

Third Senior Brother, even if you mean to coach me, wouldn't doing it in broad daylight at the training ground draw too much attention?
After all, you know outsider disciples aren't allowed the true teachings.
No, it's precisely because of the current situation that we must do this. Let's go.
Isn't this not the time for that!
...Junior Brother, we haven't sparred in a while. Want to go to the Training Ground and exchange some moves?
Two years ago? You're not pulling my leg, are you?
Junior Brother, that was two years ago already. Are you still fogged up from sleep?
Acting Sect Leader? Third Senior Brother, you... you became the Sect Leader? I remember you said just yesterday you didn't want to be the Sect Leader--mmph.
You go out first
